content: ABSTRACT Sustainable finance (SF) has increasingly been conceptualized in the literature as a mechanism linking firm‐level ESG practices to broader sustainable development outcomes. However, the field remains theoretically fragmented, with limited integrated mapping of micro–SF–macro linkages. Using scientometric and bibliometric techniques, this study analyzes 1,024 Scopus‐indexed publications (2004–2025) through performance analysis, keyword co‐occurrence, text mining, and bibliographic coupling. Thirteen keyword clusters reveal the intellectual structure of the field, spanning green finance, ESG performance, governance, climate policy, and energy transition. Bibliographic coupling identifies six thematic clusters that suggest how sustainable finance is theorized to link firm‐level actions with macro‐level sustainability transformations. Despite rapid post–Paris Agreement growth, theoretical and methodological coherence remains limited. The study outlines future research directions, emphasizing disclosure harmonization, causal identification, innovation–policy alignment, and multi‐level approaches. Accordingly, the findings capture patterns in the literature rather than empirically verified causal relationships.

title: Centralized versus conventional anaerobic digestion of sewage sludge: An environmental and economic assessment
summary: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and
content: High-solid anaerobic digestion (HSAD), in which dewatered sewage sludge from several small wastewater treatment plants is treated centrally, is an alternative to conventional low-solid anaerobic digestion (LSAD) for sludge stabilization and energy recovery from biogas. This work develops a modelling framework to compare centralized HSAD and decentralized LSAD through a coupled life cycle assessment (LCA) and economic analysis approach, supporting case-specific decision-making for sludge management under defined local boundary conditions. Four different sub-scenarios were modeled for both HSAD (S1.1-S1.4) and LSAD (S2.1-S2.4), forecasting different biogas uses, alternative sludge transportation routes, digestate valorization pathways, and ammonia extraction. The sub-scenarios were compared with the respective baselines (S1.0 for HSAD and S2.0 for LSAD), corresponding to full-scale Italian plant configurations. Under the investigated full-scale conditions, HSAD showed lower environmental impacts than conventional LSAD when transport distances were limited, due to higher credits generated by biogas and the avoided mineral fertilizer use in agriculture. However, input sludge/digestate transportation is a dominant driver of both environmental and economic impacts. Moreover, biogas upgrading to biomethane is environmentally preferable to electricity generation, but economically unfavourable at current market conditions. Overall, centralized HSAD can represent a favorable solution under regional-scale planning when logistics, digestate valorization, and gate-fee conditions are suitable, whereas optimized LSAD with dynamic sludge thickening can achieve comparable performance. Although the specific results are related to an Italian case study, this work provides a useful tool for decision-making among alternative sludge management solutions when local boundary conditions (sludge characteristics, transportation distances, HSAD/LSAD plant availability) are specified.

title: ACCOUNTING, ANALYTICAL, AND FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR SUSTAINABLE ECONOMIC GROWTH AMIDST DEMOGRAPHIC DECLINE
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: The study clarifies the essence of the theoretical and methodological regulation of the analytical, accounting, financial, and social aspects of supporting stable economic growth amidst a demographic decline. It specifies that a shrinking t
content: The study clarifies the essence of the theoretical and methodological regulation of the analytical, accounting, financial, and social aspects of supporting stable economic growth amidst a demographic decline. It specifies that a shrinking total population and rising unemployment necessitate a revision of the traditional economic growth model one that incorporates the need to sustain labor productivity and investment, mobilize financial resources, and comprehensively retrain personnel. A methodology is detailed for ranking factors that allow for the analysis of how demographic variables, workforce efficiency, and production output influence the integrated performance indicator of a business entity. The study defines the nature and significance of demographic growth, which fundamentally shapes the future trajectories of the national economy's sustainable socio-economic development. It establishes critical thresholds for a demographic crisis; exceeding these limits indicates the state's inability to offset demographic losses and signals a sustained decline in productivity across specific economic sectors. The proposed thresholds are conceptual and methodological in nature and require further empirical justification on the basis of statistical data. The methodology for the financial and accounting assessment of costs associated with maintaining demographic resources, specifically through the mobilization of additional capital required to sustain employment levels, is elaborated in detail. The concept of compensating for demographic costs is further developed, offering a means to mitigate negative demographic trends within society. Three scenarios are proposed, demonstrating the extent to which demographic costs can be offset by labor productivity without causing economic imbalances. It is noted that an increase in labor productivity should not automatically be viewed as a sign of improved economic efficiency.Therefore, it is appropriate to distinguish between overall growth in labor productivity and the surplus productivity gain that remains after the requirements for demographic compensation have been met. Ultimately, the proposed methodology establishes the necessary foundation for implementing effective financial-analytical management aimed at curbing demographic decline while creating the conditions for demographic compensation.

title: Unravelling the non-linear Impact of Energy Diversification on CO2 Emissions: Evidence from Emerging Economies
source: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
summary: Global warming is a global issue. Goal 13 of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations (UN) emphasizes the reduction of carbon emissions. Fossil fuel energy is a major source of carbon emissions. A transition to a clean
content: Global warming is a global issue. Goal 13 of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) of the United Nations (UN) emphasizes the reduction of carbon emissions. Fossil fuel energy is a major source of carbon emissions. A transition to a cleaner energy mix can be helpful, however, this dynamic is less explored. Therefore, this study assesses the nonlinear effect of energy diversification on carbon emissions in case of emerging economies including Brazil, India, Russia, Turkiye, China, Mexico and Indonesia. These countries are among the highest polluters. Results suggest that a significant U-shaped relation prevails between carbon emissions and energy diversification. An initial increase in energy diversification lowers the carbon 443emissions. This relation reverses at very high levels of energy diversification. After a certain threshold point, further increase in energy diversification increases the carbon emissions. Growth, trade openness and urbanization are among the other significant contributing factors. Dataset spanning from 1991-2023 is used for estimation. Results of the study suggest a careful selection of energy mix to optimally handle the issue of carbon emissions.

title: Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
summary: Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In
content: Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.

title: When carbon counts differ: the complexities of biogenic carbon accounting in BECCUS and why accounting choices matter
summary: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for s
content: Bioenergy with Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (BECCUS) is an important pathway towards net-zero and net-negative emissions. Its mitigation potential depends on net atmospheric CO2 removal into durable storage after accounting for system-wide emissions and removals. However, lifecycle assessment, national greenhouse gas inventories and carbon-market frameworks apply differing accounting approaches, producing divergent mitigation estimates. This study identifies key sources of variability and examines their influence on reported outcomes through a systematic literature review and illustrative calculations for a hypothetical BECCUS system. Depending on the accounting approach, the net system outcome ranges from +422 kt CO2 (net-emitting) to −2,084 kt CO2 (net-reducing), while reported carbon removal ranges from 0 to −1,688 kt CO2. These deviations arise from four interconnected sources: (1) goals and framing, including definitions of concepts, terms and carbon flows; (2) methodological and analytical choices; (3) scope and system boundaries; and (4) baselines and counterfactuals. Governance, monitoring, reporting and verification, and crediting frameworks further shape these sources. Reported outcomes therefore vary primarily because of accounting choices rather than technical performance. The study calls for better alignment of existing methodologies and frameworks so that BECCUS accounting reflects atmospheric outcomes and supports credible climate mitigation.

title: Multi-scale haplotype signatures distinguish among evolutionary processes
summary: Natural selection embeds distinct genomic signatures as populations adapt to environmental pressures. Machine learning approaches, particularly deep neural networks, have emerged as powerful tools to detect adaptive signatures from genomic
content: Natural selection embeds distinct genomic signatures as populations adapt to environmental pressures. Machine learning approaches, particularly deep neural networks, have emerged as powerful tools to detect adaptive signatures from genomic data. While machine learning has dramatically improved our ability to extract these signals from sequence variation, distinguishing among multiple evolutionary processes remains challenging. We introduce SHADES, a deep learning framework that employs information about sequence differences and their frequencies at various spatial resolutions to capture evolutionary signatures at different genomic scales. We found that SHADES has the capacity to distinguish among neutrality, selective sweeps, balancing selection, and adaptive introgression and outperformed several contemporary methods evaluated for both classification accuracy and power. In addition, SHADES remained robust to a number of confounding factors, with only modest changes in classification performance. Furthermore, application of SHADES to empirical haplotypic variation from European humans recovered previously reported signals for selective sweeps, balancing selection, and adaptive introgression, while also identifying novel genes broadly involved in immune defense, inflammatory regulation, and epithelial barrier biology.

title: Spatial and vertical variability of soil physico‐hydraulic properties and subsurface lithology in the Upper Indus Plain of Pakistan
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of soil physico‐hydraulic properties is critical for irrigation and drainage design, solute transport, soil–water–plant, and rainfall–runoff relationships. However, spatially representative datasets for th
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of soil physico‐hydraulic properties is critical for irrigation and drainage design, solute transport, soil–water–plant, and rainfall–runoff relationships. However, spatially representative datasets for these properties remain limited for the Indus Basin of Pakistan, where hydrological studies often rely on generalized parameters derived from other regions, introducing uncertainties in model‐based assessments. This study presents a basin‐scale integrated assessment of soil texture, bulk density, infiltration behavior, and soil moisture retention characteristics covering the Upper Indus Plain of Pakistan. Field‐based in situ measurements were conducted at 66 spatially distributed sites across four doabs (area between the two rivers) at surface, 0.5‐m, and 1.0‐m depths. An integrated methodological framework was employed, combining hydrometer analysis for soil texture, improved double‐ring infiltrometer tests for infiltration, pressure‐plate extractor for soil water retention, oven‐dried weight for bulk density, and resistivity survey for subsurface lithological assessment. Infiltration datasets were analyzed using the Horton and Philip cumulative infiltration models, while soil water retention behavior was quantified using hanging water column and pressure plate methods and parameterized using the van Genuchten model. Results indicate that the Horton infiltration model outperformed the Philip model for estimation of cumulative infiltration. Silty clay loam, sandy loam, and silt loam are the dominant texture classes. The soil with infiltration rates up to 30 mm/h remain predominant across the study area. This study provides robust and accurate baseline datasets along with an integrated methodological framework to support basin‐scale improved hydrological modeling, flood simulations, recharge estimation, and effective water resource management.

title: Erosion carbon dynamics extend beyond carbon accounting to ecological significance
summary: Abstract For decades, the debate over whether erosion acts as a carbon source or sink has advanced our understanding of carbon redistribution across stocks and fluxes. Yet, this quantitative perspective alone does not capture the full ecolo
content: Abstract For decades, the debate over whether erosion acts as a carbon source or sink has advanced our understanding of carbon redistribution across stocks and fluxes. Yet, this quantitative perspective alone does not capture the full ecological significance of carbon along these pathways. Carbon value lies not only in how much is stored, but also in how it functions within ecosystems. Erosion is not merely a switch governing land–atmosphere carbon exchange, but also a driver redistributing carbon among ecological states. Here, a framework is developed that interprets erosion as a reorganization of the soil functional layer, linking carbon redistribution to changes in stability and functionality across landscape contexts. This perspective helps explain the paradox in erosion management, whereby processes that reduce carbon burial may simultaneously enhance ecosystem functioning. It reframes carbon redistribution from changes in carbon stocks to shifts in ecological states, with implications for carbon accounting and ecosystem management.

title: Water‐Heat Synergistic Regulation to Optimize Water State and Enhance Thermal Effect in Solar Interfacial Evaporation
summary: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This w
content: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven interfacial evaporation is a promising solution to the global freshwater shortage. However, current evaporation systems typically suffer from low water management efficiency and poor interfacial thermal effects. This work proposes a strategy to synergistically enhance the heat and mass transport of solar interfacial evaporators by balancing water transport capacity and water activity and reverse heat compensation. A higher proportion of loosely bound intermediate water (IW) with low enthalpy of vaporization is induced by in situ construction of a hydrophilic micron‐to‐submicron hierarchical pore structure within the wood‐based biomass framework, while maintaining its water pumping capacity. Simultaneously, a biomimetic thermal compensation mechanism significantly enhances the thermal effect of the wood‐based biomass evaporation interface (temperature up to 50.7°C). This synergistic design enables a record evaporation rate of 5.12 kg m −2 h −1 in wood‐based evaporators. Furthermore, the vertically distributed hierarchical pore structure and surface polar groups endow it with excellent salt repellency and antifouling capabilities. This reported water‐heat management strategy provides a scalable, low‐cost, and environmentally friendly approach to highly efficient solar interfacial evaporation.

title: How sustainable finance initiatives and forums address environmental issues, including climate change, and the challenges they face
summary: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles an
content: Abstract An increasing number of transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums are focusing on shifting and mobilizing private finance. Consequently, it has become more difficult to grasp the big picture concerning their roles and effects, including how they overlap and synergize. This study examined how transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums contribute to scaling up private finance and investment and encourage private sector participation. It also explored the challenges that they face in achieving climate-related and other environmental goals. To assess the effectiveness and legitimacy of transnational governance, the institutional and actor-related dimensions and impacts of five major United Nations-related transnational sustainable finance initiatives and forums were analyzed using an analytical framework that included the following elements: transparency, accountability, participation, environmental and other societal impacts, and academic and practical literature. This study showed that each of these initiatives and forums differed in its governing structure and approaches, as well as in its relationship with United Nations-related institutions and actors. Furthermore, overlapping institutions and actors were involved across initiatives and forums, with areas of collaboration between them. While each initiative successfully engaged diverse actors, common challenges emerged, including difficulty in evaluating and enhancing the effectiveness of transnational initiatives and forums, the need for effective links among transnational initiatives and other governance systems (e.g., effective institutional and actor interplay between these voluntary initiatives and compulsory interventions), and the need to include diverse actors. This study showed that more research is required to explore ways of evaluating and enhancing transnational governance of voluntary multistakeholder initiatives and to address the above challenges.

title: Transformational Research on the Existing Traditional Manufacturing OEM Enterprises' Transformation Path under Excess Capacity: Quantitative Empirical Research Based on the Textile Printing and Dyeing Industry
summary: China's state-owned enterprise (OEM) enterprises in textile printing and dyeing industry face persistent overcapacity and tightened environment protection regulation, and various small and middle OEMs are trapped in a dilemma of price taker
content: China's state-owned enterprise (OEM) enterprises in textile printing and dyeing industry face persistent overcapacity and tightened environment protection regulation, and various small and middle OEMs are trapped in a dilemma of price taker (e.g. low bargaining power, narrow margins and lack of transformation momentum). The study collects data (for the years of 2010–2023) from China Industry Statistical Yearbook, China Environmental Statistical Yearbook, Wind database, constructs a panel and uses descriptive statistic, group comparison, correlation analysis and fixed-effects regression to check the logic of dropping the price competition game and entering the value competition game. The results demonstrate: (1) capacity utilization is highly and positively correlated with the profit rate, and overcapacity is a main factor for the drop in profit; (2)R&D intensity has a positive and significant effect on the company profit rate, but with a "transformation threshold effect", such as R&D transforming into profit only if the capacity utilization is more than about 0.70; (3) too large concentration of the customers decreases bargaining force and inhibits transformation; (4)moderate environmental regulation encourages upgrading and is consistent with Porter hypothesis. From the results above, the paper proposes a three-dimensional path for equipment iteration and process upgrade, customer structure optimization and migration toward value competition, which provides evidence for OEM enterprises' escape from "dilemma lock-in" and to regulators' designing policies based on issues, respectively.

title: Biotechnologies and Bioeconomics: How to Increase Resource Efficiency, Reduce Emissions, and Strengthen Energy Security (Comparing the United States, China, and the EU)
summary: The objective of the research is the national models of bioeconomics development in the three largest economies of the world. The subject of the study is the quantitative relationship between the level of biotechnology development, resource
content: The objective of the research is the national models of bioeconomics development in the three largest economies of the world. The subject of the study is the quantitative relationship between the level of biotechnology development, resource efficiency, dynamics of greenhouse gas emissions reduction, and the degree of energy independence of regions. The aim of this study is an empirical assessment of progress in the development of bioeconomics over the period 2020-2030 and the identification of regional leaders for each of the key indicators. However, bioengineering has become not only a technical field but also one of the key drivers of sustainable technological progress, with which we move towards a bio- circular economy. Microorganisms and genetically modified bacteria have reshaped and revolutionized the modern energy sector. Some key features of bioengineering make it even more valuable for the traditional energy sector: it is available now, applicable in all energy sectors (electricity, direct heat, transport), readily integrated with existing infrastructure, storable, and can support the expansion of intermittent renewables. One of the most important features is that it is capable of delivering negative emissions when linked to Carbon Capture & Storage (CCS). The methodological basis of the study is economic modeling based on OECD data presented in the Bioeconomy to 2030 report through the construction of three-dimensional regression surfaces, radar diagrams, and change matrices. China demonstrated the highest growth rates of all indicators of the bioeconomy (resource efficiency +86.2%, investment +125.8%, and bioenergy +204.2% over the decade). The United States remains the leader in terms of absolute resource efficiency−3.83% of GDP and investments −36.47 billion dollars. The European Union is the undisputed leader in environmental efficiency, with emissions of 2.90 billion tons, a 25.7% reduction, and a 14.0% share of bioenergy in the energy mix. In this study, we aimed to examine bioengineering technologies, their contribution to the transformation of global energy systems and development of a sustainable economy, and the economic and political barriers, using a multidisciplinary approach that integrates biological sciences, bioengineering, and economics.

title: An explainable graph learning framework for carbon footprint prediction: Integrating SHAP-based policy insights and country similarity networks
summary: Accurate prediction of carbon footprint dynamics is essential for climate policy design and sustainable development planning, yet complex nonlinear interactions among energy systems, environmental factors, and socioeconomic activities make
content: Accurate prediction of carbon footprint dynamics is essential for climate policy design and sustainable development planning, yet complex nonlinear interactions among energy systems, environmental factors, and socioeconomic activities make estimation challenging. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated framework combining machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and graph neural networks to predict carbon footprints across 27 European countries from 2015 to 2023. Evaluating several algorithms revealed that tree-based models substantially outperformed linear approaches, with LightGBM achieving the highest machine learning performance. SHAP analyses identified fossil fuel dependency, municipal waste generation, environmental impacts, protection capacity, and climate initiatives as the primary predictive determinants. Furthermore, incorporating a country similarity network into Graph Neural Network architectures improved predictive accuracy, with the Graph Attention Network (GAT) delivering the overall best predictive performance. Robustness checks confirmed model stability across various configurations, demonstrating that carbon footprint formation is driven by both national indicators and structural cross-country relationships. Ultimately, this framework bridges a methodological gap in environmental forecasting, offering robust predictive tools for policymakers and actionable, feature-level insights for targeted climate mitigation strategies.

title: ENERGY RESOURCE MANAGEMENT IN THE STRATEGIC PLANNING OF REGIONS IN SLOVAKIA: WIND ENERGY DIMENSION
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: The transition towards a low-carbon and energy-secure economy makes effective energy resource management an increasingly important component of strategic regional planning. In this context, the development of renewable energy sources, inclu
content: The transition towards a low-carbon and energy-secure economy makes effective energy resource management an increasingly important component of strategic regional planning. In this context, the development of renewable energy sources, including wind energy, can contribute not only to decarbonisation but also to the sustainable economic development, energy security, and competitiveness of regions. This issue is particularly relevant for Slovakia, where the potential of wind energy remains largely underutilised despite the country’s commitments to increase the share of renewable energy sources and achieve climate neutrality by 2050. The slow development of wind energy is associated with administrative and permitting procedures, regulatory and institutional constraints, spatial planning challenges, environmental and social considerations, and insufficient integration of renewable energy development into regional strategic planning. The aim of the study is to assess the role of wind energy resource management in the strategic planning and sustainable development of regions in Slovakia, identify the main barriers limiting its effective integration into regional energy systems, and formulate recommendations for improving regional and national approaches to wind energy development. The study analyses relevant strategic and policy documents concerning the Slovak electricity sector and renewable energy development, examines the current state of wind energy development, and considers the planned trajectories for increasing wind power capacity towards 2030 and the longer-term decarbonisation objectives. The results indicate that the limited development of wind energy in Slovakia cannot be explained solely by the availability of technical potential. Institutional fragmentation, lengthy permitting procedures, spatial and environmental constraints, limited regional coordination, and insufficient integration of energy considerations into regional development planning represent significant barriers. The study also demonstrates that more effective management of wind energy resources can support regional energy security, diversification of energy supplies, local economic development, and progress towards decarbonisation. The study concludes that accelerating wind energy development in Slovakia requires closer integration of energy resource management with regional strategic planning. Strengthening institutional coordination, simplifying permitting procedures, improving spatial planning mechanisms, and establishing clearer regional and national development frameworks could facilitate the sustainable utilisation of wind energy potential and contribute to the long-term development of Slovak regions.

title: Anti‐Dissolution Tungsten Alloying Stabilizes Highly Active Platinum for Industrial‐Grade Hydrogen Evolution
summary: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolu
content: ABSTRACT Platinum‐based alloys remain the most promising electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet suffer from activity‐stability trade‐offs, particularly in alkaline media where Pt‐Ni alloys undergo continuous dissolution. Herein, we report the rational design of intermetallic Pt 2 W alloy nanoparticles uniformly anchored on N‐doped carbon nanomeshes (N‐CM), leveraging tungsten's exceptional thermodynamic stability and corrosion resistance to address this dilemma. Systematic compositional optimization reveals that Pt 2 W/N‐CM delivers superior alkaline HER performance, achieving an ultralow overpotential of 7 mV at 10 mA cm −2 and outperforming both Pt‐Ni analogues and commercial Pt/C. Critically, the catalyst exhibits unprecedented long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for 200 h at an industrial‐grade high current density of 800 mA cm −2 . Combined theoretical and experimental analyses elucidate that W fulfills a cooperative trifunction whereby oxophilic sites markedly lower the kinetic barrier for water dissociation while directional electron transfer downshifts the Pt d ‐band center to optimize hydrogen adsorption. Simultaneously, the intrinsic anti‐dissolution property of W fundamentally suppresses active site degradation under harsh HER conditions, establishing a structural self‐stabilization mechanism. This work demonstrates that leveraging corrosion‐resistant tungsten enables a structurally self‐stabilizing and highly active Pt 2 W electrocatalyst for industrial alkaline water electrolysis.

title: Do Investors Price Different Types of Climate Risk Disclosure? Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
source: International Journal of Economics and Finance
summary: Do investors price all climate risk disclosures in the same way? Using annual report texts and financial data for Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2024, this paper estimates the valuation effect of different types of climate risk d
content: Do investors price all climate risk disclosures in the same way? Using annual report texts and financial data for Chinese A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2024, this paper estimates the valuation effect of different types of climate risk disclosures on Tobin’s Q. We decompose aggregate climate risk into transition risk, acute physical risk, and chronic physical risk, and use within-firm changes in disclosure while controlling for firm and year fixed effects. Firms with higher climate risk disclosure have lower Tobin’s Q, but this valuation discount is not driven equally by all risk components. The most stable discount is concentrated in chronic physical risk; transition risk provides weaker auxiliary evidence, while acute physical risk does not exhibit stable negative pricing. Further evidence shows that chronic physical risk disclosure predicts higher subsequent R&D intensity and asset impairment ratio. Its negative valuation effect is stronger among firms with a higher fixed asset ratio, and weaker among firms with higher current asset and accounts receivable ratios. High-intensity chronic physical risk disclosure also generates a larger discount and predicts Tobin’s Q within the subsequent one‑to‑two‑year window. The fixed-effects evidence supports the interpretation that capital markets place greater weight on chronic physical risk, which captures persistent exposure, asset lock-in, and long-term adjustment costs.

title: Selenocarbonyl Synthetic Strategies, Molecular Diversification, and Applications of C═Se‐Containing Compounds
summary: ABSTRACT Selenocarbonyl compounds are an important class of organoselenium compounds with unique reactivity, distinct electronic properties, and versatile biological activities. This review critically summarizes the main synthetic methods f
content: ABSTRACT Selenocarbonyl compounds are an important class of organoselenium compounds with unique reactivity, distinct electronic properties, and versatile biological activities. This review critically summarizes the main synthetic methods for C═Se derivatives, including selenoamides, selenoformamides, selenoureas, selenocarbamates, isoselenocyanates, and selenosemicarbazones. It covers both classical selenium‐transfer reagents (Woollins’ reagent, phosphorus pentaselenide, LiAlHSeH, metal selenides, selenium dioxide, potassium selenocyanate, and elemental selenium) and recent one‐pot, multicomponent, and nucleophilic strategies. Rather than treating the literature as a chronological catalogue, the discussion is organized around shared selenium sources, reactive intermediates, and downstream functions, and explicitly compares reaction conditions, substrate scope, isolated yields, operational simplicity, product stability, safety, and scalability. The review further describes applications in selenium‐containing heterocycles, metal complexes, bioactive molecules, supramolecular systems, and functional materials, highlighting reported anticancer, antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti‐inflammatory, and enzyme‐inhibitory activities. A dedicated discussion of 7 7 Se NMR spectroscopy clarifies how selenium chemical shifts connect molecular structure, electronic properties, and coordination behavior. Despite notable progress, many existing methods still rely on toxic or moisture‐sensitive reagents, strong bases, elevated temperatures, or tedious purification, and biological and materials‐related applications remain largely underexplored. Future research should focus on safer selenium sources, simpler scalable reactions, improved product stability, and better integration of molecular design with practical application.

title: Event management as a tool for implementing the strategy of sustainable development of an industrial enterprise
source: Vestnik of Samara State University of Economics
summary: The growing demands from the government, investors and society for environmental and social responsibility are forcing industrial enterprises to reconsider their strategies. They are increasingly turning to event management in search of eff
content: The growing demands from the government, investors and society for environmental and social responsibility are forcing industrial enterprises to reconsider their strategies. They are increasingly turning to event management in search of effective tools. This article uses the example of Russian companies to demonstrate how event practices help achieve sustainable development goals. The study is based on the analysis of practical cases of SIBUR, Samotlorneftegaz, IC Absolut Insurance, SEZ Avangard and the industry initiatives of the National Congress Bureau. The methodological base includes the study of corporate reports, press releases and expert publications. A lot of enterprises still perceive events as one-time actions, as a result of which they miss their systemic potential. Successful events can stimulate to review internal work processes, especially if they concern the issues of environmental safety or social support for staff. The results demonstrate that event management can be used to certify carbon neutrality, implement ESG principles, form a corporate culture and increase investment attractiveness. The conclusion is made about the need for a systematic approach to the integration of event-based practices into the strategy of sustainable development of industrial enterprises.

title: From Compliance Costs to Value Creation Mechanisms Linking AI to Competitive Advantage in Green Manufacturing among Guangdong Enterprises
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Abstract: Against the backdrop of China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals and the growing application of artificial intelligence (AI), this study examines how AI helps listed companies in Guangdong translate green compliance into
content: Abstract: Against the backdrop of China's carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals and the growing application of artificial intelligence (AI), this study examines how AI helps listed companies in Guangdong translate green compliance into competitive advantage. Drawing on annual reports from Midea, Gree, and TCL and relevant policy documents, it identifies three findings. First, AI reduces waste through energy consumption forecasting and process optimization, allowing efficiency gains to offset compliance costs. Second, its integration with green factories improves delivery and traceability, creating opportunities for orders and price premiums. Third, this mechanism depends on firms' research and development, data resources, and organizational coordination. Reported outcomes include a 23% reduction in operating costs and a 36% improvement in production efficiency at Midea's Nansha factory, 25% energy savings for Gree, and a reduction of more than 30% in emissions at TCL Zhonghuan. Manufacturing policy in Guangdong should therefore support coordinated development across AI, green manufacturing, and specific application settings.

title: Does Green Innovation Induce a “Financing Penalty” in the Capital Market?—Evidence from Chinese Textile Enterprises
summary: Green innovation is key to achieving the strategic goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality. High-carbon enterprises account for a substantial proportion of carbon emissions. Yet, prior literature overlooks the unique features of high-
content: Green innovation is key to achieving the strategic goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality. High-carbon enterprises account for a substantial proportion of carbon emissions. Yet, prior literature overlooks the unique features of high-carbon firms in the green transition. We develop an integrated framework for this analysis. Using Chinese A-share listed textile enterprises from 2010 to 2023 as the sample, this study finds that green innovation significantly increases the cost of equity capital of high-carbon enterprises by increasing cash outflows and agency costs. However, greater willingness to innovate and stronger regional green finance development can mitigate these adverse effects. Furthermore, green innovation’s upward effect on the cost of equity capital is statistically significant among enterprises facing tight financing constraints, with weak human capital, receiving limited attention from institutional investors, and operating in regions with significant climate-risk concerns. Further analysis shows that once high-carbon enterprises’ green innovation level exceeds a certain threshold, investors may reduce their required cost of equity capital. By focusing on Chinese textile enterprises, this study provides practical evidence for high-carbon enterprises to pursue green innovation. It offers guidance on broadening access to long-term capital and promoting sustainable development.

summary: This study pursued three objectives: (1) to examine the fit between empirical data and a structural equation model of energy capital influence, green acceleration and procedural injustice on community rights conflicts; (2) to analyse the di
content: This study pursued three objectives: (1) to examine the fit between empirical data and a structural equation model of energy capital influence, green acceleration and procedural injustice on community rights conflicts; (2) to analyse the direct effect of energy capital influence on those conflicts; and (3) to analyse its indirect effects through the two mediators. Framed within Southeast Asia and examined through a Thai case, data were collected with a 48-item five-point scale aggregated into 16 indicators under four latent constructs, from 630 stakeholders across renewableenergy project areas in three provinces, using disproportionate stratified sampling with cluster and purposive sampling, and analysed with two-step CB-SEM. For objective 1 the model fitted well (χ²/df = 1.101, CFI = 0.998, TLI = 0.997, RMSEA = 0.013, SRMR = 0.048), with composite reliability of 0.777–0.879, AVE of 0.538–0.603, and discriminant validity satisfied under both Fornell-Larcker and HTMT. For objective 2, energy capital influence had a positive direct effect (β = 0.206). For objective 3, significant indirect effects ran through green acceleration (β = 0.068) and proceduralinjustice (β = 0.067), totalling 0.136, with a total effect of 0.342 and 17.9% of variance explained. Nested model comparison confirmed partial mediation. Energy capitalinfluence is associated with community rights conflicts both directly and through procedural mechanisms. As the data are cross-sectional and perception-based, causal interpretation should remain cautious.

title: Sustainability Visibility, Awareness, and Student Engagement in Higher Education: An Exploratory Study
summary: This study explores students' perceptions, awareness, and engagement with sustainability and energyefficiency initiatives in higher education institutions, with particular attention to the visibility of campus sustainability practices.An ex
content: This study explores students' perceptions, awareness, and engagement with sustainability and energyefficiency initiatives in higher education institutions, with particular attention to the visibility of campus sustainability practices.An exploratory cross-sectional survey was conducted among 149 students from five universities.Data were collected through a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistical techniques, including frequencies, percentages and mean scores.Students demonstrated strong environmental concern and positive attitudes towards sustainability.However, awareness of institutional sustainability initiatives, environmental management systems (EMS) and energy-efficiency measures was generally low.Limited communication and visibility of sustainability actions were identified as potential barriers to student engagement.The findings should be interpreted in light of the convenience sampling approach and reliance on self-reported perceptions.Future studies could employ broader samples and more advanced analytical methods.Higher education institutions can strengthen sustainability engagement by improving communication, increasing the visibility of sustainability initiatives and creating more opportunities for student participation.Greater student involvement in sustainability initiatives may contribute to the development of environmentally responsible attitudes, behaviors and sustainability competencies.The study provides exploratory evidence on sustainability visibility and student engagement in higher education and highlights the importance of communication and institutional transparency in fostering sustainability awareness and participation.

title: Transiciones Sostenibles e Inequidades Extractivas: Una Perspectiva de Derechos Humanos sobre las Estructuras Neocoloniales
summary: Este artículo explica cómo la arquitectura jurídica que sostiene la transición energética global se inserta en una larga trayectoria de extracción desigual. Mostrando que los mecanismos actuales de gobernanza (desde los contratos mineros ha
content: Este artículo explica cómo la arquitectura jurídica que sostiene la transición energética global se inserta en una larga trayectoria de extracción desigual. Mostrando que los mecanismos actuales de gobernanza (desde los contratos mineros hasta los regímenes de debida diligencia) reproducen patrones consolidados durante el periodo colonial, el estudio revela que la protección de los derechos humanos sigue siendo secundaria frente a los intereses económicos del Norte global. A través del caso de la República Democrática del Congo, se analizan los efectos sociales y ambientales de la demanda creciente de minerales estratégicos, así como las respuestas normativas africanas y el uso creciente del litigio transnacional. El trabajo concluye que sin una redistribución real del poder regulatorio, la transición energética corre el riesgo de profundizar desigualdades históricas.

title: Developing age-site-density integrated biomass carbon storage models and accumulation tables for warm temperate forests in China
summary: Forest carbon sequestration rate is closely linked to stand growth dynamics; however, existing carbon storage models for warm-temperate forests in China have largely focused on individual factors such as stand age or density, without jointl
content: Forest carbon sequestration rate is closely linked to stand growth dynamics; however, existing carbon storage models for warm-temperate forests in China have largely focused on individual factors such as stand age or density, without jointly accounting for site quality and stand density. This limitation constrains their applicability for multi-factor carbon accounting across varying site and management conditions. Using data from China's 7th- 9th National Forest Resource Inventories (2004–2018), we developed carbon storage accumulation models and corresponding tables for typical warm-temperate forest types incorporating forest age, site class, and stand density index (SDI) as predictors. The models achieved satisfactory performance ( R 2 ≥ 0.647), with higher accuracy for natural forests than plantations, and for coniferous than broad-leaved species. Site quality was the primary factor associated with the asymptotic carbon storage parameter ( a ), which decreased from site class I to V. High-density stands stored more carbon than low-density stands, and the relationship between stand density and carbon storage was stronger in natural forests than in plantations. Taking Pinus tabuliformis as a representative species, dynamic simulations driven by the accumulation tables revealed that plantations accumulated carbon more rapidly-during the early stage (<30 years); however, beyond 65 years, plantation growth slowed markedly and the annual carbon sequestration of natural forests began to exceed that of plantations, underscoring the superior long-term sequestration potential of natural forests. Collectively, these models, tables, and comparative analyses provide methodological and technical support for accurate carbon measurement, potential assessment, and the formulation of differentiated, carbon-oriented management strategies for warm-temperate forests in the context of carbon neutrality.

title: Hydrophobic modification regulates the water microenvironment at the interface of Cu-based materials to promote E-CO 2 RR
summary: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (E-CO2RR) powered by renewable energy is vital for carbon cycling and carbon neutrality. Cu-based catalysts uniquely produce multi-carbon (C2+) products, yet the interfacial water microenvironment and reaction
content: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (E-CO2RR) powered by renewable energy is vital for carbon cycling and carbon neutrality. Cu-based catalysts uniquely produce multi-carbon (C2+) products, yet the interfacial water microenvironment and reaction kinetics remain poorly understood. This work fabricates hydrophobic HY-Cu2O (100) catalysts by self-assembling octadecanethiol on cubic (100)-faced Cu2O nanoparticles to tune interfacial water. Integrated characterizations, electrochemistry, and in situ Attenuated Total Reflection Surface-Enhanced Infrared Absorption Spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS) reveal how hydrophobicity regulates E-CO2RR performance. Hydrophilic/hydrophobic contact-angle measurements reveal that the surface wetting angle changes from 46.1° (hydrophilic) to 133.5° (hydrophobic). X-ray diffraction (XRD) confirms that the crystal structure remains unchanged. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results demonstrate that the Cu-S coordination environment of the material is modified. Further inference suggests that the formation of Cu-S bonds verifies the successful functional grafting of octadecyl chains onto the Cu2O (100) surface, which alters the surface hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity without inducing any variation in the crystal structure. In 1 M KOH flow cells, HY-Cu2O delivers 45.2% Faradaic efficiency for ethylene at -250 mA∙cm-2 and suppresses parasitic Hydrogen Evolution Reaction (HER), far exceeding bare Cu2O. In situ spectra and theory verify that hydrophobic interfaces accumulate K+-bound free water, disrupt interfacial hydrogen bonds, accelerate *CO protonation, and boost C-C coupling for C2+ intermediates. Higher surface CO coverage further kinetically favors C2+ formation. This work establishes an effective hydrophobic modification approach, clarifies the central role of interfacial water in ethylene selectivity, and offers guidance for the design of advanced CO2RR catalysts.

title: Ultrasensitive direct detection of HMGB1 protein via covalently modified graphene field-effect transistors
summary: High-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) is a nuclear chromatin-binding protein that can be released into the extracellular milieu during cellular stress or necrosis, or be actively secreted, where it acts as an early pro-inflammatory mediator imp
content: High-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) is a nuclear chromatin-binding protein that can be released into the extracellular milieu during cellular stress or necrosis, or be actively secreted, where it acts as an early pro-inflammatory mediator implicated in a broad spectrum of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases. Extracellular HMGB1 is therefore an attractive clinical biomarker for health conditions involving necrosis or extensive tissue damage. In this work, we present the development and characterization of a covalently modified graphene field-effect transistor (CG-FET) incorporating a DNA aptamer for the ultrasensitive detection of HMGB1. The device was fabricated using a commercially available anti-HMGB1 DNA aptamer and its successive functionalization steps were independently validated by micro-particle-induced X-ray emission (μ-PIXE). Electrical measurements were performed to monitor the changes in the graphene Dirac point throughout the functionalization process and HMGB1 binding. The sensor exhibited clear and reproducible analytical performance, enabling detection of the target protein with limits of detection (LoDs) in the attomolar range. Specificity studies confirmed selective aptamer–HMGB1 recognition and demonstrated that optimized buffer conditions reduce nonspecific interactions. These results demonstrate the performance of the CG-FET biosensor based on a commercially available aptamer and provide a basis for its further development and validation in complex biological matrices towards potential diagnostic applications.

title: EVALUATING SOIL QUALITY ACROSS MULTIPLE SOIL TYPES FOR SUSTAINABLE OIL PALM PLANTATIONS IN CENTRAL KALIMANTAN, INDONESIA
summary: Assessing soil quality is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of oil palm plantations by aligning agricultural productivity with environmental and social dimensions.This study examines the influence of soil type on soil quali
content: Assessing soil quality is essential to ensuring the long-term sustainability of oil palm plantations by aligning agricultural productivity with environmental and social dimensions.This study examines the influence of soil type on soil quality in Kotawaringin Timur District, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia.Specifically, it evaluates four representative soil types (Histosols, Inceptisols, Ultisols and Entisols) using the soil quality index (SQI) framework, identifies key indicators through a minimum data set (MDS), and proposes soil-specific management strategies.The methodology includes field surveys, biological and physicochemical soil analyses, SQI computation and statistical evaluation, with six replications per soil type.Results demonstrate significant variation in SQI values: Low for Histosols (0.245) and very low for Ultisols (0.178), Inceptisols (0.180) and Entisols (0.182).Soil organic carbon (SOC), exchangeable magnesium (Ex-Mg) and available phosphorus (Av-P) were identified as critical indicators influencing soil function.To improve soil quality, the application of organic amendments such as compost, biochar and biofertilisers derived from oil palm residues is recommended.Integrating weed biomass may further enhance nutrient availability and soil resilience, supporting sustainable plantation management tailored to site-specific conditions.

title: Study on Rock Damage Assessment Method Based on Crack Characteristic Analysis under CO2 Fracturing
summary: Abstract Carbon dioxide ( CO 2 ) fracturing is an effective new carbon neutrality technology for underground space excavation engineering. To address the quantitative evaluation problem of rock damage induced by CO 2 fracturing, a rock dama
content: Abstract Carbon dioxide ( CO 2 ) fracturing is an effective new carbon neutrality technology for underground space excavation engineering. To address the quantitative evaluation problem of rock damage induced by CO 2 fracturing, a rock damage assessment method is proposed. A numerical model was established to obtain time-series images of rock crack propagation at borehole spacings of 1.4, 1.6, and 1.8 m. Crack binary images were obtained via sequential treatments of grayscale conversion, contrast enhancement, Gaussian smoothing denoising, adaptive threshold segmentation, and morphological optimization. Feature parameters of crack area ratio, crack length ratio, and crack number were extracted from the binarized images. Dimensionality reduction and weight calculation were conducted on the feature parameters combined with principal component analysis, and a rock damage evaluation method based on the cumulative damage factor model was established. The results show that the proposed crack damage assessment method can realize accurate measurement and quantitative assessment of the rock crack damage degree. This damage assessment method can classify the damage grades of different stages of crack propagation. Under the working conditions of three different borehole spacings, the crack damage factor for the 1.6-m hole spacing case ultimately reached the maximum value of 0.84059, and this spacing shows a more favorable CO 2 fracturing response under the test conditions. This provides an effective methodological support for the damage evaluation of rock under CO 2 fracturing and a quantitative basis for the borehole spacing optimization of CO 2 fracturing engineering.

title: Orbital forcing and marine transgression controls on lacustrine organic matter enrichment during the Turonian: evidence from the lower Qingshankou Formation, Songliao Basin
summary: The lacustrine Qingshankou Formation in the Songliao Basin is a major source rock for shale oil. However, the controls on its organic matter (OM) enrichment, especially the interplay between orbital forcing and marine transgressions, remain
content: The lacustrine Qingshankou Formation in the Songliao Basin is a major source rock for shale oil. However, the controls on its organic matter (OM) enrichment, especially the interplay between orbital forcing and marine transgressions, remain unclear. This study focuses on the Lower Member of the Qingshankou Formation (K 2 qn 1 ), which was deposited during the Turonian stage (∼91.8–90.9 Ma). By integrating high-resolution well logging data, cyclostratigraphy, geochemistry, and machine learning (LSTM-SHAP), we developed the astronomical time scale (ATS) for K 2 qn 1 , reconstructed lake-level fluctuations, and quantified the controls on OM enrichment. Results show that Milankovitch cycles controlled sedimentation and lake-level fluctuations, which in turn drove facies-dependent OM enrichment mechanisms. In semi-deep lake facies, OM enrichment was dominantly controlled by redox conditions linked to lake-level fluctuations, whereas in deep lake facies, it was primarily governed by paleoproductivity. Marine transgressions, identified as episodic events at ∼91.5 Ma, enhanced bacterial sulfate reduction, which typically modulated and thereby suppressed OM enrichment across the system. The findings demonstrate that OM enrichment in large lacustrine systems results from the complex interaction of orbitally-driven climate rhythms and episodic geological events, providing a predictive model for identifying heterogeneous “sweet spots” in lacustrine shale systems.

title: Navigating the Fog: An Evaluation of European Airline GHG Emissions Reporting
summary: Abstract The Aviation Zero Emission by 2050 (AZERO2050) study systematically evaluates the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reporting practices of European airline groups, focusing on both mandatory and voluntary key performance indicators (K
content: Abstract The Aviation Zero Emission by 2050 (AZERO2050) study systematically evaluates the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reporting practices of European airline groups, focusing on both mandatory and voluntary key performance indicators (KPIs) as shaped by evolving regulatory frameworks and the long-term ambition to reach net zero by 2050. By analysing annual and sustainability reports from 16 major airline groups, the research identifies significant progress in the disclosure of core metrics such as Total CO 2 Scope 1 emissions and Emissions Intensity, reflecting growing regulatory alignment and stakeholder expectations. However, the findings also reveal persistent gaps and inconsistencies, particularly in the reporting of Scope 2 and 3 GHG emissions, energy consumption, GHG removals, and emerging metrics related to Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and non-CO 2 effects—areas critical for tracking progress towards AZERO 2050. The proliferation of voluntary KPIs further complicates comparability due to a lack of standardization and clear definitions. These challenges are compounded by risks of greenwashing, where airlines selectively report favourable data, and greenhushing, where substantive achievements are under-communicated. The study concludes that while regulatory frameworks such as the CSRD, EU ETS, CORSIA, and ReFuelEU are driving improvements, further harmonization and methodological clarity are required to ensure transparency, comparability, and genuine progress toward aviation climate goals.

title: Optimizing Battery Size and Charging Infrastructure for Public Ferry Fleet Electrification
summary: Abstract Ferry electrification plays a crucial role in reducing greenhouse gas and air emissions from transport, particularly in coastal and archipelagic countries. Current approaches typically emphasize battery electric range for continuou
content: Abstract Ferry electrification plays a crucial role in reducing greenhouse gas and air emissions from transport, particularly in coastal and archipelagic countries. Current approaches typically emphasize battery electric range for continuous daily operation with night charging to match diesel ferry performance. This study develops a mixed-integer linear programming model to minimize the total cost of ownership for a battery electric ferry fleet while determining optimal battery sizes, charging locations, and charging power capacities. The study evaluates two scenarios for the public ferry fleet in Gothenburg, Sweden, which comprises six ferries operating across 19 docks: fixed routes with current schedules and flexible route assignments that maintain the overall schedule. Results show that routing different ferries specifically for opportunity charging can reduce the required charging infrastructure power by 30%, required installed battery capacity by more than 10% and the total system cost by 10%. This cost reduction makes electrification more competitive than equivalent diesel-powered vessels. Fleet electrification provides around 95% reduction in GWP relative to the fossil option. Our optimization framework demonstrates that strategic placement of charging stations, power allocation at each location, and coordinated charging strategies enable significant system cost reduction.

title: A review on grid-forming flywheel energy storage: Enabling active support in high-penetration wind grids
summary: The transition to high-penetration wind power introduces critical frequency stability and low-inertia challenges to modern power grids. Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESS), characterized by millisecond-level dynamic response and inherent
content: The transition to high-penetration wind power introduces critical frequency stability and low-inertia challenges to modern power grids. Flywheel Energy Storage Systems (FESS), characterized by millisecond-level dynamic response and inherent electromechanical isomorphism, offer a physically backed approach to mitigating these vulnerabilities. This paper presents a comprehensive review of FESS applications in wind power generation, exploring the connection between component-level physical constraints and system-level active grid support. We first analyze the evolutionary trajectories and multi-physics limitations of core technologies, including composite rotors, magnetic bearings, and vacuum thermal management. Building upon this hardware foundation, the review systematically evaluates the paradigm shift toward Grid-Forming (GFM) control, highlighting how adaptive Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) strategies and distributed consensus protocols aim to balance transient grid support with mechanical fatigue limits. Furthermore, we synthesize recent advancements in multi-objective capacity optimization and time-frequency decoupling for flywheel-battery Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (HESS). The active defense capabilities of FESS during extreme grid events, notably black start and Low Voltage Ride-Through (LVRT), are also critically examined. Finally, the paper outlines future trajectories toward physics-informed intelligent control and Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) offshore integration, providing valuable insights for leveraging FESS as a stabilization asset in renewable-dominated power systems.

title: Sürdürülebilir Enerji ve İklim Eylem Planları Aracılığıyla İklim Dirençliliğinin Değerlendirilmesi: Türkiye’deki Beş Büyükşehir Belediyesi Üzerine Karşılaştırmalı Bir İçerik Analizi
summary: İklim değişikliği, kentlerin çevresel, sosyal ve ekonomik sistemleri üzerinde önemli etkiler oluşturarak yerel yönetimlerin iklim dirençliliğini artırmaya yönelik bütüncül planlama yaklaşımlarını gerekli kılmaktadır. Bu çalışmanın amacı, Tü
content: İklim değişikliği, kentlerin çevresel, sosyal ve ekonomik sistemleri üzerinde önemli etkiler oluşturarak yerel yönetimlerin iklim dirençliliğini artırmaya yönelik bütüncül planlama yaklaşımlarını gerekli kılmaktadır. Bu çalışmanın amacı, Türkiye’de farklı iklimsel ve coğrafi özelliklere sahip örnek kentlerde (İstanbul, İzmir, Antalya, Konya ve Erzurum Büyükşehir Belediyeleri) hazırlanan Sürdürülebilir Enerji ve İklim Eylem Planlarını (SECAP) iklim dirençliliği perspektifinden karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektir. Bu kapsamda çalışmada, yönlendirilmiş (dedüktif) içerik analizi yaklaşımı kullanılmış ve analiz, kod frekanslarıyla nicel olarak desteklenmiştir. Analiz, MAXQDA 2024 yazılımı ile gerçekleştirilmiştir. Literatür taramaları ve IPCC Altıncı Değerlendirme Raporu (AR6) temel alınarak geliştirilen kodlama çerçevesi kapsamında azaltım, uyum, risk ve yönetişim olmak üzere dört üst kod ve on yedi alt kod oluşturulmuş, seçilen SECAP belgeleri sistematik olarak kodlanmıştır. Bulgular, incelenen planlarda azaltım (%31,4) ve uyum (%30,7) temalarının en yüksek temsil düzeyine sahip olduğunu; yönetişim (%21,1) ve risk (%16,8) temalarının ise daha sınırlı ele alındığını göstermektedir. Alt kodlar düzeyinde sera gazı azaltımı, yenilenebilir enerji, doğa temelli çözümler ve mavi-yeşil altyapı uygulamaları öne çıkarken karbon yutakları, ekosistem hizmetleri ile finansman ve kaynaklar bileşenlerinin görece düşük düzeyde temsil edildiği belirlenmiştir. Bulgular sonucunda, iklim eylem planlarında risk değerlendirmesi, ekosistem temelli yaklaşımlar, finansman mekanizmaları ve yönetişim süreçlerinin daha bütüncül biçimde ele alınması gerektiği belirlenmiştir.

title: Synergistic activation of peroxymonosulfate by Fe 3 O 4 /diatomite composite for efficient tetracycline degradation: mechanistic insights from experiments and density functional theory
summary: Abstract BACKGROUND Tetracycline (TC) is a persistent antibiotic contaminant in water; because conventional treatments cannot adequately remove it, its persistence raises concerns about antibiotic resistance. To enhance degradation, magneti
content: Abstract BACKGROUND Tetracycline (TC) is a persistent antibiotic contaminant in water; because conventional treatments cannot adequately remove it, its persistence raises concerns about antibiotic resistance. To enhance degradation, magnetic Fe 3 O 4 /diatomite (DT) composites were synthesized via hydrothermal methods using natural porous DT to prevent the aggregation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles and improve the reusability of the catalyst. RESULTS Characterization confirmed the successful Fe 3 O 4 loading onto DT with uniform elemental distribution, preserved pore structure, redox‐active Fe sites, and high thermal stability. The composite with 10% Fe 3 O 4 (10‐FDT) exhibited superior catalytic activity compared to Fe 3 O 4 or peroxymonosulfate alone. Under optimized conditions (25 mg L −1 TC, 0.20 g L−1 10‐FDT, 2.5 mmol L −1 peroxymonosulfate, pH 4), 87.4% TC degradation was achieved in 3 h. Degradation efficiency improved with catalyst and oxidant dosage, moderate acidity, and elevated temperature, but was inhibited by chloride ions and humic acid, while carbonate and dihydrogen phosphate ions enhanced the performance of the system. Radical quenching and electron spin resonance analyses revealed hydroxyl and sulfate radicals, alongside a dominant non‐radical singlet oxygen pathway linked to oxygen vacancies in DT. Density functional theory showed that electron transfer from DT to Fe 3 O 4 promotes oxidant adsorption and lowers the activation barriers for the formation of singlet oxygen. Mass spectrometry and molecular orbital analyses indicated TC degradation via functional group loss and ring opening. CONCLUSION The 10‐FDT composite proves to be an effective and stable catalyst for advanced oxidation processes, retaining 68.4% of its catalytic activity after three cycles and maintaining over 75% degradation efficiency in real wastewater samples. This highlights its strong potential for practical, scalable wastewater treatment applications. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

title: Effect of Advanced High-Strength Steel Microstructure on Hydrogen Embrittlement Behavior of Resistance Spot Welded Joints
summary: To achieve automotive lightweighting and passenger safety, advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) have been developed with increasing strength levels. However, hydrogen embrittlement (HE) becomes more critical with increasing strength. Despit
content: To achieve automotive lightweighting and passenger safety, advanced high-strength steels (AHSS) have been developed with increasing strength levels. However, hydrogen embrittlement (HE) becomes more critical with increasing strength. Despite efforts to improve HE resistance through microstructural control, these steels remain vulnerable after resistance spot welding (RSW), where complex microstructures and defects are introduced. In this study, the effect of initial steel microstructure on HE sensitivity in RSWed steels was investigated using two 1.5 GPa-grade steels with identical compositions but different microstructures: complex-phase (CP) and single-phase (SP) steels. HE resistance of both base metal and welded joints was evaluated using slow strain rate tensile and slow deformation rate tensile-shear tests after electrochemical hydrogen charging. The SP steel, consisting of tempered martensite, exhibited higher HE sensitivity than the CP steel composed of tempered martensite and bainite in both base metal and welded conditions. With increasing hydrogen charging time, the crack propagation path transitioned from the fusion zone (FZ) boundary to the upper-critical heat-affected zone (UCHAZ) interior with intergranular cracking, consistent with the hydrogen-enhanced decohesion (HEDE) mechanism. In the SP steel, an additional crack propagation mode was observed at intermediate charging conditions, where cracks propagated across the FZ before transitioning to the UCHAZ, resulting in greater ductility loss. At higher charging conditions, both steels exhibited similar intergranular cracking behavior. These results suggest that the HE behavior of RSWed steels is associated with the microstructural characteristics of the UCHAZ, while differences in the initial steel conditions may also contribute to the observed HE sensitivity.

title: Well-to-Wheel Environmental Performance of a Long Haul Fuel-Cell Truck under Alternative Hydrogen Production Pathways: Route Resolved Insights from the ESCALATE Project
source: University of Surrey Open Research repository
summary: Executive Summary Decarbonising long haul heavy duty freight transport is essential for achieving European climate-neutrality targets. This study evaluates the well to wheel environmental performance of a 40 ton fuel cell heavy duty truck (
content: Executive Summary Decarbonising long haul heavy duty freight transport is essential for achieving European climate-neutrality targets. This study evaluates the well to wheel environmental performance of a 40 ton fuel cell heavy duty truck (FCHDT) developed within the ESCALATE project. A coupled MATLAB/Simulink and SimaPro-based modelling framework integrates route-resolved vehicle energy simulations with life-cycle impact assessment to evaluate the combined effects of operational strategies and hydrogen production pathways. Two operating contexts are considered: the Barcelona Geneva freight corridor and the VECTO long haul reference cycle. Results show that operational optimisation reduces hydrogen consumption and associated climate impacts by approximately 15.6% for the Barcelona Geneva corridor and 21.7% for the VECTO cycle. Hydrogen production pathways remain the dominant driver of environmental performance. Wind-powered electrolysis reduces aggregated environmental impacts to approximately 1 mPt per 100 km, compared with 13–14 mPt per 100 km for grid-based electrolysis and 4–5 mPt per 100 km for SMR-derived hydrogen. Vehicle efficiency improvements and low carbon hydrogen supply play a crucial role in improving the environmental performance of hydrogen powered long haul freight transport.

title: ZeroFlex - A New Innovative Approach for Mobility Stations in Austria
summary: Abstract The goal of the ZeroFlex project ( https://zeroflex.at/ ), funded by the Austrian Initiative for Emission-Free Mobility, is the systematization and economic viability of mobility hubs – both at the level of individual stations and
content: Abstract The goal of the ZeroFlex project ( https://zeroflex.at/ ), funded by the Austrian Initiative for Emission-Free Mobility, is the systematization and economic viability of mobility hubs – both at the level of individual stations and as a system innovation with an integrated overall offering for all stations. ZeroFlex aims to make each station economically viable, which is essential for the widespread adoption of mobility hubs – only then will they become attractive to customers such as municipalities, businesses, the tourism sector, etc. The ZeroFlex project comprises (1) the overall concept of modular, highly flexible, high-quality, and cost-effective mobility hubs that primarily offer electrically powered, single-track vehicles. Energy efficiency through photovoltaics and energy storage is a central component of the solution, as are (2) the technical and organizational development of the stations, (3) a large-scale field test under real conditions (city of Klagenfurt, Austria) including monitoring and evaluation, (4) the modelling of an optimized system as the sum of all ZeroFlex stations with regard to spatial structure and aspects of mobility behavior, (5) the development of a highly flexible business model and (6) the modelling of the climate impact or the realistically possible contribution to climate neutrality.

title: Legal-institutional inertia in circular electrification: Evidence from Swedish heavy-duty and off-road machinery
summary: Electrifying heavy-duty and off-road machinery can cut operational emissions, but cleaner-production gains depend on circular battery and component flows, interoperable charging and useable data. Transition research explains policy mixes an
content: Electrifying heavy-duty and off-road machinery can cut operational emissions, but cleaner-production gains depend on circular battery and component flows, interoperable charging and useable data. Transition research explains policy mixes and socio-technical lock-in but often treats law as an external context. We ask which legal domains enable or obstruct circular electrification, how they create system inertia, and which legal design principles can reduce it. The study combines 29 semi-structured expert interviews in Sweden with hybrid thematic analysis and targeted doctrinal analysis of relevant EU and Swedish law. Eight connected domains emerge, spanning regulatory direction, permitting producer responsibility and product–waste status, standards, data governance, finance, contracts and procurement, and regulatory experimentation. Across them, ambiguity, fragmented authority and legacy-rule misfit increase coordination and transaction costs, delay decisions, shift risk to early movers and favour incumbent-led reconfiguration over more disruptive circular models. The central contribution is to specify legal-institutional inertia as a cross-domain regime mechanism that selects both transition pathway and actors. Connecting the multi-level perspective with institutional environmental governance and product-chain management, the paper derives a coordinated policy mix based on stable long-term direction, modular implementation, interoperability, proportional responsibility and experiments linked to scaling. Cleaner production policy must therefore align legal interfaces across the product chain, not only remove isolated barriers.

title: Sustainable quinoa production in Morocco: balancing productivity and environmental performance
summary: Increasing quinoa yields through improved nutrient and water management is critical for smallholder farmers in Morocco. However, strategies are needed to minimize tradeoffs between food production and sustainability goals. For two quinoa pr
content: Increasing quinoa yields through improved nutrient and water management is critical for smallholder farmers in Morocco. However, strategies are needed to minimize tradeoffs between food production and sustainability goals. For two quinoa production scenarios, we evaluated how increasing organic and inorganic nitrogen (N) inputs influenced yields and seven environmental impact categories (global warming potential (GWP), human carcinogenic toxicity, freshwater, marine and terrestrial ecotoxicity, freshwater eutrophication, and fossil resource scarcity). The first scenario included inorganic N fertilizer with deficit irrigation while the second included organic amendments (manure and compost) with full irrigation. Across both scenarios, the primary contributors to GWP were fertilization, irrigation, machinery use, and transportation of organic amendments (9%–75%, 15%–64%, 5%–29%, and 0%–18%, respectively). With inorganic fertilization, quinoa yields increased by 30% above the control at 40 kg N ha −1 , but not at higher N rates. Even at this modest level of N inputs, GWP increased by 69% from 0.99 to 1.68 kg CO 2 eq kg −1 , which corresponded to a 63%–251% increase across other environmental impact categories. With organic amendments, both 10 t ha −1 of compost and 20 t ha −1 of manure achieved the highest quinoa productivity (1,891 and 1,852 kg ha −1 ) with the lowest GWP (1.34 and 1.42 kg CO 2 eq kg −1 ) and a 49%–55% decrease across other environmental impact categories. Here we provide the first integrated assessment of organic and inorganic N management strategies to increase quinoa productivity in Morocco while minimizing environmental impacts.

title: An Original Approach to Meeting the Challenges of the Climate Crisis Through Sustainable Transport: The Example of the Priority Research and Equipment Program in France
summary: Abstract We present the French Priority Research and Equipment Program (PREP) MOBIDEC. Its aim of this research program is to broaden understanding of mobility, based on multidisciplinary approaches, open the door to new applications in ter
