This article compares the concepts of energy security and food security, focusing on their relationship to sustainability, and asks whether invoking security enables or obstructs each sector's environmental transformation. It argues that EU energy law has integrated sustainability into the concept of energy security itself, whereas agri‐food law treats sustainability as separate from—and, in times of crisis, in tension with—food security. Two case studies illustrate the implications: in the wake of Russia's war against Ukraine since February 2022, invoking security accelerated the clean energy transition but triggered a backlash against agri‐environmental measures; the 2026 US–Israeli war against Iran largely reproduced this divergence, although the EU's response to the resulting fertiliser crisis shows early signs of convergence between food security and sustainability. Four structural elements explain these profoundly divergent effects of a seemingly similar concept: the sectors' factual situations and historical evolutions, their regulatory rationales, the temporal dimension of security and agricultural exceptionalism. The article concludes that long‐term food security requires integrating sustainability into the legal concept of food security itself.

title: Selective responsibility: Environmental, social and governance frameworks and the containment of environmental and social harm in urban real estate
summary: As environmental, social and governance (ESG) frameworks become increasingly institutionalised within real-estate investment, questions of corporate responsibility for urban social and environmental challenges become more evident. Drawing o
content: As environmental, social and governance (ESG) frameworks become increasingly institutionalised within real-estate investment, questions of corporate responsibility for urban social and environmental challenges become more evident. Drawing on the case of Zurich and applying Young’s Social Connection Model of responsibility, this paper examines how ESG shapes the ways in which real-estate investors identify, articulate and act upon their responsibilities towards urban environments and communities. I argue that rather than constituting a meaningful framework for addressing structural housing inequality and environmental harm, ESG operates primarily as a risk-management tool that translatesc heterogeneous societal concerns into discrete, auditable categories. Environmental metrics dominate due to their compatibility with existing valuation practices, while social dimensions stagnate and governance is reduced to documentation. The result is a form of selective, depoliticised responsibility that acknowledges corporate implication in urban processes while simultaneously containing and neutralising its scope. Nevertheless, ESG’s ambiguity creates organisational openings through which individual actors can advance more ambitious environmental and social agendas. The paper concludes that ESG enables incremental progress while leaving the structural drivers of housing inequality and environmental harm fundamentally unchallenged.

title: OECD ÜLKELERİNDE MALİYE POLİTİKASI ARAÇLARININ KARBON AYAK İZİ ÜZERİNDEKİ ETKİSİ: PANEL VERİ ANALİZİ
source: Cumhuriyet Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Dergisi
summary: İklim değişikliği ve çevre kirliliği, günümüzde küresel gündemin en öncelikli sorunları arasında yer almaktadır. Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi kapsamında imzalanan Paris Anlaşması ve 2030 Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma H
content: İklim değişikliği ve çevre kirliliği, günümüzde küresel gündemin en öncelikli sorunları arasında yer almaktadır. Birleşmiş Milletler İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi kapsamında imzalanan Paris Anlaşması ve 2030 Sürdürülebilir Kalkınma Hedefleri, çevre politikasını üye ülkeler açısından bağlayıcı bir zorunluluk haline getirmiştir. Bu uluslararası yükümlülükler çerçevesinde, karbon emisyonlarını azaltmaya yönelik etkili politika araçlarının belirlenmesi hem akademik hem de politika yapımı açısından kritik önem taşımaktadır. Bu çalışma, 1995-2022 döneminde 19 OECD ülkesinde enerji vergisi, çevre koruma harcamaları ve ekonomik büyümenin karbon ayak izi üzerindeki uzun dönemli etkisini ampirik olarak incelemeyi amaçlamaktadır. Bunun yanı sıra söz konusu ülkelerde Çevresel Kuznets Eğrisi (ÇKE) hipotezinin geçerliliği de sınanmaktadır. Ampirik bulgular, politika etkilerinin ülkeden ülkeye belirgin biçimde farklılaştığını ortaya koymaktadır. Bu bulgular dört başlık altında özetlenebilir: (i) Enerji vergisi, Hollanda’da karbon ayak izini istatistiksel olarak anlamlı biçimde artırmaktadır. (ii) Çevre koruma harcamaları, İspanya’da karbon ayak izini anlamlı ölçüde azaltmaktadır. (iii) Ekonomik büyüme, Belçika'da karbon ayak izini artırıcı yönde etki yapmaktadır. Ancak büyümenin, Macaristan ve Polonya’da ise negatif etkisi bulunmaktadır. (iv) Belçika’da ters U şeklindeki Çevresel Kuznets Eğrisi geçerlidir. Elde edilen bulgular çerçevesinde, üç somut politika çıkarımı öne çıkmaktadır. Birincisi, enerji vergisinin Hollanda’da karbon ayak izini artırdığı bulgusu, mevcut vergi yapısının emisyon azaltımı amacına hizmet etmediğine işaret etmektedir. Bu ülkelerde enerji vergisi gelirlerinin doğrudan temiz enerji araştırma-geliştirme faaliyetlerine ve enerji verimliliği sübvansiyonlarına yönlendirilmesi, vergilerin çevresel etkinliğini artırmaya katkı sağlayabilir. İkincisi, İspanya’da çevre koruma harcamalarının karbon ayak izini azaltıcı etkisi dikkate alındığında, bu harcamaların bütçedeki payının artırılması ve söz konusu kaynakların özellikle karbonsuzlaştırma teknolojileri ile yenilenebilir enerji altyapısı gibi daha yüksek çevresel getiri sağlayan alanlara yönlendirilmesi önerilmektedir. Üçüncüsü, Belçika'da ekonomik büyümenin karbon ayak izini artırması, bu ülkelerin büyüme süreçlerinin hâlâ fosil yakıt bağımlılığından tam anlamıyla kopamadığını göstermektedir. Bu çerçevede söz konusu ülkelerin sürdürülebilir büyüme politikalarını güçlendirmesi ve yeşil dönüşüm araçlarını daha etkin biçimde uygulamaya koyması gerekmektedir.

title: Bridging Policy and Practice: Enabling Robust GHG Emission Accounting Across Transport Services
summary: Abstract Reliable and harmonised GHG emission factors are essential for enabling fair and transparent climate impact comparisons across transport services. However, current methodologies are fragmented, with limited treatment of emerging fu
content: Abstract Reliable and harmonised GHG emission factors are essential for enabling fair and transparent climate impact comparisons across transport services. However, current methodologies are fragmented, with limited treatment of emerging fuels, inconsistent data handling, and poor integration of upstream energy carrier pathways. This paper presents the scientific and methodological basis of the CLEVER framework, a new EU supported standard to calculate lifecycle based GHG emission factors for transport fuels and energy carriers. Designed in alignment with ISO 14083 and as a core component of the upcoming CountEmissionsEU regulation, CLEVER introduces a modular, attributional LCA based approach that integrates upstream well to tank and operational tank to wheel emissions. The framework improves on existing approaches by clarifying system boundaries, harmonising modelling rules, and incorporating additional climate relevant sources such as indirect land use change, methane slip, black carbon, and hydrogen leakage. It supports both default factors and operator specific data, enabling comparability while also rewarding more accurate, fuel pathway specific assessments. CLEVER advances best practice in data quality scoring, certification linkage, and reporting granularity, creating a credible foundation for industry wide decarbonisation tracking and digital emissions integration in transport.

title: Introducing Circularity in Public Transport for Greater Sustainability: From Strategy to Action
summary: Abstract Public transport (PT) systems are vital to society, providing access to goods, services, and opportunities. However, the construction, maintenance, and decommissioning of PT assets contribute to carbon emissions, resource depletion
content: Abstract Public transport (PT) systems are vital to society, providing access to goods, services, and opportunities. However, the construction, maintenance, and decommissioning of PT assets contribute to carbon emissions, resource depletion, and ecological disruption. The CE4CE (Circular Economy for Central Europe) project addresses this by promoting a shift from a linear to a circular model using the “Avoid-Extend-Transform-Enable” life-cycle framework. This framework has been applied to develop three strategies focused on rolling stock, infrastructure, and energy, based on consultations with public transport operators (PTOs) from Central Europe and beyond. These three strategies serve as the foundation for localized, stakeholder-aligned action plans in Leipzig, Bergamo, Gdynia, and Maribor. This paper provides a concise overview of these strategies, covering: 1) the application of the life-cycle thinking framework to each pillar; 2) a status quo analysis of circularity integration in PT systems; 3) a catalogue of practical cases for implementing circularity; and 4) a set of tailored indicators for monitoring and measuring impact. The paper also discusses how these strategies have been adapted into action plans, supporting the transition from isolated initiatives to more strategic, life-cycle-oriented approach in PT, with a greater focus on resource efficiency and a significant reduction in ecological impacts.

title: CUL3-mediated NRF2 dysregulation in TP53-driven non-small cell lung cancer: neddylation-associated structural perturbations
summary: CUL3 encodes Cullin-3, the scaffold of Cullin-RING Ligase 3 (CRL3), which mediates proteasomal degradation of NRF2 through KEAP1-dependent ubiquitination. While canonical NRF2 alterations such as KEAP1 or NFE2L2 mutations are well character
content: CUL3 encodes Cullin-3, the scaffold of Cullin-RING Ligase 3 (CRL3), which mediates proteasomal degradation of NRF2 through KEAP1-dependent ubiquitination. While canonical NRF2 alterations such as KEAP1 or NFE2L2 mutations are well characterised in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), the role of CUL3 mutations remains poorly defined. We hypothesised that CUL3 missense variants are conditionally enriched in TP53-altered NSCLC, with the EGFR-oncogenic subset as a defined disease background rather than a synergistic requirement. A multi-cohort NSCLC dataset (n = 47,862; 10,228 with oncogenic EGFR mutations and confirmed CUL3 coverage) was interrogated using two-layer Fisher’s exact testing and logistic regression with an EGFR × TP53 interaction term, and validated transcriptomically in TCGA LUAD/LUSC. CUL3 mutations showed conditional enrichment in the TP53-mutant EGFR background (OR = 2.92, p = 4.68 × 10 −29 ); the non-significant EGFR × TP53 interaction (OR = 0.86, p = 0.547) confirmed that enrichment is driven by TP53 loss rather than EGFR synergy. CUL3-mutant tumours showed elevated NRF2 activation across three independent signatures, with increased proliferative signalling and altered drug metabolism. All-atom molecular dynamics simulations of wild-type, L321F, G402E and M711I CUL3:KEAP1 complexes in inactive and neddylation-active states revealed variant-specific conformational behaviour. L321F drove the neddylated complex into a conformationally restricted state with reduced backbone flexibility, decreased radius of gyration, and a shifted free energy minimum, whereas G402E showed progressive destabilisation and M711I remained comparable to wild-type. Free energy landscape analysis confirmed a shifted conformational energy minimum in L321F + NEDD8 relative to wild-type, indicating impaired catalytic flexibility despite intact complex formation. These findings define CUL3 as a TP53-associated modifier of NRF2 regulation within EGFR-driven NSCLC, operating through allosteric rigidification of the neddylation-active CRL3 complex.

title: Reel Efektif Döviz Kuru Teknolojik Kapasitenin Çevresel Etkilerini Koşullandırıyor mu? OECD Ülkeleri Üzerine Kanıtlar
source: Iğdır Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Teknolojik kapasitenin çevresel etkileri, ülkelerin ekonomik ve rekabetçi yapısına bağlı olarak farklılaşabilmektedir. Ancak bu farklılaşmada reel efektif döviz kurunun oynadığı rol henüz yeterince açıklığa kavuşturulamamıştır. Bu kapsamda
content: Teknolojik kapasitenin çevresel etkileri, ülkelerin ekonomik ve rekabetçi yapısına bağlı olarak farklılaşabilmektedir. Ancak bu farklılaşmada reel efektif döviz kurunun oynadığı rol henüz yeterince açıklığa kavuşturulamamıştır. Bu kapsamda çalışmada, teknolojik kapasitenin karbon emisyonları üzerindeki etkisini ve reel efektif döviz kuru düzeyinin bu ilişki üzerindeki koşullandırıcı rolünü incelemektedir. Analizde, 2007–2023 döneminde 20 OECD ülkesine ait panel veriler kullanılmıştır. Teknolojik kapasiteyi temsil etmek amacıyla, yüksek teknoloji ihracatı, Ar-Ge yoğunluğu ve teknoloji temelli patent göstergelerinden yararlanılarak, Temel Bileşenler Analizi (PCA) yöntemiyle bir bütünleşik teknolojik kapasite endeksi (BTKE) oluşturulmuştur. Değişkenler arasındaki dinamik ilişkiler ise iki aşamalı Sistem GMM yöntemiyle tahmin edilmiştir. Ayrıca, teknolojik kapasitenin farklı reel efektif döviz kuru düzeylerindeki etkisi koşullu marjinal etki analizi kullanılarak değerlendirilmiştir. Bulgular, teknolojik kapasitenin karbon emisyonları üzerindeki etkisinin doğrusal olmadığını göstermektedir. Reel efektif döviz kurunun düşük olduğu seviyelerde teknolojik kapasite karbon emisyonlarını artırırken, reel efektif döviz kuru yükseldikçe bu etki zayıflamakta ve belirli bir seviyeden sonra emisyonu azaltıcı hale gelmektedir. Sonuçlar, teknolojik gelişmelerin çevresel etkilerinin ülkelerin rekabet yapısı ve makroekonomik koşulları tarafından şekillendirildiğini ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Policy-Driven Good Practices for Sustainable Intermodal Transport in Rural and Urban Areas
summary: Abstract In Europe, rural and peri-urban regions face challenges in accessing integrated transport systems, digital connectivity for improving travel experience and flexible mobility services, which make the use of private vehicles predomin
content: Abstract In Europe, rural and peri-urban regions face challenges in accessing integrated transport systems, digital connectivity for improving travel experience and flexible mobility services, which make the use of private vehicles predominant. EMBRACER is a region-driven project where seven underserved regions have committed to integrating public transport with informal modes (cycling, ride-hailing, car/bike/scooter sharing, on-demand transport, and autonomous shuttles) to enhance the interconnection with urban areas and achieve seamless, intelligent, climate-resilient regional and local intermodal mobility. The focus is to build capacity based on interregional learning through a structured cooperation process that fosters a multi-stakeholder co-creation approach to the identification of innovative intermodal mobility solutions, which is further enriched by a pilot testing the viability of an autonomous shuttle service to interconnect with public transport and enhance travel in remote areas.

title: Corn straw fiber-modified asphalt for high-RAP recycled PAC-13 mixtures: preparation, rheology, and pavement performance
summary: Introduction Open burning of corn stalks causes environmental pollution, while recycled asphalt mixtures with high reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) content require adequate binder performance to maintain pavement durability. This study eval
content: Introduction Open burning of corn stalks causes environmental pollution, while recycled asphalt mixtures with high reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) content require adequate binder performance to maintain pavement durability. This study evaluated corn stalk fibers as bio-based modifiers for high-RAP recycled PAC-13 mixtures. Methods Corn stalk fibers were prepared using physical-mechanical and chemical alkali treatments, and treatment conditions were evaluated using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis. Asphalt binders containing 0.4%–2.0% fiber were tested using a dynamic shear rheometer and a bending beam rheometer. The selected binder was used to prepare recycled PAC-13 mixtures containing 20%–60% RAP, and their pavement performance was assessed. Results Chemical alkali treatment with 3% NaOH for 50 min produced fibers with superior thermal stability and oil absorption capacity. The optimal fiber content was 1.2%, improving the binder’s high-temperature shear resistance and low-temperature stress relaxation. As RAP content increased, optimum binder content, Marshall stability, dynamic stability, moisture resistance, and low-temperature crack resistance declined, while air void content increased. At approximately 40% RAP, all key performance indicators met the relevant technical specifications. Discussion Under the materials and experimental conditions investigated, approximately 40% RAP is the recommended upper limit for corn stalk fiber-modified recycled PAC-13 mixtures.

title: Waste, Resources, and Regulation: Assessing Environmental Sustainability in the European Union
summary: ABSTRACT Waste generated by economic activities has reached serious levels and threatens ecological sustainability. These activities not only prevent the economic use of natural resources but also leave behind waste that is difficult to man
content: ABSTRACT Waste generated by economic activities has reached serious levels and threatens ecological sustainability. These activities not only prevent the economic use of natural resources but also leave behind waste that is difficult to manage for the environment. Policymakers are seeking to meet some of their energy demand in a clean way while reducing the pressure on the ecology through waste management. The effectiveness of waste management may vary depending on environmental policy stringency. However, globalization affects society by changing consumption patterns and policymakers with different application examples. These factors, which drive one another, have the potential to seriously affect ecological sustainability. In this study, the impact of waste management expenditures, natural resource depletion, globalization, and environmental policy stringency on load capacity factor in selected European Union (EU) countries is investigated from 1995 to 2020. The results of the study reveal that while natural resource depletion, waste management expenditures, and globalization negatively affect environmental sustainability in France, environmental policy stringency affects it positively. Waste management expenditures in Spain and environmental policy stringency in Ireland increase environmental sustainability. To improve environmental quality in EU countries, it is recommended that environmental policies and standards be further harmonized between countries and that cooperation be increased to achieve common environmental goals.

title: Co‐Producing Environmental Resilience: Integrating Stakeholder, Legitimacy, and Co‐Production Theories to Explain Firms' Responses to Environmental Risk
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental risks challenge firms. While prior research assumes environmental resilience stems from communication or internal capability, this study reconceptualizes resilience as a relational capability co‐produced through firm‐
content: ABSTRACT Environmental risks challenge firms. While prior research assumes environmental resilience stems from communication or internal capability, this study reconceptualizes resilience as a relational capability co‐produced through firm‐stakeholder interactions. Integrating Stakeholder Theory, Legitimacy Theory, and Co‐production Theory, we test our framework using a two‐study design: Study 1 analyzes 93 multinational firms across 26 countries via hierarchical OLS, while Study 2 provides complementary evidence by tracking a matched sample of 139 Japanese firms using cross‐temporal lagged specifications. Our results indicate that stakeholder engagement alone does not mitigate environmental risk; resilience requires aligning external engagement with internal organizational readiness. Moreover, while substantive adaptation incurs immediate operational costs, our temporal evidence indicates that its financial implications are primarily contemporaneous and suggestive of temporal persistence, rather than demonstrating definitive long‐term financial causality. This study extends Co‐production Theory to corporate sustainability, reframing resilience as a strategic relational investment rather than a short‐term financial performance metric.

title: Self-organization of alternating acetate- and carbonate-based interlayer spaces in bimetallic CoZn layered hydroxide salts
summary: Layered hydroxide salts (LHS) are versatile functional materials whose properties can be tailored by the composition of metal hydroxide layers and interlayer anions. Here, a novel cobalt–zinc layered hydroxide salt (Co–Zn–LHS) containing di
content: Layered hydroxide salts (LHS) are versatile functional materials whose properties can be tailored by the composition of metal hydroxide layers and interlayer anions. Here, a novel cobalt–zinc layered hydroxide salt (Co–Zn–LHS) containing distinct intercalated layers of acetate and carbonate anions was reported. A comprehensive combination of indirect experimental data, compiled using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, Raman scattering, ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy, and thermal analysis, strongly indicated the formation of a single ordered phase with alternating mixed Co Zn hydroxide layers separated by acetate and carbonate interlayer spaces. The structure exhibited a basal periodicity of about 19.9 Å, close to the sum of typical carbonate- and acetate-LHS spacings, and showed up to twelve basal reflections with a coherent scattering domain size of approximately 500 Å, evidencing long-range ordering along the stacking direction. Anion-exchange experiments demonstrated the selective replacement of acetate FTIR bands, while carbonate bands remained essentially unchanged, which was consistent with the spatial separation of the two anionic interlayer spaces. The highest degree of ordering was achieved at near-equimolar Co/Zn ratios, where Zn preferentially stabilized tetrahedral sites and Co occupied octahedral positions. Thermal analysis revealed a sharp collapse of the layered structure at 240–300 °C, followed by transformation into a mixed Zn–Co–O oxide phase. Electrodes prepared from the optimized Co–Zn–LHS showed a specific capacity of 40 mAh g −1 (equivalent to a specific capacitance of 314 F g −1 ), with 61% capacity retention at 10 A g −1 . These results demonstrated a new route toward mixed-anion LHS materials with long-range ordered interlayer architectures.

title: A study on the four-party evolutionary game of collaborative carbon emission reduction in the petrochemical industry
summary: Against the dual backdrop of domestic green transformation and international carbon emission reduction constraints, this paper addresses the challenge of synergistic carbon governance in the petrochemical industry. Grounded in the industry’
content: Against the dual backdrop of domestic green transformation and international carbon emission reduction constraints, this paper addresses the challenge of synergistic carbon governance in the petrochemical industry. Grounded in the industry’s characteristics of long facility service life, high transformation costs, and strong policy dependence, it focuses on the interest conflicts among four parties—the central government, local governments, petrochemical enterprises, and third-party regulatory agencies—and develops a four-party evolutionary game model. Through local stability analysis and numerical simulation, the stability conditions and evolutionary trends of the four parties’ strategy choices are systematically examined. The results indicate that: (1) Raising the central government’s penalty intensity significantly shortens the decision-making time of the central government, petrochemical enterprises, and third-party agencies, yet prolongs the strategy evolution time of local governments; (2) As the central government’s subsidy coefficient increases, the central government’s strategy exhibits persistent fluctuation within the 0–1 interval and fails to converge to a steady state, while the decision-making time of petrochemical enterprises is markedly shortened, with the evolutionary trajectories of local governments and third-party agencies showing no significant change; (3) Strengthening local governments’ penalty intensity effectively accelerates the decision-making of local governments and petrochemical enterprises, whereas the evolutionary trajectories of the central government and third-party agencies remain largely unaffected; (4) Increasing local governments’ subsidy coefficient slows the evolution of local governments toward the proactive emission-reduction governance strategy, but effectively drives petrochemical enterprises to actively evolve toward proactive carbon reduction strategies. These findings offer theoretical support and practical implications for improving the multi-agent collaborative governance mechanism of carbon reduction in the petrochemical industry, assisting governments at all levels in formulating differentiated carbon regulation policies with precision, and promoting the green and low-carbon transformation of the petrochemical sector.

title: Recyclable Lignin‐Based Thermadapt Shape Memory Polymers With Near‐Infrared Light Response
summary: ABSTRACT Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have been designed to address the recycling challenges associated with thermosets, while preserving their mechanical properties. However, producing biobased CANs with intelligent response capabili
content: ABSTRACT Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) have been designed to address the recycling challenges associated with thermosets, while preserving their mechanical properties. However, producing biobased CANs with intelligent response capabilities remains challenging. We report the preparation of lignin‐polypentadecalactone‐based CANs with a high biomass content (86.2–96.4 wt%). In lignin‐PPDL CANs, acetoacetate‐modified lignin serves dual roles as the hard segment and crosslinker, while the polypentadecalactone (PPDL) soft segment exhibits a semi‐crystalline nature. Crosslinking between the soft PPDL and hard lignin segments is achieved via vinylogous urethane chemistry, resulting in CANs with markedly enhanced mechanical properties and recyclability. When applied to shape memory systems, the semi‐crystalline polymer domains act as reversible molecular switches, while dynamic bond exchange enables topological rearrangement, allowing reconfiguration of the permanent shape, characteristic of thermadapt shape memory polymers. Leveraging the photothermal conversion capability of lignin, we successfully developed near‐infrared (NIR) light‐responsive shape memory CANs. These innovative materials hold promising prospects for applications in intelligent materials, given their unique combination of mechanical strength, shape memory capabilities, and responsiveness to NIR light. Furthermore, the approach of tailoring the new material based on the specific properties of the raw material in this study offers a novel avenue for designing high‐performance multifunctional CANs.

title: Predicted soil loss and the contribution of soil map units in a tropical protected forest: Revised universal soil loss equation assessment of Ir. H. Djuanda Forest Park, Indonesia
summary: Soil erosion degrades soil and water resources in tropical protected areas.We mapped RUSLE-predicted soil loss in Ir.H. Djuanda Forest Park, West Java, Indonesia, and quantified the contribution of soil map units (SMUs) to spatial variation
content: Soil erosion degrades soil and water resources in tropical protected areas.We mapped RUSLE-predicted soil loss in Ir.H. Djuanda Forest Park, West Java, Indonesia, and quantified the contribution of soil map units (SMUs) to spatial variation in model inputs.Rainfall erosivity was derived from 2016-2025 CHIRPS precipitation using the modified Fournier index and Arnoldus relation, giving a period-mean R of 13,825.61MJ mm•ha -1 •h -1 •yr -1 .Soil erodibility was derived from a 1:50,000 soil map and SoilGrids organic carbon, the topographic factor from the DEMNAS grid using the Desmet-Govers formulation, and cover from SPOT-6 imagery (overall accuracy 82.5%, kappa 0.77).Cells with at least 300 contributing cells were treated as concentrated-flow cells and excluded from the hillslope calculation.The baseline RUSLE × SMU intersection contained 493.32 ha of valid estimates, with 93.36% below 385.14 t•ha -1 •yr -1 and a maximum predicted soil loss of 8,184.15t•ha -1 •yr -1 .SMU-4 contained 97.0% of the 32.74 ha above 385.14t•ha -1 •yr -1 .The area-weighted variance of ln(K) was 0.16% of that of ln(C), indicating substantially greater spatial contrast from land cover than from SMU-based K classes.Sensitivity testing showed that concentrated-flow treatment strongly affected the upper tail, whereas median LS changed by less than 10% between the unmasked and 75-cell scenarios.Without independent erosion measurements, the results are interpreted as modelled soil-loss potential and spatial screening information rather than measured erosion rates.

title: KÜRESEL EMİSYON TİCARET SİSTEMLERİNİN ÇEVRESEL VE EKONOMİK ETKİLERİNİN PRISMA YÖNTEMİ İLE ANALİZİ
source: Uluslararası İktisadi ve İdari İncelemeler Dergisi
summary: Emisyon Ticaret Sistemleri (ETS), iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede maliyet etkin emisyon azaltımı sağlayan önemli bir piyasa temelli politika aracı olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, ETS’nin ekonomik ve çevresel etkilerini bütüncül bir pers
content: Emisyon Ticaret Sistemleri (ETS), iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede maliyet etkin emisyon azaltımı sağlayan önemli bir piyasa temelli politika aracı olarak öne çıkmaktadır. Bu çalışma, ETS’nin ekonomik ve çevresel etkilerini bütüncül bir perspektifle değerlendirmeyi amaçlamaktadır. Bu doğrultuda, PRISMA yöntemi kullanılarak Web of Science ve Scopus veri tabanlarında tarama gerçekleştirilmiş, eleme süreci sonucunda 76 makale araştırmaya dahil edilmiştir. Bulgular, ETS’nin çevresel performansın yanı sıra enerji tüketim yapısı, endüstriyel dönüşüm, yeşil teknoloji inovasyonu, doğrudan yabancı yatırımlar ve yeşil finansman üzerinde de önemli etkiler oluşturduğunu göstermiştir. Ayrıca, kısa vadede karbon yoğun sektörlerde maliyet baskısı oluştursa da uzun vadede düşük karbonlu üretimi teşvik ederek sürdürülebilir ekonomik büyümeyi desteklediği belirlenmiştir. Araştırma sonucunda, ETS’nin çevresel hedefler ile ekonomik performans arasında denge kurabildiği ve etkinliğinin politika tasarımı ile tamamlayıcı düzenlemelere bağlı olduğu ortaya konulmuştur.

title: Implementing the 2ZERO Technology in Vehicle Parc Models: The Impact of Research and Innovation in Long-Term Outlooks for the EU
summary: Abstract The European Commission has set ambitious CO 2 reduction targets for the transport sector as part of its broader carbon neutrality strategy for 2050 (Fit for 55). In response, the 2ZERO Partnership seeks to accelerate the transitio
content: Abstract The European Commission has set ambitious CO 2 reduction targets for the transport sector as part of its broader carbon neutrality strategy for 2050 (Fit for 55). In response, the 2ZERO Partnership seeks to accelerate the transition toward zero tailpipe emission mobility focusing on affordable, user-centric technologies and services and supporting their widespread adoption. 2ZERO also supports progress in life-cycle analysis methods, the deployment of efficient charging infrastructure, and the mitigation of non-powertrain emissions and road transport-related noise within a circular economy context. LeMesurier is a Horizon Europe Coordination and Support Action that developed a framework for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of the 2ZERO Partnership in achieving its goals. It assesses progress against Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) outlined in the Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda (SRIA) of the Partnership. In this paper, long-term impacts (2025–2050) of introducing affordable, innovative zero-emission vehicle technologies (BEVs and FCEVs) are explored. A comprehensive modelling approach introduces three models: i) COPERT/SIBYL (tank-to-wheel); ii) PRIMES-TREMOVE, a techno-economic model (well-to-wheel); and iii) MOVEID, a resource optimization model (life-cycle assessment). The analysis quantifies 2ZERO innovation impacts on energy demand, CO 2 emissions and GHG intensity of vehicles, highlighting the importance of research and innovation in meeting decarbonization goals.

title: Decadal variability reveals contrasts in solar-resource stability across China
summary: Abstract Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal h
content: Abstract Solar resource assessments traditionally focus on how much solar radiation is available and how it changes over time, while overlooking how stable that resource remains throughout the decades. Here, we quantify the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of decadal variability in downward surface solar radiation (DSSR), commonly known as global horizontal irradiance (GHI) in the solar energy sector, across China’s seven major power grids during 1960–2024. We find pronounced regional contrasts in decadal DSSR variability, with the Central, Eastern, and Southern grids exhibiting greater variability, whereas the Western and Tibetan grids, combine high solar resource abundance with comparatively low variability. The Central and Eastern grids also contribute disproportionately to national variability relative to their geographical area. By converting DSSR variability into indicative photovoltaic (PV) yield, we further illustrate that resource-driven yield uncertainty is substantially higher in the volatile eastern regions; however, spatial diversification across weakly correlated grids can reduce portfolio variability by up to 29%. These findings emphasize that the geography of solar-resource climatic stability differs from resource abundance, highlighting the critical need to incorporate decadal stability and spatial diversification into long-term renewable-energy and inter-regional transmission planning.

title: Does Going Green Change the Numbers? Carbon Footprint Certification, Corporate Governance, and Firm Outcomes in Thailand
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT Voluntary environmental certification is often assumed to signal broader improvements in corporate accountability, including financial reporting quality. This study tests that assumption using Thailand's Carbon Footprint for Organi
content: ABSTRACT Voluntary environmental certification is often assumed to signal broader improvements in corporate accountability, including financial reporting quality. This study tests that assumption using Thailand's Carbon Footprint for Organization (CFO) certification, a third‐party‐verified carbon‐accounting scheme administered by the country's Greenhouse Gas Management Organization. We ask whether certification is associated with earnings quality and financial performance among Stock Exchange of Thailand‐listed non‐financial firms, and whether firm‐level corporate governance moderates this relationship. Using a staggered difference‐in‐differences design on a propensity‐score‐matched panel of 409 firms over fiscal years 2013–2024, we triangulate four estimators of increasing robustness to bias—a naive baseline, stacked two‐way fixed effects with contaminated comparisons removed, and two heterogeneity‐robust staggered‐adoption estimators—so that our conclusions do not rest on any single method's assumptions; governance moderation is tested using a hand‐collected, seven‐component governance index measured before certification. Certification shows no detectable effect on earnings management, accrual quality, or accounting profitability, and interval and equivalence tests rule out effects larger than roughly 0.3 standard deviations for each outcome. Market valuation is the one exception: certified firms show a positive association with Tobin's Q , but this result is weak and specification‐dependent, and does not survive alternative comparison groups or multiple‐testing adjustment. Governance moderation is likewise exploratory: a few raw signals emerge when governance is measured before certification, but none survives correction for multiple testing. These patterns are consistent with certification that is genuinely implemented yet decoupled from internal financial‐reporting behavior, extending institutional accounts of voluntary certification and signaling theory. Because our outcomes capture financial‐reporting spillovers rather than the scheme's environmental ends, we cannot speak to whether certification changes environmental practice itself. For policymakers and investors, the findings caution against inferring improved financial‐reporting quality, or genuine environmental commitment, from certification status alone.

title: From Diesel to Fuel-Cell Powertrains, A Virtual Retrofit Use Case for Buses and Airport Ground Service Vehicles
summary: Abstract Vehicle fleet decarbonization through electrification and alternative fuels such as hydrogen (H 2 ) is a key strategy for CO 2 emissions reduction from road transport. H 2 -powered vehicles are expected to have a significant impact
content: Abstract Vehicle fleet decarbonization through electrification and alternative fuels such as hydrogen (H 2 ) is a key strategy for CO 2 emissions reduction from road transport. H 2 -powered vehicles are expected to have a significant impact when integrated into a complete H 2 ecosystem like hydrogen valleys. This study evaluates the transition of the vehicle fleet (buses and airport’s ground service vehicles) in the vicinity of Malpensa Airport from conventional to H 2 -fuelled powertrains using a combined experimental and computational approach. Fuel consumption of the vehicles is obtained via real world data recording, while the respective simulation models are developed to represent the vehicles’ powertrain configuration. To achieve this, all the sub-models are parametrized using the technical specifications of each vehicle. The simulation models are evaluated by comparing calculation results with experimental data. These models are used as a basis for virtual retrofitting with fuel-cell systems. Results demonstrate the potential from switching to H 2 -fuelled powertrains, highlighting the reduction of tailpipe pollutants and CO 2 emissions that ranges between 35% and 93% depending on the emissions from H 2 production process.

title: From Feasibility to Profitability: Economic Evaluation of On-Board H2 Production for Rail Operators
summary: Abstract Building on TRA2024 publication “Technico-economic Feasibility Study of On-board H2 Production in a Passenger Hydrogen Train for Railway Operators” [1], which demonstrated the feasibility of on-board hydrogen production for regiona
content: Abstract Building on TRA2024 publication “Technico-economic Feasibility Study of On-board H2 Production in a Passenger Hydrogen Train for Railway Operators” [1], which demonstrated the feasibility of on-board hydrogen production for regional trains, this work compares three decarbonization solutions: a bi-mode hydrogen train (Régiolis H 2 ), a newly sized all-battery train, and a reversible hydrogen train. These alternatives were evaluated across 13 challenging French routes, selected for their length and limited electrification. For each solution, we assessed CAPEX (electrification, depot upgrades, hydro gen infrastructure) and OPEX (maintenance and energy costs over the rolling stock’s mid-life). Results reveal distinct trade-offs: the Régiolis H 2 is optimal for shorter unelectrified sections due to lower rolling stock costs but requires hydrogen infrastructure; the all-battery train offers extended range with minimal infra-structure, though at higher individual costs; and the reversible hydrogen train emerges as a versatile compromise, eliminating hydrogen infrastructure needs while providing greater range—though dependent on on-board electrolysis R&D. This analysis provides actionable insights for railway operators investing in decarbonization technologies.

title: Blockchain traceability investment in agricultural supply chains: cost sharing, fairness concerns, and channel performance
summary: Introduction This study investigates optimal decisions in a blockchain-enabled agricultural supply chain under alternative cost-sharing and fairness-concern configurations. Methods A two-stage Stackelberg game is developed with a manufactur
content: Introduction This study investigates optimal decisions in a blockchain-enabled agricultural supply chain under alternative cost-sharing and fairness-concern configurations. Methods A two-stage Stackelberg game is developed with a manufacturer as the leader and a retailer as the follower. The manufacturer determines the wholesale price and blockchain traceability level, after which the retailer determines the retail price and marketing effort. Fairness-adjusted utilities are constructed using generalized Nash-bargaining reference profits. Four scenarios are examined: no cost sharing with fairness-neutral parties (NN), no cost sharing with a fairness-concerned manufacturer (NM), cost sharing with fairness-neutral parties (SN), and cost sharing with a fairness-concerned retailer (SR). Closed-form equilibria and comparative-static results are derived and examined numerically. Results Under fairness neutrality, retailer cost sharing reduces the manufacturer's effective investment burden and increases wholesale price, retail price, traceability level, and marketing effort. It benefits the manufacturer but reduces retailer profit at sufficiently high sharing ratios; total supply-chain profit increases only below a threshold. Without cost sharing, stronger manufacturer fairness concern raises the wholesale price but reduces traceability investment and both parties' monetary profits. Manufacturer utility may initially increase before declining beyond a critical fairness threshold. Under cost sharing, retailer fairness concern lowers the retail price, marketing effort, traceability investment, and manufacturer profit. Its effects on retailer and total supply-chain profit depend on the cost-sharing ratio, bargaining power, and fairness concern. Discussion Within the configurations considered, moderate fairness concern can partly correct the incentive distortion caused by a high cost-sharing ratio, whereas excessive fairness concern weakens demand and channel efficiency. These findings highlight the importance of balancing investment incentives and distributional concerns when designing blockchain cost-sharing contracts.

title: Forecasting and Explaining Environmental Fiscal Capacity: How Informality and FinTech Shape Environmental and Biodiversity Finance
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of the shadow economy (SE) on environmental fiscal capacity (environmental tax revenue, public environmental expenditure, and biodiversity expenditure) and the moderating role of financial technology
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of the shadow economy (SE) on environmental fiscal capacity (environmental tax revenue, public environmental expenditure, and biodiversity expenditure) and the moderating role of financial technology (FinTech) across OECD countries over 2004–2022. Using second‐generation econometric techniques, with robustness assessed through the CCEMG estimator, Driscoll–Kraay fixed effects, and one‐step GMM, and complemented by machine‐learning forecasting (tensor double machine learning and a graph‐inspired machine learning model) compared using the Diebold–Mariano test. The analysis yields three main findings. First, the SE significantly reduces environmental tax revenue and public environmental and biodiversity expenditures, consistent with the hypothesis that informality constrains the fiscal capacity required for environmental protection. Second, FinTech adoption directly enhances environmental revenue and mitigates the adverse effect of the SE on environmental revenue through a transaction‐formalization channel that expands the observable tax base, although its direct association with biodiversity expenditure is negative, reflecting a countervailing frontier‐expansion effect. Third, the forecasting evidence reinforces this structural account: Environmental tax revenue is strongly forecastable and public environmental expenditure moderately so, whereas biodiversity expenditure resists accurate prediction across both models. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of digital financial innovation as a complementary instrument for reducing informality, strengthening environmental governance, and advancing biodiversity conservation in OECD economies.

title: Integrating soil erosion modelling and field verification for spatial assessment of critical land
summary: Land degradation is a global environmental issue that affects the ecological functions and sustainability of land resources.In Indonesia, degraded land conditions are commonly addressed through the concept of critical land, particularly in
content: Land degradation is a global environmental issue that affects the ecological functions and sustainability of land resources.In Indonesia, degraded land conditions are commonly addressed through the concept of critical land, particularly in watershed assessment, management, and rehabilitation.Spatial approaches have been widely applied to identify critical land over large areas; however, their representativeness is strongly influenced by input data quality and may not fully reflect site-level degradation conditions.This study assessed critical land using a spatial approach that integrated key biophysical parameters with field-based verification in part of the Serang Watershed.Critical land was identified using a multicriteria spatial approach based on P.3/PDASHL/SET/KUM.1/7/2018.Land cover was derived from Sentinel-2A imagery using Random Forest and quantitatively assessed using 45 field reference points.Soil erosion was estimated using USLE, with soil erodibility determined through laboratory analysis of 18 soil samples representing different land units.Five criticality classes were identified, with Slightly Critical land dominating 58.45% of the study area, while Critical and Highly Critical land accounted for 6.27%.Field-based verification of areas classified as Critical and Highly Critical revealed diverse degradation characteristics, including rill and gully erosion, topsoil loss, shallow soil, slope failure, and anthropogenic disturbances.These findings indicate that integrating spatial modelling with field-based verification can provide site-level information to support the interpretation of critical-land conditions and the development of site-specific soil conservation and land rehabilitation measures.

title: Functional heterogeneity among four co-occurring landfill bacteria during low-density polyethylene transformation
summary: Abstract Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) transformation is usually reported for individual isolates, whereas direct comparisons among co-occurring bacteria from the same contaminated habitat are scarce. Four Gram-negative bacteria were isol
content: Abstract Low-density polyethylene (LDPE) transformation is usually reported for individual isolates, whereas direct comparisons among co-occurring bacteria from the same contaminated habitat are scarce. Four Gram-negative bacteria were isolated from a plastic-contaminated municipal dumpsite in Ghaziabad, India, and identified by 16S rRNA gene sequencing as Pseudomonas sp. DW, Dyella japonica DP, Enterobacter sp. DLY and Pantoea agglomerans DY. Growth, extracellular enzyme profiles, gravimetric loss, microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy were compared over 45 days under a common framework. All isolates grew best at 30°C and pH 7.0. Pseudomonas sp. DW showed the highest apparent mass loss (16.07 ± 0.18%), carbonyl index (0.2444) and hydroxyl index (0.1773), the most extensive biofilm, and the only lipase/esterase activity under nutrient limitation. Enterobacter sp. DLY lost 13.96 ± 0.14% of mass and had a carbonyl index of 0.2031 without detectable lipase/esterase activity. To our knowledge, D. japonica DP and P. agglomerans DY are the first isolates of these species characterised for LDPE transformation at species level; only genus-level reports exist for Dyella and Pantoea , and Pseudomonas and Enterobacter are established LDPE-associated genera, so no taxonomic novelty is claimed for them. The principal novelty is the within-site comparison showing that similar endpoints can arise from different trait combinations, which guides strain selection for mechanistic and consortium studies.

title: Nb-DOPED TiO2 SUPPORTS ENABLE HIGH OER ACTIVITY AT REDUCED IRIDIUM LOADING
summary: The scarcity of iridium (Ir) remains a key barrier to large-scale deployment of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). To address this challenge, we demonstrate that Nb-doped TiO2 (NbTiO) serves as an optimal support to enha
content: The scarcity of iridium (Ir) remains a key barrier to large-scale deployment of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). To address this challenge, we demonstrate that Nb-doped TiO2 (NbTiO) serves as an optimal support to enhance both the electrochemical activity and durability of Ir catalytic sites toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). By balancing crystallinity and surface area, Nb-doping improves electronic conductivity without compromising the uniform dispersion of Ir nanoparticles. The optimized Ir/NbTiO catalyst (50 wt.% Ir) exhibits fine particle dispersion (~2.5 nm), high electrochemically active surface area, and tailored metal-support interactions. Consequently, the catalyst delivers an outstanding balance between high specific activity (6.2 mA C⁻¹) and exceptional durability, retaining over 95% of its initial performance following extended operation. Fundamentally, incorporating Nb into the TiO2 crystal lattice promotes the intrinsic activity of Ir while ensuring efficient charge transport and sustained stability of the active sites. These findings reaffirm NbTiO as a robust and promising support platform, offering a viable pathway to minimize iridium loading in next-generation PEMWE anodes.

title: Justice: Past, Present and Future
source: Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics
summary: The Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics (EJPE) interviewed Meyer about his early influences and how he almost did not become a philosopher (sections I and II), his path from Berlin to Oxford and the extension of liberal political p
content: The Erasmus Journal for Philosophy and Economics (EJPE) interviewed Meyer about his early influences and how he almost did not become a philosopher (sections I and II), his path from Berlin to Oxford and the extension of liberal political philosophy (section III), the threshold notion of harm (section IV), obligations to past people (section V), the supersession thesis (section VI), historical emissions and fair shares (section VII), the restitution of cultural artworks (section VIII), legitimate expectations (section IX), philosophy and the IPCC (section X), his future plans (section XI), and, finally, his advice for aspiring academics (section XII). I. EARLY INFLUENCES EJPE: If you think back, what initially drew you to philosophy generally, and specifically the kind of liberal egalitarian philosophy you practice today?

title: Минеральная карбонизация CO2 в хвостах флотации медно-никелевых руд Талнахской обогатительной фабрики: экспериментальная и термодинамическая оценка
summary: Хвосты обогащения медно-никелевых руд, содержащие Ca-, Mg- и Fe-силикаты, представляют интерес как потенциальный материал для минеральной карбонизации CO2. Цель работы – оценить потенциал использования пустой породы хвостохранилища Талнахск
content: Хвосты обогащения медно-никелевых руд, содержащие Ca-, Mg- и Fe-силикаты, представляют интерес как потенциальный материал для минеральной карбонизации CO2. Цель работы – оценить потенциал использования пустой породы хвостохранилища Талнахской обогатительной фабрики ПАО «ГМК «Норильский никель» для связывания углекислого газа в форме карбонатных фаз и определить факторы, контролирующие эффективность этого процесса. Исследование выполнено с применением комплекса минералого-геохимических методов (сканирующая электронная микроскопия, рентгенофазовый анализ, ИК-спектроскопия, ICP-MS, определение неорганического углерода), лабораторного эксперимента по насыщению породы CO2 при 25 °C и давлении 1 бар в течение 7 сут и термодинамического моделирования равновесий методом минимизации свободной энергии Гиббса (пакет программ HCh). Установлено, что хвосты, наряду с высоким содержанием сульфидов, прежде всего пирротина FenSn + 1, содержат пироксены, включая диопсид CaMgSi2O6, плагиоклазы ряда NaAlSi3O8–CaAl2Si2O8, серпентин Mg3Si2O5(OH)4 и амфиболы, представленные Ca-, Mg- и Fe-силикатами, способными участвовать в реакциях карбонизации. В эксперименте зафиксирован прирост суммарной карбонатной фазы на 1,92 мас.% преимущественно за счет доломита, без дополнительной активации материала. В модельных расчетах наиболее существенное влияние на выход карбонатов оказало парциальное давление CO2; повышение температуры в интервале 25-100 °C, напротив, снизило содержание карбонатных фаз вследствие перераспределения Ca и Mg в силикатные минералы. Показано, что вторичное силикатообразование конкурирует с карбонатообразованием за двухвалентные катионы, ограничивая реальный потенциал процесса. Хвосты могут рассматриваться как вторичный минеральный ресурс для связывания CO2, однако практическая реализация требует дальнейшей оценки кинетических ограничений и долговременной устойчивости новообразованных минеральных фаз.

title: Review of the Radon Tracer Method for GHG emission estimates: development, application guidelines, improvements, and caveats
summary: Abstract. The Radon Tracer Method (RTM) is an established, independent top-down method that can be used to cross-check bottom-up greenhouse gas (GHG) emission estimates. Furthermore, as uncertainties of Atmospheric Transport Models are redu
content: Abstract. The Radon Tracer Method (RTM) is an established, independent top-down method that can be used to cross-check bottom-up greenhouse gas (GHG) emission estimates. Furthermore, as uncertainties of Atmospheric Transport Models are reduced, the RTM can provide a convenient means of quantifying continual improvement of inversion-based top-down GHG emission estimates. While the accessibility and perceived simplicity of the RTM drive its popularity, the technique is better suited to assessing long-term relative changes in GHG emissions than absolute changes, due to short-term soil moisture influences on simulated radon flux uncertainty. Considerations for applying the RTM, based on fundamental assumptions of the technique's development, are application and season specific, making the development of a "standard protocol" for its use challenging. After proposing a novel alternative means of applying the nocturnal accumulation RTM, which improves interpretation of findings, we use measurements from a range of contrasting sites to discuss the significance of the technique's eight key considerations: (i) nocturnal window definition, (ii) radon and target gas accumulation thresholds, (iii) radon-to-target gas regression linearity thresholds, (iv) measurement height, (v) the contributing fetch, (vi) spatial and temporal radon flux variability, (vii) RTM temporal resolution, and (viii) application specific selection of a suitable radon monitor. The insight provided by these examples to the flexibility (or otherwise) of the technique's considerations will clarify the implications if users choose to relax or ignore them, potentially making future RTM studies more directly comparable.

title: Gene tree conflict between genomic and functional partitions impacts phylogenetic inference in Zygophylloideae
summary: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic re
content: Abstract The Zygophyllaceae subfamily Zygophylloideae includes seven genera and around 180 species distributed worldwide particularly in arid areas where they show adaptations to drought including C 4 and CAM photosynthesis. Phylogenetic relationships of Zygophylloideae have been analysed in several studies using Sanger sequenced markers, but none have been able to resolve all deeper relationships between genera in the subfamily. Here, we use ion semi-conductor sequencing of chloroplast and nuclear ribosomal regions to analyse these relationships and assess why they have proved so challenging to resolve. We sequenced 39 chloroplast genes and nuclear ribosomal 18S, 5.8S, and 26S genes and internal transcribed spacers (ITS) for key species of Zygophyllum sensu stricto, Roepera, Tetraena, Fagonia , Zygophyllum stapffii and monotypic Augea capensis ; and Tribulus of the subfamily Tribuloideae as outgroup. We aligned these with data from published chloroplast genomes followed by phylogenetic analyses using Maximum Likelihood and Bayesian approaches, summarising phylogenetic results separately for non-coding introns and intergenic spacers, and for genes that are, or are not, involved in photosynthesis. We combined the chloroplast data with sequences of three highly variable noncoding chloroplast regions used in previous studies of greater numbers of taxa, and similarly the nuclear ribosomal data with more densely sampled ITS sequences and assessed whether adding such data resulted in improved support for consistent topologies. We used a chloroplast sequence matrix to infer a dated phylogeny. Adding data did not always improve phylogenetic resolution which was apparently impacted by non-informative variation in chloroplast photosynthesis related genes as well as by conflicting chloroplast and nuclear signals. Chloroplast genes not related to photosynthesis provide robust support for a topology that is consistent with independent data and may therefore represent a useful species tree hypothesis. The cause of the gene tree conflicts remains unclear: potential explanations include functional constraints in photosynthesis related genes and introgressive hybridization and/or incomplete lineage sorting during an ancient rapid divergence. Further testing will require a broader sampling of lineages with different photosynthetic modes and multiple informative, independent, and selectively neutral gene trees.

title: Towards European hydrogen market design: Perspectives from transmission system operators
summary: Despite hydrogen being central to Europe’s decarbonisation strategy, only a small share of renewable hydrogen projects have reached final investment decision. A key barrier is uncertainty about how future hydrogen markets will be designed a
content: Despite hydrogen being central to Europe’s decarbonisation strategy, only a small share of renewable hydrogen projects have reached final investment decision. A key barrier is uncertainty about how future hydrogen markets will be designed and operated, particularly under Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin requirements. This study investigates the extent to which future hydrogen market design can be adapted from existing natural gas markets, and the challenges it must address. The analysis was based on a survey on future hydrogen market design targeting European gas transmission system operators, the stakeholder group responsible for operating the network and implementing the Network Codes. The survey provided an assessment of mechanism transferability and identified challenges for the early development of the hydrogen market. Core market design principles and trading frameworks are broadly transferable from natural gas markets, such as entry-exit systems and virtual trading points. Capacity allocation requires targeted adaptation to improve coupling with electricity markets. Tariffs require adaptation through intertemporal cost allocation, distributing infrastructure costs over time to protect early adopters. Balancing regimes should be revisited to reflect hydrogen’s physical characteristics and different linepack flexibility uses. Key challenges for early hydrogen markets include: temporal mismatches between variable renewable supply and expected relatively stable industrial demand, limited operational flexibility due to scarce storage and reduced pipeline linepack, fragmented regional hydrogen clusters, and regulatory uncertainty affecting long-term investment decisions. These findings provide empirical input to the hydrogen Network Codes and offer guidance to policymakers designing hydrogen market frameworks.

title: Who pays for decarbonizing homes?
summary: The decarbonization of the residential building sector requires large upfront investments in heating system replacement and thermal renovation that fall disproportionately on lower-income households. Faced with political constraints on carb
content: The decarbonization of the residential building sector requires large upfront investments in heating system replacement and thermal renovation that fall disproportionately on lower-income households. Faced with political constraints on carbon pricing and technology mandates, investment subsidies have become the main policy instrument.This paper analyzes the distributional effects and fiscal costs of this policy approach for Austria. We develop a microsimulation model that links household-level investment needs to landlord wealth distributions,allowing us to assign the incidence of subsidies and financial burden across homeowners and landlords within a unified empirical setting.We find total investment needs amount to 78–92 billion euros over the transition period to 2040 (approximately 1% of GDP annually), implying fiscal costs of 33–40 billion euros under the 2023 subsidy scheme. Despite a targeted low-income component, approximately 45% of subsidy outlays accrue to the top three income deciles. Net investment burdens remain strongly regressive when thermal renovation is required, exceeding three annual incomes for low-income single-family homeowners. We further document substantial horizontal disparities within income groups and show that Austria's fragmented housing law is a first-order determinant of investment feasibility in the multi-apartment (rental) sector.Addressing distributional and feasibility concerns under fiscal constraints may require a policy mix combining mandates, income-contingent transfers, liquidity-support instruments and housing law reform.

title: Governing climate neutrality through climate city contracts: Insights from twenty-five European cities
summary: Mission-oriented innovation policy has become an influential framework for addressing complex societal challenges and is increasingly shaping urban climate governance through the European Union's Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities Mission. Th
content: Mission-oriented innovation policy has become an influential framework for addressing complex societal challenges and is increasingly shaping urban climate governance through the European Union's Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities Mission. This paper examines how Climate City Contracts (CCCs) help cities address the principal governance barriers that constrain the transition to climate neutrality. A structured review of recent literature identifies seven recurrent governance gaps: institutional silos and systems integration; multi-level coordination; financing and institutional innovation; technical capacity and data; stakeholder participation and co-creation; ecosystem coordination; and climate justice and social acceptance. To examine how these challenges are addressed in practice, the paper analyses the Climate City Contracts of twenty-five European Mission cities. The results show that the main contribution of CCCs lies in their capacity to catalyse institutional innovation through governance arrangements designed to overcome systemic constraints. Across diverse urban contexts, six recurring families of governance instruments are identified: Mission Governance Structures, Portfolio Management Systems, Climate Finance Integration Instruments, Multi-Stakeholder Climate Platforms, Deliberative and Inclusive Participation Mechanisms, and Urban Innovation and Experimentation Platforms. Together, these instruments form an emerging governance architecture that enables cities to organise, finance, and implement climate-neutral transitions in systemic, adaptive, and socially legitimate ways. The paper contributes to research on urban sustainability transitions and mission-oriented innovation by showing how broad policy ambitions are translated into operational governance arrangements for climate neutrality at the urban level. • Climate City Contracts operationalize mission-oriented governance for climate neutrality. • Seven governance gaps shape the implementation of climate-neutral cities. • Twenty-five European cities reveal six recurring governance instrument families. • Climate City Contracts catalyse institutional innovation and systemic coordination.

title: Analysis of power transition scenarios in the Western Balkans: Evaluating air quality and health impacts
summary: Most Western Balkans (WB) economies heavily rely on lignite for electricity production, contributing to some of Europe’s most severe air pollution levels. Consequently, electricity costs are likely to rise as carbon pricing becomes operatio
content: Most Western Balkans (WB) economies heavily rely on lignite for electricity production, contributing to some of Europe’s most severe air pollution levels. Consequently, electricity costs are likely to rise as carbon pricing becomes operational, with the potential additional risk of interfering in the European Union (EU) accession process if national emission ceilings are not met. National strategies remain fragmented from the regional integrated WB electricity market, highlighting the urgent need for coherent, evidence-based transition roadmaps. To bridge this gap, we benchmarked the Joint Research Centre (JRC) integrated WB Electricity Market Model (EMM) against each economy National Energy and Climate Action Plans (NECP), highlighting synergies and divergences to guide forthcoming national strategies revisions. Then these scenarios are analysed with the JRC Fast Scenario Screening Tool (JRC-FASST), to estimate air quality and health impacts under two distinct electricity pathways from 2015 to 2040. The magnitude of benefits varies across scenarios, each of which is designed to meet specific objectives. From an economic perspective, the cost-optimisation scenario (EMM 2024) could prevent over 5340 premature deaths by 2030, compared with the previous forecast (EMM 2022). From a policy perspective, full implementation of NECP-BAT power sector measures would avoid more than 5330 yearly premature deaths in 2030 relative to a scenario that delays by five years the decommissioning of coal power plants. The emission control techniques envisaged in the same scenario would halve air pollution-related mortality in 2030 compared to business as usual (NECP-EXT).

title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
summary: Abstract The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is essential for mitigating human-induced climate change and achieving climate neutrality, requiring reliable and resilient renewable energy systems. However, global warming is e
content: Abstract The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is essential for mitigating human-induced climate change and achieving climate neutrality, requiring reliable and resilient renewable energy systems. However, global warming is expected to increase the instability of renewable energy resources, particularly during periods of simultaneous low wind and solar power generation, known as renewable energy droughts (REDs). Nevertheless, a consistent assessment of REDs that explicitly accounts for the compound dependence and joint variability of wind and solar resources remains lacking. Here, we investigate REDs globally under 1.5°, 2.0° and 3.0°C global warming levels (GWLs) using CMIP6 multi-model simulations, explicitly capturing their compound nature and the joint dependence between wind and solar resources. The impacts of global warming are evaluated through changes in RED intensity, duration and frequency across GWLs. Results show that REDs intensify progressively with warming, with statistically significant changes affecting more than half of global land area for all three characteristics at 3.0°C GWL. Machine learning analysis identifies solar radiation as the dominant driver of RED intensification, with influence strengthening under higher GWLs. These findings highlight the need to integrate compound risk assessments into renewable energy planning to ensure system reliability in a warming world.

title: Transforming the global food system for environmental sustainability and food security
summary: The global food system simultaneously drives and is threatened by intersecting planetary crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation and desertification, and pollution and waste. Food production and consumption generate ap
content: The global food system simultaneously drives and is threatened by intersecting planetary crises of climate change, biodiversity loss, land degradation and desertification, and pollution and waste. Food production and consumption generate approximately one-third of anthropogenic greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, account for 39% of global deforestation, and impose external costs estimated at US$15 to US$20 trillion annually. This is roughly double the US$9 trillion value of food consumed each year globally. While total food production has consistently increased since the Green Revolution, over 700 million people remain chronically hungry, 878 million adults are obese, and all countries face at least one form of malnutrition. Projections indicate that total food demand will rise 35% between 2020 and 2050, leading to further biodiversity loss, accelerating climate change, and worsening nutritional inequity, if we stay on a business-as-usual course. The fuel and fertilizer shortage and the resulting risk of a major food crisis triggered by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz demonstrate the structural fragility of current food systems. This paper synthesizes findings of state-of-the-art scientific literature into a set of solutions for delivering food systems that are simultaneously productive, nutritionally adequate, environmentally sustainable, and socially just. We categorize the solutions in five pathways: shifting to healthy and sustainable diets; improving crop, livestock, and aquatic food production and land-use systems; reducing food loss and waste while increasing circularity; expanding novel foods and production processes; and restructuring food industry market structures and trade. These pathways are mutually reinforcing and must be pursued simultaneously. Their combined deployment could contribute to climate mitigation, reduce global agricultural land expansion, and reduce diet-attributable disease burden — outcomes that no individual pathway achieves in isolation. Policy reforms, including subsidy repurposing, true-cost pricing, and coordinated trade policy, are critical to foster enabling conditions across all pathways. Making our food systems environmentally and socially sustainable requires urgent, coordinated, and integrated action from all actors across the food value chain.

title: Europe according to the Founding Fathers and contemporary problems of European integration
summary: Objectives The subject of the article is the evolution of European integration in the light of the original ideas of the EU Founding Fathers in the face of contemporary socio-economic and technological transformations. The objective is to a
content: Objectives The subject of the article is the evolution of European integration in the light of the original ideas of the EU Founding Fathers in the face of contemporary socio-economic and technological transformations. The objective is to assess the relevance of the vision of “unity in diversity” in the era of the digital society and global crises. Material and methods The study employs the dogmatic-legal method (analysis of selected EU legal acts and CJEU case law), source analysis of historical and contemporary documents, and a comparative approach with regard Results The analysis indicates that the contemporary dynamics of integration significantly diverge from the decentralised vision of a confederation of sovereign states. Top-down institutional polarisation and the digital redefinition of social ties generate a risk of internal tensions, weakening the existing public order. Conclusions In the discussion section, a proposal to revise the current political course of the EU is formulated as a de lege ferenda recommendation, distinct from the analytical findings. According to the author, maintaining peace and competitiveness requires moving away from centralist tendencies and the concept of a superstate in favour of respect for the cultural autonomy and legal sovereignty of nations.

title: Climate justice: Is there an individual right of citizen to climate neutrality?
summary: This paper analyzes citizens' access to climate justice under European and Spanish law. Despite ambitious legislation rendering climate neutrality targets binding and imposing corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), procedural stand
content: This paper analyzes citizens' access to climate justice under European and Spanish law. Despite ambitious legislation rendering climate neutrality targets binding and imposing corporate sustainability due diligence (CSDDD), procedural standing (legitimación activa) remains strictly constrained. Both CJEU and Spanish jurisprudence require proof of direct, individualized harm, preventing citizens from challenging public or corporate inaction on an individual basis. Currently, regulatory mechanisms reduce citizens to submitting administrative complaints or claiming post-damage civil compensation. De lege ferenda, achieving effective climate justice requires recognizing an autonomous, enforceable individual right to climate neutrality, transforming citizens into active guarantors of mandatory sustainability standards.

title: An energy-efficient approach to sludge drying: Simulation and optimization of a heat pump assisted low-temperature belt dryer
summary: Sludge drying is the most energy-intensive and carbon-emitting stage in the sludge treatment and disposal process. The thermal drying technologies currently employed generally exhibit high energy consumption, which increases the overall cos
content: Sludge drying is the most energy-intensive and carbon-emitting stage in the sludge treatment and disposal process. The thermal drying technologies currently employed generally exhibit high energy consumption, which increases the overall cost and energy demand of sludge management. To solve this problem, this study designed a novel heat pump-assisted low-temperature belt dryer with a center-return air configuration to enhance drying uniformity and efficiency. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were used to guide the drying chamber design. The results supported installing baffles at both ends to reduce local airflow velocities and positioning fans centrally to improve airflow uniformity. Thermodynamic modeling was used to identify optimal operating parameters. Results indicated an optimal refrigerant charge of 9-12 kg, and that the waste heat exchanger could meet system requirements under lower water flow and larger temperature difference conditions. The highest specific moisture evaporation rate (SMER) and lowest energy consumption per ton of sludge were achieved in the evaporation-temperature simulations at an evaporation temperature of 36°C, with values of 3.84 kg water/kWh and 173.6 kWh per ton of sludge, respectively. Lower return air temperature improved energy efficiency while meeting dryness requirements, and increasing the air flow ratio reduced energy use but required trade-offs with drying performance. Engineering-scale monitoring showed that the outlet sludge moisture content remained below 40% and the measured SMER ranged from 3.5 to 4.5 kg water/kWh during the observation period.

title: Calculation of Combined Diffusion Coefficients of Argon–Copper and Argon–Tungsten Thermal Plasma Mixtures Based on Various Interaction Potentials
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract Copper (Cu) and tungsten (W) are widely used as electrode materials in thermal plasma devices. Their erosion remains a critical challenge because metal vapors diffuse into the plasma column, significantly altering the plasma compos
content: Abstract Copper (Cu) and tungsten (W) are widely used as electrode materials in thermal plasma devices. Their erosion remains a critical challenge because metal vapors diffuse into the plasma column, significantly altering the plasma composition and, consequently, the thermodynamic, radiative, and transport properties. Accurate prediction of this effect requires reliable transport data, particularly combined diffusion coefficients, which are essential for modeling multicomponent thermal plasmas. Although the combined diffusion coefficient approach has been extensively applied to several plasma mixtures, including argon–copper (Ar–Cu) mixtures, corresponding data for argon–tungsten (Ar–W) mixtures remain unavailable. Furthermore, the available transport data for argon plasmas containing metal vapors are often calculated using approximate interaction potentials to describe collisions between different species, which may reduce their accuracy. In this work, the influence of interaction potential models on combined diffusion coefficients is first investigated for Ar–Cu plasmas, with particular emphasis on neutral–neutral and neutral–ion interactions. The uncertainties associated with commonly used approximate potentials are assessed by comparison with calculations based on more realistic interaction potentials. Subsequently, these more accurate interaction potentials are used to calculate combined ordinary, temperature, and electric-field diffusion coefficients for Ar–Cu and Ar–W thermal plasma mixtures over the temperature range 300–30000 K at a pressure of 1 bar.
