title: Dynamic Wafer Curvature Engineering Toward Ultraflat and Highly Uniform 8‐Inch GaN Heteroepitaxy
summary: ABSTRACT Large‐area GaN heteroepitaxy is essential for next‐generation electronic and optoelectronic systems, yet simultaneously achieving low wafer bow and high epitaxial uniformity remains challenging due to the dynamic evolution of therm
content: ABSTRACT Large‐area GaN heteroepitaxy is essential for next‐generation electronic and optoelectronic systems, yet simultaneously achieving low wafer bow and high epitaxial uniformity remains challenging due to the dynamic evolution of thermo‐mechanical stress during growth and cooling. Here, we develop a dynamic wafer curvature engineering strategy based on a thermal‐cycling stress‐loading (TCSL) layer to regulate curvature evolution throughout epitaxy and suppress residual bow after cooling. The TCSL layer consists of a hydrogen‐rich SiO 2 film deposited on the backside of sapphire substrates, where hydrogen‐driven viscoelastic relaxation and dehydrogenation‐induced network densification generate asymmetric stress evolution. Applying this strategy to AlGaN/GaN HEMT epitaxy, we realize ultraflat and highly uniform 8‐inch wafers on 1‐mm‐thick sapphire substrates, achieving a bow of 7.4 µm, a warp of 17.2 µm, and relative standard deviations of 0.82%, 1.2%, and 1.8% for epitaxial thickness, Al composition, and sheet resistance, respectively. The AlGaN/GaN heterostructure preserves high crystalline and interfacial quality, enabling a high‐quality two‐dimensional electron gas with a sheet density of 7.0 × 10 12 cm −2 and an electron mobility of 2040 cm 2 /V·s. This work establishes a scalable approach for simultaneous control of wafer flatness and epitaxial uniformity in large‐area GaN heteroepitaxy, paving the way toward highly integrated GaN‐based electronic and optoelectronic technologies.

title: Toward Integrated Solar Fuel Platforms: Advances in Oxide‐Based Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting and CO 2 Reduction
summary: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar‑fuel production has emerged as a compelling route to carbon‑neutral energy. Yet, its practical deployment remains limited by the intrinsic constraints of metal‑oxide semiconductors, restricted visib
content: ABSTRACT Photoelectrochemical (PEC) solar‑fuel production has emerged as a compelling route to carbon‑neutral energy. Yet, its practical deployment remains limited by the intrinsic constraints of metal‑oxide semiconductors, restricted visible‑light absorption, short carrier diffusion lengths, sluggish interfacial kinetics, and low CO 2 ‑reduction selectivity. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of advances in oxide‑based PEC materials for solar water splitting and CO 2 reduction, highlighting how nanoscale engineering has reshaped performance. We examine fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic requirements for PEC operation, including band‑edge alignment, charge‑carrier dynamics, and redox selectivity, and critically evaluate how morphology control, bandgap tuning, defect/dopant engineering, heterojunction design, surface passivation, and plasmonic activation collectively overcome long‑standing bottlenecks. We compare material‐specific progress in TiO 2 , ZnO, Fe 2 O 3 , WO 3 , BiVO 4 , Cu 2 O/CuO, and mixed‑oxide systems through reported photocurrent density, Faradaic efficiency, product selectivity, and stability. At the device scale, we discuss how membrane selection, photoelectrode architecture, and advanced reactor designs, including flow‑cell CO 2 ‑reduction systems, translate material innovations into practical performance gains. Finally, we outline techno‐economic and life‐cycle considerations, emphasizing durability, resource sustainability, and the growing role of machine‐learning‐driven material discovery. With continued progress in oxide nano‐engineering and system integration, PEC platforms are now approaching the > 10% solar‐to‐hydrogen efficiency needed for scalable solar‐fuel generation.

title: Biochar and halophyte litter synergistically enhance recalcitrant organic carbon fractions in coastal salt-affected soil via lignin phenols and microbial necromass carbon
summary: Biochar shows promise for remediating coastal salt‑affected soils and supporting potential carbon sequestration, yet its role in the halophyte litter detritusphere, particularly regarding lignin phenols and microbial necromass C (MNC), rema
content: Biochar shows promise for remediating coastal salt‑affected soils and supporting potential carbon sequestration, yet its role in the halophyte litter detritusphere, particularly regarding lignin phenols and microbial necromass C (MNC), remains unclear. Herein, we conducted a 370-day microcosm experiment with coastal salt-affected soil from the Yellow River Delta under two moisture conditions (75% and 125% of maximum water-holding capacity) to evaluate how corn straw biochar (CBC) affects lignin phenols and MNC accumulation in the halophyte Suaeda salsa litter detritusphere. Results showed that CBC and litter inputs were stronger drivers of lignin phenol and MNC accumulation than moisture conditions. Litter input significantly increased the contents of lignin phenols and MNC by 32.80–33.36% and 0.78–14.36%, whereas CBC alone decreased lignin phenol content by 12.18–12.87%, but enhanced MNC accumulation by 15.36–42.22%. Compared with litter alone, CBC addition with litter significantly increased lignin phenols, bacterial necromass carbon (BNC), and MNC by 22.43–41.15%, 165.21–233.48%, and 25.09–53.82% under both moisture conditions. Mechanistically, CBC addition with litter alleviated salinity/sodicity stress and improved nutrient availability, enriching decomposition-associated taxa ( Preussia , Talaromyces ) and taxa associated with BNC accumulation ( Thiobacillus , Thioalkalispira ). Concurrently, CBC was associated with greater aggregate stability and organo‑mineral associations, patterns that may favor the retention of lignin-derived residues and microbial necromass. These findings inform biochar as a nature-based strategy for sustainable management of coastal salt‑affected soils and carbon sequestration.

title: Sustainable Polypropylene Composites with Rod-Like Calcium Carbonate Particles Derived from Ocean-Mineralization-Based Carbon Capture
summary: Abstract Efficiently utilizing captured carbon as high-value materials is a cornerstone of achieving global carbon neutrality. In this study, we present a sustainable approach to upcycle calcium carbonate (CaCO3) microparticles, synthesized
content: Abstract Efficiently utilizing captured carbon as high-value materials is a cornerstone of achieving global carbon neutrality. In this study, we present a sustainable approach to upcycle calcium carbonate (CaCO3) microparticles, synthesized via ocean-mineralization-based carbon capture, into functional fillers to enhance the performance of polypropylene (PP) composites. The unique morphology of mineralized rod-like CaCO3 (MRC) influenced the mechanical and rheological properties of PP composites compared with commercial rhombohedral CaCO3 (CRC). The MRC particles, characterized by a high aspect ratio and narrow size distribution, significantly enhanced both Young’s modulus and storage modulus of the PP composites. To improve interfacial adhesion, surface modification with stearic acid (SA) was employed, which effectively promoted ductile fracture and energy dissipation. Consequently, the PP composite reinforced with 30 wt % of surface-treated MRC exhibited a simultaneous 2.3-fold increase in tensile toughness and a 1.2-fold increase in Young’s modulus compared with neat PP. In addition to mechanical reinforcement, the PP composite films showed high solar reflectance and mid-infrared emissivity, demonstrating their potential for radiative cooling applications. Life-cycle and techno-economic assessments further showed that the incorporation of MRC-SA reduced the carbon footprint and estimated production cost of the composites by up to 35% and 26% compared with neat PP, respectively.

title: Electrode Architectures in Biophotoelectrochemical Systems for Sustainable Energy and Environmental Applications
summary: Current energy demand and the need for environmental stewardship call for transformative technologies that can simultaneously produce clean energy and remediate waste. Biophotoelectrochemical (BPEC) systems are promising platforms that coup
content: Current energy demand and the need for environmental stewardship call for transformative technologies that can simultaneously produce clean energy and remediate waste. Biophotoelectrochemical (BPEC) systems are promising platforms that couple the light‐harvesting capability of semiconductor photocatalysts with the catalytic precision of biocatalysts using an electrically addressable electrode. BPEC systems provide tunable reaction pathways, improved scalability, easier product handling, and flexibility in coupling various reactions by modifying the electrode architecture. This review presents a comprehensive discussion of these architectures in BPEC systems, beginning with the fundamental principles of how photoelectrodes and bioelectrodes work. This review then provides a systematic examination of two different electrode architectures: separated electrodes (photoelectrode | bioelectrode) and biohybrid photoelectrodes (biophotoelectrodes). The discussion covers their configurations, working principles, and representative applications such as H 2 evolution, CO 2 reduction, N 2 fixation, pollutant removal, and energy recovery. The review also summarizes key performance metrics and current research trends. By integrating the complementary strengths of photoelectrodes and bioelectrodes, BPEC systems can overcome individual technological limitations and support sustainable energy and environmental applications through self‐biased operation and enhanced product selectivity. Finally, the review discusses the challenges and future directions of advancing BPEC systems into scalable, multifunctional platforms for next‐generation sustainable technologies.

title: A Dual‐Pathway Strategy for Upcycling Molybdenum Tailings Into Dual Adsorbents for High‐Efficiency Nutrient Control and Recovery
summary: ABSTRACT The large‐scale accumulation of molybdenum tailings (MT) presents a dual challenge: a significant environmental liability and a squandered resource of valuable aluminosilicates. To address this, we propose a dual‐pathway strategy t
content: ABSTRACT The large‐scale accumulation of molybdenum tailings (MT) presents a dual challenge: a significant environmental liability and a squandered resource of valuable aluminosilicates. To address this, we propose a dual‐pathway strategy that upcycles MT into two adsorbents for efficient nutrient control and recovery within a circular economy model. Initial characterization confirmed MT as a non‐hazardous, silica‐alumina‐rich precursor (Si avg. 45.8%). The strategy involves two concurrent pathways: (1) the solid residue of pretreated MT was hydrothermally converted into a FAU‐type zeolite (MTZ‐3), which achieved rapid ammonia adsorption (17.0 mg/g) and reached equilibrium within 30 min; and (2) the acidic leachate was reutilized to synthesize calcium‐iron metal oxides (CaFeMOs), exhibiting a phosphate adsorption capacity of 90.0 mg/g. CaFeMOs also reduced leachable phosphorus from phosphogypsum by more than 96% at a dosage of 2%. This “one‐waste, two‐products” approach valorizes mining waste while producing adsorbents for nutrient removal from eutrophic waters. Nutrient‐saturated adsorbents may further serve as low‐cost fertilizer carriers for nitrogen and phosphorus recovery and reuse. Overall, the strategy links molybdenum tailings valorization with aqueous nutrient capture, transforming a linear waste problem into a circular, value‐added resource recovery pathway.

title: Wafer‐Scale Direct Growth of Ultraclean Monolayer Amorphous Carbon on c‐Sapphire by Remote Catalytic Dehydrogenation
summary: ABSTRACT Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct grow
content: ABSTRACT Atomically thin amorphous carbon holds considerable promise for application in data storage, microelectronics, protective coatings, and flexible electronics. However, its device integration has been hindered by existing direct growth routes that rely on metal catalysts in contact with the substrate, causing metallic residue, film non‐uniformity, and the need for post‐growth processing. Here, we report the direct growth of monolayer amorphous carbon on a 2‐inch sapphire wafer via thermal chemical vapor deposition, in which a remotely positioned catalyst decomposes the carbon precursor into active carbon feedstock, keeping the growth substrate free of metallic contamination. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy detects no catalyst residue across the wafer and confirms a highly sp 2 ‐hybridized carbon network, while electron microscopy reveals a random polygonal carbon network lacking long‐range periodicity. Raman and atomic force microscopy mapping confirm uniform and atomically smooth monolayer coverage, while electrical measurements establish its insulating character with ambipolar, gate‐tunable hopping transport. This synthesis approach provides precise control over thickness and uniformity at the wafer scale, enabling direct device integration of amorphous carbon for a wide range of applications, particularly as an interlayer for epitaxial growth of freestanding semiconductor membranes.

title: Location factors for energy-intensive industry: how renewable energy changes regional attractiveness
summary: This study investigates location factors for energy-intensive industry firms on a NUTS-3 scale in Germany. In the context of the ongoing renewable energy transformation, there is an increasing imperative to innovate in production technologi
content: This study investigates location factors for energy-intensive industry firms on a NUTS-3 scale in Germany. In the context of the ongoing renewable energy transformation, there is an increasing imperative to innovate in production technologies within traditionally energy-intensive industry sectors, such as steel, aluminium, glass, paper, and chemical production. The transition of production from fossil fuel energy to renewable energy sources is contingent upon the geographical location of industrial facilities, given the significant variations in the potential for solar and wind energy generation across Germany. This is indicative of a broader phenomenon in which other location factors are also taken into consideration by firms in their decision-making process regarding location. The identification of relevant location factors is achieved through a comprehensive literature review and is subsequently validated through the implementation of spatially enhanced regression analysis on a site-specific industry dataset. The validation process incorporates the utilisation of a georeferenced data set and geographically weighted regression analysis, adjusted for the inflation of observations (=regions) that are devoid of an energy-intensive industry sector. Numerous indices are derived from identified location factors to enable comparison between regions and between the recognition of renewable energy production potential as a location factor. It has been demonstrated that regions exhibiting lower socioeconomic performance stand to accrue significant benefit from the potential of producing renewable energy. This is demonstrated by examining a ranking of German NUTS-3-level regions and their respective change after including renewable energy production. The study quantifies the impact on green industry regional attractiveness while underlining trade-offs between different location factors.

title: Institutional evolution of the Green Agenda: Global frameworks and the Russian model of pragmatic sovereignty
summary: Aim. To examine the stages and patterns of the institutional evolution of the international Green Agenda, as well as to analyze the formation of the Russian model of climate policy in the context of global trends. Objectives. To reconstruct
content: Aim. To examine the stages and patterns of the institutional evolution of the international Green Agenda, as well as to analyze the formation of the Russian model of climate policy in the context of global trends. Objectives. To reconstruct the logic of the development of international sustainable development mechanisms from the UN program plan Agenda 21 to the Pact for the Future; to reveal the specific character of Russian climate policy on the basis of doctrinal and regulatory documents of 2023–2024; to examine the systemic constraints on Russia’s transition to a low-carbon economy. Methods. The research employs general scientific methods, including institutional and historical-genetic analysis of international regimes, comparative analysis of global and national contexts, and content analysis of strategic and regulatory legal documents. Results. Fragmented environmental protection measures of a sectoral nature have been replaced by complexly organized governance systems that integrate interstate agreements, domestic strategic guidelines, corporate standards in the field of sustainable development, and specialized financial mechanisms. With respect to Russian practice, the emerging approach can be identified as pragmatic sovereignty. At the same time, the fundamental fork determining the prospects becomes the dilemma between reliance on the capacity of forest ecosystems to absorb emissions and the need for large-scale reconstruction of the production apparatus on a low-carbon basis. Conclusions. One of the main problems for Russia today lies not in the absence of declared intentions but in the noticeable divergence between the established regulatory framework and the implementation of the Green Agenda in economic practice. If there is no transition to concrete mandatory requirements, no approval of sectoral plans with clear indicators, and no provision of sustainable financing for them, then there is a high probability that the set of climate initiatives will remain predominantly public discourse and will not lead to substantial shifts in the economy. From a practical standpoint, the value of the work lies in the fact that it substantiates the need to move from general framework provisions to well-developed implementation instruments, in particular the introduction of mandatory non-financial reporting by ESG criteria and the launch of a full-fledged state registry of carbon units. It is precisely such measures that are capable of turning the Green Agenda into a driver of structural modernization.

title: Highly Ordered Flexible Fibrous Membrane Electrode With Pt Nanoparticles Supported on Fe‐Containing N‐Doped Carbon for Oxygen Reduction Reaction
summary: ABSTRACT Pt nanoparticles supported on porous carbon supports are widely used as electrocatalysts in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), but conventional carbon supports suffer from corrosion and Pt agglomeration, which limit perf
content: ABSTRACT Pt nanoparticles supported on porous carbon supports are widely used as electrocatalysts in proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), but conventional carbon supports suffer from corrosion and Pt agglomeration, which limit performance and durability. Herein, we address these issues by anchoring Pt nanoparticles on highly ordered Fe‐containing N‐doped carbon nanofibers (Pt‐FeNC). Owing to the flexible, ordered fibrous‐membrane architecture and an interfacial electronic interaction between Pt and the Fe─N─C support, charge transport and improves catalyst durability. As a result, Pt‐FeNC exhibits high oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity, with a half‐wave potential of 0.9 V. A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) employing the ordered fibrous membrane as a freestanding cathode delivers an approximately 33% higher peak power density than commercial Pt/C and only a 7.2% performance loss after 30,000 accelerated stress test cycles. The enhanced performance is attributed to the improved durability of the Fe‐containing N‐doped carbon support and the continuous electron‐ and mass‐transport pathways provided by the interconnected fibrous network.

title: Exceptional Superconducting Interfaces between Graphene and Atomic Chains in A15-MoRe
summary: Realizing highly transparent and magnetic-field-resilient superconducting contacts is a critical bottleneck for the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) quantum devices. Molybdenum-rhenium (MoRe) alloys have been empirically favored as they
content: Realizing highly transparent and magnetic-field-resilient superconducting contacts is a critical bottleneck for the advancement of two-dimensional (2D) quantum devices. Molybdenum-rhenium (MoRe) alloys have been empirically favored as they uniquely yield ballistic, highly transparent contacts to graphene that survive in high-magnetic-field regimes; however, the microscopic origin of this anomalous transparency has remained a long-standing puzzle. Here, we resolve this paradox by revealing that pristine graphene/MoRe interfaces are governed by the classical A15 superconducting phase. Combining low-temperature transport, X-ray diffraction, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy, we demonstrate that as-deposited MoRe spontaneously forms the A15 phase in direct contact with graphene, whereas thermal annealing triggers a phase transition to a hexagonal close-packed (hcp) structure that severely degrades the Josephson transparency. Crucially, the one-dimensional (1D) transition-metal atomic chains unique to the A15 structure exhibit a near-perfect lattice match (mismatch < 1%) with graphene edges. First-principles calculations further prove that the d-orbitals of these historically renowned 1D chains possibly hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone near the K point. These findings not only uncover the structural and electronic origins of optimal MoRe contacts but also establish A15-phase superconductors as a geometrically ideal, universal platform for realizing robust quantum electronics based on 2D materials.

title: Climate change litigation in Europe and the Global South: National, regional, and international perspectives
source: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law
summary: The role of courts in clarifying and interpreting existing climate law and, in doing so, contributing to its progressive development is crucial to addressing the climate emergency at all scales.The three books together provide domestic, reg
content: The role of courts in clarifying and interpreting existing climate law and, in doing so, contributing to its progressive development is crucial to addressing the climate emergency at all scales.The three books together provide domestic, regional, comparative and international legal perspectives on climate litigation.Each book has the potential to inform the other by identifying applicable climate law, framing litigation strategies and contributing to climate change governance through climate litigation.Since each book discusses climate cases in different legal and policy contexts, the extent to which one can inform the other may vary because the legal and policy frameworks and their interpretation in domestic courts may differ.

title: Thermal Emission Toxicity and Qualitative Screening of Volatile Organic Emissions and Hazard Identification from Water Hyacinth Fiber–Cassava Starch Biodegradable Composites
source: Journal of Composites and Biodegradable Polymers
summary: The rapid transition toward sustainable packaging has driven the development of biodegradable polymer composites utilizing agricultural wastes, such as water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) fibers and cassava starch matrices. However, while
content: The rapid transition toward sustainable packaging has driven the development of biodegradable polymer composites utilizing agricultural wastes, such as water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) fibers and cassava starch matrices. However, while the environmental biodegradability of such biocomposites is widely studied, the toxicological safety of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) released under thermal exposure remains critically unaddressed. This study evaluated the volatile emission profile and qualitative hazard screening of water hyacinth–cassava starch composite sheets subjected to heat (100 °C for 15 min) simulating hot-food contact conditions. Using Headspace Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (HS-GC-MS), 26 volatile compounds were tentatively identified based on NIST library mass spectral matching (similarity match factor >80%, corresponding to Metabolomics Standards Initiative Level 2). The identified profile included 9 hazardous chemical species classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC). Key hazardous emissions comprised Group 1 human carcinogens (Ethylene oxide 3.60% peak area and Formaldehyde [5.80%]), Group 2A/2B probable/possible carcinogens (Ethylenimine 19.40%, Acetaldehyde 10.50%, Trichloromethane 1.20%, Tetrachloromethane 0.90%, 1,2-Dichloroethane 0.70%, and 1,2-Dibromoethane 0.60%), alongside hepatotoxic Chloromethane (17.10%). It is emphasized that reported peak area percentages represent relative chromatographic abundances under specific headspace thermal desorption conditions and do not reflect absolute mass concentrations. Furthermore, qualitative hazard identification does not constitute a quantitative health risk assessment, as consumer exposure levels and migration limits were not established. The origin of these hazardous species stems from a plausible combination of aquatic bioaccumulation by raw water hyacinth, alkali delignification pre-treatment residuals, thermal fragmentation of the starch–glycerol matrix, and pyrolysis of residual plant proteinaceous biomass. These findings demonstrate that environmental biodegradability does not inherently ensure chemical safety for food contact materials, highlighting the necessity of integrating volatile emission toxicity screening into biopolymer safety standards.

title: Electrochemical functionalization of graphene rationalized by Hammett and Swain-Lupton parameters
summary: Graphene's sp^{2}-bonded carbon lattice makes it exceptionally resistant to covalent functionalization, with existing approaches relying on chemically specific and often harsh methods, fragmenting our understanding of its reactivity. Here w
content: Graphene's sp^{2}-bonded carbon lattice makes it exceptionally resistant to covalent functionalization, with existing approaches relying on chemically specific and often harsh methods, fragmenting our understanding of its reactivity. Here we show that electric fields of approximately 1 V nm^{-1} in non-aqueous electrolytes enable the electrochemical functionalization of monolayer graphene with a broad range of substituents, leading to two-order-of-magnitude conductance modulation stable over 5,000 cycles and semi-reversible electronic conductor-insulator transitions. Analysis of the oxidation potentials across substituents reveals trends governed by classical descriptors. Species forming localised σ bonds display increasing oxidation potentials with the meta-Hammett constant (σ_m), whereas substituents interacting via delocalised π orbitals follow an inverse dependence on the modified Swain-Lupton resonance parameter (R). These relationships indicate that graphene's oxidation potential increases with the electron-withdrawing strength of the substituent. Our results provide new insights into the electrochemical activity of inert materials under strong electric fields.

title: The Role of Economic Performance and Resource Efficiency in European Sustainable Business
summary: This study examines the structural dimensions associated with research and development investment across European Union countries through an integrated econometric framework encompassing economic performance, efficiency dynamics, environmen
content: This study examines the structural dimensions associated with research and development investment across European Union countries through an integrated econometric framework encompassing economic performance, efficiency dynamics, environmental pressures, policy orientation, and digital transformation. Moving beyond single-indicator approaches, the analysis constructs composite indices reflecting structural innovation capacity, resource and energy efficiency, green transition pressures, fiscal and policy orientation, and digital business transformation. Using panel data for EU Member States over the period 2013-2023, the empirical strategy combines hierarchical pooled regression with country fixed-effects and two-way fixed-effects models using Driscoll-Kraay standard errors, thereby accounting for unobserved country heterogeneity, common year effects, and cross-sectional dependence. Pooled estimates show strong positive associations of structural innovation capacity and green transition pressures with BERD across variation that combines between-country differences and within-country changes. These relationships differ when estimation is based on within-country variation and when common year effects are incorporated. In the two-way fixed-effects specification with Driscoll-Kraay inference, resource and energy efficiency and green transition pressures are positively associated with BERD, whereas digital business transformation is negatively associated with BERD; structural innovation capacity and fiscal-policy orientation are not statistically significant. These results distinguish relationships observed across pooled country-year variation from those identified through within-country changes and show that some coefficient patterns differ further after common year effects are incorporated. By providing a multidimensional perspective on the structural dimensions associated with business R&D intensity, the study contributes to the literature on sustainable innovation and provides policy-relevant evidence on the distinct roles of structural conditions, efficiency dynamics, environmental pressures, and digital transformation.

title: Integration of Landscape Aesthetics and Sustainable Business Models in Kaliaren Village Land Utilization
summary: This research aims to identify and optimize land use in Kaliaren Village through the integration of landscape aesthetic aspects and the development of sustainable business models. Using a descriptive-exploratory qualitative approach, this s
content: This research aims to identify and optimize land use in Kaliaren Village through the integration of landscape aesthetic aspects and the development of sustainable business models. Using a descriptive-exploratory qualitative approach, this study maps the existing conditions of land use, analyzes aesthetic and economic potential, and explores the perception of the community and stakeholders through observation, in-depth interviews, Focus Group Discussions, and spatial analysis. The results of the study show that Kaliaren Village has strong landscape potential in the form of terraced rice fields, vegetation diversity, natural springs, and authentic rural visual character. However, land use is still dominated by conventional agriculture with low economic added value, limited human resource capacity, lack of business innovation, and lack of a strong village brand. Through SWOT analysis and strategy formulation, this research offers a development concept that combines environmental aesthetics, ecological sustainability, and community-based economic strengthening through agro-tourism, aesthetic public space development, value-added products, and participatory business models. This research contributes to the development of the concept of aesthetic entrepreneurship and provides an implementable framework that can be replicated in other villages with similar characteristics.

title: Contact-free charge carrier density determination of doped sub-μm thin cubic GaN layers with terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
summary: As cubic GaN is a promising material for optoelectronic applications, its layers need to be precisely doped to realize the desired properties. While contact-based methods are established to measure the realized charge carrier density, conta
content: As cubic GaN is a promising material for optoelectronic applications, its layers need to be precisely doped to realize the desired properties. While contact-based methods are established to measure the realized charge carrier density, contact-free techniques are more advantageous for this purpose. We show terahertz time-domain spectroscopy measurements of cubic GaN layers with thicknesses between 0.6 $μ$m and 2 $μ$m with doping densities in the range from $10^{18}$ cm$^{-3}$ to $10^{20}$ cm$^{-3}$. From these measurements, we determine the charge carrier densities and verify the results with time-of-flight secondary-ion mass spectrometry measurements. The results are in accordance with simulations of the doping ranges which the technique is expected to be sensitive in. In preparation for the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy measurements, we validated the layer thicknesses by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy measurements. With this, a wide range of doped cubic GaN samples can be addressed by optical methods. In the future, these techniques could allow for a fast and non-destructive characterization of GaN layers, right after or even during the growth process.

title: Microenvironment‐controlled Li + /Mg 2+ separation in COFs : Explored using high‐throughput simulations and machine learning
summary: Abstract Separating Li + from Mg 2+ in salt‐lake brines remains challenging due to their similar hydrated diameters. Herein, covalent organic frameworks were used as model membranes to systematically evaluate how steric hindrance, hydrophil
content: Abstract Separating Li + from Mg 2+ in salt‐lake brines remains challenging due to their similar hydrated diameters. Herein, covalent organic frameworks were used as model membranes to systematically evaluate how steric hindrance, hydrophilicity, and membrane charge control ion transport. A dataset from 196 high‐throughput non‐equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations was analyzed using machine learning. Water and Cl − fluxes were governed mainly by membrane charge, whereas Li + transport depended on all three properties, and Mg 2+ flux was most sensitive to steric hindrance. A Gaussian process regression model accurately predicted fluxes and was coupled with mixed‐integer optimization to design an optimal membrane. No Mg 2+ permeation was detected in three validation trajectories of the optimized candidate, while water and Li + transport persisted. Shapley additive explanations revealed that Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity arises primarily from steric sieving at high hindrance, assisted by weak negative charge and low hydrophilicity, providing a data‐driven framework for covalent organic framework (COF) membrane optimization.

title: Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands
summary: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic
content: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach, we compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands comprising thousands of atoms. The spectra are strongly tunable and split into two regimes at a critical angle where a single moiré wavelength spans the island; beyond it, an ordered ladder of resonances emerges whenever an integer number of moiré periods fits within the overlapping bilayer. In doped islands, the interlayer coupling also produces a moiré-enabled Born--Kuhn chiral plasmon: opposite transverse dipoles in the two layers form an electric quadrupole that hybridizes with the bright dipole, opening an anticrossing near the critical angle, with a handedness that reverses with the twist direction. Triangular islands confirm that the moiré lattice, not the flake boundary, governs both effects, establishing twist as a mechanical handle on chiral graphene plasmons.

title: Green Bond Financing and Corporate Financing Costs in Highly Polluting Industries: Evidence from Baoshan Iron & Steel, China Energy Investment Corporation, and China Huadian
summary: In the context of the “dual carbon” goal and the continuous improvement of the green financial system‚ green bonds have become an important tool for enterprise green transformation financing․ Compared with ordinary bonds‚ green bonds have c
content: In the context of the “dual carbon” goal and the continuous improvement of the green financial system‚ green bonds have become an important tool for enterprise green transformation financing․ Compared with ordinary bonds‚ green bonds have clearer requirements for the use of proceeds‚ stricter requirements for information disclosure‚ and more traceable environmental benefits․ Hence‚ their involvement may improve corporate financing conditions by reducing information asymmetry‚ strengthening the green signal‚ and increasing investor preference․ This paper analyze firms in highly polluting industries as an example and investigate whether green bonds can help firms in these industries reduce financing costs․ The study used a qualitative multiple case study approach‚ with the three multiple case study organizations being Baoshan Iron & Steel‚ China Energy‚ and China Huadian․ The study showed that the reduction of financing costs brought by green bonds to enterprises in high polluting industries had conditional characteristics․ It was found that the financing effect of green bonds was better when the issuer had better credit quality and the projects were real‚ specific and disclosed enough information․

title: ตวชวดการจดการทดนอยางยงยน: แนวความคด และความทาทายในบรบทของประเทศไทย
source: Journal of Social Development and Management Strategy
summary: Sustainable land management is a critical issue that encompasses environmental, social, economic, and governance dimensions. This study aimed to develop a “Land Management Sustainability Index” capable of comprehensively reflecting the cond
content: Sustainable land management is a critical issue that encompasses environmental, social, economic, and governance dimensions. This study aimed to develop a “Land Management Sustainability Index” capable of comprehensively reflecting the conditions and challenges of land management in Thailand. The index comprises two main dimensions: Land Use Sustainability (LUS) and Soil Resources Sustainability (SRS). These dimensions are organized into seven pillars, consisting of 20 indicators and 40 sub-indicators. The assessment draws upon data from multiple sources, including the Land Development Department, the Office of Agricultural Economics, and contemporary geographic information system (GIS) datasets. The analysis identifies significant challenges in data fragmentation, inconsistent indicator definitions, and policy limitations. The study offers structural recommendations such as establishing a national land data center, standardizing land classification systems, and linking policy inputs with local-level outcomes. These improvements aim to enable the index to function as an effective tool for tracking progress and guiding sustainable land policy in Thailand.

title: Marine ranching for carbon-neutral fisheries in China: Carbon sink evidence, policy instruments, and transition pathways
source: Asian Journal of Water Environment and Pollution
summary: Marine-ranching carbon sink (MRCS) is defined as an additional, verifiable net climate benefit attributable to a bounded ranching intervention after considering baseline conditions, carbon fate, life-cycle emissions, and uncertainty. Marine
content: Marine-ranching carbon sink (MRCS) is defined as an additional, verifiable net climate benefit attributable to a bounded ranching intervention after considering baseline conditions, carbon fate, life-cycle emissions, and uncertainty. Marine ranching is increasingly discussed in China as a means to align fisheries with the national carbon-neutrality agenda. However, terms such as additional biomass, harvested carbon, long-lived storage, avoided emissions, and offset credits refer to different outcomes. This review examines when a marine ranch can deliver a defensible net climate benefit. It combines research on fishery emissions and sequestration, Chinese policy and technical standards, empirical pilot practices, and international work on blue-carbon accounting. The evidence is analyzed through 4 key dimensions: carbon pool alterations, ultimate carbon destination, emissions within the project boundary, and the additionality and verifiability of the claimed change. Chinese estimates demonstrate substantial biological uptake by shellfish and macroalgae, but they vary widely with species coverage, carbon coefficients, treatment of dissolved and particulate carbon, ecological carrying capacity, and deduction of production emissions. Although policy has advanced from demonstration zones to measurement standards and voluntary-market rules, no generally accepted method yet covers an entire ranching system. Therefore, this review interprets marine ranching as a managed area in which restoration, low-input mariculture, operational decarbonization, and monitoring can be combined and tested against a baseline. Credible MRCS claims require carbon-fate evidence, life-cycle inventories, long-term observation, conservative uncertainty treatment, and transparent allocation of benefits.

title: The Role of Carboxymethyl Cellulose (CMC) from Banana (Musa paradisiaca) Peels and Corn (Zea mays L.) Cobs as Ice Cream Stabilizers
summary: Background: The growing demand for natural food additives has spurred theexploration of agricultural waste, such as banana peels and corn cobs, as alternativesources of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). CMC functions as a stabilizer in foodpro
content: Background: The growing demand for natural food additives has spurred theexploration of agricultural waste, such as banana peels and corn cobs, as alternativesources of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC). CMC functions as a stabilizer in foodproducts, including ice cream, improving its texture and shelf life. Objectives: This study aimed to produce and analyze CMC from two types of agriculturalwaste, Musa paradisiaca peels and Zea mays L. cobs, and evaluate its application in icecream formulations. Methods: The methods used include delignification, alkalization, carboxymethylation,purification and neutralization. The CMC was synthesized through alkalization andetherification using NaOH and sodium monochloroacetate. The extracted CMC wasapplied as a stabilizer in ice cream formulations. The physicochemical properties of CMC(pH and yield) and the quality of ice cream (melting rate, overrun, and texture) wereanalyzed using descriptive and comparative methods. Results: The yield of CMC from Musa paradisiaca peels (29.5%) was higher than Zeamays L. cobs (26.9%). CMC from Musa paradisiaca peels and Zea mays L. cobs showedpH stability. Ice cream stabilized with Musa paradisiaca peel CMC demonstrated highermelting rates and better overrun than ice cream stabilized with CMC from Zea mays L.cobs. Conclusions: Musa paradisiaca peels and Zea mays L. cobs can be utilized as alternativeraw materials for CMC production. Among the two, Musa paradisiaca peel-derived CMCexhibited superior stabilizing properties in ice cream, offering a sustainable and effectivesubstitute for natural stabilizers.

title: Quantifying and attributing CO emissions over Central Asia using TROPOMI and explicit observational uncertainty
summary: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified da
content: Abstract. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a crucial atmospheric constituent influencing both air quality and climate. Using TROPOMI CO and HCHO column retrievals within the Model-Free Inversion Estimation Framework (MFIEF), this study quantified daily, gridded CO emissions in Central Asia (Xinjiang-China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan) for 2019–2024. Results reveal a marked interannual decline of ~ 38 % in mean emissions, accompanied by a weakening of emission hotspots. Seasonal peaks in winter and early spring highlight the roles of heating and industrial demand. Importantly, explicit perturbation-based uncertainty analysis showed that ~ 69 % of grid-level estimates are unreliable if observational uncertainties are ignored or using an overly simplified emissions estimation approach, underscoring the nonlinear propagation of retrieval errors. By integrating coal consumption data, we confirm the consistency between satellite-inferred emissions and bottom-up activity estimates, while also identifying missing sources such as underground coal fires. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of MFIEF in data-scarce regions, provides actionable insights for inventory improvement and mitigation strategies, and highlights the framework's potential extension to CH4 and CO2 retrieval-based emission estimation.

title: Synthesis of greenhouse gas emission factors for forest organic soils in the Köppen–Geiger Dfb climate zone
summary: Abstract. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from organic soils are a key component of land-use-related emissions, particularly in countries with large areas of organic soils. Temperate-zone forest soils remain less studied in GHG research than
content: Abstract. Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from organic soils are a key component of land-use-related emissions, particularly in countries with large areas of organic soils. Temperate-zone forest soils remain less studied in GHG research than boreal soils. However, recent work has expanded coverage in the northeastern temperate region, which, under the Köppen–Geiger climate classification, shares key climatic characteristics with the southern boreal region (Dfb). This study synthesised updated GHG flux data to evaluate carbon balance and emissions from forest organic soils in the Dfb zone, stratified by drainage status, nutrient availability, and dominant tree species. Such stratification revealed CO2 source-sink patterns, which encourage the ecological relevance of using these categories for data aggregation. The dominant tree species reflected nutrient status: drained coniferous and deciduous stands have been reported as CO2 sources, emitting 0.03 ± 0.55 and 0.47 ± 0.29 t CO2‑C ha−1 year−1, respectively, though soils tended to shift toward CO2 sinks in stands older than 25 years. In contrast, undrained soils have generally been observed to function as CO2 sinks, although not necessarily in all sites. However, this stratification was less informative for CH4 and N2O. CH4 fluxes were primarily determined by water table level rather than by other site variables, whereas N2O showed a tendency toward elevated emissions in deciduous stands, irrespective of drainage status.

title: Selection of optimal HHP conditions for processing of Tenebrio molitor paste based on a comprehensive evaluation of quality indicators
summary: This study aimed to understand the effects of different operational parameters and define the best conditions for applying high hydrostatic pressure to Tenebrio molitor paste, aiming to maximise benefits while minimising undesired effects o
content: This study aimed to understand the effects of different operational parameters and define the best conditions for applying high hydrostatic pressure to Tenebrio molitor paste, aiming to maximise benefits while minimising undesired effects on the quality of the final product. Three pressure levels (200, 400, 600 MPa) were applied to fresh mealworm paste for dwell times of 0- (control), 5-, 15-, 30-, 45- and 60-min. Microbial investigation of the studied pastes revealed a significant reduction in total viable count at pressures of 600 and 400 MPa, whereas no microbial reduction was observed at 200 MPa. A slight increase in titratable acidity was observed at every pressure, with the highest acidity measured for paste treated at 400MPa for 60 min. Complete absence of lipid oxidation was measured at every pressure, with the peroxide value showing no significant differences. Similar behaviour was also observed for TBARs at 600 MPa. An increase in TBARs from short to long dwell time was observed at 400 and 200 MPa. The total phenolic content and antioxidant activity increased notably after the HHP treatment, with the highest values recorded at 400 MPa, regardless of the treatment time. A reduction in lipase activity was also observed at every pressure level, with a clear linear effect over treatment time. The process optimisation study revealed that 510 MPa applied for 31 min is the best treatment for maximising positive effects while minimising adverse effects. However, further studies should be conducted to validate and confirm the transferability of this observation.

title: Socio-techno-ecological imaginaries: A framework for understanding future-making for and with ecology
summary: This article proposes socio-techno-ecological imaginaries (STEI) as a conceptual extension of sociotechnical imaginaries (STI). While STI has been valuable for showing how social order and technological change co-produce “desirable futures,
content: This article proposes socio-techno-ecological imaginaries (STEI) as a conceptual extension of sociotechnical imaginaries (STI). While STI has been valuable for showing how social order and technological change co-produce “desirable futures,” we argue it tends to leave implicit how visions of ecology – beliefs about what nature is and acts, how it is valued, and how humans ought to relate to it – are entangled in this process. This implicitness risks limiting STI’s explanatory power, its capacity to evaluate the desirability of imagined futures amid socio-ecological crises, and its own imaginative horizon in futures work. Drawing on literatures on socio-ecological imagination, eco-social imaginaries, and environmental and nature imaginaries, we define STEIs as institutionally embedded and publicly performed visions of desirable futures, animated by specific understandings and valuations of society, technology and ecology. STEI rests on three premises: (1) imaginaries are co-produced across social, technical, and ecological dimensions; (2) each dimension carries specific assumptions and normative valuations that condition what futures are deemed plausible and desirable; and (3) alignment or misalignment across these assumptions and valuations can be sites of conflict, lock-in, and transformation. We demonstrate the framework’s analytical value through an empirical study of the STEIs that guide the development and use expectations of sensor technologies in the Dutch agricultural sector. The study combines interviews with a corpus of public web texts to identify two STEIs, showing how divergent visions of society, technology, and ecology co-produce distinct farming futures. STEI, we conclude, strengthens critical futures research by enabling more explicit, plural, and ecologically attuned evaluations of future-making.

title: Mechanism model for long-term degradation failure of PEM water electrolyzers
summary: Abstract One of the bottlenecks restricting the large-scale commercialization of proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers lies in their poor durability. Due to numerous degradation categories and complex degradation mechanisms within el
content: Abstract One of the bottlenecks restricting the large-scale commercialization of proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzers lies in their poor durability. Due to numerous degradation categories and complex degradation mechanisms within electrolyzers, it is still difficult to quantify the ratio of one single mechanism on the overall degradation through experiments, making it impossible to fully understand the degradation characteristics. A mechanistic model for simulating the degradation process in PEM electrolyzers is proposed in this study. It describes three dominant degradation processes, including ionomer degradation, IrO 2 dissolution, and titanium passivation and corrosion. Then, these three degradation sub-models are coupled into a three-dimensional full-electrolyzer model to reveal the mechanism of long-term operation failure of electrolyzers. It captures the coupling mechanism between degradation and internal heat and mass transfer process, revealing the rapid electrolyzer degradation in the early stage is mainly caused by titanium and ionomer degradation. Increasing the temperature and current density accelerate degradation, that is, temperature primarily accelerates IrO 2 and ionomer degradation, while current density mainly accelerates IrO 2 and Ti degradation. Under low-temperature and low-current-density conditions, electrolyzer failure is mainly due to the voltage reaching the failure criterion; in contrast, electrolyzer failure is more likely caused by IrO 2 dissolution under high-temperature and high-current-density conditions. The developed model provides a foundation for understanding the mechanism of PEM water electrolyzer’s degradation and enhancing the application durability.

title: Quantitative in vitro PET/MRI and kinetic modelling of imaging agent release from a thermoreversible intranasal sol-gel
source: European Journal of Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
summary: Intranasal phase-transforming thermoresponsive gels can prolong nasal residence and enable controlled release of diagnostic or therapeutic payloads. However, quantitative real-time release characterisation of multimodal imaging probes remai
content: Intranasal phase-transforming thermoresponsive gels can prolong nasal residence and enable controlled release of diagnostic or therapeutic payloads. However, quantitative real-time release characterisation of multimodal imaging probes remains limited. Here, we developed a poloxamer-based sol–gel and established a hybrid PET/MRI framework to quantify the release of PET tracers and an activatable MnO 2 nanoflower into simulated nasal fluid. The formulations transformed from solution-to-gel at ∼ 28–29 °C with a storage modulus of 8.2−9.5 kPa attained at typical nasal cavity temperature (34 °C), while maintaining a nasal-compatible pH. PET imaging with an extended time window demonstrated diffusion-dominated release with clear size dependence: ionic [ 64 Cu]Cu 2+ reached 30.0 ± 3.0 % cumulative release at ∼42 h, whereas [ 64 Cu]Cu-Sar-OP showed 15.6 ± 3.1 % cumulative release under the same simulated conditions. PEGylated MnO 2 nanoflowers exhibited negligible apparent release in simulated nasal fluid without reductant due to the absence of redox-triggered MnO 2 dissolution to soluble Mn 2+ and electrolyte-induced nanoparticle aggregation trapping, which restricts diffusion out of the gel; but with GSH-supplementation, quantitative T1/T2 mapping enabled relaxivity-calibrated tracking of apparent Mn-equivalent accumulation, reaching 13.9 ± 0.7 % of the nominal loaded Mn (T1-based) at ∼24 h. The cytocompatibility of MnO 2 NFs–PEG was also evaluated in an RPMI 2650 human nasal epithelial cell model following 24-h exposure. Kinetic modelling (Higuchi and Korsmeyer − Peppas) supported diffusion-dominated transfer of the PET tracers, whereas the MnO 2 profile reflected coupled redox and transport processes under limited-GSH conditions. Overall, our integrated PET/MRI approach provides a quantitative framework for comparing in vitro depot release kinetics and informing intranasal PET/MRI formulation design; however, the findings should not be interpreted as direct evidence of mucosal retention or in vivo nose-to-brain transport.

title: Restored but Still Emitting: High CO 2 Fluxes From a Mediterranean Wetland Challenge Inundation‐Based Restoration Strategies
summary: Abstract Mediterranean wetlands significantly influence terrestrial carbon storage but lack comprehensive, long‐term carbon flux measurements, particularly those that distinguish fluxes between vegetated and open‐water surfaces. Inundation‐
content: Abstract Mediterranean wetlands significantly influence terrestrial carbon storage but lack comprehensive, long‐term carbon flux measurements, particularly those that distinguish fluxes between vegetated and open‐water surfaces. Inundation‐based restoration primarily aims to arrest drainage‐driven soil‐carbon loss; whether a re‐flooded wetland also becomes a net CO 2 sink is not guaranteed and depends on recovery time, wetland design, and vegetation establishment. We conducted a 3‐year (2021–2024) eddy covariance study using dual towers over a restored Mediterranean wetland (Agmon Hula, Israel) to partition CO 2 fluxes between these surfaces. Results show that the restored wetland acted as a persistent net source of CO 2 , emitting 3.8 ± 7.2 g C m −2 day −1 (∼14 t C ha −1 yr −1 ), with open water (∼80% area) as a major source (5.0 ± 8.6 g C m −2 day −1 ; ∼18.3 t C ha −1 yr −1 ), especially during summer nights driven by water‐to‐air temperature gradients and atmospheric instability, while vegetated zones acted as a net sink (−1.0 ± 11.3 g C m −2 day −1 ; ∼−3.7 t C ha −1 yr −1 ). When placed in the context of reported Mediterranean wetland fluxes, the Hula wetland exhibits the highest CO 2 emission rate observed for the region. Our findings indicate that commonly used functional relationships linking CO 2 to hydrological conditions should explicitly account for surface heterogeneity and nocturnal atmospheric coupling. Furthermore, enhancing vegetation cover may be critical for shifting open‐water‐dominated Mediterranean wetlands toward net carbon sinks under changing climatic conditions.

title: Data-driven valorization of mixed olefins byproducts via self-stabilized precipitation polymerization
summary: The transition of fossil fuels from energy sources to chemical feedstocks has generated huge amount of mixed olefins byproducts, whose efficient valorization remains an important challenge in chemical engineering. Self-stabilized precipitat
content: The transition of fossil fuels from energy sources to chemical feedstocks has generated huge amount of mixed olefins byproducts, whose efficient valorization remains an important challenge in chemical engineering. Self-stabilized precipitation (2SP) polymerization offers a promising route to directly convert these under-utilized olefins into polymer products without costly separation or other pre-treatments. However, the multi-factor nature of 2SP leaves its mechanism largely speculative, and the reaction feasibility currently relies on time-consuming trial-and-error experimentation. Here, we developed a machine learning predictor, 2SP-MLP, trained on 844 experimental data points to enable rapid and accurate prediction of 2SP outcomes. Following Bayesian optimization with 5-fold cross-validation, the XGBoost classifier achieved the best performance (ACC = 0.90, AUC = 0.96). Interpretability analysis identified the monomer-solvent solubility parameter difference (2.4-11.3 MPa1/2) as the key factor governing 2SP feasibility. Beyond solubility parameter, molecular shape, flexibility and charge distribution were found to significantly influence polymer precipitation and microparticle formation. Regression models for precipitate yield and olefin conversion both performed best with XGBoost (R2 = 0.73 and 0.89, respectively). Experimental validation under 10 newly designed conditions confirmed the model’s generalizability with 70% prediction accuracy. Overall, this work provides a data-driven tool that accelerates process design and reduces experimental cost for 2SP-based valorization of mixed olefins, demonstrating the potential of ML to advance sustainable chemical manufacturing.

title: Sawdust biochar as a dual cement and sand substitute for strength‐optimized and low‐carbon mortar with life‐cycle benefits
summary: The building industry is a major contributor to global CO 2 emissions, highlighting the need to develop low-carbon cement-based products. Biochar emerges as a promising additive for cementitious composites, owing primarily to its inherent c
content: The building industry is a major contributor to global CO 2 emissions, highlighting the need to develop low-carbon cement-based products. Biochar emerges as a promising additive for cementitious composites, owing primarily to its inherent capacity for long-term carbon sequestration, chemical stability, and sustainability benefits. In this study, biochar prepared from wood sawdust at 400 °C in a low-technology pit kiln was incorporated into mortar through two distinct series: (i) partial cement replacement at 1-5% by volume to evaluate microstructural development and mechanical performance, and (ii) 5-25% sand replacement by volume, which permits far higher biochar contents and therefore greater carbon sequestration while also reducing demand for natural sand. Owing to its irregular surface, porous structure, and low feedstock uniformity, biochar promoted hydration, potentially through internal curing and nucleation effects, resulting in greater formation of hydration products. This enhanced the strength and microstructure of biochar-modified mortar, which was compared with a cement-only control mortar. Thermogravimetric analysis of the corresponding pastes showed greater water-related mass loss, consistent with a greater extent of hydration. The maximum improvement in compressive strength, 17.3%, was achieved with a 4% cement replacement. Life cycle assessment (LCA) confirmed a 9.6% decrease in global warming potential (GWP) at this dosage with no strength penalty, rising to 22.9% when normalized per unit compressive strength. Notably, a 25% sand replacement approached carbon neutrality, with a GWP of -8.3 kg CO₂-eq/m³ under the base-case carbon permanence assumption, highlighting the potential of biochar to produce high-performance, low-carbon cementitious materials for specific application requirements.

title: Power system expansion in Ecuador: A stakeholder driven sustainability assessment of generation technologies
summary: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited inves
content: Ecuador experienced severe power shortages in 2024, with blackouts lasting up to 14 h a day, exposing the vulnerability of an electricity system that relies heavily on hydroelectric plants, is affected by drought, and has seen limited investment in new capacity since 2018. In this context, the central government has begun promoting nuclear energy as a medium- and long-term option, despite the country’s lack of experience with this technology and the Electricity Master Plan’s identification of substantial renewable potential. This study provides a sustainability assessment of eight generation technologies for Ecuador’s future energy mix: PV-US, geothermal, onshore wind, biomass, combined-cycle gas turbines, mini hydropower, small modular nuclear reactors, and conventional nuclear fission. The analysis is supported by Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis methods using ELECTRE III and HELDA (Helmholtz MCDA Tool), based on a performance matrix with 15 static baseline sustainability criteria grouped into environmental, technical, economic, and social categories, and weightings derived from a 35-stakeholder survey across the public, private, and academic sectors. Results show that stakeholders rank the availability of domestic resources as the most important criterion, followed by the levelized cost of electricity, risk to human health, and investment costs. When technologies are ranked using these weighted criteria, four renewable options (mini hydropower, onshore wind, PV-US, and geothermal) are preferred, followed by combined-cycle gas turbines and biomass, while both nuclear options are consistently ranked at the bottom. These results recommend that energy policy decisions in Ecuador should be based on transparent, stakeholder-driven assessments of technological options, rather than unilateral decisions detached from stakeholder preferences and system realities.

title: Coupling compliance and voluntary carbon markets: a system dynamics assessment in China
summary: The strategic coupling of compliance and voluntary carbon markets is emerging as a pivotal path for achieving cost-effective decarbonization. However, existing literature seldom captures the dynamic feedback loops, cross-sectoral heterogene
content: The strategic coupling of compliance and voluntary carbon markets is emerging as a pivotal path for achieving cost-effective decarbonization. However, existing literature seldom captures the dynamic feedback loops, cross-sectoral heterogeneities, and environmental economic benefits inherent in dual-market architectures. To fill this gap, this study develops a sector-specific system dynamics model to evaluate the integrated impacts of coupling China’s Emissions Trading System (ETS) and the China Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) scheme. Three distinct scenarios are modeled: no carbon trading market (BAU), Single Market (ETS-only), and Dual Market (ETS + CCER). Results indicate that the Dual Market scenario achieves emission reductions (40.3%) and energy savings (39.7%) comparable to the Single Market scenario, while the unit abatement cost advantage widens from CNY 0.02 to 0.41 per ton of CO2, and cumulative employment losses are reduced by around 0.19 million. Sectoral analysis reveals the power sector is the predominant buyer in the CCER market, accounting for 59.5% of the total transaction volume, while the cement sector acts primarily as a net seller of carbon allowances in 2030. Sensitivity analyses further confirm the robustness and advantages of coupling markets. Policy implications include gradually reducing the free allocation rate from 95% to 90%, dynamically adjusting the CCER offset rate within 5%-10% under strengthened oversight, and establishing coordinated price mechanisms. These findings provide robust evidence for optimizing dual-market architectures to advance both climate targets and a just, resilient low-carbon transition.

title: Influence of Geopolitical Risk on Energy Transition and Climate Change
summary: ABSTRACT Geopolitical tensions can influence energy transition, which, in turn, can impact climate change. Thus, we construct a framework that integrates these processes, analyzing 17 economies from 1990 to 2020 using a GVAR model. We hypot
content: ABSTRACT Geopolitical tensions can influence energy transition, which, in turn, can impact climate change. Thus, we construct a framework that integrates these processes, analyzing 17 economies from 1990 to 2020 using a GVAR model. We hypothesize that geopolitical risk shocks affect economies through domestic financial markets. The results demonstrate that geopolitical risk shocks (i) hinder national energy transitions and contribute to increased carbon emissions; (ii) induce fluctuations in financial markets; (iii) have a minor direct impact on energy transition, except in Scandinavia and the United States; (iv) indirectly influence economies through financial markets (particularly stock markets); and (v) generate spillover effects and heterogeneities. We corroborate our findings through shock identification, treating financial markets as conduits for the geopolitical risk shock. Additionally, we conduct a battery of robustness checks addressing structural breaks, time‐varying bilateral trade, and bilateral financial flows (instead of bilateral trade), all of which confirm the consistency of our results. We conclude by discussing fiscal policies aimed at counterbalancing the negative effects of geopolitical risk on energy transition and climate change, emphasizing the importance of international cooperation for the effectiveness of these policies.

title: Analysis of Beijing’s Energy Intensity Changes Based on an Input–Output Structural Decomposition Model from 2007 to 2020
summary: As China’s capital and a global megacity, Beijing has experienced sustained and rigid growth in energy demand driven by rapid population and economic expansion, rendering the analysis of energy intensity critically imperative for optimizing
content: As China’s capital and a global megacity, Beijing has experienced sustained and rigid growth in energy demand driven by rapid population and economic expansion, rendering the analysis of energy intensity critically imperative for optimizing its energy system, alleviating resource and environmental pressures, and advancing toward carbon neutrality. By constructing a long-term comparable-price series, this study applies multi-period comparative structural decomposition analysis (SDA) across five benchmark years, spanning major policy cycles. It disaggregates changes in energy intensity into energy technology, production technology, and final demand structure effects across six sectors and five energy categories. The principal findings are threefold. First, Beijing’s aggregate energy intensity exhibited a consistent downward trajectory, declining from 0.33699 tons of standard coal equivalent (tce) per 10,000 yuan in 2007 to 0.16393 tce per 10,000 yuan in 2020 (at constant 2012 prices). Second, the direct, indirect, and total energy consumption coefficients for all six sectors exhibited a broadly downward trend, with the largest reduction in the freight and postal sector, followed by industry. Third, energy technology change was the predominant driver of the decline in both aggregate energy intensity and consumption intensity across the five energy categories. Production technology and final demand structure changes exhibited heterogeneous effects across sectors and sub-periods. These findings provide policy-relevant insights for optimizing Beijing’s energy structure, and several targeted recommendations are proposed.

title: Sustainable Biochar Sorbents for Elemental Mercury Capture From Flue Gas: Review and Prospects
summary: ABSTRACT Elemental mercury (Hg 0 ), as the most dominant form of airborne mercury, is extremely hard to be captured because of its high volatility, aqueous insolubility, and thermal stability. Hg° capture from coal combustion, metallurgical
content: ABSTRACT Elemental mercury (Hg 0 ), as the most dominant form of airborne mercury, is extremely hard to be captured because of its high volatility, aqueous insolubility, and thermal stability. Hg° capture from coal combustion, metallurgical, and incineration flue gases is still challenging due to lack of cost‐efficient sorbents. Recently, biochar, as a sustainable and cost‐effective sorbent, has been extensively employed for Hg° capture due to its low price, natural abundance, renewability, carbon neutrality, and variety diversity. This review outlines the recent progress of Hg° capture by biochars in terms of biochar production, chemical activation, surface modification, and reaction mechanisms. Pristine biochar holds a lower Hg 0 adsorption activity. Chemical activation and surface modification can effectively reinforce the performance of the biochar due to improved porosity and augmented active species. Generally, the optimal mass ratio of activators to biomass is 2:1. Molten salt activation combined with sulfide modification or H 2 S plasma treatment is proposed as a prospective pathway to prepare high‐performance biochars. Mercury capture mechanisms of the biochars could likely be unraveled using theoretical calculation based on density functional theory (DFT).

title: Sanitizing the stain: a critical integrative review of sportswashing discourse
source: Qualitative Market Research An International Journal
summary: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how
content: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a critical integrative review of 45 peer-reviewed articles, identified through systematic searches of major academic databases. After two-stage screening, the corpus was analyzed qualitatively from an interpretive stance, using thematic synthesis followed by abductive theorization. Findings This study first maps the sportswashing ecosystem − stains, actors, motivations, mechanisms, phases and outcomes − revealing complexity and tensions pervading the literature. Building on this synthesis, it identifies five cleansing logics through which sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process: separation, dilution, displacement, containment and sanctification. Each logic illuminates how sportswashing operates as a contest over cultural classification through association without explicit claims. Research limitations/implications This synthesis advances a research agenda for interpretive marketing and consumer research, highlighting what qualitative inquiry could reveal about sportswashing across consumer resistance, platformization of consumer culture, CSR-washing, macromarketing, branding and reputation, marketing communications, market systems and critical and postcolonial marketing. Originality/value This paper theorizes sportswashing as a symbolic purification process, extending the CSR-washing literature from deception to associative classificatory work. Its five cleansing logics connect marketing scholarship on sponsorship, reputation, meaning transfer and brand activism; show how fan meaning-making and consumer resistance become embroiled in cultural-political reputation management; and reframe sportswashing as a contest over cultural classification, resolving persistent conceptual tensions.

title: Impacts of Ground Deformation on Annual Vegetation Carbon Sequestration in an Underground Mining Area Based on Scenario Simulation via a CA Model
summary: Impacts of mining-induced ground deformation on annual vegetation carbon sequestration have seldom been detected considering long-term plant succession after subsidence. To address this, a subsidence in the semi-arid underground mine of Chi
content: Impacts of mining-induced ground deformation on annual vegetation carbon sequestration have seldom been detected considering long-term plant succession after subsidence. To address this, a subsidence in the semi-arid underground mine of China was selected, and dynamics of annual vegetation carbon sequestration under deformation and baseline scenarios were simulated via a developed plant community succession model based on cellular automata. Results showed that ground deformation constrained tree growth, leading to a gradual transition from the original arbor forest to mixed forest under the deformation scenario. Annual vegetation carbon sequestration increased under both the deformation and baseline scenarios, but remained consistently lower under the deformation scenario. Moreover, the difference in annual vegetation carbon sequestration between the two scenarios gradually increased with spontaneous succession, from 30.56 Mg C yr−1 after 5 years to 44.53 Mg C yr−1 after 30 years. Compared with the baseline scenario, the annual vegetation carbon sequestration under the deformation scenario in the study area decreased by 6.59% to 67.36%, and showed the highest decrease (56.85–67.36%) in the area with 1–2 m’ subsidence. With the increase in succession years, the decline degree of the annual vegetation carbon sequestration in the deeper subsidence area decreased, while that in the shallower subsidence area gradually increased. In general, ground deformation affects the natural growth and community succession of vegetation, leading to the gradual degradation of tree vegetation and the decline in annual vegetation carbon sequestration. This study provides a method for quantifying impacts of ground deformation on the annual vegetation carbon sequestration, and provides theoretical guidance for the construction of green mining under the “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals”.

title: Prioritizing transport decarbonization strategies in Nigeria: An intuitionistic fuzzy decision framework for energy transition policy
summary: Nigeria's transport sector is a major and growing source of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, largely because mobility remains heavily dependent on petroleum products. Efforts to shift toward low-carbon transport are hindered by economic, ins
content: Nigeria's transport sector is a major and growing source of Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions, largely because mobility remains heavily dependent on petroleum products. Efforts to shift toward low-carbon transport are hindered by economic, institutional, infrastructural, and technological constraints. This study develops an integrated decision framework for prioritizing these challenges and identifying suitable policy responses within Nigeria's wider energy transition. Drawing on the literature, national policy documents, and the judgments of six experts from academia, government, transport, and energy, the study evaluates eight decarbonization challenges and five policy alternatives. It proposes an Intuitionistic Fuzzy (IF) extension of the RANking COMparison method (IF-RANCOM) to determine the relative importance of the challenges while considering uncertainty and hesitation in expert judgments. The resulting weights are incorporated into an Intuitionistic Fuzzy Additive Ratio Assessment (IF-ARAS) model to evaluate the policy alternatives. Compromise Fuzzy Ranking (CFR) is then used to reconcile differences among expert assessments and produce a collective ranking. The findings identify Nigeria's economic dependence on petroleum as the most important barrier, followed by weak policy frameworks and planning, inadequate infrastructure and technological capacity, and the high cost of zero-emission vehicles. Promoting mass transit is ranked as the most suitable policy response. Comparative and sensitivity analyses reveal that the main rankings remain stable under different methodological assumptions and parameter settings. The findings demonstrate the need for coordinated investment in mass transit, integrated transport and land use planning, sustainable financing, infrastructure modernization, and institutional reform. The proposed framework may also support other fossil-fuel-dependent developing economies in aligning transport priorities with energy security, social inclusion, and long-term decarbonization goals.

title: Tuning Coordination Chemistry and Composition of Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient Hydrogen Production
