Ante esta fricción estructural y limitada capacidad de sustitución de insumos energéticos en el corto plazo, se concluye que el ajuste tarifario es un fenómeno sistémico. En síntesis, se recomienda diseñar una reforma tarifaria que se ejecute gradualmente con el fin de impulsar incentivos para la eficiencia energética industrial y mecanismos de compensación focalizados que actúen sobre los eslabones finales de la cadena productiva para proteger el bienestar económico de los hogares.

title: How the European Union Fell Out of Love With Open‐Source Software
summary: ABSTRACT This article explains why the European Commission diluted the 2004 European Interoperability Framework's provisions favoring open‐source software and open standards when it revised the framework in 2010. Using an extended Multiple
content: ABSTRACT This article explains why the European Commission diluted the 2004 European Interoperability Framework's provisions favoring open‐source software and open standards when it revised the framework in 2010. Using an extended Multiple Streams Framework with a technology stream, the study shows how pro‐openness policy entrepreneurs secured the 2004 provisions and why incumbent advocacy became more effective during revision. Drawing on annotated drafts and expert interviews, the study traces actors' lobbying strategies across the problem, politics, and policy streams and examines how technology‐stream developments altered the feasibility and political salience of competing solutions. The analysis shows how changing standards and licensing dynamics, incumbent advocacy, and declining political support for the earlier pro‐openness package enabled a new coupling around business‐model neutrality and licensing flexibility, diluting the 2004 provisions. Beyond the European case, the study informs debates on open‐source artificial intelligence and advances theory on institutional dynamics in regulatory governance.

title: Numerical Computation of the Density of States of Aperiodic Multiscale Schrödinger Operators
summary: Abstract. Computing the electronic structure of incommensurate materials is a central challenge in condensed matter physics, requiring efficient ways to approximate spectral quantities such as the density of states (DoS). In this paper, we
content: Abstract. Computing the electronic structure of incommensurate materials is a central challenge in condensed matter physics, requiring efficient ways to approximate spectral quantities such as the density of states (DoS). In this paper, we numerically investigate two distinct approaches for approximating the DoS of incommensurate Hamiltonians for small values of the incommensurability parameters [Formula: see text] (e.g., small twist angle, or small lattice mismatch): the first employs a momentum-space decomposition, and the second exploits a semiclassical expansion with respect to [Formula: see text]. In particular, we compare these two methods using a one-dimensional toy model. We check their consistency by comparing the asymptotic expansion terms of the DoS, and it is shown that, for full DoS, the two methods exhibit good agreement in the small [Formula: see text] limit, while discrepancies arise for less small [Formula: see text], which indicates the importance of higher-order corrections in the semiclassical method for such regimes. We find these discrepancies to be caused by oscillations in the DoS at the semiclassical analogues of Van Hove singularities, which can be explained qualitatively, and quantitatively for [Formula: see text] small enough, by a semiclassical approach. title: Contrasting impacts of Asian sulfate aerosols on regional summer extreme precipitation under different climate backgrounds
summary: Abstract. This study investigates the impact of Asian sulfate aerosols on regional summer extreme precipitation under both pre-industrial and pre-industrial +1 K climate states, using the reduced-complexity climate model Fast Ocean Rapid Tr
content: Abstract. This study investigates the impact of Asian sulfate aerosols on regional summer extreme precipitation under both pre-industrial and pre-industrial +1 K climate states, using the reduced-complexity climate model Fast Ocean Rapid Troposphere Experiment version 2 (FORTE2) with Systematic Regional Aerosol Perturbations simulations. Results show that increased Asian sulfate aerosols reduce extreme precipitation, characterized by lower frequency and weaker intensity over East and South Asia in both climates, but the suppression is more pronounced over northern India in the +1 K climate. Atmospheric energy budget analysis reveals this is primarily due to enhanced dynamic effects in the warmer climate. When aerosols are added to the pre-industrial climate state, an increased horizontal dry static energy (DSE) gradient partially offsets the aerosol-induced dynamic suppression over northern India. Under the +1 K climate, higher atmospheric static stability weakens the local meridional circulation induced by aerosol forcing, reducing the meridional temperature gradient and thus diminishing the offsetting effect, making the dynamic suppression more dominant. Further analysis indicates that this difference in precipitation responses between the two climates results from the nonlinear effect between the aerosol-radiation and aerosol-cloud interactions under the +1 K climate, whereas the two effects combine approximately linearly under the pre-industrial climate. This study suggests that continued global warming alone will exacerbate Asian sulfate aerosols’ weakening of precipitation, including extremes, over northern India. This implies that future reductions in aerosol emissions may unmask or amplify extreme precipitation increases in this region.

title: Boundary-consistent thermodynamic and techno-economic assessment of an integrated MSW gasification–SOFC–LiBr–H2O trigeneration system
summary: The increasing generation of municipal solid waste (MSW), together with growing demand for decentralized electricity, heating and cooling, creates a need for integrated waste-to-energy systems with clearly defined thermodynamic and economic
content: The increasing generation of municipal solid waste (MSW), together with growing demand for decentralized electricity, heating and cooling, creates a need for integrated waste-to-energy systems with clearly defined thermodynamic and economic boundaries. This study develops a boundary-consistent design-stage framework for a distributed CCHP system integrating literature-sourced Norwegian MSW air–steam gasification, syngas conditioning, SOFC electricity generation, district heating, and LiBr–H₂O absorption cooling. Distinct from studies examining these subsystems separately, the framework combines cascade process integration, capacity-aware multi-response analysis, subsystem and whole-plant thermodynamic assessment, and deterministic–probabilistic economic screening using exportable net AC power. Sensitivity analysis and response surface methodology based on a central composite design were applied to evaluate the effects of feed rate, gasification temperature, equivalence ratio and steam-to-biomass ratio. Because the energy responses were expressed as absolute outputs, the upper feed rate of 100 kg h⁻¹ was interpreted as the maximum investigated design capacity rather than a thermodynamic optimum. At the selected design point, Aspen Plus confirmation produced 186.65 kW of gross DC power, 134.08 kW of heating and 27.24 kW of cooling, with surrogate-model deviations below 3% for the energy responses. After applying a 92% inverter efficiency and deducting 17.88 kW of auxiliary consumption, the exportable net AC power was 153.84 kW. The resulting net electrical efficiency, HHV-based CCHP energy-utilization efficiency and whole-system product-exergy efficiency were 25.40%, 52.04% and 28.97%, respectively. Subsystem exergy efficiencies were 69.99% for gasification, 42.29% for SOFC electricity generation and 19.79% for absorption cooling, identifying the gasifier and SOFC as the principal sources of irreversibility. A net-AC-based techno-economic assessment yielded a 12.07-year simple payback, an NPV of -USD 225.74 thousand, an IRR of 5.48% and an LCOE of USD 0.1187 kWh⁻¹. These results demonstrate the technical potential of integrated MSW-based CCHP while showing that economic viability remains dependent on capital cost, operating availability, auxiliary demand and effective utilization of the thermal products.

title: Does EU Taxonomy Alignment Reduce Corporate Emissions? Evidence From Nordic Firms
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT This paper investigates whether EU Taxonomy alignment is associated with lower corporate emissions, using 982 firm‐years from 358 Nordic firms (2022–2025). Extending targeted transparency theory, the study develops a signal‐quality
content: ABSTRACT This paper investigates whether EU Taxonomy alignment is associated with lower corporate emissions, using 982 firm‐years from 358 Nordic firms (2022–2025). Extending targeted transparency theory, the study develops a signal‐quality framework under which a mandated classification is informative only if it satisfies signal relevance, signal separation, and signal coupling. In the taxonomy's first years, each largely fails. Alignment is associated with modestly lower emissions intensity only in manufacturing, where the screening criteria impose emission thresholds; in information technology, where they reward efficiency without constraining emissions, alignment accompanies rising intensity. Emissions histories from 2012 show that firms with weaker pre‐taxonomy records report alignment more often, consistent with legitimacy‐seeking disclosure rather than performance signalling. Emissions do not change when alignment reporting begins: the label certifies pre‐existing activity rather than transformation. Signal production, rather than user attention, is the binding constraint; recalibrating the screening criteria will decide whether alignment comes to mark transformation.

title: Disclosure of Sustainability Information in Universities of BRICS Countries: A Study of the Current State and Future Prospects
source: Review of Business and Economics Studies
summary: Research question and objectives : This article aims to examine the current state of presentation and disclosure of information on the sustainability of universities in BRICS countries in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals (SD
content: Research question and objectives : This article aims to examine the current state of presentation and disclosure of information on the sustainability of universities in BRICS countries in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards, assessing the quality of public sustainability reports from top universities based on the 2024 pilot BRICS University Rankings. Research contribution: The scientific novelty of the study lies in proposing a new concept of ERSGDE reporting, based on principles of sustainable university activity (Education, Research, Social responsibility, Governance, Digital development, Environment), defining its compilation principles, content elements and structure. Research significance : The study provides a systematic assessment of sustainability reporting practices among top universities in six major emerging economies (China, Russia, South Africa, India, Saudi Arabia, and Brazil), offering a comparative benchmark and mapping current practices. Limitations: The study’s scope is limited to the top 50 universities, with a detailed analysis of a sample of 8 universities from China, Russia, and Brazil. Method : The methodological foundation relies on desktop analysis of publicly available reports. Implications: Adopting the developed ERSGDE reporting framework will enable universities to generate transparent, comprehensive, and accessible information on sustainable development. This is expected to expand the information landscape for engagement with both external and internal stakeholders, enhancing accountability and strategic communication. Future research: Directions include expanding the sample across BRICS, conducting longitudinal tracking of reporting evolution, and investigating the internal drivers and processes behind reporting quality in higher education.

title: The Main Macroeconomic Drivers of the Minimum Wage: Evidence from European Countries
source: Review of Business and Economics Studies
summary: Purpose: This study investigates the long-run effects of unemployment, the consumer price index, the level of gross domestic product, and labor productivity on minimum wages in a sample of 23 European countries over the period 1999–2024. Me
content: Purpose: This study investigates the long-run effects of unemployment, the consumer price index, the level of gross domestic product, and labor productivity on minimum wages in a sample of 23 European countries over the period 1999–2024. Method: The Cross-Sectionally Augmented Distributed Lag (CS-DL) approach is employed as the baseline estimator to examine the long-run impacts of macroeconomic variables on minimum wages. To assess the robustness of the findings, the Cross-Sectionally Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS-ARDL), Cross-Sectionally Augmented Error Correction Model (CS-ECM), and Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG) estimators are additionally applied. Finally, causal relationships among the variables are investigated using the Dumitrescu–Hurlin (DH) panel causality test. Results: The CS-DL results indicate that the consumer price index exerts a positive and statistically significant effect on minimum wages in the long run. The causality analysis reveals bidirectional causal relationships between the consumer price index and minimum wages, as well as between the level of gross domestic product and minimum wages. In addition, a unidirectional causal relationship is identified running from unemployment to minimum wages and from minimum wages to labor productivity. Contribution: This study contributes to the existing literature by providing a comprehensive analysis of the minimum wage determination mechanism in terms of both the set of explanatory variables and the econometric procedures employed. Furthermore, it offers empirical evidence on the macroeconomic dynamics shaping minimum wage decisions, moving beyond intuition-based arguments and descriptive assessments.

title: An Analysis of Consumers’ Purchase Intention and Willingness to Pay for Low-Carbon Seafood Products
source: Journal of Fisheries and Marine Sciences Education
summary: This study analyzes consumers’ perceptions, purchase intention, and willingness to pay for low-carbon seafood products. As the transition toward carbon neutrality has become an important policy agenda, reducing greenhouse gas emissions acro
content: This study analyzes consumers’ perceptions, purchase intention, and willingness to pay for low-carbon seafood products. As the transition toward carbon neutrality has become an important policy agenda, reducing greenhouse gas emissions across the seafood supply chain has emerged as a key challenge for the seafood industry. To this end, an online survey was conducted among 300 adult consumers with seafood purchase experience in Korea. An ordered logit model was used to analyze purchase intention, and an interval regression model was employed to estimate willingness to pay. The empirical results show that the perceived need for low-carbon seafood certification and the perceived influence of the Green Card program were positively associated with both purchase intention and willingness to pay. Seafood purchase frequency also showed a positive association, although its effect on purchase intention should be interpreted as exploratory. Conversely, preference for discounted foods was negatively associated with both purchase intention and willingness to pay, suggesting that price sensitivity may act as a barrier to the diffusion of low-carbon seafood products. These findings suggest that the development of low-carbon seafood markets may require a reliable certification system, consumer-oriented incentives, strengthened information provision, and initial-stage measures to reduce consumers’ price barriers. This study contributes to the literature by empirically applying the concept of low-carbon transition to seafood products and by offering policy implications for consumer demand-based strategies in the seafood industry.

title: Combining enhanced basalt weathering with soda saline soil: A novel CO₂ mineralisation strategy
summary: Enhanced rock weathering in saline–alkaline soils can couple CO₂ mineralisation with reclamation of salt-affected land. We incubated 30 g basalt with 30 g sodic saline soil for 90 days at 15 °C using three particle sizes (0.074, 0.42 and 5
content: Enhanced rock weathering in saline–alkaline soils can couple CO₂ mineralisation with reclamation of salt-affected land. We incubated 30 g basalt with 30 g sodic saline soil for 90 days at 15 °C using three particle sizes (0.074, 0.42 and 5 mm) and two water additions (30 and 60 g). Endpoint aqueous chemistry, SEM–EDS, thermogravimetric analysis and PHREEQC saturation modelling were integrated with a regional life-cycle assessment for Jilin Province, China. Endpoint Ca accounting yielded apparent weathered-basalt masses, which were converted using a primary Ca-only carbonate capacity of 0.072 g CO₂ g⁻¹ basalt and an all-base-cation carbonate-equivalent upper capacity of 0.142 g CO₂ g⁻¹ basalt. Particle-size-specific effective rates linked the incubation results to 30-year weathering trajectories. Gross CDR reached 72.45–72.47 kg CO₂ t⁻¹ basalt in the primary case and 141.92–141.96 kg CO₂ t⁻¹ basalt in the upper case. Across twelve scenarios, primary-case net CDR ranged from −5.53 to 38.45 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹ basalt, while upper-case net CDR ranged from 63.96 to 107.92 kg CO₂-eq t⁻¹ basalt. Net-removal costs ranged from USD 1327–29,328 t⁻¹ CO₂ in the primary net-removing scenarios and from USD 473–4667 t⁻¹ CO₂ in the upper case. The identified 6376,490 ha of Jilin cropland, equivalent to 482.06 Mt basalt at 75.6 t ha⁻¹ , had gross capacities of 34.93 Mt CO₂ (primary) and 68.43 Mt CO₂ (upper). Finer particles reached the composition-controlled capacity sooner, whereas coarse basalt had lower supply-chain emissions in the evaluated scenarios.

title: Valorization of drilling rock powder in cementitious grout towards greener mountainous transmission construction
summary: Rapid growth in electricity demand is accelerating the construction of transmission infrastructure across mountainous areas. Improper disposal of drilling rock powder (DRP) generated during transmission-tower foundation construction can dis
content: Rapid growth in electricity demand is accelerating the construction of transmission infrastructure across mountainous areas. Improper disposal of drilling rock powder (DRP) generated during transmission-tower foundation construction can disturb fragile mountain ecosystems and increase handling costs. This study examines the reuse of sieved DRP as an equal-mass substitute for Portland cement in cementitious grout. DRP content is expressed relative to the fixed total mass of PC, DRP, fly ash, and silica fume. Flowability and compressive strength were measured, and the pore structure and microstructure were examined using MIP, XCT, XRD, and SEM. At 28 d, mixtures containing up to 8% DRP retained compressive strengths of approximately 50–54 MPa; however, 8% and 10% DRP caused substantial flowability loss after 30 min. A content of 6% is therefore recommended as a balance between workability, strength, and powder reuse under the tested conditions, rather than as a strength-based maximum. Higher contents increased coarse capillary pore fractions and macroscopic air-void volumes, without detectable new crystalline phases in the displayed XRD interval. In the original field-planning scenario, reuse of 216 kg from 440 kg of generated DRP corresponds to 49.1% powder utilization and a conditional gross dry-grout procurement offset of CNY 324 per tower. This utilization rate is distinct from cement replacement, and the field formulation requires separate qualification because its dosage basis differs from the laboratory mixtures. The findings support source-specific evaluation of DRP reuse for transmission-tower foundations.

title: Modelling leaf heat balance and thermal-neutrality conductance of urban trees for building edge planting in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India: Effects of leaf size and stomatal behaviour in a tropical monsoon climate
summary: Leaf-to-air temperature difference (ΔT) is often read as an index of the cooling provided by trees planted along building edges. This assumption was tested in a purely numerical experiment; no field measurements were made. A two-sided, non-
content: Leaf-to-air temperature difference (ΔT) is often read as an index of the cooling provided by trees planted along building edges. This assumption was tested in a purely numerical experiment; no field measurements were made. A two-sided, non-linear leaf energy balance was forced with hourly typical-day climates reconstructed from India Meteorological Department normals (1991–2020) for Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India, a hot-humid tropical monsoon (Aw) climate. The balance included a parametric building-edge term for façade longwave emission and partial shading. Seven commonly planted trees (Neolamarckia cadamba, Alstonia macrophylla, Ficus elastica, Syzygium cumini, Ficus racemosa, Grevillea robusta and Saraca asoca) were represented by their flora-derived leaf dimensions under a shared stomatal physiology, so that the species contrasts are contrasts of leaf size; stomatal strategy was examined as a separate scenario. A thermal-neutrality conductance, g s *, was derived as the stomatal conductance at which the leaf neither gains nor releases sensible heat. Uncertainty was propagated by Monte Carlo sampling and apportioned by Sobol indices, and the robustness of the results to the forcing reconstruction was tested. Under a vapour-pressure-deficit (VPD)-closing stomatal response, leaves were warmer than air for 67–68% of daylight hours, and May afternoon ΔT ranged from 0.8 K (finest leaves) to 2.7 K (largest leaves). The required g s * (0.12–0.14 mol m −2 s −1 ) exceeded the modelled conductance by a factor of five to seven. Stomatal VPD sensitivity carried 67% and 72% of the variance in ΔT and sensible heat flux (H), whereas forcing-reconstruction errors carried less than 3%. ΔT was inversely ranked against H (Spearman ρ = −0.89): the finest leaves showed the smallest ΔT yet released the most sensible heat when stomata closed, and absorbed the most when they stayed open. A +3.0 K warming raised annual daytime heat return by 13–17%, and water limitation raised it by 76–86%. The cooling role of a leaf therefore changes with season and stomatal behaviour: during pre-monsoon heatwaves and monsoon middays, small leaves with closed stomata amplify air heating, although every tree still provides shade and other ecosystem services. Stomatal conductance is the primary indicator of latent heat exchange, yet species-level screening of this trait is lacking for most urban trees worldwide. Building-edge planting should therefore be planned around stomatal behaviour under high VPD, irrigation security and shade, with leaf size treated as an amplifier rather than as a cooling trait in itself.

title: Adaptation of EU policy during geopolitical change: the impact on forest use, bioenergy, and climate security in the Baltic region
summary: Abstract Background Forests in the Baltic Sea region store carbon, harbour biodiversity, sustain rural livelihoods and supply wood for materials and heating. Since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sanctions on Russian and Belarusian wood
content: Abstract Background Forests in the Baltic Sea region store carbon, harbour biodiversity, sustain rural livelihoods and supply wood for materials and heating. Since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sanctions on Russian and Belarusian wood and energy have disrupted these supply chains. This raises concern that the pursuit of energy security may increase pressure on forests, weaken carbon sinks and shift environmental impacts abroad. EU Member States set out how they will meet the 2030 energy and climate targets in National Energy and Climate Plans (NECPs), updated in 2024. This is the first study to examine these updates for Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Finland and Sweden through the lenses of climate security and “nexus thinking”, an approach that treats energy, land, ecosystems and society as interconnected. It combines content analysis of the five plans with 22 interviews with regional stakeholders. Results All five countries are turning to domestic bioenergy to replace Russian fuels, mainly forest residues and low-grade wood for district heating and combined heat and power. The Baltic states link forests mainly to energy sovereignty, grid integration with continental Europe and rural jobs. Sweden and Finland embed them in longer-term strategies for the bioeconomy, carbon sinks, hydrogen and carbon capture. Most plans favor using high-quality timber for products and residues for energy. Yet the plans only partly reflect the new situation: many adjustments happen in practice, outside the formal NECP framework. Climate, energy and human security are treated as parallel rather than potentially conflicting goals. Coordination is weak between EU and national levels, across sectors and among neighbouring countries. Finland’s forests, now a net emission source rather than a carbon sink, illustrate the trade-offs at stake. Conclusions Forests are becoming strategic security resources, but energy-security policies could unintentionally intensify logging, weaken carbon sinks and harm biodiversity. Forest, energy, biodiversity, climate and trade policy should therefore be governed together. Useful steps include harmonised EU reporting of fuelwood use, stronger rules prioritising material use of wood, biomass limits tied to carbon-sink and biodiversity indicators, building renovation to cut heat demand, and closer Baltic–Nordic cooperation on supply risks.

title: Resolving carbon–timber trade-offs through age-structured forest management in China
summary: Abstract Forests are critical for climate mitigation, yet minimizing harvesting may accelerate forest aging and mortality, potentially constraining long-term carbon sequestration while increasing timber dependence. Using 15.5 million tree r
content: Abstract Forests are critical for climate mitigation, yet minimizing harvesting may accelerate forest aging and mortality, potentially constraining long-term carbon sequestration while increasing timber dependence. Using 15.5 million tree records from China’s National Forest Inventory and a spatially explicit forest dynamics model, we assessed how alternative harvesting strategies affect carbon storage and wood production through 2100 under climate change. We show that current low-intensity harvesting promotes forest aging and mortality over time, reducing carbon-retention efficiency. In contrast, age-structured and spatially differentiated harvesting, expanded to suitable multifunctional forests, maintains more dynamic forest age structures, lowers mortality losses, increases total forest carbon stocks by 4.2%, and enhances timber production by 38% relative to current management regime. Despite modest reductions in standing biomass, gains in harvested wood products and reduced mortality have potential to generate a net climate benefit. Our results demonstrate that optimizing forest age structure through rational harvesting can reconcile carbon sequestration and wood supply, providing a scalable pathway for sustainable forest management.

title: Impact of Turning Operations and Fieldwork Patterns on the Efficiency of an Agricultural EV Robot
summary: Abstract The electrification of agricultural machinery offers a sustainable alternative, but the limited battery capacity of electric vehicle (EV) robots constrains their operational runtime. This study focuses on analyzing the energy consu
content: Abstract The electrification of agricultural machinery offers a sustainable alternative, but the limited battery capacity of electric vehicle (EV) robots constrains their operational runtime. This study focuses on analyzing the energy consumption characteristics of a four-wheel drive agricultural EV robot with skid steering and optimizing fieldwork patterns based on these insights. Field experiments were conducted to measure motor voltage, current, rotational speed, and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data during straight driving (SD) and four turning operations: sharp turning (ST), 1-row skip turning (1-RST), 2-RST, and 3-RST. Analysis revealed that turning generally consumed more energy than SD, with 3-RST requiring the highest energy. For practical evaluation, eight fieldwork patterns were compared, including the reference Each End turn Pattern (EEP) and seven alternatives. Although most alternatives increased travel distance and time compared with EEP, some patterns achieved higher energy efficiency, with up to 4.0% savings. A multi-criteria framework integrated time, distance, energy, and lateral imbalance into a comprehensive evaluation. Results indicated that the First turn Compact Skip Pattern (FCSP) was the most effective strategy. These findings highlight that selecting proper fieldwork patterns, considering energy characteristics, can significantly improve the efficiency and sustainability of agricultural EV robots.

title: Hierarchical Zeolites: Synthesis Strategies, Crystallization Mechanisms, and Machine Learning
summary: The revelation of the crystallization mechanism of zeolites is the key to shifting their synthesis from trial-and-error methods to predictive approaches. This review introduces the traditional and recently emerging green synthesis methods o
content: The revelation of the crystallization mechanism of zeolites is the key to shifting their synthesis from trial-and-error methods to predictive approaches. This review introduces the traditional and recently emerging green synthesis methods of hierarchical zeolites and compares their crystallization mechanisms from the perspective of synthesis strategies. Then, by discussing the classical and nonclassical theories, it analyzes the crystallization mechanisms of different synthesis strategies for hierarchical zeolites and finds that the research on kinetic control methods not only conforms to the theme of green and environmentally friendly synthesis at present but also can further explore the mechanism of zeolite crystallization. Finally, this review also presents the research results of the emerging machine learning-assisted zeolite structure design, which will bring new possibilities for the future realization of hierarchical zeolite structure design and directed synthesis through predictive methods.

title: From Lying to Standing: Anchoring Naphthoquinone via Pd─S Bonds on Pd Nanoclusters to Suppress Over‐Hydrogenation for Mild H 2 O 2 Synthesis
summary: ABSTRACT The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H 2 O 2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π‐system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─
content: ABSTRACT The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H 2 O 2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π‐system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─S anchoring strategy that constrains a dithiolated naphthoquinone ligand (SNQ), whose quinone moiety serves as a simplified structural model of AQ, in a standing configuration on low‐valent Pd nanoclusters. This directional coordination minimizes direct contact between the aromatic framework and Pd while retaining access of the carbonyl groups to activated hydrogen. Supported on XC‐72 affords a catalyst that produces H 2 O 2 through sequential H 2 hydrogenation and air oxidation under mild conditions (0.2 MPa H 2 , 30°C), achieving 300 mmol g Pd −1 h −1 and maintaining its initial activity over eight cycles. X‐ ray absorption spectroscopy supports the coexistence of Pd─Pd and Pd─S coordination, whereas in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals a reversible quinone/hydroquinone‐type redox cycle. Density functional theory calculations further identify carbonyl hydrogenation as energetically favored over aromatic‐ring hydrogenation. The Pd─S interface thus electronically promotes H 2 activation and geometrically restricts the quinone π‐system, spatially decoupling H 2 activation from aromatic‐ring adsorption and enabling selective, durable quinone‐mediated H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: The Circularity Advantage: Unlocking the Decarbonization Power of Environmental Taxation
summary: ABSTRACT Achieving sustainable industrial development requires a greater understanding of how circular economy capabilities interact with environmental policy instruments. This study examines whether circular material use directly reduces m
content: ABSTRACT Achieving sustainable industrial development requires a greater understanding of how circular economy capabilities interact with environmental policy instruments. This study examines whether circular material use directly reduces manufacturing emission intensity and whether it strengthens the decarbonization effects of environmental taxation and renewable energy deployment. Drawing on the natural resource‐based view and Porter's hypothesis, the analysis uses a balanced panel of 27 European Union Member States covering 2013–2023. Panel threshold estimation is combined with Driscoll–Kraay fixed effects, dynamic panel estimation, and method‐of‐moments quantile regression to address cross‐sectional dependence, endogeneity, and heterogeneous effects. The continuous‐threshold test does not confirm a statistically significant nonlinear relationship between circular material use and manufacturing emission intensity. Nevertheless, an estimated circular material use rate of 11.20% represents an economically meaningful regime divider. Above this level, manufacturing emission intensity is approximately 3.3% lower, while the emission‐reducing effect of environmental taxation is around 33% stronger than in the low‐circularity regime. Renewable energy reduces manufacturing emissions in both regimes, indicating that its contribution operates independently of circular material use. The findings reposition circularity from a standalone decarbonization instrument to an enabling capability that improves the effectiveness of complementary fiscal policies. The study contributes to sustainable development research by demonstrating that progress toward SDGs 9, 12, and 13 depends on coordinated policy mixes rather than isolated improvements in material circularity. EU Member States with weak circular capabilities should prioritize recycling, reverse logistics, and secondary‐material infrastructure before intensifying environmental taxation. At the same time, renewable energy deployment can proceed simultaneously across all circularity regimes.

title: Impact of hydropower construction on vegetation NPP in the Yarlung Zangbo River, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
summary: Vegetation net primary production (NPP) is integral to the global carbon cycle, especially in the alpine ecosystems of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. However, hydropower construction can profoundly disrupt ecosystem health and carbon sequestrat
content: Vegetation net primary production (NPP) is integral to the global carbon cycle, especially in the alpine ecosystems of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. However, hydropower construction can profoundly disrupt ecosystem health and carbon sequestration capacity, particularly along the Yarlung Zangbo River. Therefore, there is an urgent need to understand the impacts of hydropower construction on riparian vegetation NPP through precise, engineering-scale assessments of long-term changes. Changes in NPP may alter soil carbon inputs and turnover, with potential feedbacks on ecosystem carbon balance. Such assessments are essential for comprehensive ecological evaluations of hydropower projects. In this study, we downscaled MODIS NPP data to 30 m resolution using a convolutional neural network-based model to examine the spatiotemporal dynamics of NPP changes at the engineering scale across disturbance zones (DZs) and influence zones (IZs). We further applied a structural equation model (SEM) and a generalized linear model (GLM) to enable process-based attribution of dam- and climate-driven changes in NPP from the pre-construction, during-construction, to post-construction stages. The results showed that hydropower construction caused persistent NPP reductions in DZs due to engineered surface expansion and vegetation loss, whereas IZs experienced a sharp NPP decline during construction (88.6%), followed by widespread recovery in the post-construction stage (93.9%). The SEM–GLM framework identified dam construction as the predominant driver of NPP variations (standardized path coefficient: −0.35 in DZs; mean relative importance: 38.6% in IZs), exceeding the combined effects of precipitation and temperature. These findings provide critical insights for ecological risk assessment, sustainable ecosystem management, and the coordinated development of engineering infrastructure and the natural environment in future hydropower projects in environmentally sensitive alpine regions.

title: Geopolitical forces and strategic decision-making in multinational firms: a scorecard and heatmap comparative analysis
source: Technological and Economic Development of Economy
summary: In an increasingly interconnected world, the knowledge economy-encompassing technology, education and research-faces complex challenges posed by the evolving geopolitical dynamics. This paper examines how multinational companies strategical
content: In an increasingly interconnected world, the knowledge economy-encompassing technology, education and research-faces complex challenges posed by the evolving geopolitical dynamics. This paper examines how multinational companies strategically respond to these shifts. Through a compre­hensive analysis of regulatory changes, political instability, trade policies and decarbonization concerns, this paper highlights the composite nature of geopolitical risks and their influence on corporate strate­gy. Methodologically, the research employs a scorecard and a heatmap to provide a systematic, organ­ization‑level framework for comparing firms’ strategic responses. The scorecard evaluates regulatory compliance, supply chain resilience, risk management, strategic partnerships, innovation and carbon reduction targets across Apple, SAP and Tesla, with scores ranging from 2.00 to 4.00. Apple achieves the highest overall score (3.33/4), followed by Tesla (3.00/4) and SAP (2.83/4), indicating differences in inno­vation, policy alignment and supply chain resilience. The heatmap compares TotalEnergies, Danfoss and General Electric across eight decarbonization indicators, showing Danfoss as the sustainability leader. General Electric exhibits strong renewable‑energy capabilities, but remains constrained by legacy infra­structure. By applying this comparative framework, the study identifies improvement areas and offers strategic recommendations to help multinational companies strengthen geopolitical risk management and maintain competitive advantage in a rapidly changing global environment.

title: Predicting renewable hydrogen feasibility using a dynamic ensemble hybrid regression framework with explainable artificial intelligence
summary: Renewable-hydrogen assessment requires predictive models that distinguish independently available renewable-resource information from downstream engineered system outputs. This study proposes a leakage-controlled Dynamic Ensemble Hybrid Reg
content: Renewable-hydrogen assessment requires predictive models that distinguish independently available renewable-resource information from downstream engineered system outputs. This study proposes a leakage-controlled Dynamic Ensemble Hybrid Regression (DEHR) framework for predicting a dataset-provided renewable-hydrogen feasibility score. DEHR dynamically integrates heterogeneous base regressors through out-of-fold prediction generation, data-driven ensemble reliability estimation, training-derived reliability weighting, and ElasticNet meta-learning. To explicitly examine potential information leakage, two experimental settings were considered. The primary setting included only geographical, meteorological, and system-efficiency variables, whereas an extended diagnostic setting additionally included photovoltaic power, wind power, and hydrogen-production outputs. Model performance was evaluated using repeated 5-fold cross-validation with 10 repetitions, spatially grouped validation, and leave-one-latitude-band-out testing. Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Support Vector Regression, CatBoost, Linear/Ridge Regression, Multilayer Perceptron, Long Short-Term Memory, conventional stacking, and a separate Mixture-of-Experts model were used as benchmarks. Under the leakage-controlled primary-input setting, DEHR achieved an average MSE of 0.01543, RMSE of 0.1242, MAE of 0.0849, MedAE of 0.0641, MAPE of 2.42%, and R² of 0.9765. In contrast, the extended all-feature setting achieved an R² of approximately 0.9970, demonstrating that downstream engineered variables substantially increase apparent predictive performance. Spatial validation produced lower but still competitive accuracy, emphasizing the importance of geographical generalization assessment. Explainability analysis based on SHAP, permutation importance, accumulated local effects, and LIME showed that wind speed was the dominant independently available predictor after removal of engineered outputs. The findings demonstrate that DEHR provides accurate and interpretable renewable-hydrogen screening while also showing that exceptionally high performance can result from information redundancy in engineered predictors. The framework should therefore be interpreted as a methodological decision-support approach rather than a validated techno-economic investment model.

title: Review of Literature on Corporate Cash Holdings and Future Research Agenda in an ESG Framework
summary: ABSTRACT This study synthesizes the literature on corporate cash holdings under an ESG framework and develops a theoretically grounded future research agenda. Based on a systematic review of 116 studies screened from Scopus and Web of Scien
content: ABSTRACT This study synthesizes the literature on corporate cash holdings under an ESG framework and develops a theoretically grounded future research agenda. Based on a systematic review of 116 studies screened from Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection, the literature is categorized into five streams: impacts of aggregate ESG, environmental, social, and governance factors on cash holdings, and reverse effects of cash holdings/financial slack on ESG‐related outcomes. ESG reshapes three established cash‐holding motives: the insurance value of liquidity, the financing wedge between internal and external funds, and agency costs of retained cash. The E, S, and G pillars present distinct mechanisms tied to environmental commitments, stakeholder/labor claims, and liquidity governance. Stronger ESG can reduce cash by lowering risk, financing frictions, or agency costs, while strategic liquidity needs, stakeholder commitments, and adverse ESG shocks may increase cash demand. Reverse evidence shows accumulated liquidity funds ESG investment and supports employment resilience, forming a dynamic bidirectional ESG‐cash relationship. Methodologically, OLS and fixed‐effects regressions dominate the literature, while quasi‐experimental, structural, and machine‐learning approaches remain rare. Future research could explore nonlinear, co‐determined ESG‐cash dynamics via E‐DSGE modeling, real‐options analysis, AI‐enabled liquidity management, and ESG contagion in strategic alliances.

title: Whispers of Change: Positive Climate Communication Through ASMR and Its Potential for Climate Engagement
summary: In recent years, interest has grown in using positive climate communication, broadly understood as climate messages designed to evoke constructive emotional, cognitive, and relational responses, such as hope, efficacy, and nature connectedn
content: In recent years, interest has grown in using positive climate communication, broadly understood as climate messages designed to evoke constructive emotional, cognitive, and relational responses, such as hope, efficacy, and nature connectedness, rather than fear or anxiety, to foster climate engagement. While most research has focused on traditional journalism, Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response (ASMR) videos, featuring whispered content and natural soundscapes, may offer a novel sensory-affective format to complement such messages and foster reflective engagement with climate change. This study first explored participants’ reflections through an open-ended thought-listing, showing that ASMR videos can elicit appreciation of nature and personal responsibility for climate action. A 2 × 2 between-subjects online experiment (N = 159) then tested whether whispered narration and nature sounds influence contentment, momentary well-being, and behavioral intentions. Quantitative analyses revealed no significant effects. However, qualitative thought-listing data suggest that ASMR may present an innovative sensory-affective format that can foster emotional engagement and reflective consideration of climate action, pointing to new directions for positive climate communication.

title: Hetero‐Interface Maximized UiO‐66‐NH 2 /CeO 2−x Free Radical Scavenging Additives for Long‐Term Operation of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
summary: ABSTRACT The long‐term durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a critical hurdle for their widespread commercialization, largely because of chemical degradation of the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) by unintent
content: ABSTRACT The long‐term durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a critical hurdle for their widespread commercialization, largely because of chemical degradation of the membrane electrode assembly (MEA) by unintentionally generated free radicals during operation. Defective ceria (CeO 2−x ) nanoparticles have emerged as promising radical‐scavenging additives through reversible Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ redox cycling. However, their radical scavenging efficiency is limited by the sluggish regeneration of surface Ce 3+ species, which are the active species for radical scavenging, leading to a gradual loss of their initial scavenging capability during long‐term cell operation. Here, we report a strategy to accelerate Ce 3+ regeneration kinetics by maximizing heterointerface‐derived interactions through simple seed‐mediated growth of defective ceria on the surface of a metal‐organic framework (MOF). In particular, UiO‐66‐NH 2 undergoes partial amorphization and dissolution during the CeO 2−x nanoparticle growth, which enables intimate interfacial contact and enhanced electronic coupling with CeO 2−x . The resulting UiO‐66‐NH 2 /CeO 2−x heterostructure exhibits improved redox cycling and higher Ce 3+ retention under oxidative conditions than commercial ceria nanoparticles. Moreover, when incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer of the MEA, the UiO‐66‐NH 2 /CeO 2−x significantly suppressed the performance degradation, enabling stable single‐cell operation for over 500 h under an accelerated durability test.

title: Analysis of the global and local effects of urban green space vegetation types on early-summer near-surface O3 concentrations based on street view imagery – A case study of hangzhou
summary: With the expansion of urban development, air pollution has become increasingly severe. In recent years, ozone (O3) pollution has emerged as a major threat to air quality in China. Existing studies have rarely explored the impact of vegetati
content: With the expansion of urban development, air pollution has become increasingly severe. In recent years, ozone (O3) pollution has emerged as a major threat to air quality in China. Existing studies have rarely explored the impact of vegetation types on O3 from a micro-scale perspective. Taking Hangzhou, a city with severe O3 pollution, as an example, street-view images from eight districts were first collected. A DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation model trained on the ADE20K dataset was employed to accurately classify trees, shrubs, and grasses in the images. Meteorological and urban structural factors were incorporated, and Bayesian-optimized Optimization-based Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), and Geographically Weighted Random Forest (GWRF) models were applied to analyze the independent effects of the three vegetation-type factors on O3 concentration and their synergistic interactions from both global and local scales. The results indicate: (1) Xiaoshan District and the core urban areas such as Xihu District and are severely polluted, with an overall decreasing trend in O3 concentration (the area with O3 concentration in the range of 120.01-160.00 μg/m3 decreased from 2,100 km2 to 0 km2). (2) Meteorological factors dominate O3 variation, while the contributions of vegetation-type factors are relatively low. Nevertheless, vegetation-type factors still exhibit stable and differentiated contributions to O3 concentration. At the global scale, tree area proportion (TAP) shows either positive or negative effects on O3 concentration at high levels (average contribution = 0.002), shrub area proportion (SAP) has a positive influence, and grass area proportion (GAP) demonstrates a negative influence (average contribution = 0.006 for both). (3) At the local scale, the extremely high-importance areas of TAP shifted from northern Xihu District and Gongshu District in 2014 to southern Xihu District and Binjiang District in 2017. SAP exhibited relatively high and extremely high importance in southern Xihu District and western Xiaoshan District. The relatively high and extremely high importance areas of GAP were distributed in core urban zones such as eastern Xihu District, southern Gongshu District, Binjiang District, and Shangcheng District. The extent of extremely high-importance areas for all vegetation-type factors showed a decreasing trend. (4) High-importance areas of building density (BD) and industrial impervious surface percentage (ISP) spatially overlapped with those of vegetation-type factors, concentrating in core urban areas and the industrial zone of Xiaoshan, whereas meteorological factors played an independent role mainly in the peripheral areas of the city. This study aims to provide a scientific basis for precise O3 pollution control and optimal configuration of urban green spaces.

title: Research on Policy Response, Technological and Economic Bottlenecks, and Equitable Transition Path of China's Mining Areas under the Dual Carbon Target
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: Under the "dual-carbon" strategic framework, coal, as a cornerstone of China's energy security and local finances, faces unprecedented pressure to decarbonize. This paper, based on a micro-perspective of Shaanxi mining areas, systematically
content: Under the "dual-carbon" strategic framework, coal, as a cornerstone of China's energy security and local finances, faces unprecedented pressure to decarbonize. This paper, based on a micro-perspective of Shaanxi mining areas, systematically analyzes the policy response, operational frictions, and strategic optimization paths of coal enterprises through case studies, comparative policy assessments, and empirical survey data. The study finds that coal enterprises face severe technical and economic bottlenecks in their low-carbon transformation, including significant parasitic power consumption, a cost-price loss exceeding 60% due to the inverted cost of commercial carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), and extremely high dependence on regional finances and employment. To resolve the "energy trilemma" and achieve a balance between emission reduction and economic equity, this paper proposes a dual-track transformation framework that integrates "existing technology-based carbon reduction" with "incremental diversified development," and proposes a three-pillar institutional guarantee that includes a "just transition fund." The relevant conclusions provide specific policy references for China's low-carbon transformation that balances energy security, economic feasibility, and social equity.

title: TOURISM 5.0 IN PRACTICE: NAVIGATING THE TENSIONS BETWEEN DIGITAL EFFICIENCY AND LIVED AUTHENTICITY IN THE SAUDI CONTEXT
summary: The Tourism 5.0 paradigm is emerging as a pivotal response to the limits of a purely efficiency-oriented digitalisation, by placing people and sustainability back at the centre of innovation to create a holistic and responsible tourism ecos
content: The Tourism 5.0 paradigm is emerging as a pivotal response to the limits of a purely efficiency-oriented digitalisation, by placing people and sustainability back at the centre of innovation to create a holistic and responsible tourism ecosystem. Within the framework of Vision 2030, Saudi Arabia has adopted this orientation as a lever for economic diversification as a leading international tourism destination drawn on its cultural heritage and natural resources. However, the shift from theory to practice, in a context of very rapid transformation, raises questions about the balance between technological automation and authentic cultural experience. To address such questions and explore the tension between automation and authenticity resulted from the transition towards Tourism 5.0, a qualitative interpretive approach was undertaken. Based on 24 in-depth interviews conducted with Saudi and international experts during the TOURISE 2025 event. The reason for the interviews is to delve deeply into experts’ perceptions on how artificial intelligence and data are being integrated into the tourism sector as well as addressing the potential conflict between digitalization and authenticity. The findings reveal a strong ambition to build a Saudi "smart heritage" for enhancing, not replacing, cultural experience. There is also a need for structural challenges related to the development of hybrid skills among the workforces. The skills should include mixing technological proficiency with deep cultural knowledge and hospitality expertise proficiency. The results also emphasised the inclusion of small local tourism and hospitality businesses for successful transition. Implications of these findings are then discussed and elaborated.

title: Does water resource taxation improve firm productivity and regional ecological performance? Evidence from China
summary: Introduction Water scarcity is increasingly constraining global sustainable development, making it a critical policy challenge to improve economic performance while strengthening resource conservation. Methods Using the 2018 expansion of Ch
content: Introduction Water scarcity is increasingly constraining global sustainable development, making it a critical policy challenge to improve economic performance while strengthening resource conservation. Methods Using the 2018 expansion of China’s Water Resource Tax Pilot Policy (WRTP) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study applies a difference-in-differences approach to firm-level and county-level data from 2012 to 2022. Results The results show that the WRTP significantly improves the total factor productivity of water-intensive firms, particularly in cities with stronger industrial foundations, the Yangtze River Economic Belt, regions with relatively abundant water resources, and larger listed firms. Environmental performance disclosure strengthens this productivity effect. Green innovation and pollution treatment disclosure exhibit significant positive moderating effects, whereas environmental supervision disclosure does not exhibit a significant moderating effect. County-level evidence further shows that the WRTP reduces water consumption intensity and the area affected by soil erosion while increasing sewage treatment capacity and investment in wastewater treatment. Discussion Overall, water resource taxation improves firm productivity while enhancing regional ecological performance, providing policy insights for advancing sustainable water governance in resource-constrained economies.

title: The Characteristics and Influencing Factors of a Tourism, Cultural, and Ecological Space Network in the Yellow River Basin
summary: The coordinated advancement of cultural, tourism and ecological industry construction is of great significance to the high-quality development of the Yellow River Basin. Based on culture-tourism-ecology panel data of the nine provinces and
content: The coordinated advancement of cultural, tourism and ecological industry construction is of great significance to the high-quality development of the Yellow River Basin. Based on culture-tourism-ecology panel data of the nine provinces and autonomous regions in the Yellow River Basin from 2012 to 2022, a modified coupling model was constructed using the entropy method to measure the development levels of culture, tourism, and ecology across the provinces and autonomous regions in the basin. Separately, the modified gravity model, social network analysis, and Dynamic QAP were employed to examine the structural characteristics and influencing factors of the spatial correlation network. The results show that from 2012 to 2022, the development levels of culture, tourism and ecology in the Yellow River Basin have trended upward with fluctuations, with the relative development levels being ecology>culture>tourism, and the comprehensive development has spatial heterogeneity. Regionally, the coupling coordination degree follows a clear spatial pattern that is generally higher in the east and south, and lower in the west and north of the basin. The spatial correlation network within the Yellow River Basin is growing in density and complexity, and it is characterized by multi-threaded interconnections. Shanxi Province occupies a central position in this network, as it maintains strong linkages with other provinces, while Sichuan Province is in a marginal position in the network and has weak connections with other provinces. Inner Mongolia, Shandong, Gansu and Sichuan are “central provinces” in the spatial correlation network, and they are controlling and influencing the external radiation and spatial spillover of culture, tourism and ecology in the basin, while Qinghai and Ningxia are relatively marginalized. Among the factors influencing the spatial network structure, spatial adjacency and economic development level have significant impacts. Infrastructure differences have changed from being “irrelevant” to being “important drivers”. Differences in human capital and government macro-control have changed from marginally significant to having no impact.

title: Enterprise Valuation from an ESG Perspective: A Case Study of BYD
source: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
summary: With the rapid development of China's new energy vehicle industry, the impact of technological innovation, capital investment, and sustainable operation capabilities on corporate value is becoming increasingly prominent, while the tradition
content: With the rapid development of China's new energy vehicle industry, the impact of technological innovation, capital investment, and sustainable operation capabilities on corporate value is becoming increasingly prominent, while the traditional DCF model is still limited in reflecting ESG factors. This paper takes BYD as the research object, introduces ESG factors into the traditional discounted free cash flow model, and then modifies the revenue growth rate, weighted average cost of capital and perpetual growth rate, and compares the valuation results of the two models. This study finds that BYD's free cash flow in the early part of the forecast period was under continuous pressure due to high capital expenditures, and the present value of short-term FCFF will decrease slightly after ESG adjustments. However, the lower cost of capital and higher long-term growth expectations significantly improved the final value, increasing the enterprise value from RMB 244.424 billion to RMB 275.641 billion, an increase of approximately 12.77%, which indicates that the impact of ESG on firm value is primarily reflected in improvements in long-term capital costs and expectations of continued growth, rather than in increases in short-term cash flow.

title: Low-carbon evaluation and carbon quantification for highway reconstruction and expansion projects: framework development and engineering applications
source: International Conference on Advances in Energy and Environmental Engineering (AEEE)
summary: With the continuous improvement of the scale and level of expressway construction and the gradual advancement of the national process of "carbon peak and carbon neutrality", the low-carbon construction of expressway reconstruction and expan
content: With the continuous improvement of the scale and level of expressway construction and the gradual advancement of the national process of "carbon peak and carbon neutrality", the low-carbon construction of expressway reconstruction and expansion projects has become an important research field for the development of highway infrastructure. The green highway evaluation index system which has been proposed before emphasizes ecological and environmental protection, green concepts, and quality construction. However, it does not explicitly address the impact of new technologies on carbon reduction benefits during the low-carbon construction processes of the renovation and expansion of existing roads, such as the reuse of waste materials, the use of prefabricated components, the utilization of foam lightweight soil, and 3D printed sound barriers. Based on the reconstruction and expansion project of the section from Reshui in Heyuan to Pingnan in Huizhou of Changshen Expressway, this study systematically establishes the evaluation index system for the design and construction of low-carbon expansion and reconstruction of highways by using the expert Delphi method, proposing a method for assessing carbon reduction levels of design evaluation indicators before and after optimization, and calculating the overall carbon reduction of the project in conjunction with baseline scenario calculations. By establishing a carbon emission factor model, the reconstruction and expansion project of the Changshen Expressway from Heyuan to Pingnan in Huizhou has comprehensively applied low-carbon technologies, achieving an overall reduction rate of carbon emissions of 16.16%. The research results provide theoretical support and technical guidance for the green and low-carbon transformation of expressway reconstruction and expansion, and help achieve the "dual carbon" goal.

title: From wind-solar accommodation to potential coal-generation displacement: spatial coordination and operational CO2 mitigation in China’s power system
summary: Wind-solar accommodation does not necessarily yield equivalent reductions in coal generation or emissions. Using 2022 hourly output for 2880 county-level units, 8760-h loads for 31 provinces and data for 2985 coal units or project phases, w
content: Wind-solar accommodation does not necessarily yield equivalent reductions in coal generation or emissions. Using 2022 hourly output for 2880 county-level units, 8760-h loads for 31 provinces and data for 2985 coal units or project phases, we compare provincial self-accommodation, neighboring-province pairing, nationwide pairing and national aggregation. Absolute coal-generation displacement is measured against a constructed common reference excluding studied wind-solar generation under unchanged demand and resources: a model counterfactual, not observed 2022 dispatch. Under the benchmark assumptions, nationwide pairing increases direct accommodation by 310.59 TWh (39.04%), coal-generation displacement by 285.98 TWh (47.61%) and operational CO₂ mitigation by 250.36 Mt (41.29%) relative to provincial self-accommodation. Renewable supply, coal conversion and displaced emission intensity contribute 191.39, 90.66 and − 31.69 Mt, respectively. Although nationwide pairing and national aggregation both directly accommodate approximately 1106.15 TWh, aggregation displaces another 144.58 TWh of coal generation and avoids another 127.79 Mt of CO 2 . Additional sensitivity tests retain positive coordination benefits but show substantial dependence on matching assumptions, annual reduction allowances and eligible provincial connections. These estimates describe conditional coordination potential under fixed unit emission intensities and unrestricted transfers within coordinated domains. Renewable planning should jointly assess accommodation, access to reducible coal generation and unit-level emission differences.

title: The role of the Cu/Pr2O3 interface in methanol synthesis from CO2 thermal-catalytic hydrogenation: A first-principles study
summary: CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol is of significant potential for achieving carbon neutrality. Rare-earth metals show excellent potential to enhance the hydrogenation activity of Cu-based catalysts. Herein, the hydrogenation mechanism was inve
content: CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol is of significant potential for achieving carbon neutrality. Rare-earth metals show excellent potential to enhance the hydrogenation activity of Cu-based catalysts. Herein, the hydrogenation mechanism was investigated by focusing on the role of the catalyst interface created by the active metal Cu and substrate Pr 2 O 3 . The first-principle calculation was employed, using a Cu 3 cluster supported on the Pr 2 O 3 interface (Cu 3 /Pr 2 O 3 (111)) model and a bulk Cu(111) surface model. The adsorption of CO 2 and H 2 , the dissociation of H 2 , and the methanol generation pathways were analyzed carefully. The calculation findings indicate that the Cu 3 /Pr 2 O 3 (111) interface significantly improves the adsorption and activation of CO 2 and H 2 , compared with Cu(111). CO 2 undergoes a bent adsorption over the Cu 3 /Pr 2 O 3 (111) interface, with a high adsorption energy of -1.14 eV. The interface also demonstrates a very low H 2 dissociation energy barrier of 0.43 eV. In addition, on the Cu 3 /Pr 2 O 3 (111) interface, the reverse water-gas shift followed by the CO-hydro pathway has a significant advantage over the formate pathway for methanol formation (energy barrier 1.05 eV vs. 2.29 eV), which is different from the situation on Cu(111). This research enhances the understanding of rare-earth metal oxides’ impact on CO 2 hydrogenation catalysis and offers valuable insights for designing efficient methanol synthesis catalysts.

title: Coordinated strategy of peak-valley arbitrage and demand charge management for industrial and commercial energy storage considering battery degradation
summary: Driven by the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, commercial and industrial (C&I) energy storage has becomeacore technical approach for users to reduce costs and improve efficiency, with time-of-use (TOU) arbitrage and demandcharge
content: Driven by the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, commercial and industrial (C&I) energy storage has becomeacore technical approach for users to reduce costs and improve efficiency, with time-of-use (TOU) arbitrage and demandcharge management as its two dominant revenue streams. Existing studies on coordinated scheduling generallytreat battery life degradation as an exogenous hard constraint without internalizing degradation costs into the optimizationobjective, which easily induces excessive charge-discharge behavior and overestimates the life-cycle economy of energystorage. To address this issue, this paper proposes a coordinated optimization strategy for TOU arbitrage and demandcharge management of C&I energy storage considering battery life degradation. A depth-of-discharge basedsemi-empirical power-law model is adopted to quantify battery degradation cost, and the nonlinear degradation terms areconverted into linear constraints via piecewise linearization. A mixed-integer linear programming model aimingat maximizing daily comprehensive net revenue is established to achieve the optimal trade-off between short-termoperation revenue and long-term life loss. Case studies on a typical large industrial user demonstrate that the coordinatedstrategy can significantly improve comprehensive revenue compared with single-function optimization. Afterincorporating degradation cost, the equivalent cycle count and capacity fade rate of the battery are both reducedby53.8%. Although short-term revenue decreases by 25.8%, the life-cycle net revenue is significantly improved. Thisresearch can provide a theoretical basis for the economic operation and life management of C&I energy storage.

title: The Rise of Carbon Finance: A Bibliometric Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT Carbon finance has emerged as a critical mechanism for mobilizing capital toward climate change mitigation and supporting the transition to low‐carbon economies. However, its intellectual development remains fragmented across envir
content: ABSTRACT Carbon finance has emerged as a critical mechanism for mobilizing capital toward climate change mitigation and supporting the transition to low‐carbon economies. However, its intellectual development remains fragmented across environmental economics, financial economics, sustainability, and climate policy. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric assessment of carbon finance research, examining its growth trajectory, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, thematic evolution, and emerging research frontiers. Using 1610 Scopus‐indexed publications from 1993 to 2026, the study integrates performance analysis, citation impact, science mapping, network analysis, thematic visualization, Bradford's law, Lotka's law, journal quality indicators, and life cycle analysis. The findings reveal substantial growth, particularly following the Paris Agreement, alongside a concentrated intellectual structure in which China leads publication productivity, whereas the United States, the United Kingdom, and Japan demonstrate strong citation influence. Collaboration networks indicate increasing internationalization, although research remains concentrated among a limited number of authors and institutions. Thematic evolution demonstrates a shift from carbon markets, emissions trading, and environmental regulation toward green finance, sustainable investment, climate‐related financial risk, renewable‐energy financing, ESG integration, and digital finance. The study contributes by extending the temporal coverage of previous bibliometric reviews, integrating multiple analytical approaches, and explicitly tracing the progressive financialization of carbon finance. It reconciles divergent patterns in productivity, citation influence, collaboration, and development across countries and disciplines. By identifying structural patterns, emerging themes, and underexplored research frontiers, the study provides an evidence‐based agenda for future research and informs policymakers, standard‐setters, investors, and practitioners seeking to advance sustainable financial systems and climate transition strategies.

title: Afforestation as a dual climate strategy in Kenya's arid lands: A mixed-methods analysis of challenges and opportunities
summary: Climate change disproportionately impacts arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs), where ecosystems and livelihoods are highly vulnerable. Afforestation is used in Kenya as an adaptation and as a mitigation tool, yet little is known of the reasons
content: Climate change disproportionately impacts arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs), where ecosystems and livelihoods are highly vulnerable. Afforestation is used in Kenya as an adaptation and as a mitigation tool, yet little is known of the reasons for its limited success in the ASAL regions. This article examines the evolution of afforestation policies, challenges in implementation and ways of improving outcomes. The authors adopt a framework of social equity, institutional coherence and ecological fit, built on the Social-Ecological systems (SES) approach to explore these questions. It employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design in Isiolo and Marsabit counties. Survey data from 73 stakeholders were analyzed in STATA 18 using descriptive statistics, chi-square and one-way ANOVA and linear regression tests, while eight key informant interview data what analyzed thematically using NVivo 14. Results indicate that the respondents perceive afforestation programs have improved (Mean = 3.98, SD = 0.69, [five-point Linkert scale]), driven by policy alignment with the Paris Agreement and SDG 13, although in Marsabit the perceived effectiveness was lower compared to Isiolo. However, natural hazards (droughts, floods), land-tenure, institutional fragmentation and conflicts hinder implementation, with the under-representation of women also emerging as a challenge. Respondents associated community-centric governance, agroforestry integration and public-private partnerships with better reported outcomes. The main finding from this study is that for ecologically appropriate planting to work, there needs to be coherence at an institutional level and equitable benefit-sharing. The sample consisted of two arid counties. As a result, the findings cannot be generalized to all ASALs in Kenya. From the study, priority would be given at county level to species/site guidelines, locally accountable and transparent climate finance, and ecological monitoring over the long term.

title: Large‐scale rewetting and shading experiment reveals optimum conditions for tropical peat swamp forest restoration
summary: Abstract Introduction Deforestation and fires have caused substantial loss of tropical peat swamp forests (PSF) in Southeast Asia. Substantial efforts have been undertaken to rewet and revegetate peatlands, but these restoration measures ca
content: Abstract Introduction Deforestation and fires have caused substantial loss of tropical peat swamp forests (PSF) in Southeast Asia. Substantial efforts have been undertaken to rewet and revegetate peatlands, but these restoration measures can lead to conflicting outcomes. Knowledge is needed on how to combine revegetation and rewetting approaches to effectively restore peatlands. Objectives Using a large‐scale field manipulation in Sumatra, Indonesia, on a former Acacia plantation on peat, the effects of water table depth (WTD) below the peat surface and shading conditions on planted tree species were tested. Methods WTD was manipulated through surface treatments by lowering the peat surface to differing depths (0, −0.25, and −0.50 m) and carried out shading manipulation across 72 plots with a complementary natural Acacia tree shading experiment in 12 plots. Individual tree survival and growth of 3124 seedlings from 16 species were monitored from 24 up to 36 months, alongside natural regeneration. Results Higher water tables with prolonged inundation inhibited seedling growth, survival, and natural regeneration. Full shade treatment with artificial netting increased seedling survival but reduced growth during the first 12 months. Similar effects were observed in the natural Acacia tree shading experiment. There were significant species differences in response to treatments and continuous WTD variation. Conclusions Our findings showcase that too much rewetting has the potential to negatively influence planted seedling growth and survival and highlight the importance of shading to ensure seedling survival. These insights provide a foundation for defining optimal WTD targets and species selection strategies for PSF restoration.

title: Green Economic Benefits of Tourism Development in China: Based on Natural and Human Geographical Factors
summary: The aim of developing sustainable tourism is to harmonize economic growth with environmental protection. This study innovatively establishes a research framework to examine the impact of tourism development (TD) on urban green economy effic
content: The aim of developing sustainable tourism is to harmonize economic growth with environmental protection. This study innovatively establishes a research framework to examine the impact of tourism development (TD) on urban green economy efficiency (UGEE) through the lens of geographical factors. A slacks-based measurement model with undesirable outputs is employed to estimate UGEE. Econometric analyses reveal that TD significantly enhances UGEE, a result that remains robust under various tests. Mechanism analysis reveals that natural geographical factors mediate the relationship through the cost-effect, pollution effect, and livable and tourist-friendly effect of the development mechanism. Also, human geographical factors foster UGEE by stimulating economic vitality, optimizing industrial structure, and improving environmental protection. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the impact of TD on UGEE varies among different geographical locations, city sizes, and city types. This study provides new theoretical insights and practical policy recommendations for understanding the role of geographical factors in the relationship between TD and UGEE, thereby promoting the development of sustainable tourism in China.

title: Carbon sink potential and evolution of vegetation suitable zones in China during the dual-carbon period (2020–2060)
summary: Afforestation has been widely recognized as a typical natural solution to climate change. However, under the strategic direction of the dual-carbon target, the traditional large-scale vegetation restoration model needs to transition toward
content: Afforestation has been widely recognized as a typical natural solution to climate change. However, under the strategic direction of the dual-carbon target, the traditional large-scale vegetation restoration model needs to transition toward precision species selection. In this study, we assessed the vegetation types that provide the greatest biomass compatible with the local environment in the present and during the “dual-carbon” period (2020–2060) using the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) model, combining Shared Socio-Economic Pathway (SSPs) and Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs). The evolution of vegetation suitability zones and carbon sink potential in China under different scenarios was also evaluated. The results showed that there were significant eco-geographical differences in the distribution of suitable areas for the 11 major forest vegetation types in China.
