While the CRA frameworks do not explicitly mention compound and cascading risks, further reading in professional literature illustrates how to include these risk types through scenario analysis. Therefore, the scope of the subsequent analysis is to link compound and cascading risks with scenario analysis. We conclude that there is currently limited rigor in incorporating compound and cascading climate risks into CRA frameworks and disclosures, although the topic is emerging. This calls for deeper engagement in the coming years, from regulators financial industry, food system actors and academia.

title: Harnessing GIS to map trawl fishing grounds and reduce carbon footprint along India’s west coast
summary: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort,
content: Aim: This study examines the spatial and temporal dynamics of key commercial fish species along the west coast of India through GIS-based mapping, aiming to reduce the environmental footprint of trawl fisheries by optimizing fishing effort, minimizing scouting time, and lowering carbon emissions. Methodology: Data from customised logbooks for each fishing operation were geo-referenced using recorded latitude–longitude coordinates to delineate the spatial extent of fishing grounds. Spatial analysis and map generation were conducted using ArcGIS, while Visual Basic 6 was used for database management and query execution. The datasets were used to generate thematic layers, shapefiles, and feature classes for spatio-temporal analysis of fishing activities and species distribution. Results: Three commercially important species/groups—Trichiurus lepturus, Nemipterus spp. (N. japonicus and N. randalli), and Lagocephalus inermis—showed consistent occurrence within trawling grounds, with clear seasonal fluctuations in abundance. Peak abundances of Nemipterus spp. in January and October and Lagocephalus inermis in January and May, indicating persistent species–habitat associations across seasons. Interpretation: The findings of this study highlight the utility of participatory GIS-based mapping in identifying productive fishing grounds and supporting adaptive, season-specific fisheries management, and conservation planning. Practically, the spatial information generated can help fishers reduce scouting time, fuel consumption, and operational costs by targeting areas of consistent abundance, thereby also contributing to lower greenhouse gas emissions from trawling operations. Key words: Climate change, CO2 emission, Fisheries, Fishing grounds, Mitigation, Trawl

title: CO2 confinement by a novel molecular spring architecture via reactive molecular dynamics
summary: Abstract In this study, we propose a novel framework with a hybrid molecular spring architecture based on a spiral/helical-type nanostructure supported by slab layers and bridged by organic linkers. Hierarchically, the framework consists of
content: Abstract In this study, we propose a novel framework with a hybrid molecular spring architecture based on a spiral/helical-type nanostructure supported by slab layers and bridged by organic linkers. Hierarchically, the framework consists of symmetrical nickel (Ni)-doped α-Al 2 O 3 slabs, a sulfur-rich helical cage, and multifunctional 2,5-dimercaptoterephthalic acid (DMBDC) organic linkers. Ni/α-Al 2 O 3 supported, DMBDC bridged and helical pillared framework (SL-HPF) contributed to dynamic structural stability, the synergistic role of interfacial coupling and molecular confinement through reactive force field (ReaxFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The CO 2 confinement performance of SL-HPF was analysed by atomic arrangements via MD trajectories, self-diffusion coefficient (D), radial distribution functions (RDF), gas viscosity measurements. To isolate the contribution of the helical cage, a control system was conducted on pure Ni/α-Al 2 O 3 slabs. The D and gas viscosity of CO 2 for only control system are 1.451 × 10 –7 m 2 s −1 and 0.0163 Js m −3 , respectively. In contrast, the SL-HPF exhibited an enhanced molecular trapping because CO 2 molecules systematically penetrated the helical cage due to strong confinement effects. For SL-HPF, D and local fluid viscosity of CO 2 were calculated as 1.812 × 10 –8 m 2 s −1 and 0.0347 Js m −3 , respectively. Structural localization was further validated by a highly dense S-C pair RDF correlation peak at 1.8 Å within the helical cage. These results demonstrate that the synergy between catalytic metal sites, elastic organic springs, and high-affinity sulfur vacancies in the helical cage can successfully immobilize gas molecules through molecular trapping rather than chemical bond disruption. This work presents a novel molecular spring design and hybrid framework for next-generation environmental remediation technologies.

title: Toxic ecologies and harm stabilization: a critical realist account of social-ecological harm at Nairobi’s Dandora Dumpsite
summary: Urban waste systems can reproduce severe harm even where it is extensively documented and repeatedly targeted by policy. This article asks how unjust human-nature relations become stabilized as routine under these conditions, using a critic
content: Urban waste systems can reproduce severe harm even where it is extensively documented and repeatedly targeted by policy. This article asks how unjust human-nature relations become stabilized as routine under these conditions, using a critical realist analysis of Nairobi's Dandora Dumpsite. It proposes the concept of toxic ecology, an emergent configuration in which contaminants, infrastructures, institutions, and everyday practices cohere into durable patterns of exposure and inequality. A mixed-genre documentary corpus is synthesized through structured extraction and retroduction to identify recurring regularities and infer a conjunctural configuration of six interacting mechanisms, spanning responsibility diffusion, regulatory deferral, infrastructural lock-in, normalization, unequal valuation, and de facto control. Rival framings such as informational deficit and implementation failure are assessed as rebuttals and judged insufficient on their own. The analysis explains how chronic harm is restabilized as ordinary and governable, reframing sacrifice zones as stabilized human-nature relations rather than implementation failures.

title: PHYTOPHARMACOLOGICAL EVALUATION OF CALOTROPIS LEAF EXTRACT FOR CYSTIC FIBROSIS: A BIOACTIVE SCREENING AND MOLECULAR DOCKING APPROACH
source: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
summary: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-threatening autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, leading to defective chloride ion transport and thick mucus accumulation, primarily affecting the lungs and digestive system. Curr
content: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-threatening autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the CFTR gene, leading to defective chloride ion transport and thick mucus accumulation, primarily affecting the lungs and digestive system. Current treatment options focus on managing symptoms, yet there remains a strong demand for novel, cost-effective therapeutics with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. This study explores the phytotherapeutic potential of Calotropis gigantea and Calotropis procera, two traditional medicinal plants known for their bioactive compounds. Methanolic leaf extracts were subjected to phytochemical screening, Thin Layer Chromatography (TLC), and column chromatography. Fractionated samples were analyzed using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS), which identified key compounds such as pinoresinol and neophytadiene. Molecular docking studies were performed to assess their interactions with CFTR-related protein domains. Pinoresinol exhibited strong binding affinity, suggesting its potential to modulate CFTR function and reduce inflammation. These findings highlight the potential of Calotropis-derived compounds as a promising source for CF therapy. Further in vitro and in vivo investigations are recommended to validate their therapeutic mechanisms and efficacy. This study contributes to the growing interest in plant-based drug discovery for genetic and inflammatory disorders.

title: Rapid tetracycline degradation by a hydroxylamine/chloride- enhanced zero-valent copper/peroxydisulfate system under near- neutral conditions
summary: Abstract Limited copper(I) availability constrains peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation by zero-valent copper (Cu⁰). This study evaluates the combined effects of hydroxylamine (HA) and chloride by comparing matched Cu⁰/PDS control systems and r
content: Abstract Limited copper(I) availability constrains peroxydisulfate (PDS) activation by zero-valent copper (Cu⁰). This study evaluates the combined effects of hydroxylamine (HA) and chloride by comparing matched Cu⁰/PDS control systems and relating tetracycline (TC) removal to measured copper(I) concentrations and PDS consumption. At an initial pH of 5.0, TC removal after 10 min was 11.1% without either additive, 63.8% with HA, 23.8% with chloride and 86.2% with both; the combined-system apparent rate constant was 0.2119 min⁻¹. PDS consumption was 6%, 34%, 13% and 54%, respectively. These concurrent trends are consistent with complementary HA-assisted copper(I) regeneration and chloride-mediated stabilization, although they do not directly resolve individual copper(I) complexes or quantify an interaction between the additives. Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and quenching tests support radical involvement and possible reactive chlorine participation, without establishing copper(III) as the dominant oxidant. TC removal was 68.6% at initial pH 7.0, 77.1% in tap water and 67.7% in surface water. Total organic carbon removal was only 5.7% after 10 min, indicating limited mineralization. Alkaline precipitation and filtration reduced total dissolved copper from 7.16 to 0.673 mg/L. The study links combined-additive enhancement to copper(I) availability and oxidant consumption while identifying mineralization and copper management as limitations requiring further evaluation.

title: A drug–drug cocrystal of breviscapine and borneol: harnessing natural product synergy for synchronized release and improved pharmacokinetics
summary: A drug–drug cocrystal strategy harnessing natural product synergy was developed to address the oral delivery barriers of breviscapine (BRE), a natural flavonoid with poor solubility and extensive first-pass metabolism. BRE was integrated wi
content: A drug–drug cocrystal strategy harnessing natural product synergy was developed to address the oral delivery barriers of breviscapine (BRE), a natural flavonoid with poor solubility and extensive first-pass metabolism. BRE was integrated with the monoterpenoid permeation enhancer borneol (BO) via solvent evaporation to form a stable supramolecular assembly. Comprehensive solid-state characterization and density functional theory calculations confirmed that the cocrystal lattice is stabilized by specific hydrogen bonding between the flavonoid and terpenoid scaffolds. The optimized BRE-BO cocrystal exhibited highly synchronized release of both natural products ( R 2 = 0.86), in contrast to the discordant dissolution of the physical mixture, with kinetics following the Korsmeyer–Peppas model (n = 0.45) indicative of Fickian diffusion. In vivo pharmacokinetic evaluation in rats demonstrated that the synergy conferred by co-delivered BO resulted in a 1.6-fold enhancement in oral bioavailability ( AUC 0-24 ), a prolonged T max (from 2.3 to 3.3 h), and an elevated C max (1.2 vs. 0.8 mg/L) compared to bulk BRE. These findings demonstrate that drug–drug cocrystallization can simultaneously achieve dissolution synchronization and pharmacokinetic optimization, providing a viable strategy for the formulation of poorly bioavailable natural flavonoids without the use of polymeric excipients.

title: Yinicoelotes jiafu Zhang, Zhu & Wang, 2017 as a junior synonym of Yinicoelotes galeiformis Wang, Yin, Peng & Xie, 1990 (Araneae, Agelendiae): evidence from DNA barcoding and sex association
summary: The male of Coelotes galeiformis Wang, Yin, Peng & Xie, 1990 was recently described for the first time. This species was subsequently transferred to the newly established genus Yinicoelotes Wang, Irfan, Shi & Zhang, 2026, together with Drac
content: The male of Coelotes galeiformis Wang, Yin, Peng & Xie, 1990 was recently described for the first time. This species was subsequently transferred to the newly established genus Yinicoelotes Wang, Irfan, Shi & Zhang, 2026, together with Draconarius jiafu Zhang, Zhu & Wang, 2017, which was previously known only from the male. Yinicoelotes jiafu (Zhang, Zhu & Wang, 2017) is proposed as a junior synonym of Yinicoelotes galeiformis (Wang, Yin, Peng & Xie, 1990) based on the correction of their sex association, while the male previously assigned to Y. galeiformis presents an unnamed species. Photos, diagnoses, and detailed descriptions are provided.

title: Fiber diameter measurement for electrospun fibrous mats using scanning electron microscopic images: a protocol toward standardized characterization
summary: Fiber diameter is a key characteristic of electrospun fibrous mats. This study aims to take a step forward in developing a protocol for standardized measurement of fiber diameter using scanning electron microscope (SEM) images. Manual and A
content: Fiber diameter is a key characteristic of electrospun fibrous mats. This study aims to take a step forward in developing a protocol for standardized measurement of fiber diameter using scanning electron microscope (SEM) images. Manual and Automatic measurement (AM) methods (General Image Fiber Tool: GIFT) are applied to SEM images at magnifications of 2 kx and 4 kx. Results suggest that measurement on a synthetic image composed of fibers with constant diameter in the range studied be reported as a reference for minimum measurement variability. Fiber Based Method (FBM) which considers one contribution from each fiber in a SEM image is introduced. It was found that the average, minimum and maximum fiber diameter could be different from results obtained by Conventional Method (CM) which considers all measurements on a SEM image. FBM is suggested to be a better representative of individual visible fibers and reduce the bias associated with unequal numbers of local measurements per fiber. In addition, bin size for fiber diameter histograms is suggested to be set between the pixel size of the image for AM or the average measurement variability for manual methods, and 20% of the span of fiber diameters. Furthermore, “Fiber Index” as a criterion for evaluation and reporting of fiber diameter along with average and standard deviation is introduced.

title: Tintinnids and other microzooplankton along a transect through the Greenland Sea Gyre
summary: The present study investigates microzooplankton (MZP) species richness, vertical abundance, and organism dimensions along a transect through the Greenland Sea Gyre from 2 to 10 September 2021, at the end of the productive season. Total MZP
content: The present study investigates microzooplankton (MZP) species richness, vertical abundance, and organism dimensions along a transect through the Greenland Sea Gyre from 2 to 10 September 2021, at the end of the productive season. Total MZP abundance varied from 6.25 ind. L − 1 to 721.5 ind. L − 1 , and total carbon content from 0.01 µgC L⁻¹ to 1.7 µgC L⁻¹. Microzooplankton abundance and biomass decreased drastically in the presence of cold polar water on the Greenland slope. Vertical distribution profiles showed significantly higher organism abundance in the photic zone ( ≤ 100 m) compared to the aphotic zone (> 100 m) across the entire transect. Tintinnids, with a maximum of 613 ind. L − 1 , dominated the MZP assemblage; among them, Acanthostomella norvegica , Parafavella denticulata , Parafavella parumdentata , and Ptychocylis obtusa were the most common species. Tintinnids appeared to play a major role in the photic zone and exhibited small dimensions, with an oral lorica opening between 15 and 35 μm in 84% of the individuals. Consequently, at the end of the productive season, the amount of carbon transferred to higher trophic levels in the Greenland Sea may be constrained by the small size of the organisms, with potential effects on upper trophic levels that critically depend on efficient energy transfer. Due to ongoing changes in the Arctic, there is an urgent imperative for a better characterization and understanding of food web structures, which are key elements of the Arctic pelagic ecosystem.

title: Hydrophilic modification of superhydrophobic coatings induced by surface dielectric barrier discharge plasma
summary: Abstract The combination of surface dielectric barrier discharge (surface-DBD) plasma and a superhydrophobic coating has been proposed as an effective approach for enhancing the anti-icing capability of wind turbine blades. However, direct
content: Abstract The combination of surface dielectric barrier discharge (surface-DBD) plasma and a superhydrophobic coating has been proposed as an effective approach for enhancing the anti-icing capability of wind turbine blades. However, direct plasma exposure may alter the chemical composition and morphology of the coating, potentially reducing its hydrophobicity and could thereby undermine the synergistic effect. This work investigates three typical superhydrophobic coatings, examining how surface wettability, chemistry and morphology evolve after surface-DBD treatment and how they age. The results demonstrate that surface-DBD plasma rapidly switches the coating surface from superhydrophobic to highly hydrophilic within 60 s, with the water contact angle of all three coatings decreasing from ~ 160° to ~ 20°. XPS analysis reveals that defluorination is the dominant chemical mechanism of this modification, accompanied by oxidation and exposure of the underlying hydrophilic inorganic skeleton; this is evidenced by a significant decrease in fluorine content and reduced intensities of fluorinated carbon peaks. Morphology analysis shows that physical etching of the micron-scale rough structure is limited; nevertheless, the rough structure provides a larger effective reaction area, which may facilitate the chemical modification. Aging tests indicate that the water contact angle partially recovers to approximately 70°–78° after 10 days, but the original superhydrophobicity is not restored, indicating irreversible chemical damage. This study elucidates the hydrophilic modification mechanism and aging effect of superhydrophobic coatings induced by surface-DBD plasma. These findings suggest that the negative impact of plasma on the intrinsic properties of the coating should be considered in their combined application.

title: Extraction of Calcium from Steel Slag via Low-Temperature Chlorination Roasting and Water Leaching for the Preparation of CaCO3
summary: Abstract This paper proposes a novel coupled process of “low-temperature chlorination roasting with NH4Cl─water leaching for calcium separation─carbonation precipitation” to achieve selective recovery and utilization of calcium from steel s
content: Abstract This paper proposes a novel coupled process of “low-temperature chlorination roasting with NH4Cl─water leaching for calcium separation─carbonation precipitation” to achieve selective recovery and utilization of calcium from steel slag. Thermodynamic calculations indicate the presence of two reaction pathways in the system: solid–solid chlorination and gas–solid chlorination mediated by HCl. Among these, the gas-phase chlorination reaction exhibits a stronger thermodynamic spontaneity. Phase analysis of the raw steel slag shows that calcium is primarily found in the phases of Ca2SiO4, Ca2Fe2O5, and Al14Ca12O33, with a positive correlation to the contents of silicon, iron, and aluminum. The roasting temperature and holding time have been identified as the core factors affecting the calcium chlorination rate. Under optimal conditions (temperature of 300 °C, holding time of 40 min, mass ratio of NH4Cl to steel slag of 2:1, and steel slag particle size of 75–106 μm), the calcium chlorination rate can reach 92.47%. Kinetic analysis based on the unreacted core shrinking model confirms that this chlorination process is controlled by the diffusion of the solid product layer. The resulting calcium-containing leachate, after carbonation precipitation, yields well-formed, uniformly shaped rhombohedral calcite particles.

title: Physics-aware calibration neural network for automated TCAD-to-experiment modeling of carbon nanotube field-effect transistors
summary: Abstract Low-dimensional semiconductor devices, including carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNT-FETs), require efficient calibration methods to reconcile numerical simulations with experimentally measured electrical characteristics.
content: Abstract Low-dimensional semiconductor devices, including carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNT-FETs), require efficient calibration methods to reconcile numerical simulations with experimentally measured electrical characteristics. Conventional manual calibration is time-consuming, while purely data-driven surrogate models may provide limited physical interpretability and reduced reliability when applied to device geometries outside the training domain. In this work, we propose a physics-aware calibration neural network (PACNN) for supervised technology computer-aided design (TCAD)-to-experiment calibration of CNT-FET transfer and output characteristics. PACNN uses current–voltage curves generated by a two-dimensional intrinsic silicon TCAD model as a stable numerical reference. The architecture combines an anchor-preserving physical-affine module, which accounts for global variations in voltage alignment, current amplitude, slope, and extracted electrical parameters, with family-specific bounded residual modules that correct the remaining local discrepancies. Transfer characteristics are processed in the signed logarithmic current domain, whereas output characteristics are calibrated in the normalized linear current domain using separate amplitude and low-rank shape corrections. Model training incorporates curve-fitting, curve-level R 2 , slope consistency, device parameter, residual, and regularization objectives. Channel-length generalization was evaluated through out-of-distribution (OOD) extrapolation to $${L}_\mathrm{ch}$$ L ch = 4.5 μm and 5.0 μm. PACNN achieved macro-averaged curve-wise R 2 values of 0.947 4 and 0.876 0 for the transfer and output characteristics, respectively, with corresponding pooled pointwise R 2 values of 0.962 7 and 0.996 2. The predicted curves also preserved key electrical parameters, yielding a balanced physical consistency index of 0.918 3. These results indicate that PACNN provides an accurate and physically constrained framework for automated TCAD-to-experiment calibration of CNT-FET characteristics.

title: TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibrils increase tensile strength by 80% and enhance barrier and biodegradation performance in PLA/PBAT nanocomposites: a systematic meta-analysis
summary: Background Biodegradable poly (lactic acid)/poly (butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PLA/PBAT) blends suffer from poor interfacial adhesion and suboptimal mechanical performance, limiting their use in sustainable packaging. Methods A PRISM
content: Background Biodegradable poly (lactic acid)/poly (butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PLA/PBAT) blends suffer from poor interfacial adhesion and suboptimal mechanical performance, limiting their use in sustainable packaging. Methods A PRISMA-compliant systematic meta-analysis of 34 peer-reviewed publications (2018–2025) was conducted. Inclusion criteria required studies reporting tensile, thermal, or barrier data on PLA/PBAT blends with nanocellulose ≥2 wt%. Heterogeneity was assessed using Cochran’s Q and I 2 statistics; sensitivity analysis confirmed robustness. Data were normalized to a 70/30 PLA/PBAT reference composition using a validated linear mixing-rule protocol (R 2 = 0.91), acknowledging that this approach may introduce systematic bias for properties exhibiting nonlinear composition dependence, particularly barrier properties. Results Surface-modified TEMPO-oxidized CNFs at 5 wt% achieved the most significant improvements: tensile strength increased 80% (28.4 → 51.2 MPa), Young’s modulus increased 158% (1.2 → 3.1 GPa), thermal degradation onset temperature improved by 35 °C (295 → 330 °C), and water vapor permeability decreased 57% (15.2 → 6.5 g mm/m 2 ·day at 100 μm reference thickness). Crystallinity increased from 32% to 55%, and activation energy for thermal degradation rose from 155.8 to 205.3 kJ/mol. Nanocellulose incorporation accelerated biodegradation under industrial composting conditions (ISO 14855-1, 58 °C, 60%–65% RH), reducing half-life from 12.0 to 7.9 weeks and increasing degradation (weight loss) to 86% at 12 weeks (CO 2 -based mineralization efficiency: 81%). The tortuosity factor increased from 1.2 to 2.4, consistent with Nielsen’s tortuous path model. Conclusion Surface-modified nanocellulose enables high-performance, fully biodegradable composites suitable for sustainable packaging, with biodegradation rates meeting the ISO 14855-1 threshold of EN 13432. Full certification additionally requires disintegration and ecotoxicity data not available in the present meta-analysis corpus. Performance is comparable to, or exceeds, that of synthetic nanoreinforcements (CNTs, organoclays) in independent studies—though direct comparison under identical conditions would be needed to establish definitive superiority—while offering full biodegradability.

title: Strain-Rate Dependence of Mode II Delamination Initiation in a Polyester-Fiberglass Composite Using Dynamic ENF Testing
summary: Abstract The inter-laminar crack growth resistance in fiber-reinforced composites under Mode II (shear) loading is a critical factor for structural integrity in dynamic environments. Traditional End Notched Flexural (ENF) tests have been ex
content: Abstract The inter-laminar crack growth resistance in fiber-reinforced composites under Mode II (shear) loading is a critical factor for structural integrity in dynamic environments. Traditional End Notched Flexural (ENF) tests have been extensively used under static conditions, yet limited studies exist on high strain rate effects using dynamic setups. The objective of this study is to investigate the influence of varying strain rates on the Mode II strain energy release rate G IIi at damage initiation for polyester-fiberglass composites using a dynamic loading approach. ENF specimens composed of ± 45° glass fiber mats and polyester resin were subjected to three-point bending under different strain rates ranging from 70 s⁻¹ to 150 s⁻¹ using a Split Hopkinson Pressure Bar (SHPB) system. High-speed imaging was employed to capture damage progression, and Mode II SERR was computed using beam theory formulations based on force and displacement data. The results demonstrate a clear trend of increasing G IIi with elevated strain rates, rising from 0.64 to 7.19 kJ/m². The average increase in dynamic crack propagation energy was observed to exceed values from static testing. However, observed failure modes included fiber bridging and non-planar crack paths, contributing to variability in measured results. The dynamic ENF testing shows that Mode II fracture energy in polyester-fiberglass composites is strongly strain rate dependent. The results suggest the need for longer specimen geometries to ensure stable inter-laminar propagation in future investigations.

title: Evaluation of surrogate biomarkers of memory and cognition in aging adults with vitamin B12 deficiency: A cross-sectional study.
summary: Background: Vitamin B12 (Vit B12) is a cofactor in one-carbon metabolism, methylation reactions, myelin synthesis, and neuronal function. Its deficiency can lead to neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. This study aims to evaluate cognit
content: Background: Vitamin B12 (Vit B12) is a cofactor in one-carbon metabolism, methylation reactions, myelin synthesis, and neuronal function. Its deficiency can lead to neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. This study aims to evaluate cognitive and memory-related biomarkers in otherwise healthy aging adults with vitamin B12 deficiency and to explore whether it is an under recognized contributor to dementia. Methods: Serum levels of Aβ42, acetylcholinesterase (AChE), brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), GSH, and calcium were estimated in ninety healthy individuals, aged between 45 to 65 years. They were divided into 3 groups of 30 participants each, as vit B12 sufficient (>300 pg/ml), insufficient (201-300 pg/ml) and deficient (≤200pg/ml) groups. Serum BDNF and Aβ42 were estimated by sandwich ELISA. Calcium, GSH and AChE were measured spectrophotometrically. Results: Aβ42 levels showed a significant increase in both insufficient and deficient groups relative to the sufficient group (p<0.001) There was an apparent decrease in BDNF levels and a significant decline in AChE levels in the deficient group compared to the sufficient group (p=0.029). There was a more pronounced decrease in GSH in the deficient group (p<0.001) compared to the sufficient group. Notably, serum calcium levels demonstrated a significant increase in the insufficient group followed by normalization in the deficient group. Conclusion: Overall, the findings indicate that Vit B12 deficiency is associated with significant alterations in cognitive biomarkers and oxidative stress causing neuronal loss, which may contribute to memory deficits and cognitive decline. Therefore, vitamin B12 deficiency may be a significant, modifiable risk factor for dementia.

title: Cropland and population exposure to extreme precipitation events in Central Asia under future climate change
summary: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming and an intensifying hydrological cycle, with important implications for extreme precipitation events (EPEs). However, future changes in cropland and population exposure to EPEs remain insuffic
content: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming and an intensifying hydrological cycle, with important implications for extreme precipitation events (EPEs). However, future changes in cropland and population exposure to EPEs remain insufficiently quantified in this climate-sensitive dryland region. Here, we projected changes in EPE characteristics and associated cropland and population exposure across CA using daily precipitation simulations from five bias-adjusted ISIMIP3b global climate models under SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5. The historical period 1995–2014 was used as the reference, and future changes were assessed for 2021–2040, 2041–2060, 2061–2080, and 2081–2100. The results show increasing extreme precipitation amount, frequency, intensity, and spatial extent toward the end of the century, particularly under SSP5-8.5 and in high-mountain regions. Under SSP5-8.5, cropland exposure increases by 46.4% from 2021 to 2040 to 2081–2100, with cumulative exposure of approximately 190.7 ± 73.7 million km 2 -days during 2021–2100. Under SSP3-7.0, population exposure increases by 97.2% between the first and last future periods, with cumulative exposure reaching approximately 47.12 ± 18.8 billion person-days during 2021–2100. Exposure hotspots are mainly located in northern Kazakhstan and the tri-border region of Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. Signed decomposition shows that climatic changes dominate most increases in cropland exposure, particularly under SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5, whereas the drivers of population exposure vary strongly among socioeconomic pathways, with demographic changes either reinforcing or offsetting climate-driven exposure changes. These findings highlight increasing exposure of Central Asian populations and croplands to future extreme precipitation and suggest the importance of strengthened flood management, agricultural drainage, early-warning systems, and climate-resilient land-use planning.

title: Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis
summary: Summary When subject to damage or stress, cells develop responses in order to maintain tissue homeostasis. Two such decisions are ferroptosis and cellular senescence, but how cells decide between these outcomes remains unclear. Here we show
content: Summary When subject to damage or stress, cells develop responses in order to maintain tissue homeostasis. Two such decisions are ferroptosis and cellular senescence, but how cells decide between these outcomes remains unclear. Here we show that senescent cells increase levels of multiple membrane-bound polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), but a specific PUFA, dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA, 20:3 ω -3) is reduced. Exogenous repletion of DGLA or inhibition of delta-5-desaturase, the enzyme that metabolizes DGLA, instead results in cell death by ferroptosis. Senescent cells had elevated levels of other fezzroptosis sensitizers, including labile iron and expression of lipoxygenases – but also increased Gpx4 levels to prevent ferroptosis. Oral DGLA lowered senescent cell burden in aged mice and improved age-related functional outcomes. Finally, obese humans with lowered DGLA desaturation rates showed lower markers of adipose tissue senescence. Together, our data implicate DGLA and its desaturation as a major driver of decisions between senescence and ferroptosis.

title: Dynamic ventilation control modes for elevators: towards healthy built environment
summary: Aerosol transmission of viruses poses a significant threat to public health and socio-economic stability. Elevators, as typical frequently-used enclosed spaces in modern building transportation systems, pose growing aerosol transmission ris
content: Aerosol transmission of viruses poses a significant threat to public health and socio-economic stability. Elevators, as typical frequently-used enclosed spaces in modern building transportation systems, pose growing aerosol transmission risks. However, previous studies have not adequately optimized elevator ventilation control for intermittent door operations and with fluctuating occupancy patterns. The study emphasizes intelligent control strategies of mechanical ventilation hybrid with natural ventilation utilizing elevator door opening dynamics. It thoroughly examines factors influencing the spread of respiratory infectious diseases and proposes effective solutions. A validated Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) model is employed to analyze the spatial-temporal distribution of virus-laden aerosols in elevator cabins. Simulation results demonstrate that elevated ventilation rates may paradoxically increase aerosol dispersion due to enhanced turbulent diffusion, while insufficient ventilation prolongs aerosol residence and exposure time. Specifically, at an airspeed of 0.2 m/s, aerosol particles accumulate significantly, increasing infection risk; whereas at 2.5 m/s, particles are rapidly expelled but dispersed more widely. The study proposes an intelligent variable-speed ventilation strategy ​​based on real-time CO2 concentration levels. Compared to conventional ventilation systems​​, the proposed adaptive system combining optimized ventilation rates with door-opening operations​​ demonstrates a 43.5% improvement in aerosol dilution efficiency ​​while reducing both infection risks and energy consumption​​.The findings provide valuable insights and practical solutions for the intelligent control and optimization of elevator ventilation systems in modern urban environments.

title: Carbon Processing Domains: Seasonal and Spatial Controls on Dissolved Organic Carbon in a Montane River
summary: Abstract Lotic biogeochemical structure and function have been studied extensively, but rivers lack a functional classification system for assessing spatiotemporal variability in solute behavior. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a basal re
content: Abstract Lotic biogeochemical structure and function have been studied extensively, but rivers lack a functional classification system for assessing spatiotemporal variability in solute behavior. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) is a basal resource for aquatic communities, is chemically complex, and has aquatic and terrestrial sources and sinks. DOC is a large carbon reservoir and quantifying its transport and processing contributes to understanding riverine and global carbon dynamics. Introduction of the Nutrient Processing Domain concept provides a framework for comparing spatiotemporal variation in the relative importance of nutrient sources and sinks along rivers. Here, we extended this approach for DOC by defining carbon processing domains (CPDs) using a reach‐scale mass balance based on upstream and downstream DOC concentrations, discharges, and reach areas. We applied the CPD framework along 216 km of a snowmelt‐dominated montane river in the northern Rocky Mountains, USA, using a 3‐year record comprising 656 DOC measurements. CPD classifications revealed distinct baseflow and snowmelt behavior as river segments transitioned among diluter, enhancer, conduit, compiler, and consumer domains. Breakpoint regressions yielded inferred allochthonous DOC (C tg ) estimates of 259 ± 56 μmol L −1 at low flow and 643 ± 128 μmol L −1 at high flow. A mixed‐effects comparison supported a change in slope near the 0.42 m d −1 operational breakpoint but not an abrupt intercept discontinuity; regime‐specific inferred biological DOC consumption ( F bio ) values are therefore interpreted as descriptive extrapolated intercepts rather than evidence of an instantaneous biological shift. Together, these results show how DOC transport and processing vary systematically with hydrologic regime.

title: Rethinking digital twins in transportation: From virtual model to Human-in-the-Loop control
summary: Digital twins have emerged as a transformative concept in many fields, traffic management including. Yet their definition and practical applications remain ambiguous. This paper seeks to clarify what constitutes a true digital twin, disting
content: Digital twins have emerged as a transformative concept in many fields, traffic management including. Yet their definition and practical applications remain ambiguous. This paper seeks to clarify what constitutes a true digital twin, distinguishing it from traditional traffic simulation models, and explores scenarios where digital twins offer unique advantages. Drawing on global best practices and state-of-the-art research, we identify key challenges and provide actionable insights into their resolution. A pivotal contribution of this study is the introduction of the Digital Twin Evropská (DTE), a real-world case study focused on a critical urban corridor in Prague. We detail the motivation for its development, the methodologies employed, including real-time path-flow estimation, continuous simulation calibration, and integrated data-assimilation workflows, and the resulting insights. Under the taxonomy proposed in this paper, the currently implemented DTE is classified as a Digital Shadow with predictive capabilities, while the Human-in-the-Loop decision-support architecture represents the proposed pathway towards a fully operational Digital Twin. The findings demonstrate the practical utility of continuously synchronized digital representations for urban traffic management and provide a basis for their further development towards operational Digital Twins. The paper concludes with recommendations for leveraging DTE in operational contexts and outlines potential next steps for advancing the digital twin paradigm.

title: Groundwater quality dynamics and hydrochemical indicators of water insecurity in the semi-arid Sokoto Basin, Northwestern Nigeria
summary: Abstract Groundwater is the surest water source in semi-arid regions, where surface water is seasonal and subject to climatic fluctuations. Growing climatic stress, along with anthropogenic pressures, in the Sokoto Basin of northwestern Nig
content: Abstract Groundwater is the surest water source in semi-arid regions, where surface water is seasonal and subject to climatic fluctuations. Growing climatic stress, along with anthropogenic pressures, in the Sokoto Basin of northwestern Nigeria poses a threat to groundwater quality and the region's water security. This paper has explored groundwater hydrochemistry and identified significant hydrochemical predictors of water insecurity across different geological environments in the Western Sokoto Basin. Fifty-four groundwater samples were collected from hand-dug wells and boreholes in the basement complex and sedimentary formations. The analysis of physicochemical and heavy-metal parameters was performed according to the standard APHA (2017) methods, and multivariate (PCA, HCA, correlation) and geostatistical (Ordinary Kriging, variogram modelling) analyses were used to demonstrate spatial patterns, controlling factors, and predictive accuracy. Findings indicate that groundwater quality differs considerably with lithology: basement complex aquifers are more mineralised and enriched in metals (Mn, Cr, Al, Zn, As) than sedimentary rocks, mainly due to extended water-rock interactions, weathering, and climatic concentration processes. Spatial interpolation revealed unique hot spots of contamination, especially in low-lying and high-evaporation areas, suggesting a magnifying effect of climate stress on solute buildup. High predictability (R 2 > 0.9 in most metals) of kriging models and uncertainty zones (as revealed by nRMSE mapping) was observed in areas of hydrochemical instability. Theoretically, the research will enhance geostatistical understanding of groundwater dynamics in data-limited, climate-sensitive basins by integrating climatic, geological, and geochemical factors into a single explanatory model. In practice, the results deliver early-warning hydrochemical indicators to track groundwater insecurity and can be used to enable evidence-based interventions to meet Sustainable Development Goal 6. The research suggests that semi-arid West African areas should sustain groundwater use through continuous spatial surveillance and adaptive management to enable safe, climate-resilient groundwater use.

title: Carbon Capture Potential of Recycled Concrete Aggregates from a Full-Scale Recycling Plant in the Brazilian Federal District: A Laboratory Carbonation Study
summary: Accelerated carbonation of recycled concrete aggregates (RCA) can fix CO₂ while modifying aggregate properties, but most reported uptake values come from laboratory-produced aggregates that do not reproduce the heterogeneity of material lea
content: Accelerated carbonation of recycled concrete aggregates (RCA) can fix CO₂ while modifying aggregate properties, but most reported uptake values come from laboratory-produced aggregates that do not reproduce the heterogeneity of material leaving a real recycling line. This study assesses the carbon uptake of recycled sand and two coarse RCA fractions from a single industrial recycling plant in the Federal District, Brazil, sampled in two production campaigns. Carbonation was performed at 25°C, 60% relative humidity and 3% CO₂. Uptake was quantified by the net mass gain of crushed 1.18–2.36 mm specimens kept in moisture equilibrium with the test environment, and corroborated by thermogravimetric analysis (TG). Net mass gains ranged from 0.318% to 1.358%, and specimens derived from the coarse fractions exceeded those derived from the sand (0.318–0.638%). X-ray diffraction of the non-carbonated material showed a weak calcite reflection and no detectable dolomite peaks, indicating carbonate already present in the adhered paste rather than carbonate rock. TG mass loss in the 550–950°C range increased after treatment in all six samples, evidencing CaCO₃ formation in the adhered paste. Water absorption decreased by 0.08–0.41 percentage points and oven-dry density increased by 0.016–0.023 g/cm³ in single paired determinations, consistent with pore filling by carbonate. Accelerated carbonation therefore fixes CO₂ in industrially produced recycled aggregates, and confirmation at industrial scale requires multi-plant sampling, replicated testing and a process-level carbon balance.

title: Upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate sourced from waste plastic bottles into graphene oxide and its evaluation for CO2 absorption
summary: Abstract The human-made “plastic” resource has turned into an environmental concern for years now. The ideal solution to the problem is still under research. Our research aims to deplete the huge amount of plastic waste on Earth by converti
content: Abstract The human-made “plastic” resource has turned into an environmental concern for years now. The ideal solution to the problem is still under research. Our research aims to deplete the huge amount of plastic waste on Earth by converting it into a functional material. The carbon chain of this polymer cannot be broken; however, it can be altered into a different category. Plastic waste, specifically PET, was chosen for the experiment and was converted finally into graphene oxide. Catalytic graphitization was used to convert one carbon form into another. The obtained graphene oxide was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, energy dispersive spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy. The FT-IR and EDS results confirm the synthesis of graphene oxide. The thermal stability and magnetic behavior of graphene oxide are satisfactory. Catalytic behavior toward CO 2 adsorption is a potent application of PETGO. The desorption curve indicates CO2 adsorption on the surface through chemisorption. A high amount of desorbed CO2 indicates a high reaction surface area and electronic interaction.

title: Tribological Properties and Mechanisms of PTFE Matrix Composites Under Wide‐Temperature‐Range and Long‐Term Friction Conditions
summary: ABSTRACT To address the challenges of using polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in practical applications, it is crucial to develop PTFE matrix composites with enhanced wear resistance and prolonged service life. In this study, the effects of fi
content: ABSTRACT To address the challenges of using polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in practical applications, it is crucial to develop PTFE matrix composites with enhanced wear resistance and prolonged service life. In this study, the effects of filler materials and testing temperatures on the tribological behavior of PTFE composites were systematically investigated, and the performance under prolonged friction (0.5–15 h) at 0.33 and 0.66 m/s was thoroughly evaluated. Results indicate that the PTFE/Kevlar fibers (KF)/Polyimide (PI) composite exhibited a low coefficient of friction (COF) of only 0.09 at 250°C, with a wear rate ranging from 0.65 × 10 −5 to 1.8 × 10 −5 mm 3 /Nm. During the extended tests (1–15 h), the composite maintained a low wear rate at both 0.33 m/s (0.89–7.67 × 10 −6 mm 3 /Nm) and 0.66 m/s (1.43–7.43 × 10 −6 mm 3 /Nm). Examination of the worn surfaces reveals that the wear mechanism transfer from abrasive wear to fatigue wear with the increasing of testing temperature and sliding speed/time.

title: Pendant drop rotation in vertical, turbulent, shearing flows
summary: Abstract In natural and engineering applications, mobile drops frequently encounter nonuniform flows, and such interactions are both uncharacterized and diffcult to experimentally observe. In this study, we record the dynamics of pendant dr
content: Abstract In natural and engineering applications, mobile drops frequently encounter nonuniform flows, and such interactions are both uncharacterized and diffcult to experimentally observe. In this study, we record the dynamics of pendant drops, a natural and ubiquitous drop state, subject to the non-uniform disturbances of aerodynamic turbulence and shear. Our turbulent, shearing flow is formed by a pseudo-coaxial jet. By protruding a co-flowing jet through the center of a vertical, suction-type vertical wind tunnel, we create a novel flow field termed sheathed, coaxial jet-flow (SCJF). Tuning the jet (core) and tunnel (sheath) velocities allows us to create turbulent, shearing flow fields that arise from the interactions at the flow interface. We employ an Eulerian-based finite-volume CFD solver within Star-CCM to characterize our novel flow and understand the drop dynamics therein. Subject to turbulent, shearing flows, pendant drops may rotate. The onset of drop rotation is influenced by turbulence below a threshold Reynolds number defined by the needle diameter. We find that pendant drop dynamics in SCJF are influenced by the size of the capillary support, the velocity ratio between the core and sheath, the drop size, and the magnitudes of turbulence intensity and shear imposed on the drop. We find that pendant drops exhibit limited modal behavior compared to that observed for laminar conditions and that small drops rotate faster than large drops. We form a scaling argument based upon the energetics of a rotating drop to reveal that dimensionless drop rotation, given by a modified Strouhal number, scales with an inverse drop Reynolds number. By comparing our results to the findings of our previous work in laminar flows, we discover that turbulence does not notably influence dimensionless drop rotation.

title: Alkali-activated cementitious materials for multifunctional structural capacitors: Multi-scale architectures, structure–property relationships and engineering applications
summary: Smart infrastructure requires materials that simultaneously provide mechanical load-bearing capacity and active energy management functions. This article systematically analyzes alkali-activated cementitious materials as matrices for multif
content: Smart infrastructure requires materials that simultaneously provide mechanical load-bearing capacity and active energy management functions. This article systematically analyzes alkali-activated cementitious materials as matrices for multifunctional structural capacitors, integrating strain sensing, Joule heating, electromagnetic shielding and absorption, and thermoelectric energy harvesting with in-situ storage. The review classifies existing concepts into four archetypes and elucidates the roles of three-dimensional conductive networks, hierarchical pores and interfaces, and ion-electron co-conduction across multiple scales. Design guidelines linking precursor chemistry, filler systems, and multi-scale architectures to specific functional targets are proposed, and cross-cutting structure-property relationships are synthesized. Key challenges including long-term multi-field durability, multifunctional interference, scale-up, and standardization are discussed. This work provides a framework for developing low-carbon, high-performance structural capacitors from industrial by-products.

title: Unravelling instrumental challenges in heating power measurements for magnetic hyperthermia
summary: Heating powers of magnetic nanoparticles for magnetic hyperthermia are typically measured by non-adiabatic AC calorimetry. This technique is, however, reported to have a standard deviation in the intrinsic loss power (ILP) of 30–40% by the
content: Heating powers of magnetic nanoparticles for magnetic hyperthermia are typically measured by non-adiabatic AC calorimetry. This technique is, however, reported to have a standard deviation in the intrinsic loss power (ILP) of 30–40% by the RADIOMAG EU COST Action TD1402 round-robin study involving 21 European laboratories. In the present study, we re-examine the RADIOMAG dataset and reveal four common sources of error: i) Insufficient temperature resolution, ii) AC-field sensitive thermometers, iii) Non-physical temperature oscillations, and iv) Apparent non-linear heat losses. In total, 16 of the 21 laboratories were observed to suffer from one or more of these four measurement issues. Based on these findings, we propose minimum criteria for sufficient measurement quality and apply them to re-estimate the ILP values only for datasets with sufficient quality. Given these criteria, we demonstrate that addressing instrumentation and analysis issues can decrease the inter-laboratory ILP deviation to 17–30%, corresponding to reductions in errors of around 30% compared to previous reporting. Based on our analysis, we introduce a diagnostic protocol for identifying and solving common instrumentation challenges proactively before the data acquisition phase. In future applications, the inter-laboratory ILP deviations are anticipated to be reduced further than the 17-30% observed in this work, given that the identified instrumentation issues are resolved and the corrected slope method can be properly implemented.

title: High-throughput quantification of multiple human milk oligosaccharides by ion mobility-mass spectrometry: From standard addition to single-point calibration
summary: Quantifying human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) in breast milk is challenging due to structural isomerism, matrix effects, and the lack of a true blank milk. Here, a multiplexed standard-addition strategy was proposed to quantify simultaneou
content: Quantifying human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) in breast milk is challenging due to structural isomerism, matrix effects, and the lack of a true blank milk. Here, a multiplexed standard-addition strategy was proposed to quantify simultaneously nine HMOs in breast milk using ion mobility-mass spectrometry with single ion mobility monitoring (SIM²)-stitching acquisition on a TIMS-Tof instrument. Although, both ordinary (OLS) and weighted (WLS) least squares regressions yielded comparable results in terms of precision and accuracy, the WLS method accounted for heteroscedastic response variance and reduced dependence on the calibration range for endogenous concentration estimates. This method enabled the HMO determination in breast milk samples ranging from 0.06 to 0.92 g L⁻¹. As a simplified alternative to multi-point calibration, the performance of a single-point standard addition strategy was evaluated. This provided HMO levels very similar to those determined by multipoint standard addition, demonstrating the potential of this simple quantification strategy for high-throughput applications.

title: Promoting amine-amine cooperative interactions to increase the catalytic activity of aminosilica materials for the nitroaldol reaction
summary: Cooperative interactions between immobilized amines and surface silanols have been proposed to enhance nitroaldol reactions with aminosilica catalysts. However, current methods to measure cooperative interactions between amines and surface
content: Cooperative interactions between immobilized amines and surface silanols have been proposed to enhance nitroaldol reactions with aminosilica catalysts. However, current methods to measure cooperative interactions between amines and surface silanols such as capping the surface silanols also alter surface polarity, site mobility, and proximity of adjacent amines. Accordingly, the relative contributions of amine-silanol and amine-amine interactions remain unclear and could be distinct from current understanding of aldol chemistry. Interestingly, we find that amines grafted at high surface density have the highest site time conversion, which is contrary to aldol chemistry. As high surface densities of amines would hinder cooperative amine-silanol interactions, these results are inconsistent with the previously hypothesized beneficial role of cooperative amine-silanol interactions. Since past studies have generally assumed positive contributions of surface silanols through observing a decline in activity when silanols are capped, we attempt to define the role of silanols and conclude that high surface density allows for amine-amine interactions that affect activity more strongly than any influence of amine-silanol interactions. Thus, our results support an imine formation mechanism that involves the simultaneous participation of two amines and propose that high activity is achievable even at the expense of amine-silanol interaction when amine-amine interactions are effectively promoted. These findings establish amine proximity as an important design parameter for primary aminosilica nitroaldol catalysts.

title: The scents of summer: plant-diversity and vegetation-height drive health-relevant scent exposure in urban greenspaces
summary: Abstract Urban green infrastructure is increasingly promoted as a public-health intervention, yet the biological features that determine exposure to potentially beneficial plant-derived volatile compounds remain poorly understood. Here we q
content: Abstract Urban green infrastructure is increasingly promoted as a public-health intervention, yet the biological features that determine exposure to potentially beneficial plant-derived volatile compounds remain poorly understood. Here we quantified airborne terpenes and terpenoids across five contrasting urban greenspaces in Oxford, UK, and related chemical profiles to plant diversity, vegetation structure and surrounding habitat characteristics. Ambient air samples collected across spring and summer were analysed by thermal-desorption gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, alongside field surveys of taxonomic richness, canopy cover, vegetation volume and ground composition. Terpene and terpenoid scentscapes differed strongly among sites and through time, with monoterpenes dominating detected profiles. Sites with greater plant richness and greater vegetation volume below 1.5 m consistently showed higher terpene/terpenoid abundance, whereas total vegetation volume, canopy cover and tree abundance were weaker and less consistent predictors. These relationships were specific to plant-associated chemical classes and were not observed for predominantly anthropogenic volatile compounds. These patterns were resolved across only five independent sampling sites, and the relationships reported here should therefore be considered exploratory. Our findings suggest that human exposure to plant-derived volatiles in cities may be maximised not simply by increasing tree cover, but by designing biodiverse, structurally complex lower-to-mid-storey vegetation within the breathing zone. These results provide an empirical basis for incorporating scentscape ecology into health-oriented urban greenspace design.

title: Macrofossil evidence of Late Holocene montane pine forests in the Sierra de Guadarrama National Park (Central System, Spain)
source: Archivo Digital UPM (Universidad Politécnica de Madrid)
summary: The macrofossil assemblage from Altos de La Morcuera, ca. 1700 m asl, constitutes one of the palaeobotanical finds with the largest number of wood remains in the Iberian Peninsula. Three neighbouring sites were sampled: Raso de los Toros, P
content: The macrofossil assemblage from Altos de La Morcuera, ca. 1700 m asl, constitutes one of the palaeobotanical finds with the largest number of wood remains in the Iberian Peninsula. Three neighbouring sites were sampled: Raso de los Toros, Pena ~ Morcuera, and Los Tres Mojones, where samples of 44 trunks of different sizes and stumps in living position were recovered and identified. Nineteen samples were radiocarbon-dated, which revealed an age range from 3960 to 2350 cal yr BP and indicated the existence of an extensive natural pine forest of Pinus gr. sylvestris in the area. Furthermore, another macroremain located in the southern slope (1350 m asl, 3200 cal yr BP) has likewise revealed the occurrence of this taxon at lower altitudes for this period. The wide altitudinal range made known by these results contributes to the discussion on the limits of montane pine forests in Iberia. In addition, dendrochronological studies were also conducted in nineteen sections from twelve macroremains, and composite chronologies were elaborated to infer palaeoecological information. Thus, for the first time, we provide conclusive evidence for the presence of pine forests in the Late Holocene in this part of the Guadarrama range at different altitudes, completing the palynological information and making further palaeobotanical data available for this period. All of which could be very useful for the management of the Sierra de Guadarrama National Park, highlighting the role of montane pine forests in the natural heritage of the area and enhancing the archive value of peatlands.

title: Frequency and Risk Factors of Cancer Therapy-Related Cardiac Dysfunction in Patients Receiving Chemotherapy: A Prospective Cohort Study at a Tertiary Centre.
summary: Background: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and l
content: Background: Cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD) is an increasingly recognised consequence of contemporary oncological treatment. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is insensitive to subclinical myocardial injury, and locally validated thresholds for global longitudinal strain (GLS) are lacking in Vietnamese patients. Objectives: To determine the frequency and risk factors of CTRCD in patients receiving chemotherapy, and to validate a localised GLS threshold and a biomarker-based surveillance strategy for early detection. Methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 235 patients at Cho Ray Hospital (September 2023-December 2025). Patients were assessed at baseline and every three months with two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography (GLS), high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). CTRCD was defined by international consensus criteria. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis; as the outcome was common, associations were quantified as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated by modified Poisson regression. Results: CTRCD occurred in 82 patients (34.9%). Incidence was highest with anthracyclines (41.2%) and HER2-targeted therapy (37.2%). A relative GLS reduction ≥12.1% predicted CTRCD with 73% sensitivity and 83% specificity. hs-TnT achieved a 100% negative predictive value (NPV), and combining GLS with hs-TnT in parallel retained a 100% NPV. Hypertension (RR 2.50, 95% CI 1.78-3.50), coronary artery disease (RR 2.47, 95% CI 1.82-3.35) and dyslipidaemia (RR 2.10, 95% CI 1.49-2.97) were associated with CTRCD. HFA-ICOS stratification was strongly predictive, with a stepwise increase in risk up to the very-high-risk category (RR 18.6, 95% CI 7.94-43.6 versus low risk; 100% event rate). Conclusions: CTRCD affected one-third of patients. A locally validated GLS threshold combined with hs-TnT enables early, resource-efficient detection, supporting a shift from reactive to proactive cardiac surveillance.

title: Are Mid-Level Health Providers Prepared for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy Screening? - A cross-sectional study from South India.
summary: Background: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy is a common yet often underdiagnosed complication of diabetes. This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, perception and practice of regarding Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy in the South Indian st
content: Background: Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy is a common yet often underdiagnosed complication of diabetes. This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, perception and practice of regarding Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy in the South Indian state of Karnataka. Methods: This cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 Community Health Officers (CHO) employed in Ayushman Arogya Mandirs of the district. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire that covered details of CHOs, training of DPN, knowledge, practice, and perceptions of DPN and its screening, as well as barriers encountered during screening of the condition. Results: Among the 260 participants, 77.3% and 22.6% were females and males. The mean age of the participants was 30.9 years. We found that 66.5% of the participants had moderate knowledge regarding DPN. The majority (76.1%) of participants did not have equipment to screen for neuropathy. Though all of them received training on NCD, 11.5% received training on DPN. Overall, 82% of the participants, of whom 23.5% strongly agreed and 58.5% agreed that they were confident in their ability to screen for DPN. Around 43.5% responded that they currently screen for DPN. Lack of screening equipment was one of the main barriers to the screening of DPN. Conclusion: The study showed a moderate level of knowledge regarding DPN. Nearly half of the participants never screened for DPN routinely, which is driven largely by insufficient in-service training and a critical shortage of screening equipment. Integrating structured DPN training into their education curriculum and ensuring the availability of equipment at the centres represent high-priority policy interventions to reduce the burden of preventable diabetic complications.

title: Thermal acclimation as an emergent property of economically optimal photosynthesis
summary: Summary Leaf‐level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis ( T opt ) increasing with growth temperature ( T growth ). We investigated how this behaviou
content: Summary Leaf‐level photosynthesis acclimates to growth conditions over days to weeks, with the instantaneous optimal temperature for photosynthesis ( T opt ) increasing with growth temperature ( T growth ). We investigated how this behaviour emerges in the P model, a primary production model based on eco‐evolutionary optimality hypotheses. We evaluated the P model estimates against experimental data for three herbaceous species grown at different temperatures and examined mechanisms underlying the responses of T opt and the photosynthetic rate at T opt ( A opt ). The model yields a realistic increase in T opt with T growth and a peaked relationship between A opt and T growth . These responses emerge largely from adjustment of the stomatal sensitivity parameter ξ, which determines the internal‐to‐ambient CO 2 ratio ( c i : c a ) and its sensitivity to vapour pressure deficit. Rubisco kinetics ( K ) does not acclimate in the model, but its temperature dependence enters acclimation through optimality, mainly via ξ, shifting T opt . The decline in A opt at high growth temperatures, often attributed to heat stress, reflects the narrowing gap between T opt and T growth because the T opt shift has a slope below one. The P model provides a mechanistic explanation for observed trends in T opt and A opt and a scalable approach for representing biochemical and stomatal acclimation in land‐surface models.

title: Secure forecasting-driven scheduling of hydrogen-integrated renewable power systems under cyberattacks
summary: Accurate demand and renewable-generation forecasts are essential for reliable operation of hydrogen-integrated power systems, where electrolyzers, liquid organic hydrogen carrier logistics, storage, and PEM fuel cells provide flexibility fo
content: Accurate demand and renewable-generation forecasts are essential for reliable operation of hydrogen-integrated power systems, where electrolyzers, liquid organic hydrogen carrier logistics, storage, and PEM fuel cells provide flexibility for renewable utilization. This paper develops a cyber-resilient forecasting-driven scheduling framework for coordinated power–hydrogen systems. Forecasting quality is first assessed using actual measurements, high-quality forecasts, and medium-quality forecasts; medium-quality forecasts increase total-cost deviations by up to 22.08%. A two-stage detection–recovery framework then protects demand, photovoltaic, and wind forecasting signals against denial-of-service and ramp-type false data injection attacks. Dedicated Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models detect corrupted inputs and reconstruct compromised measurements before coordinated scheduling. Demand-targeted attacks are the most disruptive, while wind- and PV-targeted attacks increase operating costs by up to 29.55% and 12.76%, respectively. After detection–recovery, operating-cost deviations fall below 6%. The framework improves hydrogen-enabled flexibility, renewable utilization, and operational resilience under cyber-compromised forecasting conditions.

title: Exploratory Data Analysis of Sustainability Performance Metrics in Automotive MSMEs
source: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a crucial role in the manufacturing sector of India, yet they are grappling with numerous obstacles when it comes to sustainability and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices.
content: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a crucial role in the manufacturing sector of India, yet they are grappling with numerous obstacles when it comes to sustainability and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices. In this study, the sustainability performance of 127 automotive components MSMEs of Pune, Chakan, Satara, Nashik, and Kolhapur has been evaluated. The goal is to identify Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that have an impact on the performance of an organization, including economic, environmental and social indicators. A mixed-method approach of structured questionnaires and interviews was used. To find patterns in sustainability and important KPIs, Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and clustering techniques were used. Results show that Customer Retention (CR), Resource Efficiency (RE), and Training & Development (TD) are the most significant factors impacting sustainability performance. Pune- and Chakan-based firms showed marginally better sustainability practices, and there were significant variations between different levels in the hierarchy of employees. The findings offer practical implications for MSMEs, policy makers, and industry stakeholders to reinforce the implementation of ESG, enhance the performance of the organizations, and help sustainable industrial development.

title: Why policy is not enough: Renewable energy adoption in India's commercial buildings
summary: Accelerating renewable energy adoption in commercial buildings is critical for achieving climate targets, yet implementation remains uneven in many emerging economies despite supportive policy reforms. This study examines how India's Energy
content: Accelerating renewable energy adoption in commercial buildings is critical for achieving climate targets, yet implementation remains uneven in many emerging economies despite supportive policy reforms. This study examines how India's Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 and associated renewable energy policies influence renewable energy adoption in the commercial building sector. Drawing on Habermas's theory of communicative action, the study develops the concept of regulated communicative action to explain how institutional conditions shape the translation of policy into organisational practice. A mixed-method qualitative design was employed, combining a survey of 101 commercial building stakeholders with four focus group discussions across six stakeholder categories. Data was analysed using the Gioia methodology, with findings interpreted through the interconnected domains of Lifeworld, Steering Media and Systems. Over half of respondents (52.5%) were unaware of the Green Energy Open Access policy, and 65.3% reported no explicit decarbonisation plan. Our results demonstrate that implementation gaps is associated not with isolated technological, financial or regulatory barriers, but with interactions among stakeholder awareness, governance fragmentation, organisational capability and infrastructure constraints. Contrary to much of the existing literature, cost-related barriers were prominent challenge theme and operated as institutionally mediated rather than independent constraints. The study advances sustainability transition research by providing a socio-institutional explanation of implementation gap and introducing regulated communicative action as a mechanism linking communication, regulation and organisational behaviour. The findings offer practical guidance for policymakers and industry, highlighting the importance of regulatory coherence, aligned incentives, capacity building and coordinated governance.

title: Are policy uncertainty indices converging across countries? Evidence from club convergence
summary: Growing concern surrounds the uncertainty arising from economic and energy policy changes across countries, and managing it remains vital for stability and sustainable development. We therefore analyse the convergence pattern of the energy-
content: Growing concern surrounds the uncertainty arising from economic and energy policy changes across countries, and managing it remains vital for stability and sustainable development. We therefore analyse the convergence pattern of the energy-related uncertainty index (EUI) and the economic policy uncertainty index (EPU) using several convergence approaches. Beta convergence reveals a catch-up effect, yet sigma convergence shows that dispersion across countries remains stagnant for both measures. We reject full-sample convergence for both indices, which motivates a club convergence approach. EUI forms two clubs, whereas EPU forms five clubs plus one non-converging group. Connectedness analysis indicates that these clubs are economically meaningful rather than purely statistical. Overall connectedness attains 90.55 per cent for EUI, and 87.49 per cent for EPU; pairwise connectedness is greater within clubs than between them, and the more strongly connected index is also the one that forms fewer clubs. Transitions toward long-run equilibrium are therefore heterogeneous, and uncertainty trends differ across countries in ways that call for differentiated management. Our results are robust to global shocks and provide a descriptive account of the long-term evolution of these uncertainties. Policy design should reflect these findings when seeking to control and manage uncertainty.

title: Mixed‐Scale Powder Enables 3D Printing of Tungsten Alloy
summary: ABSTRACT Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) offers a promising route for manufacturing tungsten alloy components with complex geometries, whereas W–Ni–Fe alloys remain the most widely used tungsten alloys because of their excellent overall perf
content: ABSTRACT Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) offers a promising route for manufacturing tungsten alloy components with complex geometries, whereas W–Ni–Fe alloys remain the most widely used tungsten alloys because of their excellent overall performance. Using nano‐sized Ni–Fe particles can further promote the densification and strengthening of LPBF‐fabricated W–Ni–Fe parts. However, nano‐enabled W–Ni–Fe powders face a critical trade‐off between reinforcing‐phase content and powder‐bed quality of LPBF: although a higher Ni–Fe content is generally beneficial for performance enhancement, excessive nanoparticles tend to deteriorate powder flowability and thereby impair powder‐bed uniformity during LPBF. Here, we propose a mixed‐scale nano/micron Ni–Fe/W powder design to overcome this dilemma and enable the fabrication of fine‐grained, high‐quality W–Ni–Fe parts by LPBF, thereby providing an alternative mixed‐scale strategy for reinforcing‐phase design. Compared with conventional mono‐scale nano Ni–Fe/W powder, the mixed‐scale powder promotes pronounced grain refinement, resulting in an average grain size of 4.90 μm. Meanwhile, it significantly improves both the forming quality and mechanical performance, achieving a surface roughness ( S a ) of 7.56 μm, a compressive strength of 2534.2 MPa, and a compressive strain of 34.1%. This work provides an engineering‐feasible powder design strategy and processing pathway for the LPBF fabrication of high‐performance tungsten alloys, and may also be extended to the additive manufacturing of other refractory metals that face a similar trade‐off between reinforcement content and powder flowability.

title: Trimethylolpropane trioleate–ethanolamine amphiphile-based emulsions with excellent Tribological performance for water-based lubrication
source: Chemical Engineering Journal Green and Sustainable
summary: To address the critical bottlenecks of high dosage, poor load-bearing capacity, and limited temperature adaptability in traditional water-based lubricants, herein, a series of phosphorus‑sulfur‑nitrogen (P-S-N) ternary amphiphilic additives
content: To address the critical bottlenecks of high dosage, poor load-bearing capacity, and limited temperature adaptability in traditional water-based lubricants, herein, a series of phosphorus‑sulfur‑nitrogen (P-S-N) ternary amphiphilic additives (PS-TMPTO-MEA, PS-TMPTO-DEA, PS-TMPTO-TEA) were synthesized via a three-step molecular modification strategy, which can form stable oil-in-water (O/W) emulsions for water-based lubrication. Structural characterizations by FT-IR, NMR, and TG confirm the successful preparation of target additives; among which PS-TMPTO-TEA exhibited superior thermal stability with an initial decomposition temperature up to 378.9 °C. At an ultralow dosage of 0.5 wt%, PS-TMPTO-TEA achieved excellent tribological performance, maintaining a stable friction coefficient of ~0.1 and a wear rate of 3.01 × 10 −9 mm 3 /N·m, corresponding to ~91% wear reduction compared with pure water, Although 1.5 wt% gives the minimum wear rate (1.76 × 10 −9 mm 3 /N·m), the optimal practical concentration of 0.5 wt% was selected for the comprehensive evaluations due to the balanced tribological performance and low-dosage advantage. It also demonstrated good load-bearing capacity over 50–300 N and stable performance at 30–50 °C. Compared with the commercial additive JP at the same dosage, PS-TMPTO-TEA showed a lower friction coefficient and less than half the wear rate, outperforming most reported water-based lubrication systems. The superior performance originated from a P-S-N synergistic film-forming effect, generating dense organic–inorganic composite tribochemical film at the friction interface to achieve effective friction reduction and anti-wear. This work offers a new route for the design of high-performance, low-dosage water-based lubricant additives with promising industrial application potential.

title: Prevalence and patterns of high hyperdiploidy in Pakistani Paediatric B-lymphoblastic leukaemia
source: Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
summary: Objective: To determine the prevalence and cytogenetic patterns of high hyperdiploidy in Pakistani children with B-lymphoblastic leukaemia. Method: The retrospective, descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted at the Cytogenetics Labo
content: Objective: To determine the prevalence and cytogenetic patterns of high hyperdiploidy in Pakistani children with B-lymphoblastic leukaemia.
