content: El presente estudio analiza el contraste entre la producción científica global y las ineficiencias operativas de la Cadena de Suministro de Hortalizas, Oleaginosas y Especias (CS-HOE) con el fin de evidenciar el vacío investigativo en las economías en desarrollo, en particular en la articulación entre modelos de gestión y las prácticas sostenibles agroindustriales.Se empleó un enfoque de dos fases complementario: un análisis bibliométrico global y un mapeo geoespacial orientado a identificar ineficiencias entre producción y pérdidas en America.Los resultados demuestran que la producción cientifica se concentra principalmente en paises industrializados con altos niveles de eficiencia operativa.En contraste, países de Centro y Sudamérica presentan pérdidas críticas (entre 10% y 26%) con una producción académica baja o nula, revelando una desconexión metodológica insostenible entre la ciencia y la urgencia operativa regional.La investigación se restringe a la base de datos Scopus (última década) y a los datos más recientes registrados sobre pérdidas en FAOSTAT (2023), sin discriminar entre pérdidas operativas evitables y mermas técnicas inevitables.

title: Toward physiologically relevant in vitro release testing of PLGA microspheres for subcutaneous administration
source: European Journal of Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
summary: Despite nearly 40 years of clinical use, PLGA microspheres (MS) still lack reliable in vitro methods to predict drug release, limiting rational development of new subcutaneous (SubQ) formulations or generics. This study investigated how com
content: Despite nearly 40 years of clinical use, PLGA microspheres (MS) still lack reliable in vitro methods to predict drug release, limiting rational development of new subcutaneous (SubQ) formulations or generics. This study investigated how components of the SubQ environment (e.g. proteins, glycosaminoglycans, and lipids) influence drug release from PLGA microspheres containing flurbiprofen or naltrexone. Four independent SubQ-relevant release media of increasing complexity were designed based on the reported SubQ tissue composition. Drug release was evaluated using the sample-and-separate method and, for the first time with PLGA microspheres, the SubCutaneous Injection Site SimulatOR (SCISSOR) containing different extracellular matrix cartridges. Medium composition affected release in a drug- and formulation-dependent manner. For flurbiprofen-loaded microspheres, differences were mainly confined to the initial burst, with limited effects on the overall release. Naltrexone release from the MS varied markedly among media and was faster and more extensive in albumin-containing media than in electrolyte- containing medium. With the SCISSOR method, flurbiprofen release from the PLGA microspheres was comparable between cartridges, reaching approximately 25% after 7 days, whereas naltrexone release from the microspheres remained below 5% after 4 days. These findings indicate that SubQ tissue components may influence PLGA microsphere performances supporting their inclusion in in vitro release methods.

title: Análise comparativa da composição química de diferentes biomassas residuais na formação de cinzas e incrustações em caldeiras industriais
summary: O presente trabalho teve como objetivo avaliar a influência da composição química das cinzas sobre as tendências de incrustação e aglomeração de diferentes biomassas destinadas à geração de energia. Foram analisadas dez amostras de biomassa
content: O presente trabalho teve como objetivo avaliar a influência da composição química das cinzas sobre as tendências de incrustação e aglomeração de diferentes biomassas destinadas à geração de energia. Foram analisadas dez amostras de biomassa, incluindo resíduos agroindustriais e florestais, a partir da determinação do teor de sílica e do cálculo de índices empíricos relacionados à razão entre componentes básicos e ácidos, à razão de sílica, ao potencial de incrustação e à tendência de aglomeração do leito. Os resultados demonstraram ampla variação entre as amostras avaliadas, com teores de sílica entre 2,30% e 91,87%, sendo o maior valor observado para a casca de cacau e o menor para o caroço de pequi. A casca de café apresentou o maior valor de potencial de incrustação, enquanto a coroa de abacaxi e o caroço de pequi também apresentaram elevados valores desse índice. Quanto à tendência de aglomeração, a casca de café, a coroa de abacaxi, o caroço de pequi e o capim-elefante apresentaram maior propensão à ocorrência do fenômeno, enquanto as demais biomassas apresentaram baixa tendência. Conclui-se que a variabilidade da composição química exerce influência significativa sobre o comportamento das cinzas, sendo a avaliação conjunta dos índices uma ferramenta relevante para identificar combustíveis com maior risco operacional e auxiliar na seleção e no tratamento de biomassas para aplicações industriais.

title: Digitisation of Financial Reporting as a Tool for Transparency and Sustainable Business Development in the European Union
summary: Purpose: The study investigates the digitisation of financial reporting as a tool to increase transparency and promote sustainable business development in the context of regulatory transformation in the European Union. Design/Methodology/Ap
content: Purpose: The study investigates the digitisation of financial reporting as a tool to increase transparency and promote sustainable business development in the context of regulatory transformation in the European Union. Design/Methodology/Approach: The methodological basis is an empirical-analytical design based on secondary data. Quantitative content analysis and technical validation covered 312 corporate financial reports for the 2022–2024 reporting years; tagging, validation errors, completeness, machine readability and logical consistency were assessed for the 243 Inline XBRL reports, and non-financial disclosures were compared across company groups by digitisation level. Research Limitation: The study is limited to EU corporate reports for 2022–2024. Findings: Of the 312 reports, 77.9% were submitted in Inline XBRL format. The average share of tagged items in the primary financial forms was 86.4%. At the same time, only 68.7% of Inline XBRL reports were fully machine-readable and 57.2% were fully logically consistent, indicating a gap between formal digitisation and functional transparency. Companies with a high level of financial reporting digitisation achieved a substantially higher share of fully structured non-financial disclosures than companies with a low level of digitisation. Practical Implication: The results can inform regulatory oversight, corporate digital reporting practices, and transparency standards in the EU. Social Implication: Improved digital reporting supports greater corporate transparency and sustainable business development. Originality/Value: The novelty lies in measuring the gap between formal digitisation and functional transparency in the same reports and in relating digitisation levels to the quality of non-financial disclosures.

title: Financing Foundational Digital Health in ASEAN: A Narrative Review of Market Constraints and Policy Options
summary: Digital health investment in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) must account for differences in purchasing capacity, procurement arrangements and implementation readiness. Population size alone does not establish commercial
content: Digital health investment in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) must account for differences in purchasing capacity, procurement arrangements and implementation readiness. Population size alone does not establish commercial viability, and national health expenditure is not a direct measure of the digital health market. This narrative review examines how these constraints affect investment in foundational digital health systems and develops a Public–Private–Philanthropy (PPP²) framework for policy consideration. The framework distinguishes public stewardship and recurrent financing, private technical delivery, and optional philanthropic support for specified financing or capability gaps. Philanthropic participation is conditional on demonstrable additional value, alignment with national priorities, transparent governance and a credible transition beyond grant funding. Investment decisions should consider health-system needs, lifecycle costs, affordability and equity alongside financial returns. Potential regional actions include shared technical support, compatible procurement specifications and coordinated evaluation through existing ASEAN mechanisms. More complex arrangements, including a regional financing facility or coordinated regulatory testing, require separate feasibility assessment and Member State agreement. The framework is a proposition for adaptation and evaluation, rather than an empirically validated financing model. Its contribution is to clarify responsibilities and decision criteria for sustaining digital health investment under heterogeneous market conditions.

title: Grounding Political Discourse in the Body: A Computational Approach to Analyzing U.S. Energy Narratives
summary: Abstract Image schemas, recurring pre-conceptual gestalts arising from sensorimotor experience, constitute the foundational level of embodied conceptual architecture, yet their systematic identification in naturalistic language data remains
content: Abstract Image schemas, recurring pre-conceptual gestalts arising from sensorimotor experience, constitute the foundational level of embodied conceptual architecture, yet their systematic identification in naturalistic language data remains a persistent methodological challenge. Traditional introspective analyses in cognitive linguistics yield rich theoretical insights but face difficulties in scalability, inter-coder reliability, and systematic replication. This study addresses these challenges by developing a computationally assisted analytical framework that integrates semantic role labeling (AllenNLP) with large language model verification (DeepSeek R1) to detect image-schematic activations in discourse. Grounded in Fairclough’s three-dimensional critical discourse analysis model, the pipeline extracts narrative triples (“agent–action–patient”) from 10 U.S. energy policy documents (74,426 characters, 289 sentences), clusters them into conceptual domains via SentenceBERT embeddings and DBSCAN, and subjects the outputs to human–LLM collaborative validation. Against a manually annotated gold standard (50 triples from 29 sentences), the pipeline achieves an F1 score of 0.79, a 20-percentage-point improvement over the raw SRL baseline. Three image schemas (CONTAINER, PATH–GOAL, and FORCE) are identified as systematically activated through specific discourse strategies. By providing structured SRL output as input to the LLM rather than requesting annotation from scratch, the pipeline reduces hallucination while preserving the directional semantic relations needed for schematic analysis. This study offers a replicable, scalable methodology for investigating embodied language in naturally occurring discourse.

title: Circularity and Price Dynamics: A Systematic Review and Computational Analysis of Economic Mechanisms
summary: Circularity is increasingly linked to inflation, price shocks, and economic resilience, but the underlying relationships remain fragmented across disciplines and levels of analysis. This review combines systematic screening, bibliometric ma
content: Circularity is increasingly linked to inflation, price shocks, and economic resilience, but the underlying relationships remain fragmented across disciplines and levels of analysis. This review combines systematic screening, bibliometric mapping, structural topic modelling, and mechanism-based synthesis. Web of Science and Scopus searches yielded a 392-document analytical corpus, of which 72 studies met the substantive eligibility criteria for synthesis. Six mechanisms connect circularity and prices: material substitution and exposure, differential shock transmission, cost substitution and avoided costs, endogenous circular supply, circular-capacity vulnerability, and behavioural feedback. The evidence indicates a bidirectional and conditional system: circularity can alter price exposure, while prices and macroeconomic conditions also shape circular supply, investment, and behaviour. Secondary markets remain connected to virgin-resource markets, and direct aggregate evidence linking circularity to inflation is sparse. Price resilience therefore depends on substitution, transmission, cost structures, market development, and the viability of circular capacity rather than following automatically from greater circularity.

title: Generative AI in ESG Reporting: A Case Study and Process Framework
summary: ABSTRACT The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is found to have a remarkable impact on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting. Although there is abundant literature on ESG reporting, very few studies hav
content: ABSTRACT The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is found to have a remarkable impact on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) reporting. Although there is abundant literature on ESG reporting, very few studies have examined the adoption of GenAI in ESG reporting. As a result, this study examines how companies can use GenAI to generate value in ESG reporting. We obtain the following three findings that we articulate in this paper: (i) GenAI drives digital innovation in ESG reporting via automated data extraction, accelerated analytics, and dynamic reporting; (ii) GenAI‐powered platforms enhance stakeholder engagement by integrating diverse data sources and improving information accessibility; and (iii) organizations encounter significant challenges in data governance and human‐AI collaboration. We also propose a framework for adopting GenAI in digital ESG platforms.

title: Can the green intellectual capital dimension, in conjunction with fintech adoption, achieve business sustainability?
summary: MSMEs are important pillars of the Indonesian economy as economic drivers, but they also have social and environmental responsibilities in supporting sustainable development. This study aims to analyze the green intellectual capital model,
content: MSMEs are important pillars of the Indonesian economy as economic drivers, but they also have social and environmental responsibilities in supporting sustainable development. This study aims to analyze the green intellectual capital model, which not only considers profits but also contributes to environmental sustainability by leveraging fintech, thereby achieving business sustainability across economic, social, and environmental dimensions. This research method uses a quantitative approach, collecting primary data through questionnaires and analyzing them using SEM-PLS, with a sample of 220 businesses. The results of the study indicate that green intellectual capital has a significant influence on fintech adoption and on sustainability performance in all aspects, i.e., economic, social, and environmental. Fintech adoption has a significant influence on economic and social sustainability performance, but not significantly on environmental performance. Fintech adoption can mediate the effect of green intellectual capital on economic and social performance. Still, it cannot mediate the effect of green intellectual capital on environmental performance among MSMEs in the Serikat Usaha Muhammadiyah (SUMU) community of East Java. To achieve scale-up for MSMEs, specific policies are needed to direct the use of green fintech in company operations, thereby achieving a significant impact in realizing sustainable businesses, such as the use of environmentally friendly raw materials and products, energy efficiency, and access to green financing.

title: Building capacities for transformative social innovation and learning in complexity in urban climate work
summary: Organizations working on climate action face growing pressures to realize significant emissions reductions at rapid pace and scale while also navigating complex socio-economic and ecological systems. Building individual and organizational c
content: Organizations working on climate action face growing pressures to realize significant emissions reductions at rapid pace and scale while also navigating complex socio-economic and ecological systems. Building individual and organizational capacities are essential if we are to go beyond incremental changes and adaptations to existing systems, particularly when working toward justice as integral to climate action. This article presents findings from a two-year action research study with the Zero Emissions Innovation Centre (ZEIC) in Vancouver Canada, where an embedded Social Innovation Researcher in Residence supported capacity building in transformative social innovation and transformative learning approaches to advance just climate action. We tell four stories from this research that illustrate how the ZEIC staff learned to apply transformative social innovation and transformative learning approaches to deliver their ambitious just climate action mandate. The article closes with four of the most significant capacities built by ZEIC staff resulting from this action research, including: nuancing conceptions of innovation; practicing inner and outer systems work; experimentation; and shifting power and decision-making. We also discuss the significance of employing an embedded researcher in residence approach to action research, and share some key aspects of this methodology.

title: Diminuição da pegada de carbono no last mile a partir da alocação de hubs logísticos
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: No contexto de rápidas transformações impulsionadas pelo avanço tecnológico, pelas integrações comerciais e financeiras e pela competição global acirrada, a logística empresarial torna-se uma área central para as organizações, dado seu pote
content: No contexto de rápidas transformações impulsionadas pelo avanço tecnológico, pelas integrações comerciais e financeiras e pela competição global acirrada, a logística empresarial torna-se uma área central para as organizações, dado seu potencial de agregar valor aos clientes e gerar vantagens competitivas (Sakai, 2005).Segundo a Associação Brasileira da Infraestrutura e Indústrias de Base (ABDIB, 2023), foram investidos R$ 41,4 bilhões em transportes e logística em 2023, valor que representa apenas 0,39% do PIB, frente aos R$ 242,4 bilhões anuais necessários ao desenvolvimento adequado do setor.Como resposta, o Novo Programa de Aceleração do Crescimento (PAC) prevê R$ 349,1 bilhões para Transporte Eficiente e Sustentável (Governo Federal, 2023).Com esse cenário crescente, Fleury (2012) aponta a expectativa de aumento nas emissões de Gases do Efeito Estufa (GEE), tornando a logístico foco de investimentos voltados à sustentabilidade.Conforme o Net Zero Readiness Report Brasil (KPMG, 2023), o setor de transportes respondeu por 16% das emissões de GEE no país em 2022 e foi o que mais cresceu em emissões absolutas entre 2005 e 2022 (+53%), tendência associada às atividades antropogênicas e ao crescimento populacional (Ramachandra et al., 2015).Diante disso, soluções como os Centros de Consolidação Urbana (CCU) -também chamados de hubs logísticos -surgem como resposta sustentável, viabilizando a consolidação de cargas e maior eficiência na coleta e entrega urbana (Ciardiello et al., 2021).Segundo Paack (2021), tais centros reduzem custos operacionais, adaptam-se melhor ao mercado e aceleram entregas -fator considerado prioritário por 49% dos consumidores (Gava, 2022).Nesse cenário, uma empresa brasileira de moda íntima, aqui denominada Alpha por questões de confidencialidade, iniciou estudo para alocar hubs logísticos na Grande São Paulo, região que concentra seu maior market share.Atualmente operando com um centro único de distribuição em Guarulhos, a empresa busca descentralizar suas operações para ganhar agilidade no last mile e reduzir sua pegada de carbono, reforçando seu compromisso ambiental.O problema desta pesquisa reside na ausência de modelos matemáticos que apoiem a decisão gerencial de alocação de hubs logísticos com foco na redução da pegada de carbono no last mile.A questão central é: qual a melhor alocação de hubs logísticos para a empresa Alpha na Grande São Paulo, com o objetivo de diminuir a pegada de carbono da operação de last mile por meio da otimização de rotas?O objetivo principal é, portanto, propor as melhores localizações para esses hubs, contribuindo para a redução das emissões da operação logística da empresa na região.

title: Mycotoxins Produced by Fusarium spp.: Biosynthesis and Health Impact
summary: Background: This research presents a critical analysis of mycotoxins produced by fungi, particularly the Fusarium genus, which is prevalent in cereal-producing regions. Given the global impact of mycotoxins on food safety and animal health,
content: Background: This research presents a critical analysis of mycotoxins produced by fungi, particularly the Fusarium genus, which is prevalent in cereal-producing regions. Given the global impact of mycotoxins on food safety and animal health, this study addresses an urgent issue in agricultural science. It highlights the various environmental, physical, and biological factors influencing mycotoxin production, providing valuable insights for developing effective management strategies. The study also discusses the health risks associated with specific mycotoxins, such as zearalenone and fumonisins, which have been linked to serious health issues in both animals and humans. Furthermore, it emphasizes the need for ongoing prevention and control programs to mitigate mycotoxin contamination in the food chain. By exploring analytical challenges and proposing future directions for research and policy, this work contributes significantly to the understanding of mycotoxin dynamics in agricultural systems. The findings are essential for stakeholders in the livestock industry, aiming for sustainable practices and economic viability. Objective: This paper reviews the molecular mechanisms of Fusarium mycotoxin biosynthesis under different environmental conditions and the mycotoxin effects on plant metabolism and cytogenetic. Conclusion: The conclusion emphasizes the health risks associated with mycotoxins produced by Fusarium species, highlighting the urgent need for ongoing research and effective management strategies. However, it should also address specific unresolved challenges. The intricate interplay of environmental factors and biosynthetic pathways, along with their implications for human and animal health, highlights the necessity for innovation in agricultural practices, mycotoxin detection, and remediation techniques.

title: TENDÊNCIAS EM PROCESSOS DE DESCARBONIZAÇÃO E TECNOLOGIAS INTELIGENTES: UM PARALELO ENTRE SETORES DE TRANSPORTES, ENERGIA E INDÚSTRIA
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A transição para uma economia de baixo carbono é o pilar indispensável para o desenvolvimento sustentável global.Ao desatrelar o crescimento econômico da degradação ambiental, esse modelo permite a sobrevivência dos ecossistemas urbanos fre
content: A transição para uma economia de baixo carbono é o pilar indispensável para o desenvolvimento sustentável global.Ao desatrelar o crescimento econômico da degradação ambiental, esse modelo permite a sobrevivência dos ecossistemas urbanos frente à crise climática, oferecendo vantagens que vão além da mitigação ambiental, como a segurança energética, a eficiência operacional e a abertura de novos mercados financeiros.No epicentro dessa transformação estão as cidades, responsáveis pela maior parcela das emissões globais e, simultaneamente, palco das soluções mais inovadoras.Diante desse cenário, o objetivo deste artigo é analisar a interseção estratégica entre as Cidades Inteligentes (Smart Cities) e os mercados de crédito de carbono.A pesquisa explora como tecnologias de fronteira como Inteligência Artificial, Blockchain, (Mobility as a Service -MaaS), Plantas de Energia Virtuais (Virtual Power Plants -VPP) e sistemas de Captura, Utilização e Armazenamento de Carbono (Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage -CCUS) -podem operacionalizar a descarbonização urbana.Conclui-se que o sucesso do mercado de carbono em cidades inteligentes reside na convergência entre a automação sistêmica e a implementação de um método cultural para incentivar o engajamento comportamental dos cidadãos.

title: Tendencias De Sostenibilidad En La Cadena Frutícola: Mapeo De La Literatura Y Desafíos En La Gestión De Pérdidas (2016-2026)
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Este trabajo examina las realidades operativas en el sector frutícola mediante una metodología secuencial de tres etapas.En la primera etapa, se ejecutó una revisión bibliométrica en Scopus (2016-2026) sobre un portafolio de 161 artículos,
content: Este trabajo examina las realidades operativas en el sector frutícola mediante una metodología secuencial de tres etapas.En la primera etapa, se ejecutó una revisión bibliométrica en Scopus (2016-2026) sobre un portafolio de 161 artículos, donde el análisis de la sostenibilidad macro decantó el propósito de la investigación específicamente hacia la gestión de pérdidas debido a su impacto sistémico.Esta base teórica se conectó, en la segunda etapa, con el análisis de datos empíricos de pérdidas de frutas y verduras reportadas por la FAO (2000FAO ( -2025) ) dentro de la cadena de suministro global para contrastar la teoría con las cifras reales de la industria.Finalmente, la tercera etapa integró ambos enfoques, revelando un esquema de pérdidas desequilibrado y con necesidad de atención por parte del sector.El análisis demuestra que la investigación global se concentra de forma masiva en Asia y Europa (89%) mediante tecnologías avanzadas de conservación postcosecha y procesos químicos de extracción; se evidenció una importante debilidad científica hacia América del Sur con el 4% de las publicaciones mundiales, lo cual contrasta drásticamente con su alto índice de siniestralidad operativa, alcanzando un 16.02% de pérdidas reales según la FAO.Los datos demuestran que la postcosecha es el eslabón con mayor índice de pérdidas en la región, registrando un alarmante 41.25% en Venezuela y 28% en Brasil.Ante esta realidad, se concluye que la sostenibilidad del sector exige replanteare el diseño de la cadena con soluciones preventivas.

title: Beyond Protein Synthesis: The Multifunctional Role of Functional Amino Acids in Modulating Meat Quality in Ruminants
summary: ABSTRACT Meat quality is a critical economic trait in ruminant production because it directly influences consumer acceptability, market value, and the long‐term sustainability of the livestock industry. Amino acids (AAs) have traditionally
content: ABSTRACT Meat quality is a critical economic trait in ruminant production because it directly influences consumer acceptability, market value, and the long‐term sustainability of the livestock industry. Amino acids (AAs) have traditionally been regarded primarily as substrates for protein synthesis. However, growing evidence indicates that they also regulate multiple aspects of meat quality. Given the increasing demand for high‐quality ruminant meat and the growing interest in nutritional regulation of carcass traits, this review synthesizes current evidence on how functional amino acids (FAAs) modulate meat quality in ruminants, including cattle, sheep, and goats. We first summarize the core indicators of meat quality—including color, water‐holding capacity, tenderness, marbling, and flavor—and the current understanding of how these attributes are regulated by AA metabolism. We then review the specific effects and underlying mechanisms of key FAAs and their derivatives in ruminants: Lysine improves carcass leanness and nitrogen utilization efficiency; methionine enhances antioxidant capacity and exerts programming effects on fetal development; tryptophan regulates stress responses and digestive physiology via neuroendocrine pathways; branched‐chain amino acids (BCAAs) activate the mTOR signaling pathway and promote muscle protein synthesis; glutamate and glutamine support intestinal health, immunity, and reproductive performance; arginine and its derivatives (citrulline, guanidinoacetic acid, and N‐carbamoylglutamate) regulate vasodilation, energy metabolism, and endogenous arginine synthesis; and other functional AAs (glycine, serine, β‐alanine, histidine, betaine, and taurine) contribute to collagen stability, methyl‐group metabolism, meat color stability, and antioxidant defense. We further discuss strategies for practical application, including rumen‐protected delivery technologies, utilization of sustainable forage resources, and systematic evaluation of AA requirements for precision supplementation. Collectively, this review highlights the mechanisms through which FAAs regulate meat quality and identifies key research gaps and future directions in this field. The synthesized evidence provides a theoretical basis for developing nutritional strategies that simultaneously improve meat quality, production efficiency, and environmental sustainability in ruminant production systems.

title: Socio-economic Services of Living Hedges in the Sudano-Sahelian Zone of Cameroon
summary: Living hedges are among the linear agroforestry systems that structure agricultural landscapes and play an important role in the livelihoods of local populations. They provide various socio-economic services to communities. The objective of
content: Living hedges are among the linear agroforestry systems that structure agricultural landscapes and play an important role in the livelihoods of local populations. They provide various socio-economic services to communities. The objective of this study was to contribute to the promotion of living hedges. The study consisted of a survey conducted among 234 living hedge owners in 18 localities distributed along the 800, 900, and 1000 mm isohyets, with six localities selected from each isohyet. The results revealed that living hedges are established by farmers primarily to protect crops, livestock, and houses (76.5%) against wind, erosion, and, more generally, climatic hazards. In addition, living hedges provide products such as fuelwood and timber (65.3%), vegetables (59.4%), fodder (27.1%), and medicinal products (35.6%). Living hedges also serve as an alternative solution to land conflicts (57.2%) and agro-pastoral conflicts (54.5%). The main species used include Jatropha curcas, Jatropha gossypifolia, Commiphora africana, Commiphora kerstingii, Manihot esculenta, Euphorbia kamerunica, Euphorbia sp., Erythrina sigmoidea, Azadirachta indica, Senna siamea, Ziziphus mauritiana, Agave sisalana, Ipomoea carnea, Acacia polyacantha, Acacia nilotica, Eucalyptus camaldulensis, Moringa oleifera, and Thevetia neriifolia. Products obtained from this system are either consumed or marketed and contribute to improving household incomes. These findings are useful for promoting and developing sustainable management strategies for living hedges in the Sudano-Sahelian zone of Cameroon.

title: Internal Innovation versus External Coordination in Sustainable Tourism: Managerial Perspectives from Indonesia
source: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
summary: This study examines how circular economy capability contributes to sustainable tourism performance through green process innovation and green supply chain management from the perspective of tourism managers in Indonesia.A quantitative explo
content: This study examines how circular economy capability contributes to sustainable tourism performance through green process innovation and green supply chain management from the perspective of tourism managers in Indonesia.A quantitative exploratory approach was employed using survey data collected from 118 tourism managers and destination operators representing tourism destinations across Indonesia.Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM).The findings reveal that circular economy capability positively influences green process innovation, green supply chain management, and sustainable tourism performance.Green process innovation is significantly enhanced by circular economy capability; however, it does not significantly influence sustainable tourism performance and does not mediate the relationship between circular economy capability and sustainable tourism performance.In contrast, green supply chain management significantly improves sustainable tourism performance and serves as a significant mediating mechanism through which circular economy capability enhances sustainability outcomes.These findings suggest that sustainable tourism transformation depends not only on the development of internal sustainability capabilities but also on the effective coordination of environmentally responsible practices across tourism stakeholder networks.The study highlights the critical role of green supply chain management in translating circular economy capability into sustainability performance within emerging tourism destinations.This study contributes to the sustainable tourism literature by extending circular economy and sustainability research into the tourism service sector and provides managerial insights for tourism organisations seeking to strengthen sustainability-oriented operational practices.

title: Green Shipping Corridors in Brazil: Readiness of the Container Cabotage Sector
