summary: Maritime transport plays a fundamental role in global logistics but is also responsible for a significant share of greenhouse gas emissions.In response to international decarbonization targets established by the International Maritime Organ
content: Maritime transport plays a fundamental role in global logistics but is also responsible for a significant share of greenhouse gas emissions.In response to international decarbonization targets established by the International Maritime Organization (IMO), initiatives such as Green Shipping Corridors have emerged as a strategy to accelerate the adoption of low-and zero-emission fuels in maritime transport.In this context, this study analyzes the readiness of the Brazilian cabotage sector for the potential implementation of Green Shipping Corridors.The research adopts a qualitative approach combining a scoping review of the literature with documentary analysis of the Brazilian cabotage sector, including fleet characteristics, operational structures, and sustainability strategies of the main container shipping companies operating in the country.Data were collected from sustainability reports and public information released by shipping companies and sectoral institutions.The results indicate that although Brazilian cabotage operators have invested in fleet modernization and operational efficiency, these initiatives remain largely incremental and are primarily focused on fuel efficiency rather than the adoption of alternative fuels.Furthermore, structural challenges related to port infrastructure, energy supply, and regulatory coordination still limit the implementation of low-emission maritime corridors in Brazil.The findings highlight that, despite these barriers, Brazilian cabotage presents strategic potential to support the development of Green Shipping Corridors, particularly due to its role in national logistics integration.This study contributes to the literature on maritime decarbonization by providing an assessment of the Brazilian cabotage sector and identifying key challenges and opportunities for the future implementation of green maritime transport routes.

title: Eletrificação de frotas na logística de última milha: análise da competitividade, do custo total de propriedade e da sustentabilidade em entregas urbanas
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: de propriedade e da sustentabilidade em entregas urbanas Cristina Helena Arata (Unidade de Pós-Graduação, Extensão e Pesquisa CEETEPS) Kelly Cristina Capana (Unidade de Pós-Graduação, Extensão e Pesquisa CEETEPS) Fernanda Rosa Braga (Serviç
content: de propriedade e da sustentabilidade em entregas urbanas Cristina Helena Arata (Unidade de Pós-Graduação, Extensão e Pesquisa CEETEPS) Kelly Cristina Capana (Unidade de Pós-Graduação, Extensão e Pesquisa CEETEPS) Fernanda Rosa Braga (Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Industrial SENAI) Alexandre Formigoni (Unidade de Pós-Graduação, Extensão e Pesquisa CEETEPS) Eliacy Cavalcanti Lélis (Unidade de Pós-Graduação, Extensão e Pesquisa CEETEPS)O artigo realiza uma Revisão Sistemática da Literatura sobre a eletrificação de frotas na logística da última milha, com foco em competitividade econômica, eficiência operacional e redução de emissões de CO₂.A triagem inclui 421 estudos, reduzidos para 73 e, ao final, para 7 artigos alinhados aos critérios da pesquisa.Os resultados indicam que os veículos elétricos são promissores sobretudo em rotas urbanas curtas, por apresentarem menor custo de manutenção, maior eficiência energética, menor ruído e ausência de emissões diretas.Contudo, as opções econômicas dependem fortemente do equilíbrio entre custo inicial de aquisição, custos operacionais, autonomia, infraestrutura de recarga e incentivos públicos.No contexto brasileiro, as principais barreiras são o alto investimento inicial, a rede de recarga ainda insuficiente e a ausência de políticas integradas e mais robustas.Conclui-se que a eletrificação da última milha é uma estratégia relevante para a descarbonização do transporte urbano, mas sua adoção em larga escala exige planejamento, incentivos fiscais e estudos empíricos adicionais sobre custo total de propriedade e retorno em condições reais.

title: MECANISMOS DE MERCADO E CADEIA DE SUPRIMENTOS DE COMBUSTÍVEIS SUSTENTÁVEIS DE AVIAÇÃO (SAF): UMA REVISÃO EM ECONOMIAS EMERGENTES
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A descarbonização do setor aéreo global posiciona o Combustível Sustentável de Aviação (SAF) como elemento central da transição energética.As rotas tecnológicas de produção já apresentam elevado grau de maturidade.Persistem, porém, limitaçõ
content: A descarbonização do setor aéreo global posiciona o Combustível Sustentável de Aviação (SAF) como elemento central da transição energética.As rotas tecnológicas de produção já apresentam elevado grau de maturidade.Persistem, porém, limitações na integração entre logística regional, mecanismos de mercado e políticas de incentivo, o que compromete a escalabilidade do setor.Este estudo realiza uma revisão sistemática da literatura combinada à análise bibliométrica, com base em 54 artigos selecionados a partir de um procedimento metodológico estruturado.A análise foi conduzida com apoio do software VOSviewer, com foco nas dimensões de gestão, economia e governança.Os resultados indicam que a viabilidade do SAF em bioeconomias emergentes depende da maturidade de instrumentos de mercado, como o sistema Book and Claim, e da organização de cadeias de suprimentos capazes de lidar com a dispersão geográfica da biomassa.Como contribuição, o estudo integra dimensões regulatórias e logísticas, oferecendo uma base analítica para o desenvolvimento de estratégias operacionais e políticas públicas voltadas à expansão do SAF em contextos regionais.

title: Linking Environmental Commitment and Self-Efficacy to Green Entrepreneurship Behavior: The Mediating Role of Motivation and Intention in Gen Z
source: International Review of Management and Marketing
summary: Generation Z (Gen Z) exhibits distinctive characteristics compared with previous generations, including independence, creativity, technological proficiency, appreciation of diversity, and a preference for flexible and collaborative work str
content: Generation Z (Gen Z) exhibits distinctive characteristics compared with previous generations, including independence, creativity, technological proficiency, appreciation of diversity, and a preference for flexible and collaborative work structures. In Indonesia, entrepreneurship has become an increasingly attractive career option for Gen Z, making it relevant to examine their motivation and interest in green entrepreneurship. This study investigates the influence of commitment to the environment (CtE) and entrepreneurial self-efficacy (ESE) on green entrepreneurship behavior (GEB), with entrepreneurial motivation (EM) and green entrepreneurial intention (GEI) as mediating variables. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV), Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), and Social Cognitive Theory (SCT), this study employed a cross-sectional design using an online survey of 150 university students participating in business incubators across Java Island. The study was conducted over approximately seven months, from May to November 2025. Data were collected through purposive sampling and analyzed using partial least squares–structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that ESE and GEI significantly affect GEB, whereas CtE and EM do not. Furthermore, GEI significantly mediates the relationship between ESE and GEB, while EM does not demonstrate a mediating effect. These findings indicate that ESE is a strong predictor of GEI and that both ESE and GEI are key determinants of GEB. From a theoretical perspective, the findings reinforce the central assumption of TPB that intention, supported by perceived behavioral capability, is the most immediate predictor of behavior. They are also consistent with SCT, which emphasizes self-efficacy as a key mechanism in behavioral development, and with RBV, which highlights internal resources, such as individual capability, as critical determinants of performance. This study extends the theoretical integration of RBV, TPB, and SCT in the context of green entrepreneurship and offers practical insights for educators and policymakers seeking to strengthen Gen Z’s self-efficacy and intention toward sustainability-oriented entrepreneurial action.

title: Interplays Between Therapeutic Radiopharmaceuticals and Tumor Microenvironment
summary: Radiopharmaceuticals have progressed from diagnostic agents toward theranostic. With the accelerating development of therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) is being increasingly implemented in clinical practice
content: Radiopharmaceuticals have progressed from diagnostic agents toward theranostic. With the accelerating development of therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals, radiopharmaceutical therapy (RPT) is being increasingly implemented in clinical practice in oncology. However, current therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals often contribute to tumor stabilization rather than complete remission. A major determinant of this limited clinical response is the tumor microenvironment (TME), which critically influences the delivery, penetration, and retention of radiopharmaceuticals. Meanwhile, the radiopharmaceuticals can modulate multiple components of the TME, thereby contributing to antitumor effects. These interactions provide opportunities for advancing radiopharmaceuticals to enhance RPT efficacy. In this review, the bidirectional relationship between therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals and TME in solid malignancies is comprehensively discussed. First, common therapeutic strategies that modulate TME are outlined. The impact of the TME on radiopharmaceutical efficacies and how radiopharmaceuticals reshape the TME are then highlighted. In addition to elucidating the bidirectional interplay between RPT and the TME, we examine two fundamental clinical barriers that constrain RPT efficacy: dosimetric limitations and systemic immune collateral damage. Finally, critical challenges and potential strategies to enhance next-generation therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals in solid malignancies are inspected.

title: Pengaruh Carbon Emission Disclosure terhadap Cost of Capital dengan Intensitas Emisi sebagai Variabel Moderasi pada Perusahaan Pertambangan di Indonesia
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of Carbon Emission Disclosure on the Cost of Capital, with Carbon Emission Intensity serving as a moderating variable in mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). This research empl
content: This study aims to examine the effect of Carbon Emission Disclosure on the Cost of Capital, with Carbon Emission Intensity serving as a moderating variable in mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). This research employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from companies' annual reports and sustainability reports during the observation period. The sample was selected using a purposive sampling technique. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model (REM), while the moderating effect was tested using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The results indicate that Carbon Emission Disclosure has no significant effect on the Cost of Capital. Furthermore, Carbon Emission Intensity does not have a significant effect on the Cost of Capital. The moderation analysis also reveals that Carbon Emission Intensity does not moderate the relationship between Carbon Emission Disclosure and the Cost of Capital. These findings suggest that carbon emission disclosure and emission intensity have not yet become primary considerations for investors in determining the cost of capital of mining companies. Instead, investors tend to place greater emphasis on firms' fundamental factors, such as profitability, business risk, capital structure, and industry prospects, rather than environmental information when making investment decisions. This study contributes to the literature on environmental accounting and sustainable finance by providing empirical evidence regarding the relevance of carbon-related information in the Indonesian capital market.

title: When Does Smart Charging Reduce Emissions? A Systematic Review of Behavioral and Structural Drivers
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Global policy mandates accelerate transport electrification, yet the environmental benefits of smart charging (SC) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) remain uncertain and context dependent. This systematic review synthesizes 88 peer-reviewed studies
content: Global policy mandates accelerate transport electrification, yet the environmental benefits of smart charging (SC) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) remain uncertain and context dependent. This systematic review synthesizes 88 peer-reviewed studies (2011 - 2025), retrieved through a dual-branch search combining sociotechnical adoption literature (Search A, n = 57) with environmental and grid-performance evidence (Search B, n = 31), to identify conditions under which SC and V2G are reported to deliver or fail to deliver sustainability benefits. The study proposes an integrated sociotechnical framework structured as a two-tier architecture: a parsimonious primary framework (seven constructs, six directed pathways) supported by classifiable evidence, and a hypothesis-generating extension for recurrent but unvalidated constructs. The framework is explicitly calibration-derived and requires future empirical validation. Evidence indicates that behavioral determinants are associated with participation intentions but are linked to actual participation only when structural conditions are present. Model-based evidence indicates that SC and V2G may increase emissions in high-carbon grids, demonstrating that these technologies are not inherently sustainable without aligned policy and energy system conditions. Four candidate contextual conditions including grid carbon intensity, infrastructure density, market maturity, and prior experience are recurrently identified as potentially conditioning deployment and emissions outcomes. These contributions shift policy discourse from overcoming user resistance to composing enabling conditions, offering context-dependent recommendations for deployment associated with measurable environmental benefits rather than unintended emission increases.

title: Reactions to Fourteen Alternative Academic Practices
source: Perspectives of Earth and Space Scientists
summary: Abstract Addressing the challenges facing students and researchers in academia requires reimagining academic traditions to make research and teaching more equitable and effective. Kemeny et al. (2024, https://doi.org/10.1029/2024cn000240 )
content: Abstract Addressing the challenges facing students and researchers in academia requires reimagining academic traditions to make research and teaching more equitable and effective. Kemeny et al. (2024, https://doi.org/10.1029/2024cn000240 ) proposed 14 alternative academic practices, focused on the physical sciences in the United States, designed to launch discussion. These proposals spanned the graduate student experience, faculty careers, evaluation methods, peer review and publication, and conference norms. It is important to gauge levels of support for these practices in order to inform strategies for implementation. To assess support for the proposed alternative practices, Kemeny et al. included a survey that invited readers to share their quantitative and qualitative evaluations. The survey was open for 18 months and received 83 unique responses. Most practices received mean ratings above neutral, though only six were significantly above the scale midpoint after correction for multiple comparisons. The practice with the highest support was anonymous manuscript review (#9), followed by teaching‐focused faculty leading courses (#2), free conference attendance (#14), a lottery system for grant review (#7), decentralized graduate training by departments (#3), and rotating faculty editing appointments at journals (#10). Women were significantly more likely than men to support the practice of conferences not serving alcohol or hosting bar‐related events ( p , FDR‐corrected = 0.017). Respondents were also invited to propose alternative academic practices, most of which focused on reforms to the graduate student experience. While understanding public perceptions of reimagined academic practices is necessary, institutional constraints, cost, legality, and cultural resistance must also be considered when assessing implementation feasibility.

title: Extending the Ansoff Matrix to Metaverse Tourism: An Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Conceptual Framework for Digital Growth Strategies
source: International Review of Management and Marketing
summary: This study develops a strategic framework for examining how metaverse-related technologies may support tourism growth across the four domains of the Ansoff Matrix: market penetration, product development, market development, and diversifica
content: This study develops a strategic framework for examining how metaverse-related technologies may support tourism growth across the four domains of the Ansoff Matrix: market penetration, product development, market development, and diversification. The research adopts an exploratory conceptual design that combines the Ansoff Matrix with AI-assisted scenario ideation and a narrative, literature-supported plausibility assessment. Ten structured prompts were used to generate candidate scenarios. The outputs were treated as an ideation aid rather than as interviews, expert testimony, or empirical observations. Candidate scenarios were retained only when they were conceptually consistent with the Ansoff categories and supported by relevant academic literature or documented tourism practices. The synthesis identifies five cross-cutting opportunity areas: hyper-personalised and sensory-responsive experiences; multisensory services and digital twins; accessibility and social inclusion; blockchain-enabled participatory experience economies; and hybrid, sustainability-oriented tourism. The framework positions these opportunities as conditional growth options while highlighting uncertainty, infrastructure constraints, privacy risks, accessibility gaps, and the need for empirical validation. The study extends a classic strategic-growth model to metaverse tourism and offers a structured agenda for destination management organisations, tourism firms, and future research. It does not claim to predict adoption outcomes; instead, it provides a transparent framework for organising and testing alternative strategic pathways.

title: Thermodynamics-informed prefiltering framework for industrial heat pump integration: carnot-based targeting and adaptive genetic algorithm optimization
summary: Industrial heat-pump integration requires exploring competing temperature levels, heat allocations and utility choices, while detailed superstructure models make scenario exploration computationally demanding. This study develops a thermoec
content: Industrial heat-pump integration requires exploring competing temperature levels, heat allocations and utility choices, while detailed superstructure models make scenario exploration computationally demanding. This study develops a thermoeconomic prefiltering framework to identify integration targets before detailed design. The framework couples an adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) with heat allocation along residual grand composite curves to select source and sink temperature levels minimizing total annual cost (TAC). Heat-pump performance uses the Carnot coefficient of performance scaled by a second-law efficiency, nominally 0.50 and varied from 0.30 to 0.80. Boiler competition permits partial electrification, while rejected heat from fixed refrigeration services provides an additional source. Three Swiss industrial profiles, covering paper, meat and cheese production, are assessed through five-seed AGA sensitivity analyses of energy prices, operating hours, efficiency and segmentation costs. Across the investigated cases, relative energy prices and heat-pump second-law efficiency strongly influence heating coverage, whereas higher absolute prices can favor additional temperature levels. In meat processing, higher absolute prices result in six instead of three condenser levels at a fixed electricity-to-gas price ratio, while the heat-pump share remains about 96.2%. Near transitions to higher HP coverage, the influence of second-law efficiency depends on the assumed segmentation cost, which penalizes additional temperature levels. For the paper-mill reference, the AGA achieves TAC within 0.0026% of the best deterministic result under the same screening model, using 21,132 versus 2.87 million evaluations. Comparisons with detailed superstructure models identify promising thermal regions without establishing equipment-level feasibility or economic accuracy. The framework enables rapid prioritization before detailed modeling.

title: Sensemaking in the face of climate change: Latin American banks' organizational identity from a Grounded Theory perspective.
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: This study investigates how Latin American banking organizations interpret and respond to climate and sustainability regulations through the lens of sensemaking and organizational identity.Using a grounded theory approach, responses from fi
content: This study investigates how Latin American banking organizations interpret and respond to climate and sustainability regulations through the lens of sensemaking and organizational identity.Using a grounded theory approach, responses from financial institutions to the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) were analyzed.The findings reveal three overarching sensemaking dimensions: identity-preserving sensemaking (maintaining stability and routines), institutional sensemaking (seeking legitimacy through alignment with field norms), and enactive identity management (proactively shaping the environment to reinforce a leadership identity).The research shows that banks' climate responses are not merely technical but involve ongoing negotiations between existing identity, legitimacy pressures, and internal capabilities.

title: The Climate Impasse: Disavowal, Exhaustion and Everyday Life in the Climate Crisis
source: Transactions of the Institute of British Geographers
summary: ABSTRACT The consequences of climate‐related disasters and emergencies are becoming increasingly stark. And yet in many places, consensus on climate action appears unattainable. I call this problem the climate impasse. In this paper, I draw
content: ABSTRACT The consequences of climate‐related disasters and emergencies are becoming increasingly stark. And yet in many places, consensus on climate action appears unattainable. I call this problem the climate impasse. In this paper, I draw on emerging theory on affect and negativity to characterise this impasse in three ways. I argue first that, rather than solely addressing governments' failure to act, this impasse develops through people's different lived experiences of the climate crisis. Second, the paper outlines the material conditions of possibility for the climate impasse. I claim here that this impasse has arisen owing to unequal, and often highly racialised, levels of access to vital infrastructure that shape people's different experiences of a changing climate. Third, the paper extends understanding of the consequences of the climate impasse. Beyond simply a stoppage in action, impasses allow some carbon‐intensive infrastructural norms of liberal modernity to continue despite their growing implausibility as the climate changes. I expand on these claims through developing our understanding of exhaustion and disavowal as two feelings that both organise peoples' experience of a changing climate and collectively contribute to the climate impasse. These wider arguments stem from research that explores the connections between heatwaves and the racialised politics of urban planning in Louisville, Kentucky.

title: In Situ Grown Functional Interfaces for Enhanced Lithium‐Ion Transport in Silicon–Carbon Anodes
summary: ABSTRACT Chemical vapor deposition‐derived silicon–carbon (CVD‐Si/C) materials are promising Si‐based anodes for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), offering high capacity, improved initial coulombic efficiency (ICE), and mitigate
content: ABSTRACT Chemical vapor deposition‐derived silicon–carbon (CVD‐Si/C) materials are promising Si‐based anodes for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), offering high capacity, improved initial coulombic efficiency (ICE), and mitigated volume expansion. However, the fast‐charging capability of CVD‐Si/C anodes is severely limited by the discontinuous distribution of nanosized Si within the highly porous carbon framework, which disrupts Li + transport pathways. Recently, Lu et al. developed a novel CVD‐Si/C anode material (SSC@LSO) featuring a continuous Li + transport interface (Li x SiO y layer), which effectively mitigates volume expansion and suppresses parasitic electrolyte reactions. Consequently, the SSC@LSO anode delivers markedly enhanced rate capability and cycling durability. Notably, Ah‐level pouch cells demonstrate outstanding practical application‐level performance, retaining 91.7% capacity after 1000 cycles at 25°C and sustaining 86.9% capacity utilization at 5C, underscoring its promise for high energy LIBs.

title: Water‐Use Fee (WUF) and Water Productivity (WP) in the Manufacturing Industry: An Environmental Economic Approach in Colombia
summary: ABSTRACT Water is a vital resource and an essential input for the manufacturing industry, a key sector for biodiversity financing. Environmental fees are policy economic instruments designed to finance natural resource management while chan
content: ABSTRACT Water is a vital resource and an essential input for the manufacturing industry, a key sector for biodiversity financing. Environmental fees are policy economic instruments designed to finance natural resource management while changing society's unsustainable habits. An econometric model was used to analyze the relation between WUF and WP in the Colombian manufacturing industry from 2010 to 2022. An average WUF of US $50.87 million was obtained, representing an increase of +1060% since 2017. The mean WP was 1.68 US $/m 3 , with decreases recorded from 2015 to 2018 and from 2019 to 2021. While WUF did not affect WP, it showed moderate to high correlations with other environmental variables in the model, including investments, operating costs, and staff for environmental protection expenses. The potential of WUF to internalize the value of water in the economy has been recognized, and the commitment of the Colombian manufacturing industry to scale up to sustainable water use practices is remarkable. However, the present study evidences its irrelevance in econometric terms. Although changes to the WUF regulatory framework have been introduced to strengthen its environmental purpose, low water pricing remains the main barrier to policy effectiveness, not only in Colombia, but globally.

title: A review of critical properties of encapsulation and edge seal materials for suitability in packaging perovskite solar cell
summary: Perovskite solar cell (PSC) is an evolving technology with great potential to drive the solar photovoltaic industry forward, but instability arising from ingress of environmental stressors has limited the technology uptake making imminent c
content: Perovskite solar cell (PSC) is an evolving technology with great potential to drive the solar photovoltaic industry forward, but instability arising from ingress of environmental stressors has limited the technology uptake making imminent commercialisation unattractive. This study reviews the barrier, thermal, mechanical, optical and chemical properties of several encapsulation and edge seal materials and polymer composites to advise on their suitability in packaging PSC. It proposes nanofiller composite with enhanced barriers and thermal properties for effective packaging of PSC. Implementing a systematic review process achieved by deploying the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) algorithm, 11 encapsulation, 7 edge seal and 13 filler materials sourced from 110 relevant peer reviewed papers are reviewed. Graphical plot and Venn Diagram techniques are used to analyse the materials properties. The review reveals that UV cured epoxy demonstrates the potential of being the most suitable material but its relatively high-water vapour transmission rate (WVTR) of 0.16 gm -2 day -1 and low thermal conductivity of circa 0.25 W/mK limit its application. It is found that addition of boron nitride nano platelets (BNNP) to matrix of epoxy reduces the WVTR by 50%, increases the thermal conductivity significantly and is indifferent to the electrical conductivity, but addition of graphene reduces the WVTR of epoxy by 80%, increases both the thermal conductivity and electrical conductivity. Optimal weight percent of BNNP in epoxy matrix has produced composite which demonstrates suitability in packaging PSC, effectively. This review provides an insight which guides researchers on development of suitable nano-composite materials toward packaging of PSC.

title: Between symbols and substance: Voluntary impact reporting of funds
summary: Impact investing has emerged as a prominent investment approach to addressing social and environmental challenges while generating financial returns. Given its dual mandate to generate impact and financial returns, impact investing faces he
content: Impact investing has emerged as a prominent investment approach to addressing social and environmental challenges while generating financial returns. Given its dual mandate to generate impact and financial returns, impact investing faces heightened pressures on its legitimacy, making transparent impact reporting essential to counter allegations of impact-washing and to safeguard the credibility of the approach. Despite the growing relevance of impact reporting, little is known about the underlying motivations and reporting strategies of fund managers who voluntarily publish impact reports. Drawing on legitimacy theory, the paper investigates the motivations and reporting strategies behind voluntary impact reporting by fund managers using a sequential exploratory design. First, 13 semi-structured interviews with impact-reporting professionals were analyzed following Grounded Theory principles. Second, a qualitative content analysis of 141 publicly available impact reports was conducted to analyze how reporting strategies are implemented in practice. The findings of the interviews reveal that fund managers’ motivations are driven by a need to show the alignment of profit with purpose, move beyond institutional compliance, and foster impact reflexivity. These motivations are operationalized through six reporting strategies: rationalization, contextualization, verification, institutionalization, participation, and transformation, which cluster around the dimensions of justification, integration, and adaptation. The content analysis assesses the potential for more substantive forms of legitimation in individual reporting elements. The paper contributes to legitimacy theory in the context of reporting by demonstrating that reporting strategies are interdependent and to practice by offering practitioners and standard setters a starting point for critically reflecting on the design of impact reporting.

title: Knowledge in the Marketplace: The Rare Book Trade, History of Science, and the Sociology of Texts
summary: The rare book trade plays a large but almost entirely unacknowledged role in the formation of historical knowledge. This essay draws on the author's experience in both academic history of science and rare book dealing, in order to explain t
content: The rare book trade plays a large but almost entirely unacknowledged role in the formation of historical knowledge. This essay draws on the author's experience in both academic history of science and rare book dealing, in order to explain the differences between these two activities, and ways in which they might be brought closer together-to the benefit of both.

title: Medjool Date Seed Polysaccharides Attenuate DSS‐Induced Colitis and Associated Hepatic Oxidative Injury in Mice, Accompanied by Gut Microbiota Alterations
summary: ABSTRACT Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that is often accompanied by oxidative stress, immune imbalance, disruption of the intestinal barrier, and liver complications linked through the gut‐liver axis. In
content: ABSTRACT Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic intestinal disorder that is often accompanied by oxidative stress, immune imbalance, disruption of the intestinal barrier, and liver complications linked through the gut‐liver axis. In this study, we explored the protective effects of Medjool date seed polysaccharides (MDSP) in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)‐induced colitis mouse model. Structural characterization using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier‐transform infrared (FTIR), x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), high‐performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analyses showed that MDSP consisted of oxygen‐rich heteropolysaccharide structures with notable antioxidant potential. Oral administration of MDSP (150 and 300 mg/kg) markedly alleviated DSS‐induced colitis by reducing body weight loss, disease activity, and colon shortening, while improving intestinal histological architecture and restoring MUC2 expression. MDSP also reduced the levels of pro‐inflammatory cytokines, including IL‐1β, IL‐6, IL‐17, and IL‐23, and enhanced the expression of anti‐inflammatory cytokines, such as IL‐10 and IL‐4. In addition, MDSP improved antioxidant status by increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione (GSH) levels and lowering myeloperoxidase (MPO), malondialdehyde (MDA), nitric oxide (NO), ALT, and AST levels, indicating significant protection against oxidative stress and colitis‐associated liver injury. Analysis of the gut microbiota further demonstrated that MDSP helped restore microbial balance by suppressing harmful bacteria, including Klebsiella and Desulfovibrio , while promoting beneficial genera such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium . The aforementioned findings suggest that MDSP can effectively reduce intestinal inflammation, improve antioxidant defenses, protect liver function, and regulate gut microbiota composition, highlighting its application prospects as a preventive control for IBD.

title: Forecasting Renewable Energy Employing A Regularized Deep Learning Approach
source: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
summary: Renewable energy prediction has become an important research area due to the increasing demand for clean energy, the depletion of conventional fossil fuels, and the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Among the various renewable energy
content: Renewable energy prediction has become an important research area due to the increasing demand for clean energy, the depletion of conventional fossil fuels, and the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Among the various renewable energy sources, solar energy has gained considerable attention because of its wide availability, environmental sustainability, and potential for large-scale electricity generation. However, the amount of solar energy generated by photovoltaic (PV) systems depends on several environmental and meteorological factors, including solar irradiance, ambient temperature, humidity, cloud cover, wind speed, and atmospheric conditions. These factors exhibit significant temporal variations, making solar energy prediction a challenging task. The proposed approach combines the DWT and a Bayesian Optimized Deep Neural Network for forecasting renewable energy using solar irradiation dataset. It has been shown that the model attains a MAE of just 3.0 and an MAPE value of 0.03% which clearly outperforms existing baseline techniques in the domain.

title: Resilient Trade in Low‐Carbon Technologies Under Geopolitical Risk
summary: ABSTRACT This paper examines how geopolitical risk shapes international trade in low‐carbon technologies (LCTs). Using exporter–product panel data, we find that higher exporter‐level geopolitical risk is associated with lower export values
content: ABSTRACT This paper examines how geopolitical risk shapes international trade in low‐carbon technologies (LCTs). Using exporter–product panel data, we find that higher exporter‐level geopolitical risk is associated with lower export values for non‐LCT products, while low‐carbon technology exports respond less negatively and gain export share relative to non‐LCT products. The relative resilience of LCT exports varies across exporter income groups, LCT sectors, and end‐use categories. Two channels appear relevant: LCT resilience is stronger in products with more concentrated global supplier structures and when global energy prices are higher.

title: Food Properties, Bioactive Components, and Human Factors as Determinants of Low Nutrient Supply From Foods Can Be Improved With Adequate Nutritional Strategies
summary: ABSTRACT Nutrient adequacy depends not only on the nutrient content of foods but also on food‐matrix release, intestinal absorption, physiological utilization, dietary access, and the stability of food supplies. These stages are influenced
content: ABSTRACT Nutrient adequacy depends not only on the nutrient content of foods but also on food‐matrix release, intestinal absorption, physiological utilization, dietary access, and the stability of food supplies. These stages are influenced by antinutritional compounds, processing, storage, microbial activity, agricultural conditions, disease, genetics, and socioeconomic constraints. This narrative review critically synthesizes food‐level, host‐level, and food system determinants of nutrient supply and evaluates strategies for addressing them. Relevant literature was sought from PubMed/MEDLINE, PubMed Central (PMC), Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, etc. A narrative/critical synthesis was organized around nutrient content, bioaccessibility, bioavailability, utilization, and population access. Evidence was interpreted according to study design and applicability, distinguishing mechanistic and in vitro findings from human absorption studies, clinical outcomes, and program‐level evidence. Processing and bioactive compounds can either inhibit or improve nutrient availability depending on dose, food matrix, and preparation. Host conditions and structural barriers may prevent nutrient‐rich foods from translating into adequate nutrient status. Fortification and supplementation can be effective for defined deficiencies, but coverage, safety, affordability, dietary diversity, and monitoring determine impact. Emerging technologies require stronger evidence on human outcomes, safety, and cost‐effectiveness before broad implementation. Effective action requires context‐specific combinations of food processing, safe storage, dietary diversification, agricultural improvement, targeted nutrition services, and equitable food system policies.

title: Deep Temporal Learning for Carbon Allowance Price Forecasting Toward Carbon Financial Derivatives Pricing: A Multiscale Decomposition and Optimization Framework
summary: Carbon allowance-price forecasting is a multiscale sequence-regression problem: persistent price-level movements coexist with short-term disturbances and associations with observable financial, energy, and environmental indicators. This stu
content: Carbon allowance-price forecasting is a multiscale sequence-regression problem: persistent price-level movements coexist with short-term disturbances and associations with observable financial, energy, and environmental indicators. This study evaluates a CEEMDAN–LSTM pipeline in which sample entropy reduces nine intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) to five additive component targets, partial autocorrelation selects component-specific histories, and Spearman coefficients screen CSI 300, the CZCE thermal coal index, and Wuhan AQI as candidate covariates. The component predictors use a common LSTM transition structure with different input configurations. A Harris hawks optimizer incorporating Tent-map exploration and crossover–greedy updates (CRTHHO) searches for the hidden-neuron count and learning rate. On the reported Hubei carbon-market sample of 2009 aligned observations, the updated final-model comparison records MAE = 0.49394, RMSE = 0.88785, and MAPE = 0.01194, versus 0.73014, 1.13677, and 0.01988 for the untuned configuration. These correspond to observed relative error reductions of 32.35%, 21.90%, and 39.94%. The study characterizes the interface between multiscale inputs and recurrent prediction rather than proposing new CEEMDAN or LSTM theory. Results are conditional on the documented evaluation procedure; the available record does not establish complete isolation of test data during every preprocessing and tuning stage. The forecasts concern allowance prices and do not constitute a direct valuation of carbon derivatives.

title: Investigative studies on health benefits and risks of single-cell proteins★
summary: Single-cell proteins (SCPs) primarily consist of fungal proteins, yeast proteins, bacterial proteins, and algal biomass, and et al, with partial application in human food and animal feed. SCPs contain high levels of protein and dietary fibe
content: Single-cell proteins (SCPs) primarily consist of fungal proteins, yeast proteins, bacterial proteins, and algal biomass, and et al, with partial application in human food and animal feed. SCPs contain high levels of protein and dietary fiber, low fat and cholesterol, and contribute to reduced carbon emissions. However, multiple uncertainties still exist regarding their safety and functional efficacy. This review systematically evaluates several major SCPs commonly incorporated in food products, including filamentous fungal proteins, yeast proteins, bacterial proteins, and microalgal proteins, by summarizing their classification, nutritional values, safety profiles, and application limitations. Special focus is placed on their food application potential and latent health risks. Filamentous fungal proteins have mature food application models, comprehensive toxicological safety data, and available human dietary survey and intervention data. Yeast proteins are applicable in human food but have a narrower application scope and insufficient human clinical trial data, whereas bacterial and microalgae proteins are mainly used for animal feed. All these SCPs confer certain health benefits while carrying specific health risks. Accordingly, we propose that the key focus areas for the application of SCPs include efficacy verification, process optimization, and health risk assessment. We believe that the information compiled in this review will provide valuable reference for promoting microbial alternative proteins as major protein sources for human populations.

title: Urban Growth Boundaries in Urban Development: A Holistic Review of Literature From 2011 to 2025
summary: ABSTRACT The urban growth boundary (UGB) has been recognized as an effective policy instrument for controlling disorderly urban sprawl and improving the sustainability of urban development. However, summary studies in this domain are insuff
content: ABSTRACT The urban growth boundary (UGB) has been recognized as an effective policy instrument for controlling disorderly urban sprawl and improving the sustainability of urban development. However, summary studies in this domain are insufficient. Hence, this study conducted a holistic review of UGB based on 228 literature samples published between 2011 and 2025 to help resolve this academic gap. This work has four objectives: (1) to analyze principal journal sources, countries, authors, organizations, articles, and keywords in the literature on UGB using bibliometrics and science mapping methods; (2) to summarize current research topics relevant to UGB; (3) to discuss existing research gaps in UGB; and (4) to explore future research directions in UGB.

title: Reef fish functional groups show variable declines due to deforestation-driven sedimentation, while flexible harvesting mitigates this damage
summary: Abstract Sedimentation is a major coral reef stressor, with effects including suppressing algae consumption by herbivorous fish. This puts pressure on reef fish populations and the fisheries that harvest them. Deforestation causes much sedi
content: Abstract Sedimentation is a major coral reef stressor, with effects including suppressing algae consumption by herbivorous fish. This puts pressure on reef fish populations and the fisheries that harvest them. Deforestation causes much sedimentation on reefs, and is an ongoing concern in many tropical island states. Although ecosystem processes like deforestation and fish population dynamics are usually far from equilibrium, explicitly time-dependent analyses of reef fish vulnerability to deforestation are rare. Additionally, optimization methods for fisheries on heavily sedimented reefs are generally unexplored. Here, we construct a model coupling four reef fish functional groups with seabed dynamics and deforestation, parametrized to represent a wide variety of tropical coastal forests. We show that with predicted human population increases, highland deforestation could cause omnivorous fish abundances to halve within 15-30 years, and piscivorous fish and top predators to do so around 20 years later. In contrast, piscivorous fish and top predators are resilient to lowland deforestation, and herbivorous fish populations often recover after initial declines during sedimentation pressure. We demonstrate that flexible fishing approaches could lead to high and temporally stable populations of most functional groups, offsetting sedimentation-related stress. We show that the combination of deforestation and increased fishing demand due to human population growth may cause medium-term local reef fish extirpation. Our results provide sustainability guidelines for reef fisheries, and demonstrate nonlinear interactions between overfishing and deforestation.

title: How Do Soil Properties and Canopy Status Influence Potato Traits while Continuously Monitoring Soil Moisture with Iot-Based Sensors?
summary: Abstract Many soil-related factors associated with potato yield and quality are implicitly linked to soil water availability (SWA). This soil property also affects potato canopy, which could be indirectly evaluated using Unmanned Aerial Veh
content: Abstract Many soil-related factors associated with potato yield and quality are implicitly linked to soil water availability (SWA). This soil property also affects potato canopy, which could be indirectly evaluated using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The objective of this study was to quantify the optimal explanatory soil- and canopy state-related properties that determine potato ( Solanum tuberosum L.) traits: total yield (TY), dry matter (DM) content, and average tuber weight (ATW) over a rainfed production field. SWA was continuously measured using moisture sensors installed at three depths and connected via the Internet to exchange data. Soil water storage (SWS) was derived from soil moisture content (SMC). Thus, the effect of spatial and temporal changes in SWS on TY was also determined.Potatoes were grown under a suboptimal water supply during crucial stages for yield formation. More explanatory variables significantly affected ATW and TY than DM content. SWS, determined between the stages of leaf development and canopy closure, played a more critical role in forming ATW and TY than soil chemical properties. A model solely based on canopy status evaluation between the time of canopy closure and the end of flowering, and SWS determined simultaneously, was a strong alternative for forecasting TY and ATW. In the sampling area with the highest TY, the average SWS did not drop below the level that limits potato growth for most of the growing season. A sampling area with the lowest TY was characterized by the lowest water retention for most of the growing season.

title: Sacred Speech, Social Authority, and Coastal Conservation: Manahelo Oral Traditions in East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
source: Jurnal Sosiologi Reflektif (Universitas Islam Negeri, Sunan Kalijaga, Yogyakarta)
summary: Coastal conservation approaches that rely predominantly on formal regulations often overlook the role of oral traditions and customary authority in fostering collective compliance with environmental protection. This study examines how Manah
content: Coastal conservation approaches that rely predominantly on formal regulations often overlook the role of oral traditions and customary authority in fostering collective compliance with environmental protection. This study examines how Manahelo poetic speech constructs socio-religious authority and how myths and customary prohibitions (pamali) shape collective compliance with community-based coastal conservation practices in Rote Ndao, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia. Employing a qualitative linguistic ethnographic approach, the research was conducted in two coastal customary territories, Dengka and Ba’a, Rote Ndao Regency, East Nusa Tenggara Province, Indonesia. Data were collected through audiovisual recordings of 6 (six) customary speech performances, in-depth interviews with 12 informants, participant observation, and document analysis. The data were examined using initial coding, axial coding, and ecocritical thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Manahelo oral traditions function as socio-religious institutions that legitimize customary authority, cultivate moral obligations, and regulate ecological behavior. Beliefs in supernatural guardians, particularly Oematan Nitu and Tasi Nitu, reinforce customary prohibitions (pamali) and territorial restrictions (fai punu) through perceived supernatural sanctions (mula). Although collective compliance is continually negotiated in response to everyday economic pressures, Manahelo's sacred authority remains an important source of legitimacy for environmental regulation beyond formal law enforcement mechanisms. The implications of this study extend sociological understandings of religious authority, cultural legitimacy, and social control in environmental governance, while highlighting the importance of recognizing customary institutions in developing inclusive, participatory, and sustainable conservation policies. Pendekatan konservasi pesisir yang bertumpu pada regulasi formal sering kali mengabaikan peran tradisi lisan dan otoritas adat dalam membentuk kepatuhan masyarakat terhadap perlindungan lingkungan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bagaimana tuturan puitis Manahelo membangun otoritas sosial-keagamaan serta bagaimana mitos dan larangan adat (pamali) membentuk kepatuhan kolektif dalam praktik konservasi pesisir berbasis masyarakat di Rote Ndao. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan etnografi linguistik di dua wilayah adat pesisir, yaitu Dengka dan Baa, Kabupaten Rote Ndao, Nusa Tenggara Barat, Indonesia. Data dikumpulkan melalui perekaman audiovisual terhadap 6 (enam) pertunjukan tuturan adat, wawancara mendalam dengan 12 informan, observasi partisipatif, dan studi dokumen. Data dianalisis melalui pengodean awal, pengodean aksial, dan analisis tematik ekokritis. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa tradisi lisan Manahelo berfungsi sebagai institusi sosial-keagamaan yang membangun legitimasi otoritas adat, menanamkan kewajiban moral, dan mengatur perilaku ekologis masyarakat. Keperc

title: Circular construction waste management and perceived urban environmental sustainability across Ghanaian Cities
summary: Abstract Construction waste constitutes a major environmental challenge in rapidly urbanising sub-Saharan African cities, yet its governance through circular economy frameworks remains underexplored. This research used quantitative multi-ci
content: Abstract Construction waste constitutes a major environmental challenge in rapidly urbanising sub-Saharan African cities, yet its governance through circular economy frameworks remains underexplored. This research used quantitative multi-city evaluations of the effect of circular construction waste management (CCWM) on urban environmental sustainability in Ghana. A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was used to gather the data from 502 built environment professionals in the cities of Accra, Kumasi, Takoradi, Tamale and Cape Coast. The study adopted hierarchical multiple regression, MANOVA, K-means cluster analysis, and mediation and moderation analyses using the PROCESS macro to support the development of the study. The results show that the overall adoption level of CCWMs remains low (M = 2.87/5.00), due to the lowest implementation levels of design for deconstruction (M = 1.93) and on-site source segregation (M = 2.19). Three groups of adopters emerged: non-adopters (21.3%), moderate adopters (54.5%) and advanced circular firms (24.2%). The hierarchical regression results indicated that CCWM practices (β = 0.412, p < .001) were the strongest predictor, followed by regulatory enforcement (β = 0.289, p < .001) and technological capability (β = 0.175, p = .002) for sustainability outcomes. The adoption–sustainability relationship was partially mediated by regulatory enforcement, explaining 36% of the overall effect, and significant inter-city differences were observed, with Accra performing better than Tamale. Adoption–sustainability relationship was also higher in large firms than in small firms. The results confirm that awareness is not enough to bring about the adoption of a circular economy; regulation and technological tools play an important role in achieving the sustainability outcomes in the construction sector in Ghana.

title: Do Amenities Enhance the Value of Office Buildings? Dynamic Causal Impact of Modern Retrofitting
summary: Abstract The post-pandemic shift to hybrid work has redefined tenant demand, turning offices from mere workspaces into collaborative, experiential hubs. Aging properties now face an obsolescence trilemma: retrofit, convert, or decline econo
content: Abstract The post-pandemic shift to hybrid work has redefined tenant demand, turning offices from mere workspaces into collaborative, experiential hubs. Aging properties now face an obsolescence trilemma: retrofit, convert, or decline economically. Within the global “flight to quality” trend favoring modern, higher-standard space, this study quantifies the economic impact of building modernization. Using shared tenant lounge installation as a proxy for comprehensive modernization packages, we estimate its causal effect on commercial property performance. Focusing on large office buildings in Tokyo’s five central wards, we apply a staggered difference-in-differences framework to a novel, manually constructed panel dataset. Results show that modernization shortens time-on-market by 24.2%–57.0% starting one year after installation, followed by a 1.2%–1.8% decline in vacancy rates from year two onward. Rent premiums then rise dynamically, reaching 7.56% by year five. Placebo-based robustness checks, though limited, substantiate these findings. We further identify a strategic stabilization mechanism: owners first prioritize filling vacancies to restore building vibrancy, then capture rent premiums as tenants’ willingness to pay increases. These findings show that amenity-centric modernization creates functional value that mitigates obsolescence, though measured returns reflect an aggregate upgrade strategy rather than an isolated lounge effect, and apply specifically to high-grade assets in central business districts.

title: Methodological Framework for Energy - and Resource-Efficient Public Transport: The E-MED Project
summary: Abstract The E-MED project is a Euro-MED initiative that aims to improve the energy and resource efficiency of public transport systems in Mediterranean cities through the development and validation of a structured set of tools and methodol
content: Abstract The E-MED project is a Euro-MED initiative that aims to improve the energy and resource efficiency of public transport systems in Mediterranean cities through the development and validation of a structured set of tools and methodologies. These are grouped into three categories: (i) planning tools supporting decisions on network and fleet configuration, charging strategies, and integration of renewable energy sources; (ii) operational tools focused on eco-driving and analytical methods for energy consumption optimisation; and (iii) procurement-guided tools addressing sustainable and circular practices, including lifecycle-based procurement, battery reuse, rainwater harvesting, and tyre maintenance. The tools are tested through pilot applications and feasibility studies in cities such as Thessaloniki, Maribor, Lisbon, Bergamo, and Barcelona. The paper presents the methodological framework and structure of the developed tools, along with their implementation across different urban contexts. Emphasis is placed on the planning tool developed by CERTH for public transport network redesign. This tool supports the adaptation of bus routes to new vehicle technologies, additional public transport modes (e.g. tram, metro), and soft mobility. It applies operations research techniques to assess network modifications using indicators such as coverage, travel time, and environmental metrics, to support energy-efficient planning scenarios.

title: Intention of Young Adult Customers in Indonesia to Purchase Organic Food Products: The Theory of Planned Behavior and Health Self-Identity
summary: In response to growing interest in healthy and sustainable diets, this study extends the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) by integrating health self-identity (HSI) alongside attitude (ATT), subjective norm (SN), and perceived behavioral con
content: In response to growing interest in healthy and sustainable diets, this study extends the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) by integrating health self-identity (HSI) alongside attitude (ATT), subjective norm (SN), and perceived behavioral control (PBC) to examine Indonesian consumers' organic food purchase intentions, with trust and habitual behavior serving as mediating variables. A structured survey was administered to 110 organic food consumers across Indonesia, and data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4.0 -- a variance-based approach particularly suited for predictive modeling with complex multi-construct frameworks and smaller sample sizes, requiring no distributional assumptions. Structural model results indicate that subjective norms significantly influence trust (beta = 0.299, p = 0.003), perceived behavioral control significantly influences habitual behavior (beta = 0.395, p < 0.001), and health self-identity significantly influences habitual behavior (beta = 0.288, p = 0.001). Furthermore, both trust (beta = 0.294, p = 0.003) and habitual behavior (beta = 0.424, p < 0.001) significantly influence purchase intention. Notably, attitude did not demonstrate a significant direct effect on either trust or habitual behavior in the Indonesian context. These findings highlight the importance of integrating HSI into the TPB framework and suggest that interventions targeting perceived behavioral control and health-conscious self-identity can effectively promote organic food consumption habits and, consequently, purchase intentions. Future research is recommended to apply multigroup analysis (MGA) to explore segment-specific differences across diverse demographic groups and to extend the model to broader cultural and generational contexts beyond the present Indonesian sample.

title: The Future Rise of Africa in World Politics and Global Governance: Historical Foundations, Contemporary Realities, and Prospects for Global Leadership
source: International Journal of Social Science Humanity & Management Research
summary: The twenty-first century is witnessing profound transformations in the global distribution of political, economic, and diplomatic power. Among the most significant developments is the increasing prominence of Africa as an emerging actor wit
content: The twenty-first century is witnessing profound transformations in the global distribution of political, economic, and diplomatic power. Among the most significant developments is the increasing prominence of Africa as an emerging actor within world politics and global governance. Historically, Africa played a pivotal role in the development of human civilisation through its contributions to governance, commerce, science, and culture. However, centuries of colonial domination, economic exploitation, and political marginalisation limited the continent’s influence within the modern international system. This study examines the proposition that Africa is poised to become a major force in global governance during the twenty-first century by analysing historical developments, demographic trends, economic transformation, technological innovation, regional integration, climate diplomacy, and geopolitical realignments. The current study adopts an interdisciplinary approach informed by Power Transition Theory, World Systems Theory, and Constructivist perspectives to explain how shifts in global power structures create opportunities for Africa’s emergence. The findings indicate that Africa possesses several strategic advantages that support predictions of increased global influence. These advantages include rapid population growth, a youthful demographic profile, abundant natural resources, expanding technological capabilities, growing regional integration through the African Continental Free Trade Area, and increasing participation in international institutions. This study also finds that the emergence of a multipolar world order has created opportunities for African states to diversify partnerships and strengthen bargaining power within global governance frameworks. Furthermore, Africa’s leadership in climate justice advocacy, renewable energy development, and peacekeeping operations enhances its normative and diplomatic influence. Despite persistent challenges such as governance deficiencies, political instability, economic inequality, and external dependency, the evidence suggests that Africa is increasingly positioned to become a significant actor within international affairs. The present study concludes that Africa’s rise represents not merely a future possibility but a highly probable geopolitical transformation supported by both historical patterns and contemporary realities.

title: Socio-spatial patterns of energy citizenship components in contemporary Hungary
summary: Energy citizenship has recently emerged as a key concept in the social sciences related to energy transition, yet its definition, components, and societal manifestations remain underexplored. This paper contributes to this discussion by ana
content: Energy citizenship has recently emerged as a key concept in the social sciences related to energy transition, yet its definition, components, and societal manifestations remain underexplored. This paper contributes to this discussion by analysing the socio-spatial patterns of energy citizenship components in Hungary, based on a representative national survey ( N = 1000) conducted in early 2023. Based on literature, four constitutive components were operationalised: participation, pro-sustainability energy-use practices, prosumerism and pro-sustainability attitudes. Using hierarchical cluster analysis, we identified four distinct societal groups: everyday reduction practitioners, highly aware citizens, disengaged consumers, and transition pioneers, each featuring specific socio-spatial profiles. Our findings reveal that energy citizens characterised by the high level of all constitutive components are not identifiable as a distinct social group in the Hungarian context, instead, the components of energy citizenship appear in fragmented combinations across the population. This challenges ideal-typical views of energy citizenship as a coherent social condition and highlights contextual factors, including structural constraints that shape citizens' agency in becoming energy citizens, including housing type, available infrastructure, resources, the policy context and political culture. Our findings, beyond their scientific contribution, offer guidance for differentiated policy interventions to promote energy citizenship and energy transition.

title: Estimating economy-wide mineral commodity consumption using hybrid input-output modeling: a case study of fluorspar
summary: Understanding economy-wide material flows is of increasing importance as industries and governments seek to develop secure supply chains for critical minerals while mitigating negative social and environmental impacts. To advance research m
content: Understanding economy-wide material flows is of increasing importance as industries and governments seek to develop secure supply chains for critical minerals while mitigating negative social and environmental impacts. To advance research merging economy-wide material flow accounting with economic impact analysis, we adapt the integrated hybrid input-output analysis framework to build a mixed-unit model of mineral commodity processing in the United States. As a test case we apply the approach to fluorspar and derived fluorine-based chemicals, presenting one of a few models of fluorspar's domestic supply chain. We then estimate demand for this critical mineral that would be induced by projected sales of two emerging technologies, semiconductors and lithium-ion batteries, which are expected to contribute substantially to increasing demand. We find that near-term U.S. demand for fluorspar and its derivatives for use in semiconductors but not for use in lithium-ion batteries may surpass recent economy-wide domestic consumption of these materials. Modeling an increase in U.S. production of advanced chips in line with expressed targets results in 1% to 5% more fluorspar demand per year compared to the baseline. Global sensitivity analysis demonstrates an approach to factor prioritization applied to physical input-output table (PIOT) construction. We find the two major sources of physical flow data uncertainty, the ratios used to allocate national use to industries and the assumption used to partition exports into their domestic and foreign components, contribute about equally to uncertainty in the output. However, we also find the uncertainty in choice between several approaches to compiling the allocation ratios leads to most uncertainty in total physical output.

title: The assessment of the presentations at the Fourth International Conference on Real Estate Development and Management (ICREDM 2025)
summary: The climate crisis, financial fluctuations, and urbanization pressures have transformed the real estate sector from a purely economic activity into a multi-layered policy domain. This study evaluates the thematic content and sectoral reflec
content: The climate crisis, financial fluctuations, and urbanization pressures have transformed the real estate sector from a purely economic activity into a multi-layered policy domain. This study evaluates the thematic content and sectoral reflections of the Fourth International Conference on Real Estate Development and Management (ICREDM 2025), held in Ankara on February 3–5, 2025. Structured around the main theme “Residential and Commercial Real Estate Markets Under Climate Crisis and Financial Risk and Their Future,” the conference brought together more than 130 academics, experts and other stakeholders from over 20 countries and comprehensively addressed multidisciplinary topics. Through qualitative analysis, the study examines more than 100 papers presented at the conference, as well as its 14 thematic sessions, 3 panel sessions, and 1 roundtable meeting. The roundtable meeting produced strategic outcomes on the discipline's institutionalization, education reforms, and the definition of sectoral competencies. The conference covered eight topics: the impacts of disaster risk and the climate crisis on real estate markets; the integration of artificial intelligence and digital technologies into the sector; the transformation of valuation processes; the restructuring of housing security and social housing policies; and green finance and the circular economy. ICREDM 2025 stands out not merely as an academic event but also as a platform for redefining the real estate development and management discipline in line with the principles of social responsibility, sustainability, and strategic governance. The conference's output contributes to developing a collective vision for the discipline's future while also strengthening the production of practice-oriented knowledge.

title: Apigenin: Antihypertensive Effects and Underlying Mechanisms — A Comprehensive Review
summary: Abstract: Apigenin, a ubiquitous dietary flavone from vegetables, fruits and herbal teas, exhibits multi-target hypotensive effects, yet its poor water solubility limits oral bioavailability and industrial translation. Previous reviews only
content: Abstract: Apigenin, a ubiquitous dietary flavone from vegetables, fruits and herbal teas, exhibits multi-target hypotensive effects, yet its poor water solubility limits oral bioavailability and industrial translation. Previous reviews only summarized its general bioactivities and anti-atherosclerotic effects, without comprehensively analyzing its antihypertensive mechanisms. Most evidence derives from preclinical studies; human trials merely use crude celery seed extracts instead of purified apigenin, lacking reliable clinical proof for its antihypertensive efficacy. This review summarizes apigenin’s sources, chemical properties, safety and solubility-enhanced delivery systems to support functional food exploitation. We elaborate four core antihypertensive pathways, and also point out translational bottlenecks and propose strategies including food-grade nanoformulation and standardized clinical trials. This work links preclinical mechanisms to food industry application, providing theoretical evidence for developing apigenin-enriched functional foods for hypertension adjuvant intervention. Keywords: apigenin, hypertension, antioxidant, anti-inflammation, blood pressure, flavone

title: Antibody-based biosensors for tetracycline residues in foods: analytical performance, matrix effects, and practical challenges
summary: Widespread tetracycline use in livestock and aquaculture creates a need for timely residue screening across food production and supply chains. Chromatographic methods provide reliable residue quantification and confirmation, but their labor
content: Widespread tetracycline use in livestock and aquaculture creates a need for timely residue screening across food production and supply chains. Chromatographic methods provide reliable residue quantification and confirmation, but their laboratory requirements limit rapid screening at production sites. This critical narrative review examines 15 illustrative antibody-based or antibody-containing hybrid biosensor platforms, evaluating antibody format, assay architecture, signal transduction, sample preparation, and validation in relation to food quality-control decisions. Food-matrix studies are prioritized, with environmental-water evidence considered complementary. Fluorescence and membrane-based assays have the strongest direct food-matrix evidence, whereas several electrochemical, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, surface plasmon resonance, recombinant-antibody, and hybrid approaches have limited validation in food. Broad antibody cross-reactivity can support tetracycline-class screening but restricts compound-specific interpretation. These biosensors could serve as preliminary quality-control tools at production checkpoints, helping identify samples or lots requiring temporary holding, resampling, investigation, or confirmatory testing. Their use could support timely, risk-based decisions and more efficient allocation of laboratory resources. Practical implementation requires validation in authentic food matrices, reliable classification at relevant screening thresholds, reproducible device manufacturing, feasible sample preparation, and documented workflow time and cost. Positive or uncertain screening results should undergo chromatographic confirmation before definitive compliance or lot-disposition decisions.

title: Isolation and Phenotypic Characterization of Culturable Bacteria Associated with Spoiled Onion Bulbs (Allium cepa L.) Sold in Selected Markets of Dutse Metropolis, Jigawa State, Nigeria
summary: Spoilage of onion bulbs causes economic losses and may pose health risks, and bacterial contamination is one of its main contributors. This study isolated and characterised culturable bacteria associated with spoiled onion bulbs sold in Dut
content: Spoilage of onion bulbs causes economic losses and may pose health risks, and bacterial contamination is one of its main contributors. This study isolated and characterised culturable bacteria associated with spoiled onion bulbs sold in Dutse metropolis, Jigawa State, Nigeria. Ten spoiled onion samples (five each from Hakimi Street and Sabuwar Kasuwa markets) were aseptically prepared, serially diluted, and plated on nutrient agar. Isolates were characterised by colony morphology, Gram staining, microscopy, and biochemical tests. Colony counts ranged from 5.5 × 10⁴ CFU/mL (H5) to 4 × 10⁵ CFU/mL (H4) among Hakimi Street samples and from 5.5 × 10⁴ CFU/mL (SW3) to 4.5 × 10⁵ CFU/mL (SW4) among Sabuwar Kasuwa samples. Phenotypic characteristics indicated Staphylococcus spp. (30%), Micrococcus spp. (30%), Escherichia coli (20%), and Klebsiella spp. (20%). All isolates were catalase positive; the Staphylococcus isolates were coagulase positive, whereas E. coli, Micrococcus spp., and Klebsiella spp. were coagulase negative. Because identification relied on phenotypic characteristics only, the isolates are presumptive, and their occurrence indicates association with spoiled onions rather than proof that they caused the spoilage. Further studies using molecular identification and pathogenicity tests are recommended to establish species-level identities and the organisms responsible for spoilage.

title: AgriCopilot: An Offline-Capable, Edge-Native Single-Page Architecture for Precision Agronomy and Inter-Market Price Routing
summary: Smallholder farmers in developing regions face compounding challenges: unreliable soil-crop align-ment, non-transparent advisory systems, post-harvest price collapses caused by seasonal overproduction, and cycle-bound high-interest debt.Exi
content: Smallholder farmers in developing regions face compounding challenges: unreliable soil-crop align-ment, non-transparent advisory systems, post-harvest price collapses caused by seasonal overproduction, and cycle-bound high-interest debt.Existing agri-tech solutions often function in silos, depending heavily on high-cost IoT hardware or continuous cloud connectivity while lacking local language support.This study presents AgriCopilot, an offline-first Single-Page Application (SPA) designed to run edge-native Explainable AI (XAI) directly within client web browsers.Operating through HTML5 Canvas memory buffers, the system executes an image-based soil classification pipeline in under 50 ms without external server calls.The model computes a 9-dimensional color-texture feature vector-comprising CIE-L * a * b * coordinates, hematite redness metrics, or-ganic carbon indicators, Laplacian roughness, and normalized chromaticities-to categorize soils across six major Indian taxonomic orders.A biophysical stress engine applies non-linear penalties for temperature and precipita-tion anomalies using physiological thresholds established by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), generating a composite Plant Health Score and flagging visual soil mismatches.When critical stress is detected, the engine ranks climate-resilient alternative crops and updates system variables with single-tap interaction.To mitigate localized price drops, a supply-elasticity model detects regional sowing saturation (> 80%), while a geospatial routing engine evaluates road winding factors and freight costs to identify profitable interstate termi-nal markets.Finally, the platform categorizes financial support options (e.g., the 4.0% Kisan Credit Card vs. the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund) based on landholding threshold criteria, delivering explanations through client-side voice synthesis across six regional languages.

title: 户用级光伏耦合闭环温室体系:干旱高海拔区蔬菜自维持单元与阶梯扩散范式 Household-Scale Photovoltaic Coupled Closed-Loop Greenhouse System: Vegetable Self-Sustaining Units and Stepwise Diffusion Paradigm in Arid High-Altitude Regions
