title: Stabilizing High-Load Food Waste Digesters: Bioaugmentation versus pH Adjustment Effects on Microbial Consortium Dynamics and Methanogenesis
summary: High organic loading of food waste digesters often causes volatile fatty acid (VFA) accumulation, ammonia inhibition, and process failure. This study compared pH adjustment with bioaugmentation using a rumen-derived syntrophic consortium (F
content: High organic loading of food waste digesters often causes volatile fatty acid (VFA) accumulation, ammonia inhibition, and process failure. This study compared pH adjustment with bioaugmentation using a rumen-derived syntrophic consortium (FUD-BAC1) for stabilizing high-load food waste digesters, emphasizing microbial community dynamics and methane production. Three identical mesophilic (37 °C) continuous stirred-tank reactors (4.0 L working volume) were run in parallel, one reactor per treatment: an unamended control (R_Ctrl), a pH-adjusted reactor (R_pH; NaHCO₃ or NaOH added when pH fell below 6.5), and a bioaugmented reactor (R_Bio; single 10% v/v dose of FUD-BAC1). Biogas, methane, VFAs, total ammonia nitrogen (TAN), and culturable microbial groups were monitored for 27 days. The control produced minimal biogas (2.7 ± 0.8 L) and no measurable methane. R_pH produced 9.4 ± 1.2 L of biogas (43.6 ± 2.1% CH₄; 8.5 ± 1.2 L CH₄/kg VS), whereas R_Bio produced 19.4 ± 1.5 L (60.8 ± 2.5% CH4; 23.1 ± 1.8 L CH4/kg VS) and achieved the highest substrate degradation (79.2 ± 2.8%, versus 49.0 ± 3.2% for R_pH and 6.4 ± 1.5% for the control). Relative to R_pH, the specific methane yield of R_Bio was about 2.7 times higher. Final total VFA was 3,900, 2,650, and 1,800 mg/L, and final TAN was 2,800, 2,100, and 1,950 mg/L, in the control, R_pH, and R_Bio, respectively. Bioaugmentation was accompanied by higher counts of culturable anaerobic bacteria and methanogens, and by the isolation of presumptive syntrophic acetogens. Under the conditions tested, rumen-derived bioaugmentation was associated with more effective restoration of methanogenesis than pH adjustment alone; replicated, longer-term trials are needed to confirm these findings. This work relates to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production).

title: Conjugation of metal-organic framework (MIL-125) to NiFe2O4@CdS nanoparticles for enhanced photocatalytic hydrogen generation
summary: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. In this study, a ternary photocatalyst, MIL-125(Ti)/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS, was fabricated by in
content: Abstract Harnessing solar energy with semiconductors offers a feasible path toward sustainable hydrogen production via photocatalytic water splitting. In this study, a ternary photocatalyst, MIL-125(Ti)/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS, was fabricated by integrating a Ti-based metal–organic framework with a green-synthesized NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS binary core–shell heterostructure for visible-light-driven hydrogen evolution. Illicium verum Hook. f. (star anise) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for NiFe 2 O 4 nanoparticles preparation prior to the fabrication of the binary photocatalyst. The ternary composite was comprehensively characterized by structural, morphological, optical, and photoelectrochemical techniques. Compared with the individual components, the ternary photocatalyst exhibited enhanced visible-light absorption, a reduced band gap (2.42 eV), and a mesoporous structure with a BET surface area of 148.62 m²/g, pore volume of 0.5721 cm 3 /g, and a mean pore diameter of 15.0 nm. Photoelectrochemical analyses revealed improved charge separation, the lowest charge-transfer resistance, the highest photocurrent response, the largest electrochemically active surface area, and favorable band alignment. Consequently, MIL-125/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS achieved an initial hydrogen evolution rate of 1.62231 mmol g − 1 h − 1 and a cumulative hydrogen production of 10.20386 mmol g − 1 after 5 h, significantly outperforming CdS and the binary NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS. The photocatalyst retained approximately 60% of its initial activity after four reaction cycles, demonstrating good stability. The enhanced performance is attributed to the synergistic effects of MIL-125, which increase surface area, improve light harvesting, and promote efficient charge separation and transfer through a dual direct Z-scheme heterojunction. These findings highlight MIL-125/NiFe 2 O 4 @CdS as a promising photocatalyst for sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Inductive heating for photovoltaic module recycling and near-complete component recovery
summary: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) deployment is expected to generate substantial volumes of end-of-life (EoL) PV modules, given their typical lifetimes of 20–30 years. A key recycling challenge is separating polymeric encapsulants fr
content: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) deployment is expected to generate substantial volumes of end-of-life (EoL) PV modules, given their typical lifetimes of 20–30 years. A key recycling challenge is separating polymeric encapsulants from crystalline silicon solar cells without breaking the cells or leaving polymer residues on their surfaces. Here, we present an induction heating–assisted delamination method that rapidly separates ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) encapsulants from silicon cells without complex mechanical systems or hazardous solvents. Heating the cells at rates exceeding 28 °C s⁻¹ induces localized EVA decomposition at the cell–encapsulant interface without degrading the bulk EVA layer, enabling residue-free cell separation within tens of seconds. We also propose a modified glass-to-glass module design to further enhance recyclability and facilitate the recovery of individual components. The process recovers over 99.8% of module components by mass, including the EVA encapsulant, offering a rapid, scalable, and high-yield strategy for recycling EoL silicon PV modules. The growing number of end-of-life photovoltaic modules poses a major recycling challenge, particularly the removal of encapsulants without damaging silicon solar cells. Here, the authors develop an inductive heating approach that rapidly enables residue-free separation of encapsulants from silicon solar cells and achieves over 99.8% recovery of photovoltaic module components.

title: Applying the COPRAS Method for Stock Price Prediction: A Comparative Analysis of Selected Companies
summary: This paper explores the application in advanced algorithms and methodologies Stock price forecasting is extremely important as it has a significant financial impact, influencing investment decisions and market strategies accurate market for
content: This paper explores the application in advanced algorithms and methodologies Stock price forecasting is extremely important as it has a significant financial impact, influencing investment decisions and market strategies accurate market forecasting. Effective predictive models offer benefits beyond wealth creation, including early identification of failing investments to prevent market disruptions. The study acknowledges the inherent challenges in financial time series analysis—non-stationarity, nonlinearity, and high volatility—which necessitate continued development of more sophisticated analytical approaches. The research examines both internal factors (company profits, liabilities, competition) and external factors (oil prices, exchange rates, political stability) that influence stock prices. Traditional stock trend prediction algorithms rely on historical time series data, while newer approaches incorporate AI and Machine learning methods, including artificial neural networks (ANNs), are important in advanced predictive modeling and have shown better performance than traditional regression methods, though significant challenges remain in optimizing input variables and network architecture. The paper particularly highlights the promising performance The study uses Machine learning and deep learning approaches, particularly the use of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), are used to predict final prices. which outperform other methods. In addition, the research introduces a novel approach stock price prediction model, built on the basis of Dragonfly Algorithm (DFA)-optimized Deep Belief Network (DBN), which leverages market Sentiment analysis from social media data. For evaluation, this study uses the Complex Proportionality Assessment (COPRAS) method along with other multi-criteria decision-making methods (MCDM) methods, such as the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), are used in decision-making processes analysis. These methods help assess and rank different prediction models based on multiple criteria, providing a robust framework for addressing complex financial forecasting challenges. The integrated approach combining statistical methods with machine learning techniques based on technical analysis offers valuable insights for investors, particularly those focused on short-term investments. This research contributes to ongoing efforts to develop more accurate forecasting models, though acknowledges that no universal solution has yet been established.

title: Widespread tree-cover gains across Europe over two decades were strongest in regions of agricultural retreat
summary: Abstract Changes in canopy cover and spatial arrangement of trees can strongly influence ecosystem functioning and biodiversity. Yet, long-term, continent-wide assessments have largely focused on tree cover alone. Here, we develop an integr
content: Abstract Changes in canopy cover and spatial arrangement of trees can strongly influence ecosystem functioning and biodiversity. Yet, long-term, continent-wide assessments have largely focused on tree cover alone. Here, we develop an integrated framework quantifying tree cover, connectivity, and tree-cover heterogeneity, and assess their dynamics across Europe from 2001 to 2021. We further examine how trends in these metrics are associated with forest management regimes, agricultural retreat, natural disturbances, climate and human activities. The most widespread combination of structural trends, covering 23% of the analyzed area, combined increasing tree cover and connectivity with declining heterogeneity. At the landscape scale, 0.25° grid cells with larger fractions of former cropland tended to exhibit more positive trends in tree cover and connectivity and more negative trends in heterogeneity. These contrasting trajectories show that tree-cover gains do not necessarily coincide with increasing tree-cover heterogeneity, with potential benefits for carbon accumulation and forest-associated species but possible costs for species dependent on open or structurally heterogeneous habitats.

title: Polymeric nanocomposites for eco-friendly and industrial applications: a comprehensive review
summary: Abstract Polymeric nanocomposites (PNCs) are formed by dispersing fillers with at least one dimension in the 1–100 nm range in a polymer matrix, and the resulting materials often outperform either constituent alone. Because the interfacial
content: Abstract Polymeric nanocomposites (PNCs) are formed by dispersing fillers with at least one dimension in the 1–100 nm range in a polymer matrix, and the resulting materials often outperform either constituent alone. Because the interfacial area per unit volume scales inversely with the smallest filler dimension, a few volumes per cent of well-dispersed nanofiller can alter the mechanical, electrical, optical, magnetic and gas-barrier properties of the host polymer, at loadings substantially lower than those required with conventional micro-scale fillers. These benefits have attracted increasing attention from sectors such as water treatment, flexible electronics, aerospace shielding and food preservation. This review provides a thematically organised and critical overview of the PNC field. It first sets out the structure–property fundamentals (interfacial area, interphase volume, filler aspect ratio and dispersion state) that link nanoscale structure to macroscopic performance. It then compares four established fabrication routes (melt blending, in situ polymerisation, solution mixing and electrospinning) in terms of dispersion quality, interfacial bonding, scalability and environmental burden. Smart PNCs that respond to heat, light, electric and magnetic fields are compared with respect to mechanism, representative systems, advantages and limitations. The application sections compile quantitative data on dye and heavy-metal removal, sensing performance (detection limits and linear ranges), electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness and shelf-life extension, and discuss safety, migration and regulatory requirements for food-contact and biomedical uses together with life-cycle considerations. Finally, the review identifies persistent bottlenecks (filler agglomeration, cost, reproducibility, toxicological uncertainty and regulatory gaps) and sets out research priorities, including scale-up, long-term durability, standardised testing and techno-economic assessment, that could accelerate responsible commercialisation.

title: A just energy transition approach for the Global South: insights from Brazil for South Africa and beyond
source: South African Journal of International Affairs
summary: This article examines the institutional conditions shaping energy transitions in resource-dependent economies, drawing on Brazil’s experience to derive policy insights for South Africa and comparable African contexts. Transitions are often
content: This article examines the institutional conditions shaping energy transitions in resource-dependent economies, drawing on Brazil’s experience to derive policy insights for South Africa and comparable African contexts. Transitions are often framed as processes of technological substitution. This article argues instead that outcomes are determined primarily by institutional configurations that structure incentives, allocate risk and manage distributional conflict. Grounded in institutional political economy and the literature on directed technical change, the analysis focuses on four dimensions: fossil fuel rent structures; industrial policy sequencing; electricity market design; and development finance architecture. Brazil’s trajectory reflects institutional layering, with renewable electricity expansion occurring alongside hydrocarbon production. Comparison with South Africa highlights the limits of policy transfer in a more carbon-intensive and regionally concentrated political economy. Programmes such as the Renewable Energy Independent Power Producer Procurement Programme and the Just Energy Transition Partnership illustrate both the potential and constraints of procurement design and concessional finance.

title: GREEN INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL, CARBON EMISSION DISCLOSURE, AND FIRM VALUE: STAKEHOLDER PRESSURE AS MODERATOR
source: International Journal of Accounting Management Economics and Social Sciences (IJAMESC)
summary: This study aimed to examine the effects of Green Intellectual Capital and Carbon Emission Disclosure on firm value and to investigate the moderating role of stakeholder pressure in high-risk industry companies listed on the Indonesia Stock
content: This study aimed to examine the effects of Green Intellectual Capital and Carbon Emission Disclosure on firm value and to investigate the moderating role of stakeholder pressure in high-risk industry companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2024 period. The study employed a quantitative approach with a causal-explanatory design. The population consisted of high-risk industry companies, and a sample of 49 companies was selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 245 firm-year observations over five years. Secondary data were collected from annual reports and sustainability reports. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model and Moderated Regression Analysis. The results showed that Green Intellectual Capital had no significant effect on firm value, with a regression coefficient of −0.361 and a significance value of 0.392. Carbon Emission Disclosure had a significant negative effect on firm value, with a regression coefficient of −1.903 and a significance value of 0.001. Stakeholder pressure did not moderate the relationship between Green Intellectual Capital and firm value, with a significance value of 0.377, but significantly moderated the relationship between Carbon Emission Disclosure and firm value, with a regression coefficient of −5.831 and a significance value of 0.021. The adjusted coefficient of determination indicated that 78.66 percent of the variation in firm value was explained by the model, while the F-test confirmed that all variables simultaneously affected firm value with a significance value of 0.000. These findings implied that sustainability-related information was not necessarily perceived positively by the market, and that the effectiveness of sustainability signals depended on how investors interpreted the economic benefits and risks contained in the disclosed information.

title: Comparative in vitro metabolic profiling of six novel methylthiophene cathinones using different human liver systems and LC-HRMS/MS
summary: Synthetic cathinones represent a major class of new psychoactive substances associated with severe toxicological risks. Therapeutic cathinone derivatives such as amfepramone (appetite suppressant) were partially removed from the market due
content: Synthetic cathinones represent a major class of new psychoactive substances associated with severe toxicological risks. Therapeutic cathinone derivatives such as amfepramone (appetite suppressant) were partially removed from the market due to severe side effects. p-Tolyl-substituted synthetic cathinones are primarily known as new psychoactive substances and are associated with serious adverse events and abuse liability. Bioisosteric replacement of the p-tolyl ring with a 5'-methylthiophene moiety has recently emerged as a structural optimization strategy in this class and has led to the evaluation of methylthiophenes, a novel class of cathinone analogues. Knowledge of their hepatic biotransformation is essential for reliable toxicological detection and risk assessment. This study investigated the in vitro hepatic metabolism of six novel methylthiophene cathinones, 5Me-NM-BT (5-methyl-N-methyl-butanothiophenone), 5Me-NM-VT (5-methyl-N-methyl-valerothiophenone), 5Me-NE-BT (5-methyl-N-ethyl-butanothiophenone), 5Me-NE-VT (5-methyl-N-ethyl-valerothiophenone), 5Me-αP-BT (5-methyl-α-pyrrolidino-butanothiophenone), and 5Me-αP-VT (5-methyl-α-pyrrolidino-valerothiophenone) using pooled human liver microsomes (pHLM), pooled human liver S9 fraction (pHLS9), and HepG2 cells. Metabolites were characterized using reversed-phase and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry. Additionally, recombinant human monooxygenases were screened to identify isoenzymes mediating initial phase I steps. In total, 48 phase I and two phase II metabolites could be tentatively identified. Within each subgroup, the compounds showed similar metabolic profiles. Isozyme mapping revealed consistent contributions of various enzymes, including CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 suggesting a low risk of metabolism-based drug-drug interactions or single-enzyme polymorphism impact. Hydroxylated metabolites at the 5'-methyl group were consistently abundant across all models and, in combination with the respective parent compounds, represent promising analytical targets for toxicological screening.

title: CHALLENGES OF RENEWABLE ENERGY INDUSTRY IN MALAYSIA
source: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
summary: The purpose of this study is to highlight the challenges faced by the Renewable Energy (RE) industry in Malaysia. This conceptual review examines previous research and articles on renewable energy in Malaysia and internationally, including
content: The purpose of this study is to highlight the challenges faced by the Renewable Energy (RE) industry in Malaysia. This conceptual review examines previous research and articles on renewable energy in Malaysia and internationally, including current statistics, developments, and the status of renewable energy worldwide. The review covers key areas related to renewable energy, including its definitions, purposes, barriers, problems, challenges, principles, policies, strategies, and recommendations. The findings indicate that one of the major challenges faced by the RE industry is the high initial investment cost, which may discourage investors from financing renewable energy projects. Changes and inconsistencies in policies, together with insufficient government initiatives, also present significant challenges to the development of the industry. Therefore, government initiatives and appropriate measures, support from financial institutions and private investors, and cooperation among energy producers are crucial for ensuring the success and sustainable development of RE companies in Malaysia. This study is limited to reviewing and discussing the challenges affecting the RE industry in Malaysia. Future quantitative research is recommended to provide empirical evidence and further strengthen the existing literature. The findings may assist industry participants, including project developers, technology and product innovators, investors, financial institutions, and policymakers, in improving their knowledge and understanding of the challenges faced by the industry and the strategies that can be adopted. The study may also encourage greater cooperation and collaboration among stakeholders to improve Malaysia’s existing renewable energy structure and policies and support future policy development. Growing concerns regarding climate change and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues have increased global awareness of cleaner energy sources and measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and environmental impacts. Consequently, increasing demand for clean energy has strengthened the importance of addressing challenges affecting the RE industry.

title: O‘zbekistonda iqtisodiy o‘sish va issiqxona gazlari chiqindilarining ajralishi: dekarbonizatsiya ssenariylari va yashil multiplikatorlar
summary: The article addresses the assessment of the degree of decoupling between GDP and greenhouse gas emissions and of the multiplier effect of green investment in the context of rapid economic growth in Uzbekistan. On the basis of the latest off
content: The article addresses the assessment of the degree of decoupling between GDP and greenhouse gas emissions and of the multiplier effect of green investment in the context of rapid economic growth in Uzbekistan. On the basis of the latest official greenhouse gas inventory (2010–2022), the elasticity of emissions with respect to GDP is calculated and the emissions trajectory to 2035 is projected under BAU, moderate and accelerated decarbonization scenarios. A methodological framework is proposed for assessing the multiplier effects of green investment on output, value added, employment, imports and carbon on the basis of input-output tables. The results indicate relative decoupling, but absolute decoupling requires the carbon intensity of GDP to fall by more than 5.8 percent per year.

title: THE PRIVACY-PERSONALIZATION PARADOX: MAINTAINING MARKETING ROI IN A COOKIELESS, PRIVACY-FIRST WORLD
summary: For marketers, the shift to a cookieless, privacy-first digital world is a significant challenge: how to meet consumer expectations for privacy while ensuring the ability to personalize for marketing performance.The article explores the "Pr
content: For marketers, the shift to a cookieless, privacy-first digital world is a significant challenge: how to meet consumer expectations for privacy while ensuring the ability to personalize for marketing performance.The article explores the "Privacy-Personalization Paradox," discussing how regulatory policies like GDPR and CCPA are interrelated, how consumer perceptions of data use are evolving, and how third-party cookies are impacting the landscape.The paper examines the implications of this shifting landscape, drawing on insights from marketing, data ethics, and digital strategy, and proposes strategies for how organisations can adjust to the new world of non-trackable data.It examines new methodologies such as the gathering of first-party data, contextual targeting, AI-powered predictive profiling, and privacy-safe technologies, and how they may enable personalisation and compliance.The focus is on the strategic relevance of trust, with transparency and consent as key elements for customer loyalty and sustainable value creation.The conclusions of the article are that privacy requirements are not something to be avoided but an opportunity to innovate and to make privacy first practices a way to gain a new competitive edge in the future.

title: A Design of Real-Life Steel Structure: A Land Port Structure
source: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
summary: Land port buildings, formally designated as Integrated Check Posts (ICPs), constitute critical border infrastructure facilitating the regulated movement of passengers and goods across national boundaries.These structures demand large column
content: Land port buildings, formally designated as Integrated Check Posts (ICPs), constitute critical border infrastructure facilitating the regulated movement of passengers and goods across national boundaries.These structures demand large column-free enclosures to support seamless passenger flow, cargo processing, and multi-agency operations.This paper presents the structural analysis and design of a steel roof system for a land port building at the upcoming ICP at Jaigaon, West Bengal, covering a plan area of 72 m × 50 m with a clear height of 25 m.The design methodology follows a systematic approach encompassing geometry development through trial configurations, material selection conforming to IS 2062:2011, comprehensive load analysis as per IS 800:2007, IS 875, and IS 1893:2016, and structural member design using STAAD.Pro software.The final design employs double equal angle sections (2ISA) in a semi-circular arched truss configuration.All structural members achieved utilization ratios well below the prescribed safety limit of 0.90, with the maximum ratio being 0.609 for the top chord and column members (2ISA150×150×15).The total structural steel consumption was 4,214.57kN (approximately 42.95 metric tonnes of steel sections), with a total project cost of ₹6.81 crore for the steel superstructure, including roofing and cladding.Detailed structural drawings and a comprehensive bill of materials are presented to support practical implementation.

title: Cotton, Carbon, and Data: Tracing the Lineage of Environmental Injustice in the Aral Sea
summary: This paper argues that the destruction of the Aral Sea was, and remains, a structural act of environmental injustice. The paper employs a tripartite framework. It contrasts the indigenous “Traditional Nature Management” with the colonial “I
content: This paper argues that the destruction of the Aral Sea was, and remains, a structural act of environmental injustice. The paper employs a tripartite framework. It contrasts the indigenous “Traditional Nature Management” with the colonial “Ideologies of Domination” and critiques the modern aftermath through the lens of “Data Colonialism.” A closer examination of the archaeological, political, and economic record reveals a profound continuity. The Soviet fixation on cotton (“white gold”) has given way to a dual contemporary extraction: carbon, through natural gas drilling on the exposed seabed, and data, through the systematic harvesting of knowledge by international institutions. This paper demonstrates that the Aral Sea is not deteriorating through neglect; it is being actively maintained in a state of crisis to serve the interests of distant centers of power. Environmental justice in the Aral Sea basin demands the restoration of local sovereignty.

title: Financial and Technological Challenges in Sustainable Energy Infrastructure
summary: The sustainable energy infrastructure has influenced global energy networks, where the emphasis is on renewable energy implementation, grid modernization, energy storage, and digital transformation. The speed of this change is determined no
content: The sustainable energy infrastructure has influenced global energy networks, where the emphasis is on renewable energy implementation, grid modernization, energy storage, and digital transformation. The speed of this change is determined not only by technological challenges but more so by financial constraints. This review focuses on essential financial and technological challenges regarding sustainable energy infrastructure, with regard to investment volumes, investment risks, renewable energy integration, energy storage, smart grid development, digitalization, and infrastructure resilience. The authors apply a systematic review of peer-reviewed articles, global energy reports, and governmental studies for the identification of common barriers, emerging solutions, and important directions of research with regard to different economic and geographical contexts. A review of the evidence shows that finance remains a key barrier to adoption. It is predicted that clean-energy investment needs will rise by around 40% by 2030 from current levels. Apart from that, an insufficient level of energy storage capacity as well as cybersecurity threats and its lack of specialized skills constitute hurdles to clean energy use. There are some positive signs – technologies such as digital energy management, AI, advanced batteries, or smart-grid offer possibilities for making systems more efficient and flexible. In general, prosperity of the clean energy transformation demands finance and technological innovations, supportive policies, and infrastructure planning.

title: ACCOUNTING DATA AND AI FOR SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT DECISIONS: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL AND SCENARIO ANALYSIS
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: Decisions on agricultural biomass use require the integration of accounting data, technical constraints, market conditions, and the economic value of energy substitution. This study aims to substantiate a conceptual model for supporting sus
content: Decisions on agricultural biomass use require the integration of accounting data, technical constraints, market conditions, and the economic value of energy substitution. This study aims to substantiate a conceptual model for supporting sustainable management decisions that combines accounting data, artificial intelligence (AI) forecasting, and linear optimization, and to test its optimization component through scenario analysis. The methodology includes a thematic review of international research, data-provenance mapping, single-period linear programming, and sensitivity analysis using aggregated indicators from an agricultural enterprise for 2024–2025. The case examines the allocation of cereal straw among direct sales, processing into solid biofuel, and internal energy use. The model distinguishes verified accounting and operational facts from management assumptions, derived indicators, and forecast parameters, thereby linking each material input to its source, availability date, and role in the optimization problem. Under baseline conditions, 4,750 t remain for allocation from a maximum available volume of 5,000 t after 5% losses. The calculated solution allocates 4,000 t to internal energy use and 750 t to processing, with an economic objective value of UAH 25.475 million. Scenario analysis shows that the recommended allocation changes in response to losses, the finished-biofuel price, and the economic value of energy substitution. Switching thresholds are UAH 7,368.42/t for the biofuel price relative to direct straw sales and UAH 6,500/t for the value of energy substitution relative to processing, with other parameters unchanged. The contribution lies in formalizing a traceable link between accounting information, forecast parameters, and optimization-based management choices. The objective value is not accounting profit, environmental effects were not measured, and the AI module was not trained or independently tested. Future validation therefore requires dated observations, forecast-accuracy testing and comparison of realized economic decision outcomes.

title: Whose passport is it anyway? A decentralized web3-inspired architecture for sovereign digital product passports in the circular economy
summary: Abstract The circular economy (CE) relies on active consumer participation in reuse, resale, and repair markets. Digital product passports (DPPs) offer a promising approach by providing verifiable product information. Yet, current research
content: Abstract The circular economy (CE) relies on active consumer participation in reuse, resale, and repair markets. Digital product passports (DPPs) offer a promising approach by providing verifiable product information. Yet, current research neglects the asymmetric information access in the CE, particularly the disadvantaged position of end consumers. Addressing this gap, we adopt a Design Science Research (DSR) approach to develop a decentralized, wallet-based DPP architecture designed to enable sovereign, long-term product data access. Our system combines digital wallets, verifiable credentials (VCs), and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to enable issuer-independent data transferability and dynamic ownership management. Decoupling data authenticity (via VCs) from ownership (via NFTs) allows product data to remain accessible and verifiable, even if issuers exit the market. The architecture is designed to enable consumers to act as long-term custodians of product information, with the aim of granting them sovereign control across ownership transitions. We introduce four generalizable design principles that advance prescriptive knowledge on decentralized, issuer-independent DPP architectures and their potential to support end consumer data sovereignty.

title: High-Pressure Solid–Liquid Equilibrium and Volumetric Behavior of Choline Chloride-Based Eutectic Solvents
summary: Abstract Over the past two decades, eutectic solvents (ESs) have attracted attention due to their potential in various fields, from chemical processing to materials science. Despite this growing interest, their use is still restricted to fi
content: Abstract Over the past two decades, eutectic solvents (ESs) have attracted attention due to their potential in various fields, from chemical processing to materials science. Despite this growing interest, their use is still restricted to fixed stoichiometric mole ratios. This limitation arises from the difficulty in accurately identifying eutectic compositions, a consequence of the scarcity of reliable thermophysical property data. In particular, properties such as density and solid–liquid equilibrium (SLE) remain poorly documented in the literature, especially under elevated pressure. In this context, this work reports SLE and volumetric data for mixtures of choline chloride with four hydrogen-bond donors: ethylene glycol, glycerol, 1,3-propanediol, and glycolic acid. SLE measurements were performed in the pressure range between 6 MPa and 25 MPa and compared with available data at atmospheric pressure. Density measurements were carried out for the ESs at their eutectic compositions over ranges of pressure (5 MPa to 50 MPa) and temperature (293.15 K to 353.15 K). The experimental density data were correlated using the modified Tammann–Tait equation, yielding average relative deviations below 0.45 %. Based on the fitted parameters, the isothermal compressibility ( $${\kappa}_{T}$$ κ T ) and the isobaric thermal expansivity ( $${\alpha}_{T}$$ α T ) were calculated. Both properties exhibited dependence on pressure and temperature, in agreement with the behavior of incompressible liquid systems. This study enlarges the thermodynamic database of ChCl-based ESs by providing the first high-pressure SLE data along with new volumetric measurements. These results improve the understanding of ES phase behavior and offer valuable inputs for thermodynamic modeling, process design, and the development of ES-based applications.

title: DEVELOPMENT, TRANSLATION AND PRELIMINARY VALIDATION OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND GREEN LOGISTICS MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT
source: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
summary: This study develops, translates, and preliminarily validates a measurement instrument designed to assess digital transformation–driven green logistics practices and sustainability within cross-cultural logistics environments. A multi-phase
content: This study develops, translates, and preliminarily validates a measurement instrument designed to assess digital transformation–driven green logistics practices and sustainability within cross-cultural logistics environments. A multi-phase methodological framework was applied, beginning with the conceptualization of constructs and the systematic generation of items based on established literature. Content and face validity were confirmed through expert evaluations, yielding strong CVI scores and demonstrating item relevance, clarity, and representativeness. The instrument was translated using standardized forward–backward procedures, followed by expert committee review to ensure semantic and conceptual equivalence. Cognitive debriefing further verified respondent comprehension, while a pilot test involving 30 logistics professionals provided evidence of acceptable internal consistency and survey feasibility. Structural validation procedures, such as Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), were intentionally deferred due to the small pilot sample size. Although the present study produced an Arabic version, the development and adaptation processes followed internationally recognized standards, making the instrument suitable for application in other linguistic and cultural contexts with appropriate adaptation. Overall, the study delivers a culturally attuned and conceptually robust pre-final instrument that lays the groundwork for future large-scale psychometric validation and empirical investigations into the role of digital transformation in advancing sustainable logistics practices.

title: SAFETY AND QUALITY EVALUATION OF SPIRULINA-FORTIFIED MILK DURING REFRIGERATED STORAGE
summary: The microalga Spirulina (Arthrospira platensis) is a rich source of protein in dairy products and has high antioxidant properties as a functional food ingredient.The cow milk samples were fortified with 0.25%, 0.50% and 1.00% Spirulina and
content: The microalga Spirulina (Arthrospira platensis) is a rich source of protein in dairy products and has high antioxidant properties as a functional food ingredient.The cow milk samples were fortified with 0.25%, 0.50% and 1.00% Spirulina and the unfortified milk was taken as control.Milk samples fortified with Spirulina were subjected to physicochemical, phytochemical, antioxidant, microbiological, and sensory quality assessment during the 15 days of refrigeration at 4 ± 1 °C.The amount of protein, total soluble solid, total phenolic content, total flavonoid content and DPPH radical scavenging activity increased significantly (p < 0.05) after fortification of spirulina in milk, which increased the nutritional and functional properties of milk.Additionally, fortified samples showed improved physicochemical stability and microbiological quality throughout storage, as seen by increased pH stability, decreased titratable acidity, and decreased coliform, yeast, and mold counts.Due to its unique green color and the algal taste, increasing the concentration of spirulina adversely affected the sensory attributes, such as sensory color, sensory flavor and overall acceptability.Among the treatments, 0.25% spirulina gave the best results in terms of improved microbial, antioxidant and nutritional parameters with an acceptable sensory parameter.The findings revealed that spirulina is a promising natural fortifying ingredient of functional milk with added value, which enhanced its nutritional composition, storage stability, and antioxidant properties.

title: The Role of Abstractions for Humans and Machines
summary: The chapter introduces the topic of modelling from the perspectives of both valuable abstraction for humans and machine learning models. Grounded in general model theory and semiotics, it highlights the overall philosophy underlying the thi
content: The chapter introduces the topic of modelling from the perspectives of both valuable abstraction for humans and machine learning models. Grounded in general model theory and semiotics, it highlights the overall philosophy underlying the thinking and frameworks on the quality of traditional models. The chapter provides a high-level overview of the most important goals of modelling, from the perspectives of human conceptual modelling and machine learning, and of how models used in society are developed as part of a social construction process. The models serve as the basis for systems that must support sustainable behaviour in organisations, digital business ecosystems, and society at large.

title: Economic growth targets, energy consumption constraints, and transboundary PM2.5 pollution: empirical evidence from China
summary: Government target management, a core institutional tool for optimizing resource allocation and improving governance efficiency, plays a pivotal role in air pollution mitigation. Using panel data from 225 Chinese cities spanning 2006 to 2022
content: Government target management, a core institutional tool for optimizing resource allocation and improving governance efficiency, plays a pivotal role in air pollution mitigation. Using panel data from 225 Chinese cities spanning 2006 to 2022, this paper employs a spatial Durbin model to investigate how economic growth targets and energy consumption constraints shape transboundary PM 2.5 pollution. The results show that economic growth targets significantly elevate local and neighboring pollution levels, whereas energy consumption constraints reduce pollution in both areas; their antagonistic interaction amplifies PM 2.5 spillovers. The joint effect of dual-target management exhibits spatial attenuation at approximately 500 km and a temporal breakpoint around 2013, marking a governance pattern transition from zero-sum games to win–win outcomes. Mechanism analysis identifies economic linkages and strategic interactions as core transmission channels, while heterogeneity tests reveal a west-to-east declining gradient in spillover effects. These findings provide actionable empirical support for local governments to set compatible economic and environmental targets and resolve the cross-regional pollution governance dilemma.

title: Beyond Intention: The Value-Attitude-Behavior Cascade in Sustainable Fashion Consumption Among Gen-Z in Pakistan
source: International Journal of Emerging Multidisciplinaries Social Science
summary: The fashion industry's environmental footprint has intensified scholarly interest in sustainable consumption, yet the psychological pathway from personal values to actual purchase behavior remains poorly understood, particularly in developi
content: The fashion industry's environmental footprint has intensified scholarly interest in sustainable consumption, yet the psychological pathway from personal values to actual purchase behavior remains poorly understood, particularly in developing-country contexts. This study develops and tests an extended cognitive hierarchy model of sustainable fashion consumption among Gen-Z consumers in Lahore, Pakistan. Building on Cognitive Hierarchy Theory, the model positions self-transcendence values, environmental concern, and fashion leadership as antecedents of attitude toward sustainable fashion, which in turn drives sustainable purchase intention and, ultimately, sustainable purchase behavior. Data were collected from 400 Gen-Z respondents (aged 18-27) using online and face-to-face structured questionnaires, and hypotheses were tested using SmartPLS 4. Results show that self-transcendence values, environmental concern, and fashion leadership each significantly predict attitude toward sustainable fashion, and jointly explaining 31.2% of its variance. Attitude significantly predicts purchase intention but the intention-behavior link is comparatively weak, explaining only 3.2% of the variance in purchase behavior. These findings confirm the cascading structure proposed by cognitive hierarchy theory while revealing a pronounced attitude-behavior gap.

title: Dilemma in Carotenoids Versus Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) Synthesis Using Haloarchaea as Cell Factories
summary: Microorganisms of the Haloferacaceae and Halobacteriaceae families (Archaea Domain) have been revealed as key players for the bioproduction of polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), a family of natural, biodegradable polyesters produced by different
content: Microorganisms of the Haloferacaceae and Halobacteriaceae families (Archaea Domain) have been revealed as key players for the bioproduction of polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs), a family of natural, biodegradable polyesters produced by different types of microorganisms as intracellular carbon and energy storage reserves and stress-resistance tools. Recent works have optimized the production of high-quality PHAs using cost-efficient processes that involve even the valorization of residues from other industrial processes, which are used as raw material for haloarchaeal growth and PHA production. Considering the physicochemical properties of those biopolymers, poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate)(PHBV) is currently a target in many biotech-based processes aiming at the production of bioplastics. In this context, the haloarchaeon Haloferax mediterranei is probably the most well-examined archaeal cell factory for PHBV production, with some successful processes already described to produce significant concentrations of PHBV. However, the go-to-market haloarchaeal PHBV strategy continues to be limited by the capacity to produce quantities of PHBV sufficient to meet market demands due to several biological and technological limitations. In this perspective, risks and limitations to produce haloarcheal PHBV, as well as hot topics that may contribute to accelerating the efficient upscaling production of PHBV (in terms of cost and time), are also discussed.

title: Integrated Hydrothermal Carbonization and KOH Activation of Mechanically Treated Municipal Solid Waste: Optimization of Adsorbents for BTEX Removal from Water
summary: Abstract The sustainable management of municipal solid waste (MSW) remains a pressing challenge, particularly for the under-sieve fraction generated during mechanical treatment (MT), which is currently landfilled. This study proposes an int
content: Abstract The sustainable management of municipal solid waste (MSW) remains a pressing challenge, particularly for the under-sieve fraction generated during mechanical treatment (MT), which is currently landfilled. This study proposes an integrated valorization route involving hydrothermal carbonization (HTC), followed by potassium hydroxide (KOH) activation to convert MT-MSW into activated hydrochar (AHC). Response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to systematically investigate the synergistic effects of activation temperature (500–700 °C) and KOH/hydrochar impregnation ratio (0.5–1.5) on specific surface area and BTEX (benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes) removal efficiency from water. Results demonstrate that moderate activation severity (600 °C, KOH/HC = 1.0) promotes the formation of a predominantly microporous structure (BET surface area: 440.7 m2/g; micropore area: 363.9 m2/g), achieving a total BTEX removal of 84.7%. RSM analysis showed that both activation temperature and KOH/hydrochar ratio significantly affected AHC yield and surface area, whereas activation temperature was the main statistically significant factor governing BTEX removal. Overall, the developed models provide a predictive framework for tailoring AHC properties by optimizing the activation conditions. These findings establish a viable circular solution for the upcycling of urban waste streams into engineered adsorbents for environmental remediation.

title: INFORMATION-ANALYTICAL DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEMS FOR INTERNATIONAL INVESTMENT IN THE CONTEXT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: The article aims to substantiate the role and define the functional capabilities of information-analytical decision support systems in international investment within the context of digital transformation, as well as to systematize the mode
content: The article aims to substantiate the role and define the functional capabilities of information-analytical decision support systems in international investment within the context of digital transformation, as well as to systematize the modern digital tools, analytical methods, and information components that facilitate the preparation and making of investment decisions. Achieving this goal involves examining the interrelationships among digital data sources, analytical technologies, forecasting and risk assessment mechanisms, and investment outcomes. The study systematizes modern digital technologies and information resources used in decision support systems for international investment, outlining their functional purposes; analyzes the systems' capabilities regarding data collection and integration, investment attractiveness assessment, market indicator forecasting, risk identification, and the modeling of alternative international investment scenarios; and substantiates a structural-functional model for the information-analytical support of international investment decisions, defining the connections between data sources, analytical tools, digital technologies, and decision outcomes. Furthermore, the article makes a theoretical and practical contribution to enhancing the soundness, timeliness, and adaptability of international investment decisions by integrating modern digital technologies, information resources, and analytical tools into a unified information-analytical decision support system. The scientific novelty of the study lies in the refinement of the functional-structural approach to the information-analytical support of international investment decisions through the systematization of digital technologies and analytical tools based on their roles in data collection, assessment, forecasting, risk analysis, and the formulation of investment alternatives. A structural-functional model of adaptive information-analytical support is proposed, integrating data sources, digital technologies, analytical procedures, investment decision-making mechanisms, and feedback into a single closed-loop system.

title: Governing seawater desalination: Connecting technical fixes and socio-political realities
summary: As the global water stress intensifies, seawater desalination (SWD) is increasingly deployed as a supply-side strategy for enhancing freshwater availability. Critical scholarship has questioned whether technically oriented approaches to des
content: As the global water stress intensifies, seawater desalination (SWD) is increasingly deployed as a supply-side strategy for enhancing freshwater availability. Critical scholarship has questioned whether technically oriented approaches to desalination adequately address the socio-political drivers of water scarcity and the governance conditions shaping desalination policy. Through a systematic review of 78 policy-oriented publications and applying qualitative content analysis, this study draws on Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) scholarship to identify the multidimensional elements required for sustainable governance of SWD. The results revealed 49 indicators categorized into economic, social, governance, environmental, and technical dimensions. Within the policy-oriented literature reviewed in this study, economic and social considerations were the most frequently addressed dimensions, while environmental, governance, and technical considerations appeared less frequently. To bridge this gap, we discuss an approach for making the socio-technical connections more visible by illustrating the intersecting interests across these five dimensions.

title: Intelligent Monitoring System for Broiler Chicken Houses Blower using Fuzzy Logic
summary: This research presents the design and implementation of an intelligent early warning system for monitoring blower performance in Closed House broiler farms. The system aims to reduce financial losses and mitigate livestock health risks caus
content: This research presents the design and implementation of an intelligent early warning system for monitoring blower performance in Closed House broiler farms. The system aims to reduce financial losses and mitigate livestock health risks caused by poor air circulation due to blower degradation or failure. It integrates multiple sensors, including anemometers for wind speed, MQ-135 for ammonia gas, and MQ-7 for carbon monoxide. Data are processed by an ESP32 microcontroller within a distributed architecture of two monitoring boxes connected via NRF24L01 wireless modules. A fuzzy logic algorithm enables multi-variable decision-making, allowing the system to activate backup blowers, trigger alarms, and send real-time notifications through Telegram. Experimental results confirm system reliability, with anemometer accuracy ranging from 85% to 92%, buzzer intensity reaching 92–115 dB, and stable wireless communication up to 91 meters. The fuzzy logic controller successfully classified environmental conditions and blower performance, generating tiered alerts (Warning 1, Warning 2, Emergency). The findings demonstrate that the proposed system provides a proactive and intelligent solution, offering greater adaptability than conventional threshold-based methods while supporting productivity and animal welfare in poultry farming.

title: Coprecipitation‐Enabled Scalable Synthesis of High‐Energy Density Polyanion‐Integrated Disordered Rocksalt Cathodes for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt‐ and nickel‐free high‐energy density lithium‐ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries t
content: ABSTRACT Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt‐ and nickel‐free high‐energy density lithium‐ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries that have been predominantly developed via mechanochemical routes. A prominent example is polyanion‐integrated DRX (DRXPS) cathodes, which rank among the best DRX cathodes reported to date in terms of reversible energy density, but have thus far been synthesized only mechanochemically via low‐temperature ball milling. Here we demonstrate a coprecipitation–enabled solid‐state synthesis of a DRXPS cathode, Li 1.67 Mn 1.5 P 0.17 O 4 , translating a mechanochemical route into a scalable process that is compatible with established cathode manufacturing infrastructure. The workflow programs precursor chemistry via coprecipitation of Mn 2 + with HPO 4 2 − and OH − , followed by a eutectic lithium‐salt‐assisted solid‐state reaction, enabling low‐thermal‐budget DRXPS formation (450°C, 30 min) in air. The reduced thermal budget suppresses particle coarsening and yields a mixed micro‐/nanoscale particle morphology, thereby eliminating the need for post‐synthesis particle pulverization. The resulting cathodes deliver 324 mAh g −1 (935 Wh kg −1 ), demonstrating that high‐energy density DRXPS can be realized within a manufacturing‐compatible workflow. This work establishes a direct pathway toward scalable production of metastable high‐energy density DRXPS cathodes and identifies precursor engineering as the key enabler.

title: CONCEPTUAL MODEL OF SUSTAINABLE FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS FOR ENSURING ENVIRONMENTAL-ECONOMIC RESILIENCE UNDER DIGITALIZATION AND GLOBALIZATION
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: This paper aims to develop a comprehensive conceptual model for the functioning of sustainable financial instruments to ensure the environmental-economic resilience of national economies under digitalization and globalization. It empiricall
content: This paper aims to develop a comprehensive conceptual model for the functioning of sustainable financial instruments to ensure the environmental-economic resilience of national economies under digitalization and globalization. It empirically evaluates the complex time-lagged effects of green bond issuances and investigates the moderating role of institutional, technological, and socio-economic context determinants. The empirical findings reveal a distinct two-phase, time-delayed impact of green bond issuances on macro-resilience. In the short term, green bond issuances induce a statistically significant temporary reduction in environmental-economic resilience due to initial capital deployment costs and increased debt service burdens. In the long term, absolute green bond issuance exerts a significant positive effect, proving their efficacy for structural ecological transition. Conversely, an increasing ratio of green bonds to GDP causes persistent short-term negative pressures, highlighting debt sustainability risks if green debt scales too rapidly. Furthermore, Network Readiness acts as a robust inhibitor of resilience across all time horizons, indicating the negative ecological footprint of digital infrastructure and AI-driven greenwashing risks. Globalization demonstrates a protective buffering capacity against short-term debt shocks, while standard institutional metrics show no direct statistical significance. The study’s primary outcome is the development of a multidimensional conceptual model of sustainable financial instruments functioning. It integrates digital technologies and a two-tier system for preventing greenwashing to effectively transform sustainable finance into macroeconomic resilience. Given that empirical analysis has demonstrated the existence of a time lag and short-term risks of debt overhang, policy recommendations advocate a systemic shift from aggressive volume expansion to the measured, regulated issuance of green bonds. The state strategy should combine rigorous digital monitoring of the targeted use of funds raised through sustainable financial instruments with the development of environmental safeguards for digital infrastructure, thereby minimizing financial shocks and ensuring the long-term growth of eco-economic resilience.

title: Contribution of Voisin Rational Grazing and Buffalo Production to Strengthening Food Security and Ruminant Livestock Sustainability Facing Climate Change
source: Asian Journal of Science Technology Engineering and Art
summary: The integration of alternative grazing systems and non-conventional livestock species in temperate mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the integration of Voisin Rational Grazing (VRG) and water buffa
content: The integration of alternative grazing systems and non-conventional livestock species in temperate mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the integration of Voisin Rational Grazing (VRG) and water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) production into livestock systems in Zacualtipán de Ángeles, Hidalgo, Mexico, focusing on interactions among local actors, production practices, and socio-institutional conditions. Guided by Hernán Thomas’s socio-technical perspective, the study adopted an exploratory, interpretive qualitative design involving 31 key informants selected through snowball sampling. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and examined using thematic and qualitative content analysis. The findings indicated substantial acceptance of VRG, with 67% direct agreement, which producers associated with pasture optimization, reduced feed costs, and improved herd management. Buffalo production, however, remained exploratory and fragmented, with reported interest of 40%. Market uncertainty, limited specialized technical assistance, and weak institutional support were identified as key barriers to its integration. These contrasting patterns contribute to socio-technical transition research by highlighting the uneven integration of grazing and livestock innovations within the same territorial setting. The study emphasizes the importance of cohesive socio-technical networks that connect production innovation with economic viability and ecosystem service conservation. Practical implications include tailored technical support and structured market development strategies. Future mixed-methods research could complement these findings by quantifying pasture characteristics and carbon sequestration.

title: Khalifah Fil Ardh sebagai Landasan Pengelolaan Pariwisata Berkelanjutan di Indonesia
summary: The growing environmental crisis threatening the sustainability of tourist destinations in Indonesia calls for a management framework that is not only ecological and economic, but also ethical-theological. This study examines the concept of
content: The growing environmental crisis threatening the sustainability of tourist destinations in Indonesia calls for a management framework that is not only ecological and economic, but also ethical-theological. This study examines the concept of Khalifah Fil Ardh (vicegerency on earth) in Islam as a philosophical and operational foundation for sustainable tourism management in Indonesia. Using a library research method with descriptive, analytical, conceptual, and critical approaches, the study analyzes primary Islamic sources, namely the Qur’an, hadith, and exegesis (tafsir), as well as contemporary academic literature on tourism, ecology, and Islamic studies. The findings show that the concepts of khalifah, amanah (trust), and ihsan (excellence) in Islam form a cohesive environmental ethic that is relevant as a foundation for developing sustainable tourism. The integration of maqasid al-shariah, particularly hifzh al-nafs, hifzh al-‘aql, and hifzh al-nasl, expanded to include hifzh al-bi’ah (protection of the environment), provides a normative framework that bridges Islamic values and global sustainability principles. Case studies of the Komodo National Park ecotourism area and community-based tourism management in Pentingsari Tourism Village, Yogyakarta, confirm that the values of vicegerency tangibly contribute to environmental preservation and local community welfare. The study offers a conceptual model, Khalifah-Based Sustainable Tourism (KBST), as an integrative framework with theoretical and practical significance for tourist destination management in Indonesia

title: Determinants of Indonesians’ behavior to use financial services
summary: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior, this research intends to determine and validate empirically the factors affecting individuals’ willingness and actual behavior towards the use of financial services when purchasing vehicles. Data col
content: Based on the Theory of Planned Behavior, this research intends to determine and validate empirically the factors affecting individuals’ willingness and actual behavior towards the use of financial services when purchasing vehicles. Data collection was conducted through a survey whereby responses were obtained through questionnaires that were circulated through Google Forms. To make sure that the respondents fit the criteria set by the research, purposive sampling method was adopted, with only those who were Indonesians having used financial services to purchase vehicles at least once in the last two years being chosen as the participants. Within three months of collecting the responses, 197 were obtained, and the analysis of the data was done through PLS-SEM. It is revealed that all four hypothesized variables, that is, attitude, corporate reputation, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control, significantly affect positively both customers’ willingness to use the financial service and their actual behavior. It can be concluded from the findings that apart from the evaluation made by individuals concerning the leasing service and its credibility, their ability to fulfill the financial and process requirements affect positively both their intention and behavior.

title: Post-harvest storage technologies for fruits and vegetables cultivation
summary: Post-harvest storage technologies play a crucial role in extending the shelf life, preserving the quality, and minimizing the loss of fruits and vegetables after harvesting. These technologies are designed to maintain optimal conditions for
content: Post-harvest storage technologies play a crucial role in extending the shelf life, preserving the quality, and minimizing the loss of fruits and vegetables after harvesting. These technologies are designed to maintain optimal conditions for fruits and vegetables, ensuring that they retain their nutritional value, taste, and appearance for longer periods. Techniques such as controlled atmosphere storage, refrigeration, ethylene management, and the use of natural preservatives are increasingly utilized in modern agriculture to reduce spoilage and wastage. Advances in smart packaging, storage chambers, and monitoring systems have enabled better management of temperature, humidity, and gas concentrations, making post-harvest storage more efficient and sustainable. This paper explores the latest post-harvest storage technologies, their impact on food security, and the challenges and opportunities for integrating these innovations into global supply chains.

title: Stata Replication Code and Analytical Dataset for "What Aggregate Environmental Policy Stringency Conceals: Carbon Intensity across Development Contexts and Initial Energy Conditions"
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This repository provides the compiled analytical dataset, Stata replication code, and supporting documentation for the study “What Aggregate Environmental Policy Stringency Conceals: Carbon Intensity across Development Contexts and Initial
content: This repository provides the compiled analytical dataset, Stata replication code, and supporting documentation for the study “What Aggregate Environmental Policy Stringency Conceals: Carbon Intensity across Development Contexts and Initial Energy Conditions” by Mohammad Rony and Makoto Kakinaka. The study examines conditional associations between environmental policy stringency and carbon intensity across 40 emerging and advanced economies over 1995–2020. The analysis distinguishes aggregate environmental policy stringency from market-based, non-market, and technology-support instruments and investigates heterogeneity across development groups and initial energy conditions. The repository contains the compiled analytical dataset (paper4_master_final.dta), three Stata do-files covering data preparation, main estimation, and supplementary analysis, together with a README, variable codebook, data-source documentation, and license information. The dataset was constructed by cleaning, merging, and harmonizing data from publicly accessible sources identified in Data_Sources.md. The underlying third-party data remain subject to their respective providers' terms and conditions. The analyses were conducted using Stata 19.5. The scripts retain computer-specific directory paths that users must adjust before execution. Required user-written Stata commands must also be installed. The compiled dataset is provided to facilitate replication of the reported analyses, subject to these software and configuration requirements. The estimated coefficients are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects.

title: Solar Power Adoption and Perceived Energy Security in Bangladesh through Perceived Financial Sustainability
source: Journal of Global Economics & Sustainable Development
summary: The impact of household solar power is that it can add to the reliable electricity services provided that, as long as additional operation is not uneconomical, it continues to operate. This paper focuses on exploring the relationships betwe
content: The impact of household solar power is that it can add to the reliable electricity services provided that, as long as additional operation is not uneconomical, it continues to operate. This paper focuses on exploring the relationships between solar power adoption, perceived policy support, perceived financial sustainability and perceived energy security in Bangladesh. The analysis is based on the reported partial least squares structural equation modelling results of 470 households using solar electricity. Four reflective constructs comprise twenty indicators. Measurement assessment shows that there is satisfactory internal consistency, convergent, and discriminant validity. The perceived financial sustainability and perceived energy security have a positive relationship with solar power adoption. Perceived support of the policy also has positive relations with both outcomes. The highest direct coefficient of the predictors of perceived energy security belongs to financial sustainability. The exact indirect coefficients are 0.118 which is the adoption of solar power and 0.071 which is the perceived policy support which has the bootstrap confidence intervals not equal to zero. The two directions indicate complementary statistical mediation. The model accounts 21.4% variation in financial sustainability and 31.6 % in energy security. The predictive assessment yields positive predictive relevance values of all endogenous indicators, but the gains are small over linear model benchmarks. The results endorse focusing on the persistence of affordability and home solar implementation and institutional helping. The cross-sectional perceptions cannot build causal impacts and gains of national energy security. The provenance of fieldwork has not been well documented in order to be independently verified.

title: ESG FACTORS IN THE TRANSFORMATION OF UKRAINE’S FINANCIAL ARCHITECTURE: INVESTMENT DIMENSION AND SUSTAINABLE FINANCE
source: Financial and credit activity problems of theory and practice
summary: This article examines the role of ESG factors in the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture in the context of sustainable development, focusing on investment processes and the development of sustainable finance. The theoretical
content: This article examines the role of ESG factors in the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture in the context of sustainable development, focusing on investment processes and the development of sustainable finance. The theoretical foundations of the transformation of financial architecture under the influence of the concept of sustainable development and the integration of ESG criteria into investment activities are considered. The research analyzes the current trends and prospects for implementing sustainable financing instruments, in particular green bonds. Attention has also been paid to the development of sustainable banking and the incorporation of ESG factors into the operations of banking institutions. The key risks and barriers to sustainable investment in Ukraine have been identified. The challenges associated with adapting the Ukrainian securities market to international sustainable finance standards are analyzed, and the prospects for its integration into global financial flows are outlined. The article proposes a conceptual model of the impact of ESG factors on the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture. The directions for the transformation of Ukraine’s financial architecture, taking into account ESG factors and European benchmarks for sustainable finance, are presented. The research findings indicate that implementing sustainable development principles is not only a factor in modernizing Ukraine’s financial architecture but also a strategic tool for enhancing economic resilience, investment attractiveness, and international competitiveness. It is argued that building a financial architecture based on the principles of sustainable finance and the integration of ESG criteria is a necessary condition for attracting foreign investment as part of Ukraine’s post-war recovery.

title: Toughening alkali-activated construction materials using nanocarbon composites from red mud-catalyzed plastic waste upcycling
summary: Plastic waste accumulation and cement industry decarbonization demand cross-sectoral solutions, with disposal-challenged red mud (RM) offering an opportunity. We couple plastic pyrolysis with RM catalysis to co-produce H2 and binder-compati
content: Plastic waste accumulation and cement industry decarbonization demand cross-sectoral solutions, with disposal-challenged red mud (RM) offering an opportunity. We couple plastic pyrolysis with RM catalysis to co-produce H2 and binder-compatible carbon nanotubes (CNTs)/RM composites, which serve as nano-toughening additives in alkali-activated materials (AAMs). We explore effects of RM-to-plastic ratio, feedstock and RM type on H2 production, CNT yield and structure. At an optimal RM-to-PE ratio of 1:4, 21.0 mmol/gplastic H2 and 262 mg/gplastic CNTs are obtained. At 1 wt% CNT dosage, CNTs/RM composite enhances AAM compressive and flexural strengths by 33.1% and 54.3%, respectively, increasing the flexural-to-compressive strength ratio by 16.4%. This improvement arises from fiber-bridging, pore-filling and nucleation effects of CNTs, and depends on CNT structural parameters. Here, we show that this scalable route converts wastes into low-carbon, cost-effective toughening additives, reducing carbon emissions, energy demand, and cost by 65.8%, 71.1%, and 13.6%, respectively, compared with conventional CNTs production. This study converts red mud and plastic waste into nanocarbon composites that strengthen and toughen alkali-activated materials, offering a route to upcycle two major waste streams into low carbon construction materials.

title: Cross-Sectoral Patterns of Circular Consumption Behaviours: Evidence from R-Strategies
summary: Transitioning to a circular economy requires not only systemic and technological change but also consumer engagement in circular practices. While circular economy research has extensively examined R-strategy frameworks, existing studies hav
content: Transitioning to a circular economy requires not only systemic and technological change but also consumer engagement in circular practices. While circular economy research has extensively examined R-strategy frameworks, existing studies have largely focused on organisational and supply-side perspectives, with limited attention to how these strategies are reflected in consumer behaviour across product domains and how such behaviours can be addressed through policy. This study investigates reported circular consumption behaviour across three key product sectors: household appliances, consumer electronics and apparel. Drawing on data from a survey of 1,000 adult consumers in Poland, the analysis focuses on seven consumer-relevant R-strategies derived from the wider 9R framework: Refuse, Rethink, Reduce, Reuse, Repair, Repurpose and Recycle. The study examines sector-specific reported prevalence, cross-sectoral reach and associations between analogous behaviours across sectors. The results show that prolonged product use, mapped to Rethink in this study, is the most commonly reported practice and has the broadest cross-sectoral reach. Refuse and Repurpose show lower prevalence and narrower cross-sectoral reach. At the same time, analogous circular practices are positively associated across product sectors, indicating that circular consumption is sector-sensitive but partly interconnected. Exploratory CART analyses further indicate that these pairwise associations are accompanied by hierarchical and subgroup-specific cross-sectoral patterns. These findings provide new insights for consumer policy. They suggest value in considering both sector-sensitive instruments and broader practice-based approaches. Product longevity represents a relatively widespread cross-sectoral practice that may warrant particular policy attention, whereas less commonly reported behaviours such as purchase refusal, reduced consumption and repurposing may warrant more targeted attention. Circular consumer behaviours show partial, strategy-dependent cross-sectoral consistency. Prolonged product use is the most prevalent and widespread circular practice across sectors. Policy implications point to both sector-sensitive and broader practice-based approaches.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SOLID-STATE HYDROGEN STORAGE AND PGM-FREE CATALYSIS USING HYBRID METAL-ORGANIC FRAMEWORKS AND SINGLE-ATOM CATALYSTS
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: "The El-Rakhawi Integrated Framework" revolutionizes hydrogen fuel cells by solving storage and catalysis bottlenecks. It introduces Hybrid Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) designed via machine learning for safe, solid-state hydrogen storage
content: "The El-Rakhawi Integrated Framework" revolutionizes hydrogen fuel cells by solving storage and catalysis bottlenecks. It introduces Hybrid Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) designed via machine learning for safe, solid-state hydrogen storage at near-ambient conditions (<50 bar), eliminating energy-intensive 700-bar compression. Simultaneously, it replaces expensive platinum with Platinum-Group-Metal-Free (PGM-Free) Single-Atom Catalysts (SACs) using transition metals on nitrogen-doped carbon, achieving near 100% atom utilization and reducing catalyst costs by over 95%. Performance is quantified by the Hydrogen Viability Index (HVI), a strictly bounded metric (0.0-1.0) evaluating storage density, catalytic efficiency, and economic viability. This approach transforms hydrogen technology into a scalable, mass-market clean energy solution. Author: Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23842622.

title: Digital Resilience of Software Development under Crisis: The Role of Remote Operations and Green Computing in Ensuring Operational Continuity in Gaza
source: مجلة كلية فلسطين التقنية للأبحاث والدراسات
summary: This study examines the impact of large-scale technological disruptions caused by the war in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 on software development projects, and the role of Resilient Technological Strategies (RTS), which encompass remot
content: This study examines the impact of large-scale technological disruptions caused by the war in the Gaza Strip since October 2023 on software development projects, and the role of Resilient Technological Strategies (RTS), which encompass remote operations and green computing practices, in maintaining operational continuity and organizational resilience.
