A quantitative descriptive-analytical approach was employed, using data collected from 150 software professionals, including software engineers, project managers, quality assurance engineers, and UI/UX designers. Data were analyzed using SPSS and AMOS through descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling (SEM). The findings indicate that infrastructure disruption is strongly associated with the adoption of RTS and, contrary to the hypothesized direction, shows a significant positive direct effect on operational continuity. RTS, in turn, significantly enhance operational continuity and partially mediate (complementary partial mediation) the relationship between infrastructure disruption and operational continuity. The study concludes that software organizations in war-affected environments can strengthen operational continuity and adaptive capacity through remote operational models, cloud-based solutions, and energy-efficient computing practices, contributing to the literature on digital resilience and crisis-induced technological adaptation.

title: Beyond the laggard myth: time-series analysis of AI job market dynamics in construction
summary: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to inte
content: Purpose This study presents one of the first time-series, cross-industry analyses of the artificial intelligence (AI) job market for the construction sector. It benchmarks construction against both digital and traditional industries to interrogate prevailing assumptions of linear diffusion and temporal catch-up in AI workforce adoption. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on 51 months of Lightcast job postings (January 2021–March 2025), with construction defined as ANZSIC Division E, the study employs an interpretable analytical toolkit comprising Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess decomposition (period = 12), month-of-year bootstrap tests on detrended series, cross-correlation analysis with bootstrap confidence bands, Newey–West trend estimation on sectoral share ratios and conservative one-step Exponential Smoothing State-Space (ETS) forecasts. All results are re-estimated excluding the partial final month (March 2025) as a sensitivity check. Findings Construction's AI hiring is very sparse, accounting for under 1% of AI postings and is more volatile than hiring in peer sectors, but it grew fastest: annual construction postings rose more than fourfold between 2021 and 2024, against increases of 13% and 9% in the digital and traditional sectors, whose postings peaked in 2022. Construction's share of AI postings relative to both comparators therefore rises (converges) rather than falls. No delayed-follower pattern is detected: no lag at which the comparator sectors lead construction is statistically reliable, and the short-run associations that are detected are weak, near-contemporaneous and sensitive to the sample end. Unlike the comparator sectors, construction shows no statistically significant within-year seasonality and short-horizon ETS forecasts do not improve on a seasonal-naïve benchmark. These findings are robust to the exclusion of the partial final month of data. Construction thus appears as a low-base, fast-growing entrant with its own hiring dynamics, not a “laggard” following digital-sector cycles with a delay. Practical implications The findings suggest that construction firms should prioritise internal capability building and domain-specific AI skills where external hiring is thin, support flexible, year-round upskilling, and design policy and vendor strategies tailored to the sector's operational realities rather than importing digital-sector playbooks. Originality/value This study provides among the first data-driven, time-series evidence that qualifies the dominant “late adopter” narrative in construction. It shows that construction's low level of AI hiring coexists with the fastest growth and a rising share, without a delayed-follower timing pattern, distinguishing a low starting point from a lagging trajectory and offering an empirically grounded alternative to technologically deterministic accounts of cross-industry AI adoption.

title: Banking regulation, digital innovation and sustainability: a bibliometric review and conceptual framework
summary: This study examines the connections between digital innovation, sustainability and regulation-centred banking research through a bibliometric review of 502 Scopus-indexed articles and reviews published across 267 journals between 2001 and 2
content: This study examines the connections between digital innovation, sustainability and regulation-centred banking research through a bibliometric review of 502 Scopus-indexed articles and reviews published across 267 journals between 2001 and 2 July 2026. Performance analysis, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, co-word analysis and thematic mapping distinguish thematic relationships, bibliographic proximity and shared intellectual foundations. Publication output grew at a compound annual rate of 15.61% over the complete years 2001–2025. The findings identify an established intellectual core centred on regulation, supervision, efficiency, profitability and bank risk. Sustainability-related vocabulary is closely associated with financial stability and prudential concerns, while climate-related contributions have limited connectivity in the selected co-citation network. Digital innovation forms recognisable thematic and bibliographic groups and also appears within broader regulatory research, but does not emerge as a distinct intellectual foundation among references meeting the co-citation threshold. The comparison indicates partial and uneven connections across the three analytical dimensions. Drawing on these patterns, the regulatory dialectic and institutional theory, the study develops a conceptual framework and seven testable propositions concerning regulatory adaptation, possible transmission channels and contextual conditions. These relationships remain hypotheses for empirical testing. The study contributes a differentiated assessment of integration and a research agenda linking regulation, digital capabilities, sustainability practices and banking outcomes.

title: Avipoxvirus outbreak in cutaneous lesions of the red-cowled cardinal (Paroaria dominicana) and red-crested cardinal (Paroaria coronata): detection by histopathology and transmission electron microscopy
source: International Journal of Environmental and Agriculture Research
summary: The red-cowled cardinal (Paroaria dominicana) and red-crested cardinal (Paroaria coronata) are birds of the family Emberizidae naturally found in northeastern and southern Brazil, respectively. These species are targeted by illegal trade be
content: The red-cowled cardinal (Paroaria dominicana) and red-crested cardinal (Paroaria coronata) are birds of the family Emberizidae naturally found in northeastern and southern Brazil, respectively. These species are targeted by illegal trade because of their colorful plumage and are considered potential viral reservoirs owing to their migratory characteristics. Avian pox is a highly infectious disease caused by poxviruses of the family Poxviridae and genus Avipoxvirus that affects domestic and wild birds. Between January 2006 and September 2007, 72 birds, including 14 red-crested cardinals and 58 red-cowled cardinals, were referred after sudden death by CRAS-PET to the Electron Microscopy Laboratory of the Biological Institute of São Paulo for investigation of viral agents. At necropsy, small cutaneous nodular lesions were observed on the feet of one red-crested cardinal and ten red-cowled cardinals. Some birds had lesions characteristic of avian pox on the feet and/or beaks, consisting of whitish or yellowish nodules and desquamating crusts. Lesion fragments were processed for histopathology and transmission electron microscopy. Light microscopy revealed hyperkeratosis, epithelial hyperplasia, hydropic degeneration, and eosinophilic inclusions corresponding to Bollinger bodies in skin and/or mucosal cells. Negative staining identified numerous typical poxvirus particles in ten crust-suspension samples from red-cowled cardinals and one from a red-crested cardinal. Some particles were enveloped and brick-shaped, with irregularly arranged tubules on the outer membrane, and measured 280 × 260 nm. Ultrathin sections revealed type A intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies, or Bollinger bodies, containing mature or complete oval viral particles measuring 330 × 260 nm, with a biconcave nucleus or dumbbell-shaped internal core. Type B inclusion bodies, immature particles budding from dense amorphous filamentous material, developing particles with spikes on their outer surface, fibrillar inclusions, and deformed nuclei with densely condensed chromatin were also identified. Immunocytochemistry with colloidal gold labeled viral particles and antigenic sites in intracytoplasmic vacuoles and cellular debris. This is the first record of avian pox in the red-crested cardinal (Paroaria coronata) and the second in the red-cowled cardinal (Paroaria dominicana).

title: CEO power and stock price crash risk: moderating effect of environmental practices
source: Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting
summary: Abstract This paper investigates the influence of CEO power on corporate stock price crash risk in developed market context, and further examines the moderating impact of corporate environmental practices. Two environmental practices are ex
content: Abstract This paper investigates the influence of CEO power on corporate stock price crash risk in developed market context, and further examines the moderating impact of corporate environmental practices. Two environmental practices are examined: greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and Sustainable Development Goal 13 (SDG-13 supporting climate action). Analysing data from publicly listed firms in the G7 nations from 2006 to 2021, empirical results show that firms led by more powerful CEOs are generally exposed to lower crash risks. Additionally, results show that companies implementing stronger environmentally friendly practices, particularly, supporting climate actions - SDG-13, see a further reduced crash risk. This pattern is especially evident in non-crisis period, non-financial firms, and firms with high environmental and social (ES) scores, i.e., Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) performance. The findings are validated by various robustness tests using alternative estimation models, alternative measures, and additional tests. Our findings provide practical implications for firms, investors, regulators, and policymakers.

title: Building capacity in institutional voids: carbon competency development among quantity surveyors in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment
source: Journal of Knowledge Risk and Sustainable Management
summary: Purpose This study assesses the training needs and competency strategies that quantity surveyors (QSs) perceive as important for enhancing embodied carbon estimation (ECE) in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment. It addresses gap in und
content: Purpose This study assesses the training needs and competency strategies that quantity surveyors (QSs) perceive as important for enhancing embodied carbon estimation (ECE) in Nigeria’s weak institutional environment. It addresses gap in understanding how global sustainability norms may be taken up by a profession traditionally focused on cost management, in a setting where institutional pressures remain limited. Design/methodology/approach This organization-based study collected data from 132 quantity surveying firms (QSFs) in Lagos, Nigeria, using a structured questionnaire covering 21 training needs and competency strategies. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to rank the perceived importance of these items and to identify the underlying competency clusters. Findings The factor analysis identified two clusters of perceived training needs and competency strategies: (1) technical and operational capacity building comprising skills for lifecycle assessment and the use of carbon digital tools; and (2) knowledge infrastructure and strategic integration, comprising systemic support such as carbon databases and online resources and industry guidelines. All 21 competency strategies were rated as highly important, suggesting that respondents did not strongly differentiate among them and regarded all of them as priorities for improving ECE. Practical implications The findings offer insights for academia, policymakers and professional bodies in the Nigerian built environment. Suggested priorities include a local embodied carbon database, industry guidelines, collaborative knowledge-sharing platforms, continuing professional development accreditation for ECE and phased, scalable multi-stakeholder implementation roadmaps. As the findings are specific to Lagos, Nigeria, implications for other developing countries and weak institutional environments should be drawn with caution. Originality/value The study offers three contributions. First, by showing that respondents attach high importance to ECE competencies in a context where formal requirements for ECE are limited, it provides a basis for further examining whether institutional pressures are the only route to competency development. Second, it proposes distributed competency as a conceptual lens, suggesting that sustainable construction competence may be better understood as drawing on socio-technical systems rather than on individual skills and knowledge alone. Third, it provides a data-driven structured categorization of perceived priorities for ECE competency development among construction cost professionals in Nigeria’s weak institutional context.

title: Drug Discovery for Snakebite Envenoming: Wanderings Amid Historical Antidotes and Emerging Therapeutic Opportunities
summary: Snakebite envenoming is acknowledged as neglected tropical disease affecting populations of regions with limited access to healthcare systems. However, it had posed a major threat to human health since classical antiquity, when plant- and a
content: Snakebite envenoming is acknowledged as neglected tropical disease affecting populations of regions with limited access to healthcare systems. However, it had posed a major threat to human health since classical antiquity, when plant- and animal-based remedies were extensively used as antidotes to counteract bites by venomous snakes. Although the provision of safe and effective treatments by 2030 is among the strategic objectives of the World Health Organization, clinically approved therapies currently available remain animal-derived polyclonal antibodies, which suffer from significant limitations, including high production costs, limited cross-species efficacy, and risk of adverse immune reactions. In this review, we survey some historical antidotes used to treat snakebite envenoming in classical antiquity and early modern Europe such as theriac, mithridatum, Orvietan and Mattioli's scorpion oil. We then discuss natural compounds that, while found also as active ingredients in medical plants used for the preparation of the historical antidotes, over the last decades have inspired research efforts aimed at characterizing their evidence-based antivenom activity with the aim of offering potential alternatives to biologic-based therapies. Finally, we outline emerging therapeutic opportunities that, arising from drug repurposing efforts, may pave the way for the development of novel, broadly effective therapies against multiple venomous snake species.

title: Design of an in-situ CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing equipment for nuclear reactor thermocouple column
summary: The CONOSEAL seal for the nuclear reactor thermocouple column belongs to the boundary seal of the primary circuit. When the sealing surface suffers from scratches, damages, or other defects, it will directly affect the sealing reliability a
content: The CONOSEAL seal for the nuclear reactor thermocouple column belongs to the boundary seal of the primary circuit. When the sealing surface suffers from scratches, damages, or other defects, it will directly affect the sealing reliability and result in leakage. However, replacing the thermocouple column is a complex process with huge workload and long period. To address these issues, an in-situ reactor thermocouple column CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing device is designed. Due to the in-situ structure and operation conditions, the repairing device is designed in a compact modular and light weighted manner. Repair tests have been conducted on a thermocouple column to verify the repair capability of the CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing device. A prototype of cycling test platform is established to simulate the in-situ conditions of the thermocouple column. The CONOSEAL sealing surface is repaired to achieve a surface roughness of Ra 1.712 μm and pressure tests according to RCC-M standard and thermal cycling tests are both performed on the thermocouple column. For the pressure tests, the measured pressure drops do not exceed 0.2 MPa during a 10 min pressure maintenance. In the thermal cycling tests, the pressure is maintained for 10 min under the pressure of 15.5 MPa and the temperature is 310 ℃ and there are no leaks. The test results show that the dimensions and roughness of the sealing surface after repairing by the repair device meet the requirements of the in-situ operation conditions. This verifies the capability of the CONOSEAL sealing surface repairing equipment.

title: Examining green practices in healthcare via organizational support and employee awareness and attitudes: A behavioral-capability perspective
summary: Healthcare sector contributes significantly to environmental challenges through resource consumption, waste generation, and supply chain activities. This is particularly true in developing countries where sustainable healthcare infrastructu
content: Healthcare sector contributes significantly to environmental challenges through resource consumption, waste generation, and supply chain activities. This is particularly true in developing countries where sustainable healthcare infrastructure remains limited. This study examines the relationships among employees’ awareness and attitudes, organizational support, and green supply chain management practices in Bangladeshi hospitals. Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior and the Resource-Based View. We collected data from 436 healthcare professionals and analyzed them using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. The findings suggest that employees’ environmental awareness and attitudes are associated with GSCM practices both directly and indirectly through organizational support. Organizational support is strongly associated with GSCM adoption and partially mediates the relationship between awareness and attitudes and GSCM practices. It may not be sufficient to explain sustainable supply chain practices without supportive organizational mechanisms such as leadership commitment, environmental training, and resource allocation. This study contributes contextual evidence on GSCM adoption in healthcare organizations operating in a resource-constrained developing-country setting. The findings also provide practical insights for strengthening sustainability initiatives within hospitals.

title: Upcycling Cotton–Polyester Textile Waste Into High Quality Biochar and Activated Carbon for Energy Storage Applications
summary: The rapid increase in textile waste generation from fast fashion and population growth calls for innovative waste management and valorization technologies. This study converts textile waste into high‐surface‐area carbon materials through a
content: The rapid increase in textile waste generation from fast fashion and population growth calls for innovative waste management and valorization technologies. This study converts textile waste into high‐surface‐area carbon materials through a simple pyrolysis process and investigates the synergistic behavior of thermally decomposing woven cotton–polyester materials. Three waste types‐pure cotton, a 1:1 cotton–polyester blend, and pure polyester—were carbonized at 400, 500, and 600 °C with a slow heating rate (4 °C/min) under nitrogen. The cotton–polyester blend carbonized at 500 °C yielded the highest surface area (576 m 2 /g), outperforming cotton (197 m 2 /g) and polyester (287 m 2 /g). The optimized biochars were subsequently converted into activated carbons via KOH activation, significantly increasing their surface areas (2537 and 1129 m 2 /g for cotton‐ and cotton–polyester‐derived activated carbons, respectively). Electrochemical evaluation of these activated carbons revealed specific capacitances of 112 F/g for cotton‐derived activated carbon and 58.3 F/g for cotton–polyester‐derived activated carbon at 1 A/g. This work demonstrates a scalable approach to upcycle textile waste into high‐performance carbon materials, advancing circular economy initiatives and renewable energy storage technologies.

title: Who gains most from fuel subsidies and manufacturing sector strengthening? Evidence from Indonesia’s social accounting matrix
summary: This study analyses the distributional impacts of fuel subsidies and manufacturing-sector strengthening on household income and sectoral output in Indonesia. Using Indonesia’s 2022 Social Accounting Matrix (SAM), the study applies multiplie
content: This study analyses the distributional impacts of fuel subsidies and manufacturing-sector strengthening on household income and sectoral output in Indonesia. Using Indonesia’s 2022 Social Accounting Matrix (SAM), the study applies multiplier decomposition and policy simulation to trace how these policies transmit income effects across household income groups and economic sectors. The results show that high-income households received the largest nominal income gains, amounting to IDR 654.78 trillion, while low-income households experienced the highest percentage income growth, at 3.99%. The manufacturing sector recorded the highest global multiplier values across all channels, including income creation (1.47), institutions (4.88), the production sector (10.58), and commodities (9.87), confirming its role as a key driver of economic activity through strong backward and forward linkages. However, the distribution of benefits across household groups remained structurally uneven. High-income households consistently recorded higher open-loop and closed-loop multipliers than low-income households, reflecting their greater capacity to capture, circulate, and reinvest the effects of fiscal injections. These findings suggest that fuel subsidies and manufacturing-sector strengthening generate broadly positive but unevenly distributed economic effects: proportionally pro-poor but nominally pro-rich. Tighter subsidy targeting, combined with continued investment in inclusive manufacturing linkages, is essential to ensure that these policies deliver more equitable and broad-based income growth across household groups in Indonesia.

title: Rekonstruksi Indikator Kesejahteraan Ekonomi Dari GDP Menuju Falah Dalam Perspektis Ekonomi Islam
summary: Produk Domestik Bruto (PDB) sebagai tolok ukur utama kemajuan ekonomi dinilai cacat secara konseptual karena hanya mengukur transaksi pasar kuantitatif, mengabaikan dimensi ketimpangan sosial, kerusakan lingkungan, serta kesejahteraan spiri
content: Produk Domestik Bruto (PDB) sebagai tolok ukur utama kemajuan ekonomi dinilai cacat secara konseptual karena hanya mengukur transaksi pasar kuantitatif, mengabaikan dimensi ketimpangan sosial, kerusakan lingkungan, serta kesejahteraan spiritual masyarakat. Penelusuran literatur menunjukkan empat kesenjangan utama yang belum terpecahkan: kesulitan mengkuantifikasi dimensi spiritual, kesenjangan konseptual antara kategorisasi fikih klasik dan psikologi kontemporer, jarak antara teori normatif maqāṣid dengan praktik kebijakan, serta ketiadaan mekanisme non-kompensasi antardimensi dalam indeks kesejahteraan yang ada. Penelitian ini bertujuan merekonstruksi indikator kesejahteraan ekonomi berbasis konsep falah dan maqāṣid syarī'ah untuk menjawab keempat kesenjangan tersebut. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode analisis isi (content analysis) dan pemodelan konseptual-matematis atas data sekunder dari Al-Qur'an, Hadis, serta literatur ekonomi Islam klasik dan kontemporer, penelitian ini merumuskan Falah Index Framework yang mengoperasionalkan lima dimensi al-dharūriyyāt al-khams: Ad-Dīn (spiritual-etis), An-Nafs (kesehatan fisik dan psikologis-mental), Al-'Aql (intelektual), An-Nasl (keberlanjutan sosial-ekologis), dan Al-Māl (keadilan ekonomi). Skor indeks dihitung melalui rata-rata geometris berbobot dengan mekanisme ambang batas kritis dharuriyyat, yang secara matematis terbukti mampu mencegah capaian tinggi pada satu dimensi menutupi kegagalan pemenuhan kebutuhan dasar pada dimensi lain, menegakkan prinsip non-kompensasi yang absen dalam indeks-indeks alternatif sebelumnya. Kerangka ini berimplikasi pada penjenjangan prioritas anggaran negara (dharuriyyah–ḥajiyyah–taḥsīniyyah) dan optimalisasi instrumen keuangan sosial Islam, sekaligus memperkuat keterhubungan wacana ekonomi Islam dengan gerakan Post-GDP global dan SDGs. Penelitian ini masih bersifat konseptual dan memerlukan validasi empiris lebih lanjut pada data riil.

title: परस समझत क पशचत वशवक जलवय शसन: बहकदरयत, ससथगत वखडन, जलवय नयय एव करयनवयन अतरल क आलचनतमक वशलषण
summary: जलवायु परिवर्तन इक्कीसवीं शताब्दी की सबसे जटिल वैश्विक सार्वजनिक नीति चुनौतियों में से एक है। यह केवल पर्यावरणीय संकट नहीं, बल्कि विकास, न्याय, अर्थव्यवस्था, ऊर्जा सुरक्षा और वैश्विक शासन से जुड़ा बहुआयामी प्रश्न है। संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु
content: जलवायु परिवर्तन इक्कीसवीं शताब्दी की सबसे जटिल वैश्विक सार्वजनिक नीति चुनौतियों में से एक है। यह केवल पर्यावरणीय संकट नहीं, बल्कि विकास, न्याय, अर्थव्यवस्था, ऊर्जा सुरक्षा और वैश्विक शासन से जुड़ा बहुआयामी प्रश्न है। संयुक्त राष्ट्र जलवायु परिवर्तन रूपरेखा अभिसमय (UNFCCC, 1992) और क्योटो प्रोटोकॉल (1997) के पश्चात् पेरिस समझौता (2015) वैश्विक जलवायु शासन की दिशा में एक महत्वपूर्ण संस्थागत परिवर्तन का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। इस समझौते ने बाध्यकारी उत्सर्जन लक्ष्यों के स्थान पर राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर निर्धारित योगदान (Nationally Determined Contributions: NDCs) आधारित "प्रतिज्ञा और समीक्षा" प्रणाली को अपनाया, जिससे वैश्विक सहभागिता तो बढ़ी, परन्तु प्रवर्तन की क्षमता सीमित रही। यह लेख बहुकेंद्रीय शासन (Polycentric Governance), शासन-संकुल (Regime Complex) तथा जलवायु न्याय (Climate Justice) के दृष्टिकोणों के आधार पर पेरिस-पश्चात् जलवायु शासन की प्रभावशीलता का आलोचनात्मक परीक्षण करता है। लेख का तर्क है कि वर्तमान वैश्विक जलवायु शासन की प्रमुख समस्या संस्थागत अभाव नहीं, बल्कि तीन परस्पर सम्बद्ध अंतरालों—समन्वय अंतराल (Coordination Gap), न्याय अंतराल (Justice Gap) तथा कार्यान्वयन अंतराल (Implementation Gap)—का अस्तित्व है। लेख का मौलिक योगदान "त्रि-अंतराल विश्लेषणात्मक ढाँचे" (Three-Gap Analytical Framework) का प्रस्तुतीकरण है, जिसके माध्यम से यह दिखाया गया है कि संस्थागत विखंडन, उत्तरदायित्व-वितरण पर विवाद तथा नीति-कार्यान्वयन की सीमाएँ एक-दूसरे को प्रभावित करती हैं और सामूहिक रूप से वैश्विक जलवायु शासन की प्रभावशीलता को सीमित करती हैं। अध्ययन निष्कर्ष निकालता है कि पेरिस व्यवस्था की सफलता नई संस्थाओं के निर्माण पर नहीं, बल्कि मौजूदा संस्थाओं के बीच बेहतर समन्वय, न्यायपूर्ण वित्तीय व्यवस्था तथा प्रभावी कार्यान्वयन तंत्र के विकास पर निर्भर करती है।

title: A Study of Quick-Commerce Tech Boom with Special Reference to Electronics
summary: The traditional e-commerce is based on scale economies and centralized warehouses, with delivery time of 1 to 7 working days. This paradigm has been challenged by what is being called ‘quick commerce', or ‘q-commerce', which leverages decen
content: The traditional e-commerce is based on scale economies and centralized warehouses, with delivery time of 1 to 7 working days. This paradigm has been challenged by what is being called ‘quick commerce', or ‘q-commerce', which leverages decentralized, hyperlocal ‘dark stores' to deliver orders in less than 30 minutes. The model has been around since the early days of low-margin groceries but has been challenged by low Average Order Values (AOV) and high last mile logistics costs. Platforms are bringing in high margin consumer electronics and tech accessories to shore up unit economics. This is a strategic category expansion which is expected to benefit from the high margins (10-25%) (Blinkit’s Dark Store Network & AI Logistics |Jain ,2026.) and support the cost of delivery networks. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) approach, both delivery speed and convenience perception are found to narrow decision horizon and facilitate impulse buying. But the operational challenges associated with small-format dark stores are unique when it comes to handling high-value electronics: The ability to manage complex reverse logistics is limited, and the need to store high dollar items requires significant investment in secure storage and unboxing verification processes to reduce the risk of shrinkage. Geographically, metros continue to be the limit of scaling up beyond. In conclusion, q-commerce moves towards an instant e-commerce discipline with a margin focus, and is forever changing urban distribution.

title: Green Human Capital, Corporate Sustainability, dan Corporate Performance: Bukti Empiris dari Industri Logistik Maritim di Indonesia
summary: Penelitian ini menganalisis peran mediasi keberlanjutan perusahaan dalam hubungan antara modal manusia hijau dan kinerja perusahaan pada industri logistik maritim Indonesia. Data dari 100 manajer dan supervisor dianalisis menggunakan covari
content: Penelitian ini menganalisis peran mediasi keberlanjutan perusahaan dalam hubungan antara modal manusia hijau dan kinerja perusahaan pada industri logistik maritim Indonesia. Data dari 100 manajer dan supervisor dianalisis menggunakan covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM) dan uji Sobel. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa modal manusia hijau berhubungan positif dengan keberlanjutan perusahaan (0,531), yang selanjutnya berhubungan positif dengan kinerja perusahaan (0,785). Hubungan langsung tidak signifikan (p = 0,083), sedangkan hubungan tidak langsung signifikan (0,417; p < 0,001). Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya pengintegrasian kompetensi lingkungan ke dalam praktik keberlanjutan organisasi untuk mendukung kinerja perusahaan.

title: The Material Price of Easier Meadow Establishment: Sand Depth, Weeding Demand and Forb Retention
summary: Sand capping may reduce the maintenance required during urban meadow establishment, but additional material does not necessarily deliver proportional labour savings. This study compares three cap depths and examines whether jute reduces wee
content: Sand capping may reduce the maintenance required during urban meadow establishment, but additional material does not necessarily deliver proportional labour savings. This study compares three cap depths and examines whether jute reduces weeding demand while maintaining forb establishment. Weeding time was accumulated across six visits to 54 randomized plots in Royal Park, Melbourne, and twelve-month forb richness was assessed from four pooled quadrats per plot. Labour budgets were compared with nominal construction quantities, with uncertainty estimated from 50,000 whole-plot bootstrap resamples. Without jute, mean cumulative weeding demand was 19.44 hours per 100 m2 on uncapped soil, 9.76 at 10 mm and 4.65 at 80 mm. The first cubic metre of sand saved 9.68 hours, while the additional seven cubic metres saved 5.10 hours. Increasing the cap from 10 to 80 mm therefore broke even at an installed sand cost equivalent to 0.729 labour hours per cubic metre, with a 95% percentile interval of 0.380–1.164. At the deepest cap, adding jute reduced mean weeding time by 0.37 hours, although the uncertainty interval included zero, and pooled forb richness was 2.11 species lower. Richness differed little among treatments without jute, but these similarities did not establish ecological equivalence. Variation across visits and the observed labour distributions also indicated that construction choices influenced when work was required and how strongly demand was concentrated. The deepest cap produced the lowest measured weeding demand, while the initial sand increment delivered the greatest saving per unit of material. Meadow specifications should assess successive construction increments, evaluate forb establishment separately and base financial expectations on the observed establishment period.

title: Performance Management, Total Rewards, and Career Development: The Role of Employee Performance in Talent Poaching Susceptibility
summary: This study examines the effects of Performance Management, Total Rewards, and Career Development on Employee Performance and Talent Poaching Susceptibility, with Employee Performance serving as a mediating variable. The study employed a qua
content: This study examines the effects of Performance Management, Total Rewards, and Career Development on Employee Performance and Talent Poaching Susceptibility, with Employee Performance serving as a mediating variable. The study employed a quantitative approach using survey data collected from employees of oil and gas contractor companies in Indonesia. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), complemented by Importance-Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). The results reveal that Performance Management does not significantly affect Employee Performance, whereas Total Rewards and Career Development have significant positive effects. Among the three human resource management practices, Career Development has the strongest effect on employee performance. Furthermore, Employee Performance has a strong positive effect on Talent Poaching Susceptibility. The mediation analysis indicates that Employee Performance mediates the effects of Total Rewards and Career Development on Talent Poaching Susceptibility, but does not mediate the relationship between Performance Management and Talent Poaching Susceptibility. IPMA further identifies Career Development and Employee Performance as managerial priorities. These findings highlight the need to integrate employee performance enhancement with talent retention strategies.

title: Microbial Transglutaminase in Bakery Products: Mechanisms, Applications, and Safety
summary: Microbial transglutaminase (MTGase; EC 2.3.2.13), produced primarily by Streptomyces mobaraensis, is a calcium-independent acyltransferase that catalyzes the formation of ε-(γ-glutamyl)-lysine covalent crosslinks between glutamine and lysin
content: Microbial transglutaminase (MTGase; EC 2.3.2.13), produced primarily by Streptomyces mobaraensis, is a calcium-independent acyltransferase that catalyzes the formation of ε-(γ-glutamyl)-lysine covalent crosslinks between glutamine and lysine residues in food proteins. This enzymatic crosslinking substantially modifies the structural and functional properties of both gluten and non-gluten proteins, establishing MTGase as a strategically important processing aid in the contemporary baking industry. The present review systematically examines evidence pertaining to MTGase applications across four principal bakery categories: conventional wheat breads, rye breads, sourdough fermented systems, and gluten-free formulations incorporating alternative grain and protein matrices. A structured literature search was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases, covering publications from 2006 to 2025. Findings consistently indicate that MTGase improves loaf-specific volume, crumb structure, and dough handling properties in wheat-based systems, while its efficacy in gluten-free formulations remains contingent upon the availability and reactivity of suitable protein substrates. Synergistic combinations with sourdough fermentation, hydrocolloids, and advanced processing technologies including high-pressure processing and ultrasound — demonstrate enhanced rheological and shelf-life outcomes. However, the enzyme's potential interaction with celiac-immunogenic gluten peptides and the possible generation of crosslinked neoantigens remain incompletely characterized, warranting structured clinical evaluation. Future research priorities include high-yield substrate-specific MTGase variants, standardized dosage protocols for gluten-free applications, and comprehensive safety assessments for immunocompromised populations.

title: Soil constraints and baseline performance of sweet corn (Zea mays var. saccharata) under rainfed, no-input conditions in Manipur, Northeastern Hill region of India
summary: Sweet corn (Zea mays var. saccharata) production in Manipur, Northeastern Hill Region of India, is constrained by acidic, clay-textured soils, erratic monsoon distribution, and low inherent nitrogen availability. This short note characteriz
content: Sweet corn (Zea mays var. saccharata) production in Manipur, Northeastern Hill Region of India, is constrained by acidic, clay-textured soils, erratic monsoon distribution, and low inherent nitrogen availability. This short note characterizes the pre-crop soil properties, growing-season weather, and unfertilized baseline agronomic performance of sweet corn (cv. Golden Cob) at the Integrated Farming System Research Field, Central Agricultural University, Imphal (Kharif 2025; 24.81°N, 93.88°E; 780 m MSL). The initial soil characteristics showed high acidity (pH 5.71), clay texture (64.61% clay), moderate organic carbon (0.71%), and low availability of nitrogen (213.37 kg ha-1). Total rainfall during the growing season was 636.4 mm in AugustSeptember. In the no-input treatment, sweet corn produced a yield of 98.53 q ha-1 of fresh cob production and 198.01 q ha-1 of green stover, with delayed phenology (tasseling 67.33 days and silking 71.00 days). These baseline data establish a documented productivity floor for nutrient-responsive experimental comparisons and provide a reference for agro-advisory development in rainfed NEH systems.

title: Root Morphology and Adaptation of Eucalyptus grandis Growing in an Industrial Plantation Forest and the Critical Land of the Lake Toba Catchment Area, Indonesia
source: American Journal of Applied Sciences (Multimedia University)
summary: Forest rehabilitation in the Lake Toba catchment area has experienced extremely low success rates despite continuous planting programs since 2005, with plant survival remaining below 1%. This study aimed to investigate the morphological ada
content: Forest rehabilitation in the Lake Toba catchment area has experienced extremely low success rates despite continuous planting programs since 2005, with plant survival remaining below 1%. This study aimed to investigate the morphological adaptation of Eucalyptus grandis roots growing under contrasting site conditions and to evaluate their potential for rehabilitation of degraded catchment areas. Field observations were conducted in two locations, namely the industrial plantation forest of PT Toba Pulp Lestari (Habinsaran Sector) and the degraded catchment area of Lake Toba. Data were collected on environmental conditions, soil characteristics, plant morphology, stem diameter, plant height, biomass, root architecture, and root growth patterns through direct field measurements and comparative observations. The degraded catchment area was characterized by steep slopes (35–45%), shallow soil depth (0–20 cm), rocky substrates, and limited rooting space, whereas the industrial plantation site had gentler slopes (3–26%) and deeper soils (0–30 cm). Under these harsh environmental conditions, Eucalyptus grandis exhibited distinct morphological adaptations by developing laterally oriented roots that followed rock surfaces, while fine roots penetrated narrow rock crevices to maximize water and nutrient acquisition. In contrast, trees growing in deeper soils developed predominantly vertical root systems. These adaptive root characteristics explain the ability of Eucalyptus grandis to establish and survive under shallow, rocky soils where many other planted species fail. The findings indicate that root morphological plasticity is a key adaptive mechanism supporting the successful establishment of Eucalyptus grandis in degraded landscapes and suggest that this species is a promising candidate for forest rehabilitation programs in the Lake Toba catchment area and other degraded tropical watersheds.

title: Depreciation
source: International Journal of Economics and Finance
summary: Depreciation has been and remains a source of confusion and dispute amongst economists. Failure to use clear, valid and self-consistent definitions for output (GDP), depreciation (δ) and income (NDP) is one major cause. Definitions of depre
content: Depreciation has been and remains a source of confusion and dispute amongst economists. Failure to use clear, valid and self-consistent definitions for output (GDP), depreciation (δ) and income (NDP) is one major cause. Definitions of depreciation are varied and imprecise with obsolescence being the exception. It is usually assumed, without evidence, to be the most important. It is, however, measurable but it has not, as far as I can find, previously been measured. I show that it accounts for only about one third of total US depreciation, and I expect this result to surprise economists. We have no data from which we can identify the causes of depreciation which do not result from obsolescence. However, in the absence of any other cause which can reasonably be assumed to have had such a major impact, climate change is, in my judgement, likely to be the single most important cause of depreciation and even more important than obsolescence. Investment is not just needed for growth. Historically the US has needed to invest between 3.5% and 4.5% of its national income (NDP) in new capital simply to prevent living standards from falling. Standard models assume that growth is determined by changes in technology and additions to the supply of labour and capital. This assumption is rendered invalid by the evidence of the importance of non-obsolescent depreciation. A major revision to US national accounting was made by the Bureau of Economic Analysis in 2013 by altering the definition of output. This was a mistake which should be rescinded. The errors made by the advocates of this change included a bad definition of income, which they conflated with rather than distinguishing it from depreciation, which is not part of income but is in fact the cost of maintaining the current level of output and income. Another major error involved a confusion between the cost of investment and its value. Climate change appears to be accelerating. As it seems already a major hindrance to growth, it poses a major but unknown threat to living standards. With the benefits to growth promised by AI being equally uncertain, economic forecasts resemble guesses even more than they have historically.

title: YIELD PERFORMANCE AND HERITABILITY OF GAMMA-RAY-INDUCED TOMATO MUTANT LINES ACROSS THE DIVERSE LOWLAND ENVIRONMENTS
source: SABRAO Journal of Breeding and Genetics
summary: Selection of stable and high-yielding tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) genotypes is a challenging issue due to genotype-by-environment interactions.This study aimed to evaluate the yield performance and heritability among 10 tomato putative
content: Selection of stable and high-yielding tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) genotypes is a challenging issue due to genotype-by-environment interactions.This study aimed to evaluate the yield performance and heritability among 10 tomato putative M7-mutant lines derived from gamma-ray irradiation and five commercial cultivars for agronomic and yield-related traits under two lowland environments, Bogor and Kolaka, Indonesia.Fifteen genotypes incurred evaluation in a randomized complete block design (RCBD) with three replications in each environment.The results revealed that genotype-by-environment interactions significantly influenced the agronomic and yield-related traits of tomatoes.Higher fruit yield per plant and fruit number were prominent at Bogor (1069.63 g plant⁻¹ and 44.08 fruits plant⁻¹) than with Kolaka (434.29 g plant⁻¹ and 18.25 fruits plant⁻¹).It indicated that the Bogor environment was more favorable for tomato growth and yield production.The genotype G7 produced the most fruits per plant in both Bogor and Kolaka (95.58 and 30.81 fruits, respectively).Productivity showed a significant positive correlation with fruit weight and fruit diameter.Maximum broad-sense heritability was evident for plant height and fruit weight.The study revealed the potential of mutant tomato lines for developing high-yielding cultivars adapted to lowland environments.Keywords: Tomato (S. lycopersicum L.), genotype-by-environment interactions, genetic parameters, heritability, agronomic and yield traits Key findings: Genotype-by-environment interactions significantly affect the tomato's (S. lycopersicum L.) fruit yield and its components.Tomato genotypes produced a higher fruit number and yield at Bogor than at Kolaka.

title: Organic Milk beyond Certification: From Production-System Variability to Analytical Authentication and Industrial Quality
summary: Organic milk occupies a distinctive position in the dairy industry because of the assurances that certification provides. These assurances link production to organic feed and minimal synthetic inputs, and certification also sets standards f
content: Organic milk occupies a distinctive position in the dairy industry because of the assurances that certification provides. These assurances link production to organic feed and minimal synthetic inputs, and certification also sets standards for pasture or outside access, animal-welfare measures, verified traceability and more. However, certification does not guarantee that a sample has a better composition, lower levels of contaminants, or a distinctive analytical fingerprint. This critical narrative analysis examines peer-reviewed data on organic milk from 2020 to 2025, including the production system, dairy chemistry, nutritional quality, microbiological and chemical safety, authenticity testing and industrial usage. The research shows that systems rich in pasture generate higher n-3 fatty acids and conjugated linoleic acid, whereas gross fat, protein, lactose, minerals, vitamins, sensory qualities, microbial ecology, somatic cell count and residue occurrence remain strongly dependent on season, breed, lactation, location, feed quality, cleanliness, processing and storage. Thus, organic milk should not be automatically preferred over ordinary milk. The most defensible verification depends on a combination of orthogonal measures (fatty acid profiling, stable isotope ratio, FTIR/MIR/NIR spectroscopy, chromatography, nuclear magnetic resonance, residue screening and chemometric or machine learning classification) and certification records. Rapid spectral devices are expected to be utilized for regular screening. They must, however, be externally validated, transferred to instruments, shown to be seasonally resistant and tested using blind samples and a confirmatory reference technique before they can be used in industry. The review proposes a joint quality and authenticity approach for premium fluid milk, fermented products, cheese, butter, milk powders, functional foods and digitally traceable supply chains. Future research should prioritize multicountry reference databases, uniform sampling, uncertainty reporting, model explainability and validation against authorized laboratory procedures.

title: Organic Nutrient Management and Sustainable Practices for Enhancing Fruit Crop Productivity in India
source: Journal of Food Technology & Nutrition Sciences
summary: The Indian fruit industry is an important source of nutrition, rural employment, and export revenue. However, the agricultural practices being used today, such as synthetic fertilizers and artificial pesticides, are causing damage to our so
content: The Indian fruit industry is an important source of nutrition, rural employment, and export revenue. However, the agricultural practices being used today, such as synthetic fertilizers and artificial pesticides, are causing damage to our soil as well as polluting the environment, destroying biodiversity, and causing sustainability concerns. In this research project, we looked at the cost-benefit ratios of both organic and conventional fruit production systems in India by collecting data from 150 fruit producers located in various fruit-producing areas of India from 2022 to 2024. We used descriptive statistics, regression analyses, and cost-benefit analyses to analyze both the productivity, soil fertility, and sustainability indicators of the two systems. We found that the use of organic practices (i.e., animal manures, vermicomposting, biofertilizers, biopesticides, mulching, and crop diversification) resulted in an increase of 8-16% in fruit productivity, 61.54% in soil organic carbon, and 25.8% in water-use efficiency compared to using conventional methods. In addition, organic systems resulted in less reliance on chemicals, higher market prices for fruits, greater potential for exporting fruits, and more resiliency to climate change.

title: Extreme heat risk in retrofit cost–benefit analysis: probabilistic evaluation of overheating mitigation for mild climates
summary: Despite the Netherlands’ mild climate, heatwaves are becoming more frequent, and the use of mechanical cooling is rising, exposing the limitations of retrofit strategies designed primarily to reduce heating demand. While cost–benefit analys
content: Despite the Netherlands’ mild climate, heatwaves are becoming more frequent, and the use of mechanical cooling is rising, exposing the limitations of retrofit strategies designed primarily to reduce heating demand. While cost–benefit analysis (CBA) typically supports energy-efficient retrofits, it often overlooks rising cooling loads and the role of passive cooling measures. Consequently, stakeholders lack a long-term perspective on the financial implications of indoor overheating and the effectiveness of mitigation strategies under climate variability. This study proposes a probabilistic framework that integrates heat resilience into CBA by coupling building energy simulations with Monte Carlo risk aggregation to account for climate variability and extreme heat recurrence. The framework is demonstrated for a mid-century residential unit in Rotterdam over a 30-year historical reference period (1995–2024) by evaluating the Net Present Value of passive strategies (shading, high-albedo paint and their combination) and deep retrofit. The case study reveals a performance domain disparity, where passive measures reduce overheating intensity (53–59%) but yield only marginal cooling energy savings (2–6%). The study suggests that conventional CBA relying solely on energy savings underestimate the broader value of overheating mitigation, highlighting the need to consider thermal resilience and climate uncertainty in retrofit investment decisions.

title: The Role of Nanotechnology in Targeting Viral Infections at the Cellular Level
summary: Introduction: To critically synthesise evidence on how nanotechnology can be used to prevent viral entry, deliver antiviral agents to infected cells, modulate intracellular antiviral processes and improve the safety or effectiveness of anti
content: Introduction: To critically synthesise evidence on how nanotechnology can be used to prevent viral entry, deliver antiviral agents to infected cells, modulate intracellular antiviral processes and improve the safety or effectiveness of antiviral therapy. Methods: We conducted a narrative review using the literature in the original manuscript as the core evidence base. We reorganised the evidence around the viral life cycle and the nanoparticle–cell interface, with an emphasis on nanoparticle composition, surface functionalisation, cellular uptake, drug and nucleic-acid delivery, safety, manufacturing, and translation. Bibliographic records were also checked during revision, and the implications for health systems in the Global South were explicitly considered. Synthesis: Inorganic, lipid, polymeric and hybrid nanoparticles can interact with viruses or host cells through adsorption, receptor targeting, endocytosis, endosomal trafficking and controlled intracellular release. Experimental evidence supports applications in viral neutralisation, inhibition of entry, delivery of antiretroviral and other antiviral agents, vaccine development and diagnostic detection. However, much of the evidence remains preclinical. Heterogeneity in particle size, surface chemistry, formulation, dose and experimental models complicates comparisons across studies. Toxicity, reproducible scale-up, stability, regulatory requirements and cost remain important barriers to clinical implementation. Conclusion: Nanotechnology provides a versatile platform for antiviral intervention, but biological plausibility should not be equated with clinical effectiveness. Future work should prioritise reproducible formulations, rigorous toxicology, clinically relevant efficacy studies and manufacturing pathways that are affordable and feasible in the Global South.

title: RSM Optimization of Used Engine Oil Recovery Using Coal-Based Activated Carbon in a Pyrolysis–Distillation Unit
source: Advance Sustainable Science Engineering and Technology
summary: Recovery of hydrocarbon compounds from waste lubricating oil has gained considerable attention because of its potential as an alternative liquid fuel source and its contribution to environmental protection. Besides containing valuable hydro
content: Recovery of hydrocarbon compounds from waste lubricating oil has gained considerable attention because of its potential as an alternative liquid fuel source and its contribution to environmental protection. Besides containing valuable hydrocarbons, waste lubricating oil also contains sulfur compounds and heavy metals that may reduce fuel quality and cause environmental pollution. This study evaluates the recovery of waste lubricating oil through a pyrolysis–distillation process assisted by activated carbon derived from low-rank coal from East Kalimantan, Indonesia. The activated carbon was synthesized through carbonization and chemical activation and characterized using iodine number analysis to determine its adsorption capability. Response Surface Methodology (RSM) was applied to optimize pyrolysis temperature and activated carbon dosage in order to maximize liquid yield and contaminant removal efficiency. The synthesized activated carbon exhibited an iodine number of 1163.51 mg/g. Optimization predicted optimum conditions at 416.54 °C and 12.87 wt.% activated carbon dosage, producing 89.67% liquid yield and approximately 76% contaminant removal efficiency. Experimental validation confirmed the model prediction, resulting in 88% liquid yield with satisfactory fuel characteristics.

title: Beyond Corporate Responsibility: Reassessing the Financial Implications of Sustainability for Dividend Policy
summary: Corporate sustainability has increasingly become an important consideration in corporate financial decision-making, particularly in relation to dividend policy and shareholder returns. However, existing empirical evidence on this relationsh
content: Corporate sustainability has increasingly become an important consideration in corporate financial decision-making, particularly in relation to dividend policy and shareholder returns. However, existing empirical evidence on this relationship remains fragmented and contradictory. This study examines the sustainability–dividend policy nexus through a combined bibliometric analysis and critical literature review. Data were retrieved from Scopus and comprised 150 peer-reviewed articles published between 2005 and 2025. Using the Bibliometrix package in R, the study investigates publication trends, influential authors, journals, countries, collaboration networks, and thematic developments. The critical review further evaluates the relationship's underlying mechanisms and contextual conditions. The findings indicate that corporate sustainability generally supports higher and more stable dividend payments through improved profitability, reduced information asymmetry, and lower agency costs. However, this relationship is conditional upon sustainability measurement, ownership structure, financial constraints, and institutional characteristics. Notably, externally verifiable sustainability initiatives, particularly eco-labelling certifications and green bonds, demonstrate more consistent positive associations with dividend outcomes than broad ESG scores. The bibliometric analysis reveals growing scholarly interest since 2018, while highlighting the fragmented and underdeveloped connection between sustainability and dividend policy. By integrating signaling, and stakeholder perspectives, this study clarifies existing empirical inconsistencies and provides insights into how credible sustainability practices can support dividend distributions and long-term shareholder value.

title: Tata Kelola Bioenergi Pongamia Berbasis Komunitas di Wilayah Kepulauan Kering Indonesia Timur
summary: This study examines how knowledge of Pongamia (Pongamia pinnata), community governance, and feedstock readiness may be connected to support community-based bioenergy. A bibliometric mapping of 2,208 unique records retrieved through Elicit a
content: This study examines how knowledge of Pongamia (Pongamia pinnata), community governance, and feedstock readiness may be connected to support community-based bioenergy. A bibliometric mapping of 2,208 unique records retrieved through Elicit and Dimensions was complemented by a focused thematic synthesis of 32 articles (29 from the main corpus and three external contextual studies). Title–abstract mapping identified four broad thematic domains encompassing agroecology, community governance, bioenergy, and engineering. However, only a small share of the assembled corpus explicitly addresses Pongamia; consequently, thematic separation should not be generalized as fragmentation of the entire global literature. The thematic synthesis indicates that willingness to participate depends on planting material, extension support, trusted organizations, and credible economic benefits. The article develops preliminary design principles connecting seed resources, nurseries, participation, institutional arrangements, processing, and market access. The proposed framework is a literature-informed proposition rather than an empirically validated model for Lembata.

title: Effect of Agaricus bisporus extract on gene expression of some virulence genes of Aspergillus flavus
summary: Aspergillus flavus is a common filamentous fungus as well as an opportunistic pathogen of crops. The capability of fungi to infect plants relied on particular genes differentiating pathogenic fungi from their nonpathogenic counterparts. Thi
content: Aspergillus flavus is a common filamentous fungus as well as an opportunistic pathogen of crops. The capability of fungi to infect plants relied on particular genes differentiating pathogenic fungi from their nonpathogenic counterparts. This investigation aims to study the effect of Agaricus bisporus extract on the gene expression of Lipase, Aflatoxin and Metalloprotease of four highly pathogenic isolates of Aspergillus flavus in Iraq. Nine isolates were obtained from infected walnut fruits and their diagnosis was confirmed by morphological and molecular methods. The quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) for gene detection showed that the isolates (A. flavus 1, A. flavus 4, A. flavus 7 and A. flavus 8) were characterized by positive results for all virulence genes. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis of the alcoholic extract of A. bisporus showed that it contains many common compounds in high concentration in the form of esters, fatty acids, derived alcohols and ketones, as well as some aromatic compounds, all of which have varying effects in inhibiting fungal growth. The results of qRT-PCR for gene expression revealed a fundamental down regulation for the expression of lipase, aflatoxin and metalprotease genes. Lipase and metalprotease genes showed highly significant difference (P≤0.01) in gene expression for two isolates (A. flavus 4 and A. flavus 8) for lipase and Metalprotease genes while Aflatoxin gene revealed highly significant difference (P≤0.01) in three isolates (A. flavus 4, A. flavus 7 and A. flavus 8). Elucidating the molecular techniques which control the secondary metabolism of toxin-producing fungi can make it possible to deliberately silence the genes implicated, thereby planned inhibition of these fungi and reducing their virulence.

title: Integrating Research and Project-Based Learning: A Competency-Oriented Teaching Reform for the Civil Engineering Materials Course
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: Given the broad scope of the Civil Engineering Materials course, the close relationship between material properties and engineering applications, and the constraints imposed by curing ages on cementbased materials testing, this study develo
content: Given the broad scope of the Civil Engineering Materials course, the close relationship between material properties and engineering applications, and the constraints imposed by curing ages on cementbased materials testing, this study develops a research-integrated and project-based teaching reform framework through literature analysis and curriculum design, drawing on the theories of constructive alignment, project-based learning, and research-based learning. Representative research cases are selected and adapted into undergraduate projects with clearly defined variables, experimental tasks, and expected deliverables. Taking low-carbon cement mortar mix design as an example, an eight-week instructional module is designed to encompass research question formulation, mix design, specimen preparation, performance testing, and multi-criteria engineering evaluation. Five competency dimensions are identified, including application of materials knowledge, experimental design, data analysis and interpretation, sustainable engineering decisionmaking, and engineering communication. Alignment is established among project-level competency objectives, learning activities, and assessment evidence, supported by an analytic scoring rubric and mechanisms for process-based assessment and feedback. The proposed framework emphasizes the integration of research questions into course activities, coordination between experimental curing periods and instructional schedules, and evidence-based assessment of student competencies, providing a reference for curriculum reform in civil engineering materials and related courses.

title: Green and Digital Trade Between Viet Nam and Japan Through Technology Specialisation and Supply Chain Concentration
summary: Green and digital goods are central to the energy transition, yet the structure of their trade between Viet Nam and Japan has received little attention. This study aims to show how four established trade indicators, read jointly, distinguis
content: Green and digital goods are central to the energy transition, yet the structure of their trade between Viet Nam and Japan has received little attention. This study aims to show how four established trade indicators, read jointly, distinguish product groups by export specialisation, market complementarity, bilateral trade balance, and sourcing concentration. Using six-digit trade data from the World Integrated Trade Solution (WITS) and UN Comtrade for 2018–2023, it applies the Revealed Comparative Advantage index (RCA), the Trade Complementarity Index (TCI), the Grubel–Lloyd index (GL), and the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI) of Japan’s import sources to six groups: low-carbon technology goods, environmental goods, lithium-ion battery supply chain goods, industrial robots, semiconductors, and 3D printing goods. The configurations differ by group. In industrial robots, both countries show revealed specialisation, and gross bilateral trade is almost balanced. In environmental goods, Viet Nam’s export structure moved closer to Japanese import demand before revealed specialisation emerged. In semiconductors, Vietnamese specialisation coexists with unbalanced bilateral trade. Product-level checks show that the group-level HHI understates the concentration in battery goods, whereas the semiconductor result depends on the treatment of “Other Asia, n.e.s.”. The contribution is configurational: the indicator combinations show where evidence on value added, capability formation, and dependence is most needed.

title: Transforming modern drug discovery with molecular modeling and artificial intelligence
summary: Background: Techniques such as Molecular Modeling and Artificial Intelligence in drug discovery have revolutionized the field by improving target identification, virtual screening, lead optimization, and toxicity prediction. Although many c
content: Background: Techniques such as Molecular Modeling and Artificial Intelligence in drug discovery have revolutionized the field by improving target identification, virtual screening, lead optimization, and toxicity prediction. Although many computational techniques exist, the literature offers few systematic, comprehensive reviews of molecular modeling combined with AI-driven techniques. This article evaluates the application of molecular modeling technologies, such as Quantum Mechanics, Molecular Mechanics, Molecular Dynamics, molecular docking, and computer-aided drug design, using AI methods. Methodology: The author conducted a narrative review based on published information from scientific literature databases such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Results and Discussion: Molecular modeling enables structural and mechanistic models of ligand–target binding, while AI accelerates virtual screening, de novo molecular design, ADMET prediction, and lead optimization. Novel technologies such as AlphaFold, graph neural networks, and generative AI are expanding applied computational drug design. Nevertheless, several challenges remain, including data quality, model interpretability, external validation, dataset bias, overfitting, limited experimental validation, and translational reliability. Conclusion: Integrating molecular modeling and AI technologies represents a major step toward faster, more economical drug discovery processes. Future success will depend on increased use of standardized datasets, the development of explainable AI, and thorough experimental validation.

title: Market orientation and green technology adoption in agricultural enterprises: A serial mediation model of organizational learning capability and policy utilization capability
summary: Green and low-carbon development has become an important embodiment of China's path to becoming a strong agricultural country. How to enable agricultural enterprises to better adopt green technologies and conduct production and operation wi
content: Green and low-carbon development has become an important embodiment of China's path to becoming a strong agricultural country. How to enable agricultural enterprises to better adopt green technologies and conduct production and operation with the concept of sustainable development has become a key link. This article utilizes a structural equation model (SEM) to analyze the role paths and mediating effects of organizational learning ability and policy orientation in agricultural enterprises' market orientation and willingness to adopt green technologies[ The definition of green technology in this paper refers to Guo Kesha, Tian Xiaoxiao. Green technology and green transformation of industrial development mode [J]. Tianjin Social Sciences, 2024 (02) :99-107, including green manufacturing (production) technology and green service technology.]. The results show that market orientation, organizational learning ability, and policy effectiveness have significant direct positive impacts on the willingness to adopt; market orientation has a significant positive impact on agricultural enterprises' organizational learning ability, organizational learning ability has a significant positive impact on policy orientation, and market orientation has a significant positive impact on policy effectiveness; the results of mediation analysis also indicate that learning ability has a significant mediating effect between market orientation and willingness to adopt, and policy effectiveness has a significant mediating effect between market orientation and willingness to adopt. Through difference analysis, it is believed that the mediating effects of the three paths are equally important, and organizational learning ability and policy effectiveness play a partial mediating role in agricultural enterprises' willingness to adopt green technologies. Based on this, policy suggestions are proposed to improve enterprises' own organizational learning ability, increase the promotion of policies related to green technologies, improve relevant policies for the application of green technologies, and increase research and development efforts for green technologies.

title: Why Are There So Many Power Laws in Economics?
summary: Power law distributions are ubiquitous in socioeconomic contexts. While their general properties are well understood, it is often less clear why they regularly appear in empirical data. What are the generative mechanisms leading to power la
content: Power law distributions are ubiquitous in socioeconomic contexts. While their general properties are well understood, it is often less clear why they regularly appear in empirical data. What are the generative mechanisms leading to power law distributions and why do we so often observe such distributions in socioeconomic contexts? This paper aims to partly fill this gap by discussing two candidate mechanisms, cumulative advantage and random multiplication, that appear regularly, but in variegated forms, in political economy arguments. These mechanisms do not only seem especially relevant for understanding power law distributions in socioeconomic contexts, but can also be captured in simple formal setups. On this basis, we identify core formal properties and explore how these mechanisms can be mapped to real-world problems and processes. In addition, we discuss the relation of power laws and their generative mechanisms to related concepts relevant in heterodox economics, like path dependence, cumulative processes, power asymmetries or non-ergodicity.

title: Differentiating Climate Efficiency in Agrifood Systems: A Stylised Simulation Model With Carbon Opportunity Costs
summary: ABSTRACT The agrifood system generates around one‐third of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by land use and land‐use change. Existing policy assessments focus on net emissions changes, overlooking efficiency losses within market dyna
content: ABSTRACT The agrifood system generates around one‐third of global greenhouse gas emissions, driven by land use and land‐use change. Existing policy assessments focus on net emissions changes, overlooking efficiency losses within market dynamics and the carbon sequestration potential of land. This study enhances agrifood policy assessment by extending ex‐post model reporting and differentiating efficiency changes on the supply and demand side. As proof of concept, a simplified partial equilibrium model with two regions and two commodities simulates different taxation and subsidisation schemes. Incorporating carbon opportunity costs to capture land's carbon sink capacity alters efficiency rankings of production sites and commodities and changes the assessment of policies' climate impacts. Disaggregating climate efficiency into supply and demand side reveals efficiency losses obscured when assessing solely net emission changes. Accounting for carbon opportunity costs and differentiating between supply‐ and demand‐side efficiency reveals effects that net emission reporting does not capture and can, thus, inform policy design. This contribution is best read as a methodological proof of concept. Additionally, we describe the steps and the challenges to integrate the developed framework into a full‐scale simulation model for applied policy analysis.

title: Biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland
summary: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of na
content: Abstract Halting biodiversity loss requires systematic action from all sectors of society. The public sector is a significant actor globally in creating markets for goods and services, public procurement representing on average 13–20% of national gross domestic product. In this study, we assessed the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022. We applied the consumption-based biodiversity footprint model BIOVALENT, where data from EXIOBASE and LC-IMPACT databases are combined to connect economic activities in the value chains of procured goods and services with the resulting biodiversity impact. Our results indicate that (i) largest contributors to the biodiversity footprint of public procurement in Finland in 2022 were construction and maintenance services (19%), utilities consisting of water and energy consumption and rentals of real estate (15%), health and social services (11%), and medical and care supplies (10%); (ii) the greatest potential in mitigating the biodiversity footprint lies in construction and maintenance, utilities, medical and care supplies, machines and appliances, and accommodation and catering services; and (iii) according to the model on average over 90% of the biodiversity footprint was located overseas. These insights from our analysis can be used for guiding strategic prioritization, more detailed assessments, and mitigation actions towards most impactful procurement categories. The considerable role of the value chain in the harmful biodiversity impacts calls for significant changes in the public procurement practices, given their influence throughout production systems and consumption patterns.

title: Space economy and strategic development in ASEAN pathways to 2035
summary: The ASEAN space economy is entering a rapid growth phase toward 2035, alongside a global market projected to reach USD 1.8 trillion. ASEAN’s share is expected to scale to approximately USD 80–200 billion, driven by three key engines: Earth
content: The ASEAN space economy is entering a rapid growth phase toward 2035, alongside a global market projected to reach USD 1.8 trillion. ASEAN’s share is expected to scale to approximately USD 80–200 billion, driven by three key engines: Earth Observation (EO) commercialization, SATCOM expansion via high-throughput systems, and rising demand for ISR and Space Domain Awareness (SDA). EO in Southeast Asia alone is projected to triple to USD 45 billion by 2030. Thailand is positioned as a regional hub through THEOS-2, Thaicom platforms, national space policy, and a multi-orbit spaceport strategy enabling upstream and downstream integration. Using a bottom-up forecast model aligned with the Space Capacity Ladder (SCL), ASEAN is expected to sustain a 4.4–11.1% share of the global space economy by 2035, led by Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, and the Philippines.

title: From Electrification on Component-Level to Software-Defined Vehicles: The Role of Modular Smart Corner Systems in Next-Generation Electric Vehicle Architecture
summary: Abstract The transition to software-defined vehicles (SDVs) necessitates a paradigm shift in both control strategies and vehicle architecture. The EU-funded SmartCorners project addresses this challenge by developing integrated smart corner
content: Abstract The transition to software-defined vehicles (SDVs) necessitates a paradigm shift in both control strategies and vehicle architecture. The EU-funded SmartCorners project addresses this challenge by developing integrated smart corner systems (SCS), which combine in-wheel motor (IWM) propulsion, brake-by-wire, active suspension actuator, and steer-by-wire functionality in a single module. These SCS are embedded within a highly adaptable skateboard chassis architecture, enabling scalable deployment across diverse vehicle platforms. The SmartCorners project targets to demonstrate significant advancements, including improvement in real-world driving range, reduction of component and system costs, an increasement in interior volume, and a development time drop of the EV systems enabled by digital-twin-based design methodologies. Beyond these performance gains, SmartCorners establishes the foundational principles of modularity, adaptability, and software integration that underpin the evolution toward SDVs. These achievements highlight a critical bridge between electrified component innovation and the holistic software-defined mobility systems of the future.

title: Raw sugarcane bagasse hydrochar outperforms carbon nanotubes in microbial fuel cell power generation
summary: Abstract The commercialization of microbial fuel cells (MFCs) is currently limited by the high cost of standard electrode materials like carbon nanotubes (CNTs). This study introduces a high-performance, low-cost alternative: sugarcane baga
content: Abstract The commercialization of microbial fuel cells (MFCs) is currently limited by the high cost of standard electrode materials like carbon nanotubes (CNTs). This study introduces a high-performance, low-cost alternative: sugarcane bagasse hydrochar. We evaluated raw (RSBH), phosphated (PSBH), and sulfonated (SSBH) hydrochars as symmetric electrodes against a commercial CNT control. While acid functionalization enhanced thermal stability and char yields, the unmodified hydrochar yielded the most striking electrochemical results. Ni-RSBH achieved a peak power density of 1008 mW/m2, quadrupling the performance of the commercial Ni-CNT (235 mW/m2). Post-operation analysis revealed that Ni-RSBH developed exceptional biofilm compatibility, with anodic capacitance surging to 51.03 F/g compared to just 3.01 F/g for Ni-CNT. Although the phosphated variant (Ni-PSBH) offered superior voltage stability (0.68–0.71 V), the raw hydrochar provided the optimal balance of conductivity and biological activity. These findings demonstrate that minimally processed agricultural waste can outperform engineered nanomaterials, presenting a scalable, circular-economy solution for bioelectrochemical systems.

title: A 3D Multitask Graph Neural Network Framework for Ames Mutagenicity Prediction
summary: The long, complex, and costly process of drug development makes early, reliable toxicity assessment a central challenge in pharmaceutical research. Accurately predicting drug-induced toxicity and mutagenicity is crucial for guiding decision
