content: The long, complex, and costly process of drug development makes early, reliable toxicity assessment a central challenge in pharmaceutical research. Accurately predicting drug-induced toxicity and mutagenicity is crucial for guiding decision-making and reducing late-stage attrition. Deep learning approaches can predict the results of the Ames mutagenicity test, a standard screening method; however, most existing models rely on molecular descriptors that limit structural representation, lack interpretability, and do not account for Ames results of individual bacterial strains. Graph neural networks (GNNs) are chemically intuitive and overcome these limitations. This work presents a deep learning, multitask GNN model for predicting Ames mutagenicity. The proposed approach outperforms existing models, including those from the Ames/QSAR International Challenge. Furthermore, the model is highly interpretable. Explainability analysis of atom-level contributions reveal that the model is capable of learning known structural alerts associated with mutagenicity, along with additional molecular patterns and three-dimensional structural properties. Importantly, these insights are captured in a strain-specific manner, highlighting the value of a multitask approach. Finally, the model is able to identify previously unreported molecular substructures potentially associated with mutagenicity, supporting its utility in drug design and development.

title: Electricity retail pricing as incentives for load optimization in Vietnam
summary: Abstract Vietnam’s pathway to net-zero emissions by 2050 has so far relied primarily on large-scale renewable energy investments, with limited use of demand-side management. This study evaluates how alternative retail electricity pricing sc
content: Abstract Vietnam’s pathway to net-zero emissions by 2050 has so far relied primarily on large-scale renewable energy investments, with limited use of demand-side management. This study evaluates how alternative retail electricity pricing schemes - flat tariffs, Time-of-Use (TOU), Critical Peak Pricing (CPP), and a TOU-CPP hybrid - shape demand flexibility, system costs, emissions, consumer welfare, and reliability in Vietnam. The analysis uses SWITCH 2.0, an integrated capacity expansion and dispatch model with an iterative demand-response module, to Vietnam’s electricity system in 2050. Relative to flat pricing, the modeled TOU designs reduce total system costs by up to 15% and CO2 emissions by 17.2-37.5%, while increasing consumer welfare. Consecutive TOU blocks capture substantial benefits, whereas adding CPP produces little additional improvement. Endogenous block assignment achieves the lowest system cost and reduces storage investment, but does not yield the lowest emissions or highest consumer welfare. Sensitivity analysis confirms lower unit costs and emissions and higher consumer welfare under consecutive TOU than under matched flat-pricing cases across seven demand-response parameter combinations. However, the magnitude of these benefits depends strongly on the share of load available for within-day rescheduling. Demand shifting toward solar-rich hours also changes transmission utilization, relieving pressure on some corridors while increasing it elsewhere. The findings support a staged transition toward TOU pricing with simple consecutive blocks, accompanied by enabling technologies and coordinated transmission planning. The results represent conditional system-level outcomes rather than estimates of realized consumer responses or distributional effects.

title: Distributed small-reservoir pumped-storage hydropower in Europe: a GIS screening under drawdown and karst constraints
summary: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and
content: Continental pumped-storage hydropower (PSH) atlases omit schemes built from small reservoirs, although such sites could provide distributed flexibility. We screen this resource across 37 European countries, detecting closed depressions and water bodies and pairing upper and lower reservoirs under land-use, protection and grid-distance constraints. The reproducible workflow uses open pan-European data, a hybrid terrain stack (FABDEM; national lidar in Norway and Sweden) and an explicit allowable water-level variation for lake volume. At a 5-km grid distance and 1-m drawdown, exact maximum-weight matching gives an all-size screened bound of 2.57 TWh; excluding mapped-karst footprints for purpose-built reservoirs and sites above 2500 m leaves 0.58 TWh, of which a 21 115-site portfolio capped at 100 MWh per site stores 0.40 TWh (0.24 TWh, EU-27). Replacing FABDEM by national lidar cuts Norway’s and Sweden’s screened energy with 72% each (328.7 to 92.1 and 67.3 to 18.5 GWh): usable lake volume barely moves ( − 0.4 %), but pairs containing a dry basin collapse because that basin binds. A Sobol analysis makes maximum pair distance and karst treatment the joint controls (total effects 0.49 and 0.48). This is an exploratory first screening, not deployable capacity: it ranks where national feasibility studies should look, and their constraints can only reduce it.

title: Mechanical deterioration and damage evolution of coal specimens under drying–wetting cycles
summary: Abstract Utilizing underground mine reservoirs for pumped storage power stations represents a highly promising approach for large-scale energy storage. However, the long-term exposure of coal pillar dams to drying-wetting cycles (DWC) poses
content: Abstract Utilizing underground mine reservoirs for pumped storage power stations represents a highly promising approach for large-scale energy storage. However, the long-term exposure of coal pillar dams to drying-wetting cycles (DWC) poses a severe risk of structural instability. This study investigated the mechanical degradation and damage mechanisms of coal specimens, leveraging triaxial loading coupled with acoustic emission (AE) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) monitoring. The results indicated that the compressive strength and cohesion underwent non-uniform, multi-stage degradation with increasing DWC, with the most acute deterioration occurring after the first cycle. AE monitoring revealed that with increasing DWC, the frequency of high-amplitude AE events escalated, and their peaks shifted forward. Concurrently, the overall b -value exhibited a downward trend. Analysis of the RA-AF characteristics confirmed that the proportion of shear fracture events escalated significantly with increasing DWC, triggering a failure mode transition from micro-tensile cracking to macro-shear sliding. NMR testing showed that the T 2 spectra exhibited a predominantly unimodal distribution, with micropores dominating the pore network. Under the action of DWC, the dissolution and spalling of hydrophilic minerals drove the transformation of internal micropores and mesopores into macropores. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the stability assessment of underground reservoir-based PHES systems.

title: Water-soluble titanium(IV) tris-catecholate metal coordination complex as a highly negative negolyte for alkaline aqueous redox flow battery
summary: The titanium(IV) tris-catecholate metal coordination complex (Ti(cat) 3 ) is investigated as a negolyte candidate for alkaline aqueous flow batteries. The Ti(cat) 3 complex exhibits a low redox potential of −1.13 V versus the standard hydro
content: The titanium(IV) tris-catecholate metal coordination complex (Ti(cat) 3 ) is investigated as a negolyte candidate for alkaline aqueous flow batteries. The Ti(cat) 3 complex exhibits a low redox potential of −1.13 V versus the standard hydrogen electrode, which enables a high cell potential (>1.6 V) when paired with ferro-/ferricyanide. Electrochemical studies show that the redox potential of Ti(cat) 3 is pH-independent, but that highly alkaline conditions (pH > 12) significantly reduce its electrochemical behaviour. The apparent capacity fade of the battery is strongly correlated to parasitic hydrogen evolution that causes electrolyte imbalance and results in non-intrinsic capacity decay. The battery exhibits an intrinsic capacity fade of 2.51% per day at 50 mA/cm 2 . The influence of the charge and discharge cut-off voltage is investigated and evaluated by using in-situ measurements of the redox potential and pH. Here, it is found that the discharge cut-off voltage can minimize the degradation of the Ti(cat) 3 complex, and that tuning this parameter reduces the intrinsic capacity fade to 0.31% per day at 30 mA/cm 2 . These findings highlight both the opportunities and the challenges of the Ti(cat) 3 complex as a low-potential negolyte candidate for high-voltage aqueous batteries.

title: Government Failure and Corporate Reform
summary: Corporate law has been racked by a decades-long debate. Shareholder primacy theorists suggest that corporate leaders should focus exclusively on maximizing financial returns to shareholders, while stakeholder governance theorists suggest th
content: Corporate law has been racked by a decades-long debate. Shareholder primacy theorists suggest that corporate leaders should focus exclusively on maximizing financial returns to shareholders, while stakeholder governance theorists suggest that corporate leaders should consider a broader range of concerns such as impacts on workers and the environment. Though the battle has been fought intensely on many fronts for years, there is one area of apparent agreement. Most commentators view stakeholder governance as a kind of second-best regulation. Ideally, the government would tend to worker and environmental concerns through real regulations, imposing financial penalties on corporations that behave in socially destructive ways. Corporate leaders could then focus on financial returns, given the knowledge that bad behavior would not be profitable. It is only when the government fails in its basic task by refusing to issue or enforce necessary regulations that it becomes necessary for corporations to balance different concerns internally. But although it seems to be a point of broad agreement, the idea that stakeholder governance is a response to government failure is incomplete. This Article unpacks that claim and reveals its shortcomings. It is far from obvious whether the government's refusal to regulate in a space is a failure or simply a result of the democratic process given widespread disagreement. And even an "ideal" government would face limitations in its ability to drive good outcomes. Statutes and regulations are inherently limited tools, and there are many areas such as speech and dignitary interests where the government cannot interfere or provide an adequate solution. Understanding these shortcomings deepens the analysis of the relationship between corporate governance and the political process and reveals fresh insights about the debate between shareholder primacy and stakeholder governance.

title: Получение карбоната кальция с заданными свойствами крупности как фактор эффективной утилизации техногенного гипсосодержащего сырья
summary: This study focuses on developing a method for utilizing phosphogypsum, a large-tonnage waste product from phosphate raw material processing, whose disposal sites are sources of complex negative impacts on the environment. As a promising app
content: This study focuses on developing a method for utilizing phosphogypsum, a large-tonnage waste product from phosphate raw material processing, whose disposal sites are sources of complex negative impacts on the environment. As a promising approach to the utilization of gypsum-containing waste, the study considers the interaction of phosphogypsum with a sodium carbonate solution (carbonate conversion), which yields calcium carbonate, a marketable product referred to as phosphochalk. Existing technologies typically produce a fine-grained material, which hinders filtration and restricts the potential applications of phosphochalk. This study aims to determine the carbonate conversion parameters that enable the production of phosphochalk with tailored particle size characteristics while maintaining a high degree of feedstock conversion. A series of single-factor experiments was carried out to evaluate the influence of reaction conditions – temperature, Na2CO3 concentration in the carbonate solution, liquid-to-solid (L:S) ratio, and phase contact time – on the conversion of CaSO4·2H2O. The results showed that raising the conversion temperature to 90-100 °C and increasing the L:S ratio to 10 promote intensive nucleation of CaCO3 crystals and the formation of large agglomerates. A Na2CO3 concentration of 250 g/dm3 and a phase contact time of up to 3 h together yield phosphochalk with a particle size of D90 = 45 μm at a conversion degree of 98.8 %. In terms of its characteristics, the resulting product is suitable for use in the metallurgical industry as a raw material for flux production, which demonstrates its competitiveness in the secondary raw materials market. The recommendations developed in this work enable the design of a low-waste technology for processing technogenic raw materials, consistent with the principles of sustainable development and helping to reduce the environmental burden.

title: Integrating Safety and Sustainability: A Grid-Independent Ultralight Quadricycle for Secure Urban Mobility
summary: Abstract Light electric vehicles (LEVs) offer sustainable urban mobility through low energy consumption and compact design. However, broader adoption requires integrating energy autonomy and road safety assessments into the initial design p
content: Abstract Light electric vehicles (LEVs) offer sustainable urban mobility through low energy consumption and compact design. However, broader adoption requires integrating energy autonomy and road safety assessments into the initial design phase. This study introduces a novel combined evaluation of grid independence and crash safety for a pedal-assisted quadricycle featuring vehicle-integrated photovoltaics (VIPV). A Florence-based case study first optimises geometry and VIPV placement to maximise solar yield under urban conditions. Second, simulations quantify occupant injury risk in heterogeneous traffic with increasing LEV market penetration, addressing the scarcity of real-world crash data. Results show that roof-oriented VIPV and parking-agnostic geometry significantly reduce external charging reliance. Concurrently, safety analyses confirm the vehicle’s suitability for low-speed environments, specifically 30 km/h zones. This research establishes a generalisable methodology: while calibrated on Florence’s topology and solar irradiance, the framework provides a scalable tool to minimise grid dependency and enhance safety across diverse climatic and traffic contexts.

title: Accelerating Public Charging Infrastructure: Micro-Level Approach Enables Efficient Planning of Charging Locations Based on Suitability of Public Space
summary: Abstract Expanding public electric-vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is a pressing municipal need, yet planning is slowed by site-specific public-space constraints. To address this challenge, we developed a method that considers all poss
content: Abstract Expanding public electric-vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is a pressing municipal need, yet planning is slowed by site-specific public-space constraints. To address this challenge, we developed a method that considers all possible sites for charging infrastructure in public space and conducts a suitability analysis based on potential conflicts, including preservation orders, overlays with bike lanes, and vegetation protection. Our method incorporates demand data to identify hotspots for infrastructure placement. A buffer-based analysis is applied to each suitable site, assigning the best-scoring locations. We applied our method to a neighborhood in Berlin, Germany, and obtained a selection of sites that meet demand without generating conflicts in public space. This study delivers a high-resolution output and a flexible framework for diverse urban settings, making the charging infrastructure expansion process more efficient.

title: Получение удобрений из отходов различного генезиса для рекультивации нарушенных земель и благоустройства территорий
summary: This study addresses the loss of land for other uses resulting from economic activities and waste disposal, highlights the need to develop alternative fertilizers suitable for the biological stage of land reclamation and subsequent landscap
content: This study addresses the loss of land for other uses resulting from economic activities and waste disposal, highlights the need to develop alternative fertilizers suitable for the biological stage of land reclamation and subsequent landscaping, and examines the resource potential of industrial wastes for producing nutrient amendments. The most promising waste processing approaches involve producing sewage sludge-based fertilizers through composting with other industrial wastes of various origins. A combined computational and experimental approach was used to develop composting mixtures, enabling optimization of the C:N, moisture content, and pH while incorporating visual assessments during laboratory trial mixing. The fertilizers produced were assessed qualitatively and quantitatively for veterinary, sanitary, hygienic, toxicological, and agrochemical parameters in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. A plant growth experiment using artificial soil demonstrated their effectiveness in improving key plant productivity parameters, including seed germination, plant biomass, and maximum plant height. Potential factors limiting fertilizer application were identified as toxic element contents and possible imbalances between moisture retention and air exchange caused by reduced soil substrate density at high fertilizer mass fractions. These findings confirm the feasibility of reusing wastes of various origins to restore land quality and expand the range of alternative fertilizers.

title: Химический состав и экологический ущерб отходов цианирования Берикульского золотоизвлекательного завода (Кемеровская область)
summary: The article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the stored waste from the Berikul gold mining plant (Kemerovo Region), using geochemical, geophysical, and econometric methods. Using electrical tomography method, geoelectric sec
content: The article presents the results of a comprehensive study of the stored waste from the Berikul gold mining plant (Kemerovo Region), using geochemical, geophysical, and econometric methods. Using electrical tomography method, geoelectric sections (transverse and along the dam’s contour) and a 3D model of the storage facility were constructed; they describe the location of zones with a specific electrical resistance varying within the range of 3-800 Ohm·m, which makes it possible to determine the configuration of conductive zones in the internal structure. From the stored waste, which has a thickness of 5-7 m, mineralized water filters into the underground horizons, resulting in the formation of a depression characterized by an electrical resistivity (ER) of ~200 Ohm·m, which is significantly lower than the ER of the surrounding rocks. The zone of reduced resistance extends deeper than 40 m, which clearly indicates the vertical spread of the drainage system, possibly along a weakened zone in the granodiorite massif. Additionally, the formation of highly conductive areas is clearly visible on resistance maps up to 20-40 m. Samples of solid matter and water were taken from the resulting small bodies of water to determine their chemical composition. The stored waste is characterized by a contrasting composition in different parts of the storage facility; accordingly, both the physicochemical parameters and the ability of elements to transfer into solutions vary over a wide range. The majority of the waste material produces an acidic reaction in the pore waters and has a high mineralization. Water extracts from the samples cakes indicate a significant proportion of easily soluble compounds in the waste material. The content of metals and metalloids in water from surface ponds (maximum Fe 7800, Al 590, Zn 160, As 1600, Be 0.022 mg/l) indicates a high environmental hazard posed by these waste materials, while also suggesting the potential attractiveness of the site for the further recovery of useful components. An assessment has been carried out of the damage caused by the storage facility to water bodies within its influence zone – 470 million rubles.

title: Перспективы использования отходов содового производства в различных отраслях
summary: This paper presents a review and analysis of scientific articles and patents addressing the disposal and processing of soda production waste. Examples of methods for reducing the toxicity of sludge, using waste in construction (including ro
content: This paper presents a review and analysis of scientific articles and patents addressing the disposal and processing of soda production waste. Examples of methods for reducing the toxicity of sludge, using waste in construction (including road construction), and processing it into chemical compounds are provided. Particular attention is paid to the use of sludge for soil reclamation. The ammonia-soda process (the Solvay process) for producing soda ash is the predominant method worldwide. A significant drawback of this process is the generation of hazardous production waste, which necessitates compliance with environmental requirements and regulations during storage and processing. Russian practices for managing soda production waste lag behind European ones due to low prices for primary natural raw materials, the heterogeneity of waste composition and properties, the need for preliminary waste treatment, and the low level of environmental payments by enterprises for waste disposal. Tightening environmental safety requirements for soda ash production waste and the high cost of maintaining settling ponds are driving the development of processing methods. The choice of processing method depends on the plant᾽s location, energy capacity, and the company᾽s financial condition. The use of sludge in the production of building materials is limited by the presence of chloride ions, small particle size, thixotropic properties of the material, and variability in sludge composition. Road construction is the most promising avenue in terms of disposal volumes and the use of waste without additional treatment. The use of waste for land reclamation requires a selective approach to site selection and additional research. Despite the wide range of possible applications for soda production waste, the problem of its disposal remains pressing. This is due to the volumes of soda production and the resulting waste, as well as the need for financial investment to implement disposal methods

summary: Mae Hong Son (MHS) Province in northern Thailand constantly faces social and environmental crises caused by forest fires. This study designed policies to integrate hemp into the agricultural extension system to mitigate land preparation bur
content: Mae Hong Son (MHS) Province in northern Thailand constantly faces social and environmental crises caused by forest fires. This study designed policies to integrate hemp into the agricultural extension system to mitigate land preparation burning. A survey of 200 households from three communities, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions (FGDs), and observations were conducted. The results showed that forest fires cause distinct impacts on livelihoods, health, and the environment, while existing control measures are insufficient. Hemp products have significant potential as an inclusive alternative for income enhancement and value-added product development. A Social Return on Investment (SROI) of 2.5:1 illustrated significant economic and social benefits. This framework shifts toward livelihood-based mitigation, demonstrating that integrating a structured hemp value chain into agricultural extension services can effectively reduce burning and enhance community resilience in MHS.

title: Association of plasma legacy and emerging PFASs with HBV-related hepatocellular carcinoma risk: a case-control study with network toxicology and molecular simulation analyses
summary: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) have been increasingly associated with liver injury in human populations, raising concerns about their potential health effects; however, the relationship between PFAS exposure and hepa
content: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) have been increasingly associated with liver injury in human populations, raising concerns about their potential health effects; however, the relationship between PFAS exposure and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains inconsistent. Methods We conducted a case-control study involving 390 hepatitis B-related HCC cases and 390 hepatitis B surface antigen-positive controls. Logistic, linear, weighted quantile sum (WQS), and Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models assessed associations of plasma PFAS exposure with HCC and liver injury markers. Network toxicology, differential expression analyses of 103 paired clinical tissue samples and TCGA-LIHC data, and 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations explored potential molecular interactions. Results Plasma 6:2 Cl-PFESA concentrations were associated with higher risks of HCC and elevated liver injury markers, with ALT and AST statistically accounting for part of the observed association. Restricted cubic spline analyses revealed significant non-linear associations of 6:2 Cl-PFESA with HCC risk and AST levels. WQS analysis assigned the highest mixture weight to 6:2 Cl-PFESA, while BKMR analysis supported a positive association between the PFAS mixture and HCC. Network toxicology identified MAPK3 and TGFB1 as hub targets, and both were consistently upregulated in HCC tissues in the 103 paired dataset and TCGA-LIHC dataset. Molecular docking predicted the binding energy of -8.8 and -6.7 kcal/mol for MAPK3 and TGFB1, respectively, while MD simulations suggested stable ligand-protein complexes over 100 ns Conclusion 6:2 Cl-PFESA warrants further investigation in relation to HBV-related HCC, with MAPK3 and TGFB1 identified as candidate targets. Prospective studies with prediagnostic exposure measurements and fibrosis-matched controls are needed to clarify the temporality and causal relevance of these associations.

title: Criminalizing Corporate Greenwashing to Address Ecological Fraud Under the Indonesian Legal Framework
source: Bulletin of Social Studies and Community Development
summary: Greenwashing enables corporations to project an image of environmental responsibility while concealing environmentally harmful practices. In Indonesia, this conduct remains regulated through fragmented legal regimes and has not been formula
content: Greenwashing enables corporations to project an image of environmental responsibility while concealing environmentally harmful practices. In Indonesia, this conduct remains regulated through fragmented legal regimes and has not been formulated as a distinct criminal offense. This study examines how corporate greenwashing can be conceptualized as a criminal offense under Indonesian law and whether such a formulation justifies a shift from civil and administrative enforcement toward criminal liability. Using normative doctrinal legal research with statutory, conceptual, and comparative approaches, the study analyses greenwashing through the core elements of criminal liability, namely actus reus and mens rea, evaluates current Indonesian regulatory gaps, and compares selected foreign legal approaches. It finds that serious greenwashing can be understood as a form of corporate deception, but the existing Indonesian framework remains fragmented and inadequate to support coherent criminal liability. This study concludes that Indonesia should adopt an indirect criminalization model supported by a four-element offense structure to provide a clearer doctrinal and regulatory basis for addressing serious greenwashing

title: Solar powered membrane distillation for sustainable desalination from configuration selection to deployment readiness
summary: Water scarcity is increasingly coupled with energy insecurity, particularly in remote and arid regions where conventional desalination is constrained by electricity demand, brine management, and infrastructure cost. Solar powered membrane d
content: Water scarcity is increasingly coupled with energy insecurity, particularly in remote and arid regions where conventional desalination is constrained by electricity demand, brine management, and infrastructure cost. Solar powered membrane distillation (SPMD) is attractive because MD can operate with low- to moderate-temperature heat supplied by solar thermal collectors, photovoltaic-assisted subsystems, waste heat, or hybrid energy inputs. This review synthesizes SPMD from an integrated engineering perspective rather than as a catalogue of isolated technologies. A structured literature-selection procedure was applied using database searches, duplicate removal, keyword screening, eligibility criteria, and a quality check focused on configuration, membrane, module, energy, techno-economic, sustainability, and pilot-readiness evidence. The synthesis shows that DCMD provides simple operation and high flux but remains vulnerable to conductive heat loss; AGMD and PGMD improve heat recovery but typically reduce vapor transport; and CGMD/MGMD concepts attempt to recover internal heat while limiting mass-transfer resistance. The revised analysis further demonstrates that collector choice must be matched to the MD temperature window, thermal storage strategy, module geometry, membrane wetting resistance, and deployment scale. Major barriers are wetting, scaling, module heat loss, membrane lifetime, collector and storage cost, inconsistent reporting of GOR/STEC/LCOW, and limited long-duration outdoor validation. Future SPMD research should therefore prioritize collector–module co-design, durable omniphobic or low-impact membranes, standardized performance normalization, brine-management strategies, and field demonstrations that report reliability under real solar variability.

title: Rapid detection in forensic toxicology: current advances, applications, and challenges
summary: The demand for timely, on-site toxicological evidence across poisoning investigations, drug enforcement, and public health emergencies has driven the development of rapid detection technologies in forensic toxicology. This review critically
content: The demand for timely, on-site toxicological evidence across poisoning investigations, drug enforcement, and public health emergencies has driven the development of rapid detection technologies in forensic toxicology. This review critically assesses the current landscape of rapid detection technologies, including portable chromatography-mass spectrometry, handheld spectrometers, lateral flow immunoassays, aptamer-based sensors, and electrochemical devices. Instrument-based methods offer definitive identification but face limitations in cost, complexity, and sensitivity for trace analysis. Sensor-based platforms prioritize simplicity and accessibility yet struggle with matrix interference, quantitative accuracy, and differentiation of new psychoactive substances (NPS) isomers. Despite significant advances, key translation barriers include a lack of standardization and limited field-relevant validation. We outline priority areas for future research, such as validation using authentic forensic specimens, integration of machine learning for adaptive data processing, and sustained collaboration to establish standardized protocols and evidentiary frameworks. Rapid detection technologies are not poised to replace laboratory analysis but to complement it, extending the reach of forensic toxicology into the field and enabling real-time decision-making for public health and safety.

title: Who Decides What to Measure? Social Entrepreneurs’ Ethical Decision-Making Dilemmas in the New Era of Mandatory Sustainability Reporting
summary: Mandatory sustainability reporting is reshaping how organizations measure and communicate their impact, and its influence is no longer limited to large corporations. Emerging regulatory frameworks and standardized metrics are expected to tr
content: Mandatory sustainability reporting is reshaping how organizations measure and communicate their impact, and its influence is no longer limited to large corporations. Emerging regulatory frameworks and standardized metrics are expected to trickle down into the world of social entrepreneurship, a field historically grounded in impact-driven values, context-specific outcomes, and normative commitments to inclusion, justice, and systemic change. In this commentary, we argue that the rise of mandatory sustainability reporting generates ethical dilemmas for social entrepreneurs as they navigate tensions between external reporting requirements and their normative commitments. We identify five interrelated ethical dilemmas related to ideology, identity, mission, resourcing, and collaboration, and examine how they unfold across four stages of ethical decision-making: moral awareness, moral judgment, moral intent, and moral behavior. In doing so, we offer a “thick conceptualization” of mandatory sustainability reporting as a moral issue that renders accountability decisions ethically consequential for social entrepreneurs and outline the resulting avenues for future research.

title: Nicotine Equivalence Across Modern Delivery Systems: A Clinical Framework for Perioperative Assessment
summary: Background: Nicotine use is a well-established risk factor for impaired bone healing, infection, and poor outcomes following orthopedic surgery. Although perioperative assessment traditionally focuses on cigarette smoking, nicotine consumpt
content: Background: Nicotine use is a well-established risk factor for impaired bone healing, infection, and poor outcomes following orthopedic surgery. Although perioperative assessment traditionally focuses on cigarette smoking, nicotine consumption has shifted toward electronic cigarettes, oral nicotine pouches, and other alternative systems. Many of these products deliver nicotine doses that equal or exceed those of traditional cigarettes, yet no standardized clinical method exists to quantify and compare exposure across products. This review provides an updated framework for nicotine exposure equivalence using cigarette pack equivalents, enabling clinicians to estimate systemic nicotine absorption across delivery systems. Methods: A narrative review was conducted of PubMed, Google Scholar, and Scopus for studies related to nicotine delivery systems, orthopedic outcomes, bone healing, and fracture through 2024. Nicotine concentrations from major brands and route-specific bioavailability data were identified from the literature. Cigarette pack equivalents were calculated using published bioavailability estimates and standardized against estimated systemic nicotine delivery from one pack of cigarettes. Results: Our model demonstrates many alternative products deliver nicotine comparable to or exceeding traditional cigarettes: a single 5,000-puff disposable vape delivers systemic nicotine equivalent to approximately 25 packs of cigarettes, a can of 6 mg nicotine pouches is exceeds 2 packs, and a single JUUL pod approximates 1 pack. Discussion: Despite differences in delivery mechanisms and pharmacokinetics, nicotine's negative effects on fracture and wound healing remain present. As nicotine usage evolves, surgeons must evaluate usage beyond cigarettes alone. This framework provides a practical method to estimate total and systemic nicotine exposure across delivery systems.

title: Audit Committee Financial Expertise and Sustainability Reporting of Listed Deposit Money Banks in Nigeria: Moderated by Women Chairperson
source: Emirati Journal of Business Economics & Social Studies
summary: Sustainability reporting has become an integral aspect of corporate governance as stakeholders increasingly demand transparency regarding environmental, social, and governance performance. In the Nigerian banking sector, Deposit Money Banks
content: Sustainability reporting has become an integral aspect of corporate governance as stakeholders increasingly demand transparency regarding environmental, social, and governance performance. In the Nigerian banking sector, Deposit Money Banks are strategically positioned to promote sustainable finance; however, sustainability disclosures remain uneven across institutions. This study examines the effect of audit committee financial expertise on sustainability reporting of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria, while assessing the moderating role of audit committee women chairperson. The study adopted an ex‑post facto research design using secondary data extracted from the audited annual reports of all fourteen (14) listed DMBs in Nigeria for the period 2010–2024. Data were analysed using panel regression techniques with the aid of STATA. Findings revealed that audit committee financial expertise has a positive and statistically significant effect on sustainability reporting. The presence of a woman chairperson on the audit committee was also found to significantly enhance sustainability reporting quality. Additionally, the moderating effect of audit committee women chairperson on the relationship between audit committee financial expertise and sustainability reporting was statistically significant. The study concludes that audit committee financial expertise significantly enhances the quality of sustainability reporting among Nigerian deposit money banks. Similarly, audit committee women chairperson contributes positively and does significantly moderate the effect of audit committee financial expertise on sustainability reporting. The study recommends that Nigerian banks should strengthen audit committees by appointing members with strong financial and accounting expertise. Similarly, Regulators should promote gender diversity and encourage women leadership among the audit committee to improve inclusivity and ethical governance.

title: PRODUCTION OF PROTEIN-RICH PRODUCT FRACTIONS FROM OILY SEEDS AND NUTS BY SUPERCRITICAL CO2 EXTRACTION: A SUSTAINABLE APPROACH FOR MULTI-COMPONENT VALORIZATION
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Oilseeds and nuts are important sources of edible oils, proteins, dietary fibers, phenolic compounds, phytosterols, tocopherols, and other bioactive constituents. However, conventional oil extraction processes frequently generate defatted m
content: Oilseeds and nuts are important sources of edible oils, proteins, dietary fibers, phenolic compounds, phytosterols, tocopherols, and other bioactive constituents. However, conventional oil extraction processes frequently generate defatted meals and oil cakes that are primarily used as low-value animal feed despite their considerable nutritional and functional potential. Therefore, the development of integrated fractionation strategies capable of recovering multiple valuable components from a single raw material is essential for improving resource efficiency and supporting the transition toward a circular bioeconomy. Supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO₂) extraction has emerged as a promising green technology for the selective removal of lipids from oil-rich matrices because of its tunable solvating properties, relatively low processing temperatures, limited solvent residues, and potential for CO₂ recycling (Sahena et al., 2009; Chew et al., 2021). In particular, SC-CO₂ defatting can produce protein-enriched fractions while simultaneously recovering high-value oil fractions, thereby creating opportunities for multi-component valorization of oilseeds and nuts. Previous studies have demonstrated that SC-CO₂ treatment can effectively reduce the lipid content of seed and nut matrices and improve the suitability of the resulting protein-rich fractions for subsequent dry fractionation or protein extraction (Kumar et al., 1996; Rosa-Sibakov et al., 2025). Recent research has further demonstrated that SC-CO₂ processing can influence protein solubility, gelation, water- and oil-holding capacities, foaming, and emulsification properties, indicating that the technology may function not only as a defatting step but also as a tool for tailoring protein functionality (Subramanian et al., 2025). In the context of nuts, defatted oil cakes from almond, walnut, and cashew processing contain substantial amounts of protein and carbohydrates and can serve as substrates for the production of protein ingredients, peptides, dietary fiber, and other value-added products (Badgujar et al., 2022). Consequently, the integration of SC-CO₂ extraction with downstream protein concentration, dry fractionation, enzymatic hydrolysis, and bioactive compound recovery represents a promising biorefinery strategy. This approach can reduce processing waste, increase the economic value of oilseed and nut biomass, and contribute to more sustainable food production systems. Nevertheless, high-pressure equipment requirements, energy demand associated with compression, limited solubility of highly polar compounds, and the need for process optimization remain important challenges for industrial implementation. Overall, SC-CO₂-based integrated fractionation has considerable potential to transform oilseeds and nuts from single-product oil sources into multifunctional raw materials for the sustainable production of oils, protein-rich ingredients, fibers, and bioactive compounds.

title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecul
content: Abstract Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantum-transport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. This connectivity inversion is rationalized by a minimal Green’s function analysis as a layer-parity effect that changes the phase condition governing quantum interference in opposite-layer transport. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even–odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.

title: The large Hadron electron collider as a bridge project for CERN
source: Journal of Physics G Nuclear and Particle Physics
summary: Abstract The LHeC is the project for delivering electron-nucleon collisions at CERN using the HL-LHC beams. An Energy Recovery Linac in racetrack configuration will provide 50 GeV electrons to achieve centre-of-mass energies around 1 TeV/nu
content: Abstract The LHeC is the project for delivering electron-nucleon collisions at CERN using the HL-LHC beams. An Energy Recovery Linac in racetrack configuration will provide 50 GeV electrons to achieve centre-of-mass energies around 1 TeV/nucleon and instantaneous luminosities around 10^34 cm^-2 s^-1 . The LHeC program elaborated in the CDR of 2021 included a phase with concurrent operation of electron-hadron and hadron-hadron collisions, followed by a standalone phase of electron-hadron collisions only. In view of the current HL-LHC schedule, in this paper we have examined the possibilities of a program after the regular HL-LHC program with only electron-proton operation. In this operation mode, the LHeC would serve as an impactful bridge project between major colliders at CERN. The standalone physics program comprises electroweak, Higgs, top-quark, BSM and strong interaction physics. In addition, it empowers the physics analyses at the HL-LHC by retrofitting measurements and searches with significantly more precise knowledge of the proton structure and alpha-s. The accelerator technology deployed in the Energy Recovery Linac for the LHeC is a major stepping-stone for the performance, cost reduction and training for future colliders. The capital investments in the LHeC electron accelerator can be reused in a cost-efficient way as the injector for the FCC-ee. Finally, data from the LHeC are essential to enable the physics potential of any new high-energy hadron collider. The operational plan of 6 years easily fits in the period between two major colliders at CERN. Similar to the LHeC empowering the HL-LHC physics program, the FCC-eh would be an impactful addition to the FCC physics program.

title: Microbial carbon use efficiency emerges from interactions between soil structure and life-history strategies
summary: Abstract. Microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE) is believed to be a key regulator of the accumulation of persistent soil organic carbon. Microbial processing of organic carbon in soil occurs in the pore network, the properties of which are
content: Abstract. Microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE) is believed to be a key regulator of the accumulation of persistent soil organic carbon. Microbial processing of organic carbon in soil occurs in the pore network, the properties of which are known to affect microbial activity. However, the effects of interactions between pore architecture, and microbial life-history strategies on carbon dynamics, and house these interactions are modulated by moisture regime, remain poorly understood. Here, we use a spatially explicit model based on a cellular automaton, applied to realistic soil pore networks derived from X-ray tomographic images, to investigate how pore geometry and organic matter distribution shape microbial dynamics and CUE. The model explicitly represents r- and K-strategists that are either motile or immobile, and have different resource requirements for growth, maintenance and motility. The constraints imposed on substrate diffusion and the spatial domain in which motile bacteria can effectively disperse by the moisture regime are explicitly represented in the model, in order to capture how moisture regulate decomposer access to resources. The simulations show that pore architecture has a significant effect on microbial CUE. Micropores promoted high CUE and a dominance of K-strategists by limiting substrate diffusion, reducing pore connectivity, and constraining microbial access to spatially isolated resources. In contrast, macropores with high connectivity and greater substrate accessibility favor r-strategists, rapid biomass turnover and lower CUE. Motility emerges as advantageous in connected, carbon-rich macropores, but energetically unfavourable in confined or poorly connected micropores, where immobile strategies outperform motile ones. Overall, our results indicate that microbial CUE is not an intrinsic property of life-strategies alone, but emerges from the interaction between microbial life-strategies and pore-scale physical constraints. This study suggests that soil structure influences microbial strategies by limiting resource availability and dispersal.

title: Transitional calcite-aragonite stacking as a signature of hexagonal aragonite in biogenic and inorganic deposits
summary: Abstract Aragonite abundantly crystallizes in marine and continental environments and occurs ubiquitously in biominerals, despite being metastable under ambient conditions. To resolve this apparent contradiction, we studied the crystal stru
content: Abstract Aragonite abundantly crystallizes in marine and continental environments and occurs ubiquitously in biominerals, despite being metastable under ambient conditions. To resolve this apparent contradiction, we studied the crystal structure of aragonite that grew on calcite of biogenic (Berger Károly cave; Hungary) and inorganic (Sonnenberg; Italy and Erzberg; Austria) origin, in a range of natural settings and temperatures. Electron microscopy measurements show (001) stacking faults (SFs) in the first-grown aragonite. Structural modelling combined with theory-based optimization suggests that the crystal structure of this new type of SF can be explained by the presence of (000l) calcite-like layers within aragonite. Abundant (0001) calcite twins occur in the last-grown calcite, and hexarag, the hypothetical hexagonal polymorph of aragonite, was identified across the calcite twin interfaces. Oxygen isotope data indicate that both the Berger-Károly and Sonnenberg samples formed under non-equilibrium conditions, whereas the Erzberg aragonite formed near equilibrium, possibly explaining the defect-free structure. The presence of (001) SFs and (0001) calcite twins testifies to the formation of transitional calcite-aragonite structures, suggests the occurrence of a hexarag precursor phase and provides new insights into the long-debated mechanism of metastable aragonite formation in dynamically evolving (bio)geologic environments.

title: THEOBROMA: an aggregated open database of 1.13 million natural products with per-compound license auditing, three-tier classification, and stereochemistry-aware deduplication
summary: Abstract Natural products remain one of the most productive sources of pharmacologically active compounds for drug discovery. Open aggregators attribute licenses at database granularity, and the consequences of that choice have become tangi
content: Abstract Natural products remain one of the most productive sources of pharmacologically active compounds for drug discovery. Open aggregators attribute licenses at database granularity, and the consequences of that choice have become tangible as the field grows. A recent relicensing event in one constituent source (the September 2024 transition of the Natural Products Atlas to CC BY-NC 4.0) demonstrates how database-level licensing propagates across an aggregate and motivates the per-compound audit framework presented here. The same peer cohort separately leaves classification provenance and stereoisomer-family relations coarser than either layer warrants. THEOBROMA, accessible at https://theobroma.l3s.uni-hannover.de , integrates 1,132,805 natural products from 29 open sources under a per-compound license audit that resolves each compound’s license tier across all attesting sources under a most-restrictive-wins rule, identifying 900,103 compounds (79.5%) under open-use licenses and providing the per-source attestation chain and resolved tier through a dedicated audit endpoint and a query- time license filter. A three-tier classification labels all but 21 compounds by the provenance of the assignment (55.3% curated source labels, 18.2% NPClassifier tool assignments, 26.5% model-inferred). Deduplication at the full 27-character InChIKey retains 1,132,805 entries across 486,032 connectivity families, exposed via a dedicated /api/stereoisomers/<COMP id> endpoint and a radial-family display. Per-compound license provenance is the primary differentiator, while classification stratification and stereoisomer-family exposure add finer-grained access to two related axes, supporting license-compatible virtual screening and isomer-specific bioactivity analysis at corpus scale. As an evolving open resource, THEOBROMA pairs continuous pipeline maintenance with interactive geographic, taxonomic, and chemical-space exploration. Graphical Abstract THEOBROMA integrates 1,132,805 natural products from 29 open sources across three axes. A per-compound license audit resolves each compound to the most restrictive tier attested by any source, giving 891,860 permissive open, 225,536 non-commercial, 8,243 public domain and 7,166 unspecified, so that 900,103 compounds (79.5%) are open-licensed. A three-tier classification records the provenance of each label as source-supplied (55.3%), tool-assigned (18.2%), or model-inferred (26.5%), leaving 21 compounds unclassified. Deduplication at the full 27-character InChIKey retains the stereochemical and protonation variants that 14-character truncation would erase, illustrated by the (E,E)- and (Z,E)-curcumin pair shown.

title: Friction surfacing of Al2O3 reinforced aluminium coatings on low carbon steel with microstructural and tribological characterization
summary: Friction surfacing (FS) was employed to create Al–7.5 wt% Al 2 O 3 metal matrix composite coatings on low carbon steel (AISI 1018), enhancing surface performance by solid-state processing. Two parameter sets were examined to identify their
content: Friction surfacing (FS) was employed to create Al–7.5 wt% Al 2 O 3 metal matrix composite coatings on low carbon steel (AISI 1018), enhancing surface performance by solid-state processing. Two parameter sets were examined to identify their effects on coating microstructure and tribology. SEM–EDS showed dense, defect-free coatings with uniform reinforcement particle distribution, good metallurgical bonding, and a narrow compositional transition across the coating–substrate interface. The higher rotational speed and axial load promoted greater material plasticization, resulting in improved coating continuity and consolidation. The EBSD investigation showed significant grain refinement from 12.6 μm in the consumable rod to 8.6 μm in the coating, indicating dynamic recrystallization during FS. Effective microstructural stabilization was confirmed by a considerable rise in high-angle grain boundary fraction. The combination of grain refinement, strain hardening, and dispersion strengthening by Al 2 O 3 particles significantly increased microhardness from 160 HV for the substrate to 250 HV for the coating. Dry sliding tribological investigations indicated significant weight loss, specific wear rate, and coefficient of friction reductions compared to the substrate. The improved coating reduced weight loss by 67.2% and specific wear rate by 71.8%. The better performance at higher energy settings shows how FS process parameters improve coating integrity, microstructural refinement, and tribology.

title: Sustainable Maritime Fuel Pathway Resilience Under Geopolitical Corridor Disruption: A Quantitative Evaluation for Middle East Fleet Operations
source: Abu Dhabi International Petroleum Exhibition & Conference (ADIPEC)
summary: Abstract This paper evaluates the resilience of sustainable maritime fuel pathways, including biofuels, LNG, methanol, ammonia, and hydrogen, under geopolitical corridor disruptions affecting Middle East fleet operations. Building on previo
content: Abstract This paper evaluates the resilience of sustainable maritime fuel pathways, including biofuels, LNG, methanol, ammonia, and hydrogen, under geopolitical corridor disruptions affecting Middle East fleet operations. Building on previously developed efficiency-first and fuel-evaluation frameworks, the study quantifies how Red Sea rerouting, Strait of Hormuz restriction, and bunkering-infrastructure concentration risk alter fuel-pathway feasibility, lifecycle compliance exposure under FuelEU Maritime and the IMO Net-Zero Framework, biofuel volume requirements, and transition economics across a simulated sixty-vessel fleet. A geopolitical scenario overlay is applied to an interaction-adjusted efficiency baseline and phased fuel-pathway model previously validated for bulk carrier, tanker, and gas carrier segments. Three scenarios are constructed: (A) sustained Red Sea rerouting via the Cape of Good Hope, extending Middle East-EU corridor distances by approximately 3,500 nautical miles; (B) Strait of Hormuz partial restriction, disrupting Fujairah-dependent bunkering access; and (C) compound disruption combining both with war-risk premium escalation. Each scenario re-computes well-to-wake intensity exposure, biofuel blending volumes, corridor-fuel bunkering feasibility, CII trajectory degradation, and retrofit net present value. A composite resilience score is introduced to rank fuel pathways by route independence, infrastructure diversification, fuel flexibility, and capital robustness under disruption. Biofuels demonstrate the highest pathway resilience across all disruption scenarios due to their drop-in compatibility, minimal infrastructure requirements, and route-independent deployment. Under Red Sea rerouting, fleet fuel demand increases by 25 to 35 percent on affected corridors, expanding lifecycle compliance deficits under well-to-wake regimes. Efficiency-adjusted baselines absorb a significant share of this increase, reducing the biofuel blending volumes required to close intensity gaps. For a high-exposure containership and RoPax subset, post-efficiency biofuel requirements at B30 blending remain 26 percent lower than pre-efficiency baselines even under disrupted routing. Corridor-dependent LNG and methanol strategies exhibit high vulnerability under Strait of Hormuz restriction, as Fujairah, the region's primary bunkering hub, becomes inaccessible, collapsing supply reliability for fuels requiring specialized infrastructure. Ammonia and hydrogen readiness timelines extend further under disruption due to compounded infrastructure concentration risk. Onboard carbon capture retains value as a constraint-relief option where sustainable fuel access is geographically limited. War-risk premiums at 0.7 to 1.0 percent of hull value compress capital budgets, favoring low-CAPEX biofuel adoption over high-capital fuel-switching retrofits.
