title: Waste-derived aluminosilicate reinforcements in copper matrix composites for tribological applications: a critical review and future perspectives
summary: Copper matrix composites (CMCs) have attracted considerable attention for advanced tribological materials. They combine copper’s excellent thermal and electrical conductivity with enhanced mechanical and wear performance from the reinforcin
content: Copper matrix composites (CMCs) have attracted considerable attention for advanced tribological materials. They combine copper’s excellent thermal and electrical conductivity with enhanced mechanical and wear performance from the reinforcing phase. Copper’s relatively low hardness and poor wear resistance limit its application under severe sliding conditions. This review critically examines recent advances in waste-derived aluminosilicate-reinforced copper matrix composites, with particular attention to calcined clay-derived metakaolin (MK) as an underexplored potential reinforcement. This review critically analyzes peer-reviewed articles published from 2020 to 2026 within the processing, microstructure, and tribological performance framework. To examine relationships among reinforcement parameters, microstructural evolution, fabrication routes, interfacial phenomena, wear mechanisms, and resulting mechanical, tribological, and functional performance. Although conventional ceramic reinforcements such as SiC, Al 2 O 3 , and TiC can enhance the mechanical and wear performance of copper composites, their production and processing increase the cost, energy, and environmental considerations. Waste-derived aluminosilicates such as fly ash (FA) and rice husk ash (RHA) offer waste valorization benefits and also reduce the dependency on conventional ceramic feedstocks. Metakaolin (MK) is a compositionally related option with a less experimentally established reinforcement pathway, whose performance in a Cu matrix needs direct validation. For example, increasing FA from 0 to 20 wt.% in a representative Cu–FA system increased hardness from 69 to 145 HV and reduced wear rate from 908 × 10 −5 to 479 × 10 −5 mm 3 /m and COF from 0.55 to 0.35, but reduced electrical conductivity from 80 to 32% IACS. Particle agglomeration, poor wettability, weak interfacial bonding, residual porosity, feedstock and processing variability, and concerns about the retention of copper’s inherent conductivity are the major challenges that continue to limit their broad application. Priority research needs include direct validation of Cu-MK systems, interface engineering, long-term tribological performance, reinforcement optimization, hybrid reinforcement systems, conductivity-performance trade-off assessment, and computationally assisted materials design. Overall, this review provides a materials science perspective for designing aluminosilicate-reinforced Cu composite through integration of processing, microstructure, tribological performance, functional property retention, and evidence of maturity.

title: Different effects of oligomerization on frontier-orbital gaps and bright excitations in heptazine-and triazine-based carbon nitride models
summary: Abstract Understanding how molecular structure affects light absorption is important for the study of carbon nitride building blocks. Here, density functional theory and time-dependent density functional theory calculations were used to com
content: Abstract Understanding how molecular structure affects light absorption is important for the study of carbon nitride building blocks. Here, density functional theory and time-dependent density functional theory calculations were used to compare six heptazine-and triazine-based molecular models with different sizes and connectivities. The optimized heptazine-based structures were largely planar, whereas the triazine-based models showed greater deviations from planarity. The two families exhibited different changes in their frontier-orbital gaps. In the gas phase, the heptazinebased gap changed only slightly from the first to the second model and decreased further in the third, giving values of 4.32, 4.29, and 3.87 eV. The corresponding triazine-based values were 3.74, 4.80, and 4.67 eV. In contrast, the first bright excitation energies were 5.16, 3.54, and 3.28 eV for the heptazine-based models and 4.74, 3.95, and 3.96 eV for the triazine-based models, using an oscillator-strength threshold of 0.01. Analysis of the low-lying states shows that the lowest singlet excitation and the first bright transition can respond differently to oligomerization. CPCM calculations at fixed geometries revealed additional changes in excitation energies and intensities. These results show why frontier-orbital gaps, excited-state energies, and transition strengths must be considered together when comparing the optical properties of finite carbon nitride models.

title: Molecular Trends in the Oxidative H Abstraction of Organic Molecules on Oxide Surfaces: Implications for Electrolyte Reactivity at the Positive Electrode in Li-Ion Batteries
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract Oxidative degradation of carbonate solvents via C–H activation is observed on late transition metal oxide positive electrodes in Li-ion batteries. However, analogous reactivity of other classes of organic molecules on oxides is not
content: Abstract Oxidative degradation of carbonate solvents via C–H activation is observed on late transition metal oxide positive electrodes in Li-ion batteries. However, analogous reactivity of other classes of organic molecules on oxides is not well understood. Here, we used density functional theory calculations to show how C–H activation changes from deprotonation to oxidative hydrogen abstraction as the lattice oxygen activity increases by moving the Fermi level closer to the oxygen 2p-band center. By using a set of 23 small molecules with 50 nonequivalent C–H bonds, spanning a broad range of functional groups and substitutions, we show how relevant energies of the isolated molecules impact the driving force for degradation reactions at the surface of LiNiO2, an oxide with high lattice oxygen activity. We demonstrated that C–H bond oxidation free energy, measured as the free energy to substitute a C–H bond with a C–OH bond for the isolated molecule, is the descriptor with the most predictive power for the C–H activation driving force on an oxide with highly reactive lattice oxygen. Using this descriptor, we identified promising S- and F-containing compounds with enhanced stability toward C–H activation. These results pave the way for a rational design of novel electrolytes that minimize degradation and impedance growth of Ni-rich LiNixMnyCo1–x–yO2 (NMC) electrodes.

title: Adenosine A2A receptor dysfunction in the mouse hippocampus following benzyl butyl phthalate exposure through integrated transcriptomic and molecular dynamics analyses
summary: Benzyl butyl phthalate (BBP) is widely used as a plasticizer in numerous products. BBP has ability to cross the blood–brain barrier, and it accumulates in neurons. Therefore, identifying any vulnerable target pathway through which BBP opera
content: Benzyl butyl phthalate (BBP) is widely used as a plasticizer in numerous products. BBP has ability to cross the blood–brain barrier, and it accumulates in neurons. Therefore, identifying any vulnerable target pathway through which BBP operates is necessary for understanding their neurotoxicity. Here, we investigated whether BBP may disrupt adenosine A2A receptor (ADORA2A) signalling using an integrated transcriptomic and computational framework. Publicly available RNA-seq data revealed that ADORA2A expression was repressed in BBP exposed mice (3.7-fold downregulation; log2FC = −1.87, p = 5 × 10 −5 ), together with transcript isoform remodelling both annotated and novel isoforms, indicating possible effects on transcriptional regulation and transcript architecture. In addition, molecular docking was performed with ADORA2A-BBP, adenosine and preladenant as comparator ligands. BBP occupied the canonical ligand cavity, with a docking score of −7.46 kcal/mol. The findings suggest that BBP may interfere with hippocampal ADORA2A signalling, may pose a risk of neurotoxicity.

title: Land use and vegetation conditions shape the dynamics of ecosystem resilience in an arid and semi-arid region: evidence from the Fenhe River Basin, China
summary: Quantifying the spatiotemporal dynamics of watershed ecosystem resilience (ER) is crucial for ecological regulation and sustainable watershed management. In this study, long-term time-series remote sensing datasets were utilized to comprehe
content: Quantifying the spatiotemporal dynamics of watershed ecosystem resilience (ER) is crucial for ecological regulation and sustainable watershed management. In this study, long-term time-series remote sensing datasets were utilized to comprehensively characterize the spatiotemporal variations of ER in the Fenhe River Basin (FRB), China and particular emphasized on the role of vegetation cover in slowing the decline of ER. Specifically, two core ecosystem service indicators, namely carbon storage (CS) and habitat quality (HQ), as well as land use metrics were used to established a proxy for ER evaluation. The results demonstrated that CS and HQ exhibited spatially consistent distribution patterns across the basin, featuring high values in peripheral regions and low values in the central core area. Temporally, both CS and HQ exhibited slight degradation during the study period. The average CS decreased by 0.16 ton, while HQ dropped by 0.04, which correspondingly led to an overall decline in regional ER and severe fragmentation of high-resilience ecological zones. Land use transitions and fractional vegetation cover (FVC) were identified as the predominant coupled factors controlling the temporal fluctuations of ER. Importantly, this study identified a notable spatial mismatch between regional area and the spatiotemporal variations of integrated ecosystem services (i.e., CS and HQ) and ER, demonstrating that the loss of critical ecosystem service functions in core basin regions constitutes the primary driver of regional ER degradation. The improvement in vegetation conditions, reflected by an increase in vegetation coverage from 0.52 to 0.66, could not reverse the inherent degradation trajectory yet significantly mitigated the decline in ER. This study provides a robust remote sensing-based analytical framework and reliable scientific references for ecosystem health monitoring, vegetation restoration, and sustainable watershed governance, particularly in the semi-arid regions.

title: From Blue to Green: Demonstration of a pH-Dependent Fluorescence Shift of Carbon Quantum Dots
summary: Abstract Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have emerged as versatile, water-soluble nanomaterials with strong photoluminescence and tunable optical properties, making them promising candidates for applications in sensing, bioimaging, and optoelect
content: Abstract Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) have emerged as versatile, water-soluble nanomaterials with strong photoluminescence and tunable optical properties, making them promising candidates for applications in sensing, bioimaging, and optoelectronics. While inorganic quantum dots have long been established in educational settings, organic CQDs, particularly with functional responsiveness, remain underrepresented in K-12 science education. In this paper, we present a simple, safe, and low-cost bottom-up synthesis of fluorescent, pH-sensitive CQDs using ascorbic acid and sodium acetate, which were heated directly over a gas burner. The procedure takes less than 5 min and requires minimal equipment. The resulting CQDs exhibit bright blue-to-turquoise fluorescence under UV light. Under basic conditions, a bathochromic shift to green fluorescence occurs because of deprotonation of surface functional groups, accompanied by self-absorption. This pH-dependent behavior is also visible under daylight, showing a color shift from yellow to orange resulting from absorption and transmission. The experiment provides a tangible demonstration of surface chemistry, electronic transitions, and nanoscale structure–property relationships. Learners perceived the experiment as an easy procedure that contributes to a basic understanding of the nanoscale, as an accompanying assessment shows (n = 20). By combining low-cost materials, rapid synthesis, and vivid visual outcomes, we give an outlook on how this work will contribute to nanoscience education by offering a readily accessible and engaging pathway into the world of functional organic nanomaterials.

title: Combined experimental and simulation evaluation of interference-resilient and energy-efficient wireless sensor networks using ESP32, TSCH, and multi-criteria decision analysis
summary: Introduction Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) used in industrial monitoring and Internet of Things (IoT) applications must simultaneously maintain reliable data transmission, low communication delay, and efficient energy consumption under re
content: Introduction Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) used in industrial monitoring and Internet of Things (IoT) applications must simultaneously maintain reliable data transmission, low communication delay, and efficient energy consumption under resource and interference constraints. Methods This study combines an ESP32-based hardware-assisted interference-emulation platform with large-scale OMNeT++ network modeling and multi-criteria evaluation. A 300-node WSN comprising 240 end devices and 60 routers was evaluated using Star, Tree, conventional Mesh, and Mesh + Time Slotted Channel Hopping (TSCH) configurations. Performance was assessed using Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), mean transmission delay, energy consumption, and network-lifetime indicators. An additional reconstructed stochastic analysis used 20 independent runs per configuration, and scalability was evaluated for network populations from 50 to 1,000 nodes. Results In the archived scenario-level analysis, Mesh + TSCH increased PDR from 93% to 99%, reduced mean delay from 150 ms to 61 ms, reduced per-node energy consumption from 6.42 J to 2.14 J, and increased the reported LND from 30 to 120 days relative to conventional Mesh. In the reconstructed analysis, Mesh + TSCH maintained higher PDR (79.26 ± 0.83% vs. 51.46 ± 2.49%) and lower per-node energy consumption (59.02 ± 0.65 J vs. 125.96 ± 0.82 J), but showed higher mean end-to-end delay (97.18 ± 5.56 ms vs. 57.84 ± 1.44 ms). Discussion The results indicate that TSCH-enabled coordination provides robust reliability and energy-efficiency advantages, whereas its latency effect depends on scheduling and implementation conditions. The combined findings demonstrate an application–dependent reliability–energy—latency trade-off and support multi-criteria evaluation for WSN architecture selection.

title: Faulting and Hydrothermal Alteration in a Proterozoic Rapakivi Batholith: Coupling Geothermal Reservoir Formation and Element Mobility
summary: Abstract Crystalline rocks are increasingly recognized as geothermal targets, where reservoir parameters including porosity and permeability strongly reflect the coupled effects of brittle deformation and hydrothermal alteration. To quantif
content: Abstract Crystalline rocks are increasingly recognized as geothermal targets, where reservoir parameters including porosity and permeability strongly reflect the coupled effects of brittle deformation and hydrothermal alteration. To quantify how these effects modify reservoir properties in crystalline rocks, we integrate petrophysical, mineralogical, geochemical, geochronological, and structural data from the well exposed Vehmaa Rapakivi Batholith in southwestern Finland, an analogue for fault-hosted geothermal reservoirs in crystalline settings. The batholith records five alteration stages: (1) late-magmatic F-rich, (2) high-temperature cementation, (3) propylitic alteration, (4) quartz cementation, and (5) low-temperature oxidizing overprint. The strongest reservoir development is associated with Stage 3, where mineral dissolution, replacement, and microfracturing generated porosities of up to 18%, whereas Stage 2 produced dense cemented rocks with little preserved porosity. Subsequent quartz cementation and low-temperature oxidizing alteration further modified reservoir properties through localized mineral dissolution and fracture sealing. U-Pb ages of titanite and zircon confirm that Stages 1 and 2 began during the late crystallization to early cooling of the batholith at ~ 1.57 Ga, while a younger ~ 1.0 Ga age suggests much later fluid circulation or thermal resetting. Notably, kilometer-scale strike-slip faults and alteration networks transect much of the batholith, indicating that these processes can operate over rock volumes relevant to geothermal development. These processes also redistributed economically relevant elements, including REE, Sc, Sr, Sn, and Zn concentrated along the faults. Our results show that fracturing, dissolution, and cementation control crystalline reservoir quality, while fluid–rock reactions govern element mobility and mineralization, linking geothermal potential with critical element resources.

title: Palladium(II) aminoadamantane complexes: a promising approach to impair SARS-CoV-2 infection
summary: The rapid geographic spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection, the high genetic variability resulting in the emergence of new variants, and the increase in post-COVID syndrome justify the discovery of new molecules that can abrogate viral infection.
content: The rapid geographic spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection, the high genetic variability resulting in the emergence of new variants, and the increase in post-COVID syndrome justify the discovery of new molecules that can abrogate viral infection. The aminoadamantanes amantadine (atd), memantine (mtn), and rimantadine (rtd) are commercial drugs used in the clinical treatment of Alzheimer disease and Influenza A virus infection and therefore are attractive candidates for synthesis of coordination compounds to increase their biological activity. Here, we screened atd, rtd, and mtn, together with palladium (II) [Pd(II)] and their respective metal complexes Pd-atd, Pd-mtn, and Pd-rtd, for activity against SARS-CoV-2 infection. This analysis demonstrated that the complexes Pd-atd, Pd-mtn, and Pd-rtd had antiviral activity with selectivity indices of 14.2, 36.2, and 23.5, respectively. Further assays were conducted, and all Pd(II) complexes strongly inhibited >75% of SARS-CoV-2 entry. Additionally, the Pd(II) complexes were able to inhibit the Omicron (BA.2) variant, with Pd-rtd also being able to inhibit cell-to-cell spread. Pd-atd significantly inhibited all stages of the replicative cycle investigated here, showing multiple effects on virus infection. The coordination with Pd(II) resulted in more active compounds with different mechanisms of action. Resistance-associated mutations in Spike, nsp1, and nsp3 are consistent with the hypothesis that the antiviral activity of the Pd(II) complexes involves different protein interactions. The obtained results highlight the synthesis of promising Pd(II) metallodrugs with potential application for the treatment of COVID-19 infections.

title: Tunnels for Flood Control
summary: Damage caused by urban floods is on the rise. It is therefore important to understand the causes of and impacts of different types of flooding. Urban Floods in coastal areas are a growing issue of concern in both developed and developing co
content: Damage caused by urban floods is on the rise. It is therefore important to understand the causes of and impacts of different types of flooding. Urban Floods in coastal areas are a growing issue of concern in both developed and developing countries. They cause damage to buildings, utility works, housing, household assets, income losses in industries and trade, loss of employment to daily earners or temporary workers, and interruption to subway lines. Reducing the Risk then involves a set of measures contributing individually to risk reduction. Flood risk management requires the holistic development of a long-term strategy that balances current needs with future sustainability. Recognising existing risks and likely future changes is crucial. Measures are usually designed to control flood water using urban infrastructure, for example, flood tunnels, or environmental management. Measures are designed to keep people safe from flooding with the planning and management of the urban environment. The Regional Action Programmes (RAP), established by the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), provides concerted action to address rapid urbanisation with high motorisation rates, encouraging the use of digital technologies; deployment of resilient, flood protected urban transport; and transitioning towards low-carbon transport systems.

title: Nutritional content of the African horned cucumber (Cucumis metuliferus E. May. Ex Naudin) fruit grown under varying fertiliser types and growing environments, and its potential role in human nutrition
summary: The fruit sector is one of the key role players in food and nutritional security by supplying vital nutrients, increasing food availability, promoting dietary diversity, and contributing to economic stability. Currently, most fruit species
content: The fruit sector is one of the key role players in food and nutritional security by supplying vital nutrients, increasing food availability, promoting dietary diversity, and contributing to economic stability. Currently, most fruit species that contribute to food and nutritional supply in the fruit industry are exotic varieties such as mangoes, oranges, grapes, and English cucumbers, owing to the established and reputable literature on their agronomic practices and protocols. To achieve food and nutritional security globally, the introduction of indigenous fruit crops, especially in regions where they are native, appear to be a promising strategy that could accelerate the attainment of Sustainable Development Goal 2 (Zero Hunger). Additionally, this inclusion may assist in complementing existing commercial crops to substantially boost communal nutrition and food diversity by offering phytochemicals, nutrients, and minerals, which are vital for sustained health and wellness. Among such crops is the African horned cucumber ( Cucumis metuliferus E. May. Ex Naudin), an indigenous fruit crop of Southern Africa claimed to be nutrient dense due to its abundance of vitamins and minerals, which human beings require in smaller and larger quantities daily. However, literature on the fruit’s biochemical content response when subjected to differing growing environments and the use of specific fertiliser types appears to be scanty. Therefore, the current study evaluated the impact of differing growing environments (greenhouse and shade net) and fertiliser types (organic and inorganic/chemical) on the biochemical constituents of African horned cucumber fruit. In addition, the fruit nutritional content was compared with the average recommended daily intake to determine its potential contribution to human health and nutrition. The results showed that a treatment combination of shade net and chemical fertilisers increased phosphorus (577.7 mg/100g DW) and potassium (1074 mg/100g DW) compared to other treatments. As a result, growers are encouraged to consider the greenhouse environment combined with chemical fertilisers for maximising phytochemicals such as total phenols and vitamin C, whereas the treatment combination of shade net and chemical fertiliser appeared to be the best for maximising minerals such as calcium, phosphorus, and iron.

title: Transforming shores: remote sensing analyses of two decades of coastal change in the Arabian Gulf (2001–2021)
summary: Coastal zones along the Arabian Gulf have experienced extensive urban expansion and land–water transformation over the past two decades, yet comparable Gulf-wide evidence on how these changes vary across national, urban, and local scales re
content: Coastal zones along the Arabian Gulf have experienced extensive urban expansion and land–water transformation over the past two decades, yet comparable Gulf-wide evidence on how these changes vary across national, urban, and local scales remains limited. Building on a previously published regional assessment, this study extends the analysis through normalized comparisons across eight Gulf countries, quantitative assessment of 13 coastal urban centers, and examination of 33 selected 10 × 10 km Focus Zones. Landsat imagery from 2001 to 2021 and Random Forest classification were used to map urbanization, water-to-nonwater transitions, and nonwater-to-water transitions. These transitions are operationally termed reclamation and inundation, respectively, without independently attributing their causes. Regional results indicate approximately 6,827 km 2 of nonurban-to-urban conversion, 1,011 km 2 of water-to-nonwater conversion, and 1,810 km 2 of nonwater-to-water conversion. The added comparisons reveal substantial differences in transformation patterns among countries, coastal urban centers, and selected local settings. Pooled overall classification accuracies were 92.00% for 2001 and 92.96% for 2021. Although mapped nonwater-to-water conversion exceeded the reverse transition regionally, this balance does not independently establish erosion, sea-level rise, permanent land loss, or flood risk. The analysis provides a consistent framework for comparing coastal transformation at regional, national, urban, and local scales, while highlighting the need to distinguish engineered development, natural coastal processes, and acquisition-related differences when interpreting mapped changes. Future work should integrate higher-frequency imagery, tidal normalization, elevation data, and field or very-high-resolution validation to better distinguish engineered, natural, and climate-related coastal processes. This study is therefore framed as a two-date, long-term change assessment based on endpoint comparisons between 2001 and 2021, rather than a continuous time-series analysis of the timing or sequence of change.

title: S1 Dataset. Provincial panel dataset for low-carbon transition and migrant workers' employment in China, 2006–2022
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset contains a balanced provincial panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2006 to 2022 (510 province-year observations) used in the baseline regressions, mechanism analysis, panel threshold analysis, and heterogeneity analysis. Variabl
content: This dataset contains a balanced provincial panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2006 to 2022 (510 province-year observations) used in the baseline regressions, mechanism analysis, panel threshold analysis, and heterogeneity analysis. Variable definitions and data sources are provided in the Data dictionary sheet.

title: Evaluation of Wall Construction Systems in Traditional Turkish Houses According to Geographical Regions
summary: Türkiye’s diverse climate and geography have produced marked regional variation in the materials, techniques and layering of exterior walls in traditional houses. This chapter presents a comparative literature review of traditional wall con
content: Türkiye’s diverse climate and geography have produced marked regional variation in the materials, techniques and layering of exterior walls in traditional houses. This chapter presents a comparative literature review of traditional wall construction across the seven geographical regions of Türkiye, with the Black Sea Region examined in its eastern and western sub-regions. Sources published between 1950 and 2026 were selected against predefined criteria and analysed with a four-stage framework for timber, adobe, brick and stone; the results were synthesised in four material-based tables and one cross-material synthesis table. Timber-framed walls dominate the humid, forested north and west; massive adobe and stone walls of 60–120 cm characterise the continental and arid interior and east; a masonry ground floor beneath a timber-framed upper floor recurs in all seismic regions; and brick shifts from infill to protective detailing southward. Wall typologies emerge from the interaction of climate, seismicity, topography and material availability.

title: Beyond single-property retention: how multifunctional composites lose serviceability under irradiation
summary: Retention of a single measured property does not, by itself, establish the serviceability of an irradiated multifunctional composite. This critical narrative review examines differential property evolution in radiation-shielding composites,
content: Retention of a single measured property does not, by itself, establish the serviceability of an irradiated multifunctional composite. This critical narrative review examines differential property evolution in radiation-shielding composites, silicon-carbide and carbon-based thermostructural composites, and fusion-magnet insulation. Comparisons are made within documented material and irradiation conditions, without treating absorbed dose, particle fluence and displacements per atom as a universal damage coordinate. Selected SiC/SiC studies show substantial thermal-transport degradation alongside retained flexural strength; C/SiC can stiffen while losing strength and deformation capacity. Cryogenic insulation illustrates a different limitation: a high measured breakdown voltage may coexist with structural damage, and the test medium can change the failure path. Direct post-ageing attenuation measurements in PP/PbO composites show reported dose-dependent differences between shielding, tensile and impact responses, but do not establish a universal failure order or component lifetime. Serviceability is defined at component level, relative to specified functions, loading and environmental conditions. A signed margin expresses each requirement relative to its own acceptance boundary; the first exhausted margin, not necessarily the fastest-changing property, limits serviceability under this convention. The review distinguishes measured response, validated surrogate inference and component qualification, and provides a reusable failure-route test matrix. Quantitative comparisons require appropriate uncertainty treatment, traceable irradiation histories and explicit post-irradiation conditioning. Where acceptance limits or adequate source statistics are unavailable, differential response remains informative but cannot be promoted to a demonstrated service-limit crossing.

title: Mapping and Quantitative Assessment of Vegetation Cover Using Sentinel-2 Satellite Data in Hunsur Taluk, Karnataka, India
summary: Trees and green cover support ecological stability, climate regulation, biodiversity, and human well-being, highlighting the need for accurate local-scale vegetation assessment. This study mapped and quantified green cover in Hunsur Taluk,
content: Trees and green cover support ecological stability, climate regulation, biodiversity, and human well-being, highlighting the need for accurate local-scale vegetation assessment. This study mapped and quantified green cover in Hunsur Taluk, Mysore District, Karnataka, using Sentinel-2 Level-2A multispectral imagery and supervised Random Forest classification. Sentinel-2 surface reflectance images acquired from January to December 2025 were processed in Google Earth Engine through cloud masking, annual median compositing, and clipping to the taluk boundary. The normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and enhanced vegetation index (EVI) were integrated with spectral bands to improve vegetation discrimination. Classification identified 294.83 km² (32.92%) of vegetated land and 600.57 km² (67.08%) of non-vegetated land. Among non-vegetated classes, barren land occupied 484.43 km² (54.10%), built-up areas 100.90 km² (11.27%), and water bodies 15.24 km² (1.70%). Vegetation was concentrated mainly in southern and southwestern Hunsur, whereas central and northern areas exhibited more extensive barren land, settlements, fallow fields, and fragmented vegetation. Moderate to high NDVI and EVI values were associated with denser vegetation, while low values characterized sparsely vegetated and non-vegetated surfaces. The classification achieved an overall accuracy of 94.73% and a kappa coefficient of 0.9132, indicating strong agreement with reference observations. These findings demonstrate the utility of integrating Sentinel-2 imagery, vegetation indices, and Random Forest classification for taluk-level green-cover mapping. The resulting spatial baseline can support land-use planning, vegetation monitoring, conservation prioritization, and sustainable landscape management in Hunsur Taluk. As an annual median composite was used, the map represents generalized vegetation conditions rather than seasonal extremes or fluctuations.

title: State Dependence of Soil‐Moisture Responses to Meteorological Dry–Wet Abrupt Alternation
summary: ABSTRACT Meteorological dry–wet abrupt alternation (M‐DWAA) is an important compound climate extreme that can impose complex stresses on agricultural and ecological systems through rapid shifts between water deficit and excess moisture. Its
content: ABSTRACT Meteorological dry–wet abrupt alternation (M‐DWAA) is an important compound climate extreme that can impose complex stresses on agricultural and ecological systems through rapid shifts between water deficit and excess moisture. Its impacts on land‐surface and ecosystem processes depend partly on whether and how meteorological signals are transmitted into soil moisture. However, the different types of soil‐moisture responses to M‐DWAA and the factors associated with their variability remain poorly understood. Here, global M‐DWAA events during 2001–2023 were identified using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and corresponding soil‐moisture responses were classified based on whether Standardized Soil Moisture Index (SSMI) anomalies exceeded predefined dry and wet response thresholds during different phases of M‐DWAA events. Random Forest models were further employed to evaluate the relative importance of factors associated with different soil‐moisture response types. The results show that the propagation of M‐DWAA signals into soil moisture was selective. Soil‐moisture responses during both dry and wet phases occurred in only 37.77% of M‐DWAA events, whereas more than half (54.05%) produced responses during only one phase. Moreover, soil‐moisture response patterns were strongly state‐dependent. Dual‐phase responses were generally associated with stronger atmospheric forcing and antecedent soil‐moisture conditions closer to neutral states. Random Forest analysis further identified antecedent soil moisture as the most important predictor, with hydroclimatic and land‐surface conditions providing additional explanatory information. These findings suggest that soil moisture exhibits state‐dependent filtering characteristics, which are associated with differences in how atmospheric dry–wet signals are expressed in terrestrial ecosystems, rather than responding uniformly to atmospheric forcing. This study provides a global perspective for understanding heterogeneous land‐surface responses and assessing ecosystem vulnerability and agricultural water availability risks under increasing climate variability.

title: Bibliometric and bibliographic review of sewage sludge by pyrolysis
summary: The growing global generation of sewage sludge, estimated at approximately 200 million tons per year, has intensified the need for sustainable and efficient management strategies. In this context, emerging trends point to a transition from
content: The growing global generation of sewage sludge, estimated at approximately 200 million tons per year, has intensified the need for sustainable and efficient management strategies. In this context, emerging trends point to a transition from conventional waste treatment to integrated resource recovery systems. Accordingly, pyrolysis has emerged as a promising thermochemical route for converting sewage sludge into value-added products while minimizing environmental impacts. Recent advances demonstrate that pyrolysis enables the recovery of key resources in the form of biochar, bio-oil, and non-condensable gases, depending on operating conditions, particularly temperature (400–700 °C). Biochar, typically containing more than 50 wt.% carbon and exhibiting high surface area, has gained attention for applications in soil amendment, carbon sequestration, and as a functional material for adsorption and catalysis. Bio-oil, with a calorific value ranging from 15 to 25 MJ·kg −1 , is being explored as a renewable energy carrier and chemical feedstock, while non-condensable gases (e.g., CO, CO 2 , CH 4 , H 2 ) enable partial energy self-sufficiency of the process. However, challenges remain regarding contaminant management (e.g., heavy metals), product standardization, and process scale-up. For provide a comprehensive understanding, a systematic review of the literature published over the last decade (2015–2025) was conducted using the Scopus database, resulting in a final dataset of 500 documents. Furthermore, a comprehensive review of research articles on technologies for converting sewage sludge using thermochemical processes and the byproducts generated was carried out. Overall, this review identifies current trends, research gaps, and future perspectives in sewage sludge pyrolysis and its conversion into value-added co-products, supporting sustainable resource recovery and contributing to the transition toward low-carbon energy systems.

title: AI - Mars. Autonomous Multi-Material Self-Replicating Factory (AM-SRF) & Advanced Nuclear Micro-Battery Production for Deep-Space AI Infrastructure
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Autonomous Multi-Material Self-Replicating Factory (AM-SRF) & Advanced Nuclear Micro-Battery Production for Deep-Space AI Infrastructure Abstract & System Overview The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence into deep space—specifically
content: Autonomous Multi-Material Self-Replicating Factory (AM-SRF) & Advanced Nuclear Micro-Battery Production for Deep-Space AI Infrastructure Abstract & System Overview The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence into deep space—specifically targeting the hostile, high-radiation environments of the Moon and Mars—demands an unprecedented paradigm shift in power generation, manufacturing autonomy, and resilience. Traditional silicon-based electronics and solar arrays fail under severe cosmic radiation, thermal fluctuations, and dust storms. To solve this, we introduce the Autonomous Multi-Material Self-Replicating Factory (AM-SRF), a unified single-module manufacturing system integrated with advanced isotope gas handling circuits, laser-assisted Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD), and poly-diamond nuclear micro-batteries. Powered by isotope-derived energy and resilient against planetary radiation, this infrastructure enables AI systems to construct their own habitats, manufacture industrial machinery, execute self-repair protocols, and harvest extraterrestrial resources such as helium-3. 1. Unified Single-Module Manufacturing Architecture (The "1-Machine" Concept) Unlike terrestrial multi-factory supply chains that rely on fragile logistics, the AM-SRF consolidates the entire production chain into a single, highly optimized growth and post-processing module. Isotope Gas Handling & Recirculation: The system features a closed-loop isotope recovery circuit connected to high-purity precursor gas tanks (such as \bm{98\%} enriched \bm{^{14}\text{CH}_4} or tritium-doped precursors). Mass flow controllers regulate gas delivery into a coaxial injection nozzle, while a recirculation pump and mixing valve capture unreacted gases, scrub impurities with clean \bm{\text{H}_2} carrier gas, and maintain optimal reaction pressures. Dynamic CVD Chamber: At the core of the machine is a hermetically sealed quartz and sapphire reaction chamber. A UV laser beam path, focused via high-precision lenses onto a rotating molybdenum disc substrate, drives layer-by-layer crystalline growth. In-Process Feedback & Laser Slicing: Automated optical probes and re-counter feedback mechanisms monitor layer uniformity and thickness in real time. Integrated laser cutting modules slice the grown crystalline boules into precise planar and spherical micro-battery arrays and structural components without breaking vacuum. 2. Advanced Material Science: Poly-Diamonds, Tritium, and Carbon-14 The operational longevity and radiation immunity of deep-space AI systems depend entirely on the material composition of their power sources and structural chassis.
