title: Recurrent de novo ABI2 p.Tyr491Cys variants define a neurodevelopmental syndrome with corpus callosum hypoplasia and white matter abnormalities
source: The American Journal of Human Genetics
summary: Abstract The Abelson-interactor 2 gene ( ABI2) encodes a protein that functions as a regulator of Rac-dependent actin cytoskeleton dynamics, a highly coordinated structural framework essential for maintaining intracellular homeostasis and v
content: Abstract The Abelson-interactor 2 gene ( ABI2) encodes a protein that functions as a regulator of Rac-dependent actin cytoskeleton dynamics, a highly coordinated structural framework essential for maintaining intracellular homeostasis and vital in processes such as cell adhesion, communication, membrane transport, migration, cell growth, and development. As a component of the Rac-1 activated WAVE regulatory complex (WRC), ABI2 initiates the actin polymerization machinery Arp2/3 to drive lamellipodia formation, and underlying key cellular processes such as axonal guidance, cell motility, and cell adhesion. Additionally, ABI2 acts as a substrate for non-receptor tyrosine kinases ABL1 and ABL2, with downstream effects controlling neuronal differentiation and migration involved in neocortical development. Here, through exome sequencing and international collaborations, we identify eight unrelated individuals with severe neurodevelopmental delays linked to heterozygous ABI2 missense variants, including a recurrent p.Tyr491Cys in the highly conserved SH3 domain in six individuals. These variants arose de novo in cases where parental testing was available, and were associated with moderate to severe motor delay, absent or delayed expressive language, intellectual disability, seizures, autistic traits, as well as macrocephaly, thinning of the corpus callosum, and remarkable white matter signal abnormalities. This report adds ABI2 to the list of genes implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, with an additional focus on epilepsy and brain malformations.

title: A Combined MCDM Approach for Parametric Hierarchy in Friction Stir Lap Welding of Dissimilar Polycarbonate to Nylon‐6
summary: ABSTRACT The present work addresses the feasibility of friction stir lap welding (FSLW) for the joining of polycarbonate to nylon‐6 sheets in overlapped configuration. The effects of tool rotational speed, traverse speed, plunge depth using
content: ABSTRACT The present work addresses the feasibility of friction stir lap welding (FSLW) for the joining of polycarbonate to nylon‐6 sheets in overlapped configuration. The effects of tool rotational speed, traverse speed, plunge depth using different tool pin profiles (swept ratios) were studied on quality characteristics of dissimilar welds using response surface methodology (RSM). The second‐order regression models were significant for joint efficiency and weld hardness. The lowest traverse speed (15 mm/min) resulted in the highest weld strength and elongation whereas square pin indicated the weakest welds with undercut flaws. The strongest weld (31.3 MPa) without much ductility was noticed using hexagonal pin at 1600 rpm, 15 mm/min and 0.1 mm, while cylindrical pin at 2400 rpm made stronger (31.0 MPa) weld with higher ductility. The strength and ductility were balanced using AHP‐entropy weights (0.349, 0.582, 0.069 for strength, elongation and hardness, respectively). The welding experiments were ranked using CoCoSo, MABAC and grey relational analysis. All three approaches selected the same best condition (1600 rpm, 15 mm/min, 0.3 mm) using hexagonal pin (28.9 MPa, 17.1 mm elongation) that showed the highest weld ductility with adequate strength. Moreover, the rankings methods agreed high closeness (Spearman correlations of 0.951–0.991) that can precisely rank the parametric levels.

title: Peripheral nitrogen topology as a defect-chemical design parameter for electronic and magnetic states in graphene: a first-principles study of pyridinic, pyridazinic, pyrrolic, and pyrazolic configurations
summary: Defect and heteroatom engineering are powerful routes for tuning graphene's electronic and magnetic properties, yet peripheral nitrogen topology around graphene voids remains poorly understood. Using spin-polarized first-principles calculat
content: Defect and heteroatom engineering are powerful routes for tuning graphene's electronic and magnetic properties, yet peripheral nitrogen topology around graphene voids remains poorly understood. Using spin-polarized first-principles calculations, we examine four heterocyclic nitrogen configurations, pyridinic, pyridazinic, pyrrolic, and pyrazolic, affecting structure, charge redistribution, electronic states, and magnetism in graphene with a central void. Pyridinic N is energetically most favorable, and nitrogen topology controls local lattice reconstruction, shown by bond-length analysis. Charge-density-difference and Bader analyses show peripheral N atoms act as electron-accumulating centers reshaping the vacancy rim. Pyridinic, pyridazinic, and pyrrolic configurations remain metallic or near metallic, whereas pyrazolic graphene opens a narrow band gap and is spin compensated with zero net magnetization, unlike the finite moments of the other systems. This magnetism traces to N-modulated vacancy-edge states involving N 2p and C 2p orbitals, establishing peripheral nitrogen topology as a metal-free, deterministic defect-chemical switch for spintronic and semiconducting domains.

title: Reactivity of Rh(I) Complexes Toward Fluorinated Ethers: Activation of Inhalation Anesthetics
summary: The reactivity of [Rh(H)(PEt 3 ) 3 ] ( 1 ) toward α‐fluorinated ethers that are commonly used as inhalational anesthetics was studied. Unprecedented reactivity pathways include hydrodehalogenation of sp 3 C─F and C─Cl bonds under mild condi
content: The reactivity of [Rh(H)(PEt 3 ) 3 ] ( 1 ) toward α‐fluorinated ethers that are commonly used as inhalational anesthetics was studied. Unprecedented reactivity pathways include hydrodehalogenation of sp 3 C─F and C─Cl bonds under mild conditions. The reaction of 1 with sevoflurane (CF 3 ) 2 CHOCH 2 F provides an efficient route to obtain [Rh(F)(PEt 3 ) 3 ] ( 2 ) by C( sp 3 )─F bond activation. Furthermore, the phosphine ligand takes part in this reaction, and an F/Et exchange at [Rh(H)(F) 2 (PEt 3 ) 3 ] results in the formation of the fluorophosphine complex trans ‐[Rh(F)(Et 2 PF)(PEt 3 ) 2 ] ( 5 ) upon the release of ethane. On the other hand, an oxidative addition of enflurane CClFHCF 2 OCF 2 H at 1 yielded [Rh(H)(Cl)(CFHCF 2 OCF 2 H)(PEt 3 ) 3 ] ( 8 ), which is followed by a reductive elimination step to yield [Rh(Cl)(PEt 3 ) 3 ] ( 7 ) and the hydrofluoroether CFH 2 CF 2 OCF 2 H. When an isomer of enflurane, isoflurane CF 3 CClHOCF 2 H, was treated with 1 , complex 7 and CF 3 CH 2 OCF 2 H are generated by C( sp 3 )─Cl bond activation. Additionally, an in situ nucleophilic attack of triethylphosphine at the hydrofluoroether CF 3 CH 2 OCF 2 H gave a unique fluorinated phosphonium salt [CF 3 CH 2 PEt 3 ] 2 [SiF 6 ] ( 9 ). Catalytic hydrodechlorination of isoflurane at a mild condition was achieved in the presence of silane HSiPh 3 using 1 as a catalyst.

title: Tectonics on Early Earth Driven by Earth's Changing Shape During Tidal Recession of the Moon
source: Journal of Geophysical Research Solid Earth
summary: Abstract Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could
content: Abstract Few fragments of Earth's earliest crust have survived, and so this formative period of our planet's history is shrouded in mystery. To leverage the limited data available, it is important to understand all the processes that could have shaped our young planet. Here, I explore a previously neglected aspect of early‐Earth dynamics: rotation. Earth after the Moon‐forming impact was rapidly rotating with its rotation rate slowing significantly during the first tens of millions of years after the impact as the Moon tidally receded. Using planetary structure and tidal evolution calculations, I show that the initially distorted structure of Earth would likely have led to significant latitudinal variations in primary crustal thickness. Further, the subsequent changes in Earth's shape in response to its slowing rotation rate could have driven extensive tectonic activity and modulated the response of the crust to other forces. There was extension of the crust in polar regions and convergence in the equatorial regions at rates potentially comparable to those forming the Himalayas today in high‐angular momentum scenarios. Depending on the rheology of the earliest crust, such motions could have led to burial of hydrated and weathered surface material, extensive volcanism, and degassing of Earth's interior. Phase changes due to increases in internal pressure could have led to delamination of parts of the crust, producing early mantle heterogeneities. Hydrated secondary melting of the crust and the production of evolved magmas could explain the emergence of a diversity of rock types within tens of millions of years of Earth's formation.

title: Sorting out sustainability transitions: Q methodology as a tool for studying and navigating stakeholder perspectives
summary: Sustainability transitions involve genuine uncertainty, competing values, and persistent stakeholder disagreement about problems, solutions, goals and policy interventions. Understanding these contested dynamics requires methodological appr
content: Sustainability transitions involve genuine uncertainty, competing values, and persistent stakeholder disagreement about problems, solutions, goals and policy interventions. Understanding these contested dynamics requires methodological approaches that can systematically capture subjectivity while maintaining analytical rigor. In this perspective, we argue that Q methodology, a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative depth with quantitative rigor, is an underutilized yet highly valuable tool for transitions research. Drawing on our experience from Q studies on industrial decarbonization and electrification in Sweden and Norway, as well as a broader reading of transitions-related Q research, we reflect on the method's strengths, limitations, and untapped potential. We highlight how Q methodology enables the identification of distinct stakeholder narratives, reveals areas of alignment and disjointment, and brings into view discursive and normative dimensions of transitions that research drawing on frameworks such as Technological Innovation Systems and the Multi-Level Perspective has often left underexamined. We also discuss important limitations, including challenges related to statement design, participant selection, and the interpretation of factors, and share practical lessons learned from applying the method across different empirical contexts. Beyond research, we suggest that Q could complement established participatory approaches in transition governance, for instance by helping to select participants who span the range of perspectives and by feeding identified narratives back into stakeholder dialogue. We conclude by outlining a research agenda to advance Q methodology in transition studies, including longitudinal designs, cross-country comparisons, mixed-methods integration and methodological refinements.

title: Climate mobility as adaptation: Rethinking vulnerability, human security and risk governance in the Bay of Bengal
summary: Climate-induced migration has become one of the most paradigmatic characteristics of the Anthropocene, connecting it to themes of environmental change, livelihood security, and social justice, adaptation and vulnerability, human and state a
content: Climate-induced migration has become one of the most paradigmatic characteristics of the Anthropocene, connecting it to themes of environmental change, livelihood security, and social justice, adaptation and vulnerability, human and state agency, and natural resource politics. The Bay of Bengal region constitutes an intriguing sample for studying migration due to the combination of low-lying coastal deltas, large concentrations of coastal populations, exposure to cyclones and storm surges, river bank erosion, sea level rise, and salt-water intrusion, together with its reliance on climate-sensitive agriculture and fisheries. The Sundarbans region, which extends around India-Bangladesh’s border, emerges as a hotspot in this regard. Climate-induced migration, therefore, intersects with poverty, land use rights, gender, access to services, and overall vulnerability with often different development outcomes in terms of migration, displacement, immobility, and planned relocation in Bangladesh and India. This paper at hand argues that climate-induced migration should not be considered as either a failed adaptation to environmental change or a humanitarian response but rather a response strategy, which, depending on the institutional context, can have mixed results in terms of adaptation. The paper proposes a Risk-Informed Mobility Governance Framework for the Bay of Bengal, covering the key domains of natural climate occurrence, vulnerability and exposure, social protection and livelihood, safe migration, urbanization, planned relocation, ecosystem-based adaptation, gender, and regional and international cooperation. Drawing upon the IPCC mobility-risk framework, migration as adaptation discourse, sustainable livelihoods approach, political ecology, capability approach, human security, and related theories and frameworks, the article aims to demonstrate through selected case studies from Bangladesh and India the key migration governance questions that emerge in the region. These include the recognition of the need for mobility as a key adaptive capacity, the role of local, institutional, and formal policies, the impact of migration on households, communities, and countries of origin and destination, and the overall transformational role of migration for climate change adaptation. The paper concluded by emphasizing the need for the Bay of Bengal region to transition from crisis response management to promoting anticipatory adaptation policies and rights-based and risk-informed social governance, focusing on sustainable livelihoods and regional integration.

title: Plasma-Induced Surface Functionalization of Polymer Powders for Integration into UV-Resistant Functional Composites
source: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
summary: This study investigates the effects of plasma surface treatment on the thermal and morphological properties of polyamide 12 (PA12) powder. The powders were treated for 1 h and 2 h under full power in an air environment. Thermogravimetric an
content: This study investigates the effects of plasma surface treatment on the thermal and morphological properties of polyamide 12 (PA12) powder. The powders were treated for 1 h and 2 h under full power in an air environment. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) results demonstrated that the plasma action improved the maximum decomposition temperature from 449.3 °C for the untreated polyamide 12 to 461.7 °C for the 2-h-treated sample, indicating improved thermal stability. The analysis of differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed a marked increase in the temperature of crystallization (Tc) from 133.31 °C for the untreated PA12 sample to 141.7 °C for the 2-h sample, while the melting temperature is approximately constant at 185 °C. The SEM images demonstrated that plasma treatment resulted in a roughened, more homogeneous surface morphology with significantly fewer surface defects and irregularities. Plasma treatment enhanced the wettability and water dispersion of PA12, as plasma-treated powders showed fast spreading and stable suspension in water due to the introduction of polar groups and increased surface pores. The change from a water-hating grouping to a water-loving scattering provides a strong basis for water-based processing and future composite design that will need strong interfacial interactions. Thus, these results confirmed the importance of plasma treatment as an environmentally friendly method in tailoring the properties of PA12 for UV-resistant applications.

title: Neutron Depth Profiling: The Core Link Connecting the Microscopic Mechanisms of Lithium‐Ion Batteries With Intelligent Design
summary: ABSTRACT Neutron Depth Profiling (NDP) is a non‐destructive, in situ quantitative depth‐analysis technique underpinned by neutron‐induced nuclear reactions. Offering high 6 Li‐isotope sensitivity and nanometer‐to‐micrometer depth resolution
content: ABSTRACT Neutron Depth Profiling (NDP) is a non‐destructive, in situ quantitative depth‐analysis technique underpinned by neutron‐induced nuclear reactions. Offering high 6 Li‐isotope sensitivity and nanometer‐to‐micrometer depth resolution, NDP delivers isotope‐resolved lithium spatial information hardly accessible via conventional probes including secondary‐ion mass spectrometry (SIMS), X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and operando neutron imaging, yet it suffers from depth‐dependent resolution degradation, limited lateral performance, and requires large‐scale neutron‐beam facilities. This paper systematically reviews NDP fundamentals, global neutron‐source progress, and cutting‐edge battery applications, covering lithium‐ion migration in electrodes, lithium dendrite nucleation and growth, and the “reversible short‐circuit” effect at solid‐electrolyte interfaces. The unique merit of NDP for quantitative 6 Li depth‐profiling is highlighted, while noting that NDP cannot independently resolve full‐element maps or nanoscale interfaces and demands complementary characterizations. A roadmap integrating NDP with multimodal measurements and physics‐informed machine learning for intelligent battery design is outlined, alongside open challenges: inversion non‐uniqueness under low‐signal conditions and translation from model cells to practical batteries. This work provides actionable guidelines to leverage NDP for bridging microscopic lithium mechanisms and rational design of next‑generation batteries with high safety and high energy density.

title: EVALUATING ADVANCES IN INTEGRATED GEOPHYSICAL AND GEOLOGICAL METHODS FOR UNCONVENTIONAL RESERVOIR CHARACTERIZATION IN THE UNITED STATES: A NARRATIVE REVIEW
source: Magna Scientia Advanced Research and Reviews
summary: Unconventional oil and gas reservoirs have revolutionized U.S. energy, but their complex geology and low permeability demand new characterization approaches. This narrative review critically examines recent advances in integrating geologica
content: Unconventional oil and gas reservoirs have revolutionized U.S. energy, but their complex geology and low permeability demand new characterization approaches. This narrative review critically examines recent advances in integrating geological and geophysical methods for unconventional reservoir evaluation. We synthesize how multidisciplinary approaches, ranging from pore-scale imaging to seismic and electromagnetic surveys, augmented by machine learning, reveal reservoir heterogeneity and sweet spots. Key trends include high-resolution petrophysical analyses (nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR, core imaging), geophysical innovations, and data-driven inversion and modeling frameworks. The major knowledge gaps identified in this review include linking nanoscale properties to field-scale flow, robustly quantifying induced seismic risks, and integrating the full petroleum system (source, rock, fracture networks) into models. It is concluded that continued integration of diverse data (seismic, well logs, core, and micro seismic) through advanced rock-physics and AI-driven workflows promises deeper insight into U.S. unconventional reservoirs. These trends have broad implications for exploration, production optimization, and low-carbon initiatives in unconventional plays.

title: Effects of Postharvest Methyl Jasmonate (MeJA) and γ -Aminobutyric Acid (GABA) on the Quality and Storability of Granny Smith Apple Fruit
summary: This study investigated the effects of postharvest methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) treatments on the quality and storability of Granny Smith apples harvested from a private orchard in Duhok Governorate, Kurdistan Regi
content: This study investigated the effects of postharvest methyl jasmonate (MeJA) and γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) treatments on the quality and storability of Granny Smith apples harvested from a private orchard in Duhok Governorate, Kurdistan Region, Iraq. The reported treatment concentrations were 0, 0.75, 1.5, and 2.5 mM MeJA, applied by dipping for five minutes, and 0, 5, 10, and 15 mM GABA, applied by dipping for fifteen minutes. Fruit were stored for 30, 60, and 120 days at a reported temperature of 1 ± 1 ∘C and 85–90% relative humidity. The tabulated results showed that 2.5 mM MeJA maintained greater firmness and ascorbic acid content and reduced weight loss compared with the untreated MeJA level. GABA treatments also maintained firmness, while their effects on weight loss, acidity, and ascorbic acid depended on concentration. Main effects of either treatment on total soluble solids and total phenolic content were not statistically significant according to the reported Duncan groupings. Titratable acidity was numerically higher at the two highest MeJA concentrations, but the MeJA main-effect means shared the same significance letter. Superoxide dismutase and catalase activities were evaluated after 120 days and were generally greater in treated fruit, although the strongest response depended on the enzyme and treatment combination. Across storage periods, firmness and titratable acidity decreased, whereas weight loss and total soluble solids increased. Ascorbic acid and total phenolic content reached their highest storage-period means at 60 days. Overall, the results support the potential of MeJA and GABA dipping treatments to preserve selected quality attributes, while demonstrating that benefits were specific to the response variable and storage interval rather than uniform across all measured characteristics.

title: Modeling the PSN mechanism of recrystallization nuclei formation in Inconel 718
summary: This study proposes and applies a mathematical model to describe the process of recrystallization nucleation on large d-phase particles in the Inconel 718 nickel alloy during annealing (the particle stimulated nucleation (PSN) mechanism). T
content: This study proposes and applies a mathematical model to describe the process of recrystallization nucleation on large d-phase particles in the Inconel 718 nickel alloy during annealing (the particle stimulated nucleation (PSN) mechanism). The investigation employs a multilevel approach based on an extended statistical model, in which the subgrain structure is explicitly described by an aggregate of Laguerre polyhedra. The model for the formation of new recrystallized grain nuclei is based on the physical mechanisms of recovery: subgrain coalescence and low-angle boundary migration. Additionally, the model accounts for lattice rotations of subgrains near the non-deformable particle resulting from the incompatibility of prior plastic deformation, as well as the retarding effect of dispersed γ′ and γ″ particles during subgrain boundary migration. Numerical experiments were conducted on a representative volume of subgrains at annealing temperatures range 450–950 °C. It is shown that at 450 - 850°C subgrain growth near the d-phase particle is retarded due to increased misorientation, which hinders coalescence. At temperatures above 950 °C, the dissolution of the strengthening phases γ′ and γ″ leads to a decrease in the Zener pinning force and intense boundary migration near the d-phase particle results in the active formation of recrystallization nuclei. It is established that a needle-shaped d-particle promotes more intense nucleation compared to a spherical one due to its larger interfacial area. The simulation results are in qualitative agreement with known experimental data.

title: Barriers to Blockchain Adoption in Circular Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Review and TISM-MICMAC Analysis
source: Journal of Logistics Informatics and Service Science
summary: This study examines the practical challenges organizations encounter in adopting blockchain for circular supply chain management.The objective is to provide actionable insights for managers and policymakers to facilitate blockchain adoption
content: This study examines the practical challenges organizations encounter in adopting blockchain for circular supply chain management.The objective is to provide actionable insights for managers and policymakers to facilitate blockchain adoption for strengthening circularity within supply chains and enhancing circular supply chain performance.A comprehensive systematic literature review is conducted with 34 articles to identify key barriers.Subsequently, the key barriers were modeled using inputs from nine experts through Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (TISM) and MICMAC analysis.The results indicate that barriers such as lack of government regulations and lack of stakeholder involvement function as root-level drivers, while mid-level feedback barriers include cost, lack of trust, and lack of standardization.At the upper level, outcome barriers such as security, privacy, and scalability emerge as dependent effects.The findings highlight that successful blockchain adoption in circular supply chains requires first strengthening institutional and collaborative foundations, followed by addressing technical limitations.Overall, the study emphasizes realworld implementation considerations and the adoption of circular economy principles within blockchain-enabled supply chain transformation.

title: Two Niches, One Disease: Brain and Leptomeningeal Metastases in Breast Cancer: A Narrative Review
summary: Abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) metastasis is an increasingly important challenge in advanced breast cancer, yet brain parenchymal metastases (BM) and leptomeningeal metastases (LM) are often considered within a single framework desp
content: Abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) metastasis is an increasingly important challenge in advanced breast cancer, yet brain parenchymal metastases (BM) and leptomeningeal metastases (LM) are often considered within a single framework despite occupying biologically distinct CNS compartments. In this narrative review, we synthesize breast cancer-specific mechanistic and clinical evidence to examine how these two forms of CNS disease differ in metastatic entry, local adaptation, molecular evolution, biomarker representation, and therapeutic vulnerability. Parenchymal BM primarily arise through haematogenous dissemination and subsequent adaptation to a neurovascular, neural, and immune-rich environment, where successful colonization requires more than blood–brain barrier traversal and is supported by reciprocal tumour–host interactions and metabolic plasticity. By contrast, LM develops within a fluid-dominated, CSF-facing compartment characterized by distinct meningeal and blood–CSF interfaces, constrained resource availability, and dynamic immune conditions. C3–C3aR-mediated barrier remodeling and LCN2–SLC22A17-dependent iron acquisition are supported mainly by experimental LM models and selected patient-derived observations, including mixed-cancer cohorts, and require broader breast cancer-specific clinical validation. Genomic and phenotypic studies further indicate that BM and LM can share metastatic ancestry while undergoing branched and compartment-associated evolution, although observed divergence may also reflect pre-existing heterogeneity, treatment selection, elapsed time, and sampling effects. Therapeutic efficacy therefore depends not only on CNS drug access but also on target expression, tumour state, niche support, disease geometry, and prior treatment. By integrating metastatic dissemination, niche adaptation, molecular evolution, biomarker representation, and therapeutic vulnerability within a single comparative framework, this review links compartment-associated biology to molecular sampling, experimental modeling, and clinical trial design. Clinically, this framework may inform compartment-specific molecular sampling and trial stratification by BM treatment status and LM presentation, although its utility for individual treatment selection requires prospective validation. Future studies combining paired multi-compartment sampling, lineage-resolved models, and serial CSF and plasma profiling will be needed to distinguish shared ancestry from niche-associated adaptation and treatment-driven evolution. Keywords: breast cancer, brain metastasis, leptomeningeal metastasis, CNS compartmentalization, tumour microenvironment, clonal evolution, cerebrospinal fluid

title: Metal ions-associated redox dyshomeostasis in fibrosis: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutics
summary: Organ fibrosis is a common pathological feature of various chronic diseases with high morbidity and mortality, and represents a major threat to global public health. The pathogenesis of organ fibrosis involves multiple etiological factors a
content: Organ fibrosis is a common pathological feature of various chronic diseases with high morbidity and mortality, and represents a major threat to global public health. The pathogenesis of organ fibrosis involves multiple etiological factors and molecular mechanisms, posing enormous obstacles to the development of anti-fibrotic drugs. In recent years, the critical role of redox dyshomeostasis in fibrogenesis has been gradually clarified. Dysregulated metabolism of metal ions such as iron, copper, zinc, and calcium induces excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which triggers parenchymal cell injury, inflammatory responses, and fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition (FMT), ultimately leading to excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. Thus, targeting metal ions to restore redox homeostasis has become a novel anti-fibrotic strategy. This review systematically elucidates the mechanisms by which metal ion imbalances are involved in fibrosis through oxidative stress and further provides an overview and perspective on metal ion-targeted therapeutic strategies against fibrosis.

title: Examination of nitrogen accumulation rate in a Lemna minor aquatic system
summary: Duckweed species from the subfamily Lemnaceae are small, free-floating aquatic macrophytes capable of thriving in diverse environments. Studies have demonstrated that duckweed can be used to recover nutrients from its growth medium or waste
content: Duckweed species from the subfamily Lemnaceae are small, free-floating aquatic macrophytes capable of thriving in diverse environments. Studies have demonstrated that duckweed can be used to recover nutrients from its growth medium or wastewater. The plant biomass produced can be utilized as a source of protein or starch for animal feed or the production of value-added products such as biofuels. To investigate the kinetics of nitrogen accumulation within a Lemna minor aquatic system, a series of batch reactors were employed to simulate the continuous growth of the plants. The study aimed to elucidate the dynamics of nitrogen conversion in a controlled long term batch system. Lemna minor plants were cultivated for 75 days in 30 petri dishes, each containing 45 mL of synthetic hydroponic nutrient solution. Regular analyses were conducted on the reactors to measure nitrogen components, phosphates, and Total Organic Carbon (TOC). Nitrogen equilibrium was closely monitored throughout the cultivation period to assess alterations in nitrogenous components within the samples. By the end of the cultivation period, frond count and dry biomass had increased from 30 plants to 243 and from 2.5 mg to 40.2 respectively, exhibiting exponential growth after an initial lag phase lasting 31 days. During the exponential phase, protein content ranged from 28.5% to 38.8%. Nitrate concentration, the primary nitrogen source in the medium, decreased by 79.1%, while phosphorus levels were reduced by 97.4% by the end of the experiment. The results also revealed significant variations in total nitrogen content over time, ranging from a decrease of 45.6% to an increase of 8.0% compared to the initial levels, suggesting the possible contribution of denitrification and biological nitrogen fixation.

title: Políticas Públicas Federais e a Transição Energética: Fomento ao Hidrogênio de Baixo Carbono para a Descarbonização Industrial no Brasil
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Este estudo analisa o papel das políticas públicas federais para o fomento à produção de hidrogênio de baixo carbono no Brasil, a partir da articulação entre arcabouço regulatório, políticas de technology push e instrumentos de demand pull.
content: Este estudo analisa o papel das políticas públicas federais para o fomento à produção de hidrogênio de baixo carbono no Brasil, a partir da articulação entre arcabouço regulatório, políticas de technology push e instrumentos de demand pull.Metodologicamente, trata-se de pesquisa qualitativa, exploratória e descritiva, baseada em análise documental.Os resultados indicam avanços no arcabouço regulatório e no desenvolvimento tecnológico, evidenciando maior maturidade das políticas públicas de technology push.Em contraste, os instrumentos de demand pull permanecem incipientes, com lacunas na criação de mercado e na previsibilidade econômica, limitando o escalonamento industrial.Como contribuição, o artigo propõe um quadro analítico para a coordenação de sistemas produtivos emergentes, destacando a necessidade de integração entre regulação, desenvolvimento tecnológico e mercadológico.

title: Coupled hydromechanical controls on CO2 leakage through fractured caprocks
summary: Permanent containment of injected CO2 remains central to the effectiveness and safety of geologic carbon storage. Yet, uncertainties in coupled hydromechanical and multiphase processes limit assessment of leakage through fractured caprocks.
content: Permanent containment of injected CO2 remains central to the effectiveness and safety of geologic carbon storage. Yet, uncertainties in coupled hydromechanical and multiphase processes limit assessment of leakage through fractured caprocks. Here, we integrate laboratory measurements of two-phase and hydromechanical properties of fractured shales into field-scale simulations to improve evaluation of CO2 leakage potential. Regardless of the caprock sealing capacity, CO2 migration remains strongly localized along fractures, while its rate and extent are governed by non-local interactions with surrounding formations. Despite fracture breakthrough, CO2 discharge into the overlying aquifer is limited. The high-permeability aquifer promotes rapid pressure dissipation and CO2 dissolution, restricting formation of a secondary mobile plume. We conclude that reliable assessment of CO2 leakage likelihood and severity hinges on system-scale resolution of coupled hydromechanical processes. The developed framework will enable reliable integration of advances in experimental fracture characterization into site-specific modeling efforts and, where necessary, remediation design.

title: Rutas críticas sobre la transición justa en México. Territorio y trabajo en clave socioecológica
source: Bajo el volcán. Revista del posgrado de sociología. BUAP.
summary: En México y el resto de los países de América Latina, el imperativo de la transición energética está activando nuevos debates y disputas sobre lo que significa el desarrollo, la justicia social y la justicia ambiental. Este artículo analiza
content: En México y el resto de los países de América Latina, el imperativo de la transición energética está activando nuevos debates y disputas sobre lo que significa el desarrollo, la justicia social y la justicia ambiental. Este artículo analiza la expansión de proyectos minero-energéticos verdes en México a lo largo de las últimas dos décadas, identificando algunas de las demandas obreras y socioambientales que se han articulado como respuesta a tales infraestructuras. Utilizando el Atlas Global de Justicia Ambiental como herramienta principal, se recuperan las categorías de territorios sacrificados y trabajo precario como ejes clave de diagnóstico crítico. En este marco, el texto discute las limitantes para alcanzar una transición justa en México bajo modelos que reproducen la matriz productiva imperante, independientemente de si se inclinan hacia el mercado o el Estado. Ante este diagnóstico, el texto concluye contraponiendo el potencial de una perspectiva socioecológica para atender los retos ambientales y laborales del país, y sugiere algunas rutas de investigación-acción para contribuir al campo del pensamiento crítico y la organización colectiva.

title: A BAYESIAN PHYSICS-DRIVEN NEURAL NETWORK FOR ELASTIC LOG PREDICTION VIA CROSS-BASIN TRANSFER LEARNING
summary: Driven by the demands of reservoir characterization, accurate elastic log prediction remains a critical research priority that bridges rock physical properties with seismic responses for hydrocarbon exploration. Elastic logs are conventiona
content: Driven by the demands of reservoir characterization, accurate elastic log prediction remains a critical research priority that bridges rock physical properties with seismic responses for hydrocarbon exploration. Elastic logs are conventionally estimated using rock physics models (RPMs) or, more recently, machine learning (ML) frameworks. However, these RPMs are constrained by idealized assumptions and fail to account for uncertainty, whereas existing ML approaches often lack physical constraints. To address this, Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) have proven successful in quantitative log prediction by simultaneously enhancing accuracy and quantifying model uncertainty. We introduce a novel BNN framework designed for the quantitative estimation of elastic properties from well logs. By integrating rock physics constraints via a physics-based loss term derived from synthetic velocity realizations, the proposed method ensures physically consistent predictions and calibrated uncertainty. Using variational inference (VI) governed by the Kullback-Leibler divergence objective function, the framework approximates the neural network’s posterior distribution to generate ensemble predictions that closely align with the target logs. To bridge the gap between velocity measurements and rock physical properties, the network incorporates a physics-dependent loss term derived from various combinations of velocity realizations. Furthermore, we employ cross-domain adaptation via a two-stage fine-tuning transfer learning strategy to predict seismic velocities in an unseen basin. By utilizing selective layer updates and regularization on a limited subset of target well data, the framework adapts the pre-trained BNN without sacrificing prior knowledge, ensuring physically meaningful predictions and physically consistent trends despite domain shift. When tested on field datasets from the Canning Basin (Western Australia) and the Sichuan Basin (China), our proposed approach outperformed the standard BNN, delivering higher correlation coefficients, lower prediction errors, and lower uncertainties. Remarkably, this framework offers a scalable, robust paradigm for subsurface characterization in complex, data-limited regimes by synthesizing physics-informed constraints with cross-domain transfer learning.

title: A conserved cold stress syndrome defines insect chill tolerance
summary: The ability to withstand cold is arguably one of the most important traits defining the biogeographical distribution of insects. For most species, those classified as chill susceptible, cold tolerance is limited by the ability to maintain v
content: The ability to withstand cold is arguably one of the most important traits defining the biogeographical distribution of insects. For most species, those classified as chill susceptible, cold tolerance is limited by the ability to maintain vital physiological functions at low temperature. However, there is currently no unified understanding of how physiological failure develops during cold stress or how this process explains variation in cold sensitivity within and among species. Although disruption of ion homeostasis has been implicated in chilling injury, it remains unclear whether it represents a common physiological limit across cold stress intensities and degrees of chill tolerance. Here, we tested whether ion balance disruption represents a unifying physiological syndrome of chill susceptibility by simultaneously quantifying cold mortality and hemolymph [K⁺] in Drosophila . We examined this relationship across i) a broad range of cold stress intensities, ii) 25 species spanning extensive variation in cold sensitivity, biogeography and phylogeny, and iii) acclimation groups of D. melanogaster developed between 12 and 27°C. Across all comparisons, mortality was associated with the same cold-stress response, characterized by progressive hyperkalemia and mortality following a ~150% increase in hemolymph [K⁺] above baseline ([K⁺] crit ). In contrast, adaptive and plastic variation in cold sensitivity was explained by differences in the critical temperature at which ion homeostasis failed (T c ). Extending this framework to published data from other insect orders revealed a remarkably similar [K⁺] crit , suggesting that ionoregulatory collapse represents a conserved physiological constraint defining insect cold survival.

title: Contact-dependent interactions between Cutibacterium acnes and Staphylococcus lugdunensis promote biofilm matrix remodeling
summary: Abstract Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) pose a substantial burden to patients and healthcare systems. These infections are often persistent and frequently require revision procedures, increasing the risk of surgical failure and mortalit
content: Abstract Prosthetic joint infections (PJIs) pose a substantial burden to patients and healthcare systems. These infections are often persistent and frequently require revision procedures, increasing the risk of surgical failure and mortality. A major virulence determinant underlying their persistence is biofilm formation, which protects bacteria from antibiotic treatment and host immune defenses. Understanding the mechanisms that promote biofilm formation is therefore critical for improving PJI management. Staphylococcus spp. and Cutibacterium acnes are common skin commensals that are frequently co-isolated from chronic prosthetic device infections. We hypothesized that these organisms interact synergistically to enhance the persistence of polymicrobial infections. We found that C. acnes increases dual-species biofilm formation with Staphylococcus lugdunensis and Staphylococcus hominis relative to monocultures. This phenotype was specific to these species combinations and was widespread among the strains tested. To investigate the underlying mechanism, we focused on the interaction between C. acnes and S. lugdunensis . Enhanced biofilm formation required both species to be metabolically active and in direct physical contact. Notably, co-culture shifted S. lugdunensis biofilms from their typical proteinaceous matrix to a polysaccharide intercellular adhesin (PIA)-rich matrix. Consistent with this transition, co-culture with C. acnes significantly increased expression of icaA , a gene involved in PIA biosynthesis, while having no effect on expression of atlL and mgtE , genes associated with the proteinaceous matrix of S. lugdunensis . Together, these findings reveal a novel contact-dependent interspecies interaction in which C. acnes promotes a switch to PIA-mediated biofilm formation in S. lugdunensis , a mechanism that may enhance persistence on medical devices and contribute to chronic polymicrobial infections.

title: Metabolomic Signatures of Habitual Physical Activity in Childhood
summary: Physical activity (PA) supports health across the life course, yet the biological pathways linking habitual PA to long-term health remain incompletely understood. Metabolomics provides a powerful tool to study PA-related metabolic adaptatio
content: Physical activity (PA) supports health across the life course, yet the biological pathways linking habitual PA to long-term health remain incompletely understood. Metabolomics provides a powerful tool to study PA-related metabolic adaptations, but how habitual PA shapes the metabolome in childhood remains poorly characterized. Addressing this gap, we examined cross-sectional associations between accelerometer-measured habitual PA and the plasma metabolome in 515 children aged 5.5 to 11 years from the European Childhood Obesity Project (CHOP) and additionally determined whether associations differed between sexes and across the body mass index (BMI) range. Using targeted metabolomics, we quantified 315 metabolites and derived 91 metabolite sums and ratios. Associations with PA were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. Replication was performed in an independent pediatric cohort. Among the 406 metabolite variables, 73 were associated (p < 0.05) with at least one PA variable, of which 12 replicated, including lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) a C14:0 and LPCs/phosphatidylcholines (PCs) with higher levels in more active children, and PC aa C40:6, monounsaturated PCs/saturated PCs, and valine/LPC a C18:1 with lower levels in more active children. At the metabolite-class level, intensity-dependent association patterns emerged. Amino acids and acylcarnitines were lower in more active children predominantly for time spent in higher-intensity PA, whereas LPCs were higher mainly with more total PA (80% light PA) and less sedentary time. Associations were more pronounced at older ages and differed (p < 0.05) by BMI for 42 metabolite variables and by sex for 45 variables in the interaction analyses. These findings provide insights into PA-related metabolic adaptations early in life and may help elucidate biological pathways linking childhood PA to long-term health.

title: Benzotriazole-Functionalized Rh(I), Ir(I), and Ru(II) N-Heterocyclic Carbene Complexes: Synthesis, Structural Characterization, and Catalytic Hydrosilylation of Terminal Alkynes
source: Journal of the Turkish Chemical Society Section A Chemistry
summary: A benzotriazole-functionalized benzimidazolium salt together with its corresponding Rh(I) and Ir(I) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes was synthesized and comprehensively characterized using elemental analysis together with 1D and 2D NM
content: A benzotriazole-functionalized benzimidazolium salt together with its corresponding Rh(I) and Ir(I) N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) complexes was synthesized and comprehensively characterized using elemental analysis together with 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy. A previously reported Ru(II)-NHC complex bearing the same ligand framework was also employed to enable a systematic comparison of the influence of the metal center on catalytic behavior. The catalytic performances of the Rh(I), Ir(I), and Ru(II) complexes were evaluated by in situ time-resolved 1H NMR monitoring of the hydrosilylation of terminal alkynes. Under the optimized reaction conditions, the Ir(I) complex exhibited the highest catalytic activity, affording 99% conversion in the hydrosilylation of phenylacetylene with dimethylphenylsilane. In contrast, the Rh(I) complex showed lower activity (75% conversion) but provided the highest β-(E) selectivity (60%) without detectable styrene formation. In contrast, the Ru(II) complex displayed the highest β-(Z) selectivity (80%) despite its limited catalytic activity (20% conversion). Additional experiments employing different terminal alkynes and hydrosilanes indicated that variation of the substrates did not substantially improve the catalytic performance of the benzotriazole-functionalized Ir(I)-NHC catalyst. The benzotriazole functionality was selected because its pendant nitrogen donor sites provide additional coordination capability and offer a means of modifying the coordination environment and electronic properties of NHC-metal complexes. The observed catalytic behavior, together with comparison with previously reported NHC systems, indicates that both the metal center and the nature of the NHC framework are important factors governing catalytic activity and product distribution. These findings provide further insight into the roles of both the metal center and ligand design in terminal alkyne hydrosilylation and may provide useful guidance for the future design of functionalized NHC ligands for selective hydrosilylation catalysis.

title: RECENT INNOVATIONS IN SUGARCANE MICROPROPAGATION: A REVIEW OF TISSUE CULTURE PROTOCOLS, GENETIC STABILITY, AND COMMERCIAL-SCALE PROPAGATION
source: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
summary: Sugarcane is a high biomass crop with a rapid distribution system, which adds to its commercial value.To maximize economic value, genetically uniform and pathogen tested planting materials must be rapidly distributed.Conventional sett multi
content: Sugarcane is a high biomass crop with a rapid distribution system, which adds to its commercial value.To maximize economic value, genetically uniform and pathogen tested planting materials must be rapidly distributed.Conventional sett multiplication of sugarcane can be slow and may perpetuate systemic pathogens, therefore tissue culture is an essential component of modern seed cane systems.This review assesses the recent advances on the topics of explant, media, plant growth regulators, shoot regeneration, rooting and acclimatization, temporary immersion, bioreactors, genetic fidelity, somaclonal variation, molecular quality control, and commercial scale up.Recent studies have shown that protocol performance is genotype-dependent and for cases where varietal identity is of primary concern, direct meristematic or axillary regeneration is preferred.Control of immersion frequency, aeration, contamination and hyperhydricity is crucial in the temporary immersion systems, but their use can be more easily automated compared to other systems.Somaclonal variation is a major concern in the genetic uniformity of the planting material.Genetic integrity is essential for crop fidelity and therefore genetic integrity is of concern.Meristem culture and pathogen fidelity indexing shift the focus to the sanitary aspect of micropropagation.In addition, smart technologies and genome editing, as well as the use of artificial intelligence, will allow for rapid advancements in sugarcane micropropagation.Commercial potential for the micropropagation of sugarcane will be increased by addressing biological fidelity, pathogen freedom and automation.

title: A Luminescent Benzimidazole‐Linked Porphyrin Covalent Organic Polymer for Sensitive and Reversible Sensing of Roxarsone in Aqueous Media
summary: The selective detection of toxic organoarsenic compounds in aqueous media presents a significant environmental and analytical challenge. In this study, we report a luminescent benzimidazole‐linked porphyrin covalent organic polymer ( Por‐BP
content: The selective detection of toxic organoarsenic compounds in aqueous media presents a significant environmental and analytical challenge. In this study, we report a luminescent benzimidazole‐linked porphyrin covalent organic polymer ( Por‐BPI‐COP ) designed for the fluorescence‐based detection of roxarsone (ROX) in aqueous media. Por‐BPI‐COP is readily synthesized using a one‐pot, metal‐free polycondensation reaction and characterized using standard spectroscopic and microscopic techniques. It demonstrates excellent thermal and chemical stability and strong intrinsic luminescence. Upon titration with ROX, Por‐BPI‐COP exhibits efficient fluorescence “turn‐off” sensing behavior, achieving a Stern‐Volmer quenching constant ( K SV ) of 9.0 × 10 3 M −1 , a limit of detection of 6.8 nM, and a fluorescence quenching efficiency of approximately 46%. Steady‐state and time‐resolved spectroscopic studies indicate that static quenching primarily underlies the sensing response. This mechanism arises from ground‐state donor–acceptor interactions between the π ‐conjugated polymer framework and the electron‐deficient ROX, further supported by specific hydrogen‐bonding interactions. The sensor also displays high selectivity for ROX, reversible fluorescence recovery across multiple sensing cycles, and reliable performance in real water samples. Furthermore, DFT calculations provided molecular‐level insight into the interaction between ROX and Por‐BPI‐COP . This work establishes benzimidazole‐linked porphyrin COPs as a promising new class of luminescent materials for detecting organoarsenic compounds in aqueous environments.

title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. On
content: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. Once insulating sulfides become poorly connected to the electronic network, charge recovery becomes incomplete and cathode passivation rapidly accumulates. Here, we construct chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces by embedding Fe 3 C–MnO heteropoints within nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon nanotubes. The heterointerface integrates carbon‐side electronic coupling, sulfide‐side affinity, and interfacial polarization, thereby suppressing localized sulfide accumulation and sustaining charge‐stage sulfur recovery as mechanical confinement weakens. This effect is strongly pressure dependent. Under high compression, the electrochemical responses of different hosts converge, whereas under contact‐limited conditions the Fe 3 C–MnO architecture preserves markedly higher sulfur utilization, lower polarization, and superior cycling stability. Consequently, the operational pressure required to retain ≥80% of the 10 MPa discharge capacity decreases from approximately 2 MPa for the control cathodes to 0.2 MPa for Fe 3 C–MnO/NC@S. A 200 µm cathode with 8.3 mg cm −2 sulfur sustains reversible cycling at 0.2 MPa, together with a pouch‐cell energy density of 696 Wh kg cathode −1 . These results establish sulfide‐interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.

title: ISR Addiction: Co-opting a Stress Sentinel to Fuel Tumor Resilience and Therapy Resistance
summary: The integrated stress response (ISR), a conserved cellular sentinel, is pathologically commandeered in cancer to sustain survival under chronic duress. Here, we posit that tumors evolve a state of "ISR Addiction", a profound, non-oncogenic
content: The integrated stress response (ISR), a conserved cellular sentinel, is pathologically commandeered in cancer to sustain survival under chronic duress. Here, we posit that tumors evolve a state of "ISR Addiction", a profound, non-oncogenic dependency on persistent ISR signaling orchestrated through sustained eIF2α phosphorylation and ATF4-driven transcription. We delineate a three-stage continuum—utilization, dependence, and fixation—tracing how this addiction emerges under microenvironmental pressure and becomes entrenched during therapy. This dependency actively fuels metastasis and acts as a central hub for resistance to chemotherapy, targeted agents, and immunotherapy. Expanding this view, we embed ISR addiction within a multilayered "Ecosystem of Tumor Addictions", where bidirectional crosstalk with redox addiction (maintaining biochemical balance) and neural addiction (processing systemic signals) collectively creates a buffered resilience network. Crucially, this ecosystem reveals a therapeutically exploitable fragility: the addicted state is maintained in a precarious "Goldilocks" balance ("Goldilocks" refers to a "just right" condition—not too much, not too little—borrowed from the children’s tale Goldilocks and the Three Bears, where the protagonist finds the porridge that is neither too hot nor too cold, but perfectly suited), susceptible to either "enforced withdrawal" (blocking pro-survival ATF4 outputs) or "toxic overload" (hyperactivating the pro-apoptotic CHOP arm). We propose that rational combinations targeting this addiction network, particularly with standard-of-care or immunomodulatory agents, offer a transformative strategy to dismantle the resilient core of advanced malignancies.

title: Electrochemical Allylic Functionalization: A Sustainable Platform for Upgrading Allylic Compounds
summary: The upgrading of readily available allylic compounds into functionalized allylic scaffolds is of paramount importance in synthetic chemistry, given their prevalence in drug molecules and their derivatization potential. In this context, elec
content: The upgrading of readily available allylic compounds into functionalized allylic scaffolds is of paramount importance in synthetic chemistry, given their prevalence in drug molecules and their derivatization potential. In this context, electrochemical allylic functionalization emerges as a sustainable platform for this purpose, and constructs CC and C–heteroatom bonds under mild conditions. To date, however, no comprehensive review has specifically addressed this emerging area. In this review, we summarize recent major advances in electrochemical allylic functionalizations, categorized by reaction type into five classes: allylic carboxylation, allylic (hetero)arylation, allylic alkylation, allylic borylation, and allylic CH functionalization. We place particular emphasis on reaction mechanisms and substrate scope, and also discuss the limitations of the reported examples. Finally, we outline current challenges and provide an outlook on future directions, with the aim of inspiring further exciting developments in this rapidly growing area.

title: Thermochemical Hydrogen Production from Biomass: A Review of Recent Advances
summary: Thermochemical conversion of biomass offers a promising pathway for renewable H2 production while enabling waste valorization and potentially low-carbon or carbon-negative energy systems. This review critically examines advances in thermoch
content: Thermochemical conversion of biomass offers a promising pathway for renewable H2 production while enabling waste valorization and potentially low-carbon or carbon-negative energy systems. This review critically examines advances in thermochemical H2 production from biomass reported during 2020–2026, with an emphasis on the transition from conventional conversion toward integrated and intensified processes. Pyrolysis and gasification are evaluated alongside emerging routes, including sorption-enhanced conversion, chemical looping, supercritical water gasification (SCWG), and multistage systems. Particular attention is given to the evolution of catalysts and functional materials, including Ni- and Fe-based catalysts, bimetallic systems, biochar-supported materials, CaO-containing catalyst–sorbents, mixed metal oxides, and oxygen carriers. Recent advances in reactor engineering and process intensification are assessed, including staged reactors, electrified systems, membrane-integrated gasification, gas cleaning and H2 purification, continuous operation, and pilot-scale demonstration. The increasing application of machine learning for process prediction, optimization, and real-time monitoring is also examined. Techno-economic and life-cycle studies are critically considered to identify the factors governing production cost, energy efficiency, greenhouse gas emissions, and the potential benefits of carbon capture and storage. Overall, the literature demonstrates a shift from maximizing H2 concentration in individual experiments toward integrated biomass-to-H2 systems emphasizing absolute H2 yield, purity, material durability, energy efficiency, carbon management, and scalability. Future progress requires long-duration materials testing, realistic feedstock evaluation, standardized performance metrics, integrated pilot demonstrations, and harmonized techno-economic and life-cycle assessment to establish commercially viable and environmentally sustainable biomass-derived H2 production.

title: Hepatocyte‐Centered Regulation of MASH Fibrosis: From Animal Models to Molecular Mechanisms and Targeted Therapies
summary: ABSTRACT Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a major driver of liver fibrosis, with fibrosis stage being the strongest predictor of clinical outcomes. Recent advances have redefined MASH pathogenesis as a hepatocyte‐c
content: ABSTRACT Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a major driver of liver fibrosis, with fibrosis stage being the strongest predictor of clinical outcomes. Recent advances have redefined MASH pathogenesis as a hepatocyte‐centered process in which metabolically stressed hepatocytes actively regulate fibrogenesis through direct communication with hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). This review integrates findings from metabolically relevant animal models, particularly the fructose–palmitate–cholesterol model, and in vitro systems to highlight how distinct metabolic insults reprogram hepatocytes to secrete profibrotic mediators, including Indian hedgehog, osteopontin, meteorin, bone morphogenetic protein 8B, and Jagged1, as well as metabolite‐ and vesicle‐mediated signals such as orotic acid and small extracellular vesicles. These hepatocyte‐derived factors directly activate HSCs and sustain fibrogenesis, with convergent pathways such as the cholesterol–TAZ–IHH axis emerging as central drivers. In parallel, hepatocytes also produce antifibrotic signals, including SERPINA3, ANGPTL6, and TrkB‐dependent pathways, which counterbalance HSC activation but are diminished during disease progression. Building on these mechanistic insights, hepatocyte‐targeted small interfering RNA therapies, particularly GalNAc‐conjugated approaches targeting key regulators such as TAZ and JAG1, have demonstrated robust antifibrotic efficacy in preclinical and humanized models. Together, this review establishes a hepatocyte‐centered framework for MASH fibrosis and highlights precision gene‐silencing strategies as promising therapeutic avenues to disrupt hepatocyte‐driven HSC activation and fibrotic remodeling.

title: Emulate the Leader? Explaining Crisis Policy Change in the Canadian Federal System
summary: ABSTRACT In times of crises, do governments coordinate or do they make their own choices independent of what others do? Convergence of COVID‐19 policy at the beginning of the pandemic has been widely studied in federal countries. Yet, there
content: ABSTRACT In times of crises, do governments coordinate or do they make their own choices independent of what others do? Convergence of COVID‐19 policy at the beginning of the pandemic has been widely studied in federal countries. Yet, there is limited literature looking at the mechanisms that made policy between jurisdictions so similar. Utilizing Canada's decentralized federal system, this paper posits that convergence can be explained by a process of policy diffusion through emulation and a series of leader‐follower relationships. Drawing on the policy diffusion literature, this paper proposes three hypotheses for why some jurisdictions take on leadership roles in crisis policy while others follow. Synthesized as proximity, capacity, and urgency, these hypotheses are tested using a series of pairwise vector autoregressions identifying significant leader‐follower relationships between Canadian provinces. The findings suggest that policy primarily flowed from only a small number of large provinces (Quebec and Ontario), lending partial evidence, but also exceptions to the hypotheses proposed.

title: Polarization Is Required to Model Electrostatic Preorganization: The Case of Chorismate Mutase
summary: Electrostatic preorganization contributes to enzymatic catalysis through transition state stabilization and is often investigated using classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that employ fixed-charge force fields (FFs).Although polar
content: Electrostatic preorganization contributes to enzymatic catalysis through transition state stabilization and is often investigated using classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that employ fixed-charge force fields (FFs).Although polarizable FFs allow for more accurate quantification of local electrostatic effects, whether they qualitatively differ from fixed-charge FFs regarding properties such as the substrate conformation stabilized by the enzyme's electrostatics remains unclear.Here, we compare molecular dynamics simulations of chorismate mutase performed with the AMOEBA polarizable FF and the AMBER fixed-charge FF.We find that simulations using AMOEBA sample chorismate geometries resembling the transition state-like near attack conformation (NAC), while AMBER simulations sample strictly non-NAC conformations.The local substrate-protein interactions are also completely altered by the choice of FF, with AMOEBA and AMBER each sampling distinct active site hydrogen bond networks.Finally, even at matched reactive substrate conformations, the heterogeneous three-dimensional electric field experienced by the substrate is qualitatively different between the FFs.By additionally comparing to a modified AMOEBA FF with the induced dipole term turned off, we also isolate the explicit polarization in AMOEBA as the key contributor to these differences.

title: Data-driven governance for low-carbon transition in seaport-dry port intermodal systems: risk signals from Ningbo-Zhoushan
summary: This paper examines how publicly available planning and operational data can be used to identify risks associated with the low-carbon transition in seaport-dry port intermodal transport systems, and further identifies governance mechanisms
content: This paper examines how publicly available planning and operational data can be used to identify risks associated with the low-carbon transition in seaport-dry port intermodal transport systems, and further identifies governance mechanisms that could mitigate these risks. The paper integrates open data on production plans of the Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan in 2025–2026 with policy and industry resources in Zhejiang Province on intermodal transport development, digital platforms, intelligent scheduling, and hub evaluation. The evidence shows a structural mismatch: cargo throughput rose from 1.37709 billion tons in 2024 to 1.43192 billion tons in 2025, with a target of 1.45000 billion tons in 2026; container throughput is set to rise by 11.63% in 2025 and by another 9.18% in 2026. This mismatch is not seen in this paper as evidence of a direct carbon causal relationship, but as an indicator of a transition risk and is being assessed alongside other possible explanations like capacity constraints, changes in the demand structure, and policy lags. Building on this, the study constructs a four-dimensional governance framework comprising mode governance, platform governance, operational governance, and energy governance. For each dimension, this paper identifies specific mechanisms grounded in the practices of the Ningbo-Zhoushan Port and Zhejiang Province, and explains how they address the observed mismatch. The contributions of this paper lie in redefining low-carbon transition as a risk-sensitive governance issue, clarifying the operationalization of transition risks, and providing an empirically grounded framework for analyzing the Maritime Silk Road freight corridor.

title: Selective logging better preserves adaptive capacity than clear‐cutting in subtropical forests of China via tree compositional and structural recovery
summary: Abstract The adaptive capacity of ecosystems indicates their ability to cope with disturbance impacts. According to the framework of adaptive cycle theory, this capacity declines with increasing logging intensity. However, this relationship
tags: Tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests
content: Abstract The adaptive capacity of ecosystems indicates their ability to cope with disturbance impacts. According to the framework of adaptive cycle theory, this capacity declines with increasing logging intensity. However, this relationship remains empirically unvalidated. This study investigated how selective logging and clear‐cutting affect forest adaptive capacity (comprising potential, which refers to species resource accumulation; connectedness, which refers to the rigidity of species interactions; and resilience). We analysed adaptive capacity dynamics (3–5 years and 10–22 years) using three 20 × 30 m plots per treatment, as well as the effects of species diversity, functional group composition and stand structure following harvest in subtropical forests of China. Both selective logging and clear‐cutting caused a loss of forest adaptive capacity due to significant declines in potential and connectedness. Under selective logging, these attributes were at least 50% higher than those under clear‐cutting, with values approaching mature natural forest within 10–22 years. The impacts of the two forest management practices on potential and connectedness were driven primarily by species evenness, the abundance ratio of light‐demanding to shade‐tolerant species, and tree height inequality. Synthesis and applications . Our study provides experimental evidence that selective logging better maintains the adaptive capacity of subtropical forests than clear‐cutting, primarily by promoting the recovery of species diversity, tree composition and structure. Our findings not only advance the practical understanding of adaptive cycle theory but also inform policy frameworks aiming at sustainable forest management.
