title: Particle Size Distribution and Extrusion Performance of Mine Tailings-Based Mortars for 3D Concrete Printing: A Case Study from Chile and Japan
summary: The incorporation of mine tailings into 3D concrete printing offers a promising pathway to reduce cement consumption while valorizing large volumes of mining waste. This study investigates the feasibility of replacing 30% of cement with Chi
content: The incorporation of mine tailings into 3D concrete printing offers a promising pathway to reduce cement consumption while valorizing large volumes of mining waste. This study investigates the feasibility of replacing 30% of cement with Chilean copper mine tailings through two experimental campaigns conducted in Chile and Japan using different local materials and extrusion systems. Fresh-state behavior was evaluated through flowability testing and rheological characterization of the printable mixtures, while printability and hardened-state performance were assessed through printing trials and mechanical characterization. Mine tailings incorporation generally increased flowability and reduced yield stress and viscosity while maintaining adequate structural build-up for printing. However, one mine tailings-containing mixture exhibited complete extrusion blockage despite presenting flowability comparable to successfully printed mixtures. This discrepancy indicated that the flow-table results and visual workability assessment alone did not predict the extrusion blockage observed in the present case. Analysis of particle size distribution, particle arrangement, and paste film thickness was consistent with a possible interaction between paste availability, granular characteristics, and the confined flow conditions generated by the nozzle contraction. However, because the redesigned mixture involved simultaneous changes in granular composition, water content, and superplasticizer dosage, the contribution of individual factors to extrusion recovery could not be isolated. To address this issue, the mix design was revised by separating particles finer and coarser than 75 µm, treating the coarse fraction as part of the aggregate skeleton. The revised mixture was successfully extruded and printed in the investigated case study. The results highlight the importance of considering particle size distribution together with rheological properties when incorporating unconventional fine materials into 3D printable mortars and provide practical guidance for the use of mine tailings in digital construction applications.

title: Mechanistic Analysis and Optimisation of the Defluorination of Hydrofluorocarbon Refrigerants
summary: Herein we report the total-defluorination of 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (HFC-134a) and pentafluoroethane (HFC-125) using a KOtBu-DMSO mixture to generate KF. The lab production rate and space time yield of KF generated in flow reaches 3.76 g
content: Herein we report the total-defluorination of 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (HFC-134a) and pentafluoroethane (HFC-125) using a KOtBu-DMSO mixture to generate KF. The lab production rate and space time yield of KF generated in flow reaches 3.76 gh-1 and 7978 gh-1L-1 from HFC-134a, and 0.57 gh-1 and 57 gh-L-1 from HFC-125. A detailed study of the mechanism of defluorination was conducted through sampling of intermediates via flow aliquots, and analysis by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy.

title: Review on Research Progress and Industrial Development Path of New Energy Tractor: From Field Load Mechanism to Engineering Implementation
summary: Under China’s agricultural “double-carbon” strategy and the implementation of national emission standards, new energy tractors have become the core direction of green and low-carbon transformation of agricultural machinery, forming five pow
content: Under China’s agricultural “double-carbon” strategy and the implementation of national emission standards, new energy tractors have become the core direction of green and low-carbon transformation of agricultural machinery, forming five power technology systems: pure electric, series extended-range hybrid, parallel hybrid, series-parallel hybrid and hydrogen fuel cell. Unlike road vehicles, tractors in field operations are subjected to random impact loads caused by abrupt changes in soil and terrain, and to harsh conditions of ultra-wide temperature ranges, high vibration, mud, and dust; directly transplanting automotive three-electric components and algorithms reduces reliability and shortens component life. The global industry is transitioning from principle prototypes to small-batch commercialization, and medium- and large-horsepower heavy-duty models have not yet broken the industrialization bottleneck. Based on farmland random-load mechanisms, this paper reviews the technical evolution and R&D system differences of new energy tractors at home and abroad, analyzes the energy conversion mechanisms and working-condition adaptation boundaries of the five configurations, and identifies key bottlenecks in the agricultural-machinery-specific three-electric system, adaptive energy management, electrical architecture and thermal management. By comparing the performance gaps among simulation, bench and field tests, the core contradiction of R&D iteration is clarified. PEST-SWOT analysis evaluates the industrial environment, and whole-life-cycle economy is compared across business entities. Differentiated development paths by horsepower segment and six-dimensional industrial countermeasures (basic data, specialized parts, standards, business models, infrastructure, operation and maintenance) are proposed. The results show that the core bottleneck is not prototype trial-production capability but systematic problems: shortage of specialized parts, lack of a farmland load database, weak simulation-field closed-loop iteration, and lagging supporting and operation-maintenance systems. This study provides theoretical support and engineering reference for new energy tractor iteration, pilot-scale maturation, large-scale development and policy formulation.

title: Inhibitory, Anticancer Efficacy and Structural Insights of a Novel Ethyl 1‐Hydroxy‐3‐Oxo‐1‐Phenylisoindoline‐2‐Sulfonate Compound Selectively Targeting Human CA IX and CA XII Carbonic Anhydrase, Ferroptosis‐Mediated Cell Death
summary: ABSTRACT Carbonic anhydrase (CA) isoforms IX and XII are critical in anticancer drug development due to their essential roles in regulating pH and hypoxic conditions. In this study, the inhibitory potential of ethyl‐1‐hydroxy‐3‐oxo‐1‐phenyl
content: ABSTRACT Carbonic anhydrase (CA) isoforms IX and XII are critical in anticancer drug development due to their essential roles in regulating pH and hypoxic conditions. In this study, the inhibitory potential of ethyl‐1‐hydroxy‐3‐oxo‐1‐phenylisoindoline‐2‐sulfonate (1), synthesized via click chemistry, was evaluated against hCA IX and hCA XII. The cellular effects of compound on human breast cancer (MCF‐7 cells) were investigated using a combination of viability, oxidative stress, and molecular level. Compound exhibited stronger inhibitory activity than the acetazolamide (AAZ), with K i values of 11.48 ± 4.18 nM for hCA IX and 9.32 ± 2.35 nM for hCA XII. The compound exhibited a higher binding affinity to hCA IX with −8.8 kcal/mol docking score. While no cytotoxic effect was observed on MCF‐10A cells, a significant dose‐dependent reduction was observed in cell viability, confirmed loss of membrane integrity in cancer cells. ROS levels were decreased at higher concentrations, indicating that the toxicity was independent of ROS production. Caspase‐3 and LC3B expression showed strong positivity at moderate concentrations, suggesting activation of apoptotic and autophagic pathways. GPX4 and TFRC fluorescence intensities were markedly decreased that disruption of redox homeostasis and iron metabolism. These findings indicate that compound is a promising lead molecule for the development of next‐generation anticancer agents targeting tumor‐associated CA isoforms.

title: Marine Plug Flow Bioreactors Provide a High‐Throughput Assay of Potential DOC Bioavailability
summary: Abstract Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) forms the largest reservoir of reduced carbon in the ocean, yet its bioavailability and the microbial processes governing its transformation remain poorly constrained. Traditional seawater batch cultu
content: Abstract Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) forms the largest reservoir of reduced carbon in the ocean, yet its bioavailability and the microbial processes governing its transformation remain poorly constrained. Traditional seawater batch cultures have been indispensable for measuring bioavailable DOC (BDOC), but their long incubation times and limited throughput constrain comparisons across environmental gradients and treatments. Here, we adapted marine plug flow bioreactors, glass columns packed with inert glass beads colonized by natural microbial assemblages, to provide a high‐throughput operational assay of potential DOC bioavailability. After approximately 6 months of conditioning, single‐column bioreactor assays consistently removed DOC from coastal surface waters, deep seawater, and surface seawater amended with diatom‐derived organic matter within 4–7 hr. Linking bioreactors in series increased cumulative DOC removal although the number of columns contributing additional removal varied among source waters. In paired experiments, terminal bioreactor DOC removal equaled or exceeded that measured at the final sampling point of seawater batch cultures incubated for weeks to months. Bioreactor‐associated microbial communities were enriched in Planctomycetota and Thermoproteota relative to the free‐living communities in batch cultures, reflecting the distinct microbial assemblages supported by the two approaches. Because bioreactors operate under high‐biomass, attached community conditions that differ from the open ocean, their measurements represent internally comparable estimates of potential DOC bioavailability rather than realized in situ utilization. Used alongside seawater batch cultures, marine bioreactors provide a complementary framework for distinguishing potential DOC bioavailability from realized DOC utilization.

title: Fdm-based 4D printed polymer blends: characteristics and applications
summary: Abstract Shape memory polymers are a distinct category of intelligent materials that can change their configuration in response to external stimuli, such as moisture, light, or temperature. 4-dimensional (4D) printing offers the advantages
content: Abstract Shape memory polymers are a distinct category of intelligent materials that can change their configuration in response to external stimuli, such as moisture, light, or temperature. 4-dimensional (4D) printing offers the advantages of 3-dimensional printing and shape-memory capability. The use of polymer blends offers an effective strategy to enhance the overall shape memory effect, including improvements in shape recovery, shape fixity, response time, and recovery speed, while simultaneously tailoring mechanical performance. This review presents a comprehensive overview of material selection, blend composition, and relationships between structure, properties, and stimuli in fused deposition modeling (FDM)-based 4D-printed polymer blends. The key characterization techniques used to assess thermal, mechanical, and shape-memory behaviors are critically discussed. Recent advances in polymer blend systems, including PLA, PETG, TPU, PCL, and ABS-based blends, are reviewed. Further, their emerging applications in biomedical devices, soft robotics, aerospace, and smart structures are discussed. Finally, the current challenges in printability, interfacial compatibility, rheology, and reproducibility, along with future research directions, are outlined to advance FDM-based 4D printed polymer blend systems.

title: A Device‐to‐Package Perspective on Thermal Management Materials for Electronic Devices
summary: With the continued miniaturization and integration of electronic devices, power density and local heat flux have increased substantially, making heat dissipation a major constraint on device performance and reliability. Improving thermal tr
tags: Thermal management of electronic devices and systems
content: With the continued miniaturization and integration of electronic devices, power density and local heat flux have increased substantially, making heat dissipation a major constraint on device performance and reliability. Improving thermal transport inside devices through materials engineering has therefore attracted increasing attention. In this review, we systematically summarize the thermal transport mechanisms, recent progress, and manipulation strategies of materials for thermal management of electronic devices along the internal heat-dissipation pathway. At the device and die level, we discuss representative semiconductors, metals, and dielectrics, with emphasis on their thermal transport mechanisms and their thermal conductivity manipulation. In addition, thermal transport across microscopic interfaces is discussed. At the package level, we focus on thermal interface materials (TIMs) with emphasis on their structure-property relationships and thermal performance enhancement strategies. Across these different levels, a common principle emerges: intrinsic thermal conductivity alone is insufficient to determine the thermal performance of a material after integration, because dimensions, processing-induced changes, and interfaces are also important. By analyzing materials along the internal heat-dissipation pathway, this review identifies the key thermal bottlenecks and defines the material and interface requirements for a low-resistance internal heat-dissipation pathway in future electronic devices with high power density and a high degree of integration.

title: mRNA Decay Mediates Evolution and Biological Functions in Plant Gene Expression
summary: mRNA decay is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism that fine-tunes plant development and stress adaptation through dynamic mRNA stability control, bridging fundamental biology and crop improvement. Current knowledge of mRNA decay
content: mRNA decay is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism that fine-tunes plant development and stress adaptation through dynamic mRNA stability control, bridging fundamental biology and crop improvement. Current knowledge of mRNA decay mechanisms in plants, largely derived from Arabidopsis, is poorly generalisable across plant lineages owing to insufficient exploration of other species. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing have accelerated the discovery of mRNA decay mechanisms. Here, we systematically illustrate its core molecular mechanisms alongside breakthrough advances. We further dissect evolutionary characteristics of highly conserved core components and lineage-specific adaptive variations across eukaryotes. Notably, conserved since the last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA), this machinery reflects a complex ancestral eukaryote and provides high-resolution phylogenetic markers for reconstructing eukaryotic origins. We also clarify the essential biological roles of mRNA decay in developmental modulation and stress responses. Finally, we propose precision breeding strategies based on mRNA stability regulation to develop high-yielding, climate-resilient crops. This review integrates up-to-date mechanistic evidence and comparative evolutionary perspectives, consolidates consensus findings and sorts out inconsistent research outcomes, and seeks to enrich the fundamental biological understanding of plant mRNA stability modulation.

title: Chemo‐Mechanical Solid Production in Deep Carbonate Gas Reservoirs: A Mineralogical Classification and Exploratory Intensity Evaluation (Case Study From the Eastern Sichuan Basin, SW China)
summary: ABSTRACT Solid production and blockage in deep carbonate gas reservoirs can impair flow assurance and wellbore integrity. The term solid production is used here as an umbrella term covering (i) mechanically released reservoir‐derived partic
content: ABSTRACT Solid production and blockage in deep carbonate gas reservoirs can impair flow assurance and wellbore integrity. The term solid production is used here as an umbrella term covering (i) mechanically released reservoir‐derived particles, (ii) chemically precipitated or scale‐like solids, and (iii) mixed chemo‐mechanical products; the term sanding is reserved for mechanically released particles or for comparison with conventional sandstone studies. Blockage and solid‐production samples were collected from 11 representative wells in the Eastern Sichuan Basin and characterized using x‐ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy with energy‐dispersive spectroscopy (SEM–EDS), thermogravimetric analysis/loss on ignition (TGA/LOI), acid‐solubility analysis, and particle‐size measurements. A diagnostic framework was established using carbonate minerals (calcite + dolomite) and acid‐insoluble silica as mineralogical endmembers, with LOI and SEM–EDS used as an auxiliary diagnostic route for biogenic and organic/sulfide‐bearing materials. Four nonoverlapping diagnostic modes were defined: Type I, carbonate‐rich chemically precipitated solids; Type II, mixed carbonate–silica chemo‐mechanical solids; Type III, biogenic or organic/sulfide‐bearing solids identified by ancillary evidence; and Type IV, silica‐rich mechanically released particles. A bounded Combined Solid‐Production Index (CSI) is proposed as an exploratory mineralogy‐based indicator. The available data support mechanism‐based diagnosis and screening of well‐control options, but the small sample set and incomplete replicate‐level records do not provide independent predictive validation of CSI.

title: Leadership Effectiveness and Foreign Assistance: Assessing Community-Based Infrastructure Sustainability in Southeastern Nigeria
source: European Conference on Management, Leadership and Governance (ECMLG)
summary: Foreign assistance remains a major facilitator of development in developing countries, but its effectiveness is largely conditioned by the quality of leadership that mediates implementation. Effective leadership and governance of foreign as
content: Foreign assistance remains a major facilitator of development in developing countries, but its effectiveness is largely conditioned by the quality of leadership that mediates implementation. Effective leadership and governance of foreign assistance within government-established agencies are mandated to achieve sustainable development of community infrastructure. Situated within the development administration and foreign assistance effectiveness discourse, this study investigates how effective leadership shapes the transition of foreign assistance toward achieving community-based infrastructure sustainability in Southeastern Nigeria through the activities of the Community and Social Development Agency (CSDA). This study is anchored on institutional theory. A cross-sectional survey research design was adopted. The study employed a multi-stage, stratified, and purposive sampling technique with a sample size of 398 respondents. Primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire. The data collected were coded and analysed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) version 27. Both descriptive and inferential statistical techniques were employed. Descriptive statistics include frequencies, percentages, means, and standard deviation, while multiple regression analysis was used to test the hypothesis. The study finds that leadership effectiveness and foreign assistance influence the sustainability of community-based infrastructure for water, electricity, and roads and that institutional weakness, corruption, lack of transparency, and accountability challenge and shape the outcomes of infrastructure projects, with R²=0.967, indicating that leadership effectiveness and foreign assistance account for 96.7% of the variance. The study contributes to development administration by emphasising the role that national and sub-national leaders, administrators, development agencies, local communities, and donor institutions and organisations should play in achieving community infrastructure development. This study recommends strengthening local leadership and institutional capacity, inclusive governance, and transparency to enhance the sustainability of community-based infrastructure. The policy implication would inform government and policymakers about the importance of effective leadership, institutional reforms, and capacity building as desiderata in enhancing foreign assistance administration to achieve sustainable community-based infrastructure development that will enhance the socioeconomic livelihoods of local communities in Nigeria.

title: Cadmium metabolism, multi-media emissions and long-term waste burdens in China: MFA modelling, driver decomposition and sustainable management insights
summary: Cadmium (Cd) is a toxic by-product of non-ferrous metallurgy that is intentionally used in industrial materials and low-carbon CdTe photovoltaic technologies. Existing Cd studies rarely integrate historical flow accounting, long-term waste
content: Cadmium (Cd) is a toxic by-product of non-ferrous metallurgy that is intentionally used in industrial materials and low-carbon CdTe photovoltaic technologies. Existing Cd studies rarely integrate historical flow accounting, long-term waste projection and driving-factor decomposition within a unified quantitative framework, limiting the development of sustainable mitigation strategies. This study develops a national-scale Cd metabolism framework to quantify Cd flows, in-use stocks, direct releases to air and wastewater, and transfers to solid-waste management pathways in mainland China during 2010–2020, together with multi-scenario projections to 2050. Material flow analysis, logarithmic mean Divisia index decomposition, Weibull lifetime modelling and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis are integrated to improve the reliability of the assessment. Zinc-ore by-products dominate domestic Cd inputs, while Cd consumption has shifted from nickel-cadmium batteries towards PVC heat stabilisers and CdTe photovoltaic modules. Concentrate and smelting processes are the primary sources of direct environmental releases, whereas solid-waste pathways dominate Cd transfers to waste-management systems and represent –tial long-term leakage reservoirs. Economic expansion drives continuous Cd stock accumulation, while declining material and Cd-content intensities partly offset this pressure. Scenario analysis shows that accelerated substitution with Cd-free PVC stabilisers provides the strongest source-reduction lever, substantially reducing future PVC-related Cd input, stock and end-of-life flows. CdTe lifetime extension delays retirement, accelerated photovoltaic expansion enlarges future stock and retirement burdens, and enhanced recycling increases Cd recovery while reducing residual Cd waste. By linking metal resource metabolism, environmental burdens and circular governance, this study provides a quantitative decision-support framework for life-cycle management of Cd-containing products and Cd-laden solid wastes under the low-carbon transition.

title: Encoding metabolic stress into tumor evolution through ECM–integrin-dependent transcriptional plasticity
summary: Tumor evolution is driven not only by genetic alterations but also by the capacity of cancer cells to adapt to dynamic microenvironmental stresses. Emerging evidence indicates that metabolic constraints can remodel the extracellular matrix
content: Tumor evolution is driven not only by genetic alterations but also by the capacity of cancer cells to adapt to dynamic microenvironmental stresses. Emerging evidence indicates that metabolic constraints can remodel the extracellular matrix (ECM), extending stress adaptation beyond cell-intrinsic programs. Importantly, stress-induced changes in ECM composition, organization and mechanics may persist beyond the initiating stimulus and influence subsequent cell–matrix signaling. We refer to this proposed persistence of stress-associated extracellular changes as“ECM encoding”, a form of physicochemical information storage that is mechanistically distinct from genetic memory or cell-intrinsic epigenetic stabilization. Here, we critically review the ECM–integrin axis as a signaling interface linking metabolic stress, redox adaptation and transcriptional plasticity. Metabolic pressures, including hypoxia, nutrient limitation and isolation stress, reshape ECM composition, mechanics and ligand availability, thereby reprogramming integrin signaling. Through focal adhesions, cytoskeletal tension and nuclear mechanotransduction, integrin-dependent signals can influence chromatin accessibility and converge with stress-responsive networks involving YAP/TAZ, ATF4, HIF, NRF2, STAT3 and NF-κB. In parallel, matrix-dependent regulation of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production and NRF2-mediated antioxidant responses may provide mechanisms linking extracellular cues to redox adaptation. These interconnected processes can promote phenotypic plasticity associated with stemness, dormancy, metastasis, immune evasion and therapeutic resistance, although their relative contributions vary across tumor types and experimental contexts. Finally, we evaluate the therapeutic potential of targeting the ECM–integrin–redox network while considering signaling redundancy, previous clinical setbacks and the need for biomarker-guided patient selection.

title: Radical‑Mediated Formal Anti‑Markovnikov Hydroalkenylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by a Functional Alkenyl‑Radical Surrogate Strategy
summary: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hyd
content: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. Herein, we establish a novel strategy to realize the first radical‑mediated formal anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation of unactivated alkenes. This approach utilizes the combination of highly electrophilic triphenylphosphonium methyl (TPPM) radicals with weak H atom abstraction reactivity and carbonyl compounds as practical alkenyl‑radical surrogates. The transformation begins with the photocatalytic reduction of bromomethyl triphenylphosphonium bromide to generate TPPM radicals, which add to unactivated alkenes to form carbon-centered radicals that abstract a hydrogen atom from thiophenol. The resulting phosphonium salts subsequently undergo an in‑situ Wittig reaction with carbonyl compounds to furnish the devised hydroalkenylation products. This protocol exhibits good functional group tolerance, broad substrate scope covering both activated and unactivated olefins, and allows late‑stage functionalization of natural product derivatives.

title: Multifunctional hybrid Nylon/Chitosan/Hydroxyapatite/TiO₂ biocoatings for enhanced corrosion protection and cellular response of 316L stainless steel implants
summary: Although numerous polymer and ceramic coatings have been developed for metal implants, achieving long-term corrosion protection while maintaining favorable immune responses remains a significant challenge. This study developed and evaluated
content: Although numerous polymer and ceramic coatings have been developed for metal implants, achieving long-term corrosion protection while maintaining favorable immune responses remains a significant challenge. This study developed and evaluated multifunctional hybrid nylon (PA)/chitosan (CS)/hydroxyapatite (HAp)/TiO₂ biocoatings deposited on 316 L stainless steel (316 L SS) by dip-coating to improve corrosion resistance and biological performance for implant applications. Two formulations, PA84%/CS10%/HAp5%/TiO₂1% and PA89%/CS5%/HAp5%/TiO₂1%, were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), mechanical testing, cell viability assays with RAW-Blue macrophages, NF-κB activation analysis, and electrochemical evaluation in Hank's solution for 120 days. The coatings exhibited homogeneous porous morphologies, indicating integration between the polymeric matrix and ceramic phases. This microstructure was accompanied by cell viability approaching 98%, while NF-κB activation remained low compared with the inflammatory control, demonstrating a cellular response compatible with biomedical applications. Although CS, HAp, and TiO₂ incorporation reduced the mechanical performance relative to neat PA, the hybrid biocoatings retained ductility and resilience suitable for flexible coating applications, with PA84%/CS10%/HAp5%/TiO₂1% showing the best balance among the composites. Electrochemical tests demonstrated enhanced corrosion protection compared with uncoated 316 L SS. Among the evaluated systems, PA84%/CS10%/HAp5%/TiO₂1% showed the best performance, exhibiting the lowest corrosion current density (3.00E-07 mA/cm 2 ) and the highest impedance modulus (90372 Ω.cm 2 ) after 120 days of immersion. This behavior was attributed to the multifunctional protective layer, which combines barrier effect, interfacial stability, and diffusion-controlled ionic transport, due to the coating-passive layer synergy. These results indicate the potential of PA/CS/HAp/TiO₂ biocoatings to enhance long-term corrosion protection and biologically compatible surfaces for metallic implants.

title: Ensemble of ∆-ML Models for Quantum Chemistry Level of Theory Selection for Interaction Energies
summary: Ab initio quantum chemical approaches for computing interactions between molecules are useful in a wide range of applications but can be difficult to apply effectively. In particular, variations in cost and accuracy across different levels
content: Ab initio quantum chemical approaches for computing interactions between molecules are useful in a wide range of applications but can be difficult to apply effectively. In particular, variations in cost and accuracy across different levels of theory (method and basis set combinations) makes it challenging to select an appropriate level of theory for a given chemical system. In this work, we train ∆-machine learning models to predict interaction energy errors for 81 levels of theory versus a reference and simple polynomial models to quantify computational cost for a meaningful subset of these methods. We demonstrate how a large language model (LLM) can leverage these models to select appropriate levels of theory and run computations autonomously on distributed resources, significantly reducing the barrier to obtaining accurate interaction energies.

title: GOVERNING NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS IN DEVELOPING-COUNTRY CITIES: A BIBLIOMETRIC MAPPING OF URBAN SUSTAINABILITY, INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY AND CLIMATE RESILIENCE
summary: Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) have emerged as a critical instrument for advancing urban sustainability and climate resilience, particularly in developing countries where rapid economic-driven urbanization intensifies exposure to climate risk
content: Nature-Based Solutions (NbS) have emerged as a critical instrument for advancing urban sustainability and climate resilience, particularly in developing countries where rapid economic-driven urbanization intensifies exposure to climate risks. There is little theoretical coherence and well-organized knowledge regarding patterns of collaboration. The current paper aims at filling this gap by conducting a high-quality bibliometric systematic literature review (B-SLR) of 1,260 articles included in the Scopus database since 2006. The paper uses performance analysis, science- mapping methods, with the help of Bibliometrics package and VOS viewer, to analyze the results of scientific production, journals and sources impact, most active authors and institutions, citation patterns, collaboration, co-occurring keywords and thematic development. The findings show that publication activity remained modest from 2006 to 2013, accelerated after 2015 and surged markedly following global climate policy shifts, including the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals, post-COVID urban recovery and a renewed focus on sustainable development. The findings also show major governance biases between the institutions of the developed and developing countries with the knowledge creation being disproportionately generative in the Global North due to the asymmetries in the institutional capacity and bringing implications of the lack of transferability of NbS policies in various urban settings. The study provides a critical mapping of the intellectual framework and development of the NbS research in the past 20 years, which enables both scholars, policymakers and practitioners interested in developing NbS strategies to achieve sustainable and climate-resilient urban development.

title: From aldabra giant tortoises to humans: how diet and age influence gut microbiota structure and function across vertebrates
source: AMS Dottorato Institutional Doctoral Theses Repository (University of Bologna)
summary: The gut microbiota plays a crucial role in host physiology by metabolizing dietary carbohydrates via carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) and producing short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). This research explores microbiome dynamics across vert
content: The gut microbiota plays a crucial role in host physiology by metabolizing dietary carbohydrates via carbohydrate-active enzymes (CAZymes) and producing short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs). This research explores microbiome dynamics across vertebrates, integrating studies on tortoises and humans. First, in Aldabra giant tortoises, wild populations harbor greater microbial diversity than captive individuals. Infant tortoises exhibit higher CAZyme gene diversity, particularly from Bacteroides cellulosilyticus, suggesting enhanced carbohydrate metabolism early in life. Second, a human dietary fiber intervention shows rapid increases in SCFA levels, particularly acetate and propionate, alongside delayed enrichment of Parabacteroides, a CAZyme-rich genus. Third, a comparative analysis of 35 vertebrate species reveals widespread conservation of CAZyme families and SCFA-producing taxa across reptiles, birds, and mammals, despite differences in host diet and phylogeny. These findings highlight the interplay between diet, age, and microbial function, demonstrating that while microbiome composition varies, core metabolic pathways remain evolutionarily conserved.

title: Functional genomic analysis of Vreelandella zhaodongensis BS253: a new isolate from hypersaline lakes from Brazilian Pantanal
summary: Abstract Natural ecosystems harbor an immense diversity of microorganisms whose metabolic capabilities remain unexplored. Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological a
content: Abstract Natural ecosystems harbor an immense diversity of microorganisms whose metabolic capabilities remain unexplored. Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological and biochemical traits, which may be useful for biotechnological applications. In this study, we report the complete genome sequencing and functional characterization of isolate BS253, isolated in a hypersaline alkaline lake from Brazil’s Pantanal region. Using a hybrid sequencing strategy combining Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads, we assembled a circular chromosome of 3.76 Mb and two plasmids. Phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses identified the isolate as Vreelandella zhaodongensis . Digital DNA-DNA hybridization (76.4%) and ANI (96.83%) values supported the designation of BS253 as a strain of V. zhaodongensis . Genome mining revealed genes potentially associated with salt and alkali tolerance, hydrocarbon and plastic degradation, and the biosynthesis of secondary metabolites. Phenotypically, BS253 is a moderately halophilic, facultatively anaerobic, Gram-negative rod that also exhibits emulsifying activity (55.1%) under defined culture conditions. These findings highlight strain BS253 as a metabolically versatile extremophile and a promising candidate for future studies in environmental and industrial biotechnology.

title: MemPerceiver: Adaptive Multi-Scale Memory Reveals Biome-Specific Temporal Fingerprints in Carbon Flux Prediction
source: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
summary: Terrestrial carbon flux prediction is critical for quantifying ecosystem carbon sources and sinks. However, current deep learning models still struggle with cross-ecosystem generalisation across the heterogeneous biomes covered by global ed
content: Terrestrial carbon flux prediction is critical for quantifying ecosystem carbon sources and sinks. However, current deep learning models still struggle with cross-ecosystem generalisation across the heterogeneous biomes covered by global eddy-covariance networks. A fundamental reason is that different ecosystems are shaped by past climate over very different timescales: climate may continue to influence ecosystem processes for only weeks in tropical savannas but for months in temperate forests, while existing models apply a single uniform temporal context window to all ecosystems. To address this challenge, we propose MemPerceiver, a multimodal framework that augments the EcoPerceiver backbone with six ecologically motivated memory scales (−180 to −7 days) and a per-scale gating network, allowing the model to autonomously select which temporal horizons matter for each ecosystem without any ecological prior. On the CarbonSense benchmark of 385 eddy-covariance sites across 15 IGBP classes, MemPerceiver achieves state-of-the-art performance on both Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE) and Gross Primary Production (GPP), with the largest gains where cross-ecosystem generalisation is hardest: a 23% RMSE reduction on the one-shot WAT class and a 24% NSE improvement on the zero-shot SNO class. Averaging the learned gate activations within each biome yields an interpretable temporal fingerprint, and within-biome consistency analysis shows that these fingerprints provide a stable, model-derived view of biome-specific ecological memory. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MemPerceiver-C000.

title: Spatial patterns in phytoplankton community composition and their relationship to carbon export on the northwest Weddell Sea continental shelf
summary: Abstract. Typically, diatoms, haptophytes, and cryptophytes dominate phytoplankton biomass and abundance in the Southern Ocean, determining bloom dynamics and carbon transfer and respond to physical factors such as sea ice concentration and
content: Abstract. Typically, diatoms, haptophytes, and cryptophytes dominate phytoplankton biomass and abundance in the Southern Ocean, determining bloom dynamics and carbon transfer and respond to physical factors such as sea ice concentration and mixing. However, phytoplankton community composition remains understudied in many regions of the Southern Ocean. Here, we present pigment-based phytoplankton community-composition data from a summer cruise to the northwest Weddell Sea continental shelf. To our knowledge, these are the only pigment-based community composition data from this key region for deep-water formation and carbon transport. Taken together, the relative biomass of the three dominant phytoplankton groups (39.7% diatoms, 30.2% haptophytes, and 14.9% cryptophytes) explain the majority (R2 = 0.37 – 0.82) of carbon export to 150 m. These findings highlight the need to consider frequently overlooked phytoplankton types, alongside diatoms, in Southern Ocean models of carbon export due to the key, but differing, roles these groups play in production-export dynamics.

title: Functional green illusion in global semi-arid carbon uptake revealed by physics-informed AI
summary: Rising atmospheric vapour pressure deficit (VPD) is reshaping dryland carbon cycling, yet the widely held assumption that satellite-observed greening directly translates to enhanced gross primary productivity (GPP) remains untested at a glo
content: Rising atmospheric vapour pressure deficit (VPD) is reshaping dryland carbon cycling, yet the widely held assumption that satellite-observed greening directly translates to enhanced gross primary productivity (GPP) remains untested at a global scale for water-limited ecosystems. Existing studies have not quantified the global extent of this ‘functional green illusion’, nor resolved the challenge of ensuring ecophysiologically consistent projections under extreme drought conditions. Pixel-wise Theil–Sen and Mann–Kendall trend classification of NDVI and GPP (2000–2024) shows that 5.3% of global semi-arid grasslands exhibit significant structural greening without corresponding GPP gains, with Central Asia as the primary hotspot (9.9% regional incidence). Separately, a physics-informed multimodal transformer (PIMT) that embeds light-use efficiency constraints is developed to map semi-arid grassland carbon uptake and to interpret the physiological mechanism of this decoupling: VPD-driven stomatal closure acting on minutes-to-hours timescales beneath a persistent green canopy. Our findings reveal a critical bias in terrestrial carbon sink assessments that rely on satellite greenness as a productivity proxy, and demonstrate that process-guided AI is essential for credible terrestrial carbon monitoring under intensifying atmospheric drought.

title: Genome-wide and haplotype mapping reveals genetic drivers of biomass productivity per unit water and nitrogen in sorghum
summary: Abstract Background Improving crop productivity per unit of water and nitrogen is central to climate resilient sorghum improvement, yet the genetic architecture of biomass-based resource productivity remains poorly resolved across contrasti
content: Abstract Background Improving crop productivity per unit of water and nitrogen is central to climate resilient sorghum improvement, yet the genetic architecture of biomass-based resource productivity remains poorly resolved across contrasting production environments. This study integrated multi-environment phenotyping with 1.75 million SNPs derived from whole genome resequencing of 172 cultivated Sorghum bicolor and S. bicolor × S. halepense derivative lines evaluated across temperate Mediterranean and semi-arid tropical environments. Results Biomass-based water productivity and partial factor productivity of applied nitrogen displayed extensive genetic variation and high broad-sense heritability of 0.75 to 0.81, whereas grain-based indices were more strongly influenced by genotype × environment interaction. Multi-model genome wide association analyses identified 27 significant SNPs defining 22 genomic regions for biomass-based productivity. A recurrent chromosome 9 signal at S09_55037491 was detected across three analytical models and biomass-derived indices and colocalized with Sobic.009G200500, a nitrate-responsive HAT3.1 homeobox transcription factor. Haplotype analysis independently prioritized two additional loci: a chromosome 9 haplotype associated with a 2.7-fold difference in biomass-based water productivity and containing an AHP-like cytokinin-signaling gene, and a chromosome 5 haplotype associated with a 1.86-fold difference and encompassing DAD1, a phospholipase implicated in jasmonate biosynthesis. Candidate gene prioritization also implicated aquaporin-mediated transport, trehalose-6-phosphate metabolism, oxidative signaling and, provisionally, C4 carbon assimilation. Most favorable common haplotypes occurred within cultivated germplasm rather than the introgressed lines. Conclusions Together, these findings reveal genetically tractable loci and biological pathways underlying sorghum biomass productivity per unit of supplied water and nitrogen. Following independent validation, the identified SNPs and haplotypes could support diagnostic marker development and haplotype informed selection, while genomic selection remains more appropriate for environmentally sensitive grain-based productivity traits.

title: Institutional pathways of Indigenous agroecologies in Northeast India: A historical-comparative and SDG-aligned study of Apatani and jhum systems
summary: Abstract Indigenous agrarian systems in Northeast India remain marginalized in policy, despite accumulating evidence of their ecological sophistication. This article provides a historical-comparative analysis of two exemplary systems – sede
content: Abstract Indigenous agrarian systems in Northeast India remain marginalized in policy, despite accumulating evidence of their ecological sophistication. This article provides a historical-comparative analysis of two exemplary systems – sedentary Apatani rice-fish cultivation in Arunachal Pradesh and rotational shifting ( jhum ) cultivation across the Eastern Himalayas – to explore how socio-ecological resilience emerges through locally grounded governance and adaptive knowledge. Methodologically, the study employs a historical-comparative qualitative design, systematically evaluating 120–150 secondary records from major databases through the integrated theoretical lenses of traditional ecological knowledge, political ecology, and historical institutionalism. The empirical analysis reveals that the Apatani system maintains highly stable productivity (averaging 1389 kg/ha of rice and 209 kg/ha of fish) while enhancing soil organic carbon as a climate-resilient carbon sink. Conversely, spatial data indicates that jhum cultivation has faced severe decadal contractions declining by up to 97% in specific states between 2000 and 2010, driven primarily by state-led institutional displacement and fallow compression rather than innate ecological failure. The results demonstrate that when customary institutions are accommodated, both systems strongly align with ecosystem-based targets (SDGs 2, 13, and 15) and polycentric governance (SDG 16). However, both face escalating vulnerabilities from climate-induced hydrological shifts and modern demographic pressures. The study concludes that the sustainability of Indigenous agroecologies is fundamentally a function of governance autonomy and institutional continuity, necessitating context-sensitive policy alignment rather than homogenous agricultural modernization.

title: Plant nitrogen acquisition strategies impact ecosystem carbon storage under future climate
summary: Abstract. Plant nitrogen (N) use strategies affect ecosystem nutrient cycles and limitation and thereby the response of ecosystems to global change. However, their influence on future projections of nutrient limitation and land carbon (C) s
content: Abstract. Plant nitrogen (N) use strategies affect ecosystem nutrient cycles and limitation and thereby the response of ecosystems to global change. However, their influence on future projections of nutrient limitation and land carbon (C) sink remains unclear. Here, we used a nitrogen-enabled biosphere model (QUINCY) to evaluate the competitiveness of acquisitive (high uptake, low resorption) and conservative (low uptake, high resorption) N-use strategies within plant functional types (PFTs) and climate zones under a scenario of future climate change (SSP3-7.0). We assessed competitive advantage via net primary productivity (NPP) and implications for C storage and N cycling through total ecosystem C and the ecosystem N uptake/loss ratio. Our results suggest that a broad-leaved deciduous (BDS) conservative strategy has a stronger competitive advantage compared to needle-leaved evergreens (NE) conservative, as shown by the largest relative gains in NPP (+48 %) and Ecosystem C (+22 %) together with smaller increases in N losses (-7.6 %) . This overall response varies across climate zones reflecting the latitudinal gradient in nutrient limitation. In the tropics, where N is generally not a limiting nutrient, acquisitive and conservative N-use respond similarly. In contrast, temperate and boreal regions sustain a clear advantage for conservative strategies, with higher gains in NPP (+24.8 % vs. +18.7 % in temperate BDS; +18.8 % vs. +17.7 % in temperate NE; +41.3 % vs. +30.5 % in boreal BDS; +56.7 % vs. +46.5 % in boreal NE), and consistent patterns for C storage. Together, the findings underscore that the functional N-use strategy diversity within PFTs may influence future C and N projections, and represents a conceptual step toward improving model realism.

title: STRATEGIC OPTIMIZATION OF PROVINCIAL-AUTHORITY IRRIGATION NETWORKS IN WEST JAVA: A MULTI- OBJECTIVE PROGRAMMING FRAMEWORK FOR PERFORMANCE-BASED BUDGETING
summary: Provincial irrigation agencies in West Java must allocate limited operation, maintenance, and rehabilitation budgets across ageing networks in uneven condition. This study develops a Multi-Objective Programming (MOP) framework for the 99 pr
content: Provincial irrigation agencies in West Java must allocate limited operation, maintenance, and rehabilitation budgets across ageing networks in uneven condition. This study develops a Multi-Objective Programming (MOP) framework for the 99 provincial-authority irrigation areas that integrates the six-aspect Irrigation System Performance Index (IKSI) of Ministerial Regulation No. 12/PRT/M/2015 directly into the optimization model, and links it to physical-condition assessment, budget scenarios, a five-year simulation, and qualitative policy interpretation. The model minimizes public expenditure while maximizing IKSI-weighted performance and the share of crop-water requirements met, subject to water, hydraulic, regulatory, and fiscal constraints. Evidence comes from a field survey of 99 canal segments and planning and budget documents. Of the 99 surveyed segments, 38 (38.4%) were in good, 41 (41.4%) in moderate, and 20 (20.2%) in damaged condition. Under the realistic budget scenario, the good-condition share is projected to reach 45.4–48.4% by 2029, an increase of 7–10 percentage points; this is a scenario projection, not a Pareto-optimal solution. The framework reframes irrigation budgeting as a strategic portfolio-allocation problem.

title: Evaluating heavy metal risks to biomass valorization during black soldier fly larva bioconversion of municipal sewage sludge: speciation, bioaccumulation, and safety assessment
summary: Abstract Municipal sewage sludge can potentially be valorized using black soldier fly larvae (BSFL), but heavy metal contamination may pose risks to the safety and circularity of the resulting biomass and residue. This study evaluated the d
content: Abstract Municipal sewage sludge can potentially be valorized using black soldier fly larvae (BSFL), but heavy metal contamination may pose risks to the safety and circularity of the resulting biomass and residue. This study evaluated the distribution, operational fractionation, and larval accumulation of Cu, Zn, Mn, Ni, Cd, Pb, and Cr during BSFL treatment of an artificial-diet control (S0) and sludge-incorporated substrates prepared at wet-weight ratios of 1:1 (S50) and 1:3 (S75). BSFL processed all substrates, with S50 providing the best overall balance between larval growth and substrate reduction. Metal-loading analysis identified the endpoint residue as the principal sink for most metals. BCR (Community Bureau of Reference) sequential extraction showed that Zn, Mn, Cd, and Ni occurred largely in the more readily extractable F1-F2 fractions, whereas Cu, Pb, and Cr were distributed mainly in the less extractable F3-F4 fractions. Increased F4 proportions of Pb and Cr in sludge-incorporated residue indicated enhanced stabilization. Larval accumulation was assessed using the bioaccumulation factor (BAF), background-corrected bioaccumulation factor (BAF net ), and net metal retention efficiency (NRE). Cd showed the clearest accumulation pattern, with BAF values above unity under all treatments and consistently positive NRE. Regulatory comparison identified Cd as the principal constraint on using sludge-reared larvae as feed, while Cu, Zn, and Ni constrained residue use as fertilizer. Integrating metal loading, fractionation, accumulation indices, and regulatory thresholds provides an environmental risk assessment of BSFL-based sludge valorization.

title: Tropical Peatlands as Hotspots of Hidden Arcellinida Diversity: Insights from Maludam National Park, Borneo (Sarawak, Malaysia)
summary: Recent investigations on tropical peatlands have shown their extremely high efficiency as carbon sinks, far beyond better studied boreal bogs. The microbial diversity found in those ecosystems, as well as their corresponding ecological and
content: Recent investigations on tropical peatlands have shown their extremely high efficiency as carbon sinks, far beyond better studied boreal bogs. The microbial diversity found in those ecosystems, as well as their corresponding ecological and metabolic processes, are just starting to be revealed, and differ considerably from high latitudes systems. However, these efforts have been concentrated almost exclusively towards prokaryotes and fungi, leaving protist communities virtually unknown. Arcellinida (testate amoebae) are well acknowledged to play an important role in boreal and temperate peatland ecology by driving microbial community composition as top predators, but also as nutrient recyclers and carbon fixers. Yet, to our knowledge, no community–level study has addressed their diversity and its drivers in tropical peatlands. In this study, we surveyed Arcellinida communities' diversity across five functionally distinct vegetation–hydrological zones situated along a hydrological transect in a coastal tropical peatland in the Maludam National Park, Malaysia. Taxonomic composition of Arcellinida communities, characterized by a high diversity of Trigonopyxis-related taxa, indicated fundamental differences in diversity and community composition from extratropical ecosystems. Species richness was significantly higher in the zones with developed understory vegetation. Furthermore, the composition of diversity varied significantly among vegetation-hydrological zones. Altogether, this study shows unique Arcellinida communities in a Southeastern Asian peatland and suggests the importance of vegetation-hydrological characteristics for protist diversity.

title: Resource Renewability as a Regime: A RAYOBETH Classification of Natural Capital
summary: Natural resource economics divides natural capital into renewable and nonrenewable resources. This article argues that renewability is not a property of a resource but a regime of its law of motion, set jointly by biology, institutions and
content: Natural resource economics divides natural capital into renewable and nonrenewable resources. This article argues that renewability is not a property of a resource but a regime of its law of motion, set jointly by biology, institutions and the discount rate. Writing every stock and flow of natural capital as a special case of the RAYOBETH law, it proves a harvest gap theorem, an economic exhaustibility boundary, a recycling multiplier, a sink trichotomy and a service masking theorem, and assembles them into twelve regimes in five families that partition natural capital and map onto the SEEA. Open data on oil, copper, whales, fisheries, tropical land, solar and wind capital, atmospheric carbon dioxide and wildlife abundance place each class in its regime. The atmospheric uptake rate of carbon dioxide fell from 0.036 to 0.022 per year between the 1960s and the 2020s, a sink drifting from assimilative toward cumulative.

title: Process Modelling, Simulation and Technoeconomic Evaluation of Conventional Batch, Batch Reactive Crystallization, and Continuous Reactive Crystallization Routes for Enzymatic Amoxicillin Synthesis
summary: Cost-effective production of generic antibiotics remains a pressing industrial priority, particularly for high-volume β-lactam APIs where narrow profit margins and stringent environmental regulations constrain manufacturing options. This pa
content: Cost-effective production of generic antibiotics remains a pressing industrial priority, particularly for high-volume β-lactam APIs where narrow profit margins and stringent environmental regulations constrain manufacturing options. This paper presents an integrated process systems engineering framework for the in-silico design, simulation, and technoeconomic comparison of three amoxicillin manufacturing routes: (i) conventional batch enzymatic synthesis followed by separate pH-swing crystallization; (ii) batch reactive crystallization integrating enzymatic synthesis with in-situ product removal; and (iii) continuous reactive crystallization in a mixed-suspension mixed-product removal (MSMPR) cascade. Kinetic models for penicillin G acylase-catalyzed synthesis are parameterized from literature data, coupled with population balance crystallization kinetics and solubility correlations. The continuous reactive crystallization route achieves the highest reactor productivity and the lowest process mass intensity (PMI = 28.2), yet batch reactive crystallization emerges as the most economically advantageous (24.98 million GBP), narrowly below the conventional batch route (25.71 million GBP), while the continuous MSMPR route is substantially more expensive at 120.55 million GBP — approximately 4.8 and 4.7 times the cost of the two batch routes. These findings suggest that continuous manufacturing is not always the better choice; its viability depends importantly on whether the productivity gains offset the added separation complexity and catalyst recovery costs. All API masses, yields, and green metrics in this work are expressed on an amoxicillin trihydrate basis unless stated otherwise.

title: Episodic Particle Export Revealed by Combining Imaging and Optics, including the First Deployment of an Open-Faced Flux Camera ("SnoCam")
summary: Episodic particle export is difficult to resolve with conventional sampling methods, and storms further constrain ship-based observations. Here we present observations from the first deployment of a SnoCam, a low-cost, upward-facing ‘flux c
content: Episodic particle export is difficult to resolve with conventional sampling methods, and storms further constrain ship-based observations. Here we present observations from the first deployment of a SnoCam, a low-cost, upward-facing ‘flux camera’ deployed on a Lagrangian float during the EXPORTS (EXport Processes in the Ocean from RemoTe Sensing) North Atlantic campaign. Ship-board activities were interrupted by a series of intense storms and so only the autonomous vehicles were able to obtain an uninterrupted record over the entire 21 day occupation. The float-attached SnoCam was combined with a co-located optical sediment trap, and was able to resolve multiple particle flux pulses (dominated by particles > 1 mm) coinciding with storm events. Combining SnoCam area fluxes with matched imaged particle size distribution (PSD) cross-sectional densities yielded estimated population-mean sinking speeds of 30.8 ± 28.3 m d -1 for large particles and 5.8 ± 4.4 m d -1 for small particles. Comparisons between optical backscattering and imaged PSD observations showed concurrent increases in particle concentrations near the base of the mixed layer, followed by their extension to greater depths. The short flux pulses occurred within a broader period of enhanced export captured by a particle-intercepting sediment trap array spanning the upper 500 m. Together, these observations place the two shallow flux pulses within a broader period of enhanced export into the mesopelagic, and demonstrate how sustained autonomous observations can resolve episodic export variability and identify the particle size classes and types responsible.

title: Unique particulate organic carbon properties driven by turbidity currents
summary: Turbidity currents are critical mechanisms for lateral transport of particulate organic carbon (POC) to the deep sea, yet sampling challenges have created substantial knowledge gaps regarding their impact on POC biogeochemistry. Here, a sys
content: Turbidity currents are critical mechanisms for lateral transport of particulate organic carbon (POC) to the deep sea, yet sampling challenges have created substantial knowledge gaps regarding their impact on POC biogeochemistry. Here, a systematic comparison of turbidity current-driven particles (PS turb ), background sinking particles (PS sink ), and seafloor surface particles (PS surf ) via direct sampling revealed unique older, petrogenic, terrestrial POC features of PS turb in northern Manila Trench. The ~51±33-fold higher PS turb flux than PS sink suggested that turbidity currents efficiently redistributed POC, especially the petrogenic fraction derived from mountainous Taiwan. While global sediment trap POC data synthesis enabled Manila Window for regional diagnosis of turbidity-current influences using fraction of modern carbon Fm < 0.82 and total organic carbon content TOC < 1.62%, water-column particles affected by turbidity currents followed Manila Equation (Fm=0.7*TOC-0.08, R 2 =0.95, p<0.01). These results provide new insights regarding lateral POC transport processes and their importance when building global carbon cycle models.

title: Validating static food web model diet matrices using stable isotope simulation
summary: End-to-end ecosystem models, such as Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE), are valuable tools for resource management. Within these frameworks, trophic interactions, typically derived from stomach contents analyses, govern system-wide energy flow via
content: End-to-end ecosystem models, such as Ecopath with Ecosim (EwE), are valuable tools for resource management. Within these frameworks, trophic interactions, typically derived from stomach contents analyses, govern system-wide energy flow via consumption. However, stomach contents data may be unrepresentative of long-term average diets and assimilated consumption due to factors including differential digestion rates and identifiability of prey, introducing model uncertainty. Because trophic interactions define model structure, variation in modeled diets can alter predictions and management conclusions. Consequently, evaluating and reducing uncertainty in diet matrix compositions is critical for operational acceptance of ecosystem models. Stable isotope analysis provides complementary, time-integrated insight into average diets, but its application for EwE validation has largely been limited to evaluating trophic levels and isotopic niche space. Here, we present a quantitative framework for simulating consumer stable isotope signatures across food webs from parent ecosystem models using a matrix-based mixing model. Using a published Northern Gulf of Mexico EwE model as a case study, we demonstrate Monte Carlo simulation to propagate uncertainty from basal source signatures and trophic discrimination factors. Comparison of predicted signatures with empirical δ13C and δ34S measurements enables validation of primary carbon sources and benthic-pelagic pathway contributions, revealing agreement in isotope space alongside mismatch in energy pathways. Diagnostic residuals identify discrepancies in diet composition. Model scoring provides a reproducible framework for ranking alternative diet configurations. Redundancy analysis further identifies within-group species coverage differences between stomach contents and isotope datasets as a primary driver of mismatch, highlighting an important consideration for sampling design.

title: Cool-Burn: Simultaneous TRPV1 and TRPM8 Activation in Capsicum annuum via Heterologous Expression of the Mentha × piperita Menthol Biosynthesis Pathway
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

content: Cool-Burn: Simultaneous TRPV1 and TRPM8 Activation in Capsicum annuum via Heterologous Expression of the Mentha × piperita Menthol Biosynthesis Pathway Scoville Splice Research Series · Paper 9 of 11DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23743695 (Paper 1, primary reference)Iyengar Flavor Index methodology: 10.5281/zenodo.PAPER04 OVERVIEW This preprint reports the computational design and pathway modeling of a five-gene menthol biosynthesis cassette—cloned from Mentha × piperita—inserted into Capsicum annuum SS-CV-010 (D.N.R.) to produce simultaneous activation of both TRPV1 (capsaicin receptor) and TRPM8 (cold/menthol receptor). No naturally occurring food crop achieves dual activation of these two thermosensory channels simultaneously. We designate this sensory phenotype "cool-burn." The work establishes the theoretical basis for a two-gene proof-of-concept construct and a complete five-gene pathway yielding projected menthol accumulation of 20–100 µg/g FW in ripe fruit, corresponding to an Iyengar Flavor Index — Cool (IFI-C) value of approximately 85,000. Capsaicin flux and TRPV1 activation (IFI-H: 2,956,310) are preserved to within 0.8% of wild-type. PATHWAY ARCHITECTURE All five enzymes were cloned from Mentha × piperita by Mahmoud and Croteau (2003; PNAS 100(24):14167–14172), the foundational reference for this pathway. The complete biosynthetic route from the universal terpenoid precursor GPP to (−)-menthol proceeds as follows: 1. MpLS — Limonene synthase 1 (GenBank: AF514287). Catalyzes GPP → (−)-limonene. CAI native: 0.67; optimized: 0.89. 3. MpIPPO — Isopiperitenol oxidoreductase (GenBank: AF292800). Catalyzes (−)-isopiperitenol → (−)-isopiperitenone. Short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase; cytosolic. Catalyzes (−)-pulegone → (+)-menthone. NADPH-dependent. Cytosolic. Promoter: E8 (fruit-specific). CAI native: 0.72; optimized: 0.92. 5. MpMR — Menthol reductase (GenBank: AY288138). Catalyzes (+)-menthone → (−)-menthol. NADPH-dependent; final committed step. Cytosolic. Promoter: E8 (fruit-specific). CAI native: 0.68; optimized: 0.90. Umami-Enriched Capsicum: Glutamate Accumulation via GAD1/GAD4 Knockout and GDH1 Overexpression Achieves IFI-U ≥ 800 in Ultra-High-SHU Cultivars Priyanca Iyengar Ford, Scoville Splice LLC · ORCID 0000-0003-0395-1752Preprint · Scoville Splice Research Series · Paper 5 of 11 · 2026-11-01 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────OVERVIEW This paper describes a dual metabolic engineering strategy to accumulate free L-glutamate in the placental tissue of ultra-high-SHU Capsicum annuum cultivars, achieving an Iyengar Flavor Index for umami (IFI-U) of ≥ 800 without disrupting capsaicinoid biosynthesis. The strategy combines (1) CRISPR knockout of two fruit-specific glutamate decarboxylase isoforms (CaGAD1, CaGAD4) to block the GABA shunt, and (2) overexpression of Arabidopsis thaliana glutamate dehydrogenase 1 (AtGDH1) to increase net glutamate synthesis from the TCA cycle intermediate 2-oxoglutarate. This paper should be read alongside Paper 4 (Iyengar Flavor Index methodology), Paper 7 (Kokumi engineering, which shares the glutamate/N-metabolism pool), and Paper 1 (foundational capsaicinoid engineering, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23743695). ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────BIOLOGICAL BACKGROUND Free L-glutamate is the primary ligand for the umami taste receptor, metabotropic glutamate receptor 1 (mGluR1), which was identified as a taste receptor by Chaudhari et al.
