title: Hydrogen powered energy management system for sustainable industrant applications
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Current high-temperature industrial systems still rely largely on fossil fuels, with hydrogen identified as a key vector for their decarbonization. In this paper, a methodology is developed for the development of an EMS based on hydrogen us
content: Current high-temperature industrial systems still rely largely on fossil fuels, with hydrogen identified as a key vector for their decarbonization. In this paper, a methodology is developed for the development of an EMS based on hydrogen use in industry, namely in glass and ammonia manufacturing. The EMS will involve the use of renewable electricity, electrolysis for hydrogen generation, its storage, and fuel switching between natural gas and hydrogen in order to minimize the expenses and meet the restrictions related to load of furnaces and emission limits. Model Predictive Control is chosen as the EMS architecture with use of day-ahead forecasts of renewable power generation, electricity price and gas price. The proposed methodology includes the design of the system architecture, mathematical problem statement and constraints. Simulation experiments have shown that introduction of hydrogen improves the economics and increases the share of renewables. Comparison with the systems working only with fossil fuels has confirmed the potential of the proposed approach.

title: An Integrated GPRS-Based Decision Framework for Sustainable Retrofitting of Existing Educational Buildings in Hot-Arid Climates: An Egyptian Case Study
summary: Existing educational buildings in hot-arid climates face substantial challenges related to energy demand, resource consumption, and environmental performance. Although the Green Pyramid Rating System (GPRS) provides a nationally adapted fra
content: Existing educational buildings in hot-arid climates face substantial challenges related to energy demand, resource consumption, and environmental performance. Although the Green Pyramid Rating System (GPRS) provides a nationally adapted framework for sustainable building assessment in Egypt, a methodological gap remains between GPRS assessment criteria and their systematic translation into technically feasible and economically informed retrofit decisions. This study develops an Integrated GPRS Retrofit Decision Framework and an associated GPRS Implementation Matrix to bridge this gap by linking building deficiencies and GPRS requirements with retrofit strategies, quantitative evaluation methods, performance indicators, economic criteria, and implementation priorities. The framework was applied to an existing educational building at the British University in Egypt as a case study. The methodology integrates building assessment, engineering calculations, TRNSYS 18 dynamic thermal simulation, renewable-energy assessment, water- and waste-management analysis, and techno-economic evaluation. The calibrated TRNSYS model achieved an NMBE of +3.2% and a CV(RMSE) of 8.7%. Results indicate that the proposed rooftop photovoltaic system could provide an estimated annual electricity-cost benefit of approximately EGP 365,616.315, with a simple payback period of approximately 4.17 years, while fiberglass envelope insulation reduced simulated cooling demand by approximately 7.97% relative to the baseline. Additional measures, including piezoelectric flooring, water-management interventions, and waste segregation and recycling, provided complementary energy, resource, environmental, and economic benefits. The principal contribution of the study is therefore a structured decision-support methodology that moves beyond conventional GPRS compliance assessment by integrating technical performance, environmental considerations, and economic feasibility into retrofit selection and prioritization. Application to a single educational building demonstrates the framework’s operational applicability; however, further multi-building and post-occupancy validation is required before broader transferability can be established.

title: Climate Risk Assessment and Predictive Modeling
summary: This chapter examines how climate risk assessments, predictive modeling, and AI are transforming ESH Management from reactive compliance to proactive resilience. It presents climate risk assessment as a structured process for identifying, e
content: This chapter examines how climate risk assessments, predictive modeling, and AI are transforming ESH Management from reactive compliance to proactive resilience. It presents climate risk assessment as a structured process for identifying, evaluating, and managing climate-related hazards that affect people, infrastructure, operations, and long-term organizational sustainability. This chapter demonstrates how AI enhances each stage of the climate risk assessment process by integrating large-scale climate datasets, real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and the PRIM governance framework to improve risk identification, scenario analysis, and decision-making. It explores AI-enabled climate forecasting across seasonal, decadal, and long-term planning horizons, emphasizing probabilistic forecasting, uncertainty management, and the integration of climate variables into organizational risk management. This chapter also examines disaster prediction and response by illustrating how AI-supported forecasting, real-time monitoring, and predictive models enable organizations to anticipate hazards, activate protective measures, and strengthen emergency preparedness. In addition, scenario planning and sustainability simulations are presented as strategic tools that allow organizations to evaluate alternative futures, test mitigation strategies, optimize resource allocation, and improve environmental performance before implementing changes. Real-world examples, including the Netherlands’ Delta Programme, Électricité de France (EDF’s) weather-informed electricity planning, NOAA’s AI-enhanced forecasting models, and the National Renewable Energy Laboratory’s large-scale energy simulations, demonstrate the practical application of these technologies. Collectively, this chapter illustrates how AI-supported climate forecasting and predictive analytics strengthen organizational resilience, improve regulatory compliance, and enable more informed, risk-based Environmental Management decisions in an increasingly dynamic climate environment.

title: Exergoeconomic Analysis of a Gas Turbine Integrated with Supercritical CO2 Energy Storage and Cascade Heat Utilization Considering Different Operating Periods
summary: With the increasing integration of renewable energy, large-scale energy storage systems are required to improve the flexibility of energy supply and alleviate the mismatch between power generation and demand. However, the performance evalua
content: With the increasing integration of renewable energy, large-scale energy storage systems are required to improve the flexibility of energy supply and alleviate the mismatch between power generation and demand. However, the performance evaluation of integrated energy systems combining continuous power generation and periodically operated energy storage remains challenging due to the different operating time scales of individual subsystems. In this study, a gas turbine integrated molten salt thermal energy storage and supercritical CO2 energy storage (GT-TES-CCES) system with cascade heat utilization is proposed. The proposed system recovers high-temperature exhaust heat from the gas turbine through molten salt storage, provides thermal input for CO2 expansion during discharge, and further utilizes residual heat for hot water production. A comprehensive thermodynamic and exergoeconomic model is developed, and a unified 24 h evaluation framework is introduced to consistently evaluate the continuously operated gas turbine subsystem and periodically operated charging/discharging processes. The SPECO method is employed to investigate the exergy cost formation and transfer characteristics, and multi-objective optimization is performed to identify the trade-off between exergy efficiency and product cost. At the nominal operating point, the proposed system achieves an electrical efficiency of 48.71%, an overall energy efficiency of 75.97%, and an exergy efficiency of 50.29%, with an instantaneous net power output of 40.26 MW during the discharge period and useful hot water production of 14.13 MW. After multi-objective optimization, the electrical efficiency and exergy efficiency increase to 53.99% and 54.82%, corresponding to improvements of 10.84% and 9.01%. Meanwhile, the total unit product exergy cost decreases from 14.32 to 13.55 $·GJ−1, demonstrating the economic benefit of the optimized configuration. The results indicate that the proposed multi-period exergoeconomic framework provides an effective approach for evaluating and optimizing integrated energy systems involving continuous power generation and flexible energy storage.

title: Integrating biomass valorization and clean energy: Exocarp‐derived nano‐catalyst for sustainable biodiesel production from Martynia annua L.
summary: Abstract The escalating prices and dependence on fossil fuels have intensified the climatic deterioration worldwide, pushing researchers to focus on renewable and sustainable energy. Biodiesel is an ideal substitute to conventional fuels wi
content: Abstract The escalating prices and dependence on fossil fuels have intensified the climatic deterioration worldwide, pushing researchers to focus on renewable and sustainable energy. Biodiesel is an ideal substitute to conventional fuels with the potential to tackle rising energy demands. The present study emphasizes exploring the possibility of Martynia annua L. seed oil for biodiesel production. The process of transesterification was facilitated using green Al 2 O 3 nano‐catalyst synthesized from the waste exocarp of Martynia annua fruit. Characterization of the synthesized phyto‐nanocatalyst was performed by using XRD, DRS, FTIR, SEM, DLS, and EDX techniques. Reaction conditions for transesterification were optimized using response surface methodology with a Box–Behnken Design comprising 29 experimental runs. At an oil‐to‐methanol ratio of 1:12, a catalyst loading of 0.50 wt% for 100 min and at 75°C, maximum biodiesel yield (95.2%) was achieved. The physico‐chemical properties of M. annua biodiesel including density (0.857 kg/L), acid value (0.35 mg KOH/g), cloud point (−14°C), viscosity (3.81 mm 2 /s), flash point (96°C), sulfur content (0.00723 wt%), and the pour point (−10°C) were consistent with international biodiesel standards. Thus, the finding indicates that M. annua seed oil can serve as a potential feedstock for biodiesel production, while its fruit exocarp can be used for nanocatalyst synthesis, offering a cheap and viable approach to reduce production cost and support a closed‐loop production system. Engine‐based studies are further recommended to assess its suitability for use in automobile engines.

title: Hydro and Urban Structures
summary: Hydroelectric Power (HEP) Plant Tunnels offer sustainable energy solutions for many generations to come. The worldwide energy supply based on hydropower covers only 5% of worldwide demand. In times of increasing world population, green ener
content: Hydroelectric Power (HEP) Plant Tunnels offer sustainable energy solutions for many generations to come. The worldwide energy supply based on hydropower covers only 5% of worldwide demand. In times of increasing world population, green energy demand is increasing. Design is one of the challenges in preparing investments for sustainable hydropower. Construction – This must reflect the underlying contract conditions, which must allocate and balance the risk between the parties, as underground works predominantly feature the method of excavation, access to works, land beneath works, required investment, required time and environmental impact of construction. For successful completion, full consideration of these features shall be given before and during bidding. Best Practice – Hydropower is an important component of India’s renewable energy mix, and one of the earliest, cleanest and best accepted. It is therefore understandable that all stakeholders in the hydropower industry have significant interest in evaluating and optimising hydropower projects. Corresponding efforts have resulted and are reflected in the development of best practice in the design, contracting and construction of tunnelling and underground works.

title: Switchable hydrophilicity solvents and biosolvents for green microextraction in bioanalysis
summary: Sample preparation is critical in bioanalysis because of complex biological matrices and low analyte concentrations. Conventional liquid–liquid and solid-phase extraction are effective but often consume substantial organic solvents and reso
content: Sample preparation is critical in bioanalysis because of complex biological matrices and low analyte concentrations. Conventional liquid–liquid and solid-phase extraction are effective but often consume substantial organic solvents and resources. Green analytical chemistry has therefore promoted miniaturized microextraction approaches that reduce solvent use and waste while maintaining analytical performance. This review critically examines bioanalytical microextraction through two intersecting solvent-design perspectives: stimulus-responsive switchability and renewable/bio-derived solvent design, focusing on switchable-hydrophilicity solvents (SHSs) and bio-derived deep eutectic solvents (DESs)/natural deep eutectic solvents (NADESs). SHSs enable reversible changes in hydrophilicity or ionic character to facilitate extraction and phase separation, whereas bio-derived DES/NADES systems provide tunable alternatives to conventional petroleum-based solvents. Their analytical performance, matrix-related challenges, reproducibility, and greenness are critically assessed. Future developments are expected to emphasize automated and miniaturized platforms, life-cycle assessment, and computationally assisted solvent design. Although molecular simulations are increasingly used to support solvent selection, predictive COSMO-RS and artificial-intelligence approaches remain emerging directions in bioanalysis. Before drugs and other chemicals can be measured in biological samples such as blood, plasma, or urine, the target substances often need to be separated from proteins, salts, and other sample components that may interfere with the analysis. Traditional methods for this sample preparation can use large amounts of organic solvents, generate chemical waste, and require several processing steps. This review examines newer approaches that aim to make this process smaller, simpler, and more environmentally responsible. It focuses on switchable solvents, which can change their ability to mix with water when conditions such as acidity or carbon dioxide are changed, and on alternative solvent systems made partly or fully from renewable materials, including deep eutectic and natural deep eutectic solvents. These solvents can reduce the amount of conventional organic solvent required and can be designed for different target substances. However, being renewable or using a small volume of solvent does not automatically make a method environmentally friendly. Issues such as additional chemicals, energy use, waste generation, interference from biological samples, solvent stability, water uptake, and reproducibility must also be considered. Future developments are expected to combine these solvents with automated and miniaturized extraction systems and use computer-based tools to help identify suitable solvent formulations. More consistent validation and environmental assessment will be important before these approaches can be widely adopted for routine biological analy

title: Simultaneously carbonized and sulfonated mango seed husk as a solid acid catalyst for the esterification of oleic acid with methanol
summary: Abstract The Philippines has mandated an increase in biodiesel blending from B2 (2%) to B5 (5%) under the Biofuels Act of 2006, increasing the demand for efficient and sustainable catalysts for biodiesel production. Although homogeneous cat
content: Abstract The Philippines has mandated an increase in biodiesel blending from B2 (2%) to B5 (5%) under the Biofuels Act of 2006, increasing the demand for efficient and sustainable catalysts for biodiesel production. Although homogeneous catalysts are widely used, they are economically impractical since it is difficult to recover, expensive, and not reusable. This study investigated mango seed husk (MSH) as a carbon-based precursor for a solid acid catalyst (MSH-SAC) for biodiesel production through heterogeneous esterification. Nine MSH-SAC samples were synthesized using a full factorial design with varying synthesis temperatures (100, 150, and 200°C) and times (4, 5, and 6 h) through simultaneous sulfonation and carbonization. Catalytic performance was evaluated in the esterification of oleic acid with methanol at 65°C for 6 h, using a 10:1 methanol-to-oil molar ratio and 8 wt% catalyst loading. Esterification conversions ranged from approximately 61% to 84%. Catalysts synthesized at 150°C for 4 and 5 h achieved the highest conversion of 84%. The 150°C, 4 h catalyst retained approximately 78% of its initial activity after four reuse cycles, demonstrating promising stability and reusability.

title: Managing Agricultural Waste as a Resource
summary: Agricultural waste is a severe problem worldwide, particularly in countries where there are no large land reserves. Groundbreaking projects around the world implement the waste-to-resource concept, in which agricultural waste is transformed
content: Agricultural waste is a severe problem worldwide, particularly in countries where there are no large land reserves. Groundbreaking projects around the world implement the waste-to-resource concept, in which agricultural waste is transformed into valuable raw materials, clean energy, or new products. Our economic system is based on a linear and wasteful life cycle for products from “shelves to trash,” and the value of the product decreases throughout its life. In contrast, the circular-economy worldview focuses on understanding how waste can create capital instead of reducing it. From this perspective, existing waste accumulation should be thought of and treated in the same way as mining raw materials from the ground and moving from waste to resource. According to this approach, waste concentrations have a high economic value. Therefore, creating a market-based economic incentive, a partnership between landowners and entrepreneurs who will remove the waste at their expense in exchange for the construction of facilities to produce energy from renewable sources, will contribute to the rehabilitation of agricultural waste sites and reduce the need for enforcement. In this article, we will focus on using the circular economy in the agricultural sector, since the circular economy in agriculture is one of the most powerful tools for reducing greenhouse-gas emissions, preventing soil and water pollution, and creating new sources of income from agricultural by-products.

title: Coalition-based energy management of grid-connected smart homes in the day-ahead electricity market
summary: The increasing penetration of residential renewable energy resources (RESs), battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and flexible appliances enables the cooperative operation of smart homes. However, existing peer-to-peer (P2P) and coalitio
content: The increasing penetration of residential renewable energy resources (RESs), battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and flexible appliances enables the cooperative operation of smart homes. However, existing peer-to-peer (P2P) and coalition-based energy management approaches often rely on bi-level formulations, computationally complex market-clearing mechanisms, or game-theoretic approaches, which limit scalability under uncertainty. This paper proposes a scalable coalition-based Energy Management System (EMS) in which inter-household energy exchange capacity is explicitly introduced as a tunable control parameter. This mechanism regulates peer-assisted energy sharing, enabling a trade-off between expected cost reduction for the system and performance metrics such as the peak-to-average ratio (PAR). The problem is formulated as a single-level, two-stage stochastic mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework that optimizes scheduling under uncertainty in renewable generation, electricity prices, and demand, achieving coordinated operation without the computational burden of traditional structures. Simulation results for a four-household coalition demonstrate a 10.5% reduction in total electricity procurement cost relative to an independent no-exchange baseline, increasing to 14.9% during weekdays, mainly driven by the complementary consumption profiles of working and retired residents. A 20-household survey-based case study shows diminishing marginal benefits beyond moderate exchange capacities, indicating that unconstrained exchange between residents does not necessarily improve aggregate load-profile metrics. Finally, scalability tests with up to 200 households demonstrate the computational tractability of the proposed framework for large-scale residential deployment.

title: Current-Aware Adaptive Virtual Inertia Control for a VSM-Controlled Grid-Forming MMC in a Low-Inertia Grid
summary: Abstract The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and converter-interfaced generation reduces the natural mechanical inertia of modern power systems, leading to higher rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), deeper frequency devi
content: Abstract The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and converter-interfaced generation reduces the natural mechanical inertia of modern power systems, leading to higher rate of change of frequency (RoCoF), deeper frequency deviations, and reduced dynamic stability margins following active-power disturbances. Grid-forming (GFM) converters provide an effective means of restoring inertial support by establishing voltage and frequency references and emulating synchronous-machine dynamics. This paper presents a simulation-based adaptive virtual inertia control strategy for a virtualsynchronous-machine (VSM)-controlled modular multilevel converter (MMC) connected to a low-inertia grid. The proposed controller adjusts the virtual inertia according to frequency deviation and RoCoF while incorporating measured converter current as a supervisory variable to coordinate frequency support with converter operating capability. A MATLAB/Simulink model is used to compare grid-following operation, GFM operation with fixed virtual inertia, and GFM operation with adaptive virtual inertia. Under the studied 10 MW active-power disturbance, the adaptive-inertia strategy reduces the maximum RoCoF from 3.0 Hz/s to 1.5 Hz/s relative to fixed-inertia GFM operation and improves the frequency nadir from 49.994 Hz to 49.997 Hz while maintaining the same reported settling time of 0.100 s. The assessment is further extended using the electricalresponse results of the developed model under higher active-power disturbances, including converter-current magnitude, DClink voltage, frequency response, RoCoF, and virtual-inertia variation. For the most severe investigated case, the results show that adaptive and current-aware operation modifies the inertia demand according to the disturbance severity while maintaining the converter current within the imposed operating range. The current-aware supervisory action also provides improved coordination between the adaptive inertia command and the converter electrical response, particularly in terms of DC-link and inertia behavior. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed VSM-based adaptive inertia framework improves lowinertia frequency response while providing a practical means of coordinating dynamic inertia support with converter electrical constraints in GFM-MMC systems.

title: Beyond Growth: The Role of Corruption Control in Alleviating Energy Poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Despite economic growth, sub-Saharan Africa continues to experience energy poverty, threatening lives and livelihoods. While the literature predicts that rising incomes translate into improved energy outcomes, this relationship remains puzz
content: Despite economic growth, sub-Saharan Africa continues to experience energy poverty, threatening lives and livelihoods. While the literature predicts that rising incomes translate into improved energy outcomes, this relationship remains puzzling in much of the region. What helps explain this puzzle? This study examines the role of control of corruption in explaining why economic growth alone often fails to deliver meaningful energy poverty reductions. Using Instrumental Variable Generalized Method of Moments with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors for a 45-country panel, we find that corruption control plays a critical moderating role: economic growth contributes more effectively to improvements in clean cooking access, electricity access, and renewable energy consumption when corruption is better controlled in the region. Disaggregating the analysis by income reveals that in low-income countries, corruption control is a key condition that enables growth to translate into clean cooking access and broader energy development. In lower-middle-income countries, it redirects growth primarily toward electricity expansion, whereas in upper-middle- and high-income countries, it strengthens broader energy development. As noted by the Executive Director of the International Energy Agency, Dr Fatih Birol, existing technologies and investment go a long way in solving energy poverty, but our results show that how these resources are governed matter.

title: Fluidized Bed Cathodes Enable High-Rate CO2 to Formate Production and In Situ Microbial Growth
summary: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Reaction (eCO2RR) to formate offers a sustainable and promising route for storing renewable electricity in a microbial energy substrate. Conventional CO2 electrolyzers rely on flat electrodes with limited catal
content: Electrochemical CO2 Reduction Reaction (eCO2RR) to formate offers a sustainable and promising route for storing renewable electricity in a microbial energy substrate. Conventional CO2 electrolyzers rely on flat electrodes with limited catalytic surface area, mass-transfer constraints, and electrolytes that are incompatible with microbial growth, preventing direct coupling of electrochemical formate production with biological conversion. Here, we developed a biocompatible CO2 electrolysis configuration that uses fluidized particles of Sn, Bi, and In as electrocatalysts to enhance CO2 to formate conversion while supporting microbial utilization in the same chamber. The fluidized configuration enabled high formate production rates up to 0.24 mmol cm2 with Faradaic efficiencies of 86 to 92%, representing a two fold improvement over static electrodes. The system also achieved a carbon conversion efficiency of 42%, approaching the theoretical limit for co-generation of formate and bicarbonate. Importantly, electrolysis was performed in a biocompatible medium that supported direct in situ cultivation of Cupriavidus necator within the cathode chamber using only electricity and CO2/O2 as fed substrates. C. necator continuously consumed electro-generated formate for 5 to 6 days under aerobic conditions, demonstrating integrated CO2 to biomass conversion. This work establishes a fluidized electrocatalytic platform for simultaneous electrosynthesis and microbial upgrading in a single reactor, providing a scalable strategy for renewable carbon fixation and sustainable biomanufacturing.

title: Beyond cost and sustainability: a strategic value creation framework for mobility investments in SMEs
summary: Purpose The purpose and goals of the proposed research are to design and demonstrate a strategic decision-support system for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) evaluating investments in sustainable mobility under conditions of uncer
content: Purpose The purpose and goals of the proposed research are to design and demonstrate a strategic decision-support system for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) evaluating investments in sustainable mobility under conditions of uncertainty. While the emphasis of existing studies primarily lies on vehicle attractiveness and technical capabilities, the proposed study will adopt a strategic management approach, highlighting the value-creation potential of electric mobility, especially in combination with renewable energy production within the local environment, in uncertain circumstances. Design/methodology/approach The proposed framework is based on the fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making approach, which is based on the Fuzzy Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution (Fuzzy TOPSIS) approach. A Strategic Value Creation Index is proposed, which is fuzzy in nature and acts as a fuzzy economic indicator of the value-creating potential of sustainable mobility solutions that cannot be measured using economic parameters such as cost and performance. The framework integrates economic, environmental, and energy-related criteria. It is applied to an illustrative case study involving an SME evaluating alternative sustainable mobility investment options, including electric vehicles with and without photovoltaic energy support. Fuzzy logic is employed to represent uncertainty related to future energy prices, self-consumption levels, and policy incentives, enabling the realistic and flexible assessment of strategic trade-offs. Findings The illustrative application shows how incorporating strategic value creation can influence the relative evaluation of mobility investment alternatives. The proposed solution, which combines electric vehicles and solar energy systems, outperforms other solutions not only in terms of sustainability and cost-effectiveness but also in terms of creating additional value in relation to energy independence, cost predictability, and immunity to market fluctuations in the energy sector. The illustrative results suggest that evaluations based solely on cost efficiency and environmental considerations may overlook strategic opportunities associated with sustainable mobility solutions. The proposed approach illustrates how fuzzy-based value modelling can support strategic clarity in uncertain and dynamic decision-making contexts. Originality/value This research contributes to strategic management literature by shifting the evaluation of sustainable mobility from an efficiency-oriented perspective to a value creation-driven decision framework. The novelty of the current research lies in the development of a strategic value indicator based on fuzziness, which will help realise the concept of value creation in case of uncertainty. This will contribute to the gap present in current approaches to decision support, which do not consider strategic economic considerations. The integration of sustainable mobility deci

title: Navigating multipolarity: India–China relations and the reconfiguration of global and regional order in South Asia
summary: This paper examines how India and China are reconfiguring global and regional order through three interconnected objectives: the changing nature of global order and its influence on India and China as rising powers, the pragmatic cooperatio
content: This paper examines how India and China are reconfiguring global and regional order through three interconnected objectives: the changing nature of global order and its influence on India and China as rising powers, the pragmatic cooperation between the two nations under balance-of-power politics, and their competing roles in reshaping the regional order in South Asia. The analysis adopts a mixed-methods design combining qualitative process-tracing of reports, summit declarations, and policy texts with quantitative analysis of UN Comtrade bilateral trade flow data (2013–2024) from China and India to five South Asian economies. Results indicate that China outpaced India regionally, expanding its share of bilateral trade flows over the study period, with projections indicating a lead of USD 6 to 15 billion by 2030. Aggregate figures conceal substantial heterogeneity: Bangladesh remains locked into Chinese dominance, Nepal has deepened its India orientation, and the Maldives and Sri Lanka qualify as genuinely contested markets. The Sri Lankan case complicates prevailing narratives of Chinese economic dominance, with India’s trade flows reaching USD 6.37 billion against China’s USD 3.75 billion during the 2021–2022 sovereign crisis. The paper argues that navigated multipolarity, characterized by soft-balanced coexistence between rivals and politically contingent regional advantages, has become the defining condition of contemporary international relations in South Asia.

title: Efficient Battery Charging with BMS
summary: Effective energy management is essential in modern power electronics applications to maximize performance and ensure dependability. This research proposes a novel method of integrating a battery management system (BMS) with thyristor firing
content: Effective energy management is essential in modern power electronics applications to maximize performance and ensure dependability. This research proposes a novel method of integrating a battery management system (BMS) with thyristor firing angle control (TFAC) to enhance the functionality and efficiency of power electronic systems. TFAC is commonly used for power flow control and voltage regulation in power converters, motor drives, and renewable energy systems. However, traditional TFAC systems often lack flexibility to adapt to dynamic load changes and optimize energy usage. By integrating TFAC with BMS, the proposed system utilizes the BMS’s real-time monitoring and control features to dynamically adjust the thyristors’ firing angle in response to load demand, system constraints, and battery state-of-charge (SoC). This approach ensures optimal use of battery resources while maintaining stable system performance. Additionally, the system leverages BMS data for predictive maintenance and protective functions, enhancing fault tolerance and reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the integrated TFAC-BMS system improves energy efficiency, system performance, and reliability in various power electronics applications. Overall, the proposed strategy offers a practical solution for advancing energy management in power electronics, 346 facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources, and supporting overall system sustainability.

title: Cross‐Component Coupling in Rechargeable Zinc‐Air Batteries: From Reaction Competition to Device Reversibility
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of renewable energy and electrified systems is increasing the demand for safe, low‐cost, and resource‐sustainable energy storage. Rechargeable zinc‐air batteries are promising because they combine abundant Zn, a
content: ABSTRACT The rapid expansion of renewable energy and electrified systems is increasing the demand for safe, low‐cost, and resource‐sustainable energy storage. Rechargeable zinc‐air batteries are promising because they combine abundant Zn, aqueous electrolytes, and an air‐fed oxygen electrode, yet their long‐term reversibility is constrained by coupled oxygen reactions, Zn chemistry, species transport, interfacial evolution, and finite material inventories. This review develops an operating‐state‐resolved framework linking reaction‐pathway competition during discharge, charge, and rest with shared‐electrolyte transport, electrode reversibility, cross‐component coupling, inventory retention, and device reversibility. An evidence hierarchy distinguishes direct operando or component‐resolved observations from correlation, mechanistic inference, and cross‐system analogy, while practical evaluation is considered under explicit load, Zn utilization, electrolyte inventory, gas environment, cumulative output, maintenance, and failure boundaries. These elements are further integrated into reaction‐selectivity‐oriented cross‐component co‐design. The resulting framework specifies the evidence needed to attribute failure, compares cycling claims within declared load and inventory boundaries, and identifies conditions under which air‐electrode, electrolyte, and Zn‐interface modifications can remain compatible.

title: Water Footprint and Scarcity Risks of Low-Carbon Fuels
summary: Abstract Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly u
content: Abstract Production of ammonia, methanol, and hydrogen is key to decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors but is also water-intensive. However, the water implications of scaling these energy carriers under low-carbon pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we integrate direct water consumption with facility-level geospatial analysis and hydrological modeling to quantify water-scarcity exposure across each production facility in North America. Low-carbon production routes require more direct and indirect water consumption than conventional pathways, with electrolytic hydrogen and e-methanol increasing water-intensity by up to 5-fold in regions with limited renewable availability─a trade-off further amplified by supply chain effects, particularly for solar PV-based electricity and direct air capture-based CO2 feedstocks. Water scarcity already affects about 58% of methanol production in Mexico, 2% of ammonia production in the U.S., and 5% and 27% of refinery production in the U.S. and Mexico, respectively. Under midcentury climate scenarios, exposure increases in both magnitude and spatial extent. Although irrigation accounts for over 80% of local water consumption in various fuel production facilities, municipalities and manufacturing often exert the greatest pressure on low-carbon fuel production, depending on the product and country.. These results demonstrate that technology choice, system design, and facility siting are as important as hydrology considerations in determining water risks. Incorporating water availability in low-carbon fuel projects is therefore essential to ensure that decarbonization pathways are scalable, operationally resilient, and truly sustainable.

title: A scenario-based stochastic MPC framework for coordinated HVAC and battery control in residential buildings
source: Building Services Engineering Research and Technology
summary: Maintaining thermal comfort while reducing residential energy costs is challenging under uncertain weather conditions and increasing renewable energy penetration. This paper proposes a scenario-based stochastic Model Predictive Control (MPC
content: Maintaining thermal comfort while reducing residential energy costs is challenging under uncertain weather conditions and increasing renewable energy penetration. This paper proposes a scenario-based stochastic Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework for the coordinated operation of HVAC systems and battery energy storage. A validated 2R2C thermal model is integrated into the optimization process and calibrated using EnergyPlus simulations and measured residential data. Forecast uncertainty in ambient temperature and solar irradiance is represented through Monte Carlo scenario generation and scenario reduction. The controller minimizes electricity costs while enforcing thermal comfort constraints derived from ASHRAE Standard 55. Performance is evaluated across five Mediterranean climates using benchmark comparisons, ablation studies, robustness testing, and uncertainty quantification. Results show annual electricity cost reductions of 14–20% compared with conventional control strategies while maintaining comfort violations below 2%. Additional analyses demonstrate robust performance under extreme weather conditions and confirm the effectiveness of combining stochastic optimization, thermal modeling, and battery storage for residential energy flexibility. Practical Application This study provides building engineers and energy managers with a practical framework for coordinating residential HVAC systems, photovoltaic generation, and battery storage under uncertain weather conditions. Across five Mediterranean climates, the proposed controller achieves 14–20% annual electricity cost savings compared with conventional control, while keeping thermal comfort violations below 2%. Its reduced-order thermal model and scenario reduction approach support computationally efficient implementation in residential energy management systems. Practical deployment requires building-specific calibration, periodic forecast updates, and appropriate fallback controls to maintain safe and reliable operation.

title: Transmission Development in the Philippines, 2026-2050: Demand Growth, Renewable Energy Integration, and Grid Modernization
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Increasing electricity demand, renewable energy expansion, and transmission reliability requirements present significant challenges to long-term power system development in the Philippines. This study examined the National Grid Corporation
content: Increasing electricity demand, renewable energy expansion, and transmission reliability requirements present significant challenges to long-term power system development in the Philippines. This study examined the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines Transmission Development Plan 2026–2050, focusing on demand projections, infrastructure expansion, renewable energy integration, grid modernization, and asset management. A descriptive documentary-analysis design was employed using the plan's executive summary and Chapters 1–10 as primary data sources. Information was examined through structured document review, descriptive comparisons, and thematic analysis covering the Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao grids. Findings indicated that national peak electricity demand was projected to increase from 19,852 MW in 2026 to 81,151 MW by 2050, requiring substantial transmission development. Major priorities included high-voltage backbone reinforcement, substation expansion, inter-island interconnections, battery energy storage systems, digital substations, and advanced monitoring technologies. The plan also identified ₱83.383 billion in projected operations and maintenance capital expenditures, including ₱53.617 billion for the Substation Reliability Program. Implementation considerations included regulatory requirements, right-of-way acquisition, project scheduling, and coordination with generation development. The study concluded that coordinated infrastructure expansion, technological modernization, and lifecycle-based asset management were central to long-term transmission planning. Prioritizing timely implementation, operational flexibility, systematic maintenance, and continued performance evaluation was recommended to support transmission reliability and renewable energy integration. However, the anticipated benefits remained dependent on project implementation and changing system conditions.

title: Bio-electrochemical swarm intelligence with quantum constrained graph learning for distributed battery optimization in urban microgrids
summary: The integration of distributed battery storage in urban microgrids is becoming increasingly common. Yet, most existing methods for optimizing urban microgrid operation are incapable of jointly representing battery physics, device-to-device
content: The integration of distributed battery storage in urban microgrids is becoming increasingly common. Yet, most existing methods for optimizing urban microgrid operation are incapable of jointly representing battery physics, device-to-device relationships, and the temporal variability of intermittent renewable generation. Conventional swarm and deterministic methods also commonly rely on random initialization, homogeneous agent behavior, or post-hoc constraint handling. Therefore, this research proposes a unifying framework that integrates five key components into a single pipeline: (1) Bio-Electrochemical Swarm Field Initialization (BESFI); (2) Adaptive Multi-Species Co-Evolutionary Swarm Routing (AMSCESR); (3) a Spatio-Temporal Energy Diffusion Graph Transformer (STED-GT); (4) Quantum-Inspired Stability-Constrained Optimization (QISCO); and (5) a Digital Twin Reinforcement Validation Engine (DT-RVE). The novelty lies in the closed coupling of physics-aware initialization, role-diverse swarm search, relational graph learning, in-loop stability filtering, and digital-twin reinforcement validation rather than in any isolated module. On the reported 25-node urban microgrid testbed, the framework achieved 95.8% dispatch accuracy, 94.6% energy efficiency, ± 3.7% voltage deviation, ± 0.019 Hz frequency deviation, 10.6% capacity fade, and 2.3 s supervisory adaptation latency. These results indicate improved load balancing, grid stability, battery-life preservation, and adaptive operation within the evaluated simulation conditions.

title: Dynamic power quality enhancement in renewable grid with interleaved active clamp converter powered unified power flow controller
summary: Introduction. The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, particularly photovoltaic (PV) systems, has significantly influenced modern power systems by promoting sustainable energy generation. However, large-scale PV penetration
content: Introduction. The increasing integration of renewable energy sources, particularly photovoltaic (PV) systems, has significantly influenced modern power systems by promoting sustainable energy generation. However, large-scale PV penetration introduces operational challenges such as voltage instability, uncontrolled power flow, and deterioration of power quality (PQ). Variations in solar irradiance and partial shading conditions further complicate stable grid operation, requiring advanced converter technologies and intelligent control strategies to ensure reliable PV grid integration. Problem. To improve voltage regulation, power flow management, and PQ in grid-connected PV systems while maintaining efficient maximum power extraction under dynamic operating conditions. Goal. To develop a decoupled neural network (DNN)-based control strategy for a closed-loop unified power flow controller (UPFC) integrated with an interleaved active clamp boost (IACB) converter and coyote optimization algorithm – radial basis function neural network – maximum power point tracking (COA-RBFNN MPPT) to improve power flow regulation, voltage stability and PQ under dynamic renewable grid conditions. Methodology. For independent active and reactive power regulation, the system combines a UPFC with shunt and series converters. An IACB converter offers high voltage gain while reducing ripple and switching losses. A hybrid COA-RBFNN MPPT approach allows accurate tracking even in partial shade. An LC filter is used to reduce harmonics, and grid synchronization is improved via DNN control using decoupled double synchronous reference frame-based pulse width modulation. Results. MATLAB simulation results confirm steady operation and increased PQ with 96 % overall converter efficiency, 98.9 % MPPT tracking efficiency, and 1.52 % total harmonic distortion. Scientific novelty. Combination of hybrid intelligent MPPT, a high-gain IACB converter, and UPFC-based grid control for improved PV system performance. Practical value. The proposed work enhances energy efficiency, PQ, and grid reliability, which allows it for advanced renewable energy integration and smart grid applications. References 29, tables 1, figures 25.

title: The Strait of Hormuz Crisis: Resilience in Indian Energy Sector and Geopolitical Rivalries
source: The Paradigm Chronicle Journal of Academic Inquiry and Critical Thought
summary: India, an emerging economy, is a highly energy-intensive economy. The dearth of access to viable domestic sources of crude oil and natural gas to meet the domestic energy demand has forced India to rely excessively on the international mark
content: India, an emerging economy, is a highly energy-intensive economy. The dearth of access to viable domestic sources of crude oil and natural gas to meet the domestic energy demand has forced India to rely excessively on the international markets for the supply of the fuel. This dependence on the international markets has had serious vulnerabilities which were revealed during the recent geopolitical turmoil. India’s heavy reliance on Russia for crude oil imports was the first setback since late 2025 due to the increased US sanctions on Russia over its war in Ukraine. This has led India to depend more on the Arabian Peninsula for maintaining its supply of crude oil and natural gas. The supply from this region then got disrupted due to the 2026 Iran war, between Iran, US and Israel over Iran’s alleged development of nuclear weapons. In response to the US and Israel air strikes, Iran has blockaded the Hormuz Strait. Over 45% of the crude oil and 60% of the total natural gas imports by India pass through the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade has created a shortage of supply of both crude oil and natural gas across the globe, driving fuel inflation to double digits. Globalisation of the contemporary era has led to a deeper integration of the economies of the world leading to the adverse spillover effects also to be distributed all across the globe. The stability in the wider neighbourhood of India and access to alternative sources of fuel becomes imperative to India which aspires to become a developed economy by 2047, as stated in the policy of ‘Viksit Bharat.’ India’s push for renewable energy has a dual purpose of both environmental protection and to insulate India’s energy sector from the volatile geo-political conditions of the world, specifically West Asia. This research paper aims to study the supply disruptions, especially crude oil and natural gas, that India has faced owing to the blockade of the Hormuz Strait by Iran. Upon analysis, this research aims to provide feasible solutions that Indian policy makers can adopt both in the short term and in the long term to account for the risks associated with the import of fuel such as crude oil and natural gas.

title: Dynamic Business Impact Analysis and Dependency-Aware Recovery Optimization for Mission-Critical Banking Operations
summary: Abstract This study develops a Dynamic Business Impact Analysis and Dependency-Aware Recovery Optimization framework for mission-critical banking operations. The objective is to assess time-dependent service impact, model cascading disrupti
content: Abstract This study develops a Dynamic Business Impact Analysis and Dependency-Aware Recovery Optimization framework for mission-critical banking operations. The objective is to assess time-dependent service impact, model cascading disruption across interconnected banking resources, and prioritize recovery actions under constrained technical, financial, and human resources. The methodology combines operational and incident data preparation, multilayer dependency-network modeling, scenario-based simulation, dynamic impact scoring, and multi-criteria recovery optimization using service impact, customer exposure, financial loss, RTO breach, RPO breach, and recovery cost. Evaluation covers core account services, payment processing, online banking, ATM and card services, customer authentication, and fraud monitoring across cyber, infrastructure, communication, payment-network, and third-party disruption scenarios. Compared with criticality-only, shortest-recovery-time, and static business impact analysis baselines, the proposed method reduced mean recovery time to 4.6 hours and cumulative impact to 0.47, while increasing RTO compliance to 82.9% and RPO compliance to 88.6%. The findings show that dependency-aware, time-sensitive recovery prioritization provides more reliable system-level decisions than fixed service rankings. The framework supports resilience testing, impact-tolerance assessment, incident command, recovery planning, and investment decisions for banking infrastructure.

title: A load-coupled DMDc method for long-term aerodynamic load prediction in controlled fluid–structure interaction systems
summary: Abstract In controlled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) systems, nonlinear coupling between fluid loads and structural motion complicates reduced-order modeling and limits aerodynamic load prediction accuracy under different control inputs
content: Abstract In controlled fluid–structure interaction (FSI) systems, nonlinear coupling between fluid loads and structural motion complicates reduced-order modeling and limits aerodynamic load prediction accuracy under different control inputs. To address the limited ability of dynamic mode decomposition with control (DMDc) to capture nonlinear dynamics, this study proposes a loadcoupled DMDc (LC-DMDc) method that incorporates nonlinear load effects into state evolution. The method combines proper orthogonal decomposition of the flow, structural motion, and interface loads with a radial basis function mapping, so that the predicted load coefficients provide nonlinear corrections to DMDc state evolution. The resulting model preserves displacement– velocity kinematic relations and is jointly optimized using multistep state and aerodynamic load prediction errors to improve long-term prediction accuracy. For a piezoelectrically actuated flatplate airfoil, models are trained on frequency-sweep data from high-fidelity FSI simulations and evaluated against standard DMDc and three representative methods under frequency-sweep, sinusoidal inputs with piecewise-constant frequencies, multisine, and step excitations. Over continuous predictions spanning 140 s, aerodynamic force and moment errors relative to highfidelity simulations do not exceed 7.33%, and wingtip displacement errors remain within 1.25% across all four cases. Compared with the best-performing baseline for each case and response component, LC-DMDc achieves error reductions of up to 75.1%. The method improves the accuracy of long-term aerodynamic load predictions and supports rapid response prediction and control-oriented modeling for controlled FSI systems.

title: Plant Microbial Fuel Cells for Sustainable source of bioelectricity Generation
source: Journal of Energy and Environmental Sustainability
summary: The growing population is responsible for energy consumption all over the world resulting in the depletion of the fossil fuel reservoir. In recent decades out of many techniques, Microbial fuel cell (MFC) have served as three stop solution
content: The growing population is responsible for energy consumption all over the world resulting in the depletion of the fossil fuel reservoir. In recent decades out of many techniques, Microbial fuel cell (MFC) have served as three stop solution for electricity production, reducing global warming, producing value added products while simultaneously remediating wastewater. However, MFCs have certain limitation in terms of upscaling mainly due to exhaustion of organic matter at anode. The plant microbial fuel cell (P-MFC) having plants rooted at anode are reliable when it comes to continuous supply of organic matter at anode and thus are considered as a potential and sustainable source of green energy. Here, the solar energy gets converted into bioelectricity via electrochemical reactions in the roots of plant, at the anode separated by cathode chamber of the microbial fuel cell. The P-MFC provides clean and renewable energy, is eco-friendly and cost-effective. The P-MFC also produces, bio-methane, biohydrogen as by products, besides the products produced by plant itself. It is one of the emerging techniques for bioenergy, and also facing just like other microbial fuel cell based techniques challenge to increase the power density as well its long-term performance on commercial scale. This review discusses briefly about conventional MFC and elaborates plant-microbe consortium at rhizosphere region of a plant, for wide scope production of bioelectricity from P-MFC. Additionally, the parameters influencing P-MFC efficiency, the mechanism involved and challenges have also been narrated.

title: Malaysia National Energy Transition from the Oil Palm Sector
source: Malaysian Journal of Science and Advanced Technology
summary: The Malaysian government launched the National Energy Policy 2022–2040 on 19 September 2022 to enhance macroeconomic resilience and energy security, promote social equity and affordability, and foster environmental sustainability. The trans
content: The Malaysian government launched the National Energy Policy 2022–2040 on 19 September 2022 to enhance macroeconomic resilience and energy security, promote social equity and affordability, and foster environmental sustainability. The transformation of the energy sector is being carried out within the context of a global energy transition aimed at achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. The potential contribution from the oil palm sector in the energy transition was reviewed. Although renewable energy derived from various oil palm by-products presents no food-fuel conflicts, it remains unscalable due to limitations in planting areas. Treatments of palm biomass could improve fuel properties and marketability. The overall fatty acids methyl esters esterification reaction tends to follow a second-order rate with respect to free fatty acids. Anaerobic digestion of palm oil mill effluent produces biogas. Depending on the available feedstock, processes such as Fischer-Tropsch or hydrotreated esters and fatty acids could generate sustainable aviation fuel. The palm oil industrial premises also offer substantial space for clean solar photovoltaic energy on their rooftops. The energy transition from the oil palm sector requires a comprehensive and collaborative approach that involves all stakeholders.

title: Improve of power system oscillation detection accuracy based on optimal sampling rate for data-driven real-time
summary: Introduction. The rapid integration of renewable energy sources and inverter-based resources has increased the complexity of modern power systems, leading to higher risks of instability and low-frequency oscillations. Problem. While data-dr
content: Introduction. The rapid integration of renewable energy sources and inverter-based resources has increased the complexity of modern power systems, leading to higher risks of instability and low-frequency oscillations. Problem. While data-driven analysis using real-time measurements offers better adaptability than model-based methods, the use of high-resolution data leads to an exponential increase in analysis time, which hinders the effectiveness of real-time monitoring and rapid response. Goal. To improve power system oscillation detection accuracy. This goal is achieved on the basis of the developed method to determine the optimal sampling rate for real-time oscillation detection by performing a comparative performance evaluation of three major algorithms: Prony, MPM (Matrix Pencil Method), and HTLS (Hankel Total Least Squares). Methodology. To establish the optimal balance for highly accurate real-time applications, the study analyzed detection accuracy (frequency and damping ratio) and CPU execution time by varying sampling rates using simulated data from the IEEE 39-bus system and actual field measurement data from PMUs. Results. The analysis confirmed that highly accurate oscillation mode identification is successfully achieved at optimal sampling rates of 15 sps (samples per second) for real-world data and 5 sps for simulation data. The results demonstrated that while detection capabilities generally improve with higher rates, applying these specific optimal thresholds effectively suppresses noise and strictly balances the crucial trade-off between rigorous estimation accuracy and real-time processing speed. Scientific novelty. The research systematically demonstrates how optimizing the non-linear trade-off between sampling density and computational overhead directly enhances oscillation detection accuracy. By quantifying this relationship for Prony, MPM and HTLS algorithms, it establishes a novel boundary condition that guarantees highly accurate and reliable real-time applicability. Practical value. The providing technical guidelines for power system engineers to improve oscillation detection accuracy in wide-area monitoring systems. By applying the proposed optimal sampling rates, engineers can maximize detection fidelity and prevent false assessments without violating real-time constraints. References 21, tables 12, figures 8.

title: Enhancing water security: a review of water quality and treatment technologies for remote Australian communities
summary: Abstract Access to safe and reliable water is fundamental to human health and well-being and to achieving United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6. Yet many remote Australian communities, including First Nations communities, face chall
content: Abstract Access to safe and reliable water is fundamental to human health and well-being and to achieving United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6. Yet many remote Australian communities, including First Nations communities, face challenges in securing drinking water. Supplies do not consistently meet the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines, with adverse public-health and socio-economic consequences. Using a targeted literature search and narrative synthesis, this review integrates peer-reviewed literature, Australian government and utility reports, and technical case studies on drinking-water quality and decentralised treatment in remote Australia. Sources were selected for contextual relevance and analysed according to field performance, technology readiness, operational requirements and whole-of-life sustainability consideration. The review examines water-quality challenges and evaluates established and emerging treatment technologies for remote settings. Conventional approaches, including disinfection, filtration and desalination, provide proven treatment functions but may be constrained by isolation, harsh environmental conditions, ageing infrastructure and limited operation and maintenance capacity. Emerging technologies, including electrochemical processes, forward osmosis and membrane distillation, may offer context-specific advantages but lack long-term validation in remote Australian communities. A technology assessment framework guides selection of robust, adaptable and scalable solutions. The findings emphasise sustained community engagement, responsible resource stewardship, performance monitoring and maintenance, effective brine management and demonstrated technology readiness. Research and implementation priorities include emerging-technology field validation, advanced real-time monitoring, renewable-energy integration, and fit-for-purpose governance and investment models aligned with community priorities, institutional capacity, regulatory requirements and whole-of-life service delivery. These priorities would strengthen the reliability, resilience and long-term sustainability of remote drinking-water services.
