title: MAPEAMENTO DA PRODUÇÃO CIENTÍFICA: UMA ANÁLISE DA ÚLTIMA DÉCADA NOS ANAIS DO ENEGEP SOBRE A DESCARBONIZAÇÃO
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A descarbonização tornou-se uma temática estratégica para a Engenharia de Produção diante das metas globais de neutralidade de carbono estabelecidas pelo Acordo de Paris e pela Agenda 2030.Nesse contexto, cidades inteligentes, transição ene
content: A descarbonização tornou-se uma temática estratégica para a Engenharia de Produção diante das metas globais de neutralidade de carbono estabelecidas pelo Acordo de Paris e pela Agenda 2030.Nesse contexto, cidades inteligentes, transição energética e tecnologias da Indústria 4.0 passaram a integrar as discussões sobre sustentabilidade e redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa.Assim, este estudo tem como objetivo analisar como a literatura científica publicada nos anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção (ENEGEP), entre 2016 e 2025, abordaram a descarbonização no desenvolvimento de cidades inteligentes.A pesquisa é do tipo quantitativa e exploratória, utilizando análise bibliométrica e mapeamento científico.Foram analisados 32 artigos selecionados a partir das palavras-chave "descarbonização", "carbono zero" e "cidades inteligentes".O software VOSviewer foi utilizado para análise de clusters e evolução temporal, enquanto o IRaMuTeQ para análise qualitativa dos estudos.Os resultados demonstram crescimento das publicações a partir de 2021, com predominância da área de Engenharia da Sustentabilidade.A descarbonização aparece associada principalmente ao hidrogênio verde, energias renováveis, mobilidade sustentável e cidades inteligentes.Foram identificadas relações entre sustentabilidade e tecnologias digitais, como IoT, inteligência artificial, smart grids e big data, utilizadas para ampliar a eficiência energética e operacional com foco na descarbonização de sistemas industriais e urbanos.

title: Equivalent Energy Storage Characterization and Co-Optimization of Flexible Data Center Workloads Under High Penetration of Wind and Solar Power
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: [Objective] Driven by dual-carbon goals and an 80% green electricity requirement， data centers are transitioning from passive loads to flexible resources. However， a unified framework is still lacking to characterize the impact of flexible
content: [Objective] Driven by dual-carbon goals and an 80% green electricity requirement， data centers are transitioning from passive loads to flexible resources. However， a unified framework is still lacking to characterize the impact of flexible computing workloads on system planning and operation， as well as to quantitatively compare them with physical energy storage. This study develops an equivalent energy storage characterization method for flexible workloads to quantify their value in renewable energy accommodation and system regulation. [Methods] An integrated planning and operation optimization model for a data center-power grid-energy storage system is formulated across 8760 h of a year. Aiming to minimize the annualized total cost， the model jointly optimizes wind， photovoltaic， and energy storage capacities alongside workload shifting， subject to constraints on green electricity share， power balance， and workload service requirements. Furthermore， a renewable-energy-accommodation equivalent energy storage metric is proposed to evaluate the substitution effect of flexible computing workloads for physical energy storage in terms of equivalent capacity and unit economic value. [Results] For a data center with a maximum load of 0.36 MW， under a 1 h flexibility window and a 2 h storage benchmark， increasing the flexible workload share from 0% to 40% yields an equivalent storage capacity of 0.13 MWh with a unit value of 142 600 yuan/MWh. When the flexible workload share reaches 100%， the equivalent capacity increases to 0.21 MWh， while its unit value decreases to 126 700 yuan/MWh， indicating diminishing marginal returns. Sensitivity analysis reveals that reducing delay compensation and widening the flexibility window can enhance this substitution effect. In terms of storage duration， flexible computing workloads tend to substitute for long-duration energy storage at the system level. [Conclusions] The proposed metric provides a unified energy and economic basis for evaluating flexible loads against physical energy storage. It supports coordinated generation-load-storage planning and flexibility valuation for data centers under high wind and solar penetration.

title: METODOLOGIAS ÁGEIS NA TRANSIÇÃO ENERGÉTICA: CONTRIBUIÇÕES PARA A SUSTENTABILIDADE E A DESCARBONIZAÇÃO NO SETOR DE ENERGIA LIMPA
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A transição energética é o processo de substituição gradual das fontes fósseis por renováveis, como solar e eólica, visando reduzir emissões e construir um sistema mais eficiente e de baixo carbono (EPE, 2024; IEA, 2023).Tal transição é ess
content: A transição energética é o processo de substituição gradual das fontes fósseis por renováveis, como solar e eólica, visando reduzir emissões e construir um sistema mais eficiente e de baixo carbono (EPE, 2024; IEA, 2023).Tal transição é essencial para enfrentar os impactos climáticos e garantir segurança energética e a sustentabilidade, a qual consiste em atender às necessidades atuais sem comprometer as futuras, equilibrando aspectos ambientais, sociais e econômicos (USP, 2023; Artaxo, 2022).No setor energético, isso significa reduzir desperdícios, aumentar a eficiência e respeitar limites ecológicos (Siemens Energy, 2023).A integração entre agilidade e práticas sustentáveis surge como estratégia para otimizar processos e reduzir desperdícios (Epitaya, 2023).As metodologias ágeis, criadas para a indústria de software, promovem colaboração, adaptação contínua e entrega incremental.Sua aplicação em energia renovável representa oportunidade para superar barreiras tradicionais e impulsionar práticas alinhadas à sustentabilidade.Empresas como Schneider Electric e Siemens Energy já demonstraram ganhos com frameworks ágeis, como maior engajamento, rapidez na entrega e eficiência energética (BCG, 2023; Siemens Energy, 2023).Nesse contexto, esta pesquisa tem por objetivo verificar como a aplicação de metodologias ágeis contribui para acelerar a transição energética e promover sustentabilidade e descarbonização no setor de energia limpa.Estudos indicam que unir metodologias ágeis e princípios sustentáveis gera sinergias como redução de desperdícios, melhoria contínua e maior capacidade de resposta às mudanças regulatórias.No setor renovável, frameworks como Scrum, Kanban e Lean têm sido adaptados para projetos de turbinas eólicas e sistemas fotovoltaicos, reorganizando a cadeia de valor e promovendo descarbonização (Springer Link, 2023).2. Metodologia Para compreender como as metodologias ágeis estão transformando o setor de energia limpa, optou-se por uma abordagem de pesquisa qualitativa, que permite captar percepções, experiências e significados atribuídos pelos atores envolvidos, oferecendo uma compreensão mais profunda das práticas organizacionais e dos processos de inovação em contextos reais, o que seria limitado por abordagens exclusivamente quantitativas.Este estudo caracteriza-se como uma pesquisa exploratória e descritiva.É exploratória por investigar um campo emergente, a integração entre agilidade e sustentabilidade no setor energético, onde ainda há lacunas teóricas e práticas a serem preenchidas.

title: Pengaruh Penghindaran Pajak, Kepemilikan Manajerial, dan Komite Audit terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee on firm value for industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The analytical met
content: This study aims to analyze the influence of tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee on firm value for industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The analytical method employed is multiple linear regression, incorporating both simultaneous and partial tests. The results indicate that, simultaneously, tax avoidance, managerial ownership, and the audit committee have a significant influence on firm value. This suggests that these three variables, when considered collectively, are relevant determinants in shaping investor perception of a company's value. However, the partial test results reveal that only managerial ownership has a significant effect on firm value, demonstrating that the alignment of interests between managers and shareholders through equity ownership is a mechanism positively responded to by the market. Conversely, tax avoidance and the audit committee, when examined individually, do not exert a significant influence on firm value within the industrial sector during the observed period. These findings provide insights for corporate management regarding the importance of ownership structure as a signal to investors, as well as the need to evaluate the effectiveness of other corporate governance policies in optimizing firm value.

title: 中文書名 / Chinese Title: 城市能源自主性與極端環境韌性極限 65/90 | PART III | Research Working Edition v1.0 English Title: Urban Energy Autonomy and Extreme-Environment Resilience at the Limit This prospective STARLI research monograph asks whether a scaled district energy system can preserve minimum critical services during prolonged low sunlight, coupled storms, component outages and disconnection from external supply. Its research core couples energy autonomy, extreme-climate stress and resilience engineering. The permitted study systems are unoccupied microgrid hardware-in-the-loop benches, scaled resource components, independently metered control channels and auditable digital twins. It does not claim operational autonomy for a city or safety certification for inhabited infrastructure. The primary falsifiable claim is that a preregistered multi-source energy and priority-load coordination policy can improve net lifecycle energy yield without worsening actual critical-load loss-of-service time relative to competent fixed-rule microgrid dispatch under identical generation, storage, weather, sensor, computation, maintenance, personnel and energy budgets. Hidden imports, curtailed essential demand, oversized storage, unmetered cooling and selective failure exclusion are explicit rival accounts. Blind test assignments include forecast shifts, islanding events, battery thermal drift and correlated low-renewable conditions; physical frequency, thermal and essential-load stops override all average performance gains. The volume follows an exact 777-page working architecture: one cover, 14 research-foundation pages, 30 distinct candidate equation plates, 82 chapter introductions with 410 independent one-page investigations, 200 individual Research Gates, 33 conceptually different Phoenix Answer Embryos and seven research-closure pages. The research program includes port-level energy conservation, usable reserve after aging, Markov transition qualification, islanding survivability, weather dependence, tail-risk metrics, protection interlocks, second-team failure reconstruction and intergenerational maintenance. These are proposed test designs and existing mathematical methods deployed in a new research context, not newly discovered natural laws. Relevant external evidence includes published microgrid-controller hardware-in-the-loop research (DOI 10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), resilience-oriented scheduling with a probability of successful islanding (10.1049/esi2.70034), ice-storm microgrid formation (10.1109/TSG.2025.3611876), microgrid design with climate-informed multiyear uncertainty (10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.123355) and energy-system resilience reviews (10.1016/j.rser.2021.111476). Other references and their exact metadata are recorded in the separate DOI Evidence Register. The two Flagship-13 Zenodo lineage DOIs are author-supplied and remain unverified in this edition; the cited studies do not validate the new F65 integrated design. This document is a Research Working Edition, not an empirical result report or a completed sixfold-QA-certified scientific monograph. Page count, bookmark structure and representative visual output are machine-checked. Recurrent editorial language and incomplete independent formula review remain disclosed limitations; the >100,000 substantively independent English-word scientific-content threshold has not been certified. content: 中文書名 / Chinese Title: 城市能源自主性與極端環境韌性極限65/90 | PART III | Research Working Edition v1.0English Title: Urban Energy Autonomy and Extreme-Environment Resilience at the Limit This prospective STARLI research monograph asks whether a scaled district energy system can preserve minimum critical services during prolonged low sunlight, coupled storms, component outages and disconnection from external supply. Its research core couples energy autonomy, extreme-climate stress and resilience engineering. The permitted study systems are unoccupied microgrid hardware-in-the-loop benches, scaled resource components, independently metered control channels and auditable digital twins. It does not claim operational autonomy for a city or safety certification for inhabited infrastructure. The primary falsifiable claim is that a preregistered multi-source energy and priority-load coordination policy can improve net lifecycle energy yield without worsening actual critical-load loss-of-service time relative to competent fixed-rule microgrid dispatch under identical generation, storage, weather, sensor, computation, maintenance, personnel and energy budgets. Hidden imports, curtailed essential demand, oversized storage, unmetered cooling and selective failure exclusion are explicit rival accounts. Blind test assignments include forecast shifts, islanding events, battery thermal drift and correlated low-renewable conditions; physical frequency, thermal and essential-load stops override all average performance gains. The volume follows an exact 777-page working architecture: one cover, 14 research-foundation pages, 30 distinct candidate equation plates, 82 chapter introductions with 410 independent one-page investigations, 200 individual Research Gates, 33 conceptually different Phoenix Answer Embryos and seven research-closure pages. The research program includes port-level energy conservation, usable reserve after aging, Markov transition qualification, islanding survivability, weather dependence, tail-risk metrics, protection interlocks, second-team failure reconstruction and intergenerational maintenance. These are proposed test designs and existing mathematical methods deployed in a new research context, not newly discovered natural laws. Relevant external evidence includes published microgrid-controller hardware-in-the-loop research (DOI 10.1109/TCST.2024.3378989), resilience-oriented scheduling with a probability of successful islanding (10.1049/esi2.70034), ice-storm microgrid formation (10.1109/TSG.2025.3611876), microgrid design with climate-informed multiyear uncertainty (10.1016/j.apenergy.2024.123355) and energy-system resilience reviews (10.1016/j.rser.2021.111476). Other references and their exact metadata are recorded in the separate DOI Evidence Register. The two Flagship-13 Zenodo lineage DOIs are author-supplied and remain unverified in this edition; the cited studies do not validate the new F65 integrated design. title: NLP-Based Sentiment Analysis And User Satisfaction Evaluation of Solar Energy Monitoring Applications
source: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
summary: The increasing adoption of solar energy systems has created a growing demand for digital applications that help users monitor electricity generation, energy consumption, inverter performance and overall system efficiency. However, the usefu
content: The increasing adoption of solar energy systems has created a growing demand for digital applications that help users monitor electricity generation, energy consumption, inverter performance and overall system efficiency. However, the usefulness of these applications also depends on user experience and satisfaction. Application-store reviews provide valuable information about user opinions and technical difficulties, but analysing large volumes of unstructured feedback manually is challenging. This study presents an NLP-based framework for analysing user reviews and evaluating satisfaction with solar energy monitoring applications. A dataset containing 1,777 reviews collected from five applications was processed using text preprocessing and Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) feature extraction. Four machine learning classifiers, namely Multinomial Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest, were evaluated for sentiment classification. Sentiment labels were derived from numerical user ratings, with 1–2 stars classified as negative, 3 stars as neutral and 4–5 stars as positive. The study also applies keyword-based aspect identification to examine eight application features, including interface usability, real-time monitoring, data accuracy, inverter connectivity, notifications, application performance, compatibility and technical support. A provisional AspectLevel Satisfaction Index (ASI) is used to summarize rating-derived feedback associated with these features. Logistic Regression achieved the highest classification accuracy of 75.84%, while Support Vector Machine obtained the highest macro-averaged F1-score of 56.87%. The findings highlight the potential of NLP techniques to identify user concerns and support improvements in solar energy monitoring applications.

title: Alterations of Hematopoiesis Markers Induced by Exposure to Cobalt-60 or Cesium-137 in albino mice
source: AlQalam Journal of Medical and Applied Sciences
summary: Ionizing radiation from radioactive isotopes such as Cobalt -60(Co-60) and Cesium-137(Cs-137) is widely employed in medical, industrial, and scientific applications; uncontrolled exposure poses a serious hazard to biological systems. This s
content: Ionizing radiation from radioactive isotopes such as Cobalt -60(Co-60) and Cesium-137(Cs-137) is widely employed in medical, industrial, and scientific applications; uncontrolled exposure poses a serious hazard to biological systems. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the time -dependent toxicological effects of Co-60 and Cs-137 gamma radiation on hematopoietic dynamics and cell morphology in male albino mice. Forty- two adult male albino mice were divided randomly into seven equal groups (n = 6): one unirradiated control and six irradiated groups exposed to either Co-60 or Cs-137 for 6,12,24 hours. Hematological parameters, including red blood cell count, Hemoglobin concentration, platelet count, white blood cell counts, and leukocyte differential count, were analyzed alongside cytomorphological evaluations of peripheral blood and bone marrow smears. Platelets have the greatest radio sensitivity, exhibiting severe thrombocytopenia at all intervals, while leukocytes declined rapidly and erythrocytes showed delayed depletion. Blood and bone marrow smears revealed progressive morphological damage over time, transitioning from initial chromatin clumping to widespread stromal aplasia, ghost membrane formation, nuclear pyknosis, and karyorrhexis by 24 hours. High-energy Co-60 induced an earlier onset of cellular toxicity, whereas Cs-137 displayed a brief latent period before converging to equivalent systemic damage. Both Co-60 and Cs-137 induce severe, duration-dependent hematopoietic failure and bone marrow aplasia in male albino mice. While higher-energy Co-60 accelerates the initial onset of myelosuppression, both isotopes result in equivalent late-stage cytopathological destruction, highlighting the critical necessity for rapid therapeutic intervention following acute gamma radiation exposure

title: Features of Assessing and Managing Budget Deficits in the Context of Early Post-War Recovery
summary: Purpose: This paper investigates the effect of managing budget deficits in early post-war recovery. The objectives are to determine the deficit’s structural characteristics and acceptable limits, identify the factors behind it, assess the i
content: Purpose: This paper investigates the effect of managing budget deficits in early post-war recovery. The objectives are to determine the deficit’s structural characteristics and acceptable limits, identify the factors behind it, assess the impact of the deficit, debt burden, and interest payments on real GDP growth, and justify instruments to ensure medium-term fiscal sustainability. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study uses a quantitative design that compares Ukraine’s annual macrofinancial indicators for the pre-war (2015–2021) and war/early recovery (2022–2025) periods. The methodology includes structural and comparative analysis, nonparametric testing (Mann–Whitney U test), and multiple linear regression based on quarterly macrofinancial data for 2022–2025. Research Limitation: The study focuses on the war and early post-war recovery period, providing a methodological basis for further research on fiscal sustainability in transition economies. Findings: The study identified a dramatic structural break in deficit parameters between the pre-war and war periods, supported by statistically significant differences in the distribution of the deficit and primary balance. In the war and initial recovery phase, the regression shows that smaller deficits are significantly associated with faster real GDP growth, while the debt burden exerts an additional damping effect. Practical Implication: Acceptable deficit bounds in recovery should rest not on debt ceilings alone but also on the structure of the primary balance and debt service. Social Implication: These findings can inform a fiscally sustainable post-war recovery policy. Originality/Value: The results can help in setting the parameters of a medium-term budget strategy (the deficit-to-GDP ratio, primary balance, debt-to-GDP ratio and share of interest payments in expenditures) that combines recovery expenditures with fiscal prudence.

title: Da logística ao Supply Chain Management 5.0: proposição de um roadmap de maturidade aplicado ao setor OCTG

summary: A evolução dos paradigmas industriais modificou a forma como as organizações estruturam seus sistemas produtivos, coordenam fluxos materiais e informacionais e desenvolvem práticas de gestão da cadeia de suprimentos.Nesse contexto, este art
content: A evolução dos paradigmas industriais modificou a forma como as organizações estruturam seus sistemas produtivos, coordenam fluxos materiais e informacionais e desenvolvem práticas de gestão da cadeia de suprimentos.Nesse contexto, este artigo tem como objetivo propor e aplicar um roadmap de maturidade em Supply Chain Management (SCM), estruturado a partir da evolução da Indústria 1.0 à Indústria 5.0, para diagnosticar desalinhamentos entre práticas produtivas, práticas gerenciais e práticas de cadeia de suprimentos em uma organização industrial.A pesquisa possui natureza aplicada, abordagem qualitativa e caráter exploratório-descritivo, combinando revisão bibliográfica narrativa estruturada com a proposição de um artefato analítico e sua aplicação em uma empresa multinacional do setor de Oil Country Tubular Goods (OCTG).O roadmap foi organizado em seis dimensões analíticas: base produtiva e organização do trabalho; gestão e tomada de decisão; integração interna e coordenação de processos; gestão de fornecedores e integração da cadeia; visibilidade, dados e digitalização no SCM; e sustentabilidade, resiliência e centralidade humana no SCM.Os resultados evidenciaram que a empresa analisada apresenta base produtiva próxima da Indústria 4.0, porém mantém fragilidades em dimensões associadas à integração com fornecedores, visibilidade externa da cadeia e incorporação dos princípios da Indústria 5.0.Como contribuição, o estudo oferece uma estrutura prática para diagnosticar desalinhamentos de maturidade e orientar ações de nivelamento entre produção, gestão interna e SCM.

title: Thermoacoustic refrigeration systems for sustainable cooling performance configurations challenges and future directions
summary: Thermoacoustic refrigeration (TAR) is a cooling system that practices acoustic energy as an alternative of environmentally hazardous refrigerants to create refrigeration effects. This thorough review explores the extensive body of research
content: Thermoacoustic refrigeration (TAR) is a cooling system that practices acoustic energy as an alternative of environmentally hazardous refrigerants to create refrigeration effects. This thorough review explores the extensive body of research devoted to researching and developing thermoacoustic refrigeration systems with a focus on recent advancements concepts, configurations, performance metrics and practical applications. Detail study of system elements like acoustic networks, quarter-wavelength resonators, looped-tube configurations, flexible resonance tubes, tapered resonators, stacks and regenerators are highlighted. Configuration types such as standing wave, multi-stage looped-tube and traveling wave systems for looped-tube architecture, acoustic matching is thoroughly discussed. A crucial emphasis of the review is the innovative methods for diversified practices of TAR comprises, space and electronics cooling, the liquefaction of liquid natural gas (LNG) with niche applications like remote field production, liquid natural gas satellite facilities, and cold exergy recovery terminals, solar-powered refrigeration, medical, pharmaceutical storage and building heating ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC). Further, emphases on zero ozone depletion potential, impact quantification, greenhouse gas emission reduction, indirect emissions, noise and other environmental considerations. Chemical safety is also covered under environmental sustainability issues. The comprehensive deliberations of obstacles and limitations of TAR, such as coefficient of performance (COP) comparisons, acoustic streaming and nonlinear losses, thermal boundary resistance, manufacturing constraints, system complexity, component integration, commercialization barriers, and standards with certification are studied. Further, new technological advancements in TAR such as bypass configuration, flexible resonance tube technology, advanced stack and regenerator designs, acoustic impedance matching innovations, multiple regenerator configurations, mechanical resonators, integration with renewable energy and smart systems, waste heat recovery, smart control systems, hybrid configurations are also reviewed. Additionally, potential directions for future research commercialization prospects such as performance enhancement pathways, multi-objective optimization, miniaturization and microsystems, MEMS integration, compact high-frequency systems, market strategy are considered in the existing study. title: Enhancement Pathways for Urban Water Ecological Resilience
summary: Enhancing urban water ecological resilience (UWER) is increasingly essential as climate change, rapid urbanization, and ecological degradation intensify pressures on urban aquatic systems. However, knowledge of the mechanisms required to sy
content: Enhancing urban water ecological resilience (UWER) is increasingly essential as climate change, rapid urbanization, and ecological degradation intensify pressures on urban aquatic systems. However, knowledge of the mechanisms required to systematically enhance UWER remains fragmented across the ecological, technological, and governance domains. This narrative review synthesizes the current understanding of UWER by examining its conceptual foundations, key drivers, mechanisms, and enhancement pathways. Grounded in ecological resilience theory, UWER is the capacity of urban aquatic ecosystems, shaped by supporting infrastructure and governance arrangements, to resist disturbances, recover essential functions, and adapt or transform under persistent change. The Social–Ecological–Technological Systems and Three Horizons frameworks are integrated to connect these capacities with cross-system interventions and longer-term transitions. Hydroclimatic forcing, land-use intensity, ecological integrity, and institutional capacity emerge as recurrent and interacting UWER drivers, with their effects operating across scales and potentially generating nonlinear feedback, threshold behavior, and regime shifts. Three complementary enhancement pathways are identified: technological pathways, including nature-based, hybrid and decentralized infrastructure and digital tools; ecological pathways focused on biodiversity, habitat complexity, and connectivity; and governance and institutional pathways based on integrated planning, stable financing, participation, and adaptive policies. These pathways become most effective when coordinated as an integrated social–ecological–technological transition rather than implemented as isolated measures. Nevertheless, a persistent definition-to-decision gap remains because of inconsistent concepts, fragmented indicators, limited long-term observations, and the weak translation of assessments into practice. Future progress requires measurable resilience targets, validated indicators, sustained monitoring, context-sensitive coordination of ecological restoration, infrastructure innovation, and adaptive governance.

title: Effect of H 2 O 2 Etching on Properties of Spray‐Deposited Cu 2 NiSnS 4 Thin Films
summary: ABSTRACT Recently, high toxic, cyanide‐based etching methods are used to remove copper‐based impurity phases in quaternary chalcogenide materials. In this study, the hazardous and toxic cyanide etching method is replaced by the novel, eco‐f
content: ABSTRACT Recently, high toxic, cyanide‐based etching methods are used to remove copper‐based impurity phases in quaternary chalcogenide materials. In this study, the hazardous and toxic cyanide etching method is replaced by the novel, eco‐friendly, non‐cyanide etching of spray‐deposited Cu 2 NiSnS 4 thin films for the removal of the Cu x S secondary phase. The CNTS thin films are characterized using different characterization techniques to study the effect of etching on their physico‐chemical properties. The spray‐deposited CNTS thin film synthesized at a substrate temperature of 400 °C and etched by 5% H 2 O 2 solution for 6 min have exhibited the suppression of the Cu x S phase. The 6 min etched CNTS thin film reveals excellent physicochemical properties. The cubic CNTS phase exhibits a crystallite size of 13.7 nm. The suppression of the Cu x S phase is indicated by decreased Raman peak intensity at 472 cm −1 , an optimum band gap of 1.45 eV, and band‐to‐band PL emission at 752 nm. XPS spectrum reveal the presence of Cu, Ni, Sn, and S in +1, +2, +4, and −2 oxidation states, respectively.

title: GIS-Based Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia
summary: Landslides are a prevalent environmental risk in Malaysia, occurring mainly in hilly and tropical locations, often during the optimum time for heavy downpours. This study aims to assess the landslide susceptibility in Batang Kali, Selangor,
content: Landslides are a prevalent environmental risk in Malaysia, occurring mainly in hilly and tropical locations, often during the optimum time for heavy downpours. This study aims to assess the landslide susceptibility in Batang Kali, Selangor, Malaysia, utilizing the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) based on Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Based on historical records, aerial image interpretation, and remote sensing data, in combination with field verification, a landslide database of 46 identified landslide locations was produced. Sixteen influential factors, including various topographic, hydrological, environmental, and human factors, were selected for landslide susceptibility modeling. The landslide susceptibility map was created using weighted overlay analysis and classified into five levels of susceptibility, ranging from very low to very high. The resulting susceptibility map shows that 14.68% of the study area belongs to the very low susceptibility class, while 25.84%, 20.20%, 24.90%, and 14.38% belong to low, moderate, high, and very high susceptibility classes, respectively. The susceptibility map obtained from this study serves as a realistic decision-support tool for reducing landslide risk, designing infrastructure, and promoting sustainable land management in sensitive mountainous areas. Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to measure the model's predictive performance, using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) as an overall measure of model discrimination. The ROC–AUC analysis showed an AUC value of 0.722 (72.2%), indicating acceptable model performance.

title: A lightweight closed-loop adaptive intrusion detection framework for cyber resilience in critical infrastructure
summary: Abstract Most operators of energy, health, or transport facilities do not have at their disposal the kind of computational resources that large-scale deep-learning detectors require. Being energy and health care and transportation facility
content: Abstract Most operators of energy, health, or transport facilities do not have at their disposal the kind of computational resources that large-scale deep-learning detectors require. Being energy and health care and transportation facility operators, they seek an intrusion detection approach that is responsive to environmental changes. We present one such lightweight alternative. At the core of such an approach is a regularized Logistic Regression-based detector, with the closed loop comprising context-aware thresholding, behavioral profiling, recent error-rate feedback, budget-limited incremental updates, and deception-derived observations from outside. None of these approaches is, in itself, novel. Our contribution lies in the coupling of these mechanisms to displace the decision threshold using contextual and behavioral signals and in detecting confirmed outcomes that are then fed back to update the classifier, the behavioral baseline, and future decisions. We conduct the model evaluation on two levels of abstraction. The confirmation dataset includes 39,919 SWaT instances segmented into 40 nonoverlapping time windows, validated over StratifiedGroupKFold with a per-instance allowance of no more than 256 analyst-validated instances. In an ablation study over 25 such splits comparing the full model to the Logistic Regression with the static threshold, the full model achieved an F1 of 0.7526 ± 0.1074 compared with only 0.5719 ± 0.1578 for the latter (Holm adjusted p < 0.001). Most of the contribution came from budgeted incremental learning; without it, F1 dropped by 0.1704. Feedback using error rates was less important but still significant, returning 0.0048 in F1 together with a lower false positive rate. Behavioral profiling did not affect the F1 and improved specificity. Context-aware thresholding increased the false positive rate while yielding no improvement in the F1; thus, this is reported as a trade-off rather than an improvement. There were no significant contrasts with respect to the Holm correction; hence, we do not claim any synergy. Batch Logistic Regression with matching scored 0.7065 ± 0.1254 in terms of F1 score compared with Decision Tree, Random Forest, Linear SVM, Extra Trees, and MLP, none being significantly different from batch Logistic Regression. Because the labels were equally split among 256, all feedback mechanisms outperformed the case with no feedback, going from an F1 of 0.5845 ± 0.1495 to between 0.7292 and 0.7676. The deception-prioritized proxy did not make it into the winners. It beat no feedback but lost to random sampling on all the metrics that we examined. We have, therefore, referenced the previously published simulation and emulation figures as exploratory studies illustrating the behavior of this architecture. title: Impact of Silica Fume on the Mechanical Characteristics of Lime-Based Lightweight Geopolymer Mortar
source: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
summary: In recent years, geopolymer has been used as a cement replacement in the production of eco-friendly mortar and concrete. Most research used fly ash and slag as base materials for producing geopolymers. This work aimed to use lime as the bas
content: In recent years, geopolymer has been used as a cement replacement in the production of eco-friendly mortar and concrete. Most research used fly ash and slag as base materials for producing geopolymers. This work aimed to use lime as the base material for a geopolymer, with aluminum powder, to produce lightweight geopolymer mortar with different replacement levels of silica fume to enhance its properties. Many tests were done to find out the behavior of this type of mortar, such as bulk density, compressive strength, tensile splitting strength, flexural strength, and sorptivity. In addition, a statistical analysis was carried out on results after 28 days of casting. The results showed that the fresh density decreased from 1997.8 to 1783.7 kg/m3 when replacing up to 10% of lime with silica fume, and the hardened density decreased from 1896 to 1673.6 kg/m3 for the identical replacement level. Compressive, splitting tensile, and flexural strength decreased with increasing silica fume replacement level up to 10%. The sorptivity index increased with increasing silica fume replacement level.

title: Business Sentiment and FDI Dynamics in Brazil: An Econometric Assessment of Investor Confidence, 2000–2025
source: Asia Pacific Economic and Management Review
summary: Research on China has recently argued that locally sourced business sentiment is a better leading indicator of foreign direct investment (FDI) than global confidence indices. This paper asks whether that result travels to Brazil, Latin Amer
content: Research on China has recently argued that locally sourced business sentiment is a better leading indicator of foreign direct investment (FDI) than global confidence indices. This paper asks whether that result travels to Brazil, Latin America’s largest FDI recipient. We replicate and extend the design of Finley et al. (2025) using the components of the Industrial Entrepreneur Confidence Index (ICEI) of the National Confederation of Industry (CNI) — current conditions (Business Performance), expectations (Business Outlook) and the composite index — together with Brazil’s rank in the Kearney FDI Confidence Index and macroeconomic fundamentals for 2000–2025. Trend, correlation, Newey–West regression, ARDL bounds-testing and Granger-causality analyses are applied. Business Outlook declines significantly over the period (−0.42 points per year, p = 0.005), and Brazil falls from 3rd place (2012–2013) to outside the Kearney top 25 (2019, 2023). Yet FDI does not follow: FDI as a share of GDP is flat and FDI in US dollars grows by about 6.1% per year. Sentiment is uncorrelated with FDI intensity, the bounds test rejects a long-run sentiment–FDI relationship, and sentiment does not Granger-cause FDI, whereas lagged FDI does help predict sentiment. Real labour-cost growth is the only determinant that is significant across all specifications. The evidence is consistent with counter-cyclical, “fire-sale” FDI during Brazil’s 2015–2016 recession, when confidence collapsed and the real depreciated while FDI intensity peaked. We conclude that domestic sentiment is not a universal leading indicator of FDI: its predictive value depends on the motive and timing of inward investment, and Brazilian policymakers should monitor costs and asset valuations alongside confidence.

title: Uncertain panel threshold regression model and its application
source: Communications in Statistics - Simulation and Computation
summary: This study first constructs an uncertain panel threshold regression model (UPTR) and empirically examines the impact of energy structure changes on carbon emissions based on panel data from 29 Chinese provinces spanning 2012 to 2020. The re
content: This study first constructs an uncertain panel threshold regression model (UPTR) and empirically examines the impact of energy structure changes on carbon emissions based on panel data from 29 Chinese provinces spanning 2012 to 2020. The results show that there is a significant threshold effect of energy structure changes on carbon emissions, and that the level of industrial development and the intensity of renewable energy utilization are important factors affecting carbon emissions. When the energy structure crosses a specific threshold, the intensity of its impact on carbon emissions undergoes a clear shift. Specifically, before crossing the threshold, the energy structure significantly increases carbon emissions, whereas after crossing the threshold, its marginal emission-increasing effect weakens. This indicates that only when renewable energy utilization reaches a certain level can the optimization of the energy structure truly play a role in curbing carbon emissions.

title: FUEL-MIX SUBSTITUTION VERSUS SCALE: AN LMDI DECOMPOSITION OF FOSSIL GENERATION GROWTH IN UZBEKISTAN'S POWER SECTOR, 2011–2025
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This study applies the LMDI method to analyze changes in gas- and coal-based electricity generation in Uzbekistan over the period 2011–2025. The overall change is decomposed into two main factors: growth in electricity generation volume and
content: This study applies the LMDI method to analyze changes in gas- and coal-based electricity generation in Uzbekistan over the period 2011–2025. The overall change is decomposed into two main factors: growth in electricity generation volume and diversification of the energy mix associated with the expanding role of renewable energy sources. Calculations based on annual data show that growth in generation volume alone would have increased gas- and coalbased electricity generation by 4.17 billion kWh. At the same time, diversification of the energy mix generated a structural effect of 9.87 billion kWh, resulting in a 5.70 billion kWh reallocation in gas- and coal-based generation while overall electricity demand continued to grow. The structural effect remained relatively limited before 2019, whereas its importance increased substantially after 2023 alongside the expansion of solar and wind power capacity. This development reflects the gradual diversification of Uzbekistan's electricity sector and the growing contribution of renewable energy sources to the national generation mix. While growth in total generation remains an important driver of electricity-sector change in many countries, Uzbekistan demonstrates an increasingly active process of energy-mix transformation and expansion of alternative generation sources. The results indicate that, alongside continued growth in electricity demand, Uzbekistan's power sector is undergoing a gradual structural transformation characterized by an increasing role of renewable energy and a more diversified generation portfolio. title: Evaluation and Selection of Supplementary Damping Strategies for Renewable Energy Generation Units Based on Damping Reshaping Effects
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: [Objective] To address the lack of a unified quantitative criterion for evaluating supplementary damping control schemes in renewable energy units and the difficulty of jointly selecting feedback signals and injection locations， a strategy
content: [Objective] To address the lack of a unified quantitative criterion for evaluating supplementary damping control schemes in renewable energy units and the difficulty of jointly selecting feedback signals and injection locations， a strategy selection method based on the damping reshaping effect index （DREI） is proposed. [Methods] Candidate control combinations were constructed by combining voltage， current， power， DC-link voltage and phase-locked loop （PLL） angular-frequency signals with typical injection locations in the converter control loops. A positive-sequence impedance model considering machine-side dynamics was established through dq-domain impedance modeling and sequence transformation. DREI was defined as the integral of the negative region of the real part of the positive-sequence impedance， and was used to quantify the ability of each control combination to weaken negative damping and to rank candidate schemes. [Results] Impedance analysis， Nyquist stability analysis and time-domain simulation show that the impedance reshaping effect varies significantly with feedback signal and injection location. The scheme using the grid-side q-axis current as the feedback signal and injecting it into the q-axis current inner loop achieves the minimum DREI and provides the best negative-damping suppression and stability-margin improvement. [Conclusions] DREI can uniformly characterize the impedance reshaping capability of supplementary damping control over the full frequency range， providing a quantitative basis for supplementary damping strategy design and wideband oscillation stability analysis of renewable energy units.

title: BOUNDARY Ω — Integrated Recoverability-Constrained Supercomputer Architecture, Universal Continuity Systems, Executable Research Engines, Public-Data Pilots, and Evidence Archive

content: BOUNDARY Ω is an integrated experimental software and systems-engineering corpus developed within the Recoverability-Constrained Systems (RCS) and Continuity Science research programme. This release collection brings together the BOUNDARY Ω / OMEGA9 executable research architecture, finite successor-space and admissibility methods, recursive governance models, rights-oriented safeguards, resource-continuity simulations, scientific and engineering design generators, quantum-inspired computation, energy-system modelling, public-data connectors, intervention-evaluation frameworks, and reproducible Boundary Records. The archive documents an iterative series of software releases, including versions v33 through v53, where supplied in the deposited files. It preserves historical implementations alongside subsequent extensions, allowing readers to examine the development, assumptions, tests, limitations, and evidence boundaries of the system. 1. Scientific and Mathematical Foundations The architecture investigates recoverability-constrained admissibility, bounded irreversibility, finite successor spaces, continuation accessibility, distinction preservation, recursive evaluation, provenance integrity, and terminal stopping conditions. Its central methodological objective is to distinguish admissible, testable continuation from unsupported inference or irreversible action. The software implements deterministic indexing of declared finite configuration spaces, bounded hypothetical future generators, evidence-review procedures, and explicit stopping certificates. Mathematical enumeration of possible configurations is distinguished from independent scientific validation of each configuration. 2. Governance, Rights, and Continuity The collection includes proposed constitutional, institutional, legal, and humanitarian governance frameworks addressing: Fundamental rights and protection of living beings. Consent, autonomy, accountability, and independent review. Non-coercive international cooperation. Revocable delegation and limits on institutional authority. Accessible remedies, protection against retaliation, and continuity of essential services. Resource allocation, public-interest technology, and proposed universal free-at-the-point-of-use access. These materials constitute research models and proposed frameworks. They do not establish binding law or confer institutional authority. 3. Water treatment and continuity planning. Soil regeneration and ecological-resource models. Material recovery and circular-resource systems. title: Análise hierárquica dos fatores críticos de sucesso em projetos executados por empresas juniores
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: Projetos são empreendimentos temporários, únicos e orientados a entregas específicas, o que exige coordenação rigorosa de escopo, prazo, custo e qualidade (Watt, 2014; Seymour e Hussein, 2014).Nas últimas décadas, a literatura passou a reco
content: Projetos são empreendimentos temporários, únicos e orientados a entregas específicas, o que exige coordenação rigorosa de escopo, prazo, custo e qualidade (Watt, 2014; Seymour e Hussein, 2014).Nas últimas décadas, a literatura passou a reconhecer que o sucesso de um projeto vai além do cumprimento do triângulo de ferro, incorporando a geração de valor, a satisfação das partes interessadas e o alinhamento estratégico (Atkinson, 1999;Cooke-Davies, 2002;PMI, 2021).No contexto das Empresas Juniores (EJs), esses desafios se intensificam.São organizações sem fins lucrativos, formadas por estudantes de graduação, com alta rotatividade, baixa experiência acumulada e recursos limitados, mas com forte potencial formativo e impacto na empregabilidade e no empreendedorismo de seus membros (Brasil, 2016; Ziliotto; Berti, 2012;Moraes et al., 2021;Trautwein et al., 2026).Essas características tornam a gestão de projetos em EJs especialmente sensível à presença de fatores críticos de sucesso (FCS), isto é, condições cuja presença favorece decisivamente o desempenho dos projetos.Em ambientes com escassez de recursos e pouca maturidade gerencial, identificar quais fatores devem ser priorizados é essencial para evitar dispersão de esforços e aumentar a efetividade das ações (Longman;Mullins, 2004;Herath;Chong, 2021).Diante disso, este artigo analisa, hierarquicamente, os FCS em projetos executados por Empresas Juniores, combinando revisão da literatura e a aplicação do método ISM-MICMAC.O objetivo é evidenciar quais fatores atuam como vetores estratégicos do sistema e quais são mais dependentes, oferecendo subsídios práticos para a tomada de decisão em EJs e contribuindo para o avanço teórico sobre gestão de projetos em contextos estudantis (Clarke, 1999;Attri et al., 2013; Rathi et al., 2022). Fundamentação teórica Empresas junioresA literatura sobre EJs destaca que a aprendizagem ocorre por meio da vivência prática em gestão, negociação, liderança e execução de projetos, aproximando a experiência acadêmica das demandas do mercado.Ao mesmo tempo, a literatura sobre gestão de projetos mostra que o tipo de organização influencia a escolha das práticas gerenciais, de modo que estruturas pequenas e dinâmicas se beneficiam de modelos mais leves e adaptativos (Turner; Ledwith; Kelly, 2010; Weintraub et al., 2020).

title: Ultra-Low-Frequency Acoustic Dual-Resonance System for Marine Geology and Subsea Energy Detection
source: Journal of Ocean Engineering and Science
summary: Low-frequency underwater acoustic sources face a fundamental trade-off between miniaturization and output power, which severely constrains their use in marine geological exploration. To address this limitation, this work proposes a dual-res
content: Low-frequency underwater acoustic sources face a fundamental trade-off between miniaturization and output power, which severely constrains their use in marine geological exploration. To address this limitation, this work proposes a dual-resonant underwater low-frequency transducer based on the coupling of a bubble resonator and a Helmholtz resonator The device delivers controllable output waveforms at low frequencies with high pressure intensity. A research framework integrating theoretical modeling, numerical simulation, and experimental verification is established. On the theoretical side, a lumped-parameter model was developed by use of electroacoustic analogy; an equivalent relationship between volume pulsations and radiated sound pressure was formulated on the basis of monopole theory. MATLAB parameter fitting was then used to quantify the effects of key parameters on the resonance frequency and sound pressure level was quantified, while COMSOL simulations served to screen and optimize the dimensions of the prototype. On the experimental side, the bubble resonant cavity was structurally optimized, the tensile properties of the diaphragm were characterized, and mechanisms for air circulation and flow regulation were designed. Particularly, a high-pressure gas source driving a highly elastic diaphragm replaced the traditional blower-driven excitation, which miniaturized the pneumatic acoustic source while preserving broadband controllable output. Measurement in an anechoic tank and in a lake showed that the prototype produced a SPL exceeding 180 dB at its designed natural frequency of 20 Hz. This study offers a practical technical route toward compact, high-sound-intensity artificial seismic sources is of considerable engineering value for underwater low-frequency acoustic propagation and marine geological exploration.

title: INTRA- FAMILY CRISIS AND ITS EFFECTS ON THE GROWTH OF AGRICULTURE IN ONDO-STATE
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Agriculture has been one of the primitive and ancient Economic system that has been responsible for the development of town and cities, provision of food, provision of raw materials which led to development of industries which has led to th
content: Agriculture has been one of the primitive and ancient Economic system that has been responsible for the development of town and cities, provision of food, provision of raw materials which led to development of industries which has led to the growth of the industrial revolution in the world, Agriculture has also provided employment opportunities and security for people from the primitive period till date, It has also provided for environmental development and security, Agriculture forms an integral part of the economy of a country by ensuring a good sources of income and revenue export and trade the same as the citizens of such country practicing agriculture. Recently Agriculture has also been contributing to the energy production in the world through bio-fuel and this call for reduction in the reliance on non-renewable energy. Agriculture has also led to a reduction in poverty rate in Some third world countries because they depended much on Primary products gotten from Agriculture to improve and grow their economy, all these are among the numerous benefits of agriculture to individual, Countries and even the globe. Generally among the third world countries of the world who have little or no technology growth, Both the government and Family as well as individual depend largely on Agriculture as way and source of livelihood and income; hence it is pertinent to know how crisis among family members can hinder the growth Agriculture. Despite the significance of the issue, there is a lack of research on the effects of intra-family crisis on agriculture in Ondo state. This study aims to bridge this knowledge gap by investigating the impact of intra-family crisis on agricultural productivity, in the state. The study will also identify the factors contributing to intra-family crisis among farming families and explore strategies for mitigating the effects of the crisis on agriculture. Therefore this research work was carried out using Primary sources like Oral interviews, and also secondary sources from books and journal to explain and elucidate the effects of Family crisis on the output and growth of agriculture in Ondo State and how these issue can be addressed so as to ensure and enhance the effective growth and output production of Agriculture.

title: Electricity Capacity Upgrade from 450 to 900 VA and Life Satisfaction of BPBL Recipients
source: Journal of Business Social and Technology
summary: Background: Electricity is a basic necessity that supports household welfare. Through the New Electricity Connection Assistance Program (Bantuan Pasang Baru Listrik, BPBL), the Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources provides fr
content: Background: Electricity is a basic necessity that supports household welfare. Through the New Electricity Connection Assistance Program (Bantuan Pasang Baru Listrik, BPBL), the Indonesian Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources provides free electricity connections to underprivileged households. In 2023, the electricity capacity provided to BPBL recipients was increased from 450 volt-amperes (VA) to 900 VA. Objective: This study examines whether the increase in electricity capacity is associated with differences in personal and social life satisfaction among BPBL recipients. Methods: The study used primary survey data from 615 BPBL recipient households across the 2022 and 2023 cohorts. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed using three methods: nearest-neighbor matching, radius caliper matching, and kernel matching. Matching quality was assessed based on covariate balance and common support. Results: The increase in electricity capacity was consistently associated with higher social life satisfaction across all three matching methods, with estimated effects ranging from approximately 9% to 17%. For personal life satisfaction, a statistically significant effect was identified only using radius caliper matching, with an estimated effect of 7.5%; the estimates from nearest-neighbor and kernel matching were not statistically significant. Conclusion: The increase in electricity capacity from 450 VA to 900 VA showed a more robust association with social life satisfaction than with personal life satisfaction. Future evaluations should consider longer observation periods to assess whether benefits in the personal domain emerge over time.

title: Panorama da literatura sobre a descarbonização marítima e as tomadas de decisões
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: IntroduçãoO transporte marítimo é considerado o principal modal do comércio global, representando cerca de 3% da demanda energética do mundo (DNV, 2025, p. 41).Em decorrência das altas emissões de carbono, a descarbonização marítima se torn
content: IntroduçãoO transporte marítimo é considerado o principal modal do comércio global, representando cerca de 3% da demanda energética do mundo (DNV, 2025, p. 41).Em decorrência das altas emissões de carbono, a descarbonização marítima se tornou uma exigência regulatória sob a Estratégia de GEE da International Maritime Organization (IMO) de 2023, e juntamente com outros emissores, como o setor industrial, o transporte marítimo enfrenta um desafio para a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa (GEE) atrelado à competição por energia e combustíveis de baixa emissão de poluentes, como retratado nas projeções do DNV -Det Norske Veritas (2025, p.7). Em abril de 2025, foi aprovado pelo Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC) da IMO, o marco Net-Zero Framework (NZF).De acordo com o DNV (2025, p. 15), o objetivo do NZF é garantir o cumprimento das metas e estratégias da IMO para a redução de emissões de GEE, de forma que a adoção de combustíveis, tecnologias e fontes de energia ocorra de forma mais ágil e assertiva.As metas estabelecidas pela IMO para a redução de CO2 são ambiciosas e envolvem escolhas complexas (Mahmud et al, 2025), desde a escolha de combustíveis alternativos como biocombustíveis, diesel, metano, metanol, amônia, hidrogênio, até gargalos de implementação de tecnologia, infraestrutura e abastecimento (DNV, 2025, p. 6-7).A relação entre urgência regulatória e diferentes soluções compõem um problema de decisão deve levar em consideração todas as dimensões que impactam no atingimento das metas estabelecidas.Nesse contexto, Alghassab (2026) destaca a complexidade da tomada de decisão no setor de transporte marítimo, que lida com decisões complexas, múltiplos stakeholders, trade-offs, mudanças em regulamentações e rápido desenvolvimento da tecnologia.Faz-se necessário abordagens de modelos e métodos que apoiem o processo de tomada de decisão para a aceleração de ações para a redução de GEE (Alghassab, 2026), e essa é a proposta da abordagem Multiple Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM), visando o levantamento de modelos que orientem as decisões.Esta pesquisa tem como objetivo realizar um panorama da literatura sobre a aplicação de métodos de apoio à decisão à descarbonização marítima orientado pelo ProKnow-C para seleção e análise crítica de referências relevantes sobre o tema.Como objetivos específicos, busca-se: (i) realizar o mapeamento dos métodos de apoio à decisão utilizados; (ii) identificar os critérios de decisão aplicados; (iii) analisar os combustíveis mais estudados entre pesquisas;

title: Bidding Strategy of Pumped Storage Power Plants Considering Seasonal Characteristics in Integrated Electricity Spot Markets
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: [Objective] The large-scale integration of high-proportion renewable energy into power systems has intensified seasonal variations in system net load. The joint clearing mechanism of the electricity spot energy market and ancillary service
content: [Objective] The large-scale integration of high-proportion renewable energy into power systems has intensified seasonal variations in system net load. The joint clearing mechanism of the electricity spot energy market and ancillary service market further exacerbates market uncertainty， imposing substantial tail risks on the bidding decision-making of pumped storage power plants. To address this issue， this paper proposes a bidding framework for pumped storage power plants that adapts to multi-seasonal operational scenarios and fully considers market risk constraints. [Methods] First， three typical seasonal scenarios， including the spring-autumn transition season， summer， and winter， are classified based on the evolutionary characteristics of system net load. Second， a novel seasonal joint strategy index is constructed by integrating the arbitrage space characterized by the net load peak-valley difference and the tail risk characteristics of operational revenue. A 15-minute resolution bi-level bidding model is established for pumped storage power plants participating in the integrated spot market. The lower-level model replicates the joint clearing process of the electricity spot market， while the upper-level model embeds the proposed seasonal joint strategy index into the profit function and constraint system， so as to characterize the differentiated bidding behaviors of power plants under diverse seasonal scenarios. [Results] The proposed method can adaptively optimize the capacity allocation between the energy market and ancillary service market according to seasonal net load profiles and dynamic tail risks， effectively improving the tail profit level of pumped storage power plants. Moreover， the derived risk-return frontier enables adjustable bidding strategies to accommodate the diverse risk preferences of market participants. [Conclusions] The incorporation of the seasonal joint strategy index and the corresponding constraint response mechanism in the developed model provides robust technical support for the optimal bidding of pumped storage power plants in the complex integrated electricity spot market.

title: Bio-based small extracellular vesicles in cancer therapy: a sustainable approach for targeted drug delivery
summary: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide, posing challenges for healthcare systems despite advancements in diagnostics and treatments. Traditional therapies, including chemotherapy and radiation, often struggle with issue
content: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide, posing challenges for healthcare systems despite advancements in diagnostics and treatments. Traditional therapies, including chemotherapy and radiation, often struggle with issues such as non-specific targeting of cancer cells and the development of drug resistance. Recent progress in nanomedicine presents new opportunities to overcome these obstacles through refined methods of drug delivery and enhanced therapeutic efficacy. Among the various strategies, biologically derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have gained significant attention due to their natural compatibility with biological systems and potential to induce immune responses, thereby offering more effective cancer treatment alternatives. Sustainable approaches in nanomedicine focus on the use of renewable and biocompatible materials, with sEVs from natural sources emerging as promising candidates. These vesicles possess unique properties, including low immunogenicity and effective cellular uptake mechanisms, which can aid in personalized therapy. Research indicates that these sEVs can be engineered to carry therapeutic agents, enhancing targeted delivery while minimizing systemic side effects. However, challenges in isolating and purifying sEVs remain a barrier to their widespread application. This review discusses the potential of biologically sourced sEVs in nanomedicine, exploring their role in targeted cancer therapies, and addresses the hurdles in their isolation and purification processes. Our approach emphasizes the use of bio-based sEVs, like the ones derived from cell lines or plasma/serum, as a viable alternative to the traditional methods that involve isolating sEVs from animals or employing synthetic molecules. Ultimately, we aim to highlight how sustainable strategies can optimize the yield and efficacy of sEVs for their use as drug delivery system, paving the way for advancements in cancer treatment.

title: ANÁLISE DE CONCORDÂNCIA POR ATRIBUTOS PARA MEDIR A QUALIDADE E RAPIDEZ DA TOMADA DE DECISÃO COM BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE NA INDÚSTRIA 4.0
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A Indústria 4.0, caracterizada pela integração de tecnologias avançadas como Internet das Coisas (IoT), inteligência artificial (IA) e sistemas interconectados, representa uma transformação significativa na forma como as organizações operam
content: A Indústria 4.0, caracterizada pela integração de tecnologias avançadas como Internet das Coisas (IoT), inteligência artificial (IA) e sistemas interconectados, representa uma transformação significativa na forma como as organizações operam.Essa revolução permite maior eficiência, autonomia e interconexão, tornando as empresas mais inteligentes e adaptáveis (Iszczuk et al., 2021).Nesse contexto, surge o conceito de Qualidade 4.0, que combina práticas tradicionais de gestão da qualidade com tecnologias digitais, destacando o uso de dados em tempo real e análise preditiva para garantir altos padrões de qualidade (Liu et al., 2023).O Business Intelligence (BI) desempenha um papel fundamental nesse cenário, fornecendo ferramentas para coleta, tratamento e análise de dados, essenciais para a tomada de decisões baseadas em evidências.Segundo Oliveira (2022), o BI é importante para tornar as organizações mais ágeis e precisas em suas decisões estratégicas e operacionais.Na Indústria 4.0, a capacidade de tomar decisões rápidas e informadas é um fator determinante, especialmente em ambientes competitivos e dinâmicos (De Souza; Lopes, 2023).No entanto, medir a qualidade e a rapidez da tomada de decisão com o uso de ferramentas de BI, como painéis de Power BI, apresenta desafios significativos.O desenho de painéis eficazes envolve decisões complexas sobre quais dados incluir, como apresentá-los e como garantir que os usuários finais possam interpretá-los adequadamente (Schinaider; Lee; Junior, 2022).Além disso, as análises estatísticas tradicionais enfrentam limitações ao avaliar dados qualitativos, como escalas de Likert, especialmente em relação à subjetividade das avaliações humanas.Nesse contexto, a Análise de Concordância para Atributos (AAA) emerge como uma abordagem para avaliar a consistência das respostas entre avaliadores ou momentos, oferecendo uma visão mais precisa sobre os fatores que influenciam a tomada de decisão (De Oliveira et al., 2020).Este estudo visa investigar como elementos de painéis de BI, como gráficos, tabelas e alertas, impactam a qualidade e a rapidez da tomada de decisão no contexto da Indústria 4.0.A metodologia inclui o Planejamento de Experimentos (DOE) para estruturar os cenários de avaliação e a aplicação da AAA para analisar a consistência das avaliações qualitativas.O objetivo é contribuir para o desenvolvimento de um sistema de medição da qualidade e rapidez da tomada de decisão em painéis de BI, oferecendo subsídios para melhorias práticas em organizações que buscam otimizar suas decisões.

title: HEURISTICS APPLIED TO LOGISTICS LOCATION: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: In recent decades, the increasing complexity of logistics systems has intensified the need for efficient optimization methods capable of addressing facility location decisions.The present study develops a bibliometric analysis of heuristics
content: In recent decades, the increasing complexity of logistics systems has intensified the need for efficient optimization methods capable of addressing facility location decisions.The present study develops a bibliometric analysis of heuristics and metaheuristics applied to location problems in the logistics domain, with the objective of identifying trends, methodological approaches, and research opportunities.A total of 5,109 documents published between 1970 and 2025, retrieved from the Scopus database, were analyzed using the five-step method proposed by Zupic and Čater (2015).Data processing and analysis were carried out using the Bibliometrix software in R, which enabled the examination of scientific output, authors, journals, citations, keywords, co-occurrence networks, and thematic maps.The results evidence a sustained growth in scientific production since the 1990s, driven by the need to address complex problems related to network design, supply chains, and multiobjective optimization.Furthermore, heuristics such as genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization are highlighted for their capacity to solve large-scale problems subject to multiple constraints.Finally, an expansion toward sustainable and dynamic applications is identified, along with research opportunities in humanitarian logistics, resilience, and hybrid models integrated with artificial intelligence.

title: A Python Framework for Large-Scale Solar PV Potential and Techno-Economic Scenario Analysis
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: OverviewThis repository contains the complete, reproducible Python pipeline for the national-scale assessment of solar photovoltaic (PV) potential and economic viability across Iran. The code accompanies the research paper: "National-Scale
content: OverviewThis repository contains the complete, reproducible Python pipeline for the national-scale assessment of solar photovoltaic (PV) potential and economic viability across Iran. The code accompanies the research paper: "National-Scale Solar PV Potential and Investment Site Selection in Iran Using Multi-Criteria Decision Making". The pipeline is designed to process massive spatiotemporal climate datasets (76 years of hourly ERA5-Land data, exceeding 650,000 records), integrate high-resolution geospatial constraints, and evaluate complex techno-economic scenarios. It outputs high-resolution maps, comprehensive statistical summaries, and spatial decision-support data. --- 1. System Requirements & DependenciesThe code is written in Python 3.9+ and requires the following libraries. It is highly recommended to use a virtual environment (e.g., Conda) to manage dependencies:- Climate & Geospatial Processing: `xarray`, `rioxarray`, `rasterio`, `geopandas`- Numerical & Data Manipulation: `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`- Financial Modeling: `numpy_financial`- Visualization: `matplotlib` (configured for high-resolution 600 DPI outputs)- Utilities: `tqdm` (for progress bars), `openpyxl` (for Excel exports), `pickle`, `gzip`, `hashlib` (for caching). --- 2. Input Data RequirementsThe pipeline requires the following datasets, which must be placed in the directories specified in the `CONFIG` section at the top of the script: 1. ERA5-Land Reanalysis Data (NetCDF format): - SSRD (Surface Solar Radiation Downwards): Hourly accumulated radiation (J/m²). - T2M (2-meter Air Temperature): Hourly temperature (K). - Format: Files should be named systematically (e.g., `era5_land_YYYY_MM.nc`) to allow the script to match SSRD and T2M files based on the year and month extracted via regular expressions.2. Administrative Boundary: - A Shapefile (`.shp`) defining the national borders of Iran (EPSG:4326). Used for masking the ERA5-Land grid and clipping the final maps.3. Topographic Data (GeoTIFF): - DEM (Digital Elevation Model), Slope (degrees), and Aspect (0–360°). The script reprojects these to EPSG:4326 and clips them to the Iran boundary.4. Land Cover Data (GeoTIFF): - ESA WorldCover 2021 (10m resolution), providing 11 land cover classes. Used to determine usable land fractions.5. City Locations (KML): - A folder containing KML files with placemarks for Iranian cities. Used to calculate the nearest-city distance using a KD-Tree algorithm. --- 3. Detailed Computational Logic & Pipeline Phases Phase 1: Data Acquisition & Preprocessing- De-accumulation: ERA5-Land SSRD is accumulated from 00:00 UTC. The script calculates the hourly difference: `SSRD(t) - SSRD(t-1)`. Negative differences (due to the daily reset) are floored at zero, and values are divided by 3600 to convert to W/m².- Night Masking: A dynamic sinusoidal mask is applied based on the month and hour to remove non-physical positive radiation values that occur during nighttime.- Physical Filter: Values exceeding 150
