This study develops a multidisciplinary approach to quantify and optimize tug-related emissions by integrating on-board field campaigns, interviews with tug crews, Automatic Identification System (AIS) data, and full-mission bridge simulation. Initial results from Spanish ports reveal that tugboats operate inefficiently, with more than half of their time spent below 25% engine load and extended waiting periods contributing to unnecessary fuel consumption. Logistic regression applied to AIS and observer data achieved 91% accuracy in identifying manoeuvre phases, while modified power–speed models outperformed the traditional cubic method for estimating engine power. These findings confirm that tug operations are oversized relative to their actual power needs, leading to avoidable emissions. The proposed methodology enables more accurate emission inventories and offers a framework for real-time monitoring and manoeuvre optimization, providing port authorities and policymakers with actionable strategies to mitigate local air pollution and improve sustainability in maritime operations.

title: Engineering Carbon Credits to make Bharat “Net Zero 2070” Ready
source: International Journal of Research and Review in Applied Science Humanities and Technology
summary: India's shift from the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) framework to the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) sets obligatory GHG intensity standards for energy-heavy industries like steel, cement, and foundries, encouraging process optimiza
content: India's shift from the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) framework to the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) sets obligatory GHG intensity standards for energy-heavy industries like steel, cement, and foundries, encouraging process optimizations in engineering to produce tradable Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs). This research compiles literature regarding industrial decarbonization, merging lifecycle CO₂ evaluation frameworks with foundry-related actions—waste heat recuperation from induction furnace cooling circuits, transitioning fuel from furnace oil to piped natural gas in cupola melting, and optimizing scrap through near-infrared sorting in aluminum sand casting. Based on Bureau of Energy Efficiency guidelines and sector studies, the analysis reveals that melting-dominant emission hotspots (60-70% of foundry LCA) can be strategically addressed to attain measurable reductions below CCTS benchmarks. Case studies demonstrate compliance routes for small and medium enterprises encountering data and monitoring limitations, utilizing public LCA databases and hybrid modeling to facilitate involvement in India's domestic carbon market while preserving productivity. Results highlight mechanical process engineering as a scalable approach for CCTS credit creation and certification in the international voluntary market.

title: A protocol-aware learning framework for harmonizing and translating official electric vehicle range labels across regulatory standards
summary: Abstract Official electric vehicle (EV) driving-range labels are generated under distinct regulatory protocols, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Procedure (WLTP), and New Euro
content: Abstract Official electric vehicle (EV) driving-range labels are generated under distinct regulatory protocols, including the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Procedure (WLTP), and New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), and therefore are not directly interchangeable. This study develops a protocol-aware learning framework for harmonizing and translating official range labels from static vehicle specifications while explicitly modeling the reporting protocol. The compiled database contains 319 EV configurations, with 176 EPA, 88 WLTP, and 98 NEDC labels; 227 configurations have at least one of these regulatory labels, and paired coverage varies substantially by protocol. The framework evaluates single-standard estimation, pooled learning with and without protocol information, a two-stage latent-baseline-plus-correction formulation, protocol-gap learning, cross-standard translation, interpretability, robustness, and uncertainty. In held-out pooled testing, explicit protocol encoding reduced RMSE from 54.21 to 43.20 km (R² = 0.925). Across 30 vehicle-grouped repeated holdout splits, mean RMSE decreased from 46.97 km without protocol information to 32.14 km with protocol information, with zero vehicle overlap between training and testing. Translation models were benchmarked against identity, median-ratio, and linear baselines and further assessed using bootstrap and nested validation; the low-overlap WLTP–NEDC tasks are therefore treated as exploratory rather than validated conversion rules. Grouped split-conformal intervals achieved 93.4% empirical coverage for a nominal 90% target. The framework is intended for cross-market comparison and regulatory-label harmonization, not prediction of actual on-road EV range, which requires independent real-world operating and energy-consumption data.

title: Timing matters: life cycle embodied GHG emissions of circular building strategies
summary: Circular building strategies (CBS) aim to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions related to the construction, maintenance and end-of-life of buildings. However, the timing of these reductions, whether immediate or in the future, is often ove
content: Circular building strategies (CBS) aim to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions related to the construction, maintenance and end-of-life of buildings. However, the timing of these reductions, whether immediate or in the future, is often overlooked. Given the urgency of addressing climate change, accounting for the temporal dimension is crucial to understand accurately the decarbonisation effects of CBS. Existing life cycle assessment (LCA) studies on CBS are analysed for the timing of reported reductions and the connected temporal considerations in the model. The analysis of LCA studies (n = 42) shows consistent reduction patterns for upstream CBS (e.g. reuse of existing components), but the assessment model includes little temporal detail. The reductions are more inconclusive for downstream CBS (e.g. design for disassembly), and they highly depend on temporal modelling. The findings highlight the need for a consistent LCA framework that accounts for the timing of GHG emission reductions when applying CBS. The identification of when actual GHG reductions occur arising from different circular strategies will aid in the understanding of CBS’s role in meeting climate targets. POLICY RELEVANCE CBS do not deliver GHG emission reductions equally over time, which has direct implications for policy design and decision-making. CBS acting early in the life cycle (e.g. component reuse) consistently reduce upfront emissions, supporting near-term climate targets. However, downstream CBS (e.g. design for disassembly) produce uncertain or delayed benefits, limiting their effectiveness for urgent decarbonisation goals. Current assessment methods often overlook this temporal dimension, risking misaligned incentives. LCA frameworks should be updated to explicitly report and account for when GHG emissions occur, not just the overall reduction. Additionally, policy frameworks should differentiate between short- and long-term mitigation, aligning subsidies, GHG emission limits, and reporting standards accordingly. Recommendations are provided to support evidence-based decisions and ensure the building sector contributes effectively to near- and long-term climate targets.

title: Applications in Port Logistics: Mapping Global Use Cases to Support the Transition of North Sea Ports
summary: Abstract Ports play an important role in the energy transition and represent a particularly promising area for further deployment of hydrogen solutions. Within this context, the Interreg project “North Sea Hydrogen Valley Ports” aims to dev
content: Abstract Ports play an important role in the energy transition and represent a particularly promising area for further deployment of hydrogen solutions. Within this context, the Interreg project “North Sea Hydrogen Valley Ports” aims to develop hydrogen-roadmaps in four European ports (Brest, Esbjerg, Bremen, and Den Helder) for a future maritime Hydrogen Valley. This paper presents the first phase of the project, focusing on the identification of potential hydrogen use cases in port areas, that will later be applied and further developed in the aforementioned four ports. The results show that the readiness to implement hydrogen applications varies among the analyzed ports and is closely related to local infrastructure conditions and energy constraints. While some ports are linked to the ongoing development of hydrogen infrastructure, others focus on initial use cases or solutions driven by specific challenges such as grid congestion. Overall, the study highlights that hydrogen technologies can play a key role in reducing emissions in port operations, particularly in mobile and heavy-duty applications.

title: Strip tillage combines the characteristics of conventional tillage and no-tillage in terms of soil macropore structures and hydrothermal conditions
summary: Achieving sustainable utilization of black soils in Northeast China hinges on balancing exploitation and conservation. Conventional tillage (CT) degrades soil over time, while no-tillage (NT) conserves soil but often reduces yields. Strip t
content: Achieving sustainable utilization of black soils in Northeast China hinges on balancing exploitation and conservation. Conventional tillage (CT) degrades soil over time, while no-tillage (NT) conserves soil but often reduces yields. Strip tillage (ST) tills within the seed row zone (ST-IR) while maintains NT with straw mulch between seed rows zone (ST-BR), which appears to integrate the advantages of CT and NT. However, the effects of ST-IR and ST-BR on the soil macropore structures and hydrothermal properties in this region remain unclear. In this study, X-ray computed tomography (X-CT) and time domain reflectometry (TDR) were employed to compare the soil macropore characteristics and hydrothermal conditions across NT, CT, ST-IR, and ST-BR. Results showed that the soil hydrothermal conditions, bulk density (BD), penetration resistance (PR), air capacity (AC), air permeability (AP), and available water capacity (AWC) of ST-IR were similar to those of CT ( P > 0.05). However, the hydrothermal conditions of ST-BR resembled those of NT ( P > 0.05). Furthermore, ST created two distinct macropore structures. ST-IR aligned with CT in macropore size distribution, pore morphology, and connectivity ( P > 0.05), showing high macroporosity and connectivity. The macropores of ST-IR were dominated by irregular, large-volume non-biopores, with higher compactness (CP, 1978), specific surface area (SA, 0.50), and fractal dimension (FD, 2.62), yet lower degree of anisotropy (DA, 0.26). In contrast, ST-BR converged with NT ( P > 0.05), demonstrating significantly lower macroporosity and connectivity than ST-IR and CT ( P < 0.05). The dominant pore type in the ST-BR and NT consisted of tubular biopores, with CP (97), SA (0.11), and FD (2.38) all significantly lower than those in ST-IR and CT ( P < 0.05), while DA (0.42) was significantly higher ( P < 0.05). Overall, ST integrates CT and NT in soil macropore structure and hydrothermal conditions, offering valuable insights into its role in black soil conservation and utilization.

title: Asset Management Strategy and Strategic Asset Management Plan for Motorways in Ireland
summary: Abstract Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) applies an integrated, whole-life asset management approach to ensure the sustainable, safe, and cost-effective stewardship of Ireland’s national road and light rail infrastructure. In respons
content: Abstract Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) applies an integrated, whole-life asset management approach to ensure the sustainable, safe, and cost-effective stewardship of Ireland’s national road and light rail infrastructure. In response to increasing climate risks, asset deterioration, and funding pressures, TII has developed an Asset Management Policy grounded in a risk-based, data-driven framework that optimises performance, minimises lifecycle costs, and enhances network resilience. Central to this framework is the Strategic Asset Management Plan (SAMP) for Ireland’s motorway network, which translates high-level goals into tactical and operational plans, guiding long-term planning and investment decisions. The strategy incorporates structured performance monitoring, evidence-based investment planning, and continuous stakeholder engagement to drive better decision-making. This paper examines the strategic model and demonstrates the benefits of structured long-term planning in supporting national transport objectives and European sustainability targets.

title: Cover crop species and termination timing influence corn production in the mid‐Atlantic
summary: Abstract Winter cover crops support sustainable agriculture in the US mid‐Atlantic Coastal Plain by addressing challenges related to low soil organic matter and high nitrogen (N) leaching potential. We evaluated the effects of cover crop ty
content: Abstract Winter cover crops support sustainable agriculture in the US mid‐Atlantic Coastal Plain by addressing challenges related to low soil organic matter and high nitrogen (N) leaching potential. We evaluated the effects of cover crop type (monoculture cereal rye [ Secale cereale L.] vs. rye–legume mixtures) and termination timing (preplant vs. at‐planting) on cover crop performance, soil inorganic N, and corn ( Zea mays L.) production. Experiments were conducted over three growing seasons (2019–2021) at two sites in Delaware, USA. The at‐planting termination maximized cover crop dry matter production (up to 7.02 Mg ha −1 ) and total N accumulation (up to 153 kg N ha −1 ), confirming the ecological benefit of delayed termination. Rye–legume mixtures consistently enhanced residue quality, producing lower C:N ratios (<25:1 for rye–hairy vetch) and accumulating significantly more N than the rye monoculture. However, planting cover crops presented trade‐offs for corn production. Cereal rye terminated at‐planting resulted in the highest C:N ratios (38.8:1 at Middletown in 2020), suggesting a high risk of N immobilization. Furthermore, at‐planting termination consistently led to a reduced final corn stand and resulted in a yield penalty compared to preplant termination in two site‐years at the irrigated Georgetown site. Despite these challenges, no cover crop treatment resulted in significant yield drag in all site‐years. In two of the six site‐year comparisons, cover crop treatments provided a significant yield benefit over the no‐cover crop control. Our results suggest that preplant termination of rye–legume mixtures can help maintain corn yield stability while integrating cover crops in mid‐Atlantic systems.

title: Green extraction technologies for coconut oil-based biodiesel production in the Philippines: A critical review
summary: Philippine biodiesel production relies almost entirely on coconut oil (CNO) as feedstock for coconut methyl ester (CME), a dependence increasingly strained by supply volatility.Recent efforts to raise blending mandates further were suspende
content: Philippine biodiesel production relies almost entirely on coconut oil (CNO) as feedstock for coconut methyl ester (CME), a dependence increasingly strained by supply volatility.Recent efforts to raise blending mandates further were suspended after adverse weather sharply reduced coconut output and drove up CNO prices.Expanding CME supply therefore requires new feedstocks or better recovery from the existing one.Oil palm diversification remains constrained by heavy import dependence, leaving CNO recovery the more immediate lever.This review critically evaluates four green extraction technologies -microwave-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, enzyme-assisted, and supercritical fluid extraction (SFE) -against conventional milling and against one another, then ranks each technology's Philippine readiness through an Analytic Hierarchy Process weighing evidence maturity, feasibility, oil quality, efficiency, and environmental criteria.SFE emerges as the clear front-runner, backed by the most direct coconut-specific evidence among the four and compositional advantages unmatched elsewhere, including pressure-tunable lauric acid enrichment exceeding 50% and consistently low peroxide values; the ranking holds under alternative weightings.Its principal barrier is economic rather than technical: high-pressure equipment demands capital investment ill-suited to a smallholder-dominated, low-unit-value commodity feedstock.Pairing SFE with in situ transesterification to consolidate extraction and conversion could offer a route to offset this cost, alongside pilot-scale validation on Philippine copra.Doing so could position CNO recovery as a durable lever for meeting the Philippines' stalled biodiesel blending targets.

title: Advanced Photovoltaic Technologies for Sustainable on Board Railways Services
summary: Abstract The integration of photovoltaic (PV) technologies on railway rolling stock has gained increasing attention as part of the broader transition toward sustainable and energy-efficient transport systems. While conventional on-board PV
content: Abstract The integration of photovoltaic (PV) technologies on railway rolling stock has gained increasing attention as part of the broader transition toward sustainable and energy-efficient transport systems. While conventional on-board PV installations have primarily targeted auxiliary loads rather than traction, recent advances in module efficiency, flexibility, and integration approaches open new perspectives for their application. This paper reviews the transition from early amorphous silicon projects to modern crystalline, CdTe, and CIS technologies, including emerging perovskite tandem cells. A feasibility study of the ETR 1000 high-speed train auxiliary compressed-air system indicates that modern crystalline modules outperform legacy baselines by factors of 2.8–3.9, while perovskite tandems could increase yields by a further 20–35%. These results demonstrate that on-board PV, supported by Building Attached and Building Integrated Photovoltaics integration strategies, is a viable solution for meeting auxiliary energy demands in both retrofitted and next-generation train designs.

title: Amine‐Mediated In Situ Oxygen Vacancy Generation in SnO 2 Nanocrystals for Selective CO 2 Photoreduction
summary: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction over tin dioxide (SnO 2 ) is promising for solar‐to‐chemical conversion, yet its efficiency is hindered by rapid charge recombination and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. Here, we develop an amine‐m
content: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction over tin dioxide (SnO 2 ) is promising for solar‐to‐chemical conversion, yet its efficiency is hindered by rapid charge recombination and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. Here, we develop an amine‐mediated in situ oxygen‐vacancy generation strategy, in which amine‐functionalized carbon nanotubes regulate SnO 2 crystallization to construct oxygen‐vacancy‐rich SnO 2 nanocrystals with strongly coupled SnO 2 /CNT interfaces. The interfacial amine groups coordinate with Sn precursors during growth, promoting oxygen vacancy formation while enhancing interfacial coupling and CO 2 adsorption through Lewis acid–base interactions. The generated oxygen vacancies modulate the local electronic structure, facilitate interfacial charge transfer, and regulate surface reaction pathways. The optimized OV‐SnO 2 @NCNT catalyst achieves a CO yield of 174.8 µmol g −1 , approximately 4.0 times higher than that of SnO 2 @OCNT, with a high CO selectivity of 82.9%. Spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal enhanced charge separation and carrier utilization efficiency enabled by the oxygen‐vacancy‐rich SnO 2 /CNT interface. Combined in situ FT‐IR measurements and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that oxygen vacancies promote CO 2 activation, stabilize key CO 2 ‐derived intermediates, and facilitate selective CO generation by regulating intermediate adsorption behavior. This work provides an interface‐directed defect‐engineering strategy for controllable oxygen vacancy construction and rational regulation of reaction pathways toward selective solar‐driven CO 2 conversion.

title: Global Non-CO2 Greenhouse Gas Emission Projections & Mitigation Potential — 2015-2050 — Download the Report
summary: Marginal abatement curves (MAC) can be downloaded as data annexes to the Global Mitigation of Non-CO2 Greenhouse Gases report. This data allows for improved understanding of the mitigation potential for non-CO2 sources, as well as inclusion
content: Marginal abatement curves (MAC) can be downloaded as data annexes to the Global Mitigation of Non-CO2 Greenhouse Gases report. This data allows for improved understanding of the mitigation potential for non-CO2 sources, as well as inclusion of non-CO2 greenhouse gas mitigation in economic modeling of multigas mitigation strategies. The full report at https://www.epa.gov/climatechange/economics/international.html.

title: The Role of Human Rights in Transforming Economies
summary: Abstract This chapter explores the role of human rights in reimagining our economies to prioritize the inter-connections between vital life-supporting systems and the well-being of people and the planet. The chapter illuminates the capacity
content: Abstract This chapter explores the role of human rights in reimagining our economies to prioritize the inter-connections between vital life-supporting systems and the well-being of people and the planet. The chapter illuminates the capacity of human rights to shift economic thought away from traditional narratives towards a framework centred on care, community, and ecological balance through the documentation and prevention of foreseeable negative rights impacts of fossil fuel-based economies (Morgera, 2025a). In addition, human rights analysis of the environmental and socio-cultural challenges of the rush towards energy transition minerals supports a paradigm shift in economic thought, by revealing—and at the same time requiring the moving away from—extractivist, colonial, and neo-colonial economic practices, that still privilege fossil fuels-related profits over the protection of life (Morgera, 2025b).

title: Combining User Needs and Predictive Control for Efficient User-Centric Energy Management Systems
summary: Abstract The driving range of electric vehicles (EVs) is heavily influenced by thermal comfort settings, often leading to inconsistent range predictions and user “range anxiety”. While technical energy management systems exist, aligning the
content: Abstract The driving range of electric vehicles (EVs) is heavily influenced by thermal comfort settings, often leading to inconsistent range predictions and user “range anxiety”. While technical energy management systems exist, aligning them with actual user behaviour and subjective comfort needs is rarely addressed holistically. This paper presents a novel methodology from the EFFEREST research project, bridging human factors research and advanced control engineering to develop a Holistic User-Centric Energy Management System Control (HUC). First, we detail an interview study that identified specific EV driver pain points, such as “overnight” range drops and non-transparent climate automation. Based on these insights, we introduce the HUC framework. This architecture utilizes AI-enhanced system design and Adaptive Digital Twins (ADTs) to dynamically balance powertrain efficiency with personalized thermal comfort. Finally, we outline a comprehensive multi-platform validation methodology. Utilizing virtual demonstrators, thermal test benches, and a physical vehicle demonstrator equipped with a thermal manikin, this setup is designed to quantitatively assess energy savings and comfort improvements against state-of-the-art EV baselines.

title: Evaluation of deep learning models for optimised accuracy-emission trade-offs in the early detection of grain discolouration disease in rice
summary: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) constitutes a primary food source for a significant proportion of the global population and its grain quality directly influences market value and consumer acceptance. Grain discolouration (GD), largely attributable t
content: Rice (Oryza sativa L.) constitutes a primary food source for a significant proportion of the global population and its grain quality directly influences market value and consumer acceptance. Grain discolouration (GD), largely attributable to seed-borne pathogens and occasionally to insect infestation, poses a critical challenge by compromising visual quality and reducing commercial grade. This study evaluated the performance of advanced deep learning models for automated detection and classification of discoloured rice grains, incorporating criteria related to predictive accuracy, computational requirements and environmental sustainability. Among the assessed architectures, DenseNet121 exhibited the highest accuracy (98 %), followed by MobileNet (96 %) and MobileNetV2 (92 %), each demonstrating strong precision, recall and F1 scores. In contrast, VGG19 recorded comparatively lower accuracy (84 %). Computational and energy analysis revealed that DenseNet121, MobileNet and Xception required shorter training durations and lower computational resources, whereas MobileNetV2 and InceptionV3 were comparatively resource-intensive. Notably, MobileNet demonstrated superior energy efficiency, consuming 19.03 watts and generating 0.00952 kg carbon dioxide (CO₂), whereas InceptionV3 consumed 377.27 watts and emitted 0.18864 kg CO₂. To facilitate comprehensive model prioritisation, the technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) was employed, identifying MobileNet as the optimal model when considering performance, efficiency and environmental impact. The findings highlight the potential applicability of lightweight deep learning architectures, particularly MobileNet and DenseNet121, in real-time rice grading and sorting systems, supporting sustainable post-harvest management, improving grain quality assurance and mitigating seed-borne pathogen dissemination.

title: Air-Based Hazards
summary: The hazards originate from natural sources like volcanic emissions and human activities, such as industrial processes and transportation. This chapter provides an overview of air-based hazards, encompassing risks associated with air quality
content: The hazards originate from natural sources like volcanic emissions and human activities, such as industrial processes and transportation. This chapter provides an overview of air-based hazards, encompassing risks associated with air quality, composition, and behavior in diverse environments. Examples of air-based hazards encompass a range of issues including air pollution, which can lead to health problems for both people and wildlife; accidental chemical releases that pose risks to human health and the environment; airborne biological agents that may cause diseases or allergic reactions; radon gas seepage, which increases the risk of lung cancer; indoor air quality concerns that can result in discomfort and health problems; and the long-term effects of climate change driven by the buildup of greenhouse gases. Mitigating these hazards involves adopting pollution control technologies, cleaner energy sources, improved industrial practices, regulations, air-quality monitoring, and public awareness initiatives to address risks and promote preventive measures.

title: “Every professional is a climate professional”: a framework for climate responsibility in practice
summary: Professionals are an important class of actors often overlooked in efforts to address climate change. Across fields such as health, law, education, the built environment, and media, they combine specialised knowledge, institutional authorit
content: Professionals are an important class of actors often overlooked in efforts to address climate change. Across fields such as health, law, education, the built environment, and media, they combine specialised knowledge, institutional authority, and public credibility, giving them a distinctive capacity to translate sustainability science into practice, reshape organisational systems, and coordinate climate action within their domains. This paper conceptualises professionals as a distinct class of climate actors and develops a generalisable framework for how their expertise, ethical values, and institutional authority can generate systemic change. We treat the professional role as a socially constructed position, formed first in higher education and then through accreditation and institutional norms that can unintentionally reinforce unsustainable practices. Universities and the bodies that accredit their programmes are therefore central sites for forming climate-ready professionals. Building on this, we set out a framework for enabling climate-aligned practice, organised around three interrelated stages: crisis translation, which frames climate change as integral to a profession's mission; ethical activation, which grounds climate responsibility in professional values; and institutional pathways, which shape how climate action is enabled or constrained by professional bodies, training regimes, and organisational systems. These stages operate across multiple levels, from individual practitioners to professional associations and the wider policy context. The analysis turns on a central tension. Professionals hold both the capacity to catalyse meaningful climate action and the potential to reproduce unsustainable structures. Reorienting professional norms, institutions, and practices is therefore essential if their expertise is to contribute to climate mitigation and adaptation.

title: Conservation areas in the eastern Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt: a dynamic conceptual framework under land-use change
summary: Summary The Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt is a biogeographical province, and its eastern sub-province faces intense pressures from land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). This study integrates a systematic conservation planning approach, spec
content: Summary The Trans-Mexican Volcanic Belt is a biogeographical province, and its eastern sub-province faces intense pressures from land-use and land-cover change (LULCC). This study integrates a systematic conservation planning approach, species distribution models and LULCC projections to identify areas that facilitate the conservation of endemic biodiversity under a dynamic conceptual framework. We selected 13 species of amphibians and mammals as surrogates, obtained their geographical distributions and analysed the distributional patterns of species richness and rarity, which showed significant concentrations in volcanic mountain systems. Historical and future LULCC models indicated a continued expansion of rainfed agriculture, potentially reaching 70% of the study area by 2050, alongside a severe reduction in temperate forest. Currently, 65% of the potential habitat of endemic species and 43% of the potential habitat of geographically rare species are affected. Under pessimistic future scenarios, losses could exceed 95%. Although the priority conservation areas identified are relatively continuous core areas at present, future projections showed considerable fragmentation. We propose a possible dynamic conservation network linking permanent nodes with dynamic nodes and temporary ecological corridors according to ecological, seasonal or anthropogenic pressures. Furthermore, this approach integrates ecological, socioeconomic and governance dimensions to reconcile conservation with sustainable practices in highly transformed landscapes.

title: Advances in UAV-Based Methane Emission Monitoring: Sensors, Sampling Geometry, and Quantification
summary: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are one key platforms for monitoring methane due to their flexible deployment with spatial scales between ground-based sensors and crewed aircraft This review synthesises research on UAV sensing technologies,
content: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are one key platforms for monitoring methane due to their flexible deployment with spatial scales between ground-based sensors and crewed aircraft This review synthesises research on UAV sensing technologies, flight and sampling strategies, quantification methods, and validation practices. It finds that quantitative performance depends on the combined choice of sensor, platform, flight geometry, wind measurement, and estimation method. The key UAV-deployable sensor categories are contrasted based on sensitivity, response, payload restrictions, and field of use, which includes open-path tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) and closed-path TDLAS, quantum cascade laser absorption spectroscopy (QCLAS), active AirCore, non-dispersive infrared (NDIR), and thermal imaging sensors. Multirotor UAVs support repeated transects and vertical plume sampling, while fixed-wing platforms are primarily suited to broader-area screening. Mass-balance and Gaussian inversion methods can estimate emission rates, but their results are sensitive to wind uncertainty and incomplete plume coverage. Tracer-based approaches can reduce direct reliance on wind measurements when tracer and methane plumes disperse together. Controlled-release studies also show that small average bias can coexist with substantial errors in individual flights. Across sectors, methods are more developed for oil and gas facilities, landfills, and coal-mine ventilation shafts than for agriculture and wastewater. The literature reviewed identified no dedicated peer-reviewed UAV methane quantification study at an active surface coal mine. Wider use of UAVs for emissions assessment will require survey designs matched to source characteristics, stronger field validation, and more consistent uncertainty reporting.

title: Biomass and carbon estimation for three browsable native shrubs in New Zealand
source: New Zealand journal of forestry science
summary: Background: New Zealand’s native shrublands have declined markedly over the past 180 years, yet shrub species on hill-country farms provide multiple co-benefits, including slope stabilisation, biodiversity enhancement, carbon sequestration,
content: Background: New Zealand’s native shrublands have declined markedly over the past 180 years, yet shrub species on hill-country farms provide multiple co-benefits, including slope stabilisation, biodiversity enhancement, carbon sequestration, and potential for supplementary fodder. Despite this potential, robust allometric models for estimating biomass and carbon stocks remain limited, particularly for native shrubs with forage value. Methods: Above-ground biomass (AGB) was estimated by destructively sampling 54 individual shrubs of three native shrub species (Coprosma robusta Raoul, Pittosporum crassifolium Banks et Sol. ex A.Cunn. and Melicytus ramiflorus J.R.Forst. & G.Forst.) across two contrasting sites in New Zealand (Limestone Downs and Massey University). Species-specific, site-specific, and generalized allometric models were developed for foliage, branch, and stem biomass using both stem diameter (D) and height (H) as predictors under ordinary least squares (OLS). AGB models were additionally evaluated using both OLS and seemingly unrelated regression (SUR). Carbon stocks were estimated from best-performing models and projected over a 10-year period using growth functions. Results: Species-specific models outperformed site-specific and generalized models. Bivariate models incorporating both D and H consistently produced stronger fits than univariate models. OLS performed comparably to, or better than, SUR under the available sample sizes. Site effects were evident, with Limestone Downs generally supporting higher biomass and CO₂ stocks than the Massey University site. Estimated stand-level mean annual increment (MAI) ranged from 0.8 to 16.5 t CO₂ ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹, with several species–site combinations exceeding the New Zealand ETS indigenous forest default value of 6.5 t CO₂ ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹. Conclusions: The developed allometric models provide a useful basis for estimating biomass and carbon stocks in New Zealand native shrubs, with direct relevance to emissions accounting and integration into steep hill-country farming systems.

title: The Climate Effects of Transport Emissions: Models and Data to Support the Development of Mitigation Strategies
summary: Abstract Emissions from land-based transport, aviation and shipping significantly contribute to climate change. In addition to CO 2 , the emissions include short-lived species, such as nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. These short-liv
content: Abstract Emissions from land-based transport, aviation and shipping significantly contribute to climate change. In addition to CO 2 , the emissions include short-lived species, such as nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. These short-lived emission components not only affect air quality but also have important effects on the climate. This conference contribution highlights results of comprehensive global chemistry-climate model simulations that account for the transport-induced climate effects of all short-lived emission components, complemented by calculations of the corresponding CO 2 effect. For the first time, all transport-induced climate effects have been quantified in a self-consistent manner, not only for present-day conditions but also for multiple future scenarios. Following the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) developed for the sixth IPCC assessment report, these global scenarios span a wide range of emission strengths and compositions. The results confirm the important contribution of the non-CO 2 climate effects for all transport sectors at present and reveal a large significance of these effects in all considered future cases, which is of high relevance for climate protection and environmental policy. For further application of these results, we present concepts to consider both CO 2 and non-CO 2 effects when assessing the climate benefits of emission mitigation strategies in the transport sectors.

title: Predicting food waste from dynamic inconsistency
summary: Household food waste imposes substantial economic and environmental costs, yet its behavioral determinants remain imperfectly understood. Because food consumption unfolds over multiple stages, it creates scope for dynamically inconsistent c
content: Household food waste imposes substantial economic and environmental costs, yet its behavioral determinants remain imperfectly understood. Because food consumption unfolds over multiple stages, it creates scope for dynamically inconsistent choices that may turn good intentions into waste. We investigate this relationship using a nationally representative survey from Germany that combines targeted measures of food purchasing, consumption, and waste with individual present-bias parameters elicited from monetary intertemporal trade-off questions. More present-biased individuals waste significantly more food: a 10% increase in dynamic inconsistency is associated with roughly 2% more waste. This relationship is robust across specifications, replicated using a self-reported procrastination proxy, and stable several weeks later in a second survey wave. We also identify and empirically validate the mechanism linking present bias to food waste: dynamically inconsistent individuals are more likely to deviate from their own consumption intentions, and these deviations are strongly predictive of food waste. Our findings identify present bias as a systematic and previously overlooked driver of avoidable household food waste, suggesting that food policies need to address behavior along the full consumption chain.

title: STRATEJİK PLANLAR ÜZERİNDEN TÜRKİYE’DE İKLİM DEĞİŞİKLİĞİ OKUMASI: BÜYÜKŞEHİR BELEDİYELERİ ÖRNEĞİ (2020–2024)
source: Pamukkale University Journal of Social Sciences Institute
summary: İklim değişikliği, atmosferik, ekolojik ve sosyoekonomik etkileri nedeniyle yerel ve merkezi hükümetin gündeminde yer almaktadır. Yerel yönetimler iklim değişikliği ile mücadelede ve iklim değişikliğinin sosyal ve ekonomik etkilerini azaltm
content: İklim değişikliği, atmosferik, ekolojik ve sosyoekonomik etkileri nedeniyle yerel ve merkezi hükümetin gündeminde yer almaktadır. Yerel yönetimler iklim değişikliği ile mücadelede ve iklim değişikliğinin sosyal ve ekonomik etkilerini azaltmak amacıyla çeşitli görevler üstlenmektedir. Belediyeler nüfusun yoğunlaştığı, üretim ve tüketim faaliyetlerinin gerçekleştirildiği kentsel mekanlardır. Enerji tüketimi, hava kirliliği, ulaşım faaliyetleri ve atık yönetimi gibi alanların planlanması ve yönetilmesinde belediyeler yetkili ve sorumlu kuruluşlardır. Bu makale, Türkiye’deki 30 büyükşehir belediyesinin 2020–2024 dönemine ait stratejik planlarını iklim değişikliğiyle ilgili hedef ve eylemler açısından doküman analizi tekniğiyle incelemektedir. Bulgular, iklim değişikliğinin çoğu belediye tarafından kabul edilen bir mesele olduğunu, ancak planlarda somut ve uygulanabilir politikaların sınırlı kaldığını ortaya koymaktadır. Belediyeler arasında konuya yaklaşım biçimlerinin çeşitlilik göstermesi, yerel düzeydeki kurumsal kapasite, stratejik yönelim ve iklim politikası farklarını yansıtmaktadır. Bu çalışma, yerel iklim politikalarının stratejik planlara yansımasını inceleyerek kent düzeyinde iklim yönetişimine katkı sağlamayı hedeflemektedir.

title: Nanoscale-enabled cross-scale chemical sensing for underwater monitoring and beyond
summary: In aquatic environments, such as oceans, lakes, and rivers, molecular-level chemical reactions and the distribution of chemical species are related to global environmental changes through various biogeochemical processes. Understanding this
content: In aquatic environments, such as oceans, lakes, and rivers, molecular-level chemical reactions and the distribution of chemical species are related to global environmental changes through various biogeochemical processes. Understanding this relationship requires addressing cross-scale challenges at two distinct levels: overcoming interfacial physical constraints, such as Debye screening in high-salinity waters, at the sensing level and bridging local microscale measurements with macroscale environmental dynamics at the observational level. In this paper, we describe sensing technologies that can enable cross-scale sensing in aquatic environments. Here, we focus on nanoscale interfacial sensing and molecular recognition technologies, as well as lab-on-a-chip technologies for in situ measurements including power-efficient pumping technologies. Additionally, underwater observation platforms that link the local chemical sensing and global processes are overviewed. Beyond environmental applications, these sensing technologies offer a cross-disciplinary approach that can be extended to analyze biological systems facing similar physicochemical constraints.

title: External Environmental Audits and Supply‐Chain Carbon Monitoring: Cross‐Country Evidence on Corporate Environmental Accountability
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines external energy audits and reported supply‐chain carbon monitoring using 12,154 energy‐monitoring establishments in 37 countries from the 2019‐coded World Bank Enterprise Survey cross‐section. Audit is associate
content: ABSTRACT This study examines external energy audits and reported supply‐chain carbon monitoring using 12,154 energy‐monitoring establishments in 37 countries from the 2019‐coded World Bank Enterprise Survey cross‐section. Audit is associated with an 8.1‐percentage‐point higher monitoring probability after establishment, governance, country, and industry controls. The questionnaire limits monitoring to the chain up to establishment output; it does not measure complete Scope 3 accounting or emissions reduction. Positive associations persist under alternative estimators and wild‐cluster inference. Customer requirements, environmental managers, and strategy strengthen the association under false‐discovery and family‐wise corrections. Practice‐index associations remain positive after excluding energy‐management content that may overlap with audit. The decomposition is consistent with the proposed monitoring pathway, while cross‐sectional timing and instrument strength warrant an associational interpretation. These findings clarify how external assessment relates to value‐chain information collection and reported environmental practices.

title: Skills Supply and Demand Mismatch in the Offshore Renewable Energy Sector in Europe
summary: Abstract The Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) sector in Europe experiences continuous growth, given its criticality in supporting the vision to decarbonize many economic sectors, and Europe becoming the first carbon-neutral continent by 2050
content: Abstract The Offshore Renewable Energy (ORE) sector in Europe experiences continuous growth, given its criticality in supporting the vision to decarbonize many economic sectors, and Europe becoming the first carbon-neutral continent by 2050. Most ORE capacities are now concentrated in the North Sea, but new markets are also emerging (e.g. in the Mediterranean region), with the sector being characterized by a fast growth trajectory. Critical element to this, is the human factor with the sector requiring highly competent personnel capable of adhering to the challenges of the marine environment and of the projects and technologies themselves. To this end, a skills intelligence analysis was conducted, focusing on key European countries assessing both the skills demand, through an online job vacancies analysis, and the skills supply by identifying and examining relevant educational and training programmes on offer. Results enabled to define existing gaps and shortages, and propose targeted recommendations for addressing them.

title: Jet fuel production from multiple feedstocks: Technological pathways, catalytic breakthroughs, techno-economic feasibility, challenges, and future perspectives
source: Journal of King Saud University - Science
summary: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is a key strategy in the aviation industry to cut carbon emissions and reduce global environmental impacts. This review examines jet fuel production using various potential feedstocks, along with their corres
content: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is a key strategy in the aviation industry to cut carbon emissions and reduce global environmental impacts. This review examines jet fuel production using various potential feedstocks, along with their corresponding production, including hydro-processed esters and fatty acids (HEFA), Fischer-Tropsch (FT) synthesis, alcohol-to-jet (ATJ), catalytic hydrothermolysis (CH), and algal lipid-based fuels. It also discusses technologies for creating synthetic jet fuels in line with the American Society for Testing and Materials standards (ASTM D7566, 2024). The HEFA-based fuels, made by hydrotreating triglycerides from oil-rich biomass, are feasible in the near term with lifecycle emissions reductions of over 80%. Catalysts (such as cobalt and iron) are common for FT, catalysts (Pt, Pd, Ni, and Mo) show excellent activity in HEFA selectivity. HZSM-5 is cost-effective for ATJ. In future, efforts between industries and government policy are required to make bio-jet fuel a viable, large-scale solution for aviation decarbonization. GRAPHICAL ABSTRACT

title: Infrastructure for Automated Road Transport: Strategic Perspectives on Digitalisation, Governance, and Mobility Futures
summary: Abstract This paper explores the evolving responsibilities of infrastructure managers and authorities in the context of increasingly automated vehicles, from the perspective of Norwegian road authorities. As automation becomes more prevalen
content: Abstract This paper explores the evolving responsibilities of infrastructure managers and authorities in the context of increasingly automated vehicles, from the perspective of Norwegian road authorities. As automation becomes more prevalent in mixed traffic environments, infrastructure systems face new demands, both physical and digital. Through a scenario-based methodology, the study gathers insights from road owners, infrastructure managers, and regional authorities to identify key challenges and opportunities for the governance of automated transport. The findings highlight fragmented governance structures and the urgent need for coherent national strategies to support collaboration and capacity-building. Infrastructure must be strategically prioritised, with a focus on high-impact corridors and real-time information. Participants emphasise the importance of resilient digital ecosystems, robust cybersecurity measures, particularly in northern regions, and legal clarity around data ownership and system interoperability. Funding models must evolve to reflect the societal value of automation. Considering climate stressors and geopolitical uncertainties, the paper argues for infrastructure planning that not only accommodates technological change but also advances broader goals of safety, sustainability, and social equity. In sum, the study provides implications for governance stakeholders at the national and regional level based on the insights from the workshop participants.

title: Combustion Chemistry of NH3/CH3OH/H2 Blends
summary: Abstract This work aims to study the impact of H2 and CH3OH on NH3 conversion over a wide range of operating conditions, focusing on the influence of temperature, oxygen excess ratio (λ), NH3/H2 (α), and NH3/CH3OH (β). Experiments are condu
content: Abstract This work aims to study the impact of H2 and CH3OH on NH3 conversion over a wide range of operating conditions, focusing on the influence of temperature, oxygen excess ratio (λ), NH3/H2 (α), and NH3/CH3OH (β). Experiments are conducted in a quartz flow reactor at atmospheric pressure, and outlet species are quantified using a micro gas chromatograph and continuous gas analyzers. NH3 oxidation shows strong sensitivity to both oxygen concentration and fuel mixture ratio. For λ ≤ 1, NH3 conversion is significantly inhibited when CH3OH is present at concentrations comparable to that of NH3 (β ≥ 1). High H2 concentrations promote recycling of NH2 radicals back to NH3, while CH3OH inhibits NH3 oxidation through interactions with NH2, additional H2 formation, and competition for the radical pool. Under fuel-lean conditions, higher OH concentrations mitigate these effects and shift NH3 oxidation to lower temperatures. CH3OH oxidation is dominated by hydrogen abstraction, mainly producing CH2OH radicals, and its inhibitory effect decreases as the NH3/CH3OH ratio increases (β > 1). H2 exhibits a dual role, contributing to the radical pool and promoting oxidation, while inhibiting NH3 conversion at high concentrations through NH2 recycling back to NH3. This effect also decreases under fuel-lean conditions. Overall, NH3 oxidation follows highly branched pathways strongly governed by oxygen availability, whereas CH3OH and H2 exhibit simpler pathways that are less dependent on O2.

title: A method for quantifying the upfront carbon footprint of urban densification in Texas through 2050
summary: Urbanization is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change projects that urban areas may grow by up to 211% globally by 2050. Embodied emissions make up a considerable portion of the t
content: Urbanization is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change projects that urban areas may grow by up to 211% globally by 2050. Embodied emissions make up a considerable portion of the total carbon footprint of urban areas. This study explores the relationship between urban densification and its upfront carbon footprint in Texas through 2050, using a novel method that combines land cover change projections, building stock analysis, and carbon sequestration quantification. Three densification trajectories–Sprawl, Business as Usual, and Built-Up–were used to demonstrate the method's ability to quantify upfront carbon footprint for a range of plausible urbanization outcomes. The analysis found that embodied emissions from building materials made up 71% of the upfront carbon footprint in Built-Up scenarios but only 40% in Sprawl scenarios, where lost carbon sequestration from the conversion of fields and forests to buildings and roads was the most significant factor. The central finding of this study is that high levels of urban densification lead to a larger upfront carbon footprint. Dense urban cores reduce natural land conversion but at the expense of increased emissions from the construction materials required for vertical development. Therefore, urban densification comes with a tradeoff between land-carbon effects and embodied emissions from buildings that should be taken into account in development of urbanization policy. Importantly, that same densification might lead to substantial avoided carbon emissions from more efficient operation and reduced transportation distances, but operational analysis was beyond the scope of this study.

title: Redefining Decoupled Water Electrolysis as an Integrated Hydrogen‐Carrier Platform
summary: ABSTRACT The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integr
content: ABSTRACT The hydrogen economy is commonly organized around four separate tasks: production, storage, transport, and release. This Perspective redefines decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) as a framework in which these functions can be integrated within a single electrochemical redox loop. By using a proton‐coupled redox mediator to decouple hydrogen and oxygen evolution in time and space, DWE stores hydrogen equivalents in a charged mediator phase and releases H 2 electrochemically or catalytically at the point of use. This architecture shifts part of hydrogen logistics from pressure‐ or temperature‐intensive processes toward ambient‐condition electrochemical operation. DWE can therefore be viewed not merely as an alternative electrolyzer architecture, but as an integrated hydrogen‐carrier platform. Within this broader framework, this Perspective focuses primarily on solution‐phase proton‐coupled mediators because their charged inventories can function as transportable liquid‐phase carriers. Although current solution‐phase DWE mediators remain disadvantaged in gravimetric capacity relative to ammonia and liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs), their system‐level value lies in ambient‐condition storage, low‐temperature on‐site H 2 release, independent scaling of power (electrolyzer stack) and energy capacity (mediator inventory), and flexible coupling to intermittent renewable electricity. We therefore propose carrier‐relevant benchmarks including full‐system capacity, storage‐and‐release efficiency, mediator retention, gas quality, delivered cost, and closed‐loop logistics.

title: High recycled aggregate replacement in self-compacting concrete: Durability across carbonation, chloride transport and water ingress
summary: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the durability of self-compacting concrete (SCC) incorporating 50% and 100% recycled concrete aggregate (RCA), while maintaining a constant nominal W/C of 0.475 and adjusting the superplasticizer dosage to pres
content: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the durability of self-compacting concrete (SCC) incorporating 50% and 100% recycled concrete aggregate (RCA), while maintaining a constant nominal W/C of 0.475 and adjusting the superplasticizer dosage to preserve self-compacting behaviour. Durability was assessed through carbonation, electrical resistivity, chloride migration, low-pressure water absorption and SEM–EDX analysis. RCA incorporation produced only a moderate increase in carbonation rate, while electrical resistivity remained within a narrow range for all mixtures. Chloride transport showed a regime-dependent response: both RCA mixtures exhibited lower non-steady-state diffusion coefficients and longer passage times than the control, whereas the steady-state coefficient remained comparable for RCA50 but increased for RCA100. Low-pressure water uptake was slower in both RCA mixtures. SEM–EDX observations revealed increased heterogeneity with RCA content but no severe interfacial degradation. Overall, the adopted SCC mix-design strategy enabled high RCA replacement ratios without a proportional loss of durability, with RCA50 exhibiting a favourable combination of the measured durability-related properties.

title: Decarbonizing Portugal’s Taxi Fleet via Public Incentives: An Empirical Policy Evaluation
summary: Abstract Urban taxi fleets represent a high-impact segment for transport decarbonisation due to their intensive urban operation and high annual mileage. In Portugal, the Public Transport Fund (PTF), managed by the Institute for Mobility and
content: Abstract Urban taxi fleets represent a high-impact segment for transport decarbonisation due to their intensive urban operation and high annual mileage. In Portugal, the Public Transport Fund (PTF), managed by the Institute for Mobility and Transport (IMT, I.P.), has provided targeted incentives for taxi electrification since 2018, combining subsidies for electric vehicle (EV) acquisition, scrappage of fossil-fuel vehicles, and co-financing of charging infrastructure. Between 2018 and 2025, 378 applications were approved, supporting 378 electric taxis, 96 vehicle scrappages, and 227 charging systems, with total public disbursements of approximately €2.54 million. Using a conservative baseline of 6.0 tCO 2 per conventional taxi per year, cumulative avoided tailpipe emissions for 2018–2025 are estimated at approximately 2,000 tCO 2 eq, with accelerated adoption scenarios projecting cumulative savings exceeding 8,000 tCO 2 eq by 2030. The article evaluates programme uptake, environmental effectiveness, financial efficiency, and international positioning. Results indicate accelerating uptake since 2023 but still limited fleet penetration relative to Portugal’s ~12,000 licensed taxis. While infrastructure deployment has progressed significantly, cost-effectiveness remains above international benchmarks, reflecting the early-stage scale of the programme. Policy implications highlight the importance of scaling incentives, integrating regulatory measures such as ZE-only licensing, and aligning national support schemes with EU climate and transport frameworks.

title: Colored Cooler With Sandwich Structure for Sub‐Ambient Daytime Radiative Cooling
summary: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling offers a sustainable cooling strategy by simultaneously reflecting solar radiation and emitting thermal radiation through the mid‐infrared transparent window. However, the coolers that achieve sub‐
content: ABSTRACT Passive daytime radiative cooling offers a sustainable cooling strategy by simultaneously reflecting solar radiation and emitting thermal radiation through the mid‐infrared transparent window. However, the coolers that achieve sub‐ambient daytime cooling typically appear white or silver, limiting their use in applications where colored appearances are required. Herein, we report a colored cooler (CoCooler) with a sandwich structure that decouples visible coloration from near‐infrared solar heating. The CoCooler integrates a transparent polydimethylsiloxane emission layer, an inorganic‐colorant‐containing layer, an isolation layer, and a porous radiative cooling layer. The sandwich structure enables selective visible absorption for color generation, strong near‐infrared reflection to minimize solar heating, and broadband mid‐infrared emission for radiative heat dissipation. The red, yellow, and blue CoCoolers exhibit vivid color while maintaining high solar reflectance of 90.70%, 91.58%, and 89.89%, respectively, and high mid‐infrared emissivity of 0.982, 0.983, and 0.982. Under outdoor sunlight, the CoCoolers achieve sub‐ambient temperature drops of 3.7°C–5.4°C, and are 33.3°C–42.2°C cooler than the commercial‐colored paints with similar chromaticity. Building simulations further estimate an average energy savings of 23.8 MJ·m −2 and a CO 2 emission reduction of 11.7 kg·m −2 ·yr −1 . This work provides a practical strategy for colored radiative cooling surfaces toward energy‐efficient building.

title: Global Transition to Renewable Energy
summary: In recent decades, the imperative to tackle climate change and mitigate environmental degradation has sparked an intense global transition towards renewable energy sources. This transition represents a profound shift in the processes of ene
content: In recent decades, the imperative to tackle climate change and mitigate environmental degradation has sparked an intense global transition towards renewable energy sources. This transition represents a profound shift in the processes of energy production and consumption, driven by the recognition of the finite nature of fossil fuels and the urgent necessity to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Renewable energy, derived from sources such as sunlight, wind, water, and geothermal heat, offers a promising alternative that not only diminishes our reliance on environmentally harmful fuels but also promises a greater sustainable and resilient energy future. This makes it imperative to explore the motivations, challenges, and opportunities inherent in the global transition to renewable energy, emphasizing its significance in shaping the trajectory of our planet and humanity in this century.

title: On Implementing a Rail Sectoral Skills Strategy Towards a Single European Railway Area of Skills
summary: Abstract The rail sector is instrumental in achieving Europe’s sustainability goals, but is facing significant skills and workforce challenges, such as an aging workforce, a shortage of new entrants, and the need for new skills. The ERASMUS
content: Abstract The rail sector is instrumental in achieving Europe’s sustainability goals, but is facing significant skills and workforce challenges, such as an aging workforce, a shortage of new entrants, and the need for new skills. The ERASMUS+ project STAFFER, “Skill Training Alliance For the Future European Rail system”, concluded in October 2024, has been the first Blueprint on skills of the rail sector and has involved 31 full partners and 15 associated partners from 13 EU countries. This paper presents the results of the project and the identified actions to reach a Single European Railway Area of Skills. A dedicated skills strategy was defined aimed at “attracting and upskilling a qualified workforce for a smart and sustainable rail sector in Europe”. It is organised into three main pillars: “Employability, attractiveness and diversity”; “Provision of state-of-the-art and future-proof education and training for the rail sector”; “European mindsets for the European railway area”. The action plan includes more than 50 specific activities divided into five fields of actions and a roadmap for its implementation has been defined. STAFFER skills strategy and action plan are currently under implementation within the follow-up ERASMUS+ project SERAS “Single European Railway Area of Skills” started in December 2025.

title: Physicochemical interpretation of CO2 adsorption mechanisms in N-Doped mesoporous carbons via multilayer perceptron neural network
summary: Abstract Developing efficient CO 2 capture technologies requires both advanced adsorbents and robust predictive models to decode their complex adsorption mechanisms. This study evaluates nitrogen-doped mesoporous carbons (MCNs) synthesized
content: Abstract Developing efficient CO 2 capture technologies requires both advanced adsorbents and robust predictive models to decode their complex adsorption mechanisms. This study evaluates nitrogen-doped mesoporous carbons (MCNs) synthesized via a solvent-free mechanochemical route using a physics-informed Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) neural network. To overcome the limitations of traditional empirical models, our MLP architecture replaces standard mathematical activation functions with statistical physics-derived theoretical expressions. This approach enables highly accurate predictions of CO 2 adsorption isotherms R 2 >0.9998 while breaking the “black-box” nature of artificial intelligence to allow direct physicochemical interpretation. The MLP successfully decoupled the capture mechanisms, revealing that while undoped carbon relies on parallel multi-anchorage in micropores (64% Type I contribution), nitrogen doping structurally shifts the preference toward high-affinity monomolecular adsorption (74.4% Type I). Ultimately, this work validates physics-informed MLPs as robust, interpretable tools for the mechanistic evaluation and inverse design of high-performance carbon mitigation materials.

title: Next-generation precision fermentation: integrating engineered cell factories, bioprocess intensification, and smart bioprocessing
summary: Precision fermentation (PF) uses engineered microbial cell factories to manufacture defined products under controlled bioprocess conditions. In this review, PF is treated operationally as the integration of engineered hosts with metabolic e
content: Precision fermentation (PF) uses engineered microbial cell factories to manufacture defined products under controlled bioprocess conditions. In this review, PF is treated operationally as the integration of engineered hosts with metabolic engineering and process control, while traditional food fermentations without engineered production strains are excluded. The field now spans pharmaceuticals, food ingredients, industrial enzymes, specialty chemicals, and biopolymers, but commercial translation remains constrained by biological non-linearity, substrate and feedstock variability, mass-transfer limitations at scale, downstream recovery, and the cost gap with incumbent processes. This mini-review examines five connected layers: engineered microbial chassis; design build test learn (DBTL) and multi-omics-guided metabolic engineering; bioreactor intensification; Process Analytical Technology (PAT), soft sensors and AI-enabled control; and techno-economic and life cycle assessment. Quantitative case studies illustrate both the progress and the remaining scale-up gaps, including semi-synthetic artemisinin, recombinant insulin, lactic acid, succinic acid, QS-21, and polyhydroxyalkanoates. The central argument is that the next phase of PF will depend less on isolated improvements in strain performance than on coordinated integration of strain design, intensified operation, real-time process understanding, and rigorous economic and environmental assessment. This integration is essential for translating laboratory performance into reproducible, scalable, and commercially credible biomanufacturing. KEY POINTS: PF requires integration of cell-factory engineering with scalable bioprocessing rather than optimisation of any single layer. DBTL and multi-omics improve strain performance, but laboratory titres do not guarantee industrial scalability. Bioprocess intensification and real-time monitoring are required to convert strain performance into robust production. PAT, soft sensors, and AI strengthen process control when supported by reliable online data and qualified models. TEA and LCA should be integrated early to filter commercial and environmental feasibility before scale-up.

title: Influence of urban spatial structure and land-use distribution on residential and transport emissions in European urban settlements
summary: Abstract While urban spatial structure and land-use distribution play an important role in shaping greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, their sector-specific effects remain insufficiently understood in comparative urban studies. This study devel
content: Abstract While urban spatial structure and land-use distribution play an important role in shaping greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, their sector-specific effects remain insufficiently understood in comparative urban studies. This study develops a scale-independent comparative framework to examine how functional land-use distribution, spatial configuration, alternative density representations, and broader economic and climatic context jointly shape per capita residential and transport emissions across 104 European cities. Using city-level GHG inventories reported to the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) and harmonized CORINE Land Cover (CLC) data, residential and transport emissions are analyzed separately through a grouped regression framework that systematically compares alternative variable combinations and identifies supported models using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The results show that residential emissions are explained by multiple structural regimes, indicating that similar per capita outcomes can arise from different combinations of land-use distribution and urban spatial structure, whereas transport emissions converge on a single dominant regime reflecting a more stable configuration of land-use specialization, urban spatial structure, and population density. Across the supported models, 5 of the 21-landscape metrics evaluated were significant for residential emissions and 3 for transport emissions. The findings demonstrate that urban emissions emerge from integrated structural configurations rather than isolated spatial indicators, underscoring the need for multivariate and sector-sensitive approaches in comparative urban climate research.

title: Neglecting N2O Emissions Underestimates the Soil Greenhouse Gas Budgets of Rewetted Tropical Peatlands
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This deposit contains the manuscript and Supporting Information for “Neglecting N2O Emissions Underestimates the Soil Greenhouse Gas Budgets of Rewetted Tropical Peatlands.” The study examines soil carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and n
content: This deposit contains the manuscript and Supporting Information for “Neglecting N2O Emissions Underestimates the Soil Greenhouse Gas Budgets of Rewetted Tropical Peatlands.” The study examines soil carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions across four rewetted peatland land uses in Jambi, Indonesia: mixed agriculture, oil palm plantation, jelutung plantation, and secondary forest. Field measurements are complemented by a synthesis of 65 tropical peatland observation records spanning undrained, drained, and rewetted conditions. The manuscript presents greenhouse gas fluxes, their contributions to total soil greenhouse gas budgets, and relationships with environmental conditions. The Supporting Information provides supplementary figures, tables, and the synthesis database used in the comparative analyses. Overall, these materials highlight the importance of including N2O alongside CO2 and CH4 when assessing the climate benefits of tropical peatland rewetting.

title: Explaining Green Purchase Behavior: Integrating Prosocial Environmental Attitudes, Green Consumption Values, and Environmental Knowledge
summary: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the factors influencing green purchase behavior by integrating prosocial environmental attitudes, green consumption values, environmental knowledge, and openness to green communication into a structural m
content: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the factors influencing green purchase behavior by integrating prosocial environmental attitudes, green consumption values, environmental knowledge, and openness to green communication into a structural model, framed within the value-action gap perspective. Method: Data were collected from 210 consumers residing in the Special Region of Yogyakarta who had purchased, or considered purchasing, environmentally friendly products at Super Indo. Respondents were recruited through an online, self-administered questionnaire distributed via social media, with screening questions applied at the outset; the data were analyzed using covariance-based Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in AMOS, with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals (5,000 resamples). Results: All six hypothesized paths were statistically significant. Green consumption values had a significant direct effect on purchase behavior, but this direct effect was relatively weak compared with its combined indirect effect through environmental knowledge and openness to green communication, indicating that the value-action gap observed in this study is partial rather than complete. Among the direct predictors of purchase behavior, environmental knowledge and openness to green communication showed overlapping confidence intervals, so neither can be confirmed as reliably stronger than the other based on the present data. Implications & Recommendations: These findings suggest that environmental knowledge and openness to green communication are both important mechanisms for strengthening consumers' green purchase behavior, operating in parallel alongside the direct effect of values. Theoretically, this study does not claim to extend the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) or the Value-Belief-Norm (VBN) framework, since the core constructs of both theories are not modeled here; instead, both frameworks are treated as explanatory traditions whose limitations motivate a respecification of the value-action gap mechanism, positioning cognitive and communicative dimensions as parallel pathways within a single framework. Contribution & Value Added: The study contributes to the literature by demonstrating that environmental knowledge and green communication openness operate as parallel, empirically distinguishable mechanisms linking environmental values to actual purchasing behavior, and by providing evidence that the value-action gap in this setting is partial: values are translated into behavior, but that translation is stronger when accompanied by adequate cognitive and communicative conditions.

title: Marine Algae‐Derived Starch and Polysaccharides for Sustainable Bioplastics: Processing, Properties, Environmental Performance, and Future Prospects
summary: ABSTRACT Marine algae present a promising foundation for developing sustainable bioplastics, distinguished by rapid growth, abundant carbohydrates, and minimal land and freshwater demands. This paper examines the utilization of marine algae
content: ABSTRACT Marine algae present a promising foundation for developing sustainable bioplastics, distinguished by rapid growth, abundant carbohydrates, and minimal land and freshwater demands. This paper examines the utilization of marine algae‐derived starch and other polysaccharides in bioplastic manufacturing, encompassing algal characteristics, carbohydrate and polysaccharide recovery, bioplastic formulation and properties, and environmental implications. Marine algae‐derived starch and polysaccharides have emerged as promising raw materials for bioplastic development because of their carbohydrate content, functional diversity, and potential for integration into marine biorefinery systems. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of the potential of algae‐based starch in bioplastic production, exploring algal biology, starch extraction processes, and the fabrication and performance of algal bioplastics. Recent advancements, practical applications, and the challenges associated with scaling up marine algae‐based bioplastics are evaluated. Despite significant progress, several challenges continue to hinder large‐scale commercialization, including feedstock variability, energy‐intensive drying and extraction processes, limited moisture resistance, and the absence of standardized end‐of‐life management frameworks. This review critically evaluates these barriers and identifies future research directions aimed at improving material performance, process sustainability, and industrial scalability. The review underscores the potential of marine algae as a sustainable resource for mitigating plastic pollution and advancing green technologies.

title: Advancing SDG 12 and SDG 13 in a Developing Extractive Economy: Corporate Social Responsibility, Stakeholder Interest, and Supply Chain Resilience in Ghanaian Mining
summary: ABSTRACT The private sector's contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals in developing economies depends on how effectively firms convert their social and environmental commitments into development outcomes. This study examines that
content: ABSTRACT The private sector's contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals in developing economies depends on how effectively firms convert their social and environmental commitments into development outcomes. This study examines that conversion in Ghanaian mining, a sector central to SDG 12 and SDG 13, where weak formal institutions constrain the translation of corporate social responsibility (CSR) into sustainable practice. Drawing on stakeholder, resilience, and institutional voids theories, we theorise and test a serial mediation model in which CSR advances sustainable mining through sequential governance: it first activates stakeholder interest (SI), which builds supply chain resilience (SCR), which in turn drives sustainable mining (SM). We analyse single‐source, cross‐sectional data from 458 respondents across 116 Ghanaian mining firms using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM), with an artificial neural network, importance–performance map analysis, and a Gaussian copula test as robustness checks. CSR exerts no significant direct effect on sustainable mining ( β = 0.089, n.s.); its total effect ( β = 0.383, p < 0.001) is transmitted entirely through the stakeholder and supply chain pathway (CSR → SI → SCR → SM; β = 0.047, p < 0.01). The findings show that the private sector's contribution to the SDGs in extractive economies depends less on the scale of CSR expenditure than on the stakeholder partnerships and value‐chain governance that convert it into development outcomes.
