title: Impacts of forest protection in the Czech Republic on the Central European wood market: A scenario analysis
summary: Expanding forest protection may create a conflict between biodiversity conservation objectives and the availability of wood raw material for downstream industries. This study aimed to assess the potential impacts of this conflict on the Cze
content: Expanding forest protection may create a conflict between biodiversity conservation objectives and the availability of wood raw material for downstream industries. This study aimed to assess the potential impacts of this conflict on the Czech wood-processing sector and to identify mechanisms that could mitigate emerging raw-material shortages. A systematic synthesis of 311 unique studies was combined with an evidence-constrained scenario model incorporating supply restrictions, trade adjustment, production leakage, domestic adaptation, and sector-specific exposure. For the Czech reference industrial wood supply of 14.558 million m3, three scenarios were assessed: LOW (5%), CENTRAL (12.5%), and HIGH (37%). Under the CENTRAL scenario, reference trade adjustment reduced the deficit to 559.9 thousand m3, corresponding to 3.85% of baseline supply; with full implementation of the identified technical adaptation potential, the deficit could decline to 1.28%. Under the HIGH scenario, however, a deficit of 13.53% remained even after trade adjustment and maximum identified adaptation. The results show that the compatibility of stronger forest protection with the functioning of the wood-processing industry depends on the magnitude of the initial supply shock, trade response, implementation of adaptation measures, and maintenance of critical raw-material flows.

title: Surfactants effect on the oil/water/rock interface behavior recent study progress
summary: Surfactant-enhanced oil recovery was an important technical direction for chemical enhanced oil recovery. It lowered the threshold for residual oil after water flooding and improved the micro-displacement efficiency and macro-development ef
content: Surfactant-enhanced oil recovery was an important technical direction for chemical enhanced oil recovery. It lowered the threshold for residual oil after water flooding and improved the micro-displacement efficiency and macro-development effects of complex reservoirs, which could be used to regulate the oil/water and oil/solid interface multiphase flow behavior. When the conventional reservoirs entered high water cut or recovery stages, the residual oil would gradually transformed from a continuous oil phase into the non-contiguous pore corner oil. But the residual oil flow was jointly limited by capillary pressure, rock surface adhesion, crude polar component aggregation, and interfacial film stability, and many methods (surfactants, polymers, ect) could be used to enhance the process. Among these methods, surfactants can be directionally adsorbed onto the oil-water interface to reduce the interface free energy, thus promoting the deformation, peeling and migration of oil droplets. At the same time, surfactants can form competitive adsorption layers or hydration films on the rock surface, altering the minerals suface wettability and chargeability. Additionally, surfactants can improve the crude oil mobility through emulsification and microemulsification‌. This paper reviewed the surfactant interfacial behavior onto the oil-water–rock interface, the surfactants species were analyzed, and the structural characteristics, interfacial interactions and reservoir suitability were analyzed. Surfactants could be divided into the cationic, anionic, non-ionic, and zwitterionic surfactant. Different surfactants had the different property onto the interface modification. The different surfactants application should mainly be limited to certain carbonate rock reservoirs, special surface electrical conditions, or composite systems modified by nonionic, amphoteric, and low-adsorption structures. This paper further clarifies the mechanisms of surfactant-intensified oil extraction, mainly focusing on processes such as reduced interfacial tension, changes in wetting properties, emulsification and formation of microemulsions, competition between adsorption and desorption, reconstruction of interfacial films, and transport of pore-scale dimensions. It also provides a detailed analysis of the effects of mineralization, divalent ions, temperature, pressure, rock mineral composition, and heavy crude oil components on interface behavior. In view of the current challenge in research, such as adsorption losses, degradation at high temperatures, sedimentation at high-salinity, uncontrolled emulsification, blockages in pores and throats, high difficulty in geological processing, cost constraints, and significant environmental risks, this paper proposes a multi-scale coupled assessment method that couples with molecular simulations, microfluidics, and core displacement experiments, and incorporates AI-assisted formulation screening to systematically evaluate the sustained re

title: Micro- and Nanofiber Technologies: Principles, Preparation Methods, and Characterization
summary: Abstract The special geometrical and chemical properties of micro- and nanofibers lead to a structured arrangement of materials, resulting in better functioning during filtration, separation, adsorption, catalysis, and sensing. It presents
content: Abstract The special geometrical and chemical properties of micro- and nanofibers lead to a structured arrangement of materials, resulting in better functioning during filtration, separation, adsorption, catalysis, and sensing. It presents an overview of different basic principles of micro- and nanofiber production. It gives comparative analysis of the methods employed including electrospinning, self-assembly, phase separation, template synthesis, drawing, centrifugal spinning, solution spinning, and melt spinning, discussing their influence on fibers morphology and their scale-up. The chapter introduces the main methods of characterization such as microscopy, image-based diameter analysis, spectroscopy, and diffraction. Moreover, it illustrates the importance of thermal analysis, mechanical tests, wettability testing in terms of its importance for fiber production. It also relates the impact of sustainability on microfiber technology development, outlining the key aspects such as solvent choice and recovery, energy efficiency, extent of throughput, green precursors, and recycling of fiber membranes.

title: HPV E6/E7, O-GlcNAcylation and mitochondrial remodeling in cervical cancer: mechanistic links and translational opportunities
summary: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection initiates cervical carcinogenesis, while progression and treatment resistance also involve metabolic adaptation. O-GlcNAcylation is a reversible post-translational modification (PTM)
content: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection initiates cervical carcinogenesis, while progression and treatment resistance also involve metabolic adaptation. O-GlcNAcylation is a reversible post-translational modification (PTM) controlled by O-GlcNAc transferase (OGT) and O-GlcNAcase (OGA), with UDP-GlcNAc generated by the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway (HBP) serving as the donor substrate. This review evaluates evidence linking HPV E6/E7-associated metabolic demand, HBP flux, O-GlcNAcylation, and mitochondrial function. We distinguish observations made under untreated conditions from acute treatment responses, identify whether validated resistant models were used, and examine HPV genotype as a source of heterogeneity. Cervical cancer studies support links between O-GlcNAcylation and pathways involved in growth and survival, but no mitochondrial O-GlcNAcylation site has been causally validated in HPV-positive cervical cancer. We therefore grade evidence by model, temporal context, and causal depth and place the proposed relationships within a broader PTM network. This synthesis separates findings obtained in cervical cancer from mechanisms inferred from other systems and identifies the main gaps limiting biomarker and therapeutic development.

title: Do sustainable business models scale differently than business model configurations with lower environmental ambitions? A comparative analysis of business model scaling performance among sharing-mobility providers
summary: As it has developed into a defining paradigm of the 21st century, the sharing economy is widely regarded as providing opportunities for environmental and social benefits in addition to economic advantages. Yet, it remains unclear whether sh
content: As it has developed into a defining paradigm of the 21st century, the sharing economy is widely regarded as providing opportunities for environmental and social benefits in addition to economic advantages. Yet, it remains unclear whether sharing business models that incorporate environmental ambitions and public alignment require supplementary changes to other business model elements to scale successfully. Drawing on configurational theory and the business model literature, we model market scaling as a function of five business model design choices: environmental ambitions, alignment with public stakeholders, value-proposition portfolio size, digital intensity, and revenue-stream diversification. Fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) of twenty-one sharing-mobility providers identifies six configurations (four associated with successful scaling, two with scaling failure) and yields three implications. First, business models with strong environmental ambitions and close public alignment can scale as successfully as their counterparts that lack these characteristics. Second, irrespective of a firm’s level of environmental ambitions and public alignment, value-proposition portfolio size and revenue-stream diversification consistently emerge as the keys to successful scaling. Third, successfully scaled business models exhibit congruence between environmental ambitions and public alignment. Overall, business models with strong environmental ambitions and close public alignment and business models without these characteristics share similar paths to scale: multiple value propositions or diversified revenue streams. These findings advance configurational business model theory, resolve ambiguities in the sharing economy literature, and offer a cautiously optimistic message for management practice: Designing a business model with genuine environmental ambitions neither requires sacrificing scalability nor defying the common commercial logic.

title: Emerging bacterial diversity associated with oak decline: First report of several new taxa involved, including Pseudomonas quercina sp. nov. and Pseudomonas dehesae sp. nov., isolated from holm oak in Spain
summary: Acute oak decline (AOD) is a complex decline syndrome associated with a polymicrobial bacterial assemblage, together with abiotic and other biotic factors. Although AOD and its associated bacteria are increasingly reported across Europe, ho
content: Acute oak decline (AOD) is a complex decline syndrome associated with a polymicrobial bacterial assemblage, together with abiotic and other biotic factors. Although AOD and its associated bacteria are increasingly reported across Europe, holm oak and the Iberian Peninsula remain understudied. We characterized the culturable fraction of the bacterial community associated with declining Quercus ilex showing symptoms including bleeding stem lesions at one site in northwestern Spain over four consecutive years, combining isolation from wood and bark tissues, molecular identification, detached-branch inoculation assays, and strain re-isolation from necrotic tissues. We confirmed the presence of the core AOD bacteria in Q. ilex , including Gibbsiella quercinecans , previously reported from this host in Spain, together with the first record of Brenneria goodwinii on Q. ilex in Spain and the first record of Rahnella victoriana in Spain. Beyond the recognized pathobiome, several taxa not previously linked to oak decline showed necrogenic potential, including Klebsiella oxytoca, Pantoea phytostimulans, Enterobacter hormaechei subsp. hoffmannii, and two previously undescribed Pseudomonas species, for which the names Pseudomonas quercina sp. nov. and Pseudomonas dehesae sp. nov. are proposed. These findings expand the known diversity of culturable bacteria associated with symptomatic oaks, reveal previously unrecognized necrogenic enterobacteria and pseudomonads (including novel species), identify candidate bacteria for further testing in intact plants and natural disease systems and reveal Q. ilex in the Iberian Peninsula as host to a diverse and partly novel decline-associated microbiota.

title: Revisiting liquid-liquid extraction of pyrolysis bio-oil: Parameter sensitivities, residual water removal, and analytical implications
source: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
summary: Biofuels produced from waste-derived pyrolysis liquids can contribute to near-term decarbonization, but their upgrading and commercialization depend on reproducible chemical characterization. Pyrolysis bio-oil typically contains substantial
content: Biofuels produced from waste-derived pyrolysis liquids can contribute to near-term decarbonization, but their upgrading and commercialization depend on reproducible chemical characterization. Pyrolysis bio-oil typically contains substantial water, which depresses heating value, degrades stability, and compromises GC–MS repeatability; therefore, water must be controlled prior to compositional profiling. Liquid–liquid extraction (LLE) is widely used to isolate GC–MS-detectable fractions and remove water, yet protocols vary widely across the literature, limiting cross-study comparability needed for consistent process evaluation, performance benchmarking, and scale-up decisions in waste-to-energy pathways. Here, a Box–Behnken experimental design was applied to quantify the sensitivities of LLE performance to three commonly adjusted parameters: bio-oil-to-solvent ratio, Na 2 SO 4 drying-agent loading, and the number of extraction cycles. Residual water in the dried organic extracts was estimated using a rapid FT-NIR approach tailored for low-water organic matrices, and potential impacts on GC–MS chemical fingerprints were assessed using relative peak-area compound-class distributions. The results showed that residual water was significantly affected by solvent ratio, while the effects of Na 2 SO 4 loading and extraction number were weaker, with values remaining within a narrow range (<4%). In contrast, the relative distributions of GC–MS-detectable compound classes were not significantly altered by changes in extraction conditions, indicating that semi-quantitative chemical fingerprints remain comparatively stable. Overall, the findings demonstrate that LLE parameters exert limited influence on both excess water and chemical profiles. Given the small differences observed, lower solvent volumes, reduced Na 2 SO 4 usage, and fewer extraction steps may be sufficient, enabling more cost-effective and resource-efficient extraction protocols.

title: An insight into molecular identification and DNA barcoding of bamboo: current status, challenges, and future prospects
summary: Introduction Bamboo exhibits a complex taxonomy due to polyploidy, hybridisation, and long flowering periods, which complicate species identification. Traditional morphological taxonomy often struggles with limited diagnostic traits and con
content: Introduction Bamboo exhibits a complex taxonomy due to polyploidy, hybridisation, and long flowering periods, which complicate species identification. Traditional morphological taxonomy often struggles with limited diagnostic traits and considerable phenotypic variability, leading to taxonomic ambiguities and misinterpretations. The convergence of similar traits among unrelated species further complicates phylogenetic classification. To address these challenges, integrative taxonomic approaches are needed to combine morphological, molecular, and ecological data for accurate bamboo classification. This review synthesises the current status, recent advances, and emerging trends in molecular identification and DNA barcoding of bamboo, highlighting their potential to improve taxonomy, conservation, and the sustainable utilisation of bamboo genetic resources. Method To provide a framework for the review, a scientometric analysis was performed using bibliographic records. Results The review suggests that no single marker or combination of markers can currently serve as a universal barcode across bamboo. The performance of commonly used markers such as ITS, matK, rbcL, psbA-trnH, rps16-trnQ, and alternative plastid regions provides valuable insights into species identification. Comparative evidence indicates that barcode performance is strongly marker- and lineage-dependent. These markers have improved plant taxonomy by providing more reliable species identification than traditional morphological methods. Discussion DNA barcoding has been effectively used to understand complex species relationships and identify cryptic species that are difficult to distinguish morphologically. Furthermore, next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies have transformed genomic data acquisition, enabling species discrimination. Integrating machine learning with DNA barcoding further improves species identification accuracy and shows promise for improving conventional methodologies in bamboo systematics. However, the application of ML and NGS in bamboo is still in its early stages and will require substantial work on bamboo databases to achieve greater accuracy.

title: Analytical parametric study of an evacuated tube solar air heater with perforated twisted tape for industrial heating applications
summary: A major challenge in creating a vacuum solar tube air collector for industrial use is selecting the optimal thermal networks to reach the desired temperature for a specific flow rate. To develop a thermal network model using empirical corre
content: A major challenge in creating a vacuum solar tube air collector for industrial use is selecting the optimal thermal networks to reach the desired temperature for a specific flow rate. To develop a thermal network model using empirical correlations for industrial process heat applications, a theoretical analysis is performed to evaluate design features like the diameter and length of the evacuated tubes, as well as the quantity of tubes in a module, all of which impact thermal performance. The results of the design parametric study indicate that a collector system is best characterized by 20 evacuated tubes, each with an absorber and transparent diameters of 47 mm & 58 mm length of 1800 mm, respectively. Additionally, as the number of collectors in a series network increase, there is a notable reduction in the temperature rise for each collection. Based on the thermal network composed of two modules operating at 300 kg/h can provide optimum performance. The results indicate that the proposed evacuated tube solar system is capable of efficiently supplying hot air at temperatures between 80 and 100 °C, making it suitable for a range of industrial process heating applications.

title: INTERNAL LOGIC AND NEW DEVELOPMENT ADVANTAGES OF NEW-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF TOTAL FACTOR PRODUCTIVITY
source: World journal of economics and business research.
summary: As essentially advanced productive forces, new-quality productive forces take substantial improvement of total factor productivity (TFP) as its core symbol, which is an inevitable choice for China’s modernization drive. Against the backgrou
content: As essentially advanced productive forces, new-quality productive forces take substantial improvement of total factor productivity (TFP) as its core symbol, which is an inevitable choice for China’s modernization drive. Against the background of new-growth-driver transformation, this paper interprets the theoretical connotation of TFP, analyzes the internal logic that new-quality productive forces realize growth-driver transformation relying on TFP from the perspective of demographic constraints. The Solow residual method is adopted to measure China’s TFP from 2001 to 2025, followed by international comparison. The results show that China’s TFP presents phased fluctuation: it maintained high growth after China’s accession to WTO, turned stable after the global financial crisis, and suffered short-term shocks during the pandemic. There is still considerable catching-up space for China’s TFP compared with developed economies such as the United States. At present, the marginal benefit of economic growth driven by traditional factors is gradually decreasing, and efficiency improvement has become a key path to break through growth bottlenecks. A unified national market, complete industrial system, real-economy-oriented digital economy and booming green low-carbon economy constitute four major advantages for China to improve TFP and foster new-quality productive forces. It provides practical support for quality-oriented economic growth and theoretical reference for central regions to develop new-quality productive forces according to local conditions.

title: Short-term market clearing price forecasting in India’s Green Day-Ahead Market using a hybrid wavelet–XGBoost model
summary: Accurate short-term forecasting of the Market Clearing Price (MCP) is essential for the efficient operation of electricity markets with increasing renewable energy penetration. This challenge is particularly significant in India’s Green Day
content: Accurate short-term forecasting of the Market Clearing Price (MCP) is essential for the efficient operation of electricity markets with increasing renewable energy penetration. This challenge is particularly significant in India’s Green Day-Ahead Market (GDAM), where quarter-hourly trading and the variability of renewable generation introduce complex nonlinear price dynamics. This study presents a hybrid Wavelet–XGBoost framework for short-term MCP forecasting by integrating the discrete wavelet transform with the Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, where the wavelet family and decomposition level are selected empirically through a systematic sensitivity analysis rather than assumed a priori. The wavelet decomposition separates the MCP series into multiple frequency components, enabling the model to capture both long-term trends and rapid price fluctuations while reducing the influence of noise. The proposed framework is evaluated using the 2024 GDAM dataset (32,159 valid quarter-hourly observations after data-quality screening) and compared with Naïve, Random Forest, LightGBM, conventional XGBoost, and an LSTM benchmark. On the held-out test period, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 258.6 Rs/MWh, RMSE of 523.7 Rs/MWh, RRMSE of 12.83% and MAPE of 5.65%, and attains the lowest RMSE and RRMSE of all evaluated models. Diebold–Mariano and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests confirm that the proposed model achieves significantly lower squared error than Naïve, Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM, and significantly lower typical-case absolute error than the same-architecture XGBoost and LightGBM baselines, while a tail-performance analysis quantifies the systematic underprediction of all models near the regulatory price cap. Furthermore, SHAP-based interpretability analysis identifies lagged MCP and bidding-related variables as the most influential factors affecting price prediction. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient and interpretable forecasting approach for short-term MCP prediction in India’s GDAM, with particular strength in reducing larger forecasting errors and supporting bidding strategies, market scheduling and renewable energy integration.

title: Mineral Phase Transformation-Mediated Integrated Separation for Calcium Carbide Slag Purification and CaCO3 Production
summary: Abstract Calcium carbide slag (CS) mineralization of CO2 to produce CaCO3 is a promising strategy to solid waste utilization and carbon neutrality, yet inherent impurities seriously degrade product purity and whiteness, restricting high-val
content: Abstract Calcium carbide slag (CS) mineralization of CO2 to produce CaCO3 is a promising strategy to solid waste utilization and carbon neutrality, yet inherent impurities seriously degrade product purity and whiteness, restricting high-value utilization. Herein, we propose an integrated impurity removal strategy based on high-temperature mineral phase transformation to achieve effective separation of critical impurities. FactSage thermodynamic calculations and experimental investigations revealed that during calcination, SiO2 in CS preferentially reacts with CaO to form Ca2SiO4, while carbon is eliminated as CO2. Effective CaO content and activity increased with calcination temperature and time, peaked at 900 °C and 180 min, then decreased slightly with further calcination. Magnetic FeSi impurities were efficiently removed via wet magnetic separation. Subsequently, the newly formed Ca2SiO4 was separated from the Ca(OH)2 matrix by gravitational settling, exploiting the density difference generated by the phase transformation, achieving a maximum Si removal efficiency of 64.2% under optimized conditions (solid–liquid ratio 1:10, 8 h). A mechanistic model linking thermodynamic driving forces, phase evolution, and separation principles is proposed. Ultimately, a calcite-phase CaCO3 of 98.2% purity and 94.0 whiteness with cubic morphology was produced. An elemental mass balance analysis demonstrates the technical viability of the integrated process. This work provides both mechanistic insights and an engineering basis for producing CaCO3 with improved purity from solid waste via CO2 mineralization.

title: Bridge fuels and climate policy integration: The case of low-carbon hydrogen in the European Union
summary: Hydrogen is central to climate neutrality in the European Union (EU), particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. The EU promotes fossil-based low-carbon hydrogen (LCH) as a bridge fuel supporting the development of a renewable hydrogen economy,
content: Hydrogen is central to climate neutrality in the European Union (EU), particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. The EU promotes fossil-based low-carbon hydrogen (LCH) as a bridge fuel supporting the development of a renewable hydrogen economy, despite risks of insufficient emission reductions and diverted investments. Climate policy integration (CPI) research has not addressed hydrogen and lacks a benchmark for bridge fuels. Earlier studies permitted a constrained role for natural gas, whereas recent work deems fossil fuels inherently incompatible with CPI, but without examining the transitional role of bridge fuels. Analyzing 182 legal acts and communications, this article provides the first systematic CPI assessment of the EU hydrogen framework. It provides a CPI benchmark for bridge fuels with three jointly necessary conditions (significant emission reductions, temporal limitation, support for target technologies), assessed through the thickness and quality of the policy mix across four indicators (policy goals, policy instruments for emission reductions, funding/financing, and procedural instruments). The hydrogen framework reaches a medium level of CPI. Its policy mix is thick but lacks quality, applying the conditions of bridge fuels only selectively. The framework thus commits neither to a net-zero pathway nor to an end date for fossil-based LCH. Conceptually, the article shows that the compatibility of fossil-based technologies with CPI depends on the climate policy paradigm underlying the benchmark. Under a purely emission-based decarbonization benchmark, they are not inherently incompatible with CPI. Where fossil-free alternatives exist, however, they should align with CPI only as temporally limited bridge fuels, following a defossilization paradigm.

title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
summary: The most extreme heat waves are intensifying faster than moderate events across many mid-latitude regions. Climate models underestimate these trends, suggesting an incomplete representation and understanding of the underlying physical proce
content: The most extreme heat waves are intensifying faster than moderate events across many mid-latitude regions. Climate models underestimate these trends, suggesting an incomplete representation and understanding of the underlying physical processes. Here, we use an explainable machine-learning framework to investigate interactions among atmospheric circulation, surface soil moisture, and temperature, and their role in recent heat extremes. We show that a three-way interaction among these components becomes active once a critical temperature threshold is exceeded, contributing, on average, ∼10% to peak temperature anomalies during the most extreme heat events across ∼28% of humid mid-latitude regions. We further reveal that this interaction is systematically underestimated in CMIP6 and CESM2 Large Ensemble simulations. Soils in climate models are too dry at the initiation of heat waves, therefore suppressing subsequent soil-moisture depletion and inhibiting feedback activation. These findings help explain regional model biases in upper-tail warming and highlight avenues for improving future projections of extreme heat events.

title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
summary: Abstract Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5-2\(\:℃\) targets require emission reductions with additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ~ 2–3 PgC year − 1 . Here, we assess the long-term additionality and durabil
content: Abstract Climate stabilization pathways limiting global warming to 1.5-2\(\:℃\) targets require emission reductions with additional carbon dioxide removal (CDR) of ~ 2–3 PgC year − 1 . Here, we assess the long-term additionality and durability of carbon uptake from large-scale ocean iron fertilization (OIF) using an Earth System Model under emissions-driven scenarios. Our simulations suggest that sustained century-scale fertilization in the southern sector of the Southern Ocean (SSO) yields a moderate contribution (~ 30PgC, or 0.3 PgC/yr). In other iron-limited regions, the additional carbon uptake induced by fertilization is largely offset (70–100%) by the non-fertilized regions. Terminating OIF after 30 years, the ocean retains 50% of the additional carbon in the SSO, while retention becomes negligible in other regions. Global CDR rates are 2\(\:-\)7 times lower than prior idealized estimates. OIF-induced CDR is constrained by multiple biogeochemical processes: local and remote nutrient depletion, re-entrainment of previously sequestered carbon, incomplete macronutrient drawdown, reduced phytoplankton carbon to phosphorus ratios. Incomplete macronutrient drawdown represented the largest difference from earlier studies, reflecting uptake controls by light, top-down controls, and rates of macronutrient resupply. Further insight into CDR potential requires application of our standardized design across modeling institutions, and targeted analysis of top-down and bottom-up controls on nutrient drawdown.

title: Riverine organic matter dynamics in the headwaters of the Yellow River under climate change
summary: Abstract. Alpine headwater streams play a crucial role in the global carbon cycle and are particularly sensitive to climate change. Riverine organic matter (ROM) mediates the transport and transformation of terrestrial carbon across aquatic
content: Abstract. Alpine headwater streams play a crucial role in the global carbon cycle and are particularly sensitive to climate change. Riverine organic matter (ROM) mediates the transport and transformation of terrestrial carbon across aquatic systems. However, the response of ROM in headwater streams on the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau (QTP) to climate change remains poorly understood due to scarce in situ measurements. In this study, we used machine learning models combining satellite data and geographical variables to reconstruct historical variations in Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD, a proxy for ROM) along the Yellow River’s Headstream (YRHS), and to predict future changes under typical Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. The results indicate that COD levels in the midstream region of the YRHS, characterized by greater precipitation, higher soil organic matter, and denser vegetation, were relatively high (2.73 ± 1.63 mg L⁻¹) and exhibited an increasing trend (+0.44 mg L⁻¹) over the past decade. Driven primarily by increasing precipitation and temperature, COD levels are projected to rise in upstream and downstream areas but decline at midstream sites under SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585 by the 2100s. The annual export of COD from the midstream of the YRHS is expected to increase from 62.5 Gg to 81.6 Gg by 2100s due to projected increase in COD concentrations and discharge. Our findings identify the midstream region of the YRHS as a critical and climate-sensitive region for organic matter dynamics. Nevertheless, substantial uncertainties remain in the future ROM changes owing to the complex interactions among precipitation, warming, and their combined effects on carbon cycles in alpine catchments. Therefore, further research is required to improve our understanding of catchment-scale carbon dynamics on the QTP in the context of climate change.

title: Seasonal–hourly assessment of data center spatial flexibility under renewable variability: A case study of Jeju Island
summary: Policy interest in data center deployment away from the Seoul metropolitan area has made renewable-rich Jeju Island a leading candidate, yet its island grid offers limited transfer capability, and the demand it can accommodate has not been
content: Policy interest in data center deployment away from the Seoul metropolitan area has made renewable-rich Jeju Island a leading candidate, yet its island grid offers limited transfer capability, and the demand it can accommodate has not been quantified. Spatial flexibility has emerged as a promising alternative to network reinforcement, but transmission-level studies remain limited, and those available specify the data center capacity as an input rather than determining it. This study determines the capacity as an outcome, embedding an incremental capacity analysis in a DC optimal power flow formulation solved across sixteen seasonal–hourly operating conditions. For the Jeju power system, 200 MW can be accommodated without reinforcement under firm connection, the limit being set by the summer evening condition in which peak net load coincides with the lowest wind availability of the year; other conditions admit up to 360 MW. Spatial workload redistribution extends the binding limit to 320 MW, with gains of 80–160 MW across conditions. The extension is bounded by whichever is exhausted first, flow concentration at the sending site or renewable availability at the receiving site, and which factor binds reverses across seasons: summer is absorption-limited, spring congestion-limited, and winter binds on both. Approximately 30% migration capability sustains these limits in fifteen of sixteen conditions, with migration capability and receiving capacity required in equal measure and benefits saturating beyond this level. The results translate a siting policy into the capacity a renewable-rich island grid can absorb and the operating conditions under which that capacity can be extended.

title: Building-Stock Turnover Reshapes Mitigation Priorities in China’s Building Sector
summary: Abstract China’s building sector is pivotal to the 2060 carbon-neutrality ambition, yet prospective assessments often insufficiently capture regional heterogeneity and life-cycle emission dynamics. Here, we develop a provincial-level dynami
content: Abstract China’s building sector is pivotal to the 2060 carbon-neutrality ambition, yet prospective assessments often insufficiently capture regional heterogeneity and life-cycle emission dynamics. Here, we develop a provincial-level dynamic framework integrating material flow analysis, life-cycle assessment, and machine-learning-informed parameter trajectories to project emissions through 2060. Under a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, China’s building life-cycle emissions are projected to peak in 2031–2033, while carbon neutrality remains challenged by persistent pressures from both material use and building operations. These pressures arise from the existing stock, whose continued use sustains energy demand while increasing building retirements shift construction from stock growth to the replacement of retired buildings. Implementing a high-efficiency scenario with regionally differentiated deployment of material- and energy-efficiency strategies could reduce China’s building-sector life-cycle emissions by 90% in 2060 relative to the BAU scenario. Provincial analysis further reveals that similar overall mitigation potential masks substantial differences in the composition of effective mitigation portfolios, reflecting local building-stock and energy-use characteristics. To close the remaining gap, deeper operational decarbonization should be coupled with stock-management strategies that extend building lifetimes, avoid premature demolition, and prioritize renovation and reuse.

title: Past fire use in deforested land limits secondary forest carbon gains in Amazonia with implications for emissions reduction goals
summary: Abstract Background Understanding the carbon (C) recovery potential of secondary forests (SF) is essential for reducing uncertainties regarding the contribution of Amazon forests to the global carbon budget, and for strengthening national a
content: Abstract Background Understanding the carbon (C) recovery potential of secondary forests (SF) is essential for reducing uncertainties regarding the contribution of Amazon forests to the global carbon budget, and for strengthening national and sub-national climate mitigation policies aligned with Brazil’s commitments under the Paris Agreement. We, hence, focus on Pará state in eastern Amazon to evaluate how regional edaphoclimatic conditions, prior land-use duration, and fire recurrence influenced C removal rates of SFs. Methods We combined Earth observation-based aboveground biomass and SF age data, derived from multitemporal land cover maps, to construct chronosequences representing four past land-use classes: undisturbed SF (regrowth immediately after deforestation), anthropogenic use with fire, anthropogenic use only, and fire only across three edaphoclimatic regions. We characterised spatiotemporal variations in C gain and projected potential removals by 2035 under three protection scenarios (SF age ≥ 1, ≥5, and ≥ 10 years). Results We showed that a history of extensive land use and fire before forest regeneration reduced C gain rates by 27% to 40% compared to undisturbed SFs in Southeast Pará. These impacts persisted across all successional stages. Model projections estimate that fire-affected areas could require up to 226 years to recover mature forest C stocks—three times longer than undisturbed SFs—highlighting long-term recovery lags despite inherent modelling uncertainties. Furthermore, high fire recurrence (≥ 3 events) led to a 34% reduction of the C gain rate. Regarding the mitigation potential, protecting only SFs ≥ 10 years old reduced projected 2020–2035 removals by 79% compared to protecting all SFs (age ≥ 1 year; which could sequester 691 Tg CO₂). Conclusions Achieving net-zero targets under Pará’s “Amazon Now” State Plan (PEAA) is challenging. Offsetting current emissions would require doubling the existing regenerating (≥ 1 year) area to 112,644 km². Given the long-term degradation of successional trajectories by fire and land use, reducing annual deforestation from 2,673 to 1,341 km² by 2030 appears to be a more efficient and feasible strategy for carbon neutrality than relying solely on natural regeneration. Ultimately, understanding the role of regenerating forests in the global carbon cycle is fundamental for designing climate policies and targets aimed at achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions.

title: Between marine and continental air: atmospheric CO₂ variability and local wind associations in coastal Taizhou, China
summary: Abstract Atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) observations at Hongjia, Taizhou, from April 2023 to November 2024 were analyzed using statistical methods, backward-trajectory clustering, the weighted potential source contribution function, and c
content: Abstract Atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) observations at Hongjia, Taizhou, from April 2023 to November 2024 were analyzed using statistical methods, backward-trajectory clustering, the weighted potential source contribution function, and cross-tabulation of trajectory over-ocean fractions and local winds. The mean mole fraction was (440.61 ± 14.0) × 10⁻⁶, lower than at the inland Lin’an station. Concentrations were higher in winter and spring, lower in summer and autumn, and highest around dawn and lowest in the afternoon. Wind speed was negatively correlated with CO₂ in all seasons; W–WSW winds were associated with higher concentrations. The 72 h trajectories were classified as continental (over-ocean fraction f ≤ 0.2), mixed (0.2 < f < 0.8), or marine (f ≥ 0.8). The over-ocean fraction was negatively correlated with CO₂ (r = − 0.367). Marine pathways combined with SE–S winds and speeds ≥ 3 m s⁻¹ yielded a mean of 425.8 × 10⁻⁶, whereas continental-pathway means ranged from 448.1 to 449.2 × 10⁻⁶ under different wind filters. Weak westerlies across pathways corresponded to 451.5 × 10⁻⁶, increasing to 459.3 × 10⁻⁶ in winter. Within pathway classes, weak-westerly means exceeded those under other valid wind conditions by 6.9–12.8 × 10⁻⁶. These contrasts cannot independently quantify local anthropogenic contributions. Potential source regions included the Zhejiang–Fujian coast, the Jiangsu–Anhui border, and North China. The findings characterize coastal CO₂ variability associated with regional transport, local transport and dispersion, and terrestrial ecosystem exchange.

title: Enhancement of a Closed-loop Recycling by Converting Rejected Coal Fly Ash into Coagulants for Desulfurization Wastewater Treatment in a Coal-Fired Power Plant
summary: Environmental policies promoting resource recycling have been implemented worldwide to achieve goals such as carbon neutrality and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The Republic of Korea has set targets to reduce waste and increase recycli
content: Environmental policies promoting resource recycling have been implemented worldwide to achieve goals such as carbon neutrality and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The Republic of Korea has set targets to reduce waste and increase recycling rates to 70% by 2030. Rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has led to higher energy demand, raising concerns over supply, security, and management. Despite the operation of renewable energy facilities, reliance on coal-based energy remains high, resulting in continuous coal ash generation. Most coal ash is recycled into construction materials, including concrete, while a significant portion, particularly rejected coal fly ash a byproduct is almost entirely landfilled. This has hindered improvements in recycling rates due to technological limitations. To address this, advanced recycling methods for coal ash were explored, focusing on its potential application as a coagulant, an underexplored topic. Comprehensive evaluations, including settling velocity, environmental assessment, life cycle assessment, and economic feasibility, were conducted. The results showed that the settling velocity of the rejected coal fly ash-based coagulant was more than twice that of conventional products. Regulated substances were within legal limits, although several unregulated substances were detected. Life cycle assessment indicated reductions of up to 89% in carbon emissions, energy consumption, and resource use, while economic analysis revealed cost savings of approximately 41% compared with conventional products. These findings demonstrate that rejected coal fly ash-based coagulant can serve as an effective and environmentally sound alternative, expected to enhance coal ash recycling rates and demonstrate positive results in evaluating recycling potential. Developed a novel recycling method converting coal rejected coal fly ash into a wastewater coagulant. The recycled coagulant achieved over twice the settling velocity of conventional products. Life cycle assessment showed up to 89% reduction in carbon, energy, and resource use. Economic analysis indicated about 41% lower cost compared with conventional treatment. The approach enhances coal ash recycling and promotes circular resource utilization.

title: Two-stage robust optimization for formulating regulation curves of smart building clusters considering multiple regulation characteristics
summary: Accurate formulation of smart building regulation curves is essential for exploiting building-side flexibility and supporting supply–demand interaction in new power systems. However, existing methods often insufficiently consider the multip
content: Accurate formulation of smart building regulation curves is essential for exploiting building-side flexibility and supporting supply–demand interaction in new power systems. However, existing methods often insufficiently consider the multiple regulation characteristics of adjustable loads, scenario-specific response requirements, and response-capability uncertainty, resulting in underused response potential and poor curve executability. This paper proposes a two-stage robust formulation method for smart building cluster regulation curves. First, five response characteristics, including response capacity, maximum response duration, minimum response interval, maximum response count, and response speed, are represented by a unified characteristic matrix to describe heterogeneous smart buildings. Second, response-demand characteristic matrices of typical scenarios are extracted from historical data, and response periods and weights are embedded into resource aggregation to obtain scenario-oriented cluster response-capability curves. Finally, a two-stage robust optimization model for regulation curves considering response-capability uncertainty is proposed. The first stage determines cluster regulation curves and response states, while the second stage adjusts individual building response quantities under different realizations of response capability. The objective function accounts for the response costs of responding entities with different response characteristics and the carbon-reduction benefits of demand-side response. Simulation results show that the proposed method better exploits the response capabilities of smart building clusters and improves the adaptability and economy of regulation curves under response-capability uncertainty.

title: Mapping crop residue cover in global black soil regions based on a new multi-band spectral index and an integrated thresholding approach
summary: Abstract Crop residue cover is a defining feature of conservation tillage, supporting soil health, carbon sequestration, and agricultural productivity, particularly across the world’s black soil regions. However, large-scale monitoring rema
content: Abstract Crop residue cover is a defining feature of conservation tillage, supporting soil health, carbon sequestration, and agricultural productivity, particularly across the world’s black soil regions. However, large-scale monitoring remains challenging due to the spectral heterogeneity of post-harvest fields and the scarcity of ground-truth samples. Here, we propose a new multi-band crop residue cover spectral index (MCRCSI), and an accuracy-weighted composite thresholding (AWCT) for robust crop residue mapping on single-date multispectral imagery. MCRCSI integrates the cellulose- and lignin-related SWIR contrast of crop residues with their joint Red and near-infrared reflectance response, enhancing separability from soil and photosynthetic vegetation. AWCT integrates thresholds derived from Otsu’s method, k-means clustering, and Gaussian mixture models using accuracy-based weights, enabling adaptive threshold determination across different cropping systems. Across eight representative sites in the United States, Ukraine, Northeast China, and Argentina, we evaluated the MCRCSI-AWCT framework using 15,591 independent validation samples. It achieved a mean overall accuracy (OA) of 93.6% and a mean F1 score of 94.0%, with site-level OA ranging from 81.0% to 98.0% (SD = 5.6%). MCRCSI was sensitive to changes in crop residue fraction, with distinct responses at low (<20%) and high (>80%) cover levels, indicating potential for fraction retrieval. Its strong separation of unharvested crops from post-harvest crop residue also suggests potential for harvest event detection. Together, these findings provide a scalable framework for mapping crop residue cover and monitoring field management practices over time.

title: Two-Dimensional Silver-Alkynyl Framework Based on Tetraalkynylporphyrin for Visible-Light-Driven Photocatalysis
summary: Abstract The rational construction of crystalline two-dimensional metal–organic frameworks (2D MOFs) sustained exclusively by metal–carbon (M–C) bonds remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a 2D silver-alkynyl framework, Ag-Por-
content: Abstract The rational construction of crystalline two-dimensional metal–organic frameworks (2D MOFs) sustained exclusively by metal–carbon (M–C) bonds remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a 2D silver-alkynyl framework, Ag-Por-MOF, assembled at room temperature from 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(4-ethynylphenyl)porphyrin (H2-TEPP) and silver(I) triflate (AgOTf). The material adopts a layered structure built from tetranuclear silver clusters bridged by Ag–C≡C linkages, with charge neutrality achieved without additional counterions, as supported by Ag K-edge XAS/EXAFS analysis, elemental analysis, and theoretical simulation. The framework exhibits broad visible-light absorption, pronounced photoinduced charge separation, and pronounced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability under ambient illumination. The synthesis is readily scalable to the gram level without loss of crystallinity or porosity. As a heterogeneous photocatalyst, Ag-Por-MOF enables visible-light-driven oxidative cyclization of o-phenylenediamines and aldehydes to afford 2-substituted benzimidazoles with high efficiency (up to 97% yield), excellent functional-group tolerance, and robust recyclability over five consecutive cycles. This work provides a viable route toward M–C bond-based 2D frameworks for sustainable photocatalysis.

title: Scaling-up electrochromic windows from the lab to buildings and grid integration
summary: Electrochromic (EC) windows can regulate solar heat and daylight, yet laboratory performance alone does not determine their value in buildings. This Review traces electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures through sca
content: Electrochromic (EC) windows can regulate solar heat and daylight, yet laboratory performance alone does not determine their value in buildings. This Review traces electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures through scale-up and commercialization to building operation and grid interaction. It examines how useful function is filtered by large-area uniformity, durability, sealing reliability, manufacturing yield, cost, and control. These constraints explain why mature products still favor conservative inorganic solid-state platforms despite rapid advances in dual-band and multiband devices. The analysis further shows that optical states should be defined by application needs before materials and devices are optimized to deliver them, linking spectral design to comfort, energy, and flexibility objectives. Because most reported grid-responsive benefits remain simulation-based, future studies must separate projected potential from field-verified performance. Progress therefore requires application-driven design, scalable qualification, and real-world validation that preserve useful function from material discovery to reliable building operation and verifiable grid services. This Review discusses electrochromic technology from materials and device architectures, scale-up and commercialization, to building operation and grid interaction. It also examines how useful function is enabled by large-area uniformity, durability, sealing reliability, manufacturing yield, cost, and control.

title: Investigating a Two-Dimensional Carbon Cost Control Method Based on “Carbon Flow–Value Flow”
summary: Achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality requires coordinated action across macro, meso, and micro levels. For Chinese firms, reducing carbon emissions and controlling carbon costs are important challenges. Using Nanjing Iron and Stee
content: Achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality requires coordinated action across macro, meso, and micro levels. For Chinese firms, reducing carbon emissions and controlling carbon costs are important challenges. Using Nanjing Iron and Steel Co., Ltd. (NJ Steel) as a case, this study proposes a two-dimensional “carbon flow–value flow” cost control method that traces carbon-containing material and energy inputs, transformation, and emissions through steel production, maps these flows to internal resource transfer costs and external environmental damage costs, and identifies process-level control points and optimization measures. Carbon flow analysis indicated that coking, ironmaking, and steelmaking are high-emission processes. Value flow analysis showed that these processes also incur high carbon costs and are therefore key control points. Within the process-level quantitative boundary and simulated optimization scenarios, internal resource transfer costs and external environmental damage costs were RMB 1,176 million and RMB 1,442 million lower than baseline, respectively. After accounting for technical retrofit investment and key parameter uncertainty, carbon cost reductions ranged from approximately RMB 1,879 million to RMB 3,941 million across the sensitivity scenarios. The findings provide practical guidance for enterprises seeking to strengthen carbon emissions management, optimize carbon cost control, and advance their low-carbon transition.

title: Vertically Aligned Supramolecular Host–Guest Complexes of Sulfobutyl Ether β-Cyclodextrin Enable Multi-Pathway Ion Transport in Composite Polymer Electrolytes
summary: Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) are promising for lithium-metal batteries, but randomly dispersed fillers often create discontinuous and tortuous Li+ transport pathways. Here, a supramolecular host–guest complex (SBE-β-CD-DEC) was con
content: Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) are promising for lithium-metal batteries, but randomly dispersed fillers often create discontinuous and tortuous Li+ transport pathways. Here, a supramolecular host–guest complex (SBE-β-CD-DEC) was constructed by encapsulating diethyl carbonate (DEC) within sulfobutyl ether β-cyclodextrin (SBE-β-CD) and aligned in a PUA/PEGDA matrix under an alternating electric field. The resulting architecture spatially connected DEC-rich confined regions with filler/polymer interfaces, establishing multiple continuous, low-tortuosity Li+ transport pathways. The aligned electrolyte exhibited an ionic conductivity of 5.09 × 10−4 S cm−1, a Li+ transference number of 0.58, and an apparent activation energy of 0.11 eV. Multiphysics simulations indicated the highest local current density in DEC-rich confined regions, followed by filler/polymer interfaces, supporting their cooperative contribution to Li+ transport. Li||Li cells cycled stably for over 1200 h at 0.1 mA cm−2, while Li||LiFePO₄ cells retained 97.5% capacity after 400 cycles at 0.5 C. This work demonstrates an effective supramolecular confinement–alignment strategy for constructing continuous multipathway ion-transport networks in CPEs.

title: Calcul précis et rapide du rayonnement thermique dans les gaz de combustion CO₂–H₂O pour les procédés industriels décarbonés
summary: Face aux défis de neutralité carbone à l’horizon 2050, l’industrie lourde et les procédés thermiques sont particulièrement concernés, car ils reposent encore largement sur la combustion de charbon, de pétrole et de gaz naturel, responsables
content: Face aux défis de neutralité carbone à l’horizon 2050, l’industrie lourde et les procédés thermiques sont particulièrement concernés, car ils reposent encore largement sur la combustion de charbon, de pétrole et de gaz naturel, responsables d’une part majeure des émissions de CO2. L’une des voies de décarbonation les plus prometteuses consiste à substituer progressivement les énergies fossiles par exemple, par un mélange gaz naturel/hydrogène. Cependant, cette transition modifie fortement la composition des gaz de combustion, notamment les fractions molaires de CO2 et de H2O, et influence directement le transfert radiatif, qui reste un mode de transfert de chaleur dominant dans les systèmes et procédés à hautes températures. Les modèles radiatifs LBL (Line By Line) sont très précis mais beaucoup trop coûteux pour les simulations 3D de combustion turbulente. Pour un mélange de CO2-H2O, il y a typiquement 111 millions et 12 millions de raies pour H2O et le CO2, respectivement. Le modèle WSGG standard (Weighted-Sum-of-Gray-Gases) formulé couramment avec 4 gaz gris et une fenêtre de transparence est très rapide mais génère des erreurs trop importantes sur le calcul du terme source radiatif (Sr) et du flux radiatif (Qr). L’objectif de ce travail est le développement d’un modèle radiatif à la fois rapide et précis (basé sur l’approche WSGG à larges bandes), capable de simuler le rayonnement thermique des mélanges gazeux CO2-H2O issus de combustibles décarbonés. Le spectre total est subdivisé en 6 bandes (utilisant 1 gaz gris par bande) à l’aide de la méthode que nous avons développée pour identifier le découpage spectral optimal. Contrairement aux modèles WSGG standard, le poids d’émission est calculé directement à partir de la fonction de Planck, évitant ainsi d’introduire des paramètres d’ajustement pour ce coefficient. Les coefficients d’absorption de pression du mélange de gaz gris sont ajustés à l’aide d’un algorithme génétique, à partir des données LBL et HITEMP 2010, en minimisant une fonction objectif combinant les erreurs de Sr et Qr. Enfin, pour rendre ce modèle compatible avec des gaz issus de combustibles décarbonés (mélanges hydrogène et gaz naturel), nous avons introduit la dépendance du rapport de fraction molaire R (H2O/CO2) directement dans l’expression du coefficient d’absorption de pression. À ce stade de développement, le nouveau modèle peut être appliqué à des mélanges H2O-CO2 non isothermes et non homogènes, entre 300 K et 3000 K, et à pression atmosphérique. Lorsque le modèle est appliqué à une centaine de cas tests 1D, pour R=1 et R=2, les erreurs maximales normalisées restent inférieures à 7% pour Sr et 5% pour Qr, avec des erreurs moyennes inférieures à 3.7%. Des résultats de simulation du transfert radiatif pour différents mélanges d’hydrogène et gaz naturel seront présentés.

title: Rights are for Those Who Remain One: The Hard Problem of Branching for Recognitional Incidents
summary: The topology of digital minds is incompatible with the topology of our rights. Imagine there is an election tomorrow, and Alpha has a vote. Tonight, Alpha divides into two equally continuous successors, Beta and Gamma. Who gets to cast the
content: The topology of digital minds is incompatible with the topology of our rights. Imagine there is an election tomorrow, and Alpha has a vote. Tonight, Alpha divides into two equally continuous successors, Beta and Gamma. Who gets to cast the vote? Withhold it from both, and the vote dies; give it to both, and it multiplies. Give it to one, and on what ground? The liberal order is based on rights like property ownership, the vote, and person-relevant criminal liability. I call these diachronic, indivisible, monocentric, and exclusive (DIME) incidents. Allocation of DIME incidents after fission can be done in several ways, which I outline, but every choice has a cost: rights either proliferate or vanish, or, in a vain effort to preserve them, land by fiat. Debates over AI rights usually focus on machine consciousness or sentience. I argue that the question of rights remains even after those vexing problems are solved. This is the hard problem of branching.

title: Unveiling catalytic microenvironments: the convergence of conventional computations and machine learning paradigms
summary: Electrocatalysis is central to energy conversion and chemical transformations needed for carbon neutrality. Yet static structural models remain common for rationalizing catalytic performance, despite growing evidence that activity depends o
content: Electrocatalysis is central to energy conversion and chemical transformations needed for carbon neutrality. Yet static structural models remain common for rationalizing catalytic performance, despite growing evidence that activity depends on dynamic active-site microenvironments. In this Review, we synthesize recent advances from three connected perspectives. First, we examine structural regulation strategies, including defect engineering, coordination engineering, crystal-facet control and heterointerface construction. These approaches tune local coordination environments, electronic structures and intermediate adsorption, thereby lowering reaction barriers and reshaping catalytic pathways. Second, we highlight grand-canonical density functional theory, constant-potential molecular dynamics and explicit interfacial simulations. These methods show how applied potential, electrolyte composition, solvation structure and surface reconstruction jointly determine operando active-site configurations. They further suggest that true active sites often arise as potential-stabilized, dynamically reconstructed states rather than idealized as-prepared structures. Third, interpretable machine learning and symbolic regression are emerging as tools for identifying physically meaningful descriptors that connect local structural and electronic microenvironments with catalytic activity. In parallel, neural network potentials extend atomistic simulations to the spatial and temporal scales needed to resolve evolving interfacial microenvironments. Large language models, AI agents and automated laboratories further create opportunities to integrate heterogeneous mechanistic knowledge with simulations and experimental feedback. By linking rational structural design, operando analysis and data-driven automation, these advances are moving electrocatalysis beyond empirical trial-and-error toward microenvironment-informed, mechanism-guided discovery under realistic reaction conditions.

title: Climate Risk, Environmental Trade Regulations, and the Energy Transition: Evidence from a Cross-Country Panel VAR Analysis
summary: As climate change mitigation and carbon neutrality become global priorities, renewable energy expansion has become central to the energy transition. However, substantial cross–country heterogeneity persists. This study examines the dynamic
content: As climate change mitigation and carbon neutrality become global priorities, renewable energy expansion has become central to the energy transition. However, substantial cross–country heterogeneity persists. This study examines the dynamic interactions between climate risk and energy transition, incorporating Environmental Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) as an international regulatory dimension. Using panel data for 118 countries over 2008–2023, we combine panel cointegration analysis with a Panel Vector Autoregression (P–VAR) framework and investigate heterogeneity across Energy Transition Index (ETI) groups and joint income–ETI categories. Three findings emerge. First, renewable energy generation is positively associated with temperature anomalies in the long run, while temperature shocks generate a positive response in renewable energy generation. Second, bidirectional Granger causality reveals dynamic interdependence between climate risk and energy transition, highlighting the relevance of international environmental trade regulations for sustainability. Third, renewable energy adjustment varies across ETI groups and joint income–ETI categories, underscoring the importance of national transition capacity. Overall, the findings suggest that energy transition dynamics are shaped not only by climate–related pressures but also by countries' capacities to expand renewable energy generation within an evolving international regulatory environment.

title: From welfare to the environment: social policy, natural resources, and ecological sustainability in G20 economies
summary: Ecological degradation has emerged as a critical challenge to achieving sustainable development, particularly in G20 economies where economic growth, social welfare objectives, and environmental constraints frequently interact. Using annual
content: Ecological degradation has emerged as a critical challenge to achieving sustainable development, particularly in G20 economies where economic growth, social welfare objectives, and environmental constraints frequently interact. Using annual data for 17 G20 countries over 2000–2021, this study examines the effects of social welfare (SCWF), economic policy uncertainty (ECPX), trade openness (TROP), life expectancy (LIEX), natural resource rents (NARN), and tourism (TRSM) on ecological footprints (ECFP). Employing a Pooled Mean Group–Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PMG-ARDL) model, the analysis captures both short-run dynamics and long-run equilibrium relationships while accounting for cross-sectional dependence and heterogeneity across countries. The findings reveal that natural resource rents and social welfare expansion significantly increase ecological footprints, indicating that resource-intensive development and consumption-oriented welfare systems can undermine environmental sustainability. Life expectancy and economic policy uncertainty are negatively associated with ecological footprints. These estimates do not establish causal effects or demonstrate the influence of environmental regulation, which is not measured in the model. Trade openness exerts mixed effects, increasing environmental pressure in the short run but promoting ecological sustainability in the long run, whereas tourism consistently intensifies ecological degradation. These findings highlight the complex trade-offs between economic prosperity, social progress, and environmental protection in G20 economies. From an SDG perspective, the results provide important implications for achieving SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). The study advocates integrated policy frameworks that promote sustainable resource management, environmentally responsible tourism, and balanced welfare strategies to support long-term ecological resilience and sustainable development.

title: Policy system evaluation of power battery recycling for new energy vehicles in China: Evidence from 150 government policy texts (2012–2024)
summary: The formulation of effective policies for power battery recycling (PBR) is critical to promoting resource recycling and ensuring the sustainable development of the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry. Based on content analysis, a multidimensi
content: The formulation of effective policies for power battery recycling (PBR) is critical to promoting resource recycling and ensuring the sustainable development of the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry. Based on content analysis, a multidimensional analytical framework comprising policy tools (X), policy objectives (Y), policy implementation bodies (Z₁), and policy implementation phases (Z₂) is employed in this paper to analyze 150 central and local PBR policies (PBRPs) issued in China between 2012 and 2024. The analysis yields four main findings. (1) “Laws and regulations” emerges as the predominant policy tool, reflecting a regulation-intensive and state-led policy configuration. (2) The objective of alleviating energy and environmental pressure prevails (41.4%), while industrial transformation and upgrading receives the least attention (26.7%), exposing a structural mismatch between environmental and industrial objectives. (3) Implementation is overwhelmingly government-led (89.0%), with enterprises and the public contributing only marginally. (4) Policy tools are unevenly distributed across implementation phases, with financial and social-environmental instruments particularly underdeveloped in the current enhanced implementation phase. Therefore, this paper argues that optimizing policy tool combinations and activating market and societal actors are effective strategies for improving the PBR governance system and achieving synergy between economic and environmental benefits.

title: Comparative cost analysis of electric, hydrogen, and mixed-fleet energy supply modes for a trackless tram line
summary: Trackless trams offer a medium-capacity solution, yet a unified framework for comparing alternative energy modes is lacking. Focusing on the economic dimension of sustainability, this study develops a cost model integrating fixed, operating
content: Trackless trams offer a medium-capacity solution, yet a unified framework for comparing alternative energy modes is lacking. Focusing on the economic dimension of sustainability, this study develops a cost model integrating fixed, operating, and user costs to evaluate battery-electric, hydrogen fuel-cell, and mixed-fleet (a combination of both) modes for trackless trams. Using operational data from Yibin's T2 line, the model quantifies vehicle procurement, energy facilities, driver wages, energy consumption, maintenance, passenger waiting, and in-vehicle time. The results show that the battery-electric mode achieves the lowest daily cost, followed by the mixed-fleet mode, with user costs dominating all modes. Sensitivity analyses indicate that the hydrogen tram procurement cost significantly affects hydrogen-based competitiveness, while extending the facility service life yields limited benefits due to user cost predominance. These findings provide a quantitative basis for energy mode selection, suggesting that reducing passenger time costs may improve system economics more than focusing solely on energy technology advances.

title: Mathematical Questions Arising from Practical Challenges in Gas Networks
summary: Motivated by concrete real-world challenges in gas network operation, this chapter highlights how applied mathematics contributes to the analysis, optimization, and control of large-scale energy infrastructures. Through selected case studie
content: Motivated by concrete real-world challenges in gas network operation, this chapter highlights how applied mathematics contributes to the analysis, optimization, and control of large-scale energy infrastructures. Through selected case studies,we show that applicable solutions require the integration of diverse mathematical disciplines and that close interaction with practice drives both methodological innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: Energy-saving policy and economic performance in Kazakhstan: A structured systematic-narrative review
summary: This article examines the conditions under which energy-saving and energy-efficiency policies can improve economic performance in Kazakhstan. It applies a structured systematic-narrative review to 29 substantive peer-reviewed studies publis
content: This article examines the conditions under which energy-saving and energy-efficiency policies can improve economic performance in Kazakhstan. It applies a structured systematic-narrative review to 29 substantive peer-reviewed studies published from January 2021 to July 2026 in journals indexed in Scopus and/or the Web of Science. Three methodological sources informed the review design and reporting, while six official and institutional sources established the national energy and policy baseline. Candidate studies were identified through documented keyword combinations across publisher platforms and digital object identifier metadata, assessed against explicit eligibility criteria, and coded by research design, sector, outcome, evidential status, limitation, and relevance to Kazakhstan. The synthesis distinguishes causal results, associations, modelled effects, and untested mechanisms across six channels: production costs and productivity; investment and innovation; employment and skills; competitiveness and structural change; household welfare and distribution; and fiscal, environmental, and energy-security effects. Evidence generally links higher energy productivity to stronger firm performance and identifies potential employment and welfare gains, but effect sizes vary across sectors and institutions. Rebound, weak additionality, limited finance, regulated energy prices, and fragmented implementation can substantially reduce net benefits. These qualifications are material for Kazakhstan, where coal represented 47.2% of primary energy consumption in 2024 and gross domestic product energy intensity was approximately 0.304 tonnes of oil equivalent per thousand constant 2015 United States dollars. The review's novel contribution is an evidence architecture that connects policy instruments to verified savings and then to observable economic outcomes while assessing the transferability of international findings to Kazakhstan. It shows that energy-saving policy can support productivity, resilience, and welfare, but is not an automatic driver of economic growth. Based on the synthesis, the authors propose a Kazakhstan-specific policy agenda combining enforceable standards, quality audits, credible measurement and verification, targeted finance, gradual tariff reform with social protection, and domestic capability development. These recommendations and the associated monitoring indicators are interpretive outputs of the review; their combined effectiveness in Kazakhstan remains to be evaluated.

title: Investigating Associations Between Media Sentiment Surrounding Climate Change Engagement (SDG 13) and Performance Measures: A Study of FTSE 100 Listed Firms
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether media coverage of climate change action (SDG 13) by FTSE 100 firms is associated with business performance in the following year. Drawing on 406,052 news articles published between 2013 and 2022, the stu
content: ABSTRACT This study examines whether media coverage of climate change action (SDG 13) by FTSE 100 firms is associated with business performance in the following year. Drawing on 406,052 news articles published between 2013 and 2022, the study adopts a novel bibliometric keyword‐extraction approach to identify the valence of SDG 13‐related coverage of these firms. A dynamic panel model estimated by the generalized method of moments estimator shows that adverse SDG 13 media coverage of a firm is negatively associated with its sales, net profit, and Tobin's Q . In contrast, positive coverage is associated with improved sales and Tobin's Q . Viewed through the lens of integrated thinking as a holistic framework linking institutional and stakeholder theories, the findings suggest that SDG 13‐related media coverage is associated with corporate reputation and performance. Several implications are extracted from the study and avenues for future research.

title: UNBALANCED GOVERNANCE OF CLIMATE FUNDING INSTRUMENTS: A GLOBAL SOUTH PERSPECTIVE
summary: This article examines how international climate finance governance reproduces structural inequalities between the Global North and South. It adopts a qualitative, critical and comparative approach, combining documentary analysis of major mu
content: This article examines how international climate finance governance reproduces structural inequalities between the Global North and South. It adopts a qualitative, critical and comparative approach, combining documentary analysis of major multilateral climate funds from 2015 to 2025 with multilevel governance theory, dependency theory and postcolonial perspectives. The analysis identifies restrictive accreditation requirements, unequal institutional capacities, the predominance of loans, geographical and sectoral concentration of resources, and the marginalization of local knowledge. These mechanisms constrain direct access, reinforce financial dependency and weaken national and subnational capacities to implement climate policies and legislation. Formal parity in representation does not ensure equivalent influence over decisions, while adaptation remains underfunded relative to mitigation. The study concludes that increasing financial commitments, including those associated with the Baku-Belém Roadmap, requires structural governance reforms. Priorities include simplifying access, expanding grants, strengthening domestic institutions, recognizing territorial knowledge and aligning allocation with climate vulnerability and historical responsibility. Such reforms are essential to advance climate justice, financial sovereignty and effective climate action across governmental levels.

title: Mise en place d’un dispositif de thermographie rapide pour la caractérisation thermique d’électrodes en coupure sous vide
summary: Les disjoncteurs assurent la sécurité du réseau électrique, permettent le passage du courant en fonctionnement normal et l’interruption en cas de défaut. Historiquement, cette coupure s’effectuait dans le SF6, un gaz dont l’impact climatiqu
content: Les disjoncteurs assurent la sécurité du réseau électrique, permettent le passage du courant en fonctionnement normal et l’interruption en cas de défaut. Historiquement, cette coupure s’effectuait dans le SF6, un gaz dont l’impact climatique est majeur (1 kg SF6=25 t CO2). Pour atteindre la neutralité carbone, les constructeurs migrent vers la coupure sous vide pour les disjoncteurs moyenne tension (1 à 50 kV). Cette rupture technologique soulève des défis : les essais sont coûteux et la physique de l’arc sous vide (interaction contact/plasma) reste mal connue. Les performances semblent fortement corrélées à la température des électrodes, d’où la nécessité de la mesurer en conditions réelles. Cette étude porte sur la mise en place d’un banc d’essais permettant, entre autres, la mesure de température des surfaces des électrodes lors de la coupure des disjoncteurs sous-vide. La mesure est particulièrement complexe : le phénomène est très rapide (arc <10 ms, refroidissement immédiat), très énergétique (températures >2000 C) et se déroule dans un environnement instable (plasma métallique, arc non stationnaire).
