Pour relever ce défi, nous avons conçu un banc d’essais basé sur une maquette en croix reproduisant la géométrie des disjoncteurs, intégrant des périscopes et des caméras pour une thermographie à distance dans le visible et le proche infrarouge. Les longueurs d’ondes retenues tiennent compte des limitations des capteurs et de l’émission propre du plasma (CuCr). Un étalonnage ex-situ a été réalisé avec un corps noir de type cavité pour une émissivité proche de 1, couvrant une plage de température entre 1400 C et 2400 C. Cet étalonnage permet de convertir des niveaux de gris (Digital Levels : DL) en température. Nous avons appliqué une loi de type Planck, intégrant le temps d’obturation (Integration Time : IT) pour accéder à des températures élevées (IT=50 us) et plus faibles (IT=500 us) avec une seule loi d’étalonnage. L’étalonnage a été validé sur les températures de solidification de corps purs (Fe, Ni). Des essais in-situ ont été réalisés sur des contacts dont l’émissivité avait été préalablement mesurée pour différentes températures. Connaissant les transmittances et réflectances des différents objets constituants les chemins optiques, nous avons corrigé les mesures des DL, puis nous les avons convertis en utilisant la loi établie lors de l’étalonnage pour obtenir la température réelle des électrodes lors de la coupure. Les mesures obtenues lors des coupures d’arc (durée <10 ms, températures >2000 C) sont cohérentes avec la littérature. Cette méthodologie démontre la faisabilité d’une thermographie rapide (10000 fps caméra visible et jusqu’à 3500 fps caméra IR) en environnement plasma instable, ouvrant la voie à une meilleure compréhension des mécanismes de coupure sous vide. Ces résultats constituent une étape clé pour optimiser les disjoncteurs sans SF6 et contribuer à la décarbonation des réseaux électriques.

title: Decomposition of carbon emission drivers and urban typology in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area: implications for regional environmental management
summary: The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area is marked by pronounced urban heterogeneity, so that a uniform account of its carbon emission drivers is unlikely to hold. Using panel data for 11 cities from 2015 to 2023, this study applies t
content: The Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area is marked by pronounced urban heterogeneity, so that a uniform account of its carbon emission drivers is unlikely to hold. Using panel data for 11 cities from 2015 to 2023, this study applies the Generalized Divisia Index Method to decompose eight drivers of emission change and to classify the cities by their factor contribution structures. Economic growth (G) and output carbon intensity (CI) are the largest positive and negative contributors in ten of the eleven cities (mean G = +19.18%, mean CI = −9.94%), the exception being Macao. An exploratory Ward clustering of the four most variable factors, cross-validated against k-means, distinguishes four types of driving structure—carbon-intensity suppression, economic-scale driven, energy-scale expansion, and a specialized service-structure type (Macao); an innovation index combining research and development (R&D) intensity and patent density varies independently of these types. Decoupling is likewise uneven, ranging from strong decoupling in three cities (Foshan, Zhongshan and Hong Kong; Tapio elasticity t = −0.152 to −0.437) to weak decoupling in six (0.133 ≤ t ≤ 0.462) and expansive coupling in Huizhou and Macao. Per-capita emissions and energy-structure carbon intensity show marked dispersion. These findings inform a three-tiered policy discussion—differentiated measures, collaborative governance, and data support—for coordinated low-carbon governance in urban agglomerations.

title: Assessing Carbon Storage Potential in the Mediterranean Forests: A Review of Morocco’s Ecosystems
summary: Climate change poses a major global challenge, and forests are increasingly recognized for their role in carbon sequestration. This review employs a dual analytical framework, integrating a systematic bibliometric analysis with a structured
content: Climate change poses a major global challenge, and forests are increasingly recognized for their role in carbon sequestration. This review employs a dual analytical framework, integrating a systematic bibliometric analysis with a structured thematic synthesis, to assess the carbon storage potential of Morocco’s forest ecosystems across both biomass and soil organic carbon pools. Forest types examined range from humid cedar and cork oak stands to semi-arid argan woodlands. The bibliometric analysis, based on 27 peer-reviewed studies retrieved from Scopus, reveals a growing but structurally imbalanced research landscape: approximately 70% of studies address soil carbon, while forest biomass investigations remain comparatively underrepresented. Keyword co-occurrence and collaboration networks further indicate fragmented research dynamics and limited integration of forestry-specific themes. The thematic synthesis provides a quantified overview of carbon stocks: soil organic carbon ranges from 40.1 to 264.7 t C ha⁻1, with the highest values in well-preserved cedar stands, while aboveground biomass carbon ranges from 4.91 t C ha⁻1 in young argan orchards to over 200 t C ha⁻1 in mature cedar forests. These findings reveal critical methodological and spatial gaps constraining national-scale carbon accounting: the absence of species-specific allometric equations for several dominant taxa, inconsistent soil depth treatment across studies, and limited coverage of semi-arid and degraded ecosystems reduce the reliability of current estimates. Strengthening biomass-focused research, expanding remote sensing and machine learning tools, and harmonizing assessment methodologies are identified as priority actions for improving Morocco’s forest carbon reporting under international climate frameworks. This work provides the first national synthesis combining bibliometric and thematic assessment of biomass and soil carbon stocks in Moroccan forest ecosystems. Cite this article as: Naciri, Y., Mderssa, M. E., Ettaqy, A., Abbas, Y., Ibijbijen, J., & Boulli, A. (2026). Assessing carbon storage potential in the Mediterranean forests: a review of Morocco’s ecosystems. Forestist, 76, 0078, doi:10.5152/forestist.2026.25078.

title: Self-Assembly Driven Modulation of Photocatalytic H2O2 Activity in Acridine-Based Derivatives
summary: Abstract Self-assembly provides a powerful strategy for regulating the photophysical and photocatalytic properties of π-conjugated organic molecules through controlled intermolecular organization. Herein, we demonstrate that molecular aggre
content: Abstract Self-assembly provides a powerful strategy for regulating the photophysical and photocatalytic properties of π-conjugated organic molecules through controlled intermolecular organization. Herein, we demonstrate that molecular aggregation can either suppress or activate photocatalysis, depending on the structural and solubility properties of the catalyst. Two organic photocatalysts, Acr-1 and Acr-2, with distinct affinities toward water, exhibit markedly different H2O2 generation behavior upon self-assembly. Hydrophilic Acr-1 efficiently produces H2O2 in aqueous 3-(N-morpholino)propanesulfonic acid (MOPS) solution in its monomeric state, whereas self-assembly suppresses its photocatalytic activity. In striking contrast, Acr-2, which is inactive in its monomeric state, becomes photocatalytically active upon self-assembly. Spectroscopic investigations indicate that aggregation in Acr-2 suppresses nonradiative deactivation pathways and promotes productive photochemical processes, thereby enabling H2O2 generation. The resulting supramolecular assemblies remain stable under continuous irradiation for up to 4 h while retaining their photocatalytic activity. Scavenger experiments combined with spectroscopic analyses further elucidate the involvement of reactive intermediates in H2O2 generation. These findings establish aggregation state as an important molecular parameter for regulating photocatalytic function and demonstrate that supramolecular self-assembly can be harnessed to switch and maintain solar-driven H2O2 generation in organic photocatalyst.

title: Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
summary: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do
content: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. It incorporates at least one method from each major MADM family and includes strategies to enhance resilience against rank reversal. Material consumptions are aggregated into satisfaction or criticality indices, while Monte Carlo simulation captures uncertainty and variability in consumption, lifetimes, and operational conditions. The methodology is applied to the EU including eight electricity generation technologies (wind, solar PV, solar CSP, hydro, biomass and waste, nuclear, coal, and natural gas) and 33 raw materials. Despite minor differences among MADM methods, the framework consistently converges on a ranking in which wind and solar PV are the most material-critical technologies, followed by solar CSP; coal, natural gas and nuclear occupy intermediate positions; biomass and waste, and hydro are the least critical alternatives. These findings highlight that EU decarbonisation strategies must be complemented by targeted raw material policies, including diversification of supply, recycling, material substitution, and strategic planning, to ensure that the transition to renewable electricity is not only low-carbon but also materially resilient and secure.

title: Circularity
summary: Circularity marks a paradigm shift from the traditional linear economy to the necessary circular economy. This volume captures the importance of circularity and its critical role in achieving global sustainability. A sustainable circular ec
content: Circularity marks a paradigm shift from the traditional linear economy to the necessary circular economy. This volume captures the importance of circularity and its critical role in achieving global sustainability. A sustainable circular economy (SCE) is a model of production and consumption, which involves prolonging the lifecycle of existing materials and products as long as possible. SCE addresses global challenges by implementing three base principles: eliminating waste and pollution, circulating products and materials, and regenerating natural resources. Circular development builds a sustainable society through the conservation and use of environmental resources. • Circular economy addresses global challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, waste, and pollution. • Illustrates how a circular economy can be a way to mitigate society’s challenges, both from environmental and from economic and societal perspectives. • Describes how circular development becomes a model of economic, social, and environmental production and consumption that can help achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). • Demonstrates that green sustainable chemistries can and should be leading contributors in the discussion on environmental science and chemistry. • Highlights new models, processes, applications, and developments in circular economics and green chemistry, which demonstrate how sustainability is adapting in the new age.

title: Green Supply Management, Renewable Innovation, and Ecological Capacity: Implications for Sustainable Development Goal 9
summary: ABSTRACT Ecological pressures associated with industrialization, energy use, and resource‐intensive production have intensified the need to identify strategies capable of strengthening ecological capacity, particularly in major emerging eco
content: ABSTRACT Ecological pressures associated with industrialization, energy use, and resource‐intensive production have intensified the need to identify strategies capable of strengthening ecological capacity, particularly in major emerging economies such as China. This study examines how green supply management (GSM), renewable technological innovations (RTI), and energy prices (EP) influence China's ecological capacity over the period 1990Q1–2024Q4. Ecological capacity is measured using the Load Capacity Factor (LCF), while the Quantile Autoregressive Distributed Lag approach captures heterogeneous short‐ and long‐run dynamics. The results confirm long‐run cointegration among the variables and highlight distributional heterogeneity across different quantiles of LCF. GSM exerts a positive long‐run effect on ecological capacity, whereas RTI does not generate a consistent ecological payoff, indicating the importance of effective diffusion and adoption. EP exhibits a negative long‐run association, underscoring the limitations of price‐based mechanisms. The findings provide policy‐relevant insights for advancing SDG 9 through greener supply chains, effective innovation diffusion, and sustainable infrastructure development in China.

title: Unravelling the relationship between grey–green spatial structure and county-level carbon emission density across composite development typologies in the Yangtze River Delta
source: Journal of Asian Architecture and Building Engineering
summary: The transition towards urban carbon neutrality has intensified attention to the relationship between county-level carbon emission density (CED) and grey–green spatial structure across different development contexts. However, existing studie
content: The transition towards urban carbon neutrality has intensified attention to the relationship between county-level carbon emission density (CED) and grey–green spatial structure across different development contexts. However, existing studies often examine socio-economic development, spatial growth, and landscape characteristics separately, limiting understanding of their joint relationships and nonlinear responses. This study examined 303 counties in the Yangtze River Delta in 2018 and 2023, measured CED within Urban Physical Areas, and constructed 18 composite typologies by integrating socio-economic development contexts with spatial growth morphologies. Six grey–green indicators were analysed using XGBoost–SHAP, contribution-pattern clustering, and nonlinear response analysis. CED did not follow a simple growth–shrinkage gradient but varied with combinations of development context and growth morphology. PLADJ ranked first in all 18 typologies in 2018 and remained the leading contributor in 14 typologies in 2023, while AREA_MN_Green ranked first in the remaining four. Hierarchical clustering identified three recurring contribution patterns. PLADJ showed a stable cross-group response threshold of approximately 97%, whereas AREA_MN_Green and LSI_Grey showed more group-specific responses. This study provides an interpretable framework linking typology-specific contribution patterns and nonlinear responses to differentiated low-carbon spatial planning.

title: Transition pathways of coal mining and coal-based power generation industries
summary: This research investigates the strategic directions of a sunset industry sector, coal-based power. Drawing on the literature on sustainable business model innovation (SBMI), dynamic capabilities, and transition pathways, we take an explorat
content: This research investigates the strategic directions of a sunset industry sector, coal-based power. Drawing on the literature on sustainable business model innovation (SBMI), dynamic capabilities, and transition pathways, we take an exploratory approach to analyze how large coal-based businesses are developing transition pathways to reduce their environmental footprints. Analysis of secondary data on the environmental performance of 167 large companies over the period 2014–2023 is followed by an in-depth strategic analysis of five coal mining companies and five coal-based power generation companies to derive insights. The results show that leading firms in downstream businesses, specifically those involved in coal-based power generation, have identified superior transition pathways than their upstream counterparts in coal mining. We attempt to explain the phenomenon through the lens of institutional role in transition, dynamic capabilities, leveraging organizational slack, and structural limitations in pursuing SBMI. Consequently, the synthesis recommends a pragmatic approach to the fossil fuel industry for finding transition pathways. The research provides novel empirical evidence on the transition pathways of fossil fuel industries, contributes to theoretical concepts of business model innovation, and offers actionable insights for practice.

title: Constructing a FinTech Adoption Index for BRICS+ Economies: Evidence from Principal Component Analysis
source: American Journal of Applied Statistics and Economics
summary: Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), this study creates a composite FinTech Adoption Index for eleven BRICS+ economies between 2006 and 2024. The index captures key dimensions of financial and digital infrastructure through four indica
content: Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), this study creates a composite FinTech Adoption Index for eleven BRICS+ economies between 2006 and 2024. The index captures key dimensions of financial and digital infrastructure through four indicators: Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) per 100,000 adults, mobile cellular subscriptions per 100 people, fixed broadband subscriptions per 100 people, and individuals using the internet as a percentage of the population. The World Development Indicators (WDI) database is the source of data for every indicator. The BRICS+ economies differ significantly from one another in terms of the development of digital and financial infrastructure, as shown by descriptive statistics. The correlation analysis indicates moderate-to-strong positive relationships among all four indicators, supporting their suitability for PCA. The findings demonstrate a distinct upward trend in FinTech adoption throughout the BRICS+ economies between 2006 and 2024, emphasising the growing contribution of financial infrastructure and digital connectivity to the advancement of financial technology.

title: Analysis and Improvement of Building Energy Data Collection Systems for Green Remodeling of Aging Small Scale Residential Buildings in South Korea - Comparative Review of International and Domestic Practices
summary: Abstract This study aims to analyze domestic and international building energy data collection systems and propose strategies to promote renewable-energy-based green remodeling in aging small-scale residential buildings in South Korea. A fi
content: Abstract This study aims to analyze domestic and international building energy data collection systems and propose strategies to promote renewable-energy-based green remodeling in aging small-scale residential buildings in South Korea. A five-step review of the literature and relevant documents was conducted to examine European policies and financial support mechanisms, hybrid geothermal–photovoltaic demonstration projects, and building energy data infrastructure. Domestic conditions were assessed by examining the green remodeling system established under the Green Building Construction Support Act, the policies and regulations of five metropolitan cities, and public data systems, including Seumteo, V-World, Architecture HUB, and the National Building Energy Database. Spatial information was also examined using geographic information systems (GIS). The comparison identified six structural problems: the absence of systematic data collection, a policy focus on public buildings, insufficient renewable energy data, inadequate integration of passive and active systems, limited economic feasibility, and a lack of post-retrofit performance verification. Six corresponding improvement strategies are proposed: mandatory monitoring, national demonstration programs, diversified financing mechanisms, one-stop service centers, integrated design guidelines, and phased regulatory mandates. Finally, the study highlights the need to establish an integrated, multilayered data structure at the building level.

title: Towards a EU‐wide regulation for agrivoltaics—A comparative analysis of legal frameworks in Germany, France and Italy
source: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law
summary: Abstract To achieve the EU's targets for expanding renewable energies, it is necessary to use an increasing amount of land for the installation of solar panels. In regions where land is scarce, there is heightened pressure to transform agri
content: Abstract To achieve the EU's targets for expanding renewable energies, it is necessary to use an increasing amount of land for the installation of solar panels. In regions where land is scarce, there is heightened pressure to transform agricultural land into industrial land for the installation of ground‐mounted photovoltaics. As a dual land‐use system, agrivoltaics has the potential to ease land use conflicts by co‐locating solar electricity generation with agricultural activity. However, to ensure synergetic land use, the regulation of agrivoltaics must ensure that the agricultural land in question retains its agricultural characteristics. As experiences, such as those in Taiwan, demonstrate, not only efficient land use but also societal and political acceptance are at stake. This study examines how regulatory frameworks for agrivoltaics in Germany, France and Italy balance electricity production and agricultural use, with the objective of identifying similarities, differences and potential for harmonisation towards an EU‐wide approach. The three countries selected for the analysis are forerunners in national legislation on agrivoltaics, while differing considerably in their approaches towards regulating agrivoltaics. The comparative legal analysis reveals what lessons can be learned for the design of core criteria of regulation at the EU level and lays groundwork for a potential harmonised regulation of agrivoltaics. Based on the findings of the comparative analysis, we suggest harmonising criteria for agricultural production, area unusable for productive agriculture, spatial accessibility, spatial distribution and intensity of light, reversibility of the installation and their verification. Such harmonised criteria could be supplemented by optional requirements regarding water availability, soil health, microclimate and animal welfare.

title: Beyond Linear Growth: Uncovering Thresholds, Regimes, and Sustainable Development Pathways in RCEP Economies
summary: ABSTRACT Achieving sustained economic performance while advancing clean energy, productive transformation, institutional quality, and regional integration remains a challenge for economically diverse regional blocs. This study investigates
content: ABSTRACT Achieving sustained economic performance while advancing clean energy, productive transformation, institutional quality, and regional integration remains a challenge for economically diverse regional blocs. This study investigates how energy conditions, sectoral structure, governance quality, and trade integration influence economic performance across the 15 Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) economies from 2000 to 2023. The empirical framework combines dynamic and endogeneity‐robust panel estimators with nonlinear analysis, endogenous panel threshold estimation, interaction tests, and explainable machine‐learning techniques to capture persistence, heterogeneity, regime dependence, and predictive relationships. The results show that access to clean cooking fuels and technologies and overall energy use are positively associated with economic performance, whereas carbon emissions are negatively associated with it. Industry, manufacturing, and services value added contribute positively, confirming the importance of structural transformation while revealing differences in their relative economic significance. Government effectiveness and political stability also support economic performance, underscoring the role of institutional capacity. Trade effects are asymmetric: exports are positively associated with economic performance, while imports display a negative relationship. Nonlinear and threshold findings indicate that these associations vary across structural and developmental regimes rather than remaining constant throughout the development process. Explainable machine learning identifies energy‐related factors as particularly influential predictors and reveals complementary interactions among energy, governance, production structure, and trade. Overall, economic performance within RCEP emerges from an interconnected, nonlinear, and regime‐dependent development process. The findings call for coordinated policies that expand reliable clean energy access, promote productive upgrading, strengthen governance, reduce emissions, and facilitate higher‐value participation in regional trade networks.

title: Tailored gamification strategies for supporting energy efficient work behavior
summary: Abstract Improving office energy efficiency is essential for EU carbon neutrality, given their significant energy consumption and CO 2 emissions. One way of engaging people in a certain behavior is gamification, which uses game elements in
content: Abstract Improving office energy efficiency is essential for EU carbon neutrality, given their significant energy consumption and CO 2 emissions. One way of engaging people in a certain behavior is gamification, which uses game elements in a non-game context. This study explores how tailored gamification strategies can foster energy-saving behavior at office workplaces. Specifically, it investigates the gamification user type of office workers and its preferences for game elements related to energy-saving. As a result, an online survey among 358 professional office agents sheds light into the gamification user types Hexad (Philanthropist, Socializer, Free Spirit, Achiever, Player, Disruptor) and preferences for 21 game elements related to energy-saving work practices. It revealed that gamification user types significantly shape design preferences for workplace energy-saving applications. Players and Socializers were attracted to a wide range of game elements, while Free Spirits showed minimal preferences. Philanthropists were inclined toward Personal design and collaboration-oriented elements, Disruptors favored competition-oriented elements, and Achievers were particularly drawn to Personal and Performance design elements. Based on these findings, ten design guidelines are proposed for creating gamified applications that encourage energy-saving behaviors in office environments. This research extends the Hexad user typology to workplace energy efficiency and offers practical insights for researchers and practitioners in developing effective gamified strategies for promoting energy saving in office environments.

title: Conceptualizing carbon accounting disclosure and firm performance under sustainability committee oversight in Malaysian oil and gas industry
summary: Abstract In the growing global warming crisis, firms operating in high carbon-intensive industries like the Oil and Gas (O&G) sector are focusing on carbon reduction and transparency. However, Carbon Accounting Disclosure (CAD) in emerging
content: Abstract In the growing global warming crisis, firms operating in high carbon-intensive industries like the Oil and Gas (O&G) sector are focusing on carbon reduction and transparency. However, Carbon Accounting Disclosure (CAD) in emerging economies, such as Malaysia, remains voluntary and non-standardized, which reduces its effectiveness for firm sustainable performance. To address this gap, this study proposes the Sustainability Committee (SC)-Moderated CAD Framework to examine the effect of monetary and non-monetary CAD on firm’s financial and ESG performance, with the moderating role of SC among Malaysian O&G companies listed on Bursa Malaysia. Based on stakeholder and legitimacy theories for direct relationships, and agency theory for the moderating role, the model uses a weighted disclosure index to measure CAD aspects. It is expected that different types of CAD has a positive impact on firm performance, with an effective SC strengthening this relationship by minimizing information asymmetry and promoting improved environmental practices. This study is expected to contribute to the literature by differentiating between monetary and non-monetary CAD and theorizing the potential moderating role of the SC. Furthermore, it offers policy recommendations for policymakers in advancing Malaysia’s Net-Zero emissions target by 2050 through strengthened green governance and the adoption of mandatory sustainability reporting.

title: Energy, cost, and environmental assessment of low-GWP refrigerant replacement pathways for water-cooled chillers
summary: Refrigeration and air-conditioning systems contribute substantially to global energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, making the replacement of refrigerants with high global warming potential essential for water-cooled chillers. Th
content: Refrigeration and air-conditioning systems contribute substantially to global energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, making the replacement of refrigerants with high global warming potential essential for water-cooled chillers. This study compares three refrigerant replacement pathways: R1233zd(E) replacing R134a, R513A replacing R134a, and R514A replacing R123. Cooling capacity, compressor power, and coefficient of performance were measured at load ratios ranging from 25% to 100%. The experimental results were subsequently converted into capacity-normalized annual electricity consumption, life-cycle environmental impacts, and life-cycle costs over a service life of 15 years. The three replacement pathways reduce annual electricity consumption by 5.18%, 11.10%, and 5.03%, respectively, while decreasing life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions by 53.9%, 34.5%, and 10.6%, respectively. R1233zd(E) provides a stable improvement in the coefficient of performance and achieves the greatest reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. R513A exhibits the strongest annual energy-saving potential under partial-load operating conditions, whereas R514A maintains cooling capacity while reducing both greenhouse gas emissions and ozone-depletion impacts. Although all three replacement pathways increase life-cycle costs, the cost–environmental benefit matrix identifies the replacement of R123 with R514A as the most balanced near-term option. The proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for selecting and deploying low-global-warming-potential refrigerant replacement pathways in water-cooled chillers.

title: Regulatory Relief Under Uncertainty: Market Reactions to the EU's Omnibus CSRD Reform
summary: ABSTRACT This article investigates the stock market reaction to the European Commission's Omnibus package, released on 26 February 2025, which seeks to amend the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). To explore whether invest
content: ABSTRACT This article investigates the stock market reaction to the European Commission's Omnibus package, released on 26 February 2025, which seeks to amend the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD). To explore whether investors interpret this proposal as a regulatory relief or as a signal of heightened policy uncertainty, we conduct an event study on 3292 publicly listed European firms. The release was not associated with the positive reaction expected by the Commission. The evidence points instead to a negative, though modest, reaction. This may reflect uncertainty about the announcement and its timing, close to the first reporting date, which left compliance costs sunk. The most negative reactions concentrate among firms most exposed to uncertainty and compliance investments, and among firms in countries that had already transposed the CSRD into national law. These findings underline the need for clear, coherent and credible rules regarding European sustainability regulatory framework.

title: Fermi-Level Modulation in Graphene Sensors Revealed by Voltage-Dependent Raman Spectroscopy and 3D Waterfall Response Mapping
summary: Abstract The electronic properties of graphene sensors are governed by the position of the Fermi level, which determines the carrier concentration and consequently controls the electrical conductivity and sensing performance. Although Fermi
content: Abstract The electronic properties of graphene sensors are governed by the position of the Fermi level, which determines the carrier concentration and consequently controls the electrical conductivity and sensing performance. Although Fermi-level modulation is widely recognized as the fundamental mechanism of graphene-based sensing, its direct experimental correlation with the dynamic sensing response has remained insufficiently explored. In this work, we demonstrate that Raman spectroscopy provides a direct, nondestructive method for quantifying the relative Fermi-level modulation through systematic shifts of the G and 2D Raman bands associated with changes in carrier concentration. The Raman analysis reveals reversible electrical tuning of the graphene electronic structure under source-drain voltage without introducing structural defects, allowing quantitative estimation of the Fermi-level relative displacement. To investigate the dynamic behavior of the same electronic states during sensor operation, low-frequency time–frequency waterfall spectroscopy was employed under chemical and optical stimulation. The results demonstrate that external stimuli induce transient perturbations of the graphene Fermi level, producing characteristic conductivity fluctuations that depend on the magnitude and kinetics of carrier-density modulation. The combination of static (Raman spectroscopy) and dynamic (waterfall fluctuation) analyses establishes a unified sensing mechanism linking Fermi-level modulation → carrier concentration → conductivity fluctuations → sensor response. These findings demonstrate that evaluation of the Fermi level is essential not only for understanding the intrinsic electronic structure of graphene but also for interpreting and optimizing its real-time chemical and optical sensing performance, providing a comprehensive framework for the design of next-generation graphene sensors.

title: Biomass to bioenergy transition through sustainable bioconversion and circular bioeconomy strategies
summary: Access to modern electricity and clean cooking technologies remains uneven across much of Africa, despite the continent's abundant biomass resources, which have the potential to enhance energy security while supporting the transition toward
content: Access to modern electricity and clean cooking technologies remains uneven across much of Africa, despite the continent's abundant biomass resources, which have the potential to enhance energy security while supporting the transition toward a circular bioeconomy. However, a substantial proportion of agricultural, forestry, municipal, and marine organic residues is still treated as waste rather than valorized within the formal energy sector. Morocco exemplifies this disconnect. Although the country has achieved near-universal rural electrification, biomass derived from agricultural and marine resources contributes less than 2% of the modern energy mix, highlighting that the principal challenge lies not in resource availability but in the development of efficient conversion pathways and integrated deployment strategies. This review examines recent advances in biomass-to-bioenergy technologies, with particular emphasis on sustainable bioconversion processes, including enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, anaerobic digestion, and microbial fuel cells. Beyond evaluating technological progress, we assess research trends, innovation dynamics, and technology transfer through bibliometric and patent analyses to identify leading research areas, emerging technologies, and geographical disparities across Africa. We further discuss the role of life cycle assessment in evaluating the environmental sustainability of biomass conversion pathways and demonstrate its importance in identifying low-carbon alternatives capable of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. We conclude that Africa's energy sovereignty depends on moving away from generic policies toward integrated, country-specific deployment strategies that prioritize locally available biomass within circular bioeconomy frameworks.

title: Navigating external conflicts, technological innovations, and financial risks for sustainable development: evidence from the EKC and ecological footprints in the next eleven
summary: Abstract To achieve sustainable development, ongoing research needs further investigations in detail for stronger environmental protection. For this purpose, several studies have investigated the factors of ecological footprints (EF), but v
content: Abstract To achieve sustainable development, ongoing research needs further investigations in detail for stronger environmental protection. For this purpose, several studies have investigated the factors of ecological footprints (EF), but very few of them have taken external and internal conflicts with technological innovations in the context of EKC. Against this backdrop, this study applies some advanced techniques like wavelet plots and augmented mean group (AMG) methods over the panel data of 1984-2022 for the Next Eleven nations. The results find strong linkages among the variables. Moreover, reducing external conflicts can stimulate environmental quality. The results validate that the EKC, technological innovations, and financial risk are environmentally friendly. GDP is contributing to environmental degradation, while the population shows a mixed impact on environmental sustainability. The wavelet plots also show that there is a direct linkage between financial risk and ecological footprints.

title: A Multi-Level Grey Evaluation of the Eco-industrial Development Level of Industrial Parks Based on a Combination of Coefficient of Variation and AHM Weighting
summary: To support environmental management and differentiated green transformation in industrial parks, this study develops an evaluation framework that assesses eco-industrial development performance and identifies park-specific strengths and wea
content: To support environmental management and differentiated green transformation in industrial parks, this study develops an evaluation framework that assesses eco-industrial development performance and identifies park-specific strengths and weaknesses. The framework contains 39 indicators across economic development, ecological environment, material circulation, resource potential, technological innovation, and policy and management. Weights are derived using the Attribute Hierarchical Model (AHM) and coefficient of variation method, integrated via the minimum-deviation principle, and applied through multi-level grey evaluation to four Chinese parks. Findings show that policy and management is weighted highest, followed by economic development and ecological environment; overall performance ranks Tianjin, Suzhou, Dalian, and Fushun. Critically, similar aggregate performance masks distinct weaknesses in environmental governance, resource circulation, technological innovation, and resource conditions. The framework therefore enables diagnosis of differentiated management priorities and supports park-specific pathways toward eco-industrial development.

title: Deciphering the Role of Solution-Phase Species in the Ring-Opening of Unsymmetric Epoxides by Ammonia – A Combination of Experimental Analysis and DFT-Informed Microkinetic Modeling
summary: Abstract Alkanolamines, a group of versatile chemicals in gas treatment, personal care, metalworking, and coatings, are commonly synthesized through the ring opening of epoxides by amines. For unsymmetric epoxides, such as propylene oxide,
content: Abstract Alkanolamines, a group of versatile chemicals in gas treatment, personal care, metalworking, and coatings, are commonly synthesized through the ring opening of epoxides by amines. For unsymmetric epoxides, such as propylene oxide, aminolysis can generate multiple regioisomers and sequential secondary or tertiary amine products. In aqueous systems, this reaction network may be further complicated by the participation of solution-phase species, including water, ammonium ions, and alkanolamine products, which could influence reaction rates and selectivity through hydrogen bonding interactions. Here, we combined flow reactor kinetic measurements, explicit-solvation DFT calculations, and microkinetic modeling to investigate the ring opening of propylene oxide by ammonia in water. Experimental measurements across a broad range of initial conditions revealed unusual kinetic behavior with respect to water, including a low apparent activation energy and an apparent water order greater than two, suggesting the participation of multiple water molecules. These observations were used to guide the development of a detailed microkinetic model in which elementary step rate coefficients were informed by DFT calculations including explicit solution-phase species. These results indicate that, during the reaction, multiple water molecules lower the apparent activation energy by stabilizing the PO ring and bridging NH3 during ring opening, while other solution-phase species, including alkanolamine products, can also stabilize PO and contribute to product-assisted catalysis. More broadly, this work establishes a framework for connecting flow reactor kinetics with molecular-scale modeling to understand complex liquid-phase reaction networks involving explicit solvent and product participation.

title: (In)consistency on the route to Paris: EU and Swedish climate and forest-related policy mixes towards the fulfilment of the Paris Agreement
summary: In response to the Paris Agreement and the EU’s climate emergency declaration, the EU has enacted policies strengthening forests’ role in climate mitigation. This paper analyses the climate-forest policy mix at EU and national levels, using
content: In response to the Paris Agreement and the EU’s climate emergency declaration, the EU has enacted policies strengthening forests’ role in climate mitigation. This paper analyses the climate-forest policy mix at EU and national levels, using Sweden as critical case. We examine the horizontal and vertical consistency of these policy mixes, focusing on problem framings, goals, targets, roles assigned to forests, and procedural – and substantive policy instruments. Combining these aspects into a single analysis adds to previous research by creating more comprehensive understanding of challenges and (in)consistencies in the policy mix, both regarding potential goal trade-offs, approaches towards goal achievement, and (lacking) connections between objectives and policy instruments. We identify four major inconsistencies: (1) differing views on the appropriate balance of EU and Member State influence over forests; (2) numerous policy objectives but few specific targets and concrete instruments; (3) EU’s focus on regulations and market-based instruments versus Sweden’s focus on voluntary actions and ownership rights; and (4) contrasting preferences regarding forest management practices. To bridge these gaps, policymakers need to clearly delineate the EU’s and Member States’ roles, establish measurable and timebound objectives linked to tailored policy instruments, and implement mechanisms for adaptive, multifunctional, and just forest management.

title: Leveraging public finance for energy-efficient housing
source: London School of Economics and Political Science Research Online (London School of Economics and Political Science)
summary: The drive for residential energy efficiency presents both a major challenge for climate policy and an important opportunity to gain new economic, social and energy-security benefits for Europe. Yet while there is an urgent need to renovate
content: The drive for residential energy efficiency presents both a major challenge for climate policy and an important opportunity to gain new economic, social and energy-security benefits for Europe. Yet while there is an urgent need to renovate the building stock to improve its energy efficiency, the scale of the investment this will require cannot be met by public budgets alone. EU member states will also need to use public finance strategically to accelerate renovations and mobilise private investment while balancing competing policy objectives.

title: China’s New Geography
summary: This book explores China’s spatial future through 2060, a future which will be dramatically different from both the Opening Up period starting in 1979, when the rules of landscape building were rewritten, and the Factory of the World era fo
content: This book explores China’s spatial future through 2060, a future which will be dramatically different from both the Opening Up period starting in 1979, when the rules of landscape building were rewritten, and the Factory of the World era following China’s 2001 World Trade Organization (WTO) accession. Drawing on decades of participation in China’s spatial transformation, the authors explore the country’s future landscape by analyzing the intersecting forces of demographic, societal, economic, policy, and technological change. They examine a rapidly changing context shaped by population decline, the pursuit of global technological leadership, and changing lifestyles and consumption patterns. The book addresses pressing questions: How will China’s hollowing out rural landscapes be transformed as new economic nodes emerge based on alternative energy production, digitally enabled agriculture, ecological restoration, and amenity development? As urbanization level peaks at 85% and China’s urban population declines by at least 125 million between 2030 and 2060, how will the national urban system be reshaped? Which urban clusters will emerge as new “Silicon Valleys”? Which will be caught in negative rust belt cycles? And as urban outward expansion and physical development slow dramatically, how will technological change, shifting social expectations, and new mobility and production systems reshape China’s built landscape? This will be a useful resource for designers, investors, developers, and all those interested in better understanding China’s emerging new geography and landscape, as well as for students and academics across a range of disciplines, including urban and regional planning, landscape architecture, geography, and Asian studies.

title: A text-mining analysis of climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency in Chinese listed firms
summary: This study examines the association between climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency using Chinese A-share data from 2012 to 2024. A firm-level disclosure index is constructed via text mining based on the TCFD framework. Two-
content: This study examines the association between climate risk disclosure and corporate energy efficiency using Chinese A-share data from 2012 to 2024. A firm-level disclosure index is constructed via text mining based on the TCFD framework. Two-way fixed effects models show a positive association, with a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure corresponding to approximately a 3.6% increase in energy efficiency, robust to endogeneity tests. Transition risk disclosure has a stronger association with energy efficiency than physical risk; the difference widens further when standardized by each dimension’s dispersion. Mediation analysis indicates green innovation and eased financing constraints are partial channels whose separately estimated indirect effects sum to approximately 20% of the total effect, though the direct effect dominates. Heterogeneity analysis reveals stronger effects in state-owned, heavily polluting, and carbon pilot region firms, with insignificant effects outside pilot regions; the association also strengthens significantly after the launch of the national carbon market in 2021. The study contributes to the literature by shifting the focus from capital market reactions to real operational outcomes, distinguishing between physical and transition risk disclosure, and highlighting the role of institutional context in determining whether climate disclosure produces substantive effects on energy performance.

title: D6.2 – Sectoral pathways to sustainable, secure and aff ordable net-zero transition in the EU and China
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The analysis assesses alternative net-zero pathways for the European Union (EU) and China under two scenarios: Low-carbon Collaboration (S1), characterised by strong international cooperation and favourable investment conditions, and Low-ca
content: The analysis assesses alternative net-zero pathways for the European Union (EU) and China under two scenarios: Low-carbon Collaboration (S1), characterised by strong international cooperation and favourable investment conditions, and Low-carbon Nationalism (S2), characterised by geopolitical fragmentation, higher technology costs and restricted technology diffusion. The EU results show both scenarios can achieve climate neutrality under the assumed climate constraints, with electrification, renewable energy and hydrogen central to decarbonisation. However, reduced international cooperation increases cumulative energy-system costs by approximately 8%, raises electricity prices by 5–6% and increases hydrogen prices by more than 20% during its main market-development phase. Land-use modelling confirms that forests and agricultural land management contribute to balancing residual emissions. However, land-based carbon removals depend on biomass demand and competing land uses. The analysis also identifies agricultural non-CO₂ emissions as a major challenge, accounting for approximately 75% of the EU's remaining non-CO₂ emissions in 2050. The Chinese modelling framework highlights the benefits of international cooperation and accelerated mitigation technology diffusion across industrial supply chains and agriculture. Agricultural modelling indicates accelerated technology diffusion can bring the peak of non-CO₂ emissions forward to around 2030. By 2060, emissions fall by 27% under the conventional technical-potential pathway and 47% under the maximum technical-potential pathway, relative to business as usual. Restricted diffusion delays the peak until around 2050 and reduces mitigation. Overall, the results demonstrate that international cooperation can facilitate technology deployment and reduce transition costs, while additional targeted measures are needed to address persistent emissions, particularly in agriculture and other hard-to-abate sectors.

title: A reinforcement learning–based two-level low-carbon economic dispatch of integrated energy systems with liquid CO2 energy storage
summary: Integrated energy systems (IES) face increasing challenges in achieving low-carbon and economically efficient operation because of the strong inter-temporal coupling of long-duration energy storage and the limited coordination of carbon and
content: Integrated energy systems (IES) face increasing challenges in achieving low-carbon and economically efficient operation because of the strong inter-temporal coupling of long-duration energy storage and the limited coordination of carbon and oxygen utilization. However, the coordinated integration of long-duration liquid CO₂ energy storage (LCES) scheduling with carbon–oxygen recycling has received limited attention. To address this gap, this study develops a bi-level low-carbon economic dispatch framework. First, a coupled LCES–OCC–power-to-gas (P2G)–methanol synthesis system is established, in which the oxygen generated by P2G is supplied to oxygen-enriched combustion capture (OCC) and captured CO₂ is coordinated between LCES and methanol synthesis, forming a closed carbon–oxygen utilization loop. Second, a PPO-based bi-level scheduling architecture is developed for long-horizon LCES operation, with proximal policy optimization (PPO) determining the charge/discharge strategy and a lower-level mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model performing constraint-based IES dispatch. Case studies show that the fully integrated configuration reduces total operating cost by 22.47% and actual carbon emissions by 15.94% compared with a battery-only configuration, while eliminating wind and solar curtailment. Compared with the configuration without LCES, the total operating cost is further reduced by 4.12%. Under the same integrated system, PPO reduces operating cost by 7.7% relative to the no-RL MILP strategy and by 1.29% relative to deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG), while reducing actual carbon emissions by 4.32% compared with DDPG. Monte Carlo analysis achieves 97.7% feasibility with a 3.3% coefficient of variation in actual carbon emissions. These results demonstrate the potential of coordinated LCES and carbon–oxygen utilization for simultaneously improving the economic, renewable-accommodation, and low-carbon performance of IES.

title: Higher-order metabolic interactions among oral commensals gate pathobiont expansion through succinate-driven pH modulation
summary: Despite advances in defining microbiome shifts associated with inflammatory mucosal diseases, the ecological interactions that constrain or facilitate pathobiont expansion remain poorly understood. Using a six-species synthetic oral microbi
content: Despite advances in defining microbiome shifts associated with inflammatory mucosal diseases, the ecological interactions that constrain or facilitate pathobiont expansion remain poorly understood. Using a six-species synthetic oral microbial community and factorial interaction screening, we identified a higher-order interaction governing the growth of the periodontal pathobiont Porphyromonas gingivalis. The core community member Veillonella parvula was the strongest positive determinant of P. gingivalis growth, but this effect was substantially reduced by the health-associated commensal Actinomyces oris. A. oris-mediated antagonism resulted from extracellular acidification and was enhanced under anaerobic conditions. Genetic dissection of A. oris fermentation revealed that lactate dehydrogenase (ldh1) contributes to anaerobic lactate production, but ldh1 deletion only partially relieved P. gingivalis inhibition. Instead, succinate, produced through a succinate dehydrogenase/fumarate reductase pathway (sdh2), emerged as the principal driver of acidification and P. gingivalis suppression. At high cell densities, however, V. parvula consumed both lactate and succinate, reversing acidification and restoring conditions permissive for P. gingivalis growth. To assess the relevance of these interactions in vivo, we analyzed subgingival microbiome from 1,355 adults, including 555 with detectable P. gingivalis. Among these individuals, P. gingivalis abundance was negatively associated with Actinomyces abundance after adjustment for periodontitis severity, whereas this association was attenuated at high V. parvula abundance, consistent with the interaction observed in vitro. Together, these findings identify succinate as a previously unrecognized mediator of interbacterial antagonism and reveal how higher-order metabolic interactions among oral commensals regulate pathobiont expansion through pH modulation, with protective effects shaped by oxygen availability and metabolic cross-feeding.

title: Asymmetrical compositional gap between muscovite and NH 4 -bearing micas – structural constraints: a combined experimental–theoretical study
summary: The usual coexistence in nature and in synthesised samples of NH 4 -bearing micas with NH 4 -free muscovite or illite has brought us to study their structural stability and characteristics. We used a combination of density functional theory
content: The usual coexistence in nature and in synthesised samples of NH 4 -bearing micas with NH 4 -free muscovite or illite has brought us to study their structural stability and characteristics. We used a combination of density functional theory methods and updated absorption-corrected nanoscale analyses of previously studied Germunde (Portugal) and Iberian Range (Spain) samples. Energy dispersive X-ray compositional maps were acquired using high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, with high-angle annular dark-field images of ion-milled samples. The maps show the micaceous areas formed by a nano-intergrowth of major ammonium mica and minor muscovite or illite. To avoid mutual contamination between the two types of micas, zones were selected on homogeneous areas of the maps. The computer simulation allowed the structure of tobelite and various NH4/K ratio compositions to be reproduced and their energetic differences to be calculated. The overall range from pure tobelite up to 3K/1NH4 compositions is stable, but the composition 7K/1NH4 has positive cation exchange energy, being unstable. This composition coincides with a compositional gap found in the analysed real samples, which is responsible for the co-existence at the level of samples of NH 4 -free micas with the ammonium micas. The computer calculation has confirmed the structural similarity between the two kinds of micas, with the exception of the interlayer space, where H bonds play a significant role in the stabilisation of the tobelite structure. As a difference compared to K micas, the NH 4 micas mix a variety of polytypes at the sample level. Ammonium micas cover a continuous solid solution from tobelite up to a composition with major K but still some NH 4 ; hence, they should be considered to be a series name, with minor structural differences compared to muscovite, separated by a compositional gap.

title: Ocean connectedness and carbon footprint awareness among undergraduates: the serial mediating roles of ocean stewardship and moral disengagement in high-carbon behavior
summary: Abstract Achieving ocean sustainability requires not only technological and policy responses but also greater awareness of how everyday activities contribute to carbon emissions. Although ocean connectedness has been linked to pro-environme
content: Abstract Achieving ocean sustainability requires not only technological and policy responses but also greater awareness of how everyday activities contribute to carbon emissions. Although ocean connectedness has been linked to pro-environmental behavior, its relationship with carbon footprint awareness and the psychological processes underlying this relationship remain unclear. Using cross-sectional survey data from 720 undergraduates at a marine-focused university in China, this study tested a serial mediation model involving ocean connectedness, ocean stewardship, moral disengagement in high-carbon behavior, and carbon footprint awareness. The results showed that ocean connectedness positively predicted carbon footprint awareness. Ocean stewardship and moral disengagement in high-carbon behavior each mediated the relationship between ocean connectedness and carbon footprint awareness and jointly constituted a serial mediation pathway. The study extends research on human–ocean relationships to individual-level carbon-related cognition and provides theoretical and practical implications for cultivating low-carbon awareness among university students through ocean education.

title: Energy and Geopolitics
summary: This introductory textbook offers students a comprehensive and accessible overview of the complex relationship between energy supply, energy markets and international politics. The idea that energy shapes and is shaped by geopolitics is fir
content: This introductory textbook offers students a comprehensive and accessible overview of the complex relationship between energy supply, energy markets and international politics. The idea that energy shapes and is shaped by geopolitics is firmly rooted in the popular imagination – and not without reason. Very few countries have the means to secure their energy needs through locally available supplies; instead, enduring dependencies on other countries have developed. Given energy’s strategic significance, supply systems for fuels and electricity are now seamlessly interwoven with foreign policy and global politics. Energy and Geopolitics enables students to enhance their understanding of this field and sharpen their analytical skills. Per Högselius guides us through the complexities of world energy and international energy relations, examining a wide spectrum of fossil fuels, alongside nuclear and renewable energies. Uniquely, this book also shows how the geopolitics of energy is not merely a matter for the great powers and reveals how actors in the world’s smaller nations are as active in their quest for power and control. This revised and expanded edition takes into account several dramatic shifts that have occurred in recent years in the global energy arena, including the spectacular renewables boom, the quest for transnational electricity grids and hydrogen trade, and the radical restructuring of global fossil fuel flows following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and the eruption of the Iran war in 2026. Encouraging students to apply a number of central concepts and theoretical ideas to different energy sources within a multitude of geographical, political and historical contexts, this book will be a vital resource for students and scholars of geopolitics, energy security and international environmental policy and politics.

title: Self-Perception of Sustainable Practices: A Comparison Between Conventional and Organic Farmers
summary: Agricultural systems are facing the need to transform towards more sustainable production practices. Although organic farming emerged decades ago as a model for sustainable farm systems, conventional farmers are increasingly seeking to adop
content: Agricultural systems are facing the need to transform towards more sustainable production practices. Although organic farming emerged decades ago as a model for sustainable farm systems, conventional farmers are increasingly seeking to adopt practices that address specific sustainability issues. This paper assesses conventional and organic farmers' self-perceptions of their implementation of sustainable activities, how these self-perceptions differ between the two farming types, and the interconnections among sustainable practices. An online survey (n = 234) was conducted to capture German farmers´ self-perceptions in 2022. The open answers on sustainability practices were analysed using qualitative content and semantic network analysis. The qualitative content analysis revealed that organic farms primarily view their organic farming practices as sustainable practices themselves, while conventional farms mostly contribute to diverse cultural landscapes and optimised nutrient management. The semantic networks within the statements of the organic farms were more strongly interconnected compared to the network of statements from conventional farms. This signals that a common perception about how sustainable farming can be defined is more developed and more coherent among organic farmers. Respondents from both farm groups are making efforts to become more sustainable. However, organic farming seems to show limited dynamics in adopting new practices, while conventional farms seem to lack a systems-based perception of sustainability. In future, both farming types should strengthen efforts to learn from each other. These findings have important implications for designing agricultural policies that target a more sustainable agricultural system overall.

title: From comparability to sustainability: new evidence on ESG performance and financial constraints
summary: We investigate how accounting comparability enhances corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and whether financial constraints mediate this relationship in China. Using a balanced panel of 786 non-financial A-share
content: We investigate how accounting comparability enhances corporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and whether financial constraints mediate this relationship in China. Using a balanced panel of 786 non-financial A-share firms from 2010 to 2023, we employ panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE), the Sobel mediation test, and dynamic GMM estimations to address endogeneity concerns. We find that higher accounting comparability significantly enhances ESG performance, with the strongest effect observed in the governance pillar. Further analysis shows that accounting comparability reduces firms’ financial constraints by alleviating information asymmetry, whereas financial constraints adversely affect ESG performance. Mediation analyses confirm that financial constraints partially mediate the relationship between accounting comparability and ESG performance. The results are robust to alternative measures and model specifications. We suggest that enhancing accounting comparability can promote corporate sustainability by improving reporting quality and the financing environment, providing implications for policymakers, investors, and corporate managers.

title: Overview of Microreactor Technical Challenges and Opportunities
summary: Microreactors provide a new opportunity for the deployment and use of nuclear power in nontraditional markets and applications. This opportunity stems principally from the small physical size and the small power level of these reactors, whi
content: Microreactors provide a new opportunity for the deployment and use of nuclear power in nontraditional markets and applications. This opportunity stems principally from the small physical size and the small power level of these reactors, which enable the possibility of transportable and relocatable nuclear power. However, these same characteristics give rise to significant challenges of feasibility and economic competitiveness.This article seeks to compile and identify key technical and regulatory knowledge gaps in support of the development of this new class of nuclear power systems. The challenges identified include those arising in the context of reactor physics design and modeling, shielding during operation and transportation, balance of plant, fuels, structural materials, controls, licensing, siting, transportation, and economics. Specific challenges, such as high neutron leakage, fuel enrichment, decay heat removal, and regulatory requirements, are also discussed.An attempt is made to identify solutions and key considerations that must be made when attempting to address these challenges. This includes topics such as advanced materials and fuels, new technologies, and new and adapted markets that would be more amenable to microreactors.

title: Synergistic Interfacial Reinforcement and Dynamic Mechanical Properties of Wet‐Mixed Natural Rubber/Carbon Black/Silica Hybrid Composites
summary: ABSTRACT Tuning filler architecture and interfacial interaction is essential to optimizing the performance of advanced rubber composites. In this study, a series of functionalized carbon black/silica hybrid fillers (DCB) with distinct speci
content: ABSTRACT Tuning filler architecture and interfacial interaction is essential to optimizing the performance of advanced rubber composites. In this study, a series of functionalized carbon black/silica hybrid fillers (DCB) with distinct specific surface areas and pore size distributions were synthesized to reinforce natural rubber (NR) via a wet‐mixing process. Morphological characteristics have shown that surface functionalization effectively mitigates the agglomeration of fillers and ensures uniform distribution within the rubber matrix. Dynamic mechanical analysis and equilibrium swelling tests have revealed that the pore topology adaptable to DCB fillers promotes the formation of bound rubber and thus increases effective hydrodynamic volume. In particular, L‐DCB has a large pore (> 50 nm) and exhibits a reduced resistance module enhanced by the physical entrapment of rubber chains. On the contrary, the high specific surface area of DCB with a high specific surface area facilitates the strongest interfacial interaction. This was evidenced by a 10% increase in bound rubber content, achieving a superior tensile strength of 30 MPa and minimum volume loss (0.2 cm 3 ). Furthermore, analysis of the Payne effect supports that energy dissipation is mainly influenced by the chain desorption dynamics at the filler–matrix interface. Consequently, the low specific surface area of DCB/NR composite offers an optimal trade‐off between wet skid resistance and rolling resistance for green tire applications, while the middle specific surface area of the DCB/NR system displays the most balanced overall mechanical profile. This work emphasizes the synergy of pore structure engineering and surface modification in the design of high‐performance elastomer composites.

title: The Economic Sustainability of Intangible Cultural Heritage in the Platform Age With Global Evidence and Implications for Xinjiang
summary: ABSTRACT Digital platforms lower market access costs for intangible cultural heritage but can concentrate visibility, weaken community control, and disconnect revenue from cultural reproduction. This global survey integrates platform and cu
content: ABSTRACT Digital platforms lower market access costs for intangible cultural heritage but can concentrate visibility, weaken community control, and disconnect revenue from cultural reproduction. This global survey integrates platform and cultural economics with research on authenticity, intellectual property, and heritage governance. Its Platform Frictions, Cultural Rents, and Intergenerational Reproduction framework distinguishes living practices from their commercial products, recordings, and experiences. Economic sustainability requires four minimum conditions that cannot substitute for one another. These comprise adequate net market access, viable cultural reproduction, a sufficient practitioner value share, and meaningful community control. The framework distinguishes these conditions from the mechanisms through which platforms affect them. Rankings, provenance labels, copyright, and certification can improve discovery and bargaining while concentrating demand, excluding legitimate variants, or burdening small producers. Community authorization requires representation, reviewable delegation, and effective appeal. Distributional assessment separates individual earnings, collective transfers, unpaid contributions, and investment in transmission. Applications to Xinjiang differentiate crafts, performances, foodways, and community events by economic object and institutional responsibility. Longitudinal indicators of apprentice retention, repertoire in use, and contextual participation distinguish authorized adaptation from commercial hollowing. Platform growth sustains living heritage when returns support practitioners, learning, and community authority.

title: Thermally Engineered Defects and Surface Architecture for High‐Performance Reversible Solid Oxide Cells Air Electrode
summary: ABSTRACT Reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs) provide an efficient route for interconverting electricity and hydrogen fuels, but their performance is limited by sluggish oxygen electrocatalysis at the air electrode. La 0.6 Sr 0.4 Co 0.2 Fe
content: ABSTRACT Reversible solid oxide cells (RSOCs) provide an efficient route for interconverting electricity and hydrogen fuels, but their performance is limited by sluggish oxygen electrocatalysis at the air electrode. La 0.6 Sr 0.4 Co 0.2 Fe 0.8 O 3‐δ (LSCF) is the most technically mature air electrode material; nevertheless, its oxygen electrocatalytic activity and stability remain inadequate. Existing strategies generally rely on compositional modification and surface decoration, often at the expense of processing simplicity and scalability. Here, we establish thermal processing as a simple and scalable strategy to unlock the oxygen electrocatalytic potential of LSCF by coordinately regulating its defect chemistry and surface architecture. Lowering the calcination temperature from 1000 (LSCF1000) to 800°C (LSCF800) coordinately activates Co/Fe redox centers, enriches oxygen vacancies, and preserves a high‐area surface architecture, accelerating oxygen surface exchange and bulk transport, enhancing activity. Meanwhile, the lattice expansion and enlarged surface area in LSCF800 alleviate La 3+ /Sr 2+ elastic mismatch and local Sr accumulation, suppressing Sr segregation and enhancing stability. Consequently, the LSCF800 electrode exhibits a polarization resistance of 0.014 Ω cm 2 with a degradation rate of 0.057% h −1 at 700°C, below that of LSCF1000 (0.094 Ω cm 2 and 0.46% h −1 ). This work establishes thermal regulation as an effective route for developing high‐performance oxygen electrodes for RSOCs.

title: Optimal energy storage configuration for multi-energy microgrids based on hybrid multi-stage robust optimization
summary: The source-load uncertainty of a multi-energy microgrid shows markedly different fluctuation characteristics across operating scenarios, which makes an energy storage configuration that balances economy and reliability difficult to obtain.
content: The source-load uncertainty of a multi-energy microgrid shows markedly different fluctuation characteristics across operating scenarios, which makes an energy storage configuration that balances economy and reliability difficult to obtain. This study proposes an optimal energy storage configuration model for multi-energy microgrids based on hybrid multi-stage robust optimization. An electricity–heat–hydrogen multi-energy microgrid model is first established, and its objective minimizes the sum of the annualized storage investment cost and operation cost. A comprehensive-norm ambiguity set constructed from a 1- and an ∞ -norm constraint then characterizes the uncertainty of the scenario probability distribution, a box uncertainty set with an uncertainty budget characterizes the source-load fluctuation within each scenario, and a min–max–max–min hybrid multi-stage stochastic-robust storage capacity model that accounts for the worst-case scenario probability is formulated. Finally, the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm decomposes the model into a master problem and two-level subproblems that are solved iteratively, and the intra-scenario max-min bilevel problem is transformed into an equivalent single-level problem through Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions. Case studies show that the proposed method hedges against both the source-load output uncertainty and the scenario probability uncertainty, and the configured storage reduces the out-of-sample expected total cost of the microgrid by 6.7% and the worst-case daily cost by 11.3%, and it eliminates the 85.6 kWh daily average loss of load of the storage-free scheme. The conservative nature of the proposed method is tuned flexibly through the uncertainty budget and the confidence level of the comprehensive norm, and a sound balance between economy and robustness is reached.

title: Climate reporting in public sector organisations: identity construction and changes
source: Journal of Public Budgeting Accounting & Financial Management
summary: Purpose The purpose of this article is to explore climate change reporting by public sector organisations. In particular, the analysis draws attention to how public sector organisations represent themselves through climate reporting practic
content: Purpose The purpose of this article is to explore climate change reporting by public sector organisations. In particular, the analysis draws attention to how public sector organisations represent themselves through climate reporting practice to construct and reproduce their identities over time. Design/methodology/approach A comprehensive content analysis of 164 annual and stand-alone sustainability reports produced by 15 public sector organisations listed on the Australian National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting register over an 11-year period from 2014 to 2024 was used for this study. The analysis is informed by Tregidga et al.'s (2014) identity framework of sustainable organisations. Findings The analysis reveals an unbalanced pattern of identity construction in public sector climate reporting, characterised by a strong focus on compliance-oriented reporting, followed by reporting on climate leadership and limited engagement with strategically “good” practices associated with legitimacy seeking. Despite evidence of more substantive climate reporting, disclosures continue to focus predominantly on metrics and statistics reflecting regulatory and policy expectations. The longitudinal analysis reinforces this identity structure, although their climate reporting has developed into a more complex communicative space through which public sector organisations simultaneously construct multiple identities over time, implying that public sector climate reporting serves as a dynamic and ongoing process of identity construction rather than a linear transition from one identity to another. The analysis across organisational types also reveals that a compliance-oriented identity is most pronounced among local governments and moderately prominent in public service organisations, whereas a leadership-oriented identity emphasising community impact and knowledge sharing is most strongly developed in public universities. Originality/value Despite the rapid development of climate reporting in corporate contexts, research on sustainability and climate reporting in the public sector is still underdeveloped, even as these organisations increasingly recognise the importance of disclosing, governing and managing climate-related impacts. This article fills the gap by exploring how disclosures on climate change have evolved over time within public sector organisations to contribute to accountability and effective policy implementation. It extends Tregidga et al.'s (2014) organisational identity framework to a public sector context, where climate reporting is characterised by the coexistence of regulatory, public value and legitimacy considerations.

title: Exchange Rates and International Tourism Demand with Endogenous Prices and Capacity Constraints
