summary: ABSTRACT Why does destination depreciation sometimes expand tourism and sometimes leave demand almost unchanged? We develop a two‐destination equilibrium model with endogenous supplier prices, imported‐cost exposure, currency risk, and capa
content: ABSTRACT Why does destination depreciation sometimes expand tourism and sometimes leave demand almost unchanged? We develop a two‐destination equilibrium model with endogenous supplier prices, imported‐cost exposure, currency risk, and capacity constraints. Five propositions separate price transmission, destination reallocation, additional trips, and welfare. Depreciation expands demand only when its conversion benefit exceeds the associated increase in supplier costs. A binding capacity constraint absorbs further cost relief into scarcity rents and creates unequal quantity responses to favorable and adverse shocks. Destination gains can arise entirely from reallocation when total international travel is fixed. Risk protection raises demand only when its certainty‐equivalent benefit exceeds its price. These analytical results organize a critical synthesis of tourism‐demand evidence. A documented literature verification and a paired comparison of Mauritian studies distinguish measurement differences from changes in samples and estimators. Booking‐horizon alignment remains a theoretical implication requiring direct testing. The analysis identifies the observations needed to distinguish the mechanisms behind conflicting exchange‐rate estimates.

title: Modeling the moral account: a system dynamics framework for brand-induced moral licensing and behavioral rebound in sustainable consumption
summary: Introduction Quantitative models of sustainable consumption typically treat consumption as exogenous, assuming that every green purchase improves environmental outcomes. Behavioral research on moral licensing, however, suggests that purchas
content: Introduction Quantitative models of sustainable consumption typically treat consumption as exogenous, assuming that every green purchase improves environmental outcomes. Behavioral research on moral licensing, however, suggests that purchases perceived as virtuous can license compensatory indulgence that erodes some of the benefit. Recent formal work treats licensing as an environmental rebound mechanism in static consumer models; this study contributes the first dynamic stock-and-flow formalization, developed from a recent conceptual framework of brand-induced moral licensing. Methods Four communication pathways (virtue attribution, identity conferral, effort signaling, and absolution framing) feed two moral accounts with opposite mechanics: credits, which deplete when spent, and credentials, which license behavior without being consumed. The model yields closed-form steady states and a licensing-resistance condition on the rebound ratio ρ> (backfire at ρ> 1). Communication parameters were calibrated through a preregistered content analysis of 120 verbatim-archived units from eight sustainable brands, with perfect dual-coder agreement on the reliability subsample; identity internalization was calibrated from a two-country survey of 3,293 adults. The behavioral conversion parameters are literature-anchored or illustrative, so all rebound magnitudes are model-derived, order-of-magnitude results rather than empirical estimates. Results Rebound stays far below backfire: steady-state values span 0.01 to 0.19 across archetypes, preserving 81 to 99% of gross benefit, across 8,000 uncertainty samples and under structural variants allowing credential depletion, sign reversal, and alternative licensing functions. Calibration inverts the theorized risk ordering: identity-positioned brands deploy almost no identity-conferring language, decoupling the typology's conceptual categories from their communication signatures. The model further predicts that 6-month evaluations understate long-run rebound nearly five-fold, implying measurement windows of 1 to 3 years. Absolution framing is absent from the corpus, consistent with the application timeline of Directive (EU) 2024/825; in counterfactual simulation, restoring such claims forfeits up to a third of gross benefit, whereas reducing the growth signal lowers cumulative modeled benefit without reducing rebound. Discussion Licensing rebound is projected to be real but bounded; message design, not demarketing, is the effective lever within the modeled mechanism. The model supplies an auditable communication-risk map and the design brief for the longitudinal study the field lacks.

title: Heritage‐Sensitive Low‐Carbon Urban Development Through SDG ‐Linked Sustainable Policy Prioritization
summary: ABSTRACT Chinese cities face the challenge of accelerating the low‐carbon transition while preserving cultural identity, spatial quality, and social sustainability in heritage‐sensitive areas. This study develops a decision‐support framewor
content: ABSTRACT Chinese cities face the challenge of accelerating the low‐carbon transition while preserving cultural identity, spatial quality, and social sustainability in heritage‐sensitive areas. This study develops a decision‐support framework aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to prioritize strategies integrating cultural heritage preservation, renewable energy, and sustainable urban development under uncertainty. The Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to determine the relative importance of the criteria and sub‐criteria, while Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS)‐Grey analysis was used to rank the proposed strategies based on expert judgments. The findings of Fuzzy AHP identified Urban Aesthetics as the most important main criterion, followed by Renewable Energy Integration and Preservation of Historic Sites. The TOPSIS‐Grey results indicate that Renewable Energy Integration and Cultural Landmarks is the highest priority, demonstrating the importance of incorporating clean‐energy technologies into heritage sites without compromising their architectural and cultural significance. Sustainable Urban Design and Cultural Districts ranks second, emphasizing pedestrian‐friendly streets, green infrastructure, energy‐efficient public spaces, and district‐level cultural identity. Historical Building Preservation and Green Design ranks third, highlighting the value of combining building conservation with environmentally responsible materials and energy‐efficient technologies. The results indicate that integrated strategies should be prioritized in heritage‐oriented low‐carbon development. The study links SDGs 11.4, 7, and 13 within a unified urban‐governance framework and translates broad sustainability goals into practical policy priorities for Chinese cities and districts.

title: Step-adaptive residual attention network for multi-step battery temperature prediction
summary: Abstract To address the limitations of existing lithium-ion battery temperature prediction models, including insufficient utilization of input features, suboptimal allocation of gradient resources across prediction steps, and the limited re
content: Abstract To address the limitations of existing lithium-ion battery temperature prediction models, including insufficient utilization of input features, suboptimal allocation of gradient resources across prediction steps, and the limited representational capacity of convolutional modules, this paper proposes a novel multi-step temperature prediction model named Step-Adaptive Residual Attention Network (SARA-Net). First, a Broad Learning System (BLS) is introduced to efficiently expand the input feature space through mapped nodes and enhancement nodes, enhancing the extraction of deep information from limited monitoring variables. Second, a Gated Sample Convolution and Interaction Network (GSCINet) is employed to extract multi-scale local temporal features via odd-even subsequence splitting, independent processing with dual convolution kernels, and gated interaction learning. Third, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network (BiLSTM) is used to model global temporal dependencies, capturing long-term dependencies and lagged responses in battery temperature evolution. Finally, a Step-Adaptive Residual Attention Loss function (SARA Loss) is designed to dynamically adjust the loss weights of different prediction steps, effectively achieving an optimal allocation of limited gradient resources. Experiments are conducted on a dataset generated by Fluent finite element simulation under 12 charging/discharging conditions. The results show that under seen conditions, the proposed model reduces Mean Squared Error (MSE) by more than 71.2% compared to traditional models such as Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM), and by more than 63.2% compared to advanced models such as DeepTimeNet. Under unseen conditions, the MSE is reduced by more than 48.2% compared to BIATCN-Informer and other advanced models. Under noisy conditions, the proposed model still outperforms all the other compared models. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness and necessity of each module. The proposed model provides reliable technical support for battery thermal runaway warning and health status assessment.

title: Construction of an infrastructure system for high-quality development enabled by aerospace information technology
summary: High-quality development is the primary task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, which imposes all-round demands on the aerospace information infrastructure for unified benchmarks, ubiquitous precision, multi-dimensional
content: High-quality development is the primary task of building a modern socialist country in all respects, which imposes all-round demands on the aerospace information infrastructure for unified benchmarks, ubiquitous precision, multi-dimensional perception, and real-time intelligence. Starting from the deepened connotation of high-quality development, this paper demonstrates the definition, connotation, and strategic status of aerospace information as a new production factor. It systematically reviews the development trends of the three major technical systems of satellite navigation, space-terrestrial integrated communication network, and Earth observation, pointing out that aerospace information technology is undergoing a four-dimensional observation revolution in space, time, spectrum, and elements, and shows an inevitable trend of communication-navigation-remote sensing integration. A triune empowering framework of spatiotemporal intelligence, communication intelligence, and perception intelligence is proposed, clarifying that aerospace information technology supports high-quality development through three mechanisms: factor empowerment, process intelligence, and system resilience. Furthermore, the paper discusses the intelligent infrastructure characterized by the integration of professional multimodal small AI models, evolving toward system-level collaborative intelligence and embodied intelligence. With the completion of the new-generation BeiDou comprehensive spatiotemporal system, mega low-Earth-orbit communication constellations, and industry-oriented remote sensing constellations, aerospace information technology will build a multi-dimensional and all-round intelligent aerospace information infrastructure supporting China’s high-quality development, providing a ubiquitous, precise, and secure digital foundation for cultivating new quality productive forces.

title: Chain-Transfer Agent Functionalization Combines ROP and RAFT Polymerizations to Direct Amphiphilic and Thermoresponsive Polymer Self-Assembly
summary: Abstract In a reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization, the chain-transfer agent (CTA) is selected to regulate the radical polymerization, although the specific functional group retained in an amphiphilic macro
content: Abstract In a reversible addition–fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT) polymerization, the chain-transfer agent (CTA) is selected to regulate the radical polymerization, although the specific functional group retained in an amphiphilic macromolecule may influence its self-assembly and colloidal behavior. This feature can be advantageously exploited to engineer polymer nanoparticles with programmable behavior. Here, the carboxylic group of a dodecyl trithiocarbonate CTA was linked to ethanolamine to introduce a hydroxyl functionality while converting the ionizable terminus into a neutral amide. The resulting dual-purpose CTA was used as an initiator in the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of D,l-lactide and subsequently to mediate the RAFT copolymerization of di(ethylene glycol) methyl ether methacrylate (EG2MA) and N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPAM). The result is an amphiphilic macromolecule capable of self-assemblying forming nanoparticles (NPs) with a poly(lactic acid) (PLA) core and a thermoresponsive shell. Eight copolymers were synthesized by varying PLA length, EG2MA fraction, and overall thermoresponsive block length in a 23 factorial design. These same properties were benchmarked against a similar polymer library in which the biodegradable portion was obtained from a 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate-g-PLA macromonomer copolymerized with the aforementioned thermoresponsive monomers in a two-step RAFT polymerization. The reference copolymers followed the size scaling expected for micelle-like core–shell assemblies, whereas CTA-directed nanoparticles exhibited a nonconventional dependence of size on polymer composition, lower dispersity, and near-neutral to weakly positive surface charge. These findings establish CTA functionalization as a molecular design strategy that transfers information from the polymerization junction to nanoparticle self-assembly, interfacial properties, and thermoresponsive behavior.

title: THE FUTURE OF AVIATION LAW AND THE ROLE OF ARBITRATION COURTS
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The exponential growth of international air transport, coupled with the increasing sophistication of cross-border aviation finance, codeshare partnerships and infrastructure concessions, has exposed the structural limits of the existing con
content: The exponential growth of international air transport, coupled with the increasing sophistication of cross-border aviation finance, codeshare partnerships and infrastructure concessions, has exposed the structural limits of the existing conventional and judicial framework governing aviation disputes. This article examines the future trajectory of aviation law and interrogates the expanding role of arbitration as a preferred mechanism for resolving commercial, financial and regulatory disputes in the aviation sector. Employing a doctrinal methodology grounded in primary treaty texts, judicial precedent and institutional arbitration rules, the article traces the evolution of the Warsaw–Montreal liability regime, the Cape Town Convention's asset-based remedies, and the growing recourse to institutional arbitration under the rules of the International Chamber of Commerce, the London Court of International Arbitration and the International Air Transport Association. The analysis demonstrates that while passenger-liability disputes remain firmly tethered to national courts because of consumer protection imperatives, business-to-business aviation disputes are migrating decisively toward arbitration on account of its neutrality, enforceability under the New York Convention, confidentiality and access to technically specialised adjudicators. The article concludes that the future of aviation law lies in a hybrid dispute-resolution architecture that preserves judicial oversight for passenger claims while consolidating arbitration as the default forum for commercial, financing and infrastructure disputes, including those emerging from urban air mobility and carbon-offset compliance.

title: Aligning institutions and organizations for sustainable supply chains: the role of digital transformation and low-carbon practices
source: Supply Chain Management An International Journal
summary: Purpose The transition toward carbon neutrality has become a global strategic priority for achieving sustainable development and a green economy. Despite growing interest in digital transformation among scholars and practitioners, achieving
content: Purpose The transition toward carbon neutrality has become a global strategic priority for achieving sustainable development and a green economy. Despite growing interest in digital transformation among scholars and practitioners, achieving a balance between green supply chain performance and carbon performance within the context of carbon neutrality remains underexplored. Drawing on the technology acceptance model and change management theory, this research aims to provide solutions for achieving the zero-carbon target in 2060 through holistic digital transformation, and how institutional pressure and organizational readiness influence green supply chain and carbon performance through digital transformation, low-carbon operations management practices (LCOMP) and the moderating role of environmental proactivity. Design/methodology/approach Data from 442 Chinese manufacturing firms were analyzed using Smart PLS v4 to test the research hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that all three dimensions of LCOMP mediate the relationship between digital transformation, green supply chain and carbon performance. In addition, environmental proactivity strengthens the influence of digital transformation on the three dimensions of LCOMP. Originality/value The findings contribute to the literature by addressing a key gap in sustainable supply chain and digital transformation research, which has largely examined these relationships in isolation without fully explaining the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions.

title: Sustainable for Whom? Industrial Competitiveness, Sustainable Industrialization and Carbon Inequality: Evidence From a Global Panel
summary: ABSTRACT Industrialization is central to the sustainable development agenda, but its distributional environmental consequences remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how conventional industrial competitiveness and sustainable
content: ABSTRACT Industrialization is central to the sustainable development agenda, but its distributional environmental consequences remain insufficiently understood. This study examines how conventional industrial competitiveness and sustainable industrialization, the latter measured by the Sustainable Development Goal 9 Industry Index, relate to carbon inequality (CI), proxied by the carbon footprint of the top income decile. Using data for up to 99 countries over 1995‐2023, Method of Moments Quantile Regression (MMQR) and Panel Threshold Regression (PTR) are employed to uncover heterogeneity across the CI distribution and income‐dependent development regimes. The results show that both forms of industrialization are associated with higher CI, but with specific distributional patterns. The competitiveness‐CI relationship is positive across all quantiles and stronger at lower levels of CI, while the association with sustainable industrialization increases toward the upper tail. PTR estimates further show substantial regime dependence in the effect of industrial competitiveness, while the SDG 9‐CI relationship is comparatively stable across development regimes. Wealth inequality, urbanization, and globalization are associated with higher CI, whereas renewable energy and inclusive institutions generally exhibit mitigating effects. The findings remain largely robust to instrumental‐variable quantile regression, alternative CI measures, and a sample restricted to fully observed data. Overall, neither competitiveness‐driven nor sustainability‐oriented industrialization alone appears sufficient to deliver equitable environmental outcomes, highlighting the need for integrating distributional considerations and countries' development stages into industrial and climate policy.

title: A Review of State-of-Health Estimation and Prediction Methods for Lithium-Ion Traction Batteries in Vehicular Applications: Task Definition, Benchmark Evaluation, and Deployment Challenges
summary: The state of health (SOH) of traction batteries is a common basis for safety warning, residual value assessment, and second-life utilization of electric vehicles, but a gap exists between the laboratory accuracy of existing deep learning me
content: The state of health (SOH) of traction batteries is a common basis for safety warning, residual value assessment, and second-life utilization of electric vehicles, but a gap exists between the laboratory accuracy of existing deep learning methods and their on-board usability. This paper reviews the relevant research progress using on-board usability as the screening criterion. SOH estimation, SOH prediction, and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction are distinguished according to label source and evaluation protocol, and the limits on the comparability of error values are explained. Existing methods are grouped into six categories by modeling mechanism and evaluated category by category using four on-board questions: input availability, cross-domain generalization validation, uncertainty output, and edge-computing resource constraints. Six models are compared on the CALCE CS2 dataset under random splitting, temporal extrapolation, and cell-level holdout protocols. Under random splitting, the mean absolute errors of all six models do not exceed 0.0150. Under temporal extrapolation, they range from 0.0204 to 0.1392, and the R² values of three neural networks become negative. Under cell-level holdout, they range from 0.0254 to 0.0378. Under the CALCE CS2 dataset and the settings of this paper, protocol selection changes both the error level and the model ranking.

title: Balancing ecological risk and economic feasibility: A marginal-cost optimization framework for textile effluent recovery
summary: The textile sector faces increasing pressure to align stringent effluent controls with economic viability. This study develops a marginal-cost optimization framework to identify the dynamic equilibrium recovery level at which incremental tr
content: The textile sector faces increasing pressure to align stringent effluent controls with economic viability. This study develops a marginal-cost optimization framework to identify the dynamic equilibrium recovery level at which incremental treatment expenditure equals marginal environmental benefit. Techno-economic data from membrane-based and ecological treatment trains were integrated with life-cycle damage monetization, and an NSGA-II multi-objective optimization framework was used to derive Pareto-optimal recovery levels. Life-cycle assessment showed that reclaimed effluent had a GHG intensity of 5.70 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 , versus 3.66 kg CO 2 eq/m 3 for standard discharge, with electricity accounting for 49% of emissions; the indicated optimal recovery levels were 55–82%, with elasticities of 0.38 for water tariffs, −0.42 for electricity prices, and −0.15 for carbon taxation. A tiered strategy combining Class I-A discharge, constructed wetland polishing (0.1–0.23 CNY/m 3 ), and small-scale membrane recovery (15–25%) was identified as optimal. Comparative analysis of water-scarce Aksu showed that zero-liquid-discharge pathways with 50–60% recovery are justified by water-security imperatives despite higher costs. Carbon pricing shifts the equilibrium recovery level downward by 3–5 percentage points, highlighting region-specific water–carbon trade-offs that require coordinated policy design.

title: Sustainability transitions in South and Southeast Asia: The interplay of environmental, economic, and technological drivers
summary: This study investigates the environmental, economic, and technological determinants of sustainability in ASEAN and SAARC using panel data techniques, including FGLS, PCSE, Fixed-Effect OLS, and two-step System-GMM, alongside quantile regres
content: This study investigates the environmental, economic, and technological determinants of sustainability in ASEAN and SAARC using panel data techniques, including FGLS, PCSE, Fixed-Effect OLS, and two-step System-GMM, alongside quantile regression. Sustainability is assessed through two complementary indicators: renewable energy consumption (REC), capturing energy transition, and adjusted net savings excluding emission damage (ANS), reflecting long-run resource-based sustainability. The inclusion of dynamic GMM estimation allows us to address potential endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity. The findings reveal pronounced regional asymmetries. In ASEAN, energy use and CO₂ emissions significantly reduce REC, confirming fossil lock-in, although energy demand stimulates renewables at higher quantiles under expansionary conditions. In SAARC, emissions show weak or positive links with REC, while forest resources strongly promote renewable use, indicating biomass dependence. For ANS, emissions, energy use, GDP, and digital penetration exert positive effects across both regions, suggesting that industrialization-driven accumulation may dominate sustainability outcomes in the short to medium term. Forest resources exhibit contrasting effects—reducing ANS in ASEAN but enhancing it in SAARC—while FDI shows limited impact in ASEAN but negatively affects ANS in SAARC, reflecting institutional constraints. Overall, the results highlight that sustainability transitions in developing Asia are context-specific, shaped by structural conditions, institutional capacity, and stages of development. Policy implications emphasize the need to overcome fossil dependence in ASEAN, modernize biomass use in SAARC, design region-specific green investment frameworks, and leverage digitalization to align growth with SDGs 7, 8, 12, and 13.

title: Preparation of ultrafine calcium carbonate nanoparticles by carbonation in gas–liquid two‐phase impinging stream reactor
source: The Canadian Journal of Chemical Engineering
summary: Abstract In the context of ‘Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality’, carbon dioxide capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is an important technology for achieving carbon neutrality. Combining impinging stream and bubble jet, the gas–liquid
content: Abstract In the context of ‘Carbon Peaking and Carbon Neutrality’, carbon dioxide capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is an important technology for achieving carbon neutrality. Combining impinging stream and bubble jet, the gas–liquid two‐phase impinging stream reactor was designed and developed. The ultrafine calcium carbonate nanoparticles were prepared by the gas–liquid two‐phase impinging stream reactor using the carbonation method. The effects of dispersant type, dispersant dosage, gas‐phase and liquid‐phase flow rates, synthesis temperature, CO 2 volume fraction and initial Ca(OH) 2 concentration on the average particle size, particle size distribution, and synthesis time were investigated. The results showed that the average particle size and synthesis time of calcium carbonate nanoparticles reached a minimum with the dispersant SDBS. Compared with other surfactants, the average particle size and synthesis time decreased from 188 to 66 nm and from 500 to 226 s, respectively. With the increase of the gas‐phase flow rate and synthesis temperature, the average particle size of calcium carbonate nanoparticles increased and the synthesis time decreased, resulting in a broader particle size distribution. With increasing liquid phase flow rate, the average particle size of calcium carbonate nanoparticles and synthesis time decreased. The particle size distribution was uniform. Based on the reaction mechanism of calcium carbonate nanoparticles prepared by the carbonation method, the crystallization kinetic model of the carbonation reaction process was established, which could accurately predict the crystallization process of calcium carbonate nanoparticles.

title: Corporate Greenwashing: The Gap Between Zijin Mining’s ESG Discourse and Practice
summary: With the increasing attention of the ESG concept, the ESG information disclosure of enterprises has received unprecedented attention. This study takes Zijin Mining as a case, examines its ESG greenwashing practices, and identifies the under
content: With the increasing attention of the ESG concept, the ESG information disclosure of enterprises has received unprecedented attention. This study takes Zijin Mining as a case, examines its ESG greenwashing practices, and identifies the underlying motivations and corresponding governance measures. Research shows that Zijin Mining has gaps between discourse and practice at the three levels of environment, society and governance, and creates a corporate image of “good ESG performance” on the surface through strategic disclosure; At the same time, the drive of internal interests and the ambiguity of external ESG disclosure standards create opportunities for corporate ESG greenwashing. Therefore, corporate ESG greenwashing should be curbed by improving internal governance systems and strengthening external regulatory oversight. While deeply analyzing the internal ESG greenwashing practices and motives of Zijin Mining, this article provides specific practical countermeasures for the management of ESG greenwashing practices.

title: Endogenous silicon-functionalized and nitrogen-doped biochar loaded with nZVI for persulfate-activated phenol decontamination from water: Fe-N synergistic catalysis and Si-stabilized pore confinement
summary: Conventional biochars suffer from poor pore structure and limited electron transfer, restricting phenol removal. To address these bottlenecks, agricultural wastes (cotton stalk and swine manure) were upcycled via one-step co-pyrolysis to pr
content: Conventional biochars suffer from poor pore structure and limited electron transfer, restricting phenol removal. To address these bottlenecks, agricultural wastes (cotton stalk and swine manure) were upcycled via one-step co-pyrolysis to produce a silicon-functionalized and nitrogen-doped biochar (BC500). Loading nanoscale zero-valent iron onto the biochar yielded a Fe-N co-doped composite (nZVI@NBC500) for persulfate activation. The system achieved a total phenol removal capacity of 174.64 mg/g and near-complete phenol removal (98.87%) within 360 min, comprising both adsorption and catalytic degradation. Characterizations revealed that Si-O-C crosslinks stabilized hierarchical pores, pyridinic N/graphitic N facilitated electron transfer, and Fe-O bonds activated persulfate. EPR and quenching analyses confirmed the coexistence of radical (SO₄•⁻, O₂•⁻, •OH) and non-radical (¹O₂) pathways, with both O₂•⁻ and SO₄•⁻ identified as major contributors to phenol degradation. MD simulations revealed unique phenol "aggregation-dissociation" in hierarchical pores, and DFT showed Fe-N co-doping narrowed the HOMO-LUMO gap from 214.28 to 107.91 kJ/mol, enhancing electron transfer. The composite exhibited robust tolerance to variable pH, coexisting anions, and real wastewater, achieved >90% removal in the first two cycles and retained approximately 74% removal after five cycles, and alleviated lettuce phytotoxicity. Cost analysis further revealed a production cost of 2.80 USD/kg. Overall, this study provides a green strategy for upcycling agricultural wastes and offers mechanistic insights for the treatment of phenolic wastewater.

title: Multiscale Pores in 3D Printed Cobalt Phosphide‐Carbon Electrodes Unlock Mass Transfer for Hydrogen Evolution at High Current Densities
summary: ABSTRACT The high‐current‐density hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is essential for large‐scale industrial H 2 production, yet bubble release disrupts mass transport at elevated current densities, significantly impeding reaction kinetics a
content: ABSTRACT The high‐current‐density hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is essential for large‐scale industrial H 2 production, yet bubble release disrupts mass transport at elevated current densities, significantly impeding reaction kinetics and HER efficiency. We present a self‐supported cobalt phosphide‐carbon electrode with multiscale pores, specifically engineered to address these challenges. Using a hybrid gel ink composed of chitosan, ZIF‐67, and zinc trimesic acid (Zn‐BTC), millimeter‐scale pores are precisely tailored through direct ink writing with filament spacings of 2, 3, and 4 mm. Hierarchical nanopores are further refined via scaffold pyrolysis and Zn evaporation at controlled temperatures between 700°C and 950°C. The 3‐CoP‐NC‐900 electrode, developed through 3 mm grid printing and 900°C pyrolysis, facilitates efficient mass transport of H 2 O, OH − , and H 2 , achieving sustained HER at 900 mA cm −2 with an overpotential of −287 mV and a Tafel slope of 38.0 mV dec −1 . In situ confocal microscopy fluorescence imaging highlights enhanced OH − mobilization, optimizing H 2 O transport and kinetics. Simulations confirm that the 3 mm grid and 3.7 nm mesopores together optimize bubble release and internal species transport, achieving a peak diffusion flux density of 2.1 µm 2 s −1 . Integrated with a NiFe LDH/NF anode, the system delivers 0.5 A cm −2 at a hydrogen cost of $0.88–1.07/GGE. This study utilizes hierarchical pore structures to enhance mass transfer, offering insights for designing advanced electrodes in electrochemical energy systems.

title: Plastic mulching in agriculture: agronomic performance, residual film hazards, and green development strategies
summary: Agricultural film mulching is a key agronomic practice for improving water and thermal resource use and ensuring food security, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. However, long-term reliance on conventional polyethylene (PE) films
content: Agricultural film mulching is a key agronomic practice for improving water and thermal resource use and ensuring food security, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. However, long-term reliance on conventional polyethylene (PE) films has caused severe plastic pollution, while microplastic accumulation threatens farmland ecological security. This review adopts a critical review approach based on structured literature retrieval and thematic narrative synthesis of agricultural plastic mulching technology. The scope covers mulching materials, agronomic application modes, crop regulation mechanisms, ecological risks associated with residual films, and green transition strategies. Literature published between 2000 and 2026 was retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, ScienceDirect, CNKI, and other relevant databases. A total of 2,157 records were initially identified, and 247 studies were finally included for qualitative narrative synthesis after duplicate removal, title–abstract screening, and full-text eligibility assessment. Bibliometric analysis revealed a rapid increase in research output since 2010, with residual film pollution, biodegradable mulch, and soil quality emerging as major research hotspots, highlighting growing concerns over sustainable agricultural plastic management. This review traces the evolution of mulching materials from natural organics to synthetic plastics and emerging environmentally friendly and functionally enhanced materials. It further examines two major agricultural application patterns and the mechanisms through which film mulching regulates crop growth. The review then critically evaluates soil degradation risks associated with residual films, as well as the challenges of mechanized recovery and resource utilization. Based on these findings, a phased transition pathway is proposed. In the short term, priority should be given to optimizing film thickness and strength while improving mechanized recovery and film–impurity separation technologies. In the long term, emphasis should shift toward the molecular design and development of low-cost, high-performance, and controllably biodegradable materials. Overall, this review establishes a multidisciplinary analytical framework integrating material evolution, agricultural application, agronomic regulation, degradation, residual pollution, recovery, and green governance, providing theoretical and practical references for balancing agricultural productivity with ecological protection.

title: Phytotoxicity and germination responses of Zea mays L. to anaerobically digested liquid biofertilizers derived from cattle manure and fish-processing sludge
summary: Abstract Valorization of cattle manure and fish-processing sludge as liquid biofertilizers may contribute to waste valorization and potential agricultural reuse within a circular bioeconomy. This study evaluated four formulations (GC, T1, T
content: Abstract Valorization of cattle manure and fish-processing sludge as liquid biofertilizers may contribute to waste valorization and potential agricultural reuse within a circular bioeconomy. This study evaluated four formulations (GC, T1, T2, and T3) produced in three biodigesters per formulation and anaerobically digested for 15 weeks. The three biodigesters within each formulation were pooled before preparation of the 5, 10, and 100% (v/v) bioassay dilution levels. Distilled water was retained as an external reference and excluded from factorial inference. Final formulation-level composite samples showed near-neutral pH and formulation-specific nutrient profiles; the measured nitrogen concentration in the analyzed liquid fraction was higher at the final sampling point in all four composite samples, whereas P, K, organic matter, and C/N ratio showed formulation-specific variations. Most final microbiological determinations were lower than their corresponding initial measurements, although variability remained in some T2 and T3 determinations. In Zea mays L. bioassays, germination percentage and germination rate showed significant formulation × dilution-level interactions ( p = 0.0065 and p = 0.015, respectively). Root length differed significantly by formulation ( p = 0.0145) and dilution level ( p = 0.0013), without a significant interaction. The germination index (GI), used as a phytotoxicity indicator, was evaluated descriptively; T2 maintained GI > 1 and comparatively high root length across all evaluated dilution levels, whereas T1 and T3 showed lower GI and root-length responses at 100%. Overall, responses were formulation- and dilution-level dependent, supporting soil-based validation of selected combinations before field recommendation. Because biodigesters were pooled at the formulation level before downstream analyses, these findings characterize the specific composite samples tested and do not represent independent reactor-level replication.

title: The limits of green incentives: a stochastic profitability analysis of sugar kelp farming in Europe
summary: Seaweed cultivation can deliver carbon sequestration and nutrient removal, which have value beyond the market price of the biomass. If these ecosystem services were quantified, certified and compensated, they could provide additional income
content: Seaweed cultivation can deliver carbon sequestration and nutrient removal, which have value beyond the market price of the biomass. If these ecosystem services were quantified, certified and compensated, they could provide additional income for farmers. This study evaluates whether such payments, together with other green incentives, can make sugar kelp ( Saccharina latissima ) farming in Europe profitable, and how much each incentive contributes. A stochastic profitability model, informed by a targeted literature review and data from the SeaMark project, was used to compare a baseline scenario with seven scenarios introducing payments for nutrient remediation, higher carbon prices, a price premium for sustainable products, lower capital costs, and combinations thereof. Even in the most favourable scenario, mean annual profit remains negative at about -€16,300 per hectare, and the probability of breaking even is effectively zero (below 1%). All incentives together reduce the baseline loss by only 18%; ecosystem service payments contribute about €1,240 per hectare, mostly from nutrient removal, while carbon credits add about €105 per hectare. Breaking even would require a price of about €2,050 per tonne wet weight or a yield of about 31 tonnes wet weight per hectare. Even with 40% lower production costs, the probability of breaking even remains below 13%; only when combined with 25% higher yields does it reach about 33%. Operational and capital expenditure, yield and biomass price, rather than ecosystem service parameters, are the strongest drivers of profitability. Under the assumptions made, ecosystem service payments can support, but not replace, improvements in production efficiency. The results provide insights for producers, policymakers and private sector actors.

title: THE OPERATOR TRIAD 𝓟̂ ∘ 𝓣̂ ∘ 𝓡̂: THE MATHEMATICAL FOUNDATIONS OF EVOLUTIONARY MATERIAL SCIENCE AND THE TRANSITION TO PROGRAMMABLE NANOMATERIALS
summary: At the beginning of the third decade of the 21st century, humanity faced an unprecedented convergence of three interrelated crises that require a radical transformation of the material foundation of civilization, namely: the climate crisis,
content: At the beginning of the third decade of the 21st century, humanity faced an unprecedented convergence of three interrelated crises that require a radical transformation of the material foundation of civilization, namely: the climate crisis, the energy crisis, and the raw materials crisis.

title: Land degradation neutrality state and progress in the Central Region, Malawi
summary: Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of
content: Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of land that is degraded over the total land area in the Central Region, Malawi, from 2001 to 2022, using the Trends.Earth tool in QGIS. The study applied the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) Good Practice Guidance methodology for SDG Indicator 15.3.1 assessment, integrating land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon (SOC) sub-indicators. The default datasets in the Trends.Earth plugin were adopted for all sub-indicators. The study has revealed that: (i) The proportion of degraded land increased from 26.8% in the baseline period (2001-2015) to 41.2% in the monitoring period (2016-2022). Stable land area decreased from 62.2% to 55.7%, while improved land area declined from 10.0% to 2.0%. Overall, during the entire study period (2001-2022), 27.1% of the land remained degraded, 62.4% was stable, and 9.4% improved. (ii) Land with degraded productivity significantly declined from 74.5% to 29.3%. In contrast, land with stable productivity slightly increased from 1.1% to 1.9%. (iii) SOC levels remained largely stable (>97%), although slight losses occurred in cropland, grassland, and wetland areas. (iv) Land cover remained predominantly stable (96.7%) throughout the study period. The overall SDG 15.3.1 indicator indicates continued degradation trends exceeding the rate of land recovery and restoration. This study has highlighted key spatial patterns and identified insights into the priority areas for targeted LDN interventions in the Central Region of Malawi. The findings provide critical evidence for guiding sustainable land management strategies and accelerating progress toward achieving land degradation neutrality in Malawi.

title: A Bioinspired Photon‐Gated Phase‐Change Textile for Two‐Stage Heat‐Flux Regulation of Building Envelopes
summary: ABSTRACT Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsu
content: ABSTRACT Passive cooling textiles for buildings must do more than reflect sunlight; they must also buffer transient heat under real outdoor conditions. Here we report a continuous coaxial wet‐spinning strategy for fabricating a microencapsulated phase‐change material (mPCM)‐integrated radiative‐cooling meta‐fabric (MFRP), consisting of a thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU)/hexagonal boron nitride (h‐BN)/barium sulfate (BaSO 4 ) photon‐regulating sheath and a TPU/mPCM latent‐heat core. The spatially separated architecture integrates broadband solar reflection, atmospheric‐window emission, and phase‐change thermal buffering within one fiber platform. The optimized meta‐fabric shows high solar reflectance (95.44%), strong atmospheric‐window emissivity (96.21%), and a melting enthalpy of 102.28 J/g. In a representative sunny‐day test, MFRP reduced the chamber temperature by up to 10.36°C relative to the blank control; three‐day cement‐panel measurements further yielded an average peak‐temperature reduction of 7.51°C ± 2.17°C relative to bare cement. Energy‐balance analysis and climate‐scale modelling further indicate promising cooling‐energy and carbon‐reduction potential in hot and cooling‐dominated regions. These results establish wet‐spun radiative cooling/phase‐change material meta‐fabrics as continuously processable exterior textile candidates for passive building thermal management.

title: Risk Return Dynamics and Portfolio Performance of Islamic Microfinance Institutions: Evidence from Post-Digital Transformation Era
summary: Digital transformation is reshaping the operating models of Islamic microfinance institutions (IMFIs), changing how they originate financing, monitor clients, process payments, and manage portfolio risk. Yet the financial consequences of di
content: Digital transformation is reshaping the operating models of Islamic microfinance institutions (IMFIs), changing how they originate financing, monitor clients, process payments, and manage portfolio risk. Yet the financial consequences of digital adoption remain ambiguous. Digital channels can reduce transaction costs, expand outreach, and improve the timeliness of credit information, but they can also introduce cyber risk, model risk, operational concentration, and new forms of borrower over-indebtedness. This article develops a risk-return framework for evaluating IMFIs after digital transformation, with particular attention to the interaction between Shariah-compliant financing, portfolio quality, operating efficiency, and digital capability. Drawing on financial intermediation theory, portfolio theory, information asymmetry, institutional theory, and the objectives of Islamic finance, the article proposes a comparative empirical design using institution-level panel data. The framework distinguishes profitability, portfolio quality, liquidity, capital adequacy, outreach, and social performance rather than reducing institutional success to a single accounting ratio. It also treats digital transformation as a capability whose value depends on governance, data quality, staff competence, cybersecurity, and the design of financing contracts. Twelve hypotheses specify expected relationships among digital maturity, risk management, portfolio diversification, non-performing financing, cost efficiency, and risk-adjusted performance. The article’s analytical synthesis suggests that digital adoption is most likely to improve risk-adjusted returns when it is embedded in disciplined underwriting, responsible financing, Shariah governance, and portfolio monitoring. Because no institution-level dataset was supplied, the manuscript presents a theory-driven framework and research protocol rather than fabricated statistical findings.

title: Unlocking Neutral Hydrogen Evolution via a Lattice‐Proton‐Mediated Pathway on a Pt/h‐WO 3 Single‐Atom Catalyst
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable hydrogen production from abundant natural water is severely hampered by the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in neutral media, a fundamental bottleneck for large‐scale water electrolysis. Herei
content: ABSTRACT Sustainable hydrogen production from abundant natural water is severely hampered by the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in neutral media, a fundamental bottleneck for large‐scale water electrolysis. Herein, we report a novel synergistic strategy to circumvent this limitation by designing a platinum single‐atom catalyst supported on hexagonal tungsten oxide (Pt/ h ‐WO 3 ). Our theoretical and experimental results show that the H x WO 3 support acts as a lattice‐proton reservoir that captures and stores protons (H + ) from water within its lattice. The stored H + ions are subsequently utilized by the atomic Pt sites, which serve as catalytic sites that open a low‐energy pathway and bypass the high activation barrier of conventional water dissociation. This unique mechanism, directly verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy, endows the catalyst with strong acid‐like HER activity in neutral media, achieving an overpotential of only 22 mV at 10 mA cm −2 . This work establishes a powerful design principle that synergizes lattice‐level reactant storage with atomic‐level catalytic sites and offers a new paradigm for overcoming kinetic barriers in challenging electrochemical reactions.

title: Architects’ Awareness and Adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) in Smart Housing in Lagos, Nigeria
source: The Open Construction and Building Technology Journal
summary: Background and Objective As urban areas grow, the integration of IoT smart technologies offers benefits such as energy efficiency, comfort, security, and sustainability. This study seeks to explore the awareness of Internet of Things (IoT)
content: Background and Objective As urban areas grow, the integration of IoT smart technologies offers benefits such as energy efficiency, comfort, security, and sustainability. This study seeks to explore the awareness of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies for smart housing among architects in Lagos, Nigeria. Methods A cross-sectional survey of 89 Architects in Lagos was carried out using questionnaires to assess the awareness, adoption, and barriers to the adoption of IoT technologies. Results The study results show that there’s a sufficient level of awareness of IoT technologies such as surveillance cameras, smart appliances, Biometric authentication systems, and solar energy monitoring systems; however, adoption remains moderate due to financial limitations, low client demand, limited professional training, and low policy support. Factors such as perceived usefulness, along with ease of use and social influences, were seen as major drivers of adoption. Discussion The findings indicate that awareness alone is not really sufficient to ensure the adoption of IoT technologies in smart housing. Widespread implementation of these technologies will require improved professional training, better client awareness, supportive policy frameworks, and financial incentives to reduce adoption barriers among architects in Lagos. Conclusion The study reveals the need for targeted professional development, incorporation of IoT education in architectural training, increased public awareness, and government-led incentives to support adoption. These findings contribute to the broader knowledge base on sustainable urban development and emphasise the critical role of architects in facilitating the digital transformation of housing in Nigeria.

title: Synergistically Modulating Electronic Structure and Interfacial Wettability of MnF 2 /NF−CNF Toward Enhanced Oxygen Reduction in Zinc−Air Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZAB
content: ABSTRACT Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF 2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF 2 /NF−CNF). The unique interconnected fibrous and hierarchical porous architecture, together with tailored MnF 2 embedding and N/F doping, achieves an optimal balance between activity and wettability regulation. Excellent ORR performance with a high half‐wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE and limiting current density of 6.34 mA cm −2 is achieved, outperforming Pt/C and most previously reported Mn‐based/heteroatom‐doped systems. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal surface N dopants as active sites, with MnF 2 modulating p‐orbital configuration, refining ORR pathways. Meanwhile, surface F dopants, in synergy with the porous architecture, regulate wettability, equilibrate electrolyte/oxygen transport, and substantially extend triple‐phase reaction interfaces. The assembled ZAB delivers an exceptional peak power density of 181.5 mW cm −2 with high specific capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability. This work deciphers the regulatory mechanism balancing catalytic activity and interfacial wettability, proving a versatile strategy for developing advanced ORR electrocatalysts in ZABs.

title: Discursive Alignment in EU Palm Oil Policy: How Securitisation Legitimises Ecological‐Neocolonial Governance
summary: ABSTRACT The EU has long been regarded as a normative leader in global environmental governance. Yet its restrictive measures on palm oil raise questions about how it exercises environmental authority within unequal relations. Drawing on se
content: ABSTRACT The EU has long been regarded as a normative leader in global environmental governance. Yet its restrictive measures on palm oil raise questions about how it exercises environmental authority within unequal relations. Drawing on securitisation theory and ecological neocolonialism, this study examines how the EU constructed and legitimised a threat narrative around palm oil. Using critical discourse analysis in its discourse‐historical variant, it analyses a corpus traced to the problematisation of palm oil at EU level, comprising regulatory texts, advocacy material, producer‐state and producer‐country non‐state responses, and the trade proceedings that followed. The analysis shows that this securitising move did not emerge ex nihilo but relied on discursive alignment, through which the EU grafted technocratic classifications onto established moral‐affective discourses concerning deforestation and biodiversity loss. The securitisation traced here also departs from its classical formulation by operating through the calculation and management of environmental risk rather than the suspension of established rules. This alignment enabled a shift from territorial control towards standardised governance, with instruments such as RED II and the EUDR making compliance a condition of market access. The findings suggest that, although these measures are framed as scientific imperatives, they acquire an ecological‐neocolonial character where regulatory, epistemic, and political‐economic asymmetries converge. Contestation generated illocutionary frustration for producer countries, as the proceedings addressed procedural issues without resolving their substantive concerns.

title: In Situ Bulk Passivation and Carrier Transport Modulation in Te‐TeO x Films Enable Low‐Noise Monolithic Near‐Infrared Imagers
summary: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR) imagers are essential for applications ranging from material sorting and autonomous driving to biomedical diagnostics, yet their performance is often limited by severe carrier recombination and high dark current
content: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR) imagers are essential for applications ranging from material sorting and autonomous driving to biomedical diagnostics, yet their performance is often limited by severe carrier recombination and high dark current. Here, we demonstrate a low‐noise NIR photodiode based on Te‐TeO x nanocrystalline‐in‐matrix films, in which the surrounding oxide matrix provides in situ bulk passivation and enables the modulation of carrier transport to balance carrier loss and extraction. This approach reduces trap density, suppresses recombination, and prolongs carrier lifetime, while controlled oxide incorporation tunes the optical bandgap and interfacial offsets of the heterojunction photodiode, resulting in spectral response spanning the visible and NIR regions with low dark current. The resulting photodiodes exhibit a low dark current of 9.70 nA cm −2 at a bias of −10 mV, a detectivity of 3.85 × 10 12 Jones and an ultralow detectable power of 1.35 pW for NIR photodetection. The strategy is compatible with direct monolithic integration with readout integrated circuits, enabling a 256 × 256 focal‐plane imager with excellent pixel uniformity. It further supports high‐quality focal‐plane imaging in both visible and NIR regions, as well as solution identification and imaging through smoke.

title: Low-Carbon Consumer Behavior in the Digital Age: Investigating the Determinants of Green Product Purchase Intentions in E-Commerce Platforms
summary: Digital commerce is reshaping how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products, creating new opportunities to encourage lower-carbon consumption while also intensifying convenience-driven consumption and information overload. This ar
content: Digital commerce is reshaping how consumers discover, evaluate, and purchase products, creating new opportunities to encourage lower-carbon consumption while also intensifying convenience-driven consumption and information overload. This article examines the determinants of green product purchase intention in e-commerce by integrating behavioral, value-based, trust-based, and digital-information perspectives. It develops an integrative conceptual framework that links environmental concern, attitudes toward green products, subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, green perceived value, price perceptions, green trust, digital information quality, electronic word of mouth, platform affordances, and perceived greenwashing to purchase intention. The article uses a structured integrative review of recent research and authoritative sustainability reports, emphasizing studies published from 2021 onward while retaining established theories where needed to explain underlying mechanisms. The synthesis indicates that pro-environmental concern is important but rarely sufficient on its own: consumers must also believe that a product performs well, offers acceptable value, can be purchased without excessive effort, and is supported by credible evidence. Digital interfaces may reduce information costs through certification details, traceability, reviews, and product comparisons, yet they can also amplify unsubstantiated environmental claims and impulsive purchasing. Green trust and perceived information usefulness therefore emerge as central mechanisms connecting digital communication to intention, while price sensitivity, perceived risk, delivery impacts, and doubts about green claims can weaken the relationship.

title: The salinity-aridity nexus modulates eco-hydrological impacts of vegetation enhancement and desertification across saline-alkali drylands in northern China
summary: Vegetation dynamics in drylands fundamentally restructure the land-atmosphere interface, yet the resulting surface water-energy coupling across saline-alkali environments remains insufficiently understood due to the complex interplay betwee
content: Vegetation dynamics in drylands fundamentally restructure the land-atmosphere interface, yet the resulting surface water-energy coupling across saline-alkali environments remains insufficiently understood due to the complex interplay between climatic aridity and edaphic salinity. By integrating multi-decadal satellite observations with a biogeophysical decomposition framework, we quantified the growing-season impacts of vegetation enhancement (cropland expansion and grassland restoration) alongside desertification across the saline-alkali drylands of northern China from 2003 to 2020. Our results demonstrated that vegetation enhancement induced significant localized surface cooling, peaking in barren-to-cropland conversions (−0.674 ± 0.02 K), followed by grassland-to-cropland conversions (−0.066 ± 0.007 K) and barren-to-grassland restoration (−0.017 ± 0.009 K), whereas desertification exhibited a subtle warming tendency (+0.005 ± 0.0003 K). These thermal responses were primarily governed by non-radiative, evapotranspiration-mediated processes. Furthermore, the salinity-aridity nexus modulated regional energy partitioning through two divergent hydro-edaphic pathways. In reclaimed irrigated cropland, management interventions alleviated ambient matric and osmotic constraints, while intensifying regional water consumption. In contrast, non-irrigated restored grasslands exhibited a functional decoupling between canopy greening and evaporative cooling, reflecting conservative stomatal regulation enforced by compound soil matric and osmotic stresses. The marginal warming accompanying desertification indicated an impaired surface evaporative buffer following vegetation loss and secondary salinization. By elucidating how the salinity-aridity nexus modulates land-surface water-energy coupling, these findings highlight the necessity to align restoration strategies with local hydro-edaphic capacities, balancing the microclimatic cooling of irrigated agriculture against the long-term hydrological sustainability of natural grasslands under accelerating global change.

title: Generating carbon credits: Transforming agriculture into a carbon sink
summary: By 2050 the world population will reach about 10 billion and food security for that population is among the most serious concerns before the United Nations. Soil supplies about 98% of our food. In Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Prad
content: By 2050 the world population will reach about 10 billion and food security for that population is among the most serious concerns before the United Nations. Soil supplies about 98% of our food. In Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, soil organic carbon (SOC) has fallen by roughly 0.2–0.6% over the past 60 years. Carbon farming is one of the approaches to mitigate the impact of conventional agricultural methods in CO2 emissions. By generating carbon credits in the farm fields, farmers can earn carbon credits, adding extra money in their income.

title: IT report on definition of decarbonization pathways and suitable design strategies. Deliverable 7.23
summary: This report presents the national assessment of decarbonisation pathways, suitable design strategies and Whole Life Carbon (WLC) reduction targets developed for the Italian building context within the INDICATE LIFE project. The activity was
content: This report presents the national assessment of decarbonisation pathways, suitable design strategies and Whole Life Carbon (WLC) reduction targets developed for the Italian building context within the INDICATE LIFE project. The activity was led by UNIBG and developed with contributions from the Italian Consortium partners. Building upon the national baseline assessment and hotspot analysis developed in the previous national deliverables, the analysis identifies, structures and assesses a set of decarbonisation actions aimed at reducing WLC across the main life-cycle stages of buildings. An integrated methodological framework was developed, combining the Avoid-Shift-Improve (ASI) approach with the LCM structure adopted in the LCA assessment. The conceptualisation and development of a dedicated WLC measures matrix represent a key methodological contribution of the deliverable, translating this combined structure into a hierarchical structure composed of pathways, strategy packages, WLC strategies and WLC measures. The resulting matrix links broad decarbonisation objectives to specific actions that can be analysed within the scope of the INDICATE LIFE project. Building on this methodological structure, the assessment combines the review of European policy developments, scientific literature and national industrial practices with the analysis of selected WLC measures. Measures were classified according to their relevance, data availability, technical feasibility and compatibility with the available datasets. This methodological framework also defines the criteria for selecting the measures to be assessed and, where quantitative assessment is possible, the representative case studies considered suitable for remodelling. Where possible, measures were assessed quantitatively through the remodelling of representative case studies selected from the Italian INDICATE LIFE dataset. Other measures were discussed qualitatively, in relation to their applicability, methodological limitations and potential contribution to WLC reduction. The results show that the reduction potential is unevenly distributed across life-cycle stages and building typologies. Modules A1-A3 emerge as a key area for WLC reduction, confirming the central role of material and construction product production. Measures addressing the decarbonisation of production processes, the use of materials with higher recycled content and carbon capture technologies show relevant effects in this stage. Module B6 plays a different role depending on the building typology: office buildings show higher sensitivity to operational energy decarbonisation measures, while residential typologies remain largely dominated by Embodied Carbon. Measures acting on transport and end-of-life stages show lower absolute reductions, but remain relevant when considered as part of integrated decarbonisation scenarios. The aggregation of results according to the ASI framework indicates that the Improve pathway achieves the hi

title: Architectural practice and the circular built environment transition: empirical insights from Australia
summary: Circular Economy (CE) adoption is considered a crucial decarbonisation pathway for the built environment, offering the potential to reduce emissions, waste, and material consumption. However, CE implementation remains challenging, lagging t
content: Circular Economy (CE) adoption is considered a crucial decarbonisation pathway for the built environment, offering the potential to reduce emissions, waste, and material consumption. However, CE implementation remains challenging, lagging the timelines required to meet the 2050 climate neutrality goals. To deepen the understanding of these challenges, the study focuses on architects as influential mediators in building projects and their potential role as key enablers in the CE transition. The study draws insights from Australia, where per capita emissions are among the highest globally, but empirical investigations remain limited. Probing the sustainability aspirations of the architectural profession against the reality of practice, the study adopts a phenomenological approach to explore the architects’ perspectives on the CE transition. Employing in-depth semi-structured interviews with architectural professionals (n=12) and thematic analysis, the study reveals current perceptions and practices of CE and identifies key barriers and enablers to its adoption. The study identified policy gaps, knowledge and data gaps, organisational constraints, market immaturity, and cultural inertia as barriers. Conversely, collaborative project delivery, capacity building, strategic use of legal and procedural tools, and demonstration of CE value through standards and exemplars emerged as enablers. The findings provide nuanced, actionable insights to inform CE policy and architectural practice, advancing CE adoption in the Australian built environment. The study highlights that the CE transition entails a broader social transformation within the architectural profession and strong government and industry leadership to ensure a just and empowered transition. Lastly, the empirical findings contribute to circular architecture and building decarbonisation scholarship, offering comparative insights for other geographies and building sectors towards a low-carbon future.

title: O transporte marítimo internacional no contraste entre estados desenvolvidos e em desenvolvimento e o princípio das responsabilidades comuns, porém diferenciadas e respectivas capacidades
summary: International maritime transport plays a central role in the global economy while significantly contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, thus positioning itself within the contemporary debate on climate change. In this context, marked by p
content: International maritime transport plays a central role in the global economy while significantly contributing to greenhouse gas emissions, thus positioning itself within the contemporary debate on climate change. In this context, marked by profound asymmetries between developed and developing States, the research problem guiding this study is: how do structural asymmetries between developed and developing States influence the regulation of greenhouse gas emissions in international maritime transport, and to what extent can the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities (CBDR-RC) be reconciled with the legal framework of the International Maritime Organization? The general objective of this study is to analyze the influence of structural inequalities between developed and developing States on the regulation of greenhouse gas emissions in international maritime transport, assessing the possibility of reconciling the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities (CBDR-RC) with the legal regime of the International Maritime Organization. To this end, two specific objectives are established: (I) to examine the economic, social, and structural asymmetries between developed and developing States, analyzing their impacts on international maritime trade and on the distribution of greenhouse gas emissions; and (II) to analyze the conflict and possible forms of articulation between the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities (CBDR-RC) and the principles of the International Maritime Organization, particularly non-discrimination and flag neutrality, in the context of regulating emissions in international maritime transport. In conclusion, it is observed that, although the CBDR-RC principle represents an important instrument of climate justice, its application to international maritime transport faces significant legal and institutional obstacles, revealing tensions between distinct normative regimes and highlighting the need to develop more integrated, balanced, and effective solutions to address climate change.

title: Upcycling waste polyester into cobalt-molybdenum sulfide-decorated carbon foam for photothermal desalination and parametric optimization using Taguchi design of experiments
summary: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In t
content: Photothermal desalination is an emerging solar-powered technique for water desalination. One of the primary open issues in the field is the development of new materials that guarantee high photothermal efficiency and evaporation rates. In this study, waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) bottles are upcycled into carbon foam, which is then decorated with Co-Mo2S3 via hydrothermal synthesis to prepare a photothermal evaporator. The as-synthesized Co-Mo2S3/carbon foam (CF) achieved an average evaporation rate of 2.13 kg m-2 h-1 during a 1-h experiment under 1,000 W m-2 irradiation using a 3.5% NaCl solution, compared to 1.55 kg m-2 h-1 obtained for CF. A Taguchi orthogonal-array design of experiments (DOE) was used to optimize the effect of input parameters on the evaporation rate of saline water. The experimental design matrix shows a maximum water evaporation rate of 1.77 kg m-2 h-1 under real sunlight. Taguchi analysis presents the optimal operating parameters for the evaporation rate as follows: salinity 30 g L-1 (level 1), saline water pH 5 (level 2), and time 2 h (level 2). The statistical outcomes show that salinity is the main factor affecting the evaporation rate. This study addresses water scarcity and promotes the circular economy by transforming plastic waste into a valuable resource for producing clean water and provides deeper insight into the optimization of the operating parameters using statistical tools.

title: Spatiotemporal warming patterns and future temperature transitions under varied agroclimatic zones of Indian Punjab
summary: Understanding regional warming dynamics is critical for assessing climate-related risks in agriculturally intensive regions. This study evaluated historical and future temperature variability, temperature transitions and warming trajectorie
content: Understanding regional warming dynamics is critical for assessing climate-related risks in agriculturally intensive regions. This study evaluated historical and future temperature variability, temperature transitions and warming trajectories across five agroclimatic zones of Punjab, India, using India Meteorological Department (IMD) temperature data (1951–2024) and bias-corrected CMIP6 EC-Earth3 projections (2025–2100) under SSP1: 2.6, SSP2: 4.5, SSP3: 7.0, and SSP5: 8.5 scenarios. Abrupt temperature shifts were identified using Pettitt’s test, Standard Normal Homogeneity Test (SNHT) and Buishand’s range test, while long-term trends were quantified using the modified Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope estimator. Historical analysis revealed significant warming in minimum temperature (T min ) across all agroclimatic zones, with a widespread shift during 1996–1997 and a post-shift increase of 0.44–0.72 °C in the mean annual T min relative to the pre-shift period. In contrast, maximum temperature (T max ) exhibited predominantly homogeneous behaviour with weak or non-significant trends. Annual T min warming rates ranged from 0.007–0.013 °C year -1 and were considerably stronger during the rabi season (0.010–0.019 °C year -1 ) than during kharif . Future projections indicated significant warming under all SSP pathways, with the largest increases under SSP5: 8.5. Following mid-century temperature transitions, annual T max and T min were projected to increase by 1.99–2.07 °C and 2.60–2.74 °C, respectively, while rabi T min warming reached 2.63–3.37 °C. Warming intensified progressively from SSP1:2.6 to SSP5:8.5, with temperature-specific hotspots emerging across agroclimatic zones. The Sub- Mountain zone exhibited the strongest T max warming response, whereas the Central and Western zones showed comparatively higher nighttime warming intensity, emerging as regional T min warming hotspots. Maximum warming occurred during winter (November–January) and positive T min anomalies appeared earlier and persisted longer under high-emission scenarios. The predominance of nighttime and wintertime warming highlights increasing risks to crop productivity, water resources and agroecosystem sustainability, emphasizing the need for targeted climate adaptation strategies.

title: Dynamic redox reactivation of platinum sites for long-term glycolate electrosynthesis from polyethylene terephthalate wastes
summary: Glycolates are indispensable in the health, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, whereas their mainstream production involve toxic chemicals and harsh operating condition. An alternative route for glycolate production is electrifying eth
content: Glycolates are indispensable in the health, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, whereas their mainstream production involve toxic chemicals and harsh operating condition. An alternative route for glycolate production is electrifying ethylene glycol (EG) that originates from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) but suffers from poor durability of active platinum site that tend to deactivate. Herein, we demonstrate a dynamic redox reactivation strategy, which alternates between working potential for oxidizing EG to glycolate and nonworking potential for reviving active platinum sites by the chemical reduction of adsorbed EG, realizing an unprecedented stability for over 3000 hours under average current density of ∼220 milliamperes per square centimeter. Upscaling this approach, the assembled electrolyzer drives a record current of 10 amperes at 1.18 volts for repeatable 40 batches of glycolates electrosynthesis, with each batch converting 48.0 grams of PET to 11.6 grams of glycolates (52.8% yield), 37.7 grams of p -phthalic acid (95.8% yield), 248.7 grams of NaHSO 4 (95.2% yield) and ∼11.5 liters of hydrogen, showcasing a considerable revenue of ∼$1072 per ton glycolate.

title: China’s Energy Structure Transition Toward Carbon Neutrality: Carbon Emission Characteristics, Bottleneck Constraints and Prospects
source: Academic Journal of Science and Technology
summary: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and energy security pressures, promoting a low-carbon transformation of the energy structure has become a crucial pathway to achieving sustainable development. China is currently at a
content: Against the backdrop of escalating global climate change and energy security pressures, promoting a low-carbon transformation of the energy structure has become a crucial pathway to achieving sustainable development. China is currently at a critical stage of synergistically advancing economic development, energy security, and carbon emission reduction targets. This paper reviews the evolution of China's energy supply and demand structure in recent years and further explores the main constraints of energy structure, technological innovation, and grid absorption capacity on the low-carbon energy transition. Research shows that China's energy structure is gradually shifting towards a low-carbon direction, with the proportion of fossil fuel supply and consumption continuing to decline, carbon emissions from some key industrial sectors stabilizing or decreasing, and positive progress being made in energy electrification and new energy development. However, resource constraints, key technological bottlenecks, and insufficient grid absorption capacity for high proportions of new energy remain significant factors hindering the energy transition. In the future, China's energy system will further develop towards zero-carbon supply, electrified consumption, distributed energy storage, and intelligent dispatch. Accelerating breakthroughs in key technologies such as hydrogen energy, advanced energy storage, and carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is essential to support the achievement of carbon neutrality goals.

title: Bio-Based Additives from Agricultural Waste
