summary: The utilization of agricultural waste to produce bio-based additives represents a promising strategy for achieving environmental sustainability and industrial innovation. This chapter explores the conversion of agricultural and agro-industr
content: The utilization of agricultural waste to produce bio-based additives represents a promising strategy for achieving environmental sustainability and industrial innovation. This chapter explores the conversion of agricultural and agro-industrial residues, such as rice husk, sugarcane bagasse, and corn stover, into high-value chemical additives that support circular bioeconomy models. It discusses the role of biotechnology, microbial fermentation, and green chemistry in transforming biomass into functional materials for applications in food, pharmaceuticals, polymers, and cosmetics. The chapter also emphasizes the importance of integrating bio-additives into existing manufacturing systems to reduce dependence on non-renewable resources and minimize waste generation. In addition, it highlights the influence of policy measures, sustainability certifications, and international collaborations in accelerating the adoption of bio-based technologies. While challenges related to scalability, quality control, and standardization remain, emerging innovations in artificial intelligence, enzyme technology, and eco-friendly extraction methods offer new opportunities for efficiency and value creation. Overall, the chapter underscores that the widespread adoption of bio-based additives can contribute significantly to waste reduction, carbon neutrality, and the realization of global sustainability goals by linking technological advancement with economic and environmental priorities.

title: Assessing and Optimizing Sustainable Water–Energy–Food Nexus Security in the Yellow River Basin: A Focus on Water Allocation
source: Journal of Water Resources Planning and Management
summary: Abstract The interplay of population growth, climate change, and urbanization poses significant risks to the water–energy–food (WEF) nexus. This study investigates the security challenges and optimization strategies of the WEF nexus from 20
content: Abstract The interplay of population growth, climate change, and urbanization poses significant risks to the water–energy–food (WEF) nexus. This study investigates the security challenges and optimization strategies of the WEF nexus from 2015 to 2022 in China’s Yellow River Basin, a critical production base facing severe water constraints. A water footprint analysis reveals pronounced spatial inequalities, characterized by increasing water consumption for energy and declining use for food. Although the overall nexus security remains relatively stable, water resources, as represented by blue water availability and sectoral demand, inherently pose the greatest risk to regional stability. A nonlinear programming model, solved by sequential quadratic programming (SQP) following Monte Carlo-based initial-point screening, produces two optimization schemes—Nash and Rawlsian–Nash—to enhance basin security. Both strategies suggest reallocating water resources from the agricultural to the energy sector. Specifically, the Nash scheme produces a mean annual percentage change of + 7.18 % in the WEF nexus security index, whereas the equity-prioritizing Rawlsian–Nash scheme lowers overall WEF nexus security while producing a mean annual percentage change of + 0.69 % in the water resources security index. By combining water footprint analysis with equity-constrained optimization, this research provides a quantitative framework for balancing resource efficiency and sectoral security in water-scarce regions.

title: Possibility to priority: how priority sector lending can drive climate finance in India
source: London School of Economics and Political Science Theses Online (London School of Economics and Political Science)
summary: In emerging markets and developing economies, as well as advanced economies, governments have long used directed credit programmes as a central part of their industrial policy to channel finance to sectors of national importance. With gover
content: In emerging markets and developing economies, as well as advanced economies, governments have long used directed credit programmes as a central part of their industrial policy to channel finance to sectors of national importance. With governments and central banks increasingly prioritising climate mitigation and adaptation in their economic strategies, this report reviews evidence of the effectiveness of such programmes. We focus on India’s Priority Sector Lending framework and analyse the experiences of 10 other countries to identify how directed credit has and has not succeeded in mobilising climate finance. Drawing on this evidence, we set out policy recommendations designed to enhance India’s use of priority sector lending to channel credit to low-carbon and climate-resilient sectors.

title: Achieving Sustainability on a Planet in Transition Through the Instrumentality of Architecture
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: The accelerating challenges of climate change, resource depletion, urbanization, and social inequality have placed humanity and the planet at a critical juncture, where sustainability is no longer a choice but a necessity. Architecture, as
content: The accelerating challenges of climate change, resource depletion, urbanization, and social inequality have placed humanity and the planet at a critical juncture, where sustainability is no longer a choice but a necessity. Architecture, as a tangible and influential interface between people and the environment, possesses unique potential to shape resilient, inclusive, and ecologically responsive futures. This study investigates how architecture can function as a strategic tool in guiding the planet through its current transitional state, fostering sustainable development that is adaptive, systemic, and rooted in context. By examining case studies, theoretical frameworks, and emerging technologies, the paper identified key architectural strategies including circular economy, that align with the sustainable development objectives of regenerative design, low-impact material use, energy-efficient systems, vernacular adaptation, and participatory planning. It argues that architecture must evolve from being a static response to environmental challenges, into an active agent of change in the sustainable development journey. It also calls for a shift in architectural ethics to prioritize ecological balance, cultural sensitivity, and spatial justice. Ultimately, the paper posits that sustainable architecture is not a singular solution but a process, an ongoing dialogue between human needs and planetary boundaries. Through this lens, architecture becomes instrumental in designing a future where both people and the planet can thrive in harmony, through; the de-carbonization of construction materials and practices, promotion of biodiversity, material reuse and recycling, adoption of sustainable development compliant technologies and cultural practices, developing and implementing resilience through architectural strategies, adoption of circular economy and prioritization of regenerative design, compliance with policy and governance standards.

title: Alkaline Electrolysers
summary: Carbon neutrality is the key objective of the Paris Agreement, which was struck at the UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties 21 (COP 21) in Paris in 2015. The stated aim was to limit global warming to 1.5 °C above pre-industrial level
content: Carbon neutrality is the key objective of the Paris Agreement, which was struck at the UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties 21 (COP 21) in Paris in 2015. The stated aim was to limit global warming to 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels by restricting the emission of greenhouse gases (GHGs) [ 1 ]. Widespread commitment to this target was affirmed at COP 26 in Glasgow, 2021, where 153 countries made commitments to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050. Also at COP 26, 40 countries agreed to a ‘Breakthrough Agenda’ which included achieving affordable, widely available, ‘renewable’ hydrogen by 2030 [ 2 ].

title: Decarbonization benefits of municipal solid waste recovery: A cross-country analysis of 32 countries
summary: Municipal solid waste (MSW) recovery is critical to global decarbonization agendas. Existing studies have provided important insights into the environmental performance of alternative waste-treatment pathways through life-cycle and scenario
content: Municipal solid waste (MSW) recovery is critical to global decarbonization agendas. Existing studies have provided important insights into the environmental performance of alternative waste-treatment pathways through life-cycle and scenario-based assessments. However, less is known about whether recovery expansion translates into measurable reductions in observed carbon emissions. This study employs an instrumental-variable framework to estimate the economy-wide carbon-emission effects of MSW recovery using a 32-country panel from 1998 to 2023, addressing reverse-causality concerns in the recovery-emission relationship. The results show that, across the 32-country sample, a 10% increase in aggregate MSW recovery is associated with an average 0.95–1.15% reduction in per capita carbon emissions. This estimate reflects the net system-level effect of recovery expansion under the observed mix of recovery pathways and national conditions, rather than a common effect of individual recovery technologies. The effect varies substantially across recovery systems: energy-recovery-dominated systems show stronger mitigation effects than recycling-dominated systems, with further differences across recovery scale, energy structure, and socioeconomic conditions. Finally, selected non-sample countries are compared with the 32-country sample across key structural moderators to identify where recovery expansion is most likely to deliver large mitigation gains. Overall, the study provides cross-country causal evidence on how MSW recovery translates into economy-wide emission outcomes under different national conditions, offering a system-level basis for aligning recovery strategies with broader decarbonization goals.

title: Shaping regional futures in times of sustainability transitions: Territorial capital, transformative capacity and prosilience
summary: Sustainability transitions are fundamentally reshaping regional and local economic development trajectories by challenging cities and regions to not only adapt to external shocks but also actively shape their futures. This study connects th
content: Sustainability transitions are fundamentally reshaping regional and local economic development trajectories by challenging cities and regions to not only adapt to external shocks but also actively shape their futures. This study connects three emerging approaches of regional and urban development – territorial capital, transformative capacity and prosilience – to better understand how cities and regions may position themselves as agents of, as well as arenas for, sustainability transitions. In this study, territorial capital is understood as comprising both the hard and soft elements of the economic and social ‘landscape’, which significantly affect the way regional and urban economies are shaped, as well as the structural substrate from which transformative capacity is cultivated. Transformative capacity is defined here as the dynamic competences through which regional and local actors can change current socio-economic systems towards more sustainable configurations, as well as is regarded as a unique perspective of how regional and local development institutions map their future in different ‘frontiers’ to fit the changing terrain of the economic and social ‘landscape’. In this study, prosilience captures the normative horizon towards which the dynamic interaction of territorial capital and transformative capacity is directed. Drawing on existing research on territorial capital, transformative capacity and prosilience, the study contributes to policy practice by articulating how regional and local development institutions can cultivate the combinatorial constituents of territorial capital and transformative capacity to shape regional futures rather than merely react to external disturbances. Through this lens, shaping regional and local economic development trajectories is perceived as a generative and path-shaping process rather than a reactive adjustment to exogenous pressures. The study contributes to current debates in regional studies and sustainability science by offering a nuanced understanding of how cities and regions can move beyond resilience towards proactive future-making, with implications for place-based development strategies and sustainability-oriented regional policy.

title: A novel synergistic impurity-removal mechanism mediated by in-situ CO2 activation and the formation of a Ca-Mg composite carbonate framework in crude magnesium melts
summary: The selective and efficient removal of impurity elements remains a critical scientific challenge in the preparation of high-purity magnesium. To address the secondary impurity contamination and environmental burden associated with tradition
content: The selective and efficient removal of impurity elements remains a critical scientific challenge in the preparation of high-purity magnesium. To address the secondary impurity contamination and environmental burden associated with traditional flux refining, this study proposes a novel synergistic impurity removal mechanism involving in-situ activation of CO 2 in crude magnesium melt and mediation by Ca-Mg composite carbonate frameworks. In this process the electronic activation of CO 2 in high-temperature magnesium melt to generate highly reactive CO 3 2− . Through strong coordination between Ca 2+ , Mg 2+ , and CO 3 2− , stable Ca-Mg-CO 3 2− structural units are formed, which enable the selective capture and phase separation of K, Na, and Ca impurities. Thermodynamic calculations indicate that the composite carbonate phase remains stable only under conditions involving Ca participation, with its stability zone extends markedly toward lower CO 2 partial pressures. These results identify that Ca serves as the key medium for synergistic carbonation. First-principles molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the Ca-Mg composite carbonate framework can promotes the peripheral incorporation of K + and Na + while maintaining structural integrity, gradually forming multicomponent composite carbonates. Experimental results further confirm that the formation of Ca-based composite carbonate slag phases is associated with impurity enrichment. This study systematically elucidates the green impurity removal pathway of CO 2 in molten magnesium: “in-situ activation—carbonate ion formation—Ca-Mg composite carbonate framework construction—synergistic incorporation of multiple impurities—stable formation of composite carbonates”. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for the development of a green, low-carbon, and highly selective magnesium melt refining technology system.

title: Resilient growth for China in a turbulent world: how a triple logic of clean, secure and cheap can drive the country’s economy
source: London School of Economics and Political Science Theses Online (London School of Economics and Political Science)
summary: Globally, the prevailing model of economic growth is reaching its limits. Countries’ heavy reliance on fossil fuels increasingly leads to pollution, ill health and climate risk, while rising geopolitical uncertainty exacerbates the economic
content: Globally, the prevailing model of economic growth is reaching its limits. Countries’ heavy reliance on fossil fuels increasingly leads to pollution, ill health and climate risk, while rising geopolitical uncertainty exacerbates the economic challenges they face. In this environment, China provides a leading example of how the green transition can maintain growth even during periods of global instability. This policy insight shows why such turbulence strengthens the case for green growth, creating a strategic imperative grounded in energy security, industrial competitiveness and supply-chain resilience. The authors set out the foundations of resilient growth in China, drawing on examples from countries across the world.

title: Unstable carbon sink growth in alpine grasslands of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau
summary: Introduction Alpine grasslands on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP) are central to regional carbon cycling and climate regulation. Although warming and increasing precipitation have driven widespread greening and greater carbon uptake, it rem
content: Introduction Alpine grasslands on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP) are central to regional carbon cycling and climate regulation. Although warming and increasing precipitation have driven widespread greening and greater carbon uptake, it remains uncertain whether these gains are accompanied by greater ecosystem stability. Methods We examined carbon sink capacity and temporal variability using net ecosystem productivity (NEP) and proportional variability (PV), and assessed recovery resilience indirectly using lag-one autocorrelation (TAC) as a conditional proxy. Grasslands were classified into eight types based on the trend directions of NEP, PV, and TAC. Multivariate spatial regressions were used to examine hydroclimatic associations with these trends. Results Annual NEP increased across 81.7% of the grassland area between 2000 and 2024, with significant increases (p < 0.05) across 31.7%. Plateau-scale mean annual NEP increased significantly at 0.553 g C m ⁻² yr ⁻² (p = 0.006). Regional mean PV and TAC also increased, indicating greater temporal fluctuations and potentially slower recovery under the assumptions underlying TAC. Robust sinks (T1), with increasing NEP and declining PV and TAC, covered 20.2% of grasslands, whereas 61.6% belonged to T2–T4, where increasing NEP co-occurred with rising PV, TAC, or both. Vulnerable sinks were the largest category (32.6%) and were concentrated in semi-arid alpine steppes and alpine deserts, whereas robust sinks occurred mainly in eastern alpine meadows. Mean annual precipitation was the strongest predictor associated with NEP trends, and vapor pressure deficit was the strongest predictor associated with PV and TAC trends. Discussion Stronger carbon uptake does not necessarily translate into a more stable ecosystem. Evaluating carbon uptake together with temporal variability and conditional resilience indicators can inform assessments of QTP alpine grasslands under climate stress.

title: Effect of higher NOx emissions tax rates on carbon efficiency: Quasi-natural experiment based on China's NOx emissions tax rate reform
summary: Abstract This study employs a quasi-natural experiment with a difference-in-differences (DID) approach to estimate the impact of China’s nitrous oxide (NO x ) emissions tax reform on carbon efficiency (CE), defining the reform as the adopti
content: Abstract This study employs a quasi-natural experiment with a difference-in-differences (DID) approach to estimate the impact of China’s nitrous oxide (NO x ) emissions tax reform on carbon efficiency (CE), defining the reform as the adoption of rates above the national minimum to precisely capture regional heterogeneity. Results reveal that the NO x emissions tax rate reform significantly accelerates sample cities’ CE progress and has beneficial spatial spillover effects, driving CE improvement in surrounding areas. The reform exhibits more pronounced CE enhancement effects in eastern China and cities with a larger share of secondary industry. Furthermore, the reform effectively synergizes with policy measures such as clean energy promotion, air pollution prevention and control plans, and the Low-Carbon City pilot policy, yielding more positive outcomes. The NO x emissions tax rate reform enhances CE through promoting green technological innovation and curbing industrial agglomeration in pilot regions. Furthermore, synergistic NO x and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) reduction is the most comprehensive and primary channel for promoting CE progress through NO x emissions tax rate reform. The findings reveal the ancillary influence of NO x emissions tax on CO 2 reduction and their potential as an interim instrument before China enacts a carbon tax, offering a practical, efficiency-aligned mitigation pathway.

title: Digitalizing Sustainability: The Role of E-HRM and Green Employee Behaviors in Corporate Carbon Neutrality
summary: This study examines the role of Electronic Human Resource Management (E-HRM) in driving Corporate Carbon Neutrality through the mediating mechanism of Green Employee Behaviors (GEB). Positioned within the volatile, infrastructure-constraine
content: This study examines the role of Electronic Human Resource Management (E-HRM) in driving Corporate Carbon Neutrality through the mediating mechanism of Green Employee Behaviors (GEB). Positioned within the volatile, infrastructure-constrained manufacturing sector of Southeast Nigeria, the research investigates how digital workflows promote sustainable industrial outcomes. Utilizing a total enumeration sampling technique, primary data was gathered via a hybrid distribution approach from 294 full-time employees across four major firms in the Awka, Nnewi, and Onitsha clusters: Juhel Pharmaceutical, Innoson Vehicle Manufacturing, Chikason Group, and Millennium Plastics. Data analysis was executed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS v4. The empirical results reveal that E-HRM exerts a strong, direct, positive effect on GEB (β = 0.584$, t = 11.241), which in turn significantly influences Corporate Carbon Neutrality (β = 0.492, t = 8.653). Crucially, mediation analysis confirms that GEB significantly bridges the relationship between digital HR platforms and emission reductions (β = 0.287, t = 6.418). These findings demonstrate that cloud-based infrastructures do not achieve environmental targets automatically; rather, they serve as digital frameworks that support employee green behaviors that contribute toward organizational carbon reduction initiatives.

title: Light‐Driven CO 2 Hydrogenation to Methanol: Photothermal Catalysis and Beyond
summary: ABSTRACT Photothermal CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol offers a promising strategy to overcome the thermodynamic‐kinetic trade‐off effect that limits conventional thermocatalysis. The rational design of effective catalysts relies on better un
content: ABSTRACT Photothermal CO 2 hydrogenation to methanol offers a promising strategy to overcome the thermodynamic‐kinetic trade‐off effect that limits conventional thermocatalysis. The rational design of effective catalysts relies on better understanding of the roles of light in driving or assisting the hydrogenation reaction. While high‐energy photons generate the chemical potential ( µ e‐h ) of photogenerated charge carriers for non‐thermal activation, low‐energy photons are converted into localized heat to accelerate reaction kinetics. Building on this framework, we discuss the key light‐driven mechanisms governing methanol synthesis, including carrier transport and interfacial injection, electronic reconstruction and valence‐state regulation, photo‐induced defect evolution, and dynamic surface restructuring. We further highlight how localized photothermal heating and spatial thermal management can be extended from the catalyst scale to the reactor scale through dual‐temperature‐zone engineering, enabling simultaneous optimization of kinetics and thermodynamics. Finally, key challenges and future directions are highlighted, providing perspectives for the development of practical solar‐driven CO 2 ‐to‐methanol technologies.

title: A three-stage roadmap and key issue outlook for China’s hydrogen energy industry toward 2060
summary: Abstract China has recently elevated hydrogen energy to a strategic priority within its national energy security framework. As policy support, technology maturation, and regulatory integration advance, the sector is moving from preliminary
content: Abstract China has recently elevated hydrogen energy to a strategic priority within its national energy security framework. As policy support, technology maturation, and regulatory integration advance, the sector is moving from preliminary demonstration toward more systematic deployment. This study develops a three-stage roadmap for China’s hydrogen energy industry toward 2060 by integrating techno-economic modeling, scenario analysis, and policy-target cross-checking. The results suggest a staged evolution within the broader energy system: scenario-specific enablement through 2030, system regulation and cross-sector integration during 2030−2040, and a possible foundational energy-carrier role by 2060. In the current phase, hydrogen deployment is constrained by high renewable-hydrogen costs, incomplete safety regulation, and system-compatibility barriers; its role therefore remains concentrated in selected industrial and mobility applications. In the mid-term phase, declining renewable-hydrogen costs and maturing storage and transportation networks could allow hydrogen to support long-duration energy storage, renewable-power integration, and industrial decarbonization. In the long term, hydrogen may form a dual-carrier energy architecture with electricity, provided that technology, safety governance, infrastructure, and standards continue to mature. The proposed roadmap offers a structured reference for hydrogen-related policy planning, infrastructure investment, and future research under China’s carbon-neutrality transition.

title: Valorization of ‘enset’ (Ensete ventricosum) fiber for high-performance cellulose nanocrystals via acid hydrolysis followed by ultrasonication: Optimization, characterization, and barrier properties
summary: The growing accumulation of non-biodegradable synthetic plastic waste has intensified the urgent need for sustainable, bio-based alternatives. This study focuses on the valorization of underutilized Enset ( Ensete ventricosum ) fiber, an ab
content: The growing accumulation of non-biodegradable synthetic plastic waste has intensified the urgent need for sustainable, bio-based alternatives. This study focuses on the valorization of underutilized Enset ( Ensete ventricosum ) fiber, an abundant agricultural residue in Ethiopia, into high-performance cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) as a green reinforcing agent for biodegradable packaging applications. A multi-step extraction protocol was employed, involving Soxhlet dewaxing, two-stage alkaline treatment, chlorine-free hydrogen peroxide bleaching, and acid hydrolysis followed by ultrasonication. The hydrolysis parameters (acid concentration, temperature, and time) were thoroughly optimized using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on a Box-Behnken design (BBD) to maximize CNC yield and minimize particle size. The optimized conditions (59.90% H 2 SO 4 , 77.93 ℃ , 63.22 min) yielded CNC with a high yield of 73.50 ± 3.2 wt% and a mean hydrodynamic diameter of 63.22 ± 6.5 nm. The model confirmed excellent reliability (R² = 0.988). Advanced characterization via FTIR, XRD, SEM, DLS, TGA/DTG, and BET confirmed the successful removal of amorphous components. FTIR indicates the newly produced CNCs is very much rich with active sites like –OH, -C-O-C-,while SEM exposed the raw fiber surface was rough, whereas the surface of CNCs became even after the removal of lignin, fatty, and waxy compounds. Crystallinity index of 82.09 ± 5.1%. Mechanical testing of neat CNC films demonstrated a tensile strength of 150 ± 2.1 MPa, confirming their load-bearing capacity the resulting CNC exhibited low water vapor (30 ± 3.1 g/m²·day), oxygen (2.3 ± 5.2 g/m²·day·atm), and grease (<0.12 g/m²·day) transmission rates, confirming their barrier performance. These findings establish enset fiber as a sustainable, high-value feedstock for CNC production, with significant potential for subsequent development in biodegradable packaging and nanocomposite applications, contributing to agricultural waste valorization and the circular bio-economy in Ethiopia. Continued advancements in integrating CNCs into diverse applications hold significant potential to transform industries seeking sustainable, high-performance materials.

title: Polypropylene microplastics modify copper associated leaf injury and photosynthetic responses in Nymphaea ‘Black Beauty’
summary: Introduction Microplastics and heavy metals cooccur in freshwater habitats, yet it remains unclear whether microplastics intensify metal toxicity or redirect the dominant mode of plant injury. Methods We exposed the floatingleaved aquatic p
content: Introduction Microplastics and heavy metals cooccur in freshwater habitats, yet it remains unclear whether microplastics intensify metal toxicity or redirect the dominant mode of plant injury. Methods We exposed the floatingleaved aquatic plant Nymphaea `Black Beauty' for 28 d to control conditions, copper (Cu) alone, polypropylene microplastics (PPMPs) alone, or combined Cu and PPMP stress. Wholeplant phenotype, relative growth rate, leaf chlorosis and necrosis, root scanning electron microscopy, gas exchange, chlorophyll fluorescence, malondialdehyde (MDA), and antioxidant enzymes were integrated to distinguish structural damage from functional inhibition. Results Cu alone produced a necrosisdominated response: relative growth rate decreased by approximately 65%, net photosynthetic rate (Pn) by 54%, effective PSII quantum yield (ΦPSII) by 52%, and electron transport rate (ETR) by 47%, whereas MDA increased by 58% and necrotic area reached 26.4%. PPMPs alone caused moderate growth inhibition and chlorosis, with a numerically higher nonphotochemical quenching (NPQ) mean and little lipid peroxidation. Factorial analysis detected Cu × PP interactions for selected endpoints, including growth, necrosis, Pn, NPQ, ETR, and POD; these endpointwise tests were exploratory. Necrotic area declined to 2.1%, but growth and photosynthesis remained strongly inhibited. The density of morphologically assigned PPlike structures in processed root sections was 4.16fold higher under combined exposure than under PPMPs alone. Under coexposure, Pn declined while no differences in stomatal conductance or transpiration from the control were detected, while ΦPSII, ETR, and NPQ decreased markedly. The lower NPQ mean was consistent with reduced regulated thermal dissipation under the measurement conditions but was not diagnostic of a specific photoprotective defect. POD activity increased by approximately 40%, whereas SOD activity decreased by 35%, showing an enzymespecific antioxidant pattern rather than demonstrating enhanced overall detoxification. Discussion Thus, under the shared 2% Tween20 background, Cu -PP coexposure produced a lownecrosis, highfunctionalinhibition phenotype consistent with an important nonstomatal component. These responses do not establish altered Cu distribution, particle internalization, or detoxification.

title: Enhanced electrical conductivity in Mg-containing aluminum oxyhydroxide films fabricated by drop-dry deposition
summary: We explore oxyhydroxides as a transparent electronic material. Mg-containing aluminum oxyhydroxide (Al–Mg(OOH)) films were deposited by drop-dry deposition (DDD), which is a very simple and low-cost technique for thin film fabrication. In D
content: We explore oxyhydroxides as a transparent electronic material. Mg-containing aluminum oxyhydroxide (Al–Mg(OOH)) films were deposited by drop-dry deposition (DDD), which is a very simple and low-cost technique for thin film fabrication. In DDD, a small amount of deposition solution is dropped onto a substrate placed on a hotplate. As the solvent (water) evaporates, the solution concentration gradually increases, and precipitation occurs on the substrate surface. An aqueous solution containing Mg(NO 3 ) 2 ·6H 2 O, Al(NO 3 ) 3 ·9H 2 O, and NaOH was used as a deposition solution. With the addition of Al salt to the deposition solution, the Al content in the deposited films increased. Pure Mg(OH) 2 exhibited a high resistivity on the order of 10 9 Ω·cm and behaved as an insulator. The resistivity decreased with increasing Al concentration in the deposition solution. The resistivity decreased to the order of 10 4 Ω·cm.

title: Between integration and modularity: reviewing global Integrated Assessment Models for water–energy–land–economy nexus analysis
summary: Introduction Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) link human activities, emissions and the climate system, underpinning global mitigation pathways and national climate strategies. As policy questions increasingly encompass water, land and ma
content: Introduction Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) link human activities, emissions and the climate system, underpinning global mitigation pathways and national climate strategies. As policy questions increasingly encompass water, land and materials, the depth of integration across these domains is becoming as important as their representation. This study maps the current landscape of global IAM configurations and examines the trade-offs between integrated models and modular multi-model frameworks. Methods We conducted a documentation-based review of 21 globally scoped IAM configurations, including individual models and documented model couplings. Using explicit coding rules, we assessed 17 criteria and the integration depth of eight domains. Configurations were classified along an integration spectrum ranging from single code bases to institutionally maintained model stacks and bespoke multi-model pipelines. We also examined how these configurations represent welfare and evaluated the advantages and limitations of bespoke pipelines, using the modelling suite of the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) Global Climate Hub (GCH) as an illustrative case. Results Energy is represented endogenously in 16 of the 21 configurations, whereas water is represented endogenously or through two-way links in seven. Bidirectional water–energy feedback is resolved in four configurations, based on three independent model systems, while fully endogenous three-way energy–land–water modelling is present in three. Materials remain an emerging domain: two configurations endogenise bulk-material production and two account for critical-mineral demand, but none represents mineral supply, depletion or price feedback. Welfare is assessed using output indicators, cost- or surplus-based objectives, or consumption utility; beyond-GDP indicators appear only as reported outputs. Discussion The comparison highlights trade-offs between integration depth and modularity. Bespoke multi-model pipelines offer greater sectoral depth, country-level detail and flexibility in model selection, but require substantial harmonisation and may achieve looser integration when model linkages are not iterated. The GCH modelling suite illustrates this approach. These findings are not intended to rank IAM configurations, but to provide practical guidance for model selection and identify a shared agenda for strengthening both IAMs and modular frameworks.

title: Towards Policy Synergy and a Just Industrial Transition in China through Integrated Scenario Assessment of Carbon Lock In and Stakeholder Alignment
summary: Abstract Industrial decarbonisation requires low-carbon technologies and the capacity to implement them under persistent structural constraints. This study develops an integrated scenario framework for China that connects technological, ass
content: Abstract Industrial decarbonisation requires low-carbon technologies and the capacity to implement them under persistent structural constraints. This study develops an integrated scenario framework for China that connects technological, asset, institutional and network lock-in with stakeholder alignment and just-transition considerations. A two-round Delphi consultation with 15 experts informed indicator assessment and scenario design. Five scenarios compare business as usual, policy enhancement, technological change, collaborative governance and an integrated package over 2020–2050. Historical calibration of aggregate industrial energy demand over 2010–2020 gives \(\:{R}^{2}=0.93\) and a mean absolute percentage error of 6.2%. Against the 2020 direct-emissions baseline of 1,000 Mt CO₂ for the selected manufacturing sectors, the integrated scenario reaches 410 Mt CO₂ in 2050, a 59.00% reduction. It exceeds the three narrower scenarios by 17.45–39.40 percentage points and raises the Power Alignment Index from 0.4800 to 0.7730. Energy and steel have the highest weighted lock-in scores. Analytical derivation and exact numerical verification over 9,251 feasible settings per capacity response identify positive synergy when deployment and implementation improve together under multiplicative or binding-bottleneck conditions. A support-threshold mechanism identifies additional actor backing from joint measures. The findings show how integrated policy can improve emissions outcomes and implementation capacity by addressing complementary constraints. Worker protection, local adjustment and participation provide additional criteria for evaluating a just industrial transition.

title: Dynamic Decoupling as a Strategy for Highly Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
summary: Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the 2e- oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a promising sustainable alternative to conventional industrial production. Nonetheless, its practical efficiency is fundamentally capped by the inherent coupling
content: Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the 2e- oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a promising sustainable alternative to conventional industrial production. Nonetheless, its practical efficiency is fundamentally capped by the inherent coupling of catalytic kinetics, interfacial electric field, and mass transport, becoming a critical bottleneck for classical static electrolysis strategies. Here, a dynamic decoupling strategy (i.e., a temporal separation of the dominant interfacial constraint rather than a physical decoupling of involved processes) is introduced and validated on a Co-ONx-C single-atom-catalyst-based cathode, employing pulsed electrolysis to modulate the coupled processes in the time domain. This dynamic approach engineers the electrocatalytic interface through three time-separated effects of unequal weight: mass-transport replenishment during the rest interval predominantly enhances H2O2 accumulation, interfacial-field modulation across the potential of zero charge governs the selectivity improvement, and support-defect modulation enables efficient Co-site utilization. As a result, this unconventional approach promotes a 2.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 concentration over the static mode, significantly suppressing the parasitic H2 evolution reaction. Validated in a photovoltaic-driven system with over 100 day stable production, this work establishes dynamic decoupling as a smart design principle for next-generation environmental electrocatalysis.

title: Glucose transporters in health and disease: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic applications
summary: The purpose of this review is to provide a comprehensive analysis of glucose transporters, integrating molecular mechanisms, physiological roles, and therapeutic applications across health and disease states. Glucose transport across cellul
content: The purpose of this review is to provide a comprehensive analysis of glucose transporters, integrating molecular mechanisms, physiological roles, and therapeutic applications across health and disease states. Glucose transport across cellular membranes, mediated by facilitative glucose transporters (GLUTs) and sodium-glucose cotransporters (SGLTs), represents a fundamental control point in glucose homeostasis. Since the initial discovery of specific membrane components for glucose transfer in 1948, our understanding has evolved substantially, revealing complex tissue-specific expression patterns and regulatory mechanisms. Recent structural biology advances, genetic studies, and clinical developments, particularly the success of SGLT2 inhibitors in treating type 2 diabetes and their unexpected benefits in heart failure and chronic kidney disease, have transformed our understanding of these essential proteins. This review examines the structural and functional properties of glucose transporters, their tissue-specific distribution and regulation, their roles in metabolic organs, and their dysfunction in various diseases. We specifically address unresolved questions regarding tissue-specific regulation, expanding roles in disease pathogenesis beyond diabetes, and emerging therapeutic strategies. By synthesizing recent technological advances, clinical implications, and areas of continuing controversy, this review provides a framework for understanding both the fundamental biology of glucose transporters and their growing therapeutic significance in metabolic diseases.

title: Enhanced Xylene Sensing Performance of Fe‐Doped NiO Nanosheet Arrays via In Situ Growth
summary: ABSTRACT Xylene is a hazardous volatile organic compound (VOC) widely present in industrial environments, and achieving sensitive and stable detection of xylene remains a significant challenge for gas sensors. Here, a one‐step hydrothermal
content: ABSTRACT Xylene is a hazardous volatile organic compound (VOC) widely present in industrial environments, and achieving sensitive and stable detection of xylene remains a significant challenge for gas sensors. Here, a one‐step hydrothermal route was employed to in situ grow p‐type Fe‐doped NiO nanosheet arrays on ceramic tubes for xylene detection. Remarkably, trace Fe‐doping (0.2%) NiO leads to a threefold enhancement in response to 100 ppm xylene, compared with pristine NiO. This improvement is attributed to the Fe 3+ ‐induced regulation of the Ni 3+ /Ni 2+ ratio and surface oxygen states, particularly the enrichment of reactive chemisorbed oxygen species. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal that Fe incorporation subtly modulates the local electronic environment of NiO without disrupting its crystal framework. The optimized Fe‐doped NiO sensor shows high selectivity toward xylene, a wide detection range (10–200 ppm), and excellent humidity resistance, demonstrating its potential for practical VOC monitoring. This work highlights that low‐level Fe doping can effectively tailor the surface electronic structure of strongly correlated p‐type oxides, offering a viable strategy for high‐performance gas sensors.

title: Unraveling Green Innovation Drivers in High Carbon-Lock-in Process Industries: An Interpretable Machine Learning Approach with Temporal Validation
summary: Abstract The petrochemical industry, characterized by severe carbon lock-in and high asset specificity, is one of the most challenging sectors for green transition. Existing studies predominantly rely on linear econometric models that strug
content: Abstract The petrochemical industry, characterized by severe carbon lock-in and high asset specificity, is one of the most challenging sectors for green transition. Existing studies predominantly rely on linear econometric models that struggle to capture nonlinear synergies and lack industry-specific evidence. Using 380 firm-year observations from Chinese A-share listed petrochemical enterprises (2014–2024), we construct a five-dimensional driver system with 20 indicators grounded in institutional theory and the resource-based view, employing an interpretable XGBoost–SHAP framework. This study makes three key contributions: (1) revealing the conditional boundary of institutional pressure under high asset specificity, showing that only command-and-control regulation forms positive synergies with internal resources; (2) adopting expanding-window rolling validation instead of random partitioning to test temporal generalization, and introducing Kendall’s τ for the stability of SHAP feature importance rankings; and (3) uncovering single-threshold patterns across all core drivers in a high carbon-lock-in industry, providing micro-level evidence for optimizing regulatory instrument mixes. The model achieves a three-year average out-of-sample R² of 0.8352. Internal resource endowments—particularly firm size and R&D investment—dominate green innovation performance, while command-and-control regulation outperforms market-based instruments. These findings offer actionable insights for advancing the low-carbon transition of high-emission process industries, aligned with SDG 9 and SDG 13.

title: O contributo das explorações agrícolas localizadas nas zonas montanhosas para a transição energética: reflexões de Itália
source: Faculdade de Letras da Universidade do Porto eBooks
summary: The European Union has set ambitious targets for carbon neutrality through the Green Deal and subsequent measures. As a result, the urgent need to devote new land to energy transition requires consideration of how best to integrate energy o
content: The European Union has set ambitious targets for carbon neutrality through the Green Deal and subsequent measures. As a result, the urgent need to devote new land to energy transition requires consideration of how best to integrate energy objectives into the landscape. Even mountain areas, often considered exceptional for their high natural and cultural value, are increasingly becoming the location of intermittent renewable energy infrastructure. However, geographical factors in mountain areas may not encourage the presence of renewable energy projects. This is a challenge in Southern Europe, for example, where a significant proportion of the territory is not flat. This study examines whether geographical constraints can influence the spatial distribution of investments in renewable energy production. The Italian Agricultural Census 2020 provides municipal data on agricultural holdings engaged in remunerative activities related to the production of renewable energy. These data allow detailed analysis of the integration of decarbonisation targets with the agricultural sector. Multiple statistical tests and regression models were used to investigate potential differences between mountain and plain municipalities. Preliminary results show significant differences, with mountain municipalities showing lower levels of investment in profitable renewable energy production activities on farms than their counterparts in the plains. These results highlight the uneven contribution of different areas within a country to the energy transition goals. However, factors such as belonging to the province of Bolzano dominate the predictive power, suggesting that although mountain status is a critical factor, contextual factors strongly influence the commitment to renewable energy.

title: How Eco Label Credibility Social Norms and Price Premium Drive Circular Economy Product Adoption in Zhejiang China
summary: Abstract Circular economy products (CEPs) can extend the life of resources through reuse and recycling, thereby supporting more sustainable consumption. However, consumer adoption of CEPs in China remains relatively underexplored, particula
content: Abstract Circular economy products (CEPs) can extend the life of resources through reuse and recycling, thereby supporting more sustainable consumption. However, consumer adoption of CEPs in China remains relatively underexplored, particularly the roles of trust, social norms, and price-related concerns. This study surveyed 407 adults in Zhejiang Province who had prior experience with CEPs and used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to examine how eco-label credibility, social norms, environmental concern, product trust, and perceived green premium influence willingness to purchase and actual purchasing behaviour. The results show that product trust, eco-label credibility, social norms, and environmental concern positively influence willingness to purchase, with product trust emerging as the strongest predictor. In contrast, perceived green premium negatively affects willingness to purchase. Willingness to purchase also mediates these relationships and significantly influences actual purchasing behaviour. These findings highlight the importance of building consumer trust, strengthening the credibility and transparency of eco-labels, and addressing price concerns to encourage circular consumption. For marketers and policymakers, improving confidence in CEPs while making them more affordable may help bridge the gap between consumers’ positive attitudes and their actual sustainable purchasing behaviour.

title: Living on the edge: survival strategies, biofilm, metabolites, and applications of aquatic extremophilic bacteria adaptation
summary: Aquatic extremophilic bacteria from polar, deep-sea, and hypersaline environments reveal how life persists at physicochemical limits. Biofilm matrices act as dynamic interfaces that stabilize cells and organize metabolic cooperation, while
content: Aquatic extremophilic bacteria from polar, deep-sea, and hypersaline environments reveal how life persists at physicochemical limits. Biofilm matrices act as dynamic interfaces that stabilize cells and organize metabolic cooperation, while specialized metabolites extend stress tolerance. Comparing these systems highlights a convergence on matrix-mediated strategies alongside environment-specific adaptations, positioning extremophilic biofilms as key models for microbial resilience and sources of novel biotechnological potential.

title: Slurry-processing, microstructural optimization, and full-cell cycling of thiophosphate solid electrolytes: From fundamentals to applications
source: Elektronische Hochschulschriften der LMU München (Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München)
summary: In order to meet the increasing global demand for electric vehicles (EVs), the need for battery cells with high performance capabilities that go beyond state-of-the-art lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is also increasing. All-solid-state batter
content: In order to meet the increasing global demand for electric vehicles (EVs), the need for battery cells with high performance capabilities that go beyond state-of-the-art lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is also increasing. All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with well performing solid electrolytes (SEs) are promising candidates to compete with and eventually replace LIBs. Up to now, only a few SEs materials exhibit ionic conductivity values in the range of 10−3 S cm−1 or more that can compete with those of commercially available liquid electrolytes. While the ionic conductivity is arguably the most important property, SEs still suffer from high costs and scalability challenges. As long as these issues are not addressed, ASSBs will face difficulties in establishing themselves in the market. To address these issues, this thesis aims to provide a possible pathway toward scalable ASSBs production by developing slurry-processed tetragonal Li7SiPS8 (t-Li7SiPS8)-based sheets, while ensuring their chemical and structural integrity and relying on earth-abundant materials to reduce costs. By optimizing the microstructure through varying binder contents and stack pressures, the transport properties are improved for optimal performance. Moreover, the potential of t-Li7SiPS8 as SE in a full cell paired with high-capacity Si anodes is shown, paving the way for future ASSB applications. Overall, this thesis provides a comprehensive overview from production methods to device implementation. Chapter 1 gives an overview of historical battery developments and explains the working principles of batteries, including key terminologies and performance indicators. It also reviews state-of-the-art battery components and emerging post-LIBs technologies, with a particular focus on ASSBs. Additionally, the chapter discusses different SE classes and the fundamentals behind diffusion mechanisms in solids. Chapter 2 covers the introduction and explanation of selected analytical methods used in this thesis. In Chapter 3 the slurry processing of t-Li7SiPS8 to produce SE sheets is presented. With a total of six different slurry formulations involving different binders and solvent, the free-standing SE sheets are systematically investigated with regard to their chemical and structural stability. Furthermore, their transport properties are intensively analyzed, showing a positive correlation with particle size. Chapter 4 draws on the knowledge obtained in Chapter 3 and focuses on the optimization of the microstructure to maximize the ionic conductivity through varying binder contents and stack pressures. Aside from microstructural effects through pressure variation, the ionic conductivity is also shown to be influenced by atomistic effects and only reasonable reaches values under distinct conditions. title: Implementing Circular Economy Practices in Innovative SMEs : Resources and Competencies for Engaging With Net‐Zero Transitions
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT The transition toward a net‐zero economy depends increasingly on the manufacturing sector, particularly innovative small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that might help mitigate environmental impacts through circular economy (CE) ado
content: ABSTRACT The transition toward a net‐zero economy depends increasingly on the manufacturing sector, particularly innovative small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that might help mitigate environmental impacts through circular economy (CE) adoption. Despite their critical role, the specific organizational configurations of resources and competencies required to successfully implement CE practices remain underexplored. This study investigated how strategic capabilities, framed through the natural resource‐based view, enable circularity via the “take–make–distribute–use–recover” fields of action. A survey of 99 Italian innovative manufacturing SMEs and a quantile regression analysis were used to examine the heterogeneity of drivers across different implementation levels. The findings show that SMEs need behavioral, interorganizational, and technical resources and competencies to support CE implementation across different fields of action. Resources are particularly relevant when SMEs initiate and diffuse CE practices, whereas competencies sustain progress toward circularity. These insights provide a roadmap for managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen CE implementation in the context of the net‐zero transition.

title: Assessing 50 Years of Salt Effects in Heterogeneous Photocatalysis
summary: Abstract Heterogeneous photocatalysis has been studied for the treatment of recalcitrant compounds for half a century, but one of the severe limitations for practical oxidation treatment continues to be the inhibitory effect of salt found i
content: Abstract Heterogeneous photocatalysis has been studied for the treatment of recalcitrant compounds for half a century, but one of the severe limitations for practical oxidation treatment continues to be the inhibitory effect of salt found in real water matrices. The negative impact of Na+, K+, Cl–, and other ionic species is rarely quantified, as there has been no systematic way to discuss salt effects, making the evaluation of photocatalysis performance across studies difficult and imprecise. In analyzing 50 years of literature for this review, we identified >1,200 publications on heterogeneous photocatalysis in different water types, such as seawater, brackish water, and industrial brines. Just 84 studies reported degradation rates in deionized and salt-containing water, with nearly all involving TiO2 as the photocatalyst composition and charged dye compounds as the model contaminant class. To analyze the kinetic data extracted from these studies, we introduce the photocatalysis salt-effect (PSE) metric as calculated through the relative salt-effectiveness evaluation (RSEE) method, quantifying the percent change in degradation rate when the water matrix contains a salt species. We identified an unexpected correlation between PSE and ionic strength (IS), irrespective of the contaminant, at solution pH values less than the TiO2 point-of-zero-charge (PZC), which is the plausible result of salt-induced particle aggregation at high ionic strengths during photocatalyst testing. While most published results showed salt inhibition of photocatalysis (−100% < PSE < −5%), there is evidence for salt promotion (PSE > +5%) and salt tolerance (−5% < PSE < +5%), which challenges the notion that salinity is always detrimental to photocatalytic activity. These findings highlight the opportunity to study fully and systematically the relationships among contaminant structure, photocatalyst PZC, solution pH, IS, and salt type. The PSE-based framework would be critical in understanding the effects of more complex water matrices and in ultimately developing salt-tolerant and salt-promoted heterogeneous photocatalysis for practical water treatment.

title: Optimising electrocoagulation for oilfield produced water treatment
summary: Petroleum produced water constitutes the largest aqueous by-product of onshore hydrocarbon extraction in Saudi Arabia, and its saline, oil-bearing matrix restricts the options available for on-site reclamation. This study examined electroco
content: Petroleum produced water constitutes the largest aqueous by-product of onshore hydrocarbon extraction in Saudi Arabia, and its saline, oil-bearing matrix restricts the options available for on-site reclamation. This study examined electrocoagulation (EC) as a treatment stage for produced water drawn from an onshore facility in the Eastern Province. A four-factor Box–Behnken design of 27 conditions spanned applied current density from 2 to 20 mA cm −2 , initial pH from 4 to 10, electrolysis duration from 10 to 90 min and inter-electrode gap from 5 to 25 mm, with 8 treatment outcomes quantified for each condition. Untreated water carried 1238.8 ± 17.7 mg L −1 chemical oxygen demand (COD), 427.2 ± 8.9 mg L −1 oil and grease and 777.8 nephelometric turbidity units (NTU). Applied current density governed the process, accounting for 34.8% to 72.1% of the partial variance across the 8 outcomes, whereas the inter-electrode gap carried 0.8% or less for every one. Current density and electrolysis duration acted through a single quantity, the delivered charge, and conditions spanning 60 to 5400 C L −1 collapsed onto a common relationship for each determinand. The pH of maximum removal migrated with the charge delivery rate, from pH 8.2 at 2 mA cm −2 to pH 4.0, the lower boundary of the examined range, at 20 mA cm −2 . Thirteen of the 27 conditions complied with the 250 mg L −1 COD threshold and 3 complied with the 10 mg L −1 oil and grease threshold, each of the latter at 20 mA cm −2 . No condition reached the 5 NTU turbidity threshold, with a lowest value of 7.78 NTU, and total dissolved solids (TDS) removal did not surpass 20.6%. Aluminium required 3.82 kWh m −3 as opposed to 4.24 kWh m −3 for iron and yielded a treated oil and grease concentration of 5.68 mg L −1 as opposed to 50.80 mg L −1 . Anodic dissolution proceeded at 47.8 ± 1.6% of the stoichiometric expectation across 29 experiments (28 with aluminium and 1 with iron anodes). Electrocoagulation with aluminium electrodes is therefore recommended as a pre-treatment stage, operated at a specific charge dose of at least 3000 C L −1 and an initial pH not higher than 7, ahead of a polishing stage that removes the residual turbidity and the dissolved salts.

title: Laboratory evaluation of hot mix asphalt containing biochar as partial aggregate substitution
summary: Abstract Biochar is a promising material for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and is increasingly being incorporated into composite construction materials, such as concrete and asphalt. However, adding sufficient amounts of biochar to as
content: Abstract Biochar is a promising material for mitigating greenhouse gas emissions and is increasingly being incorporated into composite construction materials, such as concrete and asphalt. However, adding sufficient amounts of biochar to asphalt requires substituting mineral aggregates, which significantly alters its properties. Hence, this study explores the viability of partially substituting mineral aggregates with biochar in hot-mix asphalt, designed for use as a base course. Four substitution percentages (0, 2, 4, and 8% by mass of the mineral aggregates) were investigated for their volumetric, mechanical, and hygroscopic behaviour. The physical and mechanical properties exhibited non-monotone evolution with biochar content, as biochar significantly affected both the air void content and the optimum binder content. A biochar content of 2% by mass of the aggregates improved the mechanical performance, as evidenced by a 17% increase in fracture toughness, an average 20% increase in stiffness and a 70% reduction in permanent deformations. The improved performance was attributed to reduced air void content, resulting from potential biochar-proportion-dependent gradation changes in the mixtures. Beyond 4% by mass of aggregates, mechanical performance declined significantly, which can be attributed to both the increasing air void content with increasing biochar content and the lower mechanical strength of biochar compared to mineral aggregates. These findings indicate that biochar can replace up to 4% of the aggregates by mass to achieve greenhouse gas emission goals while maintaining technical feasibility.

title: Theoretical perspectives on sustainable aviation fuel implementation across the value chain: An integrative review
summary: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is widely recognised as a key pathway for aviation decarbonisation. However, its implementation is shaped by the interplay of regulatory, technological, economic, and social factors. Existing theoretical pers
content: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is widely recognised as a key pathway for aviation decarbonisation. However, its implementation is shaped by the interplay of regulatory, technological, economic, and social factors. Existing theoretical perspectives remain fragmented across disciplines, limiting their ability to guide practitioners and policymakers in coordinating implementation. This paper addresses this gap through an integrative review that synthesises relevant perspectives, including socio-technical transitions and the Multi-Level Perspective (MLP), transition management, innovation systems, the circular economy (CE), diffusion of innovation, stakeholder theory, and the business model literature. Drawing on these cross-disciplinary insights and the aviation sector’s established capacity for multi-stakeholder coordination, the study develops the Technology–Authority–Business (TAB) framework. This systemic lens conceptualises SAF implementation as the co-evolution of three interdependent domains and helps identify sources of momentum and pressure points that can advance implementation. Applied to a published case study of SAF development in South Australia, the framework demonstrates how factors that conventional analyses consider separately can be understood as interconnected leverage points, providing practitioners and policymakers with a clearer basis for coordinated action.

title: Green finance market development and carbon emissions trading: evidence on corporate environmental responsibility in China
summary: From the perspective of institutional–financial synergy, this paper integrates environmental regulation theory with financial development theory to construct a theoretical framework for analyzing the effects of carbon emissions trading (CET
content: From the perspective of institutional–financial synergy, this paper integrates environmental regulation theory with financial development theory to construct a theoretical framework for analyzing the effects of carbon emissions trading (CET) and green finance market development (GF) on corporate environmental responsibility (CER). Based on panel data of listed firms in high-carbon industries on China's Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share markets from 2010 to 2025, we employ staggered difference-in-differences (DID), moderating effect models, mediation effect models, and a moderated serial mediation model to examine their interaction and potential transmission channels. The findings are as follows. First, during the local carbon market pilot stage, treated firms' CER increased by 0.0214 on average, or 5.43% relative to the sample mean. When extended to the post-2021 period, the national carbon market estimates are consistent with a positive governance effect. Second, regional green finance development is significantly and positively associated with CER, and the CET × GF interaction is significantly positive, consistent with a synergistic complementarity interpretation. Conditional marginal effects show that the estimated CET effect is stronger when green finance support is higher. Third, the Bootstrap indirect effects of financing constraints, environmental information disclosure, and green technological innovation are all significant, consistent with three potential mediation channels. Fourth, the positive CET × GF interaction is stronger in state-owned enterprises, high-emission subsectors, eastern regions, and firms with higher executive environmental awareness. This study provides empirical evidence for optimizing the synergy between carbon trading policy and green finance policy and promoting corporate environmental responsibility.

title: Money myths and the epistemic opacity of monetary order: Symbolic anchors among regional politicians and business professionals
summary: Abstract Money is one of modern society’s central institutions, yet its institutional foundations remain largely opaque – even to those routinely involved in fiscal and credit-related decision-making. Drawing on survey data from regional po
content: Abstract Money is one of modern society’s central institutions, yet its institutional foundations remain largely opaque – even to those routinely involved in fiscal and credit-related decision-making. Drawing on survey data from regional politicians and business professionals in the Austrian state of Styria, this article examines widespread beliefs about money creation and money backing, such as the ideas that money is backed by gold and created exclusively by central banks. The findings show that such myths persist not only among the general population but also among politicians and business professionals. Such beliefs are often interpreted as ‘folk ideas’ or ‘fictional expectations’. We argue that the concept of money myths better captures their social and institutional significance. Money myths are socially shared belief structures that provide symbolic anchors in an otherwise opaque monetary order. The gold myth is an intensified form of money myth: it elevates the promise of monetary stability into a promise of eternity, offering a timeless anchor against financial volatility. Theoretically, money and gold myths bridge the gap between everyday financial practice and limited explicit knowledge, contributing to the social foundations of monetary governance. The article thus contributes to debates on knowledge, legitimacy, and the symbolic foundations of monetary governance.

title: Explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and traditional energy investments: A GSADF approach amidst global events
summary: This study examines explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and renewable energy ETFs, index, and equities compared to traditional energy counterparts, using the Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (G
content: This study examines explosive price dynamics consistent with bubble-like behavior in clean and renewable energy ETFs, index, and equities compared to traditional energy counterparts, using the Generalized Supremum Augmented Dickey-Fuller (GSADF) test across four subperiods: Pre-Paris Agreement, Paris Agreement, COVID-19, and Russia-Ukraine War. Using daily price data for clean energy assets (ICLN, QCLN, CELS, ENPH, AEIS) and traditional energy assets (VDE, IXC, XLE, USEG), the analysis reveals pronounced prevalence of explosive price episodes in clean energy markets, with 76.55% of explosive price episodes in the Pre-agreement period and 72.66% during COVID-19, consistent with speculative dynamics. Traditional energy assets exhibit greater resilience, with limited explosive episodes, notably only USEG during the Russia-Ukraine War. The novel segmented subperiod approach, combined with GSADF’s precise bubble date-stamping of explosive episodes, distinguishes this study by offering granular insights into sector-specific vulnerabilities, unlike prior broader analyses. The findings indicate that selected clean energy instruments exhibited more frequent explosive price episodes during crisis periods than their traditional energy counterparts, a pattern that may inform risk assessment and further research relevant to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action) but does not by itself warrant specific investment or policy recommendations.

title: Tighter Control of AVOCs/NOx atop Carbon Neutrality Mitigations for China to Meet WHO Ambient Ozone Standard
summary: Abstract. Tropospheric ozone (O₃) remains a persistent air quality challenge in China, and it is uncertain whether deep precursor emission cuts aligned with carbon neutrality can secure the World Health Organization (WHO) ozone guideline of
content: Abstract. Tropospheric ozone (O₃) remains a persistent air quality challenge in China, and it is uncertain whether deep precursor emission cuts aligned with carbon neutrality can secure the World Health Organization (WHO) ozone guideline of 60 μg m⁻³ across all major urban agglomerations. Here we simulate summertime MDA8 O₃ over China’s five largest urban agglomerations using CMAQv5.5 under a range of emission scenarios, including a national synergistic emission reduction strategy (NSERS) that reduces NOₓ and anthropogenic VOCs by 40 % and 30 % in 2030, and by 90 % and 50 % in 2060, relative to 2020. To address remaining exceedances, we introduce an exceedance-driven local emission homogenization (O₃-LEH) method that constrains precursor emissions in non-attainment grid cells by the mean of nearby compliant cells. NSERS lowers cluster-mean MDA8O₃ to 41–72 μg m⁻³ by 2060, but residual exceedances above the WHO guideline persist in high-emission hotspots, mainly in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Yangtze River Delta regions. The O₃-LEH adjustments further reduce O₃ in these hotspots, yet only partially eliminate exceedances. Relative incremental reactivity diagnostics reveal a systematic transition from VOC-limited regimes in 2020 toward NOₓ-limited regimes in 2060, accompanied by a sharp increase in the AVOC/NOₓ ratio. Our results indicate that uniform national emission reductions alone cannot guarantee full attainment of the WHO ozone guideline, and that spatially differentiated, hotspot-targeted controls are a necessary complement to deep decarbonization.

title: PTFE-modified waterborne copolyester composite coating with a soft–hard structure for enhanced wear resistance in photovoltaic backsheets
summary: In this study, a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)-modified waterborne copolyester composite coating was developed by uniformly incorporating PTFE into an environmentally friendly waterborne copolyester matrix. The waterborne copolyester offer
content: In this study, a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)-modified waterborne copolyester composite coating was developed by uniformly incorporating PTFE into an environmentally friendly waterborne copolyester matrix. The waterborne copolyester offers distinct eco-friendly advantages, along with excellent adhesion to PET substrates and high flexibility, making it particularly suitable for photovoltaic module backsheets. The microstructure, tribological properties, and environmental service reliability of the resulting coating were systematically investigated. The PTFE effectively reduced the coefficient of friction between the coating and the counterpart ball and promoted the formation of a stable transfer film, thereby enabling a continuous reduction in wear. Compared with the pure waterborne copolyester coating, the wear rate of the PTFE-modified coating decreased by 19.1%. This enhanced tribological performance is attributed to a continuous film-forming network established by PTFE within the waterborne copolyester matrix. Furthermore, PTFE synergistically reinforced the matrix, generating a “soft–hard” composite structure. At the optimal 10% PTFE content, the soft and hard phases were uniformly distributed, delivering the greatest friction reduction and wear resistance. Combining the intrinsic environmental benefits, strong PET adhesion, and high flexibility of the waterborne copolyester, this approach provides a promising new strategy for developing high-performance wear-resistant coatings for photovoltaic module backsheets.

title: Water, energy and carbon in wastewater treatment and irrigated agriculture: Review with a case study
summary: Urban and agricultural water systems are still run on a linear resource model that sits badly with climate neutrality targets. This review reads the water-energy-carbon literature from one angle: what a treatment plant or an irrigated basin
content: Urban and agricultural water systems are still run on a linear resource model that sits badly with climate neutrality targets. This review reads the water-energy-carbon literature from one angle: what a treatment plant or an irrigated basin can recover, and what that recovery costs in energy and emissions. Thirty-four studies published between 2001 and 2026 are examined, most of them life cycle assessments and techno-economic appraisals. Combined heat and power, anaerobic membrane bioreactors and electrochemical phosphorus recovery can turn plants into net producers of energy and nutrients, but only where the penalty for removing biogas impurities and the burden of sludge disposal stay inside the system boundary. Cleaner effluent is rarely free. It is paid for in kilowatt-hours and, where nitrogen removal is pushed hard, in nitrous oxide. At basin scale, Souss-Massa in southern Morocco shows how solar irrigation, wastewater reuse and biomass planning combine, and why solar pumping without metering can trade a carbon problem for a water one. Climate neutrality will require dynamic accounting that captures temporal variability, operational scale and the economics of energy transitions.

title: On the optimal location of public charging stations in a monocentric city
summary: This study examines how the location of public charging stations (PCS) shapes the spatial equilibrium of a monocentric urban economy. We develop a linear urban model in which commuters endogenously choose vehicle type (conventional or elect
content: This study examines how the location of public charging stations (PCS) shapes the spatial equilibrium of a monocentric urban economy. We develop a linear urban model in which commuters endogenously choose vehicle type (conventional or electric), charging mode (public or home), and residential location. We show that the PCS location affects these choices, which in turn determine urban spatial structure, traffic-related emissions, and social welfare. We find that placing the PCS in non-ideal locations may exacerbate urban sprawl, reduce electric vehicle adoption, and lower social welfare. We derive closed-form solutions for the optimal PCS location under alternative policy objectives and quantitatively illustrate how deviations from the optimum affect equilibrium outcomes.

title: Edge-state transport in gapped bilayer graphene
summary: We investigate the electronic transport in gapped bilayer graphene (gBLG) devices. For certain edge terminations -- typically a combination of zigzag, armchair, and bearded types -- we observe edge state conduction within the band gap, whic
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: We investigate the electronic transport in gapped bilayer graphene (gBLG) devices. For certain edge terminations -- typically a combination of zigzag, armchair, and bearded types -- we observe edge state conduction within the band gap, which is opened by a gate potential bias between the two layers. The edge states can generate a non-local resistance. Band structure calculations of gBLG nanoribbons corroborate the existence of the edge states, whose edge localization can be switched by tuning the electron energy. However, their existence strongly depends on the edge termination and does not originate from a topological bulk-boundary .

title: A comprehensive “past-future” framework for restoration priority areas identification in a coastal city: a case study of Tianjin
summary: Abstract Coastal cities are highly urbanized regions where ecological sensitivity and the continuous expansion of urban space pose significant challenges to the sustainable development of ecosystems. This study assessed ecosystem services (
content: Abstract Coastal cities are highly urbanized regions where ecological sensitivity and the continuous expansion of urban space pose significant challenges to the sustainable development of ecosystems. This study assessed ecosystem services (ESs) from an integrated past–future perspective and elucidated spatiotemporal evolution patterns, as well as trade-offs and synergies among multiple ESs in Tianjin over the past two decades and under three future scenarios. The results indicated that, from 2000 to 2020, ESs showed a declining trend, although localized improvements were observed in the peripheral zones of ring-shaped built-up areas and in coastal wetland regions. Spatial trade-offs remained the dominant pattern among ESs, although their influence was gradually diminishing. In contrast, spatial synergies increased significantly. By integrating ESs supply, spatial distribution patterns, and future trends, we identified and delineated ecological restoration priority areas (RAPs), which were classified into three sequential categories: Core Conservation Zones, Synergistic Optimization Zones, and Ecological Improvement Zones. Based on a comprehensive analysis of land-use composition and its spatial distribution within RAPs, we proposed targeted ecological restoration strategies and spatial planning recommendations. This study provides scientific spatial guidance for ecological restoration and sustainable land management in coastal cities by identifying and prioritizing RAPs.

title: Spatial spillovers and causal configurations of the digital economy driving green manufacturing transformation in China
summary: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored. Based on panel data
content: The digital economy has emerged as a critical engine for high-quality economic development, yet its specific mechanisms and configurational pathways in empowering green manufacturing transformation remain under-explored.
