title: Author response: Pain is so close to pleasure: the same dopamine neurons can mediate approach and avoidance in Drosophila
summary: Dopaminergic neurons (DANs) have long been implicated in reward, punishment, and value processing across animal phyla, yet whether individual DAN subpopulations convey generalized valence signals or serve more specialized functions remains
content: Dopaminergic neurons (DANs) have long been implicated in reward, punishment, and value processing across animal phyla, yet whether individual DAN subpopulations convey generalized valence signals or serve more specialized functions remains contested. We addressed this question directly by screening about fifty Drosophila DAN subpopulations for their ability to drive consistent approach or avoidance across different operant behavioral paradigms in which flies controlled contingent optogenetic DAN activation through their own behavior. No single DAN subpopulation drove consistent preferences across all paradigms, and DAN activation produced substantially weaker valence effects than activation of sensory neurons used as positive controls. One subpopulation produced a striking time-dependent valence switch: initial aversion gave way to approach over approximately ten minutes of operant engagement. This switch required both dopamine and active behavioral contingency, demonstrating that agency itself is a necessary condition for such a valence switch. Together, our results suggest that individual DANs function as specialized, context-sensitive reporters for specific goals rather than general-purpose value signals, and that their apparent generality under some circumstances may reflect the consequences of non-contingent DAN stimulation rather than a true unified valence code.

title: Controlling Fe-Rich Intermetallic Phase Morphology in Recycled Aluminum for Automotive Wire Applications
summary: Upcycling of post-consumer aluminum scrap into high-quality wire conductors, such as those used in modern electric vehicle applications, is severely constrained by iron (Fe) accumulation, which may induce wire breakage during high-speed dra
content: Upcycling of post-consumer aluminum scrap into high-quality wire conductors, such as those used in modern electric vehicle applications, is severely constrained by iron (Fe) accumulation, which may induce wire breakage during high-speed drawing. To define the metallurgical limits for the utilization of secondary 1xxx-series aluminum, this study systematically investigates Fe enrichment behavior, intermetallic phase evolution, and the relationship between phase morphology and mechanical reliability. For this purpose, Fe content was systematically increased from 0.079 to 1.789 wt% by controlled liquid-state diffusion, showing a strong dependence of Fe uptake on holding time and temperature. Microstructural analysis demonstrated a progressive transition from fine dispersed Fe-containing particles at low Fe levels to elongated needle-/plate-like β-Al 5 FeSi-type intermetallic phases at elevated Fe concentrations. Furthermore, aluminum derived from used beverage cans (UBCs) revealed the formation of a more compact α-Al(Fe,Mn)Si-type morphology due to the combined influence of Fe, Si, and Mn. While passive sedimentation at 600–615 °C yielded only modest Fe reduction (from 1.789 to 1.31 wt%), the persistence of elongated Fe-rich phases after treatment demonstrated that gravity-based separation alone is not sufficient to achieve the microstructural requirements for conductor-grade aluminum. Subsequent metallurgical treatment by the addition of Al5B master alloy was therefore investigated as a potential approach for grain refinement and modification of Fe-containing intermetallic phases. The treatment improved the mechanical response but showed limited capability for transforming existing precipitate morphologies under the investigated conditions. Mechanical characterization coupled with Weibull reliability analysis established that 0.2% proof stress (Rp0.2) increased from approximately 20 to 30–40 MPa, while ultimate tensile strength increased from approximately 40 to ~100 MPa, potentially due in part to second-phase strengthening. However, this strength improvement was accompanied by a reduction in elongation at fracture from ~60 to ~30%. The findings demonstrate that the successful recycling of aluminum scrap for electrical conductor applications requires not only impurity reduction but also effective control of the morphology, size, and distribution of Fe-rich intermetallic phases. A successful approach would provide a metallurgical pathway to increase recycled content in aluminum conductor applications while maintaining the mechanical reliability required for wire production.

title: Maintenance of NO homeostasis by blue honeysuckle polyphenols via EGFR/PI3K/Akt signaling protects against high-altitude pulmonary edema
summary: Abstract High-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) is a serious high-altitude illness; Dexamethasone (DEX) is widely used, but its use is limited by adverse effects including gastrointestinal and metabolic disorders. Honeysuckle (Lonicera caerul
content: Abstract High-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE) is a serious high-altitude illness; Dexamethasone (DEX) is widely used, but its use is limited by adverse effects including gastrointestinal and metabolic disorders. Honeysuckle (Lonicera caerulea L.) is an emerging cold-region berry; its polyphenols (LCP) show anti-hypoxic, anti-fatigue, antioxidant, hepatoprotective, and nephroprotective effects. LCP enhanced hypoxic mouse pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells (PMVECs) viability by 36.55% (P < 0.01). In a hypobaric hypoxia-induced mouse HAPE model, LCP extended survival time by 4.38 min (P < 0.01) and improved pulmonary capillary integrity, shown by reduced alveolar exudation and lung water accumulation. LCP showed no apparent toxicity and oral bioavailability. Integrated mechanistic approaches (metabolomics, network pharmacology, molecular docking, ELISA, qRT-PCR, Western blotting) demonstrated significant downregulation of EGFR and Akt (P < 0.01). Collectively, LCP mitigates HAPE by suppressing oxidative stress and maintaining NO homeostasis via coordinated iNOS/eNOS regulation through the EGFR/PI3K/Akt pathway.

title: Solid CO2 sorbents for medium- and high-temperature carbon capture: material design, shaping, and deployment for hydrogen-related processes
summary: Abstract Due to their high-temperature resistance and potential for process intensification, medium- and high-temperature solid CO 2 adsorbents offer significant advantages in combining carbon capture with thermochemical fuel conversion and
content: Abstract Due to their high-temperature resistance and potential for process intensification, medium- and high-temperature solid CO 2 adsorbents offer significant advantages in combining carbon capture with thermochemical fuel conversion and hydrogen production. Although significant progress has been made in terms of formulation, microstructure, cyclic stability and reaction mechanisms, practical evaluation must go beyond laboratory-scale CO 2 adsorption tests to encompass, in addition, formability, wear resistance, regeneration strength, reactor compatibility and application potential. This review provides a deployment-oriented synthesis of representative medium- and high-temperature solid CO 2 sorbents, including hydrotalcite-based materials, MgO-based sorbents, CaO-based sorbents, alkali metal silicates, and titanate-based systems. Particular emphasis is placed on the interrelationships between material design, adsorption properties, structural strategies, mechanical strength and suitability for hydrogen-related thermochemical processes. We also discuss intrinsic sorbent properties, affecting their applicability in fixed-bed, moving-bed, and fluidized systems, and compare different sorbent families from the perspectives of regeneration characteristics, reactor operability, and technology readiness. Finally, the major challenges and future research directions are summarized, with emphasis on standardized evaluation, scale-up-oriented shaping, reactor-relevant testing, and deployment-informed sorbent selection. By bridging the gap between fundamental materials science and large-scale industrial applications, this study aims to establish a practical framework to guide the translation of laboratory research findings into scalable and directly applicable adsorbent technologies.

title: Computer vision-based detection of wind turbine surface defects: Methods, performance evaluation, and offshore applicability
summary: Offshore wind turbine blades and towers are persistently exposed to strong winds, rain erosion, salt spray, high humidity, and intense ultraviolet radiation. These conditions promote leading-edge erosion, cracking, coating failure, and corr
content: Offshore wind turbine blades and towers are persistently exposed to strong winds, rain erosion, salt spray, high humidity, and intense ultraviolet radiation. These conditions promote leading-edge erosion, cracking, coating failure, and corrosion, thereby compromising operational safety, service reliability, and maintenance economics. Conventional manual inspection and some nondestructive testing methods remain constrained by operational risk, limited efficiency and coverage, and insufficient automation. Computer vision offers a non-contact and information-rich route for automated defect recognition, localization, and region extraction. This review systematically synthesizes research on the visual inspection of wind turbine surface defects, encompassing representative defects and data resources, image processing, conventional machine learning, and deep learning-based methods, and further evaluates their applicability under complex offshore conditions. The evidence indicates that deep learning has substantially improved defect classification, localization, and region extraction. However, current studies remain concentrated on blades and self-compiled datasets, with comparatively limited attention to tower defects, authentic offshore samples, and cross-scenario validation. Motion blur, low contrast, intense glare, complex backgrounds, and onshore-to-offshore distribution shifts remain major sources of performance degradation. An analytical framework integrating defect characteristics, data foundations, vision methods, evaluation metrics, and offshore applicability is established. Priorities for future research include standardized offshore benchmarks, cross-domain and data-efficient learning, lightweight deployment, and structured outputs designed for maintenance-oriented verification.

title: A quantitative assessment of Chinese county high school policies using the PMC index model
summary: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China's counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial t
content: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China's counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial to evaluate current policy texts, identify their shortcomings, and provide empirical evidence for future policy development. This study collected 55 policy texts from provincial and municipal governments, utilizing the Policy Modeling Consistency index model to evaluate 14 representative policies. The results indicate that all the assessed policies fall within the"pass","good",or"with distinction" score category, with no substandard policies identified and none achieving a "perfect" score.A detailed analysis identifies critical policy shortcomings, including the prioritization of short-to-medium-term strategies over long-term planning, fragmented enrollment systems, insufficient campus culture development, as well as limited career guidance, mental health support,and policy guidance for home-school-community joint education. Local governments adopt a conservative stance on educational policy evaluation and systemic institutional reforms.To address these issues, this study recommends that local governments integrate the enrollment systems of public and private high schools within their jurisdictions, strengthen the prohibition of on cross-regional enrollment, increase investment in students' career guidance and mental health education, and launch more programs to encourage parents and communities to participate in school education. Moreover, the central government should urge local authorities to accelerate reforms in the high school education system.

title: Gut microbiota ablation depletes secondary bile acids and shifts the cytokine balance in BCG-infected mice
summary: Abstract Background. Antibiotic ablation is the standard test of whether a host phenotype depends on the gut microbiota, but it removes the community and perturbs the host at once, so depletion alone cannot assign a metabolite shift to the
content: Abstract Background. Antibiotic ablation is the standard test of whether a host phenotype depends on the gut microbiota, but it removes the community and perturbs the host at once, so depletion alone cannot assign a metabolite shift to the community. We built a four-arm mouse model on a single BCG infection background: untreated controls (NC), BCG alone, BCG after mixed-antibiotic ablation (ABX_BCG), and BCG followed by faecal microbiota transplantation with no antibiotic exposure at any point (BCG_FMT). The ablated and transplanted arms were independent branches, not a depletion-then-restoration sequence. Results. Dual-polarity untargeted LC-MS (9,706 negative-mode and 11,589 positive-mode features) and shotgun metagenomics showed that ablation left a block of 726 negative-mode and 313 positive-mode features absent from all three ABX_BCG samples but detected in 88–94% of the other nine; total ion signal in the ablated arm exceeded that of the quality-control injections, excluding dilution and matrix loss. Twenty-seven block features were annotated, resolving to 17 unique InChIKeys, 21 of them microbial compound classes including secondary bile acids. Deoxycholic acid eluted at 437.93 s in negative mode and 437.28 s in positive mode; deoxycholic and lithocholic acid were undetected in the ablated samples. Both omics layers resolved the same four groups (PERMANOVA R² = 0.562 for the genus table and 0.635 for the metabolome) yet failed to couple at sample level; exhaustive within-group re-pairing excluded sample mismatch, identifying a shared treatment rather than an individual axis. Ablation accompanied higher TNF-α and IL-6 and lower IFN-γ and IL-10 in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and serum alike. Conclusions. The gut community contributes a set of metabolite features whose absence is specific to the ablated state rather than shared with infection or transplantation, and the same arm occupies the extreme of the cytokine readout in both compartments. Running the ablated and transplanted arms as independent branches off the infected baseline is what makes this an antibiotic-specific control, and the two omics layers carry a shared treatment structure rather than a shared individual axis.

title: Feeding the future with clean energy: poultry farmers’ adoption of renewables
summary: Renewable energy is essential for mitigating climate change, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthening energy security and promoting sustainable development. As an energy-intensive sector, poultry farming must shift from fossil f
content: Renewable energy is essential for mitigating climate change, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and strengthening energy security and promoting sustainable development. As an energy-intensive sector, poultry farming must shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy to meet current and future energy demands. This study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional survey to examine factors influencing poultry farmers’ intentions to adopt renewable energy in Bushehr Province, Iran. This study integrates the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), with TAM explaining attitudes through perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use, and TPB explains intention through attitude, subjective norms, and Perceived behavioral control. Structural equation modeling using maximum likelihood estimation in AMOS showed that perceived usefulness, attitude, and perceived behavioral control significantly and positively influence farmers’ adoption intentions. Perceived ease of use also positively affects perceived usefulness, which in turn shapes attitudes toward renewable energy. These findings highlight the need to increase awareness of the benefits and efficiency of renewable technologies in poultry farming, provide financial support for high-cost technologies through national and international funding schemes, and encourage future research that incorporating value-based theoretical models.

title: From Access to Impact: Advancing Sustainable Climate Finance for Small and Vulnerable Commonwealth Countries
summary: This report tells the story of that progress of the Commonwealth Climate Finance Access Hub (CCFAH): of countries working to turn vulnerability into resilience; of public servants, technical experts, communities, women and young people help
content: This report tells the story of that progress of the Commonwealth Climate Finance Access Hub (CCFAH): of countries working to turn vulnerability into resilience; of public servants, technical experts, communities, women and young people helping to unlock opportunities for sustainable development; and of partnerships transforming ideas and commitments into investment and action.

title: Efficient Utilization of Lithium Slag: Grinding Properties of Lithium Slag and the Hydration Mechanism of Lithium Slag-Cement Cementitious Materials
summary: Abstract In order to enhance the hydration activity of lithium slag (LS) in cementitious materials. Three grinding aids (GAs), including ethylene glycol (EG), triethanolamine (TEA), and sodium tripolyphosphate (STPP), are added during mecha
content: Abstract In order to enhance the hydration activity of lithium slag (LS) in cementitious materials. Three grinding aids (GAs), including ethylene glycol (EG), triethanolamine (TEA), and sodium tripolyphosphate (STPP), are added during mechanical grinding to explore their effects on the grinding efficiency and hydration process of LS. The results are obtained as the various GAs have optimized the particle size distribution of lithium slag powder, but the changes in specific surface area (SSA) and the relative number of bridging oxygen bonds (RBO) are minor. When the TEA content is 7 g, the leaching rates of Si 4+ and Al 3+ from LS powder are the highest, increased by 67.17% and 11.92%, respectively. During the hydration process of the LS-Cement Cementitious Materials (LCCM), when the dosage of EG is 4 g, it increases the hydration rate of C 2 S during the slow reaction stage. Due to the alkaline environment and the distortion of the albite crystal structure, the production of hydration products is increased, the proportion of harmful pores in the hardened paste is reduced, and the strength in the later-age of hydration is improved.

title: Dynamic mechanism of digital technology empowering green innovation in manufacturing enterprises
summary: Although the dual digital and green transformation has become a strategic imperative for manufacturing firms, whether and how digital technology effectively drives green innovation remains contested. This debate largely stems from concerns
content: Although the dual digital and green transformation has become a strategic imperative for manufacturing firms, whether and how digital technology effectively drives green innovation remains contested. This debate largely stems from concerns regarding digital divides and the potential for diminishing returns caused by excessive investment. To address this theoretical gap, this study develops a differential game model to examine the dynamic mechanisms through which digital technology enables green innovation across three distinct stages of the product lifecycle: research and development focused on green knowledge accumulation, manufacturing focused on product greenness, and post-sale operations focused on green service. Analytical and numerical results demonstrate three primary findings. First, digital technology, knowledge accumulation, product greenness, and service quality all exert positive effects on overall green innovation performance, with the marginal effects being stronger in the initial period. Second, green knowledge accumulation plays a dominant role relative to product greenness and green service. Third, the relationship between digital input and green innovation benefits follows an inverted U-shaped trajectory, which is regulated by a critical threshold determined by the ratio of technology sensitivity to application costs. These findings offer theoretical explanations for the digital divide phenomenon in green innovation and provide practical guidance for manufacturing firms seeking to optimize their digital investments and avoid overinvestment traps during sustainability transitions.

title: Decarbonizing U.S. power systems under extreme heat: Solar–wind penetration and multi‐pollutant emission performance
summary: Abstract Extreme heat increases electricity‐system stress, but its influence on the relationship between renewable penetration and emissions intensity remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluated heat‐conditioned associations bet
content: Abstract Extreme heat increases electricity‐system stress, but its influence on the relationship between renewable penetration and emissions intensity remains insufficiently understood. This study evaluated heat‐conditioned associations between observed solar–wind penetration and consumption‐based CO 2 , NO x , and SO 2 intensities across seven U.S. balancing authorities during 2019–2024. Hourly EIA‐930 operations, Open Grid Emissions data, and NASA POWER meteorology were integrated into 15,211 complete balancing‐authority‐day observations. Region‐specific heat thresholds were established using 2019–2023 data and retained unchanged for a separate 2024 assessment. Two model‐derived indicators, Emission Displacement Effectiveness (EDE) and the Heat‐Stress Decarbonization Performance differential (HSDP), were used to quantify and compare renewable–emissions associations across operating regimes. Extreme‐heat days were associated with 12.99% higher electricity demand during 2019–2023 and 14.19% higher demand in 2024. A 10‐percentage‐point increase in renewable penetration was associated with 13.53% and 14.60% lower CO 2 intensity under normal and extreme‐heat conditions, respectively, during 2019–2023. Corresponding estimates for 2024 were 14.88% and 16.00%, yielding closely reproduced CO 2 HSDP values of −1.07 and −1.12 percentage points. SO 2 also exhibited negative heat differentials across both periods, whereas NO x responses were less temporally consistent. Regional and technology‐specific estimates revealed substantial heterogeneity. The findings indicate that extreme heat did not weaken the pooled inverse renewable–CO 2 intensity association within the examined systems. EDE and HSDP provide observational screening indicators for evaluating heat‐conditioned emissions performance, without implying causal displacement or improved physical conversion efficiency.

title: 3D Electron Diffraction Reveals Counterion Coordination in Co‐Existing Polymorphs of Ag 29 Nanocluster
summary: ABSTRACT We unravel the complete structural architecture of the polymorphic Na 3 [Ag 29 (BDT) 12 (TPP) 4 ] nanocluster (NC) using three‐dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of microscopic crystals. By drop‐casting nanocluster solution d
content: ABSTRACT We unravel the complete structural architecture of the polymorphic Na 3 [Ag 29 (BDT) 12 (TPP) 4 ] nanocluster (NC) using three‐dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of microscopic crystals. By drop‐casting nanocluster solution directly onto microscopy grids, we achieve in situ crystallization of nanometer‐sized polymorphs and independently resolve co‐existing cubic and trigonal phases crystal‐by‐crystal from a single grid square. Using difference electrostatic potential (DESP) maps derived from empirical 3D ED data, we pinpoint the specific lattice locations of the elusive Na + counterions and observe distinct coordination environments across the two polymorphs. In the densely packed, solvent‐free cubic phase, Na + binds exclusively to thermodynamically favored pockets formed by one core‐anchored and two staple sulfur atoms. Conversely, within the open, solvated trigonal lattice, Na + occupies both these core‐anchored sites and alternative positions coordinated entirely by three sulfur atoms of an outer Ag 3 S 3 staple motif. These findings establish 3D ED as a powerful tool for resolving nanoscale polymorphic mixtures and demonstrate how macroscopic crystal packing influences local ionic interactions, providing key structural insights for the design of cluster‐based assemblies.

title: Domesticating extracellular electron transfer processes to extract value from cheese whey: opportunities and challenges
source: Reviews in Environmental Science and Bio/Technology
summary: Cheese whey (CW), a major by-product of the dairy industry, is characterized by high organic load and large production volumes, creating significant environmental and management challenges. Conventional biological treatments such as anaerob
content: Cheese whey (CW), a major by-product of the dairy industry, is characterized by high organic load and large production volumes, creating significant environmental and management challenges. Conventional biological treatments such as anaerobic digestion (AD) and dark fermentation (DF) enable partial resource recovery, but their efficiency is often limited by process instability, intermediate accumulation, and weak metabolic cooperation within mixed microbial communities. In this context, extracellular electron transfer (EET) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance microbial interactions and process performance. This review explores current CW valorization strategies, focusing on the role of EET in regulating metabolic pathways, shaping microbial community dynamics, and improving system efficiency. DF, AD, and bioelectrochemical systems are discussed as the main valorization routes, with particular attention to electrically conductive materials (ECM) and electrochemical strategies that stimulate direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET), improve redox balance, and promote the production of hydrogen, methane, and other value-added compounds. EET-based strategies can also reshape microbial community dynamics by promoting electroactive and syntrophic interactions and enhancing lactate conversion and carbon/electron flux distribution. Overall, integrating EET with microbial community control could significantly advance sustainable CW valorization within a circular bioeconomy framework.

title: Grain‐Boundary Engineering for Electrocatalysis: From Precise Structural Analysis to Reaction‐Pathway Regulation
summary: ABSTRACT Amid efforts toward carbon neutrality and rapid renewable energy development, CO 2 /CO electroreduction and water electrolysis have emerged as critical pathways for carbon resource recycling and green hydrogen production. However,
content: ABSTRACT Amid efforts toward carbon neutrality and rapid renewable energy development, CO 2 /CO electroreduction and water electrolysis have emerged as critical pathways for carbon resource recycling and green hydrogen production. However, CO 2 and CO electroreduction reaction (CO 2 RR/CORR) remain limited by complex multielectron‐transfer pathways, insufficient product selectivity, and poor stability at high current densities. Meanwhile, the hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions (HER/OER) face challenges associated with noble‐metal dependence, sluggish kinetics, and structural instability. Grain boundaries are interfacial defects that can feature low‐coordinated atoms, local strain, and reconstructed electronic structures, thus offering a promising platform for designing catalysts with enhanced activity, selectivity, and stability. This Review examines the fundamental concepts, classifications, and structure‐activity relationships of grain boundaries. It further outlines synthesis strategies for grain‐boundary‐rich materials and discusses advanced characterization approaches ranging from morphological identification and GB quantification to in situ/operando tracking. The discussion subsequently focuses on the applications and catalytic mechanisms of grain boundaries in the CO 2 RR, CORR, HER, and OER. Representative mechanisms involve regulating intermediate adsorption, promoting C–C coupling, optimizing charge transfer, stabilizing active valence states, and improving the reaction microenvironment. By integrating synthesis, characterization, catalytic applications, and mechanistic insights, this Review provides a theoretical framework for the precise design, mechanistic understanding, and practical deployment of grain‐boundary‐based catalysts.

title: Comparative Scenario Analysis of Decarbonization Pathways Toward Carbon Neutrality for Guangdong’s Energy System Using the LEAP Model
summary: Guangdong is China’s largest provincial electricity consumer (912.1 TWh in 2024). Using a Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) model calibrated to the 2024 provincial yearbook, this paper compares a Business-as-Usual (BAU) reference with
content: Guangdong is China’s largest provincial electricity consumer (912.1 TWh in 2024). Using a Low Emissions Analysis Platform (LEAP) model calibrated to the 2024 provincial yearbook, this paper compares a Business-as-Usual (BAU) reference with three decarbonization pathways over 2024–2060: Policy-Instrument-Coupled (PIC), Deep-Electrification-and-Hydrogen (DEH) and Digital-economy-with-CCUS (DCN). From 862 Mt CO2 in 2024, BAU peaks at 1143 Mt in 2040, whereas the pathways fall to 139, 99 and 35 Mt of direct emissions in 2060. After BECCS removals, only DCN approaches neutrality (21 Mt net, comparable to a conservative provincial land-sink estimate). Forty-three control scenarios show that end-use efficiency and fuel switching deliver 85–91% of the 2060 reduction relative to BAU and the capacity mix 8–10%. In 10,000 correlated Monte Carlo draws over the tested ranges, the ranking DCN < DEH < PIC never changes. In an hourly check (three ERA5 weather years, stylized load), the pathways serve every hour with at most 17 GW of four-hour storage (20–32 GW with plan-level offshore wind and nuclear), whereas the BAU capacity path falls short from 2040. By 2060, 38–57% of the pathways’ must-run output is surplus, and electricity-supply cost per MWh rises in the reverse order of emission depth.

title: Herbicide formulations: evolution, environmental risks, and green innovation prospects
summary: Weeds are the most widespread biotic constraint to agricultural production, and herbicide-based control remains the most cost-effective approach in most cropping systems. A herbicide's efficacy, safety and environmental footprint depend as
content: Weeds are the most widespread biotic constraint to agricultural production, and herbicide-based control remains the most cost-effective approach in most cropping systems. A herbicide's efficacy, safety and environmental footprint depend as much on formulation as on active ingredient. This review synthesises the global evolution of herbicide formulations, compares regional markets and regulations (European Union, United States, Brazil, Africa, Southeast Asia, China), and analyses the limits of conventional formulations and prospects for greener innovation. Herbicide formulations have evolved through three phases: rudimentary systems (1940s-1960s), environmentally improved systems (1970s-1990s) and functional, smart systems (2000s-present). Conventional formulations achieve only 10-30% delivery efficiency, with > 70% of applied active ingredients lost to drift, runoff and degradation; 512 weed species are now resistant to at least one mode of action. The global herbicide formulation market reached US$38.2 billion in 2023; China is the largest producer (about 70% of global glyphosate capacity) and consumer (US$9.7 billion). No genuinely new herbicidal mode of action has reached the market. Formulation innovation is complementary to, not a substitute for, new-chemistry discovery: improved delivery increases the efficiency and safety of existing active ingredients, but durable weed control also requires new modes of action and integration with biological and agronomic tools. Nanotechnology-enabled targeted delivery, active ingredient-optimised design, bio-based carriers and precision application offer a realistic pathway to more efficient, safer and more sustainable herbicide formulations, and to overcoming China-specific bottlenecks in adjuvants and high-value formulation technology. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and po
content: Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and polarization. Physics-based flexible-charge models capture these effects but require global nonlinear charge equilibration at every time step to obtain Born-Oppenheimer energies and forces. This process is computationally expensive and can lead to instabilities unless tightly converged. Here, we introduce a shadow molecular dynamics framework for flexible-charge models with arbitrary local nonlinearities and long-range multipolar electrostatics. We replace the exact Born-Oppenheimer potential with a nearby shadow potential obtained by exactly equilibrating a partially linearized electronic energy functional. This provides conservative forces and reduces the global nonlinear equilibration to a quasi-diagonal linear problem that can be solved directly at low cost. Auxiliary dynamical electronic degrees of freedom, propagated through an extended-Lagrangian dynamics, capture the long-range electronic response and define the reference state for the linearization of the energy functional. GPU-accelerated simulations with over 100,000 atoms demonstrate that the shadow potential closely follows the tightly converged Born-Oppenheimer surface, while maintaining long-term stability at a computational cost approaching that of a fixed-charge model. These advances establish an efficient and broadly applicable framework for machine-learned interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate long-range electrostatic interactions and environment-dependent electronic response.

title: Multi-Objective Performance Assessment and Pareto Screening of Energy Use, Photovoltaic Generation and Life-Cycle Cost for New Rural Housing Across Five Chinese Cities
summary: Improving building energy efficiency is essential for carbon neutrality. China’s rural housing consumes a substantial share of energy, yet cross-regional comparisons of energy and economic performance under consistent conditions remain limi
content: Improving building energy efficiency is essential for carbon neutrality. China’s rural housing consumes a substantial share of energy, yet cross-regional comparisons of energy and economic performance under consistent conditions remain limited. This study evaluates new rural housing performance in Guangzhou, Hefei, Beijing, Harbin, and Aksu, which span four climatic zones. Six building parameters were combined using a mixed-level orthogonal design to generate design alternatives, which were simulated in BEopt to obtain energy use intensity (EUI), photovoltaic generation (PVG), and relative life-cycle cost (LCC). Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression quantified variable-performance associations, while Pareto screening identified non-dominated alternatives. Furring exterior-wall insulation R-value was negatively correlated with EUI in five cities (p < 0.001). PV array azimuth, which co-varies with building orientation, and PV tilt were associated with PVG, whereas the variables most associated with LCC and the size of the Pareto sets varied by city. Across 24 non-dominated solutions, mean EUI decreased by 31.1%, PVG increased by 8.6%, and LCC decreased by 9.5% relative to the baseline. The largest individual improvements were a 49.7% EUI reduction in Beijing, 28.6% PVG increase in competition-based Aksu, and 20.2% LCC reduction in Harbin. These results support regionally adaptive and multi-objective design of new rural housing.

title: Integrating solar photovoltaics in river basins: advancing water–energy–climate synergies for sustainable development goals
summary: ABSTRACT The graph describes the framework for USPV siting in river basins, including site suitability analysis, scenario design for USPV plant selection, and economic and ecological outcomes assessment. Utility-scale solar photovoltaic (US
content: ABSTRACT The graph describes the framework for USPV siting in river basins, including site suitability analysis, scenario design for USPV plant selection, and economic and ecological outcomes assessment. Utility-scale solar photovoltaic (USPV) deployment in river basins involves critical trade-offs among technological feasibility, economic performance, and ecological conservation. This study proposes an integrated decision-making framework for USPV siting in the upper Jinsha River by incorporating multiple criteria under different priorities. Results show that economic-priority scenarios allocate more than two-thirds of the suitable development areas east of the river, with median economic costs of 0.33–0.34 CNY/kWh and ecological costs of 0.013 CNY/kWh. Conservation-priority scenarios shift 60% of the suitable development areas westward, increasing economic costs to 0.36 CNY/kWh while reducing ecological costs to 0.006–0.007 CNY/kWh. Although total land conversion areas remain comparable across scenarios, differences in land conversion types result in carbon emissions of 1.04–1.13 Mt CO2 under economic priorities and 0.46–0.53 Mt CO2 under conservation priorities. These findings support spatially differentiated USPV planning that contributes to sustainable development goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land), while strengthening water–energy–climate synergies in river basins.

title: Climate and Carbon Cycle Impact Assessment of Land Policies, Prospects and Challenges
summary: This Reprint gathers peer-reviewed open-access research featured in the Land Special Issue titled Climate and Carbon Cycle Impact Assessment of Land Policies, Prospects and Challenges, focusing on the intertwined links between territorial l
content: This Reprint gathers peer-reviewed open-access research featured in the Land Special Issue titled Climate and Carbon Cycle Impact Assessment of Land Policies, Prospects and Challenges, focusing on the intertwined links between territorial land governance, climate change dynamics, carbon balance, and low-carbon policy design across global and Chinese study contexts. Contributors employ diverse mainstream empirical and simulation methodologies, including difference-in-differences quasi-experimental designs, system dynamics modelling, cellular automata coupling frameworks, CASA vegetation productivity estimation, and Probit moderation regression to unpack core research themes. Featured work evaluates the carbon mitigation effects of major national land and regional coordination policies such as the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei integrated development strategy and China’s low-carbon city pilot initiative, alongside assessments of territorial space carbon sink conflicts, crop residue burning emissions, coastal zone carbon-economic trade-offs, and farmers’ climate adaptation decision-making mechanisms shaped by risk perception and attitudes. Collectively, these papers deliver actionable evidence for differentiated land-use planning, coordinated cross-regional carbon governance, targeted agricultural climate adaptation strategies, and integrated territorial development aligned with carbon peaking and neutrality goals, while identifying unresolved research gaps for future scenario modelling and micro–macro carbon linkage analysis.

title: Multi-Scenario Coordinated Planning of Distributed PV, Energy Storage, and EV Charging Infrastructure Considering Differentiated Supply-Area Requirements
summary: China’s carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality targets are accelerating the integration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems, energy storage, and electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, requiring distribution-network planning that
content: China’s carbon-peaking and carbon-neutrality targets are accelerating the integration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems, energy storage, and electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, requiring distribution-network planning that reflects local resource, demand, and reliability characteristics. This paper proposes a multi-scenario coordinated planning framework that maps the characteristics of six representative supply-area types into area-specific planning parameters, capacity limits, and reliability requirements. Each supply-area type is evaluated as a separate planning case with three probability-weighted PV weather scenarios, shared investment decisions, and fixed base-load and EV charging profiles across weather scenarios. The model jointly determines the deployment and sizing of PV systems, stationary and mobile energy storage, and EV charging infrastructure. It minimizes the equivalent daily life-cycle cost augmented by reliability and operational-performance terms, capturing area-specific economic-reliability trade-offs. A dynamic arithmetic optimization algorithm (DAOA) incorporating an iteration-dependent step-size mechanism is developed to solve the resulting model. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus system, additional representative distribution networks, and a real feeder topology yield differentiated resource configurations consistent with supply-area characteristics. On the IEEE 33-bus system, planned PV capacity ranges from 64.71 kW in the high-reliability area to 419.43 kW in the urban-village area, while stationary battery energy storage capacity ranges from 750 to 2000 kWh across the six area types. In repeated-run comparisons, DAOA achieves the lowest mean final fitness among five algorithms under identical test settings. These results illustrate how supply-area parameterization translates heterogeneous planning requirements into differentiated resource deployment decisions.

title: Impact of Policies on the Development of Geothermal Industry in China: An Empirical Analysis of Panel Data
summary: ABSTRACT Geothermal energy is a clean, low‐carbon, widely distributed, abundant, safe and high‐quality renewable energy. According to a survey of China's geothermal resources, China's annual recoverable geothermal energy resources are equiv
content: ABSTRACT Geothermal energy is a clean, low‐carbon, widely distributed, abundant, safe and high‐quality renewable energy. According to a survey of China's geothermal resources, China's annual recoverable geothermal energy resources are equivalent to 2.6 billion tons of standard coal and thus have great development and utilization potential. Using geothermal energy to realize clean heating is highly important for achieving the goals of peak carbon and carbon neutrality. Financial subsidies and tax incentives support the geothermal industry, increase additional income for geothermal enterprises, encourage enterprises to invest more in scientific and technological research and development of the geothermal industry and expand the scale of reproduction to promote the large‐scale sustainable development of the geothermal industry. However, existing policies have difficulty meeting the larger, more efficient and high‐quality development needs of geothermal energy. This paper selects geothermal industry enterprises listed on domestic stock exchanges from 2004 to 2021 as research samples, and it uses panel data to evaluate the implementation effect of geothermal fiscal and tax policies. This research reveals that direct government subsidies significantly enhance the technological capabilities of these enterprises by fostering patent output and driving technological innovation, positively affecting the sector's advancement. In contrast, both corporate income tax and value‐added tax (VAT) burdens are found to negatively correlate with technological levels and investment intentions, with the corporate income tax exhibiting a stronger inhibitory effect on enterprise growth than VAT. However, subsidy intensity and corporate income tax burdens also have complex impacts on financial metrics such as profit margins, asset‐to‐liability ratios, and asset turnover. Surprisingly, subsidies, while boosting long‐term investment, paradoxically lower profit margins and discourage broader organic asset growth. Conversely, corporate income tax, despite reducing net income, encourages stricter financial discipline and reinvestment in asset growth, potentially enhancing operational efficiency and financial health. Additionally, the interactions between different fiscal measures like subsidies, VAT, and corporate income tax show varied effects on financial outcomes, indicating that strategic financial management can mitigate fiscal burdens and enhance company performance. This study underscores the nuanced role of government fiscal policies in shaping the operational and strategic outcomes of geothermal enterprises.

title: ESG Engagement in Operations Management: A Systematic Literature Review and Research Agenda
summary: ABSTRACT Operations management (OM) research remains fragmented in explaining how firms translate environmental, social, and governance (ESG)‐related pressures and commitments into operational practices through stakeholder engagement. To ad
content: ABSTRACT Operations management (OM) research remains fragmented in explaining how firms translate environmental, social, and governance (ESG)‐related pressures and commitments into operational practices through stakeholder engagement. To address this gap, this study systematically reviews 136 peer‐reviewed articles published between 2004 and 2024 and develops an integrative process‐oriented framework organized around three main domains: contextual drivers, salient stakeholders, and operational enactment activities. The synthesis identifies three key challenges in the translation process—prioritization, participation, and execution—and develops corresponding research directions centered on adaptive benchmarking, connectivity and integration, and materiality grounding. The framework clarifies how firms interpret contextual pressures with stakeholders and embed ESG commitments in organizational decisions and activities. The study thereby advances a more coherent understanding of how OM can connect strategic ESG commitments with substantive operational practices.

title: Electron--phonon cooling noise in monolayer and bilayer graphene
summary: We study the electron--phonon heat-current fluctuations in monolayer and Bernal bilayer graphene coupled to longitudinal acoustic phonons. To do this, we construct a symmetric heat-current operator and evaluate the non-equilibrium current--
content: We study the electron--phonon heat-current fluctuations in monolayer and Bernal bilayer graphene coupled to longitudinal acoustic phonons. To do this, we construct a symmetric heat-current operator and evaluate the non-equilibrium current--current correlator at finite frequency for unequal electron and phonon temperatures. The heat-current vertices then involve the probe energy combined with twice the phonon energy, and the nonequilibrium spectral density must be calculated directly rather than inferred from a dynamic thermal fluctuation--dissipation relation. Further, we obtain full analytical expressions in the Bloch--Grüneisen (BG) and Equipartition (EP) regimes, derive their low-frequency limits, and compare them with a complete doped-intraband on-shell calculations for monolayer graphene. The numerical results connect the two temperature regimes and show how finite-frequency noise changes out of equilibrium. For representative parameters, the corrections become percent-level in the upper-gigahertz to sub-terahertz range. It is worth mentioning that in equilibrium, the results satisfy the zero-frequency thermal fluctuation--dissipation relation(FDT) and reproduce the well established cooling-power and thermal-conductance laws.

title: Quantifying CO2 Emissions from Energy Use and Mobility in a Multi-Campus University System
summary: Reducing carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions associated with higher education is a critical challenge for achieving sustainability goals. In this paper, the emissions of a multicampus university are analysed, with the goal of quantifying and ass
content: Reducing carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions associated with higher education is a critical challenge for achieving sustainability goals. In this paper, the emissions of a multicampus university are analysed, with the goal of quantifying and assessing the main emission sources and providing recommendations for improving carbon accounting and reporting practices in the context of Italian universities. Emissions are examined across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, with a specific focus on the most impactful sectors: energy consumption and transportation. The assessment provides a baseline for future emission mitigation efforts, allowing comparison with other higher education institutions in Europe. The findings indicate that indirect emissions from commuting represent the greatest contribution to the University’s overall impact. On the basis of these results, a series of strategies for emission reduction and enhanced reporting transparency are proposed. This case study contributes to the growing research on carbon management in universities by offering insights and practical guidance for sustainability reporting in the Italian higher education sector.

title: CoTCPP‐Modified Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 for Efficient Photocatalytic Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
summary: Photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia holds dual significance for nitrogen‐containing wastewater remediation and green ammonia synthesis. However, single‐component semiconductor photocatalysts are generally hampered by severe photogen
content: Photocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia holds dual significance for nitrogen‐containing wastewater remediation and green ammonia synthesis. However, single‐component semiconductor photocatalysts are generally hampered by severe photogenerated charge recombination, insufficient spectral response, and poor substrate activation. Herein, cobalt porphyrin (CoTCPP) was in situ anchored onto the surface of Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 nanorods via a solvothermal method to construct CoTCPP/Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 photocatalysts featuring strong interfacial coupling. X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis reveals a distinct interfacial electronic coupling between CoTCPP and Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 . This strong interfacial coupling synergistically enhances photocatalytic performance by facilitating rapid capture and efficient interfacial transfer of photogenerated electrons to effectively suppress charge carrier recombination, significantly broadening the near‐infrared (NIR) light response range, and strengthening the electrostatic adsorption of NO 3 − on the catalyst surface to accelerate the selective generation of NH 3 . The optimized 1.5CoTCPP/Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 achieved an NH 3 production rate of 1230.81 μmol·g −1 ·h −1 , approximately 5‐fold higher than that of pristine Bi 19 S 27 Br 3 . In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed the stepwise deoxygenation–hydrogenation reduction pathway of NO 3 − → *NO 3 → *NO 2 → *NO → *NHOH → *NH 2 OH → NH 3 . This work provides an effective strategy for constructing interfacially coupled photocatalytic systems toward efficient nitrate reduction to ammonia.

title: Unveiling the Failure Mechanisms of High‐Voltage 18650‐Type O3‐Layered Oxide//Hard Carbon Sodium‐Ion Full Cells
summary: ABSTRACT High‐voltage O3‐type layered oxide//hard carbon full cells offer a promising route toward high‐energy‐density sodium‐ion batteries, yet their high‐voltage degradation mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Here, Ah‐level 1865
content: ABSTRACT High‐voltage O3‐type layered oxide//hard carbon full cells offer a promising route toward high‐energy‐density sodium‐ion batteries, yet their high‐voltage degradation mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Here, Ah‐level 18650 cylindrical full cells were cycled under different cut‐off voltages to elucidate the underlying failure mechanisms through non‐destructive and post‐mortem analyses. Increasing the cut‐off voltage from 4.05 to 4.20 V raises the energy density from 117.5 to 144.0 Wh kg −1 , but accelerates degradation, with direct‐current internal resistance growth increasing from 181% to 387% and capacity retention after 300 cycles decreasing from 96.4% to 68.3%. Impedance analysis reveals that charge‐transfer resistance gradually becomes dominant during high‐voltage cycling. Post‐mortem analysis reveals cathode interphase thickening and heterogeneous inorganic‐rich interphase growth, accompanied by an organic‐rich anode interphase, and increased accumulation of sodium‐containing deposits. Aging‐model decoupling demonstrates that capacity fading is primarily governed by active‐material loss and electrode capacity mismatch rather than sodium inventory loss. Notably, eliminating the constant‐voltage step in the 4.15‐CC protocol shortens the high‐voltage dwell time, reduces the resistance growth from 369% to 153%, and improves capacity retention from 85.0% to 93.9%. These findings provide full‐cell insight into high‐voltage degradation and highlight charging‐protocol optimization as an effective strategy to balance high energy density and long cycle life.

title: Versatile Acetyl‐Functionalized Phenothiazine Self‐Assembled Monolayers for Efficient Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells
summary: ABSTRACT The development of versatile, stable, and cost‐effective hole‐transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next‐generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine‐based self‐assembled monolayers
content: ABSTRACT The development of versatile, stable, and cost‐effective hole‐transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next‐generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for perovskite and organic solar cells. By systematically tuning the substituents, including unsubstituted phenothiazine (PTZ), dibromo‐PTZ (PTZ‐diBr), and diacetyl‐PTZ (PTZ‐diACE), we achieve control over interfacial energetics and surface properties. The dual coordination sites of carbonyl groups and sulfur in PTZ‐diACE provide Lewis basic sites that coordinate undercoordinated Pb 2 + ions, facilitating passivation at the buried HTL/perovskite interface. Additionally, polar acetyl groups induce interfacial dipoles that reinforce the built‐in electric field, promoting efficient hole extraction. Among the series, PTZ‐diACE exhibits superior film formation, a deeper HOMO level, and stronger interfacial interactions, resulting in enhanced charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells employing PTZ‐diACE achieve a power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.5% with excellent operational stability, retaining 93% of its initial efficiency after 500 h under the ISOS‐D‐2I protocol. These advantages extend to organic solar cells, where PTZ‐diACE delivers a PCE of 20.4% in D18:L8BO devices and demonstrates compatibility across multiple active layers. This study demonstrates phenothiazine‐based SAMs as HTLs and provides design guidelines for efficient, stable interfacial materials.

title: Synergistic CNT‐Integrated Ni‐Phthalocyanine/g‐C 3 N 4 Heterojunctional Photocatalysts With Single Ni–N 4 (II) Sites for Efficient Ammonia Synthesis
summary: ABSTRACT The photochemical reduction of nitrogen offers an environmentally friendly approach for ammonia synthesis, providing an alternative to the energy‐intensive and emission‐heavy Haber–Bosch process. Despite its promise, the process is
content: ABSTRACT The photochemical reduction of nitrogen offers an environmentally friendly approach for ammonia synthesis, providing an alternative to the energy‐intensive and emission‐heavy Haber–Bosch process. Despite its promise, the process is impeded by slow nitrogen activation and excessive hydrogen evolution. To overcome these limitations, we present a tandem nickel phthalocyanine (NiPc)/CNT‐P&Cu‐BCN photocatalyst, engineered with an organic–organic heterojunction for enhanced nitrogen conversion. This system integrates boron‐doped (B), nitrogen‐deficient (N) carbon nitride (CN), modified via Cu–Cu coordination and phosphorus doping through sodium borohydride‐assisted thermal treatment, with hydrogen‐bonded, ultrathin NiPc nanosheets. This novel design yields a record ammonia production rate of 915.4 μmol g −1 h −1 under visible light, a remarkable 16‐fold increase compared to traditional BCN materials. The improvement is attributed to precise bandgap engineering; boron doping and nitrogen vacancies adjust the electronic structure, while the synergistic effects of Cu, P, and CNT enhance charge transfer dynamics. The ultrathin NiPc framework introduces atomically dispersed active sites, whereas a Z‐scheme‐driven charge separation mechanism facilitates efficient electron movement. This work, by integrating defect engineering, heterojunction design, and single‐atom catalysis, contributes to the advancement of photocatalytic nitrogen fixation, offering a scalable pathway for sustainable ammonia production. The results underscore the importance of multi‐component synergy in overcoming kinetic barriers, opening new avenues for energy‐efficient alternatives to conventional synthesis methods.

title: Axion Emission Controlled by Ion Motion in Relativistic Beam-Plasma Filamentation
summary: The interaction between relativistic electron beams and plasma can generate magnetic fields with strengths of $\sim 10^4$ T far exceeding conventional magnets, which offers a promising environment for producing weakly coupled particles. Usi
content: The interaction between relativistic electron beams and plasma can generate magnetic fields with strengths of $\sim 10^4$ T far exceeding conventional magnets, which offers a promising environment for producing weakly coupled particles. Using particle-in-cell simulations incorporating an axion-emission model, we show that a 10-GeV electron beam traversing dense plasma emits a forward-collimated axion beam during the ion-mediated nonlinear stage of current filamentation instability. Although the electron-driven linear instability seeds the filaments, ion motion governs their subsequent expansion and coalescence. This evolution reinjects cold-core electrons into large-amplitude orbits in phase space, where they repeatedly cross the strong-field flanks of neighboring magnetic vortices, thereby enhancing axion emission. At a background-plasma density of $\sim 10^{21}\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$, suppressing ion motion reduces the axion yield by a factor of 14.5. Our results demonstrate that ion dynamics play a crucial role in characterizing the emission of weakly coupled particles induced by relativistic filamentation instabilities, suggesting a new beam-driven method for probing the axion-electron interaction at accelerators.

title: Refugee Settlement-Environmental Degradation Nexus in Kassala, El Gedaref, and White Nile States, Sudan
source: CGSPace A Repository of Agricultural Research Outputs (Consultative Group for International Agricultural Research)
summary: Sudan hosts some of Africa's largest and longest-standing refugee populations in fragile drylands already strained by unreliable rainfall, land degradation, and conflict. This study examines whether refugee settlements are linked to environ
content: Sudan hosts some of Africa's largest and longest-standing refugee populations in fragile drylands already strained by unreliable rainfall, land degradation, and conflict. This study examines whether refugee settlements are linked to environmental decline across 19 camps in Kassala, El Gedaref, and White Nile states, to help guide camp siting and sustainable hosting. Using satellite imagery, we tracked changes in land use, vegetation, soil, and land conditions between 1978 and 2025. Camps were grouped by age — long-established (pre-1990, Kassala), established (2011–2019, White Nile State), and recently established (2020 onward, El Gedaref) — and changes were measured across four distance bands around each camp (0–10, 10–20, 20–30, and 30–50 km). The results show a strong, consistent link between settlements and environmental change over space and time. Because the study included no comparison landscape without camps, this is an association, not proof that camps alone caused the damage. Farmland and built-up areas expanded steadily, replacing shrublands, grasslands, forests, and wetlands. Older camps showed the greatest total change; newer camps changed the fastest each year. Degradation spread outward from inner zones to the edges, with less healthy land remaining throughout. Refugee settlements are best seen as part of wider landscapes whose pressures reach far beyond camp boundaries, weakening nature's benefits and raising the risk of drought, flood, and resource conflict. Older camps need restoration; newer ones need prevention. Humanitarian agencies, governments, donors, communities, and researchers should build environmental checks from the start, promote clean energy and nature-based restoration, manage land use by zone, and sustain shared monitoring with early warning.

title: The impact of equity structure on technological innovation efficiency in China’s listed textile firms
summary: Technological innovation efficiency is a pivotal metric for assessing a firm’s innovation capability, and equity structure is a key determinant shaping it. This study investigates this relationship within China’s listed textile sector (Shan
content: Technological innovation efficiency is a pivotal metric for assessing a firm’s innovation capability, and equity structure is a key determinant shaping it. This study investigates this relationship within China’s listed textile sector (Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share markets, 2013–2024). To isolate the true managerial performance, we employ an integrated three- stage Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) model that purges the effects of external environmental factors and statistical noise. Subsequently, a Tobit regression is used to test the impacts of distinct equity governance mechanisms. The main findings are: (1) External environmental factors significantly inflate initial efficiency measurements; after purification, the overall decline is primarily driven by reduced pure technical efficiency, highlighting managerial practices as the critical bottleneck. (2) The adjustment reveals divergent paths: state-shareholding firms show improved efficiency mainly through scale efficiency, whereas non-state-shareholding firms exhibit a decline due to deficiencies in pure technical efficiency. (3) Regarding equity structure, ownership concentration, equity checks and balances, and institutional ownership all significantly promote technological innovation efficiency. In contrast, the mere presence of state shareholding exerts no statistically significant direct effect. These findings underscore that internal governance mechanisms, rather than ownership labels, are decisive for driving innovation efficiency in traditional manufacturing industries transforming.

title: Transition Communication and Household Energy Shift: A Lived Experience from a Developing Community
summary: This study explores how transition communication facilitates household transition to modern energy solutions in Pader District, Northern Uganda. Drawing on the Diffusion of Innovation Theory and Agenda-Setting Theory, the study adopted a qu
content: This study explores how transition communication facilitates household transition to modern energy solutions in Pader District, Northern Uganda. Drawing on the Diffusion of Innovation Theory and Agenda-Setting Theory, the study adopted a qualitative narrative inquiry approach based on the lived experiences of households transitioning from traditional biomass fuels to modern low-carbon energy alternatives. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews with households, local opinion leaders, and communication agents from the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development and analysed using a narrative approach. Findings reveal that households initially resisted electricity adoption because of concerns about safety, cost, and compatibility with local practices. However, participatory and culturally sensitive communication through trusted local leaders, community dialogues, dramas, skits, and hands-on demonstrations reduced fear, strengthened trust, and improved understanding of electricity use.These processes enhanced household readiness and facilitated adoption of electricity and other low-carbon energy solutions. The findings show that transition communication facilitates adoption by combining adequate information, credible communicators, locally relevant interactions, and experiential learning. The study extends Diffusion of Innovation Theory by demonstrating how trust-building and experiential learning facilitate movement from knowledge to adoption, while Agenda-Setting Theoryexplains how trusted community actors shape the salience of energy transition messages. Although based on a single developing community, the study provides theoretical, policy, and practical insights for designing communication strategies that support household energy transitions in low-resource settings.Keywords: Household energy transition, transition communication, lived experiences, developing communities, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, Agenda-Setting Theory

title: The financial costs of corporate social irresponsibility in the US consumer staples sector
summary: This study investigates the financial market implications of negative ESG-related reputational events within the beverage industry, analysing abnormal stock returns surrounding 11,632 distinct incidents between 2007 and 2023. Significant ne
content: This study investigates the financial market implications of negative ESG-related reputational events within the beverage industry, analysing abnormal stock returns surrounding 11,632 distinct incidents between 2007 and 2023. Significant negative abnormal returns are identified, emerging up to ten days prior to public disclosure through media dissemination, suggesting strong information leakage. Investor response upon media announcement is immediate, negative, and asymmetric, often followed by rapid mean reversion, indicative of potential ESG fatigue and heterogeneity of response as a result of event perception by investors. Further, this effect is found to be moderated by both event-related factors and corporate characteristics. Interestingly, repeat ESG offenders are found to experience significantly more negative returns than first-time offenders, suggesting the presence of market learning, declining market intolerance with poor corporate behaviour and escalating accountability expectations. Such results clearly demonstrate the tangible financial consequences of corporate social irresponsibility, providing particular evidence of a particularly nuanced market response, signalling both investor desensitisation to ESG events and particular learnings from corporate ESG history.

title: Role of trace cerium on dynamic continuous cooling transformation, microstructural evolution, and mechanical properties of high-strength wheel steel
source: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
summary: To address toughness and fatigue-life limitations of high-strength wheel steel, the effects of Ce additions (0.0030, 0.0160, and 0.0340 wt.%) on dynamic continuous cooling transformation (DCCT), hot-rolled microstructure, and mechanical pro
content: To address toughness and fatigue-life limitations of high-strength wheel steel, the effects of Ce additions (0.0030, 0.0160, and 0.0340 wt.%) on dynamic continuous cooling transformation (DCCT), hot-rolled microstructure, and mechanical properties were examined. The transformation response depended on the solid-solution Ce content. The 0.0030 wt.% Ce steel, with insufficient solid-solution Ce, showed only a slight DCCT shift. At 0.0160 and 0.0340 wt.% Ce, solid-solution Ce reached ~0.0050 and ~0.0072 wt.%, respectively; the DCCT curves shifted progressively lower-right, reflecting delayed ferrite/pearlite transformation, prolonged bainite incubation, and expansion of the bainite transformation region toward lower cooling rates. Under identical rolling-coiling conditions, all steels exhibited a ferrite-pearlite-granular bainite microstructure; increasing solid-solution Ce increased the granular bainite fraction and reduced the pearlite fraction. Compared with the Ce-free steel, the 0.0160 wt.% Ce steel reduced the effective grain size from 7.61 to 4.96 μm and increased the high-angle grain boundary fraction from 53.22% to 69.84%. TEM revealed refined bainitic-ferrite (BF) laths, fewer coarse blocky martensite/austenite (M/A) islands, a higher fraction and number density of fine M/A islands, and film-like retained austenite at M/A-BF interfaces. Ce addition maintained a favorable strength-ductility balance and increased room-temperature impact energy from 85.8 to 108.6 J. Fatigue life was non-monotonic: the 0.0160 wt.% Ce steel showed the greatest improvement, whereas the 0.0340 wt.% Ce steel improved but did not surpass it. Overall, Ce altered the continuous cooling transformation path through solid-solution Ce and promoted microstructural refinement; its addition should therefore be appropriately controlled.

title: Highly twinned cobalt selenide with abundant selenium vacancies for efficient nitrogen reduction reaction
summary: Electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) offers a promising approach to produce ammonia (NH3) under ambient conditions. However, the ammonia yield rate and Faradaic efficiency were still limited by the chemical inertness of nitrog
content: Electrocatalytic nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) offers a promising approach to produce ammonia (NH3) under ambient conditions. However, the ammonia yield rate and Faradaic efficiency were still limited by the chemical inertness of nitrogen. Here, we report the introduction of Se vacancies in CoSe nanorods via an ions-exchange method. Se vacancies can improve the NRR activities by the lending of N2 activation. As a result, the ammonia yield rate reached as high as 106.7 μg h–1 mg–1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 21.2% at -0.3 V (vs. RHE). More importantly, the ammonia is directly derived from nitrogen, which was demonstrated by the isotopic experiments using 15N2 as a nitrogen source. This work not only provides a strategy for creating Se vacancies, but also offers an important pathway for the development of efficient catalysts for NRR. Ammonia (NH3) golds significant importance as carbon-free energy carrier, and industrial feedstock.[1-3] Currently, industrial-scale NH₃ is produced via the highly energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process, which operates under elevated temperatures (400–600°C) and high pressures (200-400 atm). However, this process emits substantial quantities of greenhouse gases, giving rise to significant environmental concerns. To achieve carbon neutrality, the Haber-Bosch method must be transformed into a low-carbon process. Powered by renewable energy sources, such as solar cells, the electrochemical nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) under ambient conditions offers a promising route toward sustainable NH₃ production.[4-9] Despite the numerous NRR catalysts reported to date, the Faradaic efficiency and ammonia yield of NRR remain relatively low due to the inherent chemical inertness of N₂ molecule.[8-12] Vacancy engineering is widely acknowledged in the literature as an effective strategy for enhancing the catalytic activity of electrocatalysts.[13-17] For instance, Qiu et al. demonstrated that introducing oxygen vacancies into OER and ORR catalyst significantly improves its catalytic performance,[18] while Qiao et al. enhanced the catalyst's capability to activate and adsorb nitrogen molecules by incorporating nitrogen vacancies into nitrides.[19] Nevertheless, research on vacancy engineering specifically for NRR remains limited. Investigating the impact of vacancies of different elements on NRR performance could provide crucial insights for the design of highly efficient catalysts. In this work, we report a highly twinned CoSe nanorod with a large density of Se vacancies (denoted as V-CoSe) via an two-steps ion-exchange method, which exhibits significantly superior Faradaic efficiency and NH3 production rate. The theoretical calculations suggest that the Se vacancies are essential for NRR of V-CoSe, which greatly promote the adsorption and activation of N2.
