title: TI VERDE E TRANSIÇÃO PARA O CARBONO NEUTRO NO SETOR PÚBLICO: EVIDÊNCIAS DE UMA PESQUISA-AÇÃO NO TCE-PE
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: IntroduçãoO avanço acelerado das tecnologias digitais, serviços computacionais e processamento de dados, tem ampliado significativamente o consumo energético das organizações e, consequentemente, sua pegada de carbono (Ferraz, 2024).A parti
content: IntroduçãoO avanço acelerado das tecnologias digitais, serviços computacionais e processamento de dados, tem ampliado significativamente o consumo energético das organizações e, consequentemente, sua pegada de carbono (Ferraz, 2024).A partir dessa realidade, consolidouse o conceito de Tecnologia da Informação Verde (TI Verde) como um conjunto de estratégias e práticas que visam à redução do impacto ambiental da área de TI, promovendo eficiência energética, uso responsável de recursos tecnológicos e mitigação das emissões de gases de efeito estufa (Salles; Lunardi; Thompson, 2022).No setor público, sua aplicação ganha relevância por contribuir não apenas para a eficiência administrativa, mas para o cumprimento dos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável estabelecidos pela Agenda 2030 das Nações Unidas (ONU, 2015), sobretudo no tocante aos ODS 12 e ODS 13.O Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Pernambuco (TCE-PE), alinhado à sua missão institucional de promover a transparência e o controle social, incorporou práticas de TI Verde ao Plano de Logística Sustentável (TCE-PE, 2023).No eixo Tecnologia da Informação, destacam-se iniciativas como a revisão de políticas de uso de equipamentos de informática, aquisição de hardware e software de empresas comprometidas com práticas sustentáveis, otimização de gastos com licenças, implantação de campanhas de conscientização para uso eficiente de recursos digitais e doações e o descarte correto de embalagens e lixo eletrônico (TCE-PE, 2023; Morais et al., 2024; Morais et al., 2025).Essas ações dialogam diretamente com outras medidas internas no eixo TI reforçando a trajetória institucional rumo ao carbono neutro.O termo carbono neutro refere-se ao estado em que as emissões de dióxido de carbono (CO₂) de uma organização, comunidade ou país são equilibradas por ações que promovem a remoção ou compensação dessas mesmas emissões.Apesar dos avanços observados, a literatura ainda carece de estudos empíricos que analisem, de forma integrada, os mecanismos operacionais, os resultados e os impactos das ações de TI Verde no setor público, especialmente em instituições de controle como os Tribunais de Contas.Assim, o presente artigo busca responder a seguinte pergunta de pesquisa: como as ações de TI Verde implementadas no Tribunal de Contas do Estado de Pernambuco contribuem para a redução das emissões de CO₂ e para a transição rumo a uma instituição carbono neutro no uso de tecnologias?Desta maneira, este artigo tem por objetivo analisar o processo de implementação das ações de TI Verde no TCE-PE, relacionados ao uso de tecnologias digitais, incluindo serviços computacionais em nuvem como aplicativos do Google Workspace e aplicações de inteligência artificial, com ênfase na campanha de compensação de carbono por

title: RESILIÊNCIA E DESCARBONIZAÇÃO EM CADEIAS DE SUPRIMENTOS DE PEQUENAS E MÉDIAS EMPRESAS INDUSTRIAIS: UM ENSAIO TEÓRICO SOBRE DADOS, CAPACIDADES DINÂMICAS E SUSTENTABILIDADE
source: Anais ... Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção/Anais do Encontro Nacional de Engenharia de Produção
summary: A crescente pressão por sustentabilidade, rastreabilidade, redução de emissões e resiliência tem reconfigurado as cadeias de suprimentos industriais, especialmente diante de riscos climáticos, instabilidades logísticas, exigências ESG e met
content: A crescente pressão por sustentabilidade, rastreabilidade, redução de emissões e resiliência tem reconfigurado as cadeias de suprimentos industriais, especialmente diante de riscos climáticos, instabilidades logísticas, exigências ESG e metas de neutralidade de carbono.Nesse contexto, pequenas e médias empresas industriais ocupam posição estratégica e, ao mesmo tempo, vulnerável: são elos relevantes das cadeias produtivas, mas frequentemente apresentam restrições de recursos, baixa maturidade digital, limitada capacidade de mensuração de emissões e dependência de grandes compradores.Este ensaio teórico tem como objetivo desenvolver uma estrutura conceitual para compreender como PMEs industriais podem construir capacidades organizacionais, informacionais e operacionais para atuar em cadeias de suprimentos resilientes e de baixo carbono.Argumenta-se que a descarbonização da cadeia não depende apenas da adoção isolada de tecnologias, certificações ou práticas ambientais, mas da articulação entre governança de dados, rastreabilidade, gestão de riscos, capacidades dinâmicas e reconfiguração progressiva de fornecedores, processos e fluxos logísticos.A estrutura proposta organiza-se em cinco dimensões interdependentes: rastreabilidade da cadeia; governança de dados de carbono; gestão de riscos climáticos e logísticos; capacidades dinâmicas em PMEs; e descarbonização incremental.Como contribuição teórica, o artigo reposiciona as PMEs industriais como agentes ativos da transição para cadeias de suprimentos sustentáveis, e não apenas como elos passivos submetidos a exigências externas.Como contribuição gerencial, propõe uma trajetória gradual para apoiar empresas com baixa disponibilidade de recursos na construção de práticas de resiliência e baixo carbono Palavras-chave: Cadeias de suprimentos; Resiliência; Descarbonização; Pequenas e médias empresas; Capacidades dinâmicas.1 Introdução As cadeias de suprimentos industriais têm sido pressionadas por instabilidades logísticas, riscos climáticos, exigências de rastreabilidade, metas de redução de emissões e demandas crescentes de transparência ambiental.Esse cenário desloca a gestão da produção de uma lógica centrada predominantemente em eficiência de custos para uma lógica ampliada de continuidade operacional, adaptação, governança de dados e sustentabilidade.Cadeias globalizadas, enxutas e altamente interdependentes ampliam ganhos de escala e especialização, mas também se tornam mais expostas a rupturas, atrasos, oscilações de demanda, choques de fornecimento e pressões regulatórias (Jüttner; Peck; Christopher, 2003; Kleindorfer; Saad, 2005; Tang, 2006).A literatura de resiliência em cadeias de suprimentos consolidou-se como resposta a essa vulnerabilidade, enfatizando a capacidade de preparar-se para eventos adversos, absorver impactos, responder a interrupções, recuperar desempenho e reconfigurar operações (Ponomarov;Holcomb, 2009; title: Nanophotonics for sustainable photocatalysis: Potential and challenges
summary: The transition toward sustainable energy systems requires advanced catalytic technologies capable of efficiently converting solar energy into chemical fuels. In this Perspective, we critically examine the emerging role of nanophotonics in o
content: The transition toward sustainable energy systems requires advanced catalytic technologies capable of efficiently converting solar energy into chemical fuels. In this Perspective, we critically examine the emerging role of nanophotonics in overcoming the intrinsic limitations of conventional photocatalysis, particularly the trade-off between light absorption and redox efficiency that constrains solar-to-chemical conversion. We discuss four major photonic strategies: hot carrier generation, polaritonic chemistry, enhanced photonic structures (photonic crystals), and metasurfaces/metamaterials, highlighting their potential to manipulate light–matter interactions at the nanoscale and thereby influence reaction pathways, selectivity, and efficiency. While these approaches offer compelling opportunities, including non-thermal reaction control, modification of potential energy surfaces, and improved light harvesting, their practical implementation remains hindered by fundamental and technological challenges. These include short hot-carrier lifetimes, limited reproducibility and scalability of polaritonic systems, defect sensitivity in photonic structures, and fabrication complexity and stability issues in metasurfaces. We emphasize that improvements in photocatalytic performance must be evaluated within the broader framework of overall reaction efficiency, encompassing both quantum yield and light transport. Bridging the gap between proof-of-concept studies and scalable applications will require closer integration between photonics and catalysis, along with a realistic assessment of energy costs and system-level design. Ultimately, nanophotonics provides powerful tools, but its translation into sustainable photocatalytic technologies demands a balanced and application-driven approach.

title: Nano–bio interfacial coupling regulates microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation: Mechanistic insights and multi-objective optimization
summary: Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) is governed by the coupling between bacterial physiological activity and mineral nucleation; however, regulating such bio-mineral coupling remains challenging. Nanomaterials (NMs) o
content: Microbially induced calcium carbonate precipitation (MICP) is governed by the coupling between bacterial physiological activity and mineral nucleation; however, regulating such bio-mineral coupling remains challenging. Nanomaterials (NMs) offer reactive nano–bio interfaces that can link bacterial immobilization with heterogeneous CaCO₃ nucleation, yet their contribution to biomineralization efficiency remains mechanistically unclear. In this study, we report a nano-enabled strategy in which SnO₂ NMs serve as platforms for bacterial immobilization and heterogeneous mineral nucleation. Microscopic and elemental analyses reveal that SnO₂ NMs are preferentially immobilized on bacterial spore surfaces, forming a stable nano–bio interface without compromising cellular integrity. Biological assays demonstrate a concentration-dependent dual effect, where an optimal dosage of 150 mg/L increases spore germination from 0.68 to 0.78 and calcium precipitation activity (CPA) from 29.94% to 34.79%. At higher concentrations (≥200 mg/L), CPA decreases to 30.74% despite a substantial increase in metabolic activity (ETSA up to 42.84), indicating a decoupled and non-linear relationship between metabolic intensity and biomineralization performance. Multivariate analysis and response surface modeling showed that CPA was strongly correlated with spore germination (r = 0.91), whereas its relationship with metabolic activity was negligible (r = −0.03). Multi-objective optimization identified 150 mg/L as the concentration that produced the highest biomineralization performance. Microstructural characterization showed densely packed CaCO₃ crystals with uniform elemental distribution, consistent with enhanced crystal nucleation and growth. Overall, this study clarifies how nano–bio interfacial interactions influence bacterial activity and CaCO₃ precipitation, providing a framework for optimizing nano-assisted MICP systems.

title: The Food Sustainability Composite Index (FSCI): Development and Validation of a Multidimensional Indicator Framework for BRICS Nations with 2030 Projections
summary: Since the early 1990s, rapid dietary shifts across BRICS economies have driven distinct consequences for land systems and atmospheric stability at regional and global scales. No composite metric integrating emissions, land-use, and dietary
content: Since the early 1990s, rapid dietary shifts across BRICS economies have driven distinct consequences for land systems and atmospheric stability at regional and global scales. No composite metric integrating emissions, land-use, and dietary composition has been applied to BRICS or linked to long-horizon forecasting aligned with the UN 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda. The Food Sustainability Composite Index (FSCI) operationalises environmental sustainability through an integrated, equally weighted, three-dimensional framework, combining Air Impact Dimension (AID), Land Impact Dimension (LID), and Dietary Composition Index (DCI). The index was evaluated using Pearson correlations, inter-dimensional correlation and variance inflation factor diagnostics, alternative weighting and normalisation sensitivity analyses, and an external behavioural association analysis relating animal-based food consumption to FSCI. Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) was applied to BRICS data from 1992-2013 to project indicator trends and FSCI trajectories through 2030. The projected trajectories indicate substantial divergence in FSCI across the BRICS economies, including a projected decline in China's composite score and comparatively limited change in India's score. The PMG-ARDL analysis provides evidence of an inverted-U-shaped common long-run association between GDP per capita and CO 2 emissions, with an estimated common turning point of approximately US$6,215.82 per capita in constant 2015 US dollars (95% CI : US$4,329.54–8,924.08). The FSCI offers a replicable, multidimensional monitoring tool; the SSA analysis provides a historically evaluated forecasting benchmark. Together, they highlight the potential relevance of integrating consumption-side dietary metrics into supranational sustainability-monitoring frameworks aligned with SDG 2 and SDG 13.

title: Development of H-D Exchange and C-C Bond-Forming Reactions via C-H Activation over Heterogeneous Platinum-Group Catalysts
source: Journal of Synthetic Organic Chemistry Japan
summary: The employment of hydrogen-activated, heterogeneous platinum-group catalysts has facilitated the development of C-H activation chemistry under conditions that are both remarkably mild and operationally simple. Since the discovery in 2000 th
content: The employment of hydrogen-activated, heterogeneous platinum-group catalysts has facilitated the development of C-H activation chemistry under conditions that are both remarkably mild and operationally simple. Since the discovery in 2000 that molecular hydrogen functions as a catalyst activator rather than merely a reducing reagent, a series of H-D exchange reactions has been established that allow for the direct replacement of C-H bonds with C-D bonds, with D2O serving as the deuterium source. Through precise tailoring of the metal species, site-selective deuteration of benzylic, aromatic, aliphatic, and α-C-H bonds in alcohols has been achieved under ambient or relatively mild conditions, with broad functional-group compatibility. The resulting H-D exchange reactions further led to the development of efficient H2-D2 exchange between H2 and D2O, practical laboratory-scale production of high-purity D2 gas, catalyst systems utilizing in situ-generated hydrogen, continuous-flow deuteration platforms, and mechanochemical deuterium labeling. The resulting methodologies have found applications ranging from pharmaceuticals to functional materials and have been commercialized for contract synthesis. In recent developments, the integration of heterogeneous platinum-group catalysis with microwave-assisted continuous-flow technology has extended the C-H activation chemistry established through H-D exchange to intramolecular C-C bond formation. This has enabled intramolecular C-C bond formation via C-H activation while concurrently enabling efficient hydrogen production from liquid organic hydrogen carriers. This Account provides a synopsis of approximately 25 years of research on hydrogen-activated heterogeneous platinum-group catalysis, with a focus on the mechanistic concepts, catalyst design, technological developments, and the evolution from H-D exchange chemistry to emerging C-C bond formation reactions.

title: Financialization of ESG and Institutional Investor Preferences: How Sustainability Pricing Drives Firm Valuation in Systematic Literature Review
source: International Journal of Education Vocational and Social Science
summary: This study examines ESG financialization, institutional investor preferences, and sustainability pricing in firm valuation using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach. A total of 50 scientific articles were synthesized to examine ho
content: This study examines ESG financialization, institutional investor preferences, and sustainability pricing in firm valuation using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach. A total of 50 scientific articles were synthesized to examine how sustainability information influences investment decisions and corporate valuation. The findings indicate that ESG disclosure credibility, risk perceptions, corporate governance, and market conditions shape investor assessments. However, the relationship between ESG and firm value is not consistently positive, as outcomes depend on disclosure quality, ownership structure, firm characteristics, and investor responses. Drawing on Signaling Theory, this study explains how credible ESG information communicates corporate quality and sustainability commitments. This study contributes by integrating ESG disclosure, institutional investor preferences, and sustainability pricing into a conceptual framework that clarifies how sustainability information may translate into firm valuation. It also identifies research gaps concerning information credibility, investor responses, and contextual differences, offering implications for companies, investors, and policymakers seeking to strengthen sustainability practices and support long-term corporate value creation.

title: Multi-objective screening framework for three-way catalyst selection under real conditions of gas engine-driven heat pumps
summary: The transition toward low-carbon heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems has accelerated the adoption of gas-engine-driven heat pumps (GHPs) in Korea, where balancing electricity and natural gas demand is critical to mitig
content: The transition toward low-carbon heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems has accelerated the adoption of gas-engine-driven heat pumps (GHPs) in Korea, where balancing electricity and natural gas demand is critical to mitigate summer power shortages associated with electric heat pumps. Although GHPs offer higher primary energy efficiency than conventional boilers, their combustion process produces exhaust emissions such as NO x , CO, and hydrocarbons, necessitating effective after-treatment solutions. This study proposes a practical screening methodology for selecting three-way catalysts (TWCs) tailored to GHP applications under real operating conditions specified by Korean certification standards. Unlike conventional lab-scale evaluations, the catalyst candidates were tested on an actual 2.0 L GHP engine using a dynamometer to reflect realistic exhaust characteristics. Cycle-averaged emissions of NO x , THC, and CO were evaluated under the KS B 8051 certification cycle and normalized with respect to regulatory limits. A multi-objective emission-triangle representation was then employed to enable joint comparison of the three regulated species. Six GHP-dedicated TWC candidates were experimentally compared, and the catalyst exhibiting the smallest emission-triangle area was selected for further analysis, with individual pollutant concentrations and compliance margins considered in interpreting the results. The area was treated as a geometric summary rather than a measure guaranteeing balanced emission reduction. Mode resolved time-series analysis further characterized the emission and thermal behavior of the selected catalyst under comparable engine operating conditions. The proposed framework provides a systematic and quantitative basis for TWC screening in GHP applications and can support practical catalyst selection and emission assessment under certification conditions. Future work will focus on assessing the long-term durability of the selected catalyst under extended endurance operation.

title: Monitoring Surface Water Pollution in the Lom Basin (Eastern Cameroon): Modeling the Impact of Anthropogenic Pressures on Water Quality and Mercury Transport
summary: La pollution mercurielle constitue un enjeu environnemental et sanitaire majeur dans les régions affectées par l’exploitation minière artisanale et à petite échelle de l’or (EMAPE). Cette thèse évalue ses effets sur les eaux de surface du b
content: La pollution mercurielle constitue un enjeu environnemental et sanitaire majeur dans les régions affectées par l’exploitation minière artisanale et à petite échelle de l’or (EMAPE). Cette thèse évalue ses effets sur les eaux de surface du bassin du Lom (Est Cameroun) et analyse le transport et le devenir du mercure. La démarche scientifique s’organise en quatre étapes complémentaires. Premièrement, un état des lieux de la qualité physico-chimique des eaux de surface est établi à partir de campagnes de terrain menées entre 2021 et 2023, en basses et en hautes eaux. Il repose sur des analyses hydrogéochimiques, statistiques et cartographiques, des indices de qualité de l’eau et une évaluation du risque sanitaire. Deuxièmement, les usages du mercure liés à l’EMAPE aurifère sont estimés selon trois scénarios d’amalgamation. Troisièmement, le transport du mercure total est simulé avec le modèle PEGASE pour représenter la dynamique spatio-temporelle. Enfin, un Module de Spéciation du Mercure (MSM) est développé pour simuler le partitionnement dissous-particulaire en fonction du débit, la complexation au carbone organique dissous et les transformations entre les espèces mercurielles (Hg⁰, HgII et MeHg), en tenant compte des conditions hydrologiques, physicochimiques et lumineuses. L’indice de qualité classe environ 60 % des échantillons en basses eaux et 73 % en hautes eaux dans les catégories bonne à excellente, malgré une dégradation de l’amont vers l’aval liée au mercure total et aux matières en suspension (MES), indicateurs de pollution chimique et physique. Le mercure atteint en 2021, 31 µg·L⁻¹ en basses eaux et 42 µg·L⁻¹ en hautes eaux, soit 5,2 et 7 fois la valeur guide de l’OMS pour le mercure inorganique (6 µg·L⁻¹), et 31 et 42 fois la valeur européenne pour l’eau de boisson (1 µg·L⁻¹). Les MES atteignent 452 et 20,90 mg·L⁻¹ respectivement. Les maxima observés dans les zones minières et en aval indiquent l’influence de l’amalgamation, du remaniement des sols et du lavage du minerai. Le risque non cancérigène reste inférieur au seuil de référence, mais l’ingestion demeure la principale voie d’exposition, surtout chez les enfants. Selon les pratiques d’amalgamation, l’usage estimé varie de 45 à 150 kg Hg par jour de lavage en période d’activité intense et de 31,5 à 105 kg Hg par jour de lavage en hautes eaux. Le scénario d’utilisation la plus intensive reproduit le mieux les observations (R² = 0,86 en basses eaux et 0,69 en hautes eaux). Les rejets ponctuels dominent en basses eaux, tandis que le lessivage des surfaces minières prédomine en hautes eaux. Près des sites miniers et en aval, les concentrations dépassent parfois 10 mg·m⁻³. Le MSM révèle une variation saisonnière du partitionnement : la fraction particulaire du HgII domine en basses eaux (46 à 68 %), tandis que la fraction dissoute devient majoritaire en hautes eaux (58 à 85 %). title: Leveraging Mammal Mycophagy to Determine Environmental Drivers of Truffle Diversity
source: Digital Commons - East Tennessee State University (East Tennessee State University)
summary: Many mycorrhizal fungi are hypogeous (truffle-forming), producing underground fruiting bodies. Studying truffles is inherently challenging due to their hidden nature. However, mycophagous mammals provide a unique opportunity to study hypoge
content: Many mycorrhizal fungi are hypogeous (truffle-forming), producing underground fruiting bodies. Studying truffles is inherently challenging due to their hidden nature. However, mycophagous mammals provide a unique opportunity to study hypogeous fungi because they rely on truffles as a food source. Although several truffle species have recently been described in the southern Appalachian region, their fruiting patterns remain poorly understood. To address this, we quantified truffle richness and spore loads from 670 Peromyscus scat samples collected across 42 sites spanning an environmental gradient during 2024 in the Blue Ridge Mountains of East Tennessee. We found that truffle richness and spore abundance peaked mid-season and increased with precipitation, with the strength of the precipitation effect on spore abundance varying with topographic position index. Community analyses revealed season as the strongest predictor of changes in composition. Together, these findings suggest that temporal and environmental variation structure truffle communities.

title: Research on soil improvement effects of starch-based sand-fixing agents on desertified farmland in Dalad Banner
source: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
summary: ObjectiveThis study explores the effect of starch-based sand-fixing agents on the soil properties of desertified farmland， thereby providing a theoretical basis and practical guidance for the restoration and quality improvement of desertifi
content: ObjectiveThis study explores the effect of starch-based sand-fixing agents on the soil properties of desertified farmland， thereby providing a theoretical basis and practical guidance for the restoration and quality improvement of desertified land in arid and semi-arid regions.MethodsA randomized block design was adopted， and a control （CK） and three concentration treatments of 1∶35 （G35）， 1∶75 （G75）， and 1∶125 （G125） were set up in the desertified farmland of Dalad Banner， Inner Mongolia. Soil physicochemical and microbial indicators in the 0—20 cm soil layer were measured， and the soil improvement effect was quantified by constructing a minimum dataset （MDS）.ResultsAfter 120 days of G75 treatment， the contents of soil organic carbon， total nitrogen， available phosphorus， and available potassium increased by 15.61%， 14.97%， 7.89%， and 19.74%， respectively， compared with CK. The nutrient increase under the G35 treatment was higher. Soil enzyme activity increased in a concentration-dependent manner， reaching a peak after the G35 treatment. Bacterial richness and evenness decreased by 11.9% and 2.2%， respectively， compared with CK， while the relative abundance of Myxococcota increased to 5.15%， indicating significant differences in the microbial community structure. The G75 treatment showed better ecological stability. The soil quality index （SQI） calculated from the MDS was ranked as G35 （0.69） > G75 （0.48） > CK （0.41） > G125 （0.30）， with no significant difference between CK and G125， and G35 exhibiting the best soil improvement efficiency.ConclusionStarch-based sand-fixing agents exert soil improvement effects through an “exogenous carbon-microorganisms-nutrient” coupled mechanism. High concentrations increase SQI at the expense of microbial diversity， while medium concentrations achieve a balance between soil improvement efficiency and ecological security. The findings provide theoretical support for the optimal allocation of sand-fixing agents and the sustainable management of desertified farmland in the region.

title: Property Enhancement of Electrodeposited p-Cu₂O Thin Films via Hydrothermal Ethanol Etching for Solar Cell Applications Supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
source: ASEAN Journal for Science and Engineering in Materials
summary: Electrodeposited p-Cu₂O thin films are promising absorber layers for sustainable solar cell applications, but their performance is limited by surface defects, high resistivity, and poor crystallinity. This study investigates hydrothermal et
content: Electrodeposited p-Cu₂O thin films are promising absorber layers for sustainable solar cell applications, but their performance is limited by surface defects, high resistivity, and poor crystallinity. This study investigates hydrothermal ethanol etching as a post-deposition treatment to enhance p-Cu₂O thin films on FTO substrates. The treatment improved crystallinity, refined pyramidal morphology, increased visible-light absorption, reduced surface roughness, and lowered electrical resistivity. These enhancements are attributed to the removal of disordered surface regions and resistive secondary phases. The results indicate that controlled hydrothermal ethanol etching is an effective strategy for improving electrodeposited p-Cu₂O thin films for sustainable photovoltaic applications.

title: Optimaal ontwerp van flexibele warmtenetten
summary: Space and water heating accounted for 77.1% of household energy consumption in the EU in 2024, yet the share of renewables in the heating sector reached only 26.7%. Modern district heating networks (DHNs) are widely recognized as a cost-eff
content: Space and water heating accounted for 77.1% of household energy consumption in the EU in 2024, yet the share of renewables in the heating sector reached only 26.7%. Modern district heating networks (DHNs) are widely recognized as a cost-effective pathway to decarbonize the heating sector, connecting a wide range of renewable and low-carbon heat sources - including solar thermal, geothermal, residual, and aquathermal heat - to consumers across districts and cities. Realizing this potential requires both the development of new networks and the modernization of existing ones, with individual DHN projects requiring investments in the range of tens to hundreds of millions of euros. The required annual investment across the EU-27 is estimated at 11.7 billion EUR. Designing a DHN requires interdependent decisions on heat producers, pipe topology and diameters, consumer substations, heat storages, and operational regimes. Historically, this has been addressed through iterative, manual processes based on design guidelines and simulation of predefined scenarios - an approach that is time-consuming, does not guarantee an economic optimum, and does not scale to large or complex networks. Optimization-based approaches have been proposed to address this limitation. However, the majority of existing methods rely on simplified linear formulations that cannot ensure physical feasibility or accurately capture the interdependencies between network physics and costs. Nonlinear approaches are physically more accurate but are typically not scalable when formulated as mixed-integer nonlinear programs solved by combinatorial methods. To address this gap, this thesis develops a physics-based framework for the automated design optimization of modern district heating networks. The framework belongs to the category of continuous nonlinear program (NLP) optimization, achieving scalability by initially relaxing discrete design decisions and progressively steering the solution towards discrete outcomes through penalization methods, inspired by the field of topology optimization. Four main developments are presented, each extending the framework with a new design feature. First, a heat producer optimization is developed for the optimal selection, sizing, and operation of central heat producers, including the producer supply temperature. Applied to a DHN retrofit study with a multi-objective optimization of costs and CO2 emissions, the approach enables analysis of future carbon pricing impacts on network design and operation, while reliably evaluating heat and pressure losses and temperature-dependent producer efficiencies. Second, a consumer substation optimization is developed, integrating booster heat pump (HP), electric heater (EH), and enlarged heat exchanger (HX) substation configurations into the optimization framework, jointly with the producer supply temperature. title: Photocatalytic properties of bismuth oxyfluoride thin films deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering in Ar/O2/CF4 atmosphere
summary: Bismuth oxyfluoride films were successfully deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering using different Ar/O2/CF4 gas mixtures. For a reactive gas ratio (Rf), defined as the O2/(O2 + CF4) flow rate ratio, ranging from 0 to 0.6, the films con
content: Bismuth oxyfluoride films were successfully deposited by reactive magnetron sputtering using different Ar/O2/CF4 gas mixtures. For a reactive gas ratio (Rf), defined as the O2/(O2 + CF4) flow rate ratio, ranging from 0 to 0.6, the films consist of two phase-system composed of BiO0.5F2 and metallic bismuth (Bi0); whereas for Rf = 0, a single phase BiF3 is observed when Rf > 0.5. The amount of metallic Bismuth within the oxyfluoride matrix can be tuned not only by Rf, but also by adjusting the target power or by varying a single reactive gas flow rate. Increasing the film thickness does not significantly affect the composition but enhances crystallization of the phases. Hence, we succeed in forming one-step Bi/BiO0.5F2 heterojunctions, where the metal presence improves the light absorption, the photogenerated carrier separation, and thus the photocatalytic efficiency for Methylene Orange, MO, degradation in water. Among all the conditions investigated, the film obtained with Rf = 0.3 and a deposition time, td = 20 min exhibits the best overall performance. Indeed, 90 % of MO is degraded after 2 hours of irradiation, and the catalyst remains stable over 3 photocatalytic cycles (approximately 9 hours of total use). Moreover, this material selectively photoconverts CO2 in CO, with a higher efficiency to create useful electrons (rē ≈ 29 mmol/molcata) than pure BiO0.5F2 thin film, and even nanostructured TiO2 P25 (rē ≈ 11 mmol/molcata).

title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses significant clinical challenges due to the complex and variable geometry of the left atrial appendage (LAA), whose structure complicates the development of personalized interventions like LAA occlusion (LAAO)
content: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses significant clinical challenges due to the complex and variable geometry of the left atrial appendage (LAA), whose structure complicates the development of personalized interventions like LAA occlusion (LAAO) for stroke prevention Current reliance on animal models and cadavers for the assessment of left atrium (LA) and LAA to study AF-related disease and interventions raises reproducibility concerns, necessitating the development of high fidelity, physiologically relevant tools. To address this, we present a multimodal framework combining a soft robotic benchtop simulator, a lumped parameter model (LPM), and finite element analysis (FEA) to replicate LA function in sinus rhythm, atrial flutter, and AF. The system integrates 3D-printed, patient-specific LA geometries with soft robotic actuators to reproduce realistic wall motion and hemodynamics. A compact, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-compatible flow loop, driven by a soft robotic left ventricle (LV), eliminates bulky and non-physiological pulsatile pumps, allowing precise flow measurements and LAAO device testing under clinically relevant conditions. Complementary LPM and FEA models provide mechanistic insights, quantifying systemic hemodynamic changes and LA wall stress during disease and interventions. The models effectively replicate the clinical markers of atrial dysfunction and arrhythmia disorders, and their physiological accuracy is demonstrated through validation against human imaging and porcine models. The soft robotic LV's ability to drive the mock flow loop is validated in a hybrid synthetic-biological configuration within a swine circulatory system, where the soft robotic ventricle replaces native ventricular contraction to sustain systemic circulation. This scalable and versatile framework integrates experimental and computational techniques to advance cardiovascular biomechanics, supporting device development, clinical research/training, and personalized AF treatment to improve patient outcomes.

title: A systematic map of syntheses on anthropogenic noise impacts on wildlife: evidence gaps, policy attention, and quality appraisal
summary: As systematic reviews on the effects of anthropogenic noise on wildlife increasingly inform policy, a critical evaluation of this secondary evidence is essential. We assessed the scope, quality, and policy attention of existing syntheses in
content: As systematic reviews on the effects of anthropogenic noise on wildlife increasingly inform policy, a critical evaluation of this secondary evidence is essential. We assessed the scope, quality, and policy attention of existing syntheses in this field. Following a preregistered protocol, we conducted a systematic search in Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, identifying 50 syntheses (systematic reviews, maps, and meta-analyses). We included all 50 syntheses in the systematic map, critical appraisal, and policy-attention analysis, and found that 23 had received policy citations. We included 47 syntheses in the bibliometric analysis. Syntheses were published between 2008 and 2025, with a focus on behavioural, physiological, and communication outcomes in wildlife. Most examined transportation and energy-related noise and reviewed evidence from marine, followed by terrestrial ecosystems. We found critical gaps in taxonomic coverage, with notable underrepresentation of invertebrates, amphibians, and reptiles. Most syntheses were led by researchers from the UK, Canada, and the USA, with limited participation from non-English-speaking countries. Almost half were cited in policy documents, mainly government and regulatory submissions. Syntheses on marine environments received the most policy citations, while those on urban noise received the least. There was no significant difference in quality scores between policy-cited and non-cited syntheses, and most were rated low due to methodological and reporting shortcomings. Our findings highlight the need to fill synthesis gaps and improve methodological transparency to strengthen the evidence base for policy decisions on anthropogenic noise.

title: Enhanced electrocatalytic oxygen reduction to H₂O with high selectivity via 2D 1T-MoS₂ integrated with functionalized carbon nanohorns
summary: Abstract Developing cost-effective and high-performance electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for advancing anion-exchange membrane fuel cell technologies. In this study, we report a robust heterostructure fo
content: Abstract Developing cost-effective and high-performance electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for advancing anion-exchange membrane fuel cell technologies. In this study, we report a robust heterostructure formed by covalently functionalized carbon nanohorns (CNH-N) integrated with metallic 1T-MoS₂ 2D nanosheets. Through tailored diazonium chemistry, positively charged ammonium groups were introduced onto CNHs, enabling strong electrostatic and van der Waals interactions with negatively charged exfoliated MoS₂. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirm successful functionalization, enhanced defect modulation, and intimate CNH–MoS₂ coupling. The resulting CNH-N-MoS₂ catalyst exhibits remarkable ORR performance, including an optimized onset potential of 0.80 V, reduced charge-transfer resistance, and a dominant four-electron reduction pathway with ~ 94% selectivity toward H₂O, which is comparable to commercial Pt/C. These results highlight how controlled chemical functionalization and heterointerface engineering can synergistically enhance catalytic activity and stabilize the 1T-MoS₂ phase. The CNH-N-MoS 2 heterostructures thus represent a promising class of metal-free/low-metal-content electrocatalysts for efficient fuel cell applications.

title: Effects of shoe longitudinal bending stiffness and runner level on Achilles tendon loading through musculoskeletal modelling
summary: Abstract Achilles tendon (AT) injuries are prevalent among runners, especially in experienced runners. This study investigated how runner level and shoe longitudinal bending stiffness (LBS) interact to influence AT loading and lower-limb bi
content: Abstract Achilles tendon (AT) injuries are prevalent among runners, especially in experienced runners. This study investigated how runner level and shoe longitudinal bending stiffness (LBS) interact to influence AT loading and lower-limb biomechanics. Thirty-one male rearfoot strikers (18 experienced, 13 novice) ran at 4.17 m/s in carbon-fiber shoes of three LBS levels (T1: 10.9; T2: 17.5; T3: 33.0 Nm/rad). AT force was estimated in silico from a subject-specific musculoskeletal model with static optimization, computed as the sum of soleus and gastrocnemius muscle forces. Discrete outcomes were analysed using mixed two-way ANOVA, and waveforms using one-dimensional Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM1D). Experienced runners produced greater peak AT force than novice runners (p=0.038, η_p^2=0.141). LBS independently elevated peak AT force (p=0.004, η_p^2=0.182) and AT impulse (p=0.006, η_p^2=0.189), driven by an LBS-related increase in peak ankle dorsiflexion (p<0.001, η_p^2=0.493) that redirected sagittal excursion proximally. Significant runner level × LBS interactions for peak knee extension moment, peak hip external-rotation angle, and transverse-plane hip ROM showed that novice runners adapted to stiffer shoes with proximal compensations, whereas experienced runners did not. Runner level and LBS independently elevate AT loading through complementary biomechanical pathways, and novice runners rely on proximal compensations to accommodate stiffer footwear. These findings support an individualized, U-shaped view of optimal LBS.

title: Electron-Induced Formation of C 2 on Si(100) from Acetylene and Ethylene
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract Hydrogen Desorption Lithography on Si(100) demonstrates the ability of the Scanning Tunneling Microscope (STM) to create functional atomic-scale structures and devices. The dehydrogenation of adsorbed molecules represents a potenti
content: Abstract Hydrogen Desorption Lithography on Si(100) demonstrates the ability of the Scanning Tunneling Microscope (STM) to create functional atomic-scale structures and devices. The dehydrogenation of adsorbed molecules represents a potential complementary technique that has received little attention. For example, formation of C2 could introduce local strain or act as a center for subsequent reactions and would inform positionally controlled mechanosynthesis, an approach with vast potential in surface patterning and functionalization. Here, we studied the electron-induced dehydrogenation of acetylene and ethylene on Si(100) at 4 K using STM. Excitation of acetylene at ≥+3.2 V induces configurational switching, including to a new sublayer-bonded geometry previously predicted to be an adsorption precursor, as well as migration and desorption. Excitation also induces dehydrogenation to C2. Switching between three observed C2 configurations can be induced by excitation at ≥+4.2 V. Simulations using density functional theory reproduced the experimental images based on the choice of functional, dimer-buckling averaging, and the inclusion of diffuse basis functions. In addition, dehydrogenation could be induced using field-emitted electrons on a scale ranging from a single molecule to a radius of >10 nm. These observations highlight the potential of carbon dehydrogenation as an additional tool in Atomically Precise Fabrication (APF).

title: CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
summary: Stimuli such as pH, light, and electromagnetic fields have enabled precise control over nanoscale interactions, yet gases remain relatively unexplored as regulators of material behavior despite their central roles in biology, energy, and cl
content: Stimuli such as pH, light, and electromagnetic fields have enabled precise control over nanoscale interactions, yet gases remain relatively unexplored as regulators of material behavior despite their central roles in biology, energy, and climate. Here, we introduce carbon dioxide (CO2) as a dynamic and reversible stimulus for controlling nanoscale and macroscale matter using sequence-specific peptide design. Peptide-functionalized nanoparticles exhibit pronounced and tunable responses to CO2 across orders of magnitude changes in gas flow rate, with sensitivity governed by site- and sequence-specific changes in peptide structure. The aggregation sequence-dependence is described by six design principles while quantitative modeling show that aggregation rate scales with flow rate rather than cumulative CO2 dose. This gas-controlled response translates from colloidal nanoparticles to cm-scale biocompatible hydrogels that reversibly and colorimetrically respond to CO2. Leveraging this responsiveness, we further demonstrate spatial patterning of a hydrogel through a gas-permeable mask using CO2 as a lithographic stimulus. Consequently, this work establishes gas-mediated control as a general and scalable strategy for programming responsive materials across length scales. Stimuli responsive assemblies can offer precise control over behaviour, but use of gases for this control is rare. Here, the authors report the use of carbon dioxide for tuneable nanoparticle response, directed by changes in peptide structure.

title: Effects of an intensive firefighter training program on a simulated fire-escape staircase climb
summary: Abstract To evaluate the effects of a four-week intensive training program on weighted stair-climb performance, 18 participants (17 men, 1 woman) completed 16 training sessions combining strength, power, and endurance work. Pre- and post-in
content: Abstract To evaluate the effects of a four-week intensive training program on weighted stair-climb performance, 18 participants (17 men, 1 woman) completed 16 training sessions combining strength, power, and endurance work. Pre- and post-intervention assessments included a loaded fire-escape staircase climb test, incremental VO₂max test, 30-s Wingate test, submaximal squat test, anthropometric measures, and the ANTI-Vea attentional task. Linear mixed models were used to assess intervention effects; effect sizes were expressed as Cohen's d . Stair-climb time decreased significantly after training (EMC: −1.26 s; d = − 0.88). Post-intervention performance was predicted by a composite Strength Score ( β std = − 0.65) and Wingate Score ( β std = − 0.35; model R ² = 0.86). High-load squat velocity and power, estimated 1RM, and Wingate mean power improved significantly (all d > 0.67), whereas VO₂max, ventilatory thresholds, and body mass remained unchanged. ANT-I mean reaction time improved ( d z = − 0.59), with a shift from a linear to a quadratic vigilance decrement pattern. In conclusion, four weeks of intensive firefighter training improved stair-climb performance primarily through neuromuscular and anaerobic adaptations. Training programs targeting this task should prioritize explosive strength at task-relevant loads and anaerobic endurance, while dedicated cognitive training may be required to improve higher-order vigilance components.

title: Quantum Dot Colloidosomes as Triggerable Microlasers
summary: Abstract Quantum dot (QD) supraparticle lasers are promising platforms for microscale light sources and photonic labeling, yet their optical properties are set during assembly. Here, we introduce QD colloidosomes, liquid-core/solid-shell su
content: Abstract Quantum dot (QD) supraparticle lasers are promising platforms for microscale light sources and photonic labeling, yet their optical properties are set during assembly. Here, we introduce QD colloidosomes, liquid-core/solid-shell supraparticles that combine whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) optical feedback with stimulus-triggered structural collapse. Intact QD colloidosomes exhibit narrow, cavity-defined emission consistent with WGM-assisted lasing from 4.2 mJ/cm2, with line widths of 2.2–3.7 nm, demonstrating light confinement without a solid core. We identify shell continuity as a critical determinant for WGM feedback and lasing by exploring a morphological continuum of suprastructures comprising solid supraparticles, colloidosomes, and microporous hollow shells. Intact colloidosomes support narrow cavity modes, whereas porous shells remain broadband even at high pump fluence. We show that colloidosomes can be driven to rupture and release payload through well-defined pathways, including meniscus-driven capillary failure, uniform heating, and localized near-infrared activation, thereby configuring their optical response from cavity-defined lasing to broadband emission. These results establish QD colloidosomes as stimuli-responsive microlasers that couple optical-state switching and triggered release within a single self-assembled platform.

title: Molecules in the shadows of the protoplanetary disk HD 143006. Evidence of C/O,≳,1 from simultaneously modeling fourteen ALMA lines
summary: The inner disk of the T,Tauri star HD,143006 is inclined and casts a broad shadow over a large portion of the outer disk. We use this extraordinary geometry to study the impact of stellar ultraviolet (UV) irradiation on disk chemistry, temp
content: The inner disk of the T,Tauri star HD,143006 is inclined and casts a broad shadow over a large portion of the outer disk. We use this extraordinary geometry to study the impact of stellar ultraviolet (UV) irradiation on disk chemistry, temperature, and line formation. We present new ALMA observations of this disk, covering CO, 13 CO, C^18O, CN, HCN, HCO^+$, CS, and C_3H_2. Combined with previously published C_2H, N_2H^+ and H_2CO observations, these data constitute an extensive dataset of fourteen ALMA lines from nine different molecules. We subdivide these data into two disk halves: the illuminated part and the shadowed part. We develop ProDiMo models for these two disk halves by optionally including an inclined inner disk that blocks the stellar illumination of the upper layers of the outer disk without hindering the stellar illumination of the outer disk along the midplane. The observed line flux contrasts between the illuminated and the shadowed disk sides are not very pronounced. We explain this phenomenon by introducing ``equilibrated models'' that consider a slow heating and cooling relaxation of gas parcels orbiting in and out of the shadow. Our results fit the radial line intensity profiles of all ALMA lines, both in flux and radial shape, with an overall reduced ̧hi of about 2.3, both from the illuminated and the shadowed disk sides, along with two ALMA continuum images, where we see evidence of radial drift, and the spectral energy distribution (SED) beyond 20,μm, all with one model. In most cases, the line intensities only increase slightly on the illuminated side because the gas warms up slowly, although fast UV photochemistry significantly reduces the observable molecular concentrations. The dust temperatures increase even more rapidly, but this has little effect on the line formation. However, for the lines of N_2H^+ and CS, which probe deeper layers where the gas and dust temperatures are coupled, slow UV desorption of ices such as NH_3 and H_2S plays a crucial role. This can result in a brightening of these lines on the shadowed side. Our analysis suggests with high confidence that the carbon-to-oxygen ratio in the outer disk of HD,143006 is slightly greater than one (∼,1.05). The disk mass is fit to be as low as 0.0012,M_⊙. However, almost equally well-fitting models with a fixed disk mass of $0.021 M_⊙ can be obtained after readjusting the disk shape, dust, and gas heating and cooling parameters.

title: The dearth of dustless HdC stars in the Magellanic Clouds: A metallicity-driven white dwarf merger mass effect
summary: Hydrogen-deficient carbon (HdC) stars are rare supergiants believed to form through the merger of two white dwarfs (WDs). They comprise the dust-producing R Coronae Borealis (RCB) stars and the dustless HdC (dLHdC) stars. While dedicated Ga
content: Hydrogen-deficient carbon (HdC) stars are rare supergiants believed to form through the merger of two white dwarfs (WDs). They comprise the dust-producing R Coronae Borealis (RCB) stars and the dustless HdC (dLHdC) stars. While dedicated Galactic surveys find the two subclasses in roughly equal numbers, no dLHdC star has been identified previously in the Magellanic Clouds despite 30 known RCB stars in these two galaxies. We present the first systematic search for dLHdC stars in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) aiming to measure the dLHdC-to-RCB ratio in environments of distinct metallicities and well-constrained star formation histories. Candidates were selected from the Gaia DR3 Magellanic catalogue using colour--magnitude cuts combining Gaia, SkyMapper DR4, and VMC DR6 photometry, complemented by a random-forest classifier trained on known Galactic dLHdC stars. The search reached an overall detection efficiency of ∼96%. All candidates were followed up spectroscopically with WiFeS on the ANU 2.3 m telescope. We discovered the first two Magellanic dLHdC stars, SP77 29-5 in the LMC and SMSS 005551.43-723139.2 in the SMC; the latter belongs to the rare Sr-rich subclass. The resulting dLHdC-to-RCB number ratio of ∼1:15 overall is far below the near-unity Galactic value. We argue this deficit is intrinsic rather than observational. Convolving the delay time distribution from a subclass of WD mergers with each Cloud's star formation history, we estimate that ∼80% (LMC) and about two-thirds (SMC) of HdC stars originate from mergers with short delay times, which at low metallicity are biased towards higher total WD masses and thus towards the luminous regime associated with RCB stars rather than the fainter dLHdC population.

title: A canopy heat-load threshold for fruiting-site retention and lint yield in long-staple cotton, displaced by trehalose-pathway perturbation
summary: Heat at flowering cuts lint yield through shedding of squares and young bolls, usually reported as non-transferable abscission percentages. We asked whether fruiting-site survival is a continuous function of canopy heat load, and what displ
content: Heat at flowering cuts lint yield through shedding of squares and young bolls, usually reported as non-transferable abscission percentages. We asked whether fruiting-site survival is a continuous function of canopy heat load, and what displacing it is worth. Sowing date and drip-irrigation interval gave eight environments over two seasons at one southern Xinjiang site, spanning canopy heat loads (HL, hours with canopy temperature ≥ 32 °C in ten days from anthesis) of 17.9–70.9 h. Two long-staple cultivars ( Gossypium barbadense L.) received water, melatonin, trehalose or validamycin A, alongside a source–sink manipulation. Retention of tagged first-position sites declined logistically with HL, with half-retention heat loads of 54.0 h (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 51.2–57.1) and 70.2 h (66.4–75.1) in the sensitive and tolerant cultivars; leave-one-environment-out error was 0.035 retention units. Lint yield followed boll number, falling 53% in the water-sprayed sensitive cultivar. The benefit of validamycin A grew continuously with HL: at 70.9 h retention rose from 0.109 to 0.293 in the sensitive cultivar and from 0.274 to 0.409 in the tolerant one, whose treated thresholds are extrapolated beyond 70.9 h. Averaged over cultivars in the three hottest environments, it raised retention by 55% and lint yield by 19%, with fibre properties unchanged. Leaf photosynthesis fell only 17%, whereas boll cell-wall invertase activity and sucrose-to-hexose ratio tracked retention within environments, consistent with a sink-side carbohydrate limitation. One site and two seasons establish the form of the response, not its transfer between regions; recalibrated locally, the threshold can inform cultivar, irrigation and spray decisions.

title: Pulmonary vascular abnormalities in Long COVID: a radiological perspective
source: The Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine
summary: Abstract Background Post-COVID-19 condition (Long COVID) has emerged as a major public health challenge, with survivors frequently reporting persistent dyspnea, fatigue, and exercise intolerance. While initial radiological research focused
content: Abstract Background Post-COVID-19 condition (Long COVID) has emerged as a major public health challenge, with survivors frequently reporting persistent dyspnea, fatigue, and exercise intolerance. While initial radiological research focused on parenchymal lung disease, a paradigm shift has identified pulmonary vascular abnormalities—specifically endotheliitis, microthrombosis, and maladaptive angiogenesis—as critical drivers of the Long COVID phenotype. Main Body The disease is characterized by “endotheliitis,” where direct viral entry via ACE2 receptors precipitates a pro-coagulant state and the formation of in situ microthrombi. This is further complicated by immunothrombosis involving neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and the presence of amyloid-like fibrin microclots that are resistant to natural breakdown. Additionally, structural remodeling through intussusceptive angiogenesis and “vascular pruning” (the loss of distal capillaries) reduces the effective surface area for gas exchange. Conventional CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) often fails to detect these microvascular changes, despite patients exhibiting severe symptoms. However, advanced modalities provide deeper insights. Dual-energy CT (DECT) reveals persistent, wedge-shaped perfusion defects even in morphologically normal lung parenchyma. Quantitative CT (QCT) allows for the measurement of “vascular pruning,” showing a significant reduction in small vessel volume (PBV5). Hyperpolarized xenon-129 MRI (Hp-XeMRI) has identified a hallmark Red blood cell (RBC):barrier defect, indicating impaired gas transfer from the alveoli to red blood cells—a finding that persists even when standard CT and pulmonary function tests are normal. Functional techniques like V/Q SPECT and phase-resolved functional lung (PREFUL) MRI further confirm a “mottled” perfusion pattern indicative of diffuse small vessel vasculopathy. Short conclusion This review emphasizes that Long COVID involves a distinct vascular phenotype that requires functional and quantitative imaging for accurate diagnosis. Adherence to the 2025 international consensus guidelines—recommending imaging 3 months post-infection and the use of paired inspiratory/expiratory protocols—is essential for standardizing care and differentiating vascular from airway-related symptoms.

title: A Paired Lake–Land Observation Dataset of Mesoscale Lakes over the Tibetan Plateau for Analyzing Lake-induced Thermal and Moisture Modulation
summary: Abstract Lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are sensitive indicators of climate change and important regulators of local land–atmosphere exchanges. However, continuous in situ observations remain limited, especially for mesoscale lakes with lake
content: Abstract Lakes on the Tibetan Plateau are sensitive indicators of climate change and important regulators of local land–atmosphere exchanges. However, continuous in situ observations remain limited, especially for mesoscale lakes with lake areas of 100–500 km 2 . Moreover, paired lake–land observations are scarce, constraining accurate assessments of meteorological and surface-exchange differences between lake surfaces and their surrounding terrestrial environments. To address this lack of systematic and continuous observations, we present a paired lake–land observational dataset covering three representative lakes across the monsoon, monsoon–westerly transition, and westerly climate regions. The dataset provides continuous and consistently processed observations from lake and nearby land stations during 2019–23. The dataset includes automatic weather station observations, eddy correlation, radiation components, and corresponding nearby land-station observations. The main variables include air temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, precipitation, shortwave and longwave radiation, and sensible and latent heat fluxes. All records were processed using unified procedures, including time-continuity checks, missing-value flagging, unit conversion, format standardization, and quality control. Initial analyses reveal clear lake–land contrasts. Compared with nearby land stations, lake stations generally show smaller diurnal temperature ranges, higher warm-season humidity, stronger and more persistent winds, lower sensible heat flux, and higher latent heat flux. These results indicate that mesoscale lakes can substantially modify local thermal, moisture, and surface energy-exchange conditions. This dataset provides valuable support for studies of lake–land–atmosphere interactions, remote-sensing and reanalysis evaluation, and lake model improvement over the Tibetan Plateau. The dataset is available at the Tibetan Plateau Data Center and Science Data Bank.

title: Many-objective reservoir operation optimization using NSGA-III and decision-support analysis: a sustainable management framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India
source: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
summary: Abstract Efficient reservoir operation requires simultaneous consideration of competing goals related to hydropower generation, water-supply reliability, flood management, and storage regulation. However, deriving balanced operating policie
content: Abstract Efficient reservoir operation requires simultaneous consideration of competing goals related to hydropower generation, water-supply reliability, flood management, and storage regulation. However, deriving balanced operating policies becomes increasingly complex when several conflicting objectives are considered concurrently. This study develops a many-objective optimization framework for the Indira Sagar Reservoir, India, considering four objectives: maximization of hydropower generation and minimization of water deficit, spill losses, and storage deviation. The reservoir operation model integrates hydrological inputs, demand characteristics, operational constraints, and reservoir continuity relationships. Five metaheuristic algorithms Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III (NSGA-III), Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO), Multi-Objective Ant Colony Optimization (MOACO), and Multi-Objective Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (MOTLBO were comparatively evaluated using Hypervolume (HV), Inverted Generational Distance (IGD), and computational performance indicators. NSGA-III achieved an HV of 0.9234 and an IGD of 0.0338, demonstrating effective convergence and diversity for the evaluated solutions. Pareto analysis revealed distinct trade-offs among energy generation, water shortage, spill, and storage regulation. The Weighted Sum Method (WSM) identified Solution S10 as the selected compromise policy, providing 4106.8 GWh/year hydropower generation, 352.9 MCM/year water deficit, and 92.3% reliability. Scenario-based evaluation under normal, flood, and drought conditions further demonstrated variations in policy performance across hydrological regimes. The framework provides a structured decision-support approach for strategic reservoir operation and facilitates transparent evaluation of trade-offs among competing water-resource objectives.

title: Improving LC-MS-Based Marfey’s Analysis on a Single-Quadrupole Platform through Reagent Evaluation and SIM/Scan Acquisition
summary: Abstract Marfey’s method is a widely used approach for determining the absolute configuration of amino acids in peptides and natural products. However, its broader application is often limited by challenges in resolving amino acid epimers a
content: Abstract Marfey’s method is a widely used approach for determining the absolute configuration of amino acids in peptides and natural products. However, its broader application is often limited by challenges in resolving amino acid epimers and the relatively large amount of analyte typically required for analysis. In this study, we evaluated three commonly used Marfey’s reagents (l-FDAA, l-FDVA, and l-FDLA) for their ability to resolve amino acid diastereomers and investigated whether synchronous selected ion monitoring (SIM)/scan mode in liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC-MS) could improve the sensitivity of LC-MS analysis. Using the cyanobacterial peptide micropeptin 982 (d-Gln) as a representative case study, we evaluated three acquisition modes on a widely available single-quadrupole LC-MS platform and found that synchronous SIM/scan, particularly with time-segmented SIM groups, substantially improved practical sensitivity while preserving scan-mode information. Limits of detection were achieved in the range of 11–16 pmol, and absolute configuration assignments were accomplished using as little as 50 μg of analyte. This method provides a practical strategy for stereochemical analysis of scarce peptide natural products, especially when material needs to be prioritized for downstream biological research.

title: AN INTRA-DAY AND DAILY ROLLING ECONOMIC DISPATCHING MODEL FOR ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS IN INDUSTRIAL PARK MICROGRIDS
summary: Aiming at the electricity-purchase-cost optimization demand of park microgrids equipped with distributed photovoltaics, two sets of energy-storage dispatching models are established for intra-day deterministic dispatching and long-term day-
content: Aiming at the electricity-purchase-cost optimization demand of park microgrids equipped with distributed photovoltaics, two sets of energy-storage dispatching models are established for intra-day deterministic dispatching and long-term day-by-day rolling optimization. With the objective of minimizing daily total electricity-purchase cost, the intra-day dispatching model considers power balance, energy-storage charge-discharge power, capacity limits and daily cyclic constraints. Linear programming is adopted to solve electricity-purchase and energy-storage operation strategies under 10-minute time granularity, followed by feasibility verification and sensitivity analysis of key parameters. For long-term rolling dispatching, load forecasting is realized via historical same-week load weighting and deviation damping correction. A safety margin for planned electricity purchase and high-price emergency purchase penalty mechanism are introduced to realize annual-scale optimal operation of microgrid energy storage. Numerical results prove that energy-storage greatly cuts microgrid electricity-purchase expenditure. Charge-discharge efficiency dominates dispatching performance, and a 3% reserved ratio for planned purchase balances economic cost and power shortage risk. This work provides theoretical support for practical engineering dispatching of park-microgrid energy storage.

title: MEASUREMENT OF MUNICIPAL NEW-QUALITY PRODUCTIVE FORCES AND REGIONAL DIFFERENCES
summary: Guided by the policy of developing new-quality productive forces in light of local conditions, this paper takes panel data (2015-2024) of five core cities in Jiangxi including Nanchang, Ganzhou, Jiujiang, Shangrao and Yichun as research sam
content: Guided by the policy of developing new-quality productive forces in light of local conditions, this paper takes panel data (2015-2024) of five core cities in Jiangxi including Nanchang, Ganzhou, Jiujiang, Shangrao and Yichun as research samples. An evaluation system for municipal new-quality productive forces is constructed covering scientific-technological, green and digital dimensions. The entropy-weight improved AHP-TOPSIS model is adopted for comprehensive measurement, so as to analyze its temporal evolution and regional differentiation. The results show that the overall level of new-quality productive forces of the five cities presents a fluctuating upward trend, which can be divided into three stages: steady accumulation, accelerated improvement and adjustment-divergence. Obvious echelon gaps exist among cities. Nanchang takes the lead, Ganzhou ranks second, Shangrao shows strong late-comer momentum, while Jiujiang and Yichun suffer from remarkable fluctuation and decline. Green productivity enjoys sound intra-provincial balance yet meets promotion bottlenecks; inter-city gaps are prominent in scientific-technological and digital productivity. Most cities are confronted with insufficient S&T investment, weak digital industrial foundation and heavy pressure of industrial transformation. Targeted suggestions are put forward on consolidating industrial foundation, strengthening innovation drive, promoting digital-real economy integration, advancing differentiated green-low-carbon transition, optimizing regional coordination and institutional guarantee. It provides empirical support for fostering municipal new-quality productive forces in Jiangxi.

title: A Comprehensive Hourly Land–Atmosphere Interaction Dataset from a Coordinated 15-Station Network Spanning the Environmental Gradients of the Tibetan Plateau (2021–24)
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of land–atmosphere interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is hindered by fragmented measurements, inconsistent data-processing standards, and a scarcity of integrated, multi-component observations. To
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of land–atmosphere interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is hindered by fragmented measurements, inconsistent data-processing standards, and a scarcity of integrated, multi-component observations. To address these limitations, we present an integrated dataset from 15 stations spanning monsoon-dominated, westerlies-dominated, and transitional regions of the TP. The dataset features hourly gradient meteorological variables, radiation components, soil temperature and moisture measurements, and turbulent fluxes, providing vertically resolved information on land surface processes. Processed under standardized protocols with harmonized temporal resolutions, consistent variable definitions, and rigorous quality control procedures, the data ensure high reliability and internal consistency. This dataset provides a robust observational foundation for advancing process-based understanding of land–atmosphere coupling and its representation in models over the TP. It is expected to support land surface and Earth system model evaluation, satellite product validation, and data assimilation. Furthermore, it provides a basis for developing hybrid physics-machine learning approaches for data quality control and gap-filling in-situ observations in complex high-altitude environments.

title: Radioactive fallout legacy of nuclear tests in soils of the Southern Hemisphere
summary: Abstract Fallout radionuclide (FRN) archived in soils are key tracers of soil redistribution, sediment dynamics, and associated carbon fluxes, yet their global application is limited by poorly constrained baselines in the Southern Hemispher
content: Abstract Fallout radionuclide (FRN) archived in soils are key tracers of soil redistribution, sediment dynamics, and associated carbon fluxes, yet their global application is limited by poorly constrained baselines in the Southern Hemisphere. Here, we present the first hemisphere-scale baseline and uncertainty maps of 137 Cs and 239+240 Pu soil inventories. Predictions exhibited lower spatial variability and relative uncertaintyfor 137 Cs across most landscapes, whereas 239+240 Pu showed greater spatial variability and larger relative uncertainty. The reconstructed inventories revealed strong latitudinal and topographic gradients, with the highest predicted fallout occurring in tropical and mountainous regions. We further show, under a standardized hypothetical 50% inventory-loss scenario, that uncertainty in low-inventory regions can propagate nonlinearly into soil erosion and carbon-budget estimates, producing carbon budget biases of up to 19.8 t C ha −1 . These findings provide a new benchmark for Southern Hemisphere fallout radionuclide applications and a scalable framework for integrating spatial uncertainty into sediment tracing, soil degradation assessment, and carbon cycle studies.

title: OPERATING OPTIMISATION FOR A DIRECT-CONNECTED GREEN-ELECTRICITY HYDROGEN-AMMONIA PARK BASED ON MIXED-INTEGER AND CONTINUOUS LINEAR PROGRAMMING
summary: This paper studies the operation optimisation of a direct-connected wind-photovoltaic hydrogen-ammonia park and evaluates how production flexibility, energy storage and islanded operation affect power balance, renewable-electricity indicato
content: This paper studies the operation optimisation of a direct-connected wind-photovoltaic hydrogen-ammonia park and evaluates how production flexibility, energy storage and islanded operation affect power balance, renewable-electricity indicators and operating cost. Some applications have been developed for full-load operation, discrete production scheduling, continuous power regulation, islanded dispatch, storage sizing and grid-connected comparison. The park has 40 MW of wind power, 64 MW of photovoltaic power, and hydrogen-ammonia loads for 36 t/d and 72 t/d production. At a 36 t/d full-load baseline, the self-consumption, green-electricity and export ratios are 28.16%, 69.21% and 35.92%, respectively; 54 t/d is the lowest-cost feasible output in discrete scheduling, and the unit cost is 4591.27 yuan/t. The total annual cost of continuous regulation is 1.9005 million yuan, and all three indicators have been achieved in 210 of the 360 weighted days. In islanded operation, 5000 MWh of storage increases the annual output to 25920 t, but the unit cost is still higher than that of grid-connected systems. Flexible production and storage increase the utilisation of renewable energy; however, economic feasibility requires integrated planning of production, storage and grid operation.

title: Preliminary exploration of sequential DPL and CO2 laser versus CO2 laser monotherapy for the prophylactic management of early postoperative linear scars: A retrospective cohort study
summary: Background and Objectives. Prophylactic management of early postoperative linear scars remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of sequential dye pulsed light (DPL) and fractional CO 2 laser (CO 2 las
content: Background and Objectives. Prophylactic management of early postoperative linear scars remains a clinical challenge. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of sequential dye pulsed light (DPL) and fractional CO 2 laser (CO 2 laser) versus CO 2 laser monotherapy in the prevention of scar hypertrophy, and to explore potential simplified early interventions. Patients and Methods. In this exploratory retrospective study, 38 patients with early postoperative linear scars were enrolled. They were divided into a sequential DPL-CO 2 laser group and a CO 2 laser monotherapy group (19 patients each). All received six monthly prophylactic treatments. Efficacy was assessed by two independent surgeons using the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS). Results. After six treatments, no statistically significant difference was detected in the total POSAS score between the two groups ( p = 0.988, mean difference = -0.26, 95% CI: -1.66 to 1.14). Similarly, no significant differences were found in the patient (PSAS) or observer (OSAS) component scores. However, compared to baseline, both groups showed significant improvement in several key scar parameters, including vascularization, thickness, color, stiffness, and irregularity. One case of transient reactive hyperplasia in the CO 2 group was resolved with conservative management. Conclusions. Both sequential DPL-CO 2 laser therapy and CO 2 laser monotherapy were associated with favorable clinical trajectories in early postoperative linear scars over 6 months. In this exploratory, underpowered retrospective cohort, no definitive comparative conclusions could be drawn between the two regimens. Spontaneous maturation likely contributed to these outcomes. The observed parallel trends generate a hypothesis requiring proper prospective randomized evaluation to determine the true utility of CO2 laser alone as a simplified early intervention.

title: Enhancing CO₂ uptake in concrete using activated rice husk ash and zeolite 13X: A performance evaluation on mechanical, durability and carbonation study
summary: The more carbon footprint associated with cement manufacture has enhanced the search for sustainable alternatives capable of successful concrete performance while enabling carbon sequestration. This research work studies the combined effect
content: The more carbon footprint associated with cement manufacture has enhanced the search for sustainable alternatives capable of successful concrete performance while enabling carbon sequestration. This research work studies the combined effect of agricultural and mineral-based additives, namely rice husk ash (RHA), zeolite 13X (Z13X), and along with their activated forms, on the mechanical properties and carbon capture potential of concrete. Concrete mixtures with varying replacement levels of above materials were prepared and their mechanical properties were evaluated. In addition, the carbonation behaviour of hardened concrete was evaluated depth of carbonation and CO₂ uptake capacity were assessed using the mass gain method, while the compressive strength of carbonated concrete was determined and compared with non-carbonated specimens to evaluate the influence of carbonation on structural performance. The test results show that an optimum replacement level of nearly 10% gives the most favourable balance between strength and carbonation performance. Among the investigated materials, followed by RHA with 41.11 N/mm², primarily due to enhanced particle packing and pozzolanic reactions that promote the formation of additional C–S–H gel. Activated materials exhibited significantly greater CO₂ uptake and carbonation depth, with activated rice husk ash (AR-10) achieving the peak CO₂ absorption of 1.8%. However, excessive carbonation in highly reactive activated materials slightly reduced compressive strength. The test results indicate that an optimum replacement level of 10% provides the best overall performance. The AR-10 mix achieved the highest CO₂ uptake of 1.8%, while maintaining satisfactory mechanical properties. The RHA-10 mix exhibited the highest compressive strength of 41.11 MPa , attributed to improved particle packing and enhanced pozzolanic reactions that promoted the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrate (C–S–H) gel. Activated materials showed greater carbonation depth and CO₂ absorption than non-activated. Although increased carbonation in highly reactive activated mixes resulted in a slight reduction in compressive strength, the carbonated specimens retained measurable residual compressive strength, with the extent of strength retention varying according to the replacement material and dosage. Further, the results demonstrate that the integration of agricultural waste and mineral additives can simultaneously enhance mechanical properties and carbon sequestration capacity, offering a favourable strategy for the advancement of low-carbon and sustainable concrete systems.

title: Crystal Engineering of Carbamazepine Co-Crystals for Solubility and Dissolution Enhancement: Solid-State Characterization and In-Vitro Performance Evaluation
