source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: Poor aqueous solubility remains a major limitation in oral drug delivery, particularly for Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) Class II drugs. Carbamazepine (CBZ), a widely prescribed anticonvulsant, exhibits high permeability but
content: Poor aqueous solubility remains a major limitation in oral drug delivery, particularly for Biopharmaceutics Classification System (BCS) Class II drugs. Carbamazepine (CBZ), a widely prescribed anticonvulsant, exhibits high permeability but low aqueous solubility, resulting in variable dissolution behaviour and inconsistent therapeutic response. The present study aimed to design and evaluate pharmaceutical co-crystals of carbamazepine using rational crystal engineering approaches to enhance solubility and dissolution characteristics. Cocrystals were prepared using nicotinamide, saccharin, and glutaric acid as co-formers through solvent evaporation, slurry crystallization, and liquid-assisted grinding techniques.

title: Incorporating Co-Encapsulated N-Doped Carbon Nanotube with Zn Phthalocyanine: Accelerated Water Dissociation Kinetics for Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
summary: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrite (NO2–) reduction to hydroxylamine (NH2OH) under ambient conditions is regarded as a sustainable way to simultaneously enable pollutant abatement and value-added chemical synthesis; however, the intrinsicall
content: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrite (NO2–) reduction to hydroxylamine (NH2OH) under ambient conditions is regarded as a sustainable way to simultaneously enable pollutant abatement and value-added chemical synthesis; however, the intrinsically sluggish kinetics and competing over-reduction to ammonia necessitate the rational exploration of robust electrocatalytic systems. Herein, we report the anchoring of zinc phthalocyanine (ZnPc) molecules onto bamboo-like nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes encapsulating metallic cobalt nanoparticles (Co-NCNT) for selectively converting NO2– to NH2OH. The resulting ZnPc/Co-NCNT electrocatalyst achieves a considerable NH2OH yield of 0.25 mmol h–1 mgcat–1 and a high Faradaic efficiency of 64.32% at −0.3 V vs RHE, significantly outperforming its monocomponent counterparts. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the Co-NCNT facilitates charge transfer and lowers the water dissociation barrier, securing efficient active hydrogen (*H) supply to drive the hydrogenation processes. Furthermore, the practical viability of this system is demonstrated by constructing a Zn–NO2– battery, which concurrently generates NH2OH while delivering a peak power density of 7.22 mW cm–2. This study underscores the efficacy of synergistically integrating molecular catalysts with functional carriers for selective NO2– electroreduction to NH2OH.

title: Vacuum Evaporation Enabled Economical and Eco-Friendly Composite Copper Current Collectors
summary: The composite copper current collector holds enormous potential for boosting the energy density and safety of lithium-ion batteries, yet manufacturing throughput and substrate cost remain key barriers to its widespread adoption. Here, we de
content: The composite copper current collector holds enormous potential for boosting the energy density and safety of lithium-ion batteries, yet manufacturing throughput and substrate cost remain key barriers to its widespread adoption. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid manufacturing technique combining designed vacuum evaporation and electroplating that achieves sub-second (0.38 s) metallization of economical polyethene terephthalate, dramatically improving throughput. The as-fabricated composite copper current collector demonstrates favourable attributes, including electrochemical stability and significant weight savings. For the composite copper current collector-graphite electrode, it would achieve an over 11% increase in whole electrode specific capacity, even compared to the 4.5 μm pure copper foil at 6.5 mAh cm −2 . This performance translates to the potential for extending electric vehicle range and saving 19.44 ~ 22.28 GWh in the production of lithium-ion batteries in 2025. Beyond performance, this work includes a life-cycle assessment, unveiling a reduced carbon footprint and substantial global copper conservation enabled by composite copper current collector, while also elucidating its intrinsic safety mechanism. These findings offer a potential pathway for fabricating sustainable and high-safety lithium-ion batteries.

title: Microchemical analysis in fixed and volatile oil of black pepper (Piper nigrum L)
summary: The experiment on microchemical analysis of seed powder of black pepper was performed at FTL, JAU Junagadh.and the result shown the presence of 44 peaks in volatile oil extracted with rotary evaporator in powdered materials of the Piper nig
content: The experiment on microchemical analysis of seed powder of black pepper was performed at FTL, JAU Junagadh.and the result shown the presence of 44 peaks in volatile oil extracted with rotary evaporator in powdered materials of the Piper nigrum L and 17 peaks of fatty acids in fixed oils in Soxhlet extracted oil.Most of them were found to be as intense pungent and fragrance compounds.The class of compounds in this oil were includes Aliphatic halide, Ketone, Alkane, Monoterpenoid alcohol, Alcohol (3), Bicyclic compound, Aromatic aldehyde, Aromatic ether, Aromatic hydrocarbon, Cycloalkene (4), Bicyclic hydrocarbon, Bicyclic alkene, Diene.The key Bio-marker compounds were found to be as the Caryophyllene at 21.889 minutes with peak number 29.The highest area, covering 23.21 %, was observed at 9.693 minutes, in addition to peak number 7, which showed the highest height with an area % of 20.84 at 11.51 minutes RT, and had 44 peaks in it adducts.These findings also shown the complete pictures of fatty acids too and the highest area% 32.91with 9,12-Octadecadienoic acid (PUFA).The quality oil indices were found to be in the range of SFA (36.65%),MUFA (25.81%),PUFA (37.54) %, MUFA/PUFA ratio (0.69), O/L ratio (6.24) and UnsFA/SFA (38.24).The literature cited here indicated compounds had antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and insect-related activities as well as anticancer compounds too in black pepper Keywords: Cardamom, GC MS, fixed oil and volatile oil

title: A Bayesian Functional Kriging framework for spatial interpolation of PM2.5 concentration profiles
summary: Air pollution, especially fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), is a major global public health problem, causing breathing difficulties, lung disease, heart problems, and premature death. Predicting PM 2.5 concentrations at unobserved location
content: Air pollution, especially fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ), is a major global public health problem, causing breathing difficulties, lung disease, heart problems, and premature death. Predicting PM 2.5 concentrations at unobserved locations is essential in environmental science, especially with sparse observational data. This study introduces a new Bayesian Functional Kriging (BFK) model to predict PM 2.5 concentration profiles across Pakistan’s most populous province, using MERRA-2 reanalysis data at 17 city locations across Punjab. The BFK framework combines three methodologies: Functional Data Analysis (FDA), where continuous temporal curves model discrete PM 2.5 concentration profiles through B-spline smoothing; Functional Kriging (FK), in which functional data are used for spatial prediction of curve-valued observations; and Bayesian hierarchical modeling using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling for parameter estimation. Prior empirical distributions are assumed for all parameters of interest: mean, partial sill, nugget effect, and spatial range, while posterior estimates are derived via a hybrid Gibbs-Metropolis algorithm within Gibbs sampling. Cross-validation results show that BFK is significantly better than the FK method, with RMSE and MAE differences of 30.9% (from 16.88 µg/m 3 to 11.66 µg/m 3 ) and 29.9% (from 13.03 µg/m 3 to 9.14 µg/m 3 ), respectively. In addition, we used the proposed model to estimate temporal variation in PM 2.5 concentration at five locations not sampled during data collection: Vehari, Sialkot, Attock, Khanewal, and Okara. We found that pollution is much higher in the southern areas than in the northern ones. These findings underscore BFK’s utility as a statistically principled and practically effective tool for air quality monitoring and environmental policy.

title: Public rapid-charging infrastructure and BEV adoption: Drivers of spatially heterogeneous impacts
source: Transportation Research Part D Transport and Environment
summary: Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) offer environmental benefits, but range anxiety remains a barrier to adoption. Public chargers help alleviate this concern. This paper provides causal evidence on how public rapid-charging infrastructure inf
content: Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) offer environmental benefits, but range anxiety remains a barrier to adoption. Public chargers help alleviate this concern. This paper provides causal evidence on how public rapid-charging infrastructure influences BEV adoption across local authorities in England. Instrumenting endogenous charger placement using the historical distribution of public car parks, we estimate that the elasticity of BEV adoption—measured as the annual net change in privately registered BEV stock—with respect to public rapid-charger stock is approximately 0.3. The effect is spatially heterogeneous—stronger in more deprived areas or those with better road-network connectivity, but weaker in rural areas or those with larger baseline charger stocks. It also weakens where on-street parking is widespread and home charging is consequently difficult, suggesting that public rapid-charging expansion may need complementary investment in non-rapid residential kerbside charging. These findings support geographically targeted public rapid-charger investment, an approach used in recent UK policies.

title: Sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules for the directed biosynthesis of 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid in Escherichia coli
summary: Abstract Bioconversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) confers advantages of mild conditions, high selectivity, and eco-friendliness. However, enzymatic catalysis is expensive and multi-strain microbial
content: Abstract Bioconversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) confers advantages of mild conditions, high selectivity, and eco-friendliness. However, enzymatic catalysis is expensive and multi-strain microbial catalysis is limited by the transmembrane transport of intermediates between strains, restricting the efficient synthesis of FDCA and generating a byproduct. In this study, we aimed to establish sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules in Escherichia coli to precisely control the expression of hydroxymethylfurfural oxidase (HMFO) and vanillin dehydrogenase (VDH1), enabling the directed one-pot conversion of HMF to FDCA with no detectable accumulation of the measured intermediates and simplifying the operational process. At a 15 mM HMF scale, this strategy achieved a FDCA yield of 100%, significantly higher than the 78.6% yield of the dual-enzyme cascade system established by HMFO and VDH1, and the 56.73% yield from the dual-strain catalysis constructed by two engineered E. coli strains that harbor either hmfo or vdh 1(Student’s t -test, p < 0.0001). Furthermore, at a laboratory scale (production of a fermentation broth containing 100 g of FDCA), life cycle assessment demonstrated sequential regulation of dual catalytic modules represented the lowest environmental impact among the three systems (dual-strain catalysis and dual-enzyme cascade). It reduced global warming potential, fossil fuel depletion, and ecotoxicity by 70–82% compared with the other two systems. Overall, this study establishes a more efficient and sustainable strategy for directed FDCA biosynthesis.

title: Chain Length, Unsaturation, and Conformational State Modulate ω-3 FFA Effects on POPC Bilayers
summary: Abstract Free fatty acids (FFAs), specifically the ω-3 forms α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are important modulators of lipid membrane structure and dynamics, yet how these three species
content: Abstract Free fatty acids (FFAs), specifically the ω-3 forms α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are important modulators of lipid membrane structure and dynamics, yet how these three species compare within a single, consistent framework remains unclear. Here, we employed atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the effects of ALA, EPA, and DHA (5–20 mol %) on 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) bilayers in single-FFA and mixed DHA/EPA systems. FFA incorporation induces concentration-dependent bilayer condensation, marked by decreased area and volume per lipid, increased thickness, and enhanced acyl chain order, with ALA producing the strongest effects. All three FFAs promote reorientation of POPC headgroups toward embedded FFA carboxyl groups. Using a conformational classification scheme (stretched, intermediate, coiled), we show that local ordering of neighboring POPC chains and the FFAs’ own ordering strongly depend on conformational state. FFAs exhibit higher lateral mobility than POPC. Passive transbilayer diffusion depends on FFA type and concentration; only ALA is nonmonotonic. In mixed DHA/EPA systems, lateral diffusion of EPA is enhanced relative to single-FFA systems, whereas passive diffusion of DHA is reduced. These results show that chain length and unsaturation mainly modulate FFA effects on bilayer structure and dynamics, whereas conformational state additionally shapes local acyl-chain ordering, relevant to membrane behavior under elevated and pathological FFA levels.

title: High resolution sentinel 2 mapping of rice residue burning areas and associated nutrient losses across India
summary: Post-harvest rice residue burning in India has important implications for air quality and soil nutrient retention, yet its spatial and temporal dynamics remain difficult to quantify because widely used burned-area products are relatively co
content: Post-harvest rice residue burning in India has important implications for air quality and soil nutrient retention, yet its spatial and temporal dynamics remain difficult to quantify because widely used burned-area products are relatively coarse for fragmented agricultural fields. This study provides a high-resolution, temporally resolved assessment of rice residue burning across India during the 2025 Kharif season. Sentinel-2 imagery was used to delineate rice-growing areas through spectral matching and to map the first detection of burned residue at 10-day intervals using an empirically selected threshold-separability rule. Image-interpreted Sentinel-2 reference points were used to assess spectral separability, while MODIS MCD64A1 was used for an inter-product comparison rather than as independent ground-truth validation. The analysis detected 8.33 million hectares of burned rice residue, with the five highest-burning states accounting for 72.1% of the national total. The typical burned area per district was highest in mid-November, whereas the number of districts reaching their peak first-detection interval was greatest in December. Estimated losses included 291,543 tonnes of nitrogen, 26,655 tonnes of phosphorus, 174,926 tonnes of potassium, 22,490 tonnes of sulphur and 19.99 million tonnes of organic carbon. The corresponding theoretical mass of CO₂ under complete oxidation of the estimated carbon was 73.30 million tonnes; this is not a CO₂-equivalent greenhouse-gas inventory. The nutrient-subsidy-equivalent valuation based on Government of India Nutrient-Based Subsidy rates was approximately INR 1430 crore, with a Monte Carlo median of approximately INR 1416 crore and a fixed burned-area 5th to 95th percentile sensitivity interval of INR 1023 to 1901 crore. About 31.3% of districts exceeding the analyst-defined 500-ha reporting cutoff accounted for 80% of the nutrient-subsidy-equivalent valuation. These results provide a season-specific spatial and temporal inventory of rice residue burning and identify areas where high-resolution monitoring may support targeted residue-management planning.

title: Synthesis of magnetic porous silica nanoparticles functionalized with folic acid for targeted drug delivery of quercetin
summary: Targeted drug delivery systems offer a promising strategy to enhance anticancer efficacy while minimizing systemic side effects. In this study, a multifunctional nanocarrier based on magnetic mesoporous silica nanoparticles was developed fo
content: Targeted drug delivery systems offer a promising strategy to enhance anticancer efficacy while minimizing systemic side effects. In this study, a multifunctional nanocarrier based on magnetic mesoporous silica nanoparticles was developed for the targeted delivery of quercetin. Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles were incorporated into mesoporous silica, followed by surface coating with polydopamine, conjugation of folic acid as a targeting ligand, and loading of quercetin. The successful stepwise modification of the nanoparticles was confirmed by FESEM, BET, FTIR, XRD, Zeta potential, PSA, and TGA analyses. The final formulation (Si-Fe-Q-D-F) exhibited a mesoporous structure with reduced pore size and surface area after drug loading and ligand conjugation. In vitro cytotoxicity evaluation using the MTT assay revealed that the drug-free carrier was highly biocompatible, whereas Si-Fe-Q-D-F showed superior anticancer activity against MCF-7 cells, with an IC₅₀ value of approximately 19 µg/mL after 48 h, significantly lower than that of free quercetin (57 µg/mL). The clonogenic assay further showed strong, dose-dependent inhibition of long-term colony formation by Si-Fe-Q-D-F. Moreover, the nanocarrier showed pH-responsive drug release, with accelerated quercetin release at pH 5.0 than at physiological pH. These findings indicate that folic acid-functionalized magnetic mesoporous silica nanoparticles are a promising multifunctional platform for targeted, controlled delivery of quercetin in breast cancer therapy.

title: Spring phenological timing modulates intra-annual growth: evidence of a seasonal advantage for early-flushing trees
summary: Abstract The timing of budburst is a key determinant of a tree’s fitness within its environment. While numerous studies have investigated the environmental drivers of phenology, less attention has been paid to how phenological traits influe
content: Abstract The timing of budburst is a key determinant of a tree’s fitness within its environment. While numerous studies have investigated the environmental drivers of phenology, less attention has been paid to how phenological traits influence individual tree performance within the forest. Here, we assessed at the individual-tree scale whether earlier budburst is associated with enhanced growth and how intra-annual growth dynamics differ between early- and late-flushing trees. We analyzed annual and intra-annual growth together with budburst phenology across the Spanish plots of the ICP Forests intensive monitoring network (Level II) representative of major forest ecosystems in Spain, which include Mediterranean and temperate forests. Annual growth data were obtained from 296 trees monitored over 28 years, while phenological observations covered 13 years and intra-annual growth 11 years for a subset of 127 trees. On average, trees with earlier budburst exhibited higher annual growth, and the relationship was positive in seven of the nine species, although it was individually significant only in Pinus sylvestris and P. pinaster , and the differences among species were not statistically conclusive. No significant relationship was found in P. halepensis , P. pinea , P. nigra , Quercus ilex , Q. suber , Q. petraea , or Fagus sylvatica ; in F. sylvatica the tendency was negative, possibly owing to its high sensitivity to late frosts. Neither leaf habit nor any single climatic or edaphic variable significantly modified the relationship, although the plots of the two species with a significant relationship all belonged to the group of cooler sites, and none of the species from the warmer and drier sites showed it. The seasonal course of growth differed between early- and late-flushing trees: the higher growth of early-flushing trees was not restricted to the onset of the growing season but extended over the whole growth period.

title: Removal of the antidepressant flupentixol from aqueous solution using jujube oil-based emulsion liquid membrane through hybrid optimization of RSM and ANN
summary: Recently, membrane-based separation gains significant attention among available water treatment technologies. Among the advanced techniques for wastewater treatment, emulsion liquid membranes (ELM) stand out, since it is environmentally fri
content: Recently, membrane-based separation gains significant attention among available water treatment technologies. Among the advanced techniques for wastewater treatment, emulsion liquid membranes (ELM) stand out, since it is environmentally friendly. In the present work, flupentixol (FL), an emergent micropollutant and antidepressant, was selected as the model pharmaceutical pollutant for removal using ELM system containing jujube oil (JJO-ELM). The primary effects and interactions of key independent variables, surfactant concentration (2–3 v/v %), carrier concentration (3–5 v/v %), concentration of stripping agent (HCl), (0.5–1.5 N), FL concentration (50–150 mg/L), and phase ratio (1:1–1:3 for water:JJO, respectively) were optimized using the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) design components. Optimized results showed that the ideal condition for the independent parameters, surfactant concentration; carrier concentration, HCl concentration, flupentixol concentration, and a phase ratio, respectively, were determined to be 2.41% v/v, 3.70% v/v, 0.52 N, 143.84 mg/L, and 1:1.5. The ideal condition could result in a maximum extraction efficiency of 97.40% FL. Further, the effectiveness of FL stripping was examined by adjusting the H 2 SO 4 concentration. Investigations were made into the mechanism of flupentixol extraction by JJO-ELM. The feed forward neural network (FNN) model, which has an output layer with one (flupentixol extraction) neuron and an input layer with five neurons, was used to simulate the extraction data. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Redox and Excited-State Modulation in Porphyrin Photosensitizers Controls H 2 Evolution at pH 7
summary: Abstract While ligand design for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution has attracted much attention, replacing rare elements with more abundant ones in molecular photosensitizers without losing photocatalytic efficacy remains challenging. The k
content: Abstract While ligand design for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution has attracted much attention, replacing rare elements with more abundant ones in molecular photosensitizers without losing photocatalytic efficacy remains challenging. The key is to obtain appropriate ground-state redox potentials and excited-state properties. We report a series of four new tetraanionic tin(IV)-porphyrin complexes bearing electron-donating or electron-withdrawing substituents and, compared to their zinc(II) analogues, systematically probed the influence of electronic effects on photocatalytic properties. Tin(IV) complexes proved more electron-poor than their Zn(II) analogues, resulting in distinct photocatalytic behavior. Under green light irradiation in pH 7.0 water/acetonitrile mixtures with a cobaloxime catalyst and a triethanolamine donor, the electron-rich octamethyl-substituted photosensitizer [Sn-MeP]4– achieved the highest photocatalytic turnover number of 430 molH2/molPS after 20-h irradiation and a maximum photocatalytic turnover frequency of 35 h–1 in the Sn series. Conversely, under identical conditions, the electron-poorest zinc(II) complex [Zn–F16P]4– yielded the best performance (photocatalytic turnover number of 850 and photocatalytic turnover frequency of 59 h–1). Notably, both series in this study operated via a reductive quenching pathway. This work establishes critical structure–property relationships and provides new insights into tuning excited-state redox chemistry in molecular photocatalytic systems based on earth-abundant elements.

title: Universal design as a framework for enhancing tourist friendly and well being oriented urban spaces in Luxor Egypt
summary: Urban spaces in heritage tourist cities play a central role in shaping visitors’ experience and supporting residents’ quality of life. In Luxor, Egypt, the performance of these spaces is strongly influenced by accessibility, environmental c
content: Urban spaces in heritage tourist cities play a central role in shaping visitors’ experience and supporting residents’ quality of life. In Luxor, Egypt, the performance of these spaces is strongly influenced by accessibility, environmental comfort, safety, and cultural legibility. This study investigates universal design as an integrative framework to enhance urban well-being and improve tourist experiences in heritage urban environments. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining a systematic literature review, analysis of international best practices, and empirical fieldwork. Primary data were collected through questionnaire surveys administered to 339 participants (55% visitors, 40% residents, 5% professionals) across two key urban areas: Railway Station Square and the surroundings of Luxor Temple, using a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistical analysis was applied to the survey data, including frequency distributions and mean score calculations. Independent-samples t-tests were used to compare perceptions between residents and tourists. Observational data were interpreted using universal design indicators. The findings reveal significant deficiencies: approximately 95% of respondents confirmed the lack of accessible infrastructure for all users, 88.2% reported the absence of adequate seating and shading, and approximately 82.4% considered street surfaces unsafe for movement. These deficiencies negatively influence perceived comfort, ease of movement, and overall user satisfaction. This study concludes that integrating universal design principles into heritage urban planning can substantially improve urban well-being and enhance the quality of the tourist experience, while supporting inclusive and sustainable development in culturally sensitive cities. Universal design improves accessibility and perceived urban well-being in heritage tourist cities. Empirical assessment of public spaces in Luxor reveals critical accessibility and comfort gaps. Findings support integrating inclusive design principles into heritage urban development strategies.

title: Slimming the fossil mammoth: financing defossilisation, from supply chains to end uses (Fossil Carbon Notebooks, Notebook 9)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Slimming the fossil mammoth: financing defossilisation, from supply chains to end uses. Fossil Carbon Notebooks, Notebook 9. Working version 0.9 This notebook quantifies, item by item, what defossilising the economy requires, and shows how
content: Slimming the fossil mammoth: financing defossilisation, from supply chains to end uses. Fossil Carbon Notebooks, Notebook 9. Working version 0.9 This notebook quantifies, item by item, what defossilising the economy requires, and shows how to finance it within the Geological Net Zero Pact. The pact aims to return to the subsurface, step by step, as much fossil carbon as is extracted. Producers and sellers of fossil carbon would be responsible for the carbon they extract and place on the market, including what they consume themselves. The notebook starts from 36.15 GtCO₂ of fossil emissions in 2024 (EDGAR) and divides them into five intervention families: distributed generation; transport; peaking plants; internal operations of the fossil fuel industries; power, heat and industry. For each item, a simple model separates the emissions that can be avoided from those that can be captured on the remaining flows. Across three scenarios, avoidance ranges from 8.9 to 20.8 GtCO₂ a year and the capture potential from 11.5 to 14.2 Gt. The central “balanced combination” scenario avoids 14.3 Gt and captures 14.2 Gt. The engine of the system: every tonne avoided at the customer’s site is carbon not extracted, for which the producer is no longer answerable and which it does not have to return to the subsurface. Within an appropriate framework, producers will therefore have an interest in co-financing any adaptation that avoids a tonne for less than the cost of a return, around $60–150 per tonne on the first capture and storage chains. The pact leads to three business models, aligned with the three carbon accounts of the founding article: Common infrastructure. A geological atlas, the characterisation of sequestration units and shared networks, financed by the Pact Fund: 110-115 billion dollars a year for an indicative levy of 3$/tCO₂ . The fossil obligation. It rises on a fixed timetable and is met by geological return or by co-financing customers’ energy transition. Removals. Durable storage of biogenic and atmospheric CO₂ in the same infrastructure, under separate accounting. Scaling up is the main challenge. Capture and storage capacity in operation today is 50–64 MtCO₂ a year, more than two hundred times below the central capture potential. The atlas and the characterisation of storage sites must therefore be financed early. Contents of this record: full and condensed versions, in French and English. Status: Working version 0.9, subject to revision; version 1.0 expected in December 2026. The document sets out a proposal and orders of magnitude, with no deployment timetable; it does not constitute investment advice. Related: GNZ Pact founding article, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24024055 · geologicalnetzero.org

title: Unravelling the Role of Oxygen Groups in Fe─N─C Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation
summary: ABSTRACT The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen‐doped carbon (TM‐N‐C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non‐precious‐metal proton‐exchange‐membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe‐doped MET(Zn)‐derived
content: ABSTRACT The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen‐doped carbon (TM‐N‐C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non‐precious‐metal proton‐exchange‐membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe‐doped MET(Zn)‐derived materials as a versatile platform, we unravel the role of oxygen groups in Fe‐N‐C catalyst degradation while achieving substantially enhanced fuel cell performance. DFT results indicate that carbonyl (C═O) and epoxy (C─O─C) groups lower the energy barrier of the rate‐determining step in the carbon oxidation reaction (COR), strengthen intermediate *OOH adsorption, and thereby accelerate carbon support corrosion. Based on this, a hydrogen‐thermal reduction strategy was developed to construct the Fe SA /NC‐H catalyst with low surface oxygen content. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding activity and stability of the Fe SA /NC‐H catalyst. In H 2 ‐O 2 PEMFCs, the catalyst achieves a peak power density ( P max ) of 1.32 W cm −2 , which is 1.26 times that of the reference catalyst (1.05 W cm −2 ). After 30 000 accelerated stress tests, Fe SA /NC‐H retains 77.3% of its initial P max , 1.56 times that of Fe SA /NC (49.5%). It also shows only 7.5% voltage decay during a 100 h open‐circuit voltage durability test.

title: A review of prediction and control methods on welding-induced distortions in large metallic structures
summary: Welding enables cost-effective fabrication of large structures in shipbuilding, aerospace and automotive industries, but repeated thermal cycles during multi-stage assembly inevitably cause distortions that often exceed design tolerances, d
content: Welding enables cost-effective fabrication of large structures in shipbuilding, aerospace and automotive industries, but repeated thermal cycles during multi-stage assembly inevitably cause distortions that often exceed design tolerances, degrading structural performance and requiring costly corrections. Despite significant advances in local weld modelling, predicting distortion in large, complex assemblies remains challenging due to interactions among material properties, structural geometry, heat input, welding sequence and restraint conditions, particularly for lightweight, thin-walled high-strength steels and aluminium alloys. This review synthesises research from 2000 to 2025 to assess distortion prediction and mitigation strategies for large metallic structures, emphasising industrial applicability. Thermo-elasto-plastic finite element methods provide high accuracy but at significant computational cost and inherent strain-based approaches offer efficient large-scale simulations but rely on calibration and simplifying assumptions, while local/global methods balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Data-driven surrogate models are emerging for rapid prediction and optimisation. No single approach is universally transferable across structural configurations, with scalability generally achieved at the expense of calibration requirements and application-specific assumptions. Distortion mitigation is most effective at the design stage through welding sequence optimisation and structural planning. In-process techniques such as thermal tensioning and controlled restraint further reduce distortions, while post-welding corrections remain less efficient. The literature is strongly concentrated on conventional structural steels, with only approximately 10% and 1% of the reviewed references addressing large aluminium and high-strength steel structures, respectively. Overall, major limitations concern scalability, standardisation and data availability, highlighting the need for integrated physics-based and data-driven frameworks for efficient large-scale distortion control. Graphical Abstract

title: Effect of water management on nitrous oxide emission and heterotrophic soil respiration from drained grassland on peat soil
summary: Abstract Raising groundwater levels in drained peatlands used for dairy farming aims to reduce peat decomposition, land subsidence and associated carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. However, higher groundwater levels also affect soil biological
content: Abstract Raising groundwater levels in drained peatlands used for dairy farming aims to reduce peat decomposition, land subsidence and associated carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. However, higher groundwater levels also affect soil biological nitrogen (N) transformations by decreasing N mineralization and influencing microbial processes such as nitrification and denitrification, which may affect nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions. This creates a potential trade-off, where reduced peat mineralization and CO₂ release may coincide with higher N₂O emissions. We quantified the effects of ditch water level and water infiltration systems (WIS) on N₂O emissions from peat grassland in a five-year field experiment in the Netherlands. Four peat grassland fields differed in ditch water level (20 vs 55 cm below the soil surface) and were subdivided into control without infiltration, passive WIS (PWIS) and active WIS (AWIS) treatments. N₂O fluxes were measured weekly using closed chambers and gap-filled with a generalized additive model. Averaged over five years, deep ditch levels resulted in higher dry matter yield (10.3 vs 8.8 t DM ha ⁻1 yr ⁻1 ) and plant N uptake (282 vs 241 kg N ha ⁻1 yr ⁻1 ), indicating higher N turnover. Annual cumulative N₂O emissions were also higher under deep ditch conditions (3.6 vs 1.9 kg N₂O–N ha ⁻1 yr ⁻1 ), whereas WIS had no significant effect on N 2 O emissions. In contrast, heterotrophic soil respiration was reduced by 10% under PWIS and 20% under AWIS compared to the control. These findings show that raising ditch water levels can reduce N₂O emissions by up to 47%, offering a promising water management strategy to mitigate N₂O losses with only minor yield penalties.

title: Role of cold storage in preservation of fruits and vegetables in India
summary: India, one of the world's largest producers of fruits and vegetables, continues to suffer from significant post-harvest losses estimated at 20-35%, primarily due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure, poor handling, and fragmented supply
content: India, one of the world's largest producers of fruits and vegetables, continues to suffer from significant post-harvest losses estimated at 20-35%, primarily due to inadequate cold chain infrastructure, poor handling, and fragmented supply chains.Cold storage infrastructure serves as a critical component in maintaining the quality, safety, and longevity of perishable commodities by regulating temperature, humidity, and atmospheric composition.This review synthesizes global and Indian cold storage trends, explains the technical functioning of refrigeration systems, evaluates economic feasibility, and highlights major gaps in existing infrastructure.India's cold storage capacity is heavily skewed toward potatoes (over 60%), revealing commodity and regional imbalance.Despite substantial governmental interventions through NHB, PMKSY, MSME, and NABARD schemes, infrastructural deficits remain-particularly in pack houses (99% gap) and reefer vehicles (84% gap).Emerging sustainable technologies, such as solar-based and biomass-driven cold storage, demonstrate promising solutions for regions with unreliable power supply.Case studies from Telangana, Gujarat, Bihar, and Karnataka show that decentralized cold storage systems significantly reduce losses, improve market timing, and enhance farmer incomes.The review concludes that strengthening cold chain infrastructure is essential for increasing farmer profitability, improving national food security, and reducing wastage within the agricultural value chain.

title: Selectively VO2-loaded terahertz metasurface for dual-state broadband polarization conversion and near-unity absorption
summary: A selectively VO 2 -loaded terahertz metasurface is studied for dual-state polarization conversion and absorption. The ground-backed unit cell consists of a broken diamond-shaped Au resonator, two square VO 2 loading regions, a circular VO
content: A selectively VO 2 -loaded terahertz metasurface is studied for dual-state polarization conversion and absorption. The ground-backed unit cell consists of a broken diamond-shaped Au resonator, two square VO 2 loading regions, a circular VO 2 ring, and a polyimide spacer. With VO 2 in the insulating conductivity state, the structure operates as a reflective cross-polarization converter. PCR x remains above 0.90 from 1.5150 to 2.5849 THz, while PCRγ exceeds 0.90 from 1.5270 to 2.6726 THz. In the metallic conductivity state, A x remains above 0.90 from 1.5700 to 1.9970 THz and reaches 0.9997 at 1.8050 THz. At this frequency, the normalized impedance is 0.970 − j 0.014, and VO 2 accounts for 97.14% of the dissipated power. The conversion mechanism is supported by polarization-resolved reflection, rotated-axis phase response, and asymmetric current paths. The absorber state is associated with reflection suppression, resonator-ground coupling, and loss in the metallic VO 2 regions. Four-pass and six-pass mesh solutions differ by less than 1% in the principal response measures. Angular and tolerance analyses further show that the main features of both operating states are retained under the investigated conditions. The results numerically demonstrate dual-state terahertz operation through conductivity-state switching of selectively loaded VO 2 within a single planar unit cell.

title: Adsorption-controlled electrooxidation of ensartinib at a nanostructured Al2O3–MWCNT electrode: first electrochemical insights
summary: The electrochemical behavior of the recently approved anticancer drug ensartinib (ENS) was investigated for the first time at a carbon paste electrode incorporating Al 2 O 3 –MWCNT nanostructures. A distinct anodic signal was observed, with
content: The electrochemical behavior of the recently approved anticancer drug ensartinib (ENS) was investigated for the first time at a carbon paste electrode incorporating Al 2 O 3 –MWCNT nanostructures. A distinct anodic signal was observed, with the voltammetric response indicating an irreversible oxidation event. Variation of the scan rate produced a proportional increase in peak current, supporting adsorption as the predominant process controlling the electrode reaction. Changes in solution pH were accompanied by systematic displacement of the oxidation potential, suggesting involvement of proton transfer during electron oxidation. Modification of the carbon paste surface with the Al 2 O 3 –MWCNT nanostructure increased the measured ENS response, which was attributed to enhanced interfacial adsorption and more efficient electron-transfer kinetics. These electrochemical characteristics were subsequently used to develop a differential pulse voltammetric procedure for ENS quantification at micromolar concentration levels. The method showed satisfactory analytical performance when applied to pharmaceutical formulations and spiked plasma samples. The findings establish the electrochemical oxidation characteristics of ENS at the modified electrode and demonstrate its suitability as the basis for voltammetric determination in the investigated matrices.

title: EVALUATING THE ENERGY EFFICIENCY FRONTIERS OF CLOUD DATA CENTERS: A SLACK-BASED WINDOW DATA ENVELOPMENT ANALYSIS (DEA) APPROACH
source: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
summary: Cloud data centers underpin the global digital economy, yet the surge in generative-AI training, deep-learning inference, hyperscale virtualization and edge caching is pushing up their electricity demand, straining local grids and raising g
content: Cloud data centers underpin the global digital economy, yet the surge in generative-AI training, deep-learning inference, hyperscale virtualization and edge caching is pushing up their electricity demand, straining local grids and raising greenhousegas emissions.Judging how well these capital-intensive sites turn resources into useful computing therefore calls for a quantitative framework that handles several inputs at once, credits computational output, penalizes by-product emissions that cannot be separated from production, and follows facilities across time.Conventional radial Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) falls short here: it shrinks every input by the same proportion, overlooks slack in individual resources and has no physically consistent way to treat pollutants.This chapter combines the Charnes-Cooper-Rhodes (CCR) and Banker-Charnes-Cooper (BCC) envelopment models with a non-radial Slack-Based Measure (SBM) applied in a moving-window design.The model is demonstrated on a synthetic, illustrative panel of ten facilities observed over four annual periods (forty facility-years), constructed for methodological demonstration rather than drawn from measured operator data.Each facility uses three inputs (total energy consumption, infrastructure capital expenditure and Power Usage Effectiveness), one desirable output (standardized computational throughput) and one undesirable output (carbon footprint).The analysis isolates input-specific excesses, quantifies the upward bias of radial scores, separates technical from scale efficiency, reports peer-intensity weights and derives catch-up and frontier-shift indices.In the illustrative panel, sites that combine direct-to-chip or immersion liquid cooling with fully renewable power contracts define the best-practice frontier, while legacy sites with downflow air conditioning waste roughly 24% to 35% of their energy input as non-radial slack.The chapter closes with a tiered matrix of engineering retrofits and regulatory options for greener digital infrastructure.

title: Recovery and reuse of alkaline battery residues for Ti/RuO2-MnO2-ZnO electrode synthesis and electrochemical degradation of venlafaxine
summary: Electrochemical Advanced Oxidation Processes (EAOPs) have emerged as promising technologies for the removal of emerging contaminants in aquatic environments. The technical and environmental feasibility of these processes strongly depends on
content: Electrochemical Advanced Oxidation Processes (EAOPs) have emerged as promising technologies for the removal of emerging contaminants in aquatic environments. The technical and environmental feasibility of these processes strongly depends on the selection and application of efficient, stable, and sustainable anode materials. This study reports the development of mixed metal oxides (MMOs) anodes supported on metallic titanium, using MnO 2 and ZnO nanomaterials obtained from metals recovered from alkaline batteries, and their application for venlafaxine degradation. The structural properties of the synthesized electrodes were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), which confirmed the formation of the oxides (i.e., RuO 2 , ZnO, and MnO 2 ) used in producing the binary and ternary MMOs evaluated in this study: Ti/(RuO 2 ) 70 -(ZnO) 30 , Ti/(RuO 2 ) 70 -(MnO 2 ) 30 and Ti/(RuO 2 ) 30 -(MnO 2 ) 35 -(ZnO) 35 . Electrochemical characterization revealed that the ternary anode, composed of ZnO, MnO 2 and RuO 2 , exhibited a higher electroactive surface area and improved stability compared to the binary anodes. The electrocatalytic performance of the anodes was evaluated during the electrochemical oxidation of venlafaxine, where the ternary anode Ti/RuO 2 -MnO 2 -ZnO recorded the highest degradation (99%) and mineralization (99%) rates after 90 min of electrolysis. These findings point to a reliable and sustainable route for the production of MMOs derived from recycled metals in alkaline batteries, highlighting their great application potential for the treatment of water and wastewater containing pharmaceutical pollutants.

title: Experimental and finite element analysis of coupled electro-thermal responses of concrete-encased grounding electrodes under lightning impulses
summary: Grounding systems are critical for maintaining the safety and transient stability of high-voltage and smart-grid infrastructure subjected to lightning-current impulses. This study presents an integrated experimental and three-dimensional fi
content: Grounding systems are critical for maintaining the safety and transient stability of high-voltage and smart-grid infrastructure subjected to lightning-current impulses. This study presents an integrated experimental and three-dimensional finite element method (FEM) investigation of conventional copper-bonded steel rod and concrete-encased grounding electrodes under standardized 8/20 µs impulse-current conditions. Laboratory experiments were conducted using an impulse-current generator with a maximum current capability of 1.5 kA, while a COMSOL Multiphysics model was developed and validated against the experimentally accessible current range and subsequently used to investigate higher-current conditions numerically. Three representative soil types of clay, sandy loam, and gravel were considered to evaluate transient impedance, ground potential rise (GPR), current-density distribution, soil-ionization behavior, and electro-thermal response. Experimentally, the concrete-encased configuration reduced impulse impedance by approximately 33–49% across the investigated soils. FEM analysis showed a reduction in peak current density from 69 to 43 A/m², corresponding to approximately 38%, together with a larger effective current-conduction region. Numerical predictions at higher current levels indicated delayed soil-ionization onset and lower temperature rise for the encased configuration compared with the conventional rod. These high-current results are identified as FEM predictions rather than direct experimental measurements because they exceed the 1.5 kA capability of the laboratory generator. The validated experimental numerical framework demonstrates the potential of conductive concrete encasement to improve impulse-current dispersion and reduce localized electrical and thermal stress in grounding electrodes. Further high-current experimental validation is required to confirm the predicted behavior beyond the laboratory test range.

title: Plasmonic Lightning‐Rod Effect
summary: ABSTRACT The plasmonic lightning‐rod effect refers to the formation of a strong electric near field of localized surface plasmons at the sharp features of plasmonic antennas. Although this effect is intuitively utilized in the design and op
content: ABSTRACT The plasmonic lightning‐rod effect refers to the formation of a strong electric near field of localized surface plasmons at the sharp features of plasmonic antennas. Although this effect is intuitively utilized in the design and optimization of plasmonic antennas, the relation between the magnitude of the electric field and the local curvature of the plasmonic antenna has not yet been rigorously established. Here, we provide such a study. We design sets of plasmonic antennas that allow us to isolate the role of the local curvature from other effects influencing the field. The electric near field is inspected by electron energy‐loss spectroscopy and electrodynamic simulations. We confirm the existence of the plasmonic lightning‐rod effect, demonstrate its decoupling from concurrent effects influencing the field, and establish its quantitative description, showing that its strength can be interpreted as comparable to that of the electrostatic lightning‐rod effect. We also provide a simple empirical formula for the spatial dependence of the field, which includes the effective radius of curvature significantly smaller than the geometrical radius.

title: Role of phycospheric bacteria: Promoting the growth of Isochrysis zhanjiangensis and ammonia nitrogen removal in rearing water
summary: Isochrysis zhanjiangensis is crucial in the breeding of bivalves larval as an artificially cultivated feed microalga. To investigate their roles in algal–bacterial interactions, two phycospheric bacterial strains, Halomonas piezotolerans an
content: Isochrysis zhanjiangensis is crucial in the breeding of bivalves larval as an artificially cultivated feed microalga. To investigate their roles in algal–bacterial interactions, two phycospheric bacterial strains, Halomonas piezotolerans and Alteromonas abrolhosensis , were isolated from I. zhanjiangensis and examined their effects on algal growth and ammonia nitrogen removal in aquaculture systems. The results indicated that both strains promoted the growth of I. zhanjiangensis ; with the A. abrolhosensis showing the stronger effect. At a concentration of 10⁸ cfu/mL, the A. abrolhosensis treatment reached a cell density of 1.082 × 10⁷ cells/mL on day 10, 16.22% higher than the control ( p < 0.05). Chlorophyll a content in this group was 4.985 μg/L (a 43.62% increase vs. control; p < 0.05), and the total polysaccharide content was 8.366 g/L (a 59.90% increase; p < 0.05). H. piezotolerans at a concentration of 10⁶ cfu/mL increased the soluble protein by 4.65% ( p > 0.05), and promoted soluble p rotein synthesis at lower inoculation levels. In ammonia nitrogen removal experiments, H. piezotolerans exhibited more stable and pronounced activity, while A. abrolhosensis also contributed to nitrogen reduction. Quantitative PCR (qRT-PCR) showed upregulation of nirB and nosZ genes in H. piezotolerans , and increased expression of nirB , glnG , glnL , and glnA in A. abrolhosensis , supporting their potential roles in ammonia nitrogen transformation. This study demonstrates that phycospheric bacteria isolated from I. zhanjiangensis promote algal growth and facilitate ammonia nitrogen removal during bivalves larval rearing. These results provide new insights into bacteria–algae interactions and indicate practical implications for enhancing algal productivity and maintaining environmental stability in hatchery systems.

title: Elevated early Eocene atmospheric CO2 tied to reduced Southern Ocean biological pump efficiency
summary: Abstract The Early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO) was an interval in Earth’s history when reconstructed temperatures and atmospheric CO2 concentrations were among the highest of the Cenozoic Era (i.e., the last 66 million years). The causes
content: Abstract The Early Eocene Climatic Optimum (EECO) was an interval in Earth’s history when reconstructed temperatures and atmospheric CO2 concentrations were among the highest of the Cenozoic Era (i.e., the last 66 million years). The causes of the high CO2 levels remain unclear. The Southern Ocean, a major “leak” in the global ocean’s biological carbon pump that has been implicated in the CO2 changes over recent ice age cycles, may also have played a role earlier in the Cenozoic. Here, we report foraminifera-bound δ15N measurements that show higher surface nitrate concentrations in the Southern Ocean during peak EECO. The associated venting of CO2 from the deep ocean to the atmosphere would have been amplified by the low seawater pH buffering capacity of the Eocene. Previously proposed low silicate rock weatherability during the Eocene may have weakened the “weathering thermostat”, allowing the reconstructed change in biological pump efficiency in the Southern Ocean to explain at least half of the atmospheric CO2 increase observed during the EECO.

title: Profiling of RNA 8-oxoG marks in Escherichia coli identifies critical intrinsic characteristics that contribute to 8-oxoG accumulation in bacteria
summary: Abstract Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are environmentally ubiquitous and known to have pervasive impacts on cellular homeostasis. RNA is vulnerable to oxidative chemical alterations from a variety of endogenous and exogenous sources. The m
content: Abstract Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are environmentally ubiquitous and known to have pervasive impacts on cellular homeostasis. RNA is vulnerable to oxidative chemical alterations from a variety of endogenous and exogenous sources. The most common chemical modification resulting from ROS exposure to RNA is 8-oxo-7,8-dihydroguanine (8-oxoG)—an oxidized form of the canonical guanine (G) nucleobase. While 8-oxoG modifications are known to impact mRNA processing, understanding the broader biological impact of 8-oxoG requires knowledge of how these modifications accumulate. In this work, we assessed the disparate enrichment of 8-oxoG modifications within RNAs in the E. coli transcriptome using an RNA Immunoprecipitation Sequencing technique with a high-affinity 8-oxoG antibody (8-oxoG-RIP-Seq). Our investigation of the RNA 8-oxoG enrichment landscape uncovered several intrinsic RNA characteristics that correlate with 8-oxoG enrichment. These findings suggest intrinsic characteristics of RNA, most notably relative abundance, CDS length, and G nucleotide composition, significantly influence RNA 8-oxoG accumulation. We harnessed these intrinsic characteristics to construct a simple multiple linear regression model that predicts RNA 8-oxoG accumulation, which we validated in E. coli . This model was subsequently applied to predict 8-oxoG enriched RNA species in four other bacterial species spanning a wide range of oxidative stress tolerances; these predictions suggest that 8-oxoG accumulation is largely species dependent, with limited overlap in RNAs and functional pathways that are more susceptible to elevated levels of 8-oxoG accumulation. Overall, these findings better inform understanding of RNA 8-oxoG patterns in bacteria and have broader impacts towards advancing knowledge of the connection between RNA oxidation and cellular homeostasis.

title: Band geometric transverse current driven by inhomogeneous ac electric field
summary: We develop a semiclassical theory for electron wavepacket dynamics in the presence of an inhomogeneous AC electric field. While static electric-field gradients are known to generate charge transport governed by the quantum metric, we show t
content: We develop a semiclassical theory for electron wavepacket dynamics in the presence of an inhomogeneous AC electric field. While static electric-field gradients are known to generate charge transport governed by the quantum metric, we show that AC field gradients induce an additional geometric current that vanishes in the DC limit. This response originates from a novel band-geometric quantity, the higher-order connection (HOC) tensor, constructed from cubic products of interband Berry connections. We derive explicit expressions for the AC current and identify the symmetry conditions under which it arises. Remarkably, inhomogeneous AC fields can generate an anomalous Hall-like response even in nonmagnetic systems. Applying the theory to Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene, we demonstrate that the HOC-induced response produces a measurable Hall current peaking at band edges. These results establish inhomogeneous AC fields as a powerful probe of higher-order band geometric quantities beyond Berry curvature and the quantum metric.

title: Earth system modelling of mercury using CESM2 – Part 3: Oceanic model POP2/Hg v1.0
summary: Abstract. Mercury (Hg) is a globally distributed toxicant with complex cycling in the ocean, involving redox reactions, air–sea exchange, and microbial methylation. We present POP-Hg v1.0, a new global ocean mercury model developed within t
content: Abstract. Mercury (Hg) is a globally distributed toxicant with complex cycling in the ocean, involving redox reactions, air–sea exchange, and microbial methylation. We present POP-Hg v1.0, a new global ocean mercury model developed within the ocean component of CESM2 (POP2) and coupled to the Marine Biogeochemistry Library (MARBL). POP2/Hg v1.0 simulates dissolved elemental Hg (Hg0), oxidized Hg (HgII), particulate-bound Hg (Hgp), and Methylmercury (MeHg = MMHg + DMHg), linking their transformation to ecosystem processes and dynamics of particulate organic carbon (POC). The model captures observed large-scale features of marine Hg. Surface Hg0 concentrations range from 10 to 120 fmol L-1(fM, 1 fM = 10-15 mol L-1) and are elevated in tropical and subtropical oceans due to strong photoreduction and limited evasion. Subsurface Hg0 maxima emerge in upwelling zones, reflecting remineralization-driven HgII reduction. Surface HgII concentrations peak in regions of high atmospheric deposition and productivity and rise at depth in oxygen-deficient zones. Hgp is closely associated with high POC and HgII levels in the surface ocean but attenuates rapidly with depth due to remineralization. MeHg accumulates in the subsurface and deep sea, broadly consistent with observations. Total Hg (HgT) ranges to above 2.0 pmol L-1 (pM, 1 pM = 10-12 mol L-1) in the surface, with open-ocean surface concentrations matching measurements. Deep-ocean HgT accumulation reflects sustained particle flux and remineralization. The biological pump strongly shapes vertical Hg transport. Above 1000 m, soft POC carries 98.6 % of Hgp flux, driving export and remineralization. Below 1000 m, hard POC becomes the dominant carrier, contributing over 99 % of Hgp flux to sediments, although the total flux is small (0.19 t yr-1). Sensitivity tests show that altering redox rates significantly affects the vertical distribution of Hg transformations. Reduced surface reduction and oxidation rates suppress Hg⁰ production in the upper ocean, weaken seasonal variability, and shift net reduction deeper into the water column. By embedding mercury chemistry into a fully coupled biogeochemical and physical ocean model, POP2/Hg v1.0 offers a process-resolving platform for assessing mercury cycling and its response to environmental change. It enables integrated Earth system simulations and improves predictive capacity for marine mercury under future climate and policy scenarios.

title: Multiomics Integration Reveals a Skeletal Muscle Metabolic Myopathy in Cardiometabolic HFpEF
summary: Background: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to b
content: Background: Skeletal muscle dysfunction is a major peripheral determinant of exercise intolerance and physical disability in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). Metabolic and mitochondrial dysfunction are considered to be key components of skeletal muscle dysfunction, but comprehensive profiling of metabolic pathways has not been conducted. Elucidation of dysregulated metabolic pathways is essential to determine viable targets for the treatment of exercise intolerance in HFpEF. Methods: was used to determine differential expression in all omics layers (absolute fold-change>1.5, FDR0.05, unless otherwise indicated). Additional targeted plasma and skeletal muscle (soleus and EDL) metabolomics and lipidomics were performed on HFpEF and control rats. Results: Pathway level analysis for RNA seq and proteomics revealed significant downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (NES -2.1, p<0.005), electron transport chain (NES -2.0, p<0.005), and TCA cycle (-1.8, p<0.05). The most upregulated pathways were PPAR signaling (NES 2.2, p<0.0001), tryptophan metabolism (NES 1.8, P<0.005), and amino acid oxidation (NES 1.8, p<0.005) pathways. Metabolomics revealed an accumulation of TCA cycle intermediate, isocitrate, and phosphate reduction. Branched-chain amino acids were significantly increased, whereas amino acids related to tryptophan metabolism were reduced and shifted towards increased serotonin accumulation. Phospholipid species were differentially regulated with increased palmitoylated phosphatidylcholines but reduced arachidonoyl-PC species. Phosphatidylethanolamines (PE) species (16:0/16:1-18:0/18:2) were increased. Conclusion: Our multiomics analysis of skeletal muscle in HFpEF revealed severe mitochondrial dysfunction that was characterized by reduced complex I and II activity. Mitochondrial and peroxisomal lipid overload results in a shift in membrane phospholipid accumulation and composition. Reduced BCAA oxidation and dysregulation of tryptophan metabolism are key features of amino acid metabolism that reduce anaplerosis and promote the accumulation of toxic metabolites. Comparative analysis of other skeletal muscle disorders suggests that an acquired metabolic myopathy exists in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

title: Tidal Encounters of Close White Dwarf Binaries with Spinning Black Holes
summary: Abstract When a stellar binary encounters a spinning black hole (BH), interesting phenomena might result due to the mutual interaction between the binary spin, orbital angular momentum (OAM), and the BH spin. Here, we consider such encounte
content: Abstract When a stellar binary encounters a spinning black hole (BH), interesting phenomena might result due to the mutual interaction between the binary spin, orbital angular momentum (OAM), and the BH spin. Here, we consider such encounters between an intermediate-mass spinning black hole and a close identical white dwarf binary system whose center of mass (CM) follows a parabolic trajectory. After studying a corresponding three-body problem in the point-particle approximation, we perform a suite of smoothed-particle-hydrodynamics-based numerical simulations of such scenarios. For this, we integrate the geodesic equations for the spinning BH, while considering the hydrodynamics and the self- and mutual gravitational interactions of the stars in a Newtonian approximation, an approach justified by the choice of parameters in the theory. We consider various initial configurations of the binary CM leading to equatorial and off-equatorial orbits, as also various initial inclinations between the binary’s initial spin angular momentum and its initial OAM. We find that the effects of BH spin manifest in the tidal dynamics of the binary components, while the observables of tidal encounters such as mass fallback rates are strongly dependent on the initial inclination angle. We show that the influence of the BH spin emerges in distinct ways for different initial configurations of the binary’s spin alignment. We establish that, within the ambit of the Hills mechanism, in certain cases, the fallback rate may show a three-hump structure, due to interactions between the tidal debris of the individual stars.

title: Assessing the adaptation between recreational fisheries development and aquaculture efficiency in multifunctional freshwater fisheries systems: Evidence from China
summary: Abstract To examine the synergy quality and potential mismatch risks between production and recreational functions during the multifunctional transformation of freshwater fisheries, this study constructs a composite index of recreational fi
content: Abstract To examine the synergy quality and potential mismatch risks between production and recreational functions during the multifunctional transformation of freshwater fisheries, this study constructs a composite index of recreational fisheries development using panel data from 29 Chinese provinces during 2008–2023. Freshwater aquaculture efficiency is measured using a benevolent cross-efficiency model incorporating both desirable and undesirable outputs. An integrated adaptation model is then employed to capture the spatiotemporal differentiation of the adaptation relationship between the two systems, while Random Forest and SHAP methods are applied to identify nonlinear effects and threshold characteristics of key drivers. The results indicate that: (1) both recreational fisheries development and aquaculture efficiency increased steadily over the study period, whereas the composite adaptation index remained at low-to-medium levels with limited stage-wise improvement, suggesting that efficiency gains have not been effectively translated into recreational advantages; (2) the adaptation pattern exhibits pronounced regional differentiation and path dependence, characterized by persistently higher levels in central China, gradual improvement in eastern China, increasing polarization in western China, and consistently low and weakening adaptation in northeastern China; and (3) the driving mechanisms are markedly nonlinear, with water environmental pressure and tourism reception intensity acting as key constraints. Specifically, water quality pressure shows an inverted U-shaped effect with clear thresholds, while tourism intensity exerts a sustained inhibitory impact. This study provides empirical evidence for incorporating adaptation relationships into fisheries transformation assessments and for region-specific optimization of industrial structure and spatial allocation.

title: Mid-infrared high-sensitive cavity-free in-situ CO gas sensing based on up-conversion detection
summary: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a significant indicator gas with considerable application value in atmospheric monitoring, industrial production and medical diagnosis. Its fundamental vibrational band locates around 4.6 $\upmu$m and has larger abso
content: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a significant indicator gas with considerable application value in atmospheric monitoring, industrial production and medical diagnosis. Its fundamental vibrational band locates around 4.6 $\upmu$m and has larger absorption line strength than that of overtone band, which is more suitable for the precise identification and concentration detection of CO. In this paper, the up-conversion detection is employed to convert the mid-infrared absorption signal obtained by TDLAS to the visible light band, then a silicon-based detector is utilized for detection. By which, we can achieve the highest sensitivity of 79.6 ppb under the condition of cavity-free in-situ with an absorption range length of only 0.14 m. Furthermore, the single-photon level real-time detection of CO concentration after the diffuse reflection is realized by using SPAD. This work demonstrates the merits of the up-conversion detection in terms of its functionality at room temperature and capacity for sensitivity detection. Furthermore, it presents a design and optimization methodology that has the potential to underpin the advancement of the method towards more practical applications, like industrial process monitoring, medical diagnosis and so on.

title: Sustainable crop production under future climates: national mapping of cover-crop rotations and soil organic carbon–N2O trade-offs
summary: Abstract Sustainable crop production increasingly depends on rotation designs that raise productivity while lowering reactive nitrogen (N) losses and net greenhouse gases. We conduct a national, spatial analysis for Germany, evaluating dive
content: Abstract Sustainable crop production increasingly depends on rotation designs that raise productivity while lowering reactive nitrogen (N) losses and net greenhouse gases. We conduct a national, spatial analysis for Germany, evaluating diversified 4-year rotations with alternating legume/non-legume cover crops (CCs) under future climates (RCP4.5/8.5, six GCMs). Using the DSSAT crop–soil model coupled to dynamic Tier-2 N₂O accounting (driven by DSSAT-simulated fertilizer, residue, and leached N), we map impacts on yield, N use efficiency (NUE), N leaching, ΔSOC, and net GHG relative to business-as-usual rotations. Across the ensemble, legume-inclusive CC sequences increase cereal yields by ~16–33% (zone-dependent), improve NUE, and reduce N leaching by ~40%. Systems accrue additional SOC but approach plateaus over decades; N₂O responses are climate- and soil-contingent, yet the net GHG footprint falls by ~35–45% on average through 2099 when ΔSOC and direct + indirect N₂O are jointly considered. Accounting for upstream seed and diesel for CCs may slightly attenuates (but does not negate) the net benefit. Spatial “leverage maps” reveal where rotation redesign most robustly delivers the triad of higher production, lower N losses, and lower net GHG, and where trade-offs persist. Results provide policy-ready evidence that targeted, legume-inclusive cover-crop rotations can advance cleaner crop production in temperate regions under changing climate.

title: Self-foaming Fe–Sn powder beds for durable hydrogen storage and release
summary: Abstract Hydrogen storage and release via redox cycling of oxide-metal powders offers advantages in safety and scalability as compared to pressurized tanks, but long-term storage capacity loss due to sintering and densification of powder be
content: Abstract Hydrogen storage and release via redox cycling of oxide-metal powders offers advantages in safety and scalability as compared to pressurized tanks, but long-term storage capacity loss due to sintering and densification of powder beds remains a major challenge. In this work, we demonstrate that a transient liquid-phase swelling effect, triggered by the addition of a low-melting element to a high-melting powder bed, can effectively preserve powder-bed porosity and reactive surface area during extended redox cycling. By incorporating up to 40 at. % Sn into Fe powder beds, we induce a self-foaming behavior that counteracts powder densification and enables stable hydrogen storage/release performance over 50 redox cycles at 650 ºC. In situ X-ray diffraction and thermodynamic analysis reveal that both the added Sn and the resulting Fe-Sn intermetallic phase undergo reversible transformations throughout cycling, helping maintain high hydrogen storage/release capacity. Microstructural analysis shows that the continuous formation of “liquid-depletion porosity” at former Sn powder sites and the volumetric expansion of solid particles from imbalanced diffusion contribute to the retention of a porous architecture. This strategy achieves a hydrogen capacity of up to 261 mL/g, which is 22 times higher than that of pure Fe after 50 redox cycles. It provides a new materials design approach for durable metal/oxide systems in hydrogen storage, with other potential applications in solar thermochemical water splitting, carbon dioxide utilization,and chemical looping technologies.

title: From Accurate Quantum Chemistry to Converged Thermodynamics for Ion Pairing in Solution
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to und
content: Abstract Quantitative prediction of thermodynamic properties in solution is essential for translating atomistic simulations into reliable chemical insight. As an exemplar system, the behavior of CaCO3 in water has been widely studied to understand its mineralization in seawater, with potential implications for carbon-capture strategies. However, making accurate computational predictions has been a long-standing challenge, requiring both highly accurate electronic structure methods and extensive statistical sampling. Here, we combine advances in machine learning and electronic structure theory to fully resolve the ion pairing free energy of CaCO3 with explicit solvation. We show that achieving quantitative agreement with experiment requires going beyond density functional theory up to the “gold-standard” coupled cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]. We generate a set of systematically improvable models, enabling reliable insights into the initial association mechanism of Ca and CO3 ions prior to nucleation while fully quantifying enthalpic and entropic effects. These quantitatively accurate models further resolve a long-standing lack of consensus surrounding the hydration mechanism of the calcium ion in solution. Our results demonstrate that CCSD(T)-level thermodynamic predictions of complex aqueous systems can now be routinely achieved.

title: Calculation of the impacts of aerosols on cloud microphysical properties by combining ground- and space-based measurements
summary: Abstract. The effect of aerosols on cloud properties remains poorly constrained, in part because ground-based measurements are highly local while space-based retrievals are spatially imprecise. Here, we show how the two viewpoints can be co
content: Abstract. The effect of aerosols on cloud properties remains poorly constrained, in part because ground-based measurements are highly local while space-based retrievals are spatially imprecise. Here, we show how the two viewpoints can be combined using colocated surface aerosol measurements and thermodynamic profiling from the peri-urban ATOLL (ATmospheric Observatory in LiLLe) site and geostationary-satellite cloud microphysical retrievals from the SEVIRI instrument. Focusing on low-level stratiform clouds that formed under thermodynamically stable conditions, we relate cloud properties to aerosol light scattering as a proxy for cloud condensation nucleus concentrations for two cloud liquid water path bins of 20–100 and 100–200 g m–2. Relative changes of cloud droplet number concentrations and effective radii are compared to relative changes in aerosol light scattering coefficient to find respective susceptibilities. The susceptibility of the cloud droplet number concentration to the aerosol scattering coefficient (Sn), also called nucleation efficiency, is retrieved around 0.29 for LWP (Liquid Water Path, from 20 to 100 g m-2) and around 0.30 for higher LWP (between 100 to 200 g m-2). For the same LWP ranges, the susceptibility of the effective radii to the aerosol burden (Sre) is around 0.08 and 0.07, respectively. These values are consistent with, although on the lower side of, prior studies of continental stratus. Uncertainties in this study are dominated by a small sample size and satellite retrieval biases. However, the approach is readily extensible to other ground-based sites measuring boundary layer aerosol concentrations pointing towards a method for better constraining susceptibility calculations globally.

title: Microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid regulates glucose homeostasis via remodeling of hepatic mitochondrial metabolism
summary: Abstract The gut microbiota produces metabolites that circulate to host tissues and are increasingly linked to metabolic health, yet the mechanisms by which individual microbial products regulate liver glucose metabolism remain poorly defin
content: Abstract The gut microbiota produces metabolites that circulate to host tissues and are increasingly linked to metabolic health, yet the mechanisms by which individual microbial products regulate liver glucose metabolism remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite indole-3-propionic acid (IPA) as a direct modulator of hepatic glucose production. In primary hepatocytes, a focused screen of indole metabolites revealed that several indole-containing compounds suppress glucagon-stimulated glucose output, with IPA emerging as a physiologically relevant candidate. IPA selectively reduced glucose production from mitochondrial-dependent gluconeogenic substrates while largely preserving glycerol-supported glucose production, suggesting that it does not simply shut down gluconeogenesis but instead alters how hepatocytes use metabolic fuels. Mechanistic analyses showed that IPA redirects lactate-derived carbon away from glucose production and reshapes mitochondrial metabolism, including redox balance, ATP availability, and urea cycle-linked metabolic activity. These effects occurred without detectable disruption of proximal insulin or glucagon signaling, supporting a model in which IPA acts primarily through intracellular metabolic remodeling. In mice, endogenous IPA levels varied with nutritional state, and short-term IPA administration improved fasting glycemia and glucose handling in Western diet-fed animals. Finally, microbiome-depleted mice colonized with IPA-producing Clostridium sporogenes displayed increased circulating IPA and improved glucose tolerance compared with mice colonized with an IPA-deficient mutant C. Sporogenes strain. Together, these findings identify IPA as a microbial metabolite that directly connects gut tryptophan metabolism to hepatic mitochondrial function and systemic glucose regulation, highlighting a mechanistic gut-liver pathway with potential therapeutic relevance to metabolic disease.

title: Emulsion-forcespun hollow polymer fibers as functional sorbents for uranium removal from water
source: Journal of Radioanalytical and Nuclear Chemistry
summary: Abstract This study developed hollow amidoximated styrene–acrylonitrile (SAN) fibers using a novel emulsion-assisted solution forcespinning strategy for enhanced uranium adsorption. The fabricated hollow SAN fibers, with their unique core a
content: Abstract This study developed hollow amidoximated styrene–acrylonitrile (SAN) fibers using a novel emulsion-assisted solution forcespinning strategy for enhanced uranium adsorption.
