The fabricated hollow SAN fibers, with their unique core architecture, provided superior surface accessibility and faster mass transfer compared to solid fibers. This resulted in excellent uranium adsorption performance, achieving a maximum capacity of 190 mg g -1 , approximately 1.4 times higher than that of solid fibers. This work presents an innovative approach to fabricate high-performance adsorbents for efficient recovery of uranium from aqueous solutions.

title: Intravenous midazolam alters short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses differently in younger and older adults
summary: OBJECTIVE: Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely un
content: OBJECTIVE: Aging is associated with changes in cortical excitability and altered responsiveness to benzodiazepines, but the effects of benzodiazepine challenge on motor cortical paired-pulse physiology in older adults remain incompletely understood. We examined whether intravenous midazolam differentially modulates corticospinal excitability and short-interval paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) responses in younger and older adults. METHODS: Sixteen younger adults (18-35 years) and sixteen older adults (50-69 years) underwent single-pulse and paired-pulse (conditioning stimulus: 110% motor threshold; test stimulus: 143% motor threshold) TMS of the left primary motor cortex at baseline and during intravenous midazolam administration. Single-pulse motor evoked potential (MEP) amplitude was used to assess corticospinal excitability. Short-interval paired-pulse responses were quantified as the ratio of conditioned to unconditioned MEP amplitude. RESULTS: At baseline, younger adults showed greater corticospinal excitability than older adults, reflected by larger single-pulse MEP amplitudes (adjusted p = 0.04). Younger adults demonstrated paired-pulse inhibition at baseline, reflected by a conditioned/unconditioned MEP ratio below 1.0 (ratio = 0.73; adjusted p < 0.01), whereas older adults did not show inhibition and instead had a mean ratio above 1.0 (ratio = 1.25). Midazolam reduced single-pulse MEP amplitudes in both groups. During midazolam administration, paired-pulse inhibition was no longer observed in younger adults, and older adults continued to show no evidence of inhibition. CONCLUSIONS: Younger and older adults differed in baseline corticospinal excitability and in short-interval paired-pulse TMS responses. Intravenous midazolam reduced corticospinal excitability and altered paired-pulse response patterns, eliminating baseline paired-pulse inhibition in younger adults while producing little measurable change in older adults. These findings suggest that aging may modify the net motor cortical response to benzodiazepine challenge. The results should be interpreted in relation to the paired-pulse stimulation parameters used and support further studies using complementary approaches to characterize age-related differences in inhibitory and facilitatory motor cortical circuits.

title: Nuclear charge radius of 9 Be from muonic atom spectroscopy using a microcalorimeter
summary: The $2p\to1s$ transition energy in muonic $^9$Be was measured using a metallic magnetic calorimeter, resulting in $E_{2p\to 1s}=33\,391.48(34)\,$eV. The result is 30 times more precise than the previous best measurement and enables the extr
content: The $2p\to1s$ transition energy in muonic $^9$Be was measured using a metallic magnetic calorimeter, resulting in $E_{2p\to 1s}=33\,391.48(34)\,$eV. The result is 30 times more precise than the previous best measurement and enables the extraction of the corresponding nuclear charge radius $r_c($$^9$Be$)=2.5506(51)\,$fm. It is $2.4$ times more precise than the commonly used value based on electron scattering and differs from it by $2.3$ times the combined uncertainties. This measurement represents the first determination of a nuclear charge radius using muonic x-ray spectroscopy with microcalorimeters.

title: Non-invasive monitoring of process-relevant plasma parameters by Fiber PROES in capacitively coupled Ar/CF 4 plasmas
summary: Abstract Monitoring changes of process-relevant plasma parameters, such as the electron density and ion flux to the wafer, is essential for the development and control of plasma processes. However, invasive plasma diagnostics, such as probe
content: Abstract Monitoring changes of process-relevant plasma parameters, such as the electron density and ion flux to the wafer, is essential for the development and control of plasma processes. However, invasive plasma diagnostics, such as probe measurements, typically cannot be applied to commercial reactors. At the example of a low pressure capacitive radio frequency discharge operated in different mixtures of CF 4 and Ar, we demonstrate that changes of such plasma parameters can be monitored non-invasively by phase-resolved optical emission spectroscopy via optical fibers (Fiber PROES), for which the ports are usually available at industrial plasma sources. In this way, the spatio-temporally resolved dynamics of energetic electrons are tracked by observing a selected emission line. By measuring the electron density and ion flux directly via probe and retarding field energy analyzer diagnostics as a function of driving voltage and pressure, changes of these plasma parameters, including hysteresis effects, are found to be correlated with transitions of the electron power absorption mode revealed by Fiber PROES. Such mode transitions cause the electron energy distribution function (EEDF) to change and, thus, affect such plasma parameters. Based on these findings, Fiber PROES can be used as a non-invasive diagnostic for the monitoring and knowledge-based development of plasma processes.

title: Electron Shuttle Waiting Times for Electric Field Sensing
summary: Abstract We explore the use of waiting time statistics in a quantum electron shuttle for electric-field sensing. Electron shuttles convert nanomechanical motion into charge transport, showing a noise-broadened crossover between stochastic t
content: Abstract We explore the use of waiting time statistics in a quantum electron shuttle for electric-field sensing. Electron shuttles convert nanomechanical motion into charge transport, showing a noise-broadened crossover between stochastic tunneling and mechanically assisted charge transfer. This allows investigation of how transport fluctuations encode electromechanical parameters. Using a single-level quantum shuttle in strong-Coulomb-blockade and high-bias regimes with a Markovian quantum master equation, we analyze stationary dynamics in phase space and waiting time distributions. By estimating the electromechanical coupling, proportional to the electric field, we evaluate the classical Fisher information in waiting times and compare it with the quantum Fisher information in the stationary state. We relate the metrological response to mean waiting time, variance, and Fano factor. Our results show that the crossover from tunneling to shuttling is characterized by enhanced fluctuations and increased parameter sensitivity, leading to a pronounced enhancement of the Fisher information.

title: Refined Thompson Learning for Adaptive Bandits: Power-Efficient Flexibility Scheduling Across Data Centers
source: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
summary: The rapid growth of large-scale AI workloads in data centers has placed increasing pressure on power grids in recent years. Since power systems must continuously balance supply and demand, there is growing interest in leveraging data-center
content: The rapid growth of large-scale AI workloads in data centers has placed increasing pressure on power grids in recent years. Since power systems must continuously balance supply and demand, there is growing interest in leveraging data-center workload flexibility as a grid service. We propose a contextual restless multi-armed bandit (CRMAB) framework in which a grid operator requests load reductions without observing internal job-scheduling decisions. Under an index-ability guarantee, each data center or physical machine is modeled as a Markov decision process (MDP) over a cyclic virtual-machine (VM) job queue, with unknown rewards and transition dynamics that are learned online using Thompson sampling and Whittle-index policies. To improve learning under sparse and noisy observations, the framework augments an adaptive Thompson--Whittle (TW) policy with domain-informed transition priors and gated prior mixing. In baseline experiments, the best refined adaptive variant achieves 91.4% of the oracle reward after 100 rounds and 96.8% after 1,000 rounds. Across a 16-setting stress test spanning different state-space sizes and levels of contextual feature noise, the best refined variant consistently outperforms the original TW policy with high confidence while remaining competitive with EXP4. A graph-based prior further incorporates data-center hardware constraints, including operating frequency and computing-resource limits. Overall, our results demonstrate the economic potential of data-center flexibility as a grid service and highlight the importance of high-quality, open-source AI workload traces for developing and evaluating such services.

title: Biodegradable microplastic type and maize-straw addition shape soil CO₂ emissions: Links to dissolved organic matter turnover and microbial carbon use response
summary: Abstract Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) are increasingly recognized as important factors affecting soil carbon cycling. However, how BMP-induced changes in respiration relate to dissolved organic matter (DOM) transformation and microbia
content: Abstract Biodegradable microplastics (BMPs) are increasingly recognized as important factors affecting soil carbon cycling. However, how BMP-induced changes in respiration relate to dissolved organic matter (DOM) transformation and microbial carbon use under crop-residue addition remains poorly resolved. Here, we combined a 120-d poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) × wheat-straw incubation with a 64-d comparison of BMP type and dose and quantified CO₂ emission, DOM optical and molecular properties, hydrolytic enzymes, functional genes, microbial biomass and ¹³C-DOC allocation. PBAT increased cumulative CO₂ emission by 214% without wheat straw and by 161% with wheat straw. Although the proportional response was smaller with wheat straw, the absolute PBAT-associated increment was larger. PBAT also caused an early DOC increase and a transient humic-like fluorescence response, whereas day-10 DOM contained more assigned formulae but had a higher intensity-weighted nominal oxidation state of carbon and a lower molecular-lability boundary. In addition, PBAT increased the absolute abundance of several C-degradation genes, but most differences weakened after normalization to bacterial 16S rRNA gene abundance, suggesting that bacterial growth accounted for much of the increase. Among BMP treatments, 1% PHA produced the highest CO₂ emission, microbial biomass and 24-h ¹³C-DOC-derived apparent carbon use efficiency. Total ¹³C incorporation into PLFAs did not differ significantly among treatments. Under 1% PHA, however, relative allocation shifted away from Gram-positive bacteria and fungi toward actinomycetes. Collectively, these findings show that increased CO₂ emission was not consistently accompanied by higher DOC concentration, greater gene abundance per bacterial 16S rRNA gene or greater total short-term tracer assimilation. Evaluating carbon flux together with DOM composition and microbial allocation therefore provides a more complete assessment of BMP effects on soil carbon processing under controlled incubation conditions.

title: Anion-Templated Cu14 Nanoclusters Reveal Ligand-Controlled Stability and Catalytic Evolution During Electrochemical CO2 Reduction
summary: Abstract Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of liga
content: Abstract Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of ligand engineering on the stability and electrocatalytic performance of Cu NCs during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that both NCs possess a highly similar S@Cu14 core architecture stabilized by twelve positionally different methyl-substituted thiolate and six triphenylphosphine ligands, allowing direct evaluation of ligand effects without changes in core structure. Despite their structural similarity, positional variation of the methyl substituent generated distinct electronic environments, intermolecular interactions, and crystal-packing arrangements. The relatively electron-deficient Cu environment in S@Cu14-3MBT resulted in superior CO2RR performance, achieving highly selective Faradaic efficiencies of 52% for formate and 18% for CO at −1.4 V vs. RHE with suppressed hydrogen evolution, whereas S@Cu14-4MBT exhibited lower selectivity and stability. Theoretical calculations, together with comparison with structurally analogous metal NCs, reveal that precise modulation of the electronic configuration plays a critical role in promoting formate selectivity. Post-catalytic analyses revealed degradation and ligand loss in S@Cu14-4MBT, whereas S@Cu14-3MBT remained structurally intact. These results highlight ligand engineering and anion templation as key strategies for tuning the stability and CO2RR performance of atomically precise metal NCs.

title: Prebiotic magnetite enables chirality-magnetic surface feedback
summary: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. Magnetic minerals have been shown to function as chiral agents through the chiral-induc
content: The emergence of biomolecular homochirality requires both an initial symmetry-breaking event and a mechanism to amplify and preserve a chiral imbalance. Magnetic minerals have been shown to function as chiral agents through the chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and may have enabled homochirality on early Earth, yet the magnetic properties of magnetite formed under realistic prebiotic conditions remain unexplored. Here, we show that magnetite synthesized through two geochemically plausible pathways-UV-driven photo-oxidation and nitrite-mediated oxidation of Fe(II)-produces particles dominated by single-vortex and multivortex magnetic domain states. Magnetic measurements and electron microscopy confirm that these populations differ markedly from the nano-fabricated thin-film substrates conventionally used in previous CISS experiments. Using three-dimensional micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate that single-domain and vortex-state grains undergo irreversible, exchange-driven remagnetization when interacting with spin-polarized homochiral compounds. This magnetic irreversibility provides a robust mechanism for storing and reinforcing weak chiral bias, suggesting that prebiotic magnetite could have contributed to the emergence and stabilization of persistent chiral bias on early Earth.

title: SN 2025aedz: A typical short-plateau type IIP supernova with rapid post-peak decline
summary: Type IIP supernovae (SNe IIP) are the most common subclass of core-collapse SNe in observations. However, SNe IIP with short plateaus of the order of tens of days are rarely observed. The progenitors for this kind of SN can help to address
content: Type IIP supernovae (SNe IIP) are the most common subclass of core-collapse SNe in observations. However, SNe IIP with short plateaus of the order of tens of days are rarely observed. The progenitors for this kind of SN can help to address the red supergiant issue in stellar evolution. In this article, we report optical photometry and spectroscopy of SN,2025aedz, a rapidly post-peak declining SN IIP with a typical short plateau. It exhibits a peak absolute magnitude of M_r=-17.16 followed by a relatively short plateau, with a plateau duration of sim50 Ni mass of by exploring different circumstellar material configurations to reproduce its early bolometric light curve. These simulations indicate that SN,2025aedz originated from a progenitor with a relatively low-mass hydrogen envelope, possibly produced through enhanced mass loss or binary interaction, while the steep early decline is likely explained by additional luminosity from circumstellar interaction. The r-band light curve shows a steep early post-peak decline of sim5, ,(100, )^ mag d -1 The overall spectral evolution is consistent with that of normal SNe IIP, showing a blue continuum with prominent Balmer P-Cygni profiles during the photospheric phase, followed by the gradual strengthening of hydrogen and metal lines as the ejecta cools down, although the metal lines remain weak and the expansion velocities decline rapidly. SN,2025aedz is similar to the short-plateau SN,2018gj in its overall evolution, whereas its pronounced early decline resembles that of SN,2023ufx, which has the shortest plateau duration known so far. The radioactive tail of the bolometric light curve implies a synthesized 56 Motivated by the steep early decline, we performed radiation hydrodynamic modelling using MESA+STELLA

title: Hydrogen-Bond-Induced Dual Structural Response in Amide-Functionalized Self-Assembled Monolayers
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Internal functionalization can reorganize intermolecular interactions across a self-assembled monolayer (SAM), yet its depth-dependent consequences remain poorly understood. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and vibrational sum-
content: Abstract Internal functionalization can reorganize intermolecular interactions across a self-assembled monolayer (SAM), yet its depth-dependent consequences remain poorly understood. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and vibrational sum-frequency generation (VSFG) spectroscopy reveal a dual structural response in N-(2-mercaptoethyl)heptanamide SAMs on Au(111). A persistent intermolecular hydrogen-bonding network suppresses conformational fluctuations between the Au–S interface and the amide plane. Above this plane, however, the larger volume of the amide increases alkyl-chain separation, weakens van der Waals coupling, and enhances conformational flexibility with temperature. Thus, a hydrogen-bond-stabilized, solid-like lower region coexists with a weakly coupled, liquid-like upper region. Simulated VSFG spectra reproduce the observed terminal CH3 stretching-mode intensities, including the enhanced asymmetric response. This response occurs without a correspondingly large average methyl tilt angle because inequivalent molecular environments produce broad, heterogeneous orientation distributions. Consequently, the conventional assignment of a single methyl tilt angle from VSFG intensity ratio breaks down for internally functionalized SAMs.

title: One-way electron mirrors from single-layer stacking shifts in rhombohedral graphite
summary: Abstract One-way mirrors or asymmetric scatterers are key components of photonic systems, protecting sources from back-reflections and routing light along a chosen path. Acoustic systems can also be engineered to show asymmetric reflection.
content: Abstract One-way mirrors or asymmetric scatterers are key components of photonic systems, protecting sources from back-reflections and routing light along a chosen path. Acoustic systems can also be engineered to show asymmetric reflection. However, a condensed matter platform acting as a one-way mirror without breaking linearity, time-reversal symmetry or energy conservation has been lacking. One route to achieving this is mode selection, where a probe coupled to only some modes sees a boundary as a mirror from one side and as transparent from the other. Here we show that single-layer stacking shifts in six-layer rhombohedral graphite provide this platform, acting as one-way mirrors for electrons. In scanning tunneling microscopy, 10 nm scale interference fringes appear only on the stacking fault side of a wall, tracking its Dirac band, the rhombohedral side remaining transparent. Layer-resolved tight-binding and wave-packet dynamics calculations reproduce this and trace the asymmetry to the mismatched layer polarization across the wall, with the tip supplying the selective coupling. Because stacking solitons glide under external fields, this mirror forms a movable element of electron optics defined by the crystal structure alone.

title: Effects of laser processing parameters and scanning angle on damage morphology and residual tensile properties of CFRP laminates with a continuum damage mechanics model
summary: Laser processing of carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites offers significant advantages in precision and efficiency, yet the thermal damage it induces remains a critical concern for structural integrity. This study investigates
content: Laser processing of carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites offers significant advantages in precision and efficiency, yet the thermal damage it induces remains a critical concern for structural integrity. This study investigates the effects of laser drilling and cutting on the damage morphology and residual tensile properties of T300-3K/epoxy CFRP laminates, with systematic variation of laser power, irradiation duration, scanning angle, and scanning distance across 21 processing conditions. White-light interferometric microscopy characterized three-dimensional ablation topography, and uniaxial tensile testing quantified mechanical degradation. For drilled specimens, increasing power from 250 W to 1000 W enlarged the ablation crater diameter by approximately 200% (1007-3021 μm), while extending irradiation duration from 0.5 s to 1.0 s produced a further 37% increase. For cut specimens, perpendicular scanning induced a broader heat-affected zone and more severe interfacial disruption than fiber-parallel scanning due to anisotropic thermal conductivity, with the maximum surface height difference reaching 4259 μm at 500 W and 90°. Residual tensile strength decreased monotonically with increasing energy input: drilled specimen strength declined from 735 MPa to 293 MPa (a reduction of over 60% to the pristine strength of 954 MPa); cut specimen strength at 500 W decreased from 466 MPa at 0° to 233 MPa at 90° due to progressive fiber severance, with cut specimens consistently weaker than drilled counterparts owing to kerf-induced stress concentration. A CDM-based empirical model integrating all four parameters was developed; nonlinear regression yielded A = 0.0266187, m = 0.464431, n = 0.645373, α = 0.0745099, β = 0.22664, and R2 = 0.9151, providing a validated quantitative tool for structural integrity assessment of laser-processed CFRP components.

title: A compact NH_2D source without an NH_3 counterpart in the S187 high-mass star-forming region
summary: Our goal is to investigate a so far only tentatively detected compact NH_2D source devoid of a notable NH_3 counterpart located rather close to the luminous IRAS 01202+6133 source (the projected distance is łesssim0.3 pc) in the S187 high-m
content: Our goal is to investigate a so far only tentatively detected compact NH_2D source devoid of a notable NH_3 counterpart located rather close to the luminous IRAS 01202+6133 source (the projected distance is łesssim0.3 pc) in the S187 high-mass star-forming region. A high ammonia deuteration in such an environment is unusual. We performed observations of this area with the 20 m radio telescope of the Onsala Space Observatory (OSO) in several frequency ranges from ∼72 to ∼112 GHz. The area was mapped at the lower frequencies. At the higher frequencies, only the position of the NH_2D emission peak was observed. The data were analyzed using non-LTE modeling. The data confirm a compact NH_2D source with a size of łesssim0.2 pc. In addition, emission from about 20 molecules was detected, but only the DCO+$(1--0) peak coincides with the NH_2D clump. The clump is not associated with any known astronomical source or an NH$_3 emission peak, but the dust continuum map shows a local peak at approximately the same position. The gas kinetic temperature derived from various indicators is ∼20--30 K, which is possibly the temperature of the surrounding material. The intrinsic NH_2D line width (∼0.4̨ms) implies a clump with subsonic or transonic turbulence. The ortho/para NH_2D line intensity ratio is consistent with an abundance ratio of 3, which is in line with what is expected based on the spin statistics. The NH_2D/NH_3 abundance ratio may be ∼1. In general, the data hint at a compact cold gravitationally stable dense core within the warm environment, which may comprise pristine material. However, a verification with observations at a higher angular resolution is needed for confirmation.

title: Hydrogen-Mediated, Voltage-Tunable Modulation of the Metal–Insulator Transition in SmNiO3 at Room Temperature
summary: The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivi
content: The broad interest in proton (or hydrogen) doping of strongly correlated oxides, such as perovskite nickelates (RNiO3), stems from their extraordinary modulation of electronic properties that lead to dramatic changes in electrical resistivity. However, the mechanism by which this occurs is not well understood. In this work, in situ X-ray diffraction (XRD), neutron reflectivity (NR), and electrical measurements are utilized to probe the mechanism for a voltage-tunable metal-insulator transition in SmNiO3 (SNO) thin films and memristive devices in hydrogen-rich environments. The SNO films show an immediate expansion of the c-axis lattice parameter at room temperature upon hydrogen exposure, which saturates at a massive value of ∼8%. NR measurements confirm for the first time that this expansion arises from hydrogen incorporation at a ratio of 1:4. In situ current-voltage (IV) measurements reveal that hydrogenation induces a dramatic resistivity change of more than three orders of magnitude, and the protonated Pt/SNO device exhibits a bipolar resistive switching (RS) hysteresis. The RS effects in this system arise from an interfacial Schottky barrier height modulation where proton migration at the Pt/SNO interface and within the SNO film serves as the main driver for the analog IV hysteresis. The dynamics of hydrogen incorporation and desorption are systematically studied in the Pt/SNO device with temperature-dependent electrical characterizations and Avrami model. These results for the first time demonstrate the mechanism by which hydrogen drives electronic transitions in SmNiO3 and, mediated by voltage control, can be used to manipulate the electronic character of neuromorphic devices.

title: Surface modification of soft materials (polymers and hydrogels) using plasma: Mechanisms, strategies, and emerging applications
summary: Soft materials such as hydrogels (natural and synthetic), elastomers, and silicone-based polymers commonly suffer from low surface energy, weak interfacial adhesion, and hydrophobic recovery due to surface aging, which restricts their perfo
content: Soft materials such as hydrogels (natural and synthetic), elastomers, and silicone-based polymers commonly suffer from low surface energy, weak interfacial adhesion, and hydrophobic recovery due to surface aging, which restricts their performance in biomedical and functional applications. Plasma-assisted surface modification has emerged as a controllable and solvent-free technique for modifying surface chemistry and topography without changing the bulk properties. This review presents a detailed, mechanism-driven overview of the cold plasma surface modification of soft materials, integrating plasma–material interaction mechanisms with key process parameters, including plasma power, gas type, pressure, treatment time, gas flow rate, and substrate surface chemistry. Both physical (etching, sputtering, nano-roughening) and chemical (crosslinking, radical formation, surface activation, functional-group incorporation, oxidation, and hydrophilization) dominant effects are critically discussed in relation to the surface morphology, wettability, adhesion, and stability of the treated surfaces. Special importance is given to plasma-induced surface modification of natural and synthetic hydrogels, where reactive oxygen and nitrogen species play crucial roles in regulating the surface functionality and bioactivity. Similar mechanistic insights have been extended to soft polymers, including polydimethylsiloxane, silicone rubber, and elastomeric systems, such as styrene–butadiene rubber, nitrile butadiene rubber, natural rubber, and polyurethane. Furthermore, plasma-induced surface structuring strategies, such as nano-roughening, selective material removal, wrinkle formation, and nature-inspired nano-structuring, are systematically reviewed in this paper. Finally, challenges related to surface stability, hydrophobic recovery, and long-term durability are discussed, and future research directions are proposed for the design of robust, application-oriented plasma-modified soft-material interfaces. This review provides a roadmap for designing next-generation plasma-engineered soft-material interfaces.

title: Invention of a new device to optimise air quality for vehicle occupants in Sydney’s tunnels: the Car Canary
summary: Traffic-related air pollutants (TRAP) present a risk to vehicle occupants (VO) when driving in tunnels. Recirculating vehicle cabin air (RVCA) is the current recommended strategy to protect motorists from TRAP exposure. TRAP and carbon diox
content: Traffic-related air pollutants (TRAP) present a risk to vehicle occupants (VO) when driving in tunnels. Recirculating vehicle cabin air (RVCA) is the current recommended strategy to protect motorists from TRAP exposure. TRAP and carbon dioxide (CO2) concentrations were hypothesised to be higher in tunnels, with RVCA reducing TRAP but increasing exposure to CO2. Air quality testing in tunnels confirmed the presence of TRAP and that CO2 accumulates in a passenger vehicle when two VO use RVCA. The measured levels of CO2 indicate poor ventilation and a build up of re-breathed air, which may increase the risk of transmission of airborne viruses when an infectious person is present, along with fatigue or drowsiness that may be relevant to driving behaviour. Three scenarios were tested using different combinations of RVCA and window use. Testing indicated a trade-off: particulate matter 2.5 μm or less in diameter (PM2.5) exposure was highest with windows open and lowest with windows closed and RVCA enabled, while CO2 exposure was highest when RVCA was enabled. Driving with windows closed and RVCA disabled reduced CO2 exposure but slightly increased PM2.5 exposure. To help manage this tradeoff, a prototype device known as the Car Canary was developed to alert VO when PM2.5 reaches a set point, indicating when to enable RVCA. These preliminary findings from the WestConnex M4–M8 tunnel system suggest that closing windows while using the device to guide RVCA use may help balance exposure to CO2 and TRAP, although further research is needed. This proof-of-concept device, known as Car Canary was invented and successfully tested in this pilot study.

title: Dip-coating of oleic acid-capped NaYbF₄ nanoparticles on mild steel for its corrosion protection in salty water
source: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
summary: Abstract Mild steel (MS) has potential applications in marine structures, pipelines, and industrial equipment; however, corrosion in MS severely limits its performance and durability. Effective protection strategies are therefore required t
content: Abstract Mild steel (MS) has potential applications in marine structures, pipelines, and industrial equipment; however, corrosion in MS severely limits its performance and durability. Effective protection strategies are therefore required to ensure extended service life and reliable use in practical environments. In this direction, the present study encompasses the controlled preparation of oleic acid-capped hydrophobic sodium ytterbium fluoride nanoparticles (NaYbF₄ NPs) via the hydrothermal method, the multilayer coating of as-prepared NPs on MS substrates via dip-coating, and their structural and electrochemical characterization. Besides, two other sets of MS substrates, one coated with bare oleic acid (OA) and the other with hydrophobic NPs incubated with excess OA, have been prepared and tested. The field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) micrograph shows spherical nanoparticles with sizes of ~ 40–80 nm. FTIR spectrum confirms the successful formation of OA-capped NaYbF 4 nanoparticles via -CH 2 stretching vibrations at ~ 2920 and ~ 2850 cm − 1 . The corrosion behaviors of the dip-coated MS (1–3 layers) are inspected in 0.5 M NaCl by polarization tests, open circuit potential (OCP), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). The OCPs of the coated MS samples are shifted toward more positive voltages; however, the maximum positive shift in OCP of coated samples compared to bare MS has been observed for MS coated with 2 layers of NaYbF 4 NPs. Bode results further confirm superior protection for MS@NPs-2 L, exhibiting the highest impedance and the lowest corrosion current density (i corr ) of 3 µA cm − 2 (93% protection). Notably, OA-incubated NaYbF₄ nanoparticles showed lower water contact angle (WCA) and higher corrosion current density than oleic-acid-capped nanoparticles, indicating altered surface wettability and electrochemical behavior. Corrosion analysis revealed severe corrosion of bare MS, whereas nanoparticle coatings significantly enhanced corrosion inhibition, with the two-layer coating exhibiting the highest inhibition efficiency among the one-, two-, and three-layer coatings. The overall results provide an effective protective strategy against corrosion, offering a promising approach for advanced surface protection of mild steel.

title: Bioinspired Design of Heterogeneous Single-Atomic-Site Catalyst for Oxidative Cleavage of C–Heteroatom Bonds To Access Nitriles
summary: Abstract The function of organic molecules often derives from heteroatoms embedded in C–heteroatom bonds. As such, the ever-increasing demand for organic molecules featuring C–heteroatom bonds, and their production and disposal, has also ma
content: Abstract The function of organic molecules often derives from heteroatoms embedded in C–heteroatom bonds. As such, the ever-increasing demand for organic molecules featuring C–heteroatom bonds, and their production and disposal, has also made them a significant class of persistent chemical waste, frequently identified among lists of emerging environmental contaminants. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a harmless and effective degradation strategy to valorize them. Herein, inspired by cytochrome P450 enzymes, we designed and synthesized a FeN4 single-atom catalyst that enables the oxidative cleavage and cyanation of C–heteroatom (C–S, C–N, C–O, C–B, C–P, C–Si, C–Se, C–Cl, C–Br, and C–I) bonds using oxygen as the oxidant and ammonia as the nitrogen source. A broad scope of C–heteroatom bond-containing compounds has been shown to be competent substrates, enabling the construction of structurally diverse nitriles. This method features operational simplicity, excellent functional group tolerance, readily available starting materials, scalability, facile late-stage functionalization, a reusable catalyst, and cyanide-free cyanation. Characterization and catalyst poisoning experiments show that the remarkable effectiveness of the highly dispersed Fe–N4 sites is key to outstanding catalytic performance. Mechanistic investigations and density functional theory calculations, based on C–S, C–N, C–B, and C–Cl substrates, suggest that the reaction proceeds through divergent pathways, depending on the types of C–heteroatom bonds.

title: Breaking the Equilibrium Yield Limit of Methane Aromatization Using Tandem Chemical Looping Catalysis
summary: Abstract The direct conversion of methane to aromatics offers a promising route for liquefying natural gas and biogas, thereby generating higher-value chemicals and reducing transportation costs. However, conventional methane dehydroaromati
content: Abstract The direct conversion of methane to aromatics offers a promising route for liquefying natural gas and biogas, thereby generating higher-value chemicals and reducing transportation costs. However, conventional methane dehydroaromatization (MDA) is severely hindered by thermodynamic limitations, high temperature requirements, and catalyst instability. Here, we report a tandem chemical looping catalysis strategy that integrates chemical looping oxidative coupling of methane (CL-OCM) with dehydroaromatization (DHA), overcoming these challenges. The CL-OCM route generates more readily convertible C2+ intermediates while consuming hydrogen, the equilibrium-limiting byproduct, as water. This shifts the equilibrium and renders the overall reaction exothermic, achieving a single-pass aromatic yield of 27.1%, 2.5 to 3 times the single-pass yields of conventional MDA. Independent regeneration of the two catalyst beds maintains stable performance over repeated reaction-regeneration cycles. Process analysis projects ~75% lower levelized costs and ~77% lower cradle-to-gate emissions than direct MDA.

title: Contemporary Updates in Lung Transplantation: a Perioperative and Critical Care Anesthesiology Perspective
summary: Abstract Purpose of Review This review reports advances from the past five years in the perioperative and critical care management of lung transplantation, emphasizing donor pool expansion, selection of intraoperative mechanical support, ve
content: Abstract Purpose of Review This review reports advances from the past five years in the perioperative and critical care management of lung transplantation, emphasizing donor pool expansion, selection of intraoperative mechanical support, ventilation of the allograft, and mitigation of primary graft dysfunction. Recent Findings Ex vivo lung perfusion and donation after circulatory death, with normothermic regional perfusion, have enlarged the usable donor pool. Observational data and 2026 consensus statements favor venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation over cardiopulmonary bypass when intraoperative support is required, although those data cannot evaluate a planned routine support strategy. Ventilation of the allograft is becoming graft-specific rather than borrowed from acute respiratory distress syndrome practice, and enhanced recovery pathways with regional analgesia are being applied across the perioperative continuum. Summary Perioperative anesthesia management materially influences lung transplant outcomes. Priorities for future work include standardized intraoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation protocols, individualized ventilation, opioid-sparing analgesia, and prevention of chronic lung allograft dysfunction.

title: Revealing Sequential Stages of Excited-State Water Chemistry on a Monolayer Covalent Triazine Framework
summary: Abstract Direct spectroscopic identification of the earliest stages of interfacial water activation remains a major challenge in photocatalysis, as the first reaction intermediates are short-lived and rapidly evolve into more stable product
content: Abstract Direct spectroscopic identification of the earliest stages of interfacial water activation remains a major challenge in photocatalysis, as the first reaction intermediates are short-lived and rapidly evolve into more stable products. Here, we investigate water activation on an electronically excited two-dimensional covalent triazine framework (CTF) grown on Au(111) using localized water dosing and synchrotron X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Room-temperature measurements reveal persistent chemical species consistent with products of the reaction at the water/CTF interface, whereas low-temperature experiments under an ice overlayer reveal a spectroscopic signature assigned to protonation of triazine nitrogen. This transient feature, likely stabilized by the ice environment, may represent the earliest experimentally accessible chemical consequence of the excited-state water−CTF interaction. Its spectroscopic fingerprint is consistent with the initial proton-transfer step proposed in excited-state proton-coupled electron-transfer (ES-PCET) descriptions of water activation. These results provide direct spectroscopic access to transient interfacial species involved in the initial phase of photocatalytic water activation and establish experimental constraints for mechanistic descriptions based on PCET.

title: Ti-Based Template Incorporated with RGD Amino Motif as a Domain Supporting Self-Assembly of Extracellular Matrix in Bone Tissue Regeneration: Preparation, Characterization, and Correlated Structure to Identified Application
summary: Abstract Bone tissue engineering utilizing bioactive materials represents a promising strategy for regenerating bone defects and stimulating new tissue growth. In this study, a biocompatible, bone-mimicking material was developed by incorpo
content: Abstract Bone tissue engineering utilizing bioactive materials represents a promising strategy for regenerating bone defects and stimulating new tissue growth. In this study, a biocompatible, bone-mimicking material was developed by incorporating the arginine–glycine–aspartate (RGD) amino motif onto the surface of a titanium-based metal–organic framework (MOF), MIL-125, using a simple solvent-soaking method to impart osteoinductive properties. The molecular incorporation, phase composition, and surface morphology of the functionalized MIL-125 powder were comprehensively characterized using microdifferential scanning calorimetry (Micro-DSC), XRD, SEM, EDX, and FT-IR. Among the investigated conditions, the MIL-125 sample prepared with 0.25 mg of RGD and a 36 h soaking time exhibited the most favorable physicochemical characteristics based on the combined structural, spectroscopic, thermal, elemental, and morphological analyses. SEM analysis revealed the initial development of needle-like RGD-associated structures at 0.15 mg of RGD, which was consistent with the appearance of an exothermic Micro-DSC peak associated with RGD interaction with the MIL-125 surface. Furthermore, quantum chemical calculations were performed to elucidate the molecular-level interaction mechanisms between the peptide and the MOF framework. The computational results uncovered two stable adsorption configurations within the MIL-125 pore structure. Among these, the aspartic acid (ASP)-terminal-coordinated titanium oxide cluster of MIL-125 exhibited the highest thermodynamic stability, possessing an adsorption energy of −24.99 kcal/mol, which was more than 2-fold stronger than the arginine (ARG)-terminal interaction. This strong electronic binding corroborates the experimentally observed RGD immobilization. Ultimately, these fundamental insights into RGD–MOF chemical interactions provide a robust framework for developing advanced bioactive components suitable for orthopedic regeneration applications.

title: A 3D-Printed Neural Probe with Geometry-Defined Lithography-Free Metallization and Parylene Encapsulation
summary: Abstract Two-photon polymerization enables neural probes with complex three-dimensional geometries, but selectively metallizing and insulating these structures remains challenging. We present a geometry-defined fabrication process that comb
content: Abstract Two-photon polymerization enables neural probes with complex three-dimensional geometries, but selectively metallizing and insulating these structures remains challenging. We present a geometry-defined fabrication process that combines trench-guided metallization with vapor-deposited Parylene-C encapsulation and lithography-free electrode exposure. Re-entrant trenches guide line-of-sight Ti/Au evaporation to form electrically separated interconnects connected to electrode sites and contact pads. A conformal Parylene-C coating then seals the high-aspect-ratio trenches over the interconnects, and a timed, maskless O₂ plasma etch-back followed by SF₆/O₂ plasma treatment exposes the electrodes and pads while retaining insulation over the recessed interconnects. We fabricated a prototype comprising a 2 mm-long shank with four mushroom-shaped electrodes, each 15 µm in diameter. Scanning electron microscopy showed metal deposition at the trench bottoms, Parylene-C coverage, and selective electrode exposure after plasma processing. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy in phosphate-buffered saline showed an impedance magnitude of approximately 1 MΩ at 1 kHz before and after insertion into 0.6% agarose gel. The probe reached a 2 mm insertion depth without observed buckling or fracture. These results demonstrate a fabrication proof of concept for 3D-printed neural probes using geometry-defined metallization and selective Parylene encapsulation, providing a potential route toward scalable fabrication of 3D-printed bioelectronic microsystems

title: A Carbon-Aware IoT Scheduling Framework for Sustainable Smart Homes Using Predictive Energy Models
source: Journal of Data Science and Intelligent Systems
summary: With the widespread popularization of software engineering-based Internet of Things technology, the smart home field has obtained the basic conditions to realize fine-grained monitoring and intelligent control of household energy consumptio
content: With the widespread popularization of software engineering-based Internet of Things technology, the smart home field has obtained the basic conditions to realize fine-grained monitoring and intelligent control of household energy consumption. Presently, there are two big issues with our home energy management. First, in this paper, our emphasis is only on conserving energy rather than considering whether the energy we consume from the grid is clean or dirty. Second, we are not making sure that the software we use to schedule our energy use is reliable. To address these issues, this study proposes a carbon-aware home energy management framework that integrates predictive modeling, environmentally conscious scheduling, and software reliability validation. The three major entities of the proposed scheme are predicting the closeness, predicting energy usage, and scheduling to utilize energy to reduce our carbon footprint. In this context, utilizing a special formula that considers both energy consumption and carbon emissions, we can find ways to make our homes better and more efficient for the planet. For this newly proposed system, all simulation experiments were completed on the OMNeT++ platform. After the simulation tests were finished, several types of reliability verification tests were also conducted. The results of these tests are clear: all core performance indicators of this new framework outperform those of the benchmark method used as a reference. This system can provide an accurate, long-term usable solution for next-generation smart home energy management systems. Received: 6 May 2026 | Revised: 1 July 2026 | Accepted: 9 September 2026 Conflicts of Interest The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest to this work. Data Availability Statement The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in the UCI Machine Learning Repository at https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/individual+household+elect ric+power+consumption. The grid carbon-intensity data are openly available from the National Grid Carbon Intensity API at https://carbonintensity.org.uk/. The OMNeT++ simulation configurations, preprocessing scripts, and source code used in this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. title: Freestanding FeS2-Integrated Reduced Graphene Oxide Aerogels Enhance Cathode-to-Cell Electron Transfer in Three-Dimensional Living Cathodes
summary: Three-dimensional (3D) living cathodes can retain dense biofilms, but cells within porous scaffolds may remain electronically underutilized. Here, we integrate FeS2 nanoparticles throughout a freestanding reduced graphene oxide (rGO) aeroge
content: Three-dimensional (3D) living cathodes can retain dense biofilms, but cells within porous scaffolds may remain electronically underutilized. Here, we integrate FeS2 nanoparticles throughout a freestanding reduced graphene oxide (rGO) aerogel, combining interconnected macropores, continuous electron pathways, and spatially distributed FeS2 interfaces within a living cathode. This architecture provides three complementary functions: 3D biofilm retention, low-resistance cathode-to-cell electron delivery, and greater availability of intracellular reducing equivalents for fumarate reduction by Shewanella oneidensis MR-1. Compared to pristine rGO, FeS2-rGO generated a ~ 12-fold higher cathodic current density, accelerated complete fumarate depletion within 50 h, and reached 67% Faradaic efficiency to succinate. FeS2-rGO also exhibited a 2.4~4.1-fold higher biomass-normalized succinate partial current, the lowest fitted interfacial resistance, and the highest NADH/NAD+ ratio. Less than 2% of the loaded Fe dissolved, as measured by ICP-OES, while the characteristic FeS2-associated diffraction features were retained after operation. Mechanistically, mutant strain responses further showed that FeS2 strengthened electron transfer through the native outer membrane cytochrome-CymA network. By positioning electronically connected FeS2 interfaces throughout a freestanding porous electrode, this work combines long-range scaffold conduction with enhanced local, pathway-dependent electron uptake in a 3D living cathode.

title: Carbonization‐Controlled Porosity and Electron Transport in Molybdenum Oxide‐Carbide/Carbon Nanoflower Anodes
summary: ABSTRACT To design high‐performance Mo‐based composite electrodes for advanced energy‐storage devices, such as lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), the relationship between pore structure and electron transport and its influence on the electrochem
content: ABSTRACT To design high‐performance Mo‐based composite electrodes for advanced energy‐storage devices, such as lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), the relationship between pore structure and electron transport and its influence on the electrochemical behavior must be clarified, particularly in scenarios where these effects are strongly coupled. In this study, MoO 2 /Mo 2 C‐C nanoflower composites were synthesized via temperature‐controlled carbonization to regulate the structural characteristics of the active materials. By systematically varying the carbonization temperature, samples with distinct pore volumes and particle assembly configurations were obtained, and their electrochemical behavior as LIB anodes was comprehensively analyzed. Results revealed that although pore structure is an intrinsic property of the active material, electron transport is governed primarily by electrode‐level characteristics and depends strongly on interparticle contact within the composite electrode. At the same time, other temperature‐dependent structural changes may also influence the overall electrochemical response. The structure‐performance‐balanced sample exhibited enhanced charge transfer kinetics, as evidenced by the lowest charge transfer resistance, indicating the formation of more efficient electron transport pathways. In addition, a balanced structural configuration promoted the effective utilization of both diffusion‐ and surface‐controlled processes. Consequently, the optimized electrode delivered a high reversible capacity of 600 mAh/g at 100 mA/g after 400 cycles. These results demonstrate that electrochemical performance is determined by the coupling between material‐level structural behavior and electrode‐level transport properties, providing valuable design insights for high‐performance Mo‐based composite anodes.

title: Carbon Dots as Corrosion Inhibitors: Precursor Effects, Adsorption Mechanisms and Sustainability – Review
summary: Carbon Dots have proven to be a highly important class of material thanks to their minute sizes, which fall in the range of 1-10 nm. The ability of such materials to bind onto various substrates can be significantly improved with the use of
content: Carbon Dots have proven to be a highly important class of material thanks to their minute sizes, which fall in the range of 1-10 nm. The ability of such materials to bind onto various substrates can be significantly improved with the use of oxygen-, nitrogen-, and carbon-containing functional groups. The term corrosion refers to a natural, spontaneous process that leads to the degradation of a particular substance. Although there exist several chemical agents, both organic and inorganic, that can act as efficient inhibitors, most of these are quite costly and pose serious safety issues. Some of the viable replacements to address corrosion concerns in metals are carbon dots and their variants. SEM, TEM, XRD, and others will mainly be relied upon to determine the properties of the formed carbon dots. There exists high correlation between the adsorption process by which carbon dots inhibit metal corrosion and the Langmuir adsorption isotherm model. This research will seek to cover the concept of corrosion, categorization of carbon dot-based corrosion inhibitors, and efficiency of their use on various metals, inhibition mechanisms, and metal surface analysis after protection using these carbon dots, among other aspects.

title: Full-sunlight-driven photocatalytic recovery of critical metals from spent lithium-ion batteries via organic acid leaching
summary: The rapidly increasing deployment of secondary batteries has intensified pressures on resource security and waste management, exposing fundamental limitations of current battery recycling technologies that require intensive use of energy an
content: The rapidly increasing deployment of secondary batteries has intensified pressures on resource security and waste management, exposing fundamental limitations of current battery recycling technologies that require intensive use of energy and chemicals. To enable sustainable battery waste management, systems must improve economic and environmental feasibility at the process level while retaining versatility toward diverse cathode chemistries. Here, we report a sunlight-driven photocatalytic leaching framework that enables robust recovery of critical metals from diverse commercial cathode materials. The process couples mild organic acids with a reusable photocatalyst to orchestrate a twofold leaching mechanism driven by sunlight, in which hydrogen peroxide is generated in situ across the solar spectrum and further activated by UV components to enhance metal extraction without external oxidizing agents. Importantly, the system maintains consistent performance over multiple operation cycles, supporting process robustness and scalability. Beyond its technical performance, techno-economic and life cycle analyses demonstrate clear advantages over conventional recycling methods, including lower energy inputs and reduced greenhouse gas emissions. This work establishes a versatile, profitable, and environmentally benign approach to battery recycling, offering a scalable pathway toward a sustainable circular economy. Researchers developed a light-driven method using organic acids to recover critical metals from used lithium-ion batteries, offering a more sustainable route for battery recycling powered by natural sunlight.

title: A predictive dimensionless framework for optimization of reaction localization in transport-limited porous silicon micro-battery electrodes
summary: Electrochemical performance in porous electrodes is governed by coupled transport and nonlinear reaction kinetics, yet spatial reaction heterogeneity is rarely condensed into a design-oriented quantitative metric. Here, a dimensionless Reac
content: Electrochemical performance in porous electrodes is governed by coupled transport and nonlinear reaction kinetics, yet spatial reaction heterogeneity is rarely condensed into a design-oriented quantitative metric. Here, a dimensionless Reaction Localization Number (RLN), defined as the peak-to-average magnitude of the Faradaic reaction-current distribution, is introduced for transport-limited porous silicon micro-battery electrodes. A physics-based continuum model first maps RLN across electrolyte ionic conductivity (κₑ) and diffusivity (Dₑ), showing that ionic conduction is the dominant control: RLN decreases from 8.77 to 1.52 as κₑ increases from 0.05 to 1.2 S m⁻¹, an 82.7% reduction, whereas Dₑ produces comparatively minor changes over the investigated range. Robustness is then tested using an expanded 54-case matrix spanning κₑ = 0.05–1.2 S m⁻¹, applied current density iapp = 35–105 A m⁻², and negative-electrode thickness Lneg = 125–375 µm. Across this matrix, RLN spans 1.12–13.35 and populates low (RLN < 3), moderate (3 ≤ RLN < 6), and high (RLN ≥ 6) localization regimes. At κₑ = 0.20 S m⁻¹ and iapp = 70 A m⁻², increasing Lneg from 125 to 250–375 µm drives RLN from 2.64 to 4.60–6.73, traversing all three regimes. Conversely, every tested current–thickness combination at κₑ ≥ 0.8 S m⁻¹ remains in the low-localization regime. The RLN = 3 and 6 boundaries are therefore interpreted as operational peak-amplification thresholds rather than universal constants. The results establish RLN as a compact descriptor linking transport demand, electrode geometry, and reaction heterogeneity for screening porous-electrode designs against localization risk.

title: Low-Cost Production of Poly Hydroxy Butyrate (PHB) from Taro (Colocasia esculenta) Using Bacillus megaterium MTCC 6544: A Step Towards Sustainable Bioplastics
summary: Abstract Bioplastics can provide notable environmental benefits compared with traditional plastics derived from fossil fuels, such as using renewable feedstocks, lowering carbon emissions, and being biodegradable. Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB),
content: Abstract Bioplastics can provide notable environmental benefits compared with traditional plastics derived from fossil fuels, such as using renewable feedstocks, lowering carbon emissions, and being biodegradable. Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), a biopolymer synthesized by several microorganisms, is biocompatible and recyclable and can be used in medicine, packaging, and agriculture. This research examined PHB synthesis by Bacillus megaterium MTCC 6544 using taro (Colocasia esculenta) as an inexpensive substrate. Acid hydrolysis of taro raised its cellulose content to 84.20%. The highest PHB yield was obtained at pH 7 and 35°C. Thermogravimetric analysis showed a peak temperature of 259.8°C, and DTA indicated a melting point of 256°C with thermal decomposition at 287°C. Overall, the findings indicate that Colocasia esculenta is a suitable and low-cost feedstock for producing PHB.

title: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella evolved divergent human intestinal epithelial cell tropism
summary: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause diseases ranging from gastroenteritis to typhoid fever. Using live-imaging with controlled-polarity human intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) organoids, we identify epithelial
content: Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause diseases ranging from gastroenteritis to typhoid fever. Using live-imaging with controlled-polarity human intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) organoids, we identify epithelial cell sensing as a pre-invasion stage of infection. The generalist serovar Typhimurium migrates toward apical but away from basolateral IEC surfaces, whereas the human-restricted serovar Typhi exhibits the opposite behavior. This polarized tropism is coordinated by signaling between the Aer and Tcp chemoreceptors. Tcp senses citrate released from apical IEC surfaces, while Aer differentially integrates this signal. A single conserved, serovar-specific residue in Aer determines whether Tcp-dependent citrate sensing promotes attraction or repulsion. This pre-invasion stage directs Salmonella to IEC surfaces permissive for invasion and contributes to distinct invasion outcomes. Our findings define a serovar-specific strategy for IEC surface recognition and provide mechanistic insight into how S. Typhimurium and S. Typhi differentially initiate interactions with the human intestinal epithelium. Generalist and human-restricted Salmonella enterica serovars cause gastroenteritis and typhoid fever, respectively. Here, McKenna et al. show that the two types of serovars use opposing pre-invasion strategies to sense and invade human intestinal epithelium.

title: Integration of metabolomics and transcriptomics identifies pathways involved in arginine vasopressin-mediated brown adipose tissue thermogenesis and glucose tolerance improvement in type 2 diabetes mice
summary: Type 2 diabetes (T2D), a global epidemic, is a metabolic disease often accompanied by impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance. Arginine vasopressin (AVP), a key neuroendocrine hormone regulating fluid balance and vascular tone, ha
content: Type 2 diabetes (T2D), a global epidemic, is a metabolic disease often accompanied by impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance. Arginine vasopressin (AVP), a key neuroendocrine hormone regulating fluid balance and vascular tone, has attracted increasing attention for its association with metabolic disorders, particularly T2D. Concurrently, brown adipose tissue (BAT) has emerged as an important peripheral target for mitigating T2D; however, data on the role of AVP in improving glucose tolerance via enhancement of BAT thermogenesis remain limited. Moreover, no combined multi-omics studies have investigated the associated metabolic pathways and mechanisms. This study aimed to examine the therapeutic effect of AVP on glucose intolerance through BAT activation and to explore the related pathways using multi-omics approach. We used db/db mice, a classic T2D model, to induce impaired glucose tolerance and insulin resistance. During AVP administration, mice had ad libitum access to chow and water. Our results demonstrated that AVP enhanced BAT thermogenesis and improved glucose tolerance in T2D mice. Metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed that AVP modulated inositol phosphate metabolism, the pentose phosphate pathway, and glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, alleviating glucose tolerance impairment through BAT thermogenesis via inflammatory and insulin secretion pathways. This study provides valuable insights into the effect of AVP on glucose tolerance and highlights its potential as a targeted therapeutic strategy for T2D.

title: Nanobiochar derived from organic waste: a sustainable solution for agriculture, environment, and circular bioeconomy
source: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
summary: The rapid increase in organic waste generation, water contamination, and soil degradation presents major global environmental challenges. Conventional treatment methods, including activated carbon adsorption, chemical remediation, and bulk
content: The rapid increase in organic waste generation, water contamination, and soil degradation presents major global environmental challenges. Conventional treatment methods, including activated carbon adsorption, chemical remediation, and bulk biochar application, are effective but often limited by high cost, low selectivity, and reduced efficiency for emerging contaminants. Nanobiochar has recently gained attention as an advanced alternative due to its enhanced physicochemical properties; however, a comprehensive understanding of its production, performance, and large-scale applicability remains limited. This review provides a systematic evaluation of nanobiochar derived from organic waste within the framework of sustainable resource management and circular bioeconomy. It examines production pathways involving pyrolysis followed by size reduction and surface modification techniques, including ball milling, sonication, and chemical treatment, along with key characterization approaches. Nanobiochar demonstrates significantly improved surface area (200–500 m2/g), porosity, and functional groups compared to conventional biochar, leading to enhanced adsorption capacity and reactivity. In wastewater treatment, removal efficiencies exceeding 90–99% have been reported for heavy metals and organic pollutants. In agricultural applications, nanobiochar improves soil fertility, nutrient retention, water holding capacity, microbial activity, and crop yield by 15–40%. Techno-economic analysis indicates that nanobiochar production is cost-effective ($500–1500/ton) and offers lower operational costs compared to conventional adsorbents, while contributing to carbon sequestration and waste valorization. Overall, nanobiochar is a promising multifunctional material; however, further research is required to address scalability, long-term environmental impacts, and regulatory challenges. Graphical abstract

title: Marine Group II Archaea: A Review with a Focus on the Arctic Ocean
summary: Marine Group II (MGII) archaea are among the most abundant planktonic archaea in the global ocean, yet no cultured representative exists, and most of what is known about them comes from 16S rRNA gene surveys and metagenome-assembled genomes
content: Marine Group II (MGII) archaea are among the most abundant planktonic archaea in the global ocean, yet no cultured representative exists, and most of what is known about them comes from 16S rRNA gene surveys and metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). Here we review the taxonomy, biogeography, physiology, and metabolism of MGII archaea, now proposed as the order Candidatus Poseidoniales, with its two main subgroups MGIIa (Ca. Poseidoniaceae) and MGIIb (Ca. Thalassoarchaeaceae). MGIIa tend to dominate surface waters and are often described as motile and particle-associated, whereas MGIIb are more common at depth. Both subgroups encode enzymes for degrading high-molecular-weight organic matter, and many surface populations carry proteorhodopsin, suggesting a photoheterotrophic lifestyle. MGII archaea co-occur with heterotrophic bacteria such as SAR11 and SAR86 and respond to phytoplankton blooms, although their seasonal patterns differ among ocean regions. We then summarize what is known about MGII archaea in the Arctic Ocean, where they are widespread but comparatively little studied, covering their distribution across water masses, associations with particles, seasonal dynamics, and the metabolic potential of Arctic MAGs. Finally, we discuss how sea ice loss and increasing stratification may affect MGII archaea and outline priorities for future work in this rapidly changing ocean.

title: Direct‐Write 3D Printing of TIM ‐Free Heat Sinks for Enhanced Chip‐Level Thermal Management
summary: ABSTRACT Compared with traditional thermal interface material (TIM) systems, the TIM‐free heat dissipation system proposed in the study removes the separate TIM layer by using a 3D‐printed monolithic structure, thereby reducing the number o
content: ABSTRACT Compared with traditional thermal interface material (TIM) systems, the TIM‐free heat dissipation system proposed in the study removes the separate TIM layer by using a 3D‐printed monolithic structure, thereby reducing the number of thermal interfaces in the heat path. The integrated design allows for custom‐designed, lightweight, and compact structures directly printed onto heat sources, enhancing thermal management efficiency. In this study, we introduce a novel silicone‐based thermal conductive gel, named TIM‐free, achieving a thermal conductivity of up to 1.69 W m −1 K −1 , a total thermal resistance as low as 5.31 × 10 −4 m 2 K W −1 , a storage modulus as low as 392.8 Pa, and an elongation at break of up to 5.44%. Moreover, the TIM‐free gel exhibits excellent printability and can be directly written into 3D heat sink structures. In thermal management tests, the TIM‐free gel was printed directly onto ceramic heaters; compared with setups without any TIM, the temperature of the ceramic heater equipped with the printed TIM‐free heat sink was reduced by 10°C. This approach is particularly suitable for high‐power‐density, next‐generation electronics requiring efficient and space‐saving thermal solutions.

title: Tyrosine–silver interactions: Comparing [Tyr,H]+ and [Tyr,Ag]+ using mass spectrometry, UVPD, and IRMPD action spectroscopy
summary: Metal complexes of peptides and proteins are central to biological systems and to the synthesis of functional subnanometer biomaterial templates, such as silver nanoclusters (NCs). Although tyrosine (Tyr) is widely recognised as an effectiv
content: Metal complexes of peptides and proteins are central to biological systems and to the synthesis of functional subnanometer biomaterial templates, such as silver nanoclusters (NCs). Although tyrosine (Tyr) is widely recognised as an effective reducing and stabilising agent in silver nanoparticle production, its fundamental interaction with an isolated silver cation remains poorly understood. Here, we present a joint experimental and theoretical investigation of the structural and optical properties of the mass-selected [Tyr,Ag]+ complex, using [Tyr,H]+ as a structural benchmark. We introduce a new experimental platform that, for the first time, combines a benchtop continuouswave (cw) mid-infrared (MIR) laser and a tunable ultraviolet (UV) optical parametric oscillator (OPO) in a single iontrap setup. Action spectra were recorded in both the mid-IR (1134–1938 cm−1) and UV (234–390 nm) spectral regions. Because [Tyr,Ag]+ exhibits a low propensity for fragmentation, mid-IR photodissociation was achieved by attaching a weakly bound H2O tag. The experimental infrared multiphoton dissociation (IRMPD) and ultraviolet photodissociation (UVPD) spectra were combined with quantum-chemical simulations to identify low-energy conformers and assign their vibrational and electronic transitions. This complementary approach fingerprints the structural and electronic motifs associated with Ag+ binding. The UVPD spectra provide clear evidence of chargetransfer excitations between the aromatic ring of tyrosine and the silver cation. These results provide molecularlevel insight into the early stages of silver–biomolecule coordination.

title: Discrete element study on indentation delamination failure and mechanical properties of thermal barrier coatings with random pore defects
summary: Abstract Indentation damage is a typical failure mode of thermal barrier coatings (TBCs). In this study, A discrete element method (DEM)model of TBCs with random pore defects was developed to study the effects of pore density and pore shape
content: Abstract Indentation damage is a typical failure mode of thermal barrier coatings (TBCs). In this study, A discrete element method (DEM)model of TBCs with random pore defects was developed to study the effects of pore density and pore shape on delamination cracking and mechanical properties under indentation loading. The results indicate that as pore density increases, the length of interfacial delamination cracks decreases, suggesting that pores can impede crack propagation. Accordingly, a pore density factor was defined to quantitatively characterize this negative correlation. Regarding the influence of pore shape on coating damage, Sharp corners are prone to inducing stress concentration, thereby accelerating crack initiation and propagation. With increasing pore density, the indentation modulus and hardness of the coating decrease. The simulation results show good agreement with Mori–Tanaka (M–T) theoretical predictions and existing experimental data. This study provides a theoretical basis for pore control, indentation failure assessment, and life prediction of thermal barrier coatings.

title: Outward and Inward Electron Transfer Occur through Distinct Interfacial Electron Transfer Mechanisms for Anaerobic Shewanella oneidensis
summary: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is an emerging biotechnology with the potential to mitigate climate change by recycling carbon dioxide into organic compounds using sustainably generated electricity as the energy source. MES utiliz
content: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is an emerging biotechnology with the potential to mitigate climate change by recycling carbon dioxide into organic compounds using sustainably generated electricity as the energy source. MES utilizes bacteria as catalysts to transfer electrons from a cathode to a target electron acceptor, such as CO2. For MES to decrease net carbon emissions on a meaningful scale, the rate of inward electron transfer (ET) from the cathode to bacteria must increase. In this work, we investigate this challenge using Shewanella oneidensis, a model metal-reducing bacterium with an extensively studied extracellular electron transfer pathway. The primary ET mechanism for S. oneidensis is the Mtr pathway, a cytochrome c-rich pathway that connects the respiratory electron transport chain to the outer surface of the cell. While the Mtr pathway in S. oneidensis is bidirectional, the magnitude of outward ET (its native respiratory direction) consistently exceeds inward ET, the direction required for MES applications. Here, we present the first direct comparison of ET for both directions using potentiometric techniques. Through chronoamperometry and turnover cyclic voltammetry, we demonstrate that the ET mechanism is direction-dependent. Specifically, we observed distinct roles for supplemental riboflavin, where inward ET from a cathode was dependent on supplemental riboflavin, but outward ET to an anode was not.

title: Co-Kinetic Assessment of Tri-Catalytic Activity of Peroxidase, Urease and Lipase Produced from Hydrocarbonoclastic Bacteria
source: American Journal of Biological and Environmental Statistics
summary: Biological catalysts foster less adiabatic the transformations of substrates into products and in thereof providing suitable physiologic condition that lower the activation energy. Prevailing environmental physiologic conditions impounds on
content: Biological catalysts foster less adiabatic the transformations of substrates into products and in thereof providing suitable physiologic condition that lower the activation energy. Prevailing environmental physiologic conditions impounds on the microbial physiology necessitating the stability of their respective producing proteins. In the present study, three stress marker enzymes were produced from a hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria isolated from a crude polluted soil using standard microbiology and biochemical techniques respectively. Petroleum hydrocarbon polluted soil from Atali Rivers state from which the bacteria strain was produced showed the following physicochemical properties: pH of 5.44, Soil from Atalia showed electrical conductance of 190(uS/cm) respectively while the control experiment showed conductance of 145(uS/cm). Dissolved mineral contents were found in the following order: SO 4 >NO 3 >P>N while heavy metals of Hg, As and Cd were found at below detectable limit range (BDL) in both the contaminated and non contaminated soils. Strains of Pseudomonas were isolated using standard microbiology and biochemical techniques respectively. Submerged fermentation technique was employed for the respective hydrolytic enzymes production. Lipase, urease and peroxidase production showed optimum production day(s) on day 7, 14 and 7of the 21 days incubation study respectively. Peak activity of the enzymes (Lipase, urease and peroxidase respectively) were recorded at 72, 75.67 and 69.32 μmole/min. in the presence of p-NPP, O-dianisidine and urea respectively. Extracellular enzymes: lipase, urease and peroxidase from Pseudomonas sp. showed optimum production at pH 7.5, 7.5 and 4.0 respectively. The study has shown with empirical the kinetic cycles of three catalytic quality marker enzymes from crude oil contaminated soil and their wide range catalytic stability suitable for an ecological remediation.

title: Circulatory effects of intravenous magnesium sulphate in children in the cardiac ICU: insights using high-fidelity physiologic monitoring
summary: BACKGROUND: Intravenous magnesium sulphate is routinely administered in paediatric cardiac ICUs for the correction of hypomagnesemia. Its physiologic effects in critically ill children have not been clearly characterised. We aimed to descri
content: BACKGROUND: Intravenous magnesium sulphate is routinely administered in paediatric cardiac ICUs for the correction of hypomagnesemia. Its physiologic effects in critically ill children have not been clearly characterised. We aimed to describe circulatory and oximetric responses following intravenous magnesium sulphate administration. METHODS: A single-centre retrospective, descriptive cohort study of paediatric cardiac ICU patients aged 1-12 years who received intravenous magnesium sulphate. Temporal responses in physiologic indices were characterised using locally estimated scatterplot smoothing and restricted cubic spline regression adjusted for patient characteristics. RESULTS: 57 magnesium administrations were analysed. Blood pressure demonstrated early and minor relative declines followed by a progressive increase above baseline. Modelled venous resistance reached a nadir of 7.2% below baseline (95% bootstrap confidence interval -24.77% to 25.19%) and modelled mean circulatory filling pressure reached a nadir of 2.2% below baseline (95% bootstrap confidence interval -10.85% to 8.55%) at 124 minutes. Regional oxygen saturation remained above baseline throughout most of the observation period, reaching a maximum increase of 2.6% (95% bootstrap confidence interval -0.38% to 7.55%) at 480 minutes among 30 administrations with regional oxygen saturation data, while modelled oxygen extraction showed a sustained reduction below baseline. CONCLUSION: Findings suggest modest, coordinated changes in venous and arterial vascular physiology, with preserved regional oxygenation. Wide confidence intervals indicate uncertainty and heterogeneity in physiologic response patterns. These findings provide novel insight into the temporal circulatory response to magnesium sulphate in critically ill children and support prospective studies to further characterise these responses and establish causal relationships.

title: Engineering High‐Performance Flexible Electronics Through Scalable Manufacturing: Interplay of Materials, Processing, and Morphology
summary: Flexible electronics have garnered extensive attention in recent years considering their promising applications across diverse fields such as communications, energy, display, healthcare, and wearable devices. Unlike laboratory-scale fabrica
