content: Flexible electronics have garnered extensive attention in recent years considering their promising applications across diverse fields such as communications, energy, display, healthcare, and wearable devices. Unlike laboratory-scale fabrication and integration, the transition of flexible electronics toward commercial applications demands scalable manufacturing that ensures high performance, large-area reproducibility, high yield, and throughput. However, achieving scalable manufacturing while maintaining device performance remains challenging, as fabrication scale-up often induces variations in material assembly, morphology evolution, and device integration, which may compromise functional reliability achieved at the laboratory scale. Generally, current flexible electronic devices can be divided into two categories: planar-type and fiber-type devices, representing two complementary platforms for realizing large-scale and highly integrated systems. In this review, scalable fabrication strategies tailored for each category and the latest advances are systematically summarized. In particular, the interplay among material design, scalable processing, morphology evolution, and device integration is highlighted, with emphasis on strategies that preserve device performance during manufacturing scale-up. Representative planar-type and fiber-type flexible electronic systems are further discussed to demonstrate how the synergistic optimization of material design and scalable manufacturing approaches enables high-performance devices for diverse applications. Finally, we outline remaining challenges and future directions to inform future developments in scalable flexible electronics.

title: Acid leaching reorganizes hierarchical nanoporous alteration layers on borosilicate glass
summary: Abstract Aqueous corrosion of silicate glass produces surface alteration layers whose formation may involve both leaching/in situ reorganization and interface-coupled dissolution–precipitation (ICDP). Here, selective acid leaching combined
content: Abstract Aqueous corrosion of silicate glass produces surface alteration layers whose formation may involve both leaching/in situ reorganization and interface-coupled dissolution–precipitation (ICDP). Here, selective acid leaching combined with focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy tomography, transmission electron microscopy–energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy was used to probe aluminum in a hierarchical nanoporous layer formed on borosilicate glass. Acid leaching removed aluminum almost completely while retaining a continuous porous silicate layer, consistent with an acid-soluble hydroxylated Al-containing secondary phase located outside, rather than incorporated into, the silicate network. Its removal thinned the segmented solid phase and altered the depth-dependent porosity. Associated shifts in optical reflectance and water-droplet spreading were consistent with changes in layer thickness and pore structure. These findings support contributions from both ICDP-type and leaching/in situ reorganization processes and identify aluminum speciation as an important factor governing alteration-layer structure and response.

title: Long-term time series of ground-based NDACC FTIR trace gases at Paris between 2011 and 2022
summary: Abstract. We present long‐term atmospheric trace gas measurements at Paris (48°50′04″ N, 2°21′02″ E; 60 m a.s.l.), using ground-based remote sensing technique and covering the period 2011–2022. The Fourier Transform Spectrometer of the Pari
content: Abstract. We present long‐term atmospheric trace gas measurements at Paris (48°50′04″ N, 2°21′02″ E; 60 m a.s.l.), using ground-based remote sensing technique and covering the period 2011–2022. The Fourier Transform Spectrometer of the Paris station (FTS-Paris) has been operated regularly since 2011 and has been part of the Total Carbon Column Observing Network (TCCON) since 2014. It also recently joined the Network for the Detection of Atmospheric Composition Change – InfRared Working Group (NDACC-IRWG). Here we describe the instrument setup, the automated operation mode, and the SFIT4 retrieval strategy for ten Paris NDACC-IRWG products: CH4, N2O, CO, C2H6, H2CO, NO2, OCS, HCl, HF and HCN. The nominal retrieval settings were selected by comparing and evaluating the OEM and TP methods, using spectral fit quality, vertical profiles, degrees of freedom, averaging kernels, and retrieval errors as criteria. Data quality is assessed through error characterization, instrument line shape sensitivity study, comparison with previous PROFFIT9 retrievals, and evaluation of the post-processing filtering criteria. Retrieval noise dominates the random error, while spectroscopic uncertainties are the main source of the systematic error. Post-processing filtering removes about 2–6 % of data, mostly outliers. The 2011–2022 time series show increasing trends for CH4 and N2O, decreasing trends for CO, C2H6, H2CO, NO2 and OCS, and an undefined long-term evolution for HCl. HF and HCN records only cover the 2018–2022 period and derived trends require caution. The Paris FTIR measurements have been archived in the NDACC data repository and on Zenodo using the Hierarchical Data Format version 4 (HDF4).

title: Predicting degradation in direct ammonia SOFCs: The temperature trade–off between nickel nitriding and coarsening
summary: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free fuel for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), since nickel-based anodes can crack it internally without a separate reformer. Direct-ammonia operation, however, compromises durability through nickel nitriding an
content: Ammonia is a promising carbon-free fuel for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), since nickel-based anodes can crack it internally without a separate reformer. Direct-ammonia operation, however, compromises durability through nickel nitriding and coarsening. These mechanisms respond oppositely to temperature and are usually studied separately, leading to conflicting set-point guidance. This study combines both mechanisms in a reduced-order model linking operating conditions to voltage losses. The combined response reveals two effects. First, nitriding is non-monotonic, peaking at approximately 625–665 °C under the assumed kinetics; thus, a moderate increase above 600 °C may accelerate it. Second, the mechanisms cross over at 731–741 °C, with nitriding dominating below and coarsening above. From a degradation perspective, a balanced long-term window of approximately 750–780 °C is identified. Both the crossover and the high-temperature penalty remain robust in a sensitivity analysis. The joint model supports what-if analysis and remaining-useful-life estimation for maintenance planning.

title: Photochemical CO 2 Reduction Using Zinc Vanadium Oxyhydroxide Catalysts
summary: ABSTRACT Photochemical reduction of CO 2 into value‐added chemicals such as formic acid (HCOOH) or CO is a promising approach for solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion. Mixed‐anion compounds have attracted attention as a versatile platform fo
content: ABSTRACT Photochemical reduction of CO 2 into value‐added chemicals such as formic acid (HCOOH) or CO is a promising approach for solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion. Mixed‐anion compounds have attracted attention as a versatile platform for catalyst design, yet combining catalytic activity with structural robustness under reaction conditions remains a challenge. Here, we report that Zn 3 V 2 O 7 (OH) 2 ·2H 2 O (ZVO), a layered Zn‐based mixed‐anion oxyhydroxide, functions as an efficient catalyst for CO 2 reduction under visible light when coupled with [Ru(bpy) 3 ] 2+ ( RuPS ) as a photosensitizer and 1‐benzyl‐1,4‐dihydronicotinamide (BNAH) as an electron donor. ZVO synthesized hydrothermally at 353 K afforded HCOOH with an apparent quantum yield of 1.7% at 460 nm and a CO 2 reduction selectivity of 98%, while retaining its layered structure and nanosheet morphology after the photoreaction. Heat treatment of ZVO transformed the oxyhydroxide framework into the oxide phase (Zn 3 V 2 O 8 ), together with progressive loss of hydroxyl groups. Notably, samples sharing the same Zn 3 V 2 O 8 phase exhibited markedly different photochemical CO 2 reduction activities, demonstrating that the catalytic behavior cannot be explained solely by the bulk crystalline phase. Restoring surface hydroxyl groups on inactive Zn 3 V 2 O 8 increased both CO 2 uptake and CO 2 reduction activity without substantially altering the bulk crystalline phase or specific surface area. These findings highlight the importance of hydroxyl‐rich surface chemical environments in governing CO 2 adsorption and catalytic performance in mixed‐anion photocatalyst systems.

title: Pyrolysis-Based Fire Modeling of Polyurethane Foam Incorporating a Grid-Independent Method
summary: Abstract To apply pyrolysis-based fire modeling to fire risk assessment, problems associated with coarse grids, such as inaccurate predictions of ignition and fire spread, must be addressed. Polyurethane foam (PUF) is widely used as an insu
content: Abstract To apply pyrolysis-based fire modeling to fire risk assessment, problems associated with coarse grids, such as inaccurate predictions of ignition and fire spread, must be addressed. Polyurethane foam (PUF) is widely used as an insulating material, and its constituent components are well characterized, making it suitable for pyrolysis-based fire modeling. In this study, a PUF fire model was developed using a pyrolysis model incorporating a grid-independent modeling method. PUF was represented by three components: virgin polyurethane foam, polyol beads, and a polyol layer. The combustion characteristics were adjusted by varying the area exposed to gas-phase cells and validated against cone calorimeter experiments. The proposed PUF fire model smoothly reproduced the two-stage combustion behavior, although the peak heat release rate during the second stage was overpredicted, particularly at low external radiative heat fluxes. Based on the validated PUF fire model, the grid-independent method was applied to PUF slab fire simulations. The method adjusted thermal properties and reaction kinetic parameters according to the cell temperature, which varied with grid size, while maintaining the one-dimensional heat transfer solution. The proposed method successfully reproduced the HRR and fire spread rate of the PUF slab fire, although a time delay in fire development was observed.

title: Sorption-enhanced autothermal reforming of synthetic and real agro-industrial wastewaters
summary: In this work, sorption-enhanced reforming (SER) and sorption-enhanced autothermal reforming (SE-ATR) were investigated for hydrogen production from synthetic and real olive mill wastewater (OMW) and real distillery wastewater (DW), for the
content: In this work, sorption-enhanced reforming (SER) and sorption-enhanced autothermal reforming (SE-ATR) were investigated for hydrogen production from synthetic and real olive mill wastewater (OMW) and real distillery wastewater (DW), for the first time; materials employed included a previously reported Ni–Rh catalyst supported on a hydrotalcite-derived material, promoted with La, and a commercial CaO as CO 2 -selective sorbent. Basic characterization of the catalyst revealed, through temperature-programmed reduction with H 2 (TPR – H 2 ), the reduction temperature of 750 °C. Sorption test results showed a CaO CO 2 sorption capacity of ∼2.0 mmol CO 2 ·g sorb -1 under dry conditions at 500 ℃ and p CO2 = 0.048 bar, increasing to ∼8.5 mmol CO 2 ·g sorb -1 in the presence of steam at 500 ℃ with p CO2 = 0.007 bar and p H 2 O = 0.855 bar. In the SER experiments at 500 °C, pre-breakthrough H 2 yields reached 10.85 mol H 2 ·mol OMW -1 with H 2 purities close to 99%, while the SE-ATR achieved lower yields (∼6.4 mol H 2 ·mol OMW -1 ) but improved thermal efficiency and reduced coke formation. Over four sorption-desorption cycles, sorbent capacity decreased to 58.6% of its initial value for the SE-ATR, which was attributed to sintering of the CaO sorbent. Tests with real OMW and DW achieved total organic carbon (TOC) and chemical oxygen demand (COD) removals above 98% and 99%, respectively, with total phenolic content (TPH) removal exceeding 95%. The reaction condensate of the real effluents, had a sufficiently low organic load to be discarded, according to EU regulation. These results demonstrated the potential of the SER and the SE-ATR for simultaneous renewable hydrogen production and wastewater treatment.

title: Diagenetic Evolution of Deep Tight Sandstone Reservoirs in the Lower Jurassic Strata of the Kuqa Depression, Tarim Basin
summary: Abstract Deep sandstone reservoirs are generally characterized by low permeability; nevertheless, effective reservoir rocks can still develop within them. However, the types of effective reservoir rocks and tight rocks require further chara
content: Abstract Deep sandstone reservoirs are generally characterized by low permeability; nevertheless, effective reservoir rocks can still develop within them. However, the types of effective reservoir rocks and tight rocks require further characterization, and the differences in their diagenetic processes warrant further investigation. This study examines the diagenetic evolutionary processes of different petrofacies in the tight sandstone reservoirs of the Jurassic Ahe Formation in the Kuqa Depression of the Tarim Basin, based on analyses of effective reservoir rocks and tight petrofacies. Research indicates that the sandstones of the Jurassic Ahe Formation are predominantly medium- to coarse-grained lithic sandstones with minor feldspathic litharenite. These sandstones are classified into three petrofacies: petrofacies A (ductile lithic-lean sandstone), petrofacies B (ductile lithic-rich sandstone), and petrofacies C (tightly carbonate-cemented sandstone). These three petrofacies exhibit significant differences in terms of diagenesis and diagenetic pathways. Petrofacies A is an effective reservoir rock, characterized by a relatively high content of rigid grains. During burial, fluid activity was frequent, causing this petrofacies to experience multiple episodes and types of diagenesis. Cement types are diverse but occur in low abundance, and secondary dissolution pores are relatively well developed. Petrofacies B and C are classified as tight petrofacies. Petrofacies B contains a high abundance of ductile grains; during the early diagenetic stage, severe porosity loss occurs because of mechanical compaction. Late diagenesis is dominated by clay mineral transformation, with almost no other fluid–rock interactions occurring. Similarly, petrofacies C experiences extensive pore filling by calcite cements during early diagenesis, making pore spaces exceptionally rare and leading to weak fluid–rock interactions. This study contributes to the analysis of deep tight sandstone reservoir quality and the identification of effective reservoir rocks capable of hosting hydrocarbon accumulation, thereby providing a geological basis for deep hydrocarbon exploration and development.

title: Extraction Procedures Reshape the Detectable Fumonisin Chemical Space of Fusarium verticillioides across Culture Media
summary: Abstract Fusarium verticillioides produces fumonisins and numerous secondary metabolites, yet extraction procedures may strongly shape their analytical detection. We combined targeted and untargeted LC–HRMS approaches to compare ethyl aceta
content: Abstract Fusarium verticillioides produces fumonisins and numerous secondary metabolites, yet extraction procedures may strongly shape their analytical detection. We combined targeted and untargeted LC–HRMS approaches to compare ethyl acetate, acidified ACN/H₂O, and sequential ACN/H₂O extraction across four culture media. Extraction-dependent metabolite profiles varied markedly with both culture medium and metabolite structure. Acidified ACN/H₂O procedures generated the most consistent fumonisin B1 (FB1) signals, whereas ethyl acetate yielded weak FB1 responses but revealed complementary subsets of metabolites, including fusarin A, fusaric acid, bikaverin-related compounds, and several fumonisin-related features. Structurally related fumonisins displayed heterogeneous solvent-dependent responses, and sequential extraction provided no systematic advantage over single ACN/H₂O extraction. These findings demonstrate that extraction procedures reshape the detectable chemical space of F. verticillioides and support objective-driven solvent selection for fungal metabolomics and mycotoxin profiling.

title: Nitrate salt of a hydrocarbazole oxime cation and a hydrated co-crystal of its chloride salt with cyclohexane-1,2,3-trione 1,3-dioxime
source: Acta Crystallographica Section E Crystallographic Communications
summary: In the presence of nickel(II) salts, cyclohexane-1,3-dione dioxime is transformed into a hydrocarbazole oxime cation, isolated as a nitrate salt, N ,9-dihydroxy-5-(hydroxyimino)-2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-octahydro-1 H -carbazol-4-iminium nitrate ( 1
content: In the presence of nickel(II) salts, cyclohexane-1,3-dione dioxime is transformed into a hydrocarbazole oxime cation, isolated as a nitrate salt, N ,9-dihydroxy-5-(hydroxyimino)-2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-octahydro-1 H -carbazol-4-iminium nitrate ( 1 , C 12 H 16 N 3 O 3 + ·NO 3 − ), and as a hydrated chloride co-crystal with cyclohexane-1,2,3-trione 1,3-dioxime, N ,9-dihydroxy-5-(hydroxyimino)-2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-octahydro-1 H -carbazol-4-iminium chloride–cyclohexane-1,2,3-trione 1,3-dioxime–water (1/1/3) ( 2 , C 12 H 16 N 3 O 3 + ·Cl − ·C 6 H 8 N 2 O 3 ·3H 2 O). In 1 , the cation and nitrate anion occupy mirror sites. The symmetry-related ring methylene C atoms in the cation are disordered over two positions [occupancies 0.896 (12) and 0.104 (12)]. The asymmetric unit of 2 contains one cation, one trionedioxime molecule, one chloride anion and three water molecules; one water oxygen is disordered over two sites [occupancies 0.935 (7) and 0.065 (7)]. Both cations have an intramolecular N—H...N contact, with the proton distributed over mirror-related sites in 1 but assigned to a single nitrogen site in 2 . The hydroxy group attached to the nitrogen at the 9-position of the hydrocarbazole moiety in 1 forms a hydrogen bond to the nitrate anion, whereas chloride, trionedioxime and water molecules participate in the hydrogen-bonding network of 2 .

title: Sterna migration optimization-based uncertainty-aware energy scheduling in hybrid solar and wind power systems using graph diffusion learning
summary: Operational uncertainty in hybrid networks that integrate solar Photovoltaic (PV) and wind power is considerable and primarily caused by the unpredictable changes in the generation of renewables and the demand for power, which has a negativ
content: Operational uncertainty in hybrid networks that integrate solar Photovoltaic (PV) and wind power is considerable and primarily caused by the unpredictable changes in the generation of renewables and the demand for power, which has a negative impact on reliability, power quality, and cost-effectiveness alike. In this respect, the research work under discussion puts forward a comprehensive uncertainty reduction framework that integrates optimal energy scheduling with predictive modelling in order to efficiently control the nonlinear interactions of PV generation, wind power, load demand, and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The proposed framework, called StMA-DGDNN, integrates the Sterna Migration Algorithm and a Decoupled Graph Diffusion Neural Network. In this framework, StMA minimizes Total System Cost (TSC), Annual Energy Losses (AEL), Energy Not Supplied (ENS), and Voltage Deviation (VD), thus optimizing the hybrid PV-WT-BESS dispatch. On the other hand, DGDNN captures spatial-temporal dependencies through graph diffusion and attention mechanisms, and performs uncertainty-aware nodal prediction of PV power, wind power, and load demand. The suggested system has been put into practice and examined in the MATLAB/Simulink setting, and its efficacy was measured against the performance of several current optimization methods like Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks with Particle Swarm Optimization (DCGAN-PSO), Artificial Ecosystem-based Optimization with Opposition-Based Learning (AEO-OBL), Particle Swarm Optimization with Sine Cosine Optimization (PSO-SCO), Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm (AHA), and Cuckoo Search Algorithm (CSA). The comparative results demonstrate that the proposed StMA-DGDNN achieves the lowest TSC of $1,402,300, reduces AEL to 894.24 kWh, limits ENS to 4.21 MWh, and maintains VD at 0.2724 p.u., outperforming all benchmark methods. Statistical and ablation analyses further confirm the robustness of the approach and highlight that the synergistic integration of optimization and prediction is the key contributor to the observed performance improvements. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and reliable solution for uncertainty-aware operation of hybrid PV-WT power networks.

title: Effective Traffic Impact Assessment and Enhancing Sustainable Tourism Logistics: A Case Study of Burapha Chollatit Scenic Road in the Eastern Economic Corridor
summary: Background Coastal tourism corridors experience variable traffic demand and require assessment approaches that account for weekend travel, access constraints, and environmentally sensitive locations. This study examines traffic impact asses
content: Background Coastal tourism corridors experience variable traffic demand and require assessment approaches that account for weekend travel, access constraints, and environmentally sensitive locations. This study examines traffic impact assessment (TIA) for the Burapha Chollatit Scenic Road Phase 2 project in Rayong Province, in Thailand’s Eastern Economic Corridor. Methods A case-study assessment draws on traffic counts, non-participant site observations, project engineering documentation, and secondary tourism and environmental information. Road-segment and intersection operations were examined using volume-to-capacity (V/C) ratios, control delay, and level-of-service indicators under weekday and weekend/holiday peak scenarios. Forecast improvement scenarios are distinguished from observed baseline conditions. Results Under the proposed road and junction improvements, modelled segment V/C ratios decreased from approximately 0.80–0.84 to 0.55–0.70, and average weekend-peak intersection control delay decreased from 88 to 34 seconds per vehicle. The original project materials also report tourism-demand and economic-benefit estimates; these are not independently verified post-construction outcomes and depend on the stated scenario assumptions. Conclusions Traffic counting combined with scenario-based operational assessment can inform the planning of coastal tourism corridors. Interpretation should distinguish measured baseline conditions from modelled future conditions; additional post-implementation counts and model calibration are needed to establish realised impacts.

title: Screening of Bacillus bacterial strains with capability of degrading T-2 toxin
summary: Abstract T-2 toxin (T-2) is a toxic fungal metabolite mainly produced by Fusarium species that are known to contaminate food products worldwide, posing serious risks to public health and the economy. Effective control of this toxin is there
content: Abstract T-2 toxin (T-2) is a toxic fungal metabolite mainly produced by Fusarium species that are known to contaminate food products worldwide, posing serious risks to public health and the economy. Effective control of this toxin is therefore a key objective in food safety. Recent efforts to manage T-2 contamination have focused on utilizing microbes, especially bacterial species from the Bacillus genus, as promising toxin degraders. This study evaluated the in vitro capacity of ten Bacillus strains (BC1–10) in degrading T-2. Three out of ten strains demonstrated T-2 degradation activity, with complete toxin removal achieved within 96 hours under standard culture condition. The major biotransformation product of T-2 was isolated by high-performance liquid chromatography and structurally characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy as HT-2 toxin. Toxicity assessment in kidney-derived HEK293T cells showed that HT-2 was less toxic than T-2, with EC 50 values of 12.8 and 1.8 nM, respectively. The findings supported the potential application of selected Bacillus strains as functional microbial additives to mitigate T-2 contamination and toxicity.

title: Mutant Isocitrate Dehydrogenase 1 Alters Extracellular Vesicle Secretion and Cargo Composition in Cellular Models
summary: Somatic mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) define major subtypes of adult diffuse gliomas and occur across a broad spectrum of cancers. These mutations ablate the conventional turnover of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and co
content: Somatic mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) define major subtypes of adult diffuse gliomas and occur across a broad spectrum of cancers. These mutations ablate the conventional turnover of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutarate and confer the neomorphic production of D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D2HG), which drives epigenetic remodeling. Growing evidence suggests this neomorphic activity may also affect how tumor cells communicate; small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) are elevated in gliomas, though how mutant IDH1 shapes sEV production and cargo remains poorly understood. Using glioblastoma and chondrosarcoma cell models, we show expression of mutant IDH1 correlates with a trend of increased sEV secretion, and that D2HG is packaged into sEVs that are taken up by cells. Cell-permeable D2HG treatment dose-dependently increased sEV release from IDH1 wild type cells. Untargeted proteomics showed that mutant IDH1 expression remodeled sEV cargo in a cell type-specific fashion, with mutant chondrosarcoma sEVs enriched in one-carbon metabolism enzymes, and mutant glioma sEVs in lysosomal luminal proteins and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperones. Mutant IDH1 glioma cell transcriptomics suggested expanded ER folding capacity and reduced ribosomal pathways, and sEVs from these cells decreased nascent protein synthesis in IDH1 wild type recipient cells. Together, this suggests sEVs can serve as carriers of mutant IDH1 phenotypes.

title: Standardizing industrial high-temperature heat pumps: A techno-economic analysis of modular concepts for paper and spray drying
summary: High-temperature heat pumps (HTHP) present a promising pathway for decarbonizing industrial process heat at temperatures up to 200 °C. However, widespread deployment remains constrained by high integration costs and a distinct lack of prior
content: High-temperature heat pumps (HTHP) present a promising pathway for decarbonizing industrial process heat at temperatures up to 200 °C. However, widespread deployment remains constrained by high integration costs and a distinct lack of prior research on modular concepts for HTHPs and their direct impact on cost reduction. This study addresses this gap through a techno-economic analysis targeting two specific drying processes in the paper and food industries. Thermal demands derived from market data establish the sizing basis for simulating 1 MW and 2 MW base modules. These baseline configurations are systematically scaled to 10 MW. Thermodynamically derived compressor requirements are cross-referenced with market available technologies. Performance validation confirms technical feasibility at COPs of 1.84 and 2.54. Standardized piston and screw compressor units adequately cover capacities up to 5 MW. Techno-economic modeling demonstrates capital recovery in less than one year against electric heating and 6 years for the 2 MW system versus natural gas-fired systems at €350/kW specific investment costs. Component standardization with 11 % capital expenditure reduction further accelerates payback by roughly one year. These results show that modular standardization significantly improves cost-effectiveness and thus provides a solid framework for the accelerated industrial adoption of HTHP technologies. The proposed modular framework offers a scalable design methodology for future work.

title: Ambient-cured GGBS geopolymer concrete modified with alccofine, silica fume, or nano-silica: experiments and machine learning
summary: Ambient-cured geopolymer concrete (GPC) offers a promising route toward lower-carbon infrastructure by utilizing industrial by-products while avoiding the thermal energy required for conventional heat curing. However, achieving mechanical a
content: Ambient-cured geopolymer concrete (GPC) offers a promising route toward lower-carbon infrastructure by utilizing industrial by-products while avoiding the thermal energy required for conventional heat curing. However, achieving mechanical and durability performance comparable to heat-cured GPC under ambient conditions remains a major challenge. This study investigates two multi-scale binder-modification routes for ambient-cured GGBS geopolymer concrete using Alccofine (AF) together with either silica fume (SF) or nano-silica (NS). AF was fixed at 10% of binder mass, while SF was investigated at 10–30% and NS at 1–3%. The experimental program first establishes 100% GGBS benchmark mixtures cured under ambient conditions and at 60 and 90 °C and subsequently evaluates the modified ambient-cured mixtures in terms of compressive, split tensile and flexural strengths, sorptivity, chemical resistance, freeze–thaw resistance and rapid chloride penetrability. The best-performing AF10SF20 mixture, containing 10% Alccofine and 20% silica fume, achieved compressive strengths of 51.8 and 66.0 MPa at 28 and 90 days, respectively, with corresponding 90-day split tensile and flexural strengths of 4.0 and 6.7 MPa. The mixture exhibited initial and secondary sorptivity values of 0.095 and 0.035 mm/min 0.5 , respectively, and showed strength losses of only 9.6%, 7.6%, 5.8% and 3.1% after exposure to H 2 SO 4 , HCl, Na 2 SO 4 and NaCl, respectively. After freeze–thaw exposure, the mass and strength losses were limited to 3.0% and 6.0%, while the rapid chloride penetrability was 1450 C. Notably, AF10SF20 exceeded the 90 °C-cured benchmark in several key performance indicators, including long-term compressive and flexural strength and resistance to transport and environmental deterioration. In parallel, machine-learning models were developed for compressive-strength prediction, with particle-swarm-optimization-assisted XGBoost providing the best reported predictive performance. Explainable artificial intelligence using SHAP, LIME, partial-dependence and individual-conditional-expectation analyses identified the major influencing mixture parameters and revealed nonlinear responses consistent with the experimentally observed best performed dosages. The findings demonstrate the potential of multiscale binder modification to reduce dependence on thermal curing under the investigated laboratory conditions, while further field-scale validation is required to establish its applicability under variable construction environments.

title: Taxonomic validation of Saccharomycotina yeast genome assemblies through type-material-anchored BLAST-based average nucleotide identity analysis at the NCBI
summary: The extensive genomic resources available for Saccharomycotina yeasts, including assemblies derived from type material, make this group well suited for genome-based taxonomic verification. This study evaluates the effectiveness of type-mate
content: The extensive genomic resources available for Saccharomycotina yeasts, including assemblies derived from type material, make this group well suited for genome-based taxonomic verification. This study evaluates the effectiveness of type-material-informed Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI) analysis for verifying the taxonomic assignments of Saccharomycotina genome assemblies. Public yeast genome assemblies were compared against type material assemblies using an alignment-based ANI workflow. Operational thresholds were established, and results were compared with DNA-DNA hybridization and FastANI analyses. Assemblies were evaluated by best-match status and coverage, and problematic type assemblies were flagged for further review. A 95% ANI threshold yielded high concordance with declared species assignments among query-to-type comparisons. Cases of high similarity between different species and hybrid genomes were identified, highlighting the need for expert taxonomic review in certain instances. The alignment-based ANI showed a strong correlation with traditional DNA-DNA reassociation values and agreed closely with FastANI for highly alignable assemblies. Type-material-informed ANI is a reliable tool for automated taxonomic verification of yeast genome assemblies, but its effectiveness depends on the availability and quality of type assemblies and accurate metadata. The approach enables continuous quality control and supports broader application in fungal taxonomy, with recommendations for improving reference coverage and data submission practices.

title: Forced Ignition of NH3/H2 Blends in a Mixing Layer with Different Air Temperatures
summary: Abstract Hydrogen addition has attracted significant attention due to its ability to improve the combustion performance of ammonia. However, the forced ignition mechanism of ammonia blended with hydrogen with various air temperatures under
content: Abstract Hydrogen addition has attracted significant attention due to its ability to improve the combustion performance of ammonia. However, the forced ignition mechanism of ammonia blended with hydrogen with various air temperatures under nonpremixed conditions remains unclear at present. The forced ignition process of ammonia-hydrogen blended fuel in a mixing layer is systematically investigated using numerical simulations. Three air temperatures, TO = 450, 750, and 1050 K, are considered. The results show that for the cases with TO = 450 and 750 K, a tetrabrachial flame structure, consisting of two premixed branches and two nonpremixed branches, forms in the mixing layer after ignition. The flame is dominated by a propagating mode. When the air temperature is increased to 1050 K, the edge flame initially exhibits a tetrabrachial flame structure dominated by propagation, but later an autoignition-dominated branch appears upstream, resulting in a pentabrachial flame structure. The OH transport-budget analysis indicates that the autoignition branch is dominated by chemical reactions, with diffusion playing a comparatively minor role. In addition, HO2 and H2O2 serve as key markers for the formation of an autoignition branch. Analysis of the chemical reactions in the different flame branches shows that heat release in the lean nonpremixed branch is dominated by the hydrogen oxidation reaction system, while the rich nonpremixed branch is controlled by ammonia oxidation and nitrogen chemical reaction pathways. The reactions in the autoignition branch are primarily associated with the hydrogen–oxygen chain reactions. The thermal contributions of each branch further indicate that the premixed branch is the primary source of heat release for the edge flame. Increasing the air temperature not only enhances the heat release intensity of each propagation branch, but also activates the thermal contribution of the autoignition flame branch.

title: HvMAPK5‐Mediated Phosphorylation of HvWRKY75 Enhances Salt Tolerance in Barley
summary: ABSTRACT Soil salinization is a significant constraint on crop productivity, necessitating the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in cereals such as barley. In this study, a novel regulatory module comprising
content: ABSTRACT Soil salinization is a significant constraint on crop productivity, necessitating the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying salt tolerance in cereals such as barley. In this study, a novel regulatory module comprising the ion transporter HvHKT1;2 , the transcription factor HvWRKY75 , and the mitogen‐activated protein kinase HvMAPK5 was identified. HvHKT1;2 localized to the plasma membrane, and its overexpression promoted Na + efflux at the root apex, reduced Na + accumulation in shoots, increased the K + /Na + ratio, and enhanced salt tolerance, whereas HvHKT1;2 knockdown produced the opposite phenotype. Furthermore, HvWRKY75 directly bound to the HvHKT1;2 promoter and activated its transcription. Under salt stress, HvMAPK5 interacted with and phosphorylated HvWRKY75 at Ser21, thereby enhancing HvWRKY75 protein stability and transcriptional activity toward HvHKT1;2. Consistently, HvMAPK5 overexpression increased HvWRKY75 protein abundance, upregulated HvHKT1;2 expression, and enhanced salt tolerance, whereas HvMAPK5 knockdown accelerated HvWRKY75 degradation and compromised salt tolerance. Collectively, our findings identify a regulatory module consisting of HvMAPK5 , HvWRKY75 , and HvHKT1;2 that maintains cellular Na + /K + homeostasis during salt stress, providing a mechanistic framework for breeding salt‐tolerant barley varieties.

title: Oxidative amination of 2-cyclohexenone with aniline to N- aryl aniline over supported vanadium incorporated hetropoly tungstate catalysts
summary: Vanadium is substituted into the primary structure of tungstophosphoric acid and subsequently dispersed on different supports. The physicochemical properties of vanadium-containing tungstophosphoric acid (TPAV) catalyst are derived from var
content: Vanadium is substituted into the primary structure of tungstophosphoric acid and subsequently dispersed on different supports. The physicochemical properties of vanadium-containing tungstophosphoric acid (TPAV) catalyst are derived from various spectroscopic methods. FT-IR and Raman analysis suggest that vanadium is present in the primary structure of heteropolytungstate. The TPAV retained its Keggin ion structure after dispersing on various supports. The catalytic activity of these catalysts was investigated for the oxidative amination of 2-cyclohexenone with aniline. The catalyst's activity depends on the number of vanadium ions present in the heteropolytungstate and the nature of the support. The silica-supported TPAV catalyst provides higher activity than niobia and zirconia supports. The catalyst’s elevated catalytic activity is due to its suitable acidity and redox properties. The reaction was studied under different conditions, and the optimal parameters were established. The catalyst is stable and shows consistent activity upon reuse.

title: Petrophysical Characterization of Lower Cretaceous Reservoir Intervals in the Ry‐1 Well, East Pande Block, Offshore Southern Tanzania
summary: ABSTRACT The Lower Cretaceous reservoirs off the coast of the Mandawa Basin, in the East Pande Block of southern coastal and offshore Tanzania, have been poorly studied, and their detailed petrophysical properties remain insufficiently docu
content: ABSTRACT The Lower Cretaceous reservoirs off the coast of the Mandawa Basin, in the East Pande Block of southern coastal and offshore Tanzania, have been poorly studied, and their detailed petrophysical properties remain insufficiently documented. This study integrates the interpretation of velocity deviation logs and conventional well logs, including sonic, neutron, density, gamma ray, and resistivity logs, to characterize these reservoirs. The results show that they exhibit fair to good porosity and estimated average permeability values ranging between 300 and 450 mD. Their average shale volume ranges from 27% to 33%, indicating the dominance of shaly sand units within these reservoirs. Despite the relatively high estimated permeability, the results also show that permeability becomes compromised when shaliness exceeds 30%. The results further indicate that the Lower Cretaceous reservoirs in the study area are dominated by primary porosity, with limited fractured intervals. These reservoirs are devoid of hydrocarbon accumulations and are interpreted to have been deposited during episodic water level fluctuations, agreeing with regional studies. This study provides a benchmark for future research in the region, including the integration of additional well data and core analysis to further constrain the depositional environment, and fracture and permeability distribution in the entire region.

title: Flood risk mitigation for an urban catchment: findings from a grey, nature-based solutions and hybrid strategy approach
source: Journal of Water and Climate Change
summary: ABSTRACT Flow diagram showing rainfall-driven flood modelling using HEC-RAS, comparing baseline, nature-based solutions, structural measures, and hybrid scenarios, with reductions in flood depth, velocity, and discharge across the catchment
content: ABSTRACT Flow diagram showing rainfall-driven flood modelling using HEC-RAS, comparing baseline, nature-based solutions, structural measures, and hybrid scenarios, with reductions in flood depth, velocity, and discharge across the catchment. Rapid urban expansion and informal settlements are increasing exposure to flood hazards in urbanising catchments such as the Nairobi River Catchment. The 2024 El Niño event caused widespread flooding, affecting critical infrastructure and highlighting the urgent need for effective mitigation strategies. This study evaluates three flood management approaches using the HEC-RAS model: (1) modified channels as grey infrastructure, (2) soil organic matter enhancement and reforestation as Nature-based Solutions, and (3) a hybrid strategy. Model performance showed strong agreement with observed flows (R2 = 0.88; NSE = 0.75). Spatial datasets, including Global Forest Change and Land Productivity Dynamics, were used to identify intervention zones and parameterise scenarios. Results show that NbS reduced peak discharge by 37–75% and delayed peak flow by about one hour. Grey infrastructure achieved the greatest impact, reducing flood depths by 55–60% and peak discharge by 48–75%, but increased flow velocities. The hybrid strategy provided the most balanced hydraulic performance, combining runoff attenuation with improved channel conveyance to deliver consistent reductions in flood magnitude and enhanced flow regulation. These findings demonstrate that integrated approaches combining engineered and nature-based interventions offer a resilient pathway for managing urban flood risk under increasing climatic and developmental pressures.

title: Rigorous Benchmarking of Continuous Dry-Printed CNT Networks as High-Performance Electrochemical Sensors
summary: Abstract In this study, we present a systematic evaluation of the electrochemical performance of floating catalyst chemical vapor deposited carbon nanotubes (FCCVD-CNTs) and compare their performance against conventional carbon, gold, and p
content: Abstract In this study, we present a systematic evaluation of the electrochemical performance of floating catalyst chemical vapor deposited carbon nanotubes (FCCVD-CNTs) and compare their performance against conventional carbon, gold, and platinum electrodes. Differential pulse voltammetry and cyclic voltammetry were employed to detect well-established benchmark redox species, such as methylene blue, 3,3′,5,5′-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), and acetaminophen (commonly known as paracetamol), in both buffer and human plasma, serving as proof-of-concept for the proposed approach. The FCCVD-CNTs achieved superior electrochemical sensor performance metrics, such as their signal-to-noise ratio, signal-to-background ratio, and detection limit, highlighting their potential as a novel material to redefine sensing standards in complex biological environments. Recognizing the challenges associated with processing an electrode material into a scalable, robust, high-performance, ready-to-use platform, particularly in the form of a miniaturized electrochemical cell such as a screen-printed electrode (SPE), we benchmarked our FCCVD-CNT-based dry-printed electrode (DPE) against commercially available, ink processed SPEs to assess its practical suitability for biosensing applications. The obtained results corroborate the capability of the CNT DPEs as a robust alternative for biosensing applications in a clinically representative matrix.

title: Copper/Zirconium MOF Electrochemical Sensing Platform for High Sensitivity Analysis of Bisphenol S in Real Samples
summary: Abstract 4,4′-sulfonyldiphenol (Bisphenol S, BPS) is used as a substitute for bisphenol A (BPA) in industrial plastic and epoxy resin production. However, it still retains estrogenic activity similar to BPA, with a longer biological half-li
content: Abstract 4,4′-sulfonyldiphenol (Bisphenol S, BPS) is used as a substitute for bisphenol A (BPA) in industrial plastic and epoxy resin production. However, it still retains estrogenic activity similar to BPA, with a longer biological half-life and stronger skin permeability than BPA, can lead to toxic pollution, and bring various health risks to humans. Consequently, it is crucial to develop a simple, specific, and sensitive detection method for the quantification of BPS. In this work, a copper/zirconium MOF bimetallic organic framework-based composite (CuZr-MOF/MXene/CNTs, BMC) was prepared through a hydrothermal method for sensitive electrochemical determination of BPS. The distribution of Cu-MOF and Zr-MOF around the MXene formed a tight bond, making the obtained BMC a stable structure, while the incorporation of MXene and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) significantly improved its electrical conductivity. Under optimized conditions, the sensor exhibited a well-defined linear dependence between the peak current and BPS concentration in the range from 0.2 to 50 μM, with a low limit of detection (LOD) of 0.0396 μM. The modified BMC sensor was employed to quantify trace levels of BPS in real samples and achieved good recovery rates, demonstrating its practical applicability in real samples. Selectivity tests demonstrated satisfactory tolerance toward interfering metal ions (K+, Na+, and Mg2+) and compounds with similar structures (glucose, ascorbic acid, glycine, hydroquinone, BPA, and phenol). It also demonstrated commendable reproducibility and appropriate performance in three batches of production with a relative standard deviation (RSD) of 0.409%. The sensor can also show good stability for over 35 days. This work provides a new technical strategy for the sensitive detection of toxic BPS in real samples by coupling the active sites of bimetallic MOFs and the high conductivity of CNTs and MXene.

title: Neutrophil serine proteases are internalized by glioblastoma cells and modulate cell mechanics, apoptosis, and migration
summary: Abstract Neutrophil serine proteases (NSPs) are crucial mediators of the immune response, with cathepsin G (CatG) and neutrophil elastase (NE) being prominently released by activated neutrophils during neuroinflammation. Beyond pathogen cle
content: Abstract Neutrophil serine proteases (NSPs) are crucial mediators of the immune response, with cathepsin G (CatG) and neutrophil elastase (NE) being prominently released by activated neutrophils during neuroinflammation. Beyond pathogen clearance, NSPs modulate cellular functions through surface binding and internalization. Glioblastoma (GB), the most aggressive primary brain cancer, is characterized by its significant therapeutic resistance and invasive properties. We investigated the effects of CatG and NE on human GB cell lines U87 and A172. Both NSPs were internalized, with NE being mostly sequestered to CD107a+ endocytic compartments. A172 cells were susceptible to NSP-induced apoptosis, whereas U87 cells exhibited resistance. Exposure to CatG or NE significantly reduced cellular stiffness, as revealed by biomechanical profiling via atomic force microscopy (AFM) in U87 and A172 cells, suggesting a protease-mediated transition to a more deformable state. Strikingly, CatG impaired U87 migration, indicating that while softening is often linked to invasion, proteolytic activity may destabilize the structural integrity required for movement. These findings collectively suggest NSP-mediated GB cell plasticity.

title: Construction and validation of catalyst-based biofiltration reactors for the treatment of disinfection by-products in drinking water
summary: ABSTRACT The wide application of disinfection technology in drinking water treatment leads to the formation of potentially harmful disinfection by-products such as trihalomethane (THMs) and haloacetic acid (HAAs), which poses a long-term ri
content: ABSTRACT The wide application of disinfection technology in drinking water treatment leads to the formation of potentially harmful disinfection by-products such as trihalomethane (THMs) and haloacetic acid (HAAs), which poses a long-term risk to public health. Traditional treatment methods are often difficult to completely remove these stubborn compounds. To solve this problem, a new type of catalytic enhanced biofilter reactor (CBR) was developed, and disinfection by-products (DBPs) were efficiently removed by synergistic catalytic oxidation and biodegradation. Two high-performance catalysts, FeOx/C (mixed-valence iron oxides, mainly γ-Fe2O3 and Fe3O4, supported on activated carbon) and Mn-TiO2, combined oxidative activity with biocompatibility, enabling the disruption of the stable structure of DBPs and enhancing its biodegradability. The reactor adopted a unique layered design comprising a catalytic packing zone and a biofilm-active zone and operated under intermittent aeration conditions. The reactor adopts a unique layered design, including catalytic packing area and biofilm-active area, and operates under intermittent aeration conditions. The experimental results show that compared with the traditional biofilter, the catalytic biological synergistic system significantly improves the removal efficiency of THMs and HAAs. The system achieved optimal performance under neutral to weakly alkaline conditions (pH 6.8–7.5), with the optimal dissolved oxygen (DO) concentration experimentally determined to be 3.5–4.5 mg/L during the stable operating period, compared with 2.0–4.0 mg/L during the start-up period (days 0–14). The long-term operation for 30 days confirmed the stability of the system, and the chemical oxygen demand (COD) and ammonia nitrogen (NH4+ -N) decreased continuously. In this study, an innovative, efficient, and sustainable DBP advanced purification technology for drinking water is proposed, which has broad application prospects in practical engineering applications.

title: Atmospheric CO 2 estimates during the Aptian (Early Cretaceous): New Evidence from Carbon Isotopes of Sediments in Northeast China
summary: The Aptian (Early Cretaceous) is a critical interval for understanding greenhouse climate dynamics, yet high-resolution continental records of atmospheric CO 2 remain poorly understood. Here, we reconstruct Aptian atmospheric CO 2 levels us
content: The Aptian (Early Cretaceous) is a critical interval for understanding greenhouse climate dynamics, yet high-resolution continental records of atmospheric CO 2 remain poorly understood. Here, we reconstruct Aptian atmospheric CO 2 levels using paired carbon isotopic analyses (δ 13 C org and δ 13 C carb ) from a lacustrine succession of the Jiufotang Formation in Northeast China. Our record reveals pronounced p CO 2 fluctuations, with values ranging from 337 to 1145 ppmv (mean ∼626 ppmv). These variations show higher concentrations in the lower and upper segments of the formation, separated by a mid-interval decline. Spectral analysis further identifies strong ∼165 kyr, ∼260 kyr and ∼405 kyr eccentricity cycles, indicating that orbital forcing played a key role in modulating the carbon cycle. The observed p CO 2 peaks coincide with enhanced of intracontinental volcanism and oceanic anoxic events (OAE1a), suggesting a combined forcing from volcanism, orbital rhythms, and carbon sequestration. This study provides a high-resolution continental perspective on CO 2 dynamics during the Aptian, offering a valuable continental archive to decipher carbon-climate interactions under greenhouse conditions.

title: Global urban tree leaf area under climate change: divergent projected trajectories and the limits of space-for-time inference
summary: Abstract Urban trees moderate city climates, yet how their leaf-area density relates to projected future climates is poorly constrained globally. We fitted a Random Forest model to monthly temperature and precipitation normals and the multi
content: Abstract Urban trees moderate city climates, yet how their leaf-area density relates to projected future climates is poorly constrained globally. We fitted a Random Forest model to monthly temperature and precipitation normals and the multi-year mean leaf area index (LAI) derived from a satellite-informed machine-learning urban tree product across 21,590 urban cells, then projected end-of-century change under six Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. Leave-one-continent-out validation gave $$R^2 = 0.846$$ (95% CI $$0.813$$ – $$0.873$$ from spatial-block resampling), but that spatial skill does not transfer to time: driven by observed reanalysis anomalies over exactly the satellite record, the same relationship reproduces neither the magnitude nor the pattern of observed change ( $$\rho = +0.087$$ ). The response variable is itself a machine-learning product built from overlapping climate predictors, so the spatial fit is not independent evidence of that relationship either. Under modified Mann–Kendall tests with false-discovery-rate control, 19.8% of cells greened and 5.3% browned during 2000–2022, roughly half the browning obtained without those corrections. Global mean change is positive under all scenarios, yet 32.6% of cells decline under SSP5-8.5, with declines concentrated in tropical humid cities and gains at high latitudes. Two further results bound them: 10.6% of cells fall outside the fitted climate domain under SSP5-8.5, and four algorithms agree on the sign of change at only 68.1% of cells. We report these as changes implied by transferring a spatial relationship into future climates, not forecasts: the zonal contrast is the most reproducible result across the evaluated algorithms; cell-level magnitudes and city orderings are not.

title: Biomarker analysis of liver cells exposed to surfactant-wrapped and oxidized multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs)
summary: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have great potential in industrial, consumer, and mechanical applications, based partly on their unique structural, optical and electronic properties. CNTs are commonly oxidized or treated with surfactants to facilit
content: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have great potential in industrial, consumer, and mechanical applications, based partly on their unique structural, optical and electronic properties. CNTs are commonly oxidized or treated with surfactants to facilitate aqueous solution processing, and these CNT surface modifications also increase possible human and ecological exposures to nanoparticle-contaminated waters. To determine the exposure outcomes of oxidized and surfactant-wrapped multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) on biochemical processes, metabolomics based profiling of human liver cells (C3A) was utilized. Cells were exposed to 0, 10, or 100 ng/mL of MWCNTs for 24 and 48 hr. MWCNT particle size distribution, charge, and aggregation were monitored concurrently during exposures. Following MWCNT exposure, cellular metabolites were extracted, lyophilized, and buffered for 1H NMR analysis. Acquired spectra were subjected to both multivariate and univariate analysis to determine the consequences of nanotube exposure on the metabolite profile of C3A cells. Resulting scores plots illustrated temporal and dose-dependent metabolite responses to all MWCNTs tested. Loadings plots coupled with t-test filtered spectra identified metabolites of interest. XPS analysis revealed the presence of hydroxyl and carboxyl functionalities on both MWCNTs surfaces. Metal content analysis by ICP-AES indicated that the total mass concentration of the potentially toxic impurities in the exposure experiments were extremely low (i.e. [Ni] ≤ 2 × 10−10 g/mL). Preliminary data suggested that MWCNT exposure causes perturbations in biochemical processes involved in cellular oxidation as well as fluxes in amino acid metabolism and fatty acid synthesis. Dose-response trajectories were apparent and spectral peaks related to both dose and MWCNT dispersion methodologies were determined. Correlations of the significant changes in metabolites will help to identify potential biomarkers associated with carbonaceous nanoparticle exposure. This dataset is associated with the following publication: Henderson, M., D. Bouchard, X. Chang, S. Al-Abed, and Q. Teng. Biomarker analysis of liver cells exposed to surfactant-wrapped and oxidized multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs). SCIENCE OF THE TOTAL ENVIRONMENT. Elsevier BV, AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS, 565: 777–786, (2016).

title: Advancements in Eu2O3-functionalized heterostructures: Synthetic pathways, performance mechanisms, and multi-functional sustainable applications
summary: Rare earth metal oxide nanoparticles possess unique physicochemical properties that enable diverse technological applications. Among these, europium oxide (Eu 2 O 3 ), characterized by a wide band gap energy (~ 4.4 eV) and advantageous diel
content: Rare earth metal oxide nanoparticles possess unique physicochemical properties that enable diverse technological applications. Among these, europium oxide (Eu 2 O 3 ), characterized by a wide band gap energy (~ 4.4 eV) and advantageous dielectric properties, has attracted significant research interest. This review comprehensively covers recent progress in the synthesis of Eu 2 O 3 and Eu 2 O 3 -functionalized heterostructures via diverse chemical routes, including precipitation, hydrothermal, solvothermal, sonochemical, sol-gel, and reflux methods. Particular emphasis is placed on the influence of key operational parameters, such as reaction temperature, time, and capping agents, on particle morphology and structural evolution. Furthermore, the functional performance and underlying mechanisms of these heterostructures across photocatalysis, luminescence, chemical sensing, and biological domain applications are critically evaluated, highlighting current challenges and prospects for sustainable utilization.

title: Reconfigurable Poly(Ionic Liquid) Hydrogel Electrolytes for Ultrawide‐Temperature, Damage‐Tolerant Hybrid Supercapacitors
summary: Hydrogel electrolytes for flexible energy storage devices commonly suffer from limited temperature tolerance and irreversible damage in chemical cross‐linked networks. Herein, a hydroxyl‐functionalized poly(ionic liquid) hydrogel electrolyt
content: Hydrogel electrolytes for flexible energy storage devices commonly suffer from limited temperature tolerance and irreversible damage in chemical cross‐linked networks. Herein, a hydroxyl‐functionalized poly(ionic liquid) hydrogel electrolyte (M‐C/HIL‐PAM) is synthesized via one‐step γ‐ray‐induced copolymerization of acrylamide and 1‐(2,3‐dihydroxypropyl)‐3‐vinylimidazolium chloride in an aqueous NaClO 4 /Mg(ClO 4 ) 2 solution. Reversible hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions from hydroxyl and imidazolium groups create a dynamically reconfigurable network, endowing high toughness (tensile strength ~390 kPa, elongation at break ~2025%), strong adhesion, and efficient self‐healing. Meanwhile, the synergistic hydration effect of Na + and Mg 2+ disrupts the hydrogen‐bond network of water molecules, enabling stable ion transport at −70 to 60 °C. Benefiting from these properties, the resulting activated carbon || δ‐MnO 2 hybrid supercapacitor fabricated by in situ radiation polymerization operates across this wide temperature range. The device exhibits no capacity decay after 2000 cycles at −60 °C, retains good performance after 5000 cycles at room temperature and 60 °C, and withstands 3000 bending cycles without significant loss. Furthermore, the pouch supercapacitor shows negligible capacity decay after physical damage and rejoining, demonstrating intrinsic self‐healing ability. This work offers a promising strategy for designing wide‐temperature, mechanically robust, and self‐healable hydrogel electrolytes for flexible energy storage devices under extreme conditions.

title: Multifunctional Helical Coaxial Fiber Platform Enabling Energy Autonomy and Intelligent Sensing
summary: Abstract Multifunctional self-powered fibers demonstrate significant potential for applications in wearable flexible electronics, human-machine interfaces, and Internet of Things (IoT) systems. A critical challenge in this field is achievin
content: Abstract Multifunctional self-powered fibers demonstrate significant potential for applications in wearable flexible electronics, human-machine interfaces, and Internet of Things (IoT) systems. A critical challenge in this field is achieving the effective integration and versatile application of various functional fibers. This study presents a novel multifunctional coaxial energy fiber capable of simultaneous energy harvesting, storage, and utilization. The fiber features a coaxial architecture that integrates an inner fiber-shaped zinc-ion supercapacitor (F-ZnSC) for energy storage and an outer spiral-yarn triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for energy harvesting and self-powered pressure sensor. The F-ZnSC comprises MXene-modified spiral yarn electrodes, a zinc wire anode, and a Gelatin/ZnSO₄ gel electrolyte, achieving a high specific capacitance of 455 mF cm⁻¹ along with excellent rate capability and cycling stability (e.g., ~96.6% capacitance retention after 5,000 cycles). The outer spiral-yarn TENG exhibits a high pressure sensitivity of 8 V kPa⁻¹, enabling effective and real-time monitoring of finger motions. Combining with a deep learning algorithm, the system recognizes five distinct hand gestures with an accuracy of 96.25%, demonstrating its utility in advanced game control and human-machine interaction. Furthermore, the encapsulation layer shared by the TENG and the F-ZnSC forms an additional contact-separation mode energy harvester. Ten such devices connected in parallel yield an output power of 177.1 μW, sufficient to power small electronics such as watches and calculators. This work highlights the promise of the coaxial energy fiber as a versatile platform for adaptive wearable energy systems, self-powered interfaces, and intelligent sensing.

title: Altered protein cysteine reactivity in senescent cells is a vulnerability for senolysis to ameliorate aging
summary: How diet shapes aging and age-related diseases marked by senescent cell accumulation remains unclear. Here we report vanadyl sulfate (VS), a mineral dietary supplement, as a senolytic agent. Oral VS ameliorates phenotypes of aging and diver
content: How diet shapes aging and age-related diseases marked by senescent cell accumulation remains unclear. Here we report vanadyl sulfate (VS), a mineral dietary supplement, as a senolytic agent. Oral VS ameliorates phenotypes of aging and diverse age-related disorders and extends lifespan in male mice. Integrated functional omics analyses show that senescent cells exhibit globally reduced proteome cysteine reactivity but increased expression and apparent cysteine reactivity of proteins essential for endoplasmic reticulum proteostasis. This redox–proteostasis state is linked to glutathione disulfide (GSSG) accumulation and can be recapitulated by GSSG delivery in nonsenescent cells. Mechanistically, VS inactivates reactive cysteines and promotes disulfide bond formation in senescent cells, leading to protein misfolding, aggregation and ultimately cell death. Glutathione reductase downregulation promotes GSSG accumulation, distinguishing senescent from nonsenescent cells and conferring selective susceptibility to VS. Our findings reveal an exploitable redox–proteostasis vulnerability of senescent cells with therapeutic potential to ameliorate aging. Wu, Yang, Li and colleagues identify vanadyl sulfate, a dietary supplement, as a senolytic that targets altered cysteine reactivity in senescent cells, improving age-related conditions and extending lifespan in mice.

title: Biobased poly(butadiene‐ co ‐myrcene) elastomers reinforced with treated sargassum: tailoring filler–rubber interactions through myrcene content
summary: Abstract Poly(butadiene‐ co ‐myrcene) elastomeric composites were developed using treated sargassum particles as a bio‐filler (TS), while maintaining constant low silica and silane loadings. This dual marine‐ and plant‐derived design simult
content: Abstract Poly(butadiene‐ co ‐myrcene) elastomeric composites were developed using treated sargassum particles as a bio‐filler (TS), while maintaining constant low silica and silane loadings. This dual marine‐ and plant‐derived design simultaneously valorizes β ‐myrcene as a plant‐derived comonomer and invasive sargassum biomass as a marine‐derived filler. The effects of myrcene composition and TS loading on vulcanization behavior, filler‐network response, morphology, mechanical properties, crosslink density, thermal stability, and viscoelastic behavior were investigated. Increasing myrcene content generally reduced rheometric torque, cure rate, crosslink density, hardness, and stiffness, while prolonging scorch and optimum cure times and increasing network extensibility. The effect of TS on cure kinetics depended on rubber composition and filler loading and was accompanied by increased reversion relative to the corresponding references without TS. Payne effect analysis showed a lower strain‐dependent filler‐network contribution with increasing myrcene composition, although changes in matrix stiffness and crosslink density also contributed to this response. Dynamic mechanical analysis showed that TS increased storage modulus in the biobased rubber composites with TS at appropriate loadings without substantial changes in glass transition temperature. TS also increased Young's modulus, hardness, and elongation at break, but did not systematically improve tensile strength and reduced crosslink density at higher myrcene compositions and TS loadings. Scanning electron microscopy indicated adequate physical contact at moderate TS loading but not conclusive evidence of improved filler dispersion. Overall, β ‐myrcene composition and TS loading provide complementary methods for modifying the stiffness, extensibility, filler‐network response, and viscoelastic behavior of these biobased rubber composites. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Engineering of electrospun PCL/Algal polysaccharide/HKUST-1 nanocomposites for potential biomedical applications
summary: Abstract In this study, polycaprolactone (PCL), algal-derived polysaccharides, and HKUST-1 were used to fabricate fibrous nanocomposites via electrospinning as a structural platform for potential biomedical applications. Algal polysaccharid
content: Abstract In this study, polycaprolactone (PCL), algal-derived polysaccharides, and HKUST-1 were used to fabricate fibrous nanocomposites via electrospinning as a structural platform for potential biomedical applications. Algal polysaccharides were extracted and purified from Chlorella and Tetraselmis . HKUST-1 was prepared using a hydrothermal method, with Cu(NO₃)₂·3H₂O and Cu(CH₃COO)₂·H₂O as copper precursors. HKUST-1, showed a uniform polyhedral morphology and average particle diameters of approximately 45–50 nm. BET analysis showed mesoporous structures with surface areas of 59.74 and 141.66 m²/g for the nitrate- and acetate-derived MOFs, respectively. PCL solutions with concentrations of 10, 15, 20, and 35% (w/v) were prepared, along with HKUST-1/PCL solutions containing 0.5, 1, 3, 4, and 5 wt% HKUST-1 relative to PCL. To fabricate the nanocomposites, the PCL solutions were initially electrospun to form the fibrous substrate. The three-layer PCL/algal polysaccharide/HKUST-1 nanocomposites were subsequently fabricated by adding the algal polysaccharide of Chlorella and Tetraselmis and HKUST-1 onto the PCL nanofibers. The average fiber diameters ranged from 70–1000 nm. Key fabrication parameters, including solvent type and ratio, solution concentration, and electrospinning conditions, were optimized to obtain uniform and homogeneous nanofibrous structure. The results indicated that the synthesized nanofibers exhibited nanoscale dimensions and a uniform morphology. Incorporating of polysaccharides into the PCL nanofibers increased the surface contact angle from 118° to 130–134°, indicating enhanced surface hydrophobicity. This increase was attributed to the compact molecular structure of the polysaccharides and their limited exposure at the fiber surface during electrospinning. Antibacterial tests revealed that HKUST-1 exhibited antibacterial activity against both E. coli and S. aureus , with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) values of 3.75 and 7.5 mg/mL, respectively. The Tetraselmis -derived polysaccharide exhibited bacteriostatic activity against S. aureus , with an MIC of 25 mg/mL. None of the tested samples exhibited detectable DPPH radical-scavenging activity, which may have been obscured by color interference from the samples at high concentration. This work presents the single-platform nanocomposites combining PCL, Chlorella - and Tetraselmis -derived polysaccharides, and HKUST-1 MOFs.

title: PGM-Zero™: Single-Site Fe-N₄ Electrocatalysts on Mesoporous Graphene for Complete Platinum Replacement in PEMFC Hydrogen Fuel Cells
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Preprint presenting PGM-Zero™, an atomically dispersed Fe-N₄ electrocatalyst in a mesoporous graphitic carbon matrix (SBET ≈ 1,450 m²/g) for complete platinum replacement in PEMFC cathodes. Achieves ORR half-wave potential E1/2 = 0.915 V vs
content: Preprint presenting PGM-Zero™, an atomically dispersed Fe-N₄ electrocatalyst in a mesoporous graphitic carbon matrix (SBET ≈ 1,450 m²/g) for complete platinum replacement in PEMFC cathodes. Achieves ORR half-wave potential E1/2 = 0.915 V vs. RHE (vs. 0.920 V for Pt/C), peak power density 1.18 W/cm², loss <15 mV over 30,000 DOE AST cycles, and cuts catalyst cost by 99.9% (from US$34,000/kg to US$18.50/kg), saving US$55.8 million/year for a 50,000-stack PEMFC OEM while reducing CO₂ by 99.95%.

title: A Mechano‐Electrochemical Stable Hydrogel for Flexible Energy Storage and Motion Monitoring
summary: ABSTRACT Balancing mechanical toughness, environmental durability, sensing accuracy in hydrogel based flexible devices remains challenging. This paper reports a multifunctional hydrogel P(AM‐co‐SBMA)/CMCS‐IL, synthesized via free radical po
content: ABSTRACT Balancing mechanical toughness, environmental durability, sensing accuracy in hydrogel based flexible devices remains challenging. This paper reports a multifunctional hydrogel P(AM‐co‐SBMA)/CMCS‐IL, synthesized via free radical polymerization in [EMIM][BF 4 ]/H 2 O binary solvent system, natural polysaccharide CMCS as rigid reinforcing network, AM and zwitterionic SBMA for flexibility. The hydrogen bonds provide exceptional tensile properties, enduring 961% strain and 80% compressive strain without fracturing. It exhibits strong dehydration resistance, retaining 80% of its water content after 12 h in room temperature environment. When assembled into FSC, the device has high specific capacitance of 151.6 F g − 1 at 0.2 A g − 1 and energy density of 21.06 Wh kg − 1 at 200 W kg − 1 , while maintaining 76% capacitance retention after 8,000 cycles. Crucially, the FSC shows outstanding electrochemical stability across different bending (0° to 180°) and wide temperature range (−20°C to 60°C). Additionally, a flexible strain sensor based on the hydrogel features rapid electromechanical response (response and recovery times of 0.7 s and 0.6 s) and captures bending deformations and subtle muscle activities with high signal to noise ratios. This multifunctional electrolyte provides a key design strategy for integrating smart skins and flexible energy storage systems.

title: Healthcare service structural recovery potential across Chinese provinces, 2009–2024: measurement, obstacle diagnosis, and improvement pathways
summary: Abstract Public health emergencies have exposed uneven structural recovery potential across China’s regional healthcare systems. This study measures healthcare service structural recovery potential in 31 provincial-level regions from 2009 t
content: Abstract Public health emergencies have exposed uneven structural recovery potential across China’s regional healthcare systems. This study measures healthcare service structural recovery potential in 31 provincial-level regions from 2009 to 2024 and diagnoses its internal weaknesses. We work within the "recovery" dimension of the “absorb–adapt–recover–transform” framework, build an indicator system of 7 dimensions and 10 indicators, weight them with the CRITIC method (cross-validated against three alternatives), and score structural recovery potential with TOPSIS. An obstacle degree model identifies the internal bottlenecks. The national mean rose from 0.4294 in 2009 to 0.6380 in 2024, an east-high, west-low gradient in which only the east–west gap is statistically significant. Graded-road density, basic medical insurance coverage, and daily inpatient bed-days per physician are the three largest obstacles (18.05%, 15.51%, 15.23%); the first is a support weakness, the other two healthcare-service weaknesses. The weakness structure varies across regions, provinces, and time. The resource-connectivity obstacle declines from west to east (21.29% to 15.51%). In 2024, graded-road density and physician bed-days are the leading obstacles in 19 and 12 provinces respectively. The insurance-coverage obstacle falls from 23.95% to 8.57%. The bottleneck thus shifts from expanding insurance coverage to reducing physician workload. The weighting method changes the diagnosis. The entropy method inflates the obstacle degree of highly dispersed indicators; the claim that resource connectivity is the single dominant weakness holds only under the entropy and coefficient-of-variation specifications, while the other two methods produce a more balanced structure. The paper closes with three improvement pathways: consolidate insurance coverage, reduce physician workload, and strengthen resource connectivity.

title: Effect of ZnCl2 addition to sunflower husk’s hydrothermal carbonization process: hydrochar yield, fuel properties and methylene blue removal
summary: The lack of optimal and environmentally friendly treatment of agricultural solid waste and textural wastewater are thought to be critical environmental issues. Processes such as adsorption, chemical oxidation, photocatalytic degradation, ad
content: The lack of optimal and environmentally friendly treatment of agricultural solid waste and textural wastewater are thought to be critical environmental issues. Processes such as adsorption, chemical oxidation, photocatalytic degradation, advanced oxidation, and electrochemical methods have been implemented to deals with these issues. An experimental design approach was employed in this study, to clarify the impact of ZnCl 2 addition during hydrothermal carbonization (HTC) of sunflower husk (SF) at various temperatures and reaction times. The impact of process parameters on hydrochar yield, high heating value (HHV) of HC and methylene blue adsorption capacity were studied. The maximum attained methylene blue adsorption capacities at optimum conditions were 278.4 and 195 mg/g for ZnCl 2 -assisted hydrochar (at 171 ℃ and 7.48 h) and no-ZnCl 2 -assisted hydrochar (at 169 ℃ and 7.78 h), respectively. Moreover, the mean adsorption capacity increased by 51% due to ZnCl 2 addition during the HTC process. At 220℃ and 7.5 h, about 60% and 36% improvement in HHV of HC compared to SF were attained in the presence and absence of ZnCl 2 addition, respectively. Moreover, ZnCl 2 addition caused a 7% increase in the mean HC’s HHV.

title: Controlled Cu Loading on ITO Shifts C1-to-C2 Oxygenate Pathways via Ensemble–Interface Cooperativity in CO2 Electroreduction
summary: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction provides a promising route to convert CO2 and renewable electricity into liquid fuels and chemicals, but selectively directing Cu-based catalysts toward specific C1 or C2 oxygenates remains challenging
content: Abstract Electrochemical CO2 reduction provides a promising route to convert CO2 and renewable electricity into liquid fuels and chemicals, but selectively directing Cu-based catalysts toward specific C1 or C2 oxygenates remains challenging due to competing reaction pathways. A central challenge is to control not only the identity of Cu sites, but also their spatial connectivity and interfacial electronic environment that governs the fate of *CO-derived intermediates. In this work, we report that Cu loading on indium tin oxide (ITO) can serve as a systematic control parameter to tune Cu ensemble–oxide interface cooperativity in CO2 electroreduction and alter CO2RR pathways. By increasing Cu loading from 1 wt %, 5 wt % to 10 wt %, the dominant liquid product evolves from methanol (MeOH) to mixed methanol/ethanol (EtOH) and finally to EtOH. Importantly, ethylene (C2H4) was observed across the Cu/ITO series, while the EtOH/C2H4 ratio increases progressively with Cu loading, indicating that the loading-dependent change involves the branching of C2 intermediates after C–C bond formation as well. Structural and surface analyses reveal a concurrent evolution from highly dispersed Cu species toward larger Cu-rich domains, together with systematic changes in the Cu–ITO interfacial electronic environment. Together, these observations support an ensemble–interface cooperative picture in which increasing Cu loading promotes the development of Cu-rich ensembles while maintaining an electronically modified Cu–ITO interfacial environment, thereby shifting the liquid oxygenate pathway from MeOH toward EtOH. The concurrent increase in the EtOH/C2H4 ratio further suggests that these structural and interfacial changes also influence the fate of oxygen-containing C2 intermediates and the post C–C-coupling branching between C2H4 and EtOH. This work therefore provides system-specific insight into how Cu-domain structure and oxide-support interactions can redirect oxygenate pathways in Cu-catalyzed CO2 electroreduction.

title: Confidence: Its Measurement, Relation to Behavior, and Neural Representation
summary: Confidence (certainty/uncertainty about one's own decision) has attracted considerable attention in psychology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. Yet its relation to behavior remains unclear: Some treat confidence as a cause of beh
content: Confidence (certainty/uncertainty about one's own decision) has attracted considerable attention in psychology, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. Yet its relation to behavior remains unclear: Some treat confidence as a cause of behavior whereas others view it as a state controlled by environmental variables. The unobservable nature of confidence makes its measurement validation and analyses difficult.
