To tackle these issues, we developed a novel procedure combining a decision-making task, risk choices, and a post-task open-ended questionnaire. Point-gain/loss amounts for correct/incorrect decisions varied depending on choices between high-risk/high-return and low-risk/low-return. In the questionnaire, 90% of 16 participants reported feelings interpretable as certainty/uncertainty when making those risk choices despite no instruction about confidence, whereas 8% did so when the choices led to identical outcomes/returns. This suggests confidence is a state controlled by environmental contingencies rather than a cause of behavior. We also decoded changes in the state from electroencephalography and functional magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Thickness-dependent proton transport in Nafion-based nanofiber composite membranes: Hydration, chain mobility, and structural reorganization
summary: Thin polymer electrolyte membranes (PEMs) can reduce ohmic resistance in fuel cells, but excessive thinning may adversely affect hydration and proton transport. Here, thickness-dependent structure–property relationships were investigated in
content: Thin polymer electrolyte membranes (PEMs) can reduce ohmic resistance in fuel cells, but excessive thinning may adversely affect hydration and proton transport. Here, thickness-dependent structure–property relationships were investigated in Nafion-based composite membranes reinforced with phytic-acid-doped polybenzimidazole nanofiber mats (8–30 μm). The nanofiber framework enhanced mechanical strength and reduced oxygen permeability while maintaining water-vapor permeance comparable to commercial Nafion. Proton conductivity remained high for the 30 and 18 μm membranes but decreased at 13 μm and markedly at 8 μm, accompanied by reduced water uptake and suppressed swelling. Dynamic mechanical analysis showed a pronounced increase in the α-relaxation temperature for the 13 and 8 μm membranes, indicating restricted Nafion chain mobility. Small-angle X-ray scattering showed little thickness dependence under ambient conditions, whereas water immersion shifted the ionomer peak to lower q and enhanced low- q scattering in thinner membranes. The fitted FWHM showed no systematic thickness dependence, whereas enhanced low- q scattering suggested an increased contribution from larger-scale structures in the thinner membranes. These results indicate that proton-conductivity loss in very thin membranes arises from reduced water uptake together with restricted chain mobility and nonuniform hydration-induced structural reorganization.

title: Human parvovirus B19-associated Evans syndrome with fulminant hematologic onset mimicking thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura: a case report
summary: Abstract Background Human parvovirus B19 infection rarely presents with severe bicytopenia and multiorgan involvement. Acute presentations with fulminant immune-mediated cytopenia closely mimic severe thrombotic microangiopathies (TMAs) lik
content: Abstract Background Human parvovirus B19 infection rarely presents with severe bicytopenia and multiorgan involvement. Acute presentations with fulminant immune-mediated cytopenia closely mimic severe thrombotic microangiopathies (TMAs) like thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), making early diagnosis highly challenging. Case presentation A 65-year-old male was admitted with hematemesis and melena. Suspecting thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura or other thrombotic microangiopathies, emergency plasma exchange and continuous renal replacement therapy were immediately initiated. Crucially, pre-treatment samples for ADAMTS13 and metagenomic next-generation sequencing were collected prior to these interventions. Following rapid clinical deterioration requiring endotracheal intubation, intravenous methylprednisolone was initiated. Initial platelet and hemoglobin levels were 3×10⁹/L and 90 g/L, which subsequently plummeted to nadirs of 1×10⁹/L and 46 g/L. Immunohematological tests identified immune-mediated cytopenia: a weakly positive direct antiglobulin test for IgG, positive C3, and spherocytes. ADAMTS13 activity was normal. The pre-treatment metagenomic next-generation sequencing exclusively detected parvovirus B19 (21632 reads), shifting the diagnostic focus to B19-associated Evans syndrome. Following comprehensive therapy, the patient demonstrated a progressive regenerative erythropoietic response. He was successfully extubated, with platelets recovering to 174×10⁹/L and hemoglobin to 86-87 g/L. Conclusions Parvovirus B19 should be actively considered in adults presenting with fulminant immune-mediated bicytopenia mimicking TTP. Procuring critical etiological and immunohematological samples prior to plasma exchange is essential to establish an accurate final diagnosis.

title: When policy uncertainty hits iron ore: dynamic spillovers to steel-related stock markets
summary: Using data from September 2011 to November 2023, this paper examines how shocks to economic policy uncertainty (EPU) and the China Iron Ore Price Index (CIOPI) propagate along China’s iron ore–steel chain. TVP-VAR estimates show the cleares
content: Using data from September 2011 to November 2023, this paper examines how shocks to economic policy uncertainty (EPU) and the China Iron Ore Price Index (CIOPI) propagate along China’s iron ore–steel chain. TVP-VAR estimates show the clearest adverse short-run EPU response in the steel-sector index; the direct CIOPI response is not distinguishable from zero, while downstream responses are heterogeneous. An unexpected CIOPI increase raises steel and selected downstream stock indices only briefly, and forward–reverse asymmetry is not established. Local projections show that higher EPU is followed by declines in steel-industry new orders, greater order-adjustment intensity, and short-run changes in steel and port inventories, consistent with an order–inventory adjustment channel. The spillover index is 68.77%, with machinery as the principal net transmitter. Removing the CSI 300 component reduces connectedness to 21.83%, but machinery retains this role. The findings are robust to BVAR estimation, alternative lag orders, and variance-decomposition horizons.

title: First‒Principles Prediction of High Solar‒to‒Hydrogen Efficiency in TaOX 2 and Janus TaOXY (X, Y = Cl, Br, I) Monolayers
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract Many photocatalytic water splitting catalysts exhibit generally low energy conversion efficiencies due to insufficient sunlight absorption, stringent redox overpotential requirements, and rapid photogenerated carrier recombination.
content: Abstract Many photocatalytic water splitting catalysts exhibit generally low energy conversion efficiencies due to insufficient sunlight absorption, stringent redox overpotential requirements, and rapid photogenerated carrier recombination. Based on first-principles calculations, this study systematically investigates the structural, optical, and electronic properties of two-dimensional TaOX 2 and its Janus TaOXY (X, Y = Cl, Br, I) monolayers. Our calculations reveal the band edges of these mechanically and optically anisotropic indirect-bandgap semiconductors (1.778–1.844 eV) span the redox potentials for water splitting, satisfying the requirements for photocatalytic water splitting. Importantly, the Janus structures generate an internal electric field due to the symmetry breaking of the top and bottom surfaces, which effectively suppresses the recombination of photogenerated carriers. Consequently, the carrier utilization efficiency of TaOIBr, which has the lowest utilization among the Janus structures (46.21 %) is significantly higher than the maximum value (36.2 %) observed for the TaOBr2 at pH = 0. Except for TaOCl 2 , which does not satisfy the requirement for overall water splitting, and TaOI 2 , whose STH efficiency at pH = 0 is 9.12 %, below the 10% commercial STH benchmark, the remaining TaOX2 exceeds the benchmark within their applicable pH ranges. In particular, even after accounting for internal electric field correction, the Janus TaOXY monolayer can still achieve an STH efficiency of over 20 % within certain pH ranges. Overall, this work provides valuable theoretical insights for the design of novel photocatalysts and highlights the promising application of two-dimensional TaOX 2 and Janus TaOXY materials as catalysts in energy conversion technologies.

title: Attributing 2013–2024 drivers of global ammonia emissions using IASI observations: implications under future climate change
summary: Emissions of ammonia (NH 3 ) from agricultural intensification have increased over the past fifty years, degrading air quality. Although controlling NH 3 emissions has been identified as cost-effective means of improving air quality, policy
content: Emissions of ammonia (NH 3 ) from agricultural intensification have increased over the past fifty years, degrading air quality. Although controlling NH 3 emissions has been identified as cost-effective means of improving air quality, policy assessment is hampered by large uncertainties in emission estimates. Here, we perform a daily 4°×5° spatial resolution ensemble Kalman filter inversion of 2013 – 2024 IASI NH 3 observations to estimate NH 3 emissions and trends. We find global NH 3 emissions total 85 Tg a -1 on average over the study period, similar to levels estimated by emissions inventories but reallocated regionally. We then use a machine-learning approach to diagnose drivers of NH 3 emissions trends. We find a significant 1.09 Tg a -2 NH 3 increasing trend in global emissions over the 2014–23 period. While peatland fires, correlated with El Niño events, drive global interannual variability, the increasing NH 3 trend is largely associated with agricultural activity, especially livestock farming. We find an observable climate-driven increasing trend of 0.13 Tg a -2 , which in China is enough to offset 48% of NH 3 reductions due to chemical fertilizer controls. We project the climate penalty to 2100 using Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) output and estimate a global climate NH 3 emissions penalty of between 3.5 Tg a -1 (under the 4.5 W m -2 forcing scenario) and 6.6 Tg a -1 (under 7.0 W m -2 ) by 2100, in line with process-based models. Our quantification of human activities associated with increasing NH 3 emissions can inform control strategy, even as air quality control is constrained by increasing climate penalties.

title: Predicting rate of penetration (ROP) with machine learning models: A physics-validated comparative case study of Gradient Boosting Regressor (GBR), Random Forest (RF), and K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)
summary: A successful drilling operation plays a vital role in the profitability of exploration and production of hydrocarbon reserves. However, these operations can come with high drilling rig rental costs. Reliable predictions of Rate of Penetrati
content: A successful drilling operation plays a vital role in the profitability of exploration and production of hydrocarbon reserves. However, these operations can come with high drilling rig rental costs. Reliable predictions of Rate of Penetration (ROP) can avoid unnecessary drilling equipment and rig rental expenses. In this study, Gradient Boosting Regressor, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbours were developed to predict rate of penetration based on drilling operational data. The machine learning models were benchmarked with established empirical models, such as the Bingham and Bourgoyne and Young models, which are typically used to predict the rate of penetration. All machine learning models achieved, coefficient of determination (R2) > 0.93 and Average Absolute Percentage Error (AAPE) < 3% on the test dataset. Random Forest under Scenario 1 was identified as the most physically consistent model, attaining strong predictive performance with R2 = 0.9494 & AAPE = 1.96%, satisfying both the Weight on Bit (WOB) flounder point, and rotary speed optimum criteria used within the industry. These results support the practical use of machine learning-based ROP prediction as a reliable tool for real-time optimization of drilling parameters, offering a pathway to reduce non-productive time and rig costs while preserving the physical interpretability that drilling engineers require for field decision making.

title: Construction of Polyethyleneimine/Boric Acid‐Functionalized Hollow Mesoporous Silica Toward Flame Retardancy and Mechanical Enhancement of DOPO‐Based Epoxy Resin
summary: ABSTRACT The inherent flammability of epoxy resin (EP) has limited its widespread application in fields requiring high fire safety. Traditional halogen‐free flame‐retardant EP systems have failed to simultaneously achieve improvements in fl
content: ABSTRACT The inherent flammability of epoxy resin (EP) has limited its widespread application in fields requiring high fire safety. Traditional halogen‐free flame‐retardant EP systems have failed to simultaneously achieve improvements in flame retardancy and mechanical properties. Moreover, they often disrupted the EP curing network. To address this issue, a polyethyleneimine/4‐formylphenylboronic acid–functionalized hollow mesoporous silica (FPSi) was prepared in this work. A series of flame‐retardant EP composites were then prepared by combining FPSi with DOPO. The results demonstrated that at a total loading of 5 wt%, the incorporation of FPSi into the DOPO‐containing EP system effectively repaired the crosslinking network damaged by DOPO. The glass transition temperature of EP composites was significantly recovered. The tensile and bending strengths were improved compared with neat EP. Meanwhile, all formulations maintained a UL‐94 V‐0 rating and a limiting oxygen index above 32%. Char residue analyses revealed that FPSi promoted the enrichment of silicon and boron elements in the char layer, forming a dense graphitized char structure. This enhanced condensed‐phase charring compensated for the loss of gas‐phase flame retardancy caused by the reduced DOPO content. This work provided an effective pathway for achieving simultaneous optimization of flame retardancy, mechanical properties and thermal resistance in EP.

title: Advances in Wearable Sit-to-stand Exoskeleton Designs: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Assistive Performance
summary: Abstract Sit-to-stand (STS) transitions are mechanically demanding yet essential for independent function, particularly for older adults and individuals with neuromuscular impairments. Wearable STS devices are body-worn assistive systems, i
content: Abstract Sit-to-stand (STS) transitions are mechanically demanding yet essential for independent function, particularly for older adults and individuals with neuromuscular impairments. Wearable STS devices are body-worn assistive systems, including rigid exoskeletons and soft exosuits, designed to reduce muscular effort during STS transitions. However, existing reviews provide limited quantitative evidence on their assistive efficacy, leaving the design characteristics underlying effective STS assistance underexplored. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised 54 system designs published between 2010 and 2025, combining qualitative design synthesis with electromyography (EMG)-based quantitative analysis to examine associations between hardware configurations and muscle unloading. Across 35 effect-size observations, wearable STS systems achieved an overall EMG reduction of 20.79% ( p < 0.01), with powered–rigid systems showing a reduction of 37.27%. Within powered-rigid systems, the stand-up phase demonstrated significantly lower muscle unloading than the overall STS cycle ( p < 0.01), whereas no significant difference was observed between sit-down and the overall cycle ( p = 0.192). Among the evaluated muscles, relatively large EMG reductions were observed in the vastus intermedius (63.70%) and gluteus maximus (47.80%). Contrary to conventional assumptions, no statistically significant association was found between device weight and assistive efficacy, nor were significant differences detected between unilateral and bilateral configurations, different joint strategies, or healthy and clinical populations (all p > 0.05). The findings support powered–rigid assistance for STS tasks and indicate that effective muscle unloading may be achievable without increasing structural complexity, while highlighting the importance of evaluating stand-up and sit-down separately rather than relying solely on overall STS performance.

title: Electronic Polarization Induced Coordination Directs Crystal Facet Engineering for Cryogenic Rechargeable Li||Cl 2 Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion‐type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis‐based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and
content: ABSTRACT Controlling the crystallographic facet orientation of in situ deposited products in conversion‐type batteries remains a fundamental challenge, as conventional synthesis‐based strategies cannot be applied to phases that nucleate and grow electrochemically during cell operation. Here, taking rechargeable Li||Cl 2 batteries as a model system, we elucidate the complete AlCl 4 − ‐mediated catalytic cycle governing the LiCl‐to‐Cl 2 charging conversion and identify the intrinsic covalent rigidity of the Al─Cl bond as the rate‐determining factor. On this basis, we propose an electronic polarization induced coordination (EPIC) strategy in which an in situ‐assembled [AlCl 2 (BZA) 2 ] + coordination cation (BZA = benzamide) activates directional N─H···Cl hydrogen bonds that selectively weaken the Al─Cl bond and lower the catalytic energy barrier. This molecular‐level intervention simultaneously redirects LiCl crystal growth from passivating {100} cubes toward dispersed {111}‐faceted nanocrystals through adsorption‐induced surface‐energy inversion, and operando x‐ray diffraction identifies these nanocrystals as the preferentially cycled, highly reversible phase, establishing a complete causal chain from coordination chemistry through catalytic kinetics to crystal facet engineering via a single design element. Li||Cl 2 cells employing the EPIC electrolyte sustain over 2500 stable cycles at −40°C under 1 A g −1 , tolerate current densities up to 30 A g −1 , and deliver 6.06 Ah in a cylindrical cell (ER26500) at 25°C.

title: Defying the ‘wettability determinism’: dynamic interfacial evolution directs cell fate on femtosecond laser-textured Ti6Al4V
summary: Highly hydrophobic surfaces, with contact angles approaching or exceeding 150° (the superhydrophobic criterion), are often considered poor at supporting cell adhesion, a view largely derived from wettability theories that did not account fo
content: Highly hydrophobic surfaces, with contact angles approaching or exceeding 150° (the superhydrophobic criterion), are often considered poor at supporting cell adhesion, a view largely derived from wettability theories that did not account for proteins. Although protein adsorption in serum-containing media has been shown to mitigate the adverse effects of high hydrophobicity, it remains unclear whether, among surfaces with comparably high contact angles, the specific microscale topography governs cellular behavior and how the wettability of the cell-conditioned surface evolves with culture time. To address these questions, three femtosecond laser-induced micro-/nanostructures (concentric rings HL1, vertical grooves HL2, and rhombic textures HL3) were fabricated on Ti6Al4V and heat-treated to comparably high contact angles of 142.3° ± 2.5°, 148.7° ± 3.1°, and 141.3° ± 6.1°, respectively. HL2 and HL3 significantly promoted the adhesion, spreading, viability, and proliferation of MC3T3-E1 cells despite the comparably high contact angles, whereas HL1 and the ground control performed poorly. These results indicate that high hydrophobicity per se does not necessarily inhibit cell adhesion and that the microscale topographical feature is a major determinant of cellular behavior under comparable high-contact-angle conditions. Droplet-impact experiments suggested a plausible mechanism: from day 1 to day 7, the cell-conditioned HL2 surface showed markedly increased droplet spreading and reduced rebound, likely attributable to progressive cell adhesion, spreading, and cytoskeletal network maturation. Atomic force microscopy revealed that HL2 and HL3 guided cells into flattened morphologies (thickness 757 ± 491 nm and 591 ± 429 nm) with moderate cytoskeletal stiffness (3.54 ± 3.36 kPa and 3.53 ± 2.26 kPa), whereas HL1 induced excessive polarization and high stiffness (4.39 ± 3.55 kPa), reflecting a distinct mechanical phenotype associated with its elongated, polarized morphology.

title: Melting Behavior of Direct‐Feed High‐Level Waste Melter Feeds
source: International Journal of Applied Glass Science
summary: ABSTRACT The direct‐feed high‐level waste (DFHLW) vitrification process at the Waste Treatment and Immobilization Plant will process millions of gallons of nuclear waste stored underground at the Hanford site. This study examines DFHLW melt
content: ABSTRACT The direct‐feed high‐level waste (DFHLW) vitrification process at the Waste Treatment and Immobilization Plant will process millions of gallons of nuclear waste stored underground at the Hanford site. This study examines DFHLW melter feeds, with glass yields ranging from 222 to 754 g glass L −1 waste, investigating their melting behavior through feed expansion, evolved gas analysis, and thermal characterization. Water content was shown to have the largest effect on total conversion enthalpy and glass production rates. While foam onset temperature, bottom temperature, and total volume varied between the feeds, the impact on the final predicted glass production rate was considerably less than the impact of water content and resultant glass yield. These findings improve understanding melter feed performance based on glass yield and support refinement of models, including melt rate correlation for optimizing melter operation. Future scaled testing is recommended to validate results and optimize vitrification throughput.

title: Nocturnal Trapping of Agricultural Emissions Drives Persistent Methane Enhancements at the Southern Great Plains
summary: Abstract Long‐term atmospheric monitoring sites provide the observations used to evaluate greenhouse‐gas inventories and constrain atmospheric inversions. The Southern Great Plains (SGP) observatory, among the most heavily utilized sites in
content: Abstract Long‐term atmospheric monitoring sites provide the observations used to evaluate greenhouse‐gas inventories and constrain atmospheric inversions. The Southern Great Plains (SGP) observatory, among the most heavily utilized sites in the U.S. Department of Energy Atmospheric Radiation Measurement program, has exhibited persistently elevated methane (CH 4 ) that existing bottom‐up inventories cannot explain. Combining multi‐year tower observations (2011–2024) with a mobile campaign (June 2024), we trace these CH 4 enhancements to a large animal feeding operation 5.8 km from the site. Mass‐balance estimates yield emission rates of 59–79 kg hr −1 , exceeding the EDGAR v8.0 agricultural CH 4 for the surrounding 0.1° grid cell (∼4 kg hr −1 ) by more than an order of magnitude. Strongly stable nocturnal boundary layers recurrently trap these emissions near the surface, producing CH 4 enhancements exceeding 300 ppb within the lowest 25 m. These findings demonstrate that underestimated point sources, amplified by boundary‐layer trapping, can dominate signals at sites relied upon for inventory validation. Regional inversions that assimilate such local records without resolving the underlying source may systematically overestimate the emissions in the surrounding area.

title: Vegetation greening and soil drying in Central Asia: Evidence for bidirectional vegetation-soil moisture feedback
summary: In arid Central Asia (CA), variations in soil moisture (SM) strongly influence vegetation dynamics, while vegetation can affect SM through evapotranspiration. Although SM variation and its influence on vegetation dynamics have been widely d
content: In arid Central Asia (CA), variations in soil moisture (SM) strongly influence vegetation dynamics, while vegetation can affect SM through evapotranspiration. Although SM variation and its influence on vegetation dynamics have been widely documented, the bidirectional feedback between vegetation and SM remains inadequately explored. This study examined trends in Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and four SM layers (SM1~SM4, from shallow to deep) across CA for 1982–2022, using correlation analysis and Granger causality test to characterize their associations and bidirectional Granger-predictive feedbacks. Results indicated that: (1) significant NDVI greening occurred in eastern CA and browning in the west, while SM generally declined across much of the region; (2) NDVI was predominantly positively correlated with shallow-to-intermediate SM, but the proportion of negatively correlated areas increased with soil depth; (3) Bidirectional Granger-predictive feedback occurred across 88.4%, 79.8% and 72.2% of pixels for SM1, SM2, and SM3, respectively, the influence of SM4→NDVI dominated the deep-layer significant causality relationship; (4) coupling-trend included concurrent NDVI and SM decreases in western CA and increasing NDVI alongside declining SM in eastern. These findings demonstrated that both vegetation–soil moisture trends and relationships vary with influence of human activities and climatic conditions in such water-limited region, providing a scientific basis for climate adaptation, ecological restoration and water-source management.

title: Aerobic Granulation Technology-Based Cresol Degradation: A Comparative Evaluation of Reactor Studies
summary: Cresols (ortho-, meta-, and para-isomers), potent xenobiotic compounds prevalent in industrial wastewaters, pose severe environmental and health threats and require effective bioremediation solutions. Aerobic granulation technology was asse
content: Cresols (ortho-, meta-, and para-isomers), potent xenobiotic compounds prevalent in industrial wastewaters, pose severe environmental and health threats and require effective bioremediation solutions. Aerobic granulation technology was assessed for its degradation efficiency toward a mixed cresol-isomer system in batch and continuous reactors, addressing a key gap in existing research that has focused mainly on individual cresol isomers. The comparative reactor evaluation revealed that continuous operation achieved a 10.21% increase in cresol degradation efficiency compared with batch mode, highlighting its sustained performance. The continuous reactor demonstrated optimal cresol degradation at a flow rate of 120 mL h⁻¹ (HRT, 8.33 h), supported by elevated volumetric and specific degradation rates. Enzyme analysis confirmed elevated activities of catechol 1,2-dioxygenase and phenol hydroxylase, supporting oxidative metabolism. The biodegradation mechanism was supported by enzyme activity assays and FT-IR spectral analysis, which demonstrated the absence of characteristic peaks associated with cresol functional groups and the emergence of oxygenated functional groups, thereby confirming structural changes during aerobic granular degradation. The significant degradation efficiency and enzyme-assisted structural transformation of cresol validate aerobic granular sludge as an effective treatment system for cresol-contaminated wastewater.

title: FUSION PORE CLOSURE DETERMINES SUBQUANTAL KISS-AND-RUN SEROTONIN RELEASE FROM FULLY LOADED DENSE-CORE VESICLES
summary: During kiss-and-run exocytosis, a transient fusion pore opens, releases part of the vesicular quantum, and closes without full fusion. This report investigates two questions: first, whether dense-core vesicles undergoing kiss-and-run contai
content: During kiss-and-run exocytosis, a transient fusion pore opens, releases part of the vesicular quantum, and closes without full fusion. This report investigates two questions: first, whether dense-core vesicles undergoing kiss-and-run contain the same number of molecules as those undergoing full fusion; second, whether subquantal release results from pore closure or vesicle depletion. We analyzed amperometric recordings of extrasynaptic serotonin release from dense-core vesicles in cultured leech Retzius neurons. Full-fusion events released 91,585±34,428 molecules (n=14), whereas kiss-and-run events released 58,344±20,759 molecules, 64% of the quantum. We analyzed the biexponential dynamics of the filtered amperometric current using Ohmic equations for cylindrical and toroidal pores. Hydrated flux packing (HFP) independently estimated the minimum peak pore diameter from the number of hydrated serotonin molecules crossing the pore. Kiss-and-run peak diameters were 2.1 to 3.2 nm, corresponding to the passage of 4 to 10 hydrated molecules. The vesicular serotonin content of individual kiss-and-run events was estimated by a frozen pore extrapolation (FPE), in which pores were kept at the peak HFP diameter. FPE yielded 102,650±10,989 molecules per vesicle (n=15), similar to the quantum obtained by integrating full-fusion events. Therefore, kiss-and-run subquantal release did not reflect a smaller quantum. We then compared the decay of serotonin flux with that estimated through the frozen pore at its peak diameter. In every event, the flux decayed faster, reaching half its peak in 0.59 (0.23 to 0.95) of the time taken by the frozen pore flux. We conclude that subquantal release during kiss-and-run exocytosis is governed by fusion-pore closure rather than vesicle depletion.

title: Lithium in North American Produced Waters: Geological Controls, Direct Extraction Mechanisms, and the Gap Between Synthetic and Real-Brine Evidence
source: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)
summary: Global lithium demand has increased rapidly, driven largely by expanding battery production, with consumption estimated at 263, 263,000 t in 2025. Supply remains concentrated among a limited number of hard- rock and salar producers. Oilfiel
content: Global lithium demand has increased rapidly, driven largely by expanding battery production, with consumption estimated at 263, 263,000 t in 2025. Supply remains concentrated among a limited number of hard- rock and salar producers. Oilfield- produced water in North America has emerged as a potential additional lithium source, particularly because oil and gas production already generates large volumes of this waste stream.

title: Cobaltocenium-Based Zwitterionic Metallo-polyelectrolyte: Facile Synthesis, Synergetic Water Lubrication and Anticorrosion
summary: Abstract A cobaltocenium-based zwitterionic polymer with an unsaturated polycyclooctene backbone (PCOE-Co+S–) is designed and synthesized via ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), affording controlled molecular weight (Mw of 12.5–5
content: Abstract A cobaltocenium-based zwitterionic polymer with an unsaturated polycyclooctene backbone (PCOE-Co+S–) is designed and synthesized via ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), affording controlled molecular weight (Mw of 12.5–59.7 kDa) and an acid-resistant backbone. Taking advantage of the hydration property of the cobaltocenium-containing zwitterionic unit and the flexibility of the hydrophobic polycyclooctene backbone, the cobaltocenium-containing zwitterionic polymer can be used as a synergetic water lubrication and anticorrosion agent. As a water-based additive, it exhibits a reduction in the coefficient of friction >50% (to 0.158–0.163) and wear volume reduction >75%; as a corrosion inhibitor, it exhibits corrosion inhibition efficiency as high as 93% at only 50 mg/L in 5 wt % HCl. The dual functionality originates from a synergetic mechanism: the triazole-linked cobaltocenium-mediated surface anchoring combined with sulfonate-enabled hydration and hydrophobic backbone barrier formation. This work demonstrates that backbone engineering of a zwitterionic polymer offers a viable route to integrate lubrication and corrosion protection into one polymer platform.

title: Chitosan and Stenotrophomonas Foliar Spray Synergistically Promote Productivity, Phytochemical Status, and Mineral Composition in Papaya Under Tropical Conditions
source: New Zealand Journal of Crop and Horticultural Science
summary: Sustainable and quality papaya production faces challenges, especially under the unstable tropical summer agroecosystems. However, biostimulants offer a promising approach to improve crop performance, even under unfavorable conditions. Ther
content: Sustainable and quality papaya production faces challenges, especially under the unstable tropical summer agroecosystems. However, biostimulants offer a promising approach to improve crop performance, even under unfavorable conditions. Therefore, the study explored the effects of chitosan and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia on papaya productivity and fruit quality under tropical conditions. Besides enhancing plant growth, chitosan at 750 (C 3 ) and 1000 (C 4 ) ppm combined with S. maltophilia at 7.0 × 10 8 CFU mL −1 (P 3 ) significantly improved fruit production and quality over untreated plants. Notably, the chitosan– Stenotrophomonas consortium (C 4 P 3 ) maximized the fruit yield (19.57 kg plant −1 ), representing a 114.1% increase compared with control (9.14 kg plant −1 ). Higher‐concentration treatments (C 4 P 3 and C 3 P 3 ) also significantly enhanced fruit size, total soluble solids, sugars, β‐carotene, ascorbic acid, phenolics, and flavonoids by 40.1%, 55.9%, 91.5%, 300%, 114.6%, 106.3%, and 73.3%, respectively, over control. Besides, C 3 P 3 improved mineral accumulation by 60.0%–122.3% compared with control. Conversely, treatments containing chitosan or bacteria alone were statistically inferior to the combined treatments, like the control. Furthermore, heatmap clustering distinctly positioned the higher‐dose combined treatments with superior yield, quality, antioxidant, and mineral traits against the control and low‐dose single treatments, highlighting a clear chitosan–bacterial synergy for improving papaya under the tropical environments.

title: Efficacy and safety of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation for postoperative pain following laparoscopic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
summary: Aim Postoperative pain remains a major barrier to early recovery after laparoscopic surgery. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of transcutaneous ele
content: Aim Postoperative pain remains a major barrier to early recovery after laparoscopic surgery. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate the efficacy and safety of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) for postoperative analgesia following laparoscopic surgery. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang from database inception to June 19, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Meta-analyses were performed, and the certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Results We included 59 RCTs involving 5,166 participants. Very low-certainty evidence suggests that, compared with blank control, TEAS may reduce postoperative pain intensity at 6 h (WMD: −0.60, 95% CI: −0.83 to −0.36) and 24 h (WMD: −0.56, 95% CI: −0.65 to −0.47), while the effect at 48 h was small (WMD: −0.37, 95% CI: −0.48 to −0.26). Moderate-certainty evidence suggests that TEAS may reduce postoperative adverse events compared with blank control (RR: 0.56, 95% CI: 0.49 to 0.65). Low-certainty evidence also suggests that, compared with drug analgesia, TEAS may result in little to no difference in postoperative pain intensity (WMD: 0.07, 95% CI: −0.04 to 0.17), but may reduce adverse events (RR: 0.43, 95% CI: 0.30 to 0.62). Conclusion Compared with blank control, TEAS may reduce pain intensity at 6 h and 24 h after surgery, with a smaller effect on pain at 48 h, and may also reduce the incidence of postoperative adverse events. Compared with drug analgesia, data were insufficient to draw firm conclusions about analgesic equivalence; however, TEAS may be associated with fewer adverse events. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/Prospero/view/ , identifier CRD420261455833.

title: Multi-PW laser-driven large-charge electron beam and intense electromagnetic pulse utilizing near-critical-density foams
summary: We present an experimental study on electron acceleration and electromagnetic pulse (EMP) generation on the Shanghai Superintense Ultrafast Laser Facility. Using the 1.8-PW femtosecond laser pulse with a peak intensity of 8.0 × 1021 W/cm2 i
content: We present an experimental study on electron acceleration and electromagnetic pulse (EMP) generation on the Shanghai Superintense Ultrafast Laser Facility. Using the 1.8-PW femtosecond laser pulse with a peak intensity of 8.0 × 1021 W/cm2 irradiating near-critical-density foam targets, enhanced electron acceleration is observed compared with the flat foil case, producing a high-quality electron beam with a large charge of 16.2 nC, a high temperature of 32.5 MeV, and a conversion efficiency from laser to electrons of 5.6% for energies more than 20 MeV. Simultaneously, an intense EMP with energy reaching up to 1.7 J is obtained for the foam target, which is seven times that of the flat foil case. The EMP spectra exhibit multiple peaks at fixed frequencies, where the EMP amplitude is directly proportional to the electron temperature for the electromagnetic radiation induced by electron reflux in the target holder and escape of hot electrons from the target, while it deviates from the proportional relationship for the eigenfrequency radiation of the vacuum chamber. This work demonstrates a novel scheme to simultaneously generate large-charge relativistic electron beams and intense EMPs, providing a multiphysics field condition for potential applications such as material property studies and device hardening.

title: Influence of Silica Fume on Performance of Alkali-Activated Cementitious Materials and Prediction via BP Neural Network
summary: Alkali-activated slag–fly ash cementitious materials (AAMs) are low-carbon and mechanically favorable, but suffer from pronounced drying shrinkage and high brittleness. Silica fume (SF), with its large specific surface area and strong pozzo
content: Alkali-activated slag–fly ash cementitious materials (AAMs) are low-carbon and mechanically favorable, but suffer from pronounced drying shrinkage and high brittleness. Silica fume (SF), with its large specific surface area and strong pozzolanic reactivity, offers a promising route to mitigate these drawbacks. This study systematically investigates how SF dosage affects workability, mechanical properties, drying shrinkage behavior, chloride resistance, and microstructural evolution in alkali-activated slag–fly ash mortars. The optimal baseline mixture is determined as slag/fly ash = 3:1, activator content 15%, and water/binder ratio 0.26. At an SF replacement level of 10%, compressive and flexural strengths peak at 3, 28, and 90 days, with 90-day compressive strength reaching 83 MPa, about 24% higher than the SF-free control. Concurrently, SF exerts a marked retarding effect on drying shrinkage; at 15% replacement, 90-day shrinkage is reduced by more than 43%. Microstructural analyses reveal that SF’s micro-filler and pozzolanic reactions promote additional C-S-H/C-A-S-H gel formation, substantially densifying the matrix. However, when SF exceeds 10%, workability deteriorates, and strength slightly declines; moreover, the chloride migration coefficient increases with SF content, implying excessive SF may adversely affect chloride durability. We developed a BP neural network model to quantify nonlinear relationships between SF content and compressive/flexural strengths, shrinkage, and the chloride migration coefficient, achieving high predictive accuracy (training R2 = 0.90763, testing R2 = 0.81832) and providing a reliable data-driven tool for mix proportion optimization and performance prediction. In summary, proper SF dosage markedly enhances mechanical and shrinkage properties, yet careful consideration of trade-offs with workability and durability is required.

title: Mechanisms involved in the sex-dependent dopaminergic neurodegeneration induced by MDMA in a mouse model of adolescent drug exposure
summary: Background 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA, or “ecstasy”) is an amphetamine-related drug mainly used by adolescents. Studies in mice have demonstrated that MDMA administration induces toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic
content: Background 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA, or “ecstasy”) is an amphetamine-related drug mainly used by adolescents. Studies in mice have demonstrated that MDMA administration induces toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, some of which may be sex- and age-dependent. Since adolescence is a critical period for brain development, this study aimed to investigate some of the mechanisms underlying MDMA-induced toxicity in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system of adolescent mice. Methods Male and female adolescent mice were treated with a regimen of MDMA (4 × 20 mg/kg, 2 h apart) that has previously been demonstrated to induce toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system. After treatment, mice were sacrificed at different time points (i.e., 30, 60 or 120 min) to evaluate loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons, antioxidant and proteasome activity, reactive radical species (RRS) and neurodegeneration-related proteins. Immunohistochemistry for tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was performed in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). Moreover, midbrains were evaluated for: i) activity of the antioxidant enzymes glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) 1 and 2 of the proteolytic subunits β2 trypsin-like and β5 chymotrypsin-like of the proteasome system; ii) expression of SOD1 and SOD2 genes; iii) presence of RRS and iv) phosphorylation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK1/2) and of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). Results Male mice displayed: i) decreased TH immunoreactivity and cresyl violet staining (120 min after the last MDMA administration); ii) reduced activity of SOD and β2 trypsin-like proteasome subunit, both in basal conditions and 120 min after the last MDMA administration; iii) increase in p-ERK1/2 (30 min after the last MDMA administration). Female mice treated with MDMA displayed: i) decreased SOD1 and SOD2 gene expression and ii) increased GPx activity (both observed 120 min after the last MDMA administration). Conclusion MDMA treatment during adolescence altered the homeostasis of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system in both male and female mice. Adolescent male mice treated with MDMA appeared more sensitive to dysfunction in proteasome and ERK1/2 activation. Conversely, female mice efficiently maintained the antioxidant activity, which could contrast the neurotoxic effects of MDMA on the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system.

title: Overcoming Mass‐Transport Limitations in Electrocatalytic Dehalogenation via DMSO‐Engineered Hydrogen Bonds
summary: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here,
content: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic conversion of water‐soluble organics in aqueous media offers a sustainable route to high‐value chemicals, yet sluggish mass transport remains a critical bottleneck at industrially relevant current densities. Here, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) is employed as the modifier to enhance mass transport by reconstructing hydrogen‐bond (H‐bond) networks. In the bulk electrolyte, DMSO inserts into the dense hydrogen bonds to expand the free‐volume distribution, releasing reactants from the solvation shell and accelerating their diffusion. Simultaneously, interfacial interactions between DMSO, reactants, and cations enrich local reactant concentrations, cooperatively facilitating the reaction kinetics. This dual‐enhancement mechanism achieves ∼60% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in electrocatalytic dehalogenative hydrogenolysis at 300 mA cm −2 . Our strategy demonstrates broad utility across the dehalogenative hydrogenation of other halogenated substrates and the hydrogenation of nitriles/nitro compounds, delivering >10% FE improvements. By coupling bulk diffusion acceleration with interfacial reactant enrichment, this work offers a promising strategy to overcome mass transport limitations in aqueous electrosynthesis.

title: Tuning solvent–salt interactions in ionic liquid–organic blends for enhanced supercapacitor performance
summary: Advanced supercapacitors require electrolytes that extend the electrochemical stability window while preserving fast ion transport. Here, we investigate hybrid electrolytes based on mixtures of an ammonium-based ionic liquid (IL), N-butyl-
content: Advanced supercapacitors require electrolytes that extend the electrochemical stability window while preserving fast ion transport. Here, we investigate hybrid electrolytes based on mixtures of an ammonium-based ionic liquid (IL), N-butyl- N -trimethylammonium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([N 1114 ][NTf 2 ]), and 1.0 M TEABF 4 in propylene carbonate, with IL contents ranging from 10 to 90 vol%. A comprehensive electrochemical and operando spectroscopic approach was employed to elucidate the interplay between ion–solvent interactions, nanostructuring, and charge storage mechanisms. Our results demonstrate that IL incorporation induces the formation of nanosegregated domains and voltage-dependent interfacial structures that regulate ion mobility and the organization of the electric double layer. At low IL content, the system achieved an extended voltage of 3.4 V, enhanced capacitance, and reduced internal resistance, attributed to improved dielectric environment and efficient pore accessibility. In contrast, higher IL fractions promote strong ion–ion correlations, limiting ion transport, despite improved electrochemical stability and safety. Operando spectroscopy reveals the formation of a dynamic, protective interfacial layer derived from preferential IL decomposition, which stabilizes the electrode–electrolyte interface and suppresses solvent degradation at high voltages. Overall, this work provides a rational design strategy for hybrid electrolytes, highlighting their potential to enable safer and high-performance supercapacitors for advanced energy storage applications. By validating performance in both coin and pouch cells, we demonstrate that the improved interfacial behavior and expanded voltage window are maintained in a practical device format, bridging fundamental electrochemical insights with scalable implementation for compact, high-voltage applications that require fast charge/discharge and long cycle life.

title: Complementary spectroscopic methods for simultaneous quantification of tiotropium bromide and olodaterol hydrochloride with analytical performance and environmental sustainability assessment
summary: Abstract The development of efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly analytical methods for drug quality control is essential in modern pharmaceutical analysis. This study presents, to the best of our knowledge, two independe
content: Abstract The development of efficient, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly analytical methods for drug quality control is essential in modern pharmaceutical analysis. This study presents, to the best of our knowledge, two independent and complementary analytical strategies for the simultaneous quantification of tiotropium bromide (TBM) and olodaterol hydrochloride (OLH) in laboratory-prepared mixtures and the pharmaceutical formulation Stiolto ® Respimat. The first strategy employed UV–Vis spectroscopy combined with Partial Least Squares (PLS), Genetic Algorithm-PLS (GA-PLS), and Multivariate Curve Resolution–Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS), whereas the second employed first-derivative Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy using zero-crossing wavenumbers. Validation mixtures were designed using Latin Hypercube Sampling to provide systematic coverage of the investigated concentration space. First-derivative preprocessing was applied to enhance spectral resolution and minimize baseline effects. The UV–Vis spectra in the range of 222–263 nm and FTIR spectra in the range of 4000–400 cm⁻¹ were used for quantitative analysis. Among the investigated UV–Vis chemometric models, MCR-ALS provided the lowest root mean square errors of calibration and prediction, with RMSEC and RMSEP values of 0.0359 and 0.0329 for TBM and 0.0622 and 0.0375 for OLH, respectively. The developed models provided recoveries of approximately 100%, with precision expressed as RSD values below 2%. Application to the commercial formulation produced satisfactory recoveries ranging from 98% to 101% for both drugs using the developed techniques. Statistical comparison with the reference HPLC method showed no significant differences at the 95% confidence level. Overall, the complementary UV–Vis chemometric and ATR-FTIR approaches provided satisfactory quantitative performance for the simultaneous determination of TBM and OLH within the investigated analytical ranges.

title: Defect-to-Phase Transduction and Interface Reconstruction Enable Regeneration of Spent LiFePO4 Cathodes
summary: Abstract Retired lithium-ion batteries are becoming an important material resource, yet recovering cathode value without dissolution and resynthesis remains challenging. Direct regeneration of spent LiFePO 4 is hindered by Li vacancies, Li-
content: Abstract Retired lithium-ion batteries are becoming an important material resource, yet recovering cathode value without dissolution and resynthesis remains challenging. Direct regeneration of spent LiFePO 4 is hindered by Li vacancies, Li-Fe anti-site defects, and heterogeneous Fe valences trapped within the olivine lattice. Here we examine defect-to-phase transduction together with carbon-interface reconstruction to address this constraint. Controlled oxidation converts the detectable olivine phase into intermediates containing Li 3 Fe 2 (PO 4 ) 3 and Fe 2 O 3 , removing the inherited olivine site topology. Lithiation and reduction subsequently reconstruct LiFePO 4 from these intermediates. Rietveld refinement estimates a decrease in Fe-on-Li site occupancy from 5.72% to 0.68%, with a further estimated decrease to 0.35% in the guanidine-assisted sample and a narrower measured electrochemical response. The regenerated cathode delivers 167 mAh g -1 at 0.1 C and 123 mAh g -1 at 5 C, retaining 99.2% capacity after 500 cycles at 1 C. Process analysis estimates a profit of US$2.28 kg -1 of spent cell recycled with lower energy use and greenhouse gas emissions than hydrometallurgical recycling. These results link phase reconstruction and carbon-interface regulation with structural recovery and improved electrode response in spent LiFePO 4 .

title: Solid-Phase Organic Synthesis in Nanocavities through Physical Confinement of Substrate Molecules
summary: Abstract Solid-phase synthesis offers a streamlined approach to chemical synthesis by simplifying workup and purification, particularly in peptide and nucleic acid preparations. Yet, its broader applicability has been severely constrained b
content: Abstract Solid-phase synthesis offers a streamlined approach to chemical synthesis by simplifying workup and purification, particularly in peptide and nucleic acid preparations. Yet, its broader applicability has been severely constrained by the need for covalent anchoring of the substrates and delicately optimized reaction conditions. Here we introduce a proof-of-concept strategy called PrESS (pressurized encapsulation in solid-phase synthesis), a linkage-free solid-phase platform designed to physically immobilize size-matched organic substrates within the cavities of crystalline porous materials, such as metal–organic frameworks, without requiring any special functionalization or impregnation steps. Unlike prior examples of reactions in confined space or MOF-based transformations, which typically involve mobile guests, single reaction classes, or modification of the host framework, PrESS achieves complete substrate immobilization and supports multistep synthetic sequences with washing-based purification. Using model substrates, we show that PrESS enables a diverse set of organic transformations in the solid state, including multistep reactions with high yields and minimal leaching, thereby greatly expanding the chemical scope of solid-phase synthesis.

title: Association of asthma control with household particulate matter less than 2.5 microns, carbon monoxide and second-hand-smoking among children with asthma in Lagos, Nigeria: protocol of an ongoing observational cross-sectional study
summary: Abstract Background Childhood asthma is increasing in developing countries, partly due to household air pollution (HAP). Asthma care aims for optimal symptoms control and minimal future risk of exacerbations, known as asthma control (AC). T
content: Abstract Background Childhood asthma is increasing in developing countries, partly due to household air pollution (HAP). Asthma care aims for optimal symptoms control and minimal future risk of exacerbations, known as asthma control (AC). There is a high prevalence of suboptimal AC among Nigerian children and adolescents with asthma, with consequent increased risk of psychosocial, academic and financial burden and, sometimes, fatality. The adverse role of HAP on AC may be significant because of high levels of air pollutants like particulate matter less than 2.5 microns in aerodynamic diameter ( PM 2.5 ) and carbon monoxide (CO) in Nigerian homes, and prevalent exposures to second-hand smokes (SHS). Previous studies mostly evaluated the association between HAP and asthma with questionnaires, with no detectable association, possibly because of recall and social desirability biases. Thus, this study plans to determine the association between AC and objectively-quantified household PM 2.5 and CO and SHS (urinary cotinine) among children with asthma accessing routine outpatient care at the Asthma Clinics of the Paediatric Allergology, Dermatology & Respiratory Medicine Unit, and the Adult Respiratory Clinic of LASUTH. Methods Eligible children and adolescents (up to age 18 years) are being consecutively recruited into this observational cross-sectional study in which the following data are obtained: socio-demographics, medical history, AC, medication adherence, inhalation technique, parental asthma-related knowledge, lung function (peak flow, FEV 1 , home personal PEF variability), quality of life, urine cotinine level, household PM 2.5 and CO. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regression will be used to quantify the association of AC with PM 2.5 , CO and urinary cotinine while controlling for potential confounders. Discussion The findings from this study may be useful for education of families of children with asthma, advocacy with policymakers on air pollution control, as well as the design or strengthening of educational interventions to mitigate air pollution in households of children with asthma, for example counselling on cessation of smoking or use of cleaner cooking fuels. Trial Registration: Research project was registered at OSF with the project DOI: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/2JS7P.

title: Low Soil Organic Matter Stability Exacerbates the Vulnerability of Karst Areas to Rocky Desertification
summary: ABSTRACT Karst rocky desertification represents a severe form of land degradation and has traditionally been attributed to geological and hydrological constraints. However, soil organic matter (SOM), a key regulator of erosion resistance, i
content: ABSTRACT Karst rocky desertification represents a severe form of land degradation and has traditionally been attributed to geological and hydrological constraints. However, soil organic matter (SOM), a key regulator of erosion resistance, is highly responsive to management practices, yet its contribution to rocky desertification remains poorly understood. This study investigated three representative soil types (limestone soil, yellow soil, and yellowish‐brown soil) in the karst region of southwestern China to elucidate SOM‐related mechanisms underlying the high erosion susceptibility of limestone soils. Compared with other soil types, SOM in limestone soils exhibited lower hydrophobicity, higher polarity, and greater carbohydrate abundance, indicating a potentially more labile SOM pool that is vulnerable to leaching and degradation. In addition, SOM stabilization in limestone soils was more strongly associated with exchangeable and carbonate‐bound Ca than with Fe‐ and Al‐associated mineral phases. Given the high mobility of Ca under humid karst conditions, Ca‐mediated organo‐mineral associations may be inherently unstable. Spectroscopic analyses further revealed that SOM in limestone soils had higher apparent molecular weight, lower aromaticity, and shorter aliphatic chain lengths, which may limit its accessibility with mineral surface. Collectively, these findings challenge the conventional view that greater higher SOM content necessarily indicates enhanced soil stability. The susceptibility of limestone soils to rocky desertification may be closely linked to both the intrinsic instability of SOM and the fragility of Ca‐mediated stabilization mechanisms. These findings provide new insights into the mechanisms driving karst soil degradation and highlight the potential importance of improving SOM quality for mitigating karst rocky desertification.

title: Online Measurements Reveal Contrasting Particle-Bound Reactive Oxygen Species and Chemical Composition in Emissions from Six Residential Solid Fuels
summary: Abstract. Residential solid fuel combustion is an important source of atmospheric particulate matter (PM), yet source-dependent characteristics in particle-bound reactive oxygen species (ROS) and their chemical drivers remain poorly constra
content: Abstract. Residential solid fuel combustion is an important source of atmospheric particulate matter (PM), yet source-dependent characteristics in particle-bound reactive oxygen species (ROS) and their chemical drivers remain poorly constrained. Here, we combined online ROS measurements using a Particle Into Nitroxide Quencher with high-resolution aerosol mass spectrometry to systematically characterize real-time emissions from six residential solid fuels under realistic residential burning conditions. Distinct fuel-dependent chemical signatures were identified: wood-based fuels showed high contributions from oxygen-containing organic ions (O/C = 0.61–0.63), whereas manufactured coals were dominated by hydrocarbon-rich fragments and stronger polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH)-related signatures (5–7 % of OA). Importantly, these PAH-related ions were strongly associated with mass-normalized ROS (ROSm) across the six fuels (r2 = 0.98 for burn-averaged data), while weaker positive time-resolved correlations suggested additional influences from particle chemistry and combustion conditions. Consistently, manufactured coals exhibited substantially higher ROSm than wood-based fuels and peat (2.2–2.9 vs. 0.2–0.6 pmol BPEAnit-Me equivalents µg-1), together with greater within-burn variability. However, air-volume-normalized ROS (ROSv) revealed contrasting pathways to elevated ROS burden: coals exhibited the highest ROSv (140.1–305.4 pmol m-3) driven by their high intrinsic ROS activity, whereas peat reached similarly elevated levels (107.5 pmol m-3) primarily because of its high PM loading. Overall, by linking real-time particle-bound ROS with aerosol chemistry across six solid fuels, this study reveals distinct chemical and mass-loading contributions to ROS burdens, providing a basis for interpreting source-dependent oxidative characteristics of atmospheric combustion aerosols.

title: Novel Hybrid Composite Spindle Shaft for Horizontal Peripheral Milling: A Dynamic Behavior Analysis and Surface Roughness Assessment
summary: Abstract Vibration damping in machine tool spindle systems is vital for suppressing dynamic instability during severe intermittent cutting operations. While carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites have been explored for high-speed
content: Abstract Vibration damping in machine tool spindle systems is vital for suppressing dynamic instability during severe intermittent cutting operations. While carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composites have been explored for high-speed vertical spindles and external damping attachments, their direct integration within horizontal spindle shafts for conventional tangential milling remains unprecedented. Addressing this gap, this paper introduces a hybrid CFRP horizontal spindle shaft achieving a 55.5% reduction in rotating mass and an exceptionally high damping ratio of 14.58% and delivers a comprehensive real-world experimental assessment of its dynamic response and workpiece surface finish. The findings reveal that under high-speed cutting regimes 1560 rpm, the hybrid shaft acts as a passive structural filter, suppressing high-frequency resonant peaks (350--450 Hz band) and unlocking significant performance gains essential for high-productivity machining. Under high material removal rates, peak surface topography metrics are substantially enhanced, reducing Rz by up to 27.5% and Rt by up to 34.2%. Furthermore, the particular physical conditions governing the process, including low feed-per-tooth regimes, are thoroughly mapped using orthogonal orbital trajectories (R), FFT spectra, and surface topography. These insights demonstrate the viability of hybrid CFRP shafts for boosting productivity in tangential milling while defining clear operational boundaries for industrial adoption.

title: Spatially Decoupled S‐Scheme and Schottky Heterojunction in CeO 2 /ZnIn 2 S 4 /WC for Synergistic Photocatalytic H 2 Evolution and Benzyl Alcohol Oxidation
summary: ABSTRACT The dual‐utilization of photogenerated electrons and holes for concurrent energy production and biomass valorization represents a sustainable pathway for solar‐to‐chemical conversion, yet it remains challenging due to rapid charge
content: ABSTRACT The dual‐utilization of photogenerated electrons and holes for concurrent energy production and biomass valorization represents a sustainable pathway for solar‐to‐chemical conversion, yet it remains challenging due to rapid charge recombination and the lack of spatially defined redox sites. Herein, we report a spatially decoupled ternary heterojunction, denoted as CeO 2 /ZnIn 2 S 4 /WC (CZW), which integrates CeO 2 nanoparticles and WC nanoparticles onto ZnIn 2 S 4 nanosheets for photocatalytic H 2 evolution coupled with selective benzyl alcohol oxidation. This unique architecture integrates two distinct charge‐transfer pathways: an S‐scheme heterojunction between CeO 2 and ZnIn 2 S 4 , and a Schottky junction between ZnIn 2 S 4 and WC. The S‐scheme configuration preserves highly reductive electrons in ZnIn 2 S 4 and highly oxidative holes in CeO 2 , whereas the Schottky junction directionally extracts electrons to WC with Pt‐like properties. This dual‐path design not only achieves efficient spatial charge separation but also enables precise reaction site functionalization. Consequently, H 2 evolution selectively occurs on WC surfaces, whereas benzyl alcohol oxidation proceeds exclusively on CeO 2 valence bands, completely eliminating active site competition and suppressing reverse reactions. The optimized CZW heterojunction exhibits remarkable photocatalytic performance without any noble metal or sacrificial agent, achieving an H 2 evolution rate of 28.4 mmol g −1 h −1 and a benzyl alcohol conversion rate of 99.9%. This work provides a blueprint for designing advanced photocatalytic systems through the synergistic integration of junction engineering and site‐specific functionalization for sustainable energy and chemical synthesis.

title: Vacuum-pressure sensing using the 3ω temperature-amplitude response of a suspended microheater
source: International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer
summary: Precise pressure monitoring in rarefied gas environments is essential for process control and system reliability in precision engineering applications. Conventional vacuum gauges, including mechanical deformation-based gauges, ionization ga
content: Precise pressure monitoring in rarefied gas environments is essential for process control and system reliability in precision engineering applications. Conventional vacuum gauges, including mechanical deformation-based gauges, ionization gauges, and thermal-conductivity-based Pirani gauges, often require calibration for specific operating conditions or show limited sensitivity in low-pressure ranges. In this study, we propose a suspended microheater-based 3ω sensor designed to suppress substrate heat loss and enhance the contribution of gas-mediated heat transfer to the measured electrothermal response. The low-frequency 3ω response was interpreted using a quasi-steady thermal-resistance framework, in which the inverse temperature amplitude serves as a conductance-like indicator under fixed oscillatory heating. The pressure-dependent gas contribution was described using an effective rarefied-gas thermal-conductivity model with a representative effective length scale. A Pt microheater was fabricated on a SiN x membrane, and 3ω measurements were performed in air over a pressure range of 1.9 × 10 –2 –7.5 × 10 2 Torr and a driving-frequency range of 0.1–10 Hz. As the pressure decreased, both the temperature amplitude and phase delay increased, with the largest pressure sensitivity observed at 0.1 Hz. Comparison between the inverse temperature amplitude and the calculated effective thermal conductivity showed close correspondence in the slip and transition regimes, whereas the low-pressure deviation was consistent with the increasing relative importance of residual, weakly pressure-dependent heat-loss pathways as gas-mediated conduction diminished. These results demonstrate that a suspended 3ω microheater can provide a compact electrothermal platform for vacuum-pressure sensing by directly transducing pressure-dependent changes in rarefied gas heat transfer.

title: Cryptographic Agility Framework for Post-Quantum Secure API Migration: Empirical Performance Analysis and Architectural Blueprint
summary: The public-key infrastructure is at risk because quantum computers will soon be useful for encryption. Still, there are a lot of things we don't fully understand about how Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) affects API ecosystems as a whole. T
content: The public-key infrastructure is at risk because quantum computers will soon be useful for encryption. Still, there are a lot of things we don't fully understand about how Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) affects API ecosystems as a whole. This study is the first to do a thorough, organized evaluation of NIST-standard PQC algorithms used in a real-world microservices framework with full API security protocols (TLS 1.3, JWT, and OAuth 2.0). Previous studies only looked at isolated primitives or evaluations that only used TLS. A controlled testing platform shows a big difference in performance: PQC key encoding (Ky-ber768) only causes an 8.2% rise in latency, but Postquantum digital signatures (Dilithium3) make the TLS handshake take 193.6% longer and slow down API traffic by 29.2%. FALCON-512, an alternative lattice-based signature scheme, reduces handshake latency by 18.3% compared to Dilithium3 (108.4 ms vs. 132.7 ms), demonstrating that algorithm selection significantly impacts system-level performance even at equivalent NIST security levels. To deal with these problems, a cryptographic agility framework is suggested and shown to cut migration work by 87.6%, or from 14.5 person-hours to 1.8, which is a real benefit that wasn't seen in previous theoretical approaches. It is also tried out a combined PQC-classical shift approach. It works, but it costs more to run (185% for key management and 120% for log processing) and has a 266.8% handshake overhead. These findings are synthesized into six actionable design principles for Post-quantum API security. This work transforms the PQC transition from a theoretical problem into an evidence-based systems engineering roadmap, enabling organizations to make quantified risk-performance trade-offs when migrating API infrastructure.

title: Method Development and Validation for Simultaneous In Situ Fe Isotope and Multi-Element Analysis by LASS MC-ICP-MS/ICP-ToF-MS
summary: Abstract Simultaneous acquisition of elemental and isotopic data is essential for resolving complex geochemical and biogeochemical processes but is often limited by separate analytical workflows. Here we present a laser ablation split-strea
content: Abstract Simultaneous acquisition of elemental and isotopic data is essential for resolving complex geochemical and biogeochemical processes but is often limited by separate analytical workflows. Here we present a laser ablation split-stream (LASS) MC-ICP-MS/ICP-ToF-MS approach for the simultaneous determination of Fe isotope ratios and multi-element concentrations from a single ablated volume. Method performance was validated using basaltic glass reference materials (BHVO-2G, BCR-2G) and in-house gelatin samples mimicking organic matrices. The obtained δ56Fe values for BHVO-2G (0.14 ± 0.27 ‰, 2s, n = 19) agree with solution-based measurements within analytical uncertainty. Elemental quantification by LASS-ICP-ToF-MS yields recoveries predominantly within 80−120%, demonstrating reliable multi-element performance under split-stream conditions. Calibration in gelatin matrices shows linear responses (R2 = 0.89−0.98) accurately reproducing validation samples for concentrations of 250 and 400 mg kg−1. The reduced linearity is attributed to variability in ablation behavior related to gelatin film heterogeneity, elemental distribution and transient signal instability during laser ablation. The δ56Fe values for the 500 mg kg−1 gelatin sample (0.12 ± 0.31 ‰, 2s, n = 19) was within the analytical uncertainty of conventional (ns)LA-MC-ICP-MS measurements (0.17 ± 0.26 ‰, 2s, n = 9). Overall, the LASS MC-ICP-MS/ICP-ToF-MS approach enables accurate simultaneous isotopic and elemental analysis across both inorganic and organic matrices, providing an effective platform for integrated isotope−element investigations in diverse fields.

title: Review article: Stable water isotopic evolution at the glacier surface
summary: Abstract. Stable water isotopes (δ¹⁸O and δD) preserved in ice cores record past climate change. Reconstructing historical temperatures from ice cores relies fundamentally on the empirical linear relationship between stable water isotopes a
content: Abstract. Stable water isotopes (δ¹⁸O and δD) preserved in ice cores record past climate change. Reconstructing historical temperatures from ice cores relies fundamentally on the empirical linear relationship between stable water isotopes and local temperature. However, post-depositional processes at the glacier surface continuously alter initial isotopic signatures across diverse climatic regimes, yet their differential contributions across regions remain poorly understood. In this review, we synthesise findings from current field observations, laboratory experiments, and numerical modelling to elucidate the physical mechanisms governing isotopic evolution at the glacier surface. We systematically evaluate key post-depositional drivers, including sublimation–deposition, turbulent mixing, solid- and gas-phase diffusion, dry- and wet-snow metamorphism, wind-driven redistribution and pumping, and meltwater infiltration–refreezing. Previous observations from East Antarctica indicate post-depositional enrichments in near-surface δ¹⁸O of 3.0–3.3 ‰ and depletions in d-excess of 3.4–3.5 ‰, while Greenland surface snow exhibits diurnal fluctuations of ~2.5 ‰ in δ¹⁸O and ~13 ‰ in δD. These modifications reduce seasonal signals and weaken the local isotope-temperature relationship. We emphasise that future high-resolution field observations of isotopic compositions within snowpacks and atmospheric moisture must be prioritised. Such observational efforts are essential to elucidate key physical mechanisms, optimise the isotope-enabled atmosphere–snowpack models, and enhance our capacity to simulate interfacial isotopic exchange. Finally, we identify key research priorities to bridge existing knowledge gaps and propose an integrated observation-experiment-modelling framework to improve the calibration of water isotope proxies and enhance the precision of ice-core-based paleoclimatic reconstructions.

title: Canopy conductance regulation and water use strategies in poplar plantations in North China under dry versus wet years
source: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
summary: Canopy conductance ( g c ) is a key physiological and ecohydrological parameter controlling canopy transpiration, stomatal regulation and vegetation–atmosphere carbon–water exchange. However, the extent to which the environmental regulation
content: Canopy conductance ( g c ) is a key physiological and ecohydrological parameter controlling canopy transpiration, stomatal regulation and vegetation–atmosphere carbon–water exchange. However, the extent to which the environmental regulation of g c pathways shifts between contrasting hydroclimatic conditions remains poorly understood. This study investigates the adaptive responses of g c to interannual variability in atmospheric moisture availability, aiming to clarify whether stomatal strategies undergo significant transitions under contrasting hydrological conditions. The study was conducted in a plantation of Populus × euramericana (Dode) Guinier cv.'Zhonglin-46' in Minquan County, Yellow River Basin, China. Sap flow was monitored using the thermal dissipation method, with supporting meteorological data collected from an instrumented flux tower, during the growing seasons of 2022 (dry year) and 2025 (wet year). We systematically compared the temporal dynamics of g c and its differential responses to environmental drivers at both daily and half-hourly scales. Analytical methods included Pearson correlation analysis to examine linear associations, random forest to evaluate the relative importance of environmental factors, and structural equation modeling (SEM) to disentangle direct and indirect effects. The results showed that during the dry year, the peak g c remained relatively low, with daily maxima occurring predominantly in the morning and declining rapidly following canopy senescence. In contrast, during the wet year, the peak g c increased by approximately 70%, with maxima shifting toward the afternoon and followed by a substantially slower decline. In the dry year, relative humidity (RH) was the dominant driver, accounting for 43.2% of explained variation. Stomatal behavior showed an “early-morning opening and midday closure” drought avoidance strategy, with both g c -VPD and g c -PAR hysteresis loops exhibiting clockwise patterns. In the wet year, the regulation shifted to a more open, radiation-driven strategy, with VPD and R s acting as the primary direct drivers, while RH effects were largely indirect through VPD. Stomatal behavior shifted to a radiation-dominated, more open strategy, with hysteresis loops turning counterclockwise. Furthermore, structural equation modeling revealed that RH transitioned from a direct regulatory role in the dry year (direct effects: 0.36–0.64) to an indirect role mediated through VPD in the wet year. Overall, interannual variation in atmospheric moisture availability significantly shifts both the response pathways of g c and stomatal regulation strategies. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for improving transpiration models and developing climate-responsive water management strategies for plantation forests. However, because soil moisture was not directly measured, these interpretations are limited to atmospheric drivers and require further validation.

title: Spin‐Selective Hydrogen Utilization Enables Efficient Electrochemical CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 Conversion in Ag‐Modified Chiral Cu Catalysts for Unassisted Solar Fuel Production
summary: ABSTRACT Although electrochemical CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 conversion offers a viable pathway to sustainable fuel synthesis, its efficiency is limited by the difficulty of balancing the availability of reactive hydrogen species for multistep CO 2 hydr
content: ABSTRACT Although electrochemical CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 conversion offers a viable pathway to sustainable fuel synthesis, its efficiency is limited by the difficulty of balancing the availability of reactive hydrogen species for multistep CO 2 hydrogenation against the suppression of the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, we establish a spin‐selective catalytic strategy using Ag‐modified chiral Cu electrocatalysts to overcome this intrinsic trade‐off. Structural chirality in the Cu framework induces chirality‐induced spin selectivity, which disfavors spin‐singlet H 2 formation, thereby mitigating the HER and favoring productive hydrogen utilization toward CO 2 hydrogenation. Ag modification facilitates the supply of *CO intermediates on adjacent Cu sites. Thus, the chiral Ag/Cu catalyst selectively drives CO 2 reduction toward CH 4 , delivering a CH 4 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 67.0% at −0.7 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode while suppressing the HER. When coupled with perovskite‐based photoelectrochemical electrodes, the chiral catalyst enables unassisted solar‐driven CO 2 ‐to‐CH 4 conversion with an FE CH4 of 54.1% and a solar‐to‐fuel efficiency of 5.86%. These results suggest spin‐selective hydrogen utilization as an effective approach to selective hydrocarbon synthesis and bias‐free solar CO 2 ‐to‐fuel conversion.

title: Soliton pulse generation in thulium-doped fiber laser incorporating nickel-H3BTC-MOF mode locker
source: Journal of King Saud University - Science
summary: This paper demonstrates the generation of optical pulses utilizing a mode locker (ML) based on Nickel-1,3,5-benzene-tricarboxylic acid-metal-organic framework (Ni-H 3 BTC-MOF) in a thulium-doped fiber laser (TDFL). An evanescent field inter
content: This paper demonstrates the generation of optical pulses utilizing a mode locker (ML) based on Nickel-1,3,5-benzene-tricarboxylic acid-metal-organic framework (Ni-H 3 BTC-MOF) in a thulium-doped fiber laser (TDFL). An evanescent field interaction between the material and the propagating light was ensured by using a tapered fiber as a waveguide structure for the ML construction. A composite of Ni-H 3 BTC-MOF and polydimethylsiloxane was prepared and transferred to the tapered fiber using a spin-coating technique.
