The prepared ML was characterized for nonlinear saturable absorption properties, exhibiting a modulation depth of 2.00% and a saturation fluence of 2.65 μJ/cm 2 . A mode-locked soliton pulse at 1931.94 nm lasing wavelength with a spectral bandwidth of 3.30 nm was emitted at 1109 mW pump power. The fabricated ML demonstrated a stable mode-locked pulse with a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 46 dB and maintained operational stability for 1 hour with a standard deviation of 0.03 ps in the time domain.

title: Lunar Organic Output Neutralization and Advanced Recovery (LOO-NAR): A conceptual framework and feasibility review for human waste pyrolysis
summary: Long-duration lunar habitation will require technologies that convert crew-generated wastes into recoverable resources while operating within strict limits on mass, power, volume, reliability, and resupply. Human fecal waste and associated
content: Long-duration lunar habitation will require technologies that convert crew-generated wastes into recoverable resources while operating within strict limits on mass, power, volume, reliability, and resupply. Human fecal waste and associated sanitation materials remain a major unresolved stream because current spacecraft systems emphasize collection and containment rather than downstream conversion. This review assesses the potential applicability of pyrolysis to lunar human-waste management by synthesizing evidence from human feces, simulated fecal material, fecal sludge, biosolids, sanitation-related materials, and relevant terrestrial analogs. The analysis examines torrefaction, intermediate-temperature pyrolysis, and high-temperature conversion with emphasis on product yields, gas composition, biochar properties, aqueous pyrolysis liquid treatment, contaminant fate, reactor design, and habitat integration. Across the literature, pyrolysis shows potential to support waste stabilization, moisture recovery, solid-waste reduction, biochar production, and non-condensable gas generation, but performance varies with feedstock composition and operating conditions. Based on this evidence, the review introduces Lunar Organic Output Neutralization and Advanced Recovery, or LOO-NAR, as a mission-adaptive conceptual framework linking sealed collection, pre-drying, staged thermal conversion, product separation, gas cleanup, heat recovery, water treatment, and selective resource use. The framework is designed to allow treatment intensity and product recovery to increase as mission duration and resource demands increase. Human fecal waste and sanitation materials form the baseline feedstock, with future potential for compatible organic outputs. Key gaps include reduced-gravity and vacuum validation, mixed-feedstock variability, contaminant control, product quality, long-duration reliability, and integrated systems and equivalent system mass evaluation. These findings identify a focused validation pathway for assessing the potential future lunar application of LOO-NAR.

title: Modification of an Electrochemical Abacavir-Sulphate-Specific Sensor Using Molecular Imprinting for Enhanced Selectivity in Complex Sample Matrices
summary: Abacavir sulphate residues reported in South African water resources highlight the need for monitoring pharmaceutical contaminants to assess wastewater treatment efficiency and protect aquatic ecosystems. This study aimed to determine wheth
content: Abacavir sulphate residues reported in South African water resources highlight the need for monitoring pharmaceutical contaminants to assess wastewater treatment efficiency and protect aquatic ecosystems. This study aimed to determine whether combining molecularly imprinted polymers (MIPs) with a carbon paste electrode (CPE) could improve the selectivity and sensitivity of abacavir detection while providing a cost-effective alternative to conventional methods. The optimized MIP-CPE sensor was applied to determine abacavir sulphate in real water matrices. The MIP was attained by bulk polymerization and coupled with CPE. The MIP had thermal stability of greater than 300 °C. Using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV), it was possible to quantify abacavir sulphate using a redox probe; a linear response in a range of 2 to 14 µM with a correlation coefficient (R2) of 0.991 was observed, with lower limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) of 1.47 µM and 4.47 µM, respectively. Thus, the developed MIP-CPE sensor can be used to detect analyte residues present at trace levels. The developed sensor demonstrated satisfactory accuracy and precision in real water matrices, achieving recoveries of 82.2–101.2% with RSD values of 1.27–7.34% for spiked abacavir sulphate concentrations of 8 and 12 µM. The presence of abacavir sulphate was only detected in uMhlathuzana wastewater effluent samples, with a concentration of 7.19 µM (RSD 7.40%, n = 3). The MIP-CPE showed high selectivity for abacavir sulphate when tested alongside common interferents (lamivudine, ibuprofen, nevirapine, and trimethoprim). Abacavir sulphate gave the lowest peak current (DPV) of the group (489 µA), due to the ferricyanide peak falling when the target rebinds and blocks the probe. A lower current for abacavir therefore means more rebinding, which is evidence of selectivity. The MIP-CPE sensor demonstrated rapid rebinding and strong affinity for abacavir sulphate, even in complex matrices. This study offers wastewater treatment plants as a cost-effective, sensitive, and selective analytical method for routine monitoring of antiretroviral contaminants before effluent discharge into environmental waters.

title: Enhancing shallow water habitat mapping with high-resolution pansharpened PRISMA imagery data
summary: Macrophytes are crucial elements in freshwater ecosystems and ecological processes, by supporting biodiversity, stabilizing sediments, and improving water quality. Nowadays, these ecosystems are threatened by environmental changes and the i
content: Macrophytes are crucial elements in freshwater ecosystems and ecological processes, by supporting biodiversity, stabilizing sediments, and improving water quality. Nowadays, these ecosystems are threatened by environmental changes and the increase in anthropic pressures; moreover, their spatial distribution is often highly fragmented. Considering their importance, monitoring macrophytes’ spatio-temporal variability with non-invasive observations is fundamental. Hyperspectral remote sensing offers a valuable tool for mapping aquatic vegetation and benthic substrates accurately, although its application is often limited by spatial resolution, especially in environments characterized by patch distribution and mixed pixels. To address these limits, this study exploits the PRISMA panchromatic band for a PRISMA image acquired on 09/07/2024 on Lake Garda (Italy), combining high spectral resolution (66 band in the visible-near-infrared range) with enhanced spatial resolution (5 m). The pansharpening procedure is applied to PRISMA Level 2D images using a deep learning model trained through both supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. This study focuses on the optically shallow waters of the Sirmione Peninsula (southern portion of Lake Garda), characterized by the presence of macrophytes coverage, with the goal of classifying the benthic substrate into seven classes, and retrieving bottom depth. In addition to the panchromatic product with a spatial resolution of 5 m, aggregated products with resolutions of 10 m and 30 m were also generated. The results showed overall accuracies of 80%, 68%, and 48% for resolutions ranging from 5 m to 30 m in the classification of the benthic substrate. Similar results were obtained in the validation of bottom depths when compared to data collected by the Institute of the Italian Navy (IIM) and in situ measurements acquired during the field campaign (r = 0.82 for 5 m data, r = 0.78 for 10 m data, r = 0.75 for 30 m data). The outcomes enable more accurate monitoring of spatial-temporal dynamics in freshwater ecosystems and highlight the potential of pansharpened hyperspectral products to enhance the mapping and classification of benthic substrates, with higher accuracy in detecting small patches.

title: Effects of feeding lubabegron on apparent absorption and retention of nitrogen, fractional degradation rate of skeletal muscle, and glucose tolerance in finishing feedlot steers
summary: Lubabegron (LUB; Experior®; Elanco Animal Health, Greenfield, IN), a β-adrenergic modulator, is the first U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved product that reduces ammonia gas emissions per kilogram of live weight and hot carcass weig
content: Lubabegron (LUB; Experior®; Elanco Animal Health, Greenfield, IN), a β-adrenergic modulator, is the first U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved product that reduces ammonia gas emissions per kilogram of live weight and hot carcass weight in beef steers and heifers fed in confinement for slaughter. However, there is limited information about the effect of LUB on nitrogen retention, skeletal muscle turnover, and glucose metabolism in beef cattle. Therefore, 16 Angus steers (initial BW = 553 ± 25 kg) were used in a randomized complete-block-design to examine the impact of LUB feeding on apparent nitrogen retention and excretion, fractional degradation rate of skeletal muscle, and glucose tolerance. Steers were individually housed in outdoor dirt-surfaced pens and fed a steam-flaked corn-based diet once daily in amounts to allow ad libitum access to feed over a 24 h period. Treatments were negative control (CON; no β-ligand) and LUB (fed at a rate of 3.2 g Experior/ ton of DM for the last 91 d on feed). A glucose tolerance test (GTT) was conducted twice during the study, and total fecal and urinary output were collected for 5 d on all steers. On day 96, following a 4-day LUB withdrawal period, all animals were slaughtered at a USDA-inspected abattoir, and carcass data were collected. Data were analyzed using the mixed models procedure in R. Initial and final body weights, dry matter intake, average daily gain, and feed efficiency were similar (P > 0.05) between treatments. Skeletal muscle degradation and fractional protein breakdown rate were reduced (P < 0.01) when cattle fed LUB were compared to cattle fed CON. Neither treatment nor a treatment × time interaction influenced glucose, insulin, or non-esterified fatty acids concentrations throughout the GTT. Apparent nitrogen absorption and retention were not different across treatments (P > 0.05), but total urinary output was reduced (P = 0.02) when cattle were fed LUB. Steers receiving LUB had a 9.21% reduction (P = 0.004) in calculated cumulative ammonia gas emissions compared with control steers. Longissimus muscle (LM) area was greater (P < 0.01) in steers fed LUB compared to steers fed CON, whereas yield grade tended (P = 0.09) to be greater in steers fed CON than in steers fed LUB. These results indicate that LUB supplementation decreased muscle protein turnover, improved LM area, and reduced total urinary output in feedlot cattle, without affecting nitrogen balance.

title: Imaging fast neural circuit activity in brain and nerve with Electrical Impedance Tomography (fnEIT): review, method and engineering aspects
summary: Fast neural electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT) is a technique for imaging neural activity in brains or nerves, with a resolution of milliseconds and millimetres, using an applied current and boundary or depth voltage measurement. Proof
content: Fast neural electrical impedance tomography (fnEIT) is a technique for imaging neural activity in brains or nerves, with a resolution of milliseconds and millimetres, using an applied current and boundary or depth voltage measurement. Proof of principle has been demonstrated in animal studies, but it is yet to be adopted into common use. Objective The purpose of this review is to provide an introduction and overview of the method and technical aspects of fnEIT research and its place in the biomedical sciences. Topics covered include bioimpedance of action potentials, fnEIT studies to date, similar EIT methods and technical innovations. Approach A critical review of the fnEIT literature has been performed. Promising areas of future work and their applications are highlighted, including challenges that must be overcome. Main Results It is shown that the fields of nerve imaging and neuromodulation, cognitive neuroscience in animals and humans, and epileptic seizure localisation could benefit from the ability of fnEIT to image millisecond scale neuronal depolarization throughout brain or nerve. This is achievable with existing methods but with current limitations of the need for implanted cranial or nerve electrodes and averaging to a repeated stimulus. Current approaches to overcome this include CMOS integrated active electrodes, frequency division multiplexing for parallel signal acquisition, and recording with atomic magnetometers. With these, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec. Significance. This review serves as a general guide for those working in related fields or those considering the use of EIT. With the above advances, it is a realistic possibility to achieve non-invasive imaging of fast neural activity in real-time with an electrode-atomic magnetometer helmet in human subjects with a resolution of mm and msec.

title: Hyperspectral Soil Metal Estimation Using Fractional-Order Derivatives and LSTM–KAN Modeling
summary: Abstract Hyperspectral estimation of soil heavy metals is challenging because their spectral responses are weak, indirect, and strongly affected by the soil matrix. In this study, 167 surface soil samples collected from a karst open-pit coa
content: Abstract Hyperspectral estimation of soil heavy metals is challenging because their spectral responses are weak, indirect, and strongly affected by the soil matrix. In this study, 167 surface soil samples collected from a karst open-pit coal mining area in Guizhou, China, were analyzed for As, Cr, Cu, and Hg. Spectra were processed using fractional-order derivative (FOD) preprocessing over orders of 0.0–2.0 and reorganized into wavelength-ordered sequences for a long short-term memory network coupled with a Kolmogorov–Arnold network regression head (LSTM–KAN). Random forest (RF), partial least-squares regression (PLSR), and LSTM with a fully connected regression head (LSTM–FC) were used for comparison. Using the same 117/50 sample-level holdout split across all models and elements, LSTM–KAN achieved the best overall validation performance, with a mean R2 of 0.9692 across the four metals. The holdout-selected FOD orders were 1.2 for As and Hg, 1.8 for Cr, and 1.4 for Cu. 10-fold cross-validation further supported the internal consistency of LSTM–KAN, yielding overall R2 values of 0.9148–0.9879. Spectral regions showing strong metal–reflectance correlations were mainly concentrated around 2200–2300 nm, while the FOD orders maximizing spectral correlation differed from those producing the best predictive performance. These results demonstrate that combining FOD preprocessing with wavelength-ordered sequence modeling can improve quantitative estimation of soil heavy metals within the Jinsha study area data set.

title: Charting the Structure and Functional Landscape of the SF3B1 Intrinsically Disordered Region
summary: Despite its essential role in pre–mRNA splicing, the structure and functional significance of the intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain (NTD) of SF3B1, a core component of the SF3b spliceosome complex, remain poorly understood. Here, w
content: Despite its essential role in pre–mRNA splicing, the structure and functional significance of the intrinsically disordered N-terminal domain (NTD) of SF3B1, a core component of the SF3b spliceosome complex, remain poorly understood. Here, we combine nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, small-angle X–ray scattering (SAXS), biochemistry, bioinformatics approaches, with molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the conformational landscape of the SF3B1-NTD and its phosphorylation-dependent remodelling. Specifically, we focus on the 186–341 region (186–341SF3B1), which contains at least four regulatory phosphorylation sites. We reveal that 186–341SF3B1 is highly dynamic, lacking a stable secondary structure, and that phosphorylation of T211, T235, T313, and T328 induces a shift toward more compact states driven by the formation of intramolecular interactions. Additionally, we unveil that 186–341SF3B1 interacts with RNA primarily via the arginine residues flaking one of the conserved tryptophan-centred motifs present within SF3B1–NTD. These interactions are transient and heterogeneous, reflecting a nonspecific yet sequence-dependent recognition mechanism. Collectively, this study provides a comprehensive description of the conformational landscape and functional features of the SF3B1-NTD, and expands the portfolio of its possible interactors, thus broadening our understanding of how intrinsic disorder, post-translational modifications, and sequence-encoded motifs cooperate to regulate pre-mRNA splicing.

title: Signatures for conserved phenolic-based acclimation responses to UV in a unicellular algal sister of land plants
summary: Ultraviolet (UV) light is a major stressor that particularly comes to bear in the terrestrial habitat. As such it is among the major challenges that the earliest land plants had to overcome. The closest algal relatives of land plants, the z
content: Ultraviolet (UV) light is a major stressor that particularly comes to bear in the terrestrial habitat. As such it is among the major challenges that the earliest land plants had to overcome. The closest algal relatives of land plants, the zygnematophytes, are single celled and filamentous algae that - in the context of their terrestrial and freshwater habitats - have diverse adaptations to UV irradiance. As such, contextualized with data on land plants, zygnematophyte algae harbor important information for inferring how the earliest land plants have acclimated to UV. Here we exposed the unicellular zygnematophyte model Mesotaenium to daily UV irradiance and assessed its response through microscopy, untargeted metabolomics, and global gene expression profiling using transcriptomics. Our data reveal cell biological acclimation by formation of lipid droplets. Further, we find that the cells accumulated chemodiverse coumarin-like derivatives. Altogether, our data suggest that acclimation to long-term UV exposure is composed of building blocks of a molecular chassis conserved with that of land plants, underpinned by phenolics and genes that are tied to their biosynthesis. From this chassis, divergent evolutionary trajectories have assembled them into a divergent conformation - one of which ushering in the emergence of the phenylpropanoid pathway.

title: Manipulation of light spectral quality for inducing off-season flowering in Jasminum sambac cv. CO.1 (Gundumalli)
summary: Jasminum sambac cv. CO.1 (Gundumalli), a commercially important fragrant flower crop of South India, experiences a marked decline in production during winter months (November to February), limiting year-round market availability. The presen
content: Jasminum sambac cv. CO.1 (Gundumalli), a commercially important fragrant flower crop of South India, experiences a marked decline in production during winter months (November to February), limiting year-round market availability. The present investigation evaluated the influence of driplock diffused polyfilm (light transmission 87 %; diffusion 62 %) as a polytunnel cladding material in combination with end-of-day (EOD) photoperiodic (light emitting diode (LED)) lighting (4 hr, 18:00–22:00 hr) under different spectral regimes on off-season flowering in CO. 1 (Gundumalli). The experiment was conducted in Mettupalayam, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, India during November 2024 – February 2025 in randomised block design (RBD) with 5 treatments and 4 replications. Treatments included open field control (T1), polytunnel without supplemental light (T2), polytunnel with 60 % red : 20 % blue : 20 % far-red (T3), polytunnel with 80 % red : 20 % blue (T4) and polytunnel with 80 % red : 20 % far-red (T5). Treatment T₅ significantly improved flower yield and quality parameters compared with other treatments (p ≤ 0.05), recording the highest pooled mean number of flower cymes (42.26 per plant), flower buds per plant (194.37), flower yield per plant (52.53 g), weight of 100 buds (28.49 g), length of flower bud (2.42 cm), length of corolla tube (1.59 cm) and width of flower bud (0.95 cm). Based on the pooled mean values, Treatment T₅ resulted in approximately 5–6-fold higher values for these parameters than the open-field control. The diffused polyfilm structure maintained mean temperatures 3–5 °C higher than ambient, facilitating sustained flower bud initiation during the cold season. The superior performance of the 80 % red : 20 % far-red spectrum may be attributed to enhanced phytochrome-mediated flowering responses. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating a diffused polyfilm polytunnel with EOD LED spectral lighting as an effective strategy for improving off-season jasmine production under protected cultivation.

title: Structural Engineering and Linear–Nonlinear Optical Properties of Indium Tin Oxide-Modified Poly(vinyl alcohol)/Chitosan Nanocomposite Films
summary: Abstract Polyvinyl alcohol/chitosan (PVA/CS)–based nanocomposite films incorporating indium tin oxide (ITO) nanoparticles were successfully synthesized via a solution-casting technique to investigate their structural, linear, and nonlinear
content: Abstract Polyvinyl alcohol/chitosan (PVA/CS)–based nanocomposite films incorporating indium tin oxide (ITO) nanoparticles were successfully synthesized via a solution-casting technique to investigate their structural, linear, and nonlinear optical properties. ITO nanoparticles were introduced at concentrations of 2–5 wt% to tailor the optoelectronic performance of the polymer matrix. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed a progressive enhancement in crystallinity with increasing ITO content, evidenced by an increase in crystallite size from 25.7 to 32.8 nm and a concomitant reduction in dislocation density and microstrain, indicating improved structural ordering. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy confirmed strong interfacial interactions between ITO nanoparticles and the PVA/CS matrix, including characteristic Sn–O vibrations and shifted ITO phonon modes, validating successful nanoparticle incorporation. SEM and EDX analyses demonstrated uniform nanoparticle dispersion at low loadings, with the onset of agglomeration observed at 5 wt% ITO. UV–Vis–NIR spectroscopy showed a systematic reduction in optical transmittance and a red shift in the absorption edge with increasing ITO content. The optical band gap decreased from 4.49 to 4.13 eV, attributed to the formation of localized states and enhanced electronic interactions within the nanocomposite. Optical constants, dielectric parameters, and dispersion energies derived from the Wemple–DiDomenico and Sellmeier models exhibited pronounced enhancement with ITO loading, reflecting increased polarizability and charge carrier density. Photoluminescence measurements revealed concentration-dependent quenching behavior and defect-related emissions, indicating modified recombination dynamics. Furthermore, significant improvements in third-order nonlinear optical susceptibility (χ⁽³⁾) and nonlinear refractive index (n₂) were observed, driven by reduced band gap energy and increased electronic polarization. These results demonstrate that low-level ITO incorporation effectively tailors the structural and optoelectronic properties of PVA/CS nanocomposites, highlighting their strong potential for advanced applications in flexible optoelectronics, photonic devices, nonlinear optics, and sensing technologies.

title: Herbicide Losses From Terraced Tile Inlet Technologies
summary: ABSTRACT Terraced agricultural fields in the Midwestern United States commonly use surface inlets to mitigate ponding and enhance drainage; however, these structures can also facilitate herbicide transport to downstream waters. This study e
content: ABSTRACT Terraced agricultural fields in the Midwestern United States commonly use surface inlets to mitigate ponding and enhance drainage; however, these structures can also facilitate herbicide transport to downstream waters. This study evaluated four terraced tile inlet technologies: Hickenbottom riser (HBR), water quality inlet (WQI), blind inlet (BI) and HBR with channel laterals (HBR + CL) for their effectiveness in reducing herbicide losses in run‐off. Four run‐off events were monitored during the 2024 soybean season and four during the 2025 corn season. Herbicides analysed included atrazine, chlorimuron‐ethyl, dimethenamid ‐P , fluthiacet‐methyl, glyphosate, mesotrione, pyroxasulfone, metolachlor, saflufenacil and sulfentrazone. In 2024, chlorimuron‐ethyl and fluthiacet‐methyl concentrations remained below detection limits (< 0.10 μg L −1 ) across all events. Following post‐emergence applications, glyphosate concentrations were higher for WQI (3.21 μg L −1 ) than for HBR and BI (0.77–0.96 μg L −1 ); however, no significant differences in median herbicide loads were observed among inlet types. In 2025, residual glyphosate was detected before application, with concentrations ranging from 0.25 (BI) to 1.46 μg L −1 (HBR). Atrazine concentrations exceeded the USEPA‐MCL (3 μg L −1 ) during one event, but seasonal median concentrations were below MCL when all herbicides were applied without a setback from the inlet. The BI had 61% lower median saflufenacil concentrations, while both BI and WQI had 43% lower dimethenamid ‐P concentrations compared to other inlets. Across all events in 2025, glyphosate concentrations were highest for HBR, whereas BI consistently resulted in the lowest herbicide loads, primarily due to reduced discharge. These results indicate that incorporating filtering materials, such as calcium carbonate aggregates, into BI can effectively reduce herbicide transport and improve run‐off water quality.

title: Ionic Liquid Regulated Wetting and Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of NCM811 Cathodes
summary: (NCM811) cathodes due to non-selective interfacial adhesion, causing severe structural pulverization, interfacial debonding, and unstable cathode electrolyte interfacial (CEI) growth during cycling. Herein, we reveal the cation-dependent in
content: (NCM811) cathodes due to non-selective interfacial adhesion, causing severe structural pulverization, interfacial debonding, and unstable cathode electrolyte interfacial (CEI) growth during cycling. Herein, we reveal the cation-dependent interfacial affinity of ionic liquids. An imidazolium-based ionic liquid (EMIM[TFSI]) preferentially wets and encapsulates NCM811 particles, forming a robust interfacial layer with superior elastic modulus (3.4 GPa vs. PVDF 0.49 GPa) and lower dissipation (0.15 vs. PVDF 0.27 keV), whereas pyrrolidinium- and piperidinium-based ILs predominantly plasticized the PVDF-rich phase. The conformal EMIM[TFSI] wetting buffers lattice strain efficiently, suppresses transition-metal dissolution, and induces the formation of thin, uniform, and robust CEI. Benefiting from the integrated chemo-mechanical stabilization, the EMIM[TFSI] modified NCM811 cathode delivers 83% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1 C, and 0.1 Ah pouch cells achieve 84% retention at 0.5 C. This study establishes that ionic liquid binders offer a rational chemo-mechanical engineering strategy for high-performance NCM811 cathodes.

title: High-frequency monitoring and model-assisted analysis of N2O emission pulses after cattle slurry application under contrasting soil management systems
summary: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions from fertilised agricultural soils are often dominated by short-lived emission pulses, but their regulation under contrasting tillage systems remains uncertain. This study combined high-frequency automated ch
content: Nitrous oxide (N 2 O) emissions from fertilised agricultural soils are often dominated by short-lived emission pulses, but their regulation under contrasting tillage systems remains uncertain. This study combined high-frequency automated chamber measurements, process-based estimates of mineral nitrogen availability and Random Forest analysis to investigate N 2 O emission dynamics after cattle slurry application under conventional tillage, minimum tillage and no-tillage. The experiment was conducted during a maize–barley sequence in northern Italy. Daily N 2 O fluxes, soil temperature, water-filled pore space, carbon dioxide fluxes and mineral nitrogen dynamics were analysed to identify the main controls of post-fertilisation emission pulses. Most crop-period N 2 O emissions occurred within the first 40 days after slurry application, accounting for 91–97% of total emissions during maize and 78–89% during barley. In absolute terms, cumulative N 2 O–N emissions averaged 4.68 ± 0.74 kg N ha -1 during maize and 2.04 ± 0.74 kg N ha -1 during barley. This difference was not explained by water-filled pore space alone, which was broadly comparable between crop periods, but by the interaction among soil temperature, slurry-derived ammonium and nitrate availability, microbial activity and tillage-related soil physical conditions. Random Forest models showed crop- and system-specific driver importance, with soil temperature dominant during barley and stronger roles of water-filled pore space and mineral nitrogen during maize. No-tillage reduced area-scaled emissions but caused a strong yield penalty during maize, whereas it showed a more favourable agro-environmental balance during barley. These findings highlight the need to evaluate slurry and tillage management through both emission intensity and crop productivity.

title: Estimating leaf area index in semi-Mediterranean oak forests using Sentinel-2 and machine learning algorithms: cross-comparison with global satellite products
summary: Leaf area index (LAI) provides crucial insights into forest canopy structure, vegetation density, and overall ecosystem functioning. In the Zagros Mountains of northwestern Iran, traditional silvopastoral practices rely on tree foliage as a
content: Leaf area index (LAI) provides crucial insights into forest canopy structure, vegetation density, and overall ecosystem functioning. In the Zagros Mountains of northwestern Iran, traditional silvopastoral practices rely on tree foliage as animal fodder for local communities. Understanding and estimating LAI in these forests can therefore support the adoption of appropriate strategies for sustainable management. This study aims to map LAI in the Zagros semi-Mediterranean Forests (ZMFs) in Iran using Machine Learning Regression Algorithms (MLRAs) combined with Sentinel-2 (S-2) data and a Digital Elevation Model (DEM). We employed three MLRAs, i.e., Support Vector Regression (SVR), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Random Forest (RF). To train and evaluate the algorithms’ performance, in situ LAI data were collected in 60 field plots measuring 20×20 m. The results revealed that the RF algorithm performed best, with R2 = 0.82, RMSE = 0.16 m2 m-2, and rRMSE = 16.84. We further cross-compared the generated LAI map with three satellite-derived LAI products: Sentinel-2 SNAP, MODIS, and PROBA-V. The results indicated that the uncertainty of global LAI products varies from 30% to 55% higher than that of our applied approach. The study concludes that integrating S-2 data with DEM and MLRAs provides an accurate and reliable method for mapping LAI in open-canopy ZMFs. However, global LAI products show higher uncertainty because of lower spatial resolution and the lack of suitable empirical transfer functions for these forest types.

title: Hydrocarbon-based composite membranes for PEM water electrolysis: From single-cell performance to stack-level operation
summary: Hydrocarbon-based three-layered composite membranes were fabricated for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) by impregnating polyethylene (PE) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) substrates with sulfonated poly(arylene thioeth
content: Hydrocarbon-based three-layered composite membranes were fabricated for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) by impregnating polyethylene (PE) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) substrates with sulfonated poly(arylene thioether sulfone) (SPATS). Compared with the pristine SPATS membrane, the composites showed improved dimensional stability and mechanical properties, approximately 2.5–2.8-fold lower hydrogen permeability, and enhanced hydrothermal stability due to suppressed swelling. In single-cell PEMWE tests, SPATS-PE and SPATS-PTFE achieved 6.60 and 7.79 A cm −2 at 1.9 V, respectively, outperforming the pristine SPATS and Nafion 212 membranes (6.07 and 5.36 A cm −2 , respectively). The composites also exhibited lower degradation rates, with SPATS-PTFE showing only 7.2% molecular weight loss. A three-cell stack using SPATS-PTFE delivered 6.14 A cm −2 at 5.7 V, corresponding to 78.8% of single-cell performance, and operated for 300 h at 2 A cm −2 . These results demonstrate the potential of the composite membrane for stack-level PEMWE applications and suggest that further optimization of cell components is needed to improve long-term durability.

title: Maltose-driven carbohydrate status and early raffinose synthesis enhance maturation efficiency in hybrid fir somatic embryogenesis
summary: Somatic embryogenesis (SE) is a critical biotechnological tool for the large-scale propagation of the Abies genus, which faces significant threats from climate change and high commercial demand. While sucrose is a first-choice energy source
content: Somatic embryogenesis (SE) is a critical biotechnological tool for the large-scale propagation of the Abies genus, which faces significant threats from climate change and high commercial demand. While sucrose is a first-choice energy source among conifers, firs often exhibit a dramatic preference for maltose. Using hybrid fir (Abies alba x numidica), we have shown an order-of-magnitude higher amount of mature cotyledonary embryos cultivated on maltose compared to sucrose. Determination of endogenous carbohydrate balance during maturation and post-maturation phases revealed fundamental difference in spectrum between sucrose (S) and maltose (M) variants, notably massive presence of hexoses in S variant and, remarkably, an earlier accumulation of raffinose in M variant, pointing to establishing a "mature" biochemical profile. After post-maturation desiccation treatment, though both variants accumulated raffinose family oligosaccharides (RFO), their proportion of in total carbohydrate content remained higher in M variant. Based on the results, we propose, that specific features of fir carbohydrate processing machinery (degradation and transport) resulted in slower but steady C and energy supply in M variant and represent the base of maltose superiority.

title: Dual quasi-bound states in the continuum enabled non-dispersive infrared gas sensing
summary: Abstract In this paper, we demonstrate a symmetry-engineered dielectric metasurface supporting dual quasi-bound states in the continuum (QBICs) for mid-infrared narrowband emission and non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) gas sensing. By introduc
content: Abstract In this paper, we demonstrate a symmetry-engineered dielectric metasurface supporting dual quasi-bound states in the continuum (QBICs) for mid-infrared narrowband emission and non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) gas sensing. By introducing rotational and non-centrosymmetric perturbations into an elliptical dimer, two high-Q resonances associated with symmetry-protected and Fabry–Pérot QBIC mechanisms are simultaneously realized within a single metasurface platform. The physical origins and electromagnetic characteristics of the two QBIC modes are elucidated through near-field field distributions, multipole decomposition, and coupled-mode analysis. The two modes exhibit distinct responses to symmetry perturbations, resulting in weak spectral coupling and separated control channels. Furthermore, the resonance wavelengths of both QBIC modes can be effectively tuned by globally scaling the dimensions of the elliptical dimer while maintaining high Q factors. By matching the FP-QBIC and SP-QBIC resonances to the characteristic absorption bands of CH₂O and NO₂, respectively, the proposed metasurface enables dual-channel NDIR gas sensing. This work provides a general strategy for designing multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces for infrared sensing and thermal emission applications.

title: Intra- and Intermolecular Interactions in Cellobiose: Benchmarking Accelerated Computational Methods for Cellulose
source: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
summary: Abstract Access to accelerated computational methods at the electronic and atomistic scales is important in materials modeling, as it will allow more realistic system descriptions. Against this background, a systematic study of a range of e
content: Abstract Access to accelerated computational methods at the electronic and atomistic scales is important in materials modeling, as it will allow more realistic system descriptions. Against this background, a systematic study of a range of electronic/atomistic methods applied to cellobiose monomers and dimers is presented, with the aim of identifying methods that achieve a significant acceleration of cellulose computations compared to hybrid DFT methods while retaining adequate accuracy. We benchmark such methods, namely the semiempirical quantum-mechanical tight-binding GFNn-xTB (n = 1,2) and G-xTB methods, the MACE-OMol-0 machine-learning potential, and the CHARMM36 force field, against three DFT references (ωB97M-V, B3LYP-D3, PBE-D3) for gas-phase cellobiose monomers and dimers, focusing on structures, energies, and vibrational properties. Cellobiose monomers and dimers, as presented in this work, do not represent the structural complexity of cellulose, but they provide tractable structural models for assessing the qualities of the selected computational models regarding cellobiose–cellobiose intermolecular interactions that are also present in cellulose. We find that (i) the chain–chain and sheet–sheet dimer interactions are of comparable magnitude, suggesting that both intermolecular dispersion and hydrogen bonding make important contributions to dimer stability, so accurate treatment of noncovalent interactions the calculations is essential; (ii) GFN2-xTB and G-xTB reproduce most conformations well, with a speed-up of two to three orders-of magnitude compared to the DFT calculations, but fail for puckered, strained conformations, artificially improving apparent dimer-energy agreement with DFT; (iii) MACE reaches near-DFT accuracy with a further order of magnitude speed-up, although in a few cases fails to reproduce the hybrid DFT conformations. This is especially true for the chain–chain dimer structure, which is also reflected in a significant deviation of the chain–chain energy-distance potential curve, which highlights the importance of system-dependent model validation (as was done here) and suggests a need for model fine-tuning for cellulose systems; (iv) CHARMM36 has some conformational and energetic limitations,but being 30,000× faster than G-xTB (itself orders of magnitude faster than DFT), remains practical for qualitative studies.

title: Quantum Dot‐Based Color Conversion Layers for Displays, Lighting, and Emerging Technologies
summary: Quantum dot-based color conversion layers (QD-CCLs) have emerged as key spectral-engineering platforms for next-generation optoelectronic systems, enabling precise control of light emission through efficient photon conversion. Owing to thei
content: Quantum dot-based color conversion layers (QD-CCLs) have emerged as key spectral-engineering platforms for next-generation optoelectronic systems, enabling precise control of light emission through efficient photon conversion. Owing to their high photoluminescence quantum yield, narrow emission linewidth, and size-tunable bandgaps, quantum dots (QDs) offer significant advantages over conventional phosphors for lighting and display applications. Beyond material properties, QD-CCL performance is governed by the interplay between material photophysics, optical design, and structural architecture. This review provides a unified perspective on QD-CCLs by integrating advances across QD materials (Cd-based, perovskite, and heavy-metal-free systems), device architectures, and mechanically deformable platforms. Particular emphasis is placed on optical management strategies that control photon absorption, reabsorption, and light extraction, as well as structural approaches that enhance conversion efficiency and suppress excitation-light leakage. Emerging design considerations in flexible and stretchable systems are also discussed, highlighting the coupling between mechanical deformation and optical performance. Beyond conventional lighting and displays, QD-CCLs are further explored as functional photonic interfaces in applications such as visible light communication and human-machine interfaces. By bridging materials, optics, and device engineering, this review establishes a design framework for QD-CCLs and outlines future directions toward multifunctional photonic systems.

title: Design of Compact Energy-Efficient Ternary SRAM Cells
summary: This chapter presents the design and evaluation of compact, energy-efficient ternary static random-access memory (SRAM) cells using carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNFETs), focusing on their application in modern Internet of Thing
content: This chapter presents the design and evaluation of compact, energy-efficient ternary static random-access memory (SRAM) cells using carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNFETs), focusing on their application in modern Internet of Things (IoT) and embedded systems. Ternary logic offers a promising alternative to traditional binary logic by reducing circuit complexity and power consumption. Four different ternary SRAM architectures (TSRAM0–TSRAM4) are explored, with emphasis on read-disturb-free operation, delay reduction, and improved power-delay product (PDP). The designs are implemented and simulated using the Stanford 32nm CNFET model in the High Performance Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (HSPICE) environment. Analytical models are presented to evaluate power and current characteristics. Among all the designs, TSRAM4 demonstrates superior performance in terms of reduced delay, low PDP, and better thermal stability. Static and dynamic noise margins, as well as device-level parameters like carbon nanotube (CNT) count and channel length, are analyzed to confirm the robustness of the proposed architectures. The results suggest that CNFET-based ternary SRAMs, particularly TSRAM4, are strong candidates for future low-power, high-performance memory solutions in nanoscale very large-scale integration (VLSI) systems.

title: A magnetic supramolecular solvent microextraction strategy for sensitive HPLC determination of triazoles in fruits and vegetables
source: Journal of Food Composition and Analysis
summary: In this study, a green, and rapid sample preparation method based on magnetic supramolecular solvent microextraction (M-SUPRA) was developed for the preconcentration and high-sensitivity determination of trace triazole residues in fruit and
content: In this study, a green, and rapid sample preparation method based on magnetic supramolecular solvent microextraction (M-SUPRA) was developed for the preconcentration and high-sensitivity determination of trace triazole residues in fruit and vegetable matrices prior to high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis. The magnetic supramolecular solvent was synthesized via the self-assembly of amphiphilic coacervates integrated with functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (Fe 3 O 4 ). This system offers multi-interaction binding sites (hydrophobic, hydrogen bonding, and π − π interactions) and enables rapid phase separation via an external magnetic field without requiring high-speed centrifugation or toxic organic dispersants. Key experimental parameters affecting extraction efficiency, including M-SUPRA composition, solvent volume, sample pH, ionic strength, and extraction time, were systematically optimized. Under optimal conditions, the method exhibited excellent linearity with coefficients of determination (R 2 > 0.99). The limits of detection (LODs) and limits of quantitation (LOQs) ranged from 1.0 µg L –1 to 7.0 µg L –1 and 3.0 µg L –1 to 20.0 µg L –1 , respectively, with high enrichment factors (4 – 57). The proposed M-SUPRAS-ME protocol provides a sustainable, highly sensitive, and practical tool for routine monitoring of pesticide residues in complex food matrices. Additionally, the environmental impact and analytical practicality of the developed method were evaluated.

title: Synthesis of a Polyaniline-Modified Magnetic Zn/Fe Bimetallic Sludge Biochar for Aqueous Cr(VI) Adsorption
summary: Heavy metals are recognized as a growing environmental concern due to their toxicity and long-term stability. In this study, a magnetic composite biochar material (PDFMB) was synthesized using iron-based sludge and Chinese medicine residue,
content: Heavy metals are recognized as a growing environmental concern due to their toxicity and long-term stability. In this study, a magnetic composite biochar material (PDFMB) was synthesized using iron-based sludge and Chinese medicine residue, with zinc chloride and polyaniline serving as modifiers, to adsorb and reduce Cr(VI) in water. The optimal preparation conditions were determined through preliminary experiments, and the adsorption performance was evaluated through material characterization and Cr(VI) adsorption tests. The removal of Cr(VI) by PDFMB was highly pH-dependent, with an optimal pH of 2, indicating that acidic conditions favored adsorption. The maximum adsorption capacity for Cr(VI) at 308 K and pH 5 was 111.11 mg/g. The adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model, while the Langmuir isotherm provided a good fit to the adsorption isotherm data. Thermodynamic analysis revealed that the removal process was spontaneous and endothermic. The anions Cl‒, SO42‒, and PO43‒ inhibited the removal efficiency of Cr(VI), with inhibition strength following the order Cl‒ < SO42‒ < PO43‒. The key mechanisms involved in Cr(VI) removal included physical and chemical adsorption, chelation, and the reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III). The PDFMB composite exhibited high stability and reusability, achieving an 85.25% removal efficiency after six cycles. Owing to its high efficiency, magnetic separability, and excellent recyclability, PDFMB represents a highly promising candidate for addressing Cr(VI) pollution.

title: Optical Absorption and Exciton Dispersion of Bulk Corrugated g-C3N4
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
summary: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is a promising layered metal-free photocatalyst whose optical properties are strongly affected by structural corrugation induced by nitrogen lone-pair repulsion. However, calculations for the bulk
content: Abstract Graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) is a promising layered metal-free photocatalyst whose optical properties are strongly affected by structural corrugation induced by nitrogen lone-pair repulsion. However, calculations for the bulk have largely focused on the ideal planar structure. Here, we investigate the structural, electronic, and excitonic properties of corrugated bulk g-C3N4 using density functional theory, many-body perturbation theory, and the Bethe–Salpeter equation. The absorption spectrum is dominated by bound excitons below the quasiparticle gap, with the first bright exciton at 2.75 eV (dark in the ideal flat structure) in good agreement with experiment. Bulk excitons arise from symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of monolayer excitations mixed by interlayer hopping, leading to a Davydov splitting and to states with mixed Frenkel and charge-transfer character. Their bandwidths are only a few to a few tens of meV, indicating inefficient exciton propagation both in-plane and out-of-plane.

title: Effect of a PCE-based superplasticizer on the viscoelastic stiffness of a cement paste: contrasting fresh-state and early-age behavior
summary: Abstract The impact of a polycarboxylate ether-based superplasticizer (SP) on the viscoelastic stiffness of a cement paste at an early age is examined. Ordinary Portland cement, free of tricalcium aluminate is used, and pastes prepared with
content: Abstract The impact of a polycarboxylate ether-based superplasticizer (SP) on the viscoelastic stiffness of a cement paste at an early age is examined. Ordinary Portland cement, free of tricalcium aluminate is used, and pastes prepared with and without SP are characterized with isothermal calorimetry, small-amplitude oscillatory shear rheology, and hourly three-minute creep testing. Isothermal calorimetry enables an indirect estimation of the paste hydration degree as a function of its age. The stiffness moduli, quantified from rheology and creep tests on the pastes with and without SP, are compared as a function of the hydration degree. In the fresh state, at hydration degrees below 1 %, rheology shows that the paste containing SP is less stiff than the paste without. In the hardened state, the trend is reverse and the paste with SP exhibits higher elastic and creep moduli. A discussion follows, that proposes an interpretation based on a schematic representation of the microstructure derived from the Powers-Acker hydration model, and literature. We argue that the dispersing ability of the SP, well known to induce a more evenly distributed network of particles in the fresh cement state, persists in the hardened paste. The hypothetical finer microstructure, with a finer pore distribution, in the hardened paste containing SP, tentatively explains the higher moduli measured, and clarifies the apparently inconsistent mechanical behavior of the cement pastes prepared with and without a superplasticizer.

title: Preparation of Lithium‐Ion Conducting Organic–Inorganic Polymer Hybrids via Reversible Addition‐Fragmentation Chain Transfer Polymerization and Sol–Gel Reaction
summary: ABSTRACT This study focuses on the preparation of hybrid polymer electrolyte films containing metal ions via a non‐aqueous sol–gel reaction of a vinyl polymer with terminal phosphonic acid moieties and metal alkoxides. Poly(poly[ethylene gl
content: ABSTRACT This study focuses on the preparation of hybrid polymer electrolyte films containing metal ions via a non‐aqueous sol–gel reaction of a vinyl polymer with terminal phosphonic acid moieties and metal alkoxides. Poly(poly[ethylene glycol]methyl ether methacrylate‐ co ‐4‐vinylphenylboronic acid 1,3‐propanediol ester) (poly(PEGMA‐ co ‐VPBP)) with a weight‐average molar mass of 5800 and a dispersity of 1.19 was synthesized by reversible addition‐fragmentation chain transfer polymerization using 2,2′‐azobis(isobutyronitrile) and S,S′ ‐bis(2‐ethylphosphonic acid)trithiocarbonate. MOP hybrid electrolyte films (M = metal or metalloid) containing Ti, B, Al, and Nb atoms were prepared using poly(PEGMA‐ co ‐VPBP), metal alkoxides or boron alkoxide, and lithium perchlorate. The ionic conductivities are in the order of NbOP > AlOP > BOP > TiOP at 20°C, and the NbOP hybrid electrolyte film shows an especially high ionic conductivity of 4.9 × 10 −4 mS/cm at 20°C. BOP hybrid electrolyte shows the highest conductivity of 3.0 × 10 −2 mS/cm at 40°C and the highest activation energy from the Arrhenius plots.

title: Organomineral fertilization with sewage sludge on the production and nutrient accumulation in Urochloa brizantha cv. Paiaguás
summary: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of sewage-sludge-based organomineral fertilizers, produced using different technologies, as a sustainable alternative to mineral fertilization for biomass production and nutrient accumulation in Uro
content: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of sewage-sludge-based organomineral fertilizers, produced using different technologies, as a sustainable alternative to mineral fertilization for biomass production and nutrient accumulation in Urochloa brizantha cv. BRS Paiaguás. The experiment was conducted for 120 days in a greenhouse under a randomized block design with four replicates. Treatments included mineral fertilizer (NPK), granulated biochar (GB), powdered biochar (PB), granulated composted sludge (GS), powdered composted sludge (PS), and a control (Test) without fertilization. After 120 days, granulated biochar and mineral fertilizer promoted the highest dry matter production and Mg and Ca accumulation in the uniformity cut. The unfertilized treatment did not reach 40 cm in height and therefore did not allow biomass harvesting. The granulated biochar increased P accumulation in shoots by 49% (1.48 mg plant −1 ) compared with mineral fertilizer. Root dry weight ranged from 8.28 to 13.42 g plant −1 across the fertilized treatments; no significant differences were observed between organomineral and mineral fertilizers. The GB treatment showed a total P accumulation of 5.92 mg plant −1 , close to NPK (6.20 mg plant −1 ) and 37.8% higher than the average of the other organomineral fertilizers. Furthermore, the GB and NPK treatments exhibited the highest total accumulations of N (62.90 and 70.56 mg plant −1 ), Mg (21.22 and 21.01 mg plant −1 ), and S (29.38 and 38.75 mg plant −1 ). GB fertilization increased CEC compared to mineral fertilization (NPK) and the control treatment, although the highest values were observed in the sludge-based organomineral treatments (GS and PS). These changes, linked to increased organic matter, helped reduce potential acidity and aluminum toxicity, thereby improving nutrient availability and plant uptake. Overall, the granulated sewage-sludge biochar outperformed the other organomineral formulations and represents a promising and sustainable strategy to enhance U. brizantha productivity and improve the fertility of tropical soils.

title: Temperature and precipitation extremes in the Brazilian Legal Amazon: projections under SSP5-8.5 scenario
source: Journal of Southern Hemisphere Earth System Science
summary: This study aims to investigate the projections of air temperature and precipitation climate extremes in the Brazilian Legal Amazon (BLA) through the end of the century. The Brazilian Daily Weather Gridded Data dataset is used to characteris
content: This study aims to investigate the projections of air temperature and precipitation climate extremes in the Brazilian Legal Amazon (BLA) through the end of the century. The Brazilian Daily Weather Gridded Data dataset is used to characterise the present climate, and 12 models from the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6), under the Shared Socioeconomic Pathways scenario SSP5-8.5, are employed to assess future changes relative to the reference period (1995–2014). Student’s t-test is employed to evaluate the robustness of the projected changes. Results show that warming is projected to persist throughout the BLA, but at a lower rate in the north-east (NE) than in other areas. In the south (S) and north-western (NW) sectors, the highest maximum temperatures will increase by an average of 7°C by the end of the century. Regarding precipitation extremes, in the NW, which is currently the wettest portion of the BLA, models project a reduction in consecutive wet days (CWDs) and an increase in the amount of daily rainfall that exceeds the 95th percentile of wet days (R95p). In the NE, by the end of the century, a 30-day increase in the total number of consecutive dry days per year (CDDs) is projected, combined with a reduction in annual rainfall of ~270 mm. In the south of the BLA, models project an increase across the entire sector, with an additional 15 days per year, along with a reduction in annual rainfall. The projected changes in precipitation exhibit strong seasonality, concentrating primarily in the transitional seasons and the beginning of the rainy season, rather than occurring uniformly throughout the year. Also, the projected warming intensifies during the dry season and austral spring, especially in the NW region. In this sense, it is observed that, in the future, the climate in the BLA will become warmer, keeping the trends observed in the present climate, as shown in other previous studies. However, rainfall patterns differ between regions: while in the NE and S the climate will become drier, in the NW, the intensity of extreme rainfall is expected to increase significantly by the end of the century.

title: Primary vitamin B 12 limitation and widespread stress in Antarctic phytoplankton
summary: Iron is considered the dominant limiting or colimiting nutrient for phytoplankton growth in the Southern Ocean. However, strong competition and limited biosynthesis capabilities for vitamin B 12 (cobalamin) within the microbial community cr
content: Iron is considered the dominant limiting or colimiting nutrient for phytoplankton growth in the Southern Ocean. However, strong competition and limited biosynthesis capabilities for vitamin B 12 (cobalamin) within the microbial community creates conditions suitable for cobalamin limitation. Through a nutrient enrichment experiment in the Amundsen Sea, we show that growth in a phytoplankton community comprising diatoms and prasinophytes was limited primarily by cobalamin and secondarily by iron. Protein biomarkers across a broad area of the Southern Ocean further indicate widespread cobalamin stress within diatoms and Phaeocystis . As warming-induced melting of ice-shelves increases iron supplies in the coastal Southern Ocean, shifts from iron to cobalamin limitation favor mixotrophic flagellates with low cobalamin requirements, altering community composition and function.

title: Climate change, air pollution, and pediatric health: Emerging evidence on respiratory disease, neurodevelopment, and childhood vulnerability
source: IP Journal of Paediatrics and Nursing Science
summary: Climate change and air pollution are both interrelated environmental factors that pose health risks to children with potential lifelong impacts on respiratory health, neurodevelopment, and wellbeing. Children are especially vulnerable due t
content: Climate change and air pollution are both interrelated environmental factors that pose health risks to children with potential lifelong impacts on respiratory health, neurodevelopment, and wellbeing. Children are especially vulnerable due to their immature organ systems, increased breathing rates compared to their body weights, and dependence on environmental quality established by the households, schools, and communities they belong to. Increased temperature, wildfires, a change in aeroallergens' distribution, and extreme weather events can increase the exposure to particulates and ozone and other forms of pollution. Exposures to such factors lead to respiratory infections, asthma exacerbations, poor lung development, and negative impacts on neurodevelopment. This risk is borne primarily by socioeconomically disadvantaged children, especially those from dense urban environments and low- and middle-income countries. While the connection between air pollution and respiratory disease is well-established, many questions about the effects of co-exposures to different environmental factors, vulnerable developmental periods, and long-term health outcomes remain unresolved. This literature review explores the connections between climate change, air pollution, respiratory disease, and childhood neurodevelopment. There will be specific emphasis on biological vulnerabilities, social disparities, and prevention strategies. Environmental health surveillance combined with pediatric care and public health policy could possibly decrease preventable childhood diseases.

title: Electric‐Field‐Assisted Spin Coating: A New Process for Adjusting Crystallization of Perovskite Thin Films
summary: ABSTRACT Electric‐field‐assisted spin coating is introduced as a vectorial wet‐film processing strategy for influencing methylammonium lead iodide () crystallization during hydrodynamic thinning and solvent evaporation. films were deposited
content: ABSTRACT Electric‐field‐assisted spin coating is introduced as a vectorial wet‐film processing strategy for influencing methylammonium lead iodide () crystallization during hydrodynamic thinning and solvent evaporation. films were deposited onto grounded substrates under perpendicular electric fields of 0–8 kV . The field was applied during a 25 s spin‐coating/antisolvent interval and removed before annealing. X‐ray diffraction (XRD) identified tetragonal as the dominant phase and field‐dependent changes in texture, peak displacement, microstrain, and coherent domain size were observed. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed grain coarsening, as the mean grain diameter increased from 128.8 nm for the 0 kV condition to 303.9 nm at 2 kV . The largest ‐family texture enhancement and low‐angle peak displacement occurred at 6 kV , while coherent‐domain size increased monotonically across the field‐assisted series, reaching 190.5 nm at 8 kV . A 2 kV specimen exhibited pronounced out‐of‐plane texture, showing that the deposition platform can access a strong texture‐selection pathway. These results show that an electric field applied during spin casting acts as a charge‐selective perturbation involving a vector force, and decouples grain growth, orientation, lattice displacement, and crystallographic coherence during film formation.

title: Formulation‐Driven Design of Antimicrobial Hydrogel Wound Patches 3D‐Printed by Digital Light Processing: Mapping Polysaccharide and Nanoparticle Effects
summary: ABSTRACT Wound dressings must balance antimicrobial efficacy with the printability limits imposed by nanoparticle‐mediated ultraviolet attenuation during digital light processing 3D printing. Here, we develop process–structure–property rela
content: ABSTRACT Wound dressings must balance antimicrobial efficacy with the printability limits imposed by nanoparticle‐mediated ultraviolet attenuation during digital light processing 3D printing. Here, we develop process–structure–property relationships for poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA)‐based hydrogel wound patches containing Ag/ZnO‐derived antimicrobial phases and polysaccharide/cellulose modifiers (cellulose nanofibrils, chitosan, or alginate). Beer–Lambert analysis shows that nanoparticle loading reduces optical penetration depth at 405 nm to 1.04‐1.28 mm, narrowing the usable curing margin so that radiant exposure exceeds the critical energy by only 4%–5%. Flory–Rehner analysis of swelling reveals formulation‐dependent crosslink density: alginate lowers effective crosslink density by 45% vs. neat PEGDA and increases mesh size from 0.42 to 0.60 nm. This network loosening drives 1.5× variation in water vapor transmission rate (WVTR; 346–518 g·m − 2 ·day − 1 ) and a 7× range in wettability (11.5°–81.1°). Two‐way factorial analysis identifies polysaccharide type as the dominant driver of swelling (87.5% of variance) and antimicrobial efficacy (>50%), while nanoparticle type controls contact angle (60.1%) and WVTR (76.9%). The Ag + chitosan formulation (S5) achieves 23–24 mm inhibition zones against Escherichia coli and Bacillus sp. via chitosan‐facilitated Ag + diffusion plus intrinsic contact‐killing. Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy confirms cumulative Ag + release (32.7 mg·L − 1 over 14 days), while Zn 2 + remains immobilized below detection.

title: Direct Photocatalytic Conversion of Ethylene and Water Into Butanol via C─C Coupling and Hydroxylation
summary: ABSTRACT Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long‐chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling
content: ABSTRACT Direct photocatalytic upgrading of olefins into long‐chain oxygenates using water as the sole oxygen and hydrogen source is highly attractive, yet remains challenging due to the difficulty of integrating intermolecular C─C coupling with selective hydroxylation. Herein, we report a photocatalytic pathway for the direct synthesis of n ‐butanol from ethylene and water over an in situ‐constructed Pt@Cu core–shell cocatalyst supported on TiO 2 . Under illumination, water is dissociated to generate surface *H and *OH species, which are synchronously incorporated into two activated ethylene molecules, while the remaining carbon centers undergo intermolecular C─C coupling to construct the C 4 backbone, enabling one‐step formation of n ‐butanol. The Pt core promotes directional electron extraction from TiO 2 and continuously enriches the surrounding Cu shell with electrons, thereby facilitating both ethylene activation and water dissociation. Meanwhile, dissolved Cu 2+ dynamically regulates the surface Cu redox state and preserves a Cu(I)‐rich active surface during photocatalysis. As a result, the Pt@Cu core–shell catalyst in Cu 2+ solution achieves a C 4 oxygenate production rate of 749.9 µmol g −1 h −1 with selectivity of 63.3%. This work establishes a photocatalytic strategy integrating C─C coupling and hydroxylation for solar‐driven synthesis of long‐chain oxygenates from olefins and water.

title: Bypassing thermodynamic immiscibility via electrochemical kinetic atom trapping
summary: Abstract Immiscible elemental pairs can access properties unavailable to equilibrium solid solutions, but conventional synthesis approaches suffer from phase separation and heterogeneity. Here, we establish kinetic atom trapping using ultra
content: Abstract Immiscible elemental pairs can access properties unavailable to equilibrium solid solutions, but conventional synthesis approaches suffer from phase separation and heterogeneity. Here, we establish kinetic atom trapping using ultramicroelectrodes, confining metal-ion reduction to a finite interfacial inventory. Ultrahigh-, ultrashort-current pulses deplete the preferentially reduced ion before radial diffusion replenishes the interface, forcing dissimilar ions to reduce concurrently and kinetically trapping and stabilizing homogeneous immiscible nanoalloys. The strategy produces mixed nanoparticles across diverse atomic combinations, such as Cu–Zn, Cu–Ag, Cu–Fe, Fe–Cr, and Cu–Ni systems. A quantitative pulse window, bounded by Sand’s depletion time and radial-diffusion-mediated replenishment, predicts the current density and pulse duration required for co-reduction. These mechanistic design rules establish a route to metastable immiscible alloys and enable automated exploration of non-equilibrium compositions and properties.

title: Multilabel Corrosion Morphology Classification Using Deep Learning with Multimodality Fusion
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of corrosion morphology is critical for understanding degradation mechanisms and supporting predictive maintenance. Corrosion images often exhibit multiple coexisting morphologies, making single-label clas
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of corrosion morphology is critical for understanding degradation mechanisms and supporting predictive maintenance. Corrosion images often exhibit multiple coexisting morphologies, making single-label classification inadequate. This study presents a multilabel classification framework using ResNet-18, Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP), and Swin Transformer (Swin-T), with environmental and experimental metadata incorporated through multimodal fusion. A detailed experimental evaluation examines model architecture and training configurations. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that classweighted loss functions are critical for enabling metadata fusion and improving macroF1 performance for minority labels. Transformerbased and visionlanguage models exhibit strong adaptability to complex corrosion patterns. Ablation studies further quantify the effects of input modality, loss weighting, training epochs, and batch size. The results establish a benchmark for multilabel corrosion morphology classification and highlight the importance of lossfunction design in multimodal learning.

title: The impacts of climate change on OHS: Status report and proposed actions
summary: This narrative review describes the multidimensional impacts of climate change (CC) on occupational health and safety (OHS), with a focus on the North American and European contexts. The rise in the average global temperature, which is now
content: This narrative review describes the multidimensional impacts of climate change (CC) on occupational health and safety (OHS), with a focus on the North American and European contexts. The rise in the average global temperature, which is now 1.2 °C higher than during the pre-industrial era, is transforming working conditions and exacerbating existing occupational hazards. The heat stress induced by excessive heat causes pathologies ranging from exhaustion to fatal heatstroke, while also lowering vigilance and increasing the risk of traumatic injury. Beyond the physical harms, CC increases the psychosocial risks, leading to eco-anxiety, psychological distress and a decline in workers’ emotional well-being. The intensification of extreme weather events, such as flooding, intense heat waves and forest fires, threatens the health and safety of first responders and leads to major economic losses in primary sectors (e.g., agriculture, livestock farming, forestry) by reducing revenues, weakening the viability of farming operations and lowering workforce productivity. At the same time, global warming promotes the geographic expansion of biological vectors, thus increasing the incidence of illnesses such as Lyme disease or a West Nile virus infection. The deterioration in air quality, marked by an increase in tropospheric ozone and fine particles, increases the risk of cardiopulmonary disorders and cancers. Likewise, increased exposure to solar UV radiation has been identified as a major cause of skin cancer in outdoor workers.

title: Photoconversion Behavior of a ZnO/Graphite Solar Cell
summary: Abstract This work assembled dye solar cells by replacing platinum with graphite on indium tin oxide (ITO). First, the device was tested only on the ITO; afterward, graphite was placed on the ITO and evaluated as a counter electrode in the
content: Abstract This work assembled dye solar cells by replacing platinum with graphite on indium tin oxide (ITO). First, the device was tested only on the ITO; afterward, graphite was placed on the ITO and evaluated as a counter electrode in the cell. The results showed that the presence of graphite increased the incident photocurrent conversion (IPCE) of the cell. The electrode used was a combination of zinc oxide with 4% bismuth, and characterization of the film had high reflectance in the visible region, a thickness of around 1.47 μm, and a crystallite size of around 38.5 nm. The addition of graphite as a counter electrode increased the cell efficiency by 10 times, driven by an increase in current density from 0.02 to 1.2 mA/cm and in IPCE from 0.04 to 2.26%.

title: Optimal co-planning of hybrid energy hubs and integrated electricity-hydrogen transmission infrastructure
summary: Clusters of large-scale renewable energy projects, also known as renewable energy zones (REZs), are essential elements in the transition to net zero. Hybrid energy hubs (HEHs), which incorporate other energy vectors such as green hydrogen (
content: Clusters of large-scale renewable energy projects, also known as renewable energy zones (REZs), are essential elements in the transition to net zero. Hybrid energy hubs (HEHs), which incorporate other energy vectors such as green hydrogen (H 2 ) into REZs, can further leverage economies of scale and diversity in electricity and H 2 production and demand to reduce the required capacity of connection assets and decrease overall operational and capital costs. This paper introduces a general, optimization-based framework for the co-planning of HEHs and integrated electricity and H 2 systems (IEHS), aiming to find the least-cost designs of HEHs, along with the electricity and H 2 transmission infrastructure required to connect them to the main grid. This framework features a modular HEH model that enables flexible technology selection and sizing without a predefined hub configuration, while minimizing the capacity of shared connection assets. Comprehensive case studies on the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM) that integrate HEH and system-level planning compare investment strategies between independent connection configurations and shared connection configurations within HEHs. The findings show that integrating HEHs with optimized shared connection assets into IEHS planning can not only displace investments in both electricity and H 2 transmission infrastructure, but also reduce renewable energy curtailment and enhance the utilization of existing and new assets. Moreover, although including H 2 transmission development can reduce system costs, HEHs with shared connection assets alone may provide greater cost reductions as an alternative investment strategy, enough to avoid all the uncertainty associated with building a new H 2 pipeline network.

title: Energy Audit of Building Systems
summary: Energy Audit of Building Systems: An Engineering Approach , Fourth Edition addresses the critical intersection between energy efficiency and building performance optimization. It provides specialized knowledge and systematic approaches need
content: Energy Audit of Building Systems: An Engineering Approach , Fourth Edition addresses the critical intersection between energy efficiency and building performance optimization. It provides specialized knowledge and systematic approaches needed to evaluate existing buildings while achieving maximum energy savings and carbon-neutral operation. The new edition expands coverage to include dynamic and demand response technologies such as switchable glazing systems, phase change materials, and photovoltaic (PV)-integrated shading devices. It also includes a new chapter covering proven systems and effective analysis approaches for electrifying existing buildings. Enhanced problem sets and case studies provide practical applications for both residential and commercial building retrofits. This book will benefit building energy auditors; heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) engineers; architects; facility managers; and advanced undergraduate students seeking specialized training in building energy management. Instructors will be able to utilize an online Solutions Manual for their course.

title: Dual-modal sensor for dopamine detection based on In 2 O 3 @FeMoSe 2 heterojunctions with excellent photoelectrochemical and peroxidase-like properties
summary: Abstract In this work, the indium oxide and iron molybdenum selenide (In 2 O 3 @FeMoSe 2 ) heterojunctions were synthesized using a simple hydrothermal method. The morphological and structural properties of the obtained heterojunctions were
content: Abstract In this work, the indium oxide and iron molybdenum selenide (In 2 O 3 @FeMoSe 2 ) heterojunctions were synthesized using a simple hydrothermal method. The morphological and structural properties of the obtained heterojunctions were comprehensively characterized. In-situ functionalization of the hierarchical micro-flowers of FeMoSe 2 with In 2 O 3 nanoparticles dramatically boosts electrical conductivity, photocatalytic activity and peroxidase-like activity. Benefiting from the band gap matching of In 2 O 3 and FeMoSe 2 , and dopamine (DA) as electron donors, and realizing photocurrent signals amplification. In the presence of H 2 O 2 , In 2 O 3 @FeMoSe 2 catalyzes the oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylhydrogen dioxide (TMB) to a blue product. DA capture hydroxyl radicals, thereby inhibiting the oxidation of TMB, which leads to a lighter blue color and a subsequent decrease in absorbance. Here, a photoelectrochemical and colorimetric dual-mode sensor for dopamine assay based on In 2 O 3 @FeMoSe 2 was constructed. The detection limits were 14.7 nM and 0.19 µM (S/N = 3), respectively. The sensor was successfully applied to the detection of dopamine (DA) in human serum and urine samples, exhibiting high sensitivity, excellent reproducibility, and reliable stability. To the best of our knowledge, this strategy for DA detection has not been previously reported.

title: Abnormal Increase in Thermal Diffusivity of Lignin-Based Carbon Fibers during Vacuum Exposure
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract Vacuum generally suppresses gaseous heat conduction without altering intrinsic transport of solid materials. Here we report an unexpected, time-dependent increase in thermal diffusivity (α) of lignin-based carbon fibers (CFs) durin
content: Abstract Vacuum generally suppresses gaseous heat conduction without altering intrinsic transport of solid materials. Here we report an unexpected, time-dependent increase in thermal diffusivity (α) of lignin-based carbon fibers (CFs) during vacuum exposure. At <0.08 Pa, α increases by up to ∼95% and approaches saturation, while its electrical resistance (R) shows smaller, condition-dependent changes. After ∼16 h of air re-exposure, α partially or nearly fully recovers, while R responds less consistently, demonstrating strong dependence on exposure history. Across the vacuum systems examined, the α increase diminishes as vacuum pressure rises from <0.08 to 2.13 Pa, whereas a moderate temperature rise (∼50 K) accelerates the evolution of the α increase under ∼0.21 Pa vacuum. Laser-power-normalized Raman intensities increase during air re-exposure without significant D- or G-band shifts, providing indirect evidence of reversible near-surface-state evolution rather than restructuring of the carbon framework. Atomistic simulations show that adsorbed water shortens acoustic phonon lifetimes and suppresses in-plane thermal transport. These results support vacuum-induced desorption of near-surface adsorbates as reducing phonon scattering and increasing α, as there is negligible change in volumetric heat capacity. Removal of humidity-assisted charge-transport pathways may also contribute to the increase in R observed in some sequences. It is concluded that the exposure history is an important factor in thermal and electrical measurements of carbon fibers under vacuum.

title: Sustainable AC/ZIF-67 hybrid adsorbents derived from agricultural waste for rapid dye removal from water
summary: Activated carbon (AC) derived from a mixture of walnut and almond shells was prepared via phosphoric acid activation (ACA) and subsequently combined with ZIF-67 to fabricate a series of ACA/ZIF-67 composite adsorbents for removing dye conta
