content: Activated carbon (AC) derived from a mixture of walnut and almond shells was prepared via phosphoric acid activation (ACA) and subsequently combined with ZIF-67 to fabricate a series of ACA/ZIF-67 composite adsorbents for removing dye contaminants from water. Comprehensive characterization (including FESEM, EDS, FTIR, XRD, and N 2 adsorption–desorption) confirmed the integration of ZIF-67 within the carbon matrix. The results demonstrated that the highest BET surface area (592.43 m 2 . g − 1 ) belongs to the ACA5/ZIF-67 composite with a hierarchical porous structure. The effects of operational parameters, including ACA/ZIF-67 ratio, pH (1–11), amount of adsorbent (0.1–2 g/L), time (5–60 min), initial dye concentration (10–100 mg/L), and operational temperature (25–45 °C), were systematically investigated. Under the optimum conditions of pH 7, temperature of 25 °C, and the amount of adsorbent 1.5 g/L, the ACA5/ZIF-67 composite achieved more than 98% removal of 10 mg/L MB within only 5 min. Equilibrium and kinetic data were satisfactorily well-fitted to the Langmuir isotherm (R² > 0.99) and the pseudo-second-order kinetic (R 2 = 0.9999) models, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of 35.95 mg/g. This adsorption behavior can be attributed to the combined effects of pore filling, electrostatic attraction, π–π interactions, and hydrogen bonding between dye molecules and the ACA5/ZIF-67 surface. Consequently, these outcomes highlight the potential of biomass-derived AC/ZIF-67 composites as favorable adsorbents for the simulated removal of dyes from aqueous solutions, subject to further assessment in real industrial effluents.

title: Heat stress along the 2026 Tour de France: a spatiotemporal reconstruction of exposure across race stages
summary: Abstract Anthropogenic climate change is amplifying the intensity and frequency of extreme summer heat across Europe, posing critical thermal challenges for major outdoor endurance events. However, existing sports heat protocols typically r
content: Abstract Anthropogenic climate change is amplifying the intensity and frequency of extreme summer heat across Europe, posing critical thermal challenges for major outdoor endurance events. However, existing sports heat protocols typically rely on static weather measurements, failing to capture the microclimatic variability encountered by a moving event. Here, we present a high-resolution spatiotemporal reconstruction of environmental heat stress across all 21 stages (~ 3,323 km) of the 2026 Tour de France. By integrating ERA5 reanalysis and WRF mesoscale modeling (~ 1 km resolution) corrected with ground station networks, modeled the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI) and the Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) paired with estimated peloton passage times. Strong to very strong heat stress (UTCI ≥ 32°C) accounted for 60.5% (2,009 km) of the total route distance and 57.8% (2,991 min) of estimated riding time, peaking at 44.5°C in Stage 4. Although no segment exceeded the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) threshold for stage suspension (WBGT ≥ 32.2°C), 175.9 km fell within high-risk Red band conditions (WBGT ≥ 28°C). This index divergence reveals that while dynamic athlete movement can mitigate immediate regulatory breaches, static roadside spectators endure prolonged exposure under dangerous radiant loads. These findings underscore the need for mobile, spatiotemporally resolved biometeorological frameworks in sports safety protocols and event scheduling.

title: Plant autoinhibited Ca2+-ATPases: shaping calcium signals for growth, stress adaptation, and crop improvement
summary: P-type ATPases are conserved ATP-driven ion transporters that maintain cellular ion homeostasis. Plant P-type IIB Ca 2+ -ATPases, known as autoinhibited Ca 2+ -ATPases (ACAs), are key regulators of Ca 2+ signaling networks. This review summ
content: P-type ATPases are conserved ATP-driven ion transporters that maintain cellular ion homeostasis. Plant P-type IIB Ca 2+ -ATPases, known as autoinhibited Ca 2+ -ATPases (ACAs), are key regulators of Ca 2+ signaling networks. This review summarizes the structural features, Ca 2+ /calmodulin-dependent regulation, evolutionary diversification, and biological functions of plant ACAs. By contributing to cytosolic Ca 2+ clearance and the restoration of basal Ca 2+ levels, ACAs may modulate stimulus-specific Ca 2+ dynamics and participate in diverse physiological processes, including plant growth, development, stomatal movement, immunity, and abiotic stress adaptation. Comparative analyses across plant species highlight functional specialization of ACA isoforms and their potential value for crop improvement. We further discuss current challenges in ACA functional characterization, particularly the complexity of Ca 2+ signaling networks and the limited understanding of ACA-associated genetic variation. Emerging approaches integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and precision genome editing provide new opportunities for identifying and designing ACA alleles for climate-resilient crop breeding.

title: The Impact of Vinylene Carbonate and Fluoroethylene Carbonate Mixtures in Lithium-Ion Pouch Cells with Chemically Synthesized Silicon-Carbon Containing Graphite Composite Negative Electrodes
summary: Abstract Silicon-containing lithium-ion cells provide higher energy density than cells with only graphite in the negative electrode. This paper investigated the impact of vinylene carbonate (VC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) on the per
content: Abstract Silicon-containing lithium-ion cells provide higher energy density than cells with only graphite in the negative electrode. This paper investigated the impact of vinylene carbonate (VC) and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) on the performance of lithium-ion pouch cells with NMC-type positive electrodes (Ni83-type and Ni65-type) and 20 % chemical silicon-carbon (chemical SiC) in their negative electrode. The additive blends consisted of 2 wt. % VC with either 0, 4, or 10 wt. % FEC. Insitu volume measurements were carried out to study the impact of additives on gas volume produced during the formation step. Long-term cycling tests at 40 °C and 55 °C, and storage experiments at 60 °C, were conducted to investigate the effect of the additives on cell performance. Post-cycle analyses were conducted on cells using impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The results demonstrate that 2 wt % VC is an effective additive to improve cell performance in both Ni83-type and Ni65-type pouch cells with 20 % chemical SiC. The additive blend, 2 wt % with 4 wt % FEC, shows a positive impact, however, addition of 10 wt % FEC produces minimal additional impact.

title: Plasma-assisted CO2 desorption and in situ conversion over ZSM-5 for integrated carbon capture and utilization
summary: CO 2 capture and conversion offer a promising route to reduce emissions and support a circular carbon economy. However, conventional CO 2 regeneration typically relies on temperature- or pressure-swing processes, which can limit rapid and d
content: CO 2 capture and conversion offer a promising route to reduce emissions and support a circular carbon economy. However, conventional CO 2 regeneration typically relies on temperature- or pressure-swing processes, which can limit rapid and dynamically operated capture–conversion systems. In this work, we develop an integrated CO 2 capture–desorption–conversion approach that combines low-temperature CO 2 physisorption on ZSM-5 with plasma-assisted regeneration and in situ conversion in a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) reactor. Upon plasma ignition, pre-adsorbed CO 2 was rapidly released and simultaneously converted to CO without external heating during the plasma-assisted regeneration stage. Total CO 2 desorption fractions of 81.4–85.3% were achieved, compared with approximately 40–47% during physical desorption by Ar purging alone. CO 2 desorption and conversion were strongly dependent on adsorption temperature, discharge power, and Ar flow rate. Notably, increasing discharge power promoted CO 2 desorption but reduced CO 2 conversion, whereas increasing the Ar flow rate enhanced CO 2 conversion with only a minor influence on total desorption. In situ plasma-coupled Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy revealed the formation of monodentate and bidentate carbonate species during plasma exposure. Together with the transient CO 2 and CO profiles, these observations suggest two concurrent routes for CO formation: rapid gas-phase activation of desorbed CO 2 and a possible slower surface-mediated pathway involving carbonate species. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of coupling CO 2 capture, electrically driven sorbent regeneration, and conversion within a single plasma–sorbent system, offering a flexible approach to integrated carbon capture and utilization (ICCU).

title: Wave and slope thresholds for mangrove restoration and nature-based solution design
summary: Abstract Globally, shorelines are experiencing widespread recession, promoting greater interest in nature-based solutions (NbSs) for coastal protection. Along tropical and sub-tropical coastlines, mangroves are among the habitat-forming spe
content: Abstract Globally, shorelines are experiencing widespread recession, promoting greater interest in nature-based solutions (NbSs) for coastal protection. Along tropical and sub-tropical coastlines, mangroves are among the habitat-forming species increasingly targeted for nature-based coastal protection. However, practical implementation requires tools that identify shorelines where hydrodynamic and geomorphic conditions are likely to support successful mangrove establishment and long-term persistence. This study quantifies first-order suitability envelopes (hereafter thresholds) for mangrove presence by linking wave height and bathymetric slope to observed mangrove distributions in subtropical wave-dominated barrier estuarine systems. Mangroves were most likely to be present where the 80 th percentile significant wave height ( H s ) was below 0.14 m and bathymetric slope was gentler than 0.01. Above these thresholds, the probability of mangrove occurrence decreased from approximately 23%–25% to 13%–15%, indicating strong but non-exclusive physical controls. Importantly, the probability did not decline to zero beyond these limits, suggesting that mangrove distribution is better described as a suitability threshold rather than a fixed ecological threshold. Spatial analysis indicated that approximately 26% of currently unvegetated shoreline areas in the study fell within the identified wave-slope thresholds, representing potentially suitable but unrealized mangrove habitat. These findings demonstrate that mangrove distribution is partly governed by hydrodynamic and geomorphic processes. While these potential restoration areas are identified based strictly on hydrodynamic and bathymetric thresholds, other critical drivers, such as tidal elevation, sediment supply, and salinity gradients, may further restrict suitable locations. The proposed methods of deriving thresholds in this study provide transferable, process-based criteria for identifying restoration opportunity areas and informing the design of NbSs for coastal resilience in estuarine environments.

title: Feasibility, Safety, Adherence, and Functional Outcomes of a Mobile Application-Facilitated, Unsupervised Remote Cardiac Rehabilitation Program with Exercise Intensity Optimization: A Single-Arm Clinical Trial
summary: Background/Objectives: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is essential for patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD); however, participation rates remain low because of logistical barriers. We developed a mobile application-facilitated, unsupervi
content: Background/Objectives: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is essential for patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD); however, participation rates remain low because of logistical barriers. We developed a mobile application-facilitated, unsupervised remote CR program with exercise intensity optimization and multidisciplinary support. This study aimed to evaluate its feasibility, safety, adherence, and associated changes in functional capacity among patients with CVD. Methods: This single-center, single-arm interventional study (jRCTs042230018) enrolled 30 patients with CVD who followed an unsupervised, home-based, mobile application-facilitated CR program for 5 months, with multidisciplinary video counseling every 2 weeks. The primary outcome was the relative change in the 6-min walk distance (6MWD). Secondary outcomes included changes in peak oxygen uptake (VO2), ventilatory anaerobic threshold (VAT), ventilation-to-carbon dioxide output slope, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) score, as well as program adherence. Results: All participants completed the 5-month follow-up and performed a median of 58.5 (interquartile range: 28.0, 77.8) sessions, corresponding to 89.5% (42.8, 118.6) of prescribed sessions (three per week). 6MWD improved from 468.3 ± 98.8 m to 542.6 ± 70.3 m; the mean absolute change was 74.3 m (95% CI, 47.8–100.7; relative change, 18.6%; p < 0.001). Peak VO2 and VAT increased by 16.7% and 30.1%, respectively. HADS scores decreased modestly. One participant was hospitalized for worsening heart failure (unrelated to the intervention); no other serious cardiovascular events occurred. Conclusions: This mobile application-based, unsupervised remote CR program was feasible and associated with improved exercise capacity in patients with CVD. Randomized trials comparing it with center-based CR are warranted.

title: Advances and perspectives in organic inhibitor-based anti-corrosion coatings: Biodegradable polymers, natural extracts, and synthetic compounds
summary: This review focuses on progress and advances in the preparation of anti-corrosion coatings using organic inhibitors. It looks at examples of biodegradable polymers, plant extracts, and synthetic organic compounds, revealing interesting resu
content: This review focuses on progress and advances in the preparation of anti-corrosion coatings using organic inhibitors. It looks at examples of biodegradable polymers, plant extracts, and synthetic organic compounds, revealing interesting results and offering new perspectives on their potential applications. The review provides both experimental and theoretical evidence of the high corrosion inhibitory properties of carbon steels and alloys in acidic and saline environments. Chitosan derivatives with chemical modifications, such as Schiff bases and nanocomposites, can achieve significant efficiencies in producing stable protective coatings through physical and chemical adsorption. The environmentally friendly approach of using flavonoids, phenols and alkaloids from plant or agricultural residue extracts to achieve up to significant values inhibition is also introduced. Furthermore, the review discusses synthetic organic compounds and ionic liquids acting as mixed inhibitors, with detailed adsorption mechanisms reported by quantum chemistry analysis and molecular simulations. Finally, the addition of inhibitors and additives, provides synergistic corrosion protection. Organic inhibitors offer a sustainable and effective means of protecting metals in aggressive environments.

title: Prediction of Compressive Strength of Activated Binary Cement Mortars Using Response Surface Methodology and Artificial Neural Networks
summary: This study investigates the prediction of the compressive strength of activated binary cement mortars containing ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS) using two complementary modelling approaches: response surface methodology (RSM) a
content: This study investigates the prediction of the compressive strength of activated binary cement mortars containing ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS) using two complementary modelling approaches: response surface methodology (RSM) and an artificial neural network (ANN). A database of 96 mix–curing combinations was assembled from the published literature on activated slag cement systems. Four input parameters were considered: slag replacement ratio (0–70 %), slag fineness (Blaine, 320–650 m²/kg), curing temperature (20–80 °C) and curing time (1–90 days). The output variable was the 1- to 90-day compressive strength (9–64 MPa). A second-order RSM polynomial was fitted and analysed by ANOVA, while a back-propagation feed-forward ANN with a 4–9–6–1 architecture and hyperbolic tangent activation was trained using the L-BFGS algorithm. The ANN reached R² = 0.996 and RMSE = 0.92 MPa over the whole dataset, clearly outperforming the RSM model (R² = 0.785, RMSE = 6.83 MPa). Sensitivity analysis showed that curing time was the dominant predictor (62 %), followed by slag fineness (22 %), curing temperature (8 %) and slag replacement ratio (8 %). The results confirm that ANN is a more reliable surrogate for the highly non-linear hydration kinetics of activated slag mortars and can be used to support mix-design decisions and reduce experimental effort.

title: Corrosion of Alkali‐Metal Anodes: Mechanisms, Mitigation, and Quantification
summary: ABSTRACT Alkali‐metal anodes combine high theoretical specific capacities with highly negative redox potentials, but the same thermodynamic attributes make them intrinsically reactive toward practical electrolytes. The resulting corrosion c
content: ABSTRACT Alkali‐metal anodes combine high theoretical specific capacities with highly negative redox potentials, but the same thermodynamic attributes make them intrinsically reactive toward practical electrolytes. The resulting corrosion continuously consumes active metal and electrolyte during both cycling and storage, yet it is often discussed only indirectly through solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) instability, dendrite formation, or inactive‐metal generation. This review develops a corrosion‐centered framework for Li, Na, and K metal anodes, using Li as the primary evidence base. For mechanistic clarity, operationally distinguish chemical corrosion, arising from spontaneous metal‐electrolyte reactions at the metal surface, from galvanic corrosion, in which active‐metal oxidation is electronically coupled to cathodic electrolyte reduction at a spatially distinct conductive region. Electrolyte reactivity, SEI persistence and permeability, effective metal/electrolyte contact area, current collector exposure, and electrode geometry are identified as key factors governing both corrosion pathways. Mitigation strategies are then organized by their primary interfacial targets. Particular emphasis is placed on what commonly used characterization methods actually measure and on how corrosion rates can be quantified without conflating distinct loss pathways. Finally, standardized testing principles and cross‐chemistry descriptors are outlined to relate corrosion to realistic cycling and calendar life, especially in the comparatively underexplored Na‐ and K‐metal systems.

title: Carob (Ceratonia siliqua L.) as a functional synbiotic matrix: biochemical composition, probiotic compatibility, and gut microbiota modulation in food systems
summary: Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are common worldwide, and their frequency has risen alongside the dietary shift that has stripped fermentable fibre out of everyday diets. Carob ( Ceratonia siliqua L. ) is a Mediterranean agro-indu
content: Disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are common worldwide, and their frequency has risen alongside the dietary shift that has stripped fermentable fibre out of everyday diets. Carob ( Ceratonia siliqua L. ) is a Mediterranean agro-industrial by-product that has mostly been put to low-value uses, although its composition is unusually varied for a fibre source. This review sets out what is known about that composition, covering galactomannans, polyphenols, dietary fibre and pinitol, and then examines how carob behaves during food processing. Three synbiotic roles are considered. Carob is a fermentable substrate that favours Lactobacillus , Bifidobacterium and the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFA). It carries polyphenols that act on microbial niches alongside the fibre fraction. It is also technologically compatible with fermented matrices, where it helps probiotic cells stay viable. Mechanistic work and in vitro fermentation converge on the same picture: carob belongs among differentiated prebiotic ingredients, not among substitutes for inulin, galacto-oligosaccharides (GOS) or β-glucans. Four problems still block clinical validation. The materials tested differ widely between fractions and geographical origins; in vitro fermentation models remain distant from human physiology; almost no clinical trial has been designed around carob; and strain-substrate compatibility has never been demonstrated rigorously. The review closes with a research agenda covering targeted randomised controlled trials, CAZy-based genomic screening of candidate probiotic strains, stratified precision-nutrition designs and standardised formulations.

title: Review of radiobiological dose rate effects at the edge between conventional and FLASH
summary: The shift from passive scattering to active pencil beam scanning (PBS) in proton therapy, alongside techniques such as flattening filter-free photon therapy, has increased dose rates in clinical radiotherapy from <0.4 Gy/s to 0.4-35 Gy/s. M
content: The shift from passive scattering to active pencil beam scanning (PBS) in proton therapy, alongside techniques such as flattening filter-free photon therapy, has increased dose rates in clinical radiotherapy from <0.4 Gy/s to 0.4-35 Gy/s. Meanwhile, ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy (FLASH, ≥40 Gy/s) has emerged as a novel modality that spares normal tissue while maintaining tumor control. Yet, dose rate effects within the 0.4-35 Gy/s range have traditionally been considered negligible. Recent reports of unexpected necroses after proton PBS irradiations challenge this assumption, prompting a reevaluation of potential dose-rate-dependent effects in this intermediate range. This review summarizes current evidence on dose rate effects within 0.4-35 Gy/s, derived from in vivo models (including zebrafish embryos and rodents), in-vitro experiments and water radiolysis studies. Selected experimental and retrospective observations suggest that dose rates in this inter mediate range may modify the biological response and, under certain conditions, increase toxicity relative to conventional reference dose rates (<0.4 Gy/s). The magnitude and even direction of dose rate effects appear to depend on radiation quality, total dose, temporal delivery structure, oxygenation, linear energy transfer, tissue type and biological endpoint. The observations described in this review are hypothesis-generating rather than threshold-defining, highlighting the need for further investigation in experimental conditions, preclinical models, and clinical settings.

title: Effect of Wind-Measurement Height and Photovoltaic Area on the Least-Cost Hybrid Supply of a University Critical Bus in Kaduna, Nigeria: A Screening-Level Techno-Economic Assessment
summary: This screening-level assessment tests whether small wind belongs in a least-cost hybrid plant for a critical-facility bus at Kaduna State University (10.52° N, 7.44° E), and whether that answer depends on wind-measurement height and a limit
content: This screening-level assessment tests whether small wind belongs in a least-cost hybrid plant for a critical-facility bus at Kaduna State University (10.52° N, 7.44° E), and whether that answer depends on wind-measurement height and a limit on photovoltaic capacity. An open hourly load-following model used NASA POWER (2026) meteorology for 2022 and a synthesised critical load (peak 97.1 kW; 477 MWh yr−1). A generic turbine curve gave capacity factors of 4.8% at 10 m (mean 3.41 m s−1) and 19.2% at 50 m (mean 5.34 m s−1). Among 1,350 candidate grid combinations retained only if the loss-of-power-supply probability was at most 1%, the unconstrained cost minimum under the assumed prices was 320 kW of photovoltaics, 800 kWh of storage and 40 kW of diesel, with no wind: levelised cost 0.190 USD kWh−1, renewable fraction 91.4%, and diesel CO2 40 t yr−1, against 0.351 USD kWh−1 and 505 t yr−1 for diesel only. Capping photovoltaics at 200 kW brought 40 kW of wind into the optimum and raised the levelised cost to 0.215 USD kWh−1 within the explored design space. The wind-selection result is conditional on the synthetic load, screening costs and single-year resource series; a 10 m mean should not be used as hub-height input for this site.

title: Microgrid for the mitigation of load shedding in South Africa commercial buildings
summary: Load shedding in South Africa has severely hindered governance and the operation of critical urban infrastructures, such as government complexes, leading to frequent interruptions in public service delivery. While solar photovoltaic (PV) mi
content: Load shedding in South Africa has severely hindered governance and the operation of critical urban infrastructures, such as government complexes, leading to frequent interruptions in public service delivery. While solar photovoltaic (PV) microgrids are recognised as a viable alternative to grid dependency, most existing research focuses on rural or residential applications, leaving a gap for site-specific assessments of urban office buildings that prioritize service continuity during grid instability. This study investigates the design and optimisation of a hybrid microgrid, integrating solar PV, battery storage, diesel backup, and a grid connection, to meet the power requirements of a government office complex in Johannesburg. Using Hybrid Optimisation Model for Electric Renewables (HOMER) Pro software and recorded hourly consumption data, the system was modelled by employing a load-following dispatch strategy alongside simultaneous multi-objective optimisation for cost and environmental impact. The study reported PV-Battery-Grid (PV-B-GR) configuration as the optimal solution. This configuration yielded a Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) of ZAR1.11 and a Net Present Cost (NPC) of ZAR1, 842,856. While its operating costs are slightly higher than configurations with heavier generator use, it provides the lowest emissions of pollutants such as CO₂, CO, SO₂, and NOx. This study provides a framework for achieving energy independence in commercial buildings, while offering a scalable roadmap for policymakers to mitigate the impact of the South African energy crisis and replicate it for other climes.

title: Sealing ability of two calcium silicate based experimental materials in furcation perforation repair: An in vitro study
summary: Aim The purpose of this vitro study was the comparison of the sealing ability of two experimental calcium silicate /calcium aluminate-based nano materials. Materials and methods Sealing of intentionally done perforation in the furcation are
content: Aim The purpose of this vitro study was the comparison of the sealing ability of two experimental calcium silicate /calcium aluminate-based nano materials. Materials and methods Sealing of intentionally done perforation in the furcation area in ninety extracted mandibular molars was performed using in group 1(n = 20): Biodentine, in group 2 (n = 20): experimental material A (NanoTricalcium silicate, Nano Dicalcium silicateand Nano Calcium Aluminate based material), in group 3 (n = 20): experimental material B (NanoTricalcium silicate and Nano Calcium Aluminate based material), in Group 4 (n = 20): MTA Angelus and in Group 5: Negative Control (n = 10): No repair material or coronal seal was placed, leaving the perforation site open, to ensure the dye could freely pass through the perforation. Dye penetration test was then done using 1% methylene blue dye solution, followed by recording values of dye penetration using stereomicroscope at magnification 25X. One-way ANOVA followed by Tukey post hoc test was applied to compare more than two groups in non-related samples. Results Biodentine recorded the lowest mean leakage value (8.192 ± 0.447 mm) with no statistically significant difference with both experimental A and MTA groups, which recorded mean leakage value (8.596 ± 0.580 mm) and (8.330 ± 0.916 mm) respectively. Experimental B recorded the highest mean leakage value (14.492 ± 0.459 mm) with statistically significant difference with the other three tested materials, where ( p < 0.001). Conclusions According to this in vitro study condition, that differs from the clinical situation, the experimental material A (NanoTricalcium silicate, Nano Dicalcium silicate and Nano Calcium Aluminate based material) showed promising sealing ability outcomes, while the experimental material B (NanoTricalcium silicate and Nano calcium aluminate-based material) showed inferior sealing performance, when both were compared to Biodentine and MTA Angelus.

title: Robust Iron-based Fischer-Tropsch Catalysts by Direct Joule Synthesis
summary: Abstract Converting CO2 into gasoline- and jet-fuel-range hydrocarbons offers an elegant approach to sustainable fuels compatible with existing infrastructure. However, widely applied iron-based syngas Fischer-Tropsch catalysts deactivate i
content: Abstract Converting CO2 into gasoline- and jet-fuel-range hydrocarbons offers an elegant approach to sustainable fuels compatible with existing infrastructure. However, widely applied iron-based syngas Fischer-Tropsch catalysts deactivate in CO2-rich feeds due to oxidation of active carbides in oxidising CO2 environments and the doubled H2O byproduct. Herein, we demonstrate Direct Joule Synthesis (DJS) coupled with mechanochemical treatment as an effective method to prepare metal-rich Fe-Co-Na precursors, which reconstruct during CO2 hydrogenation into carbide-containing active structures. The optimised FeCoNa sample attains 57.3% CO2 conversion, 24.1% C5+ yield, 43.7% C2+ yield, and space-time-yields of 0.40 gC₅₊ h−1 gcat−1 and 0.68 gC2₊ h−1 gcat−1 at 350°C and 30 bar, exceeding reported systems. Even more intriguing, stable operation for at least 500 h on stream is achieved due to retention of Fe5C2 as a dominant phase, stabilised by residual metallic FeCo acting as a reduction promoter, limiting carbide re-oxidation, in addition to enhancing olefin release and supply of adsorbed intermediates. These findings demonstrate the activity and stability advantages of metal-derived Fe-based CO2 hydrogenation catalysts, establishing DJS as a rapid non-equilibrium synthesis method for versatile multimetallic catalysts.

title: Síntesis y caracterización de electrolitos poliméricos sólidos basados en poliuretano de base acuosa para baterías de ion-litio
summary: El poliuretano en dispersión acuosa (WPU) es una matriz versátil para el desarrollo de electrolitos poliméricos sólidos (SPEs) en baterías de ion-litio. Su arquitectura presenta grupos éter en la cadena polimérica que favorecen la coordinac
content: El poliuretano en dispersión acuosa (WPU) es una matriz versátil para el desarrollo de electrolitos poliméricos sólidos (SPEs) en baterías de ion-litio. Su arquitectura presenta grupos éter en la cadena polimérica que favorecen la coordinación con iones de litio, lo que facilita la movilidad iónica y conductividad iónica del material.En este trabajo se sintetizó un WPU y posteriormente se prepararon SPEs incorporando cloruro de litio (LiCl) en distintas concentraciones dentro de la matriz polimérica. Los materiales obtenidos fueron caracterizados mediante espectroscopía infrarroja por transformada de Fourier, difracción de rayos X, microscopía electrónica de barrido, análisis termogravimétrico, calorimetría diferencial de barrido y espectroscopía de impedancia electroquímica.La muestra de SPE con 10 % en peso de LiCl mostró el mejor desempeño, alcanzando una conductividad iónica de 2,82 × 10-7 S cm-1 a 25 °C, valor adecuado para sistemas de SPE basados en LiCl.

title: Novel Aeschynite-Type CeTiTa1– x Nb x O6 Orange Pigments
summary: Abstract An orange inorganic pigment free from hazardous components conventionally used in inorganic pigments, such as Cd-, Pb-, Hg-, and Cr(VI)-based compounds, was developed based on aeschynite-type CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) synthesized
content: Abstract An orange inorganic pigment free from hazardous components conventionally used in inorganic pigments, such as Cd-, Pb-, Hg-, and Cr(VI)-based compounds, was developed based on aeschynite-type CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) synthesized by a solid-state reaction method. X-ray powder diffraction, Rietveld refinement, and X-ray fluorescence analysis supported the formation of a continuous CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 solid solution over the investigated composition range, with a small amount of TiO2 impurity. UV–visible reflectance spectroscopy showed that increasing Nb5+ substitution shifted the absorption edge toward longer wavelengths, while the optical band gap energy estimated from Tauc plots decreased from 2.45 to 2.12 eV. This behavior may be associated with modification of the transition-metal d-derived conduction-band states upon Nb substitution. As a result, the sample color gradually changed from yellow to orange with increasing Nb content, and CeTiNbO6 (x = 1) exhibited a high redness value (a* = +26.4). X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicated that Ce3+ was the predominant Ce species in the surface region probed by XPS. CeTiNbO6 retained its orange coloration after the acid and base treatments employed in this study and after heat treatment at 800 °C for 6 h in air. These results indicate that CeTiTa1–xNbxO6 is a promising orange inorganic pigment with composition-tunable color and good color stability under the chemical and thermal conditions examined in this study.

title: Spectral fits with full broadening for kHz-iteration high-accuracy gas-phase spectroscopy
summary: Abstract This work presents methods enabling real-time multi-species direct absorption spectroscopic fitting at kilohertz iteration rates with high accuracy of spectral line shapes on embedded systems. Precomputation of multi-dimensional po
content: Abstract This work presents methods enabling real-time multi-species direct absorption spectroscopic fitting at kilohertz iteration rates with high accuracy of spectral line shapes on embedded systems. Precomputation of multi-dimensional polynomials and effective pressures allows high accuracy approximation of HITRAN Hartmann-Tran absorption coefficients with full matrix broadening and low residual error, replacing computationally slow line-by-line simulations and inaccurate fixed-basis functions. A novel Levenberg--Marquardt solver augmented with Taguchi orthogonal array exploration accelerates fitting convergence and escapes local minima. Together, these methods enable simulated implementations that fit 1000-point spectra with simultaneous etalon fringe, temperature, and pressure estimation at 1~kHz using 0.8~W simulated computational power for a single laser system. This work further simulates a simultaneous dual-laser single-detector architecture exploiting co-prime spectral lengths, fitting six concentration parameters at 0.82~kHz using 1.6~W simulated computational power. Mid-infrared TDLAS simulations targeting CH4, H2O, C2H6, CO2, and N2O provide an approach for possible atmospheric sensing deployments and chemical kinetics studies.

title: Tobacco Stem Powder‐Modified Phenolated Kraft Lignin‐Based Phenol–Formaldehyde Adhesive for Wood Bonding
summary: ABSTRACT Lignin and agricultural residues are promising resources for wood adhesives, but the use of tobacco stem powder ( TSP ) in phenolated lignin‐based phenol–formaldehyde ( PF ) adhesives remains little studied. Phenolated kraft lignin
content: ABSTRACT Lignin and agricultural residues are promising resources for wood adhesives, but the use of tobacco stem powder ( TSP ) in phenolated lignin‐based phenol–formaldehyde ( PF ) adhesives remains little studied. Phenolated kraft lignin‐based PF ( PKL ‐ PF ) resin was prepared, and TSP partially replaced concentrated resin solution at constant spread. L 9 orthogonal designs optimized resin synthesis and hot‐pressing. At the selected pressing conditions (140°C, 140 g m −2 , 9 min), dry strength peaked at 10 wt% TSP (4.63 ± 0.72 MPa ), significantly exceeding the TSP ‐free control (3.52 ± 0.35 MPa ). Wet strength was highest at 15 wt% TSP (4.42 ± 0.73 MPa ), but did not differ significantly from the control (4.17 ± 0.47 MPa ). After boiling‐water treatment, 15 wt% TSP gave the highest bonding strength (3.60 ± 0.46 MPa ), whereas 12 wt% TSP had the highest wood failure percentage (74.00% ± 13.42%).

title: Hierarchical Carbon Aerogel With Polarized Zr─O Interfaces Enables Dynamic Iodine Regulation in Aqueous Zn‐I 2 Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT The shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides limits the cycling stability and rate capability of aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries. Herein, a ZrO 2 ‐decorated cellulose‐derived carbon aerogel (ZCA) is developed by integrating hierarchical pore
content: ABSTRACT The shuttle effect of soluble polyiodides limits the cycling stability and rate capability of aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries. Herein, a ZrO 2 ‐decorated cellulose‐derived carbon aerogel (ZCA) is developed by integrating hierarchical pore confinement with polarized Zr─O/carbon interfacial regulation. Spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal moderate O···I─I coupling with halogen‐bond‐like character for neutral I 2 at Zr‐adjacent oxygen sites, while reduced iodine species are stabilized through species‐dependent interfacial regulation within the polarized Zr─O‐containing environment. This structural‐interfacial synergy suppresses polyiodide diffusion while preserving reversible I − /I 3 − /I 2 conversion. Consequently, ZCA@I 2 delivers 187.2 mAh g −1 after 5000 cycles at 1 A g −1 and sustains 123.2 mAh g −1 after 50 000 cycles at 10 A g −1 , with a per‐cycle decay of only 0.000052%. At an iodine areal loading of 6.7 mg cm −2 , it retains 93.1% of its capacity after 6000 cycles at 1 A g −1 . These results provide a structure‐interface design strategy for durable, high‐rate, and high‐loading aqueous Zn‐I 2 batteries.

title: Phosphorescent Sensing of ADN Using Copper(I) Coordination Polymers
summary: Abstract Rapid, selective, and field-deployable detection of ammonium dinitramide (ADN) is important for the safe production, handling, and monitoring of energetic materials. Herein, we report a distinct synthetic strategy for the known Cu(
content: Abstract Rapid, selective, and field-deployable detection of ammonium dinitramide (ADN) is important for the safe production, handling, and monitoring of energetic materials. Herein, we report a distinct synthetic strategy for the known Cu(I) coordination polymer [Cu(pz)]n and reveal its previously unexplored phosphorescent sensing capability toward ADN. Inspired by the thermal reduction of related Cu(II) imidazolate frameworks, Pbca-[Cu(pz)]n was prepared from Cu(pz)2 via high-temperature reduction and vapor deposition, affording diffraction-quality single crystals for accurate structural refinement and photophysical analysis. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first application of [Cu(pz)]n as a phosphorescent sensing platform for ADN. Upon exposure to ADN, [Cu(pz)]n shows phosphorescence quenching mainly via competitive absorption (CA), with possible photoinduced electron transfer (PET) contribution. The Stern–Volmer response shows a linear relationship over the ADN concentration range of 0–80 μM (R2 = 0.987), with a Stern–Volmer constant (KSV) of 2.7 × 104 M–1 and a detection limit of 5.56 μM. Although previously reported graphene-based voltammetric and AuNP-based colorimetric methods achieve lower detection limits of 2.0 μM and approximately 0.10 μM, respectively, they rely on electrode-based measurements or multistep UV-assisted chemical conversion and derivatization. In contrast, [Cu(pz)]n enables direct phosphorescence sensing of ADN without such pretreatment and shows high selectivity over the tested energetic materials. Furthermore, [Cu(pz)]n can be incorporated into test strips for visual ADN detection, demonstrating its potential as a simple and convenient platform for rapid on-site screening.

title: Spatial Self‐Phase Modulation in SnSe 2 Nanosheets: Wavelength Nonreciprocity for All‐Optical Switching and Modulation
summary: ABSTRACT Based on spatial self‐phase modulation (SSPM) in emerging two‐dimensional nanomaterials, researchers have developed various passive nonlinear photonic devices, such as all‐optical switches, modulators, and information converters. H
content: ABSTRACT Based on spatial self‐phase modulation (SSPM) in emerging two‐dimensional nanomaterials, researchers have developed various passive nonlinear photonic devices, such as all‐optical switches, modulators, and information converters. However, the influence of wavelength nonreciprocity on their performance remains underexplored. Here, we fabricate and characterize SnSe 2 nanosheets, investigate their SSPM behavior, and exploit them for two‐color all‐optical switching and modulation. Owing to the material's nonlinear dispersion, the measured third‐order nonlinear susceptibility of monolayer SnSe 2 is 3.20 × 10 −8 esu at 532 nm and 1.41 × 10 −8 esu at 671 nm, with corresponding SSPM ring formation times of ∼0.33 s and ∼0.50 s at ∼200 W/cm 2 , respectively. Whereas previously reported two‐color all‐optical switches and modulators employ a short‐wavelength laser as the pump beam and a long‐wavelength beam as the probe beam, this study systematically investigates the influence of wavelength nonreciprocity on the performance of such devices. The results show that the pump beam plays a decisive role in determining both the switching time and modulation depth, revealing wavelength‐dominated nonlinear dynamical nonreciprocity in SSPM‐based devices. This flexible regulation of all‐optical switching and modulation performance via wavelength interchange provides a new route to break through the conventional intensity‐only control approach and to realize tunable, broadband, and multifunctional nonlinear photonic devices.

title: Ultrasonication-assisted magnesiothermic synthesis of cast in-situ graphene-MgO reinforced AZ91 magnesium hybrid nanocomposites
summary: A sustainable liquid metallurgy route was developed for the in-situ synthesis of graphene (Gr)@MgO hybrid reinforcements in AZ91 magnesium alloy via simultaneous CO 2 bubbling and ultrasonication. The magnesiothermic reduction of CO 2 enabl
content: A sustainable liquid metallurgy route was developed for the in-situ synthesis of graphene (Gr)@MgO hybrid reinforcements in AZ91 magnesium alloy via simultaneous CO 2 bubbling and ultrasonication. The magnesiothermic reduction of CO 2 enables the formation of multilayer Gr decorated with nanoscale (< 5 nm) MgO particles, as confirmed by Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The AZ91 composites exhibit significant microstructural refinement, with the average α-Mg grain size reduced by approximately 67%. This refinement, combined with the presence of Gr@MgO, leads to marked improvements in mechanical properties, with hardness, yield strength, and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) increasing by up to 20%, 96%, and 18%, respectively. Partial formation of nano-sized Al 4 C 3 was also observed, indicating interfacial reactions between Gr and the AZ91 matrix. The enhanced performance is attributed to the combined effects of grain refinement, load transfer, and dislocation pinning induced by the in-situ formed hybrid reinforcements. A four-stage mechanism is proposed to describe the formation and dispersion of Gr and MgO during CO 2 bubbling under ultrasonic treatment, involving bubble expansion, interfacial reaction, particle growth, and cavitation-assisted dispersion. These results demonstrate a potentially scalable approach for producing high-performance Mg matrix nanocomposites.

title: Contrasting Turbulent Transport of PM 2.5 and Conventional Scalars during Pollution Episodes over the North China Plain
summary: Abstract. Understanding turbulent transport similarities between PM2.5 and conventional scalars and the origins of their differences is essential for assessing particulate turbulent diffusion relationships. Using intensive wintertime observ
content: Abstract. Understanding turbulent transport similarities between PM2.5 and conventional scalars and the origins of their differences is essential for assessing particulate turbulent diffusion relationships. Using intensive wintertime observations in Dezhou, North China Plain, we developed a retrieval method that selects visibility–PM2.5 relationships for individual pollution episodes. This improves applicability across episodes compared with a single fixed relationship and yields PM2.5 mass concentration fluctuations and turbulent fluxes. Estimates were more sensitive to relationship selection under low visibility, highlighting the importance of accounting for episode differences. Comparisons with CO2, water vapour, and temperature revealed similar variance-scaling exponents but markedly lower normalized vertical transport efficiency for PM2.5. Under unstable stratification, normalized standard deviations of all four scalars approximately followed (-z/L)⁻¹ᐟ³ scaling. PM2.5 had the largest fitted coefficient, indicating stronger fluctuations relative to its flux scale, and weaker correlations with vertical velocity under both unstable and stable conditions. Strong instantaneous PM2.5 transport events were less directionally organized than those of conventional scalars, with upward and downward contributions cancelling each other. Flux contributions at different frequencies also showed stronger cancellation between opposing directions. These event and frequency characteristics jointly explain the lower normalized vertical transport efficiency of PM2.5. Our findings demonstrate that similar variance-scaling exponents can coexist with different transport efficiencies, extending scalar comparisons to net flux formation. They provide observational evidence for assessing shared turbulent diffusion relationships for particulate matter and conventional scalars in air quality models and improving PM2.5 turbulent diffusion parameterizations.

title: Zr-MOF nanocolloids prepared by pulsed laser ablation in water for tyrosine electrochemical sensing
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract This work presents the synthesis of contaminant-free Zr-MOF nanocolloids via pulsed laser ablation in liquids, a green and by-product-free top-down approach. A focused picosecond laser beam was employed to ablate a UiO-67 MOF targe
content: Abstract This work presents the synthesis of contaminant-free Zr-MOF nanocolloids via pulsed laser ablation in liquids, a green and by-product-free top-down approach. A focused picosecond laser beam was employed to ablate a UiO-67 MOF target immersed in deionized water, yielding well-dispersed nanostructures with diameters ranging from 20 to 100 nm. For comparison, the effects of direct laser irradiation on dispersed UiO-67 powders were also investigated. Scanning-Transmission Electron Microscopy revealed a distinct morphological reorganization of the nanostructures upon laser processing. The ablation products were comprehensively characterized using Dynamic Light Scattering, optical spectroscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), the latter indicating significant surface stoichiometric modifications consistent with changes in the zirconium coordination environment. Finally, the electrochemical sensing performance of the colloids was evaluated using D-tyrosine as a model analyte. The PLAL-synthesized samples exhibited outstanding sensitivity, a low detection limit of 0.10 μM in phosphate-buffered saline, and excellent selectivity toward D-tyrosine even in the presence of common interferents like dopamine and uric acid, as well as in complex media.

title: Forest Composition Controls on Water Security in Nepal's Middle Hills
summary: ABSTRACT Montane watersheds in the Himalayan region are becoming increasingly vulnerable to hydroclimatic extremes that cause floods, landslides, droughts and seasonal water scarcity. These risks are compounded by ecohydrological transforma
content: ABSTRACT Montane watersheds in the Himalayan region are becoming increasingly vulnerable to hydroclimatic extremes that cause floods, landslides, droughts and seasonal water scarcity. These risks are compounded by ecohydrological transformation resulting from shifts in forest composition, notably the widespread establishment of pine plantations, as well as climate variability and intensified land‐use activities. Understanding how forest composition influences watershed hydrological response remains a key challenge. Here, we use long‐term data and process‐based modelling of forest canopy trends to simulate ecohydrological dynamics in a headwater catchment supplying water to the Kathmandu Valley. The model is used to assess the hydrological performance of four forest composition scenarios: status quo (current forest cover), monoculture‐pine, monoculture‐broadleaf and managed‐mixed forest. The process‐based model, RHESSys, was used to evaluate seasonal evapotranspiration (ET), groundwater depth response, streamflow and canopy dynamics across scenarios. Given the uncertainty in climate forcing data and the strong topographic variability, the model reproduced observed daily streamflow reasonably well. Daily NSE, LNSE, KGE and PBIAS were 0.55, 0.65, 0.60 and 24% in calibration and 0.57, 0.72, 0.61 and 23% in validation, respectively. Monthly values were 0.61, 0.67, 0.64 and 24% in calibration and 0.68, 0.78, 0.66 and 23% in validation, respectively. Results show that pine‐dominated forests exhibit elevated year‐round water demand, and therefore lower low flows (lowest 1% of daily flows) by 7.7%. In contrast, broadleaf forests can reduce high flows (highest 1% of daily flows) by 4% while increasing low flows by 29% and reducing ET during water‐limited periods. However, the managed‐mixed forest scenario delivers the most balanced and sustainable hydrological performance, reducing high flows by 5% and increasing low flows by 16%. These findings highlight the critical role of forest type and management in shaping watershed‐scale water balance and that strategically designed, topographically informed mixed‐species restoration is essential to sustaining water availability under increasing climate pressure. This study offers a case study–based modelling framework with potential transferability to similarly vulnerable montane landscapes across the Himalayan region.

title: Asymmetric transmission of AI and renewable energy equity shocks to U.S. oil sector performance: A regime-dependent analysis for sustainable investment
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study empirically examines the dynamic and regime-dependent asymmetric effects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Renewable Energy (RE) equity returns on the performance of the U.S. oil sec
content: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study empirically examines the dynamic and regime-dependent asymmetric effects of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Renewable Energy (RE) equity returns on the performance of the U.S. oil sector. Utilizing daily closing prices from December 1, 2017 to October 31, 2025, we employ regime-dependent Vector Autoregression (VAR) models, supplemented by an illustrative Bayesian Time-Varying Parameter (TVP) VAR, to capture heterogeneous transmission mechanisms across bullish and bearish market regimes. The empirical findings show that the individual lagged effects of RE returns on oil returns emerge earlier during bearish markets – a pattern consistent with loss aversion and defensive sectoral rebalancing – whereas the cumulative contribution of RE shocks to oil return variation is larger during bullish phases. In contrast, the relationship between AI and oil shifts direction depending on the market: it is driven by growth when markets are up. Still, it acts as a direct risk transmitter during downturns. Notably, AI and oil equities co-move positively in both regimes, suggesting that their potential diversification benefits as hedges against one another may be limited, although hedge effectiveness is not formally tested here. Collectively, our results underscore that effective investment strategies and policy interventions must be explicitly conditioned on the prevailing market state. Future research avenues are suggested, including subsector-specific analysis and the use of direct technological adoption metrics, such as patent data.

title: Multi-model validation of the hydro-mechanical and soil–water characteristic behaviour of a slag-cement-amended iron ore tailings– bentonite liner material across compaction moisture states
summary: Abstract Compacted liners made from iron ore tailings (IOT) and bentonite must satisfy strength, hydraulic and shrinkage criteria concurrently, yet these properties respond in opposing directions to the compaction water content. This study
content: Abstract Compacted liners made from iron ore tailings (IOT) and bentonite must satisfy strength, hydraulic and shrinkage criteria concurrently, yet these properties respond in opposing directions to the compaction water content. This study evaluates how the compaction moisture state (2% dry of optimum, DOPT; optimum, OPT; 2% wet of optimum, WOPT) governs the performance of IOT–bentonite mixtures (20–40% bentonite) stabilised with 0–10% slag cement (CEM III), compacted at British Standard Heavy (BSH) energy and cured for 28 days. Unconfined compressive strength (UCS), saturated hydraulic conductivity ( K sat ) and volumetric shrinkage ( V s ) were measured for 25 mixtures, and Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to map the combined compliance region against UCS ≥ 200 kPa, K sat ≤ 1 × 10 − 9 m/s and V s ≤ 4%. For the 30% bentonite/10% CEM III mixture, UCS decreased from 1775 to 1800 to 1542 kPa from DOPT to WOPT, K sat from 1.37 × 10 − 9 to 1.93 × 10 − 10 to 9.73 × 10 − 11 m/s, and V s from 3.8 to 3.19 to 2.19%. DOPT was therefore the only condition that violated the hydraulic criterion, despite giving the highest strength, whereas OPT and WOPT met all three criteria. Soil–water characteristic curves (SWCCs) measured by pressure plate up to 1500 kPa were fitted with the Brooks–Corey, Fredlund–Xing and van Genuchten models; all reproduced the data closely (root-mean-square error, RMSE ≤ 0.0035) and the van Genuchten model was marginally best. Water retention increased with moulding water content. 2%WOPT placement of a 31% bentonite/10% CEM III liner is recommended.

title: Recent environmental change shapes biotic homogenisation of Orthoptera and Mantodea communities in semi-dry grasslands
summary: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. However, many grassland remnants are undergoing gradual habitat degradation due to climate change, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and the relaxation or abandonment
content: Semi-dry grasslands are among the most species-rich ecosystems in Europe. However, many grassland remnants are undergoing gradual habitat degradation due to climate change, atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and the relaxation or abandonment of traditional management. While declines of specialised insects have repeatedly been reported, the extent to which these drivers promote long-term community reorganisation and biotic homogenisation remains poorly understood. Using a nationwide resurvey of 221 semi-dry grassland patches across Germany, spanning two to three decades, we investigated long-term changes in Orthoptera and Mantodea communities. We quantified changes in species richness, community composition, and beta diversity, and related these patterns to major global change drivers. Despite an increase in total species richness, these communities became increasingly homogenised, as indicated by declining beta diversity. Community reorganisation was characterised by pronounced winner-loser dynamics, with highly mobile generalists and thermophilous species expanding, whereas threatened species, low-mobility habitat specialists, and species associated with High Nature Value farmland declined. Winner species richness increased particularly in warm and dry regions, under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition, and outside protected areas. By contrast, low-mobility habitat specialists and threatened species persisted most successfully in structurally heterogeneous habitats. High shrub cover was negatively associated with both winners and losers, indicating an overall deterioration of habitat suitability. Our findings demonstrate that environmental change does not necessarily reduce species richness but can profoundly reorganise communities through selective filtering of species. Maintaining habitat heterogeneity with appropriate management strategies is therefore crucial for buffering biodiversity loss under ongoing global change.

title: Freeform 3D Printing of Omnidirectionally Deformable Conductors via Newtonian Liquid Metal Droplet‐Mediated Stress Relaxation
summary: ABSTRACT Next‐generation soft robotics and shape‐morphing electronics demand materials that possess intrinsic softness yet processable into freeform 3D architectures. However, direct‐write 3D printing of soft elastomers suffers from a rheol
content: ABSTRACT Next‐generation soft robotics and shape‐morphing electronics demand materials that possess intrinsic softness yet processable into freeform 3D architectures. However, direct‐write 3D printing of soft elastomers suffers from a rheological trade‐off, where high yield stress required for printability increases stiffness. This work presents a ternary silicone elastomer ink that breaks this limitation by incorporating liquid metal (LM) as a Newtonian liquid filler. The fluidic LM droplets act as stress buffers, accelerating stress relaxation during flow without compromising post‐curing compliance. Additionally, they induce an excluded‐volume effect that increases the effective local concentration of the dispersed multi‐walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), thereby enhancing the percolating conductive network. This strategy enables support‐free 3D printing, achieving maximum bridging spans of 32 mm and a peak resolution of 124 µm independently. The composite exhibits high stretchability (446% elongation), a bulk conductivity of 7.08 S/m, and electrical stability under large deformation (∆R/R 0 = 0.51 at 100% strain). The versatility of this platform was further validated through reconfigurable 3D circuits, demonstrating that in addition to functioning as compliant conductors, the printed structures can also serve as robust load‐bearing structural elements. By reconciling printability, softness, and deformation‐tolerant electrical conductivity, this work establishes a general approach for freeform 3D soft electronics.

title: Melanin-Mediated Growth of Ag Nanostructures for Ultrasensitive SERS of l -Dopa
summary: Abstract Hybrid interfaces based on melanin films and electrochemically deposited silver nanoparticles (Mel@Ag) are presented as effective platforms for ultrasensitive surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). Natural melanin extracted from
content: Abstract Hybrid interfaces based on melanin films and electrochemically deposited silver nanoparticles (Mel@Ag) are presented as effective platforms for ultrasensitive surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS). Natural melanin extracted from sepia pigment was processed into homogeneous thin films on indium tin oxide (ITO) via a controlled dip-coating approach, providing a chemically stable and redox-active interface. The presence of the melanin layer promotes an anodic shift in the Ag+ reduction potential and enables controlled nucleation and growth of silver nanostructures. The resulting Mel@Ag systems exhibit enhanced plasmonic response and superior SERS performance, with optimal activity achieved at low scan rates. Experimental results combined with electromagnetic simulations indicate that nanoparticle dimers play a dominant role in generating effective hotspots, particularly under 638 nm excitation, where a larger near-field enhancement volume is observed. The analytical capability of the platform is demonstrated through the detection of l-Dopa down to 10−11 M. The melanin layer likely contributes not only to control the nanostructure growth but also to analyte preconcentration through π−π interactions, favoring molecular localization at plasmonic hotspots. Notably, the system retains measurable SERS activity in complex biological media, demonstrating the persistence of the SERS response despite increasing matrix complexity. These results highlight the potential of melanin-mediated hybrid architectures as versatile SERS platforms for sensing applications in biologically relevant environments.

title: Multi-scale biophysical modeling of fungal colony growth
summary: Fungal colony growth is shaped by the fundamental physical operating principles of hyphal elongation, branching, and anastomosis, which collectively organize into macroscopic foraging networks. While sophisticated 3D models utilizing adapti
content: Fungal colony growth is shaped by the fundamental physical operating principles of hyphal elongation, branching, and anastomosis, which collectively organize into macroscopic foraging networks. While sophisticated 3D models utilizing adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) on high-performance computing architectures can explicitly capture these discrete cellular mechanics, their immense computational cost prevents their integration into predictive ecosystem simulators. Here, building upon the Biological Modeling and interface eXchange (BMX) framework, we combine high-fidelity discrete hyphal mechanics with an analytically tractable, stochastic traveling-wave surrogate (sBARE) to provide multiscale simulations of fungal colonies at a fraction of the computational cost. By leveraging demographic fluctuations at the advancing front, our framework uniquely resolves macroscopic parameter degeneracies, separating the directed forward drift of leading tips from their effective diffusion to capture the macroscopic signature of negative autotropism in 3D networks. Simulations reproduce experimentally observed traveling wave profiles and confirm that interior network density under replete conditions emerges as an invariant self-regulated by fusion. Furthermore, global sensitivity analysis reveals that expansion speed and network density are governed by largely disjoint microscopic parameters. We demonstrate that because the physics of hyphal growth permit networks that are both exceptionally fast and dense, the empirical trade-off between sparse 'explorer' and dense 'exploiter' strategies observed in nature is not a strict mechanical constraint, pointing instead to metabolic limits on local growth rules. Our mathematically tractable approach bridges exascale-level cellular mechanics with macroscopic wave dynamics, enabling the integration of trait-driven advective fluxes and carrying capacities into the spatial transport and reaction network schemes of large-scale biogeochemical models.

title: Starve, stress, and mate: Activation of the CCAAT-Binding complex overrides sterility of mating-type heterozygous Candida albicans
summary: Sexual reproduction in the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans is typically restricted by a strict genetic lock: the a1-α2 repressor present in standard mating-type heterozygous (MTLa/α) diploid strains, which actively represses mating c
content: Sexual reproduction in the human fungal pathogen Candida albicans is typically restricted by a strict genetic lock: the a1-α2 repressor present in standard mating-type heterozygous (MTLa/α) diploid strains, which actively represses mating competency. While severe environmental pressures are known to influence fungal development, the molecular mechanisms that allow cells to override this genetic sterility block remain poorly understood. Here, we identify the highly conserved CCAAT-binding complex (CBC) as the critical developmental hub that integrates environmental stress to unlock mating in heterozygous diploids. By combining proteomic mapping (ChIP-SICAP) and transcriptomics (RNA-Seq) to define the regulatory network of the core CBC subunit Hap5, we demonstrate that CBC hyperactivation completely overrides the a1-α2 repressor. This activation triggers a robust white-to-opaque phenotypic switch and initiates a mating-competence program in MTLa/α strains genetically locked in a sterile state. Crucially, this developmental transition is antagonized by the iron-regulatory partner Hap43, but is strictly dependent on physical interaction at the chromatin level with Cap1, the master regulator of the oxidative stress response. Our findings reveal that the CBC and Cap1 couple metabolic starvation (glucose and iron limitation) and oxidative stress to a core reproductive program, providing a mechanistic basis for how C. albicans bypasses genetic constraints on sexual reproduction to generate genetic diversity under hostile host conditions.
