title: Oil and Gas Technology, Management, and Finance
summary: Oil and Gas Technology, Management, and Finance offers a comprehensive, integrated approach to understanding and solving problems in the oil and gas industry, bridging the gap between technical and nontechnical perspectives. Unlike traditio
content: Oil and Gas Technology, Management, and Finance offers a comprehensive, integrated approach to understanding and solving problems in the oil and gas industry, bridging the gap between technical and nontechnical perspectives. Unlike traditional books that compartmentalize knowledge into isolated disciplines, this work combines geoscience, engineering, management, and finance into a unified framework. It progresses from foundational concepts to advanced applications, equipping readers with the tools to address real-world challenges across the entire petroleum value chain. By emphasizing practical problem-solving and multidisciplinary collaboration, the book ensures that readers can apply their knowledge effectively in this complex and evolving industry. Features: • Explains the interplay between technologies, management, and financial frameworks at the different phases of the petroleum resource lifecycle and the entire value chain. • Illustrates best practices in decision-making, risk management, and capital allocation. • Features real-world examples and spreadsheet-based solutions, enabling readers to apply the concepts to their challenges. • Highlights emerging trends, such as AI, sustainability, and global best practices, ensuring relevance in today’s energy landscape. This book is an invaluable resource for a diverse audience of professionals, students, regulators, financiers, investors, and decision-makers in the oil and gas sector. It serves as a bridge for those in the broader energy industry and financial institutions, offering transferable skills applicable to emerging energy types. By combining academic rigor with practical insights, the book empowers readers to solve multidisciplinary problems, make informed decisions, and navigate the complexities of the petroleum industry with confidence.

title: Coupling Plasma‐Synthesized N‐Doped Graphene With Ice Templated Porous Electrode for Enhanced Aluminum Battery Performance
summary: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage owing to the low cost and abundance of aluminum. Graphene is an attractive cathode due to its high surface area and electrical conductivity, but its p
content: ABSTRACT Rechargeable aluminum batteries are promising for next‐generation energy storage owing to the low cost and abundance of aluminum. Graphene is an attractive cathode due to its high surface area and electrical conductivity, but its performance is limited by difficult production and sheet aggregation, which restrict electrolyte accessibility and ion transport. This study employs a plasma‐enabled synthesis approach to produce both pristine graphene and nitrogen‐doped graphene (N‐graphene), followed by an ice templating strategy to directly construct a three‐dimensional porous N‐graphene electrode. The effects of nitrogen doping and porous electrode architecture are systematically investigated by comparing dense and porous electrodes. Nitrogen‐doping increases the specific capacity by ∼50%, from 36.24 to 54.4 mAh/g at a current density of 0.1 A/g. Furthermore, introducing porous structure provides an additional ∼20% improvement, achieving a capacity of 65.5 mAh/g under the same conditions. This enhanced performance of porous electrode is attributed to its interconnected pores and partially aligned graphene sheets, which improve electrolyte accessibility and facilitate the adsorption and transport of AlCl 4 − anions. The robust porous structure of N‐graphene ensures excellent cycling stability, with no noticeable capacity decay over 5000 cycles. Coupling nitrogen doping with porous electrode architecture provides an effective strategy to enhance graphene‐based aluminum batteries.

title: Quantifying household food waste fractions and prevention potential through multi-seasonal composition analyses of residual municipal solid waste: evidence from six Czech municipalities
summary: Food waste represents a fundamental sustainability challenge with significant environmental, economic, and social consequences. Although considerable attention is paid to the prevention of food waste, reliable monitoring of actual food wast
content: Food waste represents a fundamental sustainability challenge with significant environmental, economic, and social consequences. Although considerable attention is paid to the prevention of food waste, reliable monitoring of actual food waste production remains challenging, particularly at the household level, where a substantial fraction of discarded food is channeled into residual municipal solid waste (RMSW) streams. This study examines RMSW as an empirical indicator of hidden household food waste streams and evaluates its relevance for food waste prevention strategies and the implementation of a circular economy. Detailed composition analyses of RMSW were conducted in six municipalities in the Czech Republic, representing various settlement characteristics. Representative waste samples of 500 kg were manually sorted into 23 material categories with a special focus on biodegradable materials and food waste fractions. Food waste was further classified according to prevention potential into avoidable and unavoidable fractions. To account for biological degradation and water evaporation during containment, an ex-ante moisture loss correction model was established and applied. To evaluate consumer wasting behavior independently of total municipal mass balances, we introduce a Screening Index of Food Waste in Residual Municipal Solid Waste (Iw RMSW ), defined as the ratio of avoidable to unavoidable food waste fractions within the RMSW stream. The results show that RMSW in all examined municipalities remains a vast repository of organic matter, with food waste accounting for up to 33% of household waste. Avoidable fractions constituted a substantial share of the discarded organic matter, accounting for up to 23.41% of the total RMSW mass. The Screening Index of Food Waste in RMSW (Iw RMSW ), was highest for the municipality of Lipno nad Vltavou at 4.35, which operates under a zero-waste fee system. During late summer campaigns, the town of Slaný exhibited an extreme peak in the amount of avoidable food waste of 33.38%, leading to an Iw RMSW of 27.82, signaling severe seasonal failures in food management. The findings of the analyses indicate a substantial prevention potential through behavioral interventions, improved household food management, and targeted municipal programs. The outcomes further demonstrate that existing separate collection systems alone do not fully prevent the disposal of food waste through RMSW. This study highlights the importance of integrating RMSW’s composition analyses into food waste monitoring frameworks. Combining physical waste data with behavioral approaches and circular economy principles can improve the evidence base for food waste prevention policies and support the transition to sustainable food systems. The results provide practical implications for municipalities and policymakers striving to achieve European goals in reducing food waste and improving resource efficiency.

title: Monomer sequence influences electron transport in aromatic amide foldamers
summary: Sequence encodes structure and function in biomolecules, but whether monomer order influences electron transport in synthetic foldamers remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate aromatic amide foldamers built from a peptide-insp
content: Sequence encodes structure and function in biomolecules, but whether monomer order influences electron transport in synthetic foldamers remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigate aromatic amide foldamers built from a peptide-inspired secondary amide and its N-methylated peptoid-inspired analogue. Single molecule conductance measurements reveal that the all-secondary-amide foldamer exhibits a well-defined conductance state (~10-3.8 G0), comparable to the substantially shorter secondary-amide building block (~10-3.7 G0), whereas incorporation of N-methylated units produces lower or less-defined conductance features. Notably, foldamers with identical composition but different sequence arrangements exhibit distinct conductance distributions, demonstrating that sequence order influences electron transport. Displacement and flicker noise analyses indicate compact junction geometries with substantial throughspace contributions, and the all secondary amide foldamer responds most strongly to changes in applied bias and molecular concentration. Computational modeling using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, density functional theory (DFT), and nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF)-DFT calculations provide insight into sequencedependent conformational variability. Overall, this work demonstrates that oligomerization can generate electron transport behavior that cannot be inferred directly from isolated monomer properties and establishes monomer order as a design variable for molecular electronics.

title: Stepwise assembly and mechanical stability of nsP3 Helical Scaffolds in Chikungunya Virus
summary: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that replicates its genome through a viral replication complex (RC) essential for successful infection. The RC consists of four non-structural proteins: nsP1, nsP2, ns
content: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA virus that replicates its genome through a viral replication complex (RC) essential for successful infection. The RC consists of four non-structural proteins: nsP1, nsP2, nsP3, and nsP4. In this study, we focused on nsP3, which comprises three distinct domains: the alphavirus unique domain (AUD), the long and intrinsically disordered hypervariable domain (HVD), and the enzymatic macrodomain (MD). Notably, nsP3 assembles into helicoidal macrostructures, termed helical scaffolds (HSs), which are components of the CHIKV replication complex and are involved in the formation of macromolecular traps in the cytoplasm of the infected cell called Alphagranules (AGs). HSs form tubular helical scaffolds assembled through the AUD, with the MD and HVD flexibly deployed to the scaffold exterior. Despite their functional importance, the mechanisms governing HS formation remain poorly understood. Using High-Speed Atomic Force Microscopy (HS-AFM) and Electron Microscopy (EM) we achieved new findings on the structure, mechanics and assembly of these macrostructures. Our results show the nsP3 monomers follow intermediate steps before completing the assembly into full helical scaffolds, with each nsP3 domain contributing differently to this process. The macrodomain (MD) provides mechanical stability, yet it fractures under tens of piconewtons of force. This rigidity acts as a mechanical regulator that constrains the position of the HVD, which in turn mediates interactions with host factors and neighboring HSs. Through this interplay, nsP3 achieves both structural cohesion and functional adaptability, promoting the higher-order organization of HSs into honeycomb-like networks.

title: Microbubble-Assisted Bioresorbable Biphasic Scaffolds Reinforced with TiO2 Nanosheets for Oral and Maxillofacial Bone Repair: In Vitro Evaluation
summary: Abstract This study presents the development of bioresorbable biphasic scaffolds incorporating titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanostructures, specifically nanoparticles (TNPs) and nanosheets (TNSs), into a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and silk fibroi
content: Abstract This study presents the development of bioresorbable biphasic scaffolds incorporating titanium dioxide (TiO2) nanostructures, specifically nanoparticles (TNPs) and nanosheets (TNSs), into a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and silk fibroin (SF) polymeric matrix using a bubbling technique followed by freeze-drying. Both TNPs and TNSs were synthesized via a hydrothermal method. The resulting scaffolds featured two distinct layers: a porous sponge-like structure and a dense film, designed to mimic the architecture of natural bone and soft tissue interfaces in oral and maxillofacial regions. Structural characterization confirmed the successful integration of TiO2 nanostructures within the scaffold matrix. X-ray diffraction showed that both TNPs and TNSs exhibited a pure anatase phase. Compared to TNPs, the nanosheet form offered significantly improved molecular mobility and dispersion within the matrix. Additionally, TNSs-incorporated scaffolds exhibited favorable porosity, compressive strength, swelling behavior, and degradation rate. In vitro studies demonstrated enhanced proliferation of both osteoblasts and fibroblasts, particularly in the TNSs scaffolds. The anatase-phase TiO2 contributed to improved cell-material interactions and scaffold performance without significant cytotoxicity. These findings suggest that TNSs-based scaffolds hold strong potential as functional biomaterials for oral and maxillofacial tissue repair, including alveolar cleft and mandibular ridge reconstruction.

title: Two Component Polyurethane/Epoxy Composite Grouting Material: Injectability, Mechanical Properties, and Engineering Applicability
summary: ABSTRACT Traditional epoxy resin (EP) grouting materials are hindered by high brittleness, excessive shrinkage, and slow curing. To address these issues, a polyurethane/epoxy (PU‐EP) interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) composite was deve
content: ABSTRACT Traditional epoxy resin (EP) grouting materials are hindered by high brittleness, excessive shrinkage, and slow curing. To address these issues, a polyurethane/epoxy (PU‐EP) interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) composite was developed using a two‐component isocyanate system (MDI/IPDI). At the optimal PU‐EP mass ratio of 10:90, the material exhibited an initial viscosity of 218 mPa·s, a setting time of 18 min, and a volume shrinkage of only 1.75%. Compared with pure EP, tensile, compressive, impact, and flexural strengths increased by 30%, 21%, 54%, and 15%, respectively, with an adhesive strength of 4.29 MPa. Microscopic analyses revealed a well‐developed IPN structure with ductile fracture features and uniformly distributed microbubbles that relieved internal stress. Thermal stability remained adequate up to 150°C. Field tests confirmed rapid crack filling (5 mm wide, 200 mm deep) within 2 min, with no secondary cracking after 30 days and a core compressive strength of 66 MPa. This composite offers a balanced combination of low viscosity, fast curing, high strength, and low shrinkage, making it suitable for rapid concrete crack repair.

title: Capacity optimisation configuration of air–electricity–hydrogen hybrid energy storage systems incorporating advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage
summary: To improve the utilisation rate of new energy sources and establish a new type of power system centred on renewable energy, this paper designs a capacity optimisation scheme for a hybrid energy storage system that integrates advanced adiaba
content: To improve the utilisation rate of new energy sources and establish a new type of power system centred on renewable energy, this paper designs a capacity optimisation scheme for a hybrid energy storage system that integrates advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage, electrochemical energy storage and hydrogen energy storage. This study employed K-means clustering combined with the cumulative median selection method to identify representative operational scenarios. A battery capacity degradation model accounting for cycle life and an advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage system model were established, whilst incorporating mechanisms for green hydrogen production and revenue from hydrogen sales. A capacity optimisation model for the hybrid energy storage system was developed, with maximum daily comprehensive net revenue as the objective function, and a coordinated operation strategy for renewable energy and the multi-storage system was formulated. Case studies utilising wind power, photovoltaic and load data from north-western China validated the reliability and economic feasibility of the proposed system. Furthermore, the impact of different hydrogen transmission capacities and various energy storage operation strategies on system capacity allocation was quantitatively assessed.

title: Effect of High-Intensity Pulsed Ion Beam Irradiation on the Mechanical Properties and Microstructure of the AlCoCrFeNi High-Entropy Alloy
summary: Abstract The effect of high-intensity pulsed ion beam (HIPIB) irradiation on the microstructure and surface properties of equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy has been investigated at two energy densities, 0.7 and 1.5 J/cm 2 . Finite ele
content: Abstract The effect of high-intensity pulsed ion beam (HIPIB) irradiation on the microstructure and surface properties of equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy has been investigated at two energy densities, 0.7 and 1.5 J/cm 2 . Finite element simulation of the thermal field shows that both regimes produce surface melting with peak temperatures of 2596 K and 3206 K, maximum melt depths of 0.45 and 0.93 µm, and cooling rates of the order of 10 10 K/s. XRD analysis reveals that the dual-phase BCC + FCC microstructure of the as-cast alloy transforms into a predominantly BCC structure after irradiation, with the complete disappearance of the FCC (111) reflection. Energy-dispersive spectroscopy confirms compositional homogenisation of the near-surface layer. The structural changes result in a non-monotonic dependence of mechanical properties on energy density. Irradiation at 0.7 J/cm 2 increases Vickers hardness by 30%, from 648 ± 52 HV 0.05 to 839 ± 68 HV 0.05 , and reduces the specific wear rate from 2.94×10 − 4 to 8.42×10 − 5 mm 3 ·N − 1 ·m − 1 , while at 1.5 J/cm 2 both hardness and wear resistance approach the as-cast values. The results demonstrate that HIPIB irradiation is an effective tool for surface modification of high-entropy alloys, enabling phase transformation and significant tribological improvement.

title: From prediction to creation: How AI-driven design is reshaping microbial biocatalysis
summary: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate struct
content: Enzyme engineering has long relied on rational design and directed evolution, yet both remain bounded by natural enzyme space - a constraint felt acutely across the largely uncharacterised microbial world. The 2021 advent of accurate structure prediction marked an inflection point, catalysing AI methods that now extend far beyond folding. These tools are organism-agnostic; the microbial domain is their proving ground because it supplies both the uncharacterised sequence space and the expression hosts. Here we examine three stages: mining microbial sequence space; generative design, whether conditioned on structure or sequence; and machine learning-guided directed evolution. We trace the trajectory from reading the protein universe toward writing it, asking where each has delivered for microbial biocatalysis. Because published claims are hard to compare, we propose a tiered framework - catalysis, selectivity, producibility, process fit - for judging whether an AI-designed enzyme is a useful biocatalyst rather than merely a functional protein.

title: New Detections of H 2 CO and c-C 3 H 2 in Planetary Nebulae: Broadening the Organic Inventory
summary: Abstract Observations of H 2 CO and c-C 3 H 2 were conducted toward six planetary nebulae (PNs; M1-7, M1-8, M2-48, M4-9, NGC 6445, and NGC 6853) at 1, 2, and 3 mm using the Arizona Radio Observatory’s 12 m antenna and Submillimeter Telescop
content: Abstract Observations of H 2 CO and c-C 3 H 2 were conducted toward six planetary nebulae (PNs; M1-7, M1-8, M2-48, M4-9, NGC 6445, and NGC 6853) at 1, 2, and 3 mm using the Arizona Radio Observatory’s 12 m antenna and Submillimeter Telescope (SMT). H 2 CO was detected toward all six nebulae on the basis of multiple transitions: the J Ka,Kc = 2 1,2 → 1 1,1 , 2 0,2 → 1 0,1 , and 2 1,1 → 1 1,0 lines at 2 mm and the J Ka,Kc = 3 0,3 → 2 0,2 transition at 1 mm. The c-C 3 H 2 molecule was identified in three sources, M1-7, M4-9, and NGC 6445, from 2 and 3 mm transitions ( J Ka,Kc = 2 1,2 → 1 0,1 , 3 1,2 → 2 2,1 , and 4 1,4 → 3 0,3 ). These detections increase the number of PNs known to contain H 2 CO from five to 11, and for c-C 3 H 2 from four to seven. From a radiative transfer analysis, column densities of N tot (H 2 CO) ∼ 3.2 × 10 11 –1.2 × 10 13 cm −2 and N tot (c-C 3 H 2 ) ∼ 6.7 × 10 11 –6.3 × 10 12 cm −2 were determined. These values correspond to fractional abundances of f (H 2 CO/H 2 ) ∼ (0.3–2.4) × 10 −8 and f (c-C 3 H 2 /H 2 ) ∼ (1.6–6.6) × 10 −9 . M4-9 exhibits the highest abundance of each molecule. Based on all known identifications in PNs, H 2 CO appears to be present in both carbon- and oxygen-rich nebulae, whereas c-C 3 H 2 is associated with only carbon-rich types. This result appears to reflect the chemistry of the previous asymptotic giant branch phase and is consistent with chemical continuity throughout PN evolution. Within the small sample, both species show fairly constant abundances across a nebular age range of 700–12,000 yr, with no statistically significant decrease. Both H 2 CO and c-C 3 H 2 are commonly observed in diffuse clouds. Therefore, their ongoing identifications in PNs suggest chemical continuity from the late phases of stellar evolution into the formation of the diffuse interstellar medium.

title: Single-Atom-Intermediated Raman Activation (SAIRA) Mechanism on Pyridine-Adsorbed Au/g-C3N4 and Periodic Trends from a 30 d-Block Element Screening
source: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
summary: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) on single-atom platforms offers a reproducible, hotspot-free sensing paradigm, yet its fundamental mechanism remains elusive. Herein, we present a comprehensive density functional theory (DF
content: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) on single-atom platforms offers a reproducible, hotspot-free sensing paradigm, yet its fundamental mechanism remains elusive. Herein, we present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation into the “Single-Atom-Intermediated Raman Activation (SAIRA)” mechanism using a pyridine-adsorbed Au/g-C3N4 model. Ground-state electronic structure analyses reveal that the cavity-confined Au single atom acts as an indispensable polarization center that triggers strong orbital hybridization and interfacial charge transfer upon molecular adsorption. Consequently, the simulated static Raman activity yields a chemical enhancement factor about 1 order of magnitude higher than that of conventional Au20 clusters. Based on a model chemistry established through systematic benchmark evaluations of DFT functionals and basis sets, this protocol successfully captured experimental observations across various probe molecules. Importantly, extending this validated protocol to a two-dimensional descriptor map based on energetic and electronic parameters for 30 d-block elements reveals that the systems segregate into three distinct mechanistic domains, exhibiting pronounced interdomain variations in Raman enhancement. Furthermore, this 2D descriptor mapping demonstrates high robustness against alternative model chemistries. Ultimately, this work establishes electronic-level design principles not only for next-generation single-atom-based SERS technologies but also for the rational design of functional single-atom catalysts.

title: Long-term consolidation effect of polyurethane with multi-concentration on sandstone cultural heritage of the Confucian Temple in Pingxiang, Jiangxi Province
summary: The Pingxiang Confucian Temple is a provincially protected cultural relic site in Jiangxi, China. Most of its stone components have long been exposed to open-air or semi-open-air conditions and suffer from severe weathering, including surfa
content: The Pingxiang Confucian Temple is a provincially protected cultural relic site in Jiangxi, China. Most of its stone components have long been exposed to open-air or semi-open-air conditions and suffer from severe weathering, including surface dissolution, powdering, and flaking, driven by high temperature–humidity and acid-rain corrosion. In this study, a polyurethane-based penetrating consolidant was applied to sandstone relics from the temple. Different volumetric proportions of deionized water were used to prepare consolidant formulations, and penetration-consolidation experiments were conducted under open-air and semi-open-air service conditions. The consolidant performance and structural evolution were systematically evaluated through long-term monitoring of morphological changes and continuous tracking of the mechanical properties of the stone substrate. The results provide methodological references and technical guidance for penetration-consolidation treatments of sandstone relics in Jiangxi Province.

title: Interpreting elemental signatures at palm-leaf manuscript inscriptions through historical and experimental evidence using synchrotron XRF
summary: Abstract Palm-leaf manuscript traditions are diverse, but many employ a common writing procedure: text is incised with a stylus and subsequently made visible by rubbing dark material into the grooves. Elevated metal signals have been report
content: Abstract Palm-leaf manuscript traditions are diverse, but many employ a common writing procedure: text is incised with a stylus and subsequently made visible by rubbing dark material into the grooves. Elevated metal signals have been reported at such inscriptions, although their origin remains uncertain. Here, synchrotron X-ray fluorescence mapping was applied to the palm-leaf manuscript collection of the Centre for the Study of Manuscript Cultures CSMC (Hamburg) and to experimental mock-ups to examine possible contributions from stylus abrasion, blackening materials, and preservation treatments. Historical manuscripts showed that these contributions may coexist. Similar elemental enrichment at inscriptions and cracks suggests an important contribution from applied materials accumulating in surface discontinuities. Conversely, apparently unblackened inscriptions retained localized metal enrichment, consistent with a contribution associated with incision. Comparisons with binding holes and edges, which are also tool-produced features, further supported a multifactorial origin. The mock-ups did not show consistently detectable enrichment from stylus use alone. However, traditionally used materials produced localized effects: neem oil increased Fe signals, and burnt candlenut increased Mn signals. Elemental signatures therefore record complex material histories including tool-derived and applied material contributions.

title: Molecular Conductance Orbital Origins of Anti-resonance Peaks in Six-Carbon Polyene Molecular Junctions
summary: Abstract In single-molecule electronics, electron transport through a molecular junction is governed by quantum effects owing to the molecular dimensions being comparable to the electron de Broglie wavelength. In this study, we systematical
content: Abstract In single-molecule electronics, electron transport through a molecular junction is governed by quantum effects owing to the molecular dimensions being comparable to the electron de Broglie wavelength. In this study, we systematically investigate the quantum transport properties of a polyene containing six carbon atoms with different bond orders and connection sites using molecular conductance orbitals (MCOs) within the Hückel model in the wide-band approximation. The transmission spectra exhibit anti-resonance peaks characteristic of destructive quantum interference (DQI), which remain largely unaffected by the bond order within the nearest-neighbor approximation. Under specific configurations, however, bond order affects the number and location of the anti-resonance peaks. The interaction between the two closest conducting orbitals frequently dominates the DQI. In particular, when the molecule is connected through the central two carbon atoms, the nearest-neighbor and second-nearest-neighbor conducting orbitals have the most significant effects on DQI away from the Fermi level. Furthermore, for certain connected sites, none of the conductive orbitals can be ignored. The dominant conductive mechanism is elucidated using MCO phases, MCO-electrode coupling strengths, MCO energy-level alignments, quantum interference maps, and projected transmissions. These findings advance the understanding of DQIs in conjugated molecular junctions and provide a theoretical foundation for fine-tuning quantum interference and developing high-performance molecular devices.

title: Hidden Currents: A Peak-Stress Water Index for Auditing AI Data Center Sustainability and Informing Disclosure Policy
summary: Data center water use is usually reported as Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), an annual, fleet-averaged ratio of water to IT energy. WUE hides two dimensions of impact on host communities: the concentration of demand on peak summer days and
content: Data center water use is usually reported as Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), an annual, fleet-averaged ratio of water to IT energy. WUE hides two dimensions of impact on host communities: the concentration of demand on peak summer days and the scarcity of water where a facility is located. Prior work has examined these dimensions separately. We propose the Peak-Stress Water Index (PSWI), the product of annual WUE, a peaking factor β (peak-day to average-day water use), and the facility’s Baseline Water Stress (BWS) from WRI Aqueduct 4.0. We apply PSWI to an open dataset of 48 hyperscale and colocation facilities run by seven operators in North America, Europe, and Asia, using only WUE values that operators publish or that can be derived from their published totals. Because none of these operators publishes facility-level WUE, facilities inherit fleet or regional values, so PSWI isolates how location changes the burden behind the same headline number. PSWI spans a factor of about 1,500 across facilities; within one operator that applies a single fleet WUE, it differs 267-fold between Henderson, Nevada and Hamina, Finland. Company rankings by mean PSWI depart from rankings by operator WUE (Spearman ρ = 0.71), although bootstrap intervals for individual company shifts include zero. Our climate-based β is strongly correlated with BWS (r = 0.84); removing it leaves facility and company rankings nearly unchanged (ρ = 0.96 for both), so the results are driven mainly by location stress. In an idealized reallocation exercise, moving 10% of workload from the highest-to the lowest-PSWI facilities lowers aggregate PSWI by 35% (95% interval 21–46% under assumed input uncertainty), showing that impact is concentrated in a small tail. None of the audited operators publishes peak or monthly water data. We outline a facility-level disclosure framework that borrows the phase-in architecture of U.S. securities disclosure rules but could be implemented through state and local water permitting. Data and code are openly released.

title: Energetic and functional development of soil food webs along secondary succession
summary: 1. As ecosystems develop, aboveground biomass and belowground organic matter accumulate, while energy turnover declines. This trend is largely supported by vegetation studies, but remains unexplored for soil food webs that channel the major
content: 1. As ecosystems develop, aboveground biomass and belowground organic matter accumulate, while energy turnover declines. This trend is largely supported by vegetation studies, but remains unexplored for soil food webs that channel the majority of energy in terrestrial ecosystems. 2. Here, we tested whether successional theory applies to soil food webs across size-based compartments, ranging from microfauna (nematodes) to macrofauna (soil arthropods and earthworms), along a secondary succession in southwestern China, using an energy-flux approach. To assess whether forest restoration by planting follows natural succession, we also compared spruce and larch plantations with secondary birch forest of the same successional stage. 3. Supporting expectations of reduced energy turnover, the results showed an increasing animal biomass-to-energy flux ratio and a functional shift from herbivory-dominated (green) to detritivory-dominated (brown) energy channelling along succession. Soil food web compartments showed contrasting trends: macro-food webs shifted towards bacterial energy channels with decreasing predation, while micro-food webs maintained similar bacterial/fungal energy flux ratios and tended towards increasing predation. The larch plantation supported lower animal biomass than the secondary birch forest, whereas the spruce plantation did not differ. We further found that energy flux correlated positively with microbial biomass and soil animal diversity, but negatively with litter biomass during succession. 4. Overall, we expand successional theory by revealing the transformations in energy use and pathways within soil food webs along secondary succession, thereby advancing understanding of ecosystem functioning and guiding ecosystem restoration. Our results further suggest that tree plantations do not necessarily replicate the belowground development of natural succession, which should be considered in ecosystem restoration.

title: The (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide is a microbe-derived NAD + precursor that drives gut stem cell renewal
summary: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here t
content: Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide (NAD) is a critical cellular coenzyme whose decline associates with various chronic and inflammatory diseases. Improved NAD restoration may reduce disease risks and extend healthy lifespan. We report here that certain commensal bacteria including specific probiotic species produce (amide-)N-methylnicotinamide (N-MNA), which is a structural isomer of methylnicotinamide, a nicotinamide degradative metabolite. Patients with gut dysbiosis and inflammation show reduced stool N-MNA. Stable isotope tracing revealed that N-MNA can be rapidly taken up and incorporated into NAD redox reactions by intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) and non-IECs of fruit fly, mouse, and human. Genetic and pharmacological analyses suggest that N-MNA is converted to NAD + via the Preiss-Handler pathway, independent of the salvage pathway. Cell-type-specific ablation or overexpression of SIRT1, an NAD-consuming enzyme, in Drosophila , along with intestinal stem cell (ISC) lineage tracing in mice revealed that systemic N-MNA supplementation promotes ISC regeneration and gut epithelial repair. Compared to known NAD precursors, N-MNA brings a methyl group into host cells, representing a class of microbe-derived NAD precursor that stimulates the tissue regenerative power.

title: Capacity-Constrained Pathways to Formal EV Battery Recycling in China
source: Advances in management and applied economics
summary: China’s retired electric vehicle (EV) battery recycling system faces rapidly increasing end-of-life supply, persistent formal–informal competition, and uncertainty over policy withdrawal. Existing models often equate strategy probabilities
content: China’s retired electric vehicle (EV) battery recycling system faces rapidly increasing end-of-life supply, persistent formal–informal competition, and uncertainty over policy withdrawal. Existing models often equate strategy probabilities with formalization and overlook unreturned stocks, consumer channel choice, and processing capacity. This study develops a 2020–2050 system dynamics model linking a cohort–Weibull retirement module with material-conserving battery flows, channel allocation, capacity expansion, authorized integration, metal recovery, relative environmental burden, and adaptive policy withdrawal. All scenarios share a fixed 25% formal-processing share in 2025. Under current policy, the formal share reaches only 52.95% by 2050, while informal processing and unreturned stocks remain substantial. Among single pathways, subsidy plus capacity support accelerates early formalization, whereas enforcement achieves the highest nominal 2050 share (60.83%). Integration is conditional on licensed capacity: 108.50 GWh yr−1 is requested for transfer in 2050, but only 51.27 GWh yr−1 is realized. Fixed, life-cycle, and staged portfolios reach 68.32%, 65.77%, and 66.49%, respectively. Relative to the fixed portfolio, the adaptive portfolios reduce model-accounted government expenditure by 29.68% and 45.14%, with endpoint losses of 2.55 and 1.82 percentage points. Across 200 Latin-hypercube draws centered on the nominal settings, suppression is the leading single pathway in 97.5% of cases, while each portfolio exceeds the best single pathway in every draw. The results support sequential governance that combines early capacity building, persistent baseline enforcement, capacity-constrained integration, and gradual withdrawal after observable maturity conditions are met. Keywords: Retired EV batteries, Formal and informal recycling, System dynamics, Extended producer responsibility, Policy portfolio, Capacity constraint.

title: Accelerated Atmospheric Drying in Neighboring Rural Areas Across China Associated With Urban Warming
summary: Abstract Neighboring rural areas (i.e., rural zones surrounding cities) experience strong urban–rural interactions and provide critical ecosystem services, yet their responses to atmospheric drying remain poorly understood. Here, we quantif
content: Abstract Neighboring rural areas (i.e., rural zones surrounding cities) experience strong urban–rural interactions and provide critical ecosystem services, yet their responses to atmospheric drying remain poorly understood. Here, we quantify urban impacts on vapor pressure deficit (VPD) in neighboring rural areas across China by comparing station observations from neighboring rural stations (NRS) and remote rural stations (RRS, stations located in rural regions far from urban influence). During 1985–2019, 69% of cities exhibited faster VPD growth in their NRS than in their RRS, with a mean drying rate 27.5% higher than that of RRS. This disparity was more pronounced in summer, particularly within urban clusters. The NRS‐RRS temperature difference dominated VPD variations, likely attributable to the urban‐rural temperature gradient, whereby temperatures gradually decline outward from urban cores. These results reveal potential urban influence on rural atmospheric drying, highlighting ecosystem risks in neighboring rural areas and targeted adaptation needs in sustainable urban development.

title: Dual-Nitrate-Releasing Electrospun PAN Nanofiber Separators to Suppress Post-Cycle Corrosion Through Anti-Corrosive Interphase Engineering in Lithium Metal Batteries
summary: Lithium (Li) metal suffers from continuous chemical corrosion in liquid electrolytes, critically limiting the calendar life of lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Conventional anti-corrosion strategies have primarily focused on stabilizing the
content: Lithium (Li) metal suffers from continuous chemical corrosion in liquid electrolytes, critically limiting the calendar life of lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Conventional anti-corrosion strategies have primarily focused on stabilizing the initial solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), while corrosion after prolonged cycling remains insufficiently understood. Here, we demonstrate for the first time that repeated Li plating/stripping accelerates subsequent Li corrosion during rest by amplifying the electrolyte-accessible surface area and destabilizing the interphase. We define this cycling-history-dependent degradation as post-cycle corrosion, a critical pathway limiting long-term LMB performance. To address this challenge, we design an electrospun AgNO 3 /Bi(NO 3 ) 3 -embedded polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofiber separator (ABPN) as a sustained reservoir of anti-corrosive interphase precursors, implementing the first sustained-release strategy based on dual nitrate species. The continuously supplied nitrate species form a low-solubility, inorganic-rich SEI composed of Li 3 N, LiN x O y , and LiF, suppressing parasitic Li–electrolyte reactions. Concurrently, the in situ formed Li–Ag/Li 3 Bi dual-alloy interphase combines complementary alloy functions to enable uniform Li deposition, enhance interfacial structural stability, and suppress cycling-induced surface-area amplification, thereby mitigating post-cycle corrosion. Consequently, ABPN-based full cells deliver 159 mAh g −1 at 5 C and retain 73.9% capacity after 500 cycles with a 4 h rest after each charge, whereas polypropylene ( PP)-based cells retain only 55.5% after 200 cycles. This work establishes post-cycle corrosion as a critical degradation mode and advances anti-corrosion design beyond SEI stabilization toward simultaneous regulation of interphase chemistry and cycling-induced morphological evolution.

title: Postharvest senescence of broccoli in the multi-omics era: molecular mechanisms, regulatory networks, and prospects for germplasm innovation
summary: Broccoli ( Brassica oleracea var. italica ) heads are harvested as immature inflorescences whose metabolism remains vigorous after detachment, making postharvest senescence and floret yellowing the leading cause of quality loss and economic
content: Broccoli ( Brassica oleracea var. italica ) heads are harvested as immature inflorescences whose metabolism remains vigorous after detachment, making postharvest senescence and floret yellowing the leading cause of quality loss and economic devaluation. Over the past decade, the molecular dissection of broccoli senescence has progressed from single-gene expression studies to integrated multi-omics atlases spanning transcriptomes, small RNA and degradome libraries, quantitative proteomes, and metabolomes. This review synthesizes the recent literature along three axes. First, we revisit the chlorophyll degradation pathway as it operates in harvested broccoli florets (from chlorophyll b reductase ( BoNYC1 ) and pheophytinase ( BoPPH ) to pheophorbide a oxygenase ( BoPaO ), RCC reductase ( BoRCCR ), and the STAY-GREEN ( BoSGR ) master switch) and we highlight how the visible yellow phenotype additionally requires carotenoid retention and biosynthesis. Second, we organize the regulatory architecture now emerging from omics studies. Its hormonal tier is an ethylene–auxin–jasmonate–abscisic acid axis that promotes senescence and is antagonized by cytokinins, brassinosteroids, melatonin, hydrogen sulfide, and the peptide signal CLE14. Its transcriptional tier is dominated by NAC, WRKY, MYB, bHLH, ERF, and TCP factors, exemplified by the BoNAC52 – BoRBOHF module that couples hormone signals to reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. A third tier is post-transcriptional: miRNAs modulate transcript abundance to fine-tune peroxidase activity, chlorophyll biosynthesis, and ROS balance. Third, we connect mechanism to application. We map how preservation technologies (1-MCP, controlled atmospheres, UV and LED irradiation, melatonin, and CLE14) converge on defined molecular nodes. We then ask how the new genomic resources of B. oleracea — the chromosome-scale broccoli reference genome and the 27-genome pan-genome — and CRISPR/Cas9 editing, now demonstrated in broccoli, provide a realistic route toward stay-green, slow-senescing cultivars. We close by identifying six priority frontiers: cell-type-resolved atlases, epigenomic time courses, standardized multi-omics protocols, GWAS for shelf life, rationally designed editing targets, and network-level validation. Broccoli thus illustrates a general arc of postharvest biology, moving from physiology to networks and from networks to designed genotypes.

title: Participatory Multi-Criteria Optimization of Hybrid Renewable-Storage Portfolios for High-Density Data Center Infrastructure in Hot Climates
summary: This study evaluates renewable and storage capacity allocations for a 500 MW peak data centre campus operating in a generic hot climate for the 2030 planning year, using 2024 USD. The existing participatory framework combines preferences fr
content: This study evaluates renewable and storage capacity allocations for a 500 MW peak data centre campus operating in a generic hot climate for the 2030 planning year, using 2024 USD. The existing participatory framework combines preferences from 50 stakeholders, the four economic, technical, environmental and social dimensions of Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and augmented epsilon constraint portfolio optimization. The original 15 record generation dataset provides the baseline technology assessment; solar PV, wind, hydropower and geothermal are retained as campus generation options, while battery energy storage systems (BESS) and thermal energy storage (TES) are co optimized through distinct power and energy variables. Continuous IT load, cooling demand, temperature dependent efficiency, PV heat derating, storage losses and a two hour residual load reserve are represented by four six hour planning balances. The original AHP priorities remain technical 0.34, economic 0.32, environmental 0.24 and social 0.10. Recomputed hybrid portfolios have annualized supply costs of USD 274.4–438.5 million/year under declared storage and climate assumptions. Generation LCOE and electrical/thermal LCOS are reported with explicit service denominators. A solar intensive comparator uses 500.0 MW/1544.0 MWh BESS to shift daytime energy while preserving reserve. The contribution is a focused extension of the existing AHP to optimization workflow to continuous digital infrastructure and cooling services, without introducing dynamic control algorithms. Reliability and allocation stability conclusions are conditional on the stated planning assumptions.

title: In Situ Tröger's Base Scaffold Reconstruction Enables Programmable Growth of Missing‐Linker Defective Zirconium Metal‐Organic Framework Single‐Crystals
summary: ABSTRACT Defect engineering of metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) offers vast opportunities for the manipulation of their local structures and has led to extensive discoveries from fundamental knowledge to property evolution. In this context,
content: ABSTRACT Defect engineering of metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) offers vast opportunities for the manipulation of their local structures and has led to extensive discoveries from fundamental knowledge to property evolution. In this context, Zr‐MOFs, known for their exceptional structural robustness and chemical stability, are at the forefront of this rapidly evolving field. However, the development of defect chemistry in Zr‐MOFs has so far been limited to only a few examples and is generally tailored at the micro or nanocrystalline scale. In this work, we report that the in situ Tröger's base (TB) scaffold reconstruction, which occurs under the modular conditions typical for Zr‐MOF crystallization, can yield linker defective Zr‐MOF single‐crystals with sizes exceeding 300 μm. We designed three carboxylate‐functionalized V‐shaped TB ligands carrying distinct substituent (H, Me, and F). Upon crystallization with Zr 4+ ions, the methanodiazocine nucleus undergoes strap elimination reactions to produce planar diamine moieties. This skeleton reconstruction, accompanied by pronounced geometry reformation, engenders substantial lattice strain during the crystal growth, which in turn drives linker elimination and generates missing‐linker defects. The missing‐linker defects within the single‐crystals were thoroughly validated through a combination of complementary techniques. We also demonstrate that the large single‐crystals exhibit higher missing‐linker defect density than the microcrystalline powders, presumably due to the greater internal stress accumulated in the former. Moreover, the large single‐crystals with higher density of Lewis acidic Zr sites exhibit enhanced reactivity than the microcrystalline powders in the heterogeneous degradation of glyphosate (GPh), producing benign N ‐formyl glycine as the major product.

title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
summary: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developin
content: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li 3 YCl 6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm −1 ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li 3 YCl 6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO 2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g −1 with a single‐crystal LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.

title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
summary: ABSTRACT The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a c
content: ABSTRACT The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g −1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

title: Donor number determined solvent‐mediated electron transfer for electrocarboxylation of C–Br bonds with carbon dioxide
summary: Abstract The electrochemical conversion of organic bromides with carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) to valuable carboxylic acids is highly desirable in chemical industries. Researches mainly focused on catalysts, with little attention to the equally im
content: Abstract The electrochemical conversion of organic bromides with carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) to valuable carboxylic acids is highly desirable in chemical industries. Researches mainly focused on catalysts, with little attention to the equally important solvents. The donor number (DN) characterizes a solvent's tendency to donate electrons and is closely associated with electron transfer. However, few research studies can reveal its impact on electrocarboxylation reactions. As a step toward more rational solvent selection, this work investigates how DNs impact such reactions. For the model benzyl bromide substrate, optimal performance was achieved at medium DNs, with doubled yields compared to either high‐DN or low‐DN solvents. A quantitative relationship based on DNs was shown to correlate strongly with carboxylation yields. Electrochemical characterization elucidated that medium‐DN solvents determine the dynamic solvation layer construction, enhancing solvent‐mediated electron transfer efficiency. The strategy was further extended to other organic bromides, demonstrating broad applicability for C–Br bond carboxylation with CO 2 .

title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
summary: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarb
content: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non‐PAH merocyanine with pure π‐π* transition character (NBMCy‐B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P . Meanwhile, a dual‐locking strategy featuring molecular‐engineered double intramolecular H ‐bonds and a new quasi‐planar benzocycloketone (5‐methoxytetralone, 5M‐TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy‐B4/5M‐TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy‐B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual‐mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet‐yielding pathways. When doped in 5M‐TL, analogous merocyanines with different N ‐Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy‐B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short‐lived NBMCy‐B2 (green) and long‐lived B4 (red) in 5M‐TL afforded an unconventional and color‐tunable time‐dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti‐counterfeiting.

title: Hydrological dynamics shape functional space in palm communities
summary: Abstract Functional diversity reflects how species respond to environmental gradients through variation in functional traits, yet the multidimensional trait structure of tropical palm communities remains poorly understood, particularly acro
content: Abstract Functional diversity reflects how species respond to environmental gradients through variation in functional traits, yet the multidimensional trait structure of tropical palm communities remains poorly understood, particularly across hydrological gradients. Here, we quantified the functional trait space of palm communities across three contrasting ecosystems in the Colombian Orinoquia: terra firme forest, seasonally flooded forest, and permanently flooded palm swamp. We measured leaf, stem, and root traits from adult palms and constructed multidimensional functional spaces to evaluate functional richness, divergence, and trait segregation among ecosystems and species. Functional trait space differed across ecosystems and plant organs. Leaf trait space was largest in seasonally flooded forests, whereas palm swamps exhibited low leaf functional richness but high divergence. Root traits showed the strongest contraction of functional space across the flooding gradient, with palm swamps displaying the lowest richness and divergence values. Species occupied distinct regions of the multidimensional trait space, particularly for leaf and stem traits, reflecting contrasting resource-use strategies. Across ecosystems, belowground traits exhibited stronger constrained variation than aboveground traits, indicating that hydrological regimes disproportionately limit root trait variation. Our results demonstrate that hydrological filtering structures palm functional diversity in an organ-specific manner, with root traits representing the primary axis of community differentiation across the flood gradient. By integrating leaf, stem, and root traits, this study highlights how multidimensional trait approaches can reveal contrasting assembly patterns among plant organs and improve our understanding of functional organization in tropical plant communities.

title: p ‐Block Catecholates: A Century‐Old Platform for Hybrid Molecular Ferroelectrics
summary: ABSTRACT p ‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p ‐bl
content: ABSTRACT p ‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p ‐block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. A series of germanium catecholato salts, [Bu 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , [Pr 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , and [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , was synthesized to assess the influence of counter‐cation size on crystal symmetry and polar order. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a counter‐cation‐dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second‐harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance‐voltage measurements, and double‐wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p ‐block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter‐cation‐controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

title: The Use, Environmental Knowledge and Climate Change Attitudes of Australian Nurses and Midwives Regarding Nitrous Oxide
summary: ABSTRACT Aim The aim of this research was to investigate the clinical use of nitrous oxide among Australian nurses and midwives, assess their pharmacological knowledge of the gas, determine their awareness of its environmental effects and e
content: ABSTRACT Aim The aim of this research was to investigate the clinical use of nitrous oxide among Australian nurses and midwives, assess their pharmacological knowledge of the gas, determine their awareness of its environmental effects and evaluate their broader attitudes toward climate change. Background Balancing clinical efficacy with environmental sustainability is an emerging priority in acute pain management. While nitrous oxide offers rapid, reversible analgesia, its substantial ecological footprint as a greenhouse gas cannot be ignored. Nurses and midwives are well‐positioned to drive sustainable analgesic practices, yet their current utilisation and awareness of these environmental impacts require further investigation. Design A cross‐sectional survey of nurses and midwives practising in Australia. Method Australian nurses and midwives who have administered nitrous oxide as part of patient management were invited to complete a 62‐item survey. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics and qualitative responses were thematically analysed. Results Responses from 446 respondents were analysed. Pharmacological knowledge of nitrous oxide was low (median 28.6%), as was awareness of its environmental impact (median 28.6%). Respondents aged 40 and under had lower awareness of nitrous oxide's impact on climate (28.6% vs. 42.9%). Climate change beliefs and intentions were high (both 80.0%). Awareness of nitrous oxide's environmental impact explained 79% of variance in climate change belief ( F = 35.211). Conclusion Administration of nitrous oxide by nurses and midwives in Australia for acute pain management occurs across diverse healthcare settings. However, significant knowledge gaps regarding its pharmacological properties and environmental impact highlight an urgent need for targeted education, clinical guidance and sustainable practice initiatives. Addressing these gaps will empower clinicians to balance patient comfort with environmental stewardship, supporting healthcare delivery that is both high quality and ecologically responsible. Implications for the Profession and/or Patient Care This study highlights a critical gap in knowledge regarding both the pharmacology and environmental impact of nitrous oxide among Australian nurses and midwives. While nitrous oxide remains a valued, safe option for acute pain management, addressing its significant ecological footprint requires bridging this knowledge gap through education, clear clinical guidance and sustainable practice initiatives. Effective pain management must balance patient comfort and clinical safety with environmental stewardship to deliver clinically effective, ecologically responsible care. Impact This study investigated the clinical utilisation of nitrous oxide for acute pain management among Australian nurses and midwives, while evaluating their pharmacological knowledge and awareness of its environmental implications. title: Exercise reshapes cellular immunity toward anti-inflammation and diminishes CCR4 levels on LFA-1αhighCD4+ T cells in multiple sclerosis
summary: Multiple sclerosis (MS) represents a multifaceted neuroinflammatory disease for which regular exercise is now recommended by many healthcare institutions. Although preclinical studies indicate robust immunomodulatory effects of exercise, ev
content: Multiple sclerosis (MS) represents a multifaceted neuroinflammatory disease for which regular exercise is now recommended by many healthcare institutions. Although preclinical studies indicate robust immunomodulatory effects of exercise, evidence from human studies is lacking. In this randomized controlled trial, persons with MS (pwMS) were assigned to three months of high-intensity interval training or a passive control condition, with outcomes assessed at baseline, after intervention, and a fourweek follow-up. Additionally, a healthy matched control group was included. Besides exercise-induced sustained increases in physical fitness, systemic inflammation was diminished and the Treg-to-TH17.1 ratio improved after exercise. Untargeted proteomic analysis of peripheral blood mononuclear cells covering >7000 proteins revealed an exercise-induced decrease in proteins implicated in inflammatory diseases (i.e., MTHFD2). This was supported by inferred transcription factor activity analysis, which indicated enhanced polarization of immune cells toward anti-inflammatory phenotypes at follow-up. Using flow cytometry, we identified an LFA-1αhighCD4+ T-cell subset that was associated with disease biomarkers and exhibited increased CCR4 expression compared to healthy matched subjects which was reduced after exercise. Our findings significantly expand knowledge of how exercise training exerts immediate and sustained immunomodulatory effects in pwMS and thereby strengthens the mechanistic rationale for exercise recommendations made by healthcare professionals.

title: A game of two leaf sides: Abaxial vs Adaxial stomata
summary: Abstract Stomata are of the utmost importance to plant function, growth and productivity, as they enable gas exchange for photosynthesis, as well as facilitate transpiration for evaporative cooling and nutrient uptake. The balance between t
content: Abstract Stomata are of the utmost importance to plant function, growth and productivity, as they enable gas exchange for photosynthesis, as well as facilitate transpiration for evaporative cooling and nutrient uptake. The balance between these two processes depends on stomatal density, size and behaviour, which together determine stomatal conductance and intrinsic water use efficiency. There has been great progress in elucidating the genetic pathways that govern the development of stomatal patterning and density, however, although many species have stomata on both surfaces of the leaf, traditionally the importance of adaxial stomata has been largely overlooked in the literature. Recent studies have started to evaluate the impact of the varying contribution of adaxial (AD) vs abaxial (AB) stomata to gas exchange, the costs and benefits of different AD:AB ratios for different species and growth conditions, as well as differences in sensitivity to environmental cues between the two surfaces. Our review focuses on the environmental drivers of differential stomatal patterning and physiological function and the potential to manipulate surface-specific stomatal patterning independently to optimize leaf gas exchange for crops growing in different environments.

title: Concluding Remarks: Tying the Threads
summary: Maritime decarbonisation is often framed as a techno-economic challenge, with most efforts toward a green future focusing on reducing the sector’s carbon output. There is no shortage of innovation in this regard, and the drive to make the t
content: Maritime decarbonisation is often framed as a techno-economic challenge, with most efforts toward a green future focusing on reducing the sector’s carbon output. There is no shortage of innovation in this regard, and the drive to make the transition happen is strong: the process demands the development of cleaner fuel alternatives and the advancement of propulsion system engineering, complemented by economic incentives, like the formulation of emissions standards or the establishment of pricing mechanisms. The framing is foundational, but it does not quite capture the whole picture. It focuses on technology and business; while, like all global industries, the maritime sector stands on the shoulders of people who perform the work and are most affected by structural changes. If the transition is going to last, it needs to account for its effects on people and communities. Nonetheless, the existing literature has not adequately addressed the interplay between climate policy and social equity. The works in this book aim to fill this gap in the literature by offering perspectives on maritime decarbonisation from the viewpoint of people, through the lens of climate justice. One recurring theme is that maritime decarbonisation is profoundly human.

title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
source: UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
summary: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substr
content: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

title: Wildfire and Fuel Treatments in Utah: A Practical Guide and Outcomes From an Oak-Maple Ecosystem
summary: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can
content: Wildfire is a natural part of Utah’s landscapes, but as wildfires become more extreme and communities continue to expand into wildland areas, it is increasingly important to understand how wildfires behave and how their negative effects can be mitigated. One way to reduce wildfire risks and protect life, property, and ecosystem services is through fuel treatments — actions that reduce the amount and arrangement of flammable vegetation through mechanical removal, wildland fire, or other methods. Information on wildfire behavior and fuel treatments is abundant but often scattered, ecosystem-specific and difficult to access. In addition, most research in the Western U.S. has focused on conifer forests, leaving other vegetation types understudied. This research addresses these gaps by summarizing wildfire and fuel treatment information for Utah and examining how fuels treatments and wildfire affect wildlands dominated by Gambel oak and bigtooth maple. Chapter II presents a practical guide to wildfire and fuel management in Utah. It explains how fire is influenced by vegetation, weather, and terrain, and describes the most common methods used to reduce fuels in Utah. Treatments can be applied alone or in combination to reduce fire risk, reduce fire severity, or improve ecosystem health. The guide also highlights planning considerations and resources available from state and federal agencies. Chapter III examines what happens to vegetation after mechanical fuel treatments and subsequent wildfire in an oak-maple ecosystem. We studied 112 plots across treated and untreated, burned and unburned areas. Overall, woody regeneration was similar across treatments and fire history, but unburned, untreated areas had the most aboveground biomass and burned, treated areas had the least. Plant diversity increased after fire, and treated areas tended to have more non-native plants. These findings show that treatments and wildfire can have complex effects on vegetation, influencing both recovery and long-term ecosystem health. Together, these chapters improve public understanding of wildfire and fuel management strategies and provide land managers with post-fire insights to guide future treatments in oak–maple ecosystems.

title: Balancing Root-Zone Oxygenation and Rhizosphere Stability: The Impact of Aeration and Hypoxia on Hydroponic Plant Growth
summary: As the global population and food demand continue to increase, growers must look to innovative and sustainable methods for plant cultivation. Hydroponics is a popular method of sustainable plant cultivation where plant roots are suspended o
content: As the global population and food demand continue to increase, growers must look to innovative and sustainable methods for plant cultivation. Hydroponics is a popular method of sustainable plant cultivation where plant roots are suspended over a liquid nutrient solution. Hydroponics uses less water compared to traditional agriculture because there is no evaporation or solution runoff. It also maximizes land use, requires fewer pesticides and herbicides, and enables year-round cultivation in controlled environments. However, indoor hydroponic systems rely on artificial lighting, which has higher energy costs than traditional farming methods. Optimizing growing conditions is therefore critical to ensure long-term economic and environmental sustainability. Oxygen, which plants require for cellular respiration, is taken up by plant roots and can quickly become limited in hydroponic solutions due to low solubility and rapid uptake. This research ultimately aims to explore which plants can tolerate low oxygen in hydroponic solutions and explores a new method for quantifying low oxygen stress experienced by plants over a growing period. The best practices for supplying oxygen to roots is also examined by manipulating aeration-induced agitation to understand its impact on plant nutrient uptake and growth.

title: From Coding to Creativity: Integrating Design Thinking into IT and Technology Education
source: JETech: Journal of Education and Technology
summary: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the fiv
content: This study examines how the integration of Design Thinking into Information Technology (IT) and technology education can bridge technical programming skills and creative, human-centered problem-solving. Specifically, it explores how the five stages of Design Thinking empathizing, defining, ideating, prototyping, and testing shape students’ creative thinking, active engagement, and collaborative learning experiences. A qualitative research approach was employed, involving teachers, students, and school principals as key informants. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, classroom observations, and documentation of learning activities, then analyzed thematically to identify recurring patterns in teaching practices and student experiences. The findings indicate that Design Thinking creates opportunities for students to move beyond coding procedures toward developing digital solutions that respond to real users’ needs. Through collaborative ideation, iterative prototyping, and feedback-based testing, students demonstrate greater involvement in learning, explore alternative solutions, and communicate their ideas more actively. The approach also provides opportunities to develop empathy, creativity, collaboration, and a willingness to experiment with and revise initial designs. Meanwhile, teachers assume a facilitative role by guiding inquiry, supporting experimentation, and connecting technical knowledge with authentic problems. This study highlights the pedagogical value of integrating Design Thinking into technology education as a framework for connecting computational competencies with human-centered innovation. Its implications emphasize the importance of designing learning activities that balance technical proficiency, creative exploration, and meaningful student participation.
