title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
summary: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combini
content: Abstract Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

title: AI-powered capabilities are associated with green new product development through exploratory and exploitative pathways
summary: Abstract Purpose – This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which AI‑powered capabilities influence green NPD in manufacturing firms. Specifically, it examines the dual mediating roles of green exploratory and green exploitativ
content: Abstract Purpose – This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which AI‑powered capabilities influence green NPD in manufacturing firms. Specifically, it examines the dual mediating roles of green exploratory and green exploitative, and tests whether the mediating effect of exploration is stronger than that of exploitation in the AI‑green NPD link. Design/methodology/approach – Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a dual mediation framework distinguishing green exploratory (sensing‑driven opportunity identification) from green exploitative (seizing/transforming‑driven process refinement). Hypotheses are tested using survey data from 333 Chinese manufacturing firms across five high‑priority sectors. Hierarchical regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4; 5,000 resamples) are employed. Findings – The results show that both green exploratory and green exploitative significantly mediate the positive relationship between AI‑powered capabilities and green NPD. Critically, the indirect effect via green exploratory is significantly stronger than that via green exploitative, supporting asymmetric mediation. The full model explains 54% of the variance in green NPD. Originality/value – This study makes three key contributions. First, it unpacks the mediation black box between AI and green NPD by specifying two distinct process architectures. Second, it challenges the “balance assumption” of ambidexterity theory by demonstrating the primacy of exploratory mediation in AI‑enabled green innovation contexts, thereby extending dynamic capabilities theory. Third, it provides a rigorous methodological template for testing dual and asymmetric mediation, offering actionable guidance for managers, AI vendors, and policymakers.

title: Urinary metal exposure and type 2 diabetes mellitus: the potential mediating role of biological aging in older adults
summary: Abstract The global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasing, and environmental exposures may contribute to diabetes susceptibility. Metals are widespread environmental contaminants associated with metabolic disorders; howeve
content: Abstract The global burden of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is increasing, and environmental exposures may contribute to diabetes susceptibility. Metals are widespread environmental contaminants associated with metabolic disorders; however, the role of aging-related processes in this association remains unclear. A total of 843 participants were enrolled. Urinary concentrations of six metals (Pb, Zn, Mn, Cr, As, and Co) were measured, and phenotypic age was calculated based on nine biomarkers. Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic spline models, weighted quantile sum regression, and exploratory mediation analysis were performed. Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr exposures were significantly associated with increased T2DM risk (all P < 0.05). Mixed metal exposure was also associated with higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.515, 95% CI: 1.277–1.884). Additionally, Pb, Zn, Mn, and Cr were positively associated with phenotypic age, and each one-year increase in phenotypic age was associated with a 39.5% higher T2DM risk (OR = 1.395, 95% CI: 1.323–1.471). Phenotypic age may partially explain the associations between metal exposure and T2DM risk, with estimated mediation proportions of 10.9%–22.2%. Urinary metal exposure was associated with increased T2DM risk and higher phenotypic age. Phenotypic aging may represent a potential pathway linking environmental metal exposure with diabetes susceptibility.

title: A decision support framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration through process-based ecosystem modeling and optimization
summary: Wetland restoration is increasingly recognized as a nature-based climate solution, but effective planning requires balancing nonlinear ecological responses with economic and implementation constraints. We propose a conceptual and computatio
content: Wetland restoration is increasingly recognized as a nature-based climate solution, but effective planning requires balancing nonlinear ecological responses with economic and implementation constraints. We propose a conceptual and computational framework for climate-oriented coastal wetland restoration that embeds process-based ecosystem modeling within restoration optimization. Restoration strategies are represented as portfolios combining discrete intervention choices with continuous decisions on implementation intensity and spatial allocation. A vertically resolved ecohydrological model simulates soil organic carbon dynamics and decomposition-driven CO$_2$ and CH$_4$ emissions, allowing environmental outcomes to arise from the interaction between restoration decisions and ecosystem processes.The framework is illustrated through a benchmark analysis and an application to the Ebro Delta. The benchmark shows that alternative objective specifications select distinct interior and corner solutions from the same ecological trade-off. In the Ebro Delta application, imposing a budget constraint reallocates restored area from the deep-rooted vegetation type toward the less expensive shallow-rooted type, while maintaining high vegetation densities and compliance with the methane target, although the CO$_2$ target is exceeded. Global sensitivity analysis identifies the density and spatial allocation of the deep-rooted vegetation type as the main drivers of restoration performance.The results show that restoration outcomes depend not only on total vegetation cover but also on portfolio composition and implementation intensity. The proposed framework provides a flexible methodology for integrating process-based ecological models into restoration planning under alternative environmental objectives and resource constraints.

title: Assurance and ESG rating divergence can limit the informational value of sustainability disclosure mandates
summary: Abstract Regulators increasingly treat disclosure quantity as the principal policy lever, assuming that more sustainability disclosure yields better-informed investors and more efficient capital allocation. This conceptual paper argues that
content: Abstract Regulators increasingly treat disclosure quantity as the principal policy lever, assuming that more sustainability disclosure yields better-informed investors and more efficient capital allocation. This conceptual paper argues that the assumption is misspecified. Disclosure moves investor beliefs only insofar as it is credible, and credibility is manufactured downstream of the reporting entity, by assurance providers who verify and rating agencies who aggregate. We develop the construct of the credibility wedge, the gap between the quantity of sustainability information a firm discloses and the reliability investors attach to it. Drawing on costly state verification, cheap-talk and signalling models, ambiguity-based asset pricing and institutional theory, we specify a three-layer architecture of preparer, assurer and rater, each with a distinct failure mode. Twelve propositions connect regime design to the wedge, and the wedge to belief revision, the cost of capital and capital allocation. A two-by-two typology is derived and applied to the four architectures observable in 2026: the narrowed European regime, jurisdictions adopting IFRS S1 and S2, the United States, and India’s BRSR Core. As the wedge grows, the marginal informational return to additional disclosure tends to zero, implying that verification and rating infrastructure must be built before disclosure scope is widened. India offers an unusually favourable research setting, and eight estimable models are specified. For the 2030 Agenda, target 12.6 and its report-counting indicator track disclosure volume rather than decision-useful information, making credible verification a precondition for reporting to advance SDGs 12 and 13.

title: Development of chitosan based multifunctional nanostructured systems for cartilage tissue engineering
summary: In the present work, we report the design and development of multifunctional chitosan (CS)-based hybrid porous nanocomposites (CPIQ I-III) through incorporation of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) within the CS matrix, followed by functional tag
content: In the present work, we report the design and development of multifunctional chitosan (CS)-based hybrid porous nanocomposites (CPIQ I-III) through incorporation of poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) within the CS matrix, followed by functional tagging with magnetite (Fe₃O₄) nanoparticles as a magnetic unit and carbon dots (C-QDs) as a fluorescent unit for cartilage tissue engineering application. The synergistic integration of polymeric and inorganic components enhanced mechanical stability, structural integrity, and antibacterial performance while generating a highly porous architecture that mimics native cartilage extracellular matrix. Among the developed formulations, CPIQ II was selected as the optimized formulation based on an overall assessment of its physicochemical, morphological, mechanical, porosity, antibacterial, and biological properties, rather than mechanical performance alone. The incorporation of Fe₃O₄ nanoparticles and C-QDs further enabled bimodal imaging, facilitating non-invasive visualization and monitoring. In addition, real-time in vitro chondrocyte proliferation and adhesion studies have been conducted to evaluate cytocompatibility and tissue regeneration potential. Overall, this study developed an advanced, multifunctional carbohydrate-based hybrid scaffold capable of supporting cartilage regeneration while enabling simultaneous imaging and healing monitoring, offering a promising platform for next-generation tissue engineering applications.

title: Linking Rural Road Infrastructure and Supply Chains: A Bibliometric Analysis and Thematic Interpretation
summary: This study reviews how transport infrastructure, especially rural roads, improves supply chain performance and economic development in developing regions. The literature shows efficient systems cut logistics costs and time, streamline flows
content: This study reviews how transport infrastructure, especially rural roads, improves supply chain performance and economic development in developing regions. The literature shows efficient systems cut logistics costs and time, streamline flows from production to markets, integrate rural areas into national and international markets, and expand access to services. Among six themes explored, supply chain management and sustainable transport infrastructure emerge as prominent research trends. Thus, the recommended future work is to develop multidimensional models, prioritize sustainable practices, and adopt advanced technologies, including recycled materials and smart transport systems, supported by multidisciplinary collaboration across engineering, environmental science, IT, economics, and public policy.

title: Application of spectral preprocessing and machine learning models for discriminating nitrogen levels in cucumber production
summary: Nitrogen is one of the most essential macronutrients for plant growth, and its improper management can reduce fertilizer use efficiency while causing significant economic and environmental consequences. In this study, a hyperspectral imagin
content: Nitrogen is one of the most essential macronutrients for plant growth, and its improper management can reduce fertilizer use efficiency while causing significant economic and environmental consequences. In this study, a hyperspectral imaging–based machine learning framework was developed and evaluated to classify different nitrogen fertilizer levels in cucumber leaves (cv. Super Arshiya-F1). Nitrogen treatments consisted of 30%, 60%, and 90% additional nitrogen applied to a nutrient solution with a base concentration of 2 g L⁻¹. Seventy-two hours after treatment application, a total of 300 leaves were collected from the treated plants, and hyperspectral images were acquired in the spectral range of 400–1100 nm, producing 327 spectral bands for each sample. To enhance signal quality and examine the influence of spectral preprocessing on class separability, three preprocessing techniques—Savitzky–Golay filtering, Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC), and Gaussian normalization—were applied exclusively to the training dataset and subsequently transferred to the independent test set. Three machine learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Decision Tree (DT), were evaluated using a 75/25 training–testing split along with five-fold cross-validation for model optimization. The results demonstrated that SVM consistently achieved the highest classification performance across all scenarios. The best results were obtained without preprocessing and with Gaussian normalization, both reaching an overall accuracy of 94%, an F1-score of approximately 0.94, and a ROC–AUC exceeding 0.98. In contrast, LDA showed moderate performance, while DT yielded the lowest classification accuracy. These findings highlight the strong potential of integrating hyperspectral imaging with SVM for accurate discrimination of nitrogen levels and for supporting efficient nutrient management in crop production systems.

title: A tree peony TCP transcription factor, PrTCP4, acts as a negative regulator of seed oil accumulation
summary: Seed oils are essential dietary sources of fatty acids (FAs) and serve as important feedstocks for industrial and bioenergy applications. However, the transcriptional networks governing their accumulation in plant seeds remain largely elusi
content: Seed oils are essential dietary sources of fatty acids (FAs) and serve as important feedstocks for industrial and bioenergy applications. However, the transcriptional networks governing their accumulation in plant seeds remain largely elusive. We previously identified an INDETERMINATE DOMAIN (IDD) transcription factor, PrIDD7, as a negative regulator of oil deposition in tree peony. Here, our work reveals TEOSINTE BRANCHED1/CYCLOIDEA/PROLIFERATING CELL FACTOR4 (PrTCP4), a nucleus‑localized TCP family TF that physically interacts with PrIDD7. Transient overexpression of PrTCP4 in tobacco leaves and stable overexpression in Arabidopsis seeds significantly reduced oil content. In contrast, silencing of endogenous PrTCP4 in tree peony seeds increased oil accumulation and was accompanied by increased expression of multiple genes governing FA biosynthesis and triacylglycerol assembly. Further transcriptional regulation assays demonstrated that PrTCP4 repressed transcription of PHOSPHOLIPID:DIACYLGLYCEROL ACYLTRANSFERASE , a key acyltransferase gene, and that interaction with PrIDD7 significantly potentiated this repressive activity. Our findings uncover PrTCP4 as a novel suppressor of seed oil accumulation and demonstrate the synergistic reinforcement of PrTCP4‑mediated repression by PrIDD7, thereby advancing our understanding of oil accumulation regulatory networks and providing a valuable target gene for improving oilseed crops.

title: Structure and photophysical properties of copper(I) photosensitizers: a computational study of substituent effects
summary: Abstract Context: Developing efficient and sustainable photosensitizers is crucial for advancing solar energy conversion and light-driven chemical processes. Ruthenium(II) and iridium(III) complexes have traditionally dominated this field d
content: Abstract Context: Developing efficient and sustainable photosensitizers is crucial for advancing solar energy conversion and light-driven chemical processes. Ruthenium(II) and iridium(III) complexes have traditionally dominated this field due to their favorable photophysical properties, but their high cost has prompted the search for alternatives using earth-abundant metals. Copper(I) complexes are promising because they are cost-effective, have a tunable electronic structure, and feature a $$d^{10}$$ d 10 configuration that avoids low-lying metal-centered excited states. However, further improvements are needed to match the performance of Ru(II) and Ir(III) complexes, with ligand engineering playing a key role. Although there has been progress, the systematic effect of R substituents on the N $$^\wedge $$ ∧ N R ligand in heteroleptic Cu(N $$^\wedge $$ ∧ N R )(NacNac) complexes remains underexplored. Methods: We investigated a series of Cu(I) complexes of the type Cu(N $$^\wedge $$ ∧ N R ) (NacNac Me ), where N $$^\wedge $$ ∧ N is 2,2 $$'$$ ′ -biquinoline and NacNac is $$\beta $$ β -diketiminate, using electronic structure calculations. The N $$^\wedge $$ ∧ N R ligand was systematically substituted with R groups including -NH $$_2$$ 2 , -OH, -CH $$_3$$ 3 , -H, -Cl, -COOCH $$_3$$ 3 , and -CF $$_3$$ 3 to examine how these modifications affect the structure and photophysical properties of copper(I) photosensitizers. Ground- and excited-state properties were evaluated using density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT), with excited-state character quantified using the TheoDORE program. We analyzed structural parameters, frontier orbital energies, and electronic transitions to correlate substituent electronic character with photophysical behavior. Local energy decomposition (LED) analyses based on DLPNO-CCSD(T) calculations were also performed to study metal-ligand interactions. The results indicate that strong electron-withdrawing groups such as -COOCH $$_3$$

title: Energysheds and the Urban Energy Transition: A Method for Assessing Spatial Imbalances in Energy Flow
summary: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address th
content: Abstract Urban areas are facing the challenges of transitioning toward a low-carbon society as a response to climate change. However, the benefits and burdens of this energy transition are not evenly distributed across cities. To address this disparity, the concept of energy justice has emerged. The issue of urban energy justice can be understood as a manifestation of geographical energy disparities where energy-consuming regions enjoy significant benefits, while energy producing regions suffer from externalities. In this paper, we propose a method that utilizes the notion of “energyshed” to align city energy consumption with power plant energy generation, addressing geographical energy (im)balances. The proposed method maps the spatial supply–demand relationships between regions and power plants without relying on proprietary algorithms or territory-specific cutoff distances. Although spatial imbalance alone does not establish energy injustice, the resulting energysheds provide a diagnostic basis for identifying energy-generating regions that bear disproportionate burdens and for informing a fairer allocation of resources during the energy transition.

title: 2026 FABLE Calculator UK UP51 v9.1.6OA
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The FABLE Calculator (FABLE-C) is an open tool created in 2018 for the FABLE Consortium . Since its launch, it has been developed, regularly updated and improved through the release of update packages by the FABLE Secretariat in collaborati
content: The FABLE Calculator (FABLE-C) is an open tool created in 2018 for the FABLE Consortium . Since its launch, it has been developed, regularly updated and improved through the release of update packages by the FABLE Secretariat in collaboration with members of the FABLE Consortium - further documentation here. This version of the FABLE Calculator for the UK builds on a version created by the FABLE Secretariat on 01 2025 including all update packages until 51 and pre-filled with data for the UK from available global and national databases. The UK version of the FABLE calculator contains many additions and customisations, including: Land area data from UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology Land Cover Map UK-specific carbon stock changes for land use transitions Grassland areas and associated livestock production divided into ‘intensive’, ‘extensive’ and ‘conservation grazing’ (on protected extensively grazed grassland) Forest area split into semi-natural forests and conifer plantations Area classes added covering agroforestry, hedgerows, shelterbelts and species-rich arable field margins Emissions savings from restoration of degraded peatland included (though not from restoration of cropland, grassland or plantation forest on peat soil) Several scenarios inferred from national policy aims and Government communications. All the update packages which have been released by the FABLE Secretariat until update package 51 have been implemented by the authors. This version of the UK FABLE calculator is intended for open access release for users to explore how it operates and investigate their own pathways of interest. The accompanying Getting Started document does not provide an exhaustive documentation or explanation of all aspects of FABLE, but intends to give a sufficient introduction for users to get started. More detailed documentation, tutorials and training materials on the generic FABLE Calculator are available at: https://fableconsortium.org/tools/fablecalculators/ The creators are part of the FABLE team for the UK, more information can be found here.

title: Coordinated Economic Growth and Decarburization in Jiangsu Using an Integrated MOO–CCD Framework
source: Journal of Environmental and Energy Economics
summary: Economic growth, carbon reduction, and environmental stewardship may all be achieved at once via the use of an optimization technique that takes trade-offs and multiple target progressions into account. Without fully grasping the complex in
content: Economic growth, carbon reduction, and environmental stewardship may all be achieved at once via the use of an optimization technique that takes trade-offs and multiple target progressions into account. Without fully grasping the complex interplay of financial, climatic, environmental, and resource implications, many current regional MOO studies aim for compromise solutions. The creation of a MOO and CCD framework in the Jiangsu Province, China, is the main subject of this study. From 2018 to 2030, we can see potential pathways for energy transition and company reorganization by analyzing eleven indicators: GDP, employment, water consumption, CO2, sulfur dioxide, NOx, PM, CO2, chemical oxygen demand, ammonia nitrogen and solid waste rounding it off. The study's basis is an input-output model with 47 components. Numerous factors are considered, including electricity-related situations, resource and emission coefficients from the past, and more. As a starting point for coordination, CCD ranks and evaluates potential MOO solutions once the optimal-point method has standardized the reduction and maximization objectives. All three scenarios put yearly GDP growth at 6.8%, with the precise number falling anywhere from 6.7% to 7.0%. We need to be more transparent about the moral judgments and assumptions that drive these changes because of the potential impact they have on the environment. There will be major shifts in the energy mix and the make-up of the industrial sector, and we need to be prepared for that. A more appropriate use of this method would be in scenario analysis rather than in making an exact forecast. Adaptive methods, such as sustainable alternatives, higher industrial advancements, and integrated governance, may replace strict annual requirements in policymaking.

title: Integrated simultaneous fermentation–pervaporation for intensified bioethanol production and recovery in a corn stover cascade biorefinery
summary: Corn stover was valorized through an integrated cascade biorefinery combining subcritical water pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, alcoholic fermentation, and pervaporation for intensified bioethanol production and recovery. Subcritical wa
content: Corn stover was valorized through an integrated cascade biorefinery combining subcritical water pretreatment, enzymatic hydrolysis, alcoholic fermentation, and pervaporation for intensified bioethanol production and recovery. Subcritical water treatment effectively solubilized the hemicelluloses while increasing cellulose accessibility in the solid residue. This enabled glucose yields of approximately 80% after 24 h of enzymatic hydrolysis. The resulting hydrolysate was then used in two strategies for the production and recovery of bioethanol. In the first one, the glucose-rich liquid was efficiently fermented by Saccharomyces cerevisiae, achieving complete glucose consumption within 15 h and an ethanol yield of 91%. Subsequently, ethanol was recovered through pervaporation, where silicone membranes were identified as the most suitable option due to their superior permeation performance. A novel integrated simultaneous fermentation–pervaporation (SFP) approach was developed as the second strategy to intensify bioethanol production and recovery by coupling both processes in a single operation. Operating the hybrid process at 38 °C substantially enhanced ethanol removal, allowing 98% of the produced ethanol to be recovered within only 15.3 h, compared with 60% recovery achieved by the sequential strategy. SFP at 38 °C achieved the highest overall yield, reaching 97% and demonstrated that integrating fermentation and pervaporation at this temperature effectively improved ethanol recovery and process productivity, providing a promising approach for sustainable lignocellulosic biorefineries. Graphical abstract

title: Study of the operation of the tractor diesel fuel supply system on reverse fuel emulsions.
summary: BACKGROUND: The use of mixed fuel in diesel engines, including renewable ethanol-based fuels, contributes to the expansion of the fuel base. This factor is relevant in the context of the transition of the Russian Federation to a low-carbon
content: BACKGROUND: The use of mixed fuel in diesel engines, including renewable ethanol-based fuels, contributes to the expansion of the fuel base. This factor is relevant in the context of the transition of the Russian Federation to a low-carbon model of development and reduction of emissions of harmful substances. Studies confirm the effect of ethanol supplementation on engine performance and emission parameters. In diesel engines, the fuel combustion process is one of the main points characterizing the efficiency of the power plant. Mathematical relationships are considered, taking into account the influence of physicochemical parameters of mixed fuel on the efficiency and stability of fuel supply. AIMS: Determine the area of limit values of the surface tension of fuel containing ethanol additive on the influence of the parameters of the injection and spraying process in the combustion chamber of a diesel engine. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A method has been developed for mathematically describing the area of the limit value of the surface tension of fuel with ethanol additives. Comparative bench tests were carried out using a mechanically driven M107-CR installation and a FD-22.455.1112010-50 fuel injector used in D-245.5S2 tractor diesels. In the transparent chamber of the stand, the injection moment was recorded in accordance with the technical requirements. To monitor pressure in the fuel line, a SS302 sensor is installed through the adapter. The signal was transmitted through the IFM Electronic DN1031 amplifier to the NI COMPACT DAQ system and analyzed using the National Instruments software. RESULTS: The proposed mathematical model effectively estimates the maximum allowable surface tension of fuel with the addition of ethanol under the condition of optimal operation of the standard fuel supply system of a tractor diesel engine. The results of studies with the addition of ethanol in the range of 0% to 60% are presented. An analysis of comparative bench tests showed that the operation of the FD-22.455.1112010-50 nozzle on fuel with an ethanol content of more than 40% does not comply with GOST 10579-2017. CONCLUSIONS: A mathematical model is considered and presented, which makes it possible to quantify the maximum permissible value of the surface tension of fuel with the addition of ethanol, at which optimal spraying is ensured. Based on the analysis of a mathematical model, an assessment was made of the operation of the fuel supply system in a tractor diesel engine. The results of the study can be used to develop new fuel compositions with improved performance, as well as to optimize injection systems in diesel engines, which contributes to their energy efficiency and environmental safety.

title: DECOUPLING OF ECONOMIC GROWTH AND CO₂ EMISSIONS IN THE PHILIPPINES: AN APPLICATION OF THE TAPIO MODEL, 1990–2022
source: International Journal of Progressive Research in Engineering Management and Science
summary: Whether a growing economy can reduce its carbon emissions is central to climate policy in developing countries.This study examined the relationship between real GDP and fossil CO₂ emissions in the Philippines from 1990 to 2022 using the Tap
content: Whether a growing economy can reduce its carbon emissions is central to climate policy in developing countries.This study examined the relationship between real GDP and fossil CO₂ emissions in the Philippines from 1990 to 2022 using the Tapio decoupling model, supported by Mann-Kendall trend tests and a decomposition of emissions into economic activity, energy intensity, and the carbon intensity of energy.Data were taken from the Global Carbon Budget 2025, the Maddison Project Database 2023, and international energy statistics, as compiled by Our World in Data.Over the whole period, GDP grew by 345% and CO₂ emissions by 270%, giving an elasticity of 0.78, or weak decoupling.The annual results, however, show three distinct phases.In the 1990s, emissions grew faster than the economy in five of ten years.From 2001 to 2010, the country achieved strong decoupling in four years and weak decoupling in three, as energy use per unit of GDP fell by 36%.From 2011 to 2022, there was no year of strong decoupling, and the period elasticity returned to about 1.0, meaning emissions again grew as fast as the economy.Decomposition shows that over 1990-2022, falling energy intensity (-32%) offset part of the effect of economic growth, but rising carbon intensity of energy (+22%), driven by coal, worked against decoupling.The findings indicate that the Philippines has not yet achieved lasting decoupling and that further gains depend on reducing the carbon content of its energy supply, particularly in electricity generation.

title: A Double-Excitation Intrinsically Dual Emissive Carbon Dot Platform Enables Multi-Channel Sensitive Detection and Imaging of Common Pesticides in Live Models
summary: Abstract Carbon dot sensors often couple one excitation condition to one analyte and one output, limiting information from a single probe. Here, we report intrinsically dual-emissive carbon dots (De-CDs) whose two excitation windows partiti
content: Abstract Carbon dot sensors often couple one excitation condition to one analyte and one output, limiting information from a single probe. Here, we report intrinsically dual-emissive carbon dots (De-CDs) whose two excitation windows partition complementary sensing functions. Under 365 nm excitation, Hg2+ quenches the 450 and 680 nm emissions and clothianidin restores them, enabling sequential on-off-on determination by ratiometric fluorescence and a complementary UV−Vis response at 441 nm. The fluorescence channel quantified Hg2+ over 0.0116−12 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0116 μmol L−1), while clothianidin showed piecewise calibration up to 45 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0031 μmol L−1); UV−Vis LODs were 0.0095 and 0.0010 μmol L−1. The dual-channel design enables simultaneous utilization of fluorescent and UV wavelengths, thereby reducing interference and enhancing selectivity during detection. Under 420 nm excitation, a red-emission redistribution quantified Zn2+ over 0.0157−3.5 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0157 μmol L−1) and provided a zineb calibration over 0.0102−9 μmol L−1 (LOD = 0.0102 μmol L−1). Hg2+ forms ground-state complexes causing fluorescence quenching, and clothianidin competitively displaces Hg2+ to restore fluorescence (“On-Off-On”). In contrast, Zn2+ induces chelation-enhanced fluorescence by restricting intramolecular motion and suppressing non-radiative decay. Measurements in soil, river water, and fruit agreed with ICP-AES, LC−MS, or GC. Excitation-dependent responses were further demonstrated in HepG2 cells, zebrafish, mice, and rice seedlings. This carbon-dot scaffold separates sensing tasks by excitation wavelength and integrates complementary readouts with multiscale imaging. This multifunctional platform integrates environmental, common foods monitoring and bioimaging for synchronous analysis of multiple pollutants.

title: Engineering Sustainable Asphalt with Biomass-Derived Surface-Functionalized Biochar through Molecular Conservation and Emission Mitigation
summary: Abstract Sustainable asphalt technologies are increasingly vital for conserving resources, reducing environmental emissions, and enabling the beneficial reuse of carbon-rich waste materials. Surface-functionalized biochar (SFB) offers a pro
content: Abstract Sustainable asphalt technologies are increasingly vital for conserving resources, reducing environmental emissions, and enabling the beneficial reuse of carbon-rich waste materials. Surface-functionalized biochar (SFB) offers a promising strategy to enhance asphalt performance, while providing a sustainable platform for mitigating volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions; however, the roles of environmental humidity and asphalt binder composition in governing SFB’s VOC-mitigation efficacy remain poorly understood. Here, we evaluate SFB-modified asphalt at relative humidity (RH) ≈ 50% and 50 °C using environmental chamber measurements, volatility- and polarity-resolved emission analysis, molecular dynamics simulations, and density functional theory calculations. Across three asphalt binders, SFB reduced total organic emission factors by 94.5%, 84.5%, and 46.7%. Intermediate-volatility organic compounds (IVOCs) and semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) were consistently suppressed by more than 70%, but light-polar VOC emissions showed an increase specifically in one out of the three binders. This in turn demonstrates that mitigation under humid conditions is strongly binder-dependent. Simulations indicate that interfacial water redistributes polar VOCs and competes with them for adsorption sites, weakening SFB–VOC interactions, particularly for small polar compounds. Unlike earlier studies focused mainly on dry-condition mitigation, the present work links binder-dependent humid-condition measurements with molecular-level competitive adsorption mechanisms. Study outcomes highlight the need to design emission-mitigation strategies tailored to specific climatic regions, where material chemistry and humidity conditions can govern suppressant effectiveness in real-world environments.

title: Alkaline Durability and Environmental-Economic Sustainability Assessment of Cementitious Composites with Manufactured Sand and Hybrid Fiber-Reinforcement
source: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering
summary: Abstract Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) are a modern class of high-performance fiber-reinforced cementitious composites (HPFRCC) designed to exhibit strain-hardening behavior through multiple steady-state cracking. Apart from the
content: Abstract Engineered Cementitious Composites (ECC) are a modern class of high-performance fiber-reinforced cementitious composites (HPFRCC) designed to exhibit strain-hardening behavior through multiple steady-state cracking. Apart from the better performance of the ECC matrix, production costs also play an essential part in large-scale applications, especially in developing countries. This study investigated the economic feasibility, durability performance, and environmental impact of ECC incorporating PVA-polyester fiber reinforcement and manufactured sand (M-sand) while maintaining the structural performance. Durability assessments were conducted for different alkaline conditions, representing the cementitious alkalinity. The immersion test results revealed that polyester fibers demonstrated considerable degradation, reaching a mass loss of 13.25% under high alkalinity at 60°C, whereas PVA fibers exhibited superior resistance. In addition, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and microstructural investigations confirmed significant hydrolysis and surface etching in polyester fibers, whereas PVA fibers experienced negligible degradation despite some molecular changes. This study also evaluated alkali-silica reactivity (ASR) potential with different geographical M-sand samples and described that the prepared ECC mixtures effectively mitigated ASR, enabling the sustainable use of varying M-sand sources. Detailed production data of M-sand were collected from multiple locations, especially coastal areas where river sand use is restricted, and their emission and energy factors were evaluated systematically. Moreover, replacing a portion of PVA with polyester fibers and river sand with M-sand reduced the material cost by 20%, overall carbon emission by 8.21%, and energy consumption by 25%. The research presented a balanced approach for ECC mixture design, which is durable, cost-effective, and environmentally sustainable, while also outlining future recommendations on material refinement.

title: Climate Village Program within the Environmental Legal Framework to Address Climate Change
summary: Global warming due to human activities has become a major factor in climate change, with widespread impacts on the environment, economy, and social life. Climate change causes ecosystem damage, increases the frequency of hydrometeorological
content: Global warming due to human activities has become a major factor in climate change, with widespread impacts on the environment, economy, and social life. Climate change causes ecosystem damage, increases the frequency of hydrometeorological disasters, and poses serious challenges to the implementation of environmental law. In this regard, a legal framework that is normative, responsive, and adaptive to the dynamics of climate change is needed. This study aims to analyze the role of environmental law in addressing climate change from a legal philosophy perspective and examine the Climate Village Program in addressing climate change within the environmental legal framework to ensure sustainable development. The research method used is normative juridical research. The findings concerning the role of environmental law in addressing climate change from a legal philosophy perspective indicate that environmental law in Indonesia has a comprehensive legal basis through the ratification of international law on climate change into national law. Furthermore, in progressive legal studies, environmental law is a social engineering tool in encouraging behavioral change, strengthening climate policy, and realizing equitable sustainable development. Regarding the Climate Village Program’s role within the environmental legal framework for ensuring sustainable development, it serves as a progressive legal implementation that positions communities as the primary subjects of policy through a participatory approach in climate change adaptation and mitigation efforts. Therefore, the integration of environmental law and a progressive legal approach is crucial for law to serve as a vehicle for social change to achieve ecological justice and sustainable development.

title: BIOCHAR APPLICATION IN MANURE MANAGEMENT: ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACTS, GAS EMISSIONS, AND NUTRIENT RETENTION
summary: Manure management in intensive livestock production represents a major environmental challenge due to gas emissions, nutrient losses, and potential air and water pollution. Biochar is a carbon-rich material produced through biomass pyrolysi
content: Manure management in intensive livestock production represents a major environmental challenge due to gas emissions, nutrient losses, and potential air and water pollution. Biochar is a carbon-rich material produced through biomass pyrolysis under limited oxygen conditions. It is used as an amendment in manure management systems due to its porous structure and ability to adsorb ammonia and other compounds present in manure. This paper reviews the available scientific literature on biochar application in manure management, with the aim of summarizing its effects on environmental impact, gas emissions, and nutrient retention. The literature most commonly indicates that biochar application may reduce ammonia and greenhouse gas emissions and improve nutrient retention in manure. However, these effects are not consistent and depend on biochar physicochemical properties, manure type, and application conditions. The reviewed findings highlight biochar as a potentially useful amendment that can contribute to reducing environmental burdens and improving the sustainability of manure management systems.

title: Ultra-High-Performance Concrete Mixtures for Strength and Carbon Efficiency Grading
summary: This dataset contains 1,087 ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) mixture records collected from 169 published studies. All mixtures have reported 28-day compressive strengths of at least 120 MPa. The database includes mixture proportions,
content: This dataset contains 1,087 ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC) mixture records collected from 169 published studies. All mixtures have reported 28-day compressive strengths of at least 120 MPa. The database includes mixture proportions, compressive strengths, and calculated carbon emission factors (CEFs). The CEFs were estimated from constituent quantities and corresponding emission factors within a consistent A1–A3 product-stage boundary. The dataset provides a reference for investigating UHPC mixture composition, mechanical performance, and embodied carbon.

title: Solvent-Controlled Switching between Electron Transfer and Type II Photosensitization in a Zinc Phthalocyanine–Flavonol Pair
summary: Abstract The impact of solvent nature on intermolecular interactions within a pair of phthalocyanine and 3-hydroxyflavone (flavonol) derivatives was examined with the aim of activating the UV-absorbing flavonol chromophore by visible/NIR li
content: Abstract The impact of solvent nature on intermolecular interactions within a pair of phthalocyanine and 3-hydroxyflavone (flavonol) derivatives was examined with the aim of activating the UV-absorbing flavonol chromophore by visible/NIR light. Unlike its metal-free analog, Zn-phthalocyanine was found to form a 1:1 complex with flavonol in nonpolar dichloromethane. This complex showed near-diffusion-limited quenching of phthalocyanine fluorescence, which, however, did not lead to flavonol emission or triplet reactivity. A thorough examination of high-level DLPNO-CCSD(T)/CBS and constrained DFT electronic structure calculations revealed that photoinduced electron transfer within the excited complex is thermodynamically feasible. Concurrently, the formation of carbon monoxide from flavonol was observed, facilitated by singlet oxygen, generated by a Type II sensitization via triplet-excited phthalocyanine. In dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), solvent ligation inhibited phthalocyanine/flavonol complexation, and a Type II photosensitization was almost exclusively responsible for the flavonol oxygenation. The suppression of this reaction pathway in degassed DMSO resulted in intermolecular quenching of the phthalocyanine triplet by the flavonol moiety. The Wigner sampling of the T1–S0 energy gaps indicates that intramolecular proton transfer can decrease the flavonol triplet energy sufficiently to enable a nonvertical proton-coupled energy-transfer pathway from phthalocyanine to flavonol. Although this pathway is energetically accessible, it is inefficient.

title: Tests of ethylene and propylene mixture adsorption and desorption
source: Journal of Thermal Analysis and Calorimetry
summary: Abstract Unsaturated hydrocarbons—ethylene and propylene—are components of the gas mixture that is released from self-heating coal hot spots together with the increase in their temperature. The concentrations of these hydrocarbons in mine a
content: Abstract Unsaturated hydrocarbons—ethylene and propylene—are components of the gas mixture that is released from self-heating coal hot spots together with the increase in their temperature. The concentrations of these hydrocarbons in mine air are used to determine fire hazard indices that allow assessing the development of the coal self-heating process. During the migration of the gas mixture through goafs, the hydrocarbons undergo adsorption on the coal, which influences their concentrations in collected mine air samples and may be the cause of incorrect fire hazard assessment. This paper presents the results of adsorption capacity and adsorption kinetics testing as well as desorption testing of ethylene and propylene mixtures with methane as dominant mine gas component. The experiments were conducted on five samples of Polish hard coals. The quantities of the adsorbed mixtures rise together with the increase in pore volume and internal coal structure availability as well as with the decrease in the coal metamorphism. In most cases, the tested coals adsorb larger amounts of propylene–methane than of ethylene–methane mixtures. The higher amounts of adsorbed mixtures with propylene resulted from the greater reactivity and stronger interactions of propylene molecules with the reactive oxygen groups present on the coal surfaces. The propylene mixture adsorption is also a longer process. Ethylene mixtures exhibit greater desorption from coals than propylene mixtures. Propylene is more difficult to release from coals due to the strength of the bonding, as well as the size and shape of its molecule.

title: Plant volatile organic compounds as mediators of plant insect communication
summary: Plants are sessile organisms exposed to a constant dialogue with various pests, insects, and microbes. After communication through various interactions (mutualism, predation, and parasitism), the plants trigger a range of volatile organic c
content: Plants are sessile organisms exposed to a constant dialogue with various pests, insects, and microbes. After communication through various interactions (mutualism, predation, and parasitism), the plants trigger a range of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) through the modulation of the host gene. Plants responded to insect interactions both specifically and broadly. These interactions are controlled by various metabolic tracks such as the cytosolic mevalonic acid (MVA) pathway, plastidic methylerythritol phosphate (MEP) pathway, the phyto-oxylipin pathway, and shikimate pathways, where terpenoids, green-leaf volatiles (GLVs), and benzenoids/phenylpropanoids like VOCs are produced. Moreover, VOCs play a central role in chemical and visual communication, primarily by attracting pollinators and deterring herbivores, although in some cases, they may also manipulate herbivore behavior. The transmission of VOCs during insect attack is orchestrated via the signaling pathways of jasmonic acid (JA) and salicylic acid (SA). VOC biosynthesis is regulated at transcriptional, post-transcriptional, and epigenetic levels, involving transcription factors (TFs), miRNAs, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), DNA methylation, chromatin remodeling, and histone modifications that modulate genes in VOC biosynthetic pathways. Subsequently, insects also developed approaches to conquer the plant hurdle as well as consequently established a plant–insect relationship. In this review, we concentrate on the roles of plant volatiles, including their production, functions, regulation, and defense system.

title: One stone, two birds? The impact of China's low-carbon city pilot policy on firms' investment efficiency
summary: Purpose Reducing carbon emissions while sustaining economic growth is a central policy challenge for most countries. Capitalizing on the low-carbon city pilot (LCCP) policy in China, we investigate how environmental regulation affects the i
content: Purpose Reducing carbon emissions while sustaining economic growth is a central policy challenge for most countries. Capitalizing on the low-carbon city pilot (LCCP) policy in China, we investigate how environmental regulation affects the investment efficiency of carbon-intensive firms. Design/methodology/approach Exploiting the staggered LCCP rollout as a quasi-natural experiment, we use a triple-difference (DDD) design comparing polluting versus non-polluting firms around pilot designation. The sample covers Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2019 (24,463 firm-year observations). Investment efficiency is the absolute residual from Richardson (2006); we employ firm and high-dimensional fixed effects with robust errors, plus parallel-trend, placebo, and robustness checks. Findings The LCCP significantly improves investment efficiency of heavily polluting firms. The effect is stronger for firms with weaker external monitoring and higher agency costs, and works mainly by curbing under-investment. Parallel-trend and placebo tests support causality. Mechanism analysis points to strengthened monitoring, lower agency costs, and better corporate social responsibility performance. Originality/value This study links China's LCCP to corporate investment efficiency, reframing climate policy as a capital-allocation intervention. Our findings speak to the “double dividend” debate in environmental economics and are consistent with the Porter hypothesis, suggesting that well-designed climate regulation can deliver both environmental and capital-allocation benefits.

title: Engineering of the Future: Combining Big Data, Analytics and Artificial Intelligence to Develop Sustainable Technological Solutions
summary: Purpose: This paper aims to critically review the integration of big data analytics and AI in engineering systems for addressing climate change, energy efficiency and resource optimisation, and to identify the key barriers to their wider ad
content: Purpose: This paper aims to critically review the integration of big data analytics and AI in engineering systems for addressing climate change, energy efficiency and resource optimisation, and to identify the key barriers to their wider adoption. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study adopts a qualitative research methodology based on secondary data analysis of 17 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2026, using thematic analysis to identify key trends and patterns. Research Limitation: Challenges associated with implementing the described systems include high costs and data security concerns, indicating the need for further research on secure and cost-effective implementation. Findings: Big Data, Analytics, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) can enhance engineering decision-making by improving sustainability and efficiency. Data-driven methods are used to monitor and optimise industrial processes, with lower energy usage and waste. Predictive analysis reduces downtime and equipment failures using machine learning. Practical Implication: The combined use of digital technologies supports resource optimisation, environmental monitoring through carbon footprint tracking and climate modelling, and the transformation of traditional reactive engineering systems into proactive and autonomous systems. Social Implication: AI- and Big Data-related solutions improve smart cities, transportation systems, and buildings through traffic flow reduction, lower emissions, and more sustainable urban planning. Originality/Value: Unlike application-specific studies, this article contributes to knowledge by synthesising big data, analytics, and AI applications in engineering into five cross-cutting themes and outlining conditions for their sustainability effect, such as integration with cyber-physical systems.

title: Micronized Biomass Silica as a Reactive Precursor in Geopolymer-Stabilized Marine Soil: Strength and Durability Assessment
source: Journal of Materials in Civil Engineering
summary: Abstract Marine soils, distributed indefinitely around the world, because of their low strength characteristics, high compressibility, high plasticity, and sensitivity have created an imperative need for their stabilization. This study aims
content: Abstract Marine soils, distributed indefinitely around the world, because of their low strength characteristics, high compressibility, high plasticity, and sensitivity have created an imperative need for their stabilization. This study aims to improve marine soil using a novel geopolymer based on micronized biomass silica (MBS), a carbon-free green product produced at a lower cost than silica fume manufactured from rice husk ash. The effects of several parameters, including binder dosage, alkali-to-binder ratio (L/B), alkali activator ratio (NS/NH), and molarity of NaOH solution, were examined to choose the best mix proportions based on strength enhancement. The durability performance was assessed using the cyclic wetting and drying method. Furthermore, this study investigated the mechanisms underlying the reported strength augmentation in treated marine soil, as well as the microstructural and physiochemical interactions, using Field-emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS), Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray Diffraction (XRD) analyses. The optimal dosage for geopolymerization in the marine soil studied was at a binder of 15%, alkali activator ratio of 2, alkali-to-binder ratio of 0.8, and NaOH of molarity 8M, which yielded the highest UCS value of 1,033 kPa at 28 days of curing, 16 times that of untreated soil. With a durability index value greater than 1, all evaluated samples endured 12 cycles of wetting and drying with little volume change and minimal surface damage. Finally, SEM, EDS, FTIR, and XRD results revealed that the cementing components in the geopolymer-stabilized clay were sodium aluminosilicate hydrate (N─A─S─H) and Zeolites, which increased the soil structure density through bonding and filling effects. A comparative life cycle assessment verified the system’s environmental advantage, demonstrating a 22% reduction in its carbon index over traditional cement-based stabilization. This investigation presents a promising approach that improves the geomechanical characteristics of marine soil through the application of waste materials.

title: Source data and supplementary code for economic and carbon implications of molten salt regeneration across spent nickel cobalt manganese cathodes
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This dataset accompanies the manuscript entitled "Economic and carbon implications of molten salt regeneration across spent nickel cobalt manganese cathodes". The deposited files include numerical source data for the main experimental and m
content: This dataset accompanies the manuscript entitled "Economic and carbon implications of molten salt regeneration across spent nickel cobalt manganese cathodes". The deposited files include numerical source data for the main experimental and modeling figures, together with a Python script used to reproduce the illustrative lithium-supplementation uncertainty scenario in Figure 6a. The source-data workbook contains structural and electrochemical data, techno-economic results, modeled process-emission contributions, and economic sensitivity scenarios for molten-salt regeneration, hydrometallurgy, and pyrometallurgy. The economic and environmental comparisons are based on the stated inventory assumptions, literature-informed inputs, and engineering estimates rather than independently validated industrial operating data. The P10–P90 band in Figure 6a represents conditional quantiles under an assumed uniform distribution, not experimental confidence intervals. The accompanying README files explain the dataset organization, units, calculation assumptions, and instructions for running the Python script.

title: Fertility policy relaxation, female executives and corporate overseas performance: evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China
summary: Purpose This paper examines how listed firms adapt to China's 2013 fertility policy relaxation. It asks whether the reform affected firms' overseas performance, identifies the female-executive channel and explores conditions that ease adapt
content: Purpose This paper examines how listed firms adapt to China's 2013 fertility policy relaxation. It asks whether the reform affected firms' overseas performance, identifies the female-executive channel and explores conditions that ease adaptation, to inform supporting measures reconciling demographic goals with corporate vitality. Design/methodology/approach Using the selective two-child reform as a quasi-natural experiment, we compare A-share firms in industries with above- and below-median female employment shares in a difference-in-differences design over 2009–2022, supported by placebo, Propensity Score Matching-Difference-in-Differences (PSM-DID) and other robustness checks. Findings Overseas revenue of treated firms fell by roughly 17%in the short-run adjustment phase, operating through a reduced share of female executives. Financial slack and supplier protection disclosure cushion the effect, which concentrates in non-high-tech, heavy-polluting and state-owned firms and eastern China – transitional frictions, not a long-run policy harm. Research limitations/implications Overseas revenue measures scale, not profitability, and the mediation evidence is associational; finer executive data and causal mediation designs are promising extensions. Practical implications Internationally exposed firms can adapt more smoothly through succession planning, flexible arrangements for executives in childbearing years and stable supplier relationships. Social implications Broader social sharing of childbearing costs and public childcare investment would ease firms' adaptation and align the reform's demographic goals with corporate international development. Originality/value The study links macro fertility policy to corporate internationalization for the first time, provides quasi-experimental evidence on the female-executive channel and reframes the debate around constructive supporting arrangements during the policy transition.

title: Data used to generate tables and figures in Holder et al. (2016) Journal of Geophsyical Research — Atmospheres 121, doi - 10.1002/2015JD024321

American Geophysical Union, Washington, DC, USA, 121(7): 3465-3483, (2016).

title: Dual-acting compounds that deliver an acidifying domain via zanamivir to the virus surface are potent influenza inhibitors
summary: Contemporary antiviral development, whether by rational drug design or forward pharmacology, primarily strives to produce ‘lock and key’ inhibitors. While the technology to identify druggable targets and create compounds to bind them has im
content: Contemporary antiviral development, whether by rational drug design or forward pharmacology, primarily strives to produce ‘lock and key’ inhibitors. While the technology to identify druggable targets and create compounds to bind them has improved dramatically over the last century it has always been constrained by the finite availability of suitable binding sites that antiviral compounds can occupy. Here we present a new approach to drug design that utilizes compounds devised to alter the microenvironment of the virion surface making it incompatible with virus entry and illustrate this strategy with inhibitors of influenza virus. We show that compounds that produce a proton-rich mantle above the virion surface induce a conformational change in the viral hemagglutinin (HA) rendering the virus unable to interact with cellular receptors and gain entry to the cell. The compounds show exceptional antiviral activity both in vitro and in vivo and protect against influenza illness in mice and ferrets after a single dose, either therapeutically or prophylactically. The work presented here lays the foundation for a brand-new category of inhibitors that could be engineered to counter many different viruses and potentially other pathogens.

title: Data Set of Load Tests and Structural Health Monitoring of a Concrete Box Girder Bridge
summary: Abstract Static and dynamic load tests were conducted on an anonymized in-service prestressed concrete box girder bridge constructed in 1972 and designed for Bridge Class 30.The bridge is instrumented as part of the Digitalization and Techn
content: Abstract Static and dynamic load tests were conducted on an anonymized in-service prestressed concrete box girder bridge constructed in 1972 and designed for Bridge Class 30.The bridge is instrumented as part of the Digitalization and Technology Research Center of the Bundeswehr-Structural Health Monitoring (DTEC-SHM) research initiative with a permanent structural health monitoring system comprising 128 sensors, including accelerometers, strain sensors, inclinometers, displacement transducers, embedded temperature sensors, and weather stations. The test program includes long-term static loading with stepwise added masses of 680, 1,420, and 2,160 kg; short-term static truck parking positions; and repeated dynamic truck crossings under loaded and unloaded vehicle configurations. The short-term static tests used a loaded truck of 21,250 kg parked at three bridge positions, while the dynamic tests used loaded and unloaded truck configurations of 21,250 and 12,340 kg at speeds up to 13.9 m/s. The published load-test data are available on Zenodo in HDF5 format and include synchronized measurements from the monitoring system, temporary laser sensors used for vehicle-position and passage-time validation, and derived tracked eigenfrequency time series from the reference and long-term static load-test period. The bridge geometry, sensor layout, acquisition system, load cases, truck geometry, and data hierarchy are documented to support reuse of the data. Plausibility checks are presented for the main response quantities, including laser-based validation of parking positions and passage windows, vibration spectra and tracked modal parameters, and repeatable strain and displacement response profiles under crawl-speed truck passages. The data set addresses the scarcity of publicly available full-scale bridge load-test data and supports applications such as finite-element model calibration, neutral-axis tracking, influence-line extraction, and data-driven anomaly detection.

title: Microbiome structure, function, and drivers across different soil groups in an agricultural region of Serbia
summary: Abstract. Soil is the largest reservoir of biodiversity, with distinct physical, chemical, and biological properties. Microorganisms play essential roles in soil formation and fertility. This study aimed to analyze the microbiomes of three
content: Abstract. Soil is the largest reservoir of biodiversity, with distinct physical, chemical, and biological properties. Microorganisms play essential roles in soil formation and fertility. This study aimed to analyze the microbiomes of three selected soil groups in an important agricultural region of Vojvodina (Serbia) by 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding and explore their association with soil properties. Soil samples from a total of 26 field plots (in 5 replicates) were analyzed using Illumina MiSeq paired-end sequencing and processed through the QIIME2 pipeline. The obtained results indicate that the analyzed soils generally exhibit physicochemical properties typical for the respective soil groups. Alpha diversity indices revealed the highest microbiome diversity in Chernozem, consistent with its favourable physicochemical characteristics. Based on beta diversity, clear separation of soil groups according to their properties was determined. Proteobacteria, Acidobacteriota, and Actinobacteriota dominate the microbial community composition at the phylum level. Redundancy analysis revealed that soil properties account for 53.8 % of the variation in community composition, with pH value, iron availability, and CaCO3 content having the strongest influence, pH being particularly significant. The functional potential of microbial communities showed dominance of functions related to metabolism, with significant representation of functions belonging to the following groups: genetic information processing, environmental information processing, and cellular processes. The analysis of genes involved in nitrogen cycling using Kruskal-Wallis test showed no statistically significant differences in their abundances across different soil groups (p-value > 0.05). This study provides the first detailed analysis of soil microbial communities across Serbia and highlights factors shaping them. These findings underscore the importance of microbial diversity for ecosystem functioning and offer a framework for soil health monitoring, while providing insights relevant for sustainable agriculture.

title: A Closer Look at Statistical Uncertainty in Forest Ecosystem Surveys Using Remotely Sensed Data and Model-Based Inference
summary: Many forest ecosystem surveys use remotely sensed data and model-based inference. Assessing uncertainties in connec­tion with such surveys is far from trivial. Focusing on continuous study variables, such as biomass, we first motivate why t
content: Many forest ecosystem surveys use remotely sensed data and model-based inference. Assessing uncertainties in connec­tion with such surveys is far from trivial. Focusing on continuous study variables, such as biomass, we first motivate why the mean square error (MSE) of predictors of population quantities of interest is a relevant measure of overall uncertainty. Secondly, we separate the MSE into four components involving (i) the variance of the predictor, (ii) the model-bias of the predictor, (iii) the variance of the true value of the quantity predicted, and (iv) the cova­riance between the predictor and the true value, and show how the different compo­nents can be estimated. Thirdly, based on simulations mimicking conditions in Eastern Africa and Western USA, we assess which components are influential in different survey contexts. Our findings show that using the variance of a predictor, alone, as a measure of uncertainty is a fair approxi­mation if the study area is large and if the model linking remotely sensed data with reference data is adequately specified and estimated. However, we identify substantial risks of underestimating the MSE if models are extrapolated beyond conditions for which they were calibrated, in which case predictors were found to be severely model-biased. The remaining terms contributed differently in large-area surveys compared to small-area surveys. In small-area surveys, the MSE compo­nent (iii) is the dominating part. An interesting observation was that the MSE of a predictor is sometimes smaller than the variance of the predictor, due to the negative contribution from term (iv).

title: Proof-of-concept of a once-through configuration to optimize H2 conversion in CO2 methanation
summary: Because of the high cost of green H2, its efficient conversion is of utmost importance for the deployment of any CO2 utilization process. In this work we show that it is possible to produce selectively e-methane from CO2 and H2 while approa
content: Because of the high cost of green H2, its efficient conversion is of utmost importance for the deployment of any CO2 utilization process. In this work we show that it is possible to produce selectively e-methane from CO2 and H2 while approaching near complete H2 conversion. We achieve this result by leveraging a once-through configuration involving two reactors in series with intermediate water condensation working under pressure. This layout represents a flexible solution particularly useful to manage possible fluctuations in the availability of green H2. Notably, by working at the space velocity of 20 L(STP)/h/g and at the pressure of 10 barg it is possible to obtain an e-CH4 productivity of 2.8 gCH4/h/gcat, with only 0.5% of residual H2. This makes the obtained stream compliant for grid injection even in the countries with the most stringent regulations. By decreasing the GHSV, it is possible to push the H2 conversion even further, reaching residual H2 concentrations below 300 ppm. This, however, comes at the expense of a lower CH4 productivity.

title: Unique and novel methanotroph taxa from the tropics: taxonomic novelty and a gateway to methane mitigation and valorization applications
summary: Methanotrophs represent a distinctive group of microorganisms characterized by their specialized metabolic pathways, unique morphological traits, and diverse taxonomic classifications. These bacteria play a crucial role in the global methan
content: Methanotrophs represent a distinctive group of microorganisms characterized by their specialized metabolic pathways, unique morphological traits, and diverse taxonomic classifications. These bacteria play a crucial role in the global methane cycle by oxidizing methane, a potent greenhouse gas, thereby contributing to climate regulation. Over the past decade, our research group has made significant strides in exploring methanotroph diversity, particularly within the Indian subcontinent. We have successfully identified and described several novel species and two new genera of methanotrophs isolated from rice fields and wetland ecosystems in India. These discoveries mark the first and only documented methanotrophs from India, highlighting the untapped microbial diversity of these habitats and underscoring the importance of regional studies in global microbial taxonomy. To facilitate these findings, we developed a modified cultivation technique that has proven instrumental in isolating and characterising these elusive organisms. This innovative approach has not only expanded the known diversity of methanotrophs but also opened new avenues for their application in biotechnology. The unique physiological traits of these Indian methanotrophs hold promise for biotechnological innovations, including methane mitigation strategies, biofertilizer development, and bioconversion processes. As climate change continues to pose significant challenges, the valorization of methanotrophs through sustainable technologies presents a compelling opportunity. Our ongoing research aims to harness these microorganisms for environmental and industrial applications, positioning methanotrophs as key players in the pursuit of climate resilience and ecological sustainability.

title: Drivers of ecological environment resilience in China’s coastal areas
summary: Scientifically measuring the ecological environment resilience and identifying its drivers is essential for advancing ecological protection and governance. This paper employs the Resistance-Adaptability-Recovery-Transformation (RART) framew
content: Scientifically measuring the ecological environment resilience and identifying its drivers is essential for advancing ecological protection and governance. This paper employs the Resistance-Adaptability-Recovery-Transformation (RART) framework to construct an index system of ecological environment resilience. The Entropy Weight–Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) method is applied to analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of ecological environment resilience in China’s coastal areas. TWFE (Two-Way Fixed Effect) and Geographically and Temporally Weighted Regression (GTWR) methods are used to investigate the drivers of ecological environment resilience. The findings reveal that: (1) Ecological environment resilience in China’s coastal areas has shown an overall upward trend, though regional development remains unbalanced. Resilience in southern coastal areas is generally higher than in the north. (2) PA and II exhibit significant negative effects in the two-way fixed-effects model, while OU exhibits a marginally significant negative effect at the 10% level. ED, IS, and SEI are not statistically significant in the two-way fixed-effects model. (3) ED and IS show opposite directional trends between the southern and northern coastal regions of China, while the differences in the other four driving factors (PA, OU, II, SEI) are reflected in their magnitudes. These insights offer valuable policy implications for strengthening ecological environment resilience and guiding sustainable development in coastal regions worldwide.

title: Macrophage-derived migrasomes promote fibrotic remodeling in endometriosis with TGF-β/Smad signaling activation
summary: Abstract Background Progressive fibrosis of ectopic lesions is a major pathological feature of endometriosis, contributing to treatment resistance and disease recurrence. However, the mechanisms driving this fibrotic process remain incomple
content: Abstract Background Progressive fibrosis of ectopic lesions is a major pathological feature of endometriosis, contributing to treatment resistance and disease recurrence. However, the mechanisms driving this fibrotic process remain incompletely understood. Methods A murine model of endometriosis was established by transplanting endometrial tissue fragments into the peritoneal cavity of C57BL/6 mice. Macrophage-derived migrasomes were isolated from cultured RAW264.7 cells, characterized by scanning electron microscopy and Western blot, and administered intraperitoneally to endometriosis-bearing mice. Fibrotic changes were assessed by histology, immunofluorescence, and Western blot analysis of signaling pathways and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers. Cytokine levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results Exogenously administered macrophage-derived migrasomes accumulated at ectopic lesion sites and markedly aggravated fibrotic remodeling. Migrasome-treated lesions exhibited cyst-wall thickening, increased stromal cellularity, and extensive collagen deposition. At the molecular level, migrasome treatment was associated with activation of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β)/Smad pathway in ectopic lesions, as indicated by increased phosphorylation of Smad2 and Smad3 without significant changes in total Smad2/3 levels. This was accompanied by increased α-smooth muscle actin and vimentin expression together with reduced cytokeratin 18 (CK18) and E-cadherin expression, consistent with EMT-like phenotypic reprogramming. In parallel, TGF-β1 and VEGF levels were elevated, whereas MMP9 was reduced, collectively supporting a pro-fibrotic microenvironment. Conclusions These findings identify macrophage-derived migrasomes as previously unrecognized promoters of fibrotic remodeling in endometriosis and support a role for migrasome-associated signaling in lesion progression. This work provides new insight into the pathogenesis of endometriosis-associated fibrosis and highlights migrasomes as a potential target for future anti-fibrotic intervention.

title: National innovation capacity and the decoupling of economic growth from carbon emissions evidence from dynamic panel analysis
summary: Abstract This paper examines whether national innovation capacity accelerates the decoupling of economic growth from carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and how institutional quality and policy context condition this relationship. Moving beyond
content: Abstract This paper examines whether national innovation capacity accelerates the decoupling of economic growth from carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and how institutional quality and policy context condition this relationship. Moving beyond emissions-level analyses and Environmental Kuznets Curve reasoning, the study adopts a decoupling-index framework that captures changes in carbon intensity rather than emissions alone. Using a balanced panel of 47 countries over the period 2005–2024, the analysis employs fixed-effects estimation, dynamic System GMM, and panel quantile regression to account for unobserved heterogeneity, endogeneity, nonlinearity, and distributional differences in decoupling performance. The results show that innovation contributes to growth–emissions decoupling within countries, but its effects are neither uniform nor automatic. Innovation exhibits clear nonlinearities, with diminishing and, in some contexts, adverse marginal effects at higher levels of innovation capacity. Institutional quality improves decoupling in some settings but operates primarily as a complementary rather than mediating factor. Distributional estimates reveal substantial heterogeneity, with innovation exerting weak effects in low-decoupling regimes and increasingly negative marginal effects in high-decoupling regimes. Evidence from the post-2015 period further suggests that innovation becomes relatively more effective when embedded within a coordinated international climate policy framework. The findings challenge simplistic innovation-led decarbonization narratives and highlight the importance of policy alignment, institutional context, and innovation direction in achieving environmentally sustainable growth. JEL Classification O33, Q53, Q55, C23, Q01, O43

title: Role of Si Alloying in the Microstructure Evolution and Corrosion Performance of ZnAlMg Coatings
