summary: ABSTRACT The impact of Si addition on the microstructure and corrosion behavior of ZnAlMg coatings prepared in a laboratory simulator using several thermal application regimes for each coating composition is described. The coatings exposed
content: ABSTRACT The impact of Si addition on the microstructure and corrosion behavior of ZnAlMg coatings prepared in a laboratory simulator using several thermal application regimes for each coating composition is described. The coatings exposed to a cyclic accelerated corrosion test Volvo ACT II were evaluated in terms of mass loss, kinetics of white and red rust formation, and release of soluble ions. Both Si addition and the thermal regime affected the coating behavior. The best corrosion stability was provided by Zn3.7Al3Mg3Si with the microstructure consisting almost exclusively of very fine binary and ternary eutectics. The electrochemical role of particular phases was studied using a modified ZRA setup. Mg 2 Si was an important electrochemical actor serving as the principal anode in the early stage of the corrosion process. After its capacity as the source of Mg 2+ had been expended, it was replaced by MgZn 2 .

title: Empowerment Through Sustainable Journalism Practices in Africa: A Walkthrough of EcoNai + and Ushahidi Digital Platforms
summary: In this article, we address the question of sustainable journalism through the case studies of two leading digital journalism platforms in Africa: Ushahidi and EcoNai + . We draw on the walkthrough method to examine the extent to which thes
content: In this article, we address the question of sustainable journalism through the case studies of two leading digital journalism platforms in Africa: Ushahidi and EcoNai + . We draw on the walkthrough method to examine the extent to which these two journalism platforms address social, economic, and environmental crises in Africa and how they co-balance these issues with the crisis facing media and journalism itself. We achieve this by examining how audiences use these platforms. This method guarantees direct engagement with an app's interface to examine its technological mechanisms and embedded cultural references, thereby understanding how it guides users and shapes their experiences. Findings suggest that both platforms demonstrate sustainable journalism practices that align with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and emphasize citizen engagement. Challenges include functionality issues and sustainable business model concerns. Nonetheless, they contribute significantly to journalism practices addressing the SDGs. As a result, this study makes three important contributions to academic scholarship and practices. First, it provides meaningful insights into how African digital media platforms uniquely cover sustainability issues. Second, it examines the user experience issues surrounding the applications. Finally, it contributes to the growing body of research on sustainable journalism, especially in the Global South.

title: Imaging biofilms in three dimensions: modalities, quantitative readouts, and the path to four-dimensional measurement
summary: Biofilms are spatially structured microbial communities whose architecture, chemistry, mechanics, and cellular states evolve over time. Bulk assays and two-dimensional projections remain useful but cannot resolve how these properties vary w
content: Biofilms are spatially structured microbial communities whose architecture, chemistry, mechanics, and cellular states evolve over time. Bulk assays and two-dimensional projections remain useful but cannot resolve how these properties vary with depth or during growth, treatment, dispersal, and regrowth. Imaging offers complementary routes to three-dimensional measurement: fluorescence microscopy provides molecular, taxonomic, and functional specificity; optical coherence tomography resolves mesoscale architecture and dynamics; quantitative phase imaging and holotomography report refractive index and biomass-related changes; Raman methods provide chemical and metabolic contrast; and Brillouin microscopy probes mechanical response. We compare these modalities using four independent descriptors-contrast provenance, live volumetric capability, perturbation, and demonstrated biofilm use-and relate their signals to quantitative biological readouts. Modality selection depends on the spatial scale, sampling rate, specificity, and perturbation acceptable for the biological question. Longitudinal imaging links changes in architecture to molecular and functional measurements when the channels are registered and their signals validated. We therefore frame four-dimensional biofilm measurement as an integrated architecture combining a low-perturbation volumetric backbone with spatially registered molecular measurements acquired continuously or at predefined validation points. This integration requires compatible cultivation formats, a controlled imaging dose, shared quantitative parameters, and cross-modality registration.

title: Occurrence of PCDD/Fs and PCBs in Parks of the Porto Metropolitan Area
summary: Persistent organic pollutants accumulate in urban soils, yet information on the occurrence, spatial variability and human health implications of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) and dioxin-like polychlorinated b
content: Persistent organic pollutants accumulate in urban soils, yet information on the occurrence, spatial variability and human health implications of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) and dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyls (dl-PCBs) remains limited, particularly in Portugal. Surface soils were collected from six urban and peri-urban green spaces across the Porto Metropolitan Area, encompassing contrasting land-use histories and anthropogenic settings. Seventeen sampling locations were analysed for the 17 WHO-priority PCDD/F congeners and the 12 dioxin-like PCB congeners. The total number of 2005 toxic equivalents (TEQs) was determined, and screening-level human health risks were evaluated for adults considering incidental soil ingestion, dermal contact and inhalation of resuspended soil particles. PCDD/Fs and dl-PCBs were detected at all sampling locations, with total TEQ concentrations ranging from 1.91 to 330.9 ng TEQ kg⁻¹ dry weight. PCDD/Fs accounted for most of the overall toxicity. The majority of the samples under analysis can be considered representative of the urban background level in Porto, at 2.51 ± 0.54 ng TEQ kg⁻¹ dw. TEQ concentrations at most sites were consistent with diffuse urban background levels reported internationally, whereas one informal urban allotment constituted a distinct contamination hotspot. This spatial pattern was reflected in the risk assessment. Non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks remained below widely accepted screening thresholds at all locations except the hotspot, where children exhibited a hazard index (HI) of 1.50 and an incremental lifetime cancer risk (ILCR) of 1.17 × 10⁻⁵. Incidental soil ingestion was the predominant exposure pathway; dermal contact contributed modestly, and inhalation contributed negligibly. Sensitivity analysis demonstrated that these conclusions were robust to alternative assumptions about soil ingestion. These findings suggest that historical land use is a major determinant of site-specific PCDD/F and dl-PCB contamination and associated human health risks in urban green spaces. Incorporating land-use history into urban soil assessments could improve contamination hotspot identification and strengthen environmental monitoring and risk management strategies.

title: Screening legacy long-closure static-chamber records for greenhouse-gas interpretation in wastewater stabilization ponds: a reproducible case study from the arid Peruvian Andes
source: Case Studies in Chemical and Environmental Engineering
summary: Legacy static-chamber records from wastewater stabilization ponds may retain information on gas buildup but can be unsuitable for flux estimation when closures exceed conventional protocols. We applied a reproducible screening workflow to c
content: Legacy static-chamber records from wastewater stabilization ponds may retain information on gas buildup but can be unsuitable for flux estimation when closures exceed conventional protocols. We applied a reproducible screening workflow to chamber-headspace records of CH₄, N₂O and CO₂ from the Omo wastewater treatment plant, southern Peru (1,410 m). The workflow applies seven sequential gates covering raw signal, quality control, chamber state, temporal design, thresholds, replication and covariate timing; the first five are flux-critical. Three campaigns (August–October 2022) yielded 36 observations per gas from one sampled cell per pond stage at post-closure days 1, 3, 7 and 9, which are temporal repeats, not spatial replicates. The audit found that 1 Hz traces, calibration and leak-test records and purge windows were not retained, that closures of 1–9 d were approximately 48–432 times longer than a 30-min protocol, and that 52.8% of ΔCO₂ fell below the operational threshold. Post-closure time was the strongest predictor of ΔCH₄, ΔN₂O and ΔCO₂ (standardized β = 0.830, 0.741 and 0.541; all p < 0.001), no Tukey-adjusted cell contrast was significant, and pond cell and organic load were aliased. The records are therefore classified as chamber-headspace accumulation, not validated fluxes. The transferable contribution is the workflow itself.

title: Chemically Fueled Amplification of Supramolecular Asymmetry with Double Chiroptical Inversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain
content: Abstract Amplification of asymmetry in supramolecular polymers is typically studied under equilibrium conditions in apolar solvents, while examples in aqueous media, under nonequilibrium conditions or under temporal chemical control remain scarce. Here we demonstrate chemically fueled amplification of supramolecular asymmetry in water using perylene diimide (PDI) derivatives. The chemically fueled reaction cycle uses sodium dithionite to reduce and depolymerize kinetically stable helical aggregates, while subsequent oxidation by dissolved oxygen restores them. This transient disassembly–reassembly process yields amplification of asymmetry in Majority Rules (MR) experiments that is absent in the kinetically trapped system. In Sergeants-and-Soldiers (SaS) experiments, the fueled cycle shows an unusual composition-dependent response characterized by a double chiroptical inversion as a function of sergeant fraction. A phase model captures the emergence of three composition regimes and rationalizes the observed CD response. Overall, we show how chemical fuels can regulate asymmetry amplification in aqueous supramolecular polymers and highlight the role of phase competition in complex chiral self-assembly.

title: Permafrost augmented simulation and forecast using hybrid modeling through spectral neural networks
source: International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat &amp Fluid Flow
summary: Purpose Global warming is impacting several crucial Earth systems, including the permafrost. This study aims to investigate the possibility of performing fast and reliable simulation and forecasting of permafrost behavior, addressing a crit
content: Purpose Global warming is impacting several crucial Earth systems, including the permafrost. This study aims to investigate the possibility of performing fast and reliable simulation and forecasting of permafrost behavior, addressing a critical gap in the existing literature related to high computation times and energy costs of the simulations. Design/methodology/approach A numerical cryohydrogeological study on water and energy transfer in a forested, continuous permafrost site has been conducted using parallel high-performance computing to simulate the permafrost dynamics. The numerical results reasonably replicate the measured soil temperature profiles and the dynamics of infiltrated waters. This work uses a spectral network to achieve a fast, reliable and stable surrogate model for the simulations to forecast over long periods of time. The surrogate is also enhanced by assimilating experimental data through the development of a hybrid modeling framework. Findings The proposed approach improves the physical simulation while maintaining the stability of the dynamic model over long periods of time. The results reveal that the proposed hybrid modeling remains stable in integration and forecasting. The final hybrid solution demonstrates a significant improvement in simulation accuracy when tested against a test set of measurements. Predictions of the permafrost behavior in the coming decade are later made based on the coupled model intercomparison project 6 (CMIP6) climate change scenarios. Originality/value This research offers a novel perspective on permafrost modeling that extends the current understanding of its behavior under different climate change scenarios. It shows a higher-than-expected temperature increase of the permafrost. Moreover, the stable forecasting of climate change effects is demonstrated.

title: Sustainability Investing in Family Offices: Evidence from Singapore
summary: Family offices are increasingly recognised as a potentially important source of capital for sustainability-related investment. However, relatively little is known about how they make such decisions, particularly in Asia. This paper fills th
content: Family offices are increasingly recognised as a potentially important source of capital for sustainability-related investment. However, relatively little is known about how they make such decisions, particularly in Asia. This paper fills that knowledge gap and contributes important new empirical evidence by analysing the decision-making processes of family offices operating out of Singapore. Based on a comprehensive literature review and twenty-two interviews with different stakeholders (including single- and multi-family offices, private bankers, service providers and a regulator), the paper concludes that sustainability is rarely an explicitly stated priority for these family offices, but is often implicitly addressed as part of long-term investing, succession planning, and/or intergenerational values. The paper also concludes that family offices’ willingness to invest in sustainability-related areas is constrained by return expectations and by gaps in data and measurement. These conclusions, combined with insights and suggestions from the interviews, point to practical strategies and conditions that might help mobilise private capital toward sustainability outcomes.

title: Toxicity effects of harmful algal blooms in aquatic ecosystems: A review of modern remediation approaches and prospects
summary: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose significant ecological, economic, and public health risks, primarily through the production of potent toxins by algae species such as cyanobacteria, dinoflagellates, and diatoms. The increasing frequency and
content: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose significant ecological, economic, and public health risks, primarily through the production of potent toxins by algae species such as cyanobacteria, dinoflagellates, and diatoms. The increasing frequency and severity of HABs have raised concerns globally, particularly as anthropogenic activities, climate change, and nutrient enrichment in aquatic environments exacerbate their occurrence. This review explores the various drivers of HAB formation, including nutrient pollution from agricultural runoff, urbanization, and industrial discharges, alongside the impacts of climate change on water temperature, stratification, and nutrient dynamics. It highlights the biological characteristics of the major HAB-forming species, such as Microcystis, Karenia brevis, and Pseudo-nitzschia, which contribute to their persistence and toxicity in both freshwater and marine systems. Additionally, the review critically examines current remediation strategies, encompassing physical, chemical, and biological approaches, as well as emerging methods like the use of biofilms and nanoparticles. Although significant progress has been made in understanding HABs and mitigating their effects, challenges remain, particularly in scaling and implementing these methods effectively across diverse ecosystems. The review concludes by identifying key research gaps and future perspectives in the field, emphasizing the need for integrated management strategies, improved monitoring systems, and innovative technologies to address the growing threat of HABs. Sustainable, eco-friendly solutions that balance efficacy and environmental impact are crucial for long-term HAB management.

title: L-Threonine production from acetate by metabolically engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum using a pH-controlled fed-batch process
summary: Acetate has a considerable potential as a non-food feedstock for microbial bioproduction, yet its use for amino acid production remains underexplored. Here, we developed a process for L-threonine production from acetate as the sole carbon s
content: Acetate has a considerable potential as a non-food feedstock for microbial bioproduction, yet its use for amino acid production remains underexplored. Here, we developed a process for L-threonine production from acetate as the sole carbon source with Corynebacterium glutamicum by integrating rational, genome-based metabolic engineering with pH-coupled fed-batch cultivation. The engineered strain AT-3 carried five chromosomal mutations that alleviated feedback inhibition of key enzymes and redirected carbon flux toward the aspartate pathway. Substrate supply was controlled using a custom Visual Basic-based feeding script that automatically adjusted the acetic acid feed in response to online pH measurements. Robust process performance was maintained during a tenfold scale-up from 100-mL DASbox to 1-L DASGIP bioreactors. The optimized process achieved an L-threonine titer of 10.04 g/L and a yield of 0.086 g/g acetate. This study provides a basis for further studies on the development and improvement of acetate-based amino acid production process. KEY POINTS: • Plasmid-free C. glutamicum strains produce L-threonine in acetate minimal medium • pH-controlled acetic acid feed in bioreactors improved L-threonine production • Acetate-based production of feed amino acids avoids competition with human food.

title: Industrial Waste Valorization and Sustainable Material Design: A Data-Driven Statistical Approach
summary: Abstract The increasing generation of industrial waste has created significant environmental and resource-management challenges, while simultaneously providing opportunities for the development of sustainable engineering materials. Industri
content: Abstract The increasing generation of industrial waste has created significant environmental and resource-management challenges, while simultaneously providing opportunities for the development of sustainable engineering materials. Industrial waste upcycling offers a promising pathway for converting waste streams into value-added materials for construction, infrastructure, composites, ceramics, and other engineering applications. However, the performance of waste-derived materials is influenced by numerous factors, including waste composition, particle characteristics, replacement level, processing conditions, and curing parameters. This chapter presents a statistical modeling perspective on the development and evaluation of sustainable engineering materials from industrial waste. Established statistical methods, including descriptive analysis, correlation analysis, regression modeling, analysis of variance, response surface methodology, and mixed-effects models, are considered for understanding material behavior and experimental variability. Machine-learning approaches are also discussed as complementary tools for prediction and model comparison. Particular emphasis is placed on using statistical models to identify important factors, predict engineering performance, and optimize material formulations under practical constraints. The chapter further connects statistical prediction with sustainability indicators such as waste utilization, energy consumption, production cost, and environmental impact. A real-data case study will illustrate how statistical modeling can support data-driven material design and contribute to the transition from conventional waste management toward a circular economy. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: Primary 62J05, 62J12; Secondary 62P30, 90C90.

title: Particulate Matter as a Carrier for Airborne Bacteria: An Integrated Assessment of Chemical and Microbiological Air Quality in Urban Nagpur, India
source: Innovation of Chemistry & Materials for Sustainability
summary: Vehicle emission-induced air pollution is a significant environmental and public health issue in rapidly urbanizing areas. This research assesses the correlation between major air contaminants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NOx, and SO₂) and airborne microb
content: Vehicle emission-induced air pollution is a significant environmental and public health issue in rapidly urbanizing areas. This research assesses the correlation between major air contaminants (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, NOx, and SO₂) and airborne microbial density across 32 urban sites in Nagpur, India. Airborne bacteria were sampled using the passive settle plate technique and analyzed for colony morphology, Gram staining, and hemolytic activity. Colony-forming units (CFU) varied between 0.68 ´103 and 10.35 ´103 CFU/m3 with higher levels regularly in regions with significant foot traffic. A significant positive association was observed between particulate matter (PM₂.₅ and PM₁₀) and microbial load (r = 0.842, p < 0.001 and r = 0.439, p < 0.05), suggesting that particulate pollutants facilitate microbial transport and persistence. SO₂ also demonstrated a strong association with microbial concentration (r = 0.943, p < 0.001), indicating synergistic chemical–biological interactions in the urban environment. Representative pure isolates were screened microbiologically, yielding a variety of Gram-negative bacillary morphotypes, with select strains exhibiting α-hemolytic and β-mediated pathogenic characteristics. These results demonstrate a connection between particle pollution from vehicle emissions and the dynamics of airborne microbes, supporting the incorporation of microbiological markers into urban air quality evaluation systems.

title: Proton conduction facilitates the hydrogen evolution reaction in heptamolybdate-protected SnO 2 nanocore
summary: Abstract Recently, the Anderson-type heptamolybdate [Mo7O24]6- ion has been used as an inorganic ligand to protect various metal oxy-hydroxides (FeOOH and NixFe1-xOOH) and oxides (SnO2 and CeO2), and these unique varieties of materials are
content: Abstract Recently, the Anderson-type heptamolybdate [Mo7O24]6- ion has been used as an inorganic ligand to protect various metal oxy-hydroxides (FeOOH and NixFe1-xOOH) and oxides (SnO2 and CeO2), and these unique varieties of materials are employed as electrode materials for water oxidation and nitrate reduction. Herein, [Mo7O24]6- covalently connected to a SnO2 nanocore, namely Mox@SnO2, is prepared through a hydrothermal route and has been fabricated on a 1 cm2 surface of a conducting carbon support to study proton conduction and electrocatalytic proton reduction. The Mox@SnO2 fabricated carbon cloth (CC) exhibits the maximum proton conductivity of 15.34 × 10−3 S cm-1 at pH 3.65 and room temperature, which increased linearly with the increment in cell temperature and reached 32.47 × 10−3 S cm−1 at 318 K. Under similar conditions, the bare SnO2 fabricated on CC shows relatively low proton conductivity, highlighting the importance of POM ligands on Mox@SnO2 to facilitate proton conduction with an extremely low activation energy of 0.13 eV, indicative of proton shuttling through the Grotthuss pathway. Further, the facile proton conduction on Mox@SnO2 and the redox participation of POMs, as depicted from cyclic voltammetric studies, enable electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) under mild acidic conditions, delivering an onset potential of -0.4 V vs RHE and a nearly two-fold higher catalytic current at -0.9 V compared to that observed for SnO2. The electrokinetic study has confirmed that the improved performance of Mox@SnO2 over SnO2 is due to enhanced charge-transfer kinetics. This study showcases a new role for covalently attached heptamolybdate anions on SnO2, facilitating proton relay and reduction.

title: Can the Spatial Planning of Livestock Production Tackle Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?
summary: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked th
content: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. This study develops a spatially explicit multiscale model system encompassing 13,000 polygons across China to assess soil N balance, NH3 emission intensity, and N concentrations in surface water, aiming to explore integrated spatial-planning (SP) strategies that maximize synergy and minimize trade-offs. Our findings reveal that single-purpose SP scenarios (e.g., reducing NH3 emissions or instream N concentrations) can effectively address one N-related issue but produce substantial trade-offs, leaving >50% of China’s population exposed to at least another N-related problem. However, an integrated SP approach could reduce harmful N exposures for 90% of China’s population while ensuring food security. This approach involves reallocating 14% of livestock production, reducing livestock numbers by one-third relative to the 2050 baseline, and implementing advanced technologies to mitigate N pollution hotspots. Thus, our findings emphasize the importance of spatially explicit N boundaries and multicriteria planning to tackle N pollution in air and water simultaneously, supporting cross-media N management policy-making and region-specific strategies.

title: Low-carbon alkali-activated concrete production using multi-waste materials
summary: This study introduces a novel multi-waste binder design approach for high-strength alkali-activated concrete (HSAAC), in which ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) content was reduced to only 20%. Ten mixtures were prepared by repla
content: This study introduces a novel multi-waste binder design approach for high-strength alkali-activated concrete (HSAAC), in which ground granulated blast furnace slag (GGBFS) content was reduced to only 20%. Ten mixtures were prepared by replacing up to 80% of GGBFS with various waste materials, including waste charcoal ash (WCA), silica fume (SF), metakaolin (MK), waste ceramic powder (WCP), waste basalt powder (WBP), quartz powder (QP), and coal powder (CP). The influence of different curing regimes, including water, heat, and steam-water curing, was evaluated based on compressive strength development, while the physical, mechanical, durability, and environmental performances of the mixtures were assessed under water curing conditions. The results show that the steam-water treatment system produced higher compressive strengths for all mixtures after 28 days compared to the other curing systems. The WCA20 mixture showed a 3.5% improvement in workability. The control, MK40, and WCP20 mixtures achieved high-strength concrete requirements, with compressive strengths of 87, 75, and 70 MPa, respectively. The QP20 and WBP20 mixtures exhibited enhanced flexural strength, with increases of up to 44% and 25%, respectively, and achieved tensile strengths of 7.16 MPa and 6.21 MPa, respectively. MK20 and QP20 exhibited superior resistance to both sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄) and magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) attack. Microstructural analysis further confirmed the strength enhancement observed after sodium sulfate exposure. The SEM–EDS results revealed denser reaction matrices and increased Ca/Si ratios of 0.31 and 0.27 for MK20 and QP20, respectively, suggesting the formation of additional Ca-bearing reaction products and continued matrix densification. Environmental assessment revealed improved sustainability across all mixtures, with WCP and WBP showing the highest environmental performance among the multi-waste blends.

title: Self-selection bias impedes electric vehicle adoption
summary: Currently, electric vehicle (EV) adoption in the United States is transitioning from early experimentation to stabilized adoption. However, barriers to mass adoption remain, particularly related to user perceptions and behavioral difference
content: Currently, electric vehicle (EV) adoption in the United States is transitioning from early experimentation to stabilized adoption. However, barriers to mass adoption remain, particularly related to user perceptions and behavioral differences between non-EV and EV users. This study analyzes survey data from 996 US adults, including non-EV, plug-in hybrid EV (PHEV) and battery EV (BEV) users, using an econometric model that accounts for self-selection bias in evaluating users’ perceived importance of charging time-related features at EV charging stations (EVCSs). Results show predictive performance in both the selection model classifying EV groups (pseudo- \( {{\rm R}^2=0.05\sim 0.06}\) ) and the outcome model estimating perceived importance ( \( {{\rm R}^2=0.36\sim 0.38}\) ). The estimated treatment effects for current PHEV and BEV users are -0.920 and -0.975, respectively, indicating lower perceived importance under their observed EV adoption states relative to their estimated counterfactual non-EV states. In contrast, perceived importance among non-EV users slightly decreases by 0.016 under the PHEV adoption counterfactual and increases by 0.913 under the BEV adoption counterfactual. On average, transitioning from non-EV status to PHEV or BEV status significantly decreases perceived importance by 0.442 and 0.076, respectively, with these shifts larger than or comparable to corresponding observed simple differences. This suggests that charging-time concerns may be less salient under the estimated EV adoption states after accounting for self-selection. Our results indicate that self-selection bias can impede EV adoption by amplifying perceived barriers among non-EV users. Furthermore, by identifying and adjusting for self-selection effects, this research offers insights for designing targeted outreach strategies and infrastructure policies to support mass diffusion of EVs.

title: Toward autonomous decision support in semiconductor manufacturing: a review of planning, scheduling, dispatching, and execution control
summary: Abstract Semiconductor manufacturing is a high-stakes cyber-physical production domain in which planning targets, scheduling feasibility, dispatching actions, process-control feedback, and human oversight must remain continuously aligned. T
content: Abstract Semiconductor manufacturing is a high-stakes cyber-physical production domain in which planning targets, scheduling feasibility, dispatching actions, process-control feedback, and human oversight must remain continuously aligned. This paper presents a structured state-of-the-art review of semiconductor smart manufacturing from the perspective of autonomous intelligent systems (AIS). The review does not treat planning, scheduling, dispatching, real-time dispatching (RTD), advanced process control (APC), manufacturing execution systems (MES), advanced planning and scheduling (APS), and enterprise resource planning (ERP) as separate production-management topics. Instead, it synthesizes them as bounded components of a human-supervised closed-loop decision architecture. The central artifact is an AIS reference model that maps fab layers to state inputs, decision-support functions, human authority, and audit or safeguard mechanisms. The review also develops a deployment-maturity matrix for classical optimization, simulation, rule-based dispatching, predictive learning, reinforcement learning, digital twins, LLM-enabled orchestration, and industrial software infrastructure. The synthesis shows that classical methods remain central because they provide interpretable constraints and executable interfaces. Learning-based and large-language-model-enabled methods can strengthen state estimation, policy adaptation, semantic mediation, and human-system interaction, but only under validated simulation or offline evaluation, bounded authority, safe fallback, access control, and auditable records. Semiconductor fabs should therefore not be described as fully autonomous systems. A more defensible AIS framing is trustworthy, human-supervised autonomous decision support: systems that sense changing fab states, evaluate alternatives, recommend or execute approved actions, and feed outcomes back into planning, scheduling, dispatching, and process-control decisions.

title: Carbon Pricing, Emission Trading System, and AIS
summary: This chapter introduces the developments in carbon pricing, in particular the European Union Emission Trading System's inclusion of shipping and the potential of using AIS for emission prediction in the context of carbon pricing. Market-bas
content: This chapter introduces the developments in carbon pricing, in particular the European Union Emission Trading System's inclusion of shipping and the potential of using AIS for emission prediction in the context of carbon pricing. Market-based measures have been introduced to harness market forces to achieve emission reduction goals by imposing a cost on emissions. Carbon levy and cap-and-trade are the widely discussed measures currently in the maritime transportation industry. The EU ETS's progressive inclusion of international shipping in the coming years will significantly affect how the vessels are employed and how operators and shippers account for the emissions in the voyages. Lastly, the chapter challenges the impractical Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) measurement that the IMO imposes.

title: Regional CO 2 Emission Reductions and Air‐Quality Implications of Carbon Capture in Energy and Hard‐to‐Abate Sectors
summary: ABSTRACT Carbon capture and storage (CCS) can reduce carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions from energy and industrial activities, but its regional air quality and health implications depend on the capture technology, transport configuration, and
content: ABSTRACT Carbon capture and storage (CCS) can reduce carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions from energy and industrial activities, but its regional air quality and health implications depend on the capture technology, transport configuration, and associated energy requirements. This study assessed six CCS configurations in the Po Valley, Northern Italy, using the MAQ integrated assessment model. Monoethanolamine‐based post‐combustion capture was applied to natural gas (NG) combustion activities in the energy sector (MS1) at 60%, 85%, and 90% CO 2 removal rates. Oxy‐fuel combustion was applied to NG industrial furnaces in the industrial combustion sector (MS3) and kept constant across scenarios. Captured CO 2 from MS1 was transported either by road tankers or pipeline, whereas the MS3 CO 2 stream was assumed to be transported by pipeline. Gross CO 2 captured, transported, and stored ranged from 121.952 to 127.946 MtCO 2 /year. After accounting for road‐transport emissions, CO 2 conditioning, and electricity demand for oxygen production, net CO 2 reductions ranged from 105.744 MtCO 2 /year for Truck‐60 to 111.925 MtCO 2 /year for Pipeline‐90. Pipeline transport provided a higher net CO 2 reduction than tanker transport at the same capture rate. All scenarios reduced domain‐average PM2.5 and NO 2 concentrations relative to the CLE2020 baseline. Mean cell‐level reductions ranged from 0.063 to 0.075 µg/m 3 for PM2.5 and from 0.234 to 0.293 µg/m 3 for NO 2 , with statistically significant differences after false‐discovery‐rate correction. Estimated avoided attributable deaths ranged from 162 to 186 deaths/year for PM2.5 and from 175 to 215 deaths/year for NO 2 . Pipeline configurations achieved the greatest air‐quality and health benefits because they avoided additional road‐transport emissions. These findings show that CCS can provide substantial net climate mitigation and modest local air‐quality co‐benefits, provided that the full energy and transport chain is explicitly accounted for.

title: Construction of Carbon Dots@Alumina Materials with Long-Lived Room Temperature Phosphorescence for Digital Encryption
summary: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) carbon dots (CDs) materials have attracted considerable attention owing to their potential applications in digital encryption. However, achieving high-performance RTP CDs materials without int
content: Abstract Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) carbon dots (CDs) materials have attracted considerable attention owing to their potential applications in digital encryption. However, achieving high-performance RTP CDs materials without introducing external emissive centers or complex substrates remains a significant challenge. Herein, CDs@Al2O3 materials were successfully prepared by a solid-state decomposition method with aluminum isopropoxide (AIP) as a single precursor. The double confinement of strong covalent bonds and a highly rigid structure is formed by calcination, which effectively suppresses the vibration of luminescent molecules and the non-radiative transition of triplet excitons and generates oxygen vacancies with suitable concentration (deeper traps) as effective trapping sites for triplet excitons. As a result, the CDs@Al2O3 material exhibits a long lifetime of 433.5 ms (more than 6 s to the naked eyes) and excellent stability. These composites show preliminary potential for applications in digital encryption. This work provides a simple strategy for the in situ construction of RTP CDs materials with a single precursor.

title: Carbon-Intensity Predictive Computing for Generative AI: Forecasting Spatiotemporal Electricity Emissions for Carbon-Aware Computational Orchestration
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The increasing deployment of generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems has created substantial electricity demand associated with large language model (LLM) inference, model loading, prompt processing, autoregressive generation, and d
content: The increasing deployment of generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems has created substantial electricity demand associated with large language model (LLM) inference, model loading, prompt processing, autoregressive generation, and distributed computational services. Although predictive computing provides opportunities to anticipate future computational demand and prepare reusable resources before actual requests arrive, the environmental consequences of these operations depend not only on how much electricity is consumed but also on the carbon intensity of the electricity supplying the computational infrastructure. Electricity carbon intensity varies across geographical regions and changes over time according to electricity generation composition, renewable energy availability, grid conditions, weather patterns, and electricity demand. Consequently, computational workloads with identical energy requirements may produce substantially different operational emissions depending on where and when they are executed. This paper introduces Carbon-Intensity Predictive Computing for Generative AI (CIP-GAI), a conceptual framework that extends predictive computational orchestration through the forecasting of spatiotemporal electricity carbon intensity. Rather than relying exclusively on historical or current carbon intensity measurements, CIP-GAI investigates whether future regional electricity emissions can be predicted and incorporated into computational preparation, workload scheduling, GPU allocation, and geographically distributed inference decisions. The proposed architecture integrates six principal functions: (1) regional electricity carbon-intensity data acquisition, (2) spatiotemporal carbon-intensity forecasting, (3) uncertainty-aware carbon emission estimation, (4) carbon-aware predictive workload preparation, (5) geographically distributed computational orchestration, and (6) continuous carbon accounting and adaptive optimization. The framework distinguishes average grid carbon intensity from short-run marginal and long-run marginal emissions, recognizing that these measures represent different environmental accounting perspectives and may lead to different scheduling decisions. It further distinguishes electricity consumption from electricity carbon intensity, thereby separating computational energy efficiency from the environmental characteristics of the electricity supply. A unified optimization formulation is developed to minimize expected operational carbon emissions while accounting for GPU energy consumption, regional carbon-intensity forecasts, prediction uncertainty, workload deadlines, response latency, geographical transfer costs, cloud resource prices, and computational preparation expenditure. Particular attention is given to the interaction between predictive computation and carbon-aware execution. Anticipated inference workloads may be prepared in advance during periods and locations with comparatively favorable electrici

title: Forward register of environmental turning points: statements to be scored by later data
summary: Dated predictions of when declared and pledged environmental turning points (global and national fossil CO2 emissions, coal and oil use, tree cover loss and other quantities) can be confirmed by the data available to the 2028 and 2033 globa
content: Dated predictions of when declared and pledged environmental turning points (global and national fossil CO2 emissions, coal and oil use, tree cover loss and other quantities) can be confirmed by the data available to the 2028 and 2033 global stocktakes and the 2030 biodiversity and forest reviews, including a statement to be scored against the 2026 emission estimates. Deposited before the Global Carbon Budget’s first estimate of 2026 emissions and before any national value for 2026 was released.

title: coastal-reclaim: analysis code for 'Coastal cities discharge as much treated wastewater to the sea as the world can desalinate'
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Release v1.0.0 — Coastal Wastewater Reuse: Global Assessment and Interactive Atlas This is the initial public release of the analysis code and interactive atlas accompanying the research article: "Coastal cities discharge as much treated wa
content: Release v1.0.0 — Coastal Wastewater Reuse: Global Assessment and Interactive Atlas This is the initial public release of the analysis code and interactive atlas accompanying the research article: "Coastal cities discharge as much treated wastewater to the sea as the world can desalinate." Overview This release provides a reproducible framework for assessing the global potential of coastal wastewater reclamation as an alternative to seawater desalination. The analysis identifies and evaluates wastewater treatment plants discharging within 50 km of the coastline, incorporates validation corrections against utility sources, distinguishes ocean and estuary outfalls from river discharges, and estimates the potential potable-water yield through a closed mass balance. The framework further evaluates electricity requirements, photovoltaic potential, brine generation, CO₂ emissions, irrigation substitution, practical reuse constraints, conveyance economics, and comparisons with desalination capacity at global, regional, national, and city scales. Key findings reported in the accompanying study 8,781 wastewater treatment plants with sea or estuary outfalls. Approximately 132 million m³/day of coastal wastewater discharge (90% interval: 123–143 million m³/day). Approximately 92 million m³/day of estimated potable-grade reclamation potential under the central mass-balance assumptions. Approximately 13 million m³/day of screened practical reclamation potential after applying substitution constraints. Assessment of 22 desalinating cities, including local comparisons of wastewater availability and seawater desalination capacity. These values are reported study results, not guaranteed outputs for every execution environment or alternative input-data version. Included in this release Complete analysis pipeline and supporting Python scripts. Plant-level coastal wastewater dataset construction and validation corrections. Global, regional, national, and city-level desalination comparisons. Monte Carlo uncertainty and sensitivity analyses. Irrigation substitution and break-even conveyance-distance assessments. Flow-validation and cross-country transferability analyses. Interactive HTML atlas (Supplementary_Software_1_atlas.html). Reproducible pipeline execution through run_all.sh. Reproducibility The analysis uses fixed random seeds for Monte Carlo simulations, bootstrap procedures, and city-level uncertainty calculations. Input-data sources and acquisition instructions are documented in data/README.md. Install dependencies and execute the complete pipeline using: pip install -r requirements.txt bash run_all.sh NASA POWER data are retrieved and cached during the initial execution. Scope and limitations This repository contains the analysis code and interactive atlas. Manuscript figures and their underlying figure-panel source data are provided separately through the article's Supplementary Information and Source Data files. The results represent a screening-level ass

title: PADL1NK-005 study design: a phase III trial of fetrastobart vedotin (Fetra-V) vs docetaxel in patients with previously treated tumor PD-L1–positive NSCLC
summary: Fetrastobart vedotin (Fetra-V or PDL1V/PF-08046054) is an investigational antibody–drug conjugate that binds to programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)–expressing tumor cells and delivers a cytotoxic payload of monomethyl auristatin E. Fetra-V mo
content: Fetrastobart vedotin (Fetra-V or PDL1V/PF-08046054) is an investigational antibody–drug conjugate that binds to programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)–expressing tumor cells and delivers a cytotoxic payload of monomethyl auristatin E. Fetra-V monotherapy has shown promising antitumor activity and manageable safety in patients with relapsed or refractory non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). PADL1NK-005 is a global, randomized, open-label phase III study assessing the efficacy and safety of Fetra-V monotherapy versus docetaxel in adults with PD-L1 ≥1% (utilizing locally tested PD-L1 expression using 22C3 or SP263 antibody clones) unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic NSCLC following disease progression. Approximately 680 patients will be randomized 1:1 to receive Fetra-V 1.5 mg/kg using adjusted ideal body weight on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle or docetaxel 75 mg/m2 on day 1 of a 21-day cycle. Randomization will be stratified by PD-L1 expression (1%–49% versus ≥50%), histology (nonsquamous versus squamous), select actionable genomic alterations (EGFR/ALK present versus absent/unknown), and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (0 versus 1). The primary endpoint is overall survival in patients with PD-L1 ≥1% and PD-L1 ≥50%. Key secondary endpoints are progression-free survival and objective response rate by blinded independent central review in patients with PD-L1 ≥1% and PD-L1 ≥50%.Clinical trial registration NCT07144280 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07144280)

title: Agricultural reuse of immobilized white rot fungal consortium treated textile effluent for improved agronomic performance and nutritional quality of Vigna radiata
summary: Growing freshwater scarcity, with increasing discharge of wastewater from textile industries, have intensified the need for wastewater treatment and agricultural reuse. The current research assessed the reusability of biological treated syn
content: Growing freshwater scarcity, with increasing discharge of wastewater from textile industries, have intensified the need for wastewater treatment and agricultural reuse. The current research assessed the reusability of biological treated synthetic textile effluent (STE), comprising anthraquinone (AQ) dyes, for irrigation of Vigna radiata . To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to report a chitosan immobilized white-rot fungal consortium (WRFC) comprising Trametes cubensis , Polyporus umbellatus , Leiotrametes flavida , and Pleurotus pulmonarius for the treatment of AQ dye-containing textile effluent using batch, continuous, and fed-batch bioreactor systems. The immobilized WRFC based fed-batch bioreactor showed the highest treatment efficiency with 99.06% decolorization, and significant reductions in chemical oxygen demand (COD) (75.04%), biological oxygen demand (BOD) (96.05%), nitrate (95.38%), lead (39.47%), and cadmium (50%). The suspended and immobilized WRFC treated effluent (IWTE) was reused for irrigation of V. radiata . Plants irrigated with IWTE exhibited superior growth performance, including maximum plant height, fresh biomass, pod yield, and enhanced photosynthetic pigments. Nutritional quality of mung grains was also improved, with higher protein (28.90 g/100 g), carbohydrate (55.54 g/100 g), and energy value (343.25 Kcal/100 g) compared to plants irrigated with untreated STE. Overall, immobilized WRFC based mycoremediation demonstrated an eco-friendly and sustainable approach for textile effluent remediation and safe agricultural reuse under water scarcity conditions.

title: Stress-Testing CBAM Under Export Reallocation with RICE-M: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Climate-Economic Model with MRIO-Calibrated Trade
source: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
summary: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) prices the embedded carbon of selected imports. Its effects depend partly on how self-interested trade partners adjust production, mitigation, and export allocation in response. Multi-agent r
content: The EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) prices the embedded carbon of selected imports. Its effects depend partly on how self-interested trade partners adjust production, mitigation, and export allocation in response. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) integrated assessment models such as RICE-N provide a way to evaluate such responses before deployment: regional agents are trained inside the policy environment, and their learned strategies identify potential weaknesses in the mechanism. The credibility of such a stress test depends on whether the simulator represents the strategic response margins available to exporters. A central concern of CBAM is the diversion of emissions-intensive exports to unregulated markets. In an aggregate model with a single composite good such as RICE-N, this cannot be represented. We present RICE-M, a disaggregated extension of RICE-N with bilateral, sectoral trade calibrated to multi-regional input-output (MRIO) data, regional damages, and transition costs. In policy-conditioning experiments, the learned policy reroutes emissions-intensive exports away from the EU when CBAM is active. Furthermore, when comparing mitigation response with and without fixed export reallocation we identify a crowd-out effect in which trade reallocation weakens the mitigation response to CBAM. We are currently exploring how this effect can be overcome by climate-finance mechanisms.

title: Does Earnings-Call Climate Exposure Improve Machine-Learning Forecasts of Stock Downside Risk? Out-of-Sample Evidence from U.S. Firms
summary: Climate-related risks are now widely regarded as financial risks, and machine learning is often proposed as a means of turning climate information into sharper risk assessments.Whether firm-level climate exposure helps forecast a stock's fu
content: Climate-related risks are now widely regarded as financial risks, and machine learning is often proposed as a means of turning climate information into sharper risk assessments.Whether firm-level climate exposure helps forecast a stock's future risk, rather than merely correlating with it in-sample, has received much less attention.We examine this question for 1,792 U.S.-listed non-financial firms (15,521 firm-years, with portfolio formation dates from 2012 to 2024), combining published earnings-call measures of firm-level climate change exposure with freely available accounting and market data.Our forecast target is each firm's downside semi-deviation over the following year.We estimate ordinary least squares and random forest models without climate exposure, with it, and with placebo climate variables randomly reassigned among firms in the same year and industry.We evaluate the forecasts in out-of-sample tests over 2017-2024 (10,836 firm-years) and use them to form sector-neutral portfolios that exclude the stocks with the highest predicted risk.Climate exposure does not improve forecast accuracy: adding it moves the random forest's out-of-sample R² from 10.25% to 10.30% (Diebold-Mariano p = 0.665), and the model with real climate data performs no better than 100 placebo versions (permutation p = 0.168).Random forests are more accurate than linear models (p = 0.022), but this advantage is only marginally significant after a small-sample correction (p = 0.069), and most of their gain over a naive past-risk forecast arises in the year after the COVID-19 shock; excluding that year, the pooled out-of-sample R² is -3.3% for the random forest and -8.4% for the linear model.Portfolios formed with and without climate information have almost identical risk.For U.S.-listed firms and a one-year horizon, earnings-call climate exposure therefore adds little to forecasts of downside risk once past volatility and basic firm characteristics are known, and the contributions of climate data and of model flexibility should be assessed separately.

title: M300-C18150 bimetal 3D printing by laser powder bed fusion: effect of process parameters on single track and layer development
summary: Abstract Powder Bed Fusion of metals using laser beam (PBF-LB/M) relies on stable single-track and single-layer deposition to produce dense, and defect-free components, a requirement that is particularly challenging in bimetallic systems wi
content: Abstract Powder Bed Fusion of metals using laser beam (PBF-LB/M) relies on stable single-track and single-layer deposition to produce dense, and defect-free components, a requirement that is particularly challenging in bimetallic systems with dissimilar thermophysical properties. This study investigated the effects of PBF-LB/M process parameters on single-track and single-layer deposition in a bimetallic system comprising M300 maraging steel and C18150 copper alloy. An SLM 280 2.0 2MA PBF-LB/M machine equipped with twin 700 W IPG Ytterbium fiber lasers was used to print the bimetal samples. Laser scan velocities (500–1100 mm/s), laser powers (300–550 W), and hatch spacings (0.08–0.14 mm) were systematically varied for deposition of M300 on C18150 substrates and vice versa. Surface integrity was quantified using surface roughness parameters (Ra and Sa), while melt pool geometry and interfacial characteristics were analysed using optical and scanning electron microscopy. For single tracks of M300 deposited on C18150, increasing scan velocity led to higher surface roughness and reduced melt pool width and depth, whereas higher laser power increased melt pool dimensions. In contrast, single tracks of C18150 deposited on M300 exhibited discontinuous tracks, high variability in melt pool geometry, and unstable deposition behaviour. Single-layer results revealed smoother surfaces for M300 on C18150 under low scan velocity, 500–700 mm/s, small hatch spacing, 0.08–0.1 mm and high laser power, 400–450 W. The reverse configuration, C18150 on M300, however, rendered better surface quality at the same velocity and hatch space ranges but at higher power, 500–550 W. The lowest surface roughness (Ra = 15.7 ± 1.9 μm; Sa = 19.9 ± 0.4 μm ) was for M300 on C18150 configuration and for C18150 on M300 (Ra = 14.9 ± 7.1 μm; Sa = 48 ± 16 μm). Interfacial analysis showed material intermixing in both configurations, with more pronounced defect formation when depositing C18150 on M300. Overall, the results of this study provide critical insights into the process–structure relationships governing bimetallic PBF-LB/M fabrication and contribute to the advancement of parameter optimisation strategies for the production of structurally sound bimetallic components.

title: When Monitoring Channels Fail—Next-Hour PM2.5 Forecasting across Unseen Beijing Stations
source: Interdisciplinary Journal of AI Machine Learning & Data Science
summary: Operational air-quality forecasts can lose local pollutant, neighboring-station, meteorological, or all current signals. Using public hourly data from 12 Beijing stations, this study stress-tested a persistence-corrected next-hour PM2.5 mod
content: Operational air-quality forecasts can lose local pollutant, neighboring-station, meteorological, or all current signals. Using public hourly data from 12 Beijing stations, this study stress-tested a persistence-corrected next-hour PM2.5 model in a leave-one-station-out, future-year design under eight matched channel-availability scenarios. On test rows with observed local PM2.5, residual gradient boosting improved equal-station MAE from 9.67 µg/m³ for persistence to 9.13 and improved all 12 held-out stations. Across all clean test rows its MAE was 9.39. Meteorological loss changed MAE only modestly (9.46–9.48), whereas masking local PM2.5 raised it to 11.51, masking neighboring PM2.5 to 33.28, joint PM loss to 38.72, and 24-hour all-signal blocks to 45.77. Coverage fell from 0.910 clean to 0.734 under joint PM loss, while interval score rose from 81.91 to 610.73. An availability-aware fallback limited MAE to 18.32 under joint PM loss and 17.64 under all-signal blocks. Robustness depended on which channels failed and on the fallback used, not merely the missing fraction.

title: PM₂.₅-Associated Variation in Airborne Antimicrobial Resistance Gene Abundance During Winter Smog Episodes in Urban Pakistan (2022–2023)
summary: Abstract Airborne particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is a major component of winter smog and has been increasingly recognized as a potential carrier of microbial contaminants, including antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). However, limited data a
content: Abstract Airborne particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is a major component of winter smog and has been increasingly recognized as a potential carrier of microbial contaminants, including antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). However, limited data are available on the distribution of airborne ARGs associated with PM₂.₅ in urban environments of Pakistan. Objective This study aimed to quantify the relative abundance of clinically relevant ARGs in PM₂.₅-associated bacterial communities across three cities of Pakistan and to evaluate their association with air pollution and meteorological conditions. Methodology PM₂.₅ samples were collected from Lahore, Islamabad, and Okara during the winter months (November–December 2022 and 2023). External DNA (eDNA) associated with particulate matter was extracted and analysed using quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR). The relative abundance of selected ARGs ( sul1, blaTEM, blaCTX-M-32, blaNDM-1, vanA, vanRA, tnpA, intI1 , and blaTEM-F ) was determined using the 2^(-ΔCt) method and normalized against the 16S rRNA gene. Environmental parameters, including PM₂.₅ concentration, Air Quality Index (AQI), temperature, and humidity, were also assessed. Results Lahore exhibited the highest pollution levels, with PM₂.₅ concentrations reaching 276.6 ± 27.4 µg/m³ and AQI values up to 289.3 ± 42.7. PM₂.₅ showed strong positive correlations with AQI (r = 0.92) and relative humidity (r = 0.91) and a negative correlation with temperature (r = − 0.38). Distinct spatial variation in ARG relative abundance was observed across the study sites. The blaNDM-1 gene demonstrated the highest relative abundance, particularly in Lahore (0.077) and Islamabad (0.056), while vanA showed a comparatively higher abundance in Okara. Other ARGs, including blaTEM-F, sul1 , and intI1 , exhibited variable distribution patterns across cities, indicating heterogeneous environmental resistome profiles. Conclusion The findings reveal significant spatial variability in airborne ARG relative abundance associated with PM₂.₅ and highlight the influence of environmental conditions on resistome distribution. These results underscore the importance of monitoring airborne antimicrobial resistance in polluted urban environments and provide baseline data for future environmental and public health assessments.

title: Climate justice, fossil fuel lock-ins and opportunities
source: International Environmental Agreements Politics Law and Economics
summary: Abstract More than thirty years after the adoption of the UN Convention on Climate Change, fossil fuel still provides 80% of the world’s total energy consumption. The escalation in renewables makes a dent in fossil fuel use, but cannot, in
content: Abstract More than thirty years after the adoption of the UN Convention on Climate Change, fossil fuel still provides 80% of the world’s total energy consumption. The escalation in renewables makes a dent in fossil fuel use, but cannot, in itself, address the climate problem. Hence, this paper asks: What blocks the transition away from fossil fuel and what opportunities are there to phase out fossil fuel? This paper integrates the results of a five-year project discussed and debated during the Climate Change and Fossil Fuels (CLIFF) Conference in Amsterdam in November 2025. It argues that the focus on politically feasible, efficient, short-term win–win solutions has exacerbated the global ability to manage climate change; and that without a just approach the climate problem cannot be addressed. Using the frame of climate system justice and lock-in, the paper identifies ten overlapping systemic lock-ins (profitability, discursive, legal, investment, economic/fiscal, infrastructural, labour, behavioural, political, professional) that operate at multiple levels of governance and across different domains. The paper identifies different strategies to unlock these different lock-ins across the different domains. Unlocking the lock-ins requires scientists, social movements and large-scale social and political mobilization to support these ideas as they clearly go against the business-as-usual and incremental policy processes. These ideas can be supported by the judiciary which holds states responsible for climate action and argues that continuing to use fossil fuel can be an internationally wrongful act.

title: Design of a glove dispenser to promote rational glove use and hand hygiene in an intensive care unit
source: Innovaciencia Facultad de Ciencias Exactas Físicas y Naturales
summary: Introduction. Healthcare-associated infections continue to pose a significant challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), where inappropriate glove use and poor hand hygiene can contribute to pathogen transmission and the unnecessary consumpt
content: Introduction. Healthcare-associated infections continue to pose a significant challenge in intensive care units (ICUs), where inappropriate glove use and poor hand hygiene can contribute to pathogen transmission and the unnecessary consumption of resources. Gloves represent an essential protective barrier against exposure to potentially infectious biological material, including blood, body fluids, and secretions. Objective. To design, develop, and evaluate a glove dispenser intended to promote appropriate glove use and support hand hygiene practices in an intensive care unit (ICU). Materials and Methods. A technological design study was conducted between January 2023 and January 2024 following a five-phase development process: needs assessment, device specification, concept generation, prototype development and refinement, and final prototype construction. The process incorporated direct clinical observations, feedback from ICU healthcare personnel, iterative usability testing, and pilot implementation in a real clinical setting. Results. A glove dispenser prototype integrated with an alcohol-based hand sanitizer dispenser was developed, incorporating visual prompts based on World Health Organization recommendations to encourage appropriate glove use and hand hygiene. During pilot implementation, 50 healthcare workers participated. Exposure to body fluids was observed in 60% of procedures; glove use was indicated in 72% of cases; 88% of participants used a single pair of gloves per procedure; and 88% reported performing hand hygiene after glove removal. Conclusion. The proposed device represents a technological strategy designed to support appropriate glove use and reinforce hand hygiene practices. Its potential impact on infection prevention and resource optimization should be evaluated in future studies.

title: Living on unstable foundations – Tracing climate change-driven housing insecurity in Bordeaux and Rotterdam
summary: This paper explores climate change-driven housing insecurity by focusing on unstable foundations. With climatic and environmental conditions changing, housing foundations, specifically those built on clay soils and in coastal areas, become
content: This paper explores climate change-driven housing insecurity by focusing on unstable foundations. With climatic and environmental conditions changing, housing foundations, specifically those built on clay soils and in coastal areas, become unstable as soil properties adapt to prolonged periods of heat and heavy rainfalls. Taking the issues of housing foundations as our point of departure, we show that unstable housing foundations are producing new forms of material insecurity and argue that we need to come to a more nuanced understanding of their political, financial, and socio-emotional repercussions. As we illustrate, technical issues regarding housing foundations are, on the one hand, highly politicized as solutions are costly and responsibilities obscure. On the other hand, they affect the subjective feeling of security and home as the material basis of housing becomes destabilized. We follow the contested issue of housing foundations in Bordeaux, France, and Rotterdam, the Netherlands. Our comparison draws on media analysis, observations during field stays in both cities, as well as key informant interviews. We argue that foundation issues expose the intertwined economic, social, and political dynamics of climate‑changed cities, demanding more coordinated policy responses.

title: Fire enhances recent carbon inputs without mobilizing ancient soil carbon in Andean páramos
summary: Abstract. Tropical Andean páramos store large amounts of soil organic carbon, including long-term carbon reservoirs whose response to fire remains poorly understood. Understanding whether fire promotes the mobilization of old soil carbon or
content: Abstract. Tropical Andean páramos store large amounts of soil organic carbon, including long-term carbon reservoirs whose response to fire remains poorly understood. Understanding whether fire promotes the mobilization of old soil carbon or primarily affects recently fixed carbon is critical for predicting carbon–climate feedback in these ecosystems. We evaluated the effects of fire history on soil carbon dynamics in a Colombian páramo in across gradients of elevation, soil depth, and time since last fire. To do this, we measured total carbon concentrations, radiocarbon signatures (Δ¹⁴C) of bulk soil organic matter, and the radiocarbon signature of heterotrophically respired carbon dioxide (Δ¹⁴CO₂) from controlled soil incubations. Bulk soil Δ¹⁴C ranged from −474 to +65 ‰, with progressively older carbon pools in deeper soils and at higher elevations. Burned soils exhibited more modern radiocarbon signatures than unburned soils (−111 ± 96 ‰ vs. −158 ± 104 ‰, respectively) and higher carbon (11.1 ± 5.8 % vs. 9.1 ± 3.8 %) concentrations. In contrast, Δ14CO2 ranged from 18.8 to 55.3 ‰ across all fire-history categories with no significant differences among burned and unburned sites, remaining consistently enriched in 14C relative to bulk soil organic matter and indicating that microbial respiration was dominated by relatively young carbon sources despite the presence of older carbon pools. Our results indicate that fires modify the age of soil organic matter primarily through the incorporation and cycling of young carbon rather than through the accelerated mineralization of old, stabilized soil carbon. Specifically, long-term post-fire vegetation recovery visibly narrows the isotopic disequilibrium between stored and respired carbon by modernizing the bulk soil pool. Similar radiocarbon values in deeper and more elevated soils suggest that long-term carbon reservoirs remain relatively resistant to individual fire events. However, increasing fire frequency and climate warming may alter the balance between carbon inputs and outputs, potentially affecting the long-term stability of carbon-rich tropical alpine soils.

title: Strengthening and safeguarding artificial intelligence for a planet under pressure
summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping sustainability science through advances in climate modeling, ecosystem monitoring, resource management, and evidence synthesis. Yet its use also raises concerns about reliability, equity
content: Abstract Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping sustainability science through advances in climate modeling, ecosystem monitoring, resource management, and evidence synthesis. Yet its use also raises concerns about reliability, equity, and environmental impacts. In this Prospective, we identify four priorities for responsible AI integration: ensuring AI-supported claims are causal, transparent, and auditable; treating model selection as an environmental decision; building sustainability-focused AI infrastructure; and engaging sustainability scientists and affected communities in AI design and governance. With these safeguards, AI can enhance sustainability science while promoting equitable and environmentally responsible decision-making.

title: Spin-induced polarization enables anodic carbon–nitrogen coupling electrocatalysis for sustainable formamide synthesis
summary: Abstract Organic electrosynthesis driven by the renewable electricity and reacted in water offers a green route to prepare higher value-added formamide by constructing carbon–nitrogen (C–N) coupling reactions. Currently, electrochemical for
content: Abstract Organic electrosynthesis driven by the renewable electricity and reacted in water offers a green route to prepare higher value-added formamide by constructing carbon–nitrogen (C–N) coupling reactions. Currently, electrochemical formamide synthesis focuses mainly on cathodic processes, required relatively expensive substrates and high electricity and equipment costs, which greatly hinders practical application in industry. Herein, we reported anodic electrosynthesis of formamide from mixed polyols and ammonia by a spin-induced polarization strategy. We proposed that alloying Fe sites into mesoporous CuO broke its long-range antiferromagnetic order and created spin-polarized surface with localized paramagnetic centers. Spin-induced polarization strategy promoted the formation and stabilization of *NH 2 intermediates without overoxidation to unreacted NO 3 − , which behaved as the dominant nucleophile to mediate concerted C–C cleavage and C–N coupling reactions for selective formamide synthesis with minor byproducts at anode. In a flow cell, it delivered a superior formamide Faradaic efficiency of 70.4% and selectivity of 99.0%, with the high net profit of US$1,598 per ton. Meanwhile, the strategy has generally been applied to mixed polyols substrates mimicking the real feedstock from renewable biomass, which further underscored promising industrial application potential. This work establishes a new paradigm to construct efficient C–N coupling reactions for various value-added amides by a spin-state engineering strategy.

title: Contrasting moisture responses of greenhouse-gas fluxes between ridge and furrow positions in a ridge–furrow plastic-mulching system
summary: Ridge–furrow plastic-mulching systems are characterized by coexisting ridge and furrow microenvironments with contrasting soil hydrothermal conditions. However, whether these spatially adjacent positions exhibit different greenhouse gas (GH
content: Ridge–furrow plastic-mulching systems are characterized by coexisting ridge and furrow microenvironments with contrasting soil hydrothermal conditions. However, whether these spatially adjacent positions exhibit different greenhouse gas (GHG) response relationships with environmental drivers remains insufficiently understood. Here, we investigated whether ridge and furrow positions within the same ridge–furrow system represent distinct observation units with different hydrothermal characteristics and gas-specific responses to soil moisture and temperature. We conducted repeated field measurements at 11 tobacco sites and quantified CO₂, CH₄, and N₂O fluxes from fixed ridge and furrow positions, together with soil temperature and volumetric water content at 5 cm depth. Linear mixed-effects models and paired-position analyses were used to evaluate positional contrasts and environmental response relationships. Ridge positions showed higher soil temperature than furrow positions, whereas volumetric water content did not differ significantly between positions. Differences in mean flux magnitude were most evident for CO₂, with higher ridge fluxes than furrow fluxes (model-estimated ridge–furrow difference: 71.44 mg CO₂ m⁻² h⁻¹), while CH₄ and N₂O positional contrasts were weaker and less consistent. In contrast, ridge and furrow positions exhibited contrasting moisture-response relationships for all three gases. CO₂ flux showed a significant positive response to soil moisture on ridges but no significant response in furrows. For CH₄, increasing soil moisture significantly weakened net CH₄ uptake in furrows, whereas no significant moisture response was detected on ridges. For N₂O, furrows showed a significant negative moisture-response relationship, whereas ridges showed a positive but non-significant response. Positional differences in temperature-response slopes were not statistically resolved across gases, whereas moisture-response contrasts were statistically supported. These results indicate that ridge–furrow plastic-mulching systems contain functionally distinct microenvironments in which GHG fluxes exhibit gas-specific moisture-response relationships. Ridge and furrow positions should therefore not be automatically treated as interchangeable observation units when monitoring, interpreting, and scaling GHG fluxes in ridge–furrow systems.

title: Asia Green Corridors: A Zero-Backend Browser Observatory for Port and Shipping Decarbonisation Decision Support in Asia
summary: Green shipping corridors are increasingly central to maritime decarbonisation in Asia, yet quantitative evidence to inform corridor choices remains limited and often requires paid data services. This paper introduces Asia Green Corridors, a
content: Green shipping corridors are increasingly central to maritime decarbonisation in Asia, yet quantitative evidence to inform corridor choices remains limited and often requires paid data services. This paper introduces Asia Green Corridors, a zero-backend browser observatory that integrates previously separate public datasets: satellite-AIS port activity for 787 ports in PortWatch's Asia-Pacific classification (including 654 with Asian country codes) and its documented disruption log; satellite-estimated emissions from 2,885 Asian international-shipping sources (Climate TRACE); 534 western North Pacific cyclone tracks since 2005 (NOAA IBTrACS); and a live sea-state feed (Open-Meteo). The 2025 emissions layer totals 266.7 Mt of CO₂-equivalent on a 100-year global-warming-potential basis. The observatory provides one-click port screening, compares six Middle East–Asia corridor hubs by vessel calls and satellite-estimated emissions, and monitors three strategic chokepoints daily. A transparent scenario sandbox and checkpoint solver estimate the green-fuel shares implied by the IMO Revised Strategy's emissions checkpoints under an illustrative 2025-normalised pathway. At the model's default settings, meeting the indicative 2030 checkpoints on time requires deployed green-fuel shares of approximately 18%–29% of energy. These exceed the IMO's separate 5%–10% fuel-uptake ambition, but differing indicators, accounting assumptions and the model's restricted mitigation levers preclude interpreting the comparison as a direct policy shortfall. Anomaly detectors are evaluated against 83 eligible documented disruption events. At an operating point chosen by a transparent, predefined rule, they detected 59.0% of events in sample, generating 1.41 alerts per monitored port per year (2.04 per actively graded port); this event-level sensitivity is not a measure of comprehensive detection accuracy. The full sensitivity grid, event-type results and limitations are disclosed. Implemented as one HTML file and five static data bundles, the application requires no backend, account or API key and explicitly identifies unavailable feeds. It is openly released as an empirical companion to the author's corridor working paper.

title: BC Instrument Field Comparison
summary: Comparison of two black carbon instruments for quantifying the black carbon emissions from a T63 turboshaft aircraft engine burning conventional and Fischer-Tropsch fuel. This dataset is associated with the following publication: Kinsey, J.
content: Comparison of two black carbon instruments for quantifying the black carbon emissions from a T63 turboshaft aircraft engine burning conventional and Fischer-Tropsch fuel. This dataset is associated with the following publication: Kinsey, J., E. Corporan, J. Pavlovic, M. DeWitt, C. Klingshirn, and R. Logan.
