title: Association of individual exposure to PM2.5 components with pulmonary tuberculosis hospitalization and the effect modification by greenness
summary: It remains unknown of the effects of short-term exposure to components of ambient particulate matter with aerodynamic diameters < 2.5 μm (PM 2.5 ) on pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) hospitalization and the effect modification by greenness at a
content: It remains unknown of the effects of short-term exposure to components of ambient particulate matter with aerodynamic diameters < 2.5 μm (PM 2.5 ) on pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) hospitalization and the effect modification by greenness at an individual level. We collected information on 4,524 PTB hospital admissions, PM 2.5 and its components (sulphate [SO 4 2− ], nitrate [NO 3 − ], ammonium [NH 4 + ], organic matter [OM], and black carbon [BC]) in Hainan, China during 2016–2019. Based on case-crossover design, we used conditional logistic regression models with stabilized inverse probability weights to explore the associations between PM 2.5 components and PTB hospitalization. We found that risk of PTB hospitalization increased by 9.77% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.60, 17.44%), 14.68% (7.25, 22.64%), 8.53% (1.84, 15.66%), 10.81% (3.84, 18.26%), 6.82% (0.78, 13.23%), and 10.07% (3.17, 17.44%) for every interquartile range increase in PM 2.5 , SO 4 2− , NO 3 − , NH 4 + , OM, and BC, respectively. SO 4 2− (41.6%) together with BC (39.0%) contributed > 80% of the total effects of the five components. PM 2.5 and its components posed higher risk for patients aged ≥ 65 years, those living in prefecture-level cities, and in the warm season. The adverse effects were statistically significant for the patients living in low-NDVI (normalized difference vegetation index < 0.45) regions, but not for those in other regions. This study provides evidence for the adverse impacts of PM 2.5 components on PTB hospitalization. Our study highlights the necessity for targeted intervention strategies to reduce the PTB burden and thereby improve public health outcomes. Specifically, reducing the emission of PM 2.5 , especially SO 4 2− and BC, and increasing green spaces in low-NDVI regions (e.g., developing new parks and gardens, encouraging rooftop greening on buildings, and restoring degraded forests) would be of great significance.

title: Carbon Break Even Conditions for Cooling Selection in Precision Turning
summary: Abstract Minimum quantity lubrication can reduce fluid consumption while increasing compressed air demand, making its carbon advantage dependent on machining quality and tooling performance. This study develops an analytical method for sele
tags: Enhanced Data Rates for GSM Evolution
content: Abstract Minimum quantity lubrication can reduce fluid consumption while increasing compressed air demand, making its carbon advantage dependent on machining quality and tooling performance. This study develops an analytical method for selecting cooling strategies using emissions per accepted turned component. The method combines machine electricity, compressed air, net fluid consumption, cutting edge service and rejected workpieces within a consistent product boundary. Closed form expressions establish the minimum acceptable yield, maximum air demand and minimum cutting edge capacity required for minimum quantity lubrication to outperform flood cooling. An explicitly assumed steel turning case demonstrates the calculations without claiming experimental validation. At the selected electricity factor, minimum quantity lubrication reduces carbon intensity from 4.7177 to 4.6949 kg carbon dioxide equivalent per accepted component, a conditional improvement of 0.48%. Increasing rejection from 2% to 3% reverses that ranking. The corresponding air threshold is 1.558 cubic metres per attempted component. Joint interval analysis also identifies conditions under which neither strategy dominates. The contribution is a reproducible decision method that connects cooling selection to measurable production limits and identifies the evidence required for industrial verification.

title: Decoupling growth from degradation: a fractional frequency Fourier analysis of India's aviation sector and the environmental Kuznets Curve
summary: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India's aviation sector from 1970 to 2021. Using the ecological footprint as an indicator
content: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India's aviation sector from 1970 to 2021. Using the ecological footprint as an indicator and a novel fractional frequency Fourier approach, it tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. The results reveal a U-shaped relationship, contradicting the EKC, and highlight the negative environmental impact of increased air freight. However, financial development supports sustainability by enabling cleaner technologies. The study aims to inform policy by proposing strategies such as carbon pricing, renewable fuel adoption, and green logistics to decouple aviation growth from environmental harm. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a fractional frequency Fourier approach to examine the long-run relationship between economic growth, air transportation, financial development, and environmental degradation in India from 1970 to 2021. The ecological footprint is used as a comprehensive measure of environmental impact. This advanced econometric method captures structural breaks and nonlinearities more effectively than traditional models. By testing the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis within this framework, the study provides nuanced insights into the dynamic interactions among the variables. The methodology ensures robustness through unit root tests, cointegration analysis, and appropriate diagnostic checks to validate the model's findings. Findings The study finds a U-shaped relationship between economic growth and ecological footprint, rejecting the validity of the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis for India's aviation sector. Economic growth initially reduces environmental degradation but worsens it beyond a threshold. Air transport freight is positively associated with ecological footprint, indicating environmental harm from increased logistics activity. In contrast, financial development mitigates environmental degradation by supporting investments in clean technologies and sustainable practices. These findings emphasize the need for targeted policies to decouple aviation growth from environmental impacts and promote long-term sustainability within the sector through green financing and eco-friendly logistics solutions. Originality/value This study offers a novel contribution by applying the fractional frequency Fourier approach to analyze the environmental impacts of India's aviation sector—an area underexplored in existing literature. Unlike traditional methods, this approach captures complex nonlinear dynamics and structural breaks over time. By using ecological footprint as a comprehensive indicator of environmental degradation, the study moves beyond CO2-focused analyses. Its rejection of the EKC hypothesis provides fresh insights into the unsustainable nature of aviation-led growth in India. The findings deliver valuable policy guidance for integrating fin

title: Torrefied Agri-Food Residues as a Coal Substitute: How the Supply Chain and the Allocation Rule Determine the Carbon Footprint
summary: Agri-food processing leaves large volumes of lignocellulosic residues for which their energy is rarely recovered, while coal-fired heat and power in Europe carries a rising carbon price. This study quantifies the carbon footprint of five fo
content: Agri-food processing leaves large volumes of lignocellulosic residues for which their energy is rarely recovered, while coal-fired heat and power in Europe carries a rising carbon price. This study quantifies the carbon footprint of five food-processing residues—spent coffee grounds (SCGs), spent tea leaves (TEAs) and walnut, pistachio and peanut shells—with spruce wood chips as a non-food benchmark, torrefied at 250–550 °C and burned in place of Czech lignite. Fuel properties were measured for all six materials at five temperatures and their replicate variances propagated. Emissions were quantified for nine process stages—from cultivation of the crop to combustion of the fuel—per tonne of dry residue under a fuel-first allocation that charges the residue with the agricultural chain and credits the food co-product by system expansion; cut-off, mass and economic allocation were compared. All six materials save emissions at their selected temperature, from −557 ± 22 kg CO2-eq t−1 for SCG to −1214 ± 23 for spruce, avoiding 36–77% of the emissions of the lignite they replace. The ranking is set by the supply chain rather than by the fuel: SCG has the highest calorific value of the set yet saves least, because 89% of its residual burden comes from roasting, brewing and intercontinental freight. The result is conditional: Under mass allocation, four of the five food residues become net emitters, and so do SCG and TEA when collected wet. At 65 EUR tCO2−1, the avoided emissions are worth 36–79 EUR t−1 against a fuel-cost advantage over lignite of 116–200 EUR t−1.

title: Polycrisis Resilience: The H Heuristics Framework
summary: Polycrisis Resilience: The H Heuristics Framework presents a development-oriented framework for reducing vulnerability to multiple interacting and compounding crises. The framework defines Polycrisis Resilience as the capacity of individual
content: Polycrisis Resilience: The H Heuristics Framework presents a development-oriented framework for reducing vulnerability to multiple interacting and compounding crises. The framework defines Polycrisis Resilience as the capacity of individuals, communities, societies, economies, institutions, and interconnected systems to withstand, adapt to, recover from, and reduce vulnerability to interconnected risks. Its central proposition is that improving underlying economic, technological, environmental, and institutional conditions progressively reduces vulnerability across multiple domains simultaneously. The framework examines how economic convergence, technological diffusion, clean energy access, climate adaptation, institutional capacity, and human development can function as resilience-building mechanisms. The report identifies eight development capabilities and nine domains of vulnerability, arguing that many global risks share common underlying drivers and therefore require integrated rather than hazard-specific solutions. Using a Development Capability Index (DCI) constructed for 194 countries, the report tests whether development capability is associated with reduced vulnerability. Results show strong negative relationships between development capability and child mortality, poverty, undernourishment, inadequate sanitation, and climate-disaster mortality. The analysis also finds that foundational deficits cluster together, creating reinforcing cycles of vulnerability, while progress in infrastructure, health, and institutional development can simultaneously reduce multiple forms of risk. The evidence suggests that development functions as a resilience strategy, but not a sufficient one. Development capability strongly reduces direct human harms but does not reliably prevent macroeconomic shocks, pandemics, or other systemic disruptions. Furthermore, historical development pathways have often increased environmental pressures, particularly carbon emissions. For this reason, the framework complements development with three additional priorities: protection through buffers and social protection systems, adaptive capacity, and a clean transition.The report places particular emphasis on the Global South, where overlapping deficits remain concentrated. While many middle-income countries have substantially reduced foundational vulnerabilities since 2000, progress has slowed in many low-income countries, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa. The framework therefore advocates accelerated convergence, clean development, technological diffusion, and institution-building as central strategies for reducing global vulnerability throughout the twenty-first century. Its ultimate objective is to reduce vulnerability across human and socioeconomic systems by strengthening the capabilities, infrastructure, institutions, and technologies that support long-term human development while protecting those gains against future shocks.

title: Do Excedente à Produção de Moléculas
summary: Três fatos de 2026 marcam o fim do ciclo do etanol como produto exclusivamente combustível e de mercado doméstico, mas não o do etanol combustível. Em 2025/26, o etanol de milho cresceu 29,8% e o de cana caiu 6,9%; em agosto, a mistura na g
content: Três fatos de 2026 marcam o fim do ciclo do etanol como produto exclusivamente combustível e de mercado doméstico, mas não o do etanol combustível. Em 2025/26, o etanol de milho cresceu 29,8% e o de cana caiu 6,9%; em agosto, a mistura na gasolina subiu para 32%, a três pontos do teto; em julho, 9,7% dos leves emplacados foram 100% elétricos, e um terço dos hatches pequenos, segmento que mais consome hidratado. Um modelo de frota por ano de venda, com trajetórias de eletrificação de 23 países, confronta a demanda de etanol de leves e motocicletas até 2050 com a expansão projetada do milho. O excedente chega a 10–18 bilhões de litros em 2035 e 14–24 bilhões em 2040, contra o equilíbrio do plano decenal, e persiste com eletrificação lenta, porque começa pelo milho. Somados, os mitigadores (mix açúcar–etanol, freio no milho, mistura a 35%, participação do hidratado no patamar de 2019) aproximam do equilíbrio o balanço central de 2035, mas deixam 4 a 8 bilhões em 2040 (0 a 5 com eletrificação lenta). Novos destinos (navegação, diesel renovável, querosene de aviação, química, exportação) podem absorver 6 a 18 bilhões em 2040, mas não estão contratados. Propõe-se tratar o excedente como plataforma: abrir esses mercados, capturar o CO₂ de fermentação e instalar biomanufatura por contrato em usinas e biorrefinarias, com piloto paulista. Com décadas de ciência agronômica tropical e uma nova geração de cientistas, o Brasil pode tornar-se fornecedor confiável de combustíveis, moléculas, proteínas e remoções de carbono.

title: Carboxymethyl cellulose aerogels with Laponite, halloysite or kaolin: effect of clay type on shrinkage, compressive and heat-transfer behavior
summary: Abstract Freeze-dried carboxymethyl cellulose aerogels are light but can shrink during drying and are mechanically weak. This study examined how the type of clay changes the structure and properties of these aerogels, comparing the syntheti
content: Abstract Freeze-dried carboxymethyl cellulose aerogels are light but can shrink during drying and are mechanically weak. This study examined how the type of clay changes the structure and properties of these aerogels, comparing the synthetic smectite Laponite (2:1 layered discs) with the 1:1 aluminosilicates halloysite (nanotubes) and kaolin (platelets). A 0.8% (w/v) carboxymethyl cellulose solution was mixed in equal volumes with clay dispersions of 0.4–2.0% (w/v) and freeze-dried. Compressive behavior was assessed by uniaxial compression, heat transfer by infrared thermography on a 200°C hot plate, and polymer–clay interactions by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Aerogels containing Laponite retained about 37% of their cast volume, compared with about 20% for those containing halloysite or kaolin. Because the compression tests ended at very different strains, the composites were compared at 10% strain. At this strain, the Laponite composites carried 2.6–10.3 kPa, 2.0–7.7 times more than the halloysite and kaolin composites, and the stress increased with Laponite concentration, whereas the halloysite and kaolin composites, which have nearly the same composition but different shapes, behaved similarly (1.2–1.6 kPa). After 30 min on the hot plate, the lowest top-surface temperatures (81.6–82.9°C, compared with 90.1°C for the neat aerogel) were recorded for 2.0% halloysite and 1.2–1.6% kaolin. The results suggest that Laponite forms a continuous network with the polymer that limits shrinkage and stiffens the aerogel, whereas halloysite and kaolin act mainly as fillers. As thermal conductivity and porosity were not measured and heights and densities were estimated, the results describe comparative trends.

title: From the 2026 Hormuz disruption to renewable resilience: energy security and decarbonization governance in import-dependent economies
summary: Import-dependent economies face a systemic governance challenge: a small number of fossil-fuel chokepoints and centralized fossil assets concentrate macroeconomic, health, and water-security risks that conventional energy-security framing s
content: Import-dependent economies face a systemic governance challenge: a small number of fossil-fuel chokepoints and centralized fossil assets concentrate macroeconomic, health, and water-security risks that conventional energy-security framing systematically underprices. Using the 2026 disruption of the Strait of Hormuz as an illustrative stress test and Israel as a semi-arid, security-sensitive case, this Perspective develops a four-component analytical framework—chokepoint-exposure assessment (distinguishing physical supply, global price, infrastructure-concentration, and cross-sector cascade exposure), quantification of domestic fossil-fuel externalities, mapping of fossil-fuel–water infrastructure couplings, and security-oriented governance instruments—and applies it to governmental, OECD, and epidemiological evidence. The analysis shows that Israel’s fossil-centric paradigm couples exposure to distant chokepoints with the concentration of domestic gas supply in three offshore platforms, a total ambient air-pollution burden of 4,641–6,166 premature deaths annually (over USD 7.2 billion in economic costs), to which fossil-fuel combustion is a major though not exclusive contributor, and a desalination system exposed to low-probability, high-impact maritime oil-spill scenarios. We argue that distributed renewable generation, energy storage, and transport electrification warrant designation and governance as critical national infrastructure, supported by binding climate mitigation legislation, targeted fiscal instruments, and resilience metrics embedded in national security assessments. The framework is operationalized in a reproducible component–indicator–data table, and we conclude by specifying screening criteria under which it may inform decarbonization policy in other small, import-dependent economies.

title: From Managerial Ability to Climate Action: The Mediating Role of Corporate Governance in Achieving SDG 13 in the UK Context
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT In line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (UNSDG) 13, which emphasizes the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change, this study investigates the role of managerial ability and co
content: ABSTRACT In line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (UNSDG) 13, which emphasizes the urgent need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and mitigate climate change, this study investigates the role of managerial ability and corporate governance in shaping firms' climate change commitments. Using a sample of 4056 firm‐year observations from companies listed on the London Stock Exchange over the period 2013–2022, the analysis employs ordinary least squares regression, complemented by generalized method of moments and two‐stage least squares estimations to address potential endogeneity concerns. Drawing on stakeholder theory and upper‐echelons and Institutional theory, the findings reveal that greater managerial ability is positively associated with more substantial corporate commitments to addressing climate change, reflecting managers' enhanced oversight capacity, strategic orientation, and ethical awareness. Moreover, the results indicate that corporate governance mechanisms partially mediate the relationship between managerial ability and climate change commitment, underscoring their role in translating managerial competencies into practical climate actions. This study contributes to the environmental and corporate governance literature by providing empirical evidence on the importance of organizational ability and governance structures in advancing corporate climate strategies and supporting the achievement of the climate objectives outlined in the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

title: A Study on Market Dynamics, Competitive Landscape, Import Economics and Trading Viability of Bisphenol A and Chloroprene Rubber for Atul Ltd
source: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
summary: India imports almost all of its Bisphenol A (BPA) and Chloroprene Rubber (CR), yet published market reports say little about who imports these chemicals, from where, and at what duty-adjusted cost. This study examines whether bulk import fo
content: India imports almost all of its Bisphenol A (BPA) and Chloroprene Rubber (CR), yet published market reports say little about who imports these chemicals, from where, and at what duty-adjusted cost. This study examines whether bulk import for resale is commercially viable for Atul Ltd., a leading Indian chemicals manufacturer, or whether each material is better used purely as manufacturing feedstock. A descriptive and analytical design was applied to 3,103 cleaned BPA import transactions (approximately 432,700 MT; FY2022–FY2026) and 10,346 cleaned CR shipment lines (100,584 MT; FY2021-22 to FY2025-26), supplemented by secondary market, pricing and regulatory sources. Importers were classified as manufacturers or traders, duty and free-trade-agreement (FTA) structures were mapped by country of origin, and landed-cost and margin models were built from first principles. BPA imports are highly concentrated: Grasim Industries (about 44%) and Atul (about 24%) together hold roughly two-thirds of volume, manufacturers account for about 90%, and about 82% of volume enters duty-free from FTA partners, leaving a pure trading model with an indicative gross margin of only about 0.8%. In CR, Japan supplies 57.9% of imports at zero duty under the India–Japan CEPA, whereas other origins bear a 10% basic customs duty; an indicative resale earns a net margin of about 3.8% on full-duty origins against about 14.9% on Japanese CEPA-origin material. Atul sources about 69% of its own CR from China at full duty. Country-of-origin duty status, rather than commodity price, therefore governs trading profitability. The study recommends retaining BPA as feedstock and repositioning CR activity as a preferential-origin, bulk-breaking distribution business. Because the datasets carry no invoice values, all price-based figures are indicative. Keywords: Bisphenol A; chloroprene rubber; import economics; free trade agreements; customs duty; trading viability; landed cost; India

title: Tower-based NDVI and chlorophyll fluorescence dataset for estimating GPP seasonality in deciduous and evergreen forests.
summary: A dataset of tower-based optical measurements and ecosystem carbon flux estimates from a European beech forest at Štítná (April–October 2017) and a Norway spruce forest at Bílý Kříž (April–October 2018), Czech Republic, at 30-minute resolut
content: A dataset of tower-based optical measurements and ecosystem carbon flux estimates from a European beech forest at Štítná (April–October 2017) and a Norway spruce forest at Bílý Kříž (April–October 2018), Czech Republic, at 30-minute resolution. Variables include gross primary productivity (GPP), total ecosystem respiration (TER), light use efficiency (LUE), NDVI and PRI variants, sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence in the O₂A (~760 nm) and O₂B (~687 nm) bands, and fluorescence emission yields. Additional data include incoming and absorbed photosynthetically active radiation, air and soil temperatures, selected spectral variables and LiDAR-derived canopy shadow fractions. GPP and TER were derived from CO₂ fluxes measured by eddy covariance. The dataset accompanies Kováč et al., “Tower-based NDVI and fluorescence measurements for estimating GPP seasonality in deciduous and evergreen forests”, European Journal of Remote Sensing. https://doi.org/10.1080/22797254.2026.2760141

title: Eco-Hype or Eco-Hope?
source: The International Journal of Social Sustainability in Economic Social and Cultural Context
summary: The Olympic Games claim to be exemplars of sustainability, aiming to inspire sustainable futures around the world. The organizers positioned Paris 2024 as the most sustainable Games ever, promising a 50% reduction in carbon emissions compar
content: The Olympic Games claim to be exemplars of sustainability, aiming to inspire sustainable futures around the world. The organizers positioned Paris 2024 as the most sustainable Games ever, promising a 50% reduction in carbon emissions compared to prior editions. The issue of greenwashing—projecting a picture of environmental responsibility without taking significant action—becomes pertinent and pressing in this situation. Because of the Games’ enormous popularity, any sustainability narrative that is adopted has a worldwide audience and can either support or contradict public views of environmental responsibility. Therefore, it is necessary to consider if the Paris Olympics indeed signify a radical change in the way that these kinds of events are planned and carried out, or if they are just an example of a more advanced kind of greenwashing. In light of this, a crucial research question arises: Was Paris’ goal to create a new standard truly intended, or was it just excellent advertising covering up unpleasant facts? This study pursued its objective by conducting a two-round Delphi survey that included a diverse range of professional expertise from the field of sports and sponsorship, among others in order to enhance the multi-faceted examination of sustainability and public opinion. In addition to shedding light on the veracity of Paris 2024’s sustainability claims, the present study advances our knowledge of how environmental narratives are created, disseminated, and challenged in the era of the climate catastrophe and media spectacle.

title: Institutional energy use and clean cooking transition pathways in public schools in southern Tanzania
summary: Public schools remain underexamined in clean cooking research despite their substantial energy demands and distinctive financing and governance arrangements. This study examined institutional energy use and expenditure, the operational cons
content: Public schools remain underexamined in clean cooking research despite their substantial energy demands and distinctive financing and governance arrangements. This study examined institutional energy use and expenditure, the operational consequences of energy insecurity, barriers to the clean cooking transition, schools’ energy-management and adaptation strategies, and the comparative suitability of alternative cooking technologies in southern Tanzania. We conducted a mixed-methods study in 27 purposively selected public schools across five local government authorities in the Ruvuma and Mtwara regions. We collected data through semi-structured interviews, field observations, and available school records. We analysed them using descriptive statistics, thematic analysis, and an equal-weight multi-criteria assessment of six cooking technologies across nine economic, technical, environmental, and institutional criteria. Firewood was the primary cooking fuel in 26 of the 27 schools, whereas grid electricity was the principal lighting source in 23 schools, revealing a divergence between electrification and the cooking energy transition. Firewood-dependent boarding schools spent approximately TZS 1.59–2.80 million per month on cooking fuel, compared with approximately TZS 1.55 million in the boarding school using LPG. Energy insecurity disrupted water pumping, grain milling, administrative activities and laboratory practical work. Limited financing, high initial investment requirements, infrastructure gaps, limited technical capacity, unreliable energy supplies, and institutional approval processes constrained the transition. Schools responded through energy diversification, backup systems, electricity prioritisation, improved cookstoves, and investment or planned investment in alternative energy systems. Under the equal-weight assessment, electricity and biogas jointly achieved the highest suitability score of 16, followed by LPG at 14. The findings demonstrate that the clean cooking transition in public schools is shaped not simply by technology availability, but by the financial, infrastructural and organisational capacity required to adopt and sustain cleaner systems. By extending clean cooking analysis beyond households, the study provides an institutional basis for planning more sustainable school energy transitions in Tanzania. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Engineering Performance and Sustainability Assessment of Concrete Incorporating Banana Leaf Ash and Rice Husk Ash
summary: The environmental effects of cement manufacturing and river sand removal have increased interest in environmentally friendly construction materials that reduce resource use and greenhouse gas emissions. This study examined concrete using ba
content: The environmental effects of cement manufacturing and river sand removal have increased interest in environmentally friendly construction materials that reduce resource use and greenhouse gas emissions. This study examined concrete using banana leaf ash (BLA) as a partial replacement for Portland cement and RHA to replace fine aggregate in concrete proportioned for an M30 target strength. Five mixes containing 0–20% each of BLA and RHA were evaluated for fresh properties, mechanical characteristics, durability, economic feasibility, and sustainability characteristics. The best-performing mix (M2) contained 10% BLA and 10% RHA and achieved the greatest 28 day compressive strength of 39.2 MPa, exceeding the control at 34.8 MPa. One-way ANOVA confirmed statistically significant differences among compressive strength values; Tukey HSD post-hoc analysis identified statistically significant differences in seven of the ten pairwise comparisons. M2 also showed higher split tensile and flexural strength and lower water absorption and sorptivity than the control. Cost comparison indicated minimal material cost savings due to substituting RHA for river sand. Sustainability analysis showed reduced cement, river sand, and embodied CO2 from cement manufacturing. These data indicate retained engineering performance overall.

title: Extension of 2-Ethoxyethanol Rotational Spectroscopy and Its Search in the Interstellar Medium
summary: Abstract Motivated by the recent detections of related alkoxy alcohols in the interstellar medium (ISM), we conducted a rotational spectroscopic study of 2-ethoxyethanol (C 2 H 5 OCH 2 CH 2 OH) to enable its search in the ISM. Quantum chemi
content: Abstract Motivated by the recent detections of related alkoxy alcohols in the interstellar medium (ISM), we conducted a rotational spectroscopic study of 2-ethoxyethanol (C 2 H 5 OCH 2 CH 2 OH) to enable its search in the ISM. Quantum chemical calculations were performed to identify the lowest-energy conformers and predict their spectroscopic parameters. The rotational spectrum of the most stable conformer, −sc +sc ap ap-, was measured using complementary spectrometers covering the frequency regions 2–20, 6.5–18, 150–220, 230–330, and 370–500 GHz. A total of 2628 distinct transitions were assigned and fitted using a Watson A-reduced Hamiltonian, allowing the determination of rotational and centrifugal distortion constants up to the octic level. The resulting spectroscopic predictions are suitable for astronomical observations in the (sub)millimeter-wave domains. Using these new data, a search for −sc +sc ap ap- 2-ethoxyethanol was carried out toward NGC 6334I using Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations. No detection was obtained, and an upper limit column density of 1.1 × 10 17 cm −2 was derived.

title: The mycotoxin zearalenone couples secondary metabolism to N -acetylglucosamine catabolism
summary: Fungal secondary metabolites are often viewed as terminal products of specialized metabolism, yet how their production influences the physiology of the producing organism remains poorly understood. Here, we show that zearalenone (ZEA) produ
content: Fungal secondary metabolites are often viewed as terminal products of specialized metabolism, yet how their production influences the physiology of the producing organism remains poorly understood. Here, we show that zearalenone (ZEA) production is functionally coupled to N -acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) catabolism in Fusarium graminearum . Transcriptome profiling of a ZEB2 -overexpressing strain revealed enrichment of GlcNAc metabolic functions, and exogenous ZEA induced key catabolic genes independently of Zeb2. Among pathway components, NAG , encoding GlcNAc-6-phosphate deacetylase, was critical for GlcNAc utilization, and its loss caused severe GlcNAc-dependent growth inhibition. Genetic impairment of NAG was poorly tolerated under elevated ZEA pathway activity. Conversely, NAG overexpression increased tolerance to exogenous ZEA and alleviated the growth defect associated with ZEB2 overexpression. Together, these findings reveal a functional connection between secondary metabolite production and primary nutrient metabolism and suggest that ZEA-associated metabolic remodeling contributes to the fitness of the producing fungus.

title: Optimizing Waste Management Systems to Reduce Greenhouse Gas Emissions on the Small Island of Kodingareng Lompo, Indonesia
summary: The absence of an effective waste management system in small island areas significantly contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly from uncontrolled open burning. This study analyzes the potential of an integrated waste man
content: The absence of an effective waste management system in small island areas significantly contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, particularly from uncontrolled open burning. This study analyzes the potential of an integrated waste management system to reduce GHG emissions in Kodingareng Lompo Island by comparing existing practices with an alternative scenario aligned with Presidential Regulation of the Republic of Indonesia No. 97 of 2017, which targets 30% waste reduction and 70% waste handling. Emission estimates were calculated using the IPCC methodology and global warming potential (GWP) approach. Under existing conditions, waste reduction is minimal (1.37%), while 98.63% of waste is handled through environmentally unsound practices, primarily open burning, marine disposal, and uncontrolled dumping. The alternative scenario introduces a resource-oriented paradigm, achieving 31.88% waste reduction and 68.12% controlled waste handling. As a result, total GWP decreases substantially from 171,708.79 kg CO₂e yr⁻¹ to 61,123.91 kg CO₂e yr⁻¹, representing a 64.40% reduction. This decline is driven by significant decreases in CO₂, CH₄, and N₂O emissions following the elimination of open burning and the optimization of biological and controlled treatment processes. These findings demonstrate that the proposed integrated waste management scheme significantly reduces GHG emissions and provides a feasible and replicable model for small island contexts facing similar infrastructural and governance constraints. Its implementation requires coordinated engagement among local authorities, communities, and waste management operators, contributing to climate change mitigation and supporting sustainable coastal ecosystem management.

title: Hybrid CMOS–MJT Circuits for High-Performance CIM Architecture
summary: The rising ubiquitous demand for artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning, Internet of Things (IoT), big data applications, etc., has been backed at both the software and hardware levels. At the software level, algorithms such as Monte C
content: The rising ubiquitous demand for artificial intelligence (AI), deep learning, Internet of Things (IoT), big data applications, etc., has been backed at both the software and hardware levels. At the software level, algorithms such as Monte Carlo tree search, convolutional neural networks, ResNet, and EfficientNet are being used; meanwhile, at the hardware level, high-performance, energy-efficient graphics processing units (GPUs) such as GeForce RTX 50 series support the implementation of these applications. The achievement at the hardware level is underpinned by the relentless advancement in fabrication technologies such as progressive downscaling of complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology and the introduction of advanced transistor architectures such as Fin field-effect transistors (FinFETs) [ 1 , 2 ] and carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNTFETs) [ 3 , 4 ], which offer improved power efficiency with high performance in modern integrated circuits (ICs). A notable example is Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which, in 2025, successfully fabricated approximately 92 billion FinFETs for NVIDIA RTX 5090 GPU using the 5-nm process technology. Despite these achievements, continued downscaling faces formidable challenges as transistor dimensions approach a few atomic layers. At such scales, quantum mechanical effects—especially quantum tunneling—become prominent, leading to increased leakage currents and elevated standby power dissipation [ 5–8 ]. This is particularly critical in volatile memory systems, where continuous power is required to retain stored information. Concurrently, the rise in operating frequencies contributes to higher dynamic power dissipation and escalates heat generation to levels nearing thermal design limits. Furthermore, as CMOS technology scales down, global interconnects become disproportionately longer relative to transistor dimensions. This results in additional dynamic power consumption and signal propagation delays [ 9 ], thereby compounding the overall power challenges in volatile memory systems. Let’s take an example of memory hierarchy as shown in Figure 10.1 . The on-chip cache levels, such as L1 and L2, primarily utilize static random-access memory (SRAM). Although SRAM offers high-speed performance, it suffers from significant standby power consumption due to subthreshold leakage currents. On the other hand, L3 and L4 cache levels, often implemented using dynamic random-access memory (DRAM), are constrained by the volatility of stored charge and require frequent refresh operations, leading to increased power demand.

title: LenoxKaplan_Role of natural gas in meeting electric sector emissions reduction strategy_dataset
summary: This dataset is for an analysis that used the MARKAL linear optimization model to compare the carbon emissions profiles and system-wide global warming potential of the U.S. energy system over a series of model runs in which the power sector
content: This dataset is for an analysis that used the MARKAL linear optimization model to compare the carbon emissions profiles and system-wide global warming potential of the U.S. energy system over a series of model runs in which the power sector is required to meet a specific carbon dioxide reduction target across a number of scenarios in which the availability of natural gas changes. Scenarios are run with carbon dioxide emissions and a range of upstream methane emission leakage rates from natural gas production along with upstream methane and carbon dioxide emissions associated with production of coal and oil. This dataset is associated with the following publication: Lenox , C., and O. Kaplan. Role of natural gas in meeting an electric sector emissions reduction strategy and effects on greenhouse gas emissions. Energy Economics. Elsevier B.V., Amsterdam, NETHERLANDS, 60: 460-468, (2016).

title: Hierarchical Source-Network-Storage Coordinated Scheduling for Low-Carbon and Economic Operation of Active Distribution Networks via Carbon Flow and Reinforcement Learning
summary: To address the coupling and timescale differences between network reconfiguration and Source-storage dispatch in active distribution networks, this paper proposes a hierarchical source-network-storage coordinated scheduling method for low-c
content: To address the coupling and timescale differences between network reconfiguration and Source-storage dispatch in active distribution networks, this paper proposes a hierarchical source-network-storage coordinated scheduling method for low-carbon and economic operation. A three-layer framework is developed to coordinate hourly network reconfiguration with 15-min source-storage dispatch, where carbon flow theory is incorporated to formulate a comprehensive low-carbon economic objective. A Trajectory-Centered Advantage-Driven Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm is proposed for high-dimensional topology decision-making, while a carbon-flow-driven three-path differential reward mechanism and curriculum learning are integrated into Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization for source-storage dispatch. The coordination layer further adjusts network topology according to source-storage operating states. Simulations on a modified IEEE 33-bus system demonstrate that, across renewable penetration levels of 20–100%, the proposed method reduces daily carbon emissions by 934.64–1091.66 kg and operating costs by 212.90–246.26 CNY, while reducing active power losses and improving voltage performance. The method also demonstrates good generalization capability under unseen renewable penetration levels and achieves scheduling performance comparable to mathematical optimization, while reducing online computation time by 98.14%.

title: Fe(III) hydrolysis-driven Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple for iron sludge-free Fenton-like oxidation
summary: Conventional Fe(II/III) cyclically mediated Fenton processes exhibit strict acid pH-dependence and excessive iron sludge output due to sluggish Fe(III) reduction. Here, we leverage the intrinsic hydrolysis of Fe(III) to strategically modula
content: Conventional Fe(II/III) cyclically mediated Fenton processes exhibit strict acid pH-dependence and excessive iron sludge output due to sluggish Fe(III) reduction. Here, we leverage the intrinsic hydrolysis of Fe(III) to strategically modulate its hydroxyl coordination, achieving efficient contaminant degradation through peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation. Theoretical and experimental results show that hydroxyl coordination accelerates electron transport from Fe(III) to PMS, lowering the energy barrier for simultaneously generating Fe(IV) and sulfate radical. Moreover, Fe(IV) further oxidizes contaminants with Fe(III) regeneration, promoting sustained and complete PMS decomposition via Fe(III/IV) redox couple. Based on this mechanism, a Fe(III)-cycled Fenton-like process operating under neutral conditions was developed for the effective treatment of actual wastewater without iron sludge output. Techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment confirm its enhanced economic viability and environmental sustainability compared to the conventional Fenton process. This work provides an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like oxidation strategy for water decontamination. This study reveals that Fe(III) hydrolysis can establish the Fe(III)/Fe(IV) redox couple to activate peroxymonosulfate under neutral conditions. This enables an iron sludge-free and acid pH-independent Fenton-like process for water decontamination.

title: The carbon at risk measure for managing carbon removal risk and guiding portfolio construction
summary: Abstract Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted remov
content: Abstract Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted removals and realized storage at a given confidence level and time horizon. We calibrate CaR in two proof-of-concept applications: forest carbon, where Monte Carlo simulations driven by satellite fire data yield a single-project 95% CaR of more than 70% over 200 years for California, and geological storage, where simulations using the Storage Security Calculator show that the 95% CaR ranges from 0.15% (well-regulated offshore) to 17% (poorly regulated onshore). Combining technologies in a portfolio can help manage tail risk cost-effectively. The minimum cost of meeting a permanence target depends on the magnitude and correlation structure of key risk factors. CaR provides a technology-agnostic basis for risk-calibrated buffer sizing, insurance pricing and reserve-fund design, over both policy- and climate-relevant horizons.

title: Joint measurements of black carbon and particle mass for heavydutydiesel vehicles using a portable emission measurement system
summary: PEMS-chasing experiments were conducted for twelve heavy-duty diesel vehicles (HDDTs) to evaluate the accuracy of mobile measurement results. Two data processing approaches were integrated to automate the calculations of fuel consumption-ba
content: PEMS-chasing experiments were conducted for twelve heavy-duty diesel vehicles (HDDTs) to evaluate the accuracy of mobile measurement results. Two data processing approaches were integrated to automate the calculations of fuel consumption-based emission factors of nitrogen oxides (NOX). With a total of 245 plume chasing tests conducted, and then averaged by vehicle and road types, we found that the relative errors of vehicle-specific emission factors using an algorithm developed for this project were within approximately ± 20% of the PEMS results for all tested vehicles. Stochastic simulations suggested reasonable results could be obtained using fewer chasing tests per vehicle (e.g., 71% for freeways and 93% for local road, equivalent to two chase tests per vehicle). This study improves the understanding of the accuracy of the mobile chasing method, and provides a practical approach for real-time emission measurements for future scaled-up mobile chasing studies. This dataset is associated with the following publications: Wu, Y., H. Wang, K. Zhang, S. Zhang, R. Baldauf, P. Deshmukh, and R. Snow. Evaluating mobile monitoring of on-road emission factors by comparing concurrent PEMS measurements. SCIENCE OF THE TOTAL ENVIRONMENT. Elsevier BV, AMSTERDAM, NETHERLANDS, 736: NA, (2020). Baldauf, R., X. Zheng, Y. Wu, S. Zhang, K. Zhang, and J. Hao. Joint measurements of black carbon and particle mass for heavydutydiesel vehicles using a portable emission measurement system. ATMOSPHERIC ENVIRONMENT. Elsevier Science Ltd, New York, NY, USA, 141: 435-442, (2016).

title: Does Corporate Accountability Towards Biodiversity Loss and Species Extinction Protection Account for Audit Efforts: New Insights from External Auditing
summary: This study investigates whether and how corporate biodiversity disclosure affects external audit efforts. Using a deep‐learning‐expanded text analysis of corporate social responsibility reports for heavily polluting Chinese companies from 2
content: This study investigates whether and how corporate biodiversity disclosure affects external audit efforts. Using a deep‐learning‐expanded text analysis of corporate social responsibility reports for heavily polluting Chinese companies from 2009 to 2021, this paper examines the relation between biodiversity disclosure and audit efforts. The empirical evidence reveals that firms with more extensive biodiversity disclosure exhibit significantly greater external audit efforts. The results remain robust to a series of endogeneity checks, including two‐stage least squares estimation and a combined propensity score matching and difference‐in‐differences analysis. Further analyses show that this positive relation is more pronounced for non‐state‐owned enterprises and firms located in eastern China. Mechanism tests reveal that biodiversity disclosure by heavy polluters triggers a ‘horn effect’, which elevates auditors' perceptions of composite audit risk, thereby driving greater audit effort. Interestingly, while biodiversity disclosures increase audit duration, they do not translate into higher audit fees. Collectively, the findings demonstrate that corporate biodiversity accountability increases audit risk and effort, highlighting the economic consequences of sustainability reporting within the auditing context.
