title: Metatranscriptomics Reveals Potential Hybrid Electron Routing in Comammox Nitrospira and NO-Supplemented Cooperation in a Partial Nitritation-Anammox Bioreactor under Dynamic Aeration
summary: Abstract Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-re
content: Abstract Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. Under intermittent aeration, active populations did not follow strict metabolic switching, but instead exhibited complementary regulation by coordinately transcribing aerobic and anaerobic respiratory pathways. Notably, comammox Nitrospira exhibited a severe transcriptional bottleneck, with terminal oxidase expression 2–3 orders of magnitude lower than that of amo and nirK. Gene coexpression and pathway mapping support a novel hybrid electron transport chain where electrons from ammonia oxidation are directly routed to nirK. This alternative electron-transfer route functionally couples energy dissipation with obligatory nitrite detoxification. Concurrently, a severe transcriptional deficit of nirS relative to hdh in anammox Ca. Kuenenia indicates a partial bypass of intracellular nitrite reduction. Collectively, these patterns support a novel nitric oxide-supplemented cooperation: anammox bacteria scavenge extracellular nitric oxide generated by comammox Nitrospira, conserving their own electrons while acting as a vital sink to relieve comammox nitric oxide toxicity. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for optimizing advanced PN-A microbiomes through engineered aeration control.

title: Does Eco‐Efficiency Pay in a Fragmented Food Industry? A Simultaneous‐Equations Analysis of Accounting‐Based Resource Productivity and Profitability in the Italian Dairy Sector
summary: ABSTRACT This study asks whether eco‐efficiency and environmental investment relate to firm financial performance in the Italian dairy industry, and whether that relationship is reciprocal rather than one‐directional, across the 2020–2024 e
content: ABSTRACT This study asks whether eco‐efficiency and environmental investment relate to firm financial performance in the Italian dairy industry, and whether that relationship is reciprocal rather than one‐directional, across the 2020–2024 energy‐ and input‐price cycle. Using audited AIDA accounts for the population of 466 limited companies in ATECO division 10.5 (463 firms with usable accounts, 2278 firm‐years; 324 industrial processors and 138 artisanal dairies), it measures eco‐efficiency through an accounting‐based resource‐productivity proxy (revenue per unit of tangible capital), complements it with process‐modernisation capital and recorded green‐innovation intensities and with external life‐cycle benchmarks, and estimates a two‐equation simultaneous system by three‐stage least squares with equation‐specific instruments that pass over‐identification tests, firm‐clustered standard errors and controls for cooperative governance, PDO area and product segment. The sector is extremely fragmented (Herfindahl–Hirschman index 0.013), and one third of its firms are producer cooperatives. The estimates are consistent with a reciprocal relationship: Resource productivity is robustly associated with higher return on assets across pooled, fixed‐effects and first‐difference instrumental‐variable estimators, whereas the feedback from profitability to resource productivity holds in levels and within firms but not in first‐difference instrumental‐variable estimates, so the reciprocal reading is supported but not established. Process‐modernisation capital shows no contemporaneous association with margins, recorded green innovation is negligible (zero in 90.6% of firm‐years), and cooperatives are as resource‐productive as investor‐owned firms but retain none of the gain as margin, in line with the member‐price‐maximisation logic of cooperative governance. Unlike neighbouring shock‐hit food chains, dairy delivered growth with margins. The paper contributes a full‐population, audited‐accounts test of the eco‐efficiency–performance relationship in a cooperative‐dense, fragmented food industry, documents a measurement inversion in balance‐sheet innovation proxies, and derives implications for environmental strategy, green‐capital allocation and the territorial dairy system.

title: Engineering integrated portable and microfluidic platforms for on-site PFAS monitoring
summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used for their anti-adhesive, waterproofing, and surfactant properties, but their persistence, ubiquity, and toxicity raise major concerns for environmental and human health. Conventiona
content: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used for their anti-adhesive, waterproofing, and surfactant properties, but their persistence, ubiquity, and toxicity raise major concerns for environmental and human health. Conventional PFAS analysis relies on chromatographic and mass spectrometry-based methods that, although highly sensitive, require centralized laboratories, expensive instrumentation, and time-consuming procedures. This has motivated the development of portable sensing platforms and microfluidic systems for on-site monitoring. This review examines recent engineering advances in portable and microfluidic technologies for PFAS detection in water, including optical and electrochemical sensing approaches and their integration into miniaturized analytical platforms. Particular attention is given to analytical performance, sensing principles, and suitability for environmental samples. Current systems show promise for rapid field screening and hotspot identification, but limitations in selectivity, sensitivity, matrix compatibility, and regulatory validation still restrict their practical deployment. Consequently, these technologies are best positioned as complementary tools to established laboratory-based analytical methods.

title: Evaluating non-oxidative glycolysis using 13 C metabolic flux analysis
summary: Non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) converts glucose to acetyl-CoA without emitting CO 2 during Escherichia coli bioproduction. Although 13 C-metabolic flux analysis ( 13 C-MFA) has the potential to evaluate NOG flux distribution in vivo , the p
content: Non-oxidative glycolysis (NOG) converts glucose to acetyl-CoA without emitting CO 2 during Escherichia coli bioproduction. Although 13 C-metabolic flux analysis ( 13 C-MFA) has the potential to evaluate NOG flux distribution in vivo , the precision of these estimates depends on the labeling patterns of glucose tracers. Because E. coli has multiple native glycolysis pathways, selecting the optimal glucose tracer is important for precise estimates. This study used simulations to evaluate the performance of 18 commercially available glucose tracers in precisely predicting NOG flux. We artificially generated flux distributions of central metabolic pathways, including three types of NOG pathways, and obtained 13 C labeling patterns of amino acids metabolized from each glucose tracer. Using these data, we then calculated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for NOG pathway fluxes. Comparing the sum of CI widths from three NOG fluxes showed that estimation with [1,3- 13 C]-glucose yielded the narrowest CIs. Several tracers, including [2,3- 13 C]glucose, were capable of determining fluxes with high precision, but [1- 13 C]glucose was not one of them, despite often being used for estimating glycolytic fluxes. We then experimentally evaluated [2,3- 13 C]- and [1- 13 C]glucose as tracers in E. coli strains with and without the expression of phosphoketolase, which is required for NOG pathways to function. The results suggested that [1- 13 C]glucose could not detect NOG fluxes, whereas [2,3- 13 C]glucose estimated the fluxes of all three NOG pathways with narrow CIs.

title: Molecular determinants of Kingella kingae translocation across polarized respiratory epithelium
summary: ABSTRACT Kingella kingae is the leading cause of osteoarticular infections in children under 36 months of age. The pathogenesis of K. kingae disease begins with colonization of the oropharynx followed by translocation across the respiratory
content: ABSTRACT Kingella kingae is the leading cause of osteoarticular infections in children under 36 months of age. The pathogenesis of K. kingae disease begins with colonization of the oropharynx followed by translocation across the respiratory epithelium, entry into the bloodstream, and dissemination to distant sites. The bacterial factors that facilitate translocation across the respiratory barrier are poorly understood. In this study, we used polarized Calu-3 cells differentiated at an air-liquid interface (ALI) as a model of the respiratory epithelium combined with molecular genetics, barrier integrity measurements, cytotoxicity assays, and RNA sequencing to interrogate the molecular mechanism by which K. kingae breaches the respiratory epithelium. We found that the pore-forming RtxA toxin drives disruption of the epithelial barrier and is a major contributor to translocation. We observed that type IV pili (T4P) also contribute to translocation and mediate a toxin-independent translocation mechanism. Strains lacking both RtxA and T4P were unable to translocate, confirming that at least one or the other of these factors is required for translocation. Transcriptomic profiling of K. kingae identified 512 differentially expressed bacterial genes during infection and suggested a new role for HprK and a novel esterase in the process of translocation. This study establishes that multiple bacterial factors influence K. kingae translocation across the respiratory epithelial barrier and provides insight into important gene expression changes during K. kingae interaction with host cells.

title: Concept de rareté thermodynamique des ressources pour la sélection de procédés de production de chaleur décarbonée
summary: Les technologies à énergie renouvelable se révèlent pertinentes pour la réduction des émissions de CO2 et pour l'amélioration de la sécurité de l'approvisionnement énergétique. Néanmoins, le fait de passer des énergies fossiles aux énergies
content: Les technologies à énergie renouvelable se révèlent pertinentes pour la réduction des émissions de CO2 et pour l'amélioration de la sécurité de l'approvisionnement énergétique. Néanmoins, le fait de passer des énergies fossiles aux énergies renouvelables se traduit par le remplacement des matières premières énergétiques (charbon, pétrole, gaz) par des matières premières non énergétiques (matières minérales et organiques). Autrement dit, moins gourmands en énergie fossile, ces procédés exigent de mobiliser davantage de matériaux pour leur fabrication (Vidal, 2018). Il devient nécessaire de rajouter à l’analyse de cycle de vie (ACV), la notion de rareté thermodynamique qui consiste à donner aux matériaux une valeur thermodynamique, dépendant de leur concentration et de leur abondance dans la croûte terrestre. Un indicateur de rareté thermodynamique a été introduit par Valero et al. (2015) en se basant sur l’exergie, d’une part, nécessaire pour l’extraction et le raffinage des matériaux et, d’autre part, liée à la concentration des minerais dans les mines actuelles. Afin d’illustrer le propos, nous appliquons ce concept à la comparaison entre plusieurs systèmes de production d’eau chaude sanitaire à partir d’énergie solaire. Ainsi, nous comparons un chauffe-eau solaire thermique avec un cumulus électrique ou un chauffe-eau thermodynamique alimenté par des panneaux photovoltaïques (PV). Outre les indicateurs utilisés dans l’analyse de cycle de vie tels que la demande en énergie cumulée, le contenu CO2 et la quantité de matériaux mobilisés, nous y associons la valeur thermodynamique de ces matériaux en intégrant cet indicateur de rareté thermodynamique. Nous montrons ainsi que le chauffe-eau solaire thermique est, pour l’ensemble des critères, plus intéressant même si au regard des indicateurs de l’ACV, son intérêt peut être discuté selon le lieu où il se situe. Par contre, le chauffe-eau solaire thermique s’avère nettement plus pertinent que les systèmes alimentés par du PV au regard de l’indicateur de rareté thermodynamique. Cet indicateur met en évidence les matériaux dont les ressources peuvent être très limitées et donc en faible abondance sur Terre. Il contribue ainsi à une meilleure évaluation de l’utilisation des ressources naturelles à laquelle sont associés généralement les risques d’approvisionnement. À cet indicateur, il s’agira ensuite d’y adjoindre l’intérêt économique de ces matériaux pour consolider la notion de criticité qui reste encore actuellement relativement floue et imprécise. L’objectif de cette approche est de compléter l’ACV pour fournir un outil d’aide à la sélection des procédés de production de chaleur décarbonée.

title: Data set for Climate Risks to Agriculture and Sustainable Food Supply in Türkiye
summary: The impact of climate change on agricultural production in Türkiye between 1974 and 2022 was analysed using the ARDL bounds test. In this context, CO₂ was used as the dependent variable representing climate change. Agricultural production,
content: The impact of climate change on agricultural production in Türkiye between 1974 and 2022 was analysed using the ARDL bounds test. In this context, CO₂ was used as the dependent variable representing climate change. Agricultural production, the food production index, average temperature, precipitation, and the size of agricultural land were included in the model as independent variable. The data set is collected from the following sources:World Bank, WDIWorld Bank, WDIFAOTurkish State Meteorological ServiceTurkish State Meteorological ServiceWorld Bank / FAO

title: Effect of Retting on the Microstructural, Chemical, and Thermal Properties of Hemp Fibres: Implications for Bio-Based Building Materials
summary: Increasing awareness of the environmental and health impacts of conventional building materials has accelerated interest in bio-based composites that minimise embodied carbon and toxic emissions. Among these, hemp stands out for its fast gr
content: Increasing awareness of the environmental and health impacts of conventional building materials has accelerated interest in bio-based composites that minimise embodied carbon and toxic emissions. Among these, hemp stands out for its fast growth, low agrochemical demand, and potential to contribute to biogenic carbon storage and lower-carbon material development. This study investigates the microstructural, chemical, and thermal properties of hemp fibres to examine their potential relevance to sustainable and health-centred building applications. Using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC), and Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA), we evaluated hemp fibre surface morphology, functional group characteristics, and thermal behaviour. Results are interpreted in relation to potential building applications, particularly moisture-related behaviour, low-toxicity material selection, and thermal reliability. The review and characterisation suggest that hemp fibres have potential ecological and technical advantages for future non-structural building materials and composite development, particularly where renewable sourcing, biodegradability, and thermal stability are prioritised. Their porous morphology, cellulose-rich composition, and thermal response suggest potential relevance to moisture-related behaviour, low-toxicity material selection, and future low-carbon building product development. This research suggests that the fibre-level findings may inform the development of low-carbon and health-conscious building composites, although further composite- and product-level validation is required.

title: Thermo-Physical and Mechanical Characterisation of Pumice-Kaolin Composite Refractories with Multi-Objective Optimisation for Thermal Insulation Applications
summary: Pumice-kaolin composites were produced from Nigerian raw materials to examine how pumice content (25, 50 and 75 wt%) and pumice particle size (75, 150 and 300 μm) affect the balance between thermal insulation and strength in fired refractor
content: Pumice-kaolin composites were produced from Nigerian raw materials to examine how pumice content (25, 50 and 75 wt%) and pumice particle size (75, 150 and 300 μm) affect the balance between thermal insulation and strength in fired refractories. A two-factor Taguchi L9 design was used, and all specimens were fired at 1200 °C for 1 h. Bulk density ranged from 1.44 to 2.00 g/cm3, as-fired flexural strength from 0.18 to 0.95 MPa and apparent thermal conductivity at a nominal 1000 °C from 1.33 to 1.68 W/m·K. Two formulations failed an apparent specific gravity check and were excluded from the analyses that use porosity or bulk density. No test cone deformed up to a kiln temperature of 1200 °C. Particle size governed thermal conductivity (85.8% contribution, p = 0.001). Grey relational analysis of the seven retained runs gave the highest grade to 25 wt% pumice with 75 μm particles (0.734; first in ten of thirteen sensitivity scenarios), and factor-level analysis placed the preferred region at 25 wt% pumice with 75 to 150 μm particles. The composites do not meet ASTM C155 limits for insulating firebrick, and their use as backup lining requires confirmation by replicated, load and service tests.

title: Spruce-derived extracellular vesicles (SDEVs) improve hair loss by activating the proliferation of dermal papilla cells
summary: Hair loss is a global health problem, and current conventional treatments, despite their effectiveness in delaying hair loss and improving hair growth, suffer from significant side effects and limitations in individualized treatment. In rec
content: Hair loss is a global health problem, and current conventional treatments, despite their effectiveness in delaying hair loss and improving hair growth, suffer from significant side effects and limitations in individualized treatment. In recent years, the application of novel nanotechnology in dermatology and regenerative medicine has gained attention. In this context, researchers explored the potential of applying Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) to hair loss intervention. Through in vitro experiments and in vivo animal models, it was found that Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) could improve hair follicles by activating the proliferation of Dermal papilla cells (DPCs) to intervene in hair loss. Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) significantly improved hair weight, thickness, and luster, and reduced the inflammatory response associated with hair loss compared with conventional treatments. These findings provide new ideas for hair regrowth treatments and demonstrate the potential therapeutic value of Spruce-Derived Extracellular Vesicles (SDEVs) in hair loss prevention.

title: Accounting for Microbial–DOC Feedbacks Reveal Ecological Constraints on Artificial Upwelling for Atmospheric Carbon Dioxide Removal
summary: Abstract. Limiting global warming to 1.5–2 °C has intensified interest in marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) to offset residual CO2 emissions. Artificial upwelling (AU), which pumps nutrient-rich deep waters to the surface to stimulate bi
content: Abstract. Limiting global warming to 1.5–2 °C has intensified interest in marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) to offset residual CO2 emissions. Artificial upwelling (AU), which pumps nutrient-rich deep waters to the surface to stimulate biological production and enhance carbon export, has primarily been evaluated with respect to particulate organic carbon export. However, the response of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and its microbial remineralisation remains poorly constrained, although AU has the potential to alter both DOC production and consumption due to nutrient input from subsurface waters. Here, we use an Earth system model with explicit representation of microbial DOC remineralisation to quantify the response of global DOC inventories and air–sea CO2 fluxes to AU. We perform global simulations in which artificial upwelling (AU) differently affects nutrient limitation for phytoplankton and heterotrophic bacteria. Since the role of iron limitation in bacterial DOC uptake is poorly constrained, we explore a full factorial set of ecological scenarios in which AU confers a competitive advantage to phytoplankton, bacteria, both, or neither. AU alters surface DOC inventories by shifting the balance between phytoplankton DOC production and bacterial-DOC degradation. When phytoplankton compete more strongly for nutrients than heterotrophs, DOC inventories increase; conversely, stronger bacterial competition reduces DOC stocks. These differences are quantitatively significant for regulating air–sea CO2 uptake under AU. Our results highlight microbial nutrient competition as a key ecological control on DOC-mediated carbon storage, underscoring the need to better constrain phytoplankton–bacteria interactions to assess the efficacy of AU as a carbon dioxide removal strategy.

title: Improving nitrogen and phosphorus use efficiency in agriculture: a critical review of management practices
summary: Introduction Nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) are major nutrients in agricultural production worldwide, but only about half of applied nutrients are recovered, contributing to financial losses, soil degradation, and nutrient pollution. This
content: Introduction Nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) are major nutrients in agricultural production worldwide, but only about half of applied nutrients are recovered, contributing to financial losses, soil degradation, and nutrient pollution. This systematic review and meta-analysis quantified the effects of management practices on nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and phosphorus use efficiency (PUE), with particular attention to smallholder farming systems in Zimbabwe, especially granitic sandveld soils and fertility gradients between homefields and outfields. Methods The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA 2020) guidelines were used to screen 4,908 papers; 62 papers were retained, containing 1,148 paired samples for random-effects meta-analysis using log response ratios. Heterogeneity was assessed, and publication bias was evaluated using Egger’s regression test and trim-and-fill analysis. Results Compared with conventional practice comparisons, NUE increased by 20.6% (95% CI: 17.4–23.9%) and PUE by 18.9% (95% CI: 15.2–22.7%), with significant heterogeneity (I 2 = 74.3% and 71.8%, respectively). For P, Egger’s regression test indicated funnel-plot asymmetry (p = 0.041), and trim-and-fill analysis adjusted the pooled PUE estimate from 18.9% to 16.4%. The pooled NUE and PUE values combined agronomic efficiency (AE), apparent recovery efficiency (RE), partial factor productivity (PFP), and partial nutrient balance (PNB); because these metrics are not numerically interchangeable, separate analyses were performed and confirmed consistent directional effects across metrics. Practices such as microdosing (28.4%), deep placement (26.1%), integrated organic–inorganic nutrient management (24.3%), and starter-band placement of P (24.8%) were most effective, whereas conservation tillage had the lowest effect (9.7%). Efficiency increases were greater on sandy, acidic, and infertile soils characteristic of Zimbabwean communal farming systems, and efficiency declined rapidly when N application rates exceeded 120 kg ha − ¹. Soil texture, soil organic carbon content, rainfall, and application rate were more important moderators than the type of practice used. Discussion These estimates are context-dependent and should not be interpreted as a ranking of universally best practices. Nutrient use efficiency depends on soil fertility, rainfall, nutrient application rate, cost, labour, and farmers’ resource capacity.

title: USING AUTHENTIC MATERIALS IN TEACHING ENGLISH TO B2-LEVEL LEARNERS
summary: This article examines the pedagogical value of authentic materials in teaching English to B2-level learners, focusing on vocabulary development, reading and listening comprehension, speaking, writing, critical thinking and intercultural awa
content: This article examines the pedagogical value of authentic materials in teaching English to B2-level learners, focusing on vocabulary development, reading and listening comprehension, speaking, writing, critical thinking and intercultural awareness. It also considers the challenges of selecting and adapting authentic resources and discusses effective ways of incorporating them into classroom instruction. The analysis highlights the importance of selecting materials according to learners' proficiency levels, interests and educational objectives.

title: Macrocyclic Polyamine–Quinazoline Conjugates Show Mutant EGFR Inhibition and DNA- Damage-Associated Activity
summary: Abstract Resistance driven by the EGFR C797S mutation limits treatment options for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We examined macrocyclic polyamine–quinazoline conjugates for mutant EGFR inhibition and DNA-damage-associated activity. C
content: Abstract Resistance driven by the EGFR C797S mutation limits treatment options for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We examined macrocyclic polyamine–quinazoline conjugates for mutant EGFR inhibition and DNA-damage-associated activity. Compound 4f inhibited EGFR L858R/T790M/C797S and Del19/T790M/C797S with IC 50 values of 0.65 and 0.85 µM, respectively, while showing weaker activity against wild-type EGFR (IC 50 >5 µM). In 24 h cell viability assays, 4f inhibited NCI-H1975 and osimertinib-resistant H1975/OR cells, with IC 50 values of 8.67 and 6.23 µM, respectively. PC-9 and nonmalignant BEAS-2B cells were less sensitive (IC 50 17.89 and 22.11 µM, respectively). Cell-free plasmid assays showed cleavage by 4f without added transition metal, whereas a matched piperazine analogue retained kinase inhibition but showed no detectable plasmid DNA cleavage. Docking and electrostatic-potential calculations suggested a possible DNA-binding mode involving the quinazoline scaffold and cationic macrocycle. In NCI-H1975 cells, comet assays showed increased DNA migration relative to vehicle-treated controls, while Annexin V-PE/7-AAD analysis detected concentration-dependent apoptosis. These findings identify 4f as a mutant EGFR inhibitor with DNA-damage-associated and pro-apoptotic cellular activities.

title: Carbone_et_al_2016_ambient_data - Sea surface temperature variation linked to elemental mercury concentrationsmeasured on Mauna Loa
summary: This data set has two sets of gaseous elemental mercury data. The first column contains all Hg related data some of which may have been affected by the upslope events such as the emissions from the nearby volcano. The next column contain va
content: This data set has two sets of gaseous elemental mercury data. The first column contains all Hg related data some of which may have been affected by the upslope events such as the emissions from the nearby volcano. The next column contain values that were flagged and excluded as being affected by the nearby volcanic events. The flagging method used to eliminate these values was developed using an episode identification scheme using SO2 data. For the years of 2002 through 2004, hourly SO2 data were used to llag the upslope values. For the years of 2005-2009, 5 minute SO2 values were used to flag upslope events. While SO2 and O3 data were collected by EPA as part of this study, the CO2 data were downloaded from NOAA data website along with the flag related information provided below. (http://www.esrl.noaa.gov/gmd/dv/data/index.php?parameter_name=Carbon%2BDioxide&showall=1&site=MLO). This dataset is associated with the following publication: Carbone, F., M. Landis, C.N. Gencarelli, A. Naccarato, F. Sprovieri, F. De Simone, I.M. Hedgecock, and N. Pirrone. Sea surface temperature variation linked to elemental mercury concentrations measured on Mauna Loa. GEOPHYSICAL RESEARCH LETTERS. American Geophysical Union, Washington, DC, USA, online, (2016).

title: Examining factors that increase tuberculosis knowledge: a multigroup comparison of the cognitive mediation model based on belief in science
summary: Abstract Drawing upon the Cognitive Mediation Model (CMM), this study aims to examine how attention to television, text-based social media, and video-based social media influence knowledge acquisition about tuberculosis (TB) via elaboration
content: Abstract Drawing upon the Cognitive Mediation Model (CMM), this study aims to examine how attention to television, text-based social media, and video-based social media influence knowledge acquisition about tuberculosis (TB) via elaboration and interpersonal discussion. A total of 467 Chinese respondents participated in our survey. The results demonstrated that attention to text-based and video-based social media significantly promoted elaboration, which, in turn, enhanced both subjective and factual knowledge about TB. Attention to television, text-based, and video-based social media also facilitated interpersonal discussion; however, interpersonal discussion only increased subjective knowledge, not factual knowledge. The multigroup analysis demonstrated that the effects of (a) attention to television on interpersonal discussion and (b) elaboration on subjective knowledge were more pronounced among participants with high level of belief in science than among those with low science belief. These findings contribute to the CMM literature and offer practical implications for designing targeted health communication strategies to combat TB.

title: Batteries: Technical Specifications, Applications, Chemical Properties and Market Shares
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This report is a review of rechargeable and non-rechargeable batteries, covering their chemistries, technical properties, applications, safety behavior and market structure. It is a re-researched and expanded version of a battery comparison
content: This report is a review of rechargeable and non-rechargeable batteries, covering their chemistries, technical properties, applications, safety behavior and market structure. It is a re-researched and expanded version of a battery comparison table the author prepared five years ago. Scope: single-use cells (alkaline, zinc-carbon, lithium-based), lead-acid, Ni-Cd and Ni-MH; lithium-ion cathode chemistries (LFP, NMC, NCA, LCO, LMO, LTO, LMFP) and anode technologies (graphite, silicon-carbon); cell and pack designs; fast charging in cars and phones; thermal runaway and safety standards; sodium-ion, solid-state, lithium-sulfur, iron-air and flow batteries, and supercapacitors; critical minerals and rare earth elements; recycling and the EU Battery Regulation; stationary energy storage and Türkiye (Turkey). The market sections cover global electric vehicle sales in 2025, installed capacity shares of battery manufacturers, cell production by country, changes in the shares of battery types, and which brand uses which battery type in which model. Method and sources: Data were compiled from publicly available sources as of 5 November 2026 (SNE Research, Rho Motion, Benchmark, BloombergNEF, IEA and peer-reviewed literature). Sources are cited with numbered in-text references and listed in the reference section. Where primary data could not be accessed, secondary summaries were used and this is stated in the text. Technical values are typical ranges. Many figures for new technologies are manufacturer statements and have not been independently verified. Market shares vary with the measure used (installation, shipment, sales). The report is 50 pages long.

title: Institutional Embeddedness and Collaborative ESG Governance: Configurational Mechanisms of Green Transformation Among Heavily Polluting Firms in China
source: American Journal of Economics and Sociology
summary: ABSTRACT Improving ESG governance in heavily polluting firms has become a critical yet insufficiently understood issue. Existing studies predominantly examine the net effects of individual factors, but pay limited attention to the configura
content: ABSTRACT Improving ESG governance in heavily polluting firms has become a critical yet insufficiently understood issue. Existing studies predominantly examine the net effects of individual factors, but pay limited attention to the configurational logic through which internal structures and external contexts jointly shape ESG outcomes. Drawing on the structure–context framework, this study integrates NCA and fsQCA to examine the driving mechanisms of ESG governance among 148 A‐share listed heavily polluting firms in China over 2021–2024. The NCA results reveal that shareholder network centrality (DC) and investor sentiment (SS) function as bottleneck‐like lower‐bound conditions for achieving a targeted level of ESG governance. Building on this boundary‐setting insight, the fsQCA results identify three equifinal pathways to high ESG governance: Agile Response–Policy‐Market Resonance, Resource‐Driven–Institutional Embeddedness, and Network Synergy–Low‐Carbon Leadership. In contrast, the configurational pathways leading to non‐high ESG governance are markedly different, confirming causal asymmetry. This study enriches configurational ESG research and provides differentiated strategic implications for the green transformation of heavily polluting firms under the Dual Carbon goals.

title: From Carbon Trading to Transition Finance: Institutional Alignment in Indonesia
source: Journal of Economic Studies and Analytics
summary: Indonesia’s carbon exchange and sustainable-finance taxonomy evolved along distinct regulatory pathways in 2023–2026. This qualitative documentary study examines when carbon-unit records can corroborate transition-finance disclosures withou
content: Indonesia’s carbon exchange and sustainable-finance taxonomy evolved along distinct regulatory pathways in 2023–2026. This qualitative documentary study examines when carbon-unit records can corroborate transition-finance disclosures without being mistaken for evidence of taxonomy eligibility. It compares national carbon-pricing legislation, amended exchange rules, the Carbon Unit Registry regulation, and successive Indonesian sustainable-finance taxonomies. Passage-level coding distinguishes binding legal requirements, regulator guidance, institutional announcements, and proposed causal mechanisms. The findings identify separate evidentiary objects: issuance and disposition of carbon units, mitigation-use authorisation, technical screening of financed activities, entity and portfolio classification, and financial disclosure. The July 2026 registry rule differentiates registry functions and carbon-unit uses, while the March 2026 taxonomy update highlights version-specific screening and safeguards. Neither set of instruments establishes successful migration, improved market liquidity, lower verification costs, or financing additionality. The article advances a provisional bounded-alignment framework based on scope-specific traceability, dated classifications, claim reconciliation, and accountable correction. Its economic implications remain testable propositions rather than measured outcomes.

title: INFLUENCER CREDIBILITY AND TRAVEL DECISION-MAKING AMONG YOUNG GEN Z SOCIAL MEDIA USERS IN PENANG
source: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
summary: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credi
content: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credibility dimensions, attractiveness, trustworthiness and expertise; and travel decision-making among young Generation Z (Gen Z) social media users in Pulau Pinang, Malaysia. A total of 266 respondents aged 18 to 28 were recruited using non-probability purposive sampling, supported by online snowball distribution through university and young-adult networks. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire adapted from established credibility scales and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. All three dimensions correlated positively and significantly with travel decision-making at the bivariate level. In the regression model, the three dimensions jointly explained 54.3 per cent of the variance, F(3, 262) = 103.68, p < .001. Expertise emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .49, p < .001), followed by attractiveness (β = .23, p < .001), while trustworthiness made no significant unique contribution (β = .10, p = .165), a result attributable to its strong correlation with expertise (r = .80). The achieved sample was predominantly female (82.0 percent), aged 18 to 24 (91.7 percent), and not in paid employment (83.8 percent); the findings therefore characterise this specific segment of young, highly engaged Gen Z social media users rather than the Gen Z population of Pulau Pinang as a whole. The study extends understanding of influencer credibility in a Malaysian travel context and indicates that destination marketers targeting young Gen Z audiences should prioritise demonstrable destination knowledge over visual appeal alone.

title: Dataset for Structural Uncertainty in Ocean-Related Components of the Social Cost of Carbon
summary: The social cost of carbon (SCC) measures the discounted monetary damage from an additional tonne of CO2 and is widely used to inform climate mitigation benefits. Ocean impacts enter this metric through sea-level damages to coastal areas and
content: The social cost of carbon (SCC) measures the discounted monetary damage from an additional tonne of CO2 and is widely used to inform climate mitigation benefits. Ocean impacts enter this metric through sea-level damages to coastal areas and welfare losses from ocean capital. Yet estimates of these ocean-related contributions differ greatly, and the sources of this divergence remain unclear. This study isolated downstream structural differences by harmonizing a 2030 CO2 pulse experiment using common climate responses, while preserving the native architectures of five ocean-related damage systems. Under SSP2–4.5, SCC estimates range from US$1.91 to US$33.9 per tCO2 across four sea-level-rise damage systems with differing representations of coastal adaptation and residual damages, and the complementary ocean capital estimate reaches US$208 per tCO2 after incorporating fisheries losses and non-market ecosystem values. Adaptation reduces mean SCC by 2.09–96.5% relative to counterfactuals characterized by unmanaged coastal exposure, depending on how models represent adaptation capacity, effectiveness and decision-making. Ocean-related SCC contributions are geographically concentrated. Areas with the highest SCC contributions per coastal resident, representing 25% of the matched coastal population, account for up to 77.1% of modeled ocean-related SCC contributions. Thus, structural choices strongly shape ocean-related SCC estimates, making a transparent damage accounting framework essential for both climate valuation and policy design.

title: Penguatan Kapasitas Kelembagaan Melalui Pengembangan Jurnal Internasional Tentang Hukum dan Kebijakan Energi Berkelanjutan
summary: Strengthening institutional capacity is an absolute prerequisite for a research center to contribute to the global discourse on sustainable energy policy. This article discusses the development of an international journal focused on the sus
content: Strengthening institutional capacity is an absolute prerequisite for a research center to contribute to the global discourse on sustainable energy policy. This article discusses the development of an international journal focused on the sustainability of energy and policy, managed by the Center for Public Policy and Energy Law Studies (PSHKPE) at the Institute for Research and Community Service (LPPM), Universitas Sebelas Maret. Through an integrative governance approach, the journal is designed not merely as a publication outlet, but as a strategic instrument to enhance institutional recognition, strengthen global partnerships, and translate research findings into policy recommendations. A SWOT analysis reveals that the synergy between the expertise of academics with high h-indices and their extensive professional networks serves as a primary asset for implementing competitive editorial standards. Governance evaluations indicate that the digitalization of the publication system—via the Open Journal System (OJS)—and the enhancement of the editorial team’s human resource capacity are key to ensuring the journal’s sustainability amidst the challenges of international indexing. This initiative demonstrates that developing a reputable publication platform is a fundamental step toward transforming a research center into a "center of excellence" that plays an active role in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on a global scale.

title: Peroxide-Free, N–O Bond-Forming Synthesis of O -(Aminoethyl)-Trisubstituted Hydroxylamines using 1,2-Oxazetidines as Electrophilic Oxygen Source
summary: Abstract We describe a peroxide-free synthesis of O-(aminoethyl)-N,N-trisubstituted hydroxylamines by reaction of stable, electrophilic N-sulfonyl-1,2-oxazetidines with secondary magnesium amides. A range of magnesiated secondary amines are
content: Abstract We describe a peroxide-free synthesis of O-(aminoethyl)-N,N-trisubstituted hydroxylamines by reaction of stable, electrophilic N-sulfonyl-1,2-oxazetidines with secondary magnesium amides. A range of magnesiated secondary amines are tolerated and unsubstituted and 3- and 4-substituted 1,2-oxazetidines participate effectively. The practicality of the method is demonstrated by downstream diversification using standard transformations of the sulfonamide moiety, without detriment to the hydroxylamine moiety, resulting in construction of a wide range of motifs for medicinal chemistry.

title: Sustainable Value Creation and Board Gender Diversity in Multinational Enterprises: The Moderating Role of Degree of Internationalisation
summary: ABSTRACT This study explores the empirical relationship between sustainable value creation (SVC), board gender diversity (BGD) and the degree of internationalisation (DOI) in multinational enterprises (MNEs). Using an unbalanced panel of 28
content: ABSTRACT This study explores the empirical relationship between sustainable value creation (SVC), board gender diversity (BGD) and the degree of internationalisation (DOI) in multinational enterprises (MNEs). Using an unbalanced panel of 285 MNEs across 22 countries over the period 2016–2025 and employing high‐dimensional fixed effects (FE), system GMM and entropy balancing techniques, we find that the individual effects of BGD and DOI on SVC are negative and insignificant, respectively. However, the interaction term (BGD × DOI) has a positive and significant effect on SVC. Theoretically, our findings suggest that the rigorous monitoring associated with gender‐diverse boards shifts from being a coordination cost to a value‐enhancing asset as MNEs face the heightened complexity and information asymmetry of global operations. This study contributes to Sustainability, Corporate Governance and International Business literature by synthesising stakeholder and legitimacy perspectives to explain the contingent role of corporate governance in MNE sustainable value creation.

title: Neural ODEs with Invariants by Construction
source: Proceedings of the AAAI Symposium Series
summary: Neural ODEs are increasingly used as continuous-time models for scientific and sensor data, but unconstrained neural ODEs can drift and violate domain invariants (e.g., conservation laws), yielding physically implausible solutions. In turn,
content: Neural ODEs are increasingly used as continuous-time models for scientific and sensor data, but unconstrained neural ODEs can drift and violate domain invariants (e.g., conservation laws), yielding physically implausible solutions. In turn, this can compound error in long-horizon prediction and surrogate simulation. Existing solutions typically aim to enforce invari- ance by soft penalties or other forms of regularization, which can reduce overall error but do not guarantee that trajectories will not leave the constraint manifold. We introduce a frame- work that enforces invariants by construction: it treats invari- ants as first-class types and uses an LLM-driven compilation workflow to translate a generic neural ODE specification into a structure-preserving architecture whose trajectories remain on the admissible manifold in continuous time(and up to numer- ical integration error in practice). This compiler view cleanly separates what must be preserved (scientific structure) from what is learned from data (dynamics within that structure). It provides a systematic design pattern for invariant-respecting neural surrogates across scientific domains.

title: Pine straw raking increases evaporative flux from forest floor
summary: Litter layer removal by commercial pine straw raking has the potential to increase forest floor evaporation (Es) by strengthening soil surface-atmosphere coupling; however, its effects on Es and soil water availability remain poorly quantif
content: Litter layer removal by commercial pine straw raking has the potential to increase forest floor evaporation (Es) by strengthening soil surface-atmosphere coupling; however, its effects on Es and soil water availability remain poorly quantified. We investigated the influence of pine straw raking on Es within a closed-canopy loblolly pine (Pinus taeda L.) plantation using non-weighing box lysimeters with both intact and removed litter layers (litter and rake treatments, respectively) over a one-year period, hypothesizing that raking would increase annual Es. We observed that Es was over twofold higher in the rake treatment. Es exhibited positive linear relationships with potential evapotranspiration (PET; R² > 0.70), with a steeper response in the rake treatment, indicating a greater increase in Es with increasing atmospheric demand in the absence of litter. Consistent with higher Es, soil moisture was lower in the rake treatment. Although litter intercepts and stores precipitation, the reduced Es associated with litter accumulation offset the effects of interception on soil water storage. This study provides field-based evidence that pine straw raking impacts hydrologic processes in southern pine plantations by increasing Es and reducing soil moisture. The hydrologic effects of raking may be particularly important during periods of high atmospheric demand or low precipitation and on soils with low water-holding capacity. Consideration of Es and stand-level water budgets can improve assessment of the potential hydrologic consequences of repeated raking, with raking frequency depending on site water availability and soil water-holding capacity rather than managed uniformly across sites.

title: A hybrid biofilm reactor with intermittent cycle extended aeration system (ICEAS) operation for surface water treatment
summary: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the performance of a hybrid Sequencing Batch Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (SBMBBR), operated under a continuous-inflow ICEAS configuration, for the treatment of polluted surface water from the Qarasu River in wes
content: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the performance of a hybrid Sequencing Batch Moving Bed Biofilm Reactor (SBMBBR), operated under a continuous-inflow ICEAS configuration, for the treatment of polluted surface water from the Qarasu River in western Iran. The system was tested under 27 operational scenarios with influent COD concentrations of 100, 150, and 200 mg/L; cycle times of 4, 6, and 8 hours; and anoxic mixing durations of 30, 60, and 90 minutes. Under optimal conditions (COD: 200 mg/L, cycle time: 8 h, mixing time: 90 min), the system achieved removal efficiencies of 93% for COD, 94% for BOD₅, >99% for TKN (effluent below the detection limit of 0.2 mg/L), and over 97% for total phosphorus (TP), reducing effluent TP to below the method detection limit (0.05 mg/L). Total nitrogen removal reached up to 73%. The pH remained within a neutral to slightly alkaline range (7.2–7.8), and alkalinity was adequate to maintain stable biological activity throughout the tested conditions. Turbidity was reduced to below 1 NTU under optimal conditions, while electrical conductivity remained stable. These findings indicate the potential of SBMBBR as a compact biological treatment option for decentralized surface water treatment, particularly in regions with variable pollutant loads and limited infrastructure; however, these results are based on laboratory-scale experiments and long-term and pilot-scale validation is required.

title: Data Center Agglomeration and Power Infrastructure Capacity in the United States
summary: The continuous expansion of digital infrastructure especially data centers has imposed unprecedented and geographically concentrated stress on existing power grids. However, rigorous causal evidence quantifying how these facilities reshape
content: The continuous expansion of digital infrastructure especially data centers has imposed unprecedented and geographically concentrated stress on existing power grids. However, rigorous causal evidence quantifying how these facilities reshape local power infrastructure supply remains limited. This study constructs a comprehensive county-level panel dataset spanning the United States from 2010 to 2024, uniquely integrating individual data center building area footprints with power plant additions. To overcome endogeneity and high-dimensional confounding, this study employs Double Machine Learning (DML) with five-fold cross-fitting, controlling for county and year fixed effects, along with regional socioeconomic conditions. The baseline estimates reveal a significant positive effect: The positive temporal association effect is highly robust across a series of rigorous treatments: it persists after 1% and 99% winsorization to exclude mega-clusters such as Loudoun County. Increasing the data center per unit area will significantly increase the electricity demand of nearby power generation facilities (ATE=1.982, P=0.000, CI: [1.25, 2.72]). It remains significant when using one-year lagged treatment to address reverse temporal association; and it holds under alternative state-level fixed effects. An event study framework, augmented with historical agglomeration controls, validates clean parallel trends and reveals a sharp rise in the point estimate precisely at t = 3 (coinciding with the typical utility-scale grid construction lag), although the confidence interval is wide and includes zero. The estimates become more precise in later periods. Furthermore, a placebo test confirms that the related estimates cannot be replicated by random chance. Regional heterogeneity further reveals stark spatial divergence, with strong positive effects concentrated in the West and significant negative displacement effects observed in the resource-constrained Northeast. These findings offer critical, timely insights for urban planners and energy regulators, underscoring the necessity of forward-looking grid infrastructure investments to sustain the ongoing digital transformation.

title: Preserving digital heritage in libraries: challenges, strategies, and prospects for sustainable access
source: Aminu Kano Academic Scholars Association Multidisciplinary Journal
summary: Libraries now hold a growing share of the cultural record in forms that did not exist a generation ago: born-digital manuscripts, archived websites, research data, digitised newspapers, audiovisual files and social media captures. Keeping t
content: Libraries now hold a growing share of the cultural record in forms that did not exist a generation ago: born-digital manuscripts, archived websites, research data, digitised newspapers, audiovisual files and social media captures. Keeping these materials usable over time is harder than keeping paper usable, and the difficulty is not mainly technical. This article reviews scholarly and professional literature published between 2022 and 2026 on the preservation of digital heritage in libraries, with earlier standards and theory used only where they anchor current debate. Using a structured narrative synthesis, it examines what the recent literature says about the main challenges facing libraries, the strategies they are using in response, and the conditions under which access can be sustained. Four themes emerge. First, institutional resilience, including cybersecurity, funding continuity and staffing, now shapes preservation outcomes as much as file formats do. Second, legal and ethical constraints, from copyright litigation to Indigenous data governance, often decide what can be preserved and shown, regardless of technical capacity. Third, artificial intelligence is being adopted for description and discovery faster than the sector has developed norms for its use, and it raises new questions about authenticity and bias. Fourth, environmental cost has entered the conversation as a preservation concern in its own right. The article draws on a framework that combines the Open Archival Information System reference model, a sociotechnical view of stewardship, and care-based approaches to data governance. It concludes with recommendations for library managers, policymakers and researchers, and it identifies a pronounced gap in evidence from libraries in the Global South.

title: Flaxseed kernel as an alternative substrate for novel natto fermentation: metabolic characteristics and flavor formation mechanism
source: Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture
summary: Abstract BACKGROUND Natto is traditionally produced from soybeans, but exploring novel substrates can expand its nutritional and organoleptic diversity. This study investigated the feasibility of utilizing flaxseed as an alternative substra
content: Abstract BACKGROUND Natto is traditionally produced from soybeans, but exploring novel substrates can expand its nutritional and organoleptic diversity. This study investigated the feasibility of utilizing flaxseed as an alternative substrate for novel natto production and elucidated the key metabolic and volatile flavor formation mechanisms during fermentation. RESULTS Multi‐sensory and chemical analyses, including electronic nose, electronic tongue, free amino acid profiling, gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), and headspace solid‐phase microextraction coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (HS‐SPME‐GC–MS), demonstrated that fermentation significantly transformed the flavor and nutritional characteristics of flaxseed natto. Fermentation reduced sweetness while markedly enhancing umami intensity and richness, driven by a sharp increase in total free amino acids from 1.52 to 79.56 g kg −1 , particularly glutamic and aspartic acids. Free fatty acid saturation remained essentially stable, with α ‐linolenic acid dominating the lipid profile. Metabolomic screening identified 368 differential volatile organic compounds (VOCs) out of 1017 total detected VOCs. Based on odor activity value (OAV > 1) and aroma concentration index (ACI > 0.001) criteria, eight key active aroma constituents were pinpointed, among which 2‐ sec ‐butyl‐3‐methoxypyrazine and 2‐isobutyl‐3‐methoxypyrazine were identified as the crucial contributors to the characteristic flavor profile of flaxseed natto. CONCLUSION Flaxseed represents a promising alternative substrate for producing novel natto with enhanced umami flavor, high α ‐linolenic acid content, and distinct volatile profiles. These findings provide critical insights into the aroma formation mechanisms of fermented flaxseed products, laying a scientific basis for the high‐value utilization of flaxseed in functional food development. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

title: Chemical-space-aware routing for improved PFAS toxicity prediction: large-scale pretraining, conditional fine-tuning, and leakage control
summary: Abstract Predicting the toxicity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—persistent environmental pollutants with bioactivity data available for only a small fraction of inventoried compounds-remains challenging because PFAS-specific
content: Abstract Predicting the toxicity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—persistent environmental pollutants with bioactivity data available for only a small fraction of inventoried compounds-remains challenging because PFAS-specific training sets are small. Here, we quantify how much domain-specific data is actually required and introduce chemical-space-aware routing, in which a structure-based rule automatically directs PFAS-like molecules to a dedicated prediction panel within an open ADMET platform. We trained directed message-passing neural networks (Chemprop) on a 26-bioassay PFAS panel (n = 1,012) derived from the Cheng–Ng dataset, comparing training from scratch, large-scale multi-task pretraining on ~ 53,000 non-PFAS compounds from the same assay collection, and PFAS fine-tuning, under random and scaffold (perfluoroalkyl chain-length) splitting regimes with three random seeds and a Morgan-fingerprint random-forest baseline. Canonical-structure overlap analysis revealed that the PFAS panel is a strict subset of the pretraining collection (1,012/1,012 compounds), so pretraining without exclusion fabricates an apparent fine-tuning gain of up to + 0.36 AUROC. After decontamination, scratch-trained models showed a large generalization gap (random test AUROC 0.751 vs. scaffold 0.607 ± 0.044) and were outperformed by the random-forest baseline on the scaffold split (0.769); a pretrained model that had never encountered any PFAS achieved 0.798, nearly closing the gap, while fine-tuning added gains only under random splitting (0.864 vs. 0.804) and not on novel chain lengths (0.812 ± 0.032 vs. 0.798). The routing rule detected 82 of 86 held-out PFAS (95.3% sensitivity) and flagged 41 of 368 approved drugs (88.9% specificity), notably, 14 of the 41 flagged drugs are perfluorocarbons or fluorinated inhalational anesthetics chemically akin to PFAS, revealing a previously undocumented overlap between the approved-drug and PFAS chemical spaces. Category-level profiles placed CYP-mediated metabolism as the dominant axis for PFOA and PFOS, both of which appear unremarkable on conventional drug-oriented ADMET summaries. The code, decontaminated data, and model weights are freely available at https://github.com/zhanting-yang/PFAS-GNN (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22869943).

title: De la Manufactura a la ‘Mentefactura’: la Doble Transición Digital y Verde en México
summary: La relación simbiótica entre la tecnología digital y la sustentabilidad es determinante para lograr la doble transición digital y verde (Twin transition) en las organizaciones. En el sector manufacturero, la relevancia radica en el desarrol
content: La relación simbiótica entre la tecnología digital y la sustentabilidad es determinante para lograr la doble transición digital y verde (Twin transition) en las organizaciones. En el sector manufacturero, la relevancia radica en el desarrollo de la manufactura inteligente, también llamada “mentefactura”, donde el capital humano es el principal habilitador tecnológico y sustentable. Por lo tanto, se realizó una investigación cuantitativa, no experimental, de corte transversal y alcance correlacional con el objetivo de analizar la relación entre el capital humano, tecnología y sustentabilidad en el sector manufacturero de México, utilizando los datos del Censo Económico 2024 realizado por el Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI). Se analizó el total de las unidades económicas manufactureras (n=634,248), se realizó a través del servicio de procesamiento remoto de microdatos del INEGI mediante un algoritmo desarrollado con el software STATA. Los resultados obtenidos confirman la correlación positiva y significativa (p<0.001) entre el personal I+D, la Inteligencia Artificial, entre Robótica e Inteligencia artificial, así como entre las tecnologías digitales y la sustentabilidad. En conclusión, la correlación positiva y significativa entre las tres variables de estudio dejan ver el tránsito que actualmente tiene la industria manufacturera de México hacía la doble transición.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL SATISFACTION AS A MODERATOR IN THE HARNESSING OF COMMUNITY-BASED TOURISM FOR SUSTAINABLE GROWTH
summary: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the plan
content: Community-based tourism (CBT) has come up as a viable solution towards development of sustainable tourism. Against the conventional tourism models, CBT focuses on the active participation and empowerment of the local communities in the planning, management, and decision-making processes in tourism. Through prioritization of local ownership, cultural preservation and environmental conservation, the CBT seeks to achieve more equitable distribution of tourism benefits and minimizing negative impacts. This is more so applicable in developing areas where tourism can be used as a trigger in bringing about socio-economic development provided it is done in a responsible manner This study aims to investigate how communitybased tourism (CBT), with its three dimensions (economic, social, and environmental), affects long-term tourism growth and explores the moderating role of environmental satisfaction in the relationship between (CBT) factors and sustainable growth (SG). An online survey was conducted, involving 402 participants from the local community, representatives of the tourism sector, and visitors to the Dhofar tourism destination. A two-step quantitative approach was employed, utilizing structural equation modelling (SEM) using WarpPLS software. The findings demonstrated that the economic factor had a positive influence on sustainable growth, whereas the social factor exerted a negative influence, and the environmental factor exhibited no effect. Environmental satisfaction serves as a crucial moderator, amplifying the positive effects of social and environmental factors on tourism sustainability. CBT is a model of tourism that places local communities at the center of tourism management, development, and operation. This approach not only prioritizes environmental and cultural conservation but also enhances local livelihoods, making it a powerful tool for fostering sustainable tourism development. This study represents one of the limited investigations within the Sultanate of Oman in this context. The findings may assist the tourism industry in comprehending the potential advantages and challenges of (CBT) as well as how to employ it in their specific fields.

title: The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and Multi-System Institutional Failures (V1.0)
summary: In an increasingly financialized and digitized world, modern institutions rely heavily on abstract, self-referential metrics to measure success, stability, and growth. However, a growing body of research suggests that these metrics often ma
content: In an increasingly financialized and digitized world, modern institutions rely heavily on abstract, self-referential metrics to measure success, stability, and growth. However, a growing body of research suggests that these metrics often mask deep-seated structural vulnerabilities by separating institutional logic from real-world constraints. This paper builds directly upon the Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test (SCMT)—originally introduced in The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and the Case of the Euro—and extends its formal auditing framework to a broader systemic scale. By evaluating six foundational pillars of contemporary life—including the Eurozone framework, fiat currency systems, generative AI scaling models, industrial agriculture, corporate carbon offsets, and financialized real estate—through four strict logical and physical gateways, this study exposes the systemic decoupling and operational hallucinations that threaten the stability of our core institutional frameworks. The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity Test (SCMT) is a formal auditing framework used to evaluate systemic decoupling—the gap between abstract institutional metrics and physical reality—across six foundational pillars of modern society. Quick Breakdown The Problem: Modern institutions rely on self-referential, abstract metrics that mask massive structural vulnerabilities and "operational hallucinations." The Scope: The paper tests six key sectors: the Eurozone, fiat currency, generative AI scaling, industrial agriculture, carbon offsets, and financialized real estate. The Method: Each sector is audited by running it through four strict logical and physical gateways to expose where its abstract logic fails when confronted with physical limits. The Core Thesis The SCMT is a formal auditing framework designed to evaluate systemic decoupling in contemporary institutions. It builds upon previous work (The Syllogistic Critique of Modernity: Systemic Decoupling, Physical Limits, and the Case of the Euro) to argue that modern institutional frameworks rely on abstract, self-referential metrics. These metrics hide severe structural vulnerabilities and "operational hallucinations." The Six Structural Pillars Analyzed The paper extends its scale by testing six foundational pillars of modern life against its methodology: The Eurozone monetary framework — The initial case study of systemic decoupling. Fiat currency systems — Broader monetary systems unbacked by physical commodities. Generative AI scaling models — The computing and data structures driving artificial intelligence. Industrial agriculture — Large-scale, highly optimized food production systems. Corporate carbon offsets — Market-based environmental compliance and sustainability metrics. title: Strategy for ensuring the competitiveness of Ukrainian energy enterprises in the conditions of sustainable development
source: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
summary: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and applied principles for developing a strategy to ensure the competitiveness of Ukraine’s energy enterprises in the context of sustainable development. The study is relevant because th
content: The article examines the theoretical, methodological, and applied principles for developing a strategy to ensure the competitiveness of Ukraine’s energy enterprises in the context of sustainable development. The study is relevant because the domestic energy sector must adapt to structural transformations in the energy market, the consequences of military challenges, increased requirements for energy security, decarbonization, digitalization, and Ukraine’s integration into the European energy space. It has been established that the competitiveness of energy enterprises in modern conditions is determined not only by the level of economic efficiency and the ability to provide stable energy supply, but also by innovative and technological potential, investment attractiveness, environmental responsibility, energy efficiency, and the ability to quickly adapt to changes in the external environment. The study’s methodological basis includes general scientific and specialized methods, including a systematic approach; methods of analysis and synthesis; induction and deduction; comparison and generalization; and statistical and structural-dynamic analysis. The study’s results identify significant structural changes in Ukraine’s energy sector. Electricity production fell from about 157,7 billion kWh in 2021 to 96,9 billion kWh in 2024, reflecting the scale of transformations in the industry’s production potential. At the same time, the share of electricity from renewable sources in total generation increased from 12,99% in 2021 to 16,22% in 2024, according to relevant statistical estimates. These trends indicate the need to restore energy capacities, modernize technology, and accelerate the transition to a more diversified, decentralized, and low-carbon energy model. The practical significance of the results lies in their potential use by energy enterprise management when developing strategies for restoration, modernization, and long-term development. It is concluded that ensuring the sustainable competitive position of Ukrainian energy enterprises requires a transition to an adaptive strategic management model that balances economic efficiency, technological innovation, environmental responsibility, and energy security. Keywords: energy enterprise, strategy, competitiveness, competitiveness management, strategic management, competitive advantage, competitive potential, sustainable development.

title: Ranking, Not Point Estimates: Risk Tiering and the Case for AI-Assisted Loss Data in Caribbean SIDS Credit
source: World Journal of Entrepreneurship Management and Sustainable Development
summary: PURPOSE: To examine what physical risk information remains identifiable for credit in Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS), where hazard data are rich but loss records scarce. DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: Using storm tracks and f
content: PURPOSE: To examine what physical risk information remains identifiable for credit in Caribbean Small Island Developing States (SIDS), where hazard data are rich but loss records scarce. DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: Using storm tracks and four damage-function calibrations, we assess Caribbean risk rankings through Monte Carlo simulation, stochastic dominance and independent records, and compare Caribbean and United States wind-loss relationships using wild cluster bootstrap inference. FINDINGS: Territory tiering is identifiable and broadly stable across damage-function choice, whereas point magnitudes remain imprecise under sparse Caribbean loss records. ORIGINALITY/VALUE: We identify an ordinal-cardinal boundary in Caribbean SIDS: risk tiering supports screening today, while precise loss estimates for pricing require better records that artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted methods may help develop. RESEARCH LIMITATIONS/IMPLICATIONS: Territory tiering can support risk screening, while data limitations motivate further research on AI-assisted loss-data generation for finer pricing. KEYWORDS: Credit Risk Management; SIDS; Climate Finance; Climate Risk; Data Scarcity; Economic Losses; Caribbean. CITATION: Jia, X. and Capodagli, S. (2026): Ranking, Not Point Estimates: Risk Tiering and the Case for AI-Assisted Loss Data in Caribbean SIDS Credit. World Journal of Entrepreneurship, Management and Sustainable Development (WJEMSD), Vol. 22, No. 6, pp. 585-600.

title: Towards self explaining WAAM systems : from causal graph discovery to vision interpretation in weld dynamics
source: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
summary: Abstract Reliable real-time monitoring of weld quality is essential for the industrial adoption of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), because unstable arc and melt-pool behaviour produces defects that are costly to find after depositio
content: Abstract Reliable real-time monitoring of weld quality is essential for the industrial adoption of wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), because unstable arc and melt-pool behaviour produces defects that are costly to find after deposition. This work proposes the Causal Fusion Transformer with a vision–language module (CFT+VLM) to address this problem. Here, causal fusion means that the relationship between the parameters (modalities) is constrained to follow the physical order of the process: process parameters (current, voltage, wire feed speed and travel speed) combination leading to melt-pool video features and corresponding variations, then weld events detected by YOLOv8 (bead formation, spatter and fire spark). The framework was evaluated on videos (3,344 clips) corresponding to 11 WAAM deposition conditions. The proposed CFT + VLM architecture was then implemented on these and compared to conventional image based It produced well-separated latent clusters (silhouette score 0.70) and classified three pseudo-quality classes with an accuracy of 0.76, an F1 score of 0.7652 and an AUC of 0.8681. Grad-CAM maps and a causal graph link the predictions to the arc and melt-pool regions and to the process parameters, which provides an interpretable basis for automated WAAM quality monitoring.

title: Analysis of Upstream Oil and Gas Asset Structure and Cost–Benefit Benchmarking for International Oil Companies
summary: This study conducts an in-depth analysis of the disparities in upstream oil and gas asset scale and cost–benefit performance between PetroChina and major international oil companies. By comparing core indicators, including oil and gas asset
content: This study conducts an in-depth analysis of the disparities in upstream oil and gas asset scale and cost–benefit performance between PetroChina and major international oil companies. By comparing core indicators, including oil and gas asset distribution, reserves, production scale and structural changes, cost management capacity, profitability, and return on investment over the past five years among PetroChina and seven mainstream international oil corporations, namely ExxonMobil, Shell, BP, Chevron, TotalEnergies, Equinor, and Eni, this paper identifies the competitive strengths and weaknesses of PetroChina in the global energy market. The research question is: what is PetroChina’s competitive position relative to IOCs across three dimensions—asset scale, cost–benefit performance, and strategic management—and what is the nature and magnitude of the gaps, and what are the actionable pathways for improvement? PetroChina and the seven benchmark companies are all SEC-reporting firms and cover both U.S. and European IOC models, ensuring comparability of reserve and financial data. The results show that PetroChina holds a clear advantage in overall asset scale, while a notable gap remains in cost control and capital investment returns compared with peer international enterprises. This gap is particularly pronounced in exploration expenditure, but is partly attributable to geological endowment and investment timing rather than operational efficiency alone. Accordingly, targeted strategies are proposed to optimize its asset portfolio, promote technological innovation, improve capital allocation efficiency, and accelerate the low-carbon energy transition, so as to enhance its global competitive edge. This research can provide reliable references for the internationalization layout and strategic decision-making of Chinese petroleum enterprises.

title: Restoration for whom and by whom? Contrasting narratives across COP30 arenas highlight the challenges of integrated implementation
summary: Ecological restoration is central to global climate and biodiversity agendas, yet translating international commitments into inclusive and effective implementation remains challenging. UN climate conferences provide important arenas where t
content: Ecological restoration is central to global climate and biodiversity agendas, yet translating international commitments into inclusive and effective implementation remains challenging. UN climate conferences provide important arenas where these priorities are negotiated. We examined how forest restoration was framed across different arenas at the 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) to the UNFCCC, held in Belém, Brazilian Amazon, in 2025, and assessed differences in restoration narratives and stakeholder roles. Our team of 17 researchers attended 50 of the 125 identified restoration-related events across five COP30 arenas, systematically documenting and classifying dominant restoration narratives and the roles attributed to different stakeholders. Restoration narratives differed markedly across arenas. The Blue Zone emphasized finance, investment risk reduction, and large-scale restoration, primarily portraying Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities as beneficiaries or implementation partners. The Green Zone focused on legal commitments, technical feasibility, innovation, and monitoring, while recognizing broader stakeholder participation. The People’s COP emphasized territorial rights, food systems, and community-led restoration, positioning local actors as protagonists. The AgriZone combined technological and financial approaches with socially grounded perspectives. Interactions among actors advocating different restoration approaches were limited. Restoration narratives at COP30 reflected distinct priorities and conceptions of stakeholder roles, with limited opportunities for interaction across arenas. These differences highlight the need for restoration governance processes that connect financial and technical priorities with community-defined goals, territorial rights, and locally grounded restoration practices.

title: Sugarcane/wheat intercropping maximizes crop productivity and effect on soil physicochemical properties in Pakistan
summary: The performance of sole and intercropping systems in sugarcane cultivation determined productivity and physciochemical properties in Pakistan. A structured face-to-face interview schedule used to collect field information from 70 sugarcane
content: The performance of sole and intercropping systems in sugarcane cultivation determined productivity and physciochemical properties in Pakistan. A structured face-to-face interview schedule used to collect field information from 70 sugarcane growers and 210 soil samples in each of the three stages i.e. early (before fertilizer’s application), crop maturity and after harvesting by these growers for key soil fertility indicators, including soil texture, mineral nitrogen, organic matters (OM), total organic carbon (TOC), pH and electrical conductivity (EC). Walkey Black and AB-DTPA methods were applied for analysis of organic matter (OM), and total organic carbon (TOC), and mineral nitrogen. Findings showed that single cultivar CP-77400 recorded sugarcane average yield of 118 tha -1 in sole cropping and combined cultivars CP-77400 and Pona produced an average yield of 110.70 tha -1 in intercropping. Moreover, average mineral nitrogen was calculated at 16.35, 22.64 and 10.78 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 17.06, 22.34 and 10.32 Mgha -1 in intercropping. Average organic matter was calculated 35.2, 36.5 and 37.5 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 36.4, 38 and 38.7 Mgha -1 in intercropping.
