The total organic carbon (TOC) was calculated 20, 20.30 and 21.80 Mgha -1 in sole cropping and 21.71, 23.27 and 22.41 Mgha -1 in intercropping. Although soil pH (7.91 to 8) remained within optimal ranges under both systems, EC (21.51 to 27.01) was higher in intercropping plots, indicating possible long-term salinity buildup. This research highlights the importance of crop-soil compatibility, varietal selection and cultivation method in optimizing sugarcane production. Policy recommendations include expanding access and utilization of recommended planting material and enhancing farmer training on sustainable soil and crop management.

title: Symbolic or substantive? Discursive features of moral legitimation in CSR communication
summary: Scholars have advanced competing accounts of how discursive features of corporate social responsibility (CSR) communication relate to firms’ moral legitimation. We examine two such features, discursive distinctiveness and topical diversity,
content: Scholars have advanced competing accounts of how discursive features of corporate social responsibility (CSR) communication relate to firms’ moral legitimation. We examine two such features, discursive distinctiveness and topical diversity, asking for each whether it more often serves symbolic moral legitimation (general value statements and aspirations not anchored in specific actions) or substantive moral legitimation (claims linked to concrete practices, events, or resource-backed commitments). A multilevel analysis of 2,090 manually coded CSR text segments from 15 European media firms (2018–2020) shows that discursive distinctiveness is more often associated with symbolic legitimation, and topical diversity associates more often with substantive legitimation. Our findings provide evidence on competing accounts of each discursive feature’s relationship to moral legitimation, contributing to developing a deeper understanding of the theoretical link between CSR communication and its role in moral legitimacy construction.

title: Evaluating gender equality policy alignment and institutional barriers to women’s retention in the Australian construction industry
source: Journal of Engineering Design and Technology
summary: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives align with the key factors influencing women’s retention in the construction industry. Despite an expanding policy landscape, women
content: Purpose This study aims to evaluate how Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives align with the key factors influencing women’s retention in the construction industry. Despite an expanding policy landscape, women remain underrepresented, indicating persistent institutional and organisational barriers. Design/methodology/approach A five-step evaluative review integrated a PRISMA-guided systematic literature review, analysis of 30 government initiatives and expert validation involving 12 academics and industry practitioners. Guided by Feminist Institutionalism and the Policy Cycle Model, the analysis assessed alignment with four retention factors: Work Hours and Family Commitment (WHAF), Gendered Culture and Informal Rules (GCIR), Career Opportunities and Available Roles (COAR) and Perceptions of Women’s Ability (POWA). Findings Policy attention to gender equality has increased; however, alignment with women’s retention factors remains uneven. Most initiatives focus on career opportunities and workforce participation, while fewer address workplace culture and informal institutional barriers. Legislative and procurement-based initiatives include stronger accountability mechanisms than voluntary initiatives. Practical implications Improving women’s retention requires policy frameworks that integrate stronger accountability mechanisms with initiatives that promote workplace culture, flexible work practices and leadership pathways. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first systematic evaluation of Australian federal and state government gender equality initiatives in relation to women’s retention in the construction industry. By integrating Feminist Institutionalism and the Policy Cycle Model, this study offers a theory-informed framework for assessing policy alignment and informing future gender equality policy development.

title: Next-Generation Interconnect Design
summary: Continuous scaling of the complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology has exacerbated the power-delay bottlenecks in global on-chip interconnects, posing critical challenges in achieving energy-efficient and high-speed data tr
content: Continuous scaling of the complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology has exacerbated the power-delay bottlenecks in global on-chip interconnects, posing critical challenges in achieving energy-efficient and high-speed data transmission. This chapter explores a spectrum of innovative solutions to mitigate these issues, including low-swing signaling schemes, magneto-electric (ME) effect-based receivers, and spin-torque (ST) sensor-driven interconnect frameworks. Specifically, it analyzes techniques like multi- V dd and multi- V th voltage scaling, current-mode signaling, and the advanced modified Junction (MJ) driver to achieve low dynamic and static power consumption. Furthermore, it introduces a capacitively driven interconnect architecture utilizing ME-MTJ devices for efficient signal restoration without analog amplification, and a pipelined repeater framework employing ST buffers with domain wall (DW) motion for delay optimization. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in energy efficiency and signal integrity. These hybrid architectures provide promising pathways for scalable and low-power on-chip systems. Future developments will hinge on advancements in materials, device modeling, and integration strategies for deployment in emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators and neuromorphic processors.

title: From Spent NiMo Catalysts to Marketable Metal Products: A Critical Review of Recovery Selectivity, Process Integration, Mass Balances, and Industrial Feasibility
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Spent nickel–molybdenum (NiMo) hydroprocessing catalysts combine recoverable strategic metals with complex alumina supports, deposited carbon, sulfur, residual hydrocarbons, and feed-dependent contaminants. This critical review evaluates pa
content: Spent nickel–molybdenum (NiMo) hydroprocessing catalysts combine recoverable strategic metals with complex alumina supports, deposited carbon, sulfur, residual hydrocarbons, and feed-dependent contaminants. This critical review evaluates pathways from spent catalyst handling to saleable molybdenum and nickel compounds, emphasizing process-wide selectivity rather than isolated leaching yields. The literature was screened by feed identity, phase transformation, separation performance, completeness of material balances, product specification, and evidence scale. Thermal conditioning, alkaline conversion followed by molybdate leaching, direct acidic and oxidative leaching, biohydrometallurgy, selective solvent extraction, precipitation, and integrated flowsheets are compared. A normalized accounting framework distinguishes extraction, purification yield, overall metal recovery, chemical consumption, effluent load, and support disposition. Alkaline-first processing offers a compelling basis for separating molybdenum from nickel when feed phases and reagent demand permit, whereas direct hydrometallurgy can reduce thermal complexity at the cost of solution purification. Reported laboratory recoveries cannot by themselves establish industrial feasibility or product marketability. The review proposes explicit acceptance gates covering compositional variability, phase-resolved deportment, sulfur and aluminum balances, recycle chemistry, saleable product quality, and pilot-scale operability. These gates provide a technically auditable basis for route selection and subsequent engineering validation.

title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms
summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information proc
content: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing. It then develops the algorithmic core of the field, examining how quantum principles can be systematically translated into high-impact procedures for searching structured and unstructured spaces, solving optimization problems, and achieving provable computational advantages under realistic hardware constraints. This book: Provides a comprehensive treatment of the broader quantum ecosystem. Covers quantum cryptography and post-quantum security, error correction and fault tolerance, programming frameworks and software stacks, hardware platforms, and the emerging interface between quantum computing and machine learning. Critically engages with real-world applications in finance, logistics, pharmaceuticals, climate science, cybersecurity, and materials discovery which demonstrate the transformative reach of technology. Engages with future trajectories, commercialization, ethics, governance, and global equity. Equips readers to understand both the power and the limits of quantum computation. Designed for researchers, advanced students, engineers, and technology strategists, this volume presents quantum computing not as an abstract scientific curiosity, but as a structured computational discipline grounded in qubits, unitary gates, circuit architectures, interference engineering, and algorithmic complexity. It is an essential reference for anyone seeking to navigate the technical depth, interdisciplinary scope, and strategic significance of quantum searching and optimization in the coming computational era.

title: The Soft Side of Circularity: Rethinking Fashion Resale for Sustainability Transitions
summary: Despite growing adoption of circular economy (CE) principles and circular business models (CBMs), global circularity remains in decline. As empirical evidence increasingly challenges the effectiveness of leading CE approaches in supporting
content: Despite growing adoption of circular economy (CE) principles and circular business models (CBMs), global circularity remains in decline. As empirical evidence increasingly challenges the effectiveness of leading CE approaches in supporting sustainability, identifying the conditions required for a meaningful CE transition that successfully breaks with unsustainable, linear economy patterns becomes critical. Focusing on fashion resale business models (RBMs) we argue that genuine change does not foremost rely on technological development or the scaling of large-scale, standardised solutions. Instead, we contend that human-dependent factors and capabilities, including materials knowledge, sensitivity to changing cultural tastes, and the tacit knowledge and practical skills required to assess, handle, and recirculate garments, are particularly adept at supporting inner loop circularity. We therefore propose that the realisation of CE ambitions requires a greater emphasis on less tangible human aspects. Suggesting that such are vital and yet remains both underexamined and underappreciated in the current CE landscape, we argue that the 'soft’ side of circularity warrants greater attention across academic and practical domains.

title: Avrupa’dan Eko-Mahalle Örnekleri: Sürdürülebilir Kent Yaşamı için Uygulanabilir Modeller
source: Ömer Halisdemir Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Bu çalışmanın amacı, çevresel kirliliğin ve ekolojik sorunların azaltılmasına, kentte sürdürülebilir yaşam alanlarının oluşturulmasına katkı sağlayan eko-mahalleleri karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemek ve Türkiye’ye öneriler sunmaktır. Bu bağl
content: Bu çalışmanın amacı, çevresel kirliliğin ve ekolojik sorunların azaltılmasına, kentte sürdürülebilir yaşam alanlarının oluşturulmasına katkı sağlayan eko-mahalleleri karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemek ve Türkiye’ye öneriler sunmaktır. Bu bağlamda Avrupa’dan BedZED, Bo01, ZAC de Bonne, Vauban, Hammarby Sjöstad ve Lombok olmak üzere toplam 6 eko-mahalle, farklı planlama rejimlerini, dönemleri ve gelişim türlerini temsil edecek biçimde amaçlı örnekleme ile seçilmiştir. Çalışmada nitel karşılaştırmalı vaka analizi deseni kullanılarak eko-mahalleler; tarihsel arka plan, planlama yaklaşımı, ulaşım, enerji, su ve atık yönetimi, toplumsal katılım ve sosyal kapsayıcılık temalarında ve bu temalara ait göstergeler üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Bu çerçevede eko-mahallelerle ilgili literatür, resmi planlama ve izleme raporları ile kurumsal belgeler incelenmiştir. Türkçe literatürde eko-kent ve ekolojik planlama üzerine çalışmalar bulunmakla birlikte, birden fazla Avrupa eko-mahallesini ortak bir çerçevede karşılaştıran çalışma sayısı sınırlıdır. Uluslararası literatürde ise önemli sayıda çalışma bulunmakla birlikte bu çalışmaların büyük bölümü tek bir eko-mahalleye odaklanmaktadır. Bu nedenle çalışma, 6 vakayı ortak bir gösterge çerçevesiyle karşılaştırması ve tasarım hedefleri ile gerçekleşen performans arasındaki farkları görünür kılması bakımından literatüre katkı sunmaktadır. Çalışmadan elde edilen bulgular değerlendirildiğinde; BedZED ve Vauban öncü projeler olarak enerji verimliliği, pasif tasarım ve düşük karbon salımı hedefleriyle öne çıkmaktadır; ancak BedZED’de biyokütle kojenerasyon sisteminin devre dışı kalması, tasarım hedefi ile gerçekleşen performans arasında belirgin bir açık yaratmıştır. Bo01 ve Hammarby Sjöstad belediye öncülüğünde yenilenebilir enerji ve entegre altyapı (enerji-su-atık) çözümlerinde öne çıkmakla birlikte sosyal karışım bakımından eleştirilere konu olmaktadır. ZAC de Bonne’da sosyal konut oranının hedeflenen %35’ten %40’a ulaşması sosyal karışımda olumlu sonuç verirken ölçülen enerji tüketimi hedeflerin üzerinde kalmıştır. Lombok ise topluluk girişimleriyle dönüşen mevcut bir mahalle olarak katılım ve akıllı enerji uygulamalarında öne çıkmakta, ancak soylulaştırma baskısıyla karşı karşıya kalmaktadır. Bu bulgular, eko-mahallelerin teknik başarısının sosyal kapsayıcılıkla her zaman örtüşmediğini; bununla birlikte eko-mahallelerin katılım, karma mülkiyet ve ölçüme dayalı izleme konularında Türkiye’ye örnek olabileceğini göstermektedir.

title: ALKALINE-EXTRACTED SUGARCANE BAGASSE AS A PLANT-BASED COAGULANT FOR CATTLE SLAUGHTERHOUSE WASTEWATER
summary: Effluent from the Banda Aceh municipal slaughterhouse, Indonesia, receives only bar screening, and a single grab sample exceeded the national chemical oxygen demand (COD) limit. Plant-based coagulants are proposed alternatives to metal salt
content: Effluent from the Banda Aceh municipal slaughterhouse, Indonesia, receives only bar screening, and a single grab sample exceeded the national chemical oxygen demand (COD) limit. Plant-based coagulants are proposed alternatives to metal salts; sugarcane bagasse has been studied as an adsorbent and activated-carbon precursor but, to our knowledge, not as a coagulant for slaughterhouse effluent. We screened a crude alkaline bagasse extract (2% NaOH, hotplate set to 120 °C, 2 h, open beaker) as a coagulant for cattle slaughterhouse wastewater. Three stock concentrations (0.1–0.3% w/v) were each dosed at four volumes (5–20 mL; nominal doses 5–60 mg/L) in single-run jar tests, with a settling-only control. Raw COD was 1,422 mg/L, and settling alone reduced it by 53.3%. The lowest COD (155 mg/L; 0.2% stock, 20 mg/L nominal dose) was 76.7% lower than the control and below the 200 mg/L COD limit; pH stayed within 6.5–6.8, but other regulated parameters were not measured. Over-dosing increased COD, and in one treatment (0.3% stock, 60 mg/L) it exceeded the control. Three conditions met the COD limit (0.2% stock at 20 and 30 mg/L; 0.3% stock at 15 mg/L). Because equal nominal doses from different stock concentrations gave inconsistent results and each treatment was run once, these results identify conditions for further testing rather than an optimum. Replicated jar tests with a control in every batch, and characterisation of the extract, are needed.

title: Assessing a large language model for consistent and discriminatory performance in wound care bioengineering research and development tasks
summary: background Despite the growing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare-related contexts, their integration into applied academic and industry research workflows remains underexplored, particularly with respect to reproducibil
content: background Despite the growing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare-related contexts, their integration into applied academic and industry research workflows remains underexplored, particularly with respect to reproducibility and semantic stability of their outputs. objectives To evaluate the semantic consistency, discriminatory performance, and response stability of ChatGPT-4 (GUI-accessed) in supporting biomedical and bioengineering research tasks, using wound-care research and development as an early test case, with an exploratory GPT-4o (API-accessed) extension screening output stability under varied hyperparameters. Methods Two structured 30-query datasets, comprising wound-related queries, semantically equivalent paraphrases, and unrelated controls, were evaluated using GPT-4 via a graphical user interface (GUI). Four natural language processing text representation methods (TRMs): TF-IDF, Word2Vec, Sent2Vec, and Bag of Words, were used to compute similarity scores between outputs. Additional evaluations included device- and time-dependent variation testing and an exploratory case study on wound dressing stiffness using API (OpenAI) across parameter-space screening of varied hyperparameters. Results Sent2Vec demonstrated the highest discriminatory power, with similarity-score differentials of 0.49 and 0.50 in the LLM-generated and expert-generated query phases, respectively. ChatGPT-4 (GUI) maintained semantic consistency across reworded queries and under different usage conditions. In the exploratory case study, GPT-4o (API)-generated stiffness values remained relatively stable across parameter settings. The resulting mean stiffness values ranged from 25.3 to 36.5 kPa and fell within the approximately 15-90 kPa range reported for hydrogel-based dressing materials in the cited biomechanical literature. Conclusions ChatGPT, evaluated as GPT-4 (GUI) for semantic consistency and GPT-4o (API) for the stiffness screening, offers preliminary evidence of semantic consistency and stable output behavior when responding to wound care research and development queries. These findings are exploratory and should be interpreted strictly as preliminary hypothesis generation and textual exploration, not as evidence of scientific reliability, predictive validity, or decision-support capability. This study presents a novel and pilot framework for characterizing LLM output consistency and stability in specialized biomedical contexts, intended to inform the design of future, more comprehensive validation studies.

title: A soberania econômica dos Estados africanos:
summary: La soberanía económica de los Estados africanos: Sanciones internacionales, competencia entre grandes potencias y los límites y posibilidades del Derecho Internacional Económico Resumo Este artigo investiga a soberania econômica dos Estados
content: La soberanía económica de los Estados africanos: Sanciones internacionales, competencia entre grandes potencias y los límites y posibilidades del Derecho Internacional Económico Resumo Este artigo investiga a soberania econômica dos Estados africanos a partir de três eixos que a atravessam simultaneamente: o regime jurídico das sanções internacionais (multilaterais, regionais e unilaterais) e seus reflexos sobre a autodeterminação econômica; a disputa geoeconômica entre China, Estados Unidos, Rússia, União Europeia e potências médias por minerais críticos, mercados e infraestrutura; e as respostas construídas pelo Direito Internacional Econômico, com destaque para a Zona de Comércio Livre Continental Africana (AfCFTA), a reforma da arquitetura de reestruturação de dívida soberana e a consolidação de bancos multilaterais africanos. Defende-se que a leitura binária dependência-autonomia, recorrente na literatura, não dá conta da complexidade do fenômeno contemporâneo. A soberania econômica africana é mais bem compreendida como campo relacional de barganha assimétrica, no qual Estados e blocos regionais acumulam instrumentos jurídicos cada vez mais sofisticados, ainda que insuficientes, para converter recursos naturais em capacidade normativa efetiva

title: The translational journey of human pluripotent stem cells
source: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
summary: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), comprising embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), have emerged as a versatile platform connecting developmental biology with disease modelling, drug discovery, and regen
content: Human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs), comprising embryonic stem cells (ESCs) and induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), have emerged as a versatile platform connecting developmental biology with disease modelling, drug discovery, and regenerative medicine. Their capacity for indefinite self-renewal and differentiation into derivatives of all three germ layers provides an essentially renewable source of human cells that are otherwise inaccessible from patients. In this review, we discuss the biological principles governing hPSC identity, with emphasis on the transcriptional, epigenetic, metabolic, and extracellular signalling networks that regulate pluripotency and the distinct features of naive and primed states. We further examine culture systems for maintaining pluripotency and directed differentiation strategies for generating lineage-specific cell types. The application of hPSCs to disease modelling and therapeutic discovery is considered through two-dimensional cellular models and increasingly sophisticated three-dimensional organoids and organoid-on-chip systems, which provide progressively greater tissue complexity and physiological relevance. We also highlight the integration of CRISPR-based genome editing with hPSC platforms to generate isogenic disease models, establish genotype–phenotype relationships, identify therapeutic targets, and enable precise correction of disease-associated variants. Finally, we review the emerging clinical applications of hPSC-derived cell therapies and clinical translation, which remains constrained by challenges related to genomic stability, cellular heterogeneity and maturation, immune compatibility, tumorigenicity, manufacturing, and scalability. Addressing these challenges through improved differentiation, quality control, genome engineering, and scalable manufacturing will be essential for translating the broad potential of hPSCs into safe, reproducible, and accessible clinical therapies.

title: Payment bases and performance logic in China’s subnational compensation for cultivated land protection in the context of ecological and environmental law codification: a two-tier content analysis of 155 legal and policy documents
summary: Introduction China’s policy framework calls for integrated protection of cultivated land quantity, quality, and ecological functions, but how this objective is reflected in subnational compensation rules remains unclear. Methods From 650 in
content: Introduction China’s policy framework calls for integrated protection of cultivated land quantity, quality, and ecological functions, but how this objective is reflected in subnational compensation rules remains unclear. Methods From 650 initial records, this study constructed a two-tier corpus of 155 legal and policy documents: 108 dedicated compensation documents and 47 containing embedded provisions. Content analysis distinguished payment bases, performance logic, and institutional linkages. An independent assessment of coding covered 46 documents from the original corpus (29.7%), and a separate screening assessment covered 61 records. The 2013–2020 and 2021–2026 issuance cohorts were compared across all documents and among 124 historical rule-setting instruments. Corpus coverage ended on 30 June 2026, with only two documents from 2026. Results Agreement varied by indicator, with weaker chance-corrected agreement for rare ecological and institutional-linkage categories. Area-based allocation and administrative-compliance linkages appeared in 98 documents (63.2%) and 97 documents (62.6%), respectively. Cultivated land quality informed payment standards or allocation in 26 documents (16.8%), while 48 documents (31.0%) linked payment consequences to quality, maintenance, or environmental conditions. A supplementary assessment identified specified quality-linked financial consequences in three of the 26 quality-related documents; details on measurement and verification were limited. No dedicated payment for ecological outcomes was identified; one document used ecological outcomes to allocate broader ecological protection compensation. Institutional linkages appeared in seven documents (4.5%), all in the embedded-provision corpus. Among rule-setting instruments, quality-related allocation occurred in 13.9% of the earlier cohort and 26.9% of the later cohort, with the contrast concentrated in Zhejiang. Under the primary definition, condition- or outcome-linked provisions occurred in 38.9% and 36.5%, respectively; the direction of this contrast reversed under an extended definition. Discussion Because Zhejiang contributed 85 documents (54.8%), pooled frequencies describe the assembled corpus rather than nationwide prevalence. The limited institutional linkages do not establish a substantial trend toward coordination between the two compensation systems. The evidence supports geographically uneven institutional layering, combining fiscal allocation and administrative accountability with selectively incorporated quality and environmental conditions. It does not establish a system-wide transition toward result-based compensation or demonstrate that proposed reforms improve agricultural or environmental outcomes.

title: Dynamic Mechanisms of CCS-EOR Technology Diffusion Driven by Carbon Market Policies: An Evolutionary Game Analysis and Carbon Price Threshold Study
summary: Large-scale diffusion of carbon capture, storage, and enhanced oil recovery (CCS-EOR) technology requires coordinated decisions by CO2 capture and utilization enterprises, yet their economic incentives are interdependent. This study aims to
content: Large-scale diffusion of carbon capture, storage, and enhanced oil recovery (CCS-EOR) technology requires coordinated decisions by CO2 capture and utilization enterprises, yet their economic incentives are interdependent. This study aims to explain how carbon allowance prices and allocation constraints affect bilateral CO2 pricing and the subsequent adoption of CCS-EOR technology. An alternating-offer bargaining model for determining the CO2 transaction price is coupled with a two-population evolutionary game describing the adoption decisions of capture and utilization enterprises. This integrated approach examines how carbon-market policies shape bargaining outcomes, economic returns, and adoption strategies of both enterprise types. Four techno-economic scenarios calibrated to Chinese CCS-EOR projects are examined using equilibrium analysis, numerical diffusion simulations, a ±10% parameter sensitivity analysis, and stochastic allowance price robustness tests. The critical allowance prices are 64.9 and 110.0 USD/tCO2 for low- and high-capture-cost scenarios, respectively, a difference of 45.1 USD/tCO2 (approximately 69.5% of the low-capture-cost threshold). A ±10% change in operating capture cost shifts these thresholds by ±6.15 and ±10.66 USD/tCO2, whereas the same change in levelized fixed capture cost shifts both thresholds by ±0.34 USD/tCO2. Simulations using a 19 × 19 grid of initial adoption probabilities quantify the basin of attraction of joint adoption; the critical carbon price depends on capture costs, while oil recovery benefits and other techno-economic factors affect the diffusion trajectories below the threshold. Robustness analysis is conducted, considering allowance price fluctuations under a mean-reverting process across different noise intensities (σ = 0 and 6 USD/tCO2). The findings show that carbon pricing influences utilization enterprises indirectly through bargained CO2 transaction prices and that coupling bilateral price negotiations with evolutionary adoption decisions offers a more comprehensive explanation of CCS-EOR technology diffusion and differentiated policy requirements.

title: Conformational inhibitors of the HIV-1 Rev response element identified through a FRET-based screening approach
summary: The complex formed between the HIV-1 protein Rev and the Rev Response Element (RRE) in the genomic RNA of the virus represents an attractive target for antiretroviral therapy. To date, however, there are no RRE-Rev inhibitors in clinical us
content: The complex formed between the HIV-1 protein Rev and the Rev Response Element (RRE) in the genomic RNA of the virus represents an attractive target for antiretroviral therapy. To date, however, there are no RRE-Rev inhibitors in clinical use. In this study we have applied a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay based on placing Cy3- and Cy5-labeled oligomeric probes at distal domain locations within the RRE to identify small-molecule compounds capable of perturbing the spatial organization of RRE domains and disrupting the association of Rev monomers. After screening a library of bioactive compounds and approved drugs, we identified two molecules, myricetin and raloxifene, that recognize the RRE and inhibit the RRE-Rev interaction in vitro and in cellulo. Both compounds exhibited antiretroviral activity with favorable selectivity indexes, and further analyses involving RRE mutants suggested that myricetin modulated the conformation of the RRE through binding to a four-helix intersection. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for targeting the RRE-Rev complex and identify myricetin and raloxifene as promising starting points for the development of novel anti-HIV agents.

title: NFT-Mediated Digital Creativity: A Conceptual Model for Reimagining Jingdezhen Ceramic Heritage through Cultural Translation
source: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
summary: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) can connect digital artworks to identifiable blockchain records, but neither tokenisation nor a platform listing independently authenticates the underlying cultural object or confers copyright. This article develo
content: Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) can connect digital artworks to identifiable blockchain records, but neither tokenisation nor a platform listing independently authenticates the underlying cultural object or confers copyright. This article develops an NFT-Mediated Digital Creativity Model to explain how the affordances of digital tokens and platforms may interact with cultural translation in the reinterpretation of Jingdezhen ceramic heritage. This article adopts a conceptual synthesis and uses Jingdezhen ceramic heritage as an analytically illustrative context; it does not report an empirical investigation of identified Jingdezhen NFT collections.Its three linked dimensions are creative-technical conditions (token and metadata structure, traceability, interface design and discoverability), translation-creative practices (iconographic interpretation, narrative recontextualisation and creative reassembly), and contingent circulation outcomes (visibility, interpretive hybridity and participatory engagement). Jingdezhen provides a historically situated context because its ceramic technologies, production networks and visual conventions have undergone repeated adaptation across markets and communities. The analysis separates verifiable token histories from claims about artistic authorship, cultural legitimacy and audience reception. It argues that NFTs may serve as one optional layer within broader digital heritage systems, rather than as a necessary or inherently superior means of safeguarding heritage.The model yields testable expectations concerning metadata quality, community participation, interpretive diversity and platform governance, while identifying intellectual-property, cultural representation and infrastructure risks. Its contribution is a cautiously specified framework for analysing when token-mediated creative circulation might support, rather than substitute for, historically informed heritage interpretation.

title: Shock transmission and risk diversification between regional REITs and clean energy markets
source: International Journal of Strategic Property Management
summary: This study examines risk transmission among regional real estate markets and evaluates the diversification potential of clean energy stocks within regional REIT portfolios. A quantile time-frequency vector autoregressive model is used to an
content: This study examines risk transmission among regional real estate markets and evaluates the diversification potential of clean energy stocks within regional REIT portfolios. A quantile time-frequency vector autoregressive model is used to analyse interconnectedness between regional REITs and clean energy markets over the period from November 2008 to March 2025. The results reveal significant risk spillovers between regional housing stock markets under bullish and bearish conditions. Most interconnectedness occurs over short-term horizons and gradually weakens over time, indicating that contagion effects are largely temporary. Clean energy markets act as a shock absorber and provide hedging benefits for REIT portfolios. Under low-risk, shocks from Asian, European, and UK REITs affect the US and South African markets, while the green bond index serves as a diversifier. In normal markets, European, UK, and US real estate shocks transmit to Asia and South Africa, with renewable energy acting as a buffer against risk. During periods of high uncertainty, other regional markets transmit shocks to the US listed real estate market, yet renewable energy continues to offer diversification benefits. Therefore, clean energy stocks consistently mitigate risk in regional REIT portfolios across market conditions and investment horizons.

title: Decomposing the Short and Long‐Run Effects of ESG Performance and Materiality on Corporate External Financing Needs
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance on corporate external financing needs (EFN), using a global panel comprising 3437 firms and 11,075 firm‐year observations. Drawing on theories
content: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance on corporate external financing needs (EFN), using a global panel comprising 3437 firms and 11,075 firm‐year observations. Drawing on theories from institutional, risk management and behavioral finance, we decompose short‐ and long‐run dynamics using correlated random effects models, addressing endogeneity through two‐stage least squares (2SLS) estimations. Our findings show that higher ESG performance significantly reduces EFN, with the greatest benefits accruing over the long term. Formal mediation analysis reveals that this relationship operates through four economic channels: enhanced asset tangibility, improved free cash flow generation, eased financial constraints and superior investment efficiency. A key contribution of this study is the identification of a U‐shaped relationship between the materiality of ESG reporting and EFN. Above an optimal threshold, information overload and compliance costs dominate, thereby increasing EFN. We also document that the mitigating effect of ESG varies across pillars and time horizons. These results emphasize the temporal, contingent and mechanism‐driven nature of ESG in corporate financing, providing actionable guidance for managers and policymakers seeking to align sustainability practices with financial resilience.

title: Capital flight? Do airlines move fuel-efficient planes to high-fuel-tax routes?
source: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
summary: This paper shows that airlines operate fuel-efficient planes on routes with high fuel taxes. It builds on a large data-collection effort compiling information on fuel taxes at the airport level, which is used to generate route-level taxes f
content: This paper shows that airlines operate fuel-efficient planes on routes with high fuel taxes. It builds on a large data-collection effort compiling information on fuel taxes at the airport level, which is used to generate route-level taxes for thousands of nonstop airline routes in the US. The paper extends previous work exploring the connection between fuel prices and airline operations, with a new focus on the taxation of inputs. The results are used to derive the local pollution benefits from a route-specific fuel-tax increase.

title: Can policy-induced fair competition promote firm cooperative green innovation? Evidence from China’s Competition Review System
summary: Amid the global pursuit of sustainable development, aligning competition policy with green innovation has become an important institutional challenge. This study examines the impact of China’s Fair Competition Review System (FCRS) on firms’
content: Amid the global pursuit of sustainable development, aligning competition policy with green innovation has become an important institutional challenge. This study examines the impact of China’s Fair Competition Review System (FCRS) on firms’ cooperative green innovation (CGI), using a quasi-natural experiment based on panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2011 to 2023, excluding the 2016 transition year. The results show that firms in regions with greater pre-policy market segmentation experience larger post-FCRS increases in CGI, whereas independent green innovation does not change significantly. The increase is evident in both firm-firm and firm-university/research-institute co-patenting. The effect is stronger in regions with higher marketization, areas where the FCRS is embedded in government performance assessment, and among high-tech and state-owned enterprises. Channel tests are consistent with improved green innovation disclosure, stronger market competition, and lower transaction-related cost burdens. Further analysis shows that the FCRS reduces inefficient investment, increases environmental investment and narrows green total factor productivity gaps. Its effect is also strengthened by low-carbon city policies, environmental taxation and green credit policies. These findings highlight the role of fair competition policy in supporting cooperative green innovation and green transformation.

title: AI Washing as the New Corporate Misrepresentation
summary: Corporate misrepresentation has long threatened the integrity of financial markets, from financial fraud and inflated product claims to deceptive disclosures.This article examines an emerging form of such misconduct: "Artificial intelligenc
content: Corporate misrepresentation has long threatened the integrity of financial markets, from financial fraud and inflated product claims to deceptive disclosures.This article examines an emerging form of such misconduct: "Artificial intelligence (hereinafter AI) washing", in which companies exaggerate or fabricate their use of capabilities in AI to increase valuations, attract investors or gain a competitive advantage.Although scholarship has extensively examined the analogous phenomenon of greenwashing, the prevalence, legal consequences and regulatory treatment of AI washing remain comparatively underexplored.This article addresses that gap by asking when AI-related corporate claims constitute actionable securities misrepresentation and whether existing doctrine, particularly Rule 10b-5 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (hereinafter Act), is adequately equipped to address them.It also examines the challenges of detecting misleading AI claims given the technical opacity and rapidly evolving nature of AI systems.Drawing on a textual analysis of more than 5,000 U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (hereinafter SEC) filings from 2020 to 2025, a comparative examination of greenwashing enforcement and a qualitative analysis of recent AI-related enforcement actions, the article finds that AI washing may satisfy Rule 10b-5's materiality and scienter requirements when corporate representations materially diverge from operational reality.The analysis further identifies a 15-20% valuation premium associated with unsubstantiated AI claims that dissipates following scrutiny, suggesting potential investor harms comparable to those observed in greenwashing.Building on these findings, the article proposes tailored SEC disclosure guidance, an expanded role for auditors and stronger incentives for private enforcement.These reforms seek to improve the verifiability of AI-related corporate disclosures while preserving space for legitimate communication about emerging technologies. AnnotasiyaKorporativ mühitdə yanlış təqdimat uzun müddətdir ki, maliyyə fırıldaqçılıqlarından və məhsullar haqqında şişirdilmiş iddialardan tutmuş, aldadıcı açıqlamalara qədər müxtəlif formalarda maliyyə bazarlarının bütövlüyünə təhlükə yaradır.Məqalədə belə pozuntuların yeni formalarından biri olan "AI washing" araşdırılır.Bu anlayış şirkətlərin bazar dəyərlərini artırmaq, investorları cəlb etmək və ya rəqabət üstünlüyü qazanmaq məqsədilə süni intellektdən (bundan sonra -Sİ) istifadə etdikləri barədə həqiqətə uyğun olmayan məlumatlar verməsini və ya bu imkanları olduğundan daha geniş göstərməsini ifadə edir.Elmi ədəbiyyatda "greenwashing" anlayışı geniş şəkildə araşdırılsa da, "AI washing"in yayılma səviyyəsi, hüquqi nəticələri və tənzimlənməsi məsələlərinə nisbətən daha az diqqət yetirilmişdir.Məqalə bu boşluğu aradan qaldırmaq məqsədilə Sİ ilə bağlı şirkət iddialarının hansı hallarda qiymətli kağızlar bazarında hüquqi məsuliyyətə səbəb ola biləcək yanlış təqdimat hesab edildiyi

title: Effects of Carton Redesign following Package Insert Digitization on Usability and Carbon Footprint of Vaccine Vials
summary: We evaluated the impact of changes in carton specifications for two-vial, human-use vaccine products on usability and carbon footprint. The modifications were implemented to enhance functionality and usability following the digitization and
content: We evaluated the impact of changes in carton specifications for two-vial, human-use vaccine products on usability and carbon footprint. The modifications were implemented to enhance functionality and usability following the digitization and elimination of package inserts. Although sensory evaluations conducted among healthcare professionals involved in vaccination exhibited substantial individual variation, ratings for carton openability, resealability, vial removability, and vial holding position improved after the changes when comparing mode scores. By contrast, ratings for cushioning and disposability were higher before the changes, indicating areas for further improvement. Following the specification changes, the carton became heavier because of the increased surface area required for cushioning, resulting in a higher carbon footprint for the carton alone. However, when the reduction in package insert usage was considered, the overall carbon footprint decreased. Furthermore, the number of vial breakage reports from the market introduction of the revised products through the end of fiscal year 2025 declined substantially compared with the pre-change period, confirming the feasibility and safety of real-world implementation.

title: Micropropagation and Genetic Fidelity in Strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duch.): Current Status and Future Directions
summary: Morden strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is an economically important octoploid fruit crop, prized for its nutritional value, commercial returns and antioxidant-rich fruit. Its conventional propagation through runners, however, is lim
content: Morden strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is an economically important octoploid fruit crop, prized for its nutritional value, commercial returns and antioxidant-rich fruit. Its conventional propagation through runners, however, is limited by a low multiplication rate and a high risk of systemic pathogen transmission, creating a clear need for alternative methods capable of producing uniform, disease-free planting material at scale. In vitro micropropagation has become the technique of choice for rapid clonal multiplication, though prolonged culture duration and callus-mediated regeneration can induce somaclonal variation and compromise clonal fidelity. This review critically examines recent progress in explant selection, surface sterilization protocols, culture media optimization, plant growth regulator combinations, direct versus indirect regeneration pathways, rooting strategies and acclimatization techniques for strawberry micropropagation, with particular attention to the assessment of genetic stability through molecular markers such as RAPD, ISSR, SSR and EST-SSR. Evidence drawn from multiple studies shows that direct organogenesis from nodal or shoot-tip explants, combined with optimized cytokinin concentrations, substantially reduces the risk of genetic instability relative to indirect, callus-based regeneration. Molecular marker analyses have repeatedly confirmed high genetic uniformity among micropropagated plantlets raised under controlled, standardized protocols. Despite this progress, challenges remain in standardizing protocols across cultivars, achieving cost-effective scale-up and detecting the subtle epigenetic or somaclonal changes that conventional markers can miss. Future work should focus on integrating high-throughput and epigenetic screening tools, automating micropropagation systems and developing cultivar-specific protocols to further improve efficiency and reliability. Taken together, pairing optimized micropropagation systems with robust molecular validation offers a sustainable pathway for commercial nursery production, germplasm conservation and genetic improvement programs in strawberry.

title: Assessing response strategies for maritime chokepoint disruptions: An integrated routing–simulation framework with application to the Suez Canal
source: Transportation Research Part A Policy and Practice
summary: This study presents an integrated routing–simulation framework to evaluate response strategies to maritime chokepoint disruptions. The framework combines disruption-route generation using the A-star algorithm with stochastic modeling of can
content: This study presents an integrated routing–simulation framework to evaluate response strategies to maritime chokepoint disruptions. The framework combines disruption-route generation using the A-star algorithm with stochastic modeling of canal queuing, demand, and shipping dynamics through Monte Carlo and discrete-event simulation. The framework examines the disruption and operating conditions under which waiting, normal-speed rerouting, or increased-speed rerouting becomes the preferred response strategy. Strategy performance is assessed using a multi-perspective societal-cost framework, complemented by sensitivity analysis and random forest (RF) modeling to evaluate factor importance. A case study of container vessels affected by blockages on routes between selected European and Asian countries via the Suez Canal shows that rerouting reduces time-related costs by approximately 7–22% but increases fuel consumption, resulting in substantially higher operational (60–245%) and emissions (80–300%) costs than the waiting strategy, which serves as the baseline scenario. Overall, rerouting results in higher societal costs, making waiting the preferred strategy under most conditions. A disruption duration of approximately 25 days represents the transition point at which normal-speed rerouting and waiting yield nearly equivalent societal costs. Sensitivity analysis indicates that the preferred adaptation strategy depends on fleet characteristics. Highly energy-efficient vessels favor increased-speed rerouting in all blockage scenarios. Conversely, moderately energy-efficient vessels favor different strategies depending on market conditions, either normal-speed or increased-speed rerouting. Additionally, congestion levels influence the transition point between alternative response strategies. RF analysis further identifies the relative importance of key economic and technical parameters that shape societal cost outcomes for each strategy.

title: Debittering Methods in Lupinus Species: A Comprehensive Review
summary: ABSTRACT Lupinus species (spp.), commonly known as lupins, represent a promising source of plant‐based protein and bioactive compounds for food applications. However, their utilization in food products is constrained by the presence of quin
content: ABSTRACT Lupinus species (spp.), commonly known as lupins, represent a promising source of plant‐based protein and bioactive compounds for food applications. However, their utilization in food products is constrained by the presence of quinolizidine alkaloids, which impart characteristic bitterness and pose toxicity risks. This narrative review examines traditional, chemical, biological, and emerging debittering techniques, assessing their effectiveness, impact on nutritional composition, and technological relevance. Traditional aqueous methods, such as soaking and boiling, effectively reduce alkaloid content but require prolonged processing times and excessive water consumption. Chemical treatments, including alkaline and acid solutions, accelerate debittering, but they raise environmental concerns. Biological approaches, such as fermentation and enzymatic hydrolysis, offer potentially sustainable alternatives. Emerging technologies, including ultrasound, microwave‐assisted extraction, supercritical and subcritical fluid extraction, adsorption, and extrusion, offer promising pathways for sustainable lupin processing. The review highlights the need for optimized, scalable, and eco‐friendly debittering processes to facilitate the industrial‐scale application of lupin‐based products. Overall, no single emerging technology provides a universal solution. Integrated and hybrid strategies may offer the greatest potential by balancing alkaloid removal, nutrient retention, water and energy consumption, and scalability. Future research should focus on optimizing and validating sustainable processes at the industrial scale for Lupinus spp.

title: Why being right can be wrong: intellectual humility as a key driver of responsible management education
summary: Purpose This article, written for the inaugural issue of the Journal of Responsible Management Education, argues that business schools, in their worthy pursuit of answers to management problems, often settle on one right answer to a problem
content: Purpose This article, written for the inaugural issue of the Journal of Responsible Management Education, argues that business schools, in their worthy pursuit of answers to management problems, often settle on one right answer to a problem. Yet rarely is the same answer right for everyone, everywhere and always. The notion of responsibility recognizes that the right answer often depends on the context. It proposes intellectual humility as the capacity that responsible management education most needs to cultivate. Design/methodology/approach The authors, who were the Chair and Vice Chair of the Advisory Board of the UN’s Principles for Responsible Management Education (PRME), develop a conceptual argument drawing on critiques of management education and the literature on intellectual humility. They illustrate the argument with PRME initiatives and extend it to the wider UN Global Compact. Findings Answers to management problems are contextual: they depend on whose perspective is taken and on the scale, place and time at which they are applied. Treating answers as universally right can close people off from others’ views, obscure the harms that emerge when actions scale up or persist and inhibit learning among both students and faculty. Grades, rankings and promotion criteria that reward the single right answer reinforce these tendencies. Originality/value The article reframes responsible management education as the cultivation of intellectual humility rather than the pursuit of a different set of right answers. It shows how PRME’s communities provide a foundation for widening the lens across perspectives, scales, places and time and proposes four research priorities organized around these lenses.

title: Slow Violence, Suspended Justice: Speculative Futures after the Baghjan Blowout
summary: What are the temporal boundaries of petrochemical catastrophes? How are justice and compensation calculated and contested in their aftermath? And how do speculative finance and ecological harm shape the governance of fossil-fuel extraction?
content: What are the temporal boundaries of petrochemical catastrophes? How are justice and compensation calculated and contested in their aftermath? And how do speculative finance and ecological harm shape the governance of fossil-fuel extraction? This article examines these questions through a joint analysis of differing media formations of the 2020 Baghjan gas blowout in Assam, northeast India: discourse analysis of government reports; intersections of history and temporality; depredations of extraction; and elemental media. The six-month-long leak and fire caused severe ecological damage, displacement, and loss of life. Six years later, affected communities remain in a state of suspension, awaiting final rulings on compensation, while extraction continues. Drawing on fieldwork, interviews, and media analysis, I critique dominant framings of the blowout as a bounded event. I argue that while the disaster has been widely understood through the lens of slow violence, the Baghjan blowout reveals forms of petrochemical harm that are not only temporally delayed but also structurally produced and elementally mediated. Through comparative analysis of three forms of disaster media—(1) a Supreme Court–mandated expert report, (2) Inside the Burning (a corporate documentary by Oil India Limited), and (3) Baghjan Reels (an independent film amplifying community perspectives)—I examine conflicting narratives of harm, accountability, and justice. Bringing theories of expertise from science and technology studies into dialogue with elemental media theory and environmental humanities scholarship on speculation and temporality, I argue that dominant media forms tend to contain petrochemical violence within event-based logics. By contrast, an elemental media approach enables attention to the durational, saturated, and historically embedded nature of extractive catastrophe, foregrounding how land, water, and air act as media that store and transmit toxic residues across time and space. This article situates Baghjan within a longer history of colonial and developmentalist violence, highlighting how both corporate and state narratives foreclose more expansive notions of justice. I propose ecological reparative justice as a relational, long-term framework—intimate, historical, and future oriented—for reckoning with the ongoing afterlives of extractive disaster.

title: Cocoa Root Morphology, Leaf Nutritional Status, and Bean Characteristics under Different Shade Tree Species
summary: Cocoa is known to require shade during its growth phase. This research is a structured comparative field study to evaluate the effect of different shade tree species on cocoa root morphology, leaf nutritional status, and certain bean charac
content: Cocoa is known to require shade during its growth phase. This research is a structured comparative field study to evaluate the effect of different shade tree species on cocoa root morphology, leaf nutritional status, and certain bean characteristics (100-bean dry weight and protein content). The study was conducted on cocoa plants under three species of shade plants and one control without shade, such as Albizia chinensis (sengon), Cocos nucifera (coconut), Cassia spectabilis (ramayana), and without shade. In the research field conditions, the planting ratio is that every 1 shade tree shades 1 cocoa plant sample being evaluated. The parameters observed included total root length at various soil depths, cocoa leaf nutrient content (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, B), dry weight of 100 beans, and protein content of cocoa beans. The results showed that shade tree species significantly influenced the total length of cocoa roots at certain soil depths (0–10 cm and 20–30 cm), and significantly influenced the dry weight of 100 beans and protein content. The C. spectabilis shade tree produced the highest dry weight of 100 beans and the highest protein content under the conditions of this study compared to A. chinensis and C. nucifera. Cocoa grown under C. spectabilis exhibited favorable bean and leaf nutrient characteristics under the conditions of this study. However, a full evaluation of causality requires further research using a multi-site design.

title: Site layout and waste management system design for on-site construction waste sorting: Danish practitioners' insights into challenges, mitigation practices, and future approaches
summary: The unprecedented rate of construction waste and its improper handling pose environmental risks and contribute to project cost overruns. Together with stricter regulatory requirements, tighter certification boundaries, and comprehensive Lif
content: The unprecedented rate of construction waste and its improper handling pose environmental risks and contribute to project cost overruns. Together with stricter regulatory requirements, tighter certification boundaries, and comprehensive Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), this highlights the importance of on-site construction waste sorting (CWS) and systematic documentation. This study investigates challenges, mitigation practices, and future approaches related to CWS focusing on site layout and waste management system design from practitioners’ perspectives under new Danish regulations. A workshop with 25 participants was conducted using a non-probability sampling method, with participants divided into three focus groups, each comprising different stakeholder roles. Statements were first deductively grouped into challenges, existing practices, and future approaches. Subsequently, inductive thematic analysis refined the statements into descriptive sub-themes, resulting in 39 challenges, 17 mitigation practices, and 9 future approaches grouped into categories. Most challenges fell under operational constraints (9), while most mitigation practices related to communication, training, and documentation (7). Future approaches were more evenly distributed, with container design and choice, standardization, and regulatory framework each containing two approaches. Challenge-solution mappings revealed that some challenges are addressed, whereas others rely on normative practices that overlook practical implementation or lack mitigation measures. The interconnected nature of the identified challenges highlights the need for adaptive and combined practices. The findings suggest that current practices require development to bridge the gap between new regulations and practical implementation. Improved CWS can support recycling and reuse, reduce waste transport and treatment emissions (A5), and lower material, landfill, and sorting errors costs.

title: NPSBZn fertilizer rate and variety effects on carrot yield, quality, and soil acidity in the central highlands of Ethiopia: a two-year field trial
summary: Carrot (Daucus carota L.) is a valuable vegetable crop in Ethiopia, yet national average yields remain low due to soil nutrient deficiencies, unbalanced fertilizer use, and limited access to improved varieties. Most existing research is sin
content: Carrot (Daucus carota L.) is a valuable vegetable crop in Ethiopia, yet national average yields remain low due to soil nutrient deficiencies, unbalanced fertilizer use, and limited access to improved varieties. Most existing research is single-season, which limits the robustness of fertilizer recommendations across varying climatic conditions. Additionally, the recently introduced blended NPSBZn fertilizer lacks crop- and site-specific recommendations. To address these gaps, a two-year (2020–2021) field experiment was conducted in the Hadiya Zone, central Ethiopia. Two carrot varieties (Nantes and Haramaya I) were subjected to seven NPSBZn rates (0 to 150 kg ha⁻¹) in a randomized complete block design with three replications. Across both years, Nantes consistently outperformed Haramaya I in stand count, mean root weight, marketable yield, total soluble solids (TSS), and β-carotene content, while Haramaya I produced longer but often cracked roots. Increasing NPSBZn rates from 0 to 150 kg ha⁻¹ steadily improved all yield and quality parameters, with no plateau observed at the highest rate. Marketable yield reached 38.5 t ha⁻¹ in Nantes at 150 kg ha⁻¹, with marginal returns exceeding 1200%. However, soil pH declined from 5.94 to 5.56, indicating progressive acidification likely due to nitrification of ammoniacal nitrogen from urea and NPSBZn fertilizers. We conclude that NPSBZn fertilization at 150 kg ha⁻¹ combined with the Nantes variety is economically viable and agronomically superior in the short term, but integrated soil management including liming or organic amendments is required to mitigate long-term acidification and sustain soil health.

title: Banana fruit with nutritionally significant concentrations of iron and zinc: results from the field evaluation of genetically modified bananas ( Musa spp.) in Australia
summary: Summary Iron deficiency remains a major public health problem in East Africa, where banana is a staple food for > 30 million people. This study investigated whether genetic modification could produce banana fruit containing nutritionally si
content: Summary Iron deficiency remains a major public health problem in East Africa, where banana is a staple food for > 30 million people. This study investigated whether genetic modification could produce banana fruit containing nutritionally significant concentrations of iron while maintaining agronomic performance under field conditions. Six transgenes associated with iron homeostasis were expressed singly or in combination in Cavendish and Lady Finger bananas. In total, 450 genetically modified plants were field evaluated in Australia and fruit mineral concentrations assessed in the first planting crop. Elevated fruit iron and zinc concentrations, reaching 45.5 and 51.9 mg kg −1 dry weight, respectively, were associated with increased nicotianamine (NA) accumulation following expression of OsNAS . Iron concentrations sufficient to meet 50% of the estimated average requirement for children were achieved in 28 lines, with elevated NA suggesting improved iron bioavailability. Increased mineral accumulation negatively correlated with yield; however, this effect was partly mitigated by co‐expression of OsVIT1 . Early indicators of yield penalty included low corm iron, high leaf zinc concentrations and reduced photosynthetic efficiency. These findings demonstrate the potential of using genetic modification for the mineral biofortification of bananas in East Africa while highlighting factors that may assist in the early identification of high‐performing biofortified lines.

title: An enforcement pyramid for greenhouse gas emissions trading systems
source: Review of European Comparative & International Environmental Law
summary: Abstract Enforcement is crucial for ensuring compliance by regulated entities in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions trading systems (ETSs). This article identifies potential non‐compliance and enforcement issues behind officially reported high
content: Abstract Enforcement is crucial for ensuring compliance by regulated entities in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions trading systems (ETSs). This article identifies potential non‐compliance and enforcement issues behind officially reported high compliance rates, emphasising the need to complement existing ETS enforcement strategies to enhance their effectiveness. These issues encompass the Harrington paradox in ETSs, reported quantity‐based compliance rates (which fail to reflect the number of non‐compliant entities), potential ‘black figures’ for unreported GHG emissions and potentially weak implementation of enforcement regimes. Drawing on responsive regulation, this article proposes an ETS enforcement pyramid in which regulatory agencies can adjust enforcement tools based on entities' various, changing motivations and actions. It also highlights that the enforcement regimes of the EU ETS and China's national ETS share certain features of this enforcement pyramid. The reasons why these ETSs do not fully use the pyramid model may reveal limitations in the model. These limitations include relatively high administrative costs associated with the enforcement pyramid, information problems, difficulties in shifting between cooperation and deterrence, potential waste when entities are unresponsive and issues related to regulatory capture, proportionality, equality and consistency.

title: Integrating recycled concrete carbonation and calciner electrification for low‐carbon cement: Techno‐economic assessment
summary: Abstract This study evaluates the techno‐economic feasibility of integrating a recycled concrete fines (RCF) wet carbonation process into an electrified‐calciner cement plant focusing on energy consumption, CO 2 avoidance, and cost implicat
content: Abstract This study evaluates the techno‐economic feasibility of integrating a recycled concrete fines (RCF) wet carbonation process into an electrified‐calciner cement plant focusing on energy consumption, CO 2 avoidance, and cost implications at an industrial scale. The proposed system is compared with a stand‐alone electrified calciner, an electrified‐calciner plant using non‐carbonated RCF directly in the cement blend, and an electrified‐calciner plant equipped with monoethanolamine (MEA)‐based capture. Results show that the RCF carbonation process is energy‐intensive (3.35 MJ el /kg) and provides limited decarbonization compared to MEA capture. Under the European energy mix, the CO 2 avoidance rate reaches 61.7%, only slightly higher than calciner electrification alone and largely driven by clinker substitution rather than by CO 2 uptake during carbonation. Economically, the increased cement production and lower capital expenses associated with carbonation result in a modest improvement in CO 2 avoidance cost (200.7 €/t) compared to the MEA‐based capture option (217.4 €/t).

title: RECYCLING HYDROALCOHOLIC WASTE AS A LOW-COST AND SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT STRATEGY
summary: Laboratory routines in Botany and related fields generate substantial volumes of hydroalcoholic waste, which is frequently thrown away despite its potential for recovery. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a low-cost distillation appa
content: Laboratory routines in Botany and related fields generate substantial volumes of hydroalcoholic waste, which is frequently thrown away despite its potential for recovery. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a low-cost distillation apparatus constructed from readily available materials for recycling such residues in university laboratories. Hydroalcoholic waste collected from four Botany laboratories was homogenized and subjected to simple distillation, followed by adsorption with activated carbon and filtration. From 1500 mL of waste (~70 °GL), 1100 mL of ethanol at a volume-weighted concentration of 73.6 °GL were recovered. After dilution to 70 °GL for comparison with commercial ethanol, the final volume corresponded to 1156 mL. The mean electrical energy cost per distillation run was R$ 1.68, resulting in an estimated production cost of R$ 1.45 per liter of 70% ethanol. This value represents an approximate 85% reduction relative to the average market price, as the average market price of 1 L of 70% ethanol was R$ 9.95. The proposed protocol demonstrates technical feasibility and economic viability while reducing the volume of hazardous liquid waste generated in teaching and research laboratories. By integrating accessible materials and fundamental physicochemical principles, the method offers a practical and sustainable alternative for decentralized laboratory waste management in public institutions.

title: Public Priorities Between Worker Protection and Renewable Power in the AI Transition: Evidence From a Novel Randomized Survey Experiment
summary: ABSTRACT The development of artificial intelligence (AI) creates simultaneous fiscal pressures on welfare provision and energy infrastructure, requiring governments to support workers exposed to technological displacement while also financi
content: ABSTRACT The development of artificial intelligence (AI) creates simultaneous fiscal pressures on welfare provision and energy infrastructure, requiring governments to support workers exposed to technological displacement while also financing the low‐carbon energy generation needed by expanding data‐centre systems. This article investigates how citizens allocate priority between the social policy and energy demands generated by AI, and the political conflicts that may arise around it, using a survey experiment fielded in 2025 in six European countries (France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Spain and the United Kingdom). Findings show that European public opinion favours an equal allocation of resources between social protection for workers negatively affected by AI and investments in renewable energy for data centres. Although economic insecurity raises support for welfare spending, partisan identity drives the greatest divide: Voters of all mainstream parties favour investment in renewable energy, whereas only radical left and radical right voters prefer an even allocation of resources between the two policy domains. Variation in the type of social policy proposed—income support or training—yields only a weak and blurred effect on public preferences.

title: Are the Hedges of Funds Green?
source: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
summary: Abstract Over the past decade, hedge funds have increasingly embraced green investing. We develop a novel return-based measure of fund greenness and find that greener funds earn higher average returns, consistent with capturing a positive g
content: Abstract Over the past decade, hedge funds have increasingly embraced green investing. We develop a novel return-based measure of fund greenness and find that greener funds earn higher average returns, consistent with capturing a positive green premium, and are associated with lower risks, especially during adverse periods. We further show that performance gains are greatest among directional funds, whereas risk reduction is most pronounced among nondirectional funds. We also provide evidence that managers of these funds exhibit superior green investment skills through green stock selection and green factor timing. Finally, investors reward greener hedge funds only when they demonstrate strong performance.

title: Exploring the sustainable scaling of AI dilemma: a projective study of corporations’ AI environmental impacts
summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), raises environmental concerns extending beyond greenhouse gas emissions. Limited transparency from major providers hinders companies’ ability to ev
content: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), raises environmental concerns extending beyond greenhouse gas emissions. Limited transparency from major providers hinders companies’ ability to evaluate their AI-related environmental impacts and achieve their net-zero targets. This paper proposes a methodology to estimate the environmental impact of a company’s AI portfolio, delivering actionable insights without requiring deep AI or Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA) expertise. Using a modeling approach that incorporates increased AI usage, hardware efficiency, and electricity mix changes aligned with IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) scenarios, we forecast AI impacts through 2030. Under a high adoption scenario, driven by complex generative AI models and frameworks, AI electricity consumption could rise by a factor of 24.4. Mitigating this impact by 2030 demands coordinated efforts across the AI value chain. Isolated measures like hardware or model efficiency alone are insufficient. We call for standardized environmental assessment frameworks, increased transparency, and a “Return on Environment” metric to align AI development with sustainability goals.

title: Impact of women’s use of digital finance on household consumption expenditure in India: a propensity score matching approach
summary: Consumption is a strong factor driving India's economic growth. The emergence of digital services has transformed individuals' transaction behavior. Among them, its impact on women's consumption behavior is particularly significant. This pa
content: Consumption is a strong factor driving India's economic growth. The emergence of digital services has transformed individuals' transaction behavior. Among them, its impact on women's consumption behavior is particularly significant. This paper examines the impact of digital financial services adoption on women's household expenditure behavior. The analysis focuses on four categories of household expenditures: necessities, homegrown products, durable goods and non-durable goods. Using the 2019 All India Debt and Investment Survey (AIDIS), the study employs the propensity score matching estimator to account for the selection bias associated with adopting digital financial services. The empirical results suggest that women who access to digital financial services exhibit a 42 percentage points higher monthly per capita consumption expenditure in a household than those who do not use. The robustness of result is shown by applying different matching methods with sensitivity analysis. The study suggests that there is a need to increase supply-side efforts and reduce societal and cultural barriers prevalent in Indian households, particularly to provide specialized support for poor, rural, and less-educated women. Our study addresses Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 3 and 5.

title: Rule-Based Delegation or Reward-Based Contracting? Central-Local Governance of China’s CCER Program
summary: Abstract The 2024 relaunch of China’s Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) program creates a dual-track carbon market, posing a key governance dilemma: how should the central government set the CCER offset rate when local governments possess
content: Abstract The 2024 relaunch of China’s Certified Emission Reduction (CCER) program creates a dual-track carbon market, posing a key governance dilemma: how should the central government set the CCER offset rate when local governments possess private information on emissions but hold divergent policy goals? We model this challenge using a principal-agent framework featuring the central government, local governments, as well as abatement firms and CCER suppliers. Our core contribution is to derive and unify the optimal delegation mechanisms for two distinct institutional settings: “Greenfield” regions without policy history and “Brownfield” regions with established path dependence. We find that local governments’ “status quo veto power”, acquired from historical practice, drives a governance shift from ex-ante control (rules) to ex-post incentives (rewards). For Greenfield regions, the optimal policy is partial discretion with a cap , theoretically justifying China's national 5% limit. For Brownfield regions, this veto power necessitates a menu of contracts with financial rewards to manage information rents, explaining why some pilot regions maintain their original, higher standards. Our analysis also confirms the “double-edged sword” effect of CCERs, which lower costs but can dilute the carbon market's environmental effect by crowding out firms' internal abatement efforts. The optimal offset rate is shown to be sensitive to key economic and policy parameters.

title: Moving the Goalposts: The Changing Objectives of Industrial Policy
summary: ABSTRACT This paper relies on a novel dataset of more than 31,000 industrial policies in around 150 economies over the period 2009–2022 to codify and examine the stated objectives and design characteristics of these policies. Using large‐sc
content: ABSTRACT This paper relies on a novel dataset of more than 31,000 industrial policies in around 150 economies over the period 2009–2022 to codify and examine the stated objectives and design characteristics of these policies. Using large‐scale machine learning methods applied to policy texts, we systematically classify policy objectives at a global level and document several new stylised facts. We find that industrial policies increasingly pursue multiple objectives, often ones that may be hard to reconcile. In a two‐way fixed effects framework, we show that industrial policies with environmental objectives are more common in Western economies while secure supply objectives are more common in economies geopolitically aligned with China. The majority of industrial policies exhibit features that may make them prone to capture by special interests: they discriminate against foreigners, are firm‐specific and lack ‘sunset clauses’. Industrial policies which reduce firms' costs (such as subsidies, as opposed to taxes) have become more common over time, in particular in rival geopolitical blocs. These features of industrial policies highlight the importance and challenges of evaluating their value‐for‐money, which, in turn, requires clear identification of the primary objective of each policy.

title: Range-based finishing enhances omega-3 fatty acids and forage-derived metabolites in bison meat across a seven-treatment comparison
source: Journal of Animal Science and Biotechnology/Journal of animal science and biotechnology
summary: BACKGROUND: Finishing practices influence the biochemical composition of bison (Bison bison) meat, with potential implications for animal health and human nutrition. This study evaluated seven representative finishing systems spanning a ran
