content: BACKGROUND: Finishing practices influence the biochemical composition of bison (Bison bison) meat, with potential implications for animal health and human nutrition. This study evaluated seven representative finishing systems spanning a range of extensive and intensive production systems, with additional contrasts in forage diversity, corn supplementation, and stocking density to determine their effects on the fatty acid and phytonutrient profiles of bison striploins (M. longissimus lumborum). Treatments included range-finished bison grazing either diverse native pastures (~200 plant species) or lower-diversity pastures (~90 plant species), with or without corn supplementation, as well as pen-finished bison managed under varying feed formulations and stocking densities, including a conventional total mixed ration (TMR) group. Fatty acids were analyzed by gas chromatography-flame ionization detection (GC-FID), and targeted metabolomic profiling of phytonutrient-derived metabolites was performed using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). RESULTS: Range-finished bison exhibited higher concentrations of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA; C18:3n-3; P < 0.0001), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA; C22:5n-3; P < 0.0001), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; C22:6n-3; P < 0.0001), and lower n-6:n-3 ratios (2.8-3.6) than pen-finished bison (5.0-7.3; P < 0.0001). Metabolomic profiling revealed enrichment of hippuric acid, catechol, and shikimic acid (candidate biomarkers associated with forage intake and polyphenolic metabolism) in range-finished systems, whereas 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)lactic acid, a potential grain-associated metabolite, was higher in pen-finished bison than in the unsupplemented range-finished systems (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Range-finished systems enhanced omega-3 fatty acid and phytonutrient-related metabolite profiles, whereas the conventional TMR feedlot treatment yielded the lowest levels and the free-choice corn-and-hay pen system yielded an intermediate profile. Overall, the clearest nutritional contrast was between range-finished and pen-finished systems, whereas differences attributable to forage diversity or stocking density were comparatively modest. These findings indicate that finishing system strongly influences the biochemical composition of bison meat, although comparisons involving the conventional TMR feedlot treatment should be interpreted cautiously because that group originated from a separate breeding herd.

title: Planning operational costs and CO2 emissions of municipal solid waste collection: A case study in Italy
summary: This study aimed to evaluate and compare the environmental and economic performance of street-bin and door-to-door waste collection systems under different territorial conditions using field-derived data in a context-sensitive modelling fra
content: This study aimed to evaluate and compare the environmental and economic performance of street-bin and door-to-door waste collection systems under different territorial conditions using field-derived data in a context-sensitive modelling framework. A field campaign in central Tuscany (Italy) monitored 238 collection routes operated with different vehicle types and fuels. Measured total fuel consumption was used to derive collection-phase consumption and estimate associated CO 2 emissions. These data were integrated into a predictive model applied to 116 collection areas, using linear population density (LPD) and per capita waste generation as territorial variables. Monitoring results showed that collection-phase fuel consumption and CO 2 emissions were systematically higher than standard transport inventory values across the six vehicle categories considered, with heavy-duty vehicles showing values two to three times higher. Modelling results revealed an inverse relationship between LPD and both operational costs and CO 2 emissions per tonne of collected waste. Under study-area reference conditions, street-bin collection became more carbon-efficient above 76 inhabitants · k m ⁻ 1 , with CO 2 emissions up to 17% lower than door-to-door, whereas door-to-door was economically competitive only below 8 inhabitants · k m ⁻ 1 . Sensitivity analyses placed the environmental and economic crossovers at 53–100 inhabitants · k m ⁻ 1 and 4–12 inhabitants · k m ⁻ 1 , respectively, without altering the overall LPD-dependent performance trends. Updated 2026 fuel prices slightly shifted the reference economic crossover to 9 inhabitants · k m ⁻ 1 and widened the sensitivity range to 4–14 inhabitants · k m ⁻ 1 . Overall, LPD emerged as a key spatial driver of collection-system performance, highlighting the importance of considering local territorial conditions when planning collection strategies to reduce operational costs and carbon emissions.

title: Electro-isomerization of lactose into lactulose with simultaneous purification from coloring molecules (color) in situ of the electro-activation reactor: comparative study between anion exchange resin and activated carbon
summary: This study investigated an in situ purification as a color-removal strategy by simultaneous electro-activation and decolorization during lactose isomerization into lactulose. Anion-exchange resin and granular activated carbon (AC) were inco
content: This study investigated an in situ purification as a color-removal strategy by simultaneous electro-activation and decolorization during lactose isomerization into lactulose. Anion-exchange resin and granular activated carbon (AC) were incorporated directly into the cathodic compartment during electro-activation of 5–30% (w/v) lactose solutions at 600 mA current intensity for 60 min, followed by a 10 h relaxation period. Decolorization performance was monitored using UV–Vis absorbance at 296 and 420 nm, corresponding to low-molecular-weight degradation products and high-molecular-weight colored compounds, respectively. The anion-exchange resin exhibited markedly superior decolorization efficiency compared with AC. At 7.5% resin loading, absorbance at 296 nm decreased by 80.25% and 78.13% for 5% and 10% lactose solutions, respectively, while at 420 nm it ranged from 88.43% to 93.46% across the studied lactose concentrations. Resin-based purification eliminated color development during relaxation, indicating its ability to limit both already formed coloring compounds and reactive color precursors. Kinetic analysis showed that second-order behavior best described the resin-mediated decolorization, particularly during relaxation, with R² values of 0.94 and 0.97 at 296 and 420 nm, respectively. Isotherm analysis indicated a Langmuir-type adsorption at 296 nm and Freundlich-type adsorption at 420 nm, suggesting different interaction mechanisms for the low and high-molecular-weight coloring compounds. HPLC analysis confirmed that the in situ process affected sugar profile in a concentration-dependent manner. The anion-exchange resin provided an effective integrated purification process to reduce the color intensity of electro-activated lactose solution in lactulose production.

title: Investigating Autonomous Vehicle Usage Intentions with a Technology Acceptance Model: The Türkiye Example
summary: Autonomous vehicles are expected to support safer, more efficient, and potentially more sustainable mobility systems, yet their widespread adoption depends strongly on user acceptance. This study examines how perceived risk, perceived ease
content: Autonomous vehicles are expected to support safer, more efficient, and potentially more sustainable mobility systems, yet their widespread adoption depends strongly on user acceptance. This study examines how perceived risk, perceived ease of use, perceived value, perceived safety, and subjective norms influence intention to use autonomous vehicles in Türkiye. Data were collected from 280 participants through an online survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The results show that perceived risk negatively affects intention to use (β = −0.085, p = 0.028), whereas perceived ease of use (β = 0.103, p = 0.045), perceived value (β = 0.162, p = 0.012), perceived safety (β = 0.327, p < 0.001), and subjective norms (β = 0.300, p < 0.001) have positive and statistically significant effects. The model explains 66.5% of the variance in intention to use (R2 = 0.665). Perceived safety and subjective norms emerge as the strongest positive predictors, indicating that safety perceptions and social influence are central to adoption. These findings provide empirical evidence from Türkiye and offer implications for manufacturers, mobility service providers, and policymakers seeking to facilitate the transition toward intelligent and sustainable mobility systems.

title: Big Data and Predictive Analytics Capability and Triple Bottom Line Sustainability Performance: A Resource‐Based Perspective From BRICS Nations
summary: ABSTRACT This study aims to investigate the relationship between big data and predictive analytics (BDPA) capability and triple bottom line (TBL) sustainability performance in BRICS manufacturing firms. Grounded in the resource‐based view (
content: ABSTRACT This study aims to investigate the relationship between big data and predictive analytics (BDPA) capability and triple bottom line (TBL) sustainability performance in BRICS manufacturing firms. Grounded in the resource‐based view (RBV), we conceptualise BDPA capability as a third‐order hierarchical construct comprising tangible resources (data infrastructure and technology), intangible resources (organisational culture, organisational learning and data‐driven culture) and human‐related skills (technical skills and management skills). Survey data have been used from 304 IT and analytics professionals representing different organisations across BRICS economies and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM) with 5000 bootstrap samples; we test six hypotheses examining both the resource‐capability link and the capability‐performance link. Results reveal that all three resource categories significantly contribute to BDPA capability, with human‐related skills exerting the strongest influence. BDPA capability, in turn, significantly predicts environmental performance, social performance and economic performance, explaining 40%, 50% and 55% of variance, respectively. The study contributes to the literature by providing an empirically validated, multi‐level resource‐capability‐performance framework for analytics‐driven sustainability in emerging economies.

title: Landfill methane recovery and use under deep uncertainty: a satelliteconstrained Monte Carlo decision model for the Norte III landfill, Buenos Aires
summary: Very large landfills are major methane sources, but site decisions rarely join operator-reported capture, independent emission estimates and the economics of competing gas uses. We built a Latin-hypercube Monte Carlo decision model (300,000
content: Very large landfills are major methane sources, but site decisions rarely join operator-reported capture, independent emission estimates and the economics of competing gas uses. We built a Latin-hypercube Monte Carlo decision model (300,000 draws, 78 inputs) of landfill-gas generation, collection, surface emission, oxidation, selective covers, biomethane upgrading, additional power generation and photovoltaics, and applied it to the Norte III landfill in Buenos Aires. A bottom-up generation prior is constrained by satellite emission estimates at their own date (2022) and carried to 2025–26. The inferred collection efficiency, 0.13 (0.09 to 0.19) in 2022 and 0.14 (0.10 to 0.21) in 2025–26 (median, 90% interval), follows from the emission, oxidation and reported capture, is conditional on the data and not a measurement, and increases to 0.24 (0.15 to 0.37) with an independent 2025 observation that the model overpredicts by a factor of 3.5. Under no-credit conditions none of eight integrated scenarios has a positive median net present value; wellfield optimization with a selective cover abates methane at a median US$3.6 per tCO2e. Additional engines are profitable in 99% of draws that have surplus gas, but in 69% of all operating states after the planned expansion; biomethane needs US$0.46 per Nm3 (US$14 per MMBtu). A cover helps only if the captured share of blocked gas exceeds an analytic break-even (median 0.14). Conclusions hold under alternative generation histories, satellite scaling and dated Argentine benchmarks.

title: Performance, emissions, and predictive modelling of a CI-ICE operating in LPG–diesel dual-fuel mode
summary: This study presents an experimental assessment of a compression-ignition internal combustion engine (CI-ICE) operating in dual-fuel mode with diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), without fuel preheating or combustion enhancers. The obj
content: This study presents an experimental assessment of a compression-ignition internal combustion engine (CI-ICE) operating in dual-fuel mode with diesel and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), without fuel preheating or combustion enhancers. The objective is to evaluate the effect of LPG substitution on engine performance, emissions, and operational fuel costs under electric power generation conditions. Additionally, an artificial neural network (ANN) was developed using TensorFlow and Keras to capture relationships among key process variables at high altitudes; the model was trained on experimental data from the test campaign. Tests were conducted at several engine load conditions, comparing diesel operation with LPG–diesel dual-fuel blends, where diesel was partially substituted by LPG at three mass flow rates (0.18, 0.36, and 0.54 kg/h). Dual-fuel operation increased brake thermal efficiency by up to 10%, reaching 29.4% at 0.54 kg/h, while reducing brake specific fuel consumption. Specific emissions of CO and HC decreased significantly at medium and high loads, whereas NOx increased at full load. Fuel cost reductions reached 73% at full load. The ANN models achieved high predictive accuracy (R²>0.95), confirming their robustness for predicting CI-ICE performance in LPG–diesel dual-fuel mode. Therefore, ANN models provide a reliable tool for reducing experimental testing campaigns and associated operational and research costs. Finally, the findings confirm the technical feasibility of operating a CI-ICE in LPG–diesel dual-fuel mode with minimal intake manifold modifications. This approach maintains CI-ICE operational stability and power output while offering environmental and economic benefits, reinforcing its applicability for electricity generation systems.

title: Functional edible films and coatings enriched with flower extracts: advances in bioactivity and food preservation
summary: Although flower-derived bioactive compounds have gained attention as potential functional additives in edible packaging materials, no recent review has critically focused on their extraction strategies, interactions with film-forming biopol
content: Although flower-derived bioactive compounds have gained attention as potential functional additives in edible packaging materials, no recent review has critically focused on their extraction strategies, interactions with film-forming biopolymers, and applications in food preservation. This review critically discusses recent research on the extraction, characterization, and application of important flower-derived bioactive compounds, including anthocyanins, flavonoids, phenolic acids, carotenoids, and essential oils, in active and intelligent edible packaging. Contemporary extraction techniques, such as ultrasound-assisted extraction, microwave-assisted extraction, deep eutectic solvents, and supercritical fluid CO 2 , provide higher yields (up to ~14 mg/g phenolics and over 70% pigment recovery) compared to traditional techniques. Nevertheless, each method has specific advantages and drawbacks. These flower-derived bioactive compounds modify the mechanical behavior and physicochemical characteristics of natural polymer-based packaging matrices, including starch, pectin, chitosan, and protein systems, mainly through hydrogen bonding and polyphenol–matrix interactions. Active films show improved oxidative stability. Antioxidant activity may increase two fold to tenfold, while antimicrobial action can reduce microbial load by approximately 1–3 log CFU/g. Moreover, the mechanical response to these compounds depends on extract–matrix compatibility, with phenolic compounds acting either as plasticizing or strengthening components depending on the polymer system and concentration. Anthocyanin-rich flower extracts from hibiscus and butterfly pea provide pH-responsive color-changing behavior, making these intelligent packaging systems capable of tracking food spoilage. Food applications show shelf-life extension of 5–21 days in fruits, vegetables, and meat systems, mainly through antioxidant activity, antimicrobial effects, delayed oxidative deterioration, reduced microbial growth, and improved moisture regulation. In contrast, biodegradability and renewable biopolymer use should be viewed as sustainability advantages rather than direct preservation mechanisms. However, wider application of flower-extract-based edible films still requires further validation of scale-up feasibility, food-contact regulatory approval, migration behavior, sensory acceptability, and safety of released bioactive compounds.

title: Natural hydrogen in the Middle East and North Africa: Geological prospectivity, global analogues, and a play-based exploration roadmap
summary: Natural hydrogen, free molecular H 2 generated by water-rock reaction and radioactive decay, has moved from curiosity to exploration target since production began at Bourakébougou, Mali. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) hosts several
content: Natural hydrogen, free molecular H 2 generated by water-rock reaction and radioactive decay, has moved from curiosity to exploration target since production began at Bourakébougou, Mali. The Middle East and North Africa (MENA) hosts several settings that generate H 2 elsewhere, yet has attracted little dedicated study. This review assesses the region as eleven plays from a documented literature search, each with a chance of detectable surface expression and of a preserved accumulation, given as screening estimates. The Egyptian case rests on the base rate: no hydrogen measurement has been published from an Egyptian ophiolite, so its chance, about 0.9 (80 % interval 0.8–0.9), comes from the record of surveyed ultramafic massifs, 20 of 21 positive where the outcome is clear, audited against primary texts where obtainable. That base rate, 0.95, is likely biased upward; counting the indeterminate massifs as negative gives 0.69. On the central inputs no single soil-gas survey reverses a decision: a negative Egyptian survey would leave the play at about 0.7, above the assumed threshold of one half. The decisive uncertainty is therefore the base rate, and reducing it is the research priority. Soil-gas surveys of the Egyptian and Saudi ophiolites and a re-screening of legacy mud-gas records are tied on expected information per working day at stated efforts. On central grades no play reaches a median chance of a preserved accumulation of 0.1; trap and preservation are unmeasured everywhere. Existing petroleum and mining law can license the surveys where an instrument could be identified.

title: A Contrastive Analysis of Discursive Representations of EVs in Newspaper Coverage across Four Countries
summary: Driven by rapid technological innovation and industrial transformation, Electric Vehicles (EVs) have become the new center of the global automotive industry. Different media interpret the EV transition from different perspectives. This stud
content: Driven by rapid technological innovation and industrial transformation, Electric Vehicles (EVs) have become the new center of the global automotive industry. Different media interpret the EV transition from different perspectives. This study combines corpus linguistics and Fairclough’s three-dimensional model to systematically analyze the reports on electric vehicles from People’s Daily from China, The New York Times from the United States, Süddeutsche Zeitung from Germany, and The Straits Times from Singapore. These newspapers are located in countries that play different roles in the transformation of global electric vehicles. The study found that although corporate and government sources dominate in the reports of the four newspapers, there are significant differences in the semantic classification of electric vehicles. The institutional positioning, information acquisition habits and domestic industrial environment of each newspaper all affect the content of its reports, thus shaping a specific cognition of electric vehicle transformation for readers. This study not only provides an empirical paradigm of cross-language and cross-country linguistic discourse analysis for the electronic entertainment industry in international communication, but also helps the industry to understand the global discourse ecosystem more deeply, and provides a practical reference for multinational enterprises to overcome cultural barriers and adapt to narrative differences between different markets.

title: Making water ecosystem services count: a purpose-driven systematic literature review of economic valuation
summary: This systematic literature review examines the economic valuation of water ecosystem services (WES) through a purpose-driven perspective, relating valuation methods and value concepts to the stated purposes for which monetary evidence is pr
content: This systematic literature review examines the economic valuation of water ecosystem services (WES) through a purpose-driven perspective, relating valuation methods and value concepts to the stated purposes for which monetary evidence is produced. A total of 137 peer-reviewed studies were analyzed, categorized by valuation method, geographic distribution, ecosystem type, value concept, and policy purpose. The review reveals a strong concentration of research in North America and Asia, while freshwater ecosystems represent the main empirical focus of WES valuation. Recurring gaps include limited treatment of ecosystem service bundles, infrequent use of biophysical information within monetary estimation and causal policy-evaluation designs, underrepresentation of option and non-use values, and few studies directed toward ecosystem or natural capital accounting. The review further shows that valuation methods are not used uniformly across purposes: planning-oriented studies draw on a broad mix of approaches, ex-ante appraisal relies mainly on stated preference methods, and accounting-oriented applications primarily use cost- and market-based methods. By relating valuation choices to their intended use, the review provides a basis for interpreting WES monetary evidence according to whether the objective is strategic planning, policy appraisal, or ecosystem accounting.

title: Terbium-Doped Graphene Quantum Dots: A Highly Efficient and Selective Fluorescent Nanoprobe for Vanillin Detection
summary: Abstract Vanillin, an extensively used flavoring compound in our daily life, may lead to health problems when overused, adulterated, or poorly controlled in commercial settings, necessitating the development of sensitive and rapid detection
content: Abstract Vanillin, an extensively used flavoring compound in our daily life, may lead to health problems when overused, adulterated, or poorly controlled in commercial settings, necessitating the development of sensitive and rapid detection techniques. In this work, terbium-doped graphene quantum dots (Tb-GQD) were synthesized using carbonization and chemical conjugation methods for developing an efficient fluorescent probe for vanillin detection. The structural and optical characteristics of Tb-GQD confirm that terbium is doped in GQDs, without disturbing the sp2 graphitic core of GQD, and efficient energy transfer from GQD to Tb3+ was observed from the photoluminescence emission studies. Upon addition of vanillin to Tb-GQD, a decrease in fluorescence emission intensity and a change in lifetime were observed, suggesting a dynamic, photoinduced electron transfer mechanism. The Tb-GQD shows a linear detection range of 0.2–85 μM with a detection limit of 13.2 nM. The synthesized fluorescent probe shows excellent selectivity, and was implemented in real-sample analysis with a good recovery range of 96.4–100.06% and an RSD below 3.6%. These findings show that Tb-GQD will serve as an efficient platform for detecting vanillin.

title: Multi-decadal maize yield gains at varying nitrogen rates have lowered grain-specific nutrient concentrations but improved nutrient harvest indices
summary: Decades of maize ( Zea mays L.) improvement have steadily increased plant productivity across varying nitrogen (N) regimes, yet how these gains have influenced grain and stover macro- and micronutrient stoichiometry remains poorly understoo
content: Decades of maize ( Zea mays L.) improvement have steadily increased plant productivity across varying nitrogen (N) regimes, yet how these gains have influenced grain and stover macro- and micronutrient stoichiometry remains poorly understood. We evaluated 38 elite Bayer commercial hybrids released between 1983 and 2020 in four field experiments conducted in Illinois and Indiana, USA, during 2021–2022 under contrasting N supply. Best linear unbiased predictors (BLUPs) of grain yield regressed against year of hybrid release estimated annual yield genetic gains (GG) of 77 and 86 kg ha −1 yr −1 under Low-N (45 kg N ha −1 ) and High-N (202 or 246 kg N ha −1 ) conditions, respectively. Under Low-N, grain N concentration declined more than stover N concentration from the oldest to the newest hybrids (11.3% vs. 2.6%), whereas both declined by comparable magnitudes under High-N (7.0% and 7.8%, respectively). Ratios of macro- and micronutrients to grain N increased with year of release under Low-N, particularly in modern hybrids, suggesting shifts in grain nutrient stoichiometry associated with long-term selection. Yield gains were accompanied by concurrent shifts in grain composition, including increased starch, reduced N, and stable oil concentrations. Increased starch concentration was associated with lower grain K and S concentrations but higher concentrations of Ca and some micronutrients (e.g., Cu). The relationship between nitrogen harvest Index (NHI) and nutrient harvest indices (NutHI) was positive for all nutrients studied, with stronger gains under Low-N than High-N, and showed no statistical evidence of plateauing. These results suggest that, within the range of hybrids evaluated, nutrient partitioning into grain has not yet approached a physiological ceiling, particularly under limited-N conditions, and that long-term maize improvement has been associated with changes in whole-plant uptake and grain allocation of multiple macro- and micronutrients.

title: Advances in Wire-Laser Metal Deposition: Bimetallic Fabrication, Defect Mitigation, and Future Directions
source: Lasers in Manufacturing and Materials Processing
summary: Abstract Wire-Laser Metal Deposition (W-LMD) is a transformative additive manufacturing technology that utilizes a laser heat source to melt metallic wire feedstock for the high-efficiency fabrication of large-scale, near-net-shape componen
content: Abstract Wire-Laser Metal Deposition (W-LMD) is a transformative additive manufacturing technology that utilizes a laser heat source to melt metallic wire feedstock for the high-efficiency fabrication of large-scale, near-net-shape components. The technology is distinguished from other manufacturing processes due to its high material utilization efficiency and superior safety compared to metal powder-based systems. W-LMD systems are composed of a focused laser, a wire feeder mechanism, a multi-degree of freedom motion system, cooling system, and a shielding gas supply to prevent oxidation. Deviation in process parameters of the system components can lead to external defects such as stubbing (insufficient melting) and dripping (melting above the melt pool), or other forms of internal defects such as porosities. A key feature of W-LMD systems is their capability of fabricating bimetallic structures. This paper reviews key studies on W-LMD systems and their advancements in bimetallic fabrication. The review highlights the current gaps and required research work in the field for bimetallic W-LMD manufacturing and its significance.

title: Fuzzy–AI digital twins for sustainable, resilient food supply chains
source: International Journal of Information Management Data Insights
summary: This study proposes a prescriptive Fuzzy–AI Digital Twin framework for food supply chains operating under deep uncertainty. The digital twin streams real-time operational data from production, cold storage, transport, and retail into a lear
content: This study proposes a prescriptive Fuzzy–AI Digital Twin framework for food supply chains operating under deep uncertainty. The digital twin streams real-time operational data from production, cold storage, transport, and retail into a learning optimization loop. Uncertainty in demand, lead times, capacities, spoilage, and emissions is modeled using adaptive fuzzy sets, while a deep-learning surrogate accelerates a multi-objective NSGA-II optimizer to co-design decisions across cost, CO₂e, and resilience. In a perishable dairy case, the hybrid approach reduces total cost by 12.2%, lowers emissions by 15.2%, and raises the resilience index by 22.5% relative to the Fuzzy–AI model without Digital Twin integration. The optimizer stabilizes in ∼35 generations, and under severe disruptions the network recovers to 95% capacity in ∼5 h (vs. >10 h traditionally). Conceptually, the framework operationalizes resilience via adaptability (sensing disruptions, simulating alternatives, and reallocating resources in real time) rather than costly redundancy. Managerially, it enables simulate-before-implement orchestration and transparent cost–carbon–resilience trade-offs aligned with Scope-3 reporting. The results indicate that digital twins combined with fuzzy reasoning and learning assisted optimization can deliver simultaneously lower cost, lower emissions, and higher resilience for perishable food chains.

title: Learning-enhanced rolling-horizon optimisation for port-centric freight systems
summary: This paper presents a centralised rolling-horizon framework for dynamic freight matching in port-centric supply chains. Rather than solving one large static assignment, the framework advances through the planning horizon in short steps, spl
content: This paper presents a centralised rolling-horizon framework for dynamic freight matching in port-centric supply chains. Rather than solving one large static assignment, the framework advances through the planning horizon in short steps, splitting the dynamic many-to-many problem over time into a sequence of small per-step assignments. Within each step, a Graph Neural Network makes the real-time match or wait decisions. The Hungarian algorithm then solves that step’s assignment optimally. Vicinity-based consolidation groups nearby movements, with full and empty containers handled jointly. Many-to-many consolidation emerges as trucks are assigned further demands at later steps, and because each step solves only a small assignment, the framework stays tractable and supports scalable coordination under intermodal and operational constraints. Using throughput data from Sydney’s Port Botany, eight scenarios are simulated across fleet compositions and optimisation priorities. Results show clear trade-offs: small-truck-dominant fleets maximise timeliness and demand coverage but raise cost and emissions, whereas large-truck strategies lower cost and carbon intensity at the expense of service levels. Export flows consistently achieve the highest timeliness.

title: Evaluation of recovered Carbon black as a sustainable alternative to commercial Carbon black in solid tyre cushion compounds
summary: Pyrolysis is a sustainable solution for waste tyre (WT) management. Recovered carbon black (rCB), is a second highest by-product of tyre pyrolysis process, contains a high amount of carbon, ash and inorganic impurities. In the present study
content: Pyrolysis is a sustainable solution for waste tyre (WT) management. Recovered carbon black (rCB), is a second highest by-product of tyre pyrolysis process, contains a high amount of carbon, ash and inorganic impurities. In the present study, rCB derived from WTs was upgraded through magnetic separation, ball milling, and purified treating twice with 2M HCl and once with 2M NaOH at 60⁰C for one hour using 2 g/mL rCB: leachate ratio to obtain demineralized rCB(drCB). Both raw rCB and drCB were characterized by particle size analysis, proximate and ultimate analyses, TGA, ICP-OES, FT-IR, XRD, and iodine adsorption. The drCB exhibited a substantial reduction in ash content from 22.20% to 3.42 % (by weight) and an increase in carbon content up to 94.41 % (% wt). The upgraded drCB was subsequently incorporated into solid tyre cushion compounds as a partial replacement for commercial carbon black (CCB, N550) to evaluate industrial feasibility. Physico-mechanical properties of the drCB compound demonstrated improved modulus, tear strength, hardness, and other properties such as tensile strength, rebound resilience within the industrial standard limits. These findings confirm the technical feasibility of rCB as a partial replacement of the filler in industrial solid tyre cushion compounds, supporting circular economy concept in the rubber and tyre industry.

title: Concepts of Machine Learning for Life Sciences
summary: Machine learning touches our lives in quiet and remarkable ways. It helps doctors detect illnesses sooner by recognizing subtle patterns in scans and helping them make sense of medical data with speed, judgment, and care. It helps us care f
content: Machine learning touches our lives in quiet and remarkable ways. It helps doctors detect illnesses sooner by recognizing subtle patterns in scans and helping them make sense of medical data with speed, judgment, and care. It helps us care for our fields and forests by tracking changes that unfold over time. It helps us study the weather with a memory far longer than our own, and notices small signs that equipment may soon need attention. And when we find ourselves in unfamiliar places, it helps us translate words, find our bearings, and discover new corners to explore. And yet, even as it becomes part of daily life, its inner workings can still feel distant when you first encounter them. Concepts of Machine Learning aims to bring it within reach. This book offers a clear and steady introduction to how machines learn from data. It explains how models begin to understand, decide, improve, and sometimes falter. Ideas build gradually, one upon another, supported by real examples and datasets in Python. The focus is insight over jargon, clarity over complexity. As these ideas become familiar, they also hold the promise of supporting the works of scientists, engineers, and students — by opening new pathways of exploration. Inside the Book • How learning algorithms discover patterns • Supervised, unsupervised, and other ways machines learn • Regression, decision trees, neural networks, and more • Working with data and understanding results • Ethics, fairness, and responsible use Warm, practical, and approachable, Concepts of Machine Learning encourages readers to build confidence step by step, to make sense of new ideas in their own time, and to discover how understanding machine learning can enrich the way we work, learn, and see the world.

title: Agroforestry ambitions fifty years after launch of a governance-people-science boundary concept
summary: A novel word connecting agriculture and forestry, agroforestry, originated in 1976 with ambitions for radically better land use. At its 50’th anniversary, we reflect on its use in boundary work interfacing governance, people and science. Ag
content: A novel word connecting agriculture and forestry, agroforestry, originated in 1976 with ambitions for radically better land use. At its 50’th anniversary, we reflect on its use in boundary work interfacing governance, people and science. Agroforestry as applied science started with describing the worlds’ farmed lands with trees’ in their eco-geographical and socio-historical context as plot/farm-level agroforestry (‘AF1’). In the 1990’s, attention shifted to the landscape scale AF2 and to a policy scale AF3. Simultaneously, climate-tree-soil-crop interactions, bio-economic, and social-ecological systems were further analysed. Searching in the Google Scholar database for ‘agroforestry’ we selected a 1007 well-cited publications (1979–2025) corpus with a total of 175,081 citations. These publications included AF1 (64%), AF2 (19%) and AF3(17%) as system scales. Research topics on Knowledge, Telecoupling, (local) Environment, Markets, Identity, and Rights accounted for 28, 25, 20, 10, 10, and 7%, of citations, respectively. The ambitions of ‘Productive AF’, ‘Multifunctional farms’ and ‘Landscape integration’ were linked to 28, 29% and 29% of citations, respectively; the ambitions on ‘Socio-cultural values’ and ‘Societal transformation’ only to 8% and 5%, respectively. Beyond the low-hanging fruit of existing AF farms, a ladder to reach more ambitious goals may inspire renewed forms of AF-boundary work.

title: Operational Integration: Sea-Shore Interactions
summary: The maritime industry is undergoing a profound structural transformation driven by advances in satellite communications, enabling closer integration between autonomous oceangoing vessels and shore-based control centers. This chapter examine
content: The maritime industry is undergoing a profound structural transformation driven by advances in satellite communications, enabling closer integration between autonomous oceangoing vessels and shore-based control centers. This chapter examines the operational integration paradigm and evaluates how low-Earth orbit (LEO) connectivity and real-time data flows are transforming traditionally isolated vessels into fully synchronized extensions of shore-based corporate management systems. The analysis systematically explores this ship–shore integration across three strategic dimensions: economic optimization, environmental sustainability, and social well-being. First, the chapter investigates the transition from manual and model-based decision support systems to artificial intelligence-driven, knowledge-based systems. It demonstrates how voyage optimization algorithms balance complex variables—including fuel consumption, fluctuating freight rates, and weather-dependent routing decisions—to enhance profitability and improve tactical decision-making. Second, the chapter examines how operational integration aligns maritime practices with increasingly stringent global governance frameworks. In particular, it highlights the role of digital monitoring and data-driven compliance systems in meeting environmental regulations such as the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and the European Union Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). Third, the social dimension of sustainability is assessed through an evaluation of the dual impact of high-speed connectivity on seafarers’ well-being, contrasting reductions in social isolation with emerging operational challenges associated with technostress and continuous connectivity. The findings suggest that ship–shore integration extends far beyond immediate operational efficiencies and cost reductions. By transforming raw operational data into actionable strategic capabilities, continuous connectivity is fundamentally reshaping maritime business models and enabling shipping companies to simultaneously enhance environmental compliance, strengthen human capital, and achieve resilient competitive advantages within an increasingly dynamic global supply chain environment.

title: Psilocybin modulates nucleus accumbens activity via astrocytic transcriptional regulation
summary: Psilocybin is a serotonergic hallucinogen that acts primarily through 5-HT₂A receptor signaling, yet the mechanisms by which it regulates mesolimbic inhibitory tone remain poorly understood. Here we investigated how psilocybin and structura
content: Psilocybin is a serotonergic hallucinogen that acts primarily through 5-HT₂A receptor signaling, yet the mechanisms by which it regulates mesolimbic inhibitory tone remain poorly understood. Here we investigated how psilocybin and structurally related synthetic tryptamines modulate inhibitory signaling in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) and whether astrocyte-associated mechanisms contribute to this process. Psilocybin-like tryptamines that generalized to the psilocybin cue increased NAc neuronal activity while reducing extracellular GABA levels, identifying diminished NAc GABAergic tone as a neurochemical correlate of psilocybin-like behavioral responses. Consistent with this interpretation, local pharmacological modulation of NAc GABA receptor signaling altered psilocybin-appropriate responding. We next examined the cellular and molecular basis of this GABAergic regulation. Ex vivo whole-cell recordings revealed that psilocin, the active metabolite of psilocybin, reduced tonic GABA current in NAc medium spiny neurons without affecting miniature inhibitory postsynaptic currents, indicating preferential modulation of tonic rather than miniature synaptic inhibition. Cell-type-specific analyses further showed that psilocybin selectively reduced intracellular GABA levels in astrocytes, but not neurons. Psilocybin increased astrocytic NFATc4 and ALDH5A1 protein expression together with enhanced H3K27 acetylation, and ChIP-qPCR analysis showed increased NFATc4 occupancy at the Aldh5a1 promoter. Consistent with upstream serotonergic signaling, psilocin-induced calcium responses in astrocytes were attenuated by 5-HT₂A receptor antagonism. Together, these findings support a model in which psilocybin modulates mesolimbic inhibitory tone through astrocyte-associated regulation of NAc GABA homeostasis. Our findings further identify astrocytic NFATc4-associated transcriptional regulation as a mechanism linked to ALDH5A1 expression, astrocytic GABA homeostasis and tonic inhibitory regulation in the NAc.

title: THE RETURN OF TERRITORY? STATE, REGIONS AND STRATEGIC GOVERNANCE IN EUROPE AND INDIA - CONVERGING STORIES OF MAHARASHTRA POWER IPOs, LAND TOKENISATION AND AI STACK
summary: India is poised to shift from AI user to AI builder over the next decade with a call for a homegrown AI stack and infrastructure. At Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai on 9 September, it was stated that Year One for building India's own AI
content: India is poised to shift from AI user to AI builder over the next decade with a call for a homegrown AI stack and infrastructure. At Global Fintech Fest 2026 in Mumbai on 9 September, it was stated that Year One for building India's own AI has begun. The country now has its own models, GPUs, and skilled talent. The belief is that in next 10 years India will lead in both adoption and building of AI. The advantage is not only scale but ability to build at cost that works for a large population. The warning is that without a full-stack AI alternative, India risks becoming a digital colony, repeating the pattern of being primarily a consumer of technology. The push for homegrown AI stack is linked to a pitch for an AI stack that Indian enterprises, particularly banks and financial institutions, can control without dependence on few vendors. Organizations need an ecosystem approach to deploy AI safely and at speed in regulated sectors and financial inclusion. At infrastructure layer, call is for India-based AI infrastructure operating with no data retention and outside extraterritorial laws like US Patriot Act. Need is for token factories to work in India under domestic jurisdiction. Dependence on one or two vendors at model layer should be avoided; financial institutions should have choices including homegrown open-weight and custom models. This AI sovereignty debate converges with territorial governance experiment in Maharashtra. Maharashtra is working on India's first legislative and blockchain-based framework for tokenisation of land, announced at same Fest. It is putting in place Maharashtra Digitisation and Exchange of Land Tokenisation Act, with framework developed with SEBI, BSE, NSE, industry and academia. Proposal envisages tokenising 7/12 land records - about 2.5 crore parcels - into tradable digital tokens with fractional ownership and mortgage token, enabling farmers to monetise without selling, reducing litigation where 60% civil cases are land-related, and preventing Benami transactions. Both illustrate return of state not as old licence raj but as strategic platform orchestrator - Law provides trust, DPI provides scale, AI provides intelligence - transforming territory from physical container to tradable trusted digital stack. This paper uses case studies and mixed methodology to examine AI Business and Management, AI Governance, Public Policy and Ethical Implications of AI token factories and Land token factories, arguing India must enforce efficacious solutions to rescue world from growth without workers and avoid deprivation of demographic dividend.

title: SiO2-Crosslinked Molecularly Imprinted Hybrid Nanostructures for Solid-Phase Extraction of Bisphenol A
summary: Abstract Previously, a molecularly imprinted hybrid (MIH) was synthesized by imprinting bisphenol A (BPA) within SiO2-crosslinked poly(styrene-co-methyl methacrylate) nanoframeworks. In this work, its adsorption and solid-phase extraction (
content: Abstract Previously, a molecularly imprinted hybrid (MIH) was synthesized by imprinting bisphenol A (BPA) within SiO2-crosslinked poly(styrene-co-methyl methacrylate) nanoframeworks. In this work, its adsorption and solid-phase extraction (SPE) performance toward BPA in complex matrices was systematically investigated and compared with two commercial sorbents, C18 and SupelMIPBPA. MIH exhibited a high adsorption capacity of 49.5 mg/g with a large Langmuir coefficient (KL = 3.16 × 10−2 L/mg) and high BPA selectivity with factors of 1.53 and 35.4 relative to 2BPF and phenol, respectively. Moreover, it exhibited 12 and 1120 times higher specific adsorption ability than SupelMIPBPA and C18, respectively. The tailored binding sites embedded within the hydrophobic polymeric matrix and stabilized with rigid, hydrophilic SiO2 crosslinks contributed to stable adsorption over pH 2−9 and in the presence of humic acid up to 20 mg/L while enhancing BPA adsorption by 1.5-fold at NaCl concentrations up to 3000 mM. MIH maintained stable adsorption over 11 regeneration cycles across synthesis batches and retained its adsorption capacity after more than six months of storage. When applied to SPE, the optimized MIH-SPE method effectively enriched BPA while reducing matrix interference, achieving enrichment factors of 52.0−60.0. Coupled with HPLC-photodiode array detection, the method achieved matrix-specific MDLs of 1.3 ng/mL in DI water and 0.2−3.1 ng/mL in environmental waters. Recoveries of 88.8−118.7% and RSDs of 0.2−9.6% demonstrated satisfactory accuracy and precision across the tested water matrices. In contrast, C18- and SupelMIPBPA-based SPE exhibited inferior performance due to limited adsorption capacity or less efficient analyte elution.

title: Valorization of Rice Husk: Simultaneous Extraction of High-Purity Lignin and Silica via Organic Acid Treatment
summary: Abstract Valorization of elements in agricultural rice husk waste benefits a circular society and can significantly reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) and PM 2.5 emissions from burning and landfilling. The research evinces the extraction of high-p
content: Abstract Valorization of elements in agricultural rice husk waste benefits a circular society and can significantly reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) and PM 2.5 emissions from burning and landfilling. The research evinces the extraction of high-purity lignin and silica from rice husk waste using a primary acetic acid solution with a hydrochloric acid catalyst followed by calcination. The new concept reveals that treating rice husks with this acid solution under hydrothermal conditions can combine three essential processes of rice husk pretreatment, lignin extraction, and silica refinement into a single step. Consequently, it can reduce the total processing time. The treatment exhibits a synergistic mechanism wherein acetic acid facilitates dissolution while both HCl and acetic acid cooperatively catalyze the cleavage of lignin bonds. The resulting high-purity lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) obtained under condition A50-H0.3-T120 are hydrophobic, rich in aromatic compounds containing guaiacyl, syringyl, and p-hydroxyphenyl monomers in a ratio of 65.7:0.3:34, and possess a molecular weight of 2129 Da. Meanwhile, the high-purity silica obtained under condition A50-H0.6-T120 forms mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) with a specific surface area of 257 m2/g and a pore volume of 0.36 cm3/g. Finally, a techno-economic evaluation at a small- and medium-enterprise (SME) scale confirms that this process is economically favorable. The gate-to-grave life cycle assessment demonstrates that this process is a sustainable alternative for lignin and silica extraction as its enhanced biodegradable material recovery offsets total greenhouse gas emissions from the process.

title: Bacillus cereus MHI 86 and Bacillus thuringiensis 5-29 both produce the antilisterial bacteriocin thuricin S – analysis of antimicrobial spectrum, stability, and producer strain suitability, including cytotoxicity evaluation
summary: Abstract Thuricin-like bacteriocins are known for their potent antibacterial properties. This study characterizes thuricin S from Bacillus (B.) cereus MHI 86 and B. thuringiensis 5–29 previously isolated from foods. Cell-free supernatants a
content: Abstract Thuricin-like bacteriocins are known for their potent antibacterial properties. This study characterizes thuricin S from Bacillus (B.) cereus MHI 86 and B. thuringiensis 5–29 previously isolated from foods. Cell-free supernatants and partially purified thuricin S exhibited antibacterial activity against Gram-positive species, including Listeria and Bacillus . Thuricin S production started at mid exponential growth phase. Minimum inhibitory concentrations against L. monocytogenes were 5.73 µg/mL (MHI 86) and 10.77 µg/mL (5–29). Both genomes harbor thuricin S-encoding open reading frames. From 8 h of growth, transcription of the bacteriocin gene cluster was consistently detected with most prominent bands at 120 bp. Accordingly, antibacterially active peptides were found at ~ 3.1 kDa, consistent with the size of thuricin S. Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization mass spectrometry confirmed the molecular mass of the partially purified peptides as 3137.6 Da. The bacteriocins were active at neutral and acidic pH (3–7) and up to 80°C. In conclusion, this study is the first to provide a comparative characterisation of thuricin S in two different Bacillus spp. It sheds light on the genetic and transcriptional basis of thuricin S production, as well as its growth and production kinetics, antimicrobial activity, molecular weight, stability, and associated toxin production and cytotoxicity. Notably, thuricin S can be used as a natural agent against L. monocytogenes to control post-pasteurisation contamination.

title: Blue-Green Economy
summary: Youth unemployment across Africa has pushed policymakers toward the blue and green economies, water-based and low-carbon sectors spanning aquaculture, clean energy, waste management, and marine conservation, as sources of decent work. This
content: Youth unemployment across Africa has pushed policymakers toward the blue and green economies, water-based and low-carbon sectors spanning aquaculture, clean energy, waste management, and marine conservation, as sources of decent work. This chapter maps that terrain in Kenya, tracing how soft innovation, borrowed from the creative Orange Economy, shapes whether young entrepreneurs can protect and profit from their ideas in markets where intellectual property remains poorly enforced. However, the chapter’s real concern lies deeper than access. Billions have moved into these sectors through donor and government channels, and still grassroots ventures keep stalling at the same transition point: the moment external funding ends. Drawing on recent evidence from Kenyan mariculture and clean energy programs, the chapter argues that funding architecture itself is the problem: financing rewards what institutions can easily monitor and report within a project cycle, not what an enterprise needs to survive without one. This distinction, it suggests, matters more than how much capital moves at all.

title: Para-authenticity, ontological flexibility, and ontological detachment: how creatives construct and manage virtual endorsers
summary: Research on virtual endorsers has largely focused on consumers, leaving the creative strategies behind their development underexplored. This study examines how creatives construct and manage the authenticity of virtual influencers and brand
content: Research on virtual endorsers has largely focused on consumers, leaving the creative strategies behind their development underexplored. This study examines how creatives construct and manage the authenticity of virtual influencers and brand ambassadors while navigating an evolving ethical landscape. Based on in-depth interviews with eleven practitioners, our findings suggest they deliberately construct virtual personas plausibly situated in recognizable social and material worlds despite their artificiality. To manage the tension between brand control and perceived relatability, practitioners integrate imperfections and contextual cues to evoke para-authenticity – a strategic illusion of plausibility. We also explore the business case for virtual endorsers and how practitioners navigate ethical complexities through strategic disclosure, ontological flexibility (the capacity to vary an endorser’s form), and ontological detachment (the ethically ambivalent use of such flexibility to move beyond human embodiment and its associated demographic categories). Overall, this study reframes authenticity as a strategic construction in a synthetic advertising landscape.

title: Who owns the land after regime collapse? Shifting land claims and tenure governance in post-2021 Afghanistan
summary: In Afghanistan, land ownership has long shifted with political power. Successive regime changes have reshaped who is recognised as an owner, who can occupy property, and how territorial resources are redistributed. The Taliban’s return in 2
content: In Afghanistan, land ownership has long shifted with political power. Successive regime changes have reshaped who is recognised as an owner, who can occupy property, and how territorial resources are redistributed. The Taliban’s return in 2021 did not produce formal land reform, but it reopened a familiar pattern in which political transition unsettles property relations and enables new forms of control. Drawing on qualitative interviews with Afghan landowners now living in exile, this article examines how ownership moves between informal occupation and formal recognition. Houses, plots, and commercial spaces often remain legally tied to former owners while authority is renegotiated on the ground. In some cases, occupation becomes institutionalised through administrative approval, new documentation, or policy measures that regularise access for politically aligned actors. Property change therefore unfolds less as a single act of confiscation than as a layered process through which possession, mediation, and emerging governance practices redefine ownership. The analysis shows how struggles over land operate as a mechanism for reassembling political order. Ownership becomes increasingly difficult to exercise across distance, producing conditions in which property may persist on paper or be reassigned through governmental decree, while recognition and effective control shift in practice. By foregrounding absent owners and unsettled claims, the article contributes to land use policy debates on restitution, return, and post-conflict land administration, with implications for other fragile political environments.

title: Gaia Ecotrack: Renewable energy tokenization platform on the Solana blockchain
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This technical whitepaper details the architecture, tokenomics, and economic models of Gaia Ecotrack, a decentralized infrastructure for the tokenization of renewable energy generation evidence on the Solana blockchain. The platform address
content: This technical whitepaper details the architecture, tokenomics, and economic models of Gaia Ecotrack, a decentralized infrastructure for the tokenization of renewable energy generation evidence on the Solana blockchain. The platform addresses the barrier of high fixed certification costs for small and medium-sized self-generators by aggregating verifiable generation data via an IoT oracle and minting non-speculative evidence tokens (GAIA-E). The document outlines a dual-token economy, a three-layer revenue architecture (SaaS, environmental attribute monetization, and infrastructure services), and two distinct business models: an SPV-owned solar mini-farm model (Model A) and a zero-CAPEX B2B revenue-share model (Model B). Furthermore, it provides a rigorous regulatory function allocation framework designed to operate within Colombia's current energy (CREG), financial (SFC), and data protection jurisdictions without requiring public utility licenses. Financial projections are stress-tested using conservative market assumptions for I-REC prices and fully loaded OPEX, explicitly excluding non-additional carbon credit revenues from the base case. The protocol is designed to scale across jurisdictions with compatible regulatory frameworks, providing cryptographic traceability for environmental attributes while preventing double claiming in compliance with ICVCM and Verra standards.

title: Sulfated polysaccharides and metallothioneins from microalgae: a dual-platform model for next-generation pharmaceuticals
summary: Microalgae are sustainable sources of structurally diverse biomolecules with growing pharmaceutical relevance. Among these, sulfated polysaccharides (SPs) and metallothioneins (MTs) have attracted increasing attention because of their diver
content: Microalgae are sustainable sources of structurally diverse biomolecules with growing pharmaceutical relevance. Among these, sulfated polysaccharides (SPs) and metallothioneins (MTs) have attracted increasing attention because of their diverse biological activities and stress-responsive biosynthesis. This review proposes an integrated SP–MT dual-platform concept, providing a conceptual framework for exploring how the complementary extracellular functions of SPs and intracellular protective roles of MTs may collectively inform future pharmaceutical research and biomanufacturing. Current knowledge on their biosynthesis, structural diversity, biological activities, and production technologies is critically evaluated. Experimental evidence demonstrates that SPs possess antiviral, anticoagulant, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and anticancer activities, whereas MTs contribute to metal homeostasis, detoxification, redox regulation, and protection against oxidative stress. Although their co-induction under environmental stress provides a biological rationale for coordinated applications, evidence supporting synergistic therapeutic effects remains limited, and the proposed dual-platform concept requires rigorous experimental and clinical validation. The review also highlights recent advances in cultivation engineering, systems biology, synthetic biology, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence that may accelerate the discovery, optimization, and standardized production of these biomolecules. The key priorities for future research include elucidating biosynthetic pathways, establishing structure–activity relationships, developing scalable manufacturing processes, and conducting comprehensive preclinical evaluation to support their future pharmaceutical translation.

title: Mapping the Computational Turn: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Migration Research
summary: This study systematically maps the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in migration studies. We searched the academic literature published in major databases between 1990 and 2025, conducting an in-depth a
content: This study systematically maps the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in migration studies. We searched the academic literature published in major databases between 1990 and 2025, conducting an in-depth analysis of 117 search records that used computational methods to investigate migration-related research questions. The study disaggregated four AI approaches (Rationally Acting AI, Humanly Acting AI, Rationally Thinking AI, Humanly Thinking AI) and three ML approaches (Supervised ML, Unsupervised ML, Reinforcement ML) then intersected them with key research questions in migration studies. The study makes three main contributions. First, it reveals Supervised ML and Rationally Acting AI as the most preferred computational approaches in migration studies, clearly dominating over other computational approaches of study. Second, it transposes each computational approach to the research questions of study, identifying methodological patterns, disciplinary preferences, and opportunities for novel applications. Third, and most importantly, computational migration research continues to be concentrated on forecasting, prediction, optimization, and classification about migrants as opposed to computational research being conducted for migrants. Accordingly, we set out an agenda and call for further computational migration research and design centering migrant rights and wellbeing rather than solely supporting the institutional and administrative efficiency of migration management.

title: Spatial pattern evolution and its driving factors for the fruit industry in China
summary: In this study, we investigate China’s fruit production patterns, spatial evolution characteristics, and driving factors, with the goal of providing scientific evidence surrounding the high-quality development of the fruit industry. Based on
content: In this study, we investigate China’s fruit production patterns, spatial evolution characteristics, and driving factors, with the goal of providing scientific evidence surrounding the high-quality development of the fruit industry. Based on the provincial panel data of fruit production in China from 2000 to 2024, this study explores the spatial evolution characteristics of China’s fruit industry using the production concentration index, the production scale index, the gravity center migration model, and the standard deviational ellipse model; further, we explore the factors influencing the fruit industry using the spatial autocorrelation analysis and the spatial Durbin model. The results show that the gravity center of fruit production in China has been consistently shifting westward, with this trend showing signs of further intensification. Notably, significant spatial autocorrelation and spatial spillover effects exist in China’s fruit production distribution, with spatial dependence particularly strengthening progressively in western regions. The spatial variation in fruit production in China is influenced by certain factors: sunshine hours, disaster intensity, comparative returns, urbanization level, effective irrigation area, technological progress, and fiscal agricultural policies. Meanwhile, the degree of impact exerted by these driving factors on changes in production distribution varies significantly across different fruit-producing regions. Therefore, based on the spatial dynamics of China’s fruit production patterns, in this article, we propose that the spatial distribution of fruit production is optimized by leveraging region-specific resource endowments. Simultaneously, it is important to fully harness technological progress, as the primary driver, and to effectively capitalize on the positive spillover effects from other contributing factors. Accordingly, it is possible to enhance the industry’s support systems, with the ultimate goal of achieving the optimized spatial distribution of fruit production in China.

title: Sustainable bioactive membranes based on κ-carrageenan and açaí seed extract for potential topical application
summary: Açaí ( Euterpe oleracea Mart.), an Amazonian fruit widely exported worldwide, generates seeds corresponding to approximately 85% of the fruit weight, which are commonly discarded despite their valorization potential. In this study, κ-carrag
content: Açaí ( Euterpe oleracea Mart.), an Amazonian fruit widely exported worldwide, generates seeds corresponding to approximately 85% of the fruit weight, which are commonly discarded despite their valorization potential. In this study, κ-carrageenan bioactive membranes containing açaí seed extract were developed and characterized as candidate materials for topical applications. The açaí seed extract showed antioxidant capacity in chemical assays, with a DPPH radical-scavenging activity of 95.75 ± 0.75% at 10 mg/mL and an EC₅₀ of 7.78 ± 0.41 mg/mL, while ferric reducing capacity was 0.19 ± 0.02 mg GAE/g (EC₅₀ = 1.49 ± 0.01 mg/mL). The açaí seed extract showed antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 3.13 mg/mL. HPLC analysis confirmed the presence of catechin (0.03 mg/mL) and epicatechin (0.01 mg/mL). Membranes were prepared and mechanical analysis showed tensile strength of 3.63 ± 0.34 MPa and elongation at break of 35.97 ± 2.19%. Adhesion force was 26.35 ± 5.53 g and the membranes remained structurally intact for up to 7 days under the evaluated PBS conditions. FTIR analysis showed preservation of the characteristic functional groups of κ-carrageenan after extract incorporation, while SEM revealed increased structural heterogeneity in the açaí membrane. Cytotoxicity assays demonstrated that the extract and membranes were non-cytotoxic at most tested concentrations. The membranes exhibited water vapor permeability of 1.05 ± 0.75 g·mm/kPa·day·m² and swelling capacity of 0.42 ± 0.08 g/g. Overall, the developed membrane showed promising potential as a sustainable platform for topical applications, although further biological studies are required to establish its antimicrobial performance and wound-healing potential.

title: Novel halotolerant microbial system enhanced by gamma irradiation for advanced multimetal bioremediation
summary: BACKGROUND: Saline industrial effluents are difficult to treat because elevated ionic strength can inhibit biological treatment and alter metal speciation. This study evaluated two moderately halotolerant microorganisms recovered from seawa
content: BACKGROUND: Saline industrial effluents are difficult to treat because elevated ionic strength can inhibit biological treatment and alter metal speciation. This study evaluated two moderately halotolerant microorganisms recovered from seawater and shark-associated samples and examined whether gamma selection altered the performance of the more radioresistant isolate. RESULTS: The isolates were identified as Serratia proteamaculans PX875896 and Rhodotorula mucilaginosa PX876763 by 16 S and 18 S rRNA gene sequencing, respectively. Both grew at 3-5% (w/v) NaCl but not at 10% or higher. In synthetic saline medium, S. proteamaculans showed the highest removal after 72 h for Cd (50.71%), Mo (42.56%), Cu (34.13%), and Co (25.26%); no net Cr removal was detected. S. proteamaculans was not recovered after 0.5 kGy, whereas R. mucilaginosa survived exposure up to 4 kGy. Relative to the wild yeast, gamma-selected yeast derivatives showed higher removal for several metals, including Co (22.61% at 48 h) and Cu (12.34% at 72 h) by the 4 kGy derivative and Mo (14.73% at 72 h) by the 3 kGy derivative. The 4 kGy derivative also contained more total carotenoids (67.30 µg/mL) than the wild strain (44.40 µg/mL). In textile wastewater, the 4 kGy derivative yielded the greatest removal of Mo (93.05%), Cr (77.88%),Co ( 60.80%) and Cd (51.42%), whereas S. proteamaculans yielded the greatest removal of Mo ( 58.43 %, Cr 57. 14 %, Fe (52.17%) and V (74.68%). CONCLUSIONS: Saline-derived Serratia proteamaculans PX875896 showed greater metal removal in synthetic saline medium, while Rhodotorula mucilaginosa PX876763 exhibited broader metal tolerance and greater gamma resistance.The 4 kGy yeast derivative improved multimetal removal from textile wastewater, coinciding with a more carotenoid-rich phenotype.These findings highlight the value of moderate halotolerance, gamma-assisted selection, and complementary bacterial-yeast approaches, while showing that tolerance alone does not predict removal efficiency. l.

title: Space-Based versus Land-Based AI Data Centres: A Comparative Environmental Assessment Centred on Google's Orbital Compute Programme
summary: This paper compares space-based AI compute against terrestrial hyperscale data centres across six environmental parameters, using Google's published research programme on solar-powered TPU constellations in dawn-dusk low-Earth orbit as the
content: This paper compares space-based AI compute against terrestrial hyperscale data centres across six environmental parameters, using Google's published research programme on solar-powered TPU constellations in dawn-dusk low-Earth orbit as the reference case (Arcas et al., 2025). The comparison uses a dual functional unit — 1 MW-year of delivered IT power, and 1 MW of IT power over 1-, 5- and 10-year missions — under a cradle-to-grave boundary that includes launch and re-entry for the orbital case. Three findings emerge. First, the carbon result is functional-unit dependent: per kWh of energy delivered to the payload, orbital systems are 1.5–1.95× more carbon-intensive than terrestrial ones (52.1–66.3 versus 34.0 gCO₂e/kWh) (Ohs et al., 2025); but per MW of IT capacity against real-world grids, launch-phase emissions of 1,032–2,585 t CO₂e are repaid within the first year and amount to only 5.5–13.7% of five years of terrestrial operation at the 395.65 gCO₂e/kWh global data-centre average (Vries-Gao, 2025). Break-even occurs at grid intensities of 21.6–54.1 gCO₂e/kWh over five years. Second, water and land are where space wins categorically: no evaporative cooling, and no terrestrial land conversion of the tens-to-hundreds of hectares a hyperscale facility requires (Hlabisa, 2025). Third, the binding physical constraint in orbit is not compute silicon but radiative heat rejection — 33–67 cm² of radiator per watt of waste heat, or 3,333–6,667 m² per MW (Vicente, 2021) — which converts thermal inefficiency directly into launch mass and launch carbon.

title: Integrated vehicle and bidirectional charging scheduling for V2G-enabled electric bus system
summary: Abstract Electric bus (EB) fleets are transformed into flexible energy resources through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology while maintaining regular transit services. This paper investigates the joint optimization of vehicle operations and b
content: Abstract Electric bus (EB) fleets are transformed into flexible energy resources through vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology while maintaining regular transit services. This paper investigates the joint optimization of vehicle operations and bidirectional charging decisions for a multi-route EB system with limited bidirectional and unidirectional chargers. A time-expanded network is constructed to capture EB's daily operations, supporting optimization of partial charging and discharging decisions. Considering the effect of upward and downward regulation demands of the power grid, a mixed-integer programming model is established to minimize operating costs and regulation deviation. Then, a column-generation-based diving heuristic algorithm incorporating two dominance strategies is further designed to efficiently search for a high-quality solution. Finally, numerical experiments based on real-world bus routes are conducted, and results indicate that the optimized scheme enhances both the economic performance and grid-friendly operation of the EB system. Specifically, the discharging revenues effectively offset the electricity purchase and battery degradation costs, while the EB fleet meets 86.3% of the regulation demand. In addition, the two dominance strategies reveal different advantages, dominance strategy I reduces total costs by 28.7 CNY, whereas dominance strategy II shortens the solution time by 39.6%.

title: Amyloid‐Guided Assembly of Magnetically Recyclable Enzymatic Nanofibers Toward Sustainable Biocatalysis
summary: ABSTRACT The rational construction of recyclable protein‐based catalytic materials requires connecting molecular enzyme design with higher‐order supramolecular organization and functional recovery interfaces. This study establishes a hierar
content: ABSTRACT The rational construction of recyclable protein‐based catalytic materials requires connecting molecular enzyme design with higher‐order supramolecular organization and functional recovery interfaces. This study establishes a hierarchical design strategy that integrates fusion‐enzyme engineering, amyloid‐guided self‐assembly, and magnetic immobilization. The primary amine oxidase DPAO4 and the flavin‐containing amine oxidase DMAO7 were joined through flexible or rigid linkers, and the rigid (EAAAK) 3 variant provided broad substrate coverage, greater tolerance to process‐relevant stresses, and lower interdomain fluctuations in molecular dynamics simulations. N‐terminal Sup35 1‐61 or Ure2 1‐80 domains promoted the formation of ThT‐responsive fibrillar assembly, and the resulting enzymatic nanofibers were coupled to amino‐functionalized Fe 3 O 4 @SiO 2 ‐NH 2 nanoparticles. The composites enabled magnetic separation within 30 s, catalyzed the degradation of eight biogenic amines under acidic, thermal, saline, and ethanol‐containing conditions, and retained an average of 53.2% of their initial activity after four recovery cycles. As proof‐of‐concept evaluation in complex matrices, selected systems removed up to 70.6% of total biogenic amines from fermented beverages and 69.7% from soy sauce. The distinct responses of the Sup35‐ and Ure2‐based composites suggest an association between assembly‐domain identity and catalytic performance in complex matrices. This work demonstrates a hierarchical design approach for recyclable protein‐based catalytic materials and sustainable biocatalysis.

title: Productive, profitable and energy-efficient Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based vegetable intercropping system under Northern Telangana zone
summary: Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based intercropping systems offer considerable scope for improving productivity, profitability and resource-use efficiency (RUE) under sustainable agricultural production systems. An experiment was conducted in r
content: Brassica juncea (L.) Czern. based intercropping systems offer considerable scope for improving productivity, profitability and resource-use efficiency (RUE) under sustainable agricultural production systems. An experiment was conducted in rabi season 2022 at the Agricultural Research Station, Adilabad, Telangana to test the efficiency of intercropping different vegetables in mustard with different row ratios. A total of 13 treatments comprising sole crops such as mustard, sole root vegetables (radish, beetroot, carrot and potato) and their combination under 2 : 2 and 3 : 3 row ratios were considered in the randomised block design (RBD) of the experiment. It was found that the highest total economic yield (24212 kg ha-1), mustard equivalent yield (5775 kg ha-1), gross returns (₹338968 ha-1), net returns (₹264526 ha-1) and benefit-cost ratio (B : C) ratio (4.55) were obtained from the monocropping of radish. While among intercropping combinations, mustard with radish under 3 : 3 row ratio yielded the highest total economic yield (13515 kg ha-1), mustard equivalent yield (3964 kg ha-1), mustard oil yield (351 kg ha-1), gross returns (₹216033 ha-1), net returns (₹160966) and B : C ratio (3.92). These results were statistically comparable with mustard with radish at ratio 2 : 2. An energetic efficiency analysis concluded that the performance of the mustard with radish (3 : 3 and 2 : 2) was favourable with respect to high energy productivity (0.60 and 0.61 kg MJ-1) and low specific energy (1.66 and 1.63 MJ kg-1) among the intercropping methods. Therefore, mustard intercropping with radish at 3 : 3 and 2 : 2 row ratios could be considered the most beneficial and lucrative intercropping method in northern Telangana. Further multi-season and multi-location studies are required to validate the findings before making broader recommendations.

title: Physicochemical, microbial, and sensory characterization of quinoa-based vegan yogurt as a functional plant-based fermented product
summary: Background This study aimed to develop quinoa-based vegan yogurt products in response to the increasing interest in plant-based diets and to evaluate their sensory, chemical, and microbiological properties. Methods In the first phase, four
content: Background This study aimed to develop quinoa-based vegan yogurt products in response to the increasing interest in plant-based diets and to evaluate their sensory, chemical, and microbiological properties. Methods In the first phase, four quinoa-based yogurt formulations were prepared using different starter culture and activation strategies, and fermented under controlled conditions. In the second phase, samples were subjected to sensory analysis by 12 trained panelists and 80 consumer panelists, evaluating appearance, taste, color, aroma, texture, flavor, and overall acceptability. Additionally, functional properties (total phenolic content [TPC] and antioxidant capacity [CUPRAC]) and proximate compositions (crude protein, total fat, and moisture content) were analyzed and compared with a commercially available rice-based vegan yogurt. Results The findings indicated that quinoa-based vegan yogurts are a promising alternative in terms of nutritional value, functional properties, and sensory acceptability. Microbiological analyses revealed viable lactic acid bacteria (LAB) counts ranging from 6.9 to 8.2 log CFU/g, confirming successful fermentation. Conclusion Quinoa-based vegan yogurts exhibit superior protein content, strong antioxidant capacity, and high consumer acceptability compared to commercial rice-based alternatives, demonstrating their strong potential as functional plant-based fermented products.

title: Fuel Price Transmission and Public Policy: Evidence from the UK Road Fuels Supply Chain
