summary: This study examines cost pass-through and price transmission mechanisms within the supply chain of the United Kingdom road fuel sector, focusing on how changes in input prices affect wholesale and retail fuel prices. Empirical analysis is c
content: This study examines cost pass-through and price transmission mechanisms within the supply chain of the United Kingdom road fuel sector, focusing on how changes in input prices affect wholesale and retail fuel prices. Empirical analysis is conducted using distributed lag models following Nakamura and Zerom (2010) and Deltas and Polemis (2024). Levels and double-log specifications are applied to ensure robustness. Asymmetric price transmission is tested using the two-step nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) model. The aim of the study is to estimate the amount of cost pass through of an input price change to the wholesale road fuel prices and of a wholesale to the retail prices. The findings reveal product pretax results mild asymmetry and moderate rockets and feathers phenomena for super and premium products; and almost complete post tax cost pass through in the UK road fuels sector, shedding light to pre- and post-tax effects.

title: Readiness assessment for construction 5.0 using fuzzy logic: a case of construction organisation
summary: The construction industry is fast transforming to become more and more empowered by the next phase of the digital evolution, Construction 5.0, which is based on the use of new digital tools alongside human-centric, sustainable, and climate-
content: The construction industry is fast transforming to become more and more empowered by the next phase of the digital evolution, Construction 5.0, which is based on the use of new digital tools alongside human-centric, sustainable, and climate-resilient methods to address sustainability, labour shortage and climate resilience challenges. Organizational readiness for Construction 5.0 is still unclear as more technologies like AI, IoT, BIM and modular construction are being adopted, especially in developing countries such as India. Currently, this study proposes a fuzzy logic-based framework for evaluating the Construction 5.0 readiness in three major enablers, which are decomposed into seven criteria and twenty-six attributes: Resilience, Human Centricity and Environmental Sustainability. The framework is based on expert judgments from a medium-scale construction company in India, which quantifies the readiness of the enterprise using a Fuzzy Construction 5.0 Index and weak attributes by a Fuzzy Performance-Importance Index. In this single-case application, results indicate the case organisation is in the ‘Ready’ to ‘Very Ready’ range, with stronger resilience and basic human-centric practices and weaker advanced sustainability and assistive technologies. The fuzzy logic approach provides a structured, repeatable diagnostic and prioritisation roadmap to guide capability development toward Construction 5.0.

title: The Effects of Fuel Price Changes on Financial Planning of SMEs in Mtendere Township, Lusaka
source: Journal of economics, business and commerce.
summary: This study assessed the effect of fuel price changes on the financial planning of SMEs in Mtendere Township, Lusaka, focusing on operational planning, profit projection, and price planning. The study adopted a quantitative approach and used
content: This study assessed the effect of fuel price changes on the financial planning of SMEs in Mtendere Township, Lusaka, focusing on operational planning, profit projection, and price planning. The study adopted a quantitative approach and used a purposive sampling technique to select 50 SME owners and managers. Structured questionnaires were used to collect data, which was analyzed using MegaStat Software. The study found that 60.0% of SMEs reported that fuel price changes negatively affected their operational costs, while 28.0% reported a significant negative effect. Regression analysis confirmed a statistically significant relationship between business dependence on fuel and the effect of the price changes on operational costs, F(1,48)=5.70, p=0.0210, with R2 = 0.106 and r = 0.326. Regarding profit projection, the study found that 36.0% of SMEs sometimes revised their profit projections, while 32.0% reported that their six-month profit projections were unreliable and 24.0% considered them very unreliable. A statistical association between frequency of profit projection revisions and perceived reliability was found through a chi-square test (df = 16, X2 = 46.46, P = 0.0001). On price planning, 50.0% indicated that fuel volatility forced them to abandon fixed price planning to a large extent. The association between business activity and abandoning fixed prices was confirmed through a chi-square test with the values of df = 12, X2 = 29.12, and P = 0.0038. The study recommends that SMEs adopt flexible budgeting, scenario-based profit forecasting, contingency reserves, and responsive pricing strategies to strengthen financial resilience against fuel price volatility

title: Low‐Melting‐Point Alloys for Printable Rear Electrodes in Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells: A Review
summary: ABSTRACT Noble‐metal rear electrodes deposited by high‐vacuum thermal evaporation impose a major bottleneck for the development of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and organic solar cells (OSCs), owing to high material costs, unstable interfac
content: ABSTRACT Noble‐metal rear electrodes deposited by high‐vacuum thermal evaporation impose a major bottleneck for the development of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) and organic solar cells (OSCs), owing to high material costs, unstable interfaces, and poor manufacturability. Low‑melting‑point alloys (LMPAs) represent a versatile alternative rear‑electrode candidate that supports direct patterning under low‑temperature, vacuum‑free conditions. Upon ambient air exposure, LMPAs spontaneously develop an in‑situ surface oxide layer, which can mitigate Schottky‑barrier effects to facilitate efficient charge extraction and suppress ion/atom migration to improve device stability. In addition, the intrinsic mechanical compliance and self‑healing capacity of LMPAs render them particularly promising for flexible and stretchable photovoltaic devices. This timely review first introduces fundamental properties of LMPAs and their unique merits for photovoltaic applications. Recent advances in LMPA rear electrodes for OSCs and PSCs are reviewed, with focused emphasis on fabrication strategies for finely patterned LMPA electrodes. We thoroughly discuss the critical functions of the in‑situ oxide layer, alongside the mechanical advantages of LMPAs for bendable and stretchable devices. Design principles and performance trade‑offs are then summarized. Finally, remaining challenges and future research opportunities for LMPA‐electrode‐based solar cells are highlighted.

title: Lithium Metal Phosphate Cathodes for Energy Storage: Production Routes, Structure–Performance Relationships, Scale‐Up Challenges, and Recycling Perspectives
summary: ABSTRACT Olivine‐type LiMPO 4 (M = Fe, Mn, Co, Ni, and mixed‐transition‐metal compositions) cathodes are among the most robust positive‐electrode families for rechargeable lithium‐ion batteries, offering high thermal stability and favorable
content: ABSTRACT Olivine‐type LiMPO 4 (M = Fe, Mn, Co, Ni, and mixed‐transition‐metal compositions) cathodes are among the most robust positive‐electrode families for rechargeable lithium‐ion batteries, offering high thermal stability and favorable safety characteristics for transportation and stationary energy storage. Practical performance is strongly governed by synthesis–structure–interface coupling: modest variations in particle size and morphology, anti‐site disorder, carbon topology, or surface chemistry can shift the dominant limitation from bulk diffusion to interfacial charge transfer or interphase transport. This review summarizes recent progress in LiMPO 4 production routes and relates processing parameters to microstructure and electrochemical behavior. Solid‐state, sol–gel, hydro/solvothermal, precipitation‐assisted, and rapid‐heating approaches are discussed in terms of how they control nucleation and growth and thereby determine primary‐particle geometry, secondary agglomeration, and accessible surface area. Strategies to mitigate intrinsic transport limitations are evaluated, including conductive‐carbon architectures, aliovalent and isovalent doping, mixed‐cation tuning in Li(Fe,Mn)PO 4 , defect engineering to reduce Li/Fe anti‐site formation, and interface stabilization via electrolyte/additive selection and surface coatings. Finally, electrode engineering, testing protocols, and scale‐up constraints are considered to outline practical pathways toward manufacturable LiMPO 4 cathodes with balanced rate capability, durability, and sustainability. By integrating production routes, structure–performance relationships, scale‐up constraints, and recycling perspectives, this review provides a practical framework for selecting LiMPO 4 cathode design strategies according to the dominant limitation of each chemistry.

title: BIOSSURFACTANTES MICROBIANOS COMO BIOINSUMOS APLICADOS NA AGRICULTURA COMO ESTRATÉGIA SUSTENTÁVEL
summary: A elevada demanda por alimentos vem intensificando o uso de insumos químicos na agricultura, gerando impactos ambientais que induzem a busca por alternativas biotecnológicas sustentáveis. Nesse contexto, destacam-se os biossurfactantes micr
content: A elevada demanda por alimentos vem intensificando o uso de insumos químicos na agricultura, gerando impactos ambientais que induzem a busca por alternativas biotecnológicas sustentáveis. Nesse contexto, destacam-se os biossurfactantes microbianos, compostos anfifílicos produzidos principalmente por bactérias, leveduras e fungos filamentosos. As espécies do gênero Bacillus demonstram elevado potencial biotecnológico para a síntese de lipopeptídeos com propriedades antimicrobianas e na promoção do crescimento vegetal. Esses compostos apresentam biodegradabilidade, baixa toxicidade e diversidade estrutural, características que ampliam seu potencial como bioinsumos agrícolas. Esta revisão apresenta o potencial dos biossurfactantes microbianos como estratégia biotecnológica para uma agricultura sustentável, abordando classificação, características físico-químicas e microrganismos produtores, alternativas de produção usando resíduos agroindustriais como substratos e principais aplicações agrícolas. Os lipopeptídeos como surfactina, iturina e fengicina são produzidos por bactérias do gênero Bacillus apresentam efeitos relevantes na promoção da germinação e no desenvolvimento radicular inicial de diferentes espécies vegetais, além de atividade antagônica contra fitopatógenos como Rhizoctonia solani, Fusarium spp. e Colletotrichum spp., contribuindo para o manejo de doenças de plantas. No entanto, a aplicação em escala industrial é limitada, considerando os desafios relacionados aos custos operacionais de produção, recuperação e purificação. Portanto, os biossurfactantes constituem alternativa promissora para o desenvolvimento de bioinsumos multifuncionais, como indução da germinação, promoção do crescimento e capacidade de aliar proteção vegetal e sustentabilidade produtiva.

title: Carbon Emission Disclosure, Environmental Disclosure, Capital Intensity, and Corporate Financial Performance in Indonesia
summary: Purpose: This study analyzes the effect of carbon emission disclosure, environmental disclosure, and capital intensity on the financial performance of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024.Research
content: Purpose: This study analyzes the effect of carbon emission disclosure, environmental disclosure, and capital intensity on the financial performance of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024.Research Methodology: This quantitative study uses the annual and sustainability reports of 38 companies selected through purposive sampling, yielding 190 firm-year observations. Carbon emission disclosure and environmental disclosure are measured with 18-item and 31-item indices, capital intensity with fixed assets to total assets, and financial performance with an adjusted return on assets series. The Random Effect Model is selected through the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests in EViews 12.Results: Carbon emission disclosure (B = 1.825225; p < 0.001) and environmental disclosure (B = 1.297164; p < 0.001) are positively and significantly associated with financial performance, whereas capital intensity is not significant (B = 0.027686; p = 0.8971). The three variables are simultaneously significant (F = 65.21017; p < 0.001), with an adjusted R² of 0.504757.Conclusions: Transparent carbon and environmental reporting is associated with stronger financial performance, whereas the proportion of fixed assets alone does not differentiate performance among energy companies.Limitations: The study covers one sector over five years, measures disclosure breadth rather than quality, and relies on an adjusted performance series that cannot be fully reproduced.Contributions: This study integrates stakeholder value-creation, legitimacy, signaling, and agency theories by demonstrating how carbon and environmental reporting jointly signal financial performance, providing insights for Indonesian firms, investors, and regulators.

title: Organizational Integration: Past–Present Interactions
summary: This chapter examines organizational integration as a critical dimension of maritime digital transformation, focusing on how historical data can be integrated with current operations to support decision-making. Drawing on the pyramid of com
content: This chapter examines organizational integration as a critical dimension of maritime digital transformation, focusing on how historical data can be integrated with current operations to support decision-making. Drawing on the pyramid of competence framework and the concept of declining computing costs, the chapter demonstrates how artificial intelligence and big data transform raw operational information into actionable strategic knowledge. The analysis focuses on the highly fragmented chartering process, covering activities from pre-fixture market negotiations to post-fixture operations, including demurrage calculations, bunker planning, and voyage reporting. Traditionally, these activities have relied on manual procedures, email-based communication, and informal intermediary networks. However, the emergence of integrated digital platforms is fundamentally changing the way these processes are managed. By automating complex laytime calculations, standardizing charterparty contracts, and organizing large volumes of operational data, shipping companies can reduce operational risks, improve efficiency, and accelerate contract administration. The chapter further argues that embedding experience and accumulated knowledge into digital workflows lowers computational barriers and supports a transition from intuition-based decision-making to machine-assisted, data-driven strategic management. In addition, these digital ecosystems strengthen operational integration and commercial transparency by connecting ship operations with shore-based commercial objectives. The findings suggest that organizational integration should be viewed not simply as an administrative improvement but as a fundamental business transformation. By redefining traditional corporate roles, improving resource allocation, and enhancing decision-making capabilities, digital integration provides the technological foundation necessary for long-term competitiveness and resilience in an increasingly complex global supply chain environment.

title: Poly-L-Lactic Acid in Aesthetic Dermatology: Injection Techniques, Clinical Protocols, Skin Quality Outcomes, and Risk Management
summary: Poly-L-lactic acid is a synthetic, biodegradable collagen biostimulator that has evolved over more than two decades from a corrective agent for human immunodeficiency virus-associated facial lipoatrophy into a widely used tool in regenerati
content: Poly-L-lactic acid is a synthetic, biodegradable collagen biostimulator that has evolved over more than two decades from a corrective agent for human immunodeficiency virus-associated facial lipoatrophy into a widely used tool in regenerative aesthetic dermatology.Unlike hyaluronic acid fillers, which provide immediate volume by occupying space, it acts indirectly: its microparticles elicit a controlled subclinical foreign-body response that drives macrophage polarization, transforming growth factor-beta 1/Smadmediated fibroblast activation, and progressive type I neocollagenesis.In this narrative review, PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through August 2026 for Englishlanguage, peer-reviewed studies, which were appraised narratively to summarize the evidence on injection techniques and reconstitution, clinical protocols and patient selection, clinical efficacy and skin quality outcomes, and the prevention and management of complications.Consensus statements and comparative studies associate higher reconstitution volumes, thorough suspension, subdermal placement, non-bolus delivery, and structured post-treatment care with fewer papules and nodules, although much of this guidance rests on expert opinion and observational data rather than head-to-head trials.A small number of randomized controlled trials report improvements in cheek wrinkle severity, skin elasticity, hydration, and dermal thickness compared with no treatment or saline, and indications are extending to the neck, décolletage, body, and patients with facial volume loss during glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy.However, the available trials are few, heterogeneous in protocols and outcome measures, and frequently at some or high risk of bias.Non-inflammatory nodules and inflammatory granulomas differ in mechanism and are managed along distinct pathways.Standardized protocols, a core outcome set for skin quality, and adequately powered comparative trials are needed before firm conclusions about the relative effectiveness of poly-L-lactic acid can be drawn.

title: Effects of vacuum frying on carotenoid content and profile in fresh jackfruit pulp and jackfruit chips
summary: Jackfruits, especially the ripe ones, are a local functional food in many developing countries as they have vital nutrients, including beta carotene that can serve as pro-vitamin A. In many Asian countries, jackfruit chips are a popular del
content: Jackfruits, especially the ripe ones, are a local functional food in many developing countries as they have vital nutrients, including beta carotene that can serve as pro-vitamin A. In many Asian countries, jackfruit chips are a popular delicacy. The process of turning jackfruit into chips is usually done by vacuum frying. Food processing may affect the biological activity of many bioactive compounds, though not all processing results in loss of quality and health properties. Therefore, it is crucial to evaluate and quantify the carotenoid content and composition during vacuum frying to understand how food processing affects the carotenoid properties. Carotenoid content and composition were measured by UV-visible spectrophotometer and HPLC PDA. The study showed that the carotenoid content of jackfruit chips decreased due to processing, from 31.97±1.31.6 µg/g (dry basis (db)) in fresh fruit to 3.73±0.20 µg/g (db) in chip products. An increase in the carotenoid composition was marked by an increase in the number of isomers in the cis form. Those changes were also confirmed by the spectral pattern of carotenoid pigments analyzed using a UV-visible spectrophotometer, which shows an increase in absorption below a wavelength of 350 nm. In conclusion, vacuum frying affects commercially available jackfruit chips' pigment content and composition.

title: DNA confirms barbarian tribe’s mythic tale about its origins
summary: The Goths believed they swept south from Scandinavia centuries before sacking Rome. Skeletons from across Europe say they were right.
content: The Goths believed they swept south from Scandinavia centuries before sacking Rome. Skeletons from across Europe say they were right.

title: Development of Potent METTL1 Inhibitors Using a Nanoscale Direct-To-Biology Strategy
summary: Abstract The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report
content: Abstract The RNA methyltransferase METTL1/WDR4, which catalyzes N7-methylguanosine (m7G) modification in tRNA, has emerged as a key regulator of mRNA translation, and its dysregulation is associated with cancer development. Here, we report the development of a potent series of METTL1 inhibitors by combining conventional structure−activity relationship (SAR) studies with a tandem direct-to-biology (D2B) approach. Lead compound VK238 inhibited METTL1 enzymatic activity at nanomolar concentrations and exhibited selectivity across a panel of methyltransferases and kinases. In a cellular context, pharmacological METTL1 inhibition reduced m7G levels in tRNAs, leading to apoptosis-mediated cell death in several acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cell lines. Mechanistic studies combining biophysical experiments, photoaffinity labeling (PAL), and molecular docking suggested that this inhibitor series occupies the (S)-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding pocket of METTL1. Collectively, these findings highlight METTL1 as a tractable and pharmacologically relevant target for therapeutic intervention in AML.

title: Allocation Rules Gate Carbon-Price Thresholds in Park-Level Source–Grid–Load–Storage Systems: Institutional Trade-Offs in Six Chinese Provincial Reform Scenarios
summary: Whether a carbon price changes how energy users dispatch their own generation is usually treated as a technical question rather than an institutional one. This paper asks when, and under what institutional conditions, a carbon price crosses
content: Whether a carbon price changes how energy users dispatch their own generation is usually treated as a technical question rather than an institutional one. This paper asks when, and under what institutional conditions, a carbon price crosses the technology-substitution threshold in demand-side daily operation. We build a dispatch model of a park-level source–grid–load–storage system, solve it exactly as a mixed-integer linear program alongside a rule-based heuristic, and simulate six Chinese provincial electricity-market reform scenarios and a constructed high-carbon reference, with unit-commitment, multi-day, Monte Carlo and auxiliary-regression checks. Emissions respond in thresholds rather than linearly, governed by an hourly switching-price distribution that is equivalent to an implied demand-side marginal abatement cost curve and coincides with the exact optimum. Three institutional gates—the allocation rule, the pass-through it implies, and the kinked free allowance—determine whether that curve operates, and none is the price level. The regression confirms that the price acts only through these gates, its effect on emission intensity reversing sign across allocation regimes. We read the rules as deliberate trade-offs sustaining industrial output and employment rather than as policy failure, and quantify the implicit subsidy they convey: a headline price of 100 CNY t−1 carries a revealed shadow value near 8. Allocation reform, not a higher price, restores the signal.

title: Exploring socio-technical facilitators of blockchain adoption in agri-food value chains: an interpretive structural modelling (ISM) approach
summary: Blockchain technology has significant potential to promote transparency, efficiency, and sustainability in the agricultural sector. However, successful implementation depends not only on the availability of technology but also on organizati
content: Blockchain technology has significant potential to promote transparency, efficiency, and sustainability in the agricultural sector. However, successful implementation depends not only on the availability of technology but also on organizational readiness, infrastructure, and coordinated effort among stakeholders. This paper identifies the key facilitators that support the adoption of blockchain across agri-food value chains spanning farm-level precision-agriculture practices and downstream supply-chain operations and analyzes the interdependencies among them. A literature review identified ten Facilitators of Blockchain Adoption (FBA), which were reviewed and validated by a panel of five experts spanning academia, agro-industry, farming, non-governmental organizations, and information technology. The interrelationships among these facilitators were analyzed using Interpretive Structural Modelling (ISM), a structural method for organizing expert judgments about pairwise influence into a hierarchical model; ISM does not estimate causal effect size or statistical significance. Applying transitivity consistently to the expert-derived reachability matrix revealed that nine of the ten facilitators form a single, tightly interdependent cluster, while enhancing trust among stakeholders emerges as the sole outcome-level factor at the apex of the hierarchy. A complementary MICMAC analysis confirms that these nine facilitators exhibit both high driving power and high dependence power (a “linkage” profile), indicating that the blockchain-adoption system is mutually reinforcing rather than governed by a small set of independent root causes. These findings suggest that ICT infrastructure, stakeholder collaboration, shared responsibility, service quality, auditability, usability, and fast-payment capability function together as a coupled socio-technical system that ultimately builds stakeholder trust. The results can inform extension professionals, educators, policymakers, and technology developers seeking to prioritize interventions that support a more coordinated and sustainable introduction of blockchain into agri-food value chains.

title: AHL-producing PGPR biopriming induces endogenous phenolic-rich accumulation associated with the suppression of Pseudomonas syringae infection in Cicer arietinum
summary: Molecular communication plays a critical role in plant-pathogen interactions. Pseudomonas syringae (Psy) infects chickpea ( Cicer arietinum ) by utilizing quorum sensing (QS) to coordinate virulence factors. This study evaluates biopriming
content: Molecular communication plays a critical role in plant-pathogen interactions. Pseudomonas syringae (Psy) infects chickpea ( Cicer arietinum ) by utilizing quorum sensing (QS) to coordinate virulence factors. This study evaluates biopriming as a biological strategy to induce endogenous defence mechanisms. Drawing from previously published in silico evidence [ 1 ] identifying the flavonoid Quercetin as a high-affinity quorum sensing inhibitor (QSI). we evaluated whether specific rhizobacteria could induce endogenous phenolic accumulation. FEG-SEM analysis confirmed successful rhizoplane colonization and the presence of multicellular bacterial aggregates. Using exogenous Quercetin as a positive control, a 32-day pot experiment compared the efficacy of AHL (N-acyl homoserine lactone)-producing PGPR ( Ensifer meliloti and Klebsiella pneumoniae ) against the Psy pathogen. The results indicate a significant priming effect; while the Quercetin control inhibited the pathogen, biopriming with AHL-producing PGPR triggered a superior systemic biochemical defence response. Bioprimed plants challenged with Psy showed improved growth parameters, with shoot lengths reaching 52.3 cm and a 12-fold increase in Total Phenolic Content (~ 987 µg/g). The substantial increase in Phenylalanine Ammonia-Lyase (PAL) activity (271 µ g/min/g ) confirms that rhizobacterial AHL signalling directly activates the host phenylpropanoid pathway, accelerating the accumulation of protective phenolic compounds and phytoalexin precursors to suppress pathogen proliferation. This research demonstrates that AHL-producing PGPR can enhance chickpea resistance by modulating host secondary metabolism and potentially interfering with pathogen quorum sensing.

title: Predictive Urban Scale Digital Twins For Optimising Solar Panel Energy Yield
summary: Abstract The adoption of smart, renewable energy systems in developing regions is often challenging due to the cost associated with obtaining proprietary spatial data and dependence on forecasting models that do not adequately capture local
content: Abstract The adoption of smart, renewable energy systems in developing regions is often challenging due to the cost associated with obtaining proprietary spatial data and dependence on forecasting models that do not adequately capture localised microclimate phenomena. We present a physics driven AI digital twin to optimise solar energy infrastructure planning using an educational institution as a case study for the pilot application in this research work. Current solar assessment methodologies often isolate spatial mapping from temporal forecasting. They also utilise machine learning models that neglect thermodynamic laws and in some instances, they ignore region specific energy drawbacks such as periodic harmattan dust soiling, and extreme thermal degradation. We resolve these limitations by integrating open source geospatial intelligence (OpenStreetMap) and physics constrained machine learning. The methodology utilises a modular physics engine to calculate metrics such as building level shading factors and baseline thermal degradation. These physical representations serve as the features for an optimised LightGBM gradient boosting predictive model trained on hourly ERA5 meteorological data, to accurately forecast 8,760 hour temporal energy yields. We also deploy a spatial nearest neighbour algorithm to triangulate unnamed structures with local road networks/landmarks to generate an automated operational directory. The resulting framework is an interactive 3D WebGL digital twin which includes financial and environmental dashboards that can be localised based on the region. The model quantifies the exact energy losses attributed to seasonal dust or heat and the deployment strategy targets the highest yield, lowest shading facilities.

title: A Conceptual Blockchain Architecture for Ecological–Financial Risk Management in Blue Carbon Markets
summary: Blue carbon finance is constrained by unreliable ecological data, information asymmetry, and high compliance demands. This study develops an ecological–financial governance interface within a conceptual six-layer blockchain architecture for
content: Blue carbon finance is constrained by unreliable ecological data, information asymmetry, and high compliance demands. This study develops an ecological–financial governance interface within a conceptual six-layer blockchain architecture for blue carbon finance. The design combines versioned on-chain and off-chain records with a multi-party signature approval workflow and five contract modules. It is intended to support traceable hand-offs among ecological monitoring, methodology-governed accounting, MRV, credit-state management, and financial risk review. The contribution is a defined sequence from versioned ecological evidence to accounting review, credit-state records and authorised financial decisions. A synthetic worked example makes these decision rules explicit while retaining independent MRV and registry authority.

title: Assessing the Carbon Footprint of Wrap-Faced Retaining Walls: A Comprehensive Life-Cycle Evaluation in Bangladesh
summary: In the field of geotechnical engineering, there's a growing emphasis on climate-friendly and sustainable approaches, leading to a heightened demand for solutions that integrate technical, ecological, and aesthetic considerations. In respons
content: In the field of geotechnical engineering, there's a growing emphasis on climate-friendly and sustainable approaches, leading to a heightened demand for solutions that integrate technical, ecological, and aesthetic considerations. In response, life cycle assessment (LCA) has become increasingly important as a method for assessing the environmental effects of geotechnical engineering projects. This paper focuses on a soil and water soil and water bioengineering construction project that utilizes geotextile to construct a wrap-faced retaining wall. The objective is to evaluate the wall's contribution to global warming potential (GWP) by evaluating its CO2 emissions. The results highlight the significant environmental advantages of soil and water soil and water bioengineering compared to conventional approaches, especially in terms of global warming potential (GWP). The selection of materials is crucial in determining this benefit, as wrap-faced walls exhibit significantly reduced carbon footprints in comparison to conventional alternatives such as reinforced concrete (RC) walls and mechanically stabilized earth (MSE) walls. The carbon footprint of soil and water soil and water bioengineering constructions is estimated to be nine times lower than RC walls and three times lower than MSE walls, indicating a notable reduction in emissions associated with their construction and utilization. This comprehensive approach ensures a thorough examination of the environmental impact throughout the entire lifecycle of soil and water soil and water bioengineering projects, facilitating informed decision-making and sustainable practices in construction and bioengineering.

title: Integrating Urban Air Mobility Into Commercial Airspace: A Bibliometric Review of Regulatory Challenges
summary: Abstract Urban Air Mobility (UAM) has emerged as a transformative aviation concept with the potential to alleviate ground congestion losses and redefine passenger and cargo transportation within urban environments through the deployment of
content: Abstract Urban Air Mobility (UAM) has emerged as a transformative aviation concept with the potential to alleviate ground congestion losses and redefine passenger and cargo transportation within urban environments through the deployment of electric and autonomous aerial systems. However, the integration of UAM into commercial airspace remains significantly constrained by fragmented and underdeveloped regulatory frameworks. This research investigates the challenges and gaps associated with global UAM regulatory frameworks through a multi-phase methodological approach integrating PRISMA screening, bibliometric analysis, and hybrid deductive–inductive coded literature review. Bibliometric assessment conducted using VOSviewer identified thematic evolution, academic collaboration patterns, influential contributors, and citation relationships across the existing body of knowledge. The findings indicate that current research remains predominantly technology-oriented, with comparatively limited focus on regulatory frameworks. Coding literature review identified airspace management, infrastructure, vehicle certification, and societal acceptance as the most critical regulatory challenges, while legal liability and AI governance remain substantially underexplored. The study further highlights collaborative harmonisation among regulators, policymakers, and industry stakeholders as the most widely proposed mitigation strategy. Overall, the research establishes a significant gap between technological advancement and regulatory preparedness, thereby underscoring the necessity for globally coordinated, scalable, and adaptive regulatory frameworks to support safe and sustainable UAM integration.

title: Hybrid aerogel-loaded ticagrelor cationic hyalurosomes as a platform for wound healing management; in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo studies
summary: Background This study aims to evaluate the restorative effects of ticagrelor (TIC), a well-known antiplatelet drug, on wound-healing capacity using cationic hyalurosomes loaded into an aerogel. Methods The ethanol injection method was used
content: Background This study aims to evaluate the restorative effects of ticagrelor (TIC), a well-known antiplatelet drug, on wound-healing capacity using cationic hyalurosomes loaded into an aerogel. Methods The ethanol injection method was used to produce cationic hyalurosomes, which were then optimized using a D-optimal design with the type of surfactant (X1), hyaluronic acid (HA) amount (mg) (X2), and phospholipid (PC) amount (mg) (X3) as independent variables. The impact of these variables on the entrapment efficiency (EE%, Y1), particle size (PS, Y2), and zeta potential (ZP, Y3) was evaluated. Results In vitro assessments revealed that the spherical optimum formula had an EE% of 73.23% ± 0.27%, a PS of 162.95 ± 0.05 nm, a polydispersity index (PDI) of 0.471 ± 0.004, and a ZP of 27.76 ± 0.77 mV. The optimum formula was stable for up to 90 days. Ex vivo examination using confocal laser scanning microscopy revealed that the optimum formula, labeled with fluorescein, was well deposited throughout the skin. Differential scanning calorimetry studies showed complete encapsulation of TIC within vesicles. The in vitro release study showed a sustained release profile from the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes-loaded aerogel compared to TIC suspension, TIC aerogel, and the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes. In vivo assessments concluded better skin deposition of the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes-loaded aerogel and good healing capacity. Moreover, histopathological assessment confirmed the safety of using the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes aerogel, with no evidence of inflammation. Conclusion In conclusion, the optimum TIC-loaded hyalurosomes-loaded aerogel facilitates wound healing and is a viable option for wound management.

title: The Structural Transformation of Climate Policy: A Comparative Content Analysis of Turkish and International Climate Policy Discourses
summary: Global climate change has evolved into a multidimensional crisis reshaping national and international policy priorities. The primary purpose of this study is to examine the structural transformation of the global climate regime and comparat
content: Global climate change has evolved into a multidimensional crisis reshaping national and international policy priorities. The primary purpose of this study is to examine the structural transformation of the global climate regime and comparatively evaluate Türkiye’s discursive and institutional positioning within this landscape. Specifically, this research answers two key questions: (1) Through which policy documents can the historical and thematic turning points of the global climate regime be identified? and (2) Which conceptual frameworks dominate Türkiye’s national climate documents, and how closely do they align with global texts? Grounded in a qualitative document analysis framework exploring policy discourse, the methodology employs a document-based comparative content analysis utilizing deductive and interpretive approaches. Supported by ATLAS.ti25, 64 international and national policy, scientific, and institutional documents were systematically coded across five themes: mitigation, adaptation, loss and damage, finance, and just transition. Findings reveal that while Türkiye’s policies show increasing thematic diversification and institutionalization after 2010, alignment with the international agenda remains partial. Mitigation and financing themes frequently lack the thematic depth and detailed financial models present in global texts. Crucially, while emergent global concepts such as "Just Transition" are late and underdeveloped, the "Loss & Damage" theme remains entirely absent from Turkish policy documents. The study concludes that Türkiye requires a more proactive, multi-sectoral approach to achieve full thematic depth and financial sustainability in its climate governances.

title: Research dynamics and future direction of Korean pine (Pinus koraiensis): a global bibliometric analysis
summary: Korean pine is a five-needle big arbor pine species that dominated at natural coniferous broadleaved mixed forests in temperate regions, with the functions of high-quality timber, and pine nut production as well as potential ornamental and
content: Korean pine is a five-needle big arbor pine species that dominated at natural coniferous broadleaved mixed forests in temperate regions, with the functions of high-quality timber, and pine nut production as well as potential ornamental and healthy wood entablement.However, a quantitative analysis of the global research landscape of Korean pine has been lacking and hindering a unified understanding of the field's trajectory.This study employs bibliometric analysis on 682 articles from the Web of Science database , to map the global research landscape of Korean pine and to identify future research directions.Result exhibits an average annual publication growth rate of 9.15% with overall trend best described by a logarithmic model (R 2 = 0.832), dominated by 76.83% publications from China, and Northeast Forestry University emerged as the leading institute.The collaboration network is highly polarized, with China at the center of it having strong Asia-Pacific affiliation and presenting a significant opportunity to deepen scientific ties with Western countries.Thematic evolution has no longer been grounded in studies on growth and ecology, but new frontiers are being set on climate change resilience, genetic diversity, and biotechnology.This strategic analysis references researchers to priority research on genetics & breeding, and ecological interactions of Korean pine, and supports two management innovations: genetically informed restoration using improved or locally adapted Korean pine material, and adaptive ecosystem-based management that integrates species interactions, mixed stand planning, and ecological monitoring.

title: A Targeted Review on Lignin and Its Depolymerization Methodologies
summary: The surge in demand for renewable energy and bio-based chemicals has heightened attention on lignocellulosic biomass as an alternative to fossil-derived resources. Lignin, a major component of lignocellulosic biomass, is not used to a suffi
content: The surge in demand for renewable energy and bio-based chemicals has heightened attention on lignocellulosic biomass as an alternative to fossil-derived resources. Lignin, a major component of lignocellulosic biomass, is not used to a sufficient extent despite its potential as a renewable resource for multiple important chemicals and biofuels. This survey examines extraction, characterisation, and decomposition of lignin, highlighting recent innovations and hurdles in lignin valorisation. Various lignin isolation techniques, such as kraft lignin, soda lignin, organosolv lignin, ionic liquids, hydrolysis lignin and deep eutectic solvents, are explored, emphasizing their impact on lignin purity and structural integrity. Analytical methods including NMR, FTIR, GPC, TGA, and DSC provide critical insights into lignin’s complex chemical structure and physicochemical properties. The review also investigates diverse depolymerisation strategies: acid-catalysed, base-catalysed, metal-catalysed, hydrogenolysis, electrocatalytic oxidative and reductive reaction pathways and microwave-assisted processes focusing on their efficiency, selectivity, and applicability for industrial-scale to convert lignin into value-added products. Despite technological advancements, problems such as lignin’s structural heterogeneity, high energy requirements for processing, low yields, and catalyst costs impede widespread commercialisation. Future research should address cost-effective, recyclable catalysts, process integration within biorefineries, and optimisation strategies to enhance economic feasibility. Advancing lignin valorisation technologies is vital for achieving a circular bioeconomy and reducing dependence on fossil-based resources.

title: Exogenous γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) application delays physiological damage caused by acute water deficit in Persian lime
summary: Persian lime (Citrus latifolia) is one of Mexico's most important fruit crops and is increasingly exposed to sudden drought events caused by climate change. This study evaluated the effect of foliar γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) application on
content: Persian lime (Citrus latifolia) is one of Mexico's most important fruit crops and is increasingly exposed to sudden drought events caused by climate change. This study evaluated the effect of foliar γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) application on the physiological response of Persian lime plants subjected to acute water deficit. Six-month-old plants grafted onto Volkameriana rootstock were treated with 100 mM GABA and subjected to 14 days of irrigation withdrawal, followed by 7 days of rewatering. We assessed chlorophyll fluorescence, gas exchange, and plant water relations. Untreated plants exhibited severe physiological decline, irreversible tissue dehydration, and failed to recover after rewatering. In contrast, GABA-treated plants maintained photosynthetic performance, delayed physiological damage, and showed a clear trend toward physiological recovery after rewatering. Two-way ANOVA showed significant effects of irrigation, GABA, and their interaction. Foliar GABA application enhanced tolerance to acute water deficit by preserving photosynthetic function.

title: The role of benefit-cost analysis in water supply and sanitation project decisions: A qualitative study of three multilateral development banks
summary: Abstract Benefit-cost analysis commonly guides resource allocation in multilateral development banks (MDBs), but there has been limited qualitative evidence exploring its role in decision-making processes. This study examines how benefit-co
content: Abstract Benefit-cost analysis commonly guides resource allocation in multilateral development banks (MDBs), but there has been limited qualitative evidence exploring its role in decision-making processes. This study examines how benefit-cost analysis is deployed in water supply and sanitation projects financed by three major MDBs: the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank, and the African Development Bank. We employed an applied qualitative approach, utilising interviews and focus group discussions with MDB staff. Topic guides focused on experiences from 13 recent projects, and on processes through which benefit-cost analyses were developed and how results informed decision-making. We analysed data using an interpretivist approach, applying both inductive and deductive coding in framework analysis. In doing so, we develop a conceptual framework for benefit-cost analysis development in MDBs, and its use in their decision-making. We find that benefit-cost analysis is generally performed before project approval and regarded as a critical element of project appraisal. However, we identified several barriers, including data quality limitations, difficulty in identifying and measuring health and non-health impacts, and inadequate planning for the monitoring of benefits during project implementation. Furthermore, while stakeholders beyond MDBs (e.g. partner governments) are often consulted during model development, their role in the process was typically limited to provision of input data and contextual information rather than in-depth contributions. Recommendations emerging from the analysis include: updating guidelines (particularly with respect to identifying benefit types); linking benefits to external data sources; training MDB staff on guideline implementation; and establishing a database of benefit-cost models to support cross-learning across projects and contexts.

title: From digital to green: the effect of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity
summary: Digital transformation is a key driver of the optimization and upgrading of China’s economic structure and a core element in the transition of China’s economic and social development towards green growth. This paper empirically analyzes the
content: Digital transformation is a key driver of the optimization and upgrading of China’s economic structure and a core element in the transition of China’s economic and social development towards green growth. This paper empirically analyzes the impact of corporate digital transformation on pollution emission intensity and its mechanisms. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly enhances corporate pollution emission intensity. The effect is more significant for enterprises in labor-intensive enterprises, and heavily polluting enterprises. Management efficiency, green technological innovation, and total factor productivity are important mechanisms through which digital transformation improves pollution emission intensity. This study provides empirical evidence and policy references for China to explore new paths for green and transformative development.

title: Twin transformation – an empirical analysis of the interplay between sustainability and digital transformation in German legacy media companies
summary: Sustainability and digitalisation are two transformations reshaping the economy, ecology, politics, and society. Their synergy, known as twin transformation, is becoming increasingly important for decision-makers and academia. This study ex
content: Sustainability and digitalisation are two transformations reshaping the economy, ecology, politics, and society. Their synergy, known as twin transformation, is becoming increasingly important for decision-makers and academia. This study examines twin transformation in large German legacy media companies through document analysis and qualitative expert interviews. Media companies are of particular interest due to their dual role as both sustainable actors and influential communicators, influencing public perception while navigating complex digital shifts. The results indicate that sustainability and digital transformation are predominantly approached separately in German legacy media, with only a few projects embodying the twin transformation approach. Structural decentralisation, regulatory gaps, and fragmented IT systems present major challenges to implementation. Nevertheless, the interviewees regard twin transformation as a valuable, though organisationally demanding, approach to business development.

title: Economic and mathematical modelling of innovative development of the agricultural sector.
summary: Purpose: To develop an economic and mathematical model of innovation development in the agricultural sector to quantitatively assess the impact of capital investment, human capital, and energy efficiency on agricultural value added in Ukrai
content: Purpose: To develop an economic and mathematical model of innovation development in the agricultural sector to quantitatively assess the impact of capital investment, human capital, and energy efficiency on agricultural value added in Ukraine, accounting for energy efficiency factors. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study combined a systematic review of scientific literature with economic-statistical and economic-mathematical modelling. The analysis was based on official data from the State Statistics Service of Ukraine and Eurostat for 2014–2024 to evaluate relationships between investment, human capital, energy efficiency, and agricultural performance. Linear and log-linear regression models were estimated by ordinary least squares (11 annual observations for 2014–2024), with multicollinearity testing (VIF) and residual diagnostics; EU-27 trends were analysed using descriptive and correlation analysis. Research Limitations: The analysis relies on macro-level data and does not examine enterprise-level differences. Future research should incorporate firm-level indicators and institutional factors. Findings: Capital investment promotes technological modernisation and production efficiency, while qualified human capital enhances labour productivity and innovation capacity. Energy-efficient technologies reduce resource consumption, optimise production costs, and strengthen sustainability. Hybrid and digital analytical models improve forecasting accuracy and support management under market and environmental uncertainty. The findings confirm that investment, technology transfer, human capital, and energy efficiency significantly contribute to agricultural competitiveness and sustainable growth in Ukraine and the European Union. Practical Implication: The results support evidence-based policies promoting investment, workforce development, and energy-efficient technologies. Social Implication: Innovation strengthens rural development, environmental sustainability, and food security. Originality/Value: The study provides an integrated quantitative framework linking investment, human capital, and energy efficiency to agricultural value creation. The novelty lies in including energy consumption as an explicit factor alongside capital investment and human capital indicators (employment, personnel costs and wages) in a single value-added model for Ukraine, complemented by an EU-27 analysis of energy productivity and labour dynamics, whereas existing approaches assess these factors separately (Table 1).

title: States Matter
summary: National policies have dominated public policy research, teaching, and discourse in India, yet states have authored impactful innovations in their quest for solutions to problems specific to their requirements. States Matter places the stat
content: National policies have dominated public policy research, teaching, and discourse in India, yet states have authored impactful innovations in their quest for solutions to problems specific to their requirements. States Matter places the states at the core of India’s public policy story through twenty carefully curated case studies of major policy initiatives across eleven states over four decades (1970–2010). Drawing on the policy cycle framework, this book explains how states identify problems, place them on the public agenda, design state-specific interventions, choose policy instruments, negotiate implementation challenges, and shape long-term outcomes. The study combines comparative case analysis with archival research and insights drawn from the authors’ extensive administrative experience and access to policymakers across state and central governments. Case studies cover a wide range of state interventions from Nagaland, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Delhi, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh, examining sectors including education, electricity, sanitation, forestry, livelihoods, and urban infrastructure. This book offers one of the few systematic applications of tools of policy analysis to the Indian context. It is essential reading for students, scholars, and practitioners in public policy, political science, public administration, development studies, and South Asian studies. Bridging academic theory and administrative practice, it provides unique comparative insights into four decades of policymaking across states and sectors, reshaping discussions on federalism, decentralization, state capacity, implementation challenges, and political economy.

title: Water‐Conscious Governance: The Role of Co‐Opted Members in Water Withdrawal
summary: ABSTRACT This study investigates the impact of co‐opted board directors on water withdrawal. Based on a U.S. sample of 4194 firm‐year observations between 2008 and 2022, we find that the presence, independence and tenure of co‐opted directo
content: ABSTRACT This study investigates the impact of co‐opted board directors on water withdrawal. Based on a U.S. sample of 4194 firm‐year observations between 2008 and 2022, we find that the presence, independence and tenure of co‐opted directors reduce firm water withdrawals. Co‐opted directors can play a constructive role in improving corporate water management by aligning with the CEO environmental initiatives, responding to legitimacy pressures, and supporting strategies that balance profit with stakeholder concerns. Additional analyses reveal that this relationship is stronger when the CEO and board chair roles are separated and in firms with strong corporate governance and environmental performance, as well as in firms that link executive compensation to CSR performance. Also, we show that the effect is prevalent in firms with CSR and nomination committees. Our findings offer new insights for regulators and managers seeking to address water management issues and encourage firms to improve their board structure by increasing board co‐option to better align board decisions with CEO water management policies.

title: Combating Urban Air Pollution in Indonesia: Recent Advances in Electrospun Nanofiber Membranes for High-Efficiency Particulate Matter Capture
summary: Indonesia faces a severe air pollution crisis, with average PM2.5 concentrations exceeding WHO guidelines by more than sevenfold and contributing to an estimated 13% of annual deaths nationwide. Emerging evidence further links PM2.5 exposur
content: Indonesia faces a severe air pollution crisis, with average PM2.5 concentrations exceeding WHO guidelines by more than sevenfold and contributing to an estimated 13% of annual deaths nationwide. Emerging evidence further links PM2.5 exposure to increased vulnerability to viral infections, including COVID-19 and influenza, compounding the country's public health burden. Conventional personal protective equipment, predominantly petroleum-based polypropylene masks, offers only short-lived electrostatic filtration and generates substantial non-biodegradable waste, undermining both protective efficacy and environmental sustainability. Electrospinning has emerged as a promising alternative, enabling the fabrication of nanofiber membranes with diameters from 10 nm to the submicron scale that achieve high particulate filtration efficiency at low pressure drop through mechanisms including interception, inertial impaction, Brownian diffusion, and electrostatic capture. This review synthesizes recent advances across single- and multi-spinneret fabrication techniques, bead-on-string architectures, and post-treatment strategies for optimizing filtration performance. It further examines the development of biodegradable polymer membranes, upcycled waste-derived nanofibers, and multifunctional designs incorporating antimicrobial, antiviral, and humidity-resistant properties tailored to tropical urban conditions. These innovations collectively achieve filtration efficiencies exceeding 99% while addressing plastic waste accumulation. This review proposes a practical roadmap toward sustainable, multifunctional electrospun membranes capable of mitigating both urban air pollution and airborne pathogen transmission in Indonesia's rapidly urbanizing tropical cities.

title: From Lab to Plant: Metrics‐Driven Scale‐Up Routes and Application Deployment of Covalent Organic Frameworks
summary: Comprehensive Summary The transition of Covalent Organic Frameworks (COFs) from laboratory‐scale curiosities to industrially scalable technologies has been constrained by challenges in cost‐effective, large‐scale synthesis. Most COF researc
content: Comprehensive Summary The transition of Covalent Organic Frameworks (COFs) from laboratory‐scale curiosities to industrially scalable technologies has been constrained by challenges in cost‐effective, large‐scale synthesis. Most COF research has focused on small‐scale production, whereas practical applications require processes that scale to kilogram‐ and ton‐level manufacturing. Recent advances, including solvent‐free melting polycondensation, mechanochemical synthesis, mild aqueous methods, and continuous flow techniques, are overcoming these obstacles, making large‐scale COF production increasingly viable. This review introduces the principles for scalable COF manufacturing, emphasizing quality control, synthetic efficiency, sustainability, and economic feasibility. We provide a comprehensive over‐view of the latest synthetic strategies that enable the high‐quality production of COFs at scale. We also highlight the applications of large‐scale COFs in environmental remediation, gas and liquid separations, catalysis, CO 2 capture, and energy storage, emphasizing the impact of scalability on real‐world deployment. Finally, we discuss the future industrialization of COFs, focusing on expanding chemistry diversity, enhancing processing techniques, and improving device integration, ultimately paving the way for COF‐based technologies to transition from lab‐scale discoveries to industrial realities. Key Scientists

title: Robonomics
summary: ROBONOMICS: A Toolbox for Analysing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems presents a systematic framework for an emerging discipline devoted to the study of how artificial intelligence, robotics, and automation are reshaping contemporary soc
content: ROBONOMICS: A Toolbox for Analysing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems presents a systematic framework for an emerging discipline devoted to the study of how artificial intelligence, robotics, and automation are reshaping contemporary socioeconomic systems. Combining insights from economics and sociology, Riccardo Campa develops an interdisciplinary approach to analysing the robonomic system. Through conceptual, scientometric, and socioeconomic analyses, the book examines the evolution of industrial revolutions, the rise of intelligent machines, and their impact on productivity, employment, and social organisation. More than a survey of current debates, this book provides both a conceptual foundation and a diagnostic toolbox for understanding one of the most profound socioeconomic transformations of the twenty-first century.

title: Scientific Symbiosis: Bridging Expertise and Fostering Effective Collaborations with Mass Spectrometrists
summary: Mass spectrometry (MS) is increasingly used to answer biological questions, yet effective collaboration between mass spectrometrists and researchers in other fields can be limited by differences in terminology, expectations, and familiarity
content: Mass spectrometry (MS) is increasingly used to answer biological questions, yet effective collaboration between mass spectrometrists and researchers in other fields can be limited by differences in terminology, expectations, and familiarity with analytical workflows. This review provides a practical and accessible guide to incorporating MS into biological and environmental research with an emphasis on improving communication and collaboration. In the review, we walk through the MS workflow including defining the scientific question, selecting an analytical approach, sample collection and preparation, instrumental analysis, data processing, quality assessment, and interpretation. Particular attention is given to concepts that commonly create confusion across fields, including quantitative strategies, analytical controls, sample handling, instrument monitoring, and data reporting expectations. We also discuss the respective roles of both experimentalists and mass spectrometrists throughout the research process and highlight areas where early communication can prevent downstream problems. To support real-world application, the review includes a glossary of commonly used MS terminology and a checklist of key considerations for collaborative studies. Together, these resources are intended to make MS workflows more approachable and to foster the kind of scientific symbiosis between researchers and mass spectrometrists that is needed to generate high-quality, interpretable, and meaningful data.

title: Improper destruction of seized illicit drugs in Asian countries causes environmental and forensic harm and requires a sustainable disposal framework
summary: Drug destruction is a key part of a holistic approach to drug control management-not only within Asian countries but worldwide-due to the vast volumes of illicit drugs confiscated every year. Despite the fact that the emphasis on drug contr
content: Drug destruction is a key part of a holistic approach to drug control management-not only within Asian countries but worldwide-due to the vast volumes of illicit drugs confiscated every year. Despite the fact that the emphasis on drug control has been on seizures, the techniques for destroying seized drugs are still generally archaic, scientifically deficient and environmentally damaging. This is particularly true in many Asian countries that seize vast amounts of illegal substances each year. A comprehensive review of drug destruction methods and environmental contamination potential and public health impact within various Asian locations are discussed here. Problems with current destruction practices from a chemical and environmental viewpoint are outlined. The topic of environmentally sustainable drug destruction techniques that do not compromise the integrity of forensic evidence is certainly one that must be addressed.

title: Mechanical Optimization of the UPMSat-3 Platform for Satellite Constellation Industrialization
summary: The rapid expansion of the satellite constellation market requires spacecraft platforms designed for highly scalable manufacturing, increased production throughput, and agile integration workflows. This work presents the mechanical optimiza
content: The rapid expansion of the satellite constellation market requires spacecraft platforms designed for highly scalable manufacturing, increased production throughput, and agile integration workflows. This work presents the mechanical optimization of the UPMSat-3 microsatellite bus to facilitate its transition toward serial industrial production. A modular structural redesign is developed based on Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DFMA) principles, shifting traditional serial stacked integration into a parallel assembly scheme enabled by kinematic self-aligning guides, thereby decoupling assembly tasks, eliminating integration bottlenecks, and streamlining production line efficiency. Concurrently, high-pressure injection molding and fused deposition modeling (FDM) using 30% short-carbon-fiber-reinforced polyetheretherketone (PEEK-CF30) are evaluated as industrial manufacturing alternatives to conventional machined Aluminum 7075-T6. Preliminary structural feasibility is analyzed through Finite Element Method (FEM) simulations under representative launch load conditions. Quantitative results demonstrate an 8.43% reduction in global assembly complexity (CTotal) driven by a 38.36% drop in handling complexity (C1) alongside the potential for structural mass reduction through the use of PEEK-CF30. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating modular architectures with high-throughput polymer processes as a viable strategy to enhance manufacturing capacity and shorten lead times in the industrialization of future satellite constellations.

title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas
summary: Abstract HFO-1336mzz(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).
content: Abstract HFO-1336mzz(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhalation toxicity, bone marrow micronucleus, and embryonic developmental toxicity experiments were conducted, and the potential toxic effects and mechanisms were comprehensively analyzed through the integration of molecular docking, functional enrichment analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that the 4-h LC50 of HFO-1336mzz(E) in both male and female rats was approximately 31,600 ppm, which is classified as Category 5 according to the Globally Harmonized System (GHS). Under high-dose exposure, the primary target organs were the lung and liver, characterized mainly by acute tissue responses dominated by congestion. Following low-to-moderate dose exposure, the physiological condition of the animals gradually recovered, and no extensive structural damage to tissues was observed. Under short-term inhalation exposure and repeated exposure during pregnancy, this compound did not induce significant genotoxicity, while only limited developmental toxicity effects were observed under the tested conditions. Further mechanistic analyses suggested that its potential toxic effects may involve disturbances in heme-dependent redox systems and energy metabolism pathways. These effects may be associated with the regulation of oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling pathways, which could subsequently influence local microcirculatory homeostasis and tissue perfusion status. This study systematically provides insights into the biological basis of the acute inhalation toxicity of HFO-1336mzz(E). Moreover, a multidimensional toxicological evaluation and mechanistic analysis framework for novel environmentally friendly insulating gases was established, providing important scientific support for risk assessment, safety standard formulation, and refined management in engineering applications.

title: HPLC-MS/MS enantiomeric profiling of amino acids in honey for authentication and traceability using a dilute-and-shoot strategy and a teicoplanin-based chiral stationary phase
summary: Honey authentication and traceability require analytical approaches capable of capturing chemical features related to botanical and geographical origin. In this study, a sensitive high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrome
content: Honey authentication and traceability require analytical approaches capable of capturing chemical features related to botanical and geographical origin. In this study, a sensitive high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method based on direct chiral separation was developed and validated for the enantiomeric profiling of amino acids in honey. A teicoplanin-based stationary phase was employed to separate 19 amino acid pairs, including proteogenic and non-proteogenic compounds, without derivatisation. A simple dilute-and-shoot-based strategy was selected as sample treatment involving dilution with water, centrifugation, filtration and methanol addition was optimised to minimize matrix effects (<±20%) and improve method performance. Under the optimised conditions, 18 amino acid enantiomers were successfully resolved within 40 min, whereas histidine was not enantio-resolved. The method showed high sensitivity, with limits of detection and quantification ranging from 2 to 100 μg/kg and from 6 to 340 μg/kg, respectively. Calibration responses were linear over the investigated concentration range, precision was good enough (relative standard deviations were below 9%), and recoveries ranged from 86 to 113%. The analytical procedure also showed favourable performance according to two different analytical metrics (Blue Applicability Grade Index; Violet Innovation Grade Index). The method was applied to 15 honey samples of different botanical and geographical origins. L-amino acids predominated, with L-proline being the major compound, while D-aspartic acid showed the highest D/L ratio. Principal component and discriminant analyses demonstrated a stronger differentiation according to botanical than geographical origin, highlighting the potential of amino acid enantiomeric profiles as chemical fingerprints for honey authentication and traceability.

title: Natural Capital Measurement and Applications in Economic and Financial Analysis1
summary: ABSTRACT Natural capital refers to environmental assets that produce economic goods or services used in production or consumption. Today, the concepts of natural capital and the associated ecosystem service flows are being applied beyond th
content: ABSTRACT Natural capital refers to environmental assets that produce economic goods or services used in production or consumption. Today, the concepts of natural capital and the associated ecosystem service flows are being applied beyond their traditional applications in cost‐benefit analysis to a range of topic areas in economics and finance. These broader applications include assessment of physical risks to real estate, insurance, and supply chains, and advancements in modelling economic growth, productivity, and financial risk. These developments have the potential to shift perspectives on economic measurement to include more comprehensive concepts of output and consumption, increase the accuracy of measured productivity and risks, and add precision to our understanding of tradeoffs in resource allocation. We provide an overview of the economic theory underlying natural capital valuation and recent initiatives in natural capital measurement and discuss how new data sources, modeling advances, and frameworks are broadening the application of natural capital concepts and metrics. We include open questions integrated throughout to inform or prompt future scholarly research, model development, and economic measurement.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship and Sustainability in Kenya’s Blue-Green Economy
summary: This volume explores the intersection of youth unemployment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development within Kenya's emerging blue and green economies. Through rigorous analysis and compelling case studies, it illuminates innovative pa
content: This volume explores the intersection of youth unemployment, entrepreneurship, and sustainable development within Kenya's emerging blue and green economies. Through rigorous analysis and compelling case studies, it illuminates innovative pathways for youth-led social enterprises that balance economic viability with positive social and environmental impact. The chapters masterfully examine how soft innovation and creative imitation can address youth unemployment while clarifying the transformative potential of social entrepreneurship for inclusive growth. The text offers a sophisticated theoretical framework complemented by practical strategies for navigating blended finance and developing sustainable business models in resource-constrained environments. What sets this work apart is its seamless integration of academic rigor with actionable insights, making complex concepts accessible without sacrificing intellectual depth. The book presents a holistic approach that transcends traditional economic development paradigms, emphasizing the interconnectedness of innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainability. This volume will be of interest to scholars and students of social work, development studies, business studies, youth studies, social enterprise. It will also appeal to policymakers and stakeholders concerned with youth empowerment, entrepreneurship development, and economic growth initiatives.

title: Agrobiodiversity Renewed by Visionary Farmers: The Role of Underutilized Crops in Mobilizing Local Knowledge, Activating Alternative Food Networks, and Building Resilience
summary: Abstract This research analyses several case studies of underutilized crop farms across Europe, including bere barley grown in Orkney, Scotland; local beans’ landraces in Peloponneso, Greece; local wheat landraces in Piedmont, Italy; and lo
content: Abstract This research analyses several case studies of underutilized crop farms across Europe, including bere barley grown in Orkney, Scotland; local beans’ landraces in Peloponneso, Greece; local wheat landraces in Piedmont, Italy; and local leafy greens in Azore Islands, Portugal. Local neglected and underutilized crops are landraces, varieties, or cultivars that currently have limited use in a given geographic, social, and economic context. However, they play a fundamental role in the local biocultural context and hold great promise for diversifying agricultural systems, enhancing diets, creating resilient agroecosystems, and creating economically viable dynamic value chains. Our research, part of the Horizon 2020 Project RADIANT, Realizing Dynamic Value Chains for Underutilised Crops, highlights how farmers have successfully valourized underutilized crops. They achieved this by collecting and multiplying these crops, rebuilding or reinventing alternative value chains, and building narratives that convey the great potential of such crops. The revival of these underutilized crops in these contexts has played a fundamental role for farmers and the surrounding communities in mobilizing local knowledge, building networks, diversifying economic streams, and strengthening agroecological pathways and agricultural resilience. Underutilized crops play a pivotal role in advancing agroecological transitions by supporting the systematic changes needed to create more sustainable, resilient, and equitable food systems.

title: Agroecological typology of farming households and sustainable agricultural practices in the Equatorial High-Altitude Zone of South-Kivu, Eastern DRC
summary: In the Equatorial High-Altitude Zone (EHAZ) of South Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, smallholder farmers face severe land degradation and climate vulnerability, yet patterns of agroecological practice adoption remain insufficien
content: In the Equatorial High-Altitude Zone (EHAZ) of South Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, smallholder farmers face severe land degradation and climate vulnerability, yet patterns of agroecological practice adoption remain insufficiently characterized. A stratified sample of 374 households in the high-altitude parts of Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu was surveyed on the adoption of sixteen practices during cropping season B of 2025. A typology was built by principal component analysis (PCA), Ward hierarchical clustering and K-means consolidation. Factors associated with type membership were analysed with a bias-reduced multinomial logistic regression (MNLR), and adoption constraints were compared across types with χ² or Fisher tests adjusted by Holm's method. Six principal components (64.0% of the variance) were retained for clustering. Four farmer types were identified: Type 1 (19.8%), conservation-oriented systems combining contour farming, minimum tillage, agroforestry and mulching with little use of external inputs; Type 2 (36.9%), soil-fertility systems based on composting, residue incorporation and minimum tillage, with limited soil cover; Type 3 (11.2%), integrated systems with high adoption of nearly all practices, including external-input practices; and Type 4 (32.1%), soil-cover systems relying on composting, mulching and cover crops but rarely using physical conservation or external inputs.
