Practices formed four co-adoption families (resource-intensive, physical soil management, ecological regulation and foundational practices). Type membership was associated mainly with territory and farm-structural characteristics (land position, farm size, perceived soil fertility and, for Type 2, hired labor), but not with age, gender or farming experience; Kalehe households were found almost only in Types 1 and 3. Lack of resources was most frequently reported in Types 1 (97.3%) and 4 (88.3%), lack of information in Types 1 (97.3%) and 2 (85.5%), high workload in Type 2 (68.1%), and lack of interest in Types 4 (85.0%) and 1 (71.6%). These findings show that farmers combine practices into territory-specific packages and face type-specific constraints. Extension programmes should therefore be differentiated by farmer type, combining access to resources, training and participatory approaches that take farmers' preferences into account.

title: Aligning investment governance for a just energy transition and sustainable development in West Africa
summary: West Africa faces a critical energy deficit affecting around 200 million people, necessitating a shift towards a sustainable low-carbon energy system. The region’s energy framework is heavily influenced by legacy bilateral investment treati
content: West Africa faces a critical energy deficit affecting around 200 million people, necessitating a shift towards a sustainable low-carbon energy system. The region’s energy framework is heavily influenced by legacy bilateral investment treaties (BITs), which favour fossil fuel investments and utilise investor-state dispute settlement mechanisms. This creates conflicts with climate goals and social equity, highlighting the need for a comprehensive overhaul of investment strategies to support decarbonization while reducing legal risks for states. This study employs doctrinal legal analysis and comparative policy assessment to explore the tension between international investment law and the need for a just energy transition in West Africa. It examines key legal instruments, including the ECOWAS Energy Protocol, ECOWAS Common Investment Code (ECOWIC) and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Investment Protocol, revealing a significant disconnect between traditional BITs and modern climate objectives. The study advocates for a shift towards a regional investment framework under the AfCFTA that aligns investor protections with development rights and social equity. Findings indicate that the existing BIT regime poses substantial legal and financial obstacles to regional energy development. By pinpointing these regulatory gaps, the study argues for a harmonised investment framework that reconciles investor protections with climate mandates. It suggests adopting climate-sensitive policy tools, such as climate carve-outs and local content requirements, alongside revitalising financially distressed utilities. This strategic approach aims to enhance economic viability and promote social equity, providing a robust framework for aligning international investment obligations with the urgent needs of a just energy transition.

title: Bridging Vulnerability and Readiness: ESG Disclosure and Climate Change Adaptation in GCC Countries
source: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
summary: ABSTRACT The rising urgency of climate change has resulted in the need for corporations to embrace effective climate‐related strategies to achieve the goals of global sustainability. ESG has become a key strategy through which companies hav
content: ABSTRACT The rising urgency of climate change has resulted in the need for corporations to embrace effective climate‐related strategies to achieve the goals of global sustainability. ESG has become a key strategy through which companies have been advised to promote their corporate responsibilities as well as climate change adaptation. Despite the availability of studies on the link between ESG performance and climate change adaptation, there has been limited empirical evidence for this relationship in the context of Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries. This study aims at investigating the impact of ESG performance on climate change adaptation among publicly listed companies in the GCC. The study employs an unbalanced panel data of 393 firms, which consists of 1714 firm‐year observations over the period of 2014–2024. We apply the two‐step System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) estimator to control for endogeneity, dynamic panel biases, and heterogeneity. The results of the study indicate that aggregate ESG performance enhances the climate change adaptation among companies operating in the GCC countries. Moreover, the environmental, social, and governance components of ESG all have a positive and significant effect on the climate change adaptation, suggesting that companies which demonstrate better sustainability practices are more likely to adapt climate change‐related initiatives, manage their climate risks more efficiently, and make climate change‐related disclosure improvements. These results point out the necessity to incorporate ESG practices into business strategies in order to speed up climate‐related actions and promote sustainable development. The study makes an important contribution to the existing literature on ESG and climate change as it provides empirical evidence from one of the most carbon‐intensive parts of the world.

title: Maize phytochemicals in stressful environments: impacts and adaptation
summary: Maize ( Zea mays L.) is a globally important cereal crop and a major source of nutrients and bioactive phytochemicals that contribute to food security, human health, and industrial applications. However, increasing environmental stresses, i
content: Maize ( Zea mays L.) is a globally important cereal crop and a major source of nutrients and bioactive phytochemicals that contribute to food security, human health, and industrial applications. However, increasing environmental stresses, including drought, salinity, extreme temperatures, heavy metal contamination, nutrient deficiency, and pathogen attacks, adversely affect maize growth, productivity, and phytochemical composition. In response to these challenges, maize activates intricate adaptive mechanisms involving signaling cascades, transcriptional regulation, metabolic reprogramming, hormonal and reactive oxygen species (ROS) crosstalk, epigenetic regulation, stress-memory mechanisms, gene alteration, and diverse biochemical responses. Stress perception initiates intracellular signaling networks that activate transcription factors regulating stress-responsive genes and metabolic pathways. These processes promote the accumulation of protective phytochemicals, osmolytes, antioxidants, and defense-related metabolites that mitigate oxidative damage and maintain cellular homeostasis. Hormonal interactions with ROS coordinate growth-defense trade-offs, while epigenetic modifications and stress memory enhance tolerance to recurrent environmental stresses. Gene alterations through natural variation, molecular breeding, and genome editing further strengthen stress resilience by improving physiological and biochemical performance. Collectively, these adaptive mechanisms preserve the synthesis and beneficial utilization of maize phytochemicals, including phenolic compounds, flavonoids, carotenoids, anthocyanins, phytosterols, and terpenoids, which possess significant antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, and industrial value. Understanding the integration of these molecular, physiological, and biochemical processes provides a foundation for developing climate-resilient maize cultivars with enhanced phytochemical quality, improved stress tolerance, and sustainable productivity under changing environmental conditions.

title: Optimisation of Biogas Production from Co-Digestion of Organic Waste Streams of Kolhapur Municipal Corporation Using Response Surface Methodology
summary: Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC) generates approximately 488 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, of which nearly 57% is biodegradable organic matter presently disposed of without energy recovery. This study characterises five major o
content: Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC) generates approximately 488 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, of which nearly 57% is biodegradable organic matter presently disposed of without energy recovery. This study characterises five major organic waste streams of KMC — food waste, vegetable market waste, fruit market waste, cattle dung, and slaughterhouse waste — and optimises their co-digestion ratio using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) with a D-optimal mixture design. Individual substrate characterisation revealed complementary carbon-tonitrogen (C/N) profiles, motivating a co-digestion strategy. A 38-run mixture design was executed in bench-scale CSTR digesters, yielding a statistically significant model (F = 48.52, R² = 0.981). The optimised blend — 40% food waste, 25% vegetable waste, 20% fruit waste, 10% cattle dung and 5% slaughterhouse waste — achieved a C/N ratio of 24.8:1 and a specific biogas yield of 724 mL/g VS, validated experimentally within 1% of the model prediction. A conceptual 200 MT/day plant based on this formulation shows techno-economic viability (IRR 18.4%, payback period 6.8 years). The findings demonstrate that systematic co-digestion optimisation, grounded in a rigorous waste characterisation and experimental design methodology, can substantially improve biogas recovery from municipal organic waste in Tier-2 Indian cities.

title: WHOSE CARBON, WHOSE BENEFIT? PANCASILA SOCIAL JUSTICE AND COMMUNITY BENEFIT-SHARING IN INDONESIA'S FOREST CARBON GOVERNANCE
source: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: Indonesia is rebuilding its forest carbon market at the same time as it accelerates the recognition of customary forests, yet the rules that decide who receives carbon revenue have received little legal scrutiny. This article asks whether I
content: Indonesia is rebuilding its forest carbon market at the same time as it accelerates the recognition of customary forests, yet the rules that decide who receives carbon revenue have received little legal scrutiny. This article asks whether Indonesia's emerging benefit-sharing arrangements meet the standard of social justice that the state's foundational philosophy, Pancasila, and the 1945 Constitution impose on the use of natural resources. It first translates three Pancasila principles (just and civilized humanity, deliberative democracy and social justice) into recognitional, procedural and distributive dimensions of justice, and operationalizes them through the four indicators of "the greatest prosperity of the people" developed by the Constitutional Court. It then applies the resulting standard to three instruments: Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025, the benefit-sharing plan of the East Kalimantan jurisdictional emission reductions program, and the project-based rules introduced by Forestry Minister Regulation No. 6 of 2026. The analysis finds that the jurisdictional program performs best on distribution and procedure, that project-based trading performs worst, and that all three tie access to benefits to formal recognition of customary rights, which covered about 345,000 hectares in October 2025 against a target of 1.4 million hectares by 2029. The article proposes six design principles, including a statutory community floor share and eligibility based on de facto stewardship, to close the gap between constitutional promise and carbon practice.

title: Safer sustainable nail polish removers using mechanisms toxicity analysis green solvents and a quantitative sustainability health efficacy framework
summary: Sustainability drives the rethinking of nail polish removers, highlighting the need to balance efficacy, human health, and environmental impact within a single formulation. These products remove nail lacquer through solvent diffusion into t
content: Sustainability drives the rethinking of nail polish removers, highlighting the need to balance efficacy, human health, and environmental impact within a single formulation. These products remove nail lacquer through solvent diffusion into the polymer film, primarily composed of nitrocellulose networks combined with resins and plasticisers, causing swelling and facilitating film dissolution or detachment. Acetone has long dominated because of its rapid and effective action, typically removing polish within 30–60 s. However, its high volatility, strong skin-defatting effect, and contribution to volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions raise concerns for human health and the environment. Ethyl acetate and isopropyl alcohol provide alternative solvent options, although their removal performance depends on formulation and application conditions. Emerging bio-based solvents, including ethyl lactate, γ-valerolactone, and d-limonene, offer potential environmental and toxicological advantages, although their suitability depends on their performance, hazard profiles, cost, odour, and compatibility with formulations. This review synthesises evidence on molecular mechanisms of film dissolution, solvent performance, toxicological risks associated with short- and long-term exposure, occupational evidence from nail salons, and life-cycle environmental impacts. It also evaluates alternative delivery systems, including gel-based removers, pre-soaked wipes, and water-based formulations, in terms of their practicality and potential benefits. As a methodological contribution, the Sustainability–Health–Efficacy (SHE) Index is proposed as a transparent, multi-criteria screening framework for organising existing evidence on nail polish remover solvents. A Hansen-sphere screening approach, a literature-based evaluation of gelled-solvent systems, and a cost-per-treatment scenario are also presented. Illustrative calculations based on literature-derived data demonstrate the framework’s structure and the influence of weighting choices; they do not constitute validated rankings or formulation recommendations. The framework and associated calculations remain unvalidated experimentally, and their interpretation is subject to limitations in data availability, scoring criteria, normalisation procedures, and weighting assumptions. Future progress requires standardised experimental validation, particularly through controlled dissolution tests, nail-plate compatibility assessments, environmental toxicity studies, and verified techno-economic analyses. Such evidence is essential to advance the development of balanced formulations that simultaneously address efficacy, human health, and environmental sustainability.

title: Acceptance before deployment: a systematic review and measurement audit of public acceptance research on four emerging net-zero energy technologies
summary: Abstract Deep decarbonisation increasingly depends on technologies that most citizens have never encountered: small modular reactors (SMRs), hydrogen energy systems, carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), and offshore wind. Public
content: Abstract Deep decarbonisation increasingly depends on technologies that most citizens have never encountered: small modular reactors (SMRs), hydrogen energy systems, carbon capture, utilisation and storage (CCUS), and offshore wind. Public acceptance is widely treated as a make-or-break condition for deployment, yet the evidence has grown in technology-specific silos and has never been audited for how acceptance itself is measured. This PRISMA 2020 systematic review spans all four families. A frozen, benchmark-validated search of Scopus and OpenAlex (16,806 unique records) was screened with a calibrated human–machine workflow (kappa = 0.821; 100% benchmark recall), yielding 689 full-text candidates and 534 included primary studies. Three findings stand out. First, the field is expanding rapidly and asymmetrically: 57% of the evidence post-dates the most recent comprehensive review, with CCUS (217 studies) and hydrogen (186) dominating, offshore wind (136) consolidating, and SMRs (17) markedly under-studied relative to policy salience. Second, study-level associations are directionally consistent for perceived benefit (70% positive), trust (58% positive) and perceived risk (54% negative), but inconsistent for proximity and socio-demographics, challenging distance-based siting heuristics. Third — the central result — the measurement base is thin: only 1.5% of studies reused a pre-validated acceptance instrument, 71.3% relied on ad hoc measures, 82.8% were one-shot cross-sections, 35.2% did not measure familiarity, and 72.7% examined pre-deployment technologies. Much of the literature thus appears to record unstable constructions of unfamiliar objects rather than settled public judgements. A measurement-first agenda — shared instrument cores, mandatory familiarity assessment, deployment-stage-explicit reporting, and longitudinal designs — is proposed.

title: Preferential sub-surface gold layer dissolution during electrical stimulation stability testing of neural electrodes.
summary: OBJECTIVE: Electrode stability is critical for ensuring long-term neural stimulation and recording. This work aims to identify and characterize abiotic failure mechanisms resulting in electrode degradation during stimulation. We studied the
content: OBJECTIVE: Electrode stability is critical for ensuring long-term neural stimulation and recording. This work aims to identify and characterize abiotic failure mechanisms resulting in electrode degradation during stimulation. We studied the stimulation stability of flexible cuff electrodes designed for vagus nerve stimulation, comprised of thin-film Ti/Ir/IrOx electrodes with Ti/Pt/Au traces, under accelerated conditions. Approach: Microfabricated polyimide-based flexible electrodes were stimulation stability (stim-stab) tested using 109 cathodic-leading biphasic current pulses at 12 (n=3) or 16 mA (n=2) (current density of 4.98 A/cm2 or 6.64 A/cm2, respectively). Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and voltage transients (VT) were utilized before and after the stimulation to characterize electrochemical changes. Optical microscopy was used to screen for damage, backscattered scanning electron microscopy to evaluate electrode degradation, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy to examine the composition of the metal stack. Additionally, focused ion beam with scanning electron microscopy captured cross-sectional images of the metal stack, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy was used to measure and image changes in electrode surface composition compared to controls. Main Results: Optical microscopy identified damaged regions on some electrodes, corroborated by backscattered scanning electron microscopy showing damaged areas through morphological and compositional differences. Energy dispersive X-ray analysis determined that visibly damaged regions lost Ir and gold from the electrode stack, while Pt and Ti from electrical traces remained. Focused ion beam cross-sectional analysis revealed regions where highly selective degradation of the gold layer occurred, implicating this process in the failure mechanism. Significance: Gold is frequently employed for neural electrodes due to its bio-inert character, conductivity, and compatibility with microfabrication. Our findings show it can selectively dissolve during neural stimulation relative to the adjacent Ti and Pt layers, beneath a surface that appears intact.

title: Resistance mechanisms and emerging therapies for Proteus mirabilis
summary: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Proteus mirabilis represents a critical challenge for both clinical medicine and food safety. This opportunistic Gram-negative pathogen transmits through contaminated food chains and exhibits intrinsic, acq
content: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Proteus mirabilis represents a critical challenge for both clinical medicine and food safety. This opportunistic Gram-negative pathogen transmits through contaminated food chains and exhibits intrinsic, acquired, and adaptive resistance mechanisms. Intrinsic resistance is driven by constitutive lipopolysaccharide modifications, efflux pumps, and chromosomal β-lactamases. Meanwhile, horizontal gene transfer mediates the acquisition of extended-spectrum β-lactamases, AmpC enzymes, carbapenemases, and aminoglycoside-modifying enzymes. Adaptive traits, including swarming motility, urease-driven alkalinization, and crystalline biofilm formation, further enhance tolerance and persistence. Conventional antibiotics are increasingly ineffective against multidrug resistant (MDR) and extensively drug resistant (XDR) strains, highlighting an urgent need for innovative therapeutic approaches. Complementary strategies such as phage therapy, CRISPR-Cas gene editing, nanoparticles, urease and swarming inhibitors, and plant-derived phytochemicals, have emerged as promising alternatives. Each approach offers unique advantages such as biofilm disruption, precision targeting, or multi-site antimicrobial activity, but faces limitations related to delivery, toxicity, or potency. Future directions require standardized manufacturing, rapid diagnostics, and innovative trial designs that integrate combination therapies to maximize efficacy while minimizing resistance risks. By advancing multi-targeted interventions, the scientific and clinical communities can counteract the resilience of P. mirabilis and safeguard public health and food systems.

title: AI Agents as supporting infrastructure for all-solid-state battery development
summary: Materials discovery increasingly depends on a multiscale ecosystem of simulations, experiments, and shared facilities, yet advances in individual AI tools do not by themselves connect the decisions that link these components. This gap is es
content: Materials discovery increasingly depends on a multiscale ecosystem of simulations, experiments, and shared facilities, yet advances in individual AI tools do not by themselves connect the decisions that link these components. This gap is especially severe in all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), whose development couples electrochemical performance to interfacial stability, mechanics, processing, manufacturability, reliability, safety, and cost. Here we argue that AI agents could support ASSB development toward commercial viability by maintaining a shared decision–evidence state that links materials discovery and optimization to cell-level validation and manufacturing constraints. We develop this argument through three complementary dimensions of scientific agency: coordination across heterogeneous resources, method augmentation across models and scales, and project-level adaptation over time. Cross-domain demonstrations establish several relevant capability primitives, including stateful tool planning, task execution, and delegated analysis. Agents should therefore be evaluated as supporting infrastructure for concurrent ASSB engineering rather than as autonomous replacements for scientific expertise. Their value ultimately lies in driving materials development in the context of interfaces, cell architectures, and manufacturing processes toward the performance, reliability, safety, and cost requirements of ASSB commercialization. context & scale Commercializing all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) requires more than identifying high-performing materials: ion transport, interphase chemistry, mechanics, processing, cell architecture, reliability, safety, and cost impose coupled constraints that can invalidate otherwise promising candidates. This Perspective argues that AI agents could serve as auditable infrastructure, maintaining a decision-evidence state that connects objectives, specimen histories, models, uncertainties, actions, and validation to support ASSB development. Such infrastructure could broaden research across instruments and engineering stages, strengthen validation by linking atomistic, mesoscale, continuum, and experimental descriptions, and preserve evidence and revisions throughout development cycles. Future efforts should move beyond task-level demonstrations toward systematic ASSB development, establishing whether agents can contribute to the development of reliable and economically viable ASSB systems.

title: Chapter 10: IoT-Driven AI for Sustainable Mobility, Resource Optimization, and Green Automotive Technologies
summary: The worldwide transformation of urban transportation toward electrified, shared, and automated mobility creates profound systemic interactions between transportation networks and electrical power grids. While the widespread adoption of elec
content: The worldwide transformation of urban transportation toward electrified, shared, and automated mobility creates profound systemic interactions between transportation networks and electrical power grids. While the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) eliminates tailpipe emissions, uncoordinated fleet charging induces severe distribution substation load spikes, exacerbates transformer thermal aging, and elevates marginal grid carbon intensity. Conversely, when integrated with ubiquitous Internet of Things (IoT) connectivity, advanced artificial intelligence, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) power interfaces, electrified fleets transition from passive electrical loads into distributed, cyber-physical energy storage assets capable of balancing intermittent renewable generation and decarbonizing urban mobility.

title: Governing Travel Through AI-Based Information: Passenger Well-being, Behavioural Change, and Green Choices
summary: Abstract This paper investigates the transformative potential of AI-based real-time crowding information in shaping travel behaviour, passenger well-being, and environmentally sustainable choices in rail transport—addressing both technologi
content: Abstract This paper investigates the transformative potential of AI-based real-time crowding information in shaping travel behaviour, passenger well-being, and environmentally sustainable choices in rail transport—addressing both technological innovation and its socio-economic impacts. Drawing on original stated-preference data from the capacity-constrained “Cinque Terre” railway corridor in Italy, we integrate behavioural indicators with a discrete choice experiment to examine how passengers respond to AI-generated predictions of crowding, delays, fares, and information sources. Our results demonstrate that exposure to such AI-driven information significantly increases passengers’ propensity to adjust departure times and opt for less crowded, lower-emission services. The analysis reveals a substantial willingness to incur delays or monetary costs to avoid severe crowding, highlighting the critical disutility of peak-period congestion. These findings suggest that AI-based information systems can serve as effective demand management tools, delivering well-being gains while supporting sustainable mobility and decarbonisation strategies.

title: Comparing Biosecurity Measures between Commercial Broiler and Layer Farms: Exploring Poultry Farming Biosecurity Practices in Gujarat
summary: Abstract Background Poultry farming is crucial to India's economy, but global trade and the movement of people and animals have raised concerns about disease transmission and antimicrobial resistance. Implementing biosecurity measures on fa
content: Abstract Background Poultry farming is crucial to India's economy, but global trade and the movement of people and animals have raised concerns about disease transmission and antimicrobial resistance. Implementing biosecurity measures on farms can control the spread of infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance. This study aimed to compare the biosecurity practices of commercial broiler and layer farms in Gujarat and provide insights into the measures adopted by farmers in the region. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted using survey questionnaires collected from 74 commercial poultry farmers including 39 broiler and 35 layer farmers. The cleaned data was analyzed using descriptive statistics, factor analysis of mixed data, and hierarchical clustering on principal component. Results The four clusters, with each cluster having a predominant farm type were identified. The biosecurity measures significantly differentiated farms, were: type of farm, rearing system, production cycle per year, level of biosecurity knowledge, source of income, farm previously encountered the disease outbreak and mode of operation. Comparatively layer farmers are well educated, experienced, have good biosecurity knowledge and follow strict biosecurity protocol than the broiler farmers. Additionally, the 79.49% broiler and 71.43% layer of farmers were not knowledgeable about antimicrobial resistance and 38.46% broiler and 91.43% layer farmers were not maintaining records. The majority of farmers agreed that lack of knowledge, skilled manpower and investment limit the implementation. Conclusions The analysis findings can guide strategies to reinforce compliance with critical biosecurity practices by farm type. Educational programs, such as workshops and information sessions, are vital to raise awareness and compliance with biosecurity practices among farmers. Further, establishing a partnership between authorities and farmers can facilitate better implementation of biosecurity measures. This collaborative approach highlights the importance of biosecurity while empowering farmers, fostering a unified effort to prevent diseases in the poultry sector.

title: When the music changes, so must your dance: Technology-forcing regulation and the shifting geography of automotive invention
summary: Technology-forcing regulations can compel incumbent firms to develop capabilities in technologies that lie outside their established knowledge bases. We examine how firms respond to this challenge by reconfiguring the geography and organiza
content: Technology-forcing regulations can compel incumbent firms to develop capabilities in technologies that lie outside their established knowledge bases. We examine how firms respond to this challenge by reconfiguring the geography and organization of invention. Focusing on the automotive industry's transition toward low-emissions technologies, we investigate whether more stringent environmental policies increase incumbent firms' reliance on technological hotspots—locations with specialized knowledge in low-emissions vehicle technologies. We examine two mechanisms through which firms can access this geographically concentrated knowledge: locating inventive activity in hotspots and collaborating with hotspot inventors. Using a comprehensive panel dataset covering more than half a million patent families from incumbent automotive manufacturers and their first-tier suppliers across 311 regions from 1990 to 2020, we find that technology-forcing regulation increases firms' propensity both to locate invention in low-emissions technology hotspots and to collaborate with inventors located there. These findings reveal an important spatial dimension of technology-forcing policy: by increasing firms' need to access specialized knowledge, regulation can reshape not only the direction of technological change but also where and with whom incumbent firms innovate.

title: Post-lithium energy storage selection for the extended sustainable supply chain: a conceptual AHP-based framework illustrated on the Moroccan logistics–energy nexus
source: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
summary: Purpose The paper develops a conceptual framework for selecting post-lithium storage technologies across the heterogeneous nodes of the extended sustainable supply chain, treating strategic sovereignty as a decisional dimension alongside te
content: Purpose The paper develops a conceptual framework for selecting post-lithium storage technologies across the heterogeneous nodes of the extended sustainable supply chain, treating strategic sovereignty as a decisional dimension alongside technical, economic and environmental criteria, and illustrates it on the Moroccan nexus. Design/methodology/approach A four-cluster, twelve-sub-criterion analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is instantiated on five alternatives. The instantiation is illustrative rather than survey-based: each pairwise matrix is generated deterministically from published benchmark values for the 2024–2026 window through a Saaty-capped ratio rule, making the demonstration reproducible. Consistency ratios, a ±20 per cent perturbation test and a prospective 2030–2035 re-parameterisation probe its stability. Findings At 2024–2026 benchmark values no technology dominates: the four leading priorities fall within a 0.034 band, and node re-weighting fragments the ranking into four dominant designs – lithium-ion for long-haul transport (0.226), redox flow for stationary storage (0.237), sodium-ion for micro-grids (0.235) and supercapacitor hybrids for intralogistics (0.275). Three hold across the whole perturbation envelope; long-haul is contested. Separately, under the illustrative 2030–2035 re-parameterisation, long-haul shifts toward sodium-ion and solid-state, which demonstrates horizon dependence rather than forecasting it. Research limitations/implications The elicitation is illustrative: the priorities demonstrate the discriminating capacity of the framework rather than measuring expert preference. An empirical Delphi, a life-cycle-assessment module and an analytic network process (ANP) portfolio extension are the priority developments. Practical implications A time-phased four-pillar hybridisation roadmap for Morocco is derived and stated as testable propositions, conditional on 2024–2026 baseline parameters, with governance and financing corollaries. Originality/value The paper extends sustainable supply chain management by articulating a resource–logistics–energy nexus, raises strategic sovereignty to a fourth decisional dimension and offers a reproducible node-specific selection framework for an African logistics hub.

title: Development of Polymeric Films Based on Gummy Plant Exudates and Natural Plant Fibers
summary: Abstract This study addresses the fabrication of biodegradable polymeric films using gummy plant exudates from Euphorbia cotinifolia ("liberal rojo") and Euphorbia laurifolia ("lechero blanco") as the primary matrix, reinforced with Musa pa
content: Abstract This study addresses the fabrication of biodegradable polymeric films using gummy plant exudates from Euphorbia cotinifolia ("liberal rojo") and Euphorbia laurifolia ("lechero blanco") as the primary matrix, reinforced with Musa paradisiaca (plantain) and Guadua angustifolia (guadua bamboo) fibers. A solvent casting technique was employed to evaluate three formulations with varying exudate concentrations, using glycerol as a plasticizer, poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) as a crosslinking agent, and Tween 80 as an emulsifier. Formulation 2 (60% v/v exudate) exhibited superior mechanical performance, reaching a tensile strength of 9.52 MPa and an elongation at break of 416.52% in E. laurifolia films, significantly outperforming conventional biopolymers. Although natural plant fibers did not improve mechanical resistance due to weak interfacial adhesion with the matrix, they substantially enhanced moisture resistance. Biodegradation assays conducted under ISO 14855 and ASTM D 5988 standards confirmed high biological assimilation and mineralization of the material by soil microorganisms.

title: Beef-on-Dairy Crossbreeding: A Multidimensional Analysis and Gaps for Pasture-Based Production Systems
summary: Beef-on-dairy (BoD) crossbreeding, defined as the planned use of beef sires on dairy dams, has expanded as a strategy to increase the value of dairy-origin calves while maintaining herd replacement requirements. This review critically synth
content: Beef-on-dairy (BoD) crossbreeding, defined as the planned use of beef sires on dairy dams, has expanded as a strategy to increase the value of dairy-origin calves while maintaining herd replacement requirements. This review critically synthesizes research published since 2016 across six interconnected dimensions: genetics and genomics, management and productive efficiency, carcass performance and meat quality, farm economics, environmental sustainability, and animal welfare. The available evidence indicates that BoD can increase calf market value and improve selected growth and carcass traits, although the magnitude of these effects varies with sire genetic merit, dairy breed, reproductive performance, calf management, and finishing conditions. Genetic selection involves balancing calving ease and other functional traits against postnatal growth and carcass merit. Economic outcomes depend not only on calf prices but also on semen costs, reproductive efficiency, replacement requirements, and rearing and finishing expenses; therefore, improvements in individual production traits do not necessarily translate into greater whole-farm profitability. Environmental performance is similarly context-dependent and requires explicit consideration of system boundaries, functional units, emissions intensity, and potential soil carbon sequestration. Animal welfare must also be evaluated throughout the production chain rather than inferred from productive performance alone. A major limitation of the available evidence is its concentration in intensive and semi-intensive production systems, which restricts its transferability to permanent-pasture environments. Further research should prioritize longitudinal, farm-level evaluations from birth to slaughter under defined pasture-based conditions, integrating genetic and management decisions with productive, economic, environmental, and welfare outcomes.

title: Drivers of participation in agribusinesses by agricultural cooperatives: evidence from Thailand
summary: Agricultural cooperatives (ACs) are known for their extensive economic and social contributions. Meanwhile, ACs in Thailand suffer from declining participation in agribusiness operations. Therefore, this research identified the drivers shap
content: Agricultural cooperatives (ACs) are known for their extensive economic and social contributions. Meanwhile, ACs in Thailand suffer from declining participation in agribusiness operations. Therefore, this research identified the drivers shaping agribusiness participation by ACs in terms of agribusiness volume in the northeastern and southern regions of Thailand using primary data collected from 334 ACs. The Tobit regression results showed that the number of members, level of participation, operating capital, number of product types, average payback, goods sold on credit, daily produce collection, and agribusiness network have a positively significant influence on the cooperatives’ participation in terms of agribusiness volume. The study results revealed that agribusiness volume is approximately 12.02 million THB higher in ACs that offer credit sales opportunities and 13.84 million THB higher in ACs that maintain agribusiness networks, compared to ACs that do not provide these services. The findings provide policy direction for the promotion of ACs.

title: CGW-DETR: a multi-scale feature enhanced RT-DETR Qianxi cherry tomato maturity detection model for dense small targets
summary: Detecting the ripeness of QianXi cherry Tomatoes is critical to intelligent harvesting. There are three major challenges associated with this task: (1) Complex environmental interference makes it difficult to extract surface features from t
content: Detecting the ripeness of QianXi cherry Tomatoes is critical to intelligent harvesting. There are three major challenges associated with this task: (1) Complex environmental interference makes it difficult to extract surface features from the tomatoes; (2) High rates of missed detections and false positives when detecting densely clustered small targets; (3) High computational costs due to the large number of model parameters and the significant computational load. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight detection model, CGW-DETR, based on an improved RT-DETR architecture. First, we propose a lightweight feature enhancement module, CAS, to optimize target feature perception and suppress interference from complex backgrounds. Second, we introduce a gradient-space pyramid pooling layer (GSPP) that balances local and global feature extraction through multi-scale spatial pyramid pooling and an efficient layer aggregation network, improving the model’s detection of small and densely clustered targets. Finally, we introduce the WIoU loss function and optimize the gradient gain allocation strategy to improve detection accuracy while maintaining the model’s low computational complexity. Experimental results show that, on our self-built QianXi cherry Tomato ripeness detection dataset, compared to the baseline model RT-DETR, the proposed model achieves a detection accuracy of 94.2% (an increase of 2.0%), a recall rate of 88.2% (an increase of 4.4%), an mAP50 of 91.3% (an increase of 3.1%), and an mAP50:95 of 74.6% (an increase of 5.5%). Under the experimental settings of this study, CGW-DETR showed relatively favorable detection results for densely distributed small-scale QianXi cherry tomatoes in complex environments. Its performance was compared with several mainstream models on the self-built dataset.

title: Basin-Scale Heterogeneity in CO2 Geological Storage: Mechanisms, Prediction, and Management
summary: Abstract Large-scale CO2 geological storage is evolving from stand-alone sites toward million-tonne-scale, clustered, and basin-coordinated deployment, making basin-scale heterogeneity a key constraint on capacity utilization, sustained inj
content: Abstract Large-scale CO2 geological storage is evolving from stand-alone sites toward million-tonne-scale, clustered, and basin-coordinated deployment, making basin-scale heterogeneity a key constraint on capacity utilization, sustained injection, and long-term storage security. However, existing studies have largely focused on individual reservoirs, capacity estimation, or localized risks, while a systematic review integrating tectono-sedimentary evolution, reservoir–caprock assemblages, fault-controlled hydrodynamics, and multisite interference remains lacking. Based on representative sedimentary basins and engineering projects, this study reviews multisource characterization, scale transformation, multiphysics coupling, probabilistic prediction, monitoring-informed updating, and coordinated management within a “geological foundation–storage performance–prediction and regulation” framework. The results indicate that reservoir–caprock discontinuities, fault connectivity, and pressure boundaries jointly control dynamic storage capacity, pressure footprints, plume migration, trapping efficiency, and leakage risk; although multilayer utilization can increase storage capacity, it may intensify pressure superposition and cross-formational flow. This study proposes development pathways centered on pressure-constrained capacity assessment, probabilistic prediction, full-life-cycle simulation, and basin digital twins, providing a basis for regional resource allocation, coordinated multiproject injection, and long-term risk management.

title: Take a chance on green? Agent-based banking (ABBA) model inference for banking system greening via microprudential policy
source: Journal of Economic Interaction and Coordination
summary: Abstract Motivated by the European Commission’s proposed “green supporting factor” and Hungary’s de facto implementation through preferential capital treatment, we augment the Agent-Based B[A]nking (ABBA) model of Chan-Lau (2017) with prefe
content: Abstract Motivated by the European Commission’s proposed “green supporting factor” and Hungary’s de facto implementation through preferential capital treatment, we augment the Agent-Based B[A]nking (ABBA) model of Chan-Lau (2017) with preferential risk-weight and interest-rate discounts on green loans, examining the consequences for banking system topology and systemic risk across twelve regulatory regimes. Our simulations indicate that the discounts compress both the demand for and the supply of interbank liquidity, though the binding constraint differs across the matrix. Where regulation is loose, supply collapses as banks are too fragile to lend to one another in the aggregate, and liquidity run-driven failures are pronounced. Where regulation is adequate, demand recedes as banks hold sufficient capital and reserves not to need to borrow, and failures are mitigated. Capital requirements alone do not resolve this, as failures under the loosest reserve ratio persist at every capital level tested and are eliminated only by the reserve requirement. Green supporting factors therefore require joint calibration with both prudential standards.

title: Lost in translation: financial barriers to new technologies
source: London School of Economics and Political Science Research Online (London School of Economics and Political Science)
summary: Advanced economies are reshaped by transitions from old to new technological paradigms. These transitions rely on complementary innovations that spread new technologies across industries. What happens when a financial crisis disrupts invest
content: Advanced economies are reshaped by transitions from old to new technological paradigms. These transitions rely on complementary innovations that spread new technologies across industries. What happens when a financial crisis disrupts investment in these innovations? Using a Schumpeterian endogenous growth model with financial frictions, we show that investment in new technologies is more sensitive to tighter financial conditions than investment in mature technologies. The key mechanism is path dependence: firms build expertise in the technologies they previously developed, leading young firms to self-select into emerging technologies. As young firms are more financially constrained, shocks to financing disproportionately depress innovation in new technologies. We validate this mechanism using causal evidence on green patenting by German firms around the Global Financial Crisis. The aggregate fraction of patenting in carbon reducing technologies stagnated after the crisis. Quantifying our model using the causal estimates from the micro data implies that the slowdown of the sorting of young firms into new technologies accounts for about a fifth of the macro trends in such green innovation.

title: The Efficacy of Management Interventions to Restore Perennial Ryegrass Tiller Populations, Content and Production in Dairy Pasture
source: New Zealand Journal of Agricultural Research
summary: Three interventions aimed at restoring perennial ryegrass populations and the herbage production of run‐out dairy pastures based on mid‐season or late‐season heading perennial ryegrass cultivars were compared with a control (CON) treatment
content: Three interventions aimed at restoring perennial ryegrass populations and the herbage production of run‐out dairy pastures based on mid‐season or late‐season heading perennial ryegrass cultivars were compared with a control (CON) treatment over 3 years in Waikato. The treatments were: short deferral of grazing (47–48 days) in spring (SD); long deferral (112–123 days) in spring/summer (LD) and undersowing in autumn (US). Compared with all other treatments, LD increased ryegrass ground score and tiller density in year 1 post‐treatment but there were few differences thereafter. Compared with CON over all 3 years, LD led to: 2260 kg DM/ha/yr greater ryegrass herbage accumulation (HA); lower content of white clover (−50%), other grass species (−60%) and broadleaf weeds (−20%); higher metabolisable energy (ME) content (+5%); but no difference in total pasture HA. The ryegrass HA advantage of LD declined over time but was still significantly greater than other treatments by the third response year. Short deferral and undersowing had little effect on any variables, though a small benefit to ryegrass HA was detected when SD was applied to mid‐season cultivars but not to late‐season cultivars. Implications of net differences between CON and LD in total harvestable ME supply are analysed and discussed.

title: Evaluating Wasserstein-robust inventory decisions: a five-gate framework and a plant-level coal inventory study
source: Journal of Industrial and Production Engineering
summary: Robust layers on inventory models are costly to build, calibrate and explain, yet whether one changes decisions, or the data support its protection, is rarely asked. Two pre-adoption diagnostics become five ordered gates, exercised in a con
content: Robust layers on inventory models are costly to build, calibrate and explain, yet whether one changes decisions, or the data support its protection, is rarely asked. Two pre-adoption diagnostics become five ordered gates, exercised in a controlled study and a retrospective plant-level coal benchmark over 35 rolling origins. For a cost-form type-1 Wasserstein program with hinge loss on unbounded support, the worst case adds a decision-free term, leaving prescriptions unchanged; relocating robustness into the service constraint restores sensitivity. Under a common conditional residual law, a uniform cushion minimizes average expected shortfall at a matched budget; a closed-form example shows targeting can win. The layer changed prescriptions yet matched a quantile-plus-cushion policy at equal inventory, and most pile-build targets had no precedent; the controlled study found it worse on both criteria. The gates demonstrate stopping specificity, not sensitivity. Changed prescriptions need not add value; planners should ask these questions before adoption.

title: Behavioral and governance dimensions of circular economy willingness and commitment: An integrated TPB-norm activation model approach
summary: The circular economy transition is a strategic imperative for developing economies like Vietnam, yet the mechanisms translating intentions into genuine commitment remain insufficiently understood. An extended version of the theory of planne
content: The circular economy transition is a strategic imperative for developing economies like Vietnam, yet the mechanisms translating intentions into genuine commitment remain insufficiently understood. An extended version of the theory of planned behavior was used to examine how environmental concern, attitude, perceived behavioral control, and subjective norms shape behavioral intention, perceived circular economy role, and ultimately circular economy willingness and commitment (CEWC), while testing the moderating role of institutional and governance quality. Survey data from 752 Vietnamese businesses were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) (Hair et al., 2018). Results show environmental concern as the strongest predictor of behavioral intention, which completely mediates the effect of perceived circular economy role on CEWC. Unexpectedly, institutional and governance quality weakens the intention-commitment link, offering critical insight for accelerating the transition in emerging markets.

title: Commercial Integration: Company–Customer Interactions
summary: This chapter examines how digitalization is transforming commercial relationships between shipping companies and their customers in increasingly complex business-to-business maritime markets. Using the customer value proposition framework,
content: This chapter examines how digitalization is transforming commercial relationships between shipping companies and their customers in increasingly complex business-to-business maritime markets. Using the customer value proposition framework, it evaluates how shipping firms create and deliver value through digital technologies and compares different digitalization strategies adopted within the container shipping sector. In particular, it examines the failure of ambitious blockchain-based ecosystems, showing how governance challenges, concerns over data ownership, and a lack of trust among stakeholders limited their widespread adoption. In contrast, more focused digital solutions, such as online container booking platforms and remote container management systems, have achieved success by improving supply chain visibility, increasing operational predictability, and automating key business processes. These technologies deliver tangible benefits without requiring fundamental changes to the broader maritime ecosystem. The chapter also explores the growing adoption of the electronic bill of lading (eBL) as a key example of commercial digitalization. By replacing paper-based documentation, eBL systems can significantly reduce transaction times, lower administrative costs, improve sustainability performance, and decrease the risk of fraud. However, their broader implementation continues to face challenges related to interoperability, regulatory alignment, and the development of globally accepted standards. Overall, the chapter argues that successful commercial digitalization in shipping is more likely to emerge through gradual, standards-based innovation than through disruptive ecosystem-wide transformation. This process enables shipping companies to evolve from traditional transport providers into integrated, data-driven logistics partners capable of delivering greater value to customers.

title: Effect of TDZ treatment on the regeneration of shoots in recalcitrant grain legumes: Cicer arietinum, Glycine max, Phaseolus vulgaris, and Vigna unguiculata
summary: In vitro regeneration remains a major bottleneck for the genetic improvement of recalcitrant grain legumes. The present study evaluated a TDZ-mediated flooding approach for rapid and high-frequency apparent direct shoot regeneration, with n
content: In vitro regeneration remains a major bottleneck for the genetic improvement of recalcitrant grain legumes. The present study evaluated a TDZ-mediated flooding approach for rapid and high-frequency apparent direct shoot regeneration, with no visible callus formation based on gross morphological observations, in Cicer arietinum (black gram and white gram), Glycine max (soybean), Phaseolus vulgaris (common bean), and Vigna unguiculata (cowpea). Seedlings raised on N 6 medium containing 1.0 µM TDZ produced 4.5 shoots/seedling in black gram, 2.45 in white gram and 1.9 in common bean, while soybean and cowpea showed no shoot regeneration. Flooding TDZ-raised seedlings with distilled water and sucrose (D.W + S) enhanced shoot formation, whereas flooding with N 6 medium supplemented with 1.0 µM TDZ produced the strongest response, yielding 17.7, 16.4, 24, 23 and 41 shoots/seedling in black gram, white gram, soybean, common bean and cowpea, respectively. The maximum regeneration was recorded in cowpea (41 shoots/seedling), followed by soybean (24), common bean (23), black gram (17.7) and white gram (16.4). The regeneration response was associated with shoot-apex expansion and formation of additional shoot-forming regions, with no visible callus observed. These findings demonstrate that TDZ flooding substantially enhances shoot regeneration and extends its application to additional recalcitrant grain legumes. These findings demonstrate that the timing and mode of TDZ delivery are critical determinants of regeneration efficiency and extend the flooding approach to additional recalcitrant grain legumes. The protocol provides a simple, regeneration platform with potential applications in genetic transformation and genome editing.

title: Driving human resources-based transformation for sustainable competitive advantage in circular economy
summary: The circular economy (CE) has become a crucial framework for ensuring sustainability in small and medium enterprises (SMEs). However, resource limitations remain a significant challenge in achieving both sustainability and competitive advan
content: The circular economy (CE) has become a crucial framework for ensuring sustainability in small and medium enterprises (SMEs). However, resource limitations remain a significant challenge in achieving both sustainability and competitive advantage. This study investigates the role of the aggregator business model (ABM) in facilitating SME transformation towards sustainable competitive advantage. Using a survey of 390 randomly selected SMEs in the creative economy sector in West Java, Indonesia, data were analyzed with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings reveal that resource availability significantly relationships SME transformation, with ABM playing a moderating role in optimizing most resources, except for organizational psychological resilience. By facilitating resource configuration, ABM enhances SMEs' ability to transition towards sustainability-driven competitive advantage. This research contributes to the resource-based view by highlighting ABM's role in accelerating CE-aligned business transformation for SMEs.

title: Integrated Marketing Communication for Trust Building: Wuling Motors in Indonesia's Automotive Market
summary: This study examines how Wuling Motors employs integrated marketing communication (IMC) to build consumer trust and strengthen its market presence in Indonesia's automotive industry despite the long-standing dominance of Japanese brands. A q
content: This study examines how Wuling Motors employs integrated marketing communication (IMC) to build consumer trust and strengthen its market presence in Indonesia's automotive industry despite the long-standing dominance of Japanese brands. A qualitative case study approach was employed using purposive sampling, in-depth interviews, and thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Wuling's market penetration was achieved through trust-building strategies integrating local legitimacy, consumer experience, and adaptive marketing communication. This study contributes to the existing literature on integrated marketing communication, market penetration, and country-of-origin effects by explaining how IMC strategically reconstructs consumer trust and brand legitimacy for an emerging Chinese automotive brand in a market dominated by established Japanese manufacturers. The findings suggest that managers should prioritize integrated marketing communication to build consumer trust and strengthen market penetration, while policymakers should promote policies that support fair competition and innovation in the automotive industry

title: Integrated Biodigester, Fermenter, and Composter System for Biogas, Liquid Organic Fertilizer, and Compost Production from Palm Oil Mill Waste
summary: Palm oil mill effluent (POME) is a high-strength organic wastewater that poses significant environmental challenges if not properly managed.Although anaerobic digestion, composting, and liquid fermentation have been widely applied, comprehe
content: Palm oil mill effluent (POME) is a high-strength organic wastewater that poses significant environmental challenges if not properly managed.Although anaerobic digestion, composting, and liquid fermentation have been widely applied, comprehensive performance evaluations of fully integrated biodigester-composter-fermenter systems remain limited, particularly regarding the role of hydraulic retention time (HRT) and process bottlenecks.This study evaluates the HRT-dependent performance and limitations of an integrated POME valorization system using a laboratory-scale continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) operated at HRTs of 10-250 days.System performance was assessed based on digester stability, solid compost quality, and nutrient and heavy metal characteristics of the liquid effluent.POME exhibited high organic strength (COD 45,000 mg L -1 ; BOD 35,000 mg L -1 ; VS/TS ratio 0.82), supporting effective anaerobic digestion (COD removal up to 92 %, VS destruction up to 88 %, biogas yield up to 0.60 m³ kg -1 VS, and methane content up to 71 % at an HRT of 250 days).The solid fraction was successfully valorized through composting of empty fruit bunches using biodigester effluent, producing compost that met Indonesian National Standards.The resulting compost had a moisture content of 33 %, organic carbon content of 20.14 %, nitrogen content of 1.34 %, phosphorus content of 0.79 %, potassium content of 2.48 %, and magnesium content of 2.07 %, thereby meeting six of seven SNI 19-7030-2004 parameters; only pH at 8.85 exceeded the standard range of 6.8-7.49.In contrast, the liquid fraction showed limited agronomic potential, characterized by low organic carbon and macronutrient contents, and elevated lead (Pb) concentration exceeding permissible limits.These results identify the liquid effluent as the primary performance bottleneck of the integrated system, driven by nutrient depletion and heavy metal accumulation, and highlight the need for targeted post-treatment strategies.Overall, the integrated biodigester-composter-fermenter system demonstrated strong potential for solid-phase resource recovery and circular POME management, while effective liquid-phase utilization requires further process optimization.

title: How to Calculate Dimensionless Numbers in Fluid Mechanics and Their Applications in Chemical Engineering Processes: Reynolds, Mach, Froude, Euler, Power, Stokes, Weber, Capillary, and Cavitation Numbers
source: ASEAN Journal for Science and Engineering in Materials
summary: This paper explains how to calculate and interpret dimensionless numbers in fluid mechanics for chemical engineering applications, focusing on the Reynolds, Mach, Froude, Euler, Power, Stokes, Weber, Capillary, and Cavitation numbers. The f
content: This paper explains how to calculate and interpret dimensionless numbers in fluid mechanics for chemical engineering applications, focusing on the Reynolds, Mach, Froude, Euler, Power, Stokes, Weber, Capillary, and Cavitation numbers. The first part presents each dimensionless number individually based on its definition, formula, required variables, threshold values, physical meaning, calculation example, interpretation, and handling strategy. The second part presents integrated case examples to show how several dimensionless numbers can be used together to analyze more complex chemical engineering systems. The examples include pipe flow, gas flow, heat exchangers, slurry pipelines, pumps, valves, nozzles, mixing vessels, wastewater aeration basins, aerated fermentation bioreactors, spray drying systems, cyclones, and particle-laden flows. Through these examples, this paper aims to help readers connect dimensionless-number calculations with process behavior, engineering interpretation, and practical decision-making in chemical engineering.

title: High-throughput mineralogical characterization using automated in-situ microscopy and Raman spectroscopy
summary: Abstract Mineral precipitation in natural and engineered systems is controlled by complex interactions among physicochemical variables and organic molecules, making large-scale systematic exploration of mineralization pathways challenging.
content: Abstract Mineral precipitation in natural and engineered systems is controlled by complex interactions among physicochemical variables and organic molecules, making large-scale systematic exploration of mineralization pathways challenging. Here we present a high-throughput experimental and analytical workflow that enables rapid, particle-resolved characterization of mineral formation. The platform integrates miniaturized mineralization experiments in multi-well plates with automated optical microscopy, particle detection, morphometric analysis, machine-learning classification, and targeted Raman spectromicroscopy. Applied to calcium carbonate precipitation mediated by organic additives, the workflow enables particle-resolved morphological analysis and mineral phase identification. Across 307 experiments involving 23 organic additives, automated imaging revealed ten reproducible particle morphologies. Raman spectromicroscopy showed that each morphotype consistently corresponds to a single mineral phase, either calcite or vaterite. A Random Forest model trained on morphological descriptors classified particle types with a mean accuracy of 97 ± 1%, enabling automated quantification of morphotype populations across experimental conditions. Systematic screening showed that organic additives strongly influence particle populations, modifying particle number, size distributions, and accessible particle morphologies. Time-lapse imaging further enables rapid estimation of particle growth rates, providing a practical metric to identify conditions that promote or inhibit mineralization. This integrated workflow provides a scalable framework for mapping mineralization pathways across multidimensional chemical spaces.

title: Household energy, tuberculosis, and poverty: which national signals track the rising global burden of interstitial lung disease? A 204-country longitudinal study, 2000–2021, with projections to 2050
summary: Abstract Rationale. Global studies show that interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary sarcoidosis are increasing and unequally distributed, but potentially modifiable national correlates of this burden remain poorly characterized. Our
content: Abstract Rationale. Global studies show that interstitial lung disease (ILD) and pulmonary sarcoidosis are increasing and unequally distributed, but potentially modifiable national correlates of this burden remain poorly characterized. Our aim is to identify potentially modifiable national factors associated with ILD burden and estimate burden trajectories to 2050. Methods. We linked GBD 2021 estimates with World Bank and WHO indicators for 204 countries, 2000–2021, and directly standardized reconstructed both-sex outcomes. We fitted country and year fixed-effects models with country-clustered standard errors and policy-relevant lags, then projected empirically shrunk country trends to 2030, 2040, and 2050. Results. Four potentially modifiable national factors were associated with ILD burden. Higher tuberculosis incidence (+ 68/100,000) was associated with a 1.00% higher DALY rate at 3 years (95% CI, 0.48–1.53%); greater clean-cooking access (+ 4 percentage points) with a 1.00% lower rate at 10 years (0.32–1.68% lower); higher societal poverty (+ 4.1 percentage points) with a 1.52% higher rate at 5 years (0.04–3.04%); and greater universal health coverage (+ 5.1 points) with a 1.90% lower rate at 1 year (0.32–3.46% lower). Tuberculosis associations reflected partial structural confounding rather than an independent causal effect. Global DALYs rose from 2.09 to 4.04 million (2000–2021), reaching a projected 9.53 million by 2050 under continuation of 2010–2021 trends. Conclusions. Tuberculosis burden, household energy, poverty, and health-service coverage were the principal modifiable national correlates of ILD burden. Their distinct mechanisms support an integrated agenda of infectious-disease control, clean energy, social protection, and equitable respiratory care, though ecological associations do not establish intervention effects.

title: Integrative physiological and transcriptomic analyses reveal divergent chilling tolerance mechanisms in contrasting zoysiagrass cultivars and protective effects of exogenous chitosan
summary: Abstract Background Chilling stress is one of the major factors affecting the green period and turf quality in zoysiagrass (Zoysia spp.). However, the physiological and molecular mechanisms of differential chilling tolerance among zoysiagra
content: Abstract Background Chilling stress is one of the major factors affecting the green period and turf quality in zoysiagrass (Zoysia spp.). However, the physiological and molecular mechanisms of differential chilling tolerance among zoysiagrass cultivars remain largely unexplored. Results The objectives of this study were to elucidate differences of chilling tolerance between the two cultivars with different chilling tolerance through integrating physiological and transcriptomic analyses, and to investigate protective effects of exogenous chitosan on the sensitive cultivar. The results showed that the chilling-tolerant cultivar ‘Nannong NT1’ suffered less injury than the sensitive ‘Nannong LG’ under chilling stress, as evidenced by lower electrolyte leakage, reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and higher survival rate. Transcriptomic analyses further identified that ‘Nannong NT1’ specifically up-regulated carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, while concurrently down-regulating photosynthesis and carbon fixation. In contrast, ‘Nannong LG’ activated carotenoid and flavonoid biosynthesis, and repressed amino acid metabolism and protein export. Additionally, foliar application of chitosan (50 mg·L-¹) significantly alleviated chilling injury in ‘Nannong LG’ by enhancing chlorophyll content, relative water content, osmoprotectant accumulation, and survival rate, while reducing electrolyte leakage and ROS accumulation. At the transcriptional level, chitosan specifically modulated the expression of several critical differentially expressed genes, such as ZsNAC2, ZsNAC3, ZsLecRLK1, ZsLecRLK2, and ZsBAM. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that differential chilling tolerance was attributed to the divergent regulatory and metabolic strategies. Exogenous chitosan offers a complementary approach to enhance chilling tolerance in the sensitive cultivar in zoysiagrass.

title: NAD+ as a metabolic immune checkpoint in cancer
summary: Abstract Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) functions in cancer as a compartmentalized signaling currency, coupling tumor cell fitness to immune competence within the tumor microenvironment (TME). In malignant cells, NAD+ sustains red
content: Abstract Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) functions in cancer as a compartmentalized signaling currency, coupling tumor cell fitness to immune competence within the tumor microenvironment (TME). In malignant cells, NAD+ sustains redox balance, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)-dependent DNA repair, sirtuin-mediated chromatin remodeling, and metabolic stress adaptation. In immune effector cells, the same metabolite governs mitochondrial integrity, effector persistence, and resistance to exhaustion. This duality is the basis of the explanation advanced here for why first-generation inhibitors of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), the rate-limiting salvage pathway enzyme, failed clinically when deployed as cytotoxic monotherapies without an immunometabolic rationale. This review synthesizes the field around a central premise: NAD+ operates as a context-dependent metabolic immune checkpoint whose therapeutic value depends on where in the tumor immune ecosystem the pathway is perturbed and whether checkpoint blockade is deployed concurrently. The therapeutic landscape is reorganized around five pharmacological classes, which differ in how far each has been tested: (i) NAMPT catalytic inhibitors, evaluated clinically and withdrawn; (ii) bifunctional NAMPT/programmed death-ligand (PD-L1) compounds and proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC)-mediated NAMPT degradation, both preclinical; (iii) NAD+ precursor-based immunorestorative strategies, including ex vivo rescue of age-associated chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell dysfunction through NMN/CD38 inhibitor combinations; (iv) adenosinergic axis targeting, in which anti-CD38 and anti-CD73 agents are approved or in trials while the proposed triple-blockade of CD38, CD73, and PD-1/PD-L1 remains untested; and (v) combinations with PARP and indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) inhibitors, which rest on mechanistic rationale. A tripartite pharmacological taxonomy distinguishes intracellular (iNAMPT), extracellular (eNAMPT), and vesicle-associated (vNAMPT) NAMPT as discrete drug targets. The analyses examines how TME acidification, precursor competition, and extracellular NAD+ catabolism through the CD38–CD203a–CD73 noncanonical adenosine axis reshape immune fitness, and why biomarker-guided separation of tumor-directed NAD+ depletion from immune-directed NAD+ restoration is required for rational clinical translation. Throughout, findings that are experimentally established are separated from those that remain contested or hypothetical, and the criteria under which the checkpoint designation is analytically useful, together with the conditions under which it is not, are stated explicitly.

title: From root entry to harvested commodity: Transport checkpoints governing toxic metal(loid) accumulation in major cash crops
summary: Toxic metal(loid) contamination of cash-crop commodities is determined not only by root uptake but by successive transport and retention processes that govern delivery to the harvested organ. This review synthesizes evidence for Cd, As, Pb,
content: Toxic metal(loid) contamination of cash-crop commodities is determined not only by root uptake but by successive transport and retention processes that govern delivery to the harvested organ. This review synthesizes evidence for Cd, As, Pb, Ni and Cr transport in six major cash crops: tea, tobacco, cacao, coffee, cotton and sugarcane, representing leaf, bean/seed, fibre and stem commodities. We organize these processes within a conceptual Root-to-Commodity Transport Continuum comprising six operational components: rhizosphere availability, root entry, root retention, xylem loading, phloem redistribution and harvest-organ loading. Mechanistic resolution was strongly metal- and crop-dependent: direct transporter and isotope evidence was concentrated in Cd studies of tobacco, tea and cacao, whereas As, Pb, Ni and Cr were supported mainly by crop-level partitioning, model-crop inference or unresolved mechanisms. To distinguish evidence strength, transporter and checkpoint claims were classified as direct crop-native causal or directional-flux evidence, strong crop-specific mechanistic evidence, crop-specific associative or descriptive evidence, or model-crop or homology-based inference. The synthesis shows that similar whole-plant metal burdens can produce contrasting commodity contamination because the dominant transport bottleneck differs with crop architecture and metal chemistry. The proposed framework is therefore conceptual and experimentally operational rather than presently predictive. It identifies the measurements required for future quantitative models, including stable-isotope tracing, vascular flux analysis, spatial elemental imaging and crop-native functional genetics, with the long-term objective of reducing commodity metal(loid) loading while preserving essential micronutrient homeostasis, yield and product quality.

title: Expert insight on the design, implementation, and monitoring of future community benefit funds within the energy transition
summary: Increasingly, citizen and public participation are considered central to achieving the energy transition to a low carbon future. Such participation has different dimensions in new energy infrastructure, in terms of both renewable energy ins
content: Increasingly, citizen and public participation are considered central to achieving the energy transition to a low carbon future. Such participation has different dimensions in new energy infrastructure, in terms of both renewable energy installations and additional electricity grid developments. Participation includes active involvement in decision making, the ability to invest in developer-led projects, and capacity for community owned renewable energy projects. This also includes community benefit funding (CBF), whereby a local fund is established by the developer and provided to communities impacted by infrastructural developments. There is a growing body of experience with CBF, but it has not received much attention in the scientific literature. In addition, there is a paucity of analysis of the design, implementation, and evaluation of CBF schemes. This research intervention addresses this gap using a modified Delphi panel approach to explore areas of consensus and divergence on these dimensions of CBF programs. We bring together national and international experts on community benefit funding who work on key areas of relevance such as policy formation, strategy design, fund administration, and community development to deliberate on the role of CBF in supporting future developments towards energy system change. The method implemented draws out lessons learned concerning community benefit funding and insights concerning its future design, implementation, and monitoring from a range of sectors and perspectives. While participant experts within the study are made up of three groups: the public, private and academic sectors, the results have specific application in relation to CBF associated with renewable energy production whereby the financial benefit accrued is long lasting over time. This is critically important in the context of the scale of growth planned and the significant associated levels of CBF that will transfer from private funds to public good. The results highlight where there is consensus and divergence of opinion for the design, delivery, and monitoring of CBF, which can usefully inform policy deliberations as well as advancing knowledge as we see CBF growing in significance both in Ireland and internationally.

title: Intercalation of O2, H2, and CO beneath epitaxial graphene on Ir(111): A review of atomic-scale decoupling mechanisms and pathways to catalysis, sensing, and energy applications
summary: Intercalation of gases and metal species beneath graphene supported on transition-metal substrates has emerged as a powerful strategy for tuning graphene–substrate interactions and tailoring its electronic, chemical, and mechanical properti
content: Intercalation of gases and metal species beneath graphene supported on transition-metal substrates has emerged as a powerful strategy for tuning graphene–substrate interactions and tailoring its electronic, chemical, and mechanical properties. Numerous studies have investigated these phenomena using surface-sensitive techniques, including X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). This review examines the intercalation of oxygen, carbon monoxide, and hydrogen, with particular emphasis on graphene grown on Ir(111). Oxygen intercalation proceeds under ultrahigh-vacuum conditions through atomic oxygen formation on bare Ir terraces and requires elevated temperatures (~355 K), whereas hydrogen intercalation occurs at much lower temperatures (~140 K). CO intercalation takes place near room temperature but requires millibar-range pressures. In all cases, substrate step edges and graphene flake boundaries serve as critical pathways for intercalant penetration. These structural features have been consistently identified as key entry points for intercalant diffusion. Intercalation provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling the properties of 2D materials, enabling modulation of electrical conductivity, thermoelectric response, and catalytic activity. The process significantly modifies the electronic, chemical, and mechanical characteristics of the graphene layer, while also partially decoupling it from the underlying substrate.
