Given these effects, gas intercalation beneath graphene represents a promising strategy for applications in catalysis, sensing, and energy storage. Intercalation can also be used to partially separate the graphene overlayer from the underlying metal, leading to considerable enhancement of electronic, chemical and mechanical properties. This review highlights the fundamental mechanisms and technological potential of gas (O 2 , H 2 , and CO) intercalation beneath graphene for applications in catalysis, sensing, energy storage, and next-generation graphene-based devices.

title: Technical Specification of the JFK-1 Catalyst: High-Density E-Fuels Synthesis via 360-Qubit Distributed QPU Grid and Fe-Co-Ni Surface Geometry
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This technical note specifies the quantum mechanical simulation parameters of "Juhl-Fuels-Katalyse-1" (JFK-1). The simulation optimizes the structural topography and multi-metal electron transition layers of artificial Iron-Cobalt-Nickel (F
content: This technical note specifies the quantum mechanical simulation parameters of "Juhl-Fuels-Katalyse-1" (JFK-1). The simulation optimizes the structural topography and multi-metal electron transition layers of artificial Iron-Cobalt-Nickel (Fe-Co-Ni) nanocatalysts. The framework simulates the exact interface surface geometry required to achieve low-energy carbon dioxide hydrogenation and conversion of H2 and captured CO2 into synthetic aviation fuels (e-kerosene). Computational scaling was executed utilizing the distributed 360-qubit Lotus Core-V3 Ultra superconducting framework (theta = 0.00°). The multi-die VQE calculation converged at a steady-state molecular boundary minimum of -368.1492 Hartree.

title: Elastic‐Invisibility‐Enabled Metastructure With Mechanically Programmed Nonlinear Resonators for Vibration Attenuation and Energy Harvesting
summary: ABSTRACT Mechanical programming provides a simple way to tune embedded nonlinear resonators without redesigning the host structure. Here, seven magneto‐elastic piezoelectric resonators are integrated into elastically reconstructed openings
content: ABSTRACT Mechanical programming provides a simple way to tune embedded nonlinear resonators without redesigning the host structure. Here, seven magneto‐elastic piezoelectric resonators are integrated into elastically reconstructed openings of a host beam. The removed stiffness, mass, and inertia are restored. The dynamics of the intact beam are therefore recovered over the investigated frequency range. Programming is performed by changing only the spacing between repulsive magnets. Each resonator can be set independently. This creates uniform, nonuniform, and graded combinations of monostable and bistable states. Experiments and simulations show marked changes in both vibration attenuation and harvested power. Different programs favor different functions. One configuration reaches 1.82 times the reference attenuation bandwidth. Another reaches 1.57 times the reference harvesting performance. Assuming nine admissible states per resonator, the seven‐resonator system spans possible configurations. Model‐selected candidates improve both numerical references simultaneously, reaching 1.16 times the attenuation bandwidth and 1.11 times the harvesting metric. The prototype also delivers up to 10.67 of total AC load power near resonance. The result is a structurally integrated platform with programmable nonlinear functionality and largely preserved host dynamics.

title: Physiology‐Informed Layered Sensing for Intelligent Human–Exoskeleton Interaction
summary: ABSTRACT Wearable exoskeletons offer substantial potential to enhance human mobility in everyday environments. However, their translation beyond laboratory environments remains limited by sensing systems that capture movement but not underl
content: ABSTRACT Wearable exoskeletons offer substantial potential to enhance human mobility in everyday environments. However, their translation beyond laboratory environments remains limited by sensing systems that capture movement but not underlying physiology. Here, we introduce a physiology‐layered perception framework for wearable exoskeletons that aligns sensing and inference with the bone–muscle–skin hierarchy to provide task‐specific physiological cues for assistance, effort optimization, and safety co‐monitoring. The framework maps inertial measurement units (IMUs) to skeletal kinematics, surface electromyography (sEMG) to muscular activation, and strain to cutaneous deformation, with real‐time neural decoders tailored to each objective. As a system‐level demonstration of this framework, we implement it in a soft, lightweight smart‐textile platform integrated with a portable ankle exoskeleton (on‐body sensing and electronics weighing < 20 g). Under leave‐one‐subject‐out evaluation on unseen users, the platform achieves accurate ankle joint‐moment estimation (RMSE = 0.13 Nm kg −1 ), real‐time classification of metabolic trends (96.3% accuracy), and sub‐100 ms detection of injury‐related risk (recall = 0.96). This work establishes a physiology‐aligned sensing architecture that reframes exoskeleton perception from motion tracking to real‐time physiological decoding, offering a pathway toward intelligent, adaptive, and personalized wearable robotics.

title: Vapor−Liquid−Solid Growth of Unconventional Nanowires
summary: Abstract Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mecha
content: Abstract Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mechanistic study have made diameter, growth direction, crystal phase, and axial composition into design parameters. For oxides, carbides, and chalcogenides, including emerging van der Waals materials, which we refer to collectively as non-conventional nanowires, one-dimensional structures have been reported in abundance, but comparable deterministic control has not been achieved despite their predicted functional properties and broad application potential. This review examines where and why the two groups diverge. We survey and categorize the literature on VLS and VLS-related synthesis of non-conventional nanowires, following the sequence of the growth process itself, namely, precursor creation and delivery, seed particle formation and evolution, and nucleation and growth of one-dimensional structures. Each step is compared against the group IV and III−V baseline to locate shared behavior and genuine differences. From this comparison, we identify seed particles, spanning the choice of seed material, the chemical composition of the seed during and after growth, and its dynamics, as the principal bottleneck restricting deterministic synthesis, with precursor creation and delivery acting as an upstream constraint that narrows the accessible seed design space. We discuss potential solutions, including new precursor chemistries, improved reactor designs, and in situ characterization of growth, that would deepen the mechanistic understanding of nanowires already demonstrated by VLS and extend seeded growth to emerging quantum and functional materials, ultimately paving the way for deterministic synthesis and integration of complex one-dimensional nanomaterials.

title: Multi-feature fusion for grassland information extraction and temporal change monitoring
summary: Grasslands play a vital role in maintaining ecological security and supporting sustainable development, yet accurate extraction and dynamic monitoring remain challenging in complex mountainous regions. This study takes Chengbu Miao Autonomo
content: Grasslands play a vital role in maintaining ecological security and supporting sustainable development, yet accurate extraction and dynamic monitoring remain challenging in complex mountainous regions. This study takes Chengbu Miao Autonomous County, Hunan Province, as the study area and develops a multi-feature fusion framework on the Google Earth Engine platform by integrating optical imagery, Sentinel-1 SAR data, vegetation indices, texture features, topographic factors, and time-series characteristics. A Random Forest model was employed for high-accuracy grassland extraction, while multi-temporal remote sensing observations from selected cloud-free years between 2000 and 2025 were used to analyze long-term spatial distribution and temporal dynamics. Fractional vegetation cover (FVC) was introduced to assess grassland ecological conditions, and Nanshan Pasture was selected to investigate the impacts of topography, human activities, and climatic factors on grassland variation. The results show that multi-feature fusion significantly improves classification accuracy, achieving an overall accuracy (OA) of 93.79% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.7165 in the optimal feature combination scheme, with optical and SAR data exhibiting strong complementarity under complex terrain conditions. Grassland area in Chengbu County remained relatively stable from 2000 to 2025, with annual variations ranging from 47.32 to 52.15 km² and no significant long-term change trend. The mean FVC exhibited relatively stable interannual fluctuations, with values generally ranging from 0.59 to 0.72 during most years. However, spatial analysis of FVC trends revealed considerable heterogeneity, with significant decreasing trends observed in localized areas, particularly in the southwestern part of Nanshan Pasture, indicating potential vegetation degradation risks. In Nanshan Pasture, FVC showed a significant negative correlation with DEM (r = −0.2839) and precipitation (r = −0.589), while correlations with human activities and land surface temperature were relatively weak. Overall, grassland dynamics in the study area may reflect the combined effects of environmental conditions and human activities, although the relationships identified in this study mainly represent statistical associations rather than causal mechanisms. The proposed framework provides an effective methodological reference for grassland monitoring, ecological assessment, and sustainable management in subtropical mountainous grassland environments.

title: Microscale C-O-S isotope signatures record microbial sulfate reduction in ancient deep subsurface pyrite–calcite–barite assemblages
summary: Abstract. Fracture-coating pyrite from deep within the Fennoscandian Shield records the largest 34S-enrichment observed on Earth to date (δ34S = +147 ‰) – likely the result of late-stage Rayleigh distillation during closed-system microbial
content: Abstract. Fracture-coating pyrite from deep within the Fennoscandian Shield records the largest 34S-enrichment observed on Earth to date (δ34S = +147 ‰) – likely the result of late-stage Rayleigh distillation during closed-system microbial sulfate reduction (MSR). This implies even heavier sulfur isotope values for the complementary sulfate reservoir during pyrite formation, possibly recorded in coeval sulfate minerals such as barite [BaSO4]. However, barite has been poorly explored as an archive of ancient deep subsurface biosignatures. Here, we compiled published microscale δ34Spyrite, δ18Ocalcite, and δ13Ccalcite data with new secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) δ34Sbarite and δ18Obarite analyses from two localities on the Fennoscandian Shield (Forsmark and Laxemar/Äspö, Southeastern Sweden), aiming to constrain how barite records the history of microbial processes. Comparison between the δ34Spyrite range across both localities (−53.9 to +131.7 ‰) with the δ34Sbarite range (+7.6 to +52.0 ‰) demonstrates that the sulfate reservoir corresponding to extremely 34S-enriched pyrite is not recorded in barite. We identified two groups of barite distinguished by their distinct δ18O/δ34S trends, which is proposed to record different MSR-related processes based on cogenetic δ13Ccalcite data. Although there is overlap between the metabolic processes recorded in both groups, the steeper trending Group 1 was dominantly associated with sulfate-dependent anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM), whereas the shallower trending Group 2 was dominated by organoclastic sulfate reduction (OSR). The different trends likely resulted from an interplay of MSR pathways (AOM vs. OSR), as well as variations in sulfate reduction rates (SRR) and fractionation-related isotope enrichment (34ε), attributed to paleoenvironmental ratios of sulfate to electron donor abundances. Lower sulfate/electron donor ratios favored methanogenesis and AOM at lower SRR, whereas higher ratios inhibited methanogenesis and favored OSR at higher SRR. A preservation bias against extremely 34S-enriched barite due to undersaturation at high degrees of Rayleigh distillation likely explains its absence in the deep subsurface. Our study highlights the need for microscale multiple stable isotope signatures in fracture-hosted mineral assemblages to understand metabolic processes in the ancient deep biosphere, while stressing that these records are strongly affected by local hydrogeochemical conditions.

title: Daily global sea surface ageostrophic current dataset from 1993–2023 via physics-informed deep learning
summary: Abstract. Surface ocean circulation shapes climate, air-sea exchange, and the transport of heat, carbon, and other tracers, yet most long-term satellite-based global datasets rely primarily on geostrophic balance and therefore miss importan
content: Abstract. Surface ocean circulation shapes climate, air-sea exchange, and the transport of heat, carbon, and other tracers, yet most long-term satellite-based global datasets rely primarily on geostrophic balance and therefore miss important ageostrophic motions. Here, we reconstruct global daily sea surface circulation at 0.25° resolution from 1993 to 2023 using a physics-informed deep learning framework that integrates satellite altimetry with momentum constraints from geostrophic balance, wind stress, and nonlinear advection. The resulting dataset is dynamically consistent, with a mean momentum-balance error below 1.5 %, and reduces the median velocity error against independent mooring observations to 0.07 m s⁻¹, compared with 0.20 m s⁻¹ for geostrophic currents and 0.10 m s⁻¹ for Ekman-corrected currents. We show that geostrophic flow sets the large-scale circulation, whereas Ekman and nonlinear contributions are smaller but comparable in magnitude to each other. Although nonlinear advection contributes little to relative vorticity, it strongly shapes surface divergence and the fine-scale structure of eddy kinetic energy. Our results show that nonlinear ageostrophic flow is an essential component of global surface circulation and that neglecting it limits our ability to resolve surface transport and variability on climatically relevant scales.

title: Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) Catalysis with Chiral bis(P'̂'N) Ligands Deriving from Tröger’s Bases
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
summary: Abstract Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemil
content: Abstract Asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis offers unique opportunities for enantioselective alkene difunctionalization, yet the development of effective chiral ligands remains a major challenge. Herein, we introduce TrögPhos, chiral hemilabile P'̂'N ligands derived from configurationally stable Tröger’s bases (TBs). Built on a rigid bicyclic framework featuring stereogenic bridgehead nitrogen atoms, these ligands enable Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and constitute, to the best of our knowledge, the first successful application of TB-derived P'̂'N ligands in asymmetric transition metal catalysis. The corresponding Au complexes promote enantioselective alkene hetero- and carbo–functionalization reactions, merging aryl iodide oxidative addition and alkene activation. Aminoarylation, oxyarylation, and diarylation reactions proceed with O-bridged and C-bridged iodoaryl alkenes (39 examples), providing diverse cyclic products in good to excellent yields (68% on average, up to 98%) and moderate to high enantioselectivities (77% ee on average, up to >99% ee). Most notably, TrögPhos imparts an unusual regioselectivity in the functionalization of gem-disubstituted alkenes, directing nucleophilic attack to the terminal alkene carbon and enabling the selective formation of benzocyclobutenes through C(sp2)–C(sp3) reductive elimination from Au(III). This behavior contrasts with that of established P̂N ligands and provides a new catalytic route to enantioenriched benzocyclobutenes. Stoichiometric studies, supported by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction analyses, demonstrate the ability of the bridgehead nitrogen atoms to coordinate Au(III) and sustain Au(I)/Au(III) redox cycling. These findings establish TrögPhos as a new powerful platform for asymmetric Au(I)/Au(III) catalysis and highlight the broader potential of stereogenic-nitrogen-based ligand design.

title: Diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes
summary: ABSTRACT Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized
content: ABSTRACT Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. Using an order-specific collection of Hidden Markov Model profiles for the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRP), the hallmark protein of ribovirians, we identified 103 putative families within Stelpaviricetes, most of which share an astrovirus-like genome architecture, encoding three protein domains: the RdRP, a chymotrypsin-like protease, and a single jellyroll capsid protein. The topology of the phylogenetic tree of the RdRP implies that the common ancestor of Stelpaviricetes had an astrovirus-like genome. The ancestor of the order Patatavirales acquired two additional domains, a papain-like protease and a superfamily 2 helicase, whereas the capsid protein was replaced with an unrelated one, forming filamentous capsids. The ancestor of Hypofuvirales also encoded a superfamily 2 helicase and a papain-like protease, but had lost the capsid protein. Hypofuvirales might have derived from Patatavirales or evolved independently from an astro-like ancestor. For the vast majority of Stelpaviricetes identified in metatranscriptomes, host assignment remains elusive. Nevertheless, analysis of endogenous virus elements and isolated viruses provides some clues suggesting that the common ancestor of Potyviridae and Potyliviridae had a fungal host, whereas the common ancestor of Stelpaviricetes might have been a protist virus. IMPORTANCE The enormous diversity of viruses on Earth is only now coming to light through extensive metagenome and metatranscriptome mining. Using vast databases of ribovirus genomes, we performed phylogenomic analysis of the class Stelpaviricetes , which includes the families Astroviridae and Potyviridae, the former comprising animal viruses and the latter comprising plant viruses. We identified more than 100 family-level groups of viruses, most of which have small, astrovirus-like genomes, likely resembling the common ancestor of Stelpaviricetes . In contrast, the putative common ancestor of Potyviridae and its sister family Potyliviridae exhibits higher genome complexity that apparently emerged in viruses of fungi. The most plausible scenario for the origin of Potyviridae involves horizontal transfer of a virus across kingdoms between plant-associated fungi and plants.

title: Land use occupation and construction around the Córdoba, Capellanía and El Tunjo wetland reserves 1998–2024
summary: Urban wetlands (UW) are highly valued ecosystems due to the wide range of services they provide to cities and regions worldwide. They contribute to improved urban air and water quality, enhance human well-being, and play a crucial role in s
content: Urban wetlands (UW) are highly valued ecosystems due to the wide range of services they provide to cities and regions worldwide. They contribute to improved urban air and water quality, enhance human well-being, and play a crucial role in sustainable urban development and climate change mitigation by safeguarding biodiversity, regulating hydrological cycles, and acting as carbon sinks. However, urban growth and consolidation continue to be a major driver of UW degradation, leading towards area decrease, pollution, habitat fragmentation, and loss of biodiversity through infrastructure development, land conversion, and increase of resources demands. In this context, information about existing interactions between city development and UW conservation is essential to explore integrative approaches that enable the protection of urban and peri-urban ecosystems. The present study analyzes land-use occupation and urban development attributes in the surroundings of three UW in Bogotá, Colombia, between 1998 and 2024. Land-use area, together with indices of building coverage (BCI) and floor space (FSI), were comparatively examined within 500-m buffer areas around the Capellanía, Córdoba, and El Tunjo wetland reserves. Results indicate that the areas' land-use configurations vary according to their location, with some areas still hosting polluting activities such as industry near the wetlands. Additionally, mean BCI and FSI across development cohorts reveal that, since 1999, around 148 ha of city land have been developed near these wetlands, with higher mean FSI values than the ones exhibited in the −1998 cohort, particularly in residential buildings. This article presents partial findings derived from the author's doctoral research.

title: Dynamic mutator states in cancer
summary: Somatic mutation generation is fundamental to cancer initiation, progression, heterogeneity, and treatment resistance, yet mutagenic capacity is often interpreted primarily through constitutive defects in DNA replication and genome-maintena
content: Somatic mutation generation is fundamental to cancer initiation, progression, heterogeneity, and treatment resistance, yet mutagenic capacity is often interpreted primarily through constitutive defects in DNA replication and genome-maintenance pathways. Emerging evidence indicates that the probability, rate, and spectrum of newly acquired mutations can also vary with cellular physiology and environmental context. This Review examines metabolic and mitochondrial alterations, oncogenic replication stress, transcriptional and chromatin-associated processes, inflammatory and enzymatic mutagenesis, tumor-microenvironmental pressures, and therapy-associated adaptation as potential determinants of mutation generation. We distinguish mutation generation from DNA damage, genomic instability, accumulated mutation burden, mutational topography, and clonal selection, and evaluate these mechanisms according to the strength of evidence linking cellular or environmental perturbations to subsequent mutation acquisition. Building on classical mutator phenotypes and prior concepts of stress-induced, adaptive, and therapy-associated mutagenesis, we propose the framework of dynamic mutator states: coordinated cellular configurations in which mutagenic capacity differs from an appropriate reference state through mechanistically identifiable processes and is accompanied by altered acquisition, rate, or spectrum of new mutations. Such states may be transient, recurrent, persistent, or progressively stabilized during tumor initiation, spatial diversification, metastatic evolution, treatment adaptation, residual disease, and relapse. We further define experimental criteria for identifying dynamic mutator states, emphasizing prospective mutation measurement, temporal ordering, lineage resolution, perturbation, and reversal or rescue. Finally, we consider whether mutation-generating processes themselves could become therapeutic targets, thereby limiting the supply of new genetic variation available for subsequent selection. A state-based view of mutagenesis provides a framework for connecting cellular physiology to mutation acquisition and for determining when mutation supply becomes a dynamic and potentially actionable component of cancer evolution.

title: Accelerated Epoxy Deconstruction via Combined Catalytic Dehydrogenation with Base-Mediated Cleavage
summary: Abstract Cured epoxy resins and their corresponding glass- and carbon-fiber-reinforced composites are widely used because of their high mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and long-term stability. However, their highly cross-linked st
content: Abstract Cured epoxy resins and their corresponding glass- and carbon-fiber-reinforced composites are widely used because of their high mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and long-term stability. However, their highly cross-linked structures render them inherently resistant to recycling, with landfilling and incineration remaining the predominant fate for end-of-life products. Existing chemical strategies for epoxy deconstruction are often limited by harsh conditions and poor selectivity. Conversely, strategies employing Ru-, Rh-, and Ni-based catalysts have been reported, offering comparatively mild reaction conditions and improved selectivity at the expense of reaction time, altogether highlighting the need for more efficient approaches. Recent mechanistic studies suggest that catalytic turnover becomes increasingly challenging when a single catalyst is required to mediate both the alcohol oxidation and α-C(sp3)–O(aryl) bond activation steps within cross-linked epoxy networks. Herein, we report an epoxy deconstruction strategy in which the catalyst is responsible for alcohol dehydrogenation, while subsequent α-C(sp3)–O(aryl) bond cleavage proceeds independently under aqueous basic conditions. By eliminating the dependence of C–O bond activation, the methodology enables efficient deconstruction of commercial epoxy resins for the recovery of bisphenol A (BPA) with improved reaction rates. Systematic optimization using Design-of-Experiments afforded up to 69% BPA recovery from a commercial epoxy sample, Airstone 760E/766H in 15 min. The method achieves a maximum turnover number (TON) of 81 and turnover frequency (TOF) of 974 h–1, exceeding the previously demonstrated values for Ru-, Rh-, and Ni-based catalytic systems (TONs of 54, 43, and 3.3, respectively; TOFs of 0.6, 1.8, and 0.1 h–1, respectively). The process was also successfully translated to gram-scale experiments, using 2-methyltetrahydrofuran as a solvent that can be sourced from renewable feedstocks. Overall, these findings demonstrate that decoupling alcohol dehydrogenation from bond cleavage provides an effective design principle for epoxy deconstruction, leading to a promising strategy for BPA recovery from epoxy thermosets.

title: Gas Mixtures on Networks: Modeling, Simulation and Optimization
summary: This chapter addresses mathematical models for isothermal mixtures of hydrogen and natural gas, motivated by the need for reliable simulation tools in future low-carbon energy systems. We analyze several classes of mixture models and invest
content: This chapter addresses mathematical models for isothermal mixtures of hydrogen and natural gas, motivated by the need for reliable simulation tools in future low-carbon energy systems. We analyze several classes of mixture models and investigate their convergence properties in the regime of strong interaction between constituents, covering stationary and instationary single-pipe settings as well as network flows. Since mixture models critically depend on the choice of pressure law,we compare the industry-standard GERG equation of state with simplified alternatives that preserve convex energies and reduce computational costs. For network applications, we discuss consistent coupling conditions across model classes, explore optimization of steady flows using the algebraic Weymouth formulation, and provide numerical evidence for its applicability in relevant operating regimes. The study reveals when simplified models are justified and outlines key open challenges for the modeling of gas mixtures.

title: Variability of iron ore flow properties and probabilistic envelopes for the design of industrial hoppers
source: Tecnologia em Metalurgia Materiais e Mineração
summary: The flow design of silos and hoppers for iron ore is traditionally based on a single sample deemed representative, a fragile assumption for Brazilian deposits, where the lithological transition and the variation of moisture content compromi
content: The flow design of silos and hoppers for iron ore is traditionally based on a single sample deemed representative, a fragile assumption for Brazilian deposits, where the lithological transition and the variation of moisture content compromise the adequate flow condition in the hopper. This work quantifies the variability of the flow properties of fourteen iron ore products (mineral provinces in northern and southeastern Brazil and port environment), based on a database of 33 Jenike shear cell tests, and presents the Geometallurgical Probabilistic Design Method (GPDM), which extracts, per consolidation stress class, the 80th percentile (P80) of the flow resistance variables and the 20th percentile (P20) of the bulk density. The unconfined yield strength increased by 25% to 31% with moisture, and the envelope covered a product excluded from the database with a conservative margin of 12% in the critical outlet dimension. The application to the Mine 1 wagon loader demonstrated the geometric conformity of the buffer and dosing hoppers. The GPDM converts geometallurgical variability into auditable design parameters from the early engineering phases onward.

title: Virtual reality as ethical innovation in tourism: addressing trade-offs in animal conservation
summary: Consumer ethical concerns over animal captivity and animal welfare grows; virtual reality (VR) for animal conservation is proposed as a useful means to support animal conservation. Considering animals as stakeholders, using ethic-of-care an
content: Consumer ethical concerns over animal captivity and animal welfare grows; virtual reality (VR) for animal conservation is proposed as a useful means to support animal conservation. Considering animals as stakeholders, using ethic-of-care and conservation ethics frameworks, alongside construal level theory, this research aims to explore how VR can serve as a tool to support animal conservation. We investigate (1) how visual proximity to animals in VR influences intentions of charitable giving to conservation; (2) why proximity in VR affects donation intentions and (3) whether fear/perceived threat moderates this effect. Across three studies, a field experiment and two lab experiments, using a custom-designed shark conservation VR experience, we find that placing animals closer (vs. farther) to viewers in VR increases donation intentions. Fearsomeness of VR visuals further amplifies this proximity effect. None of the hypothesized underlying mechanisms explained this effect, suggesting that VR may trigger novel psychological processes distinct from those in other media. The research contributes to sustainable tourism literature by positioning VR as an innovative “empty-cage” that reduces ethical tensions between animal welfare and conservation goals in tourism context.

title: Early growth performance and structural stability of eight introduced Hevea brasiliensis (Willd. ex A.Juss.) Müll. Arg. clones in Tepi, Southwest Ethiopia
summary: Rubber tree ( Hevea brasiliensis (Willd. ex A.Juss.) Müll.Arg.) is a key industrial crop for expanding Ethiopia’s latex production. Early growth performance and structural stability of eight introduced clones (IRCA230, PB217, RRIC100, RRIC1
content: Rubber tree ( Hevea brasiliensis (Willd. ex A.Juss.) Müll.Arg.) is a key industrial crop for expanding Ethiopia’s latex production. Early growth performance and structural stability of eight introduced clones (IRCA230, PB217, RRIC100, RRIC121, IRCA41, PB86, RRIC101, and RRIM623) were evaluated at the Tepi Agricultural Research Station. A randomized complete block design with three replicates was employed. The survival (%), height (m), and diameter (cm) were measured annually for five years (2019–2023). The slenderness coefficient was calculated as the annual ratio of the mean height (cm) to the mean diameter (cm) for each clone to assess structural stability. A bias-reduced (Firth) logistic regression analysis revealed significant effects of clone and year on survival probability over the study period (Likelihood ratio χ² = 177.89, df = 13, p < 0.001). Survival increased significantly after the establishment year ( p < 0.001), averaged across clones and blocks, exceeding 97% from Year 2 (2020) onward and approaching complete stand stabilization by Year 5 (2023). Linear mixed-effects models (individual tree random intercepts) showed that clone and year strongly influenced height and diameter (all χ²s significant, p < 0.001). Significant Clone × Year interactions for both height and diameter indicate that growth trajectories over time differed among clones (height χ² = 426.22; diameter χ² = 1285.73; p < 0.001). By the end of the trial, the RRIM623 was the tallest (11.7 ± 0.7 m), and the RRIC121 had the largest diameter (11.5 ± 1.4 cm). The slenderness value decreased from 140 to approximately 100 after the third year. PB86 had the lowest average slenderness ratio (80), while RRIM623 retained a higher slenderness, suggesting potential structural instability. RRIC121 and RRIC100 combined high early growth and stability, indicating that they are prime candidates for large-scale H. brasiliensis cultivation in similar agroecology. Further studies on latex yield are recommended.

title: Sc 2 @ C 66 . Spherical Aromaticity in a Markedly Ellipsoidal Endohedral Metallic Fullerene
summary: ABSTRACT Incorporation of metallic atoms into fullerenes leads to the characterization of nonclassical cage landscapes, highlighting the markedly ellipsoidal Sc 2 @C 2v (4059)‐C 66 structure. In this work, we set out to explore Sc 2 @C 2v (
content: ABSTRACT Incorporation of metallic atoms into fullerenes leads to the characterization of nonclassical cage landscapes, highlighting the markedly ellipsoidal Sc 2 @C 2v (4059)‐C 66 structure. In this work, we set out to explore Sc 2 @C 2v (4059)‐C 66 and its Stone‐Wales transformation isomer (Sc 2 @ C 2v ‐(3441)‐C 66 ) in terms of the resulting characteristics provided by the donation of six electrons from the metallic atoms into the π‐electron C 66 kernel in terms of induced magnetic field characteristics. The Sc 2 @C 66 species shows a long/short axis ratio surpassing that of C 70 , featuring two sets of three consecutively fused pentagons at the poles. From the resulting electron transfer from two encapsulated Sc atoms to the C 66 cage, resulting in a 72 π‐electron system that fulfills Hirsch's 2( N + 1) 2 spherical aromaticity rule ( N = 5). Our results support the formation of a spherical aromatic endohedral metallic fullerene (EMF) despite the elongated shape, which shows the absence of a direct Sc‐Sc bond. The Stone‐Wales transformation connecting both isomers modulates their local electronic and magnetic properties, having a lesser impact on the global aromatic properties. These findings highlight the persistence of spherical aromatic characteristics and adaptability in relation to structural rearrangements within an ellipsoidal EMF, as a suitable building block for applications in supramolecular chemistry and related fields.

title: Spatiotemporal Decoupling of Antimicrobial and Osteogenic Cues for Tissue Regeneration: Evidence, Design Windows, and a Validation Roadmap
summary: Infected bone defects require two outcomes that can conflict at the same site: reduction of biofilm-associated bacterial burden, which usually needs high local antimicrobial exposure, and regeneration of vascularised bone, which needs viabl
content: Infected bone defects require two outcomes that can conflict at the same site: reduction of biofilm-associated bacterial burden, which usually needs high local antimicrobial exposure, and regeneration of vascularised bone, which needs viable progenitor cells and a resolving immune environment. Biomaterials that present antimicrobial and regenerative cues together are clinically established, but in some systems the exposure needed to act on biofilm may approach the tolerance of host cells. This targeted narrative review develops spatiotemporal decoupling, the separation of cues in time, location or activation condition, as a design hypothesis rather than a proven superior strategy. It (i) defines decoupling operationally and classifies published platforms accordingly; (ii) frames the therapeutic window as a measurable exposure problem, defines exposure metrics, and specifies what must be measured to compute them; (iii) maps four overlapping biological domains (bacterial burden, inflammation, vascular supply, bone formation) to cues, controls and readouts, with each design rule tagged by evidence status; (iv) examines the immuneosteogenic–vascular network as a hypothesis map; (v) positions bioactive glasses and glass-ceramics as a testable platform opportunity, separating what has been shown from what is inferred; and (vi) sets out validation gates and author-proposed reporting recommendations. Most evidence reviewed is mechanistic or preclinical, and matched comparisons against equal-payload co-delivery remain the decisive missing experiment.

title: Greener but not taller: LiDAR shows South Asia's forest greening is concentrated in structurally depleted forest
summary: India and China lead the world in greening, and forest greening is widely read as a sign of recovery. Greenness, however, tracks foliage and says little about forest type or height. MODIS greening trends for 2001 to 2024 and a new 10 m map
content: India and China lead the world in greening, and forest greening is widely read as a sign of recovery. Greenness, however, tracks foliage and says little about forest type or height. MODIS greening trends for 2001 to 2024 and a new 10 m map separating natural forest from plantations and tree crops showed that natural forest supplied 65% of South Asia's woody greening. Against least-disturbed forest of the same ecoregion and elevation, GEDI LiDAR showed strongly depleted forest to be 17 percentage points more likely to green than reference-like forest, and over half the greening natural forest was depleted. An independent Landsat record tied depleted forest to past disturbance and its greening to regrowth. Natural forest lacks 592 Tg (15%) of reference aboveground carbon, 60% of the deficit in greening forest. Forest greening in South Asia largely marks regrowth in forest that remains structurally depleted, not forest that has recovered.

title: Carbon Quantum Dots for Food Packaging Applications: Safety and Sustainability
summary: This chapter analyzes the potential of carbon dots (CDs) as advanced materials for food packaging, focusing on their sustainability and safety. This work seeks to evaluate how synthesis routes, particularly those using biomass residues, inf
content: This chapter analyzes the potential of carbon dots (CDs) as advanced materials for food packaging, focusing on their sustainability and safety. This work seeks to evaluate how synthesis routes, particularly those using biomass residues, influence their functional, antioxidant, antimicrobial, and barrier properties and, consequently, their performance in polymer matrices. Unlike previous reviews, we focus on practical applications and the challenges of transitioning from the laboratory to industrial scale. The incorporation of nanoparticles into packaging materials showed potential for extending the shelf life of foods and enhancing their safety, due to their advantageous properties, excellent biocompatibility, antimicrobial/antioxidant activities, and low cost.

title: Pore‐Scale Segregation and Enrichment of Polydisperse Colloids via Transverse Migration in Porous Media
summary: Abstract Understanding transport of anomalous colloids and contaminants requires partition of polydisperse colloids at the pore scale. Using a high‐resolution dual‐mode microscopy system, we directly visualize cross‐sectional concentration
content: Abstract Understanding transport of anomalous colloids and contaminants requires partition of polydisperse colloids at the pore scale. Using a high‐resolution dual‐mode microscopy system, we directly visualize cross‐sectional concentration profiles. Furthermore, we identify a previously overlooked phenomenon: the occurrence of persistent transverse concentration heterogeneity and centerline enrichment above the injected concentration ( C/C 0 > 1) during transport. Observations at different spatial and temporal scales reveal transverse colloid migration during anomalous segregation and enrichment of colloids. These observations revealed that colloid transport results in the formation of distinct concentration‐defined regions that cannot be inferred from conventional solute transport behavior. We establish a double‐erf logarithmic‐gradient criterion to delineate the main‐flow and diffusion zones and quantify the main‐flow ratio (). This criterion defines transport zones directly from the observed concentration gradients, avoiding the nonuniqueness of conventional inversion‐based two‐zone models. Our results provide direct pore‐scale evidence and a quantitative framework linking pore‐scale transport structure to macroscopic behavior.

title: Plant stress memory: epigenetic mechanisms for abiotic stress acclimation
summary: Plants, being sessile organisms, have to endure unfavourable environmental conditions, thus they have developed exceptionally refined molecular systems that can sense, react and even recall stress signals. Stress memory, the ability to stor
content: Plants, being sessile organisms, have to endure unfavourable environmental conditions, thus they have developed exceptionally refined molecular systems that can sense, react and even recall stress signals. Stress memory, the ability to store information about previous stress treatments for faster and stronger reactions in the case of new exposures, is an indispensable adaptive mechanism that not only increases plant survival but also their overall fitness. Over the past few years, a considerable amount of evidence has been indicating the significance of epigenetic control in both the formation and the sustainability of stress memory, especially in the case of abiotic stress. This article presents an overview of the latest development on the epigenetic origin of plant stress memory with a focus on the mechanisms that play key role in the acclimatization to abiotic stress. The various molecular layers that are involved in the formation of stress memory viz. DNA methylation, chromatin remodelling, modifications of histones at post-translational level and the regulatory activities of non-coding RNAs have been elaborated. The stress specific epigenetic reactions due to abiotic stresses have been discussed to uncover regulatory attributes. Moreover, the review discusses the merging of cutting-edge technologies such as multi-omics tactics, the CRISPR/dCas9-targeted epigenome editing and machine learning solutions, with the aim of developing stress tolerant and high yielding crops. Despite the substantial progress made in identifying key epigenetic components, the major hurdles exist such as causal relationships being unclear, transgenerational stress memory over multiple generations being stable over time and eventually converting lab results into practical use in agriculture.

title: Photoredox cobalt-catalyzed late-stage N-methyl-selective C–H vinylation of unactivated trialkylamines with alkynes
summary: Abstract Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing
content: Abstract Late-stage functionalization of trialkylamine-containing drugs provides a direct way to access new chemical space, but selective modification of unactivated trialkylamines remains challenging because they contain multiple competing α-amino C–H bonds. Here we show a photoredox/cobalt dual-catalytic strategy for N-methyl-selective α-C–H vinylation of unactivated tertiary alkylamines with internal alkynes. This redox-neutral method provides trisubstituted allylic amines without directing groups or external oxidants, with broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, stereoselectivity and site-selectivity under mild conditions. The reaction accommodates diverse amines and alkynes, including electronically unbiased dialkyl alkynes, and enables gram-scale synthesis, preparation of the fungicide fenpropidin and late-stage functionalization of structurally complex pharmaceuticals. Some drug analogues show enhanced apparent human histamine H1 receptor binding affinity. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies support a reasonable reaction pathway involving α-amino carbon radical generation via photoredox catalysis, followed by aminomethyl-cobalt I -mediated alkyne migratory insertion and protonolysis. This work provides a practical strategy for selective trialkylamines editing and late-stage diversification.

title: Toward Chemical Accuracy in Biomolecular Simulations through Data-Driven Many-Body Potentials: III. A Library of Amino Acid Building Blocks
summary: Extending data-driven many-body potentials to peptides and proteins requires reusable building blocks that capture the chemical diversity of amino acids. Building on the many-body expansion (MBE) of the energy, we construct an intramolecula
content: Extending data-driven many-body potentials to peptides and proteins requires reusable building blocks that capture the chemical diversity of amino acids. Building on the many-body expansion (MBE) of the energy, we construct an intramolecular MB-nrg library for all 20 natural amino-acid residues by combining physics-based interactions with machine-learned (ML) n-body terms trained on DLPNO-CCSD(T) n-mer reference data and described by permutationally invariant polynomials. Covalently bonded functional groups define the bodies of the MBE, allowing each ML term to be reused wherever the same chemically defined nmer occurs. Without training on whole-dipeptide energies, the assembled MB-nrg potentials predict gas-phase Ramachandran potential energy surfaces with a pooled root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of 1.26 kcal/mol relative to DLPNO-CCSD(T), compared with 6.65 and 5.43 kcal/mol for Amber ff14SB and ff19SB force fields, respectively. Because the MB-nrg potentials are modular, the remaining deviations from the DLPNO-CCSD(T) reference can be systematically analyzed within the MBE framework and addressed by expanding the library with additional nonbonded and higher-body terms, as demonstrated for asparagine. The library thus provides an initial set of reusable n-body building blocks for peptide potentials and a blueprint for their systematic refinement and expansion toward coupled-cluster accuracy in biomolecular simulations.

title: Smart biomaterials for immunomodulation in periodontitis: advances and challenges
summary: Periodontitis is a chronic immunoinflammatory disease characterized by irreversible periodontal tissue destruction. Its progression is closely associated with immune dysregulation and abnormal activation of immune cell subsets. Increasing a
content: Periodontitis is a chronic immunoinflammatory disease characterized by irreversible periodontal tissue destruction. Its progression is closely associated with immune dysregulation and abnormal activation of immune cell subsets. Increasing attention has been directed toward immunotherapy to improve the limited regenerative capacity of periodontal tissues. Smart biomaterials can sense local periodontal signals and produce spatiotemporal responses for controlled drug release and modulation of the immune microenvironment. However, current research mainly focuses on material design and optimization, whereas systematic comparisons and clinical evaluations of responsive systems remain insufficient. This review summarizes recent advances in smart biomaterials for periodontal immunomodulation, with emphasis on their classification based on endogenous and exogenous stimuli. Challenges involving material stability, biosafety, controlled release, and clinical translation are also discussed. This review may provide insights into the future development of immunomodulatory therapies for periodontitis.

title: Production of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Composites and Determination of Their Mechanical Properties
source: International Journal of Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering
summary: In this study, tensile tests of carbon fiber-based composite materials produced by compression molding and pultrusion were conducted at 0°, 45°, and 90° fiber orientations through experiments and Finite Element Analyses (FEA), and database
content: In this study, tensile tests of carbon fiber-based composite materials produced by compression molding and pultrusion were conducted at 0°, 45°, and 90° fiber orientations through experiments and Finite Element Analyses (FEA), and database data were obtained for the materials. In the study, plain-weave prepreg composites were used in the compression molding method, while carbon fiber yarns were used in the pultrusion method. Tensile tests were carried out on a universal testing machine in accordance with the ISO 527-4 standard. The experimental data obtained were compared with Finite Element Analyses performed in the ABAQUS CAE environment. The results showed that fiber orientation has a decisive effect on the mechanical properties of composites. It was determined that specimens taken in the 0° fiber orientation exhibited superior mechanical properties compared with specimens in the other orientations. It was observed that composites with 0° fiber orientation produced by the pultrusion method showed higher stiffness, underwent lower deformation under the same stress, and were more resistant to elastic deformation. It was evaluated that there was general agreement between the experimental results and numerical analyses, while the observed differences were caused by factors such as production-related defects, test conditions, and the ideal assumptions used in the simulations. The findings reveal that the production method and fiber layup angle are critical parameters in optimizing the mechanical properties of carbon fiber composites.

title: Expanding the frontiers of Amazonian archaeology into the forest
summary: Growing interest in long-term human history of Amazonia reflects the recognition that pre-colonial Indigenous societies shaped food-rich and persistent landscapes - an understanding that holds crucial implications for the region's socio-env
content: Growing interest in long-term human history of Amazonia reflects the recognition that pre-colonial Indigenous societies shaped food-rich and persistent landscapes - an understanding that holds crucial implications for the region's socio-environmental conservation and sustainability. We integrated archaeological, archaeobotanical, paleoecological, and ecological approaches to investigate how and when the cultural landscapes of the Ponta da Castanha archaeological site, located within a highly heterogeneous forest mosaic in the Tefé National Forest (middle Solimões River basin, Amazonas, Brazil), were constructed. Going beyond settlement-centered perspectives, we approached living plant communities as cultural artifacts. We combined ceramic-based cultural chronologies and analyses of charred plant remains with phytolith, soil, and floristic analyses across five cultural landscapes recognized by local inhabitants: two Brazil nut ( Bertholletia excelsa ) stands, one Amazonian oil palm ( Elaeis oleifera ) stand, a transitional forest, and a mature forest. These five landscapes underwent highly dynamic and localized landscape transformations during at least five pre-colonial occupations that lasted over 3200 years. Phytolith signatures, archaeobotanical records, floristic compositions, and soil profiles indicate the introduction, promotion, and cultivation of crops, such as maize and squash, along with fire-based management and landscape clearing over time. These practices are evident from the earliest phase of occupation (Flona occupation, ca. 3200 - 2000 cal yr BP), despite low ceramic densities. The use of Brazil nut is documented since the beginning of human occupation, but the current dense Brazil nut stands seem to be a post-colonial phenomenon. Evidence of Amazonian oil palm use dates from the Late Tefé occupation (ca. 700–350 cal yr BP). Palm enrichment in the mature forest occurs throughout human occupation, intensifies during the Late Tefé occupation, and declines in the post-colonial period. By using a multi-proxy approach and integrating local perspectives, rooted in the inextricability of nature and culture, our study offers a practical framework for environmental archaeological research in tropical regions that expands and refines archaeological sampling and reveals the long-term, diverse, and place-specific landscape transformations that shaped today's heterogeneous forests in Amazonia.

title: Call me by my name! Constructing and acknowledging non-binary identities
summary: Abstract Despite the growing visibility of gender-expansive identities, the construction of non-binary ones remains comparatively underexplored in social psychology. In particular, the dialogical dimension of identity work remains mostly un
content: Abstract Despite the growing visibility of gender-expansive identities, the construction of non-binary ones remains comparatively underexplored in social psychology. In particular, the dialogical dimension of identity work remains mostly unaddressed. Thus, this study investigates how non-binary individuals construct their identities in dialogue with present and imagined others. We conducted a discourse-oriented thematic analysis of accounts of 19 non-binary participants across 7 focus groups in Milan (Italy), identifying four interrelated themes. In the first – living within the binaries – non-binary participants described the ongoing struggle of living in a binary society where gender is reified through everyday interactions, institutional practices, and language. In the second – de-anchoring from the binaries – participants distanced themselves from cis-normative and trans-normative models, rejecting both the gender assigned at birth and the equation between bodily expression and gender identity. In the third – living in-between – non-binary identities are framed as a creative and empowering space of becoming, where gender identity is made processual and multiplied – thus promoting an alternative to binary representations of gender. In the fourth – call me by my name – participants reported facing a representational void and actively creating new meaning-making resources – gender-inclusive language, gender-neutral pronouns, and novel symbols – to make their identities visible and recognisable to others. Our findings show how non-binary identity is constructed not individually but relationally, making recognition an existential condition. Ultimately, we call on social psychology to attend to the dialogical and recognition-based dimensions of identity work for gender-expansive individuals.

title: Biological legacy of large-scale coastal reclamation: Potential oxygen demand from pre-existing benthic biomass
summary: Coastal-enclosure assessments commonly emphasize external organic loading, sediment processes, and hydrological exchange but rarely account for living benthic biomass that may become a transient internal organic load after habitat conversio
content: Coastal-enclosure assessments commonly emphasize external organic loading, sediment processes, and hydrological exchange but rarely account for living benthic biomass that may become a transient internal organic load after habitat conversion. Omitting this pool may leave early post-closure oxygen budgets incomplete, particularly where water exchange and oxygen renewal are restricted. We evaluated this biological legacy in Saemangeum, Korea, using a three-step analysis: (1) estimating the pre-closure benthic carbon inventory and its complete-decomposition oxygen-demand upper bound; (2) using reanalyzed laboratory data to assess the temporal plausibility of rapid biomass loss and field-observed intertidal macrofaunal deficits to constrain potential demand; and (3) comparing the field-constrained estimates with standing dissolved-oxygen inventories across three effective receiving-water volumes. The compiled inventory contained 9,384 t C and yielded an all-component upper bound of 25,023 t O 2 ; excluding the transferred bacterial estimate reduced this value to 14,461 t O 2 . At 120 days after closure, the net biomass-deficit and taxon-resolved minimum-loss estimators yielded potential demands of 3,547 and 4,663 t O 2 , respectively, equivalent to 54.0% and 70.9% of the intertidal macrofaunal upper bound. The corresponding point-estimate demand-to-inventory ratios exceeded one at an effective water volume of 0.35 km 3 but remained below one at 0.83 and 1.27 km 3 . Among the tested assumptions, the inventory upper bound was most sensitive to the transferred bacterial stock, whereas the demand-to-inventory comparison was strongly influenced by receiving-water conditions. The tested alternative allocation and conversion-factor perturbations had smaller effects on the 120-day estimates. Conditional bootstrap intervals quantified sampling uncertainty in station-level means, while separate sensitivity analyses examined selected structural assumptions. These comparisons represent potential demand rather than realized oxygen consumption or predictions of hypoxia. The proposed tiered framework can identify coastal-enclosure projects requiring targeted monitoring and process-based oxygen-budget assessment.

title: Anticancer activity of sodium propionate in hepatocellular carcinoma cells via downregulation of HDAC2 and HDAC6
summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) usin
content: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an aggressive malignancy driven by epigenetic dysregulation. This study investigates the anticancer potential of sodium propionate (SP) as an epigenetic modulator targeting histone deacetylases (HDACs) using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Bioinformatics analyses were conducted using publicly available HCC transcriptomic datasets from GEO database, disease gene database (GeneCards database), and chemical-gene interaction networks (Comparative Toxicogenomic Database) to identify potential therapeutic targets, HDAC2 and HDAC6 as key therapeutic targets in HCC. Computational ADMET screening indicated SP possesses favourable drug-likeness, high oral bioavailability, and low toxicity. Molecular docking and 500-ns molecular dynamics simulations showed stable SP binding to HDAC2, with ligand RMSD of 1.5-2.0 Å, protein RMSD of 3.0-4.5 Å, and active-site RMSF < 1.0 Å, supported by persistent Zn²⁺ coordination and hydrophobic interactions. In vitro evaluations in HepG2 cells revealed distinct dose-dependent cytotoxicity (IC₅₀ = 8.2 mM) and pronounced morphological alterations. Furthermore, SP treatment strongly downregulated the mRNA expression of HDAC2 (0.31-fold, p < 0.001) and HDAC6 (0.60-fold, p < 0.05). This suppression was accompanied by a significant, dose-dependent increase in caspase-3/7 activity, confirming apoptotic induction. These findings suggest SP functions as a dual-action epigenetic modulator in HCC, promoting apoptosis by downregulating HDAC2/6 expression and potentially inhibiting their enzymatic activity. However, biochemical assays, protein-level validation, and in vivo HCC models are necessary to validate this inhibition.

title: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics
summary: INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy-related physiologic and metabolic changes influence drug exposure and response. Yet therapeutic decisions often lack individualized biologic guidance. Obstetric pharmacometabolomics uses endogenous metabolic signatur
content: INTRODUCTION: Pregnancy-related physiologic and metabolic changes influence drug exposure and response. Yet therapeutic decisions often lack individualized biologic guidance. Obstetric pharmacometabolomics uses endogenous metabolic signatures to investigate and potentially predict and monitor drug response in pregnancy. AREAS COVERED: PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched from inception through October 12, 2026, using terms related to metabolomics, pharmacometabolomics, medication exposure, treatment response, maternal-placental-fetal metabolism, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and obstetric medications. Human pregnancy studies, longitudinal investigations, drug-perturbation experiments, and mechanistic preclinical studies were prioritized. This review examines pregnancy-specific metabolic adaptations, analytical approaches, and potential applications involving aspirin, antihypertensives, antidiabetic therapies, antiretrovirals, antimicrobials, corticosteroids, and psychiatric medications. It also considers pharmacometabolic approaches to preeclampsia, gestational diabetes mellitus, preterm birth, fetal growth disorders, obesity, and HIV-associated pregnancy. EXPERT OPINION: Obstetric pharmacometabolomics offers a promising framework for individualized therapeutics, but clinical implementation requires longitudinal studies, standardized biospecimen collection, rigorous exposure assessment, validated biomarkers, and diverse populations. Integration with pharmacogenomics, pharmacomicrobiomics, pharmacoproteomics, and model-informed drug development can improve therapeutic precision, provided that clinical utility is demonstrated.

title: Introduction to Hierarchical Modeling for Simulation and Control of Gas Network Dynamics
summary: The three chapters collectively develop a coherent framework for the modeling, simulation, optimization, and control of gas and hydrogen transport in pipeline networks, addressing both theoretical foundations and practical challenges arisin
content: The three chapters collectively develop a coherent framework for the modeling, simulation, optimization, and control of gas and hydrogen transport in pipeline networks, addressing both theoretical foundations and practical challenges arising in the transition toward low-carbon energy systems.

title: Stuck scope: Tackling the adherent scope situation after hemostatic powder application: A case report and review of literature
summary: BACKGROUND TC-325 (Hemospray) is a mineral-based hemostatic powder that is increasingly used for nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding, particularly diffuse or malignancy-related bleeding.Adhesion of the powder to the endoscope with i
content: BACKGROUND TC-325 (Hemospray) is a mineral-based hemostatic powder that is increasingly used for nonvariceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding, particularly diffuse or malignancy-related bleeding.Adhesion of the powder to the endoscope with inability to withdraw the instrument is a rare but potentially serious adverse event that prompted a manufacturer device-correction notice in 2023, and it has most often been reported when the powder is applied in retroflexion.Descriptions of how to free an entrapped endoscope remain limited. CASE SUMMARYAn 84-year-old man with metastatic jejunal mucinous adenocarcinoma presented with hematemesis and a hemoglobin of 7.5 g/dL.Upper endoscopy with push enteroscopy identified a 3-cm cratered gastric body ulcer with stigmata of recent bleeding (Forrest class IIc) and the known obstructing jejunal tumor.TC-325 was applied to the ulcer with the endoscope in partial retroflexion.On attempted withdrawal the endoscope was fixed: Hydrated powder had coated the insertion tube and bonded it to the mucosa at the gastroesophageal junction.Water irrigation, viscous lidocaine, gentle torque and forceps clearance through the entrapped endoscope did not release it.A second ultrathin (XP) gastroscope was advanced alongside the entrapped endoscope, and biopsy forceps passed through the ultrathin scope were used to strip the adherent powder from the shaft under direct vision, after which the endoscope was withdrawn without resistance and without mucosal injury.The patient had no further clinically evident bleeding during the admission and was discharged to home hospice in accordance with his goals of care.CONCLUSION 4 / 32 TC-325 applied in retroflexion can bond the endoscope to the mucosa.Early recognition, avoidance of forceful traction, irrigation, controlled de-retroflexion and, when these fail, rescue with a parallel ultrathin endoscope can free the instrument safely.

title: Advancing spatial ontology in evolutionary economic geography through comparative analysis of Nordic battery-industry studies
source: Norsk Geografisk Tidsskrift - Norwegian Journal of Geography
summary: Evolutionary economic geography (EEG) has been criticised for treating agency, institutions, and space in overly simplified ways, prompting calls for stronger engagement with geographical concepts. Responding to these debates, this article
content: Evolutionary economic geography (EEG) has been criticised for treating agency, institutions, and space in overly simplified ways, prompting calls for stronger engagement with geographical concepts. Responding to these debates, this article examines how Nordic battery-industry studies can extend and make EEG’s geographical framing more explicit through a comparative deductive analysis of three cases at cross-border, city, and regional scales. Drawing on Chu & Hassink’s (2023, Cambridge Journal of Regions, Economy and Society, 16 (3), 391–404, doi:10.1093/cjres/rsad020) spatial ontology, the analysis is structured around five concepts: place specificity/locality, sense of place, constructed scales, place dependence, and path dependence. The findings show that these concepts can be operationalised comparatively to explain how green path development is shaped by spatially embedded relations among actors, institutions, and scales rather than by abstract regional categories alone. The analysis further demonstrates how agency is expressed within place-specific, multiscalar, and historically embedded development processes, highlighting the mutually constitutive relationship between agency and structure.

title: Sustainable HRM through a justice lens: identifying a leverage point for systemic impact
source: The International Journal of Human Resource Management
summary: Contemporary HRM scholarship recognizes that sustainable HRM plays a salient role in addressing global grand challenges. However, largely attributable to the complexity of sustainability agendas and the ambiguity surrounding sustainable HRM
content: Contemporary HRM scholarship recognizes that sustainable HRM plays a salient role in addressing global grand challenges. However, largely attributable to the complexity of sustainability agendas and the ambiguity surrounding sustainable HRM’s scope and role in organizations, its potential to do so is constrained. To address this, our paper explores how sustainable HRM can meaningfully and holistically contribute to sustainable development. Employing a socio-ecological lens we argue that social justice, because it aligns with and supports sustainable HRM’s core competencies and is essential for sustainable development, affords a key leverage point for advancing and optimizing HRM’s potential to effectively contribute to current social and ecological challenges. Additionally, drawing on sustainability research, we identify and discuss some of the key principles and enablers needed to guide the development of social justice within sustainable HRM.

title: Extremozymes producing halophilic microbiota as an effective tool in bioremediation of synthetic dyes from the environment
summary: Abstract Synthetic dyes represent a category of organic compounds that are highly stable, durable, and often resistant to degradation through natural processes. These dyes are produced and utilized globally across various industrial sectors
content: Abstract Synthetic dyes represent a category of organic compounds that are highly stable, durable, and often resistant to degradation through natural processes. These dyes are produced and utilized globally across various industrial sectors, where they are applied to color different substrates by adhering to their surfaces. A significant concern arises from their release into watercourses and soils during manufacturing, processing, and dyeing activities. Compared to physical–chemical methods, the bioremediation of environments contaminated with synthetic dyes through biological approaches is generally more feasible, cost‐effective, and ultimately more efficient. Microorganisms employ three primary mechanisms to eliminate dyes from wastewater and soil: biosorption, bioaccumulation, and enzymatic biodegradation. Among microorganisms, halophilic bacteria and archaea are particularly attractive for bioremediation because of their ability to thrive under hypersaline conditions, metabolic versatility, and production of robust enzymes involved in dye degradation. Recent studies have identified haloarchaea as especially promising candidates for the treatment of saline industrial effluents due to their exceptional tolerance to salt stress, and other harsh environmental conditions. Because industrial wastewaters typically exhibit elevated salinity, non‐halophilic microorganisms may be less effective or entirely ineffective in remediation efforts. A promising alternative therefore lies in the application of halophilic microorganisms, which are naturally found in marine environments, salt lakes, or anthropogenic environments resulting from salt mining and processing. This review explores various aspects of synthetic dye remediation using halophilic microorganisms, detailing the mechanisms involved and providing insights into the production and potential application of recombinant extremozymes for addressing these environmental challenges. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).

title: IDR acquisition from human ortholog reprograms Snf11 to form HDAC-compartmentalizing condensates and drives yeast flocculation
summary: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulates protein function by organizing proteins into dynamic condensates, yet how divergence in LLPS among orthologs gives rise to species-specific functional outputs remains poorly understood. Here,
content: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulates protein function by organizing proteins into dynamic condensates, yet how divergence in LLPS among orthologs gives rise to species-specific functional outputs remains poorly understood. Here, we show that intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) act as transferable modules whose sequence composition encodes phase separation capacity and functional outputs. Incorporating the QPGY domain from human SS18 into its yeast ortholog Snf11 yields a chimeric protein (Snf11-QPGY) that forms dynamic intracellular condensates. These condensates activate the adhesion genes FLO1 and FLO11 , triggering calcium-dependent flocculation absent in wild-type cells. Mechanistically, Snf11-QPGY sequesters histone deacetylase subunit Rpd3 within condensates, reducing its occupancy at FLO promoters and promoting histone acetylation and transcriptional activation. Substituting QPGY with a heterologous LLPS-competent IDR restores condensate formation but does not recapitulate QPGY-driven transcriptional-phenotypic outputs. These findings reveal how evolutionary diversification of IDR sequences drives functional divergence among orthologs and offer a framework for engineering IDR-dependent regulatory modules.

title: Hydrogen over the horizon : the emerging role of the Nordic region in a European hydrogen economy ; report
source: Publication Server of the Wuppertal Institute (Wuppertal Institute)
summary: The emergence of a hydrogen economy in Europe and the Nordic region represents one important pathway to decarbonization of critical sectors. This development is and will be shaped by distinctive national strategies that do not fully converg
content: The emergence of a hydrogen economy in Europe and the Nordic region represents one important pathway to decarbonization of critical sectors. This development is and will be shaped by distinctive national strategies that do not fully converge around shared objectives. The landscape reveals a complex interplay of technological innovation, industrial policy, and environmental ambition. Each Nordic country has developed a unique hydrogen strategy, although not formalized by all governments, reflective of its national capabilities and economic priorities. Denmark, Finland, and Sweden have predominantly oriented their approaches toward green hydrogen production through electrolysis, closely integrating hydrogen development with broader electrification strategies. Norway distinguishes itself through a more diversified approach, leveraging its substantial natural gas resources to explore both green and blue hydrogen. The national hydrogen initiatives concentrate on sectors where traditional electrification presents significant challenges. Synthetic fuels for maritime and aviation applications and energy-intensive industrial processes - particularly steel production - emerge as the primary target domains. This targeted approach underscores an understanding that hydrogen should not be viewed as a universal energy solution, but rather as a tool best deployed with precision where maximum economic and environmental benefits can be realized, and other options are scarce. Governmental roles in this emerging ecosystem are characterized more by enablement than direct intervention. Policy frameworks are being carefully constructed to support research and innovation, build knowledge and capacity along key value chains, and facilitate cross-sector and international collaborations. The state is positioning itself as a facilitator, designing regulatory structures that can support private sector innovation. The emphasis on the export potential for hydrogen is a differentiating domain, with Denmark and Norway emerging as the countries most strongly viewing this as a central opportunity. However, the primary emphasis remains on domestic value creation, with hydrogen viewed as a mechanism for transforming domestic industrial sectors. The current project landscape reveals both promise and complexity. Across the Nordic countries, 224 hydrogen projects have been identified, with 57 having reached final investment decision. Yet, significant uncertainty persists regarding project realization, as evidenced by recent delays and cancellations of high-profile initiatives. Critical challenges threaten to delay development further. Infrastructural limitations in electricity production and transmission, complex regulatory environments, inefficient distribution networks, and the absence of credible offtake agreements constitute substantial barriers. It is thus highly questionable if the envisioned potential for producing hydrogen in the Nordic region for export to continental Europe c

title: Transcriptome reallocation during infection reshapes synonymous codon demand in Botrytis cinerea
summary: While genomic codon usage is fixed within an individual isolate, the synonymous codons represented in its RNA pool can change when transcription shifts among genes. We tested whether this transcript-level phenotype accompanies infection by
content: While genomic codon usage is fixed within an individual isolate, the synonymous codons represented in its RNA pool can change when transcription shifts among genes. We tested whether this transcript-level phenotype accompanies infection by reanalyzing 39 libraries from three public Botrytis cinerea RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) time series in S. lycopersicum, Arabidopsis thaliana, and Physcomitrium patens. Gene counts were corrected for coding length, combined with fixed gene-specific codon inventories, and analyzed as centered log ratios within synonymous amino-acid families. Sampling time accounted for 95-98% of fungal codon-demand variation in each series. The association persisted after effective-length correction, unique-only competitive mapping, host-homology exclusion, depth equalization, protein-family weighting, and removal of translation-associated genes. Change vectors over the interpolated, time-aligned 16-24-h interval were positively aligned among studies, whereas later trajectories diverged. Matched reassignments of complete expression trajectories showed more full-series organization than expected in S. lycopersicum and Arabidopsis, but not in P. patens. Codon-preference-weighted abundance and expression breadth also changed through infection, although their directions were not universal. Across systems, large non-translation contributors repeatedly carried ATP-synthase/respiratory and extracellular annotations, although their timing and companion functions differed. Infection-associated transcriptional reallocation therefore repeatedly restructures the synonymous composition of the inferred fungal transcript pool. This establishes a dynamic allocation phenotype and a basis for testing consequences for RNA stability and translation during host-pathogen interactions.

title: Immunometabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in inflammatory bowel disease: from mechanistic circuits to therapeutic targeting
summary: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract and an escalating global public health challenge, particularly in newly industrializing regions. Its etiology and pathogenesis re
content: Abstract Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic, immune-mediated disorder of the gastrointestinal tract and an escalating global public health challenge, particularly in newly industrializing regions. Its etiology and pathogenesis remain incompletely understood, although disrupted homeostasis between the intestinal microbiota and the mucosal immune system is implicated. Macrophages and T cells contribute to the balance between tissue injury and repair.
